name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin
detailed_description: You are Outlander. Once adrift upon the Ageless Sea, you now find yourself on the shores of a dying world. From the consuming darkness emerges a figure cloaked in white: the Shepherd of Wayward Souls, who burdens you with the task of hunting down the remaining Guardians of the Old World. You must journey into the vast gloom to explore ancient ruins, discover forgotten secrets and battle the horrors that lurk within. Equipped with weapons of exceptional might and an inventory of powerful artifacts, you must traverse ancient crypts, sunken ruins, corrupted temples and howling forests to bring death to your enemies. But do not underestimate your adversaries, for they are great in power and number. Your mind must be as sharp as your blade if you hope to survive the dangers ahead. Fueled by legendary Quake 1 technology, the veins of WRATH pump with the DNA of revered '90s shooters. The world of WRATH is rich with engaging combat, diverse environments and captivating lore. Every element is deftly intertwined to create an authentic and enchanting experience as timeless as the games that inspired it. Highlights: Travel with the Shepherd of Wayward Souls across 3 unique hubs and 15 maps Explore a vast world shrouded in darkness, passionately crafted by the hands of longtime veterans of the Quake scene. Lay waste to 15 unique enemies lurking in the shadows, thirsting for your blood. Defeat the 3 Godlike Guardians of the Old World Exert your dominance through the aggressive dance of combat with 10 unique artifacts Comb each level thoroughly, uncovering secrets to help you survive Immerse yourself in haunting music born from the twisted mind of Andrew Hulshult (Quake Champions, Dusk, Amid Evil and DOOM Eternal: The Ancient Gods Part One).

short_description: Blast, slice and shred through your enemies in this hardcore FPS inspired by the icons of the '90s, powered by the legendary Quake-1 Tech. Taking place in a realm left to rot, take up arms, unearth long-forgotten secrets and hunt down the Guardians of the Old World.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is made with a Quake SourcePort engine, and since I really love the look and feel of Quake, I really like this game as well. It's different than Quake of course. The maps are really large with many secrets. There are new enemies compared to Quake. There is no map to help you navigate and the maps being so large, they're getting confusing some times, but overall not a problem if you save often. And about saving you better enable infinite tethers to save. This game uses a "tether" game to save, along with autosaves and save shrines. These tethers, you have to gather, so it might be a problem if you want to save often and you don't have infinite tether saving enabled in the options. The sound and ambient is perfect. You feel the isolation and this weird world to explore. The level design is very good in my opinion. It also has a system to use special artifacts that you gather and give you short bonuses like invincibility and other perks, which is a nice addition. The different weapons also feel great and you can feel the impact of the shotgun. Overall, in the end the devs delivered a good game.The reason this game had a lot of negative reviews during Early Access was because the publisher and game devs were not sincere about the progress of development. But now that is released, this is easily one of the best (if not the best) game made with a Quake SourcePort. I have not finished the game yet, but it is an easy recommendation to old school gamers like myself that like Quake.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't get it.The movement is incredibly janky, slidey, in all the worst ways.The enemies are very very stale, simplistic, and the only thing they do is turn every room they're in into bullet hell gameplay. There's just no challenge to them, nothing that makes them unpredictable or unique.The level design is bland. It looks a looooot better in the store page than whilst playing. It's all very... linear. Smooth.It is like they picked the worst games of the early 3D era to base this on. Everyone only plays those out of nostalgia, because better games with better tech came along.Even the WAD and Build engine games play a lot better than this, come on!

_childDocuments_.review: It's fantastic. A true competitor to Dusk, although we need to wait and see how the game escalates on in the later levels. For now we just have a demo, and it will last you 1-2 hours. The mechanics are in place. I can see the potential of this achieving Dusk / Amid Evil level of greatness. As for the current build, it's still a little bit rough, although it's completely playable and enjoyable. There are some issues like the AI enemies that sometimes ram themselves into a wall instead of attacking you, the balancing isn't perfect as you pick up an overpowered Goo Gun that melts big enemies, and generally plenty of ammo and health dispersed around the world even on Hard and you never had to bother using the save system / Life Siphon / other power ups. But is it worth your money? Absolutely. It's 3d Realms. They could've taken your money and ran with Ion Fury but they didn't. So I think you can trust em and support em with this Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: The FPS, yet using a particularly aging engine, therefore takes all the codes of its ancestors with bravery to allow players to evolve in levels built with intelligence, to participate in joyful and dynamic clashes and to observe sublime panoramas. However, taking the old formula literally, the title is sorely lacking in identity. We will then have to face a universe that we have already crossed 100 times. Unfortunately, this is not the only problem with retro production. The title also suffers from a certain repetition, the fault of a particularly shy bestiary.

_childDocuments_.review: Right away: the game so far is good! It has fun combat, it is fast, it is very oldschool, however, I have a few complains:For example: there are no Quicksaves, instead it works like that that you find save items and you have to place them manually!This isn't that bad on paper, but the problem is that often once you collect them or are about to collect them enemies spawn arround them and it makes getting them a pain in the ass, because often you haven't saved for 10 minutes and you just want to save again after all that ♥♥♥♥ you've done, but then the game get's cruel with it...Then there is no map, I know: Quake haven't had a Map as well, but quake had small levels, this one has super levels, meaning a level can take an hour to complete (!), there are currently 2 levels, but it took me 2 hours for the whole thing, and with that huge levels with no map, well you can think what that means.To be frank: the level design is straight forward and you don't get lost often, but there were a few instances where I did get a bit lost and ran in the false direction for a bit.Jumping isn't that great, which isn't that much of an issue, because the game isn't designed with that much of jumping in mind, but often it is hard to tell how high or how far you can jump and when it's needed it's just confusingBut there is also a lot of fun stuff in it: the game is very fast paced, there is a good chunk of enemy variety so far, each of them behave completely different and you have to use different weapons at different situations to fight them head on, and each weapon has an altfire, all though they could be tweaked (especially with the shotgun, which can be loaded to fire a stronger blast, but that blast is far to weak).I'd say wait for a later release with that, things probably get fixed and while it's already fun, is is also a bit frustrating (and I played just on normal difficulty).

_childDocuments_.review: 5 years later and the game is finally out of development hell. Was it worth it? Not exactly.While not bad, this game is easily the weakest of the new breed of retro shooters. While I completed it, it was an absolute chore to get through. Repetitive looking worlds and nothing interesting (other than a new weapon here and there) to spice up the gameplay as you progress; the first level didn't feel any different or memorable from the last. Enemy variety gets repetitive. Some of the levels are way too long. I also felt like the game itself was too long; you know how sometimes a game can overstay its welcome because it gets absolutely tedious? Unfortunately Wrath falls under that category.Cultic, Ion Fury, and Turbo OverKill are all outstanding boomer shooters that keep you in your seat from beginning to end. While I didn't hate Wrath, I simply can't recommend it when there's better options out there. 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: So I've purchased this game in its early-access days way back and played through the available content then as well (chapter 1 of 3, excluding the chapter's boss) and I was generally hyped for this one to finally reach 1.0.Now that I've played through chapter 1 again (this time including the boss) and the majority of chapter 2, I somehow – unfortunately – struggle to recommend this game. I still give a thumbs up since I don't think this is a bad game, but let me just say that I did not complete it and I'm really not sure if I actually want to finish it. I'll try to explain below.Let's start with the things I really like and think are well done. First, the graphics and general art style work perfectly for this kind of retro-inspired shooter. The game builds up a really good atmosphere, especially when also considering the music and general ambiance in the levels.I also think that the core gameplay is rock-solid. There's a good variety of weapons, each one serving its very specific purpose within the combat scenarios the game throws you into (i.e. melee, close combat, medium-ranged combat, and long ranged combat). These also feature some great design and each weapon has a secondary fire mode, mixing things up quite nicely. All of these serve late-game purposes as well, so there's no "obsolete" weapon (at least in my opinion).There's also a variety of "artifacts" that can be found throughout the game. These are basically some consumables that grant special effects for a limited amount of time, e.g. getting health back upon killing enemies or double damage. There's also some more interesting stuff, but I mostly thought these are a bit "gimmicky" and not really required to proceed.Particularly noteworthy is the melee weapon you get from the beginning of the game. This wrist blade can be used to engage in combat, obviously, and it does massive damage. Additionally, it can also be used for traversal, allowing for some mid-air jump control and in general faster movement speed (you can do some sort of lunge forward when charging up the blade). Pretty cool in my opinion!Movement is also very well done, which comes as no surprise considering the engine the game is using (source-port of the original Quake engine). So, all good in that department as well.Regarding enemies: As with the weapons, there's some decent variety here, and they all have a distinct role to play in the combat encounters (some will rush you and try to engage in melee, others stay back and fire at you from range, and so on). Since Wrath's levels feature an insane amount of enemies, these make for some quite intense combat scenarios.So this all sounds pretty good right? Unfortunately, for me at least the game kind of falls apart though because of one major flaw: Most of the levels in wrath are outright massive and often times drag on for what seems like forever. Bigger is not always better in that regard! I don't want to fight endless hordes of the same monsters in samey-looking environments for 45 to 60 minutes, it just becomes tedious. There are also rarely any "slower" parts, you are basically in combat non-stop, which just gets annoying after a while.This one major flaw basically affects all the positive stuff I've mentioned above: Enemy variety is solid, but not when your game just goes on and on and on and just lets you fight against the same types of enemies from level 1 till level 15. Same holds true for the weapons. No matter the chapter you're in, you're always fighting the same monsters you fought in the chapter that came before using the same weapons you've used all along (for the most part). Most of all the stuff Wrath has to offer (including enemies, weapons and artifacts) basically don't change all that much after 1/3rd of the game.I also have a problem with the structure of the game. There's a hub-world in each chapter where you can choose the order of levels however you like. Not sure why you would want that though in that kind of game. The problem here is: The levels have to work regardless of which one you choose first, meaning that each level basically starts the same... low-level enemies only until you find the better weapons, which is just boring. This is especially true if you consider starting each level with just the wrist blade (e.g. after dying and without any save-artifacts left in your inventory)While I'm at it, I also have to mention the save-system, which I just... hate. There's three different methods of saving in this game: There's an auto-save at the beginning of each level, there's shrines to find throughout the level (which serve as save-points while also replenishing the players health), and there saving through an artifact (basically quick-saves, but limited in number since you have to find those in the levels). Funny thing is: You can actually disable this limit in the gameplay options, so I guess they knew that this system kinda sucks? Why not just allow quick-saving/quick-loading instead of whatever this is? The most annoying part for me though: Whenever the game saves, it "freezes" for like a second, which is just annoying and immersion-breaking.So, like I said in the beginning, I don't think this is a bad game, far from it. It's actually pretty good, and the core gameplay mechanics work perfectly fine. This might also just be a "me-thing", maybe for you this whole "this game is too long" isn't that big of a deal. I just think that there are more interesting games out there within the same genre, but that's just my humble opinion. There just isn't anything super "special" about Wrath which makes it stick out from the rest.

_childDocuments_.review: My review used to be positive. That was during the early Early Access, before the game didn't receive any updates other than the skeleton crew noting their progress towards the final goal.I commend the developers for actually finishing the game. However, I honestly can't recommend WRATH for anyone.The first chapter is great and is the most fleshed out, since it hadn't been changed from Early Access. The second chapter is - without sugar coating it - terrible. All it does past the first chapter is rely on ambushes and extremely limited resources to give a sense of difficulty. Combined with enemies that can chew through your health in seconds (if you aren't dead instantly), all that does is make playing WRATH a slog than anything enjoyable.P.S. _childDocuments_.review: Wrath is a game that took a very, very long time to come out. For years, you spent thirty dollars on Episode 1, that never ever updated. The ability to choose which level you go to first is great, the sketches in the notebook are great, the enemy designs and placement and weapons are all great. The stages are huge, easily taking about an hour each, and they change depending on what weapons you have, it's incredible. It's just a great game. No complaints whatsoever; a pure-blooded boomer shooter, no fluff.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game. My feeling are complicated, and this is no straight recommendation, but here we are.I did not recommend this game while it was in early access. Its future was uncertain, and what was a solid foundation and a shaky construction above. My core issues were the development hell, the questionable encounter design, and the pacing. Well, the first is obviously fixed. So, the other two.Tweaks were made even to the old levels and weapons, and I could appreciate them well enough. Less teleport squads, smoother sailing in combat, that sort of thing. But was anything fundamentally changed? No, for better or for worse. This is still a game of intricate levels and less-than-intricate fights, for all the boomer shooter fundamentals it gets right.This ties into the other issue: the pacing. Every area's sprawling, every portal entered the starting line to an endurance race. It wears on you, really. This is not a game you burn down in one run, it's a game best enjoyed a level at the time.Something's missing though. Four years has this game been in the oven, and the additions are more of the same, for better or worse, and what little isn't... isn't that great. There's now a story. It respects the traditions of its predecessors in how little it means, but sure, you have some notes to pick up here and there.This game could have been more, I feel, but it also could not. There were things happening behind the scenes, and an end needed to be in sight, again, for better or worse.Still, it's a miracle it came out at all. It's not grabbing me, the way I hoped. For my own part, I'll keep plinking away at it as the mood strikes me, eventually beat it, and probably be, on the whole, positive about the experience. Wrath has gone over quality hump needed so that it might be the perfect 10/10 game for someone out there. That someone isn't me.

_childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS REVIEW - POST CONTENT UPDATE 1:"So far, so good!"Really loving this.  Feels like a spiritual successor to Q1 / an evolution of that design.  Sprawling marathon levels, each carefully curated and with distinct and unique art direction a la Arcane Dimensions (makes sense when you consider the people on the team).  Sound design is superb; music is tasteful and ambient, and weapons sound extremely punchy and satisfying.  Speaking of which, the weapons are all incredibly fun to use and are all useful in their own way; the coachgun might be my favorite pistol analog in any game, and it's not a junk weapon by any stretch - you'll be using it fairly often well into your play-throughs.I'm really excited to see where the team continues to take this.  So glad I grabbed this early.  Truly a must-have for any fan of old-school FPS, especially if you have any love for Q1 and Arcane Dimensions.EDIT - Post Update #2:The game continues to move in a very positive direction.  Weapon balance had been adjusted in a very good way - Shogun alt is still powerful but not OP. Fang Spitter got a goo damage buff and alt no longer trivializes Heretics. Retcher got a MUCH needed damage buff (though self damage is still way too high lol).  The new Slag Cannon is really fun.  Finally, the Coachgun continues to shine as the best pistol analog ever - decent damage buff and the alt fire tweaks have made it even more of a staple in my weapon rotation.  The player's damage output is arguably too high at times, but things still feel like a healthy challenge at the highest difficulty.The new map is not only gorgeous but really fun to play - easily my favorite map now.  I've dump almost an additional 40 hours into this game since my initial review post.  Needless to say, I'm still a huge fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros - Cant say no to Old school strafe shooters! - Fast moving, smooth and awesome controls!  - Pretty Challenging - Love how we can scale the Graphics  from Quake 1 to Quake 2-esque- Creative and Straightforward Level Design!- Unique Save System    Potential Improvements to make ( I don't use "Cons" for early access games in development) -  Perhaps bring back the Grenade Launcher, Lightning gun and Rocket Launcher? -  Have the option to Auto Save as many times as we want. Loved the new save system.. but    make it an option instead of mandatory?  -  Please Please Please ignore the request to slowdown movement speed for immersion,    story telling and ease. These are the same people who watch X Hamster for the plot and    never get invited to parties. -  Instead...Keep the story as a readme.txt novelty (think you summed it well in the outline) -  Make a troll FAQ manual like Quake addressing dumb ass questions while mocking modern fps.   -  Have the option to run at door switches, etc instead of pressing E for total Boomer     experience. Final Remarks I've found "love in a hopeless place". This is the closest thing we'll ever get to a new Quake game that relives the vibes of Quake 1. People made allot of comparisons to Turok or Hexen, but this feels more like a Quake game to me.  I'm very excited to see how this game will develop! Please don't go on the Sci Fi or Hexen route! Then again this is just my take on the game. Awesome game nonetheless!

_childDocuments_.review: There is something horribly wrong with the movement system, I can't figure out what is it exactly, but it just feels bad. Especially bad when you are on the stairs or there are height differences on the floor. Maybe it's the thing you need to get used to, will give it another try in future.---So, I did disable strafe tilting, surprisingly it fixed everything about "wrong feeling".There are still some questionable things, like inability to activate powerups while shooting, inability to switch weapon right after firing, mostly claustrophobic\dangerous to freely move environments and how powerups and saves works in general (storable activatable things).Kinda forgivable if you ask me, but I can see how it can become problem for anyone else.Can't say much about shooting, it's just ok. Maybe I'm just getting tired of it after things like Dusk or Ion Fury. Maybe there are still things to tune, like visual impact or how shots sounds. But it didn't feel as great as in other superpopular pseudo-old-school games I did play before.Areas are mostly pretty, there are a lot of secrets and places you can discover, and it will never be straight (or slightly bended) corridor even to just finish the level. Game loses pace because of it, still maintains enough speed to be entertaining. But somehow... I didn't have feeling that I want to replay level. For a note - after beating Doom Eternal on 4\5 difficulty and finding all secrets, I immediately started playthrough on 5\5 difficulty, reopened every secret again and enjoyed every bit of it. Nearly same with Dusk (started as filthy pirate, hehe). Still, maybe it's just me, I don't have anything objective to say, only feelings.After all enjoyable experience. Game can eat your time like it's mini macaroons, until you die and discover that you forgot to use that activatable quicksave. Again. And you totally don't want to replay whole section.

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed the game so far. But terribly disappointed they're charging $31.00 NZD for a game that I finished in under two hours. I got 3 of the relics and then told 'Thanks for playing'. This game should be a tenner for the current content.Aside from that I was thoroughly enjoying the challenge and game art design. A retro feel with atmosphere, and I enjoy not having my hand held. Reminded me of Shadowman, or Legacy of Kaine with Lovecraftian undertones. The movement is pretty horrible, especially on slopes.... feels like you're sliding around on ice, but I get that they're trying not to follow the tried and true Quake method of movement. I can't recommend due to the severe lack of content - basically 3 large levels and that's it. They should've waited until they had fleshed out the game some more.

Its just NOT FUN.So sadly, I really can not recommend this game, it's tedious and not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Had a smile on my face the whole time I was playing this. Now, many people say this is the real Quake 2 we always deserved (nothing against regular Q2 myself, one of my favorite games) and while that may be true, as it does use the famous Q1 engine, to me it just feels like DOOM 2 in 3D, which is of course a great thing, allow me to explain:1.The double-barreled shotgun feels exactly the same as in DOOM 2, which is a great thing. It has that same click-clack-clack reloading sound, the animation length is the same and god does it feel beefy blowing stuff away with it. Strong DOOM 2 vibes from this alone.2. They removed strafe jumping mechanic from the Quake engine. This is a negative and I just can't help but try to gain speed by strafe-jumping and here it's just not possible. This alone takes that Quake feeling out, you run more and jumping doesn't give you speed. In DOOM 2, you don't jump at all, you run and gun, I get the same feeling here. 3. The enemies feel DOOM-like to me, and not Quake-like except for that Scrag looking flying thing. The environments have a heavy gothic vibe which is amazing and I do enjoy it a lot. All in all, I have to say, after that amazing game Ion Maiden, 3D realms is onto something even better, they just know how to make these old-school games, it's just a joy to play them. As of now, this game checks all of the boxes when it comes to old-school FPS.Maze levels, check.Beefy guns with great sounds, check.Run and gun gameplay, check.Secrets, check.Great atmosphere, check.Attention to detail, check. I LOVE IT. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: is an odd case of a game beign less than the sum of it's parts. If you take all the game's different elements, the weapons, the level design, the art, the enemies, it all  like a respectable throwback shooter, but putting it all together it gradually becomes apparant that things are just . If Steam review had a sideways thumb this would definately get it, but as it stands the game is still good enough to be... .To start with the good, the level designs are  impressive even if their length does cause some issues. I think if the combat loop was better most of the issues I have with the level pacing would be gone. There are some striking visuals in  and despite the levels being absolutely massive I never got lost as to where I need to go in even the longest, most complex levels and that's certainly no small accomplishment.The weapons are also pretty good, each one has a purpose and any shooter where I'm still finding value in the basic pistol by the end of the game has done at least a little something right.Where the game really starts to fall apart is the enemies, or rather how it uses them. Each enemy in isolation is well designed, looks nice, and fills some kind of niche, but the combinations of them are where  really starts to show it's cracks.  has an odd tendency to throw the tankier, more bullet spongey enemies at you  and if you try shooting them to death you will run out of ammo pretty quickly. Despite that, your melee weapon can one or two-shot most of these tankier enemies pretty quickly. In a more considered game like  enemies like Shamblers and Vores pop in as a little surprise to switch things up, to make you stop and be more careful and engage a bit differently. In  you've got that tier of enemy popping up almost constantly, except they aren't hard because you can almost instantly kill them with your melee weapon, but they're still annoying because they usually spawn in 5 or 6 more of them after you kill that wave. The worst offender is the Cacodemon type enemy which goes down in one hit from your blade, but takes an absolutely massive amount of ammo to shoot down, so any time you encounter them, the best strategy is to bait them near you so you can melee them which takes a long time since they're pretty slow, and then once you clear them out there's a decent chance the game will spawn in another wave.That's my real beef with . The parts are all there, but the way it uses them just becomes . There's a difference between a worthwhile challenge and a rote use of dominant strategy, and  falls into the Dominant Strategy zone far too often, even as it tries to give you different combos of enemies. I found myself basically having a particular weapon or strategy for each enemy and while that's also the case in better games like  or ,  punishes you from deviating even the slightest bit by making every non-humanoid enemy an ammo sink that will drain your supplies if you don't kill them "the right way". See a lava golem? Better two-shot him with the rail-gun. Big blob-shooting guy? 3 alt-fires from the blob gun and he's done, so you better not use that weapon on the small-fry enemies. It  fun to gib a group of lesser enemies with something like the rocket launcher or the goo gun, but if you use the heavy weapons on weak enemies even once you're probably screwing yourself out of killing a tankier enemy later on and it all just feels so locked-in and rigid. If they'd just trimmed a wave or two off of most of the enemy encounters they could probably still have a fun and dynamic game, but it's so locked in that it becomes boring after a while.All that's a shame too, because taken in small doses, the game is still fun, but you have to really meter your playtime so it doesn't become too much. There were multiple points where I'd quit and go do something else in the middle of a level, not because it was too hard or I couldn't figure out what to do, but because I was just getting tired of it. At the time of this writing only 2.9% of players have even entered the third world and I think that speaks volumes, but it's also kind of a shame because that was my favorite world visually and it also gave you one of the most fun weapons in the game.There are other gripes I have too, it's absolutely crucial to go into gameplay options and disable the game's weird save system.  tries a noble, but failed experiment in making death actually mean something by having quicksaves be an expendable resources, which I should point out is one of the more maligned ideas  tried, but the problem is since the game's pacing is so off it's hard to tell when you actually should save, since a spot that feels like you're near the end of the level frequently . I was constantly mistiming my saves, and when the game's biggest issue is already tedium, forcing the player to replay a big chunk they've already played while starving them of quicksaves is insanity, and they don't really advertise that this can be disabled. I only found out about the option to turn it off when I entered the second world, and I'd estimate at least a few hours of my 18.3 hour playtime were added because of that system. The game also annoyingly puts the "restart level" button dead-center in the screen, so if you die there's a good chance you'll accidentally click on that instead of the button you want, which isn't the worst but the game's load times are rather long. I also found it annoying that they don't flash the name of the level you're about to enter before you enter their portal in the hubs, the hubs are pretty big and some of the entrances can look pretty similar, so there were a few bits where I was wandering around just trying to enter a level I hadn't gone into yet, only to find I went into the wrong one and now had to go through even more loading screens just to try again. Speaking of levels, since you can to into them in any order, I frequently saw ammo for weapons I didn't have yet and while it wasn't a huge deal and obviously is less of a problem later on as you get more of an arsenal, it is frustrating to see when ammo-scarcity can be such an issue early game.It might sound like I'm dumping on the game and there are a lot of issues, but I feel like with a year or so of tweaks this could be a really tight, lean shooter and even in its current state it's still really fun in bursts. I  the levels, I like the artwork, the atmosphere is really coold and it  fun to kill enemies. I just wish the combat encounters were pared down some or certain enemies were rebalanced to make things a bit faster. Personally I'd love to see what these levels feel like ported into , with the better weapon and enemy balancing that game has to offer. That could be really fun. If you haven't already played the real heavy hitters of the retro shooter revival like  or  yet, I'd say to play those first, and I don't think  is a real drop-everything-play-this-now kind of game, but if you like this genre and you've burnt through most of it,  is good enough to check out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm through most of the areas (working on Priory now), and I'd recommend the game but with some serious draw backs.  The game overall *kinda* feels like Hexen 2 slash Quake, but without the charm of either.  Biggest points:Pros:1. Level design is serviceable.2. Save system forces you not to save every two seconds with quick save (as quick save doesn't exist).  This is a HUGE pro for me!  I LOVE this system!Cons:1. Music - basically none.  Just ambient noises.1.5. Enemy noises - lots of groans.  Actually, except screamers, it's basically all groaning.2. Weapons are the same we've seen a million times over (pistol, shotty, minigun, grenade launcher).3. The large levels lead to SO many situations where the game spawns many flying enemies but puts them miles away from you.  The only hit scan weapon you have is the first pistol.  This just leads to frustrating fights that are super tedious.4. With a few exceptions most of the game is just peeking and popping shotty off or using the minigun (sorry, the spike gun) as it kills enemies extremely quick (I mean, granted, that's half the weapons as there's only 4 guns).  The basic enemies are fairly boring (one hitscan, one shoots blue projectiles, one basic flying enemy shoots blue projectiles, etc) so this gameplay loop just isn't very satisfying.5. Many of the levels are DARK.  Not dark as in spooky, dark as in the textures are straight up black because it's so damn dark.  That's not fun.  It leads to a completely unmemorable experience as my memory of many levels is just running into near black.6. Running down stairs = airborne, every time.  This is frustrating as hell.I think the game tries to be a middle ground between things like Quake/Serious Sam/Hexen 2, but can't really decide and can't really capture the benefits that either provide.  Big open levels with lots of flying enemies a la Serious Sam?  Ok, then give me a sniper or a true hitscan minigun and actually give me lots of room to maneuver.  Close quarters and nitty gritty?  Ok, then you need more enemies that are melee oriented.  Actually, I think adding a lot of melee type enemies would improve the game in every aspect.A gore-y nightmare aesthetic isn't enough to carry a shooter and isn't by itself what made Quake fun.EDIT: I've come back weeks later and I still haven't finished this game.  I put it down one day and since then I've had zero desire to come back.  The boring sound and music design, boring flying enemy fights without a good hitscan weapon, and the overall MEH attitude I have towards the game isn't drawing me back.As such, I'm changing my review to a negative.  The enemy sound design, music, and pacing just aren't fun.  I just don't see any strong aspect of this game that would draw me to it over any other Doom/Quake/Serious Sam -esque games.

_childDocuments_.review: It really pains me to have to write this review, because I want to love Wrath: Aeon of Ruin. It's a fun game, based off of old-school Quake source code magic. The world is very well thought out and evokes that 90's old-school shooter vibe, right down to the Godspeed You! Black Emperor otherworldly Dead Flag Blues vibe the world gives off. The combat is good, but I honestly don't think it's a whole lot to write home about, especially compared to the games that the genre produced while this game was stuck in development hell for five years.The problem I have with this game is that it's too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ long. This by itself isn't a problem - but I am a sufferer of ADHD and the way I play boomer shooters (taking in the sights, tasting/chewing/digesting the combat, making little asides to find the roughly 20 secrets per level), the levels take an hour and thirty minutes to two hours for me to finish. Two hours per level at max is a pretty big ask for me, and the game itself has to justify it. I will gladly pour 20 hours into something like a full playthrough of Doom Eternal, because that game is very, very good at putting me into a murderous rampage headspace. However, that's the product of thousands of hours of refinement in level and combat design. It took four years to get right, and it feels like it used that time well (in the parts that matter, in other spots, wellll.... uh....)I don't know why it took this game five years to finish from its Early Access beginnings in 2019. I am not sure what went on between then and 2024 when it was finally pulled out of Early Access. What I do know is that the original developer left some time in 2020, then some other people were brought in to clean up the mess from 3D Realms and too many cooks got involved, and evidently there was some weird ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ behind the scenes and then finally it was pushed out after layoffs started happening. And the end product is fine? But it just feels like it's not well-tuned. The enemies feel a little bit too tanky, the weapons don't feel great... what was going on?Playing this game is like trying to watch the first Blade Runner movie, or only eating good but tough and gristly steak for a month. For the life of me, I have never, ever been able to watch Blade Runner all the way through without falling asleep. And the thought of chewing tough steak until it's finally ready to swallow for a month straight sounds unappealing. So what I'm saying is, Wrath: Aeon of Ruin is good until I personally got sick of it. It's fine, but I don't want any more after level three or so.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I'm gonna give this a possitive review, I would give it a "meh" but it's got some things right and some bad, but the overall quality pushes it up a bit.TLDR, it's good but the fights suckAlso, if you're having issues with the mouse jumping, go to WRATH's directory, find a file called "default.cfg" and set "cl_maxfps" to 0, I think this uncaps the fps and it may cause issues, but it fixed the mouse issueSo I'll start off with the good stuff1: sound design, this has to be the best part of the game so far, all the enemies make good grunts, moans and growls, the music which was made my Andrew Hulshult from Dusk and Amid Evil fame, needless to say he's very good and sort of the indie Mick Gorden at this point, the guns sound incredible, each one is punchy and deadly sounding, and all the other ambient sounds are pretty good too.2: Art style, this game has a very unique "sort of neo-gothic but more techy" art style, the enemies look good, the guns look great and the levels design and textures are gorgeous.3: "most of" The guns, all the guns feel fun to use and sound just as good as they should, each packing an alt fire to add a bit of depth to the firefights.and now the bad1: the problems with the guns, they're a pretty mixed bag at this point, either feeling really powerful or really weak, take the shotgun for instance, the primary fire lets out this beefy bang and pretty much kills anything you're looking at in a 30 degree radius, the alt fire charges up your shot and feels exactly the same as the primary and it sounds weaker, the Coach _childDocuments_.review: Nobody sets out to make a bad game, and even the metric for 'bad' can vary from person to person. I don't think this is inherently a bad game, but rather a game with bad design sensibilities. Please note, I have not completed this game, nor have I specifically progressed farther than two mission maps.Gameplay: 8/10Inasmuch as how it feels to play the game, it's overall very solid, makes fairly good use of the engine it uses, and is fairly intuitive without needing constant or consistent reminders of what you can do and how to do it. There is the caveat that I personally had to occasionally refer to the controls to figure out how to do or use a specific thing, but that's a me problem.Where this game shines particularly well is how smooth the movement feels, there's rarely a moment where I feel like I'm out of control, or that the game has screwed me over. That being said, it's far from perfect. This game has limited saves- itself not a bad idea, but in practice has some detriment to me. I'm the kind of player who likes to save scum, I will ruthlessly and relentlessly abuse saving to get through something if I can get away with it. Limited saves curbs this, which is otherwise fine with me, except it's your only real consistent means of saving your progress.There are roughly two 'save points', Soul Tethers and Shrines. Shrines are few and far between and at first I did not recognize what they were because I never noticed any tutorial message explaining what they were.I won't pretend to have any idea why the developers chose this as their main method of saving, all I care is that I have opinions on the matter- namely that the system needs work, players need to have a clear and definite explanation of what save shrines are, and moreover, players need to be able to use the same shrine multiple times for saving. This can allow for levels built around this mechanic, rather than trusting players to always use their Soul Tethers appropriately.Enemy Design and Combat: 5/10Allow me to preface with, the combat feels overall good. There's good feedback and the enemies have unique and memorable visual designs. Under most circumstances, that would be at least a solid 9/10. Where combat suffers is that combat never really feels like you're doing anything more than reacting to ambushes. It's the design philosophy of punishing players for progress or exploration.It always feels like there's always an enemy just around the corner who will swipe at you if you're not constantly checking corners, to the point where any time I feel like I'm starting to enjoy playing the game, a corner monster has to remind me that I have to be paranoid and check every corner. Which leads to the game becoming somewhat predictable. When half of the battles you fight are ambushes or enemies teleporting in, looking at any collectible just becomes a guessing game of whether or not it will spawn enemies. This is not going into instances where the game decides to waste your time.While thankfully rare, there have been instances where an ambush is designed specifically to trick you- if there weren't bog standard ambushes around every corner, these would be shocking, perhaps even terrifying. But after ambush 394, you just get this sense that you've now lost half of your health to a really cheap enemy placement, or worse, been shoved into an unwinnable situation because you didn't have the right gun equipped. More on that later.Which brings me down to the crux of my issue with this game. Enemies feel random. Moreover, there isn't any sense of what's really dangerous except which enemies specifically tank hits. Three specific enemies come to mind, shield-bearing chargers, cyst-launching spiders, and floating three-mouthed heads. Any time these guys show up, I break out the cyst launcher and waste them because they will kill you if you bother with smaller enemies.I always feel like the developers just threw a bunch of dudes together without really considering where they're placing them. When everyone except maybe one enemy (the chargers) show up all of the time, there's never any panic, just a resigned, 'It's these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ again.'Weapons: 4/10The Shotgun and the Cyst Launcher are the only weapons you need, and in my experience, the latter of the two is the only one that you really need to watch your ammo count on.You start with a wrist-mounted blade, it slashes things, it lets you leap over gaps. You will rarely use this for actual combat.Next is the Pistol, it's a good pistol, it carries its weight and like all guns has an alt fire that is significantly stronger. It is decent, and once you get the shotgun, you will rarely need to use it except to conserve ammo.The Shotgun is basically the strongest gun in the game save the Cyst Launcher. It takes down almost every enemy in one shot, and when it doesn't, its alt fire will generally hit a little harder (albeit at the cost of a charge up, which is fine), and the Cyst Launcher will do the work it can't.The Fang Spitter is this game's chaingun, it is arguably the worst weapon because it's death by a thousand cuts, has a surprisingly small maximum ammo count of 150, and a slower alt fire that doesn't really feel any stronger than the main fire in terms of DPS. It will stunlock a lot of enemies, and exists solely to keep you from switching to the Cyst Launcher in a pinch. (There is a quick swap key, for the record.)The Cyst Launcher is the strongest gun in your arsenal, simply because its alt fire will kill the tankiest enemies in one go, provided they hit your target. Its biggest downside is it has an arc and relies on enemies either getting hit, or being near the launched cyst when it eventually explodes.Please note, these are the only weapons I have acquired, if there are others, I haven't gotten them and have no opinion on them.Overall, the balancing between these weapons feels extremely skewed, to the point where I'm honestly disappointed that a cool weapon like the Fang Spitter feels worse than the pistol.The pistol is fine for where it is, it's a solid gun that doesn't give the sense of being useless, but still not quite on the level of using over the shotgun.The shotgun, I honestly think it's okay where it is, I think the biggest issue is that it's easy to keep it stocked up. The alt fire is fine, the charge up feels a little too long, and for what is effectively a ricochet bomb, doesn't really shine against large groups from what I've experienced.The Fang Spitter needs a higher maximum ammo capacity, at least 300. While it also has plentiful ammo, the biggest annoyance I have with it is I feel like I have to go out of my way to collect ammo for it. In one room, I came across so much ammo, that even though I'd spent all of its stock, I had plenty more remaining. Having a higher capacity would incentivize me to use it more often, maybe as a main weapon if its damage was buffed by a fraction.The Cyst Launcher is perfect where it is, with the caveat that I also think it's kind of overpowered. Its biggest drawback is the relative scarcity of ammo, this forces me to be smart about how I use it, which I like. More of this, please.Level Design: 3/10Don't get me wrong, the levels are absolutely stunning, and I love how they capture the overall aesthetic. That said, they are a nightmare to navigate. On top of a lack of a map, (I checked the controls, there was no map key binding,) the levels are often labyrinthine without any clear indication of where progress is, exactly. Many games use lighting to direct players to points of interest, and more specifically, they use different lighting to signal there's something interesting. Marking the path to progress gives the player a visual cue as to where they need to go without outright telling them how to progress, freeing up exploration.Overall Score: 5/10. It needs work, it needs more polish, and given that, it could really shine. But as it is now, I can't really recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's not a horrible game and it's decent boomer shooter, but the dev's lack of respect and communication for their customers is appalling and that is why you should avoid this project at all costs.Especially considering it's an "Early Access" project right now, so you're essentially paying for a buggy and inconsistent feeling demo with a promise that it will be fully featured and patched out by a certain date. But so far, they have given us zero reasons to believe any promises they make about this game and its development.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my favorite Boomer Shooter to come out in the past few years.The mechanic of needing a consumable to save is really unique and ramps up the tension (though it may not to be to everyone's liking) and the player movement along with being able to charge the melee weapon and fly forward makes for some really fun and dynamic options in both combat and platforming.Absolutely recommend this to anyone that is a fan of the original Quake series or Boomer Shooters in general and is interested in a fun, challenging game.

_childDocuments_.review: The main problem of Wrath is not repetiveness of encounters imo, but overextension of some later maps, which are Arcane Dimensions huge with like 600 mobs. And you are playing this map and cannot stop asking yourself: why is it so large? There are no changes in scenery while following the same theme, there are no attempts to surprise you with new tricks and secrets - you are simply walking an overbloated castle which serves a single purpose of extension of playing time.I put positive mark on my review because the game was still fun, but I have to say that it was razor thin close to a negative review.P.S. special thanks to a person who thought that single attempt timing secret at Shadow Pantheon is a good decision for a boomer shooter. At least you offered something special. Remarkably bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Wrath is the perfect example of why you shouldn't pay for a product that doesn't exist yet.  The 5 maps that are currently available show promise, but they are a bit rough around the edges.  Guns feel good, enemies are diverse, and the level design is interesting.  However, Kill Pixel and 3D Realms have been extremely shady with this title in regards to transparency.. They've missed several deadlines and have made silly excuses for those misses, if they get enough pressure from the community.  The most egregious response: Covid is hampering the development process. This is after they had bragged about having a team that is spread out all over the world. It doesn't make sense and is dishonest to those of us that gave them our money.

_childDocuments_.review: WRATH is one of the best old-school shooters in recent memory, an obvious labor of love that should appeal to anyone who is looking for a spiritual successor to QUAKE.The levels are massive and have to be seen to be believed. You will easily spend an hour on each, pushing your perseverance whiletesting your pathfinding and spacial awareness skills, not to mention your ability to hunt down LOADS of ridiculously well-hidden secrets.The arsenal consists of all the genre staple tropes with their own clever spins, such as a three-barreled revolver, a wooden machine gun that fires monster fangs and a laser that arcs between enemies. There's a super shotgun (a good one). Every weapon, from the starting pistol to the BFG variant are useful all the way through to the end of the game-- special mention goes out to the starting blade, which is easily one of the best fallback weapons ever in an FPS and it's secondary attack makes it an integral tool for solving puzzles and locating secrets.You have access to a dozen or so deployable powerups to give you an edge in combat, such as force-fields, invincibility, breathing apparatus, life-leeches and gas clouds that cause baddies to fight amongst themselves.The enemy roster are quite creatively designed and varied enough to keep you on your toes and changing tactics on the fly to compensate for their unique attack strategies.Most controversial is the save system, which is limited to collectible "soul-tethers", shrines, and the occasional autosave. These are split about 50/50 between obvious pickups and secret areas. Anyone remotely competent with the genre should have no problem managing these; I only ever came close to running out during the hectic boss fights. Alternatively, you can switch this system to a regular quick-save setup in the options menu if it becomes problematic, but you'd be robbing yourself of some of the tension.Worth noting is the "story", which is quite light to the point of being background noise but told surprisingly well through an unnerving series of notes (one per level) along with brief dialogues from a mysterious "shephard" character who hangs around in the hub worlds. These messages, while brief, are completely skippable, but you'd be doing yourself a disservice as they are quite professionally done and add a welcome dash of flavorful intrigue to an otherwise bleak and lonely landscape.If I had to give any criticisms it would be that the game is a completionist's nightmare: each level is so jam packed with enemies (several hundred) and secrets that the casual player will without a doubt miss something on their journey from A to B. Also, that Cacodemon enemy can eat **** and die.Ignore the "top" reviews that bicker and nit-pick about the combat being too exhausting, the music too muted, the lack of enemy variety, the "troubled development cycle" (who cares?) and non-issues like the over-saturation of titles in the boomer-shooter market. These aren't legitimate criticisms of WRATH, moreso petty gatekeeping by an increasingly entitled player-base that has been spoiled by Early Access. Nobody OWES you entertainment. You're not going to die of starvation or dehydration if a game doesn't exceed your lofty expectations.Here is a solid twitch shooter with killer combat, level design and atmosphere, currently on sale for 12 bucks ensuring at least 30 hours of gameplay for those inclined to soak it all in instead of constantly complaining about this-that-and-the-other-thing.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have so much bad things to say about this based off first impressions, that i honestly only would for a paid review. What you need to know is that weapons have no utility, and enemies are just a culmination of everything annoying there is about older games. Suicide enemies? Check, enemies that fly, charge at you, and shoot projectiles? Check. Enemies that shoot one-shot pellets that are indistinguishible from the ammo for the same weapon? Check. Enemies that rush and stagger you in the corner? Check. Enemies that the only purpose is to fly around and make your life miserable as you get stuck in the open-field geometry? Check. And so on.I'm just getting started, but enemies and weapons are the most important part of an FPS experience, that much you need to know. Weapons are all bland "point and shoot" type of guns, if a game is less creative than Daikatana in a weapons department, then it's not trying hard enough. Basic weapons can work, if there is a proper justification for such, but there is none. You can't defend this game at all, second function for all weapons is the same function, shoot 3 pellets instead of 1. That's it. (I'm not gonna mention the horrendous melee that has no practical use outside of just doing charge jumps) All this game does, is propose a "hardcore fast paced shooter" but it limits your options and movement at any point possible. This here, is the death sentence to a premise. If you think that placing a savepoint has any creative gameplay use, then you are wrong, it's just a gimmicky quicksave, and it functions as such, you still lose progress and the game controls how many quicksaves you are allowed to do. Nothing creative is made out of the inventory function. You can choose a level to start from at the beginning hub, but there are no interesting combinations to use with the items that you gather from other levels, so there is no point to this, "we do this because xxx did it", that's all there is. (and it shows just how many games devs actually played and understood, here's a hint, they barely make up for ONE game)Enemies chasing the player from the beginning of the lvl for a cheap shot, boring secrets (having 1 ammo pack in a lot of them), the annoying enemy spawn which spawns even more enemies after you've cleared out a room, having a feature like serious sam did with constant trolling of the player by picking up a minor health item and having a room filled with enemies out of the blue (serious sam was an arcade game and did this for a joke, in some ways it even created situations AND you knew what to expect when a game did this, this game does NOT translate ANYTHING to you, it just does it because "xxx did this, so we copied" as always.), having a huge swamp areas that are empty and add nothing, despite knowing well that players barely function in deep waters on this engine (thus restricting movement further), and SOOO much more GARBAGE. This was horrible and just adds to the pile of things that are blindly copied for nostalgia, don't support this behavior, people. Ion Fury is much better, and what it lacked, it is slowly improving, DUSK was okay and I definetely loved the first chapter (can't say much about the rest, it's tough to love) although what it did to a wave of "oldschool" shooters is very questionable at best. Amid Evil was very cheaply made, but it had some merit of fun, nontheless. There is none to be found here. This game has a head-shot and a limb-chopping system, but does it as a gimmick, and not mechanic-wise. I guess you be the judge of what's the real deal, who tries, and who's a scumbag show-off. Played on hard. I test levels with pistol-start, if that adds any value to anything I say in here.Edit After Launch:Horizontal underwhelming crowd control nightmare of horrible ideas (if you think charge type weapons and Unreal's bio rifle is fun, then Wrath is up your alley) and every weapon feels like shooting a different type of pistol with useless inventory gimmicks, because there is NO reliable splash type damage, every weapon is penetrative damage, there is at least 3 weapons that are "point and shoot" rifle type weapons, one arc type weapon, a shotgun (which feels very Doom 2016), a rare rocketlauncher that is probably one of the weakest in FPS genre, a machine gun with zero to none ammo capacity, and levels with wasted effort, that are downplayed by how horrible the core gameplay isBy the end I would play with only the main melee weapon, only using weapons because I was annoyed and bored by the enemies, attacking everybody beforehand with ricochet. The weapon switch in this game is super-fast, so you can stack damage, by knowing how many shots it takes to kill each enemy, which shots stagger them and etc. But the enemies are just basic quake enemies, and are just as spongy, it doesn't help that on top of that they all still charge at you, and you have to switch from your melee, because some explode in your face afterwards, or leave toxic/fire trails which all damage your step, in this sense they want you to finish them off by shooting, which is a horrible, awkward design, because you also want to take their ammo after death. Items allow for 'some' experimentation, but by how the main arsenal sucks, they feel too restricting, in fact, they are basic fps mechanics (not even Hexen type inventory system) like 'forced infighting', 'instakill enemies in a circle' and etc.Verdict: It sucks, play 'Episode Enyo' Slave Zero X to see how a quake based game should play like. Or play WGREALMS for duke, if you beat this, you will probably have patience for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Major Pros:1. The weapons are SOOOOOOO GOOD! This might be my new favorite arsenal of weapons in any shooter, it's definitely my favorite in any retro-shooter. In particular the shotgun is, like, my new favorite weapon in any game ever. I thought Dusk's super-shotgun couldn't be topped but boy am I glad to be wrong.2. The aethetics of the game are amazing. The environments look amazing and strike the perfect balance between being aethetically pleasing and easy to navigate. More importantly, the readability mid-combat is near-perfect. Enemies, ammo pickups, and projectiles all have completely different silhouettes and colors to one another, making situational awareness effortless. And yet, despite the visual variety, none of it looks out of place. Genuinely top-notch 10/10 visuals.3. The melee weapon deserves a special shout-out. The core gimmick of Wrath's movement is that the starting melee weapon is also your traversal tool, and it's amazing to use. It's a near-flawless balance of high mobility without letting the player disregard good positioning, and it makes exploration super fun.4. The levels stay super engaging despite their length. They're around 30 minutes to an hour and they don't feel stale or boring for even a minute of that duration. They feel like small worlds that you're exploring, and the game's extremely limited resources make it feel great to plunder every inch of them for any resources you can find. Minor Pros:1. It feels like we don't get many hub-worlds these days. Most games nowadays seem to either go for large interconnected open worlds or a purely-linear series of levels. Wrath's fantastic hub worlds, full of tone-setting visuals and cool secrets to uncover, shows why it's a shame that we don't get them too often.2. Enemies are pretty fun to fight. Their projectiles are appropriately difficulty, but not too difficult to dodge, and there's a strong emphasis on funneling enemies into your attacks and micromanaging lines of sight. It's very well-balanced, and the variety keeps the game and its encounters interesting. My favorite enemies are the flying jaw-creatures since it's fun to bait them in for a melee attack and then kill them with a charged melee attack.Minor Cons:1. The journal is completely useless, and that's a shame. You get rough sketches of all of the enemies and weapons but no explanation of how they work. If any enemies have increased or decreased damage from specific weapons, I wouldn't know. I particularly don't like that the weapons get no explanation. I know I swore my undying love for the shotgun above, but I still have no idea how its alt-fire works. I've fired it like 200 times and I still can't tell how to get the pellets to go where I want them to.2. The game's limited-save system isn't very impactful because of how many you get. Even when I was most struggling and constantly saving I still had like 50 tokens left over. They recently changed the system to only let you carry 9 quicksaves at a time, but that just means I always have 9 quicksaves on me for any situation.3. The fodder enemies are way too annoying. The elite enemies actually feel pretty well-balanced and fun to fight, but the fodder is aggravating. The revolver enemies constantly barrage you with nearly-hitscan projectiles. The plasma-spitting enemies never seem to stop shooting. Also, the fodder enemies being difficult to melee because of projectile spam and exploding on death feels contradictory to the game's mechanics of having a powerful melee and strictly-and-highly limited ammo resources. 4. The artifact system, or whatever it was called, has some wack-ass balance. One of Wrath's unique systems is that you can pick up power-ups which can be taken across levels and used whenever you want. Some of these power-ups are good compliments to the core gameplay, like one that grants a bit of health when you get kills or a shockwave that requires you to be point-blank to fry enemies. However, most artifacts just trivialize battles, like a potion that makes the enemies fight eachother, or sentry guns that can wipe out entire enemy legions by themselves, or a bubble shield that you can shoot through but enemies can't. The end result is that the enemies in Wrath are only threats for as long as you decide not to trivialize them.So if enemies barely pose a threat, how do players die in Wrath? We need to give them a reason to use those quicksave tokens.Major Cons:1. And I'm FREEEEEEEEEEEEE- FREE FAAAAAAALLING!!!Okay seriously, what is with this game's obsession with perilous jumps over instant-kill pits? All throughout the game and especially in the second and third hub areas, there are instant-kill pits EVERYWHERE, and you constantly fall into them because of the slippery Quake-engine movement.It really feels that the Quake engine wasn't meant to do what this game puts it through. The movement struggles when walking on uneven terrain, making it a good fit for Quake 1's boxy arenas and a bad fit for Wrath's well-defined environments.2. The level design's core philosophy is basing levels around a central hub area that gets unlocked more and more as you explore the level, hit switches, and grab keys. It's a great idea, and a lot of fun, but the game pays a dire price for taking this route: Because you would otherwise be constantly walking through empty levels full of dead enemies, enemies constantly appear out of absolutely nowhere because you hit a random trigger on the opposite side of the map. Sometimes this works, like more enemies appearing after you take a long detour down one of the level's paths, but it often just leads to enemies feeling like they pop out of thin air whenever you turn your back to the level.In a word, this makes the level extremely unsatisfying. It feels like your ability to proceed through the level in a smart manner and clear the enemies out is highly limited. If you want to avoid enemies, you can't because you're constantly hitting invisible trigger lines that spawn more. If you want to hunt enemies down, you'll need to scour the entire map for every invisible trigger line that spawns more. It kills immersion because instead of organically trying to spot traps and ambushes within a level, you're instead trying to suss out where the devs hid an invisible spawn trigger.3. Why are the controls like this? Why? I'm done giving retro shooters any leniency. I'm not pressing '8' to swap weapons, and I don't want to spoil myself on the upcoming arsenal by going into the options menu to tinker with the binds. To retro shooter devs: You are needlessly handicapping your games by having awful control and expecting players to fix them for you. My enjoyment skyrocketted as soon as I rebound the controls, but doing so also caused me to get spoiled on the last weapon, which I hadn't acquired yet. Don't do this to yourselves, you and your games deserve better.

_childDocuments_.review: Of all the indie boomer shooter, this is one of the highest quality. The gun-playis not too innovative, it has everything you want from the genre, but the maps is where the game stands out: Beautiful visuals, very atmospheric, it gets suprisingly complex, yet intuitive to navigate. Exactly what what makes a classic boomer shooter great.   So you can really tell that veterans of of the Quake mapping scene have worked on this game. In fact, the whole thing is running on a Quake source port!     So if you are a fan of the genre, this is the next must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough game to review for a few reasons, but if you meet certain criteria, you may find a shockingly satisfying shooter experience within this game.What you will need to enjoy the game:-A willingness to play on a higher difficulty than you were ready for.This game can be monotonous if you play it on lower difficulty levels. But I believe this is because the design is weighted to favor the game at its most ball-crushingly difficult moments. -A willingness to replay sections overThis game has a save system that relies on you, the player, to set your own checkpoints, and as these checkpoints are a finite resource, you WILL find yourself overreaching at times and losing yourself progress. This is part of the game, and part of the satisfaction.-If the enjoyment of succeeding at something difficult, is greater for you than the frustration of failing at it until you succeed.This game is meant to be played on hard, and if the frustration diminishes your enjoyment, more than your triumph increases it, this isnt the game for you.With all that saidThis game is a lovingly crafted quake-like experience. it has satisfying weapons, challenging enemies, great level design, and even greater art design. But on lower difficulties, it can definitely feel like going through the motions. If you like games like dark souls (I hate making that comparison because its so overused), and also enjoy fps games, this is a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Very mid Doom/Quake like shooter, 6.0/10, if you're a fan of boomer shooters and want a power trip, give it a go. The game is not as bad as peeps say, just poorly balanced.- Aesthetics and designs within the game are top notch- Gameplay is fun, old school shooter with modern Doom mechanics (mixing and switching weapons in battles)- Item design is okay i guess- Item mechanic itself is kinda OP - No type of challenge mode or arena mode is existent and it should as the combat is fun and has potential- For some reason there is an item wheel but not a weapon wheel???- Weapons are unoriginal, you've seen em before- Too many projectile type of enemies- Game has enormous balancing issues (weapons, enemies, enemy spawns)- Story is your classic kill all the bad gods type of thing - Acts/Chapters are too long, this shouldn't be the case for this type of game- After finishing the first act or half of the second act, the game is kinda exhausting and feels like a chore to play- Due to balancing issues, parts of the game are extremely easy or hard- Level design is meh, as they look good but are confusing at times - No type of map is existent, due to the levels being confusing at times you easily get lost- First melee weapon is badly balanced, able to insta gib normal enemies while bigger ones only take 2 hits!

_childDocuments_.review: The inevitable comparison to Ion M.... erm... Fury, being a new game on an old engine is obviously obvious. And I'm glad to say that this game seems to be for Quake what Ion Fury is to Duke3D. The atmosphere is that otherwordly dark fantasy, but with guns. And that is precisely what I loved about Quake. Both the graphics and music + sound combine to let the game succeed with this.I'm glad it is in EA, as it does have some rough edges and balancing issues as of late November 2019. There's plenty of stuff to love about it at this point too though, so I'd gladly recommend it to any fans of Quake, Hexen and Blood.I love the gibs and gore. And I love most of the level design and texture work. It's often a beautiful game in the darkest sense. Some areas do seem a bit too colorful though, as is the case with the outdoor snowy blueish rock-based textures. I'd love for that to get grittier. The underground crypt- , sewer- and cavelike areas look fantastic!The monsters are also delightfully obscure. Biped acid slingers, 3-faced beholders, zombies, shotgunners. It's all in here and I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I died on level 1, because I was just using the arm-knife lunge attack on everyone. Presented with a choice of loading from a limited-resource savepoint (hadn't dropped any), a checkpoint (didn't think I hit any), and restarting the level.I hit checkpoint thinking surely at the worst that'd restart the level if I hadn't tagged any.It loaded the tutorial level...As far as the game, the first few weapons aren't inspiring. Pistol is a pea-shooter unless you use its altfire, which takes several seconds to recover. Shotgun spreads a ton, can't be relied upon for a close-range kill, and takes a long time to reload. Nailgun is not bad but ammo is very limited. Grenade launcher shoots bouncy things, but not nice quake-style things where it's easy to predict where it goes, but more like they're coated in super-lube.Movement feels pretty good--fast, high control, and your first weapon is an arm-knife that gives you a burst of mostly-horizontal speed when you use its secondary lunge attack. You don't seem to be able to jump as high as the rest of your movement suggests you should be able to, but overall very good. Would love a dedicated "lunge with the arm knife" button regardless of currently equipped weapon.Enemies are varied and interesting. I wish the guy who shot grenades didn't also explode on death, because I was having fun doing the sword lunge attack on everyone I came across. But you have melee zombies, mixed shotgun-and-melee, weak grounded guys shooting fireballs at a high rate, fliers shooting fireballs at a low rate, grenade hurlers, heavy melee bruisers, good variety.Technical options are excellent. It runs well and it's easy to configure it the way you want.Art style is great and stands out very well. The screenshots are representative. A lot of care was put in the details while not drawing your eye away too much from what's going on. One issue, at least in early snowy levels, is that light-blue enemy attacks blend with the white and light blue of the snow too often.Sound is okay. Music is almost entirely airy ambient tracks, which is a missed opportunity. Weapon sounds work. I had to re-launch the game to make sure monsters actually bark at you, and they do, but it's a collection of mostly-indistinct moans mixed in with some screeches. Nothing distinctive.The levels are honestly a bit too big. Circling around where you've been 4 or 5 times is common. But you get a good variety of close-up and long-range fighting, interesting architecture, cool vistas, good environmental art.The tyranny of "would you recommend this to other players" makes a score here tough. The game was made with great care, and the issues it has could be fixed well by mods (if supported?) and turn it into something special. But I can't really point to any fun experiences I've had with it. I'd fire it up over and over during early access, but it was never "I should play that fun game again", but rather "is it finally good yet?"There are some players I'd recommend it to, the issues it has are not insulting, and we all know there's way worse on steam doing better, so it gets the up. But definitely try it first and see if it works for you--if you don't like the first hour, you won't like the rest.

_childDocuments_.review: Boring; too easy. The visuals are great, the sound design is on point, the artifact system and the restriction of savescumming is a great innovation, the Armblade lunge functioning as a mid-air dash is an awesome idea, the gore and gunplay is especially UNF -- but the game just flunks the enemy/level design. The levels are huge and detailed, but also meandering and too reliant on ez forgettable filler encounters. 90% of the time I can nullify the challenge in any indoors encounter by simply backpedaling out of a doorway and forcing enemies to fight me one by one in a chokepoint. The levels rarely force you in a disadvantageous situation where you have no escape routes or safe corners, so they feel way too easy and repetitive because you can always apply the same winning strategy. Outdoors encounters are just circlestrafefests, with no enemy type (other than the Executioner, who appears only rarely) actively preventing you from hiding or running circles around everything. Most enemies are basic-ass and don't intrude on your personal space like the enemies in Quake would. You can outrun and outstrafe all enemies since nobody moves as fast as you and because everyone fires easily dodgeable straight/arcing projectiles. Even the hitscan enemies are consistently dodgeable on medium range when you circlestrafe them. Only the Executioner is again the exception because he will home in on you when he charges instead of running in a straight line; forcing you to use the Armblade lunge to get away, which is cool. But again, he's almost never used. At the very least the green blobs fired by the infected could leave a larger pool of damaging acid behind to restrict your movement.Except for the Armblade, all the alt. fire modes are just uninspired. For the Coach Gun, Retcher and Fang-Splitter, the alt. fire is always firing three projectiles at once, instead of something more unique. The Shotgun can be charged to fire ricochet rounds, but they are too inaccurate to be of any real use. And more often than not these alt. fires are highly situational and don't add much to your decision-making process, on top of them just being shallow in function and execution. The Armblade's neat, but the game isn't doing much with it. It's largely used to cross obvious gaps that lead to a "secret". There's barely any platforming challenges or arenas that have you make the most out of it, or more enemies like the Executioner where you need to lunge yourself out of the way. Unfortunately there's no mid-air control, so jumping doesn't feel as fluid. WRATH also doesn't let you cancel all forwards momentum in mid-air when holding backwards like you could in Quake, so it makes first-person platforming a lot harder by making you more prone to overshoot your landing.The save system is great, but it's made somewhat redundant by having save tokens appear too often and having the game be so easy and forgiving with ammo/health pick-ups that you never feel compelled to save just in case. Same goes for all the other artifacts, I had max stacks on all of them most of the time.Enemy pathfinding is also pretty bad, as they can't deal with heights at all. They'll get stuck on ledges and walls where they're easy to finish off. Some enemies are simply too big to pass through certain doorways, which makes them look incredibly silly when they try anyways. I don't have much faith in this repetitive maximalist level design philosophy producing anything better in the future, on top of the current enemy roster being too weaksauce for anything interesting to be done with them.EDIT: The newest patch added--on top of some very welcome balance changes and QoL features, a newer difficulty setting where the enemy damage output is actually lethal, meaning there's some actual challenge to be had now. Unfortunately many of the aforementioned level design and enemy design problems still persist. These are likely to be addressed down the line of Early Access, but given the game's current state I cannot yet recommend it.
