_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me tell you about the early access period of this game which lasted wayyyyyy longer than it should have, all that to have features completely scrapped like multiplayer, some weapons and whatnot.If people are mad at this game, it's totally legit, I am too ! (especially since I own the game since day 1 of early access)Despite the many problems and the long time in EA where I suspect the devs did not work on game leading to the decision to cut content, the game is still pretty decent.This is a boomer shooter alright, it plays well, graphics are excellent, level design is beautiful, music is shy but very atmospheric, sound effects and animations do a very good job at delivering that action and the feeling you're looking for to  relax and decompress from a long day.This said, enemies are legion (maybe a bit too much) due to levels which are wayyyyyyyy too long, convoluted and without any map whatsoever, so much that you're getting bored and lost and wish for the level to end already. (seriously, you take about an hour to finish a level if you don't speedrun it and more if you die !)The game being divided into 3 acts of 5 levels each.The big issue with saving is real, you've got a number of saves which are limited by the number of items to save you can find which can be an issue, especially when levels are so big and dying can make you lose 20 to 30min of progress because you were scared to lose a save item which you might need later.Enemies spawn a lot out of the blue for a yes or a no ! And you do really get all kind of monsters, luckily, there are a lot of piece of armor and health lying around. Also, monsters do aim a bit too well and do a lot of damage, they notice you from far away so you really need to be careful and move a lot to avoid being hit.Weapons are a bit weird as some are pretty nice while the others feels like a failure. For example: The blade, your traversal tool, lets you jump further and is a pretty cool weapon doing a lot of damage while the shotgun, while delivering the blow and get the expected feeling has a  failed secondary fire which requires you to hold the button which will automatically release  into an explosion after a time (this makes the alternate fire very hard to use effectively since you don't control the release), there are also other weapons I totally hate and all this is coupled to a bunch of items you will keep in your inventory until you decide to use them. (which is very nice and made me think about Heretic)Controls can feel unresponsive at times, especially when you're trying to make a big jump which is VERY problematic as it can lead to your death. Speaking of jump, the system to press jump then crouch to climb a bit higher is very unnatural, they'd better have given players a double jump mechanic instead of this.I don't really want to recommend it but it still has some nice things about it, the game has some frustrating moments (hope the devs will look into this) but in the end, they're not too bad and if you can also overcome them, you will like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game I didn't know I needed.Gameplay is classic 90's pickup-based shooting, which is a total blast and a welcome departure from the modern shooting game styles. Plenty of enemies, exploration is a must, and on top of all that the level design and texturing is on-point.Definitely recommend, even if the price is a hair steep.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished as of this review but fantastic so far. The ambient soundtrack of this game fits the dead world theme and is absolutely incredible. The art design clearly takes from Quake and does it well. Weapons are visceral and enjoyable to use and the Enemy roster is varied. Game difficulty is not a joke assuming you are decently familiar with these types of games. Ammo does seem too plentiful sometimes but this really doesn't hurt the game much in my opinion. 8/10 ~ Could be more difficult for my tastes but a solid and great game
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Early Access review; this game is not finished and I will update the review once the full product is completed. WRATH: Aeon of Ruin is a Quake-styled First Person Shooter (or if you want to get more memetic, a Boomer Shooter) that (if I'm not mistaken) runs on Quake's source code. Your main objective is to (eventually) collect 5 Artifacts scattered throughout the 5 levels. With weapons such as a very useful Ruination Blade, an above-hand blade that can be charged to propel you forward, almost like bunnyhoping. A slug-shell triple barreled pistol that fires in single or triple-pellet slugshot. A double barrel shotgun that behaves like Quake's Super shotgun, but with a long-distance and hyper powerful mid-range projectile that kicks you back a little, A Nail-gun like Teeth launcher that fires projectiles in automatic or 2-shot semi-auto capability. And finally, the Retcher, a grenade launcher that utilizes a green substance to fire in single, high powerful shots or a volley of 3.The music from the levels and the hub area are simply great, you know things can only get better when Andrew Hulshult is making the music.Overall, This is shaping up to be another great entry into the modern-day Quake-style shooter. However, keep in mind that the game (as of this review) only features 2 levels and the aforementioned weapons only.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: It has a strong identity of its own, iterating on Quake's basic gameplay, but with larger variety in level design and enemy design. It doesn't stray too far from its forbear, but has a solid selection of satisfying weapons, dense level design, a diverse roster of very well animated enemies, and excellent sound design. I wouldn't call its art style Lovecraftian, though, it goes in a unique more alien-fantasy direction that is not predictable. If you're an old school FPS fan at all, you really need to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Avoid. Game is stuck in early access limbo and I doubt it's ever going to be released. The only thing happening right now is devs writing bi weekly posts to create an illusion that there's work being done.Even early on the game wasn't very good. The thing that stood out the most for me were incredibly dumb enemies that frequently got stuck on corners etc.It's the only title on Steam I truly regret buying. There are SO MANY better retro fps titles out there. Buy those instead.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's just not for me.I enjoy the movement and crunchy gunplay, but there is just so much unavoidable damage, platforming is very slippery(dash to a ledge and slide right off it), a lot of pick ups are in spots that require precise body placement to pick up even though you move a mile a minute, weapon swap speed can be painfully slow leaving you open to a lot of damage and the checkpointing system just... not for me.Definitely toooo retro for my tastes, but it may suit others.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, it came out of early access and surprisingly, after so many people bitterly declared it abandonware, it actually manages to deliver the goods. Although Wrath was repeatedly outshined by a bunch of other boomer shooters that came out during its lengthy development cycle, it still manages to be a solid FPS that I could heartily recommend to anyone who's been waiting for it all those years. Especially since it's a REALLY lengthy game for a first playthrough, and there's a clear vision here that was clearly crafted with a lot of love for the genre and attention to detail. For that price, you're absolutely getting your money's worth. The full version introduced a ton of new content and worked out all of the problems that I had with it during early access, which makes it an overall vastly superior experience. For someone who's into games like Quake, Doom, or Hexen, this is going to be a feast.The only thing that was sorely missing for me here is a decent soundtrack to accompany the gameplay. There are some ambient tracks that play in the menu and I think heard some brief pieces of music here and there during gameplay. But otherwise, the majority of the the game's soundscape is filled with the cacophony of monster slaying, with some occassional environmental sounds and not much of anything else. It feels kinda odd to play such an intense game without any tunes in the background to hype you up, or to even add another layer of atmosphere when you're outside of combat and exploring. Perhaps some of that guitar driven metal mayhem from always reliable Andrew Hulshult would do the trick, but I also wouldn't mind a more moody and horror-themed score either, much like Trent Reznor's soundtrack for Quake. Either way, it would make the game so much better to play in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this are the occasional reminder that not all new releases have to push the industry forward in terms of graphic fidelity, mechanics, story telling, and player progression. Sometimes less is more and as Doom modders will tell you, Clicking enemies until they explode into red giblets never gets old, its been ingrained in us since the first ape picked up a controller. Games like this are timeless, it doesnt matter if it came out 5 days ago, 5 years ago, or 50 years from now, people will still be playing this game like its 1997.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Wrath is a fantastic boomer shooter and does exactly what I want from one. Shooting, movement, & enemies all offer a high skill ceiling, rewarding you for your ability to take advantage of each one. It also does enough mechanically and artistically to separate itself from others that makes it worth the purchase. Instead of feeding the nostalgia of the boomer shooter era, it instead feels like it's being made during that era just without the technology limitations. You can definitely feel 3D Realms' influence here with large, open level design and the usable items you can find and carry around. Being on the Quake Engine with 3D Realms' design makes it feel like a mechanically Quake game with the design of Duke Nukem and that's really enjoyable. While I don't care too much for graphics, I must say that the game just looks and sounds beautiful. Enemies are all distinct and visible with clear indications of what they do at first sight.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: After 5 years, the game feels like it was rushed, or only worked on when there was a pause in other, more important projects.Features like lore entries and multiplayer were completely axed.This feels like a project that got left behind, and was then only finished when the consequences of not doing so outweighed the inconvenience for the publisher.Ultimately its... Fine. It's an okay game. It just feels like a tremendous waste of what seemed like such an interesting and uncommon flavor of FPS environments and weapons.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Quake 1 but with a updated Quake 1 engine, one enemy type is pretty much straight from quake 1 with a new texture. But it's very good and fun. _childDocuments_.review: Moving and shooting feels good, the enemies are ok, a bit static and generic.The levels are way too large and uninspired, ambushes continuously and not very interesting.The save system is just terrible. Yes, I can probably finish all of those huge levels on the hardest difficulty, killing 400-500 enemies without dying or stopping for hours. But if I need to stop for a while and quit mid-level, don't waste my time taking them back to the last shrine that was visited 40 minutes ago. The quake engine for sure supports quick saves, no need to force this king of bullsh*t "to be more hardcore", at least make it optional.Just play the original Quake instead, Arcane dimensions is top tier. The new episode included in the remaster is fantastic too.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After spending more time with the game I feel the need to change my review to a thumbs down.Putting it bluntly, this does not feel like a game that was in development for six years. It feels like an average Quake mapset with nicer than usual graphics. Enemy encounters are tedious as enemy variety is poor and the enemies have annoying mechanics that are difficult to avoid.  Weapon feedback is poor - oftentimes it feels like enemies do not react and this makes the game rather unsatisfying to play. Levels are long and severely overstay their welcome. I respect the developer and what they tried to do but the end result is more tedious than it is fun.Original review:The fourth horseman of the boomshoot apocalypse of 2018 finally arrives in its full version. Does it measure up to the likes of Dusk, Amid Evil and Ion Fury?I suppose that depends on how much you like Quake, as this game is essentially a polished, commercial total conversion for Quake, in the same vein as Hexen 2 or X-Men the Ravages of Apocalypse.If you're familiar with the genre (and you almost certainly are if you're here) there's not much new under the sun here. Fairly standard weapon loadout with a couple nice surprises such as an obvious nod to the bio rifle from Unreal (though I greatly appreciate how every weapon has a secondary firing mode) and enemies that while they aren't straight up reskins of Quake enemies they definitely wouldn't feel out of place in Quake or Doom. It seems to be attempting to set itself apart with light platforming here and there, aided by its 'air dash' ability, and limiting the amount of saves the player can make, turning quick save into a currency that is spent every time you make a save. I do appreciate the attempt to fight the quick save/quick load gameplay that plagues most boomer shooters, as it will make you think twice about dropping a save in every room. It is still fairly generous about it however, you'll likely find yourself carrying 5-8 save 'tokens' most of the time and there are shrines you can step into that will save the game once free of cost, like a mid-level checkpoint.There's also a slew of consumable items to help you in combat, ala Hexen, and many of the more difficult encounters seem to be balanced around their use - if you can remember to use them.Overall I have enjoyed my time with it so far, as derivative as it might feel.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: It's Quake. A modern Quake if you want, a legacy! An oldschool FPS with a HUB structure, some tweaks to a formula, yet quake nevertheless. Graphics: Decent, dark, creepy, immersive. Good.Sound and Music: Support the gameplay. The ambient is nice to listen to listen to, monsters and weapons sound really great. Nothing that will stand out too much, yet absolutely great in a context of a game itself.Gameplay: Run, gun, dodge, use items, kill enemies and stay alive! There's really nothing more you can ask from an oldschool shooter of Quake style. It works, it does it job, it's fun to play! Although diffrences come in a form of difficulty; on medium you can play agressive, there are rooms for mistakes, you can be a little bit reckless, and the only difficult parts may come during final parts of levels. On Hard however you have to be more cautious, plan ahead, dive in into that spinal tactical mind of yours and use your whole arsenal of weapons and moves. In conclusion: it's still an EA game, but what it is in there is worth your time and money if you like oldschool shooters. This game just hits that spot, for both more hardcore auditory as well as casual one.

_childDocuments_.review: a truly splendid game, I hath never had so much amusement and fun. In one word this game is very good. _childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: WRATH is a solid and challenging boomer shooter that expands on everything that Quake did. It's no longer some basic Quake mod, it's far more than that.Hub one is a touch generic: utilising elements from our original Quake 1 experiences, such as dungeons and castles, but it really comes into its own space in future hubs, becoming a far more complex gameplay experience with more verticality, and complex maze-work and layouts. Weaponry again, moves from basic, to interesting; with most of your weapons roster being built out in hub one, but, future hubs begin to include interesting, or more creative weapons, that make the experience unique. (That crystal gun and mace)Movement is at the core of the game here; and with the use of the Ruination Blade, speed and maneuverability became an essential skill to develop. Saving is weird; mixing weird limited "Tether" saves, which are a resource you can use up, and checkpoint saves in the form of Shrines. But then also unlimited saves if you select this option. Again, weird, and I'd have liked to see dev rather than just give us unlimited quick saves.The Story isn't groundbreaking either, sure it's there, and I can see the dev took time to return to narrative points and develop it out; but, it doesn't feel like anything out of the ordinary (though the final twist was nice), but I just didn't care. I do recommend WRATH though, even with its weird difficulty spikes, if you like a challenge, and you've had 25 years to get good, you'll love this, even if you're not good, you'll enjoy this challenge, just be aware the gap between easy and medium is massive, and easy itself being easy, until randomly not. Have fun! I know I did.Find my full review here, if you prefer a video:

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the game on medium difficulty and I think overall it's a mostly solid game with some missteps. I don't particularly get the negative reviews but they have a few points. Levels are well designed and fun but can be overly long. Some levels take a whole hour to beat. This game also begs for a map system of some kind. Paths will overlay and wrap into each other and it can get a bit confusing especially if you're on a level for an extended period. _childDocuments_.review: Let's put aside all of the developers' unfulfilled promises of the last 2-3 years, and just focus on what this game offers RIGHT NOW. It took me almost 14 hours to complete as it is on hard difficulty, which is actually more gameplay than many finished games offer. There are still bugs in the game, such as certain items (ammo/health) not picking up when you clearly have room for them, but they're not common enough to ruin the gameplay.For me, I found that the further you progress into the game, the better it becomes. I didn't particularly like the first level because I found it just too repetitive and monotone. Either you're walking through gloomy, gray corridors, or you're running around a vast snow-filled landscape. At about 2/3 of the level I started feeling like it was dragging on for too long, and got impatient to get to the next one. I felt the second level was better designed, but still something felt lacking.The third level, however, was a major step up in terms of both visuals and gameplay. The higher design quality was noticeable right from the start, everything was just feeling more complete. It was the first place I actually felt that the game was genuinely fun to play. This level takes much better advantage of the 3D world as well - for the first time, there are many vertical mazes and pathways that you have to make it through to complete the level. The fourth level was better still, and the fifth was by far the best, with far more environment variety and some surprises near the end.The single worst part of the game has got to be the saving system. While I understand that the developers wanted to prevent save/reload abuse where players just get through challenging parts by saving and reloading every two seconds, the current soul tether system is just garbage. The soul tether pickups are rare, in particular on levels 2 and 3, which makes sense given what this system is trying to achieve. But then two things happen. You make it through a reasonably long section which is doable without saving, so you don't use a soul tether, trying to save it for later. Then, without warning, you are ambushed by fast zombies and killed in two seconds. So you have to re-do that long section all over again. Or, sometimes you simply need to suddenly stop playing and do other things, but you are all out of soul tethers. So there goes all your progress from the previous soul tether up to that point. The game is more generous with soul tethers on the other levels, but still a simple checkpoint system would have been perfectly fine. At this point, I'm not getting my hopes up for this game to be completed anytime soon (or maybe ever). But even as it currently is it's all in all a fun old-school style FPS worth playing, especially if you can get it at a discount.

Also, in some areas, it was kind of dark so maybe add a torch that you could use with F or something idk. _childDocuments_.review: It's a little bit of Quake 1 mixed with Hexen. I think the save system works, instead of regular autosaves you have to obtain save devices(kinda like Resident Evil's ink ribbons though you can save anywhere with this game) so you need to plan out your save points in order to get the most out of them.The absence of maps, tutorials and guidance compasses is certainly felt here. If you're weaned on modern-day AAA games with plenty of crutches to help you out expect nothing of the sort with Wrath - you're gonna have to do the mental legwork yourself. Can be a frustrating process if you're not used to it, I myself had to double back in a couple of spots after leaving for the day and reloading to ascertain where I was, goals-wise. Whether that's a desirable challenge or not depends on you.Without really bothering to seek out all the obscure secrets I got through the whole thing on Normal(all relics collected) in ten hours. It's a nice little experience. There isn't much of a story going on here but that's no big deal. I did wish there was a couple of boss battles on top of the flurry of enemies though, would've given a bigger sense of satisfaction on completing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin is a great game. Let none of my review detract from thatSo I have mixed opinions about this game. I really enjoy some parts, but others felt samey or empty.GUNPLAY: One of the best things about this game. The guns here feel punchy and have the appropriate amount of "boom" to them. You have your Coach gun replacing the usual pistol, the double barreled shotgun cause there's no single barrel in this game, all the way up to the Retcher which feels like the Biogun from a certain other game. You also have the Ruination Blade which is actually functional as a basic melee and has a high powered dash which you can use to traverse the environment and gib smaller enemies. Each gun also has an alt-fire which helps spice up how you use them. Examples of this are the coach gun firing all 3 barrels at once and the shotgun firing a ball of shot that scatters on impact and ricochets off walls. By the way, I have seen some people confused as to what the shotguns alt-fire is meant to be used for given how powerful it is already. You use it to essentially make the thing a psuedo elephant gun. This gunplay with the movement exemplifies the games strengths and helps to hide some of its faults.MOVEMENT: The movement in this game is a bit nonstandard, the closest I can think of off the top of my head right now is DooM 2016. There is no bunny-hopping/strafe-hopping in this game with you instead moving full speed at all times. This does help newer players get comfortable with how the game plays without requiring them to learn a different form of movement which they may not be used to. There's no real faults I can find with it except that if you are looking for more dynamic movement system like in Dusk, you might be disappointed with what is on offer here.THE ENEMIES: So far this game has a small enemy roster, or at least one that doesn't seem to varied. The formula for enemies largely goes like this, you have a small version then a big daddy version. An example I can think of off the top of my head right now is how the Fallen have their counterpart, the Widows. These larger/more deadly versions drop ammo for their respective weapon with Widows dropping teeth and the Stricken (as does its smaller version, uniquely) dropping ammo for the Retcher. The main fault I have with this and why I say the roster doesn't feel varied, is that you can beat most of them by fighting the exact same way. Just pull out big gun then strafe a little side to side rinse repeat. There was only 2 enemies which made me do otherwise and that was the Heretics and the Executioner . Both of these I ended up using the alt fire on the shotgun to take them out in short order, only because both of them move very fast and have a sizeable chunk of health to them. The attacks for the larger versions also feel very similar to their smaller versions, such as the Stricken doing a multishot version of the Afflicted's attack and the Heretic shooting faster than the Wraths and having a bite attack. The vast majority of damage you will encounter will be from either getting shot or slapped. Only other form I can find is the Afflicted having an on death AoE explosion.LEVEL DESIGN AND THEME: Probably this games biggest strong point in my opinion. So far we have 2 levels and one hub. The levels themselves are long (around 30-60m to complete) and for the most part offer lots of variation to fight your opponents in. So far we have a gothic inspired snowed in map that to me gives some castlevania vibes, then we have the swamp which in my opinion is the standout of the two. The design of the gothic map can be samey after a while, I myself getting turned around a few times, and can lead to each new area feeling similar to the last. However you don't notice it too much unless you really look for differences and try to pick it apart just cause of how well designed it is as a whole which is a tick in my books. The swamp map is a lot more varied and so far from what I've played (Note, as of this review I have done the first level and completed a 1/3 of the second so take that as you will) it has more defining features in it than the gothic map does. This section of my review may feel a bit vapid as I haven't covered too much apart from how things look, but I can't talk about pacing much because of how this game fundamentally works which I'll get on too in a minute. The final thing about the levels is that they're all joined by a hub world which has secrets and pickups to restock yourself with between levels as well as it gives you an idea as to what the next level will be based off how the environment around that levels portal looks. This serves really well to communicate to the player about what they're about to thrust themselves into.THE PACING: Pacing in this game is weird. Really weird. This game technically has more levels than it says it has because depending on what order you play the available levels in, it will adjust the others accordingly. I played the gothic level first so it started off simple and when I got to the swamp map, it started from 100 at the beginning. The pacing in its current state the weakest part of the whole experience, as it introduces everything in the first level and doesn't leave anything for the second. This means it gives you all the weapons and items, as well as introducing every enemy in the very first level. I hope this is fixed as more levels are added because in its current state, this makes the game pretty boring for the second level as your hoping of seeing something new but never do.THE ITEMS: This game has items which you can pickup. I know, shocking right? Except in this game they actually are pretty fun to use and don't just sit in your inventory or have you use them after each fight (I think you know what items I'm referring to....). Instead of a consumable medpack, you instead have a consumable buff that heals you for each enemy killed within a timeframe after use. Also this game shirks the usual invincibility powerup and instead has it be a consumable item instead. This item has the offside of taking a very large chunk of health from you in exchange for its invincibility, meaning you have to be more careful about when it wears off lest you get 1 shot afterwards. The final item is the soul tether, this games main form of saving apart from rare shrines you find. You consume one of these guys and it drops a soul tether where you are standing and that is where you will now spawn from. This in theory does help save scumming excessively for every room, but in practice the game just gives you so many that I found I was always at max capacity so I never felt pressured.THE DIFFICULTY: Oh boy. In my opinion, this is the main section where this game fails HARD. This game in its current state only had me dying by an obvious blunder on my part (such as shooting my legs off with a Retcher shot) or the occasional situation where I didn't see something spawn behind me. Combine this with the VERY powerful consumable items and the absurd amount of Soul Tethers, and you pretty much can never get stuck or go "Damn, I wonder what I have to do differently here". Playing this game on high difficulty does alleviate the issue, but it would be nice if we didn't have to play on that level to feel any sort of challenge. The game in its current state with its pacing also doesn't handle pacing its difficulty well either with the second level feeling largely the same all the way through. The reason why I gave my disclosure at the start is that I am sure that the devs can iron a lot of this out by the time the game fully releases. They appear to be a very talented group of people who have a strong vision for what this game should end up being and I congratulate them for what they have done. Everything in this review is my first impressions after 1.1 hours of playtime so it is highly subjective and as such can be disregarded as idle chatter really. I hope the best for this game
_childDocuments_.name: WRATH: Aeon of Ruin

_childDocuments_.review: Review done only after the levels from the initial beta release. I still haven't played the newly added content, but...Returning to play the new content for WRATH wasn't a very fun experience for me. This could be a good game one day if the developers figure out the balance and get rid of the idiotic save system that doesn't increase difficulty, but punishes players who are conditioned to be careful with their resources, or get screwed by the game into a death pit you can't escape from. More in the cons section on saves.At this point I don't recommend this simply because it has some regressive ideas that don't fit current gaming environment and there's very little improvement on Quake's formula.More about pros and cons below.Pistol and shotgun feel really good to fire. Both of them had their alternate-fire modes changed during the beta and the changes were for the better. Pistol now fires piercing shots, while shotgun can charge up to fire two shrapnel-exploding slugs that are better at long range than primary fire. Weapons have nice models and animations and the sound design is perfect.With Dusk being a mix of Blood and Quake, WRATH is taking it's place as a true Quake throwback, which is commendable. Out of all classic shooters, Quake is deffinitely the one that could use some improvements on the formula as it was more of a tech demo than a full game (they didn't even make an upgrade for the lightning gun, even though it was planned).Levels are large and pretty nice to look at. They are also pretty internally diverse, meaning during each level you will fight in different environments that stick to a specific theme.A point of biggest contention amongst the fans. The inclusion of the item-based save system where you need specific items to "create" a save point you can then return to is supposed to fight "save-scumming". In reality the amount of these items in levels are so large that it's an artificial limitation and devs seem to stick to their original idea even though they have bastardised it to the point of uselessness.The biggest gripe for me with regards to the limit itself is that you have no idea whre to save as a player who plays for the first time, and a lot of properly difficult games condition you to be very careful with wasting your resources. This means a lot of gamers will not save for the majority of the level until they die in one of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ inta-kill pits by being thrown off a cliff by an exploding enemy. This will be the biggest reason of losing lots of progress.My second-biggest gripe is that you don't really "save" the game so to speak. As in you don't create a save state on a list like you would in any normal game. Instead you make a single return-to point. When you die you have an option to choose to return to the lastly-made save point, a checkpoint or restart the whole map. However the click "area" for each of these choices is wonky and you can easly have your cursor pointing at "return to checkpoint" option, but what's going to be highlighted is the "restart level" option. Needless to say if you click, thinking that you are pointing at the checkpoint option and instead you get teleported to the beginning you will immediately lose all your progress in the level.This would have been just a minor annoyance if the game had a normal save system, but instead we have this piece of trash idea that accomplishes nothing (you can still savescum as fk thanks to the amount of the items), but punishes you for the game's problems and bugs.Also you can't have a ♥♥♥♥♥ shooter with insta-death pits AND limited saves. FFS choose one or the other...Here are things that have to be fixed in this game:1. Item saving system needs to be changed or made opt-out.2. The choices after dying have to be fixed so that there is no chance to click wrong option even if you point to the one you want. Or make a proper save-state list to save your game into and load from.3. Insta-death pits Have to be changed so that you can either escape them somehow (not a new idea, most games have level design that enables escape if you got enough health), or they could just take some health and teleport you back like it is in Amid Evil.Bio gun and nail gun are meh. Nail gun's secondary is pretty fun, but primary lacks punch in comparison to the pistol and shotgun. It fires huge stakes at people - you'd think it would have a proper, booming sound effect. And it does - in the alt fire... Bio gun is another story. The weapon doesn't look nice, doesn't sound nice and the biggest problem - it's overpowered. Thanks to the abundance of ammo for it (multiple enemy types always drop them on death) and it's incredible damage it's going to be used a lot. It's not satisfying, but strong enough to make you use it. Eh...Levels often have open areas with w few enemies in them and after that you are exploring large amounts of terrain with very little of importance to find. The problem here lies in some area's design - too open with many side areas being unsubstantial.A meh game with serious problems. improved upon Duke 3D with very detailed environment and effects. took Wolfenstein 3D and introduced really cool, upgradable weapons with amazing spritework.'s weapon sprites look better than many fully 3D models in modern games and the level design is near-perfect in comparison to Heretic which was mostly just a Doom clone. fixes itself to be a proper Doom throwback the likes of which we won't see from ID again since the new Doom games opted to go in the hero-shooter direction.And  was an interesting mix between Quake looks and more Blood-like atmosphere and maybe Redneck Rampage added in for good measure.WRATH is a Quake 1 clone, but hardly improves on the ideas and introduces questionable mechanics. I thought that after Daikatana game designers would understand that limited saves don't belong in shooters and yet here we are. Aside from adding alt-fire modes to weapons and making levels huge there's not much changed in comparison to Quake 1.You can grab Quake 1, install Darkplaces mod and have a modern version of that game similar to WRATH for a fraction of the price. Plus - Quake has many amazing map packs and full on mods that add new weapons and mechanics. Going back to play some of the Quake's mods I've never got around to trying was a godsend after WRATH.I'd give WRATH aMediocre experience. Wait for a full release and then decide if you want to commit money to this. Unless you already played to death all the other throwback shooters I mention in the Lowdown section there's little reason to give time to this.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are expecting a retro shooter, this is it. You get at the same time low polygonal models, unfiltered textures (if you choose so) and even more graphical limitations, there is a fair list of options for you to choose. But alongside with that, you can set your game to the whole resolution of your monitor, have butter smooth speed, V-Sync and enjoy some dynamic lighting. But nothing of that hurts the nostalgic feeling the game is trying to bring.Wrath is standing in the shoulder of giants and delivers high quality and fast paced gameplay, exactly what fans of the genre are looking for. Expect a hell of a good time. The guns feel great with dual shooting modes and items to help you defeat hordes of monsters, as you explore creepy cripts and medieval structures. _childDocuments_.review: After almost 5 years of Early Access, Wrath: Aeon of Ruin is finally fully released and all I can really say about it is that the relentless march of time hasn’t been kind to it. When the game was released into Early Access back in 2019, it was envisioned and advertised as a sort of modern take on . But while the promise of another high-quality retro first-person shooter was quite thrilling back in 2019, coming hot on the heels of the likes of , ,  and , I feel like .There was a time when shooter releases with proper old-school sensibilities were few and far between, so fans of this type of game needed to take whatever they could get. Times have changed, however, and now  in a highly saturated genre, and has to go up against the likes of , when   – which might be a rarely used design idea, but I wouldn’t exactly call it a good selling point.I think I’d only ever suggest Wrath to people who are still looking for an experience just like the original  – but knowing the retro shooter crowd, I think even those people would point out how Wrath’s gameplay differs from  in some miniscule way, like “movement speed is 0.02 % slower, so it’s a terrible game and I knew I shouldn’t have bothered playing another game after ”. Other than that, I fail to come up with anything that Wrath does particularly well. , I guess, but they all become , as you’re constantly assaulted by the same handful of enemy types. As far as I’m concerned, the game could’ve even kept my attention, .As is, . Which might not sound too bad, but at a time when there are plenty of options for any type of shooter fan, from the early 2000s /-inspired  and the nonstop nineties slaughterfest of  to the first tentative indie steps towards imsim-inspired gameplay of ,  and , this means Wrath: Aeon of Ruin just ends up being yet another retro shooter in a sea of retro shooter releases.P.S.: I feel it's actually pretty interesting to directly compare Wrath to 3D Realms’ other recent release, . Both games were trapped in development hell for quite some time, but say what you will about  and its numerous bugs and sometimes nonsensical design ideas – at least ’s gameplay ideas allow the game to clearly distinguish itself against the vast number of other shooters on the market, while Wrath may be more bug-free and well-designed, but fails to do anything original to set itself apart.

_childDocuments_.review: (Mixed review)WRATH: Aeon of Ruin is disappointingly a very mid shooter that suffers with a few flaws that stop it from being a top tier game in the genre. I enjoyed the hub aspect and getting to choose what levels I can play in what ever order I like. I also enjoyed the games weapon roster and found them all to be creative and good to use. The visuals are awesome and look definitely  like something that would of come out in the late 90's (The game is using the OG Quake engine via the source port DarkPlaces after all!). I also really like the use of the Soul Tether save system as it makes your saves a limited resource and makes you think more about when to save (You can turn this off in the options to have unlimited saves if you wish.). Here are my gripes.I felt like the first hub had the best designed levels compared to the second and third, also I feel that levels tended to drag on a bit to long at times. I also found the ammo balancing to be quite scarce as I seemed to be running out of ammo quite a bit through out the games levels and found myself having to back track a lot to find more resources. The game also has a roster of 15 enemies to fight and kind of makes you yearn for a bit more variety when approaching the end of the game as combat encounters kind of start feeling samey by the end. I would of also loved if they gave the enemies cosmetic differences for each hub theme to give a bit of variety to them. The story is really nothing at all to be honest and the soundtrack is also pretty bland and forgettable.It took me just over 14 hours to finish and while I did certainly did enjoy certain parts, I feel that it doesn't really stack up to plenty of the other modern Boomer Shooters out there at the moment. I do recommend for those that love the genre, but wait for a decent sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for November 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before December 7th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A game based on the Quake engine, the Quake 1 engine. Wrath: Aeon of Ruin is a classic FPS, and means that in every sense of the word.  While there’s a lot here, this is a game running on an engine from over 25 years ago, a heavily modified version of the original Quake 1 engine, and is doing pretty well with it.  There are updated weapons, enemies, and even a crazy new save system where you have to find items to save.  It’s pretty fun. At the same time, this is an ancient engine and shows its age.  There’s no controller support, the menus are pretty bad, and while the save system is good, it’s also a little wonky.  The game is decently difficult, but difficult for a 25-year-old game, it’s going to be a heavy challenge.  It’s a game made for fans of Quake and fast-paced shooters, which is good for those players but this is a game that knows the audience it is aiming for. Pick this up if you want a game similar to Quake or old-school FPSes.  If you remember Project Warlock from the Humble Choice in February 2020 and want an even faster-paced game, this is perfect for you.  I’m not a huge fan but this is an impressive effort.  Though I will mention this is still Early Access, it does seem close to finished from what I can find. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Eh, what can I say?  I'm more than halfway through the game, and I'm really bored.This game shows real promise in the first few hours.  It's sort of this "Metroid Prime meets Dark Souls" old-school FPS setup with a grimdark atmosphere combined with a platforming focus.  The central mechanic of the game is the Ruination Blade which lets you do a mid-air dash using the charge attack.  So at first it's a lot of fun zipping back and forth with the dash attack and collecting guns.  After you get to the third stage or so, then reality starts to set in:- All of the enemies that you're fighting are mostly the same 3-5 types, and they're all very predictable in how you approach them and what types of ammo they drop.  Each of the three hub worlds have a different biome/setting, but the enemies largely do not change even though the environment drastically changes every 5 stages.  They may toss a few new enemy types in here and there, but it's mostly going to be fighting those 3-5 types for the entire game.- The level designs are really repetitive.  You enter a room, grab a key, etc. and all of a sudden the game spawns a wave of enemies to fight so you hunker down behind some cover or in a corner, try to pick them off, finally clear the room, move to the next room, have a new wave spawn, rinse, repeat...  The enemy placements get worse and worse as the game progresses with one of the favorite choices being enemies that spawn behind you or next to you, and it ends up feeling like the goal of the game is to spawn as many enemies as possible as frequently as possible in the worst initial placements possible.  Also, the boss fights aren't really that fun.- The weapons that you collect along the way aren't that interesting, and the ones that are interesting aren't that practical for use in combat and/or have very rare ammo drops.  In general though, most of the weapons are interchangeable, and you're just using whatever weapon you have the most ammo for.  The consumable items aren't that interesting either and using them is so cumbersome that you're often just better off not trying to use them at all in combat.- The game's progression isn't that great either.  You cannot revisit a hub after completing it which really cuts down on the exploration.  Also, the enemy counters for the stages seem to always be broken which is frustrating if you just want to casually revisit a stage and explore some more while 100%'ing the enemy kills.- Making things more tedious is the fact that the game has about the most ridiculous save system I've ever seen.  It has not 1, not 2, but THREE types of game saves: an autosave that triggers between stages, quicksaves that are limited-quantity consumables (Soul Tethers), and checkpoints within the stages that you can only use once per file (Shrines).  The three types of saves are all stored in their own category in the save menu, and it's really hard to keep track of which type of save you used last without looking at the timestamp for each of your save categories and figuring out which one is the newest.So given that the enemy and level designs don't really change much (or at least change for the better) as the game drags on, I'm just bored.  I started getting concerned about the game's repetitiveness partway through the first hub, but by the middle of the second hub I was truly bored.  I decided to stick with it until the third/final hub just to see if it changed things up at all, but it's just more of the same stuff as the first hub but with more "lock you in a room and spawn enemies" nonsense.I like old-school shooters and even find newer retro-styled shooters like Ion Fury to be OK, but this one is really a "one-trick pony" when it comes to creativity.  You'll have a great time for the first few stages but then the monotony will set in and you'll find yourself wanting to play something else.  I may be able to one day convince myself to finish off the rest of the game, but the 25-30 hours that I've put into it feel like an eternity - and not in a good way.EDIT: I decided to finish it.  If anything, the level design gets even worse in the final world.  The levels are even more labyrinthine, and the insta-kill traps in the Rending Chambers were a seriously bad mechanic.  The enemy roster also stays mostly the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only cleared 1 out of the 5 rather large main areas, but unless the game has labyrinth level design going forward I don't get the complaints and low review scores.-People say the levels can be confusing, but they push you forward and they follow Romeros level design philosophy of if you can see it, you can get there. Big red door blocking your way? What about that red key you could see on the top of a tower a little ways back? It makes sense.-Gameplay is awesome, the gore and gibs are great, and a lot of the enemy types are really cool. There's a Cacodemon right out of DOOM, but instead of it basically slowly flying around and shooting projectiles at you, if they get within a certain range they charge you. They also visually look pretty freaky, they put me on edge a bit once they start charging.-Weapons feel good. Lot of familiar stuff but they feel powerful, mainly because of the enemy feedback like limbs going flying off as well as heads. There's a slime gun that is out of Unreal Tournament, a DOOM double barrel, a pistol that is weak but makes up for it with its secondary fire, some cool sub-items(think Duke 3D) and more I haven't gotten to yet.-The game has a Quake style hub world. You pick one of 5 huge levels to play through. I imagine there's a "right" order to do them Megaman style, but I'm not sure on that. The first level I went into was the early access level which felt familiar and a lot more fleshed out.TLDR: If you like boomer shooters, you will like this game. Visually the game is quite stunning too. I enjoy so much I'm going to try to snag a physical PS4 copy, I'd like me a PS4 physical copy of DUSK too but I might have missed my window on that one.

_childDocuments_.review: Defeated the first and second boss and its pretty neat so far.+ Nice oldschool pixely graphics, beautiful enviroments > the good type of diversity.+ Controls good maybe a little too fast with the movement, fluid gameplay overall > one complaint is how bad you move on stairs / ramps, hold shift in places with an abyss next to the stairs or you will fall and die.+ Shooting feels real nice and weapons have an altfire, but melee so far feels a little wanting (but it sure is effective if you get the drop on enemies, also multihits are neat) > have found the mace, much more usefull weapon the altfire is amazing. Sadly I feel like these weapons are useless in most cases because most enemies shoot .Other than the altfire of the doublebarrel you dont have a good mid- slightly into longrange weapon (you have a longrange, very slow "sniper" type weapon later on in world 2), the revolver is just meh for killing anything but at least fairly precise. I usually use it to take out the small fries that I can not reach in melee. Its damage is crap, altfire is ok-ish at times (similar to shotgun thou). Most other weapons are too imprecise to be used at long range, at least without wasting massive amounts of ammo.One of the ranged weapons:  is fairly imprecise on longer range and the "bullets" have a long traveltime > making misses even more common, altfire is basically more RPM but way more imprecise > sure useful on the big guys in tight quarters but otherwise a little wasteful.Suggestions:> Weaponwheel would be nice, the artifacts have one as well. Please?> Perhaps add different weapon upgrades that have drawbacks, like more precision on sustained fire but slower RPM. Or a small bonus to reloadspeed for shotgun. Something to choose. For a personal note from the player. Could be aquired for collecting the runes in each level or as challenges.> The higher RPM weapons deserve a little more space in the ammo department.+ Enemytypes are ok, new types are slowly introduced > first world had a new enemytype right in the last level and the second world had a new one right away. You can tackle the levels in any order you want. I went natural order as I came across. World 3 went hard with 2 new enemytypes that are pretty strong. Really nice surprise, it literally killed me.The pathfinding is a little weird and enemies can get stuck on corners, mostly the screaming freaks that rush you. When you stand on a ledge the melee enemies will rush to underneath you in order to attack which does not work of course.+ The first boss felt a little simplistic at first but had a little bit more in there instead of only fighting, I am not going to spoil it. There were no adds in the fight, just 1v1 > GREAT.+ Second boss was a little bit more of a puzzle boss and then went into his proper boss fight, was a little hard to evade with the fast movement of your character > yes I did not mistype.How you are supposed to evade: , but you are too fast to stand in the correct spot, with shift you can switch to slower movement but I felt it was a little hard to manage  I can not imagine how to deal with this in the higher difficulties.- Enemy prefiring is annoying, tracking through walls is also a thing. _childDocuments_.review: UPDATE ON FULL GAME:WRATH: Aeon of Ruin is a $25 Quake community mod that delivers fluid gameplay in a dark gothic mood coupled with modern flourishes that diminish the short experience.Some notes while playing the full game*Having interpolation off adds a great deal to the immersion*A dash of pixelation goes a long way to crafting the perfect retro experience*Pop Tarts give me an unhealthy amount of gasA special shoutout to the ham fisted Developer/Publisher with the unicode trademark symbol in their name.  Imported Red Bull with 38% more bull testicle will not repair the atrophied executive function that has misled so many people over the decade.  The demo for Phantom Fury left a John Homes sized revelation to the community that in fact, those in charge have no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idea what they are doing.--Wrath is already outdated in the neo-fps era which is concerning since it's yet to be fully released after 4 years of development.  Of course, we've had a lot happen in those years...Like a fly darting toward the nearest pile of excrement, I hoped I'd find some golden corn kernels in the process.  It's a beautiful game and the large open areas in the Quake DarkPlaces source port is something to experience.  The movement is classic Quake tuned just right and features a cast of interesting weapons... except the Retcher.  While great for crowd control, it has too many similarities to the Bio Rifle from Unreal which has caused the world much suffering.The build I played feels like a prototype than an early access game.  My mind would constantly dart off and I would go on autopilot as I tore through enemies.  The antiquated save system didn't work in Daikatana and it fairs the same here.  I think it was about 15 minutes into the game before I got to use my weapon to pierce zombie flesh.The flavor so far has "been there, done that" and there is simply too much out there that does it better.  Reading that there will be no more bi-weekly updates on the game, I hope they are at the home stretch.  I'll be ready to fire up a new game when they release it, regardless of my rating of not recommended at this time.PROTIP: Turn the music up and the sound effects down.

_childDocuments_.review: A great 90s inspired shooter that i tried before but had to refund because it lacked a run toggle function and was too fast for my taste.Finally the developer added a way to toggle auto running off.I enjoy those games much more at a lower pace, being able to speed up using a sprint button if i need to.As i prefer to explore and look at the environment, finding secrets and breath in level design which might reveal some story elements or at least impressions to make your thoughtsThe good about such an option is, that i can playthrough at least twice. Once exploring slowly and doing it in my own speed/pace, the second time i can tryhard.It has only like 5 Levels so far. That doesnt sound like a lot and it isnt, but the levels are actually really long, branch off, feel very open and are packed with secret paths and other things.Now, take my playtime as the time needed to do one playthrough with the current content on normal difficulty and by taking your time exploring and looking for secrets without using a guide.The graphics are actually great and keep that aestetic of old shooters while appearing more modern This comes from the games good use of the Quake Engine by using modern techniques on lighting, shadows and shaders, particle effects and skyboxes/backgrounds.The hired Modders doing their job with that old engine clearly know their stuff.The overal style is a mix of Lovecraftian Horror and a Gothic architectured theme.Or in terms of game references, it plays and looks like a mixture of Doom, Hexen/Heretic and Quake.Coming with the current amount of levels, there are only five guns yet, each with an alternate firemode.Melee, pistol, double barrel shotgun, a Gatling Gun shooting Fangs/Bones instead of bullets and an Acid Grenade Launcher.Except for their appearance pretty basic stuff.Maybe theres more i havent found yet, but i doubt so.On top you can find items giving you special powers if you activate them. They are onetime use abilities like gaining a vampiric effect for a few seconds or creating a shield that deflects shots at you.Those items allow for some experimenting and are interesting enough to give the game some depth.Using one item allows you for example to turn an enemies aggression towards other enemies.The melee weapon, your main weapon, is also used for faster movement by using a charging attack, for more movement options.Enemy variety is a bit scarce. After having played 4 out of 5 levels i have seen the same enemies plenty of times, nothing new.You have your zombie, your zombie equipped with a gun being weak but ranged, your shooty alien, your flying a-hole alien, your charging fast zombie, your poison/acid zombie that explodes and a few more tanky enemies like the good old charging brute with lots of health and heavy melee attacks or the flying head shooting orbs at you.Pretty much exactly like Dooms Enemies with a bit of a different look, if you want a fast summary.Sound and ambience is great. Couldnt be better i guess. Music is "depressing" setting a mood, enemy sounds and other ambient sounds generate a feeling of urge and insecurity.Weapon sounds are meaty and are satisfying.Wraths Systems on their own arent really special if you think about it and most of the content comes off quite basic.However, the execution is top notch and the composition of all systems and features coming together make the game a really good pick, fun to play, interesting and enjoyable.Finally a rating on whats to come, meaning the roadmap:It looks like development follows a solid concept however without going an overly promising route.I would love to see the developer implementing a few more twists to the games core besides the standard levels.Maybe some sort of New Game+ Mode with infinite ramping up difficulty. Maybe a coop mode (multiplayer seems planned, but looking at how Levels are designed i assume its entirely focussed on versus).Or maybe a randomizer mode, a trend that seems to be growing more popular for other games like Super Mario Land, Dark Souls and whatnot, randomizing enemies, their locations or equipment drops.All of that could add more replayability and longevity to a really good game.Another alternative would be to use the Hub World in a more clever way than just making it a setpiece.For example it could whenever you finish a level you chose, have a changing effect on other levels and thus playing the levels in a different order provides a different experience, making them harder, block a passage or spawn more enemies of a certain type, well or the opposite and causing that an enemy appears less often.Right now the Hub World is a cool idea that isnt utilized in any way other than acting as a fancy level selection menu.A bit of a waste i would like to see being worked on.All in all i can recommend it.I bought Wrath in a pack with Ion Fury and thus making it more attractive.But i cant say i would regret this purchase at all. Wrath can stand against games like Prodeus or Amid Evil, maybe not against a game like Dusk, as its too light weight on story elements (pretty much empty).But it doesnt fall behind other games of its kind and makes an impressive appearance.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start from the beginning; WRATH Aeon of Ruin is not a bad game. It's a fun romp through some cool-looking environments, with fun weapons and nasty enemies to shoot at with them. It's a blueprint for a fantastic game. However, it's a game bogged down by strange design decisions, undercooked mechanics, annoying level structure, and generally a bit underwhelming.   -   The movement and action feel fantastic. Other than some noticeable jank with slopes and such, just moving the character around is a delight; there's no sliding, no weird weight or floaty jumping, and you're gonna spend much of the game's runtime weaving in and out of enemy crowds and strafing around big guys.   -   The weapons are quite distinct and varied, and all of them feel really good to use. Even if they're generally tried and true archetypes (revolver, shotgun, machine gun, grenade launcher) with a fantasy-themed coat of paint, they've got cool, creative designs, and are a joy to fire thanks to some fine audio design.   -   The enemies have really fun and interesting designs.   -   Graphically, it's a very pretty game, combining that chunky classic style with a high level of drawn detail, using colours and lights to enhance every piece of scenery you come across. While the art direction can be a bit generic at times, it's still got some striking sights to show you.   -   The big one: the saving system. It's a mess. The game gives players two options to save; either rest at a shrine, a one-time specific location that also regenerates your health, or deploy one-use items, called soul tethers, at any point you desire. While looking for soul tethers rewards exploration, you're never really gonna be strapped for them; they're frequent enough to always have one in store, but infrequent enough to have frustrating sections where dying will send you back ten minutes. Additionally, instead of just saving the last save point you made, the game seems to store two save slots at once; one for the shrine, and one for the soul tether. Even if it can be fixed with just loading up a save file, it's still annoying clicking the incorrect option and being sent back through a loading screen for no reason.   -   Oh my god does this game love its ambushes. In the first five levels it's a bit more tempered, but starting at the second act, the game's trick quickly begins degenerating into just throwing enemy after enemy at you: spawning them behind you, putting them in corners to jump you, making ten dudes just emerge from a room the moment you pick up an item. With how quick some enemies can whittle away your health, it gets old real fast.   -   Speaking of which, the enemies need a lot more variety. Their designs are cool and distinct, and they can all be identified easily; but a lot of them mainly serve to throw projectiles at you. There's no interesting gimmicks, no different archetypes to pay mind to. You get introduced to five or six different enemies in the first level, and it's not until the fifth you're introduced another one; I'm halfway through the game and I can only add one more to that list.   -   While the guns are very fun to use, their balancing is horrible. The revolver is reliable, but way too weak for what the game will throw at you at times; and the stronger guns meant to gib big dudes run out of ammo after two to three seconds of firing them. Imagine if in Quake, the nailgun chewed through its ammo in an instant, barely giving you enough firepower to take out a Shambler; forcing you to slowly peck away at the other four Shamblers in the room with your shotgun or your axe.   -   The artifact system; while neat in concept, the items the player can activate range from utterly useless to game-breaking. Things like the rebreather to breathe underwater are completely situational, while stuff like the force shield will allow you to cheese bosses in seconds.   -   The levels are way too large. A level will easily take you from forty minutes to an hour to complete, with just way too many dudes to kill. I ended up rushing to the exit the moment I grabbed the rune some times. Additionally, while the ambience for the levels isn't bad, they're so affixed to the theming of their hub that they feel really boring to get through. One desert level is fun; five desert-adjacent levels back to back are a slog.   -   The bosses are, for lack of a better word, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious. They're all about moving up and down different levels, while a static boss throws one of two immensely damaging attacks, drilling its sound effects into your skull as you die over and over until you remember to use your artifacts to cheese it.   -   The soundtrack is made by boomer shooter legend Andrew Hulshult, the type of guy you definitely want to get for a game like this. However, I don't know if it's just not his best work, or it was a direction thing, but the soundtrack feels completely aimless and boring; it's not punchy when it needs to be, or atmospheric when it needs to be, with tracks mostly consisting of slow, ethereal synths that are way too quiet, with the occasional metal feedback, with no building tension when showing a new enemy or a blast of energy when a fight ensues. A boss fight being almost silent in a game like this is an absolute sin.In my opinion, there definitely is some fun to be had with WRATH Aeon of Ruin, but that fun is only available to those willing to overlook a ton of strange decisions and frustrating sections. Only give it a try if you're really in the mood for something in this style, and you've already slammed through the big ones of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels smooth. As you would expect it to, coming from some of the fellas at 3D Realms, powered by the legendary Quake engine (Or id Tech 2). The movement is near perfect (A few issues regarding momentum and slopes) Weapons feel nice, they have enough impact behind them to make them fool good to use, with satisfying sound effects to really drive it home, although this isn't the case for all weapons, we'll touch on that later.There's a new save system, seeing people complain about it so much had me worried but after playing the game for myself, the complaints are unfounded. Basically, you can't quicksave unless you use a specific resource, of which the game throws a massive amount at you anyway. Playing on Outlander for my first playthrough, I finished all three stages at this point in time with 30 of the things leftover. And there's also a few save shrines dotted about the absolutely massive maps, to boot.The maps look gorgeous and are absolutely massive, with lots of winding paths and secrets, this is an absolute peak in terms of how a level can be made for an FPS. There is one issue, however. Enemy placement. Enemy placement for some of these maps is honestly just atrocious. There are a few examples of this but the worst one by far is the ending segment of the Gardens stage.Basically, you take an elevator down and they spawn a bunch of Wraiths, which is fine. And then they spawn a stupid amount of Heretics, we're talking like 14 of them at least, and these things have a hard-hitting projectile, an even harder-hitting melee attack, and they have a high stun value, so you can't just sit there and stunlock the lot of them. I died a good 15 times on this segment with the use of relics and every time I felt my deaths were the fault of the game. They spawn a few hard-hitting enemies after that, but the main issue for the segment are the Heretics.Besides that, 2 of the 3 levels are great, my favorite being the Mire. The Undercrofts are great, too. The Gardens need some enemy placement tweaks, and maybe some progression changes. I was bored for the first half, and the second half was mostly amazing, until the end.Let me preface this by saying that the game is in early access, so I don't fault them for having issues. Some of these are bugs, some of these are balance issues, and some of these are nitpicking.Slopes and momentum: As I said before, slopes can cause issues. I've had a few times where landing on one either cancels my momentum entirely or multiplies it by a factor of 10. It seems to be random what one it does if any, but it's frustrating.Enemy AI: AI is good for the most part, it does its job. However, sometimes they have issues getting around, I mostly spotted this with the 'boss' enemies and the Widow enemies.Enemy Balance: This is a big one. Most of the enemies here are balanced extremely well. The only ones that stick out like a sore thumb are Heretics (So much health, only get put into their stun animation by Fang Spitter's alt-fire, game will spawn them up your ass with zero issues) and the Widows (Game really enjoys hiding these dudes around corners for cheap hits, they hit hard, move fast, and don't seem to have a stun animation)Weapon Balance Coach Gun has no use once you get the Shotgun and Nail Gun Fang Spitter. The shotgun is way too powerful, I found myself using this thing for basically every enemy the majority of the time because the alt-fire is just that broken. Even on Outlander, the Shotgun alt-fire can 1 shot all but a single enemy in the game, the charge time isn't long enough to warrant how much damage it does, and to top it off, once the shots hit a wall or enemy, standard shotgun projectiles bounce all over the room, so 9/10 times this is your room clearer which invalidates the Bio-Rifle entirely. And if your first shot with the Shotgun alt-fire doesn't kill that pesky boss enemy, the bouncing projectiles probably will. This thing desperately needs a nerf, make it use more ammo, make it deal less damage, remove the bouncing projectiles, ANYTHING.The Fang Spitter can stunlock Heretics with its alt-fire, but it takes 15 shots to kill a single heretic, in exactly 1/4th of that time, you can charge the alt-fire on the Shotgun and one-shot one. The only reason to use any other weapon right now is because the enemies may be out of the (VERY GENEROUS) range of the Shotgun alt-fire. And then you use the Fang Spitter anyway.Good game. Some balance issues here and there, some bugs, which are to be expected, but nothing game-breaking. Nothing takes the game over its knee and breaks it in half (Besides maybe the Shotgun). And nothing ruins the enjoyment. The visuals are great, the levels are mostly great, and the enemies are incredibly well designed for the number we have at this point in time.

_childDocuments_.review: By all means considered, this game can be a great standalone play. However, it has a lot of glaring issues. The pistol feels too weak for what is essentially your only ranged weapon in the game. The Fangspitter got nerfed HARD recently against the only enemy it was really useful for, and it no longer has a decent ammo capacity to use it as crowd control. The enemy placement is a little unfair sometimes and the levels are (over all) a little boring in the artistic direction right now. Lastly, there is just some god AWFUL lighting in places that shouldn't be remotely as dark as they are. Turning your brightness up in the settings is an option, sure, but snow turns into god's light when you step outside.When you look beneath these issues though, you have a fine addition to the collection for this genre. But that brings up my last complaint, which is the hefty price point for a game that rides on the tails of Quake. I hope there is a lot more variation in the environments other than just castles and snow, because the level design and structure itself is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ excellent. We'll have to see if the game shapes up to be worth the price point, but for now, I would recommend the EA if you have some money to blow. 8/10.PS: Weapons, other than the pistol, feel pretty good. Maybe if the Fangspitter's damage and stun were beefed up a little more, I'd say it's almost a perfect arsenal. Just please, add a rocket launcher in the future. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: If you looked at screenshots or gameplay footage for this game or read some reviews of the Early Access version you might have considered getting this title, but read this first! Yes the premise is great: it runs on a source port of the very first Quake engine (Darkplaces) and fits designwise somewhere in between Quake and Hexen II. The weapon arsenal is similar to that of other shooters from this era: nothing we haven't seen in similar form before but they'll do the job. You have your melee blade, pistol, shotgun, rapid fire, grenade-likes, etc. Enemies consist of zombie types, semi-mechanical, biomutants and more eldritch creatures. They do not specifically match to the environmental themes of the maps but are well designed. As for the environments, some are really beautiful. You have your snowy necropolis, murky swamps, treehouses and oriental temples. That was the good part...Now for the problematic part: during the game you collect so-called soul tethers which function as save points for manual saving. the other save options being autosave at the beginning of each level and shrines at certain locations which also fully restore your health but are one-use only. You have the option to turn on infinite manual saves which I recommend you should do because this game does not value the player's time due to horrible balancing and pacing issues.Let's start with the enemies: they are dumb but they never miss, also they are complete bullet sponges. Some give you ammo upon defeat but it's only a small percentage of what you need for killing them. That's a bad ROI. They also do spawn in on certain scripted events a lot more than is needed.Next is the levels: there are 15 of them spanning over three epsiodes which also have one hub level and boss level each. They are huge and much much longer than they should be. I don't remember any level containing fewer than 300 enemies, most of them not being the cannon fodder type but the spongy one. Also often there is no clear path where to go next due to confusing and repetitive level design. Item placement is also very unbalanced. Most of the ammo is for weapons which are only effective at close range which is not very helpful if you get attacked from enemies on the other sider of the map. So it may take you an hour or more to finish a level. And yes that goes for *all* levels of this game. It does not change and it does not get better to the end.Playing through this felt like an absolute chore. I don't really remember playing a worse shooter than this in recent years. The sad thing is that this could have been great, like what Ion Fury did for the Build engine games this could have done for the Quake engine games. The artists did a very good job but the lack of pacing and balancing and therefore not having the feeling of making progress completely ruined the experience for me.What could have saved this game? First cut the level to the core removing any unnecessary repetition or areas that are just dead ends. This also should lead to better item and enemy placement. Maybe consider a linear approach instead of hubs. Second the enemies are way too spongy. Make them smarter instead or more vulnerable to specific weapons.I guess these changes will never be made so I cannot recommend this game. Don't be fooled by the attractive looks. It's not what it seems but a major disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first started playing Wrath: Aeon of Ruin, developed by KillPixel Games, and published by 3D Realms and 1C Entertainment, I immediately got a 90’s run and gun vibes. The game is very similar to Doom, Quake, etc. A reason for this is due to the fact that Wrath: Aeon of Ruin is a modified and upgraded version of the Quake engine ( a certain gaming engine that powered the game Quake.) The game itself is quite simple and there are only two main goals -- killing monsters and making it to the end checkpoint alive. Throughout different missions, the player will encounter a wide variety of enemies, weapons, consumables, items, and maps.As for enemies, there is a huge variety ranging from slow-moving weak units named Fallen, to quick flying enemies that fire blue orbs of energy known as Afflicted, and many more. This variety of enemies keeps each new level exciting and challenging. Players do not know what enemies they will be facing and must adapt and evolve based on certain enemies.At the beginning of the game, your character only starts off with a small wrist knife. As your character goes through upgrades and progressions, so does your arsenal. Throughout the different missions, players can scourge the map and unlock new and improved weapons. At the time of the early access, there were five weapons in total that could be used. Each of these weapons had their own strengths and weaknesses. The shotgun was great at up close and personal encounters but lacked in range. The fang spitter had an insanely fast firing speed but was very weak against tougher enemies. This leads to players using a wide variety of weapons in each level.In most video games, there is usually a large number of items or consumables the player can use. Wrath: Aeon of Ruin is no exception. There is a huge variety of these items that the player can use to give themselves a certain advantage in the game. Some examples are the vials of life that give players health, shotgun shells, as well as fangs that can be used as ammunition for your character's weapons. These consumables can either be found randomly on the ground or off of the bodies of fallen foes. The game also uses a unique respawning system based off a certain item players pickup called Soul Tethers. These items allow players to place down a marker surrounded by a white aura. If the player were to die, they would have the choice to respawn at the beacon. The player would then be teleported back to the exact time they placed down the tether. This concept was confusing at first, especially since there was no explanation, but most players could get the hang of it eventually.As for maps, there are three total realms with several missions in each realm. This variety gives the game a good amount of locations, but it does not have enough to confuse the players. This wide variety of maps gives the players the feeling of freedom and allows players to free roam.Overall, I feel that Wrath: Aeon of Ruin is a simple throwback shooter. The game may lack in actual story, but it makes up for it in action. If you are looking for an easy and fun shooter, Wrath: Aeon of Ruin is a great choice.
