_childDocuments_.review: I would have rated this game with the nonexisting middle option at first, but i encountered more and more flaws and problems, that made me abandon my neutrality.First the positives:- It has different weapons that use different attacks. Nice and diverse!- You can use two currencies to upgrade und customize all of your stuff.- Movement feels really nice with lots of dashes and default double jump, also you recieve more movement abilities later.- Enemies use different attacks á la Dead Cells.- The game looks really good!- Secrets exist.However, a lot of the good stuff is rendered meaningless by the problems:- The level design is AWEFUL! The game consists of a long winding corridor leading from start to finish that contains the exact same four-ish types of enemies in small groups. That is it. Different areas are not distinguished by anything but the "tier" of the basic enemy types (melee, ranged, big guy, spawner, critter, turret). It almost feels like basic random generation, but without the benefits.- The plot and the main charater are extremely bland. Sometimes when entering a certain area she will say some oneliner like "This looks really bad! I should hurry." which just adds to the depressing feeling of unfinishedness. They just should have left it (as well as the rest of the voice acting) out.- Your skilltree and your weapons let you aquire some passive skills that provide some kind of bonus damage, cc or protection. However, they are completely meaningless and add exactly nothing to the gameplay. The game also makes you chose between the skills you get, disabling the other half of the tree permanently. But since they have no impact, you don't care! The only useful thing is you being able to skill more movement speed to get through the boring corridor faster, be sure to pick it up.- While having different attacks, the weapons all feel the same. Especially they all have this insanely annoying delay before the first swing of each "combo". That means, you will not be able to hit an enemy before they hit you. With EVERY SINGLE ENEMY. However, this can be circumvented by using the one existing aerial attack, that does have not this lag, and, if timed right, skips the first delayed attack of the ground combo. That means, with every single weapon, you either spam the one aerial, or spam the one aerial into two other ground attacks to clear an enemy. On every enemy of the game.Therefore the weapons are reduced to BIGGER NUMBER? BIGGER DAMAGE!- I really do not like the random drop system for each equipment slot. It makes weapons feel so much less meaningfull if every single enemy in the game drops some kind of weapon, that will be recycled anyways - until your inventory is full...- Enemy attacks are either unavoidable or will never hit you. There is no inbetween. But since the long boring corridor is long, there are lots of enemies until the next checkpoint. Therefore you have two options. Either you take the heal skill and trivialize enemies completely, and, since the game solely consists of enemies in the long corridor, remove the small amount of gameplay you have left. Or you leave it out to make things interesting and get hit by unavoidable attacks and die.It gets especially awful, when there is a bunch of enemies clumped together. Either you randomly kill them fast enough or you slightly move in their direction and get hit by a bunch of attacks at the same time and die instantly from full health.- Basic sidesscroller combat mechanics are missing! Namely: Staggers and invincibility time. Since the game has no invincibility time after you getting hit, if you get hit, you will always get hit by multiple things at once. It also is always fun to take multiple unavoidable hits from the same single spike hitbox to lose you whole hp in less then half a second.Staggering: Most games have enemies stagger a little or get knocked back when you hit them, you just won't notice. But you WILL notice, when it is missing. Since the enemies will just do whatever they want and you can not do anything about it or get them off you. Also, it really looks weird and makes your attacks feel like they lack impact when they just stand still or continues their attack animation when getting hit.- The secrets are sadly very bland as well: See wall with hole, use movement ability fitting the type of hole. Secret done!- The bosses are quite interesting at first, since you can not trivialize them using the heal. However, they get hard by having huge amounts of health and - same as with common enemies - their attacks will either never hit you or are unavoidable.Therefore the best strategy is to stand in the boss, mashing attack (or jump attack, if the boss attacks really fast) and moving to the other side if the boss attacks. Repeat for a loooong time until either you die or the boss dies.The most annoying part is, that the whole game really has a lot of potential. Everything just is so rushed and bland. It feels like the developers never actually played any sidescroller and were just implementing things from a checklist "What you can use in YOUR sidescroller game!" But since they had no idea WHY they should be included, all features and mechanics end up being mediocre at best, and completely awful in way too many cases.If you want a "long corridor with enemies" game with random drops, just play Metal Unit instead! At least the levels are somewhat random and the weapons are way more interesting there!If you want to play a metroidvania with a world of connected areas and picking up upgrades and abilities, stay away from this game entirely!If you want to shut your brain off and have a casual, yet sometimes a little frustrating experience while traversing a corridor, you can pick up this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 80/100. This is a beautiful game, and no doubt everyone and their mother's compared Forgone to Dead Cells. My two cents is Forgone does its own thing, and while minimal, the storytelling is there, and combat is adequate with decent controls. Some improvements Forgone could use are fleshed out info on the various upgrade systems--the currency penalty to respec is too high to make you want to experiment with different combos. It's a shame, because I really wanted to test different melee and ranged weapon combos--there's just too much of a time and grind investment to make it worthwhile. Sadly, I found myself using the same spell set for the entire game because of the upgrade/respec costs. The same bit goes for spells/effects, weapons, etc. A bit of info on how weapons work and their pros/cons would be great. It doesn't really make much sense to me that there's so much loot, but you're restricted from experimenting and upgrading due to the currency and xp limitations. Another thing that could improve the experience is to scale up equipment resale value--pretty early in the game you'll start finding that reselling equipment doesn't give you as big a ROI as at the start of the game, which sucks, since it brings you back to grinding. The whole grinding process (doing side missions at the Outpost repeatedly) detracted from focusing on the game--basically you can pick game progression, or spend an hour grinding for coin and XP to experiment with one or two items/spells. So tldr, I enjoyed this game, but the upgrade system isn't rewarding enough to be worth the time investment. Overall, though, it's an enjoyable romp, and has its own style which I greatly appreciate!

_childDocuments_.review: You ever finish a game and just go “yeah, I guess that was okay?” Well, that’s Foregone in a nutshell. It’s a 2D action-platformer that is just now making its way to Steam after being locked behind Epic exclusivity.You travel through a bunch of areas linked together as this one, bigger world while also having the ability to warp back to a hub area through teleporters. Each area has its own boss and set of enemies, all of which drop a bunch of loot – be it a melee weapon, gun, or armor piece. These items can then be brought back to the hub area to be upgraded or salvaged, and you’ll definitely need to do this as they will quickly clog up your inventory. Otherwise, the looting, upgrading, and customization is fairly straightforward – you just pick whichever one has the bigger number.The combat is a bit better though. It’s simple in that there is effectively only one combo string per weapon, but it does feel good to play. There’s a nice amount of feedback, the dodging and movement abilities are responsive, the controls are intuitive, and the dynamic between having a melee and ranged weapon equipped simultaneously makes it more than just a button masher. There are also combat skills, including stuff like attack buffs, AOE attacks, and defensive ones too. The different weapon types add another layer on top of that. The spear, for example, is very fast, but doesn’t do as much damage, whereas the heavy sword is the exact opposite. Pair the heavy sword with the short-ranged, but powerful shotgun and you have quite the damage-heavy build. Or maybe you want to go heavy sword, but with a faster ranged weapon, like the burst rifle – the options are there. There aren’t too many different weapon types, but for how long the game is, there was enough for the combat to avoid that feeling of monotony.I saw the devs mention it would take between 10-12 hours to beat, but I finished it in just under 5 – and that’s with doing a decent amount of secret-hunting too. It’s not a game with much (or really, any) replayability – and that’s fine by me, but might be an issue for others. There is a new game+ mode at least, but I honestly can’t see myself ever taking advantage of it – it’s much more of a one-and-done kind of game.One of the Steam tags is metroidvania and I would say that’s only partially correct. You do unlock additional movement abilities and such that open up the exploration more as you progress, but the level design is incredibly linear and the exploration is limited as a result. On one hand, this does remove a lot of the backtracking that the genre usually brings, but it also leaves the game’s movement abilities feeling under-utilized. There’s a balance to be had there and Foregone tilts a bit too far to one side.I can’t say I was a fan of the story. It’s one of those “barely there” kind of stories, told mainly through info-dumping text logs found while playing and the occasional bit of dialogue or two. It’s more so a means to connect together the levels in a coherent manner rather than to tell anything of interest, which might not even be a problem for many.The pixel art has a decent amount of detail to it and the backgrounds are okay, but where it really shines is animation. It’s very fluid and helps give the combat that extra touch of visual feedback. The music has a couple nice tracks, but the rest is mostly forgettable – it’s not something I would come back to and listen outside of the game.On the technical front, the game is flawless. I had no issues running it at 1440p, 144 fps with no bugs or technical issues of any kind. The controls on both controller and keyboard and mouse are solid and I felt no need to rebind them, although the option is there. In fact, the keyboard and mouse controls were intuitive enough that I didn’t even need to look up the bindings when testing them for this review – it just worked and played well right out of the box.Foregone is a competent action-platformer overall, not really bringing anything new, but not being outright bad in any one area. It’s one of those indie games that serves as a nice palate cleanser in-between other games and I know that sounds bad, but as someone that plays a ton of longer games, it’s always nice to have something smaller to break them up. Still, I would not recommend it as an immediate buy. Rather, give it a look if you can find it on sale or if you’re really into the genre. Otherwise, give it a pass.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!!

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty good overall.Gameplay:-It's draws inspiration from the metroidvania style of games, but is more linear (the linearity is not a bad thing- as it's more narrative driven).The world isn't one large map to explore, but rather different zones that have their own maps. Backtracking/ grinding is made easier this way.-The overall difficulty of the base difficulty setting is not that bad, and welcomes any possible newcomers looking to get into metroidvania style games.-The progression of your character is through upgrades, you buy for your skills, and weapons that drop from crates and enemies, instead of leveling up. This makes grinding waaayy less painful if needed.-Loot drops are extremely generous in this game and you will be getting higher tier items for stuff before you can complete an entire set of any current tier you may currently have equipped (like in a Diablo, or Borderlands game).-Game has higher difficulties upon beating it, and even a New Game+ on top of those.-Contains voice acting for three characters, and they are decent.Story:-Is pretty short, and I do wish it was longer. If nothing else to flesh out the world and lore more. The story feels like a draft that was turned in as an essay, but struggled to meet the word count.-I finished normal difficulty in 6.9 hours (nice).Game will take longer to 100% for achievements and map exploration (I.E: get new skill, and go to previous area to see where you can explore now with it).-The story is good, but extremely done before, and EXTREMELY predictable.I was able to guess every "twist" they tried to introduce Every.Single.Time.-The game ends immediately after last boss with no pan-over the world during credits, end scenes, etc. So the impact that final scene was supposed to have is a bit "Meh" to me.-The lore in the world isn't hidden/ doesn't make you piece it together akin to a Souls, or Hollow Knight game; which is fine, as you know what's going on at all times.But it's extremely light, and makes the story very very predictable.Graphics:-I enjoyed the pixel art styles used.The backgrounds are pretty darn cool looking, and in my opinion the art for the scenery looks much better than the character models for your character and the monsters.-If you played Hollow Knight, there is one map in this game that looks pretty damn similar to the City of Tears from that game. Rain, structures, and all.I straight up DARE the devs to say that map wasn't inspired by The City of Tears.-Bosses looked bland compared to other games.Soundtrack: -Pretty decent. The songs are long enough to not loop in an annoying fashion if you spend more time in any given area.-The sounds used though sound like a cheaper Vst/ library of instruments used though. Like some songs sound brilliant, but others it's easy to tell it's not a real orchestra playing, etc.Though the ost is decent, the only stand-out tracks to me are the credits song, and the after any boss fight song. Those two are pretty darn nice.Summary:-Overall a decent purchase for it's base price of 20 bucks, or less on sale.I can see myself coming back to it to play with a different build, or 100% it, or play on the New Game+ mode.-I do recommend this game if you want to get into Metroidvanias, but are intimidated by their difficulty, as this one is not too difficult at all.

_childDocuments_.review: My first impression was the following..."so it's kind of a subpar version of dead cells but instead of a roguelite its a story based arpg with randomized loot and handcrafted levels. You would think by ditching the roguelite genre and going for a handcrafted singleplayer experience it would at least be able to differentiate itself from dead cells enough to be worth playing, even if the combat wasnt quite as good. But the story is generic, the randomized loot and skill trees are not interesting, and the maps might as well have been randomly generated. Otherwise the gameplay is almost an exact clone of dead cells (though slightly scuffed).So at the end of the day, unfortunately I have to agree with most of the other negative reviews. It is just a bad imitation of Dead Cells. Just go buy and play that game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Likes💚 Very fast combat and movement.💚 Choose your fighting style via weapon type.💚 Talents and stats allow you to create your own build synergies.💚 Melee + Ranged gameplay offers interesting choices and combinations to experiment with.💚 Excellent telegraphing animations give you the opportunity to dodge multiple attacks like an action hero.💚 Advanced movement techniques available from the beginning (Slide + Jump + Jump).💚 "Animation cancels" add depth to combat (Shotgun -> Dash -> Melee).💚 Novel pixelart using mixed 2D and "down-rendered" 3D with dynamic shadows and lighting effects.💚 Dropped currency automatically moves toward you when close enough.  No need to slow down to pick things up!💚 Forgiving "ledge grab" animation when jumping to the side of a ledge.💚 Secrets hidden throughout each zone. Some are only unlockable after certain tech is acquired.💚 Death doesn't feel frustrating; you're able to retrieve your currency from the spot you died at.💚 Very few cutscenes; most are just short boss introductions.Dislikes❌ Weak story doled out via journal entries kills the pacing.❌ Getting the character to aim at your intended target can be difficult.❌ Crit Chance and Crit Damage seem to be missing from the stats screen.❌ Fighting enemies on the end of ledge from below can be really frustrating because you keep grabbing and falling.Summary📖 Blazing fast gun & sword combat right out of a fighting game, progressive loot to fit your playstyle, and interesting enemies & bosses.  If you like fighting games and/or platformers with more depth to their combat, definitely give Forgone a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I am probably going to highlight all the things that keep this from being a good to great game, and instead keep it mired in just being OK. It's still a recommend if you really like the genre and are comfortable abusing animation cancels etc. to make the combat feel like it's probably supposed to.It's a competent game but it falls short in essentially every aspect, where some more attention to detail or getting feedback would have gone a long way. The graphics are pretty but they are very flat, and this leads to them being less appealing than they should be, as well as numerous issues of enemies sometimes being hidden behind other enemies or corpses. The weapon variety is interesting except they aren't balanced, at all. There are essentially 2-3 viable melee types, 1-2 ranged types, and everything else is niche or hindering yourself. This is compounded by the clunkyness of the natural combat, but if you animation cancel the combat feels a lot more "right", to the point where I think you're SUPPOSED to play via animation cancelling. The abilities are all fairly different, except using them locks you into an animation where you can get chunked, so you have to use them proactively and not reactively. Also you can only have two at a time, and the heal is so essential that you need to have it, so you really have 1 at a time, and have to return to base (or find one of the rare skill stations that are in locations where you find new ones) to swap them. Honestly even if you had access to all of them at once it wouldn't affect you that much.The talent tree is pretty pointless. It's a bunch of small, passive boosts, some of which aren't explained at all in the details, and respeccing takes a bunch of time but since they are mostly small passive boosts it's also not worth your time to do it. The boost you get from investing in abilities is a little better but you just want to invest in Heal and whichever other ability you like, and just maxing those out will take the entire run or so.The boss fights are mostly good but the second phase is always mostly running from things and periodically hitting them, which makes certain weapons and abilities even more pointless as you have to always be moving and only have small windows to retaliate. Also, only 2 bosses have skippable intro scenes, so if you die you have to endure those each time (the fact that 2 of them are skippable indicate they know how to do that, and just... didn't?).The random loot suffers from the same issue as most tiered loot games, once you start seeing a new tier drop the other ones become completely garbage. Which means there's just a bunch of junk dropping all the time. Also, it's not clear how important the primary stat of everything - power - actually is, but it is important and often you just want that to be highest on everything you wear which takes away mostly everything choice-wise. You can reroll modifiers on weapons but it costs resources AND you have to complete a challenge level to get to that NPC which means it's not really worth your time until you're near the end of your current run because you're just going to replace that gear in 10 minutes anyway. Despite all of these shortcomings, the game is still an OK action platformer, it just is constantly reminding you of how it could have been better. I would say for $10 it's fine but I would have been more unhappy at $20. So I recommend it for fans of the genre looking for more, as it's a bit different, not too long, and has some ideas. It's a shame it couldn't polish everything together though.Edit: I know on the surface the graphics resemble Dead Cells, and it's a 2D action platformer, but honestly the similarities end there. They don't feel even remotely close even though weirdly, they share a lot of similar shortcomings, but in their own respective ways.

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game because personally I enjoy it. With that being said; this game suffers from an identity crisis. It took the visual aesthetics of Dead Cells, the map and weapon design of Symphony of the Night, but it brought absolutely no originality of its own to the table. I mean no disrespect to the developers, but this isn't a small indie genre anymore. A true exquisite example of making a game like Symphony of the night while adding your own character and essence is Record of Lodoss War-Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth. They came to steam early access, and they have taken their time to make a fantastic action adventure platformer. Forgone is not a metroidvania, people need to stop adding that tag to everything. On the flip side the game really works well; this game is competently made. The combat is crisp and fluid, the scenery is vibrant and surreal. The problem is, everything the game has to offer has been seen before and done better. Superior offerings maybe few and far between, but in our contemporary gaming space they can all be found on steam easily. You can't go to Epic game store then come out on steam with a lackluster offering. Gamers are precisely the ilk that are petty and have long memories. Big Blue Bubble's exclusivity choice didn't stop me from purchasing and recommending this game, but the lack of improvement and that choice may have stopped others. So while I do recommend this game, I hope Big Blue Bubble have updates at the ready to make this an offering worth more attention. In days gone, this game would have been a record setting Indie offering, but the age of Mediocrity is quickly dissipating. Indie developers have to be more than just competent now, they have to be imaginative. That isn't something you can just emulate, and slap a price tag on.

_childDocuments_.review: Foregone (FG) was another of those games that I was on the fence about for a while because I wasn't sure that it'd be for me. Fast-paced action can be enjoyable, but with the trailer skipping around so much, I wondered how tight the timing is, or how heavily punished mistakes might be. Despite trying to get a better sense of this game before picking up a review copy, only by trying it myself was I able to experience some of the problems others hadn't more strongly pointed out.  Despite coming into FG with decent hopes, it didn't take long before I saw some bad signs and how elements of the gameplay don't work together well. For instance, when the stage layouts are designed a specific way, having loot drop randomly doesn't make much sense. Systems like that work more logically in procedurally-generated games, where you'll see different results across random scenarios and encounters. In FG's case, I'd rather earn specific weapons at set times, as they should be well-balanced for the developer's laid-out maps, “Try this spear, as it's a good weapon for these kind of conditions. Just kidding, I hope you like those nunchucks, because that's what RNG gave you.”Another bad sign was when I got a healing ability near the very beginning, as that suggests avoiding damage, even early on, isn't as reliable or easy as you'd expect. Despite having firearms, with enemies afflicting you with poison and sometimes blasting you from point-blank range, you'll quickly rack up damage while not feeling as if you've been hit that much. Instead of mechanics where you're better able to maneuver and beat enemies, it's like you're expected to absorb some hits, use resources to heal, recuperate from killing other enemies, and continue this cycle until you reach a checkpoint. If the melee weapons didn't have such stupid handling, as they all have a basic combo system that includes significant delays, you might not deal with so many cheap shots.   Something that was bothering me early on was menu navigation, as all of them seemed to have sub-menus, and would be accessed with either set of shoulder buttons. I kept mixing up the inputs and changing the wrong thing. Even choosing what upgrades I wanted or selling excess weapons seemed unnecessarily clunky. However, after some time with it, I adjusted to how it works. With regards to platforming, I didn't seem to run into the same problems others were having.  During the game's introduction, matters look bleak, setting the stage for a grim location as you try to hold back an invasive force. When that dissipated into a dream sequence, with such a different environment and no further explanation on what's actually going on, I felt misled by this cutscene. Even if something like that actually did happen in the past, why can't you catch me up to speed on what's happening now? These people are theoretically your allies, so can you expand on anything pertaining to them? I'm confused by this introduction and lack of knowledge.  I'm usually not too picky about how a game looks, but there are aspects to FG's design that I don't enjoy. A simple but recurring one was not having a better sense of items that are in the fore or background. When I'm running around an area, smacking random junk to see if it'll break, it's nice when I can easily distinguish between decorations and something worth a few coins. Many times though, I'll find something that looks like junk I could break, but it's indestructible. This also happens when trying to find secrets, as I'll try jumping to a higher area, but it's actually just background matter. I find the main character and her movement a bit uncanny as well, as it seems like she should have a higher resolution, but looks blurry. Plus, her run cycle looks stilted and awkward.  Setting-wise, the game makes me think of a sci-fi area, where things may or may not be at the post-apocalyptic level. Based on how the music sounds though, it makes me think of a more tribal location, especially with the woodwind notes. Although I enjoy the music, it's a bit discordant, clashing with soldiers and firearms. Despite that small misstep, I otherwise enjoyed the tunes, and don't have any complaints with the composer(s) who worked on them.  🌟 I was intrigued by the store when it first started. They just dissolved it away with a dream sequence. Otherwise though, that'd have been an interesting beginning. 🌟 You're a female protagonist, but not being displayed as eye candy.  ❌ Even though enemies are clearly sentient, if you hit and run, they'll forget about your existence after a few seconds. They should be a bit more advanced than bugs. ❌ Bosses seem like massive damage sponges when you do such little amounts of damage to their health bars. Especially when using upgraded gear.❌ The game's grindy. 🔍 Although I was making use of the dash slide, I'd spam melee attacks and jumps more than anything. Jumping will cancel your long, annoying attacks, but let you use the faster ones. They're generally better anyways, so it's not a detriment. 🔍 Make use of your healing ability and firearms frequently. You'll replenish the ability and ammo from killing enemies.  From what I played of FG, I didn't find its game design invigorating. Even when I was getting resources for upgrades, the increments I'd purchase were so minuscule that it seemed pointless. Increasing my health by 1% isn't going to do much when enemies knock off chunks of it at a time. Plus, the small tidbits of a story were scattered across journals with far too little frequency to hold my interest or give me any sense that I know what's happening. Exposition isn't your enemy. I found many of the elements misfired in FG, taking the skin of a popular title, Dead Cells, and ending up without its soul.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up for 5$ and am glad I did not pay more for it. This game tried to add so much and got nothing right.Story:  Could have been interesting, but ends up all over the place. Lore is dumped on you by books on pedestals (which look out of place) and comments by the MC (which make no sense in some contexts). The "twist" was not really one and you will find it hard to give a damn.Art: The background art of the levels is very nice and would have been the saving grace of this game if it wasn't packed into the most uninspiring level design ever. The character models are ok, and the menus look like they were ripped out of a mobile game. Sound: Decent enough. The MC had nice voice acting, the last boss was a total miss though making it seem almost comical.Design: Simply bad. You go through 2-3 boring levels and fight a boss. You do this 4 times. Then you do this 4 more times because the bosses get recycled. Speaking of which, you will be fighting the same 5 enemies in every level. You will be using the same 4 weapons which are uninteresting stat sticks. The skill trees are a joke and do not invite you to experiment with any synergy. Respecs cost a lot of gold which you will not want to spend in the story. This is just a typical grinding skinner box only without satisfying rewards. The "secrets" are just more uninteresting randomized low level loot or upgrades to skills that you will never use because you can only equip 2. The "missions" are pointless unless you love the combat (which you wont). I can guess the devs wanted to go for replayability with the random loot and missions and upgrades. The only problem is, you will want to uninstall this chore as soon as you are done with it and never touch it again. If you must get it, get it on a deep deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and kind of simple, but what's there is *really* polished. The animations are fantastic, combat is fluid and feels great, sound design is on-point... it's a good game, just don't expect something with much replay value.EDIT:After writing the above, I reinstalled just so I could play a few more hours. That's a good sign! The gear in this game is in the vein of something like Diablo, where each item has a random selection of affixes. Some are simple, like "+15 to health" but others interact with the combat mechanics or skills. Between the item affixes, skills, skill trees for both skills and your base character, there's plenty of room for a lot of different builds. Skill points can be refunded at any time for free, so it's easy to experiment.There are basically two game modes: the main story, and "missions", which are timed challenges. Personally, I like the timed aspect, because it forces the player to consider their gear and think about what kind of synergies would help them kill things fast enough to beat the timer, rather than just relying on dodging.Speaking of, dodging is really easy, because the AI is way too lenient. Every attack has a long wind up, and for at least the first 80% of the game, the enemies don't track you after the windup starts. At the very end, enemies learn how to turn around, but this comes way too late in the game. And in New Game+ mode, the AI in the early game remains unchanged, which renders the combat pretty brain-dead. There's also not much variety in enemies. At the very end, there's a few twists that I liked, like how the guy who does the electrical slam attack and shoots lighting to the sides. That sort of enhancement is a great way to keep enemies interesting, and it's disappointing that there's not more of that. The level design is serviceable, but very linear. That's not terrible in itself, but it does feel weird when combined with the necessity of replaying the early levels in order to collect all the secrets. That part isn't very fun. The main flaw of this game is that while it's mechanically polished, the content is shallow. Still gets a thumbs up from me -- a game doesn't have to be perfect to be fun. And the negatives provide some good lessons in what not to do, should I ever follow my dreams and make a similar game myself.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a "meh" review. A good example of a "sorta ok" game. An action platformer (not a metroidvania) that blatantly tries to copy dead cells, instead of being its own thing, and fails due to lack of depth and polish (don't be fool with how pretty its graphics are)Combat can be fun, but most of the time you're going to be clipping near an enemy, which interrupts your dodging mechanic, making you stutter in place and getting hit. level design and enemy variety are plane and repetitive. Abilities offer some variety i guess, but the dashing attack is so useful i don't see a reason to change it and why would you ever change the healing ability since is the only way to effectively heal (which also stuck you in place the more damage you receive, while still getting hit) The damage feedback is really lacking. Sometimes is a little, sometimes is a lot, sometimes you wont notice and die. Also, upgrading your abilities (with some blue shard thingys)  cost so much you are going to focus on 2 or maybe 3, without any chance to re-spec points. The only way to further upgrading them is by farming the blue things (yes, you can farm in this game...) but it takes so long i didn't bother at all. the story and plot are so generic and shallow I guarantee you wont care at all. Boss fights are good, until they start spamming ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ attacks. but at lest they're not impossibly hard and enough of a challenge to keep trying a few times. Overall, is it a good  non-roguelike, dead cells-like game? no, but is a step in the right direction i guess. And it did manage to "entertain me" enough to finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: Foregone is very good! So good that I've been procrastinating writing this review by playing the game. The combat is fantastic. The whole experience is smooth with plenty of weapons, upgrades, and enemies to keep it interesting.The key to Foregone is the ridiculous amount of weapons. You're constantly finding new weapons to compare. It's similar to Borderlands or Diablo. Weapons have different kinds of attacks so they matter. For example, the Falchion attacks much slower but it replenishes your skills more. So there's a lot of depth to consider when you're comparing the weapons, leading to some panicked moments. Do I choose the weapon I enjoy the attacks or select the weapon with better stats? There are plenty of ranged weapons as well.The thing about Foregone. No matter what the combat always felt fluid, fast, and fun. The controls are responsive enough to go through a gauntlet of spikes with ease. So the game throws a lot of enemies at you on different levels. Ones shooting from up high with larger melee enemies on your same level. So you need to prioritize which enemies are the most dangerous and take them out first. There's a surprising amount of enemy variety. Although they do some repeats later on it's about which enemies are grouped up rather than different types.Overall, I had tons of fun playing Foregone. The levels remind me of Dead Cells and the weapon comparisons have me hooked. I wish I could have played a higher difficultly from the start since it ended up being pretty easy. This one really surprised me.Video review,

_childDocuments_.review: This is an OK game but very short and only worth buying if it's on sale. Definitely don't pay full price for it, I'm glad I didn't.Gameplay suffers from death by a thousand papercuts. Some examples:- Enemy collision is poorly done, with a slow pushback that makes your character spaz out, can get you stuck, or ledge hog you. - Traversal is regularly frustrating - Level design is filled with barely-out-of-reach ledges that require circuitous horizontal routes to reach, ledge/platform grabbing gets totally jorked if you do anything in mid air, many hazards are excessively narrow, and the wall jump is buggy as hell and half the time causes a double jump instead. - Item acquisition/randominity can be either great or frustrating with no middle ground, and with most of the talent/passive upgrades being so minimally impactful you can get really boned if you don't get lucky. - It's way too easy to get locked into weapons you don't like if you get a powerful drop followed by a wasteland.- Very few passives are interesting, fun, useful, or meaningful.- The heal very rapidly becomes total garbage no matter how much you upgrade it.- Time trial side missions are neat in theory, but in practice jerky level design and trap placement can screw you way too easily.- Stat rerolling has terrible stat pools and blowing resources on it feels really bad half the time, meh a quarter of the time, and ok when you actually get something you want.- Bosses are extremely gimmicky rather than challenging, except for the last boss, that just puts a ton of unreadable effects on your screen but I beat almost exclusively by mashing attack.Finally, I think we can admit that nobody plays metroidvanias for the story but if you're going to subject players to one, hire a real writer please. I couldn't come up with a more tropey story if I used a bingo sheet. The good guys are actually the bad guys and the protagonist caused everything but good intentions and also the villain is her son? Oh dear where I have I seen this story before just kidding it's literally every Saturday morning cartoon.

_childDocuments_.review: Positive review but strings: [TLDR: Good for 7-9 hours. Buy on sale]Core game play loop was enjoyable, but I wish it were easier to try different builds. Each build (I can imagine several viable ones: Bombs [what I used], Tethers, Aftershocks, Plague, Skill Spam, & Straight auto attack) is based on skill choice and item lines. Skills can be reset for gold, but resetting them would weaken you unless you had a whole other set of items ready to go for the new build. You can roll new lines on items, but it costs increasing nongold currency and is random. You also should only upgrade gear after getting the lines you want. The items progress in color rarity through the game and appear to end on red. The red items have random special lines on them that cannot be reset. I imagine there is some fun to be had with the unique abilities granted by them, but it is costly to get the right lines on the right special lined item. I played through the game using bombs and upon starting NG+ wanted to try something new. The time involved to get to test my new idea burnt me out. The items dropping at the start of NG+ were exceptional, but the difficulty ramp made it not exciting anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't sleep on Foregone. It plays pretty much the same as the most 2d sidescroller hack & slash games but it is still fun and surely can entertain for a weekend. I finished it in one sitting (6.5 hours total) and while it's pretty much a straightforward game I was enjoying its gameplay. It has enough enemy variety and weapon variety to keep you invested in the game. The level design is straightforward, although there are portals and you can re-visit the previous levels you rarely have a reason to do so. Bosses are mostly unique and fun. Unfortunately, 3 of the bosses repeat (and there is a reason for it story-wise) and I am not exactly a fan of it. Regardless of that three repeats, the bosses are unique and can be somewhat challenging. With the right build, you become almost unstoppable. It is pretty much the same scenario for almost every rogue-lite & metroidvania available but since Foregone is already a short game I can say at least 1/3 of the game becomes run and gun (or run and melee in the game's context). It's fine given what is Foregone's mentality and I can assure you it's not copying Dead Cells as some people suggested -although they look akin they play differently- and I think weapons are balanced enough overall to make me wanna try and use each and every one of them. Some of them did feel better however, I can easily vouch for any ranged & melee weapons in the game. You also get to upgrade your weapons (as well as armors and trinkets) and you do not need to re-visit older places or repeat the same sections to grind as there are missions (time-limited, they are tense) and they also reward you upon completion you also get to grind while doing those. The good thing is you don't lose your currencies (for both upgrading weps and acquiring skills) while you do those missions unlike playing on a regular level. Normally, you lose your currencies upon death and you need to get back and pick them up (or make a deal with the ferryman and let him keep half of it and get back the other half without risking losing it completely). It's pretty much a common mechanic today and I did not think it was a big deal either, I have used Ferryman's service only once. It is easy to turn Foregone into a cakewalk after a short while. Honestly, I would have wished if it was a little bit longer and there were boss fights with 2 phases. Additionally, I loved the idea of requiring to hit enemies with melee in order to replenish ammo. In that way, you try to make the best out of your weaponry. Combining ranged and melee attacks feel good. Controls are responsive, animations are pretty much solid and combat & platforming are fluid. The story is there but it's not entirely stunning and blazing. Tbf, I found the ending weak despite the final boss fight being enjoyable, the identity of the final boss was pretty much a good revelation and you get to choose an ending. But upon completion, it felt trivial. It's a good effort at the end of the day and I would like to see more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid Metroidvania title that has a lot going for it, although it doesn't 'break new ground' in a sense.For me, personally, this has all of the traits I look for in a genre like this: fluid, fast motion, fun combat, a good sense of exploration, and enough platforming to be nice without being frustrating.  The backdrops are pretty varied: from forests, to sewers, to an extremely well-done cemetery/mausoleum, the retro-style graphics all capture it quite well, and make for a lot of awesome screenshot moments.The weapon system is nicely varied, and while it's fun to experiment with all of the ranged and melee types, you'll probably find your favorites early on.  The frustration is that the loot quality/drops are random, so you could like how the daggers feel, but you may never get a high-level legendary or mythic version of them.  Thankfully, most of the weapons feel great to use.What really makes me love this game is that the motions feel so smooth and fluid, and the retro-style really compliments that well.  Sliding or dashing through an enemy wind-up to unleash a quick combo on their free side feels nice, all the way to the end.It's not without drawbacks: I played almost the entire way through without realizing there was a map that I could access through the inventory screen; a tutorial or early reminder on that would have been nice, because it's almost necessary for accessing prior-level secrets that you couldn't get to at first.I also did my first playthrough only using the first two skills that you could gather, and never felt truly pushed to switch my skill loadout at any point.  I applaud the developers for not creating bosses or blockpoints where you are forced to switch skills just to progress, but if you can go an entire 10-hour run without touching the others, it feels a tad wasted.CONCLUSION: B+.  This is a very good addition to the Metroidvania genre, and it gets my personal recommendation for any fans of action-platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought at £2.32, an 85% discount. At this price, give it a try. I've played less than 2 hours but I'm not going to refund but probably won't play this again. It's entirely possible that playing more would prove me wrong and if anyone has any corrections, feel free to comment.If you like the game, I'm happy for you but here are my personal issues with it, your mileage may varyAs far as I can tell there have been NO patches since steam launch, just under 2 years ago so any issues I list (if you would consider them issues) won't be addressed. This was just dropped and forgottenTooltips are terrible. -You can't find out your crit rate on the stats page, literally the easiest thing to implement, why isn't this a thing? Literally amateur hour ♥♥♥♥. You have no indication what base crit rate is and the only way to find your crit rate bonus is to tab through your equipped items, individually and keep track of that, mentally-"Power" rating on weapons, armour and accessories isn't explained and seems to have no actual impact on actual effectiveness, how about an actual breakdown of damage? What does "Power" mean on a necklace? Is it the rating of the bonuses listed below it?-DPS doesn't seem to be a reliable indicator of actual DPS. It apparently doesn't take crits into account either.-When you proc an effect like leech or haste their should be an icon to signify this, as far as I'm aware, there isn'tThe "Diablo-like" loot system doesn't seem to mesh with the rest of the gameplay and is severely undermined said tool tip problems, most of the time, the pop up showing what the item on the ground is, doesn't show up, so you're forced to enter your inventory to actually check, interrupting gameflowAttacks don't feel like they have great amount impact, jumping and attacking an enemy on the edge of a platform seems to push you off. Controlling your character just feels "off" in generalThe skill tree is hugely limited, you can very easily max out one of the basic trees early game and honestly, I didn't see a huge difference. Abilities don't scale with weapons or any universal levelling, only via random modifiers and the underwhelming skill tree which means most of the time your abilities will be severely outclassed by weapons or become underpowered and obsolete. Useful early game, not so much laterThere isn't a dodge cancel (as far as I'm aware), it detracts from what should be fast paced, skill based gameplay and feels horrible when you should be able to get another hit inThe dodge range seems just a bit limited, the first boss has a continuous swinging arm attack that the dodge is just to short to dodge through. This may be a case of git gud but am I going to restart the game to check if I just needed to be really really close to him and time it better? No.I know there's going to be the age old riposte of "must be a dead cells fanboy lol" but no, my criticisms are completely divorced from me comparing this to dead cells. I happen to prefer Metroidvanias without roguelike elements so I really should prefer this but the quality just isn't there.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun for the price, however it has some shrotcomings. The combat is very smooth and the loot system and progression feels good for about 70% of the game. For me it wasn't a challenge because I've played metroidvanias quite a bit, so it was a bit boring at the end. The story is lackluster and it can't decide if it is cyberpunk or medieval themed. It is nicely voiced, so I will give them that. Unfortunately the bosses are very easy if you do a good job with your loot and skills, and the last boss was literally easier than the first boss which is silly. The lategame also suffers, as the NG+ option is kind of dull. You play again but all the maps and upgrades in secret areas have already been taken/revealed, so there is no point other than just getting more loot and maxing out some skills. Kind of disappointing. The secrets in this game are very predictable and that also makes it disappointing. _childDocuments_.review: It's pretty. The "Dead Cells" comparisons are warranted. I want to like it. So much of it just short of the mark. The plot has an interesting idea and then just never really develops. The weapon system is simple and annoying. It really wants you to synergize with abilities but, it more tries to pigeonhole you into doing one thing and then you just find a way better weapon that breaks your synergies anyway. I'd rather the upgrade system track across the weapon types always? You swap/acquire new gear so fast that upgrading feels silly most the time and then you just do it because you have way too much gold all of the sudden. But you'll never have enough of the crystal/essence. That's just an endless grind for the achievement since you won't use any of the skills after the first 2. Combat itself is fine. There's a questionable collision detection with enemies that kicks your dodge weird directions and will get you killed through stagger locks. New Game+ is just kinda pointless.Maybe I'm just bitter since I did everything except for a grindy achievement that almost doubled my playtime for absolutely no reason and that just gave me a lot of time to build contempt. The game has good bones and just needs to be fleshed out. Hopefully it gets some updates or free DLCs.Oh yeah, a lot of stuff just kind of fades into the background (e.g. hazards and ledges). _childDocuments_.review: Like most people who have played Dead Cells (DC), Oof course I will compare this game to it.The Pros:+ Animation: It's pixel art, similar to DC.+ Combat: The the weapons have combo of more than 3 hits, and that looks cool, cooler than DC (I think).But that is just about it for the nice things. The rest are bad.The Cons:- Story: They try to come up with somgthing with more depth than that of DC, ended up having nothing more than a lot of boring text. Confusing.- Map Design: There are hidden locations, but the devs use them to hide a few valuable items and the upgrades for Special Moves and that are supposed to be available for the users in the upgrade tree. You can only access 80% of those locations after having acquired 2 certain abilities: Ground slam, and Wall climb. This makes the upgrade tree completely useless, at the same time forces the player to return all the locations to dig. It's a TEDIOUS process.- Leveling up: Just lots of grinding and looting. TEDIOUS.- Control: Wall jump is so stoopid.- Weapons: A variety of melee and ranged, but they are not different enough from one another to change the play style. You end up choosing only the swiftest ones. You can re-roll the buffs, but the stat pools are so random it cannot help the items in your inventory to work together. Oh and each re-roll costs, and it gets more expensive each time. So at some point you have got to accept what you have, or the grinding will just be even more TEDIOUS.- Combat: Yes, it does have problems. A LOT. (1) Combo: While it may look cool, it is clunky AF. Some animations have to finish before you can do anything else, even Dash. (2) Speaking of which, Dash doesn't actually parry. (3) Ground slam: The only thing it does is breaking some breakable floor. I bearly does any damage to the enemy, not to mention that you need time to actually stand up. It is FAR FROM the dynamic combat and movement system of DC.- Special Moves: Most of them are lackluster. You end up choosing Surge and Restoration. Surge is like a second Dash that deals damage, while Restoration heals. Restoration requires you to stand still and hold the button until the entire process finishes, making it vulnerable in boss fight.- Enemies: Only a handful of types. They only get stronger as you progress. That's all. They can spot you almost off screen, so they can shoot you in the same manner. They sometimes stand on some narrow platforms, and since you cannot walk through them, most of the time you have to "jump attack" constantly on the low ground because you will be pushed away if you try to land on those same platforms.- Side missions: Are supposed to help you with leveling up your items and special moves. Most of them require you to clear 100% enemies in a time limit. If you miss 1 enemy and have already passed a location of no reture, you're gonna do it all over again. And guess what, if you have like 30 seconds to spare by that point, you will have to WAIT. No way to cancel the run immediately. There are Side shops for re-roll, but they are located in all the side missions and can only be accessible after you finish that mission by the rules. TEDIOUS.- Bosses: They are ok. I don't like difficult bosses.- Misc: After you die, you're given a choice of gaining back half of the money you had, or not. Is that even a choice?Nope, don't play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing i noticed that just sort of really really bothered me was the main character's movement and the overall animations she has (extremely weird to look at), it seriously reminds me of a Flash game's animations. This game has combat that just feels sluggish/slow and clunky (other reviews will state the same issue). You have a ranged weapon that you really can't aim, essentially your character shoots the first enemy she sees and is able to shoot aka is in range for example, although now that i think about it, i think it was the same in Dead Cells lmao, so wow i guess i'm not that surprised anymore. The third and final thing would be that the game just didn't feel exciting or interesting to play (yes i only got to the first boss and killed it but during that time i already felt like i will have to force myself to play this). It also didn't help that the skill tree, for me at least was completely broken, i literally allocated a skill into a slot or something like that and nothing happened, i got the achievement for it as well or maybe the skill tree was just made to be confusing.I just think that the developers took a majority of their inspiration from Dead Cells but didn't really manage to catch the energy and excitement that Dead Cells has where you're always on edge when playing it on higher difficulties or even on the default difficulty. Dead Cells is also straight forward and simple, here you once again have a hub that you have to frequently visit and interact with in order to stay up to par with what the next levels have in store for you. I got the game on sale but i'd rather refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those few games that I bought based off of pretty much the art alone. Granted, I got it on sale for around $5, but it saddens me that it really isn't worth a penny more than that. The art is indeed very well done in the style akin to dead cells and the bosses especially have incredibly smooth movement. The basic gameplay can be pretty mindless outside of the few weapons to mess around with and switch it up and the enemy attacks are interesting enough. The real problem here lies in both its story and levels though. The story reminds me of a stripped down, dumbed down version of something like iconoclasts where they give you a bunch of names of places and societies without ever really immersing you in it. But unlike iconoclasts, Foregone has voice acting that completely ruins any possible attempt at immersion that existed to begin with. It's so incredibly cliche. The level design is as simple as it gets. There's snaking hallways with the occasional branch off to hit a switch and open a door, but it just gets so tedious and boring. If the game wasn't as too easy as it was, I probably would have dropped it without a second thought.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. I have played it every night for the past two weeks and beat it. I did a little bit of grinding to level up my equipment and special powers. The game is fluid af, great controls, fun fighting experience. I like the leveled equipment... justifies a little bit of grinding. But the equipment doesn't gain any new powers when you level up, so it becomes bland after awhile. The AI is not well developed, so their attack patterns just get stronger as the game moves forward, so once you learn the enemies' patterns you can progress quite easily. There isn't much to the secret areas. And the gameplay doesn't really change as you move forward... you basically just get new weapons with new styles. But it is a very fun game, and doesn't get boring even though the game doesn't change much. I would love to play a sequel. Or some DLCs would be nice. The artwork is beautiful. And the story is somewhat interesting... some more writing to it and it could become something really special. I think the levels were designed before the asset placement..... sometimes it just seems like you are running through a wide open area, admiring the artwork. There are hidden objects you can smash for gold, but sometimes they blend in with the background so much you cannot tell the difference. I think that is a compliment.... if your assets blend in THAT well with the landscape.I will definitely play through at least one more time.... challenge myself with a harder level and use weapons that I have not become comfortable with. Looking forward to more from this developer!

_childDocuments_.review: Foregone is a great action platformer. It has ultralight metroidvania feels too, where you will gain new movement abilities and unlock shortcuts, but revisiting areas isn't entirely necessary. The various weapon types are interesting and give some meaningful choices. For the most part, though, the game encourages you to just use the strongest item of each category you have. The storyline is interesting. I didn't pay too much attention to it at first, but it grabbed me by the middle and I was interested in learning more about it. I like the Greek mythology tie-ins. There's a lot of lore to explore as well.  Overall if you're into sidescrolling action platformers, this is one to check out, it's great!

_childDocuments_.review: you can tell this game was made with alot of love but the enemy animations and voxel characters can only bring so much enjoyment. its more Dead cells then it is Metriod or symphony of the night while both those games are massive inspirations it really branches far of what made those games classic side-scollers. _childDocuments_.review: Like other reviews have said, this game is like a non-rogue-like Dead Cells. The combat felt fine, although I really only liked using the dual-knives finding the combos with the other weapons to be pretty unsatisfying. I guess one gripe with the game is that they could have had more weapons or more variety of weapons. They had like four main weapons and four other ranged weapons. Also the game doesn't give you a lot of experience points or whatever their equivalent is to those, so maxing out the skill tree is basically out of the question unless you do the side mission things which I didn't bother with. Similarly, they don't give you a lot of money to upgrade your gear if you just play through the game without doing the special missions. They do grade the equipment on a colored-rarity scale, so by the end of the game I did feel like I had "good" gear.  I didn't really play the as much of the game as I could have but I did beat it, and it was a decent amount of fun. I barely paid attention to the story, something about a war and "Project Hera?" I think with regard to the combat, towards the end of the game I found myself mashing X a little more than I was comfortable with in terms of how long it took to kill enemies, especially bosses. I'm not sure if this is due  to me not doing the side missions and leveling up enough, but that made the game hard in a way that didn't feel intentional. It does look nice, some of the animation is really smooth.  I got it on sale, not sure I'd pay $20 but I'm happy I played through it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a first game came out from this studio it's actually good, it's not buggy, controls are responsive which is important for 2D games with some platforming.Technical part is great.Background art is great!Models are good, Bosses are especially memorable.Boss fights are impressive! i see devs were more inspired by Castlevania bosses rather than Dead Cells.But gameplay-wise it's a boring version of Dead Cells without Rogue-like elements.Variety of enemies is low, but on bright side their AI is good, they know how to land their attack.Levels are done lazily, it's either a set corridors placed on each other, or vertical corridors with platforms stitched to walls.Menu map shows how much secrets are left in current area, and tries to hint which of them are at the beggining of area or at the end of area. Unfortunately it's also misleading, since map thinks last ones should be obtained after getting new abilities. Best example is first map: there is unreachable are in the middle of map, so you have to go under it first time around. Map thinks this is the last secret, but it should be the middle one.There are some status effects implemented, but they are usually useless, upgrading weapon damage is more important.Conclusion.Good game for first release of studio, but overall boring, Dead Cells is more fun.Would rather see what other games this studio will do.

_childDocuments_.review: God this absolutely breaks my heart to say but please don't buy this game.When I saw gameplay I was stoked to try a Dead Cells style metroidvania with more story and progression than roguelike elements. Much to my surprise the combat manages to be on par with Dead Cells and actually improves on some of the extra nonsense that can weigh down the experience.The environment design is at least nice enough and the enemies are varied and interesting to fight.So why the negative review? Because, dear reader, there is literally no excuse for a menu this bad. I kind of couldn't believe it when I first had to navigate the menu and got lost for nearly five minutes. I really don't know what to say because you need to see it to believe it can actually be that bad. I showed it to a friend and they were stunned by how at odds the awfulness of the menus are to the overall fantastic design of the rest of the game.I wish I had more to say but after three hours of play time, the only thing I could think about was how much I dreaded levelling up or finding new items because it would mean having to spend twenty minutes wrestling with an interface that seems to have been an experiment in how small of a detail can ruin an otherwise spectacular game.I'm sorry but until they completely re work the entire menu, map, and inventory, I will not be playing or changing this to a positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much a grey area game for me. I think the style is great, the animations are fluid, and the combat is passable. Everything else left a lot to be desired though. I think a lot of people were sold on this game being an insanely well animated pixel art game, but it is in reality just a filter put over the models to give it that satisfying retro look. It’s a bit soulless, in my opinion, considering the game is being praised for the fluent motions of its "sprites" despite said "sprites" actually being drastically toned down models. Maybe the game would look questionable without this effect, who knows? In hindsight, it did seem a little too good to be true that this was all drawn, but then again, the developer did more or less confirm that it was indeed a filter, so, I can forgive that misinformation as being a result of having read other reviews prior to having researched the game myself. The backgrounds very well could be actual pixel art, most of it at least, but I’m not sure. Although I was disappointed by this, it’s not why I this is a “negative review.” I wouldn’t even say that I dislike Foregone, it’s just not very memorable outside of the style.Don’t go into this expecting souls-like and or metroidvania type gameplay, cause despite the tags it is neither of these. There’s secrets and journals put off the beaten path, but it’s a pretty linear game. When you die you do lose gold and points to upgrade your skills, but you have the option to get them back after you respawn via a grim reaper type salesman. It’s a good feature if you’re playing on a harder difficulty, but the thing is, you won’t be your first play through as the game forces you to play on normal. I used him once I think, just to try the mechanic out. You’ll never likely need to use him either as it’s unlikely that if you do play the game once you won’t be playing it again. Foregone being as straight forward as it is isn’t inherently bad; I felt very overwhelmed with other games such as Hollow Knight and Salt and Sanctuary because of how vast they could be at times, so this game may definitely appeal to a specific crowd. I was banking on this not being an open world title in fact, but later was disappointed for this same reason: the story is pretty barren. Again, the game may not be "pure pixel art", at least by my definition, but it is undeniably gorgeous. Even if the story was complete bogus I might have still enjoyed exploring a bit more. That’s another issue I have with Foregone though: the narrative. You’re given very little context as to what’s happening. Only through the introductory text and some things the Arbiter blurts out (the heroine you play as cause as far as I’m concerned she doesn’t have an actual name) do you learn anything about the world of Calagan. I did mention journals earlier, but if I can’t tell what’s going on in the core game why would I bother with reading them? Lore texts appeal to specific players, and although I can get very into those in certain games I had zero incentive to do it here. If the game is failing to compel an interesting narrative, or just a narrative in general, it’s failing to be an interesting game. Well, that’s almost true, cause game play often overrides story elements, but again, the combat in this game is only passable, nothing crazy. The voice acting is actually very solid, but there’s very little voice work in the game at all. Outside of the Arbiter’s spoken aloud thoughts and some generic evil stuff the final boss says there really isn’t much. The bosses are the best part of the game too as the standard slog through linear yet meticulously detailed hallways can get repetitive over time. The game was definitely designed for multiple play-throughs, but by the end of it I had no interest in playing again. Foregone isn’t a bad game, it’s just sort of a let down with what I thought would be more. It’s with games like this that I really wish there was an option for writing a “neutral review.” If you've got a podcast in mind maybe get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Foregone is a great 2D action-platformer. While the game looks and plays very similarly to Dead Cells, Foregone is just one tier below Dead Cells. So if Dead Cells is a 9/10, Foregone is an 8/10. To be clear, Foregone is still a great game. It's better than the Castlevania games (like 6-7/10) in my opinion.Let's start with the positive notes by comparing Foregone to the Castlevania series. In regards to offense, similar to the Castlevania games, you have a melee attack and you can use a special skill (e.g. throwing knives in Castlevania). What's different in Foregone is that you have access to a secondary weapon, specifically a ranged weapon. Your ranged weapon typically does more damage than your melee attacks BUT it has limited ammo which can only be gained through melee attacks (i.e. there's no reloading). Thanks to this 1 addition, combat becomes a lot more dynamic. In the Castlevania games (and hell, a lot of 2D action games), you would use the same attack over and over again when you didn't have enough mana/hearts to use your special abilities. In Foregone, you're encouraged to mix in melee attacks with ranged attacks in order to maximize your damage. It's also worth mentioning that skills in Foregone recharge as you attack, and quite quickly might I add. So mixing up melee attacks, ranged attacks, and your skills in order to maximize your damage is a lot of fun.In regards to your defensive options, similar to the Castlevania games, you have a double-jump and a wall jump available to you. In Foregone, you also have a dodge and air dodge (back dash in Castlevania doesn't count). The dodge in Foregone makes the combat so much more enjoyable by making it fast-paced. While Castlevania is a good game, the lack of a dodge meant that combat had to be slower paced. After all, you could only move, crouch, and double-jump. You had no way to gain invulnerability frames. Hell, you couldn’t even move while attacking. So combat revolved around essentially taking turns where the enemy would attack, you'd have to get out of the way, they would stand around for a second or two doing nothing, which was your cue to attack, and then repeat. So almost for the entire game in Castlevania, you would be fighting 1 enemy at a time, maybe 2, where you constantly jump attack until the enemy is dead. In Foregone, no such restrictions on the enemies is necessary. You will very often be facing multiple enemies at once and you'll have to learn all of their attacks in order to avoid damage. This keeps combat fresh and interesting throughout the entire playthrough as new enemies get steadily introduced all the way to the end of the game. While fighting regular enemies is fun enough, the highlight of Foregone is hands down the bosses. The bosses have a large variety of attacks and are very fast. Not only that, but some of their attacks are pretty tricky to dodge. Some of Foregone's bosses can attack on one side but leave tracking bullets on the other side. So if you dash behind them, you'll get hit. But if you stay away from them, you won't be able to damage them. Seriously, the bosses in this game have a really nice moveset that makes them a joy to fight.So Foregone basically has excellent core gameplay. What's not to like? Well…..while I am comparing Foregone to Castlevania, Foregone is not a Metroidvania. It's a linear 2D action-platformer with little to no exploration. Personally, I much prefer Metroidvania's to linear level design because there's a sense of adventure in Metroidvania's. As you unlock abilities, it's fun to wonder where you need to go in order to progress further or what new items you can collect thanks to your new abilities. It's also fun to just generally go off the beaten path in search of new loot. In Foregone, there's no similar sense of wonder, which is a real shame.Another flaw with Foregone compared to Castlevania is the progression system. There's 2 types of progression systems within Foregone, none of which are all that interesting:	• Loot: You can get various items (melee weapon, ranged weapon, armor, necklace, ring) with varying rarities. The higher the rarity of the item, the more passive modifiers it will have (e.g. a rare necklace might give +% critical chance, but an epic necklace will give +% critical chance AND +% critical damage). I've seen a lot of developers try to copy and paste this type of Diablo loot system, which makes me think they don't understand what makes these loot systems work in THOSE games. See, this type of loot is exciting in Diablo because you're going for a specific BUILD, so rolling the perfect modifiers is a huge deal. When you don't have a build in mind, you don't really give a ♥♥♥♥ what the modifiers are. Why do I care if this necklace has +% critical chance? It's not like I am relying on "effect triggers on critical hit" abilities or anything similar. So ultimately, I didn't really care about the loot in Foregone. I just equipped whatever I think increased my damage the most. In Castlevania, there's at least this feeling of achievement you get for collecting all the items, but you don’t even get that in Foregone.	• Skill Tree: There's a small skill tree where you can unlock new passive skills as you kill enemies. Unfortunately, pretty much all the abilities provide boring +% increases that aren't exciting such as +% damage or +% critical chance/damage. There's not even much choice in this "tree" because it's so small and not every interconnected. Again, if you're not going for a specific build, none of these passive effects are exciting.Those are the flaws comparing Foregone to Castlevania. However, there's another major flaw when comparing Foregone to a game like Dead Cells. Simply put, Foregone doesn't provide enough of a challenge despite having very similar fast-paced gameplay. The main reason for this is that the game is too forgiving and enemies don't do enough damage. Also, you can heal almost instantly. This means that while the game is fast paced, you don't need to really master a lot of it. For a lot of the time I was playing Foregone, I was very often getting hit by certain enemies and I simply didn't care because I knew I would just heal back the damage (remember that skills recharge by attacking, and healing is a skill). There are also a few bosses that I had no right to beat as early as I did, as I got hit like 10-15 times during the fight. That would be unthinkable in games like Dead Cells, Hollow Knight, Dark Souls, etc…So ultimately, Foregone has great combat but no exploration, a poor progression system, and it could stand to provide a more satisfying challenging. The lack of exploration is probably never going to change because it would require completely changing the entire level design. While the progression system is unlikely to change, it's not impossible. However, it would require a major re-work, as the developers essentially need to find a way to make the loot, skill tree, and skill bonuses work together such that there are honest to god builds for players to create. As it stands, all of the systems are far too independent from each other, so there's not much player choice as it's pretty clear what the best choice is for each progression system. I think providing a more satisfying challenge is the easiest to change as it should simply require a Hard Mode. Just have enemies do more damage, the player do less damage, and make it much more difficult to heal.I really don't want it to seem like this is a bad game even though I am pointing out so many flaws. I really do like this game. It's just that I see all these small things that can be improved to make the game better. Having said all of the above, even if nothing changes, I think Foregone is a great game. The combat, enemies, and bosses are just that good. Despite its flaws, I would much rather play Foregone than a lot of other games. This is why I hope it gets updates to make the game even better :)

Does this remind you of anything?Sonic, The Hedgehog. I see it even in the Protagonist's design now, and that's not a bad thing. Not even by a long shot.This game is so close to Sonic with a shotgun that it makes me wish that was a thing. Is that what Doom Eternal is?Anyway, that's why I say this game is confused, and it's got me all dazed and unsure of how to feel. On one hand, the core gameplay is great, but the level design is clunky and counter-intuitive to how I actually want to and enjoy playing the game, and every time I have to stop to open my bag or go back to "town" to "upgrade my gear" it makes me mad, dazed, and confused.
