_childDocuments_.review: +Unique artstyle;+Smooth animations;-Completely linear, no sidequests, no freedom in choosing which order to get abilities;-Terrible problem with backtracking. There's no fast-travel system, so even by just following the objectives, you end up retracing steps on uninspiring corridor-like mazes;-Collectibles are comprised of only hearts and hats, hidden walls are no different visually from normal ones, there's no ability to detect nearby chests or anything of the sort. Either bump into every centimeter of terrain in the game or follow a guide if you want to get them all;-Animations are smooth but unsatisfying to pull off, both in combat and when zooming around. Dash is the last ability given to the player, it should've been the first;-Lacking soundtrack. It might have like 5 tracks, they're so similar and repetitive. The combat music is one and the same throughout the entire game;-The flashing lights when saving are excessive and almost caused me headaches.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Fluid and dynamic with a great aesthetic.Tabby controls like a charm, the kunais are fun to use. It's too short, and that's a shame, but what's there is a polished metroidvania with great moment to moment gameplay.I'm almost done, I just need a couple of hats and some heart pieces, and after that I will probably start speedrunning it.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Kunai is a beautiful game with some really cool mechanics that's honestly just not fun. The level design is boring for the most part and it's extremely linear for a metroidvania. Like in most metroidvanias there is a lot of backtracking, but it's for the most mundane of things, like a chest with 40 coins in it (The hats are fun though). The backtracking itself is also pretty lame since it's typically limited to walk back to place you've been, use new weapon on blockade, go in get 40 bucks. There's rarely any new or hidden adventures to be found, they exist but are few and far between.The combat is repetitive in general but the boss fights are especially egregious.  The final boss is the worst offender,  The grappling kunai are the best part of the game but are ironically underutilized. You'll get a spike pit to grapple over every now and often climb upwards with your kunai, but that's it for the most part. Of course there are some areas that have you utilize the kunai in unique ways, but most don't.Kunai is a game with a lot of potential that ends up being mediocre. I prefer Snailiad tbh.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Kunai is one of many newer Metroidvanias to hit the indie market. It may draw comparisons to Hollow Knight, but I believe it's a bit different but still good.Kunai is an extremely well polished game visually. All of the actions feel good and everything that moves is running through a downscaler shader to fit the pixel art style with an interesting physics feel. Some of the character designs indeed seem to be using pixel art, but the objects such as cloth and hand movements appear to be using tweening and physics quite nicely.I would give Kunai a positive for its visuals and themeing consistency. The theme of an apocolyptic future with a tablet robot (that is extremely expressive) that acts like a 1980s kung-fu action hero when weilding his weapons is hilarious, and while the story felt arcade-like moreso than deep (the game does have an interesting premise, but the lore is not that deep) I still went away appreciating it as it stayed consistent. Over-the-top action with good comedy relief. Not a long game, but still plenty to do.Now what's the negatives of Kunai?-The controls "felt" off because I never seemed to get much chance to experience the full arcs that the tether effect of the Kunai gave to your movement when swinging on ceilings. As such, when I was given harder tether platforming challenges, I didn't immediately feel like I was guided in the difficulty curve to understand them. The early areas were all cramped and tiny, keeping me from seeing all of the capabilities of the Kunai until later, making me feel as if I wasn't "progressing" at mastering the Kunai tether mechanic.As such, it will take you some time to get used to Kunai's movement mechanics-While I loved the choice of limited color pallets in Kunai, the constant use of the dull tan color for background and some foreground elements made seeing wall spikes hard to see in my peripheral vision. I'd take damage and ask "what hit me?" Turns out it was wall spikes I did not see because they didn't have enough color contrast with the floor, spikewall, and backgroun all having the same tan color.-I did not feel like the map layout of Kunai was that fun to traverse. There is no fast travel in the game at all (or if there was, I didn't ever run into it from beginning to end) It made trekking levels backwards an absolute pain, as I simply wanted to proceed to a new level, but got held in one place too long with no quick way to change locations. Because of this map travel issue, and coupled with map layout that didn't feel like it guided me in a certain direction when exploring, I also had no desire to obtain extra collectibles. While I loved the hats as a nice collectible, it just felt like a hassle to go collect them. The reward didn't fit the massive amount of time of traveling and attempting to find illusory walls.-upgrades were neat, but felt too expensive to complete. Since each common enemy would only drop about 1-3 coins on death, I didn't feel like I could easily collect 300 coins for the next upgrade. I appreciated it kept it from being too easy, but it was just enough that I wish there was a reward to get that much. I wasn't able to find those challenges to earn more to be rewarded with the extra upgrades. Coupled with the hassle of exploring the map, I didn't feel the desire to go to search for challenge rooms to find more, as I felt like reward chests I'd find would only produce about 20 coins. It was easier to spam farm coins from a few of the games bigger enemies.Overall, I believe the game is good as a metroidvania. I don't feel as if it hit the masterpiece level wholeistically, but it was still fun to play despite its weaknesses and flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this metroidvania in 5 hours (minus the last boss as I grew weary) and it had serious backtracking issues.Backtracking happens in metroidvanias but this one is shameless about it. Also the rope mechanic is so unreliable that they couldn't even find a way to make the last boss implement it, their one special gimmick.For a ninja game, the combat is very stunted. Lots of recoil on hit so we always have to hit->walk back to the enemy->hit, also a lot of enemies have poorly communicated invincible moments/angles, which also hurt the flow pretty much.Flow is also hurt by the unreliability of the rope mechanic/travelling. First, the rope pretty much decides where it wants to go. Then ropes stuck to ceiling behave wildly differently from ropes on walls. What I mean is that the action on a wall rope is to hoist using the up button and on a ceiling rope is to swing using the left and right button. So you never really can get used to either as you never know when your rope will be stuck on either in jagged surfaces. Also you have like 3-4 different jumps: The normal jump, the jump from a wall and the jump from the edge of a wall. They all have wildly different propulsion height and angle, so it's hard to get used to that.Flow is also hurt by the wall-sliding. This thing is waaaaay too slow. It's just frustrating, so a meta game for me was to avoid touching walls. Also these ivy things in the forest that let you... float? without much feedback, it should earn the award for worst level element of the year.So all in all, the game sells flow but a lot of its mechanics deliberately or slyly break that flow.Also, bosses are quite underdeveloped: easy simple patterns repeated to death, the pattern just repeats faster and for longer times.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: This falls into more of a 'meh' category. Not really anything wrong with the run-of-the-numbers game, per se, just nothing really stands out from it, either. Short, and very linear, I never felt motivated to scour each area looking for secrets. I did play it all the way through though, so if that says anything about the game, then there it is.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay action/platforming game, but as a Metroidvania it's completely unremarkable.The art style is nice, the main character you play as controls extremely well (bar some annoyances with the kunai itself, which works as a grappling hook, sometimes getting caught on surfaces you didn't intend to), and the music is also decent.But I've never seen a Metroidvania that works as hard as this one to demotivate the player from continuing to explore. Sure, it's not a massive game like other major titles in the genre, but imagine happening upon chests, thinking it's going to be something important or useful, only for it to be a cosmetic item that serves no other purpose and doesn't help or improve your character in any way. And this happens a lot.Less often you'll find actually useful chests with money or heart pieces that you can collect for health upgrades. Otherwise, there's nearly no incentive in backtracking with better weapons and upgrades to hunt for chests.If you just want a regular 2D action game and liked how this looks, I'd say go for it. If you want a quality Metroidvania, however, sadly you won't find it here.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: What I don't like about the game:-The fighting system against normal enemies is not that fun-The boss fights are not good either-There is no fast travel which is a bigger problem at the end-game-I changed the controller button from B to right shoulder but it is still saying to press B to fire alt weapon-The text bubble don't show on screen if you are standing too close to the right side of the screenWhat I like about the game-the alternative weapons are fun and upgrades are fun as well-The art and style of the game is goodI will not call it a bad game and I will have given it a neutral rating if that existed but will not recommend it either
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: A solid metroidvana where your face is a tablet that makes funny and cute expressions, while the hookshot mechanic makes you feel like a deadly spiderman, and it all controls extremely well. Took me about 7 hours to complete.Graphics are nice and the soundtrack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slammin. Like a traditional metroidvania you'll get new abilities and weapons which were all a treat. Bosses are a lot of fun too as their patterns are really good and not just damage sponges. My only gripes with the game are that yes there's places to explore and items to get, but most of them are useless hats that for some reason many indie devs love to put in their games nowadays. There's life pickups to be found to extend your health bar, but nine out of ten times I would get let down because it would be just another dumb hat. Also, the ending is...well there's hardly one at all. With all the dialogue from meeting npcs and from your chief throughout the game, the ending leaves a lot to be desired. All in all though I enjoyed it as it's another solid game in the metroidvana genre.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't finish this game and don't think I'll come back to it. Kunai has some interesting premise, original art-style and promising platforming machanics. But the story falls short very soon and meets you with some quirky cringe humor. Visuals get tiring, because of the off-color theme where, although environments have different "texture", they still look kinda the same. And finally platforming and fighting feel more frustrating than novel and interesting. Finally, progression feels pretty forced, there is some freedom of exploration, but it just introduces complexity by obscurity, and then  punishes you with some useless hat collectibles ()I was able to enjoy the game for a while, but then those negative impressions started accumulating, I got stuck somewhere and after a few tries just couldn't bring myself up to play it anymore. It felt like an incomplete experiense that was overall more of a waste of my time than an unfinished fun adventure.P.S. At first I thought that it's a  lightweight homage to , but then I realized that it was released before Haiku. Regardless of who inspired whom (and there are quite some similarities), Haiku is a better game in every aspect and is definitely worth your time if you like metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: I had wanted to review this game earlier, but I forgot this game existed for a while.In short, KUNAI is half-baked and doesn't provide much more than a pretty basic metroidvania experience. The only thing to do in the game is the main storyline, so your gameplay is very linear. There are collectibles in the game, but they're either heart pieces (collect 4 and you get more HP) or cosmetic hats. Nothing that's incredibly cool to find. Only having extra HP as any kind of collectible seems pretty dull.The worldbuilding is... Bland. Just so little about this game is memorable. The NPC's all look/say the same, areas aren't all that distinct, and the way levels are built is quite elementary. No real clever puzzles or secrets in this game to be found.The bosses are sometimes mediocre sometimes okay. Most have one or two attacks they constantly repeat until they die. The only interesting boss is the final one. Overall KUNAI provides a pretty lackluster metroidvania experience. From a metroidvania I expect open, connected worlds with memorable NPCS and upgrades. KUNAI has none of that. On top of this, there are some serious Quality of Life problems with the game. like the fact that it has NO fast travel. None. Walking all the way back is boring. If there would have at least been a late-game upgrade where you could teleport between the save points that would have been okay, but now going back to collect everything was really not something I would ever want to do. You also can't view the map of an area you're not in. So you have to go there just to see you can't progress, otherwise you could have seen earlier on.So yeah, pretty underwhelmed by this game, which is a shame, since it looked nice. Could have really used some more work.3/10
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Really good game, minor issues, would recommend if you liked hollow knight or similar metroidvania style games. 9/10Really good game, definitely underrated. Reminds me a lot of hollow knight which I greatly enjoyed and I love the weapons. The facial expressions are amazing, and the hats are awesome. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who was a fan of hollow knight or games similar. All that said this game does have it's issues, minor graphical things such as your hat not showing when you do flips or when going by hidden areas you can see the fake wall clip through the real one. But those aren't much of an issue, my biggest one is the fact you can't change controls while in a game, you have to go back to the main menu. Which doesn't seem important but when you're trying to rebind and see what works, it's annoying to change the bind, go into the game, realize it doesn't work well for how you play, then have to go back to the main menu. I hope the add the ability to rebind controls while in the game and I expect great things from their future games. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Anyway, if you're expecting all the typical mechanics of a Metroidvania, then you're correct. Kunai has a sprawling map with a ton of locked off areas until you find an item that magically bypasses that block. Is that bad? Nope! I'm not sick of Metroidvania games yet.What's interesting is how much back and forth you do without a fast travel option. It's a lot of running around between new and old areas as Kunai takes full advantage of the map. The game opens new shortcuts when you return, but if you're a doofus like me, then you'll go back through the same areas.Going the long way around isn't so bad since the movement mechanics with the kunai are so much fun. You can get good at swinging, it's a skill. So good that you'll probably start swinging right by enemies if you're trying to get through the area quickly. Movement is a massive part of the game and an even more critical role than combat. It's much more crucial to land the kunai and climb than fight. This holds true with the boss battles too. If you can jump around and dodge everything, you'll have plenty of opportunities to land an attack. Overall, Kunai is terrific, even if it follows the same formula as other Metroidvanias. With its own style and slick movement system, it's a joy to play. The entire robot world is where I want to live. I realize there are no humans, but maybe they could download me into a PC? It's the complete package with graphics, mechanics, and music all being top-notch. I can't believe how many amazing Metroidvanias we're getting these days, it's incredible.For a complete picture please see the video review,
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Kunai from the TurtleBlaze studios, presents himself as a metroidvania full of action, movements and samurai weapons that make the player quickly feel like a real badass.The plot is set in a post-apocalyptic and post-human world, full of robots made of garbage.A group of robots that resists the regime, dominated by malicious robots that have been infected with viruses, wakes up the protagonist, Tabby, the only hope of overcoming the affront to the well-being of the population. The character played by the player has the soul of a warrior within him, but the face of an iPad.Although the protagonist is always silent, he is far from being expressionless. As he jumps, runs and uses one of his weapons, Tabby presents a variety of different facial expressions. The lack of a life bar is represented with the symbol of lack of energy that gives it a somewhat comic touch.The humorous moments also present in the writing of this title offer an additional charm to all the present history and that give some laughs, here and there.Regarding gameplay, it features a shorter variety of weapons.Initially the player sees himself only with a katana as the main weapon in his quest to overthrow the regime and help the resistant group to survive the adversities of this confrontation. This weapon provides the ability to take down enemies as well as a defensive strand, as it allows you to deflect the shots fired by the bad guys.It is clear that throughout the game new weapons and game mechanics will be presented, however, the main one all of them is the use of "katana" and "kunai". A ninja weapon consisting of an iron blade with a large hole in its base.Once this ability is unlocked, the game mechanics become very clear. The player will have at his disposal two "kunai", each referring to one of the triggers, left and right. So, it is possible to launch this weapon to help with faster locomotion or to reach higher points, a little bit like the spiderman webs work. A mechanics well implemented, intuitive and quite fun.The remaining weapons allow the player to inflict damage, but mostly serve to make way for places that were previously inaccessible.The "shuriken" can be used to power certain switches and allows you to stun enemies. The sub machine guns, which are two machine guns that do little damage but fire a large number of bullets that allow the player, with the help of the jump, to reach more distant places. Finally, the “rocket launcher” that will be used to destroy rocks. It also allows the player to jump higher and knock down enemies faster, as it inflicts a lot of damage.Kunai is a very expressive metroidvania, with a touch of retro, either in its type of mechanics, or for its graphic style that resembles the color palette of a Game Boy Color. The feeling of mastering the main mechanics of the use of “kunai” is quite satisfactory and a very fluid control of everything that happens on the screen give this title a good hours of fun, however, the variety of weapons leaves a little to Wish. For those who like to complete the games 100%, there are plenty of “secret” boxes with accessories that allow you to change Tabby's appearance.Check more recommendations from Exile
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is pretty nice, and the music is decent, but other than those things, there isn't much going for this metroidvania. If you're hoping for a good story, look elsewhere; this tale is your bog-standard rebels fighting against a big bad (the oddly named Lemonkus) in some sort of robot-dominated post-apocalyptic future, and the player character is the Chosen One. There's a few nice gags, but in general, the story isn't anything particularly memorable.Some other reviews have mentioned the backtracking being annoying and oh boy, is it ever. There is quite a lot of it, plus thanks in part to the muted color scheme, many areas can feel samey after awhile. While backtracking is a key part of many metroidvanias, it feels a bit excessive here. On top of that, not only are many hidden rooms (themselves frequently samey) tough to find, but so are some of those that you need to get through in order to continue on with the story. Part of this is because of the "room" format; for example, a block you need to attach to with your kunai to progress could be just out of sight, but you won't be able to see it by jumping and forcing the map to scroll up... because it's in the next room. The area I'm referring to was so frustrating that I had to look up a Let's Play to get a hint as to where to go next. Oh, and there are also a couple of areas which become inaccessible after beating their bosses, so good luck with those to any completionists out there.Getting around with the grappling hook-like kunai is a little fussy, but the weapons pretty much work as advertised, though one has to get used to reload times for most of them. The worst weapon is the katana, which has a small range and an attack time that's a little too quick. Upgrades can be purchased for the kunai and weapons, but in the case of the charged attacks, you will never, ever need to use them. The katana also gets a special set of additional upgrades, but unlocking these is done by beating an optional boss which is best approached after said katana becomes redundant. Heart pieces to expand your health bar, money, and hats round out the collectibles, plus there are a couple of special moves, one of which is unlocked surprisingly late in the game.As for the enemies, most of them are either not much trouble, annoying, or Capital A Annoying, particularly a certain one in the mountains which requires some precise timing with the katana to beat. The difficulty is uneven in a few spots, such as with an auto-scrolling section featuring bottomless pits which appears  too early in the game. Likewise, the bosses vary in difficulty and quality; some are fun and well thought-out, while others make you want to bang your head on your desk. The final boss is very much in the latter category,  it's preceded by multiple gauntlets of standard enemies, each round more difficult than the last. At least the game automatically saves for you in between these gauntlets.There's a lot of potential here, but it feels squandered on the novelty of its tablet-faced hero, and hats. I'm curious about what this studio does next, though for their next project, I hope they spend more time refining their level designs, weapons (if applicable), and difficulty curve to make a more engaging and fun game. Oh, and a genuinely interesting story (again, if applicable) would be great, too.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvanias have been around for just about 34 years or so. Majority of people are familiar with it but in case you aren't, A metroidvania is typically an action oriented game that takes place in one large map, usually having you backtrack after obtaining new abilities. Up there with rogue-lites, it's a very popular game genre, especially in the indie scene. So without wasting too much time, lets dive into the recently released Kunai, developed by TurtleBlaze and published by The Arcade Crew.Majority of people I feel aren't going to play a metroidvania for its story, while there are narrative based vanias, it isn't really my thing when I want to dive into one. Kunai's story is fairly straightforward and one you've heard before. Human life is on the brink of extinction thanks to an evil genius, and it's up to Tabby to save humanity with the help of the resistance to restore balance. What Kunai lacks in narrative it makes up for in its execution. It's a very quirky and actually kinda funny game. It doesn't really take itself too seriously for the most part and I feel it's an advantage. Other than that it continues to be fairly standard for the genre with some lore scattered here and there with computers and other robots.Actually playing Kunai I think it'd be hard for a person NOT to have a good time. Not too far into the intro you get a set of Kunai that you use propel yourself forward and grapple onto certain surfaces. It gives the game a unique momentum that helps it stand out on its own. It plays well into the combat of the game and of course the majority of the boss fights. You do get some more movement based abilities later in the game but the kunai is the main thing. You get a small arsenal from a trust katana to a pair of dual p90s. All of which is upgradable. The enemies are nice and varied to keep you on your toes, but sometimes can be a tad bit tedious in my eyes. You never are without the appropriate tool though. On top of all that, there are a bunch of hats to collect to make your own personal Tabby. Who doesn’t love hats?The art style of Kunai fits the vibe it's going for. The cutscenes have this cutesy anime feel to them, but I do feel as though monotone-esque colors in the background can take away from the world they crafted. Arguably the most important part of a metroidvania is its map. It's a whole other character the player gets to know. So it's unfortunate that a lot of the places tend to blend together after a while. The accompanying music and occasional lack there of certainly help the atmosphere, but I can't really find anything sticking out regardless if good or bad.I had no issues with the performance at all. A constant 60FPS, no crashes, no game breaking glitches, nothing. Which is always a dope thing.The experience I had with Kunai is a short but for the most part good time. You can complete it in about 5-6 hours. My hours representing a regular playthrough in which I did NOT go for 100% completion. Which I feel is fair for the $16.99 asking price, though I wouldn't blame you if you wanted to wait for a sale. I felt as though Kunai peaked just before the final segment. I had a good time with every boss except the final one, which is always a bummer. In the end though I feel that Kunai has enough going for it to be worth your time, and would recommend for you to pick it up if you wanted a quick romp through a quirky metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun. It's simple and enjoyable. Plays a lot like a mix of Mega Man Zero and Metroid. I love this kind of pixel-art. And playing as a ninja-hitman iPad is pretty cool. Oh, and you get hats that you can wear for cosmetic effect. They don't add bonuses, they're just something cool thrown in by the devs.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Underappreciated little Metroidvania game that has never bored me during its 5-7 hour playthrough. Traversal is so smooth, the frequency of finding new abilities is just right, and I also liked its visuals/sound. Nothing to complain about here. If you like Metroidvania games, give this game a try. Don't expect the next Hollow Knight or Ori in terms of general quality. Nevertheless, as a Metroidvania fan, I enjoyed this game more than Bloodstained ROTN, Shantae 5, Metroid 2 remake, or Dandara.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Solid metrovania game. Decent character interactions, good weapons, good boss fights, solid game length, the labyrinths aren't too much of a hassle. I hate the tablet's face. No fast-travel (100% OCD people beware).In a less terse manner: This feels like a "joke" game. Like a student's assignment that had a lot of potential, so it was produced into a full game. It never takes it self seriously at all.I mean, you're playing a tablet with a katana and can rocket jump that makes poopy faces every time you wall-climb or charge an attack. I hated those bloody expressions. Wore a mask to hide them throughout my playthrough.Furthermore, there's not much of a story. Things just happen, and the game just ends after you finish off the last boss.So, what I'm saying is: gameplay wise, this is a solid game. Art-style is also very robust. But everything else is a bit meh. Don't pay full price for this one.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: I was browsing the Steam Store page today, bored out of my skull, hoping to find a gem of a game amidst all thepassable junk. When looking through what was on sale, I noticed KUNAI, a game with a simple enough title and a brilliant art style from the jump. Naturally pulled in by the pretty presentation, I gave the demo a try. Before I had even cleared 5 minutes worth of the demo, I knew this would be an instant purchase.  Normally, I'm not a huge fan of metroidvanias, but I was sucked in impossibly deep by KUNAI. I couldn't put the damn thing down. The gameplay is fast-paced and delightful, the kunai grapple feels wonderful when traversing, and the game is packed to the brim with metroidvania secrets. The progression feels natural and the layout of the game's different environments makes moving between locales a breeze. I finished this the game in two sittings on one day but, honestly, it felt like the perfect length. My only complaint is that some of the boss fights were less of a challenge and more of a chore, but the rest of the games many perfect traits make up for this in almost every way. My final score for KUNAI is a 4.3/5, 100% recommendation to anyone you know
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Good game play, nice sound and animation so satisfied.The reason I don't recommend this game cause it have a bad UX.I want to use WASD to move but it is impossible, this point can be accepted.But why use "Enter" to interact when it should be "Space" this so annoying for me but also acceptable.Here the point that can't be accepted. Map quite large and you need to jump a lot before reach each point but this game not have teleport function. And level was design like this  "A > B > C > A > B" this loop is nonsense when it force player to run from that point and must run back to other point. Need to do a lot of suicide for respawn.And checkpoint that player easily to die in a few sec have a cut scene and it always run the cut scene every time you die. It can skip but I don't see an different between skip and not skip cause it still have loading time for skip which took time equal to you watching it with spamming next.I didn't finish this game yet and I don't think I will. It feel very boring from running again and again.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to give this game a simple recommendation. It looks cool and has some cool mechanics, but the overall experience is not that much fun.Movement and combat feel rather sluggish with some mechanics that don't make any sense. If you strike a target with your katana you are pushed back a bit which often leads to losing control, falling into spikes etc. Feels just like bad design.The other problem I have is, that most levels are huge but empty...just isn't fun to explore. Smaller, nicer designer maps would have made the experience a bit more memorable.You will fave fun for a few hours if you can get it for a small price....but it's nothing memorable.

There are some rewards that are acquired only from backtracking but they are generally not required.If fun, fast, and energetic movement is what you're looking for, then Kunai is just what the doctor ordered, even if there are some disappointing aspects to the design.

_childDocuments_.review: Begrudging recommendation. Movement in this game is phenomenal which is sadly all it has to recommend itself. Swinging with the kunai is fluid and satisfying, but it completely fails to mesh with the combat. Despite being a very momentum-based and aerial game, melee combat is disjointed and erratic, and the ranged options are often blocked by enemies or extremely difficult to aim. Areas are large and overly padded with no way to mark where on the map you would like to revisit (or even a way to zoom into areas of the map you aren't in). It's common to explore your way to a secret area that you can't unlock yet and have nothing to do but slowly meander back to the single path that is open. The final boss is where the game really loses itself, with an enormous difficulty spike and a complete lack of reliance on any of the game's core mechanics. The racing area where you had under 30 seconds to find a path to the end was more of an interesting and gestalt challenge than the final boss.6/10, for the 6 hours out of the 10 I enjoyed playing. Just play Hollow Knight if you haven't already. And if you have played it, reminisce on how many of the areas have memorable layouts and unique ambiance compared to Kunai's endless expanses of chiptune sepia.

_childDocuments_.review: Kunai is a fast-paced metroidvania with a distinctive visual style that doesn’t use a lot of colors and sometimes looks almost like a comic.Your main attack is a sword, you can later collect extra weapons like shurikens that stun enemies, SMGs to shoot from afar or fly for a short time (shooting down in style) and a rocket launcher. Even then your sword remains your main weapon until the end, even able to deflect bullets and overall pretty useful, as you can aim downward and just kill enemies by jumping on them and slash them to death from above.The game isn’t too hard overall and pretty generous with health, which you even recover if you kill enemies in melee and not with either the SMGs or the rocket launcher, which means if you always press forward and don’t make too many errors you can get through most of the levels without much of a difficulty.While it’s a metroidvania with mostly ground-based levels where falling to your death isn’t an option and at worst you have some spikes on the ground or lava (who only take a bit of health away), two times you’re on an airship with some medium-difficult and medium-length platforming sections, nothing all that arduous but they are there.The most irritating sections of the game are when it switches format to timed action sequences, one is the 2nd part of a boss battle where you have to flee from rockets up a mountain, which is hindered in that you can’t actually climb that far up and have to wait on the screen while trying to guess where the next block to climb is. Another section is where you flee from a robot jumping from hovercar to hovercar. Both sections aren’t terribly hard, but they really aren’t suited to the game overall and feel like a misstep in game design (people who play metroidvania usually do because they specifically want to avoid playing stuff like that).So far I haven’t mentioned that early in the game you collect two Kunai, that you use like grappling hooks to climb up walls or swing on ceilings (though they don’t work on all of them). Most games at best have only one grappling hook (Super Metroid or Environmental Station Alpha for example), but the added second one really changes how you use them. In general, I rarely enjoy grappling hooks in games, but here they really help you get around at an incredibly fast pace or climb up long tunnels at insane speeds and are just a joy to use.That’s basically what convinced me in the demo to get the full game, Kunai is just fun to play moment to moment. The sword attack, the kunai to climb up walls, killing basic enemies, the game is really good about minute feedback loops and making everything feel fast and fun. And while the game doesn’t have a lot of bosses (and some are more gimmicky), at least three of them including the final boss are really well designed and fun to beat.While the overall story isn’t all that great and more or less forgettable (evil wants to take down humanity and the robots, yadda-yadda), the distinctive aesthetics coupled with the fun movement and action-based gameplay make for a very decent, maybe even the best metroidvania of the year. Size-wise I spent around 10 hours, though some of it due to backtracking and collecting hats (don’t ask). It’s medium in size, not small, not as massive as say Hollow Knight, but a good chunk of levels with unique enough themes for each of them.

_childDocuments_.review: I was about to recommend this game. It's a mediocre metroidvania but a good platformer, and it's very cheap so why not? But then I reached the combat gauntlet at the end of the game.You see, this game has some amazingly irritating enemy design. They teleport, the float just out of attack range, they fly at you from offscreen, they knock you backwards, they explode if you get too close. The list goes on. In the lead up to the end of the game you fight every single one of these heinous enemies, multiple times, in combination with each other. It is insufferable. Best part is that you're deep enough into the game that sunk cost fallacy takes effect. You're so close to the end you just have to finish, no matter the frustration. I hate it. Honestly I wish I had just played Hollow Knight for a tenth time instead.There is another thing I want to complain about, though it is much more minor. The visual style is problematic. Don't get me wrong, it looks really good, but it's bad for metroidvania level design. The muted colour palette makes the various areas quite difficult to separate from each other in hindsight. This is obviously a problem for a genre which expects you to want to go back to the unreachable places you found earlier.Credit where credit is due, this game has really good movement, both in terms of mechanics and animations, but it's not enough in my estimation. I'm sure there will be a sequel though, since steam metroidvanias always seem to come in twos. Maybe that will be worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Kunai feels like a bunch of usually open levels put together, with occasional one-way platforming segments. While it may technically be a metroidvania, there is only a little bit of backtracking.  The game has surprises, with unexpected platforming segments littered throughout to mix up the gameplay a little bit, which gives it that adventure platformer feel.I can't help but wonder if Haiku's visuals and style drew a little inspiration from Kunai, with the similar donut shaped currency and little robots.  Kunai reminds me occasionally of Donkey Kong Land games for the gameboy, and segments like the airship are a clear ode to those segments in the Mario games.  The music and sound is all quite decent.I've read the occasional review that has pretty bad information regarding the games difficulty.  It wasn't that hard of a game, but people less used to certain mechanics within the platforming genre could certainly find it trickier.  The difficulty felt balanced and fair throughout.  The grappling hooks are very easy to use, unlike something like Rusted Moss.  One reviewer cited a boss as being difficult that i killed in one try.. He obviously is unfamiliar with the concept of down-pogo (bouncing off of enemies by slashing downwards on their head), which you will get to utilise throughout the game, which I found to actually trivialise some of the early boss fights.  For endgame cleanup, it would have been handy to have fast travel.  It isn't much of an issue during the main story however, because your character is quite fast and it never takes long to get from A to B.  Another feature I would've liked for the endgame would be some kind of item finder to help you finish uncovering the last of its secrets.I enjoyed Kunai, and while I found it somewhat mid given some of the great games out there, the experience was worthwhile and satisfying enough.===================== =====================  Aeterna Noctis |  Astalon: Tears of the Earth | Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom | Hollow Knight |   Blasphemous 2 | Cathedral |  Doomblade^ | Afterimage |  Elderand | Ori and the Will of the Wisps | Environmental Station Alpha |  Ender Lilies: Quietus of the Knights | Depths of Sanity |  Blast Brigade |  Alwa’s Legacy | Steamworld Dig 2 | Islets | Blasphemous | After Death | Pronty^ | Haak | Mortal Manor | Escape From Tethys | Treasure Adventure Game | Chasm | Monster Sanctuary | Elliot Quest |  Haiku, the Robot | Rabi-Ribi | Outbuddies DX |  |  Lone Fungus | Momodora: Reverie under the Moonlight | Ghost Song | Grime | Death’s Gambit: Afterlife |  Aggelos | Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night | Plague of Yamorn | Sheepo | Infernax | MF-01 Aerostrike^ | Xanthiom Zero | Carrion^ | Wuppo | Iconoclasts | Catmaze | Omega Strike |  Rusted Moss^ | Moonscars | The Messenger | Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth | Ato | MindSeize |  Castle In The Darkness | Alwa’s Awakening | Pharaoh Rebirth | Yoku’s Island Express | Guacamelee! _childDocuments_.review: KUNAI is a game about a robot and his journey which takes place in an era where there are no humans but cyborg like beings.I saw this game on steam and was instantly drawn by the artstyle, I played for a couple of hours before I got stuck in a dungeon, a month later I finally decided to finish it.The game was fun, the bosses were challenging, some were too easy and others were hard.My only problem with the game was having to travel to the mission areas, since there was no fast travel.Overall I'll give it a 7/10 :3

_childDocuments_.review: KUNAI is a fun metroidvania. The movement and the way it controls feels great, it has an adequate selection of skills and abilties you learn throughout your playthrough. There isn't too much of a story or at least i didn't care for it, you just go and slash some evil robots. The level design is mostly fine, i dislike the auto-scrollers and insta-death pits but other than that it is a good mix of varied platforming challenges. The combat is good but in the middle of the game there are a lot of enemies that are not worth fighting because it takes to long to fight them before you get your final "gun".Weapons:I wish the sword was stronger, i only got enough money to upgrade it once and at some point it didn't do the job anymore. Also every new weapon you find is just stronger than the last one and you eventually never use your earlier ones anymore. I think there is some room to balance the combat better.Bosses:The bossfights are all rather easy except the final boss which requires you to replay the fight a couple times to learn his patterns. The final boss can feel cheap at times because some of his moves are basically unavoidable if you aren't dodging preemptively but it certainly isn't a dealbreaker for me.Collectibles:Getting all steam achievements for this game was pretty easy, it requires a decent bit of backtracking but it wasn't too bad. Finding a hidden chest that just contains a hat is a bummer especially if the chest was hidden well.

_childDocuments_.review: At first the limited color scheme put me off a bit, but you'll quickly forget about that when you start to play. The first thing you'll notice is how tight the controls are. They feel exactly right and become even better when you get your hands on the kunai (grappling hooks). The left hook is mapped to the left shoulder button and the right one to the right, which feels so natural I'm kind of surprised I've never seen this before. You'll be blazing through the environments in no time.The soundtrack is excellent and really helps set the mood. Some parts of the game can be frustrating; sometimes it's a bit unclear what you're supposed to do. But that's kind of the point, it's a Metroidvania after all ;)

_childDocuments_.review: More frustrating than fun, KUNAI is a pretty mediocre metroidvania that is personally hard to recommend. Its faults mainly lie in a lot of unnecessary backtracking and combat that is a lot more stilted than I'm sure the developers intended. Piled on to the unremarkable level designs, characters, story, and bosses, KUNAI is a game that I would probably skip if I initially knew what I was getting myself into.

_childDocuments_.review: A lenient metroid-vania platformer, Kunai delivers platforming and boss mechanics that are challenging for first-timers to the genre and simple/fun to a veteran. The story is easy to follow even if you're like me and tend to speed through the text. Hats offer some unique flair to your character to allow for some light utilization. Weapon selection is limited but upgrades offer variety once you've grinded enough coins to purchase them.The Rocket Launcher is OP once unlocked from Zensei IMO, makes most enemies one-shottable coming back down the mountain that were challenging on the way up.At the time of this review I have NOT beaten the full game but I have unlocked all weapons and most of the router upgrades thus far. I'd say the game has 2-3 more hours left of content if I had to guess so figure an 8-10 hour playthrough depending on how much exploring you do for all the secrets.EDIT: Finished the Game in approx 7 hours, Rocklet Launcher remained OP throughout end-gameIf you have played through games like Celeste, Super Meat Boy, Hollow Knight, etc you will find the 'precision' platforming and respawn portals MUCH more forgiving. If you are new to the genre this is an excellent game to experience Metroid-vania without feeling overly punished for your mistimed jumps, kunais, etc

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable platformer that you can blast through the screens! So enjoy exploring everything to find then hidden chests and interactions!I agree with others that the map ability should be given sooner but I was able to make my way deep enough in the initial playthrough to get the map before having to stop playing for the day.This game feels a lot like Hollow Knight except that you can move faster and the Kunai add a different type of movement. It's a really cool game and I strongly suggest you give it a try if you love Metroidvania games, like finding hidden areas, getting new abilities, upgrades and boss battles!

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful graphics and music. Cute and simple metroidvania, not as complex as say, Hollow Knight but enjoyable overall. Controls are not really good if you play on a keyboard but I suppose this game is meant to be played on a controller. If it had more precision platforming or combat in it, it would have been almost impossible with a keyboard given how confusing it can get.Game design was overall okay. I enjoyed the boss fights a lot except for the last one, where the difficulty increase is substantial. And one could argue that the other boss fights were far too easy. Other than that, no complains. Upgrades are OK, not much to say about them. Not great, not terrible.I had a nice ride with it. Recommended and would definitely buy a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this up to the airship and to the point were you have to go jumping under the ship.Falling off a platform was an instant kill that tossed you back to the previous save point at least three rooms and one cutscene away from the start of the section.To get out of the save point room you then had to shoot the grappling hook thingy to the just right bit of the ceiling or you wouldn't get high enough and would just fall back down. This took at least two tries to pass each time.Then the repeating cutscene, thankfully skippable at least, but still why not flag it seen after the first time as it's not that fast to skip either?Then the jumping bit that I usually failed by getting stuck too close to the ceiling in a wrong position with no space to retreat and retry the jump to hook into a better position, or indeed an ability to change the length of the rope, or even the angle that it's shot at. Just have to commit suicide and do the whole thing from beginning.After ten tries I made it almost to the end of that section only for one grappling hook swing to toss me up to the electrified ceiling that killed me.After that I decided that If the difficulty is going to only increase from there, on this checkpointless instant death pit is where I might as well quit this game. I also got the charge attack as my first upgrade and it seemed to get you stuck into the level 4/5 time I tried to use it, but devs seem to be aware of that bug already.So that's my about 90 minutes of play time.Had there been a demo to try I would not have even bothered to to complain, but since Steam allows you to review games you have refunded, I thought I might as well write down what turned me off this one.No harsh feelings, most people seem to like the game so maybe I retry it at some later date.But for now if need to frustrate myself this much I got other platformers to do it with.Might as well try to get those last nailmasters in Hollow Knight that I still don't have. That insanely long optional spike pit corridor dash, pogo, wall jump -sequence doesn't seem so bad anymore. At least you respawn back to where you last stood until you run out of health...

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs some work for me to recommend it to friends.Here's what I want to see:- Deadzone for crouching (controller): You sometimes crouch accidentally because the the controls are really sensible when pressing just a slightly bit down on your movement stick- Re-visiting the controls in general: The controls feel overall kinda clunky and unreliable. Especially the grappling hooks.- Explanations on the enemies and combat: Only find out via trial and error that most of the time you can (and apparently are supposed to) just spam your attack. Did you know you can kill a lot of enemy types by deflecting their projectiles? I don't know if the game tells you that (and I missed it), but I just found out way too late into the game.- Re-visiting the death mechanics: If you fall down, you die completely and respawn at a checkpoint much further from where you'd just jumped down. Really unnecessary and frustrating on some passages. Just make me lose some HP and respawn me at the platform where I just jumped down from.- Re-visiting early levels / learning curve: The game kind of pushes you from "Press A to jump." immediately to difficult platforming and unforgiving combat sections. For an experienced metroidvania player this may totally fine, but I believe that you restrain potential fans from your game by this imbalanced level progression.Besides these complaints, I really like:- art style- electronic/digital themed design choices- soundtrack

_childDocuments_.review: first impressions after approximately a half hour:+ lovely pixel art and adorable character designs.+ tight music, gets you into a good, energetic mood.+ punchy sound effects.+ solidly responsive controls.+ amusing traversal with the two titular kunai that make for some fun platforming and melee combat at the beginning. you can zip around levels a la Spiderman, and it's as exhilarating as that should be.+ clever placement of secret areas.+ after losing to the first boss once (and not really being sure how I was supposed to beat it), I was able to learn all of the tells and come together with my tactics on my second, victorious attempt. so it seems to play fair with the difficulty.so far, I'm enjoying it quite a bit. it hasn't blown me away completely, but this seems like a great action/platformer that I'll be dipping further into.

_childDocuments_.review: I am psychic. Here is the line you'll get stuck on in the game: "The Tablet has reached the stern! He will fall to his doom!"And you know what, he is right. No reason to repeat that cutscene everytime I need to reload though. In short: the dual grapling hook mechanic in the game is needlessly complicated and as such makes platfroming really awkward. Additionally you have to manage momentum to swing over pits but if you time your hooks wrongly then you lose all momentum and are stuck. That is the main offender, the other is the story. You get a intro cutscene and that is it. After that you get faceless robots without personality or even names and really nothing worth engaging with. You just get a vague goal, ie find rebel base or ohno rebelbase destroyed kill evil guy, and otherwise you just do metroivania running around trying to find switches that open doors. The first 2 hours or so I really thought I liked the game but then the platforming got to obnoxious and with out a story as motivation I will not endure any more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: KUNAI

_childDocuments_.review: Kunai is well executed aesthetically, but unfortunately it fails to deliver a good experience because of design and production flaws.I want to start with the obvious and the crucial by pointing out that this is NOT a metroidvania game. It is a completely linear, 2D action platformer game. The fact the developers chose to tag their game as a metroidvania means that they are either amateurs that have no idea what they are talking about, or that they tried to draw extra interests from players by riding on this trendy genre, which is worse.The game itself starts pretty straight forward with some tutorials. You unlock the Kunais which are the main unique mechanic that the entire game leans on. It is a fun mechanic, but it not intuitive to control. You can either choose to shoot in a 45 degrees angle to the right or to the left, or both, you can't aim it freely. I did get a grasp on having it feel intuitive until I reached the mid game, where I just couldn't feel like I could rely on those Kunais due to messy level design work.As you progress you unlock new abilities (again, in a linear way), but they fail to shine because of the bad level design, The bosses at this part of the game also get more boring, it feels more like a platforming challenge than an actual fight.The more I progressed, I just felt like the developers became lazy with their work and decided to simplify things. There was no challenge anymore, when you have all your abilities and upgrades (which are also easy to achieve) you simply become overpowered, it feels like you are playing with cheats. I wasn't engaged anymore, I simply wanted to get done with it.It is a real shame because the pixel art and sounds are cute, the game is clear and it is easy to distinguish between enemies and other things that go on the screen, and the cutscenes are nice too. But I feel like they put all their effort on their "nice to have" rather than on what matters first.It was so important for them to invest in so many cosmetic hats that you find in chests followed with long animations and without a skip button, or add robotic cats and add cat references here and there, or shove childish jokes to every monologue, instead of investing in the game itself by adding other interesting abilities, tweaking the levels, and fixing bugs.I got the game because I wanted to play something that is not taken too seriously (after playing Sekiro). It looks cute and silly but it doesn't feel like it, it falls very fast and just becomes annoying.Finally, given the low value of this game, the price is too high for what it is.Potentially, it could be a really nice game. But the developers preferred to focus on how it looks rather than how it functions, which is a fundamental design principle.At least they have all their assets ready, so if they really want to, they can rework the game to make it more fun.Until then, I cannot recommend it, it is just not worth your money and time.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Game was fun, final boss ruined it all with overly difficult and uninspired game play.- This game was quite fun. The game play felt fairly good, the music was pleasant to listen to, and I really liked the style with the limited palette.However the final boss ruined the whole game for me. It felt lazily put together as well unreasonably hard compared to the rest of the game. You're expected to use an ability you get towards the end of the game in a way that has no leeway, and there is no instance of this prior to the fight. You either do it perfect or take a chunk of damage. On top of that the boss feels very uninspired and rushed.I would like to give this game a positive review but I can't, I wouldn't recommend this game to a friend so I can't recommend it to you. I quite enjoy difficult games and bosses, but I also like having fun. I do hope the TurtleBlaze team makes better games in the future.

I took this as an excuse to enjoy more of the soundtrack and art, however.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't think of any greater sin a Metroidvania can commit than to not allow you access to the map function from the beginning.  This game will not allow you to see where you've been, and will expect you to bumble around a forest map until you find the room you're looking for (presumably - I never made it there because I couldn't tell where I hadn't been yet!).Metroidvania games DEPEND on using the map. _childDocuments_.review: KUNAI is yet another of literally thousands of 2D retro pixel platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.  This console ported 2D retro pixel platformer (sigh) is a metroidvania brawler/slasher with a bizarre theme where you're a computer headed person/robot/whatever.  Or a tablet headed person/robot/whatever made by computer headed robot/person/whatevers.  It doesn't really matter, it's all just lazy pixel blobs anyway.  Gameplay itself is uninspired, controller handling and feel is a little floaty but it "works", putting this slightly above most 2D retro pixel garbage, but being close to the top of the pile of garbage doesn't change the smell. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.  Worse, the developer couldn't work out how to use colours properly, despite the fact modern PC displays are capable of more than 16 million colours, the developer here simply didn't know how to make the game display with even as many colours as a Commodore 64 is capable of.  Ouch... talk about epic failure. There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.KUNAI has the ridiculous price of $17 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  This costs more than Hollow Knight, and the developers there hired someone who knew how to at least do computer graphics beyond crappy lazy pixel "art".  This game, for reference, costs more than the Mass Effect Trilogy... so is the developer delusional and thinks this 2D retro pixelcrap is better than Mass Effect?  Or just setting out to insult gamers with a cash grab?  Either way, don't buy it.  This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Kunai is a bit of an awkward game for me to rate. It’s closer to a thumbs up than not; it has an interesting game play mechanic that other games don’t have. It falls on the easy side though (albeit with a few jarring difficulty spikes (I’m looking at you, Furious Ferro)), and for me it’s kind of just “meh”. There’s also a bit of false advertising with this game. It purports to be like a Metroid game; while there *is* backtracking in it (you can’t even fast travel AT ALL! You *will* be walking everywhere.), the game is actually *very* linear. The game takes a page out of Mega Man Zero’s opening to start. An ancient robot (an AI-driven tablet on a humanoid chassis, nicknamed “Tabby”.) that is somehow simultaneously more advanced than all the other robots has been hanging out in a tube for however long. Then a resistance force on the run from an oppressive government finds it and activates it just in time for it to rescue them from their attackers. Then the player fights their way through area after area at a breakneck pace, defeating a boss towards the end of each area and then moving on. Returning to previous areas is always possible, but almost always unnecessary except to go after missed health expansions or other pick-ups.The bosses are mostly pushovers, though Furious Ferro’s final attack sequence is unreasonably difficult, and the final part of the Zensei fight being able to insta-kill the player + making it so that the player has to hug the top of the screen to prevent that from happening + getting hit making the fight reset every time it happens was a cruel and unusual set of design missteps that came out of nowhere. I digress. The game play consists of side-scrolling platforming and combat. Players are given an energy-absorbing katana to start with, which they can use to slice at enemies in 4 directions. Health in this game is reframed as battery power, and Tabby is fighting other robots, so destroying other robots causes them to drop particles of energy which are absorbed by the katana, recharging Tabby. TL; DR: kill enemies, get health drops. Side note: the katana can also be used to casually deflect projectiles back at enemies, which feels awesome to do.A little later, players get a pair of kunai (thus the name of the game). This is where the game gets a little more interesting. Each kunai in the pair are mapped to a different button (On a keyboard: A for the left kunai, S for the katana, D for the right kunai), and they’re actually used as rope darts for traversing the environment, not as weapons. Each kunai is automatically thrown upwards in the direction it’s associated with when the player uses it, snapping to (presumably) preprogrammed points in the environment. The ropes are also elastic; if the player attaches both kunai to two nearby surfaces and then holds and releases the down key, they can launch themselves upwards (though the release window for the launch part is a little finicky). There are rarely any times where the launching thing is actually useful (or even possible), but it’s a fun little extra thing. Once the player gains access to the kunai, the entire game becomes “2D Spider-Man by way of kinda-sorta-but-not-really Metroid”.Eventually players are given a few other things to augment their abilities. These include electrified shuriken (which stun enemies, or open doors and move platforms when thrown at special receptacles), an SMG (which lets players “spray-and-pray against enemies, or allows players to “hover” across large gaps by firing down), and a rocket launcher (which can be used to blast large rocks obstructing certain paths out of the way, as well as obliterating all the robots players hit with it within a rocket’s blast radius). Players also get a dash chip towards the end of the game, which allows Tabby to dash through the gaps in certain metal bars, as well as the final boss' beam attacks.Aside from all ^^that^^, there’s also an in-game store where players can use in-game currency (also dropped by enemies) to buy performance enhancements for all of Tabby’s weapons, as well as a smithy bot that can upgrade the katana’s base damage output. Some of these upgrades are especially useful; once I got the ability that let me charge up Tabby’s katana attacks to perform an iai slice that transitions through multiple additional iai slices via flash-stepping to annihilate all the enemies on the screen as long as I kept hitting the katana button, I was using either that or rockets for most of the rest of the game. Then there’s the rocket jump upgrade, which would’ve been a no-brainer even if there wasn’t an optional time trial challenge in the game that literally can’t be beaten without it as far as I can tell.There are also hats to collect throughout the game. Yay. All in all, the game is a decent amount of fun. As of me deciding to come back and write this review, this is my second time through it, and I do remember getting to the end of the game the first time and thinking, “Really? That’s it?” The game’s ending does kind of race up and smack you upside the head. It’s just like: get mech. Go to moon. Defeat boss. Roll credits. It’s all just very abruptly over.If I step back and give the game the Metroid test as far as length goes, it’s actually twice as long as more recent Metroid games, or *four* times as long as the older ones, but it didn’t *feel* like it was longer.  It felt like the game just honestly didn’t have that much too it compared to other games in the genre, and then it was over, in spite of how long it actually seemed to take for me to beat it. I would call this a soft recommendation. Kunai is a fun game. If you take a look at it, and you think you’d like it because it looks like other things you’ve played, you’re right. It looks like the other things you’ve played because it is similar, and you will probably like it. Other side note: the soundtrack is pretty good. Especially the songs that play in areas that players spend the most time in. If nothing else, the soundtrack is worth a listen even if you don't buy the game. "Artificial Desert" is my favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game when taken on its own merits. It's a fun and short action-platformer romp with the metroidvania stuff basically being used to control the pace of ability & weapon progression. There is no openness whatsoever, it's incredibly linear, to the point it will even mark your next destination on the map. Normally when a game does that I'll go out of my way to explore every other direction first, but you can't do that here. The game is interested in one thing, action-platforming and boss fights, with the kunai serving as your main mobility aid. Taken on those merits I had a good time with it. Once I got it through my head (early on) that the game isn't going to  let me explore on my own and just sat back and enjoyed the ride I was on, I had a pretty good time. There are some issues, sometimes the game expects you to reach platforms you can't see (same issue applies to enemy placement) and the game isn't interested in explaining anything really, figure it out or don't, the game isn't bothered. I also found the cosmetics system of different hats you can find somewhat annoying. It was fine during normal exploration, but when I was doing an optional platforming challenge or backtracking in order to try to get an extra health upgrade or two it was somewhat annoying to be "rewarded" with another silly hat. But these are overall minor issues that didn't really cause me much problem for my playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: I never saw much point in tablets. They lack the power and ease of use of computers, but also lack the portability of phones. This has nothing to do with my opinion on KUNAI, except perhaps the fact that I didn't like it as well.What I did like about it was the music, at least early on. Also, once I got the kunai I also was surprised by how fun it is to use them to swing around! Made me feel like I'm using ninja rope in old Worms games. And then there's the detailed, bouncy look of Tabby, our protagonist; that part is pretty good at making you think this game looks nice.Let me rephrase that: Tabby looks nice, the enemies look nice as well, the UI is crisp, but the environments... they're very samey and flat. No real landmarks or anything to help orient yourself. And this is a Metroidvania, so orienting yourself is a huge part of the game. Luckily, there's a map to help... you... with... that?There is no map...?Actually, there is. As an unlockable upgrade that you get roughly 45 minutes in, in a particularly confusing part of the third area of the game. And by "there is no map" I don't mean that you only get what your character has visited. No - the feature is completely absent (until you get it). Mix that with confusing, samey environments, and you'll understand why I spent some good 20 minutes of my playtime walking in circles.To wrap things up, let me mention the titular kunai. The way they work is simple: you shoot a little rope at a 45 degree angle either to the left or to the right (separate buttons for greater control). This makes using them very quick, easy and indeed fun; that said, whenever a level of precision is needed things slow down a lot. Because you can't control the angle of your kunai shot, it's all about being in the right place so that your 45 degree shot hits what you want. And not all surfaces are suitable for you kunai to latch onto. Take it or leave it, I guess.Okay, one last thing. The facial expressions. Tabby makes all sorts of weird faces. Normally he has a smile on his, uh, screen, but when you attack his expression changes to this hardcore fighter frown. When you slide down the wall, the expression changes to... I don't even know. Grinning teeth? And there's more, but I feel like Tabby doesn't really have a personality, it's just "make my face into an emoji" kind of thing. Is he silly or determined? Is he cool or happy? I don't know, and I don't care anymore.So there you go. I just don't think KUNAI is that fun to play. If you're looking for a good Metroidvania involving cute robots I'd suggest checking out  instead.

_childDocuments_.review: A ridiculous and over the top metroidvania adventure that will take you about 5-8 hours depending on how thorough you are. The game will keep you entertained during those hours as the pacing is really good. This is on one hand due the constant progress of your movement/combat abilities as you navigate new environments and on the other hand because movement is fast and snappy. You can traverse the dozen or so zones at lightning speed, dashing and grappling whilst destroying everything in your path. This is extremely satisfying as you can tear through hordes of enemies very quickly. Combat and movement are thus solid which is one of the halmarks of a good metroidvania, the other being good level design. Here kunai also does pretty well, the environments are varied enough both in visuals and gameplay, with backtracking & multiple branching paths, shortcuts and secrets to discover. Sadly a lack of fast travel makes it too stingey to 100% the map. Visuals are fine, good pixel art but nothing spectacular/memorable. The character designs are pretty solid though, with distinct and easy to indentify characters to meet. Music is not my cup of tea, but it's a nice callback to the soundtracks of old, which works well in this game. Performance is great, and there's no bugs that i encountered so it's a well polished game. Lastly story is unremarkable (although hilarious at times) but that's fine as that's sort of like the cherry on top of a GREAT metroidvania. This one isn't one of those, but it's a good one nonetheless, especially because of the fun movement mechanics. i'd recommend it to any metroidvania/platformer fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I was bored this morning, and decided to play through this after picking it up in the summer sale. It took me about 5 hours, and it was pretty fun. Expect a semi-metroidvania; it isn't as open as Super Metroid, or even Hollow Knight (I rarely got lost), but you do have the option of going back and finding secrets and such with your new abilities. There was a difficulty spike near the end of the game, but that might have been partly my fault, rushing off to fight the boss without collecting everything beforehand. Overall, this is a polished experience and I would highly recommend this to anyone who wants a short, charming platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: KUNAI flips weapon progression systems on their head. You start with nothing but a katana, which is already the most powerful weapon in the game (and you can make it stronger), letting you heal yourself by attacking with it. Then it gives you a RIGHT kunai (grappling hook), making you go "oooh so its like Twilight Princess with the double clawshots" and then not 5 seconds later you find the LEFT kunai and you go "ooohh...?". From there on, its pretty standard, but still some surprising twists: you get throwing stars, but they don't do damage! By the time you get the BIG EXPLODY GUN, you've probably mastered every other weapon and know when its best to use the weaker guys and when to pull out the big guns. The only things I don't like about the weapons is that their charged attack upgrades are too slow to use when you'd need them most, and the best one (the one for the katana) trades off with health, so you will probably quickly stop using it. Also, the katana upgrades cost a ♥♥♥♥ ton. I think that's because they are meant to be a last resort, but even then, where do you make that much money?Shockingly this game has absolutely no transport/teleport/quick travel mechanic. It's like a perfect case example of how sorely needed quick travel is in action platformers (idk if you can truly call this a metroidvania), because you will FEEL IT when you need to backtrack, and it almost seems like this game wants you to backtrack. Sometimes it's almost ridiculous, with one dungeon requiring you to walk across its entire length to go through a door you just flipped open, and then do the same thing but in reverse. It sucks and also demotivated me from going back to previous areas to find all the hidden chests.Speaking of hidden chests... This game very much falls prey to the "invisible wall with a room behind it" torture that is a staple of metroidvanias now, I guess. Like collecting or finding hidden stuff? Settle in, because you are going to be rubbing against EVERY WALL to make sure you don't miss anything cool. Blegh, please no more.The boss fights actually featured some great variety, which confirms this isn't a metroidvania. But... Zensei... Again, it's like a case study in why some bosses need checkpoints, or just like, a way to not have to redo the entire fight because the last section is inexplicably much harder than the rest. I was so fed up with Zensei by the time I beat him, it was not at all a "YES! I DID IT!" it was a "the pain is over, and now i can begin healing".The music is sick, Quantum Forest made me just want to spend more time there. However, I was pretty surprised to find the Final Boss music was... the same as every other boss. And the credits music... was the boss music again. I think. Or maybe it was the main menu music? Anyways, the extremely sudden credits roll with the reused track made me feel like I was giving too long of a speech at the Oscars. Like, "ok ok you did it, nice job, hurry up and get outta here".Mixed feelings across the board. Definitely a fun time, but very much having some sore spots of major frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun, but it kinda falls off towards the end.This game has a colorful world with plenty to explore. The movement feels nice and the combat works really well. The bosses are also really fun to fight. The game kinda falls off towards the end though. The level design starts to feel unfair with a lot of blind jumps and platforms off screen that you're expected to somehow jump to without taking damage, and the final boss, as well as the final world right before the boss, are really generic and underwhelming. The final boss especially was underwhelming compared to the other really creative fights throughout the game. Despite this criticism, Kunai is still a great metroidvania that I strongly recommend! The game has solid mechanics, and it is was fun from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game. The story was ok, wasn't really fantastic. Really loved the pixelated graphics and the animations. The best thing was to play around with the kunais. There are also different types of weapons sword, rocket launcher, smg, etc.. You can also buy upgrades and unlock abilities like dash. The bosses were interesting, the final one was a bit hard but it's not impossible.There are a few downsides with this game. First downside is that, there are not teleporters. Once you complete an objectiv like "investigate the power source in a city" you have to go all the way back to your base. And the base is  very far away, it gets worse if you die cause you spawn at your last checkpoint. The second downside is that in the game has a "Blacksmith" that gives you upgrades for your sword, and it is quite expensive. The point is those upgrades are pointless. They don't give you anything. And the last thing is the dash. You unlock the dash almost at the end of the game, i think you should unlock it at the beginning.But overall i enjoyed it. Recommend it.
