_childDocuments_.review: Good game, or at least to me. "Through the Darkest of Times" has similar vibes to "Papers, Please" and the "Beholder" series, all of which I have played and enjoyed before. But, the real historical events and political connotations in this game might turn some people away. Real events stir real scars. They are simply more difficult to play with than dystopian fantasies.This game also needs some seriously patch work. I really hope the devs can fix the following general issues/bugs in the future. 1) The mechanics around hiding people from persecution simply don't work. There are minimal requirements for fulfilling these quests when encountered in the main story, and there are no follow-ups/consequences of you doing the quests, and they don't trigger the corresponding achievements (I am pretty sure I have saved at least one person), and the action of setting up "hideouts" is lacking significance as well. 2) The story mode is too easy if you ignore all the starred missions and too hard if you don't. "Where it hurts" is the hardest among all playable starred missions and you need to save/load for some preferable RNG results, which takes away the significance of choices. 3) I have completed all starred missions except for "Crossing the Border" in chapter 2, which couldn't be completed at all because "getting fake passports" seems to be bugged. tbc.

_childDocuments_.review: As a test of character, the game is fantastic. Bring this game up in conversation and if your friend tries to defend the Nazis and/or compare the actions of the Nazis to a group like Antifa, communists, Democrats, or whatever, then you know that you need new friends.As a game, it's fairly simplistic. You and your small ragtag band undertake missions to organize a resistance and fight back against the Nazis. _childDocuments_.review: WHY I LIKE THIS GAME AND WHY YOU SHOULD TOO!This game has attracted the hatred of Trump followers, who resent that it uses historical analogy to shed light on current affairs.  They have spammed the reviews and discussions with blatantly false accusations, trying to convince each other and everyone else not to play, even to the point of making up untrue criticism.Why?  How could a computer game about Nazi Germany evoke such an extreme response in 2020, almost a century later, among people mostly in their 20s and 30s?  What does this behavior tell us?First, note that virtually all of the accusations against this game are simply not true.  It's not designed by a bunch of communists.  It's not some kind of spyware to violate your privacy and divulge your sensitive information to third parties.  It's not "fake history."  Lies are the first and last resort of those who seek to do harm.  You can verify for yourself that this game is not spyware, is not designed by communists, is not fake history.  I won't even stoop to that level of argument.  Just check for yourself.A better explanation, I think, than that this game's detractors have legitimate grievances, is that the truth hurts.  We do live in a time reminiscent of Nazi Germany.  We in the US have a leader who is above the law, who spouts hate at every turn, who threatens, bullies, and retaliates against anyone who does not exhibit blind obedience ... very similar to Nazi Germany.  This creates a dilemma for every reasonable person.  Do nothing?  Or, try to act in solidarity with other reasonable people to reduce the harm caused by the leader and his followers?  This was a problem for every reasonable person in Nazi Germany in the 1930s and '40s, and it is a problem for every reasonable peson in the United States today.  The immense value of this game is this:  it explores this dilemma.  What would you do if you were a reasonable person in Nazi Germany?  What do you do, now, as a reasonable person in Trump's America?  Do nothing?  Or, try to raise awareness?  What moral principles do you abide by?  If this question strikes a chord, then you, too, will like this game.  THROUGH THE DARKEST OF TIMES takes you through four chapters in Nazi history, from Hitler's appointment as Germany's Chancellor, through the 1936 Olympic games, the invasion of the Soviet Union, and finally the battle for Berlin.  Each chapter has 20 one-week turns, in which you, as leader of a clandestine group of marginalized and oppressed champions of Truth, Reason and Justice, strive to awaken your compatriots and the world at large to the true nature of the evil which has overwhelmed your country, and which will lead to things like Germany's Aktion T4 program to kill hundreds of thousands of children with medical diagnoses like Asperger's Syndrome, then the Holocaust, and ultimately to the greatest mass slaughter in Human History, World War Two.  Can you change the course of events?  Can you change just a few minds?  Or will your own conscience be overwhelmed by the hate surrounding you?Each turn, you and your fellows choose among various missions to undertake in different neighborhoods of the German capital, Berlin, like networking and recruiting new members, raising money, and ordinary everyday acts of resistance like engaging in political speech, printing leaflets, painting grafitti, smuggling banned books, and more audacious endeavors like spying and hiding fugitives.  While doing that, you must navigate SA thuggery, survive Gestapo interrogation, avoid being sent to a concentration camp, engage characters in consciousness-raising conversation, and make decisions that will allow you and your group to survive and grow.  The visual and sonic artwork is quite good, with a dark, expressionistic, graphic novel feel, along with a great soundtrack of Nazi-banned 1930s jazz music, to which your characters can occasionally spend a night dancing as an act of subversion to Nazi oppression.No, it's not a perfect game.  But it's got a lot of content, and as you play it, you seem to really get a feel for how it can be to have your whole society seemingly captured by hate.  You also feel the victory of small accomplishments, like changing someone's mind about the Nazis.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it is true, what you do in this game does not matter and it’s ultimately about survival.The far from the center politics on both sides of the spectrum are guilty of  a vehicle to set apart and vilify the opposition. This is relevant because this game is accused of showcasing parallels between WW2 Nazi Germany and current post 2016 events. I don’t know the history of the studio or its creators, so can’t assume their intentions, but judging by the description and my play experience, I see them as noble and successfully spread their message even if the game play part should’ve been much more explored.The premise of the game is very clear: you’re part of a resistance group born from the rise of Hitler whose job is to disrupt that totalitarian power by sabotage and counter-intelligence. It does not shy away from all the key events, even if it does ignore many of its official symbols. What it doesn’t show it prefers to tell through characters that represent various views, some opposing others favoring the regime. Catholic Conservatives, Christian Liberals, Social Democrats, Communists, all are working together against the perceived evil despite ideological disagreements. Only the most reactionaries /radicals of the respective groups are either totally in favor the regime or against. Regardless, you can expect character to be faced with this conflict. Family members being truly radicalized or having to work for the Reich to survive, and during dialogue, you can either agree or disagree with some of it, without losing sight of the objective, which is keeping morale up and garner popular support to be able to plan more activities that are more risky but also highly rewarding. That is the main gist of the game, and if your morale goes completely down, group disbands and game over.What I feel it’s the root cause of many criticism (and praise) is confirmation bias. When reading the cut scenes and what each character opinion on the Reich is, it’s easy to notice many of the sentences can be found today on media outlets and internet activism about the current political climate. Whether something it’s true or not is irrelevant at this point because it has already become a meme. Policy is ignored and the trade off is an ideological arms race where everyone is looking for tribe approval, signaling support at each other not only to show how the other is not alone but also how we, our own person, is also powerless to change anything. It originates one big circle jerk but it’s ultimately a better survival chance than being quiet and without purpose, if not for the fear of our silence being mistaken for being in support of the other when most of out family and friends already picked a side, even if when they talk, it’s a reputation score contest. This is important in the game too. While I did not feel like I was being fed ideas – maybe because I also believe fascism is not a good ruling system – I couldn’t help but draw comparisons between the ideas presented and many of current events. The caveat here is I do not believe anything being done today is automatically comparable to WW2 Germany, but is certainly easy to look at both sides of the aisle, take a good look, and find a Hitlerism. The issue is, it has become so easy it also became so ridiculous,  has become a fair rebuttal –  We could go as far as Herodotus if we really looking to criticize modern society and modern politics, but it doesn’t prove a point. It isn’t recent enough, and most importantly, not shocking enough.  The game’s shock value feels like it’s “for the sake of it” because whatever we do, we are not changing history. I think there are opportunities to do so, but requires good planing, timing and luck, something you might not find in a first play through. We are not visually shocked because the art is suggestive, but the added descriptions surely do the job. But if the game didn’t do that it would instead be accused of being tame and not having the courage of being honest about the War, and remember I already accused it of not going all the way with the symbolism. While you don’t need a high quality drawing to know what they’re trying to tell you,  the audience surely is expected to immerse itself and think hard on the subjects. The game and its peers seem to claim to be historically accurate, or as much as game play allows. While I’m very familiar with WW2 from a zoomed out and geopolitical perspective, I’m not knowledgeable on the resistance, their methods, philosophy and historical operations within Germany. I  did not read any newspapers of the era either. I’m taking everything at face value with a pinch of salt, having in mind many things had to be simplified for the sake of presenting the project. Still, I came out feeling like there were many gray areas. Each party and eventual coalitions had legitimate reasons for their attitudes towards the Reich, positive or negative, and any perceptions of it are proportionally acceptable. You will mediate conflicts between Christians and Communists in the resistance hideout, and if you send a Catholic into a workers union to gather donations, you won’t get much help. But if you send a Social Democrat or Communist to the Union, you’ll have much more success. Similar predicament if you send a Communist to a Church community. During the game, these conflicts are not that intense though they might inflict blows on morale, but I would consider normal in the real life resistance if the Catholics and Communists, even if they shared a goal against Fascism, they would refuse working with each other altogether. In real life, Catholics would work only with Christian Liberals and Communists would work only with Social Democrats, but entirely possible for Christian Liberals to triangulate with the Communists via Social Democrats to gather intelligence and support. Maybe this could be explored more deeply in the game play but I think the message was sent nonetheless.The years pass and you’re in the next Chapter (There’s Four). You start over. I think the only things that carry to the next chapter are the leveled up traits (Secrecy, Empathy, Literacy, Fitness and Communication) and some inventory(?). You’ll go back to default morale and support and have to plan activities to unlock new ones all over again. It is possible that by doing the “Big Bang” type activities you may “change history”, but unfortunately RNGesus was throwing me around like a puppet and was stuck on money donations and brochures 60% of the time so I could get to Intel and Prisoner Release missions (for example), which are higher tier but not the top tier ones. At the end of the Chapter, history happens and you just got to accept it. You won’t be stopping The Blitz nor giving Berlin to the British.  I finished the campaign thinking this feeling of “nothing I do really matters” was intended, or at worst, fits the experience. It represents the oppressive influence of the government you’re fighting against and the direct consequences of a War not just prompted by resources but raw power grabbing. It is a relatable time because just like today, old grievances are making a come back to politics, just like Germany at the time was fed up with the rest of the world after World War I. The economic crisis of 2008-2011 started a chain of events that rose skepticism of Neo-Liberalism and the pandemic deepened wounds, data now suggesting young people are becoming way more comfortable with authoritarianism than they should; comparable with back then when the Great Recession was felt and affected the lives of millions, which helped autocracy gain immense power worldwide. It is a story about a group of people with a higher purpose fighting in a time where the world was at risk of collapsing. It is a lesson about surviving
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: A combination of addictive & challenging mechanics combined with the tragedy of WW2 in Berlin make this a moving and highly recommended title. Even with the proliferation of media on this topic, this is highly recommended. There are some bugs throughout, but they largely added to the experience of uncertainty for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: I think for how it works mechanically it is an overpriced  "casual" strategy game. Aside from that it is a significant piece of media that I don't believe anyone should recommend against. It is chilling and terrifying to consider that most of what you witness playing this is not some fantasy but rather a situation that was a reality. It is a mini history lesson in game form which also points to the fact that not EVERY German followed Hitler and that, whilst he was undoubtedly supported by the majority of the nation at the time, the percentage reports of said support were heavily doctored. I have quite a few German friends on Steam and playing this could well be more uncomfortable for them but I'm not under any illusion as to the fact that they are painfully aware of a stain that labels them just through the fact of where they were born.In gameplay terms it's a fairly simplistic management game where you recruit and allocate characters and resources but its story is always going to outweigh its gameplay and it is fairly impossible to tell just how well or badly you are doing at any given time. Unless you have a perverse desire to be horrified by mankind's capacity for atrocities towards itself then you should get this when on sale or through this month's Humble Bundle as I did.In short, whilst it is not BAD in terms of what it offers as a game and i can't possibly call it fun or enjoyable due to the nature of its uncomfortable narrative content, it undoubtedly has lasting value as an interactive learning experience for generations that will be less aware of, or want/need to know more about the setting. I don't DISLIKE it as a game but it is an uncomfortable reminder of how bad we can be despite its message of perseverance through extreme adversity and resistance to the immoral.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game. Nicely done, nice music, graphics, text. However, the replayability is completely hampered by the gameplay: impossible to tell the result of actions. If the goal is only to survive, then maybe it the difficulty level is too low. Considering the game can be finished in 4 hours, that's a bit an issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game that pushes you right back into Nazi Germany. Playing a normal person you have to live in constant fear of your life and the loved ones, while you try to make a meaningful impact against the atrocities that are happening around you. The game-play is turn-based and you try to balance actions like public resistance and sabotage, with recruiting members and money. All while trying not to get caught in times, when buying a can of colour might end you in prison. It's a great history lesson and makes you understand resistance on a much deeper level than any school lesson could. Highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: The game is solid, but I would rather trumpet the merits of the narrative and setting and the dialogue and description, they each pull their weight in providing for a greater context for this historical period in general and is necessary and important food for thought and reminders for vigilance against the dangers of ignoring the rise of a fascist society. Thumbs way up.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Berlin, lead the Revolution and save Germany from the Führer whilst fighting against his brainwashed followers. In general, the game felt very good, and I actually had lots of fun, let's take a glance at what I saw.You think you already know everything about Hitler, right? . Moreover, pay attention to the dialogues! They feel quite real as they reflect the mindset of the German population of the decade. The developers are German, which is a nice bearing in mind this is a historical-accurate game. During the game you will not only encounter interesting details about Germany during WW2, but also about other countries affected by the conflict all around Europe (even Spain, whose participation in war is often lost in history!). Definitely a game that any WW2 fanatic will enjoy, although you must like reading because the entire game is pretty much text-based. In addition, I also have to mention that if you like politics this is a game you'll enjoy.As far as I know, most of the stories from the game are real, which makes the game very emotional as it makes you think about how cruel and inhumane human beings are. An outstanding way of learning about Hitler's rise to power whilst having fun (after all, it's a videogame and it has to be enjoyable), very recommended for anyone interested in the topic.The game has its very own unique and amazing art style, a very cool move by . Even though it's cartoonish, it gets dark when you encounter Nazi officers, something that works great with the sepia, black and grey and sometimes bright colours popping in the screen. Enjoyed it a lot.Paying attention to its music, even though I enjoyed it, I believe it could have been better. Don't get me wrong, I actually enjoyed the music playing in the background during different missions and cinematics, although it's such a pity they didn't use iconic songs from the war period that could have fit perfectly within the atmosphere of the game.Honestly, I was only interested in playing the normal difficulty as I wanted to enjoy the game as much as I could. I got familiarised with the game pretty fast and it wasn't especially hard, although it definitely made me plan my moves beforehand. Moreover, it's important to mention that minor decisions during cinematics may lead you to different situations and even change the future of your group.On the other hand, completing all achievements seems doable, although it looks like it might take you at least two runs.Possibly one of the best things from the game. Every single character has a different ideology and personality, so you have to choose wisely before any mission as you don't really want to send an Anarchist to a Christian convention. Moreover, you will see how even though all of your comrades fight for the same purpose, they may clash between each other because of their thoughts about your actions. A very cool feature of the game which I enjoyed, very well performed.I found a huge bargain for the game, although after playing it I feel like 5 to 10€ is a fair price range for it. Play it, you won't feel disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Gut-wrenching. That's the only term I can think of that can sum up the exprience of playing this game. It certainly succeeds at portraying the horror and moral conflicts of the rise of fascism in Germany. Couldn't help but feel angry and compare it with the world situation today. Are people blind? Does screaming at their faces that they're wrong help? Are we doing enough to fight it all back? It's all too much to handle. The way the story is written here is almost impeccable. Are there small plotholes here and there? Yes, but nothing that takes away from the whole experience. The connection between player and character is basically instantaneous - ordinary people trying to survive, well, the darkest of times. After completing it, I feel sad, but also energized. Let's keep the good fight going - and ♥♥♥♥ the fascists.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: I love this type of game where it is an educational experience and an entertainment experience.It's great to play a game taken from the perspective of German civilians, a part of history under recorded and this game address that historical oversight.So it educates you, but is it any good , well yes it's a good game in the way that Valiant Hearts is an educational and good game.It's stop short of being brilliant but that said it is definitely worth playing and definitely worth buying, so yes I can confidently recommend it, there are a few things I would of improved that would of made it a brilliant game like This War is Mine, but these things would be more about polish than fixing something broken.In way of comparison , it has the same dark feel of This war is mine and the cartoon look of Valiant Hearts, if you loved those games then you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: The balance of risk of dying very painfully and the chance to achieve anything meaningful seems very realistic to me. This brought me better udnerstanding of what it really took for anyone to participate in the resistance. Education about the history is also a big part. Not about dates of events. But things that really happend and one after another are unbelievable terrifying.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great at telling the story of the rise of Nazi Germany from a personal perspective. Although gameplay is quite limited and difficult, the way the game exposes you to this era feels very personal and even heartbreaking at times. I would greatly recommend the game for any person with an interest in history or story driven games.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically a combination of "Papers, Please" with "911 operator".Like "Papers, Please" we're living in a dystopian totalitarian state. The only difference is here it's a historical reality of 1930s Germany under Nazi rule.And like "911 operator", it's a level-based tactical game, with minimalistic graphics.Both these games btw, I gave a negative review.But I can't give this game a negative review.If only for the fact that it deals with such an important topic.A topic that is forgotten more and more as years go by...But game-play wise - the game doesn't have much content.The missions are monotone and repetitive. The variation is not very large.And in any case, the result of the mission are of a limited variation: money, supporters, morale, "heat" reduction, items or a new character (if you have an open slot).You have stats, missions have requirements, and a random "dice toss" decides if you succeed or fail.Another thing detrimental to the gameplay, is the fact that you have story-related "cutscenes" between every 2 days of the game, which disrupt the flow of the tactical part of the game.So instead of playing one game-day, setting up a long-term plan, and following-up on them the next day... You play one game-day, then get a "cutscene" with lots of text, and choices you need to take, which are in no way related to the actions you took on the tactical part of the game, yet can affect it on the next day. And only then start the next day of the game, when you already forgotten half the things you wanted to follow up on from the previous day.I think it's important to come to this game with proper expectations.If you come expecting an interesting and engaging gameplay, of a strategic resource management simulator OR a choices matter text adventure game - you will be disappointed.Instead, this is a dystopian dictatorship games (like Beholder, Papers Please, Do not feed the monkeys, etc.) that shows the horrors of war/dictatorship (like This war of mine, Valiant Hearts, 11-11 Memories Retold, etc.), that gives a lot of backstory and world-building background of real historical events.This is more of an important historical lesson, less a piece of digital entertainment.P.S. If you like this theme, I suggest you watch the critically acclaimed 2023 mini-series "A small light".Which tells the story of the people who hid Anne Frank's family in Nazi-occupied Holland.And has a very similar look & feel, of how was it like living under the Nazi rule, while trying to resist it.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: This game gives a fascinating roleplaying opportunities whilst remaining both sort-of-historical and sort-of-educational (if this time period is interesting to you and you would like to know more about NSDAPs rise to power and decline). Good game mechanics and the sound and art is of high quality. Some game immersion breaking stuff here and there but nothing to bad. In my opinion there are some inconsistency in the way the game behaves, but all over a very good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: A strategy/sim game where you play a small resistance movement in Nazi Germany. I appreciate what the game is doing and the concept is interesting, but the gameplay itself is iffy. The core gameplay of sending agents to accomplish missions which then give you resources (money, followers, items needed to do other missions) is a bit repetitive, which wouldn't be so bad if you felt like you were actually making some kind of progress. But succeeding at missions doesn't seem to impact the flow of the game or the narrative at all, and then at the end of each chapter everything is reset and you have to start all over. It seems like the game has potential as an educational resource on the rise of the Nazis in Germany, but as a game it felt hollow and unsatisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: As far as strategy games go this is a clear "meh, boring". However, here the game is just the wrapping, and the actual content lies in reliving history, through the darkest past of Germany.The perspective is from a resistance cell in Nazi Germany, and spans from the early days of the fascist regime in January 1933 to it`s complete and utter collapse in May 1945. The narrative does a good job of telling the half-plunge / half-fall of Germany into the abyss from the viewpoint of a group of civilians in Berlin. It is filled with many heart-rending and soul-crushing moments and stories, and as such, I feel this game should actually have some place in student's history classes (and not just Germans).However, like many such works of art, it falls (deliberately?) short of giving more relevant context: How could the Nazis come into power? How did the war actually go? How did life in Germany change after the war? What is the situation in 2020? The entire experience could be greatly improved by adding a meaningful and deep prologue & epilogue, which in the end left me feeling a little disappointed. I did, however still learn some new things, and liked it overall. The game even has some replayability, so all things considered I can actually recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let history repeats itself. There are Nazis everywhere today who try to use "patriotism", "freedom", and "unproven election fraud" to justify their psychotic violence against people who do not share their nationalistic racist ideology. This game reminds us that nationalism and fake patriotism may lead to Nazism and Fascism. The music of this game is good. The gameplay is not complicated. This game isn't very difficult. It gives some historical background about what happened inside Germany during WWII. The pace of this game can be slow at times. And I don't know how to save the game. So, I let my computer run while I went to sleep. This game is worth buying if it is on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Experienced multiple gamebreaking bugs. I cant continue playing my current save and tbh im not exactly motivated to restart. The gameplay is bland, rng heavy and feels ponitless. surviving is easy, but the "objectives" the game shows you are seemingly impossible. Most maps/time frames either dont even have the required items in the necessary quantities or are way to short to actually get all of them. I think it nassumes that everything went perfect all the time. If one diceroll isnt in your favor, you can basically reload or just turn of your brain and watch until the current timeframe ends, cause there is nothing else to do if the big objectives become unattainable.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: The storytelling aspect is the best part, and the sense of anxiety.  Play through it once, and treat it like a continuous one-shot experience (don't save and reload to optimize your progress).  Ask yourself how you would really behave in each situation.  Try to accomplish one of the big goals in each chapter (there's usually a few to choose from).  I'd recommend this game to kids who are learning about the history of Germany and WW2.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good idea but way too constricted. You get a whopping 19 turns in the first chapter to complete your objectives. This is way too little and prevents you from seeing what the game really has to offer. Basically, if you don't luck out on RNG at all times, you will be stuck breaking teammates out of prison every turn. It's a shame because this is a great idea with stupid limits.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: It feels more like a story than a game, which delivers a powerful message of the horrors of World War 2. I would love to leave a positive review but due to the fact that it has several broken achievements that have not been fixed (and probably will never be) I cannot recommend this game.If you're an achievement hunter, feel free to check out my curator for more reviews!
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: I hate the game that fails to entertain but tries to make it up by giving some sloppy messages.Yeah we know Nazis were bad and we need to remember the pain and the history.The game's initial purpose is probably to intensify the emotion& the feelings of those times.But i felt this is somewhat an insult. Games are one of most effective ways to wash the guilt of violence away.With just few clicks, i felt nothing so special about abandoning my crews to death and the game is designed to make some people die and get beaten up. There's nothing I can do about it.The violence it depicts is horrible in a way that it really occurred in the past but the way it depicts with funny-looking, ugly pictures wasn't impressive. Am i expected to cry or feel pain? I felt like the devs handing me a bag of tissues to cry at the moment they want. Why are they making me feel like a horrible person by saying i'm not impressed with their work?  The gameplay is not intuitive at all. It seems I can do a lot on a map but there are so many actions that require something to be done as prerequisite. Why didn't they make them appear after I've done the work? Everything is so random except the fact Nazi is bad. Even if you try to do something to progress, the nazi police appears so you have flee, hide or confront. The best result after choosing the option is just getting what i was supposed to get and that never happens much. All the progress and deep consideration just goes to waste by random nazi police. How convenient. Without Nazi sign, this game would have gotten so much worse rating than this. They keep putting scripts and stupid skits to say "Hey, Nazi was this bad. So the game is good because we are saying nazi is bad. right? If the game's not fun, it should be because Nazi thing is a serious matter not to laugh about. right?"  Yeah nazi is bad and so are you devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Quite an excellent game that in some ways reminds me of the board game Black Orchestra, only on a smaller scale and more personal. The historical backdrop is accurate as are the choices you have to make. My first go at it, my group of resistance fighters resigned after six months, by summer of 1933. This time around, my team has survived into June of 1941, but not without scars. One member ended up beaten up by the SA, another quit, and yet another ratted the group out to the Nazis. Still, we survived... The game takes place on a map of Berlin, with a multitude of choices ranked by how dangerous they may be, which can be mitigated somewhat by the abilities of your members. The turns are interspersed with historical events that often impact your decisions. Also, there are narrative bits in which your character has to make personal decisions that can open up other possibilities for the group. As the game progresses, the other-arching story shifts, from trying to stop the Nazis, trying to let outsiders know of atrocities, to resisting the war effort. I'm still in the middle of it, so I don't know how my group will do. I can see by all the missions that I didn't do or that I failed at that the game does have more replay value than I had expected. If you enjoy the theme and like a game with some RPG aspect, some strategic planning, and a decent narrative, you may like this game. I don't think the game is that difficult--I'm playing it without being able to redo turns. But if you're looking for a light-hearted game, this isn't it. The gameplay isn't as dark as This War of Mine, but the overall story is about totalitarian oppression, genocide, and war. Sometimes it's fun to play the underdog doing what you can to throw a monkey wrench in Der Fuhrer's plans.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a well written story which really educates you and describes how it must have been like for the people back then.The only thing I didn't quite like was the gameplay - there's not much to it. You just send people on missions and except the random outcomes. There's not much strategy to it.But I still recommend it because of the story and how it's presented.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. The gameplay is admittedly a little dry and there is quite a lot of reading, which did give me a headache because of a lazy eye. But as a history nerd, I like it. There is a great show of Nazi Germany's descent into fear dominant regime from a German perspective. I was able to learn a lot about the German home life during the war and the plotline does well to show just how frustratingly hopeless resistance within Germany would have been during the time.  One thing that does annoy me a little is that Swastikas are removed from the game. Hear me out. I know that in Germany the display of any Nazi symbolism is heavily regulated but from what I've seen, this game would be applicable for exemption under German law. In the game, there are multiple scenes which describe the flags everywhere and with the symbol missing, it takes away from the immersion of the game as actually being resistance in Germany. I can understand why they would choose not to include it though. I got the game through Humble Bundle and for once I can say that I am happy with the games on offer. Its a well made game with an interesting historical perspective and a lot of tiny details that can change each playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: This game sets out to show players what it was like to live through Hitler's rise to power as an everyday person who was opposed to the Nazis' murderous ideology. It does a great job of showing the hopelesness and despair that was slowly growing as democracy gets dismantled around you and a brutal and inhumane autocracy is built in it's stead. It does so by combining turn based management sim gameplay with narrative events and the two layers really work well together. It's not necessarily a fun game, but instead very challenging, both on an emotional and mechanical level and ultimately a more rewarding experience than more lighthearted games.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Through the Darkest of Times is an intensely historical computer game that immerses the player in an eerily accurate depiction of the Third Reich's grip over Germany and the German people. The gameplay is engaging and keeps the player attentive as the tragedy that was the rise to power of the National Socialists is depicted in events that affect both the player's comrades and average Germans that one encounters on the street in historical events. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game and played it all in 2 sittings. It tells a great story where you can choose what happens to your group, do you struggle to survive the Nazis crackdowns, do you want to be a bastion fighting the regime liberating prisoners and fighting for the people. Although the gameplay is pretty lackluster it is still very enjoyable and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hurts when you see your members being arrested or killed. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts off strong, the premise, the atmosphere are all set, each decision matter and you have to really replay a lot to understand the game... much to the frustration of some or enjoyment of others... but I think what made me give a negative review of this game is that in the 2nd act of the game you literally start by doing the same missions that you did in the 1st sequence
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start by saying I have no finished this game yet.  I am on Chapter 3, about 6 hours in.  It is very unique, the only games I've played that were anything like it were Republic: the Revolution and to a lesser extent This Is The Police.  It really humanizes the tragedies that occurred in Western Europe during the later years of the first half of the 20th century.  However, there is one design decision that I think was a huge mistake.  Despite being 2 chapters in, I have seen only 1 swastika.  We see crowds of people waving red flags with white circles... with nothing in the circle.  For a game so unafraid to show the human cost of fascism, being unwilling to show a certain shape seems silly and significantly detracts from the horror.  I would still recommend the game to anyone who is interested in 20th century history and likes story-driven management sims.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Not the most exciting game and I think it could use more instructions on what exactly is happening as I didn't really figure it out until the final chappter.But the story is where this thing is so important and was super well done. A lot of history packed in here, gave me a different viewpoint then the typical war games out there. Made me feel things throughout the game, anger, sadness, shock and more.I highly recommend anyone who is interested in WW2 type stuff or is worried about what is going on today to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: At the time I'm writing this, I've played exactly 64 minutes, It was gonna be more, but the game crashed.Technically this game is simple AF in it's graphics and mechanics but it keeps lagging when doing simple drag and drop operations that only require a few extra mathematical operations in the back end.I don't know if they are gonna fix those issues, but at this time the game is not worth more than 5 bucks.I'm now considering applying for a refund or keep on playing and struggling with the stability issues.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10For an indie game, it contains the right amount of history and drama with an artful way to describe it.Game mechanics are interested. Feeling of the game between resistance RPG and 1933's Germany simulation.While the game making all of these, also telling the story with real history and newspaper examples and big events.I hope this game takes a good place in reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Meh, this is not a must-play by any means. I'm usually not one to say this, but there's way too much text and reading. It's tiring. And as soon as you're getting a hang of the management aspect (map-based management sort of reminds me of This is the Police), the chapter ends and resets everything. Not sure if my choices are having any effect? Left wondering what the point is.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Taking a trip to see the rise of Nazi Germany, its peak and eventual downfall is definitely on the unique side as far as experiences go and, if nothing else, Through the Darkest of Times excels at it. Shame it falters at other aspects you'd expect a strategy of this type to handle far better.Aforementioned problems quickly rear their ugly heads as it doesn't take long for you to realize this immersive period is built on rather simplistic turn-based strategy. After randomly rolling your character you have a leader of your resistance group. With time you expand it with more generated members, each with their traits and proficiency in matters of subterfuge, propaganda, etc, and map of Berlin offers hotspots to interact for missions. You assign members to task, possible modifiers like equipment come into play for risk/success rates, and off you go. Problem? Even though it may make some narrative sense in order to stay alive, game almost encourages you to play passively and forego high profile missions. Only things that actually matter are those that directly affect group's longevity prospects aka funds, supporters and lastly morale. Keep those decent and you can stroll through game's four chapters with ease.Apart from those mechanical bits that affect the math you also have evocative narrative CYOA pieces which are, sadly, mostly there for the fluff. Game is obviously geared very much against the Nazis and definitely does not hold back any punches in terms of what topics are broached. Morality boils more down to how OTHERS see the regime, how people are converted to it, etc. Historic events are the highlight of the game and serve as milestones. To feed into the above they're also arbitrary time skips so you have no idea just how long you'll spend in each chapter. This ended up backfiring more than once and I never got to set off that bomb during the Summer Olympics in 1936. Or smuggle out those prisoners when I had the chance...

_childDocuments_.review: Antifa Simulator 2020. No but really, it's a pretty engaging game with an excellent eye to historical accuracy with very pretty valuable lessons not only on the events surrounding Germany under Nazi rule, but also Fascism in general. Too many games attempt to focus on humanizing Fascists, but this one takes the route of showing humans turning to fascism. This is a very important distinction, and I'm happy that it is made here. It's also nice to see Nazi resistance in gaming that isn't just killing a ton of Nazis. While I'm all for punching Nazis and do find enjoyment in those kinds of games (we all know I'm talking about Wolfenstein), it's nice to see resistance being carried out through a united coalition of Antifascists. You're not communists, you're not anarchists, you're not American soldiers. You are Antifascists, first and foremost. As for the gameplay itself, it's a fun enough resource management loop. Maintain morale, money and supporters while carrying out operations and keeping your resistance fighters in fighting condition- while also responding to both random and scripted events. I don't see this having much replay value, but I honestly don't see it as a game that particularly needs it.

_childDocuments_.review: Through the Darkest of Times is an iPhone ported interactive novel/resource management/RNG game where you control a cell of German resistance during the rise and fall of Nazi Germany from 1933 to the bitter end. The subject matter is dark and heavy. It's a grim story, and an important one, but I don't believe this kind of video game format is the best way to tell it.  As far as games go, unfortunately, this is typical, low quality mobile ported shovelware.   The majority of the gameplay is just clicking through endless dialogue.  You're presented with choices, but they don't influence the outcomes, they seem to be just there to make players feel like they're interacting with the game for a change. You make decisions on the activities of your resistance cell members, but like many iPhone tappers such as Dead in Bermuda, it's all just punishing RNG, and ultimately unsatisfying gameplay. Finally, we have the problem of an iPhone game being on PC with questionable treatment of the PC platform by the developers.  This is a $4 iPhone game with a $15 price tag on PC.   Are PC gamers somehow second class citizens that the developers expect can be gouged just because they have a better gaming platform?  It's unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers. People who are interested in the important lessons that can be learned from this period of history should check out documentaries like The World at War distributed by Thames Television.   Video games are not the best format for this kind of content, especially not ones as bad as The Darkest of Times.

_childDocuments_.review: In a landscape of historical games which are, for the most part, first-person shooters or war strategy games, Through the Darkest of Times sets a high standard for what historical video games can and should be. This immersive game puts you in what feel like (and surely were in some ways!) the shoes of real people trying to push back against the destructive tide of fascism as it worked its way into their politics, their careers, their relationships, and so on. As the story progresses and different lives are destroyed you can't help but think it is all a little too real - because it is. Almost every action you do or try to do in the game was attempted and done by real people many times over, a powerful thought to keep in mind while playing.Some will find this game challenging. Common complaints are the simplistic and at times confusing gameplay, or the fact that the player's actions ultimately "don't matter". While these complaints are obviously valid from a gamer's perspective, I think they point to one of the real strengths of the game. As the name suggests, Through the Darkest of Times has an incredible ability to reflect the emotional toll of being part of the resistance in Nazi Germany: trying to progress through self-set challenges where there is no set goal, no reward, and no indication that what you are trying to do is the right thing or will even "matter". It's all up to you and the importance you place on what you are trying to do, just as in real life. (To be honest, does anything you do in a game "matter"??)This isn't to say that you can't be successful in what you try to do, because you can. Just remember that this is one of the more unpredictable games you might play. Will you successfully hide from police officers? Will your meeting with a known socialist attract the suspicion of the Gestapo? Are your contacts trustworthy? You can do things to affect the outcome, but ultimately you never know what will happen. As someone with a lifelong fascination with history, this must be one of my favourite historical video games I've ever played. My only regret is that I doubt I'll find another like this any time soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Although the mechanics can be a bit winky and repetetive, it is one of the games that stayed with me the most of all I have played. I thought a lot about the story and how it resembles the stories of so many people during that time. I also searched a lot for actual resistance groups and learned that there were many more than I knew of.I recommend it to anybody only slightly interested in (german) history, antifascism or resistance movements in general.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story rich historical strategic simulation of running a small resistance group in Nazi Germany. The games merits rest on how well it captures the feeling on those times rather than simply using history to provide a context for a strategy game.Thus the authors have, rightly, gone for realism giving you a taste of the situation and dilemmas facing a resistance group rather than a game focused on outcomes ie you will not be overthrowing the Nazi regime or other major changes to history. Things more or less play out as they did historically. That is this game is about the experience not your actual score. That said there are plenty of achievements to focus on and sufficient to encourage additional play-throughs to try and pull off that mission you failed to complete the first time round.The game is based on the principal of recruiting members, supporters, raising finances and acquiring resources to be able to carry out or unlock different operations. However some of these operations are time critical and are lost once a chapter has completed, thus you need to decide which missions have priority as you may not have the time and resources to complete them all.Each chapter is set in a different time period and thus faced with different conditions, with the resistance group having to more or less start from scratch  having suspended its activities in the interim. This changes the emphasis of the game from building up capacity over time to carrying operations with what limited resources you are able to  put together in a short period of time.The game is very much story driven and after each turn an event often happens which unfolds the story and can  open up more missions.  All in all you get a good feel of the kind of operations and dilemmas even a non-violent resistance group faces. The overall message is an ethical and existential one. Why resist? Why risk your life? One resists not because such resistance could stop a war, genocide or even be able  over throw the regime but because it is the right thing to do and it is true to who you are. The precious few who resist, despite the majority who allow themselves to be used by the system, is what gives us hope for a better tomorrow even if tomorrow never comes...In terms of game play the apparent reset after each chapter robs one of a sense of any progress achieved in the previous chapters. Though this is realitic with groups having to keep restart from scratch, the implementation of some kind of persistent cache for some hard to get items like uniforms, weapons or critical intel, etc would help to keep a sense of progress and lessen the frustration of trying reacquire those resources each chapter. Also maybe having your level of supporters and funds in previous chapter influence how much you get as a % above base in the next chapter. I do not think this would hurt the realism, as a resistance group could operate a small cache of monies and resources buried somewhere ready for the future and some previous supporters would come out of the woodwork when resuming operations.This game is a must play, not just for those interested in history, but also for those of use fighting similar dark forces in modern times and those who may not off spotted the signs yet. That is the game is very relevant to what is happening in many countries today. If you are wondering what I am talking about you really need to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Starting in Berlin 1933, this game follows a historical timeline. Game rounds are one week.In Through the Darkest of Times, you lead a group of resistance fighters, who in the background try to weaken the influence of Hitler and his minions.The setting and timeline is historically quite accurate - be it from the day that Hitler took the power to assassination attempts, the beginning of war, the setback in the war to the end of war - it is covered in weekly steps. There is always the chance of one of your team to be imprisoned, if you are not careful. You may also run out of funds and resources rather easily, so look at them frequently. You decide, which of the tasks you want to do yourself and which one you assign to which NPC.The mechanics in this game is simple - this is a game, where your people-/task-/resource management skills are put to a test. Recommended for someone, who does want to play something completely different from action games. Simulation at its purest.

_childDocuments_.review: Great premise for the game, I'm someone who greatly appreciates the trope of "undercover agents working together in secret against a greater Goliath power", and weaving in the richness of WWII history only made purchasing this game a no-brainer for me. The art style seen in the game is also really great, and I couldn't think of a better soundtrack. I give this game 8/10 for visuals and *written* storyline, and 10/10 for sound design.The issue for me comes with the gameplay:1. The time limit is too short. This has been something that people have complained about a lot so I'm not sure why the developers haven't done anything about it yet. But so far, I've played a first attempt with 3 chapters completed before failure (morale fell too low and my group disbanded) and a second attempt with 1 chapter completed. This is all on story mode, and so far I haven't been able to complete a single major objective. The devs should definitely either increase the time limit of story mode, or keep it the same and add a third difficulty caused "easy" or something where there's plenty of time to get things done. Because having a game that is too difficult really removed for me the sense of active involvement in the plot because I simply wasn't able to get things done to sway the course of Hitler's regime.2. An indirect way of tackling the problem would also be to enable liasing and coordination with other resistance groups in real-time. Maintaining relations with other AI-controlled groups and working in unison with them to achieve objectives would add another layer of bureaucracy and diplomacy to the game, while simultaneously letting the player get things done quicker. Despite this, I concede that implementation of such a feature may prove to be difficult and costly.Overall, the game is good, but takes a little too much time to learn and warm up to - not due to overt complexity of game mechanics; the mechanics are simple and straightforward enough, but simply due to the fact that the time limits are too short, thereby undercutting a large portion of the game's immersive experience. 6.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Set during the early years of Hitler’s rule in Germany, the player is put at the head of a small resistance movement who attempt to undermine Hitler by finding allies, disrupting fascist activity, spreading liberal propaganda, and engaging in guerilla warfare. The gameplay centres around team management: the player assigns certain tasks to certain members of the resistance, each of whom have different strengths, weaknesses, and attributes. Occasionally, you will find a resistance member who is perfect for a certain task, and can reliably do it on their own without too much trouble. However, running into these resistance members is largely a matter of luck, as is the probability of certain tasks being completed successfully or agents running into obstacles. This is all threaded through with a compelling narrative documenting Hitler’s decisions and actions after being appointed Chancellor.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat little strategy/simulation game where you play is a resistance movement during the rise of the nazi regime. You can't change history, but you can do your best for the people around you.Pros:-Very strong and tactful story telling of life within Germany during the time period. Does its best to humanize all of the regular citizens, so that you can understand how their viewpoints came about from a historical standpoint.-Large amount of freedom, you can take many different approaches to rebellion, and there are plenty of side missions that relate to actual occurrences.Cons:-Not always super obvious what to do. There's a lot of stuff that is hidden until you complete other missions. This is rough because your not always sure of what you need to do in order to get the materials required for the "big missions". Especially when you're on a time limit it can be very easy to miss objectives.-You can make decisions that affect the lives of the side characters, but the main story will pretty much always progress the same regardless of your decisions. While understandable as a historical/creative decision, it is sort of a bummer since it means there's no real in-game point in completing a bunch of the objectives.-Gameplay can become sort of min-max with hoping that you don't get screwed by rng.Overall this game is a very strong narrative accompanied by an okay game. The game itself is pretty generic so you're basically just playing it for the story and characters, which imo is well-written.Rating: 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming little game that takes about 4-5 hours, I think it gets its message effectively across while still being engaging. There isn't much ludonarrative dissonance. I like the characters and the illustration that sometimes you have to not help someone so that you can survive yourself. That being said the downsides is that there isn't really replayability since all the events are the same and honestly a bit tedious the second time around. The game does feel a little grindy since you basically raise money get supporters or get items each turn. Each turn is relagated to a time period of 19 weeks/ turns which makes big (optional) missions really hard since you have to have already planned to do them and know how to get the items required for those missions. It's very unlikely you'll get them on your first playthrough unless you had a walkthrough, and as I mentioned doing another playthrough is less fun. Ludonarrative-wise it does fit since its pretty rare and takes a lot of luck to pull off big heists like spreading the truth, or blowing up an important resource. Good luck getting that 1000 marks achievement too since that is a grindfest.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, though it's not a game in a classical aspect. If you try to identify with your group, it really crawls underneath your skin. It really catches the atmosphere (as far as I can tell) and makes you shudder - because you know, that the developers didn't exaggarate with their depictions. The game shows how hard it must have been to be (and stay) in the resistance. The game can be frustrating - your group members can randomly die to british bombardmend fire (R.I.P Horst... one week more and you'd have survived the war), leave the group (Franziska was pregnant and afraid for her child, who could have blamed her?) or be taken prisoner/executed by the Nazis because of a botched mission.But since the game is rather short (6-7 hours for one gameplay), you're okay with it. It's not so much of a challenge for you as a gamer and more of an interactive drama. The nice thing about that is that while it's a lot to read, it keeps you engaged. There are seldomly walls of text - you decide how you react before a new text snippet appears, so it's quite easy to stay focused.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: As a strategy gamer myself, I won't recomend it for the strategic factor. Is not really a great strategy game. But it's a great Visual Novel. The history is one of the best, the mechanics are somewhat adapted to the era and make you feel in the game, and the emotional shock is... just heavy. Recomended for every good day, because the bad ones will feel just hopeless.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: It takes a serious dose of courage to make a game centered around Adolf Hitler which isn't some kind of shooter where your main objective is to shoot that Hitler in the face.Through the Darkest of Times is  in order to show the world that video games can be something much, much more than simple entertainment for kids. With games such as TtDoT, one day we will show them that video games are just as valuable and meaningful part of our culture as books or movies. Once and for all.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: An immersive artistic story that puts you in the role of a resistance group during the darkest times of humanity. Game mechanics are simple, although it takes some time understand them. The story evolves through random and scripted story events which paint a very good picture of those terrible times but most importantly make you understand how easy it is for people to support, succumb or disregard the obvious evil in our everyday lives. This story helps us - the younger generations - perceive and understand this.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: A very thoughtful and moving game about resisting the rise of fascism. Knowing what eventually transpired in Germany makes some of the riskier decisions easier to make (eg we HAVE to save that man who is being questioned by the SS, no question) but without foreknowledge of how atrociously evil Hitler would prove to be, would I have sacrificed as much? Current events may answer that question for me. Very well done and anything but boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Through the Darkest of times puts you in the shoes of small group of Germans from all walks of life with one common goal, to destroy the Nazi dictatorship. There is 4 chapters, from the rise of the Nazis to the end of the war. Through interactions with  characters you see the hardships which Germans faced. You see the lies and manipulation by the Nazis at work as most of the people you interact with in the early game are full of hope and admiration for the regime, compared to the later chapters where the effects of war destroy it all. The gameplay is not the focus of this game, instead it is the history which you experience and learn as the game goes on.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it! It's not reinventing the wheel, but it's pretty enjoyable. And, once you played it through, you can start again and do everything differently, leading to a completely different outcome. The only thing I did not really like, is that every action took a week, which made it hard to really achieve anything major. But apart from that? Go for it! (You should be interested in WWII or history, because otherwise you might not enjoy it at all.)
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: Building up a resistance group against Nazi Germany, with lots of dialog text, interesting events, and background information? Sounded great, so I tried this.Main problem for me was a crash bug which left my save game corrupted, and I couldn't finish the last few rounds of chapter 2.Gameplay-wise, I often could not reach the higher up missions, because they had absurd requirements. Which means stuff that is hard to get (like an SA uniform), but you need three of those.So I had to go for simpler missions, which kept morale and supporter count high. This was enough to finish chapter 1. Unfortunately I couldn' finish chapter 2, but it had the same problems. Very simple on one hand (morale + support), but high profile missions are not feasible.I would still recommend the game because of uniqueness. The stories and events give you an insight into the plight of free-thinking people during the nazi dictatorship. If you are focussed more on playing a good strategy game, don't buy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed this game very much. There's a good choice of customising your character as leader of the group. You also get to add other characters to the group, with useful or limiting traits. Inventory items collected during the game are historically accurate and there use during missions can make a big difference to success or failure. Missions completed can unlock characters who are also useful to boost your team's resources. The fact that the game starts in the mid-1930's helps to give a sense of depth to the overall campaign. The map gives hints via red shading on which missions are more dangerous, this is particularly realistic near the end of the war when patrols were fewer because of reduced manpower in Berlin - a nice touch! I would like to see another version of this game released, but based on the Resistance in France.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: The game's abstracted art style is a breath of fresh air. When I first heard about this game couple months back I though that the art style would demolish my immersion, I was wrong gladly, I was fully immersed and thrilled to play as different characters with different ideologies and skills. Even thought the game is a point and click strategy game, it still manages to be fun and exciting. I would defiantly recommend this to anyone who has any interest in the history during the regime.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: You play a resistance group in Germany in the time between when Hitler was appointed chancellor in 1933 to the end of world war II. With a limited amount of time, you must scramble to get the resources to carry out one of the 3 main missions in each chapter (4 in all) i.e. smuggling refugees over the border or spreading anti nazi propaganda.If we look solely on the game mechanics, it's very much a game about managing your time, resources and members of your resistance group. Over time, you will fight against a constant depletion of supporters and moral. To counterbalance this, you must carry out missions, but as you do so, your members run the risk of gathering "heat". Get to much heat, and the member risks getting arrested and/or killed. Do too little, and you risk your members losing morale and ultimately leaving the group.The game is sometimes interrupted by cutscenes, which offers a bit of backstory about the events during the nazis seizure of power and world war II. It's either a nice bit of insight or an annoyance depending on how many times you have seen the same cutscene before.The good:It's a nice game, which challenges you and keeps you on your toes. Every chapter is a puzzle, where you must choose which missions to prioritize and which to ignore, and when you finally get it right and you are able to strike a blow against the regime, it's not something you just cruised through.The bad:The game offers very little explanation of it's mechanics, and there is a lot of stuff you will have to find out through trial and  error. It can be frustrating and it can leave you with a feeling that you have spent a lot of time and energy, and it was all for naught. Be ready to start over a few times before you get the hang of it.There is either no saves at all, or the games saves after each turn, overwriting the last save. This is both good and bad. On one side, you can't just reload the game and try again. On the other side, you can't just reload the game and try again. If you fail in carrying out your main mission, the game just skips to the next chapter. If you are anything like me, you will find this hugely frustrating. Why cant I at least restart the chapter?Final verdict:In spite of it being a sometimes frustrating game, I recommend that you give it a try. It offers a little insight in the events that led to the nazis seizing power, and how they slowly but surely escalated the oppression of their political opponents and ultimately started a war. Also, as I explained above, it's a challenging game.
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very interesting. Requires much planning while playing and remembering what your party members are good at and where they will benefit you.Two things that are slightly nitpicky though that annoy me a little bit: -You can't see all traits a person has when recruiting them which can just put you in annoying situations where all your party members just are effectively useless for certain objectives.-Can't name my own character. (which really means noting, but it made me slightly sad :( )
_childDocuments_.name: Through the Darkest of Times

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly amazing. The game-play is fun and interesting, yet challenging. The art style is extremely unique and fits the dark atmosphere of the game and the heavy subject it is covering. It is also extremely informative and provides a really interesting perspective on WW2 and the tragic events that took place. This game made me emotional if I'm being honest and deserves more recognition. I recommend this game to anyone who likes strategy based games with interesting art styles, heavy story* and/or wants to experience a unique view of WW2. Overall, this game is extremely well made and truly was both very enjoyable yet made me emotional because of the subject matter. *I feel bad saying story since WW2 was a tragic event that killed millions, but for the purpose of this review it works to an extent

_childDocuments_.review: A Small Indie Game showing that political Games can be a great thing. Its frightening to walk in the shoes of someone who doesnt want to march in line in a fascist government, and to see how the rhetoric of these people get a revival in several countries today. We need Games to become more self aware of their role as an Art. At least one cannot "burn" digital copies of a game if it comes to that.

It does a very good job of creating a sinister atmosphere, and I often found myself thinking "what would I really do in this situation?"Id love to see more, perhaps a Soviet edition.Great job guys i give it a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of the game sends shivers down my spine, but at the same time it captivates and encourages me to continue playing. In a way, Through the darkest of Times is also a horror game. But there is a desire to save a few more people, to put up a little more resistance, without falling under the wheels of the regime’s terrible mills.Through the darkest of Times conveys in a stirring way what it must have been like to have been an average citizen back then. What courage it takes to go into resistance when the mass movement is moving at full speed into barbarism. It shows how many Germans took part out of conviction.(German Voiceover, many subtitles)The game accuses and conveys a deep feeling for the hopelessness of the victims. It shows how many people became followers because it was so nice and comfortable, but also why many pretended to be followers out of fear. It shows how horrible life was for the persecuted, and how cruel the actions of many who were not persecuted. Through the darkest of Times is an enormously emotional game.As for the scope, the game has 4 chapters that represent different parts of the story. There is a narrative mode, which includes some simpler gameplay and a mode called “Resistance”, which at least offers some more realistic conditions concerning the probability of failure and the danger of being pursued.All in all, I even think that the game is still very forgiving to the player in both modes. Considering how many members of the resistance died in the Third Reich, the game should be almost unmanageably difficult, but then any motivation to play the game would be lost. This balancing act has probably been discussed at length by the developers. And here a middle way was found, which lies between a perceived hopelessness and a not completely demotivating level of difficulty.Through the darkest of Times is a special game in many ways. It’s not technically extremely elaborate, but you have to consider that Paintbucket Games is a small indie team. With 14,99 € the price is also more in the lower range.Within the framework of the stylistic devices used, the game is artistically high-quality and technically flawless. It is a courageous project and provides completely new insights into the history and stories of the darkest times of our country.It has touched me emotionally, it has given me new insights. And despite the hopeless starting position and the deeply gloomy mood of the game, as a strategy game it was also fun, challenging and entertaining. It deals with the topic respectfully, offers new perspectives and stimulates many thoughts. And with the special graphics and harmonious music, it is close to being a work of art.I’d be happy to have more different game content, but what is offered is absolutely fine for the price. The price-performance ratio is very good here in this area. That’s why I would like to give Through the darkest of Times a 90% rating. If you want to save some money you can still get a discount on the game when you buy at my partner site Gamesplanet.You can also find a lot more Reviews here:on my profile -> on my curator page ->  | or on my blog ->

_childDocuments_.review: A well designed strategy game, beautiful graphic and wonderful narrative. You can be the kind of violent rebel or stick to non-violence approaches. There are risk and opportunity in every step you take. Depressing and memorable; the theme alone is meaningful in our history. This game reminded me the darkness of the humanity that is not so far away.

Few would stand and fight the monstrosity that was the German Reich. Will you? Lead an underground resistance group Through the Darkest of Times.

name: WRC 8 FIA World Rally Championship
detailed_description: The WRC championship is the most challenging motor racing competition in the world. With the new dynamic weather system, climatic conditions have true-to-life effects: rain and snowfall is now an important game feature as variable traction, different set-ups for each stage, tyre choice and shrewd use of the weather forecasting team all need to be considered. The single-player Career mode has been rebuilt from the ground up: calendar management, R&D to improve performance, staff recruitment and management (mechanics, engineers, medical and weather teams, finance manager, etc.). For multiplayer, weekly challenges and WRC eSports return, but the challenge and competition is now even stiffer. With 50 teams, 14 rallies and over 100 special stages in the 2019 season, WRC 8 has the deepest content ever included in an off-road racing game.
