_childDocuments_.review: kickstarter backed. promising game i waited years for only to be tricked into an experience that was all style with little substance. a very short experience as advertised from the beginning. quickly falls apart midway through with no sense of direction using a meta twist in an attempt to excuse the incoherent disjointed plot. the battle system is very repetitive and your attacks don't really do much damage. also minus points for the self-pity self insert boss fight.I collected all the achievements and I have to change my review. Buckle up, because it's kind of a lot:This game saved my life.I am 26.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realise that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: This review might say "Recommended", but it's a very slight one.  This game, while it has some strong points, also has some serious issues you should know about up front.Biggest problem I have with the game is the combat.  Enemies generally go first, can often open fights with free attacks, and can sometimes take multiple actions per turn.   The minigames take a long time to resolve and If you don't do absolutely perfectly, you usually eat a big chunk of damage (which you can turn down in the "♥♥♥♥ It, You Balance The Game, I Can't Be Arsed" settings list).  Some screens have 4+ encounters on them.  That's a lot of the same 3 circus hoops in any given area to jump through.Your own attacks do seemingly random amounts of damage (worsened by how each regular attack randomly chooses between 3 very different minigames for each character), and that basically undoes everything else:  stats don't feel meaningful, so leveling doesn't feel like anything, getting gear doesn't feel like anything, statuses don't mean anything, most items are useless, and most abilities are pointless.  Which means exploration serves little purpose except achievement hunting and seeing if the game's bits are funny.The game even introduces a Summon/Limit Break """system""" that I thought was gonna work like the Djinn from Golden Sun but it literally just summons a random thing you have no control over.  Don't fret, though, they all do the same thing: damage, a bit more than usual.  So don't worry about collecting all of them, I guess, because once you've gotten one, you've gotten them all.Bosses are worse:  pretty much all of them are gimmick fights with a bunch of scripted events and chatter, so nothing matters.  [Protagonist] and [Interchangeable Party Member] just need to minigame perfectly for seemingly eternity until [Cool Thing Happens] and the plot advances.For a game that seems to have a chip on its shoulder about Undertale, to the point of interrupting the proceedings to huff its own farts about how it isn't like Undertale, it sure does like to do the things Undertale does, but worse.So, accepting that the RPG stuff is basically wet cardboard, what's left?  Well, the plot definitely goes places.  And then it leaves those places behind and doesn't return until the very final scenes of the game.  Knuckle Sandwich starts off with an *incredibly strong* set of hooks, and then kinda squanders it all on a boring, saggy midgame that goes on a few two chapters too long before it looks you in the eye, admits it was being pointless, and starts to pay anything off.  Then about an hour later, it's over.Now, why do I (mildly) recommend this game, in spite of all that?  Because the stuff it's good at, it's *really* good at.  The artsy weirdness, asset design, script, and so on are still worth experiencing.  Just go to the "You Be The Dev, Then, IDK How ♥♥♥♥ Works" options and minimize your contact with the combat system until it gets a balance pass.Also, side note, here's an amusing bug I found:  If you switch attacks from Manual to Automatic, so they (supposedly) behave like a more normal RPG, each time you swing, the game's sound will get progressively more corrupted.  I thought this was part of a boss fight until it persisted.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I'd finish a game before reviewing it, but after playing through quite a bit of this one I unfortunately felt like I had enough of it already. I wish I could give "mixed" reviews for games on Steam because the game was made by only one guy (that in itself is very admirable and deserves respect), and I like a lot of things it offers, music, art style, WarioWare minigames, sadly there are more things I don't like in Knuckle Sandwich than things I liked, so I'm gonna have to give it a negative review, the game just doesn't respect your time and attention, I can't even remember the number of the chapter I'm on, I think I was going to board a cruise?I feel like the first thing I have to criticize is the price, there are many other games that I prefer to this one (Stray, Ultrakill, World of Horror) that cost 20 USD and are less expensive when buying with my country's currency. It's on me for buying it compulsively without thinking about it, but that contributed for my bad time since I was so excited to finally play it, I loved the demo so much, only to get a lot of style with no substance; The demo made the game looka lot  like a "delicious sandwich" that was going to develop into an interesting story, but when I sank my teeth in it it tasted like nothing, it doesn't give me a reason to keep playing or to keep me hooked on the story, the characters look nice and cute but the game never makes an effort to make me give a ♥♥♥♥ about any of them. I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about the busdriver and his ugly goblins, I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about my party members, hell, I don't even give a ♥♥♥♥ about myself, there are no stakes, no party bonding moments, no reason to keep going, the game just keeps piling on names and characters without any meaningful change to the story or world building.TLDR; the game becomes a chore quickly; managing your inventory is very limiting; despite it having a cool WarioWare style battle system it becomes boring rapidly; and it all comes together to be very frustrating because I wanted it to be more, much more. Please don't stop making games developer, but please please please don't compromise your vision to appeal to discord or twitter users, because that's what the game feels like, just another wannabe Earthbound or Mother 3 made to satisfy contemporary sensibilities, without soul or anything creative.

_childDocuments_.review: I must agree with most of the lengthy negative reviews that currently exist.The game lacks in many fronts:-Smoothness/variability of the mini games. It is nice that at first they are on the lowest difficulty and then change a bit, but it's not enough to matter.-Story is not focused enough and reminds me more of dreamscape Omori, yet somehow feels even more disjointed. There doesn't seem to be a lot of impact that your character makes, even though the end of the story implies otherwise.-Some puzzles are just... annoying. Like in the ice sliding puzzle you CAN'T see the end of the arena/next point, so you have to guess where to go and it just becomes a time waster. Same with the switches and other puzzles. It's not even done in a "hoho, quirky bad puzzle on purpose" way and made for a potential laugh, it's just... bad for no reason. -Health/EP items don't matter on non Hard difficulty(which you can get WAY too early into the game and screw yourself, if you don't know how to turn it off. PLUS, why would you need to go to the main menu to turn it off and not just in game settings?). You can just abuse the full restore points forever and it just makes most of the items(status removals too) to not matter at all. -The fact that you have only 3 slots at best, but in reality 2 slots is annoying. How come a pin/clothes are in the same slot as holding a booster ticket? The fact that there are just 16 slots when you are alone and you have to slog your way to a PC to deposit something is... not the best.-Secrets are annoying to find. Like, how come 23% of the people have beaten the game, but most of the secrets are lower than 10% of the people? That just seems like a bad way of telegraphing what player needs to do. Overall, despite trying to give it a fair chance many-many-many times, it feels like this game tried to focus on too many things at once and be "lol, random" for the sake of it, without a clear vision. Which is sad. In some aspects it does improve on the Omori/Undertale, but in many others it just makes a worse impression.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I don't like to do this, but I'll be honest with you: Knuckle Sandwich is a  disappointment. First of all.. The game didn't manage to make the plot palatable to me. There was just nothing... exciting! I start the game as an ugly someone with a triangle nose & without a name. (The name I choose was immediatly rejected). Anyway, we're trying to find a job. Well, the job center gives me several job offers and get to know some mini games, which are fun and I do VERY well...  but I still don't get the job. Because the plot said to.The protagonist picks up a flyer and ends up with an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss who lets him grill burgers. So far so good, then things escalate very quickly but I ask myself WHY the protagonist doesn't simply quit. The world soon falls into pieces and somebody who randomly appears explains to me things that seem to me like they were thought up by someone who smokes a lot of weed. In short: In order so save the world I have to find some lost things (like keys) in dungeons that are filled with monsters. So much for the story, at least to the point where I didn't have any nerves for it anymore.Gameplaywise..  somehow the name "Untertale" and "Knuckle Sandwhich" sounded convenient to me, but they really don't have that much in common.The turn-based battles are filled with minigames (which quickly become repetitive and monotonous) and the characters' abilities are varied, but somehow boring, at least to me. They randomly throw wario ware like games at you. Besides that.. the dungeons are pretty ugly and really tiring in the long run, although the puzzles were quite okay (like finding switches that let you explore it further.. imagine zelda dungeons just with lots of random encounters!).I would like to positively emphasize the really good music of the game, which always fits well with the respective sections.The graphics of the landscapes outside the dungeons are also really nice. I found it strange that the female characters were somehow all cute or pretty, but the guys looked like they had lost their noses somewhere.Overall, a game that bored me very quickly. I expected more, especially a more interesting story that somehow fascinated and kept me guessing. Instead, it just seemed like that the good ideas where missing some more developement and refinement.

_childDocuments_.review: I watched this game for 5 years and lurked in their discord. There are obviously some things I don't agree on from there, but I'll cut to the chase and just single out what I liked and didn't like. Oh also should mention  Almost 100% that's a minor. If that doesn't tell you who it's for,  This is the games discord moderator. It doesn't leave much room to guess why when, most the staff are like this that the game came out so jank. Also  It just feels like the game was fueled by discord mental illness, and supplemented by cope.>Minigames were entertaining>Main Cast (Echo, Dolus, Thea)>Somewhat unique enemy design>Some funny moments>Neat combat aesthetic>The Gym fight>Strong demo/start story >>Lot of unexpected animation for the game>Limited inventory, especially when key items are needed, you must throw away things in your inventory. Dumb!>The beginning and end of the story was thought out, everything in the middle didn't feel the same...>Total lack of shops, I maybe visited them 3-5 times throughout the story.>> >>Some attacks are worse than others Crit Bars<Vertical<Circle, Circle is the best.>Poorly paced debuff notice very early in game (Because debuffs kick in later stages...)>Acknowledging bad mechanics doesn't make them fun>The story is thrown at you, you are getting a feel when suddenly Goblin Design Tower???>Unoriginality, -10 points!>Lack of a pause menu to reload a save in combat>Bad minigames ()>Enemies spamming repetitive unavoidable debuffs>>You kill someone, then get this- You never do it again and it barely matters.>The Cry & Shame Battle didn't need to exist when there's only 1 valid option. Dumb!>Multiple soundtracks contain various amounts of strange burping etc. I just don't jive with that.>>Strange 3D cutscenes with no expression, why have that at all? It's barely different from talking in 2D...>I spectated this game for 5 years, a lot of time passed and I feel like a lot of content was just recycled to hastily create a story. There are obvious things I hate about the game, What I dislike the most, is that what is an obvious at the start suddenly becomes this HUGE reveal at the end,  I feel like, and this bothers me the most.  this explains why you only make people unconscious (particularly bosses), while you constantly attack unexplained monsters that just say they love fighting.  I feel this game had a lot going for it, and definitely could have been refined into a much better craft, Overall, is it worth $20? Sure. Is it worth $10? Definitely. Is it worth more than either? No. Not at all.I'd write more here about how it shares blatant similarities to other games say , or obvious tropes "Hey lets have everyone gather on Bad Guy island what could go wrong!", but to gist,  So much more could have been done with the game I feel and the premise definitely was a good hook, but it quickly just fell off, and rams a bunch of information down your throat at the end. It feels sloppy, like it was just rushed out because he had been sitting on it for so long.Oh another thing that bugs me. The twist was extremely predictable. It was constantly explained away by a singular party member apparently being into amateur detective work, but who would have guessed they're bad at it?I want to note that cope, cringe, whatever- I don't usually use these words. But genuinely a lot of the game is just that. "Oh it's good enough.", I expected a lot more out of the game, and I think at one point direction was a lot different than what we got. But what we got leaves me wanting anything else. The game has it's ups and downs, but every time the characters do an animation to represent how you the player feels, doesn't make that sequence suck any less. It just helps affirm "Oh they really, didn't know what they were doing."The fight between 2  against you and Dolus was probably my favorite part of the game. It did have some things I didn't like (how you can't do any variety beyond spamming a fight and specials) but I loved it. I loved the commentators commenting, I loved that it wasn't about damage but spectator appeal, I loved it so much. It really struck a chord with me with how great it was. _childDocuments_.review: I am being 100% honest when I make this review, and truly I don't care if there are people who disagree.I found this little indie game almost 2 or so years ago, and it was at a stage where it didn't seem like it was going anywhere with developement, and truthfully, I cant really give any kind of criticism because I dont make any games, however I can say my opinion of the game, and how long it took.Was it worth it? not really, no.Was it worth the wait to be more specific? its hard to say, but no.Was it worth spending 11 hours of your life on? It was alright, i'll give minor props to andy brophy on that one.Would you recommend this to others? well, compared to many other indie games on the market, truthfully, this game is less replayable and more experimental if anything. This is a game in which it is better to watch your favorite streamer play, than it is to buy the game itself.What would you rate it 1-10? I am giving it a solid 6 overall, the art style is really nice, the gameplay is cool, but the story is not really something I personally enjoy, mainly because it lacks any direction. Don't get me wrong, most games that lack direction (like pizza tower for example I guess) can be done really well, however Knuckle Sandwich struggles to make any form of consistency, or better yet, any expectations met. This game's story is very much like the Bee Movie in the sense where, it does what it wants, and it throws you curve balls constantly.But yeah, this is my review, I wanna just say to Andy, I am not a game-dev, and more importantly I am not familiar with coding, but I can say this for sure, This game could've been done like 3 years ago. My opinion here doesn't matter because once again, I am no game dev. however I can say from an outsiders perspective, this game took way to long to make, and was not worth the wait in my honest opinion.That said, I respect anyone that had a fun time, however, I did not.

_childDocuments_.review: Knuckle Sandwich falls flat on its face. From its dull storytelling to its frustrating gameplay, there's little to redeem this sorry excuse of an RPG.The story is a joke, characters are hollow, and humor falls flat. Combat becomes a tedious painful chore. The pacing is the worst I've ever experienced in a game, dragging on endlessly without any sense of progression.Despite all this, I'm not angry or wanting my time back. In fact, I'm grateful that Knuckle Sandwich exists and that I played it. It sets a new low bar for RPGs that I can use as a future comparison.It's as if every decision was made with the intention of frustrating the players. Knuckle Sandwich is either the greatest RPG parody ever created or just impressively horrible.I'm never harsh in my reviews, but this is the first time I've played a game with so much potential end up being this abysmal.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game. It's not often that you play something with Australian flora/fauna around. I loved WarioWare and was keen to try a game that incorporated microgames creatively within its story.Unfortunately, all of the intrigue and fun leaves the game after you finish Chapter One. The game devolves into an uninspired Pokemon overworld, with ~lol im so random~ humour crammed in from every direction. The microgames end up occurring for every attack -- each member of your party and each of the enemies you face -- making you go through endless repetitions of the same microgames just to defeat random enemies on the map.Levelling your characters feels basically useless as it still takes the same amount of turns to defeat each enemy, not counting bosses, who become steadily harder to hit, and who hit massively harder than regular enemies. You can only hold 8 items including key items, and managing inventory is a constant pain in the ass.The plot feels half baked and wildly inconsistent, as if it was written by a 13 year old. The background music is great the first few times it loops through in each area, before becoming abundantly clear that it's all way too short and doesn't actually loop properly. The game doesn't respect your saves, in the Undertale style of doing things, which means if you accidentally click through a line of dialogue and you want to read it again, you can't. Because you reloaded, and the dialogue changed to something that assumes you read the original dialogue.The game just seems like it was made as a "screw you" to its players, which sucks. If making this game was such a burden to you, you should have just not made it. Don't buy it, don't play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Infusing WarioWare-style microgames into an irreverent turn-based RPG may seem like a stroke of genius, but unfortunately, the concept ends up being a chore the deeper players work through the experience. Couple that with a meandering story, strange player progression, and aggressive difficulty spikes Knuckle Sandwich comes across as a flawed labor of love. The eclectic soundtrack will at least keep your head bobbing in its more trying moments.Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: An excessively tedious game that is rarely funny but tries very, very hard to be. Its idea of a funny joke is having something wacky happen and then have a character react with something insipid. Like, very early on, a character reacts to their own zany antics by just saying "WHAT." And that's the punchline. "WHAT." It's one step away from "well THAT just happened!" It's like someone thought that the appeal of Earthbound and WarioWare was in surface level zaniness after having only watched someone else play each, then made a game using only that to go by. The only good jokes in this game are a few puns, and there are no good gameplay moments, only a few tolerable ones. This is the antichrist of post-Undertale indie RPGs.Edit after playing just a little bit more: the game gets somewhat less tedious LITERALLY 10 MINUTES OF GAMEPLAY after when I reviewed. But I was already 10 hours in at at well over 60% completion. So I still do not recommend this game, since it's fundamentally never going to fix its tedium, because to do so would require completely redoing large portions of the game, everything from combat to overworld traversal to dialogue and more, so you don't just end up tediously plodding around through uninteresting maps even when "running" while constantly playing the same boring minigames over and over against enemies that have little to no personality. And as for the "humor," I don't think this creator is going to be able to change their sense of "humor." It's very much "someone who never got over their 'lol randum xD' phase but is trying to cover it up with heaps of ironic detachment and using depression as a 'theme' of their work" vibes. This game would have been a total smash hit if it released 15 years ago, I reckon...

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR in advance: read WigsIncorporated's review for a more in-depth and intelligent review of this game that says everything I think. They did a great job.This is my first game review on Steam, THAT'S how disappointed I am with this game. I watched a streamer play the demo years ago, forgot about it, and came back when someone reminded me of it. Have you ever seen a trailer that makes the movie seem great, pay to see the real movie, only to realize you're watching schlock and realize the trailer edit was the only good part? Yeah, that's the demo. I can't stress enough how disappointed I would be if I was a backer for this game. Heck, I'm disappointed I spent $20 on it when I expected something like No Delivery, which costs 1/4th the price but is actually memorable and interesting.Of course I don't know what happens in game development or working on a project for 7 or so years, but you really can't just bring in and drop, bring in and drop, bring in and drop story concepts over and over and expect me or people who care about plots in an RPG to care. Characters? Cute designs but felt very like "a man designed these" because the male characters looked different and all of the women were ~manic pixie dream girls~ with different hair colors. Not to get too much into the story, or should I say loosely tied together vignettes that go nowhere, but Surely the gameplay had to be good? Half of the """100+ minigames""" are Galaga or variants of each other. The controls of them + length of battles in general would make my left hand cramp and ache after playing the game for too long. Don't want to compare, but felt like a more colorful, less fun Undertale/Deltarune. This review isn't done and I've already compared it to two games I would've rather been playing; that pretty much summarizes the experience of playing this game—being reminded of things you like more and inevitably being disappointed at what could've been.Good parts: The music was great, no complaints. The colors were nice. I liked running around the towns when the plot sparingly allowed me to rest.Besides those aspects, very meh game. I wouldn't be writing if it was just "meh" though—the visceral feeling of disappointment and my time being wasted stuck with me for a few days after beating the game.Don't let the blind followers in the Discord convince you with their memey, 1-sentence positive reviews of this game. It might have a cult-classic-esc following, but I will never have the hype for it again that I did when there was only a demo and the game didn't exist.For best experience, listen to the soundtrack while looking at screenshots, then play Mother 3 and Wario Ware instead.Edit: I'm watching a play-through of YIIK and it's a ripoff of that game too!

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral review I could give this game, as someone who waited for a few years for this game to come out it just seems I can't get interested or invested into whats going on. I still think this game has so much love and care poured into it, the WarioWare-type minigames being in the game at all is technically impressive and super creative for a RPG game and lets it stick out for all the right reasons. The art, music, and overall look and feel of the game is fantastic, but it falls completely flat on its on face when it comes to actually being a game. To me it just seems like a less interesting Earthbound, it's still a fine game that I think is worth the money for all the time and effort the (mostly single) dev put into the game, but I would stay away if you're looking for something super intriguing with great game play. I'm not disappointed or anything, I just know the game can get better and probably will with updates and stuff, which I will be looking forward to and hope to be able to revisit this game one day. :D

_childDocuments_.review: The game's a fine time I'd say. I'll preface this review with a warning: this game's combat isn't very deep. It has close to as much depth as your average barebones rpg. Yet despite this, I didn't get bored of it. I owe this to two things. One, the microgames. The reason I say "close to as much depth" is because the game's real "gimmick" is the microgames. If it weren't for them, I'd probably say the game is boring and not worth your time and money. However, they inject  enough into the gameplay that it manages to be somewhat interesting. The second reason I didn't get bored of it is the game's length. It's pretty medium length, around 10 hours. This works to the game's benefit, as since it's not that long I didn't really have the space to get bored with each part and enemy of the game. Because of these reasons, the gameplay is pretty bearable all things considered! So, you're able to enjoy the amazing presentation, the unique visuals, and the very nice sounding OST. Not a hard recommend, but a recommend nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: I deeply enjoyed my time with this game, and despite its flaws, I would absolutely recommend to people who like RPG's, minigame collections, or just indie games in general. As long as you go in with the knowledge that this game doesn't take itself super seriously all the time, I think you will enjoy your time with it. This game's battle system is one of the most creative ones I have seen or played, the humor and character writing is utterly fantastic, and the game's entire music library is beautifully eclectic, with excellent scores from each of the composers. "Go! Go! Power Muscle!" is one of my newest favorite pieces of video game music ever. My only major complaints are with the game's inventory system and the game's ending. The inventory is mostly fine, my major issues lie in how nearly every item required for progression requires a spot must be open in one of your party member's inventory; I feel it would've been better if progression items had their own inventory section. Thankfully, some items are discarded immediately after being used, somewhat alleviating this problem, however, there were many moments in which I had to discard an item just to make room for another item that would get used up moments later. On to the ending (no spoilers, don't worry), I found the game's finale to be somewhat disappointing. Not necessarily bad, but not great either, which makes it disappointing considering I really liked this game's story and characters. It's not devastating though, as I still hold a very positive view of this game, regardless of its ending.All in all, I had a wonderful time with Knuckle Sandwich, and I would absolutely play it again. I look forward to what the developers have cooking next, and I would be happy if their next project was even half as good as this game was.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A great wacky game that is highly worth playing. It has some flaws, but they are mainly a me issue and could easily be non-issues to someone else. Ok details timeStarting with some issues I encountered:- Your inventory is very limited and you get a lot of items making inventory management a total pain- The special attacks are a lot of fun to do, but they feel very weak compared to the regular attack. It also    doesn't help that they take up one of 3 equip slots that can be used for something else. (maybe having a    slot dedicated to the CD Roms used for specials could fix this)- I kept on running into some (POSSIBLE) memory leak issues. The game would sometimes freeze up really    bad forcing me to shut down the game with Task Manager. I couldn't find anyone else with this issue so it    could just be a me issue. - I had a hard time following the story. But again that is most likely a me issue.OK now on to the good stuff:- The art style is incredible! All the art in the game blew my mind, there are so many unique styles the game    uses and all of them are amazing!- The sound track fits the game so perfectly, each song fits in with what is happening in game so well!- I adore the characters and comedy in the game. So many parts of the game made me laugh. All of the   characters are interesting and well thought out. I loved talking to every NPC's to see what wacky things   they had to say. - The combat is highly engaging and very fun. I went out of my way to fight every enemy just to play the   mini-games they had to offer. And being able to do a counter attack by perfecting the combat mini-games   is incredibly rewarding! - The game had perfect balance. I never felt like the game was to hard or to easy. I still felt like I could easily   lose encounters if I wasn't paying attention (even at max level).Overall, this game is a masterpiece. It may not be perfect, but I still had an incredible time with my play through. I would highly recommend playing this game if you are a fan of RPG's or indie games. Besides the random freezing I experienced on my play though, the issues aren't enough to bring this game down. I loved every moment of this wacky game, and I can't wait to go back to collect the last few achievements I have missing.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Innovative and fun gameplay that left me always wanting more. Amazing scene writing, with a good-if-not-too-remarkable story. Instant buy for quirky RPG fans, or anyone who likes Mario & Luigi or WarioWare gameplay.Love this game to bits. The gameplay is genuinely innovative and incredibly fun. I've seen people say that the game is repetitive or doesn't value their time, and I honestly think that's an insane take. I mean people are entitled to their opinions, but there's not one moment in the game where I felt like my time was being wasted, and I found myself actively getting into random battles that I could have skipped just because the combat was fun and engaging. How many RPGs can you say that about? Outside of combat, the overworld exploration and puzzles are well done. The dungeons aren't the most innovative, but they've got enough meat to be miles ahead of most RPG puzzles without being too onerous.The story has a strong hook, and I don't really have any complaints about it. It's not the greatest story I've ever seen in an RPG, but it's far from the worst. I would put it on a level similar to Earthbound, not really hitting the same highs as Mother 3 or Undertale, but it's a good vehicle for the game's beat-by-beat writing, which is stellar. Good comedy writing is hard, and games trying to be quirky often fall into a writing style that ends up being a little on the nose. This is not that. The game is just consistently hilarious, unexpected, and weird. One of the funniest RPGs I've ever played, maybe the funniest honestly.Basically, the game has some things it does really really really really well, and everything else it does competently enough to build a foundation for the really great stuff.

Though I suppose after a while the same mini-games may get stale. There's also a few I found a bit difficult like the UFO mini-game and the one where you have to wait for the guy to pull out his sword. Otherwise the majority of the mini-games were very enjoyable. The battle I most enjoyed was The story was somewhat confusing for the first half, at least for me. Though I suppose in the end things did get a proper explanation. It just felt a little hard to get a feel for the goal I was trying to achieve. Then again that might have been the goal of the story.  The side characters were all colorful and fun. _childDocuments_.review: Knuckle Sandwich is a good game, but flawed as an RPG. I enjoyed the story, the witty writing, the overall weirdness. The gameplay is fun, the microgames are engaging, though few feel truly novel. If you enjoy the very specific genre of quirky RPGs, you'll have a good time here.The problem is balance. I very quickly found that it's simply not worthwhile using skills over regular attacks, they just don't deal enough damage. This causes the battle system to feel pretty bland; the best strategy is just to use regular attacks, buffing your attack when you can, and just get good enough at the microgames to minimise the damage taken. Overall, this game is very enjoyable and worth your time, but it just doesn't quite work as an RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Interesting setting- Top notch presentation- Interesting characters- Dungeons aren't annoying at all- Combat system is fun: normal attacks consist of timed hits/dodges with a few twists and special attacks consist of microgames like mashing buttons, catching an object or shooting down a space ship. - No random combats, although you may have to do a little bit of grinding for some bossesCons:- The first 40 minutes, right until the title drop, are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible. The initial set up is fun, unique and gives you high expectations on what's to come. Then the plot becomes a "solve the mystery" story and kinda throws everything away.- The inventory, which is by far the worst aspect of this game and objectively a bad design choice. For some reason, weapons and accesories occupy an inventory slot even while having them equipped and key items don't have a dedicated slot. There's also a lot of items on the ground, which should be a good thing, but the inventory space you have is so limited (partly because of the weapons, accesories and key items issues) that getting those items is counterproductive. The game also has a PC system which allows you to deposit or withdraw items... and, of course, it's badly implemented. I haven't seen PCs in accesible places so you'd have to go back and forth if you wanted to order your inventory before an important bossfight or something. This is a JRPG, not a survival horror, managing an inventory shouldn't be this annoying.- Movement. It's shoddy. You can walk horizontally, vertically or diagonally, but the walking speed is rather slow so you'll end up running. That's when you'll find out you CANNOT run diagonally. Why is this a thing? Being able to walk diagonally but not run is a major issue that needs to be fixed.That's all from me. Game's fun and charming, but the inventory system and the movement need to be fixed ASAP.PS: READ THE REVIEW THAT SAID SOMETHING ABOUT THE DIFFICULTY SETTINGS AND BE CAREFUL WHEN MODIFYING THEM. IT MAY GREATLY HINDER YOUR EXPERIENCE.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is VERY good, but I do have some mixed feelings. It is definitely not a game for everybody.Its aesthetics are absolutely outstanding. I love the art, I ADORE the music, I love the minigames, I love the overall concept, I love the characters, I love pretty much everything.The least amazing part of this game is definitely its story. I did thoroughly enjoy it, but I can definitely see how a lot of people wouldn't. It goes in what feels like a million different directions, and it is very hard to tell what is going to be important and what isn't. While I did enjoy the ending, it definitely did leave a lot to be desired. The story was tied together decently well, but it felt like it wasn't able to hold on to one idea for very long at all. There were things that stayed until the end, but there were just as many if not more things that were seemingly dropped as quickly as they were introduced.The first 30 minutes of this game were outstanding. I really liked what the game seemed like it was doing. But after about an hour it felt like all of the darker tones of the game I liked so much were just completely dropped. I wouldn't say it made for a less enjoyable story, but it definitely was a little disappointing. I wish the game stayed more focused on the things it seemed like it was setting up rather than jumping around so much. There was so much untapped potential and it was just a little bit upsetting.Despite its flaws, this game is VERY charming. It is unlike almost anything I have ever played and has so many unique and creative ideas that are (for the most part) executed extremely well. While it never quite reached the peak of the first 30 minutes for me, it was still a fun and satisfying game through to the end.My personal rating for this game would probably be 9/10, but i think a more objective measure of how good it is would be 7.5/10. If the quality of the story really matters to you, then you will honestly probably not love this one. But if you are just looking for a unique and fun experience with great humour and amazing aesthetics, then this is more than worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good, but not all that I was hoping it would be. Worth the price IMO. Solid 7/10 for a little indie game.Best thing about the game is that it's really funny. Not every joke lands, but the style and characters are  extremely charming & the game got some laughs out of me. The music rocks, the visual style is great with some really neat twists here and there. It's the type of game people are going to compare to undertale & earthbound, but IMO the game's tone & animation feel a lot more like Mario & Luigi Superstar Saga which was a wonderful surprise to me.That being said, the gameplay gets repetitive and boring by the midgame and the "every enemy attack is a unique minigame" gimmick wears out it's welcome fast. Most minigames are riffs on a couple of very basic ideas. I started to dread combat sequences by the end and was zoning out & spamming just to get to the next couple of jokes. Would work great for a shorter game but not here.My last gripe is that the story is pretty loose and nonsensical. Not really in a cool surreal way, more of like an unfocused, non-cohesive way. The story starts out seeming to be about running a crazy restaurant, which I wish the game leaned into more. Instead you just go from one random area to the next, fighting enemies and waiting for the game to make its next big non sequitur setpiece gag. The story just needed a bit more to bite into. Also, I'm not personally a fan of the "the game world is falling apart, there's glitchy textures everywhere!" trope and there's a bit of that here.Also, I haven't finished the game yet. I wanted to finish it before reviewing, but after booting it up and staring down the next line of enemies to fight, I just couldn't move myself to keep playing. Combat needs to move faster somehow. Also, the game needs way more inventory slots. I wish the fights were more fun because I'd love to go and explore more of the world, but I have no drive to keep doing these fights rn.Overall, a fun time. Very funny game, extremely charming. It's weird how the overarching plot feels so poorly structured while the moment-to-moment tone and jokes are so endearing. I don't think this game's going to change your life or anything, but it's fun and cheap and the devs seem cool on twitter. I think there's also a BADBADNOTGOOD reference in the game which I dig. I'll definitely be following their next projects closely!

_childDocuments_.review: Holy Moly, this game is such a treat. I remember seeing a trailer for this game a while back, and I thought it looked amazing. Fast forward to a few days ago, I got reminded of this game once again, and upon hearing that there was a demo, I downloaded it immediately. After finishing the demo, I quickly rushed out to buy a steam gift card to buy Knuckle Sandwich. I can not state enough how great this game is. The artwork, gameplay, and characters are amazing. The pixel style is great, and makes it feel like I'm playing another Earthbound. The story is a nice blend of both realistic setpieces and magical elements, making the world feel so familiar, yet so new at the same time. As for the gameplay, this is absolute perfection. Normal attacks being a little quick time event is great, as it makes sense for a person to dodge a normal attack at the right time. The minigames can sometimes be a bit similar to each other, but they always keep you on your toes, not giving you a chance to rest until it's your turn. Overall, this game is a masterpiece and I heavily recommend buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get it, I really don't. I keep coming back to this game, trying to understand what it was about it that went so wrong, and I think there's a few good places to talk about.For one there's the story, which most people know from the demo. All of that gets dropped the moment you defeat the first boss you have party member with. The plot's bus driver (a guy referred to as "bus driver") takes you away from the mystique and intrigue surrounding the setting so you can spend the rest of the game screwing around until it comes back to the mystique right at the end, which by then you'd have forgotten that there was a plot you actually cared about which was put on pause.Two, there's the gameplay. For an RPG that hates being an RPG it sure does love to make you pretend it's an RPG. Your attacks aren't regular attacks, they're little minigames - and when I say little, I mean "long." They do pitiful damage, take forever to ramp up the DpS (Damage per Smack), and you don't get to choose which attack you're doing so if you wanted to do the timed hit that at LEAST has a chance to deal like 15x damage, well sorry. Every enemy gets to attack first due to how screwed up speed is, but hey that's not a bad thing! Enemies get to do these little microgames like it's Warioware, and sometimes "little" means "little" and sometimes it means "space shooter" and I mean so many space shooters you'd think you're playing Action 52. No really, it's a good thing - you deal damage if you complete the microgame's objective. Sadly, this means that many fights take as long as like two fights in YIIK, a game with comparable terrible attacks and battles that take way way way too long. The big issue here is that Warioware microgames usually take like 3-6 seconds long, whereas microgames in this game take like 10-15 seconds every time.Three, there's the characters. They're very expressive, but in the same way so they all kinda feel like the same quirky character type. Some dudes who seem really important, like Vance, end up sitting out most of the game after you kick his ass the first time. Other characters, like Apricot, only serve the purpose of being "The guy who helps move the plot forward" while being thoroughly uninteresting (his bit is that he's a rich snob!), or you could have the "rivals" to the party who are just some random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who aren't actually evil but also they murdered a guy and nobody really wants to talk things out. Speaking of talking, get ready for a main character who only talks around the guy who doesn't listen to him, while remaining completely silent around the coworkers he befriends. Even that Dolus guy is expressive when he isn't speaking. I get not wanting to have the main character speaking directly into your face for half an hour every few steps, but it might be nice to play as someone who has more agency or personality than a corpse drifting downstream. Well, that's not entirely fair. The main character had personality riiiiight up until where the plot gets thrown off the rails completely.

_childDocuments_.review: For disclosure, I was one of the KS backers for Knuckle Sandwich and have been excited for it from its trailer and music drops ages ago.It can be a bit gauche to talk about other games in a review, but it's particularly relevant here - Knuckle Sandwich swings for the fences to sit amongst the canon of Surrealist RPGs (The Mother series, Undertale, Hylics, etc) and it offers up a lot of great things to place it there... but it takes on a few archaisms and doesn't quite deliver on its story.If, in the trailers, you've been charmed by the visuals and music on offer and you want to see the full extent of what Knuckle Sandwich throws at you in those departments, then absolutely grab this game; it's an aesthetic delight from start to finish.The story is a wild ride and goes places fun enough where I won't spoil it. Always great to see mundane modern locations reframed as RPG dungeons. it made some decisions with plot pacing and reveals I did not personally agree with but stands as an experience, albeit with some holes.If you're someone very particular about tight and polished gameplay experiences, you're going to have a tougher time. Combat is very involved and demands focus, but can run long, and even longer if you make mistakes with your timed attacks.A big mechanic in combat are battle minigames, where you'll avoid an enemy's attack and deal counter damage if you clear it without mistakes. There are some enemies that only really take damage from successful minigame clears and not your standard attacks. Some (though not all) of the minigames are notably harder to clear without mistakes - and you'll take damage instead. This makes a few select fights feel sluggish or a little frustrating.There are in-game options to make the minigames simpler, slow down the speed of combat, or reduce the amount of damage you take. In the end I reduced the enemy damage by 40% and had a more pleasant time with combat for the rest of the game. What I'd actually prefer is a way to increase the damage you DEAL, since that would make combat swifter overall.There's also a very old-school inventory system, where every character as 8 item slots, that include any equipment or key items they're carrying. It's not impossible to navigate, but you'll grow to have a 'use it or lose it' mentality with consumables, and be endlessly paranoid over if a non-consumable is now useless, or if you'll need it again later (keep the torch in your storage, you'll use it more than once).All in all, I'm delighted Knuckle Sandwich is finally here! If you're in that space of Earthbound/ENA/Digital Circus brainworms, this dose of webcore weirdness will tide you over.

_childDocuments_.review: Just hit credits for the first time and while I'm not quite done with the game now, I think I've got my thoughts on this game together enough to put them out there:I like knuckle sandwich a lot. The writing and humor might not be to everyone's tasted, but I liked it.Game play wise I do have some nitpicks: firstly I feel like the normal attack lacks a little oomph. I'm also not a fan of the random nature of the three different gauges. I also wish the characters got a little more in the way of abilites or even if there was some kind of progression for them. It's nice that you get some choices for the protagonists abilities, though. I also didn't seem to come across any new weapons more than halfway through.Combat is overall very fun though. The minigames are tough but fair for the most part. Some a better than others, but there's very few that I'd say I didn't like at all.I think my only major gripe is the inventory. _childDocuments_.review: Going into this blind was the best. Knuckle Sandwich takes you on a 3200rpm spin-cycle with a story that’s packed with crazy fun silliness. You never know what’s around the corner. There’s highs when you’re fighting against the silliest of enemies alongside trusted allies, and lows when you and your team are so defeated that you think all hope is lost.The art style and its consistency is amazing and like nothing I’ve ever seen before. For the most part it’s whimsical and fun just like the world itself and its many thoughtful characters, but it also leans into a weird creepy/dark side at times that really complements and contrasts with the whimsy that you come to expect. Knuckle Sandwich keeps things fresh and also doubles down on its weirdness by regularly taking you on jolting twists and turns as you navigate the story, and often plucks you from the world to an unfamiliar place as you go between chapters. Spoiler + opinion: The music in this game..! A quality bunch of music artists worked on the soundtrack for this game and in my opinion, really does wonders for Knuckle Sandwich. The music always feels correct. It’s so dynamic and diverse, changing with the vibe of encounters, tone of the story and the place you’re in. It all feels so rich and really brings this game’s world and its characters to life.The various mazes across the game are pretty fun, and always make for an interesting puzzle to solve. There’s usually no wrong way to go, as you might surprise yourself by finding a hidden item instead of a dead-end. You usually have a choice whether to try to avoid enemies or instead target them to build up your level. There were probably only a couple of moments where I was doing more than a few battles with the same enemies and found that a little bit tedious, but pretty quickly things would switch up from there so that feeling never lasted long.I disagree with the notion I’ve seen expressed by some people that the inventory management system is annoying. Yes, there will likely be more than a few times where you don’t have enough room to carry something you just found, but I found every time that I could always toss something to make room. There is an inventory storage system that you can access at plenty of convenient locations, making it easy to deposit and withdraw items and if used wisely you can avoid maxing out always.When I finished the story, I continued to go find all the things I missed along the way. Knuckle Sandwich is packed with hidden areas, items and challenges so the post-game experience is great, too. Using items in interesting ways leads to really cool results. I’m yet to find everything but there’s something about Knuckle Sandwich that makes me want to find every little detail and thing that I can get out of it. You can tell a lot of love went into this project, and I would absolutely recommend that everyone experiences it.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved this title! It has a very solid identity and the reveals in the plot are quite fun. At a first look, it's easy to jump to the conclusion that this is another "depression earthbound-like" game, but that's not quite right. The gameplay is an extremely fun combo of traditional RPG elements and MANY WarioWare-like mini games. I'll leave more detailed thoughts below:Combat in this game is genuinely so smart. The game cleverly rewards players for interacting with its mini-games by offering big amounts of damage from perfecting them - especially enemy attacks. This means you are always on the offensive in combat, making battles very exciting for those that may not be "into" the turn based format. I love that statuses are also new and exciting in this game. Long gone are the days of turn based poison damage, here statuses effect you're ability to interact with the mini-games, which effects your damage. However if you are a skilled player, you will be able to overcome these hurdles - I really like this, the game is always finding ways of rewarding the player for playing it well.The art style is very charming - I've genuinely not seen a game that looks quite like it. It's not afraid to throw little doodles in your face for a laugh and the switch from 2D sprites to 3D models in cutscenes is really interesting! It artistically separates the areas of interest very very well. A lot of the animations are also interesting in this game? They are strangely fluid in a way that scratches my brain lmao. The 2D sprites have non-tile based animation in battle, giving them a particularly lively look. (i really love how the applebat moves for instance)The music knocks it out of the park, I really love all the tracks of the game and I'll be adding quite a few to my playlist soon : ]I really only have a few criticisms - I think in the first 3-4 hours of the game there are quite a lot of cutscenes. I think it could do well to cut down on a few or allow the player to explore a little earlier. I also wish the girl characters in this game were allowed to be sillier - none of them really reach the silliness in design or personality of B-side, Dolus, Mr. Apricot, etc.Otherwise, I really adored this game - I could definitely find myself coming back to it to replay one of these days. I really don't see where the lower scores are coming from - but one word of warning, please make sure to pick up the game again once you beat it!

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the game - it's okay, solid 3/5 for me. There was definitely a lot of love put into this game.The art style and presentation is sick. Music is great, and the sprite work is fantastic. The characters were likable enough, and the plot kept me engaged to the end (although the pacing was a bit slow and I definitelyHowever, I felt like some of the mini-games were a bit obnoxious. The controls for some of the shoot 'em up ones didn't feel good; I'm willing to bet this was an intentional decision. The main attack of characters is 1 of 3 slider mini-games similar a golf-swing mechanic, or the Active Reload mechanic from Gears of War. 2 out of the 3 mechanics allowed for additional hits as long as you could keep up with the pace of the mini-game. This was neat, except sometimes the battle music or on-screen animations would distract me.Other than that, Knuckle Sandwich was surprisingly-solid. _childDocuments_.review: This game rules. It's an RPG with warioware-esque minigames for combat. This means, if you don't suck at the minigames, you can effectively dodge 99% of the attacks in this game, which is cool.I'm writing this review quick and dirty so I'm just going to touch on some things here: the story is great albeit loses it's way for a few chapters maybe, but! catches itself and continues being great for entire rest of the game, the writing is genuinely funny throughout, and despite the obvious multitudes of inspirations from the games you'd figure a game like this would be inspired by, it still remains entirely it's own person (or, game, in this case). There are so many jokes and puns that I didn't notice at first that I only realized hours later after the fact, I don't know how many I've missed, but I did spend basically my entire playthrough combining groups of people's names together trying to parse the pun (as an early example from the demo chapter, Gorg and Zola are two characters you can talk to)I thoroughly loved my time playing KNUCKLE SANDWICH, from finding random secrets (thanks to a specific scarecrow) to backtracking for more secrets to every combat encounter, I feed off what this game delivers to the player. I certainly have seen my fair share of complaints with this game in the discussions and reviews claiming "combat is too slow and boring" and as nicely as I can say this, those people just suck at what the game wants you to do. I happen to be pretty good at extremely simple timing minigames and warioware-esque minigames, not exactly something to brag home about, but playing the game with the minigames set to Hardest, I had absolutely no problem trucking through the entirety of this game, taking it a chapter at a time. The music has some of the craziest samples I've ever heard, I swear I heard both Terry Crews Old Spice WHAT and FFX Titus Laugh soundbytes used in two different tracks. Genuinely one of the craziest OSTs in a game I've heard in years, I think.The only performance problem I had was a combination of awkward vsync settings and a very specific room with a very large reflecting pool, that room, no matter what I did, ran at about 40fps instead of the usual 60, but from the game being slow for a few seconds, it didn't effect anything important.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to sum this one up, so here's a little anecdote.At first, I hated the pacing of the game, it felt very slow and drawn out for no reason. I played half of the game and would still have recommended it but with caveats. Why is this minigame oriented game so sluggish? I hated grinding for levels even though it should be more fun than its inspirers.Then while my wife was watching TV I just played it on the laptop screen instead of connecting to the TV and realized the HDMI cable from my laptop had been slowing everything down. Oops! The flow turned out to be excellent. What felt like a lowkey chore became something I couldn't put down until it was finished. The microgames are well paced and it's a great WarioWare spiritual successor. The story  is very nonsensical and even though most things are *technically* explained, it does feel like a tenuous string tying a whole bunch of tangents and characters together. But the graphics are very fun and span tons of genres/levels of pixels and polys.As with most small town mysteries, the answers never quite scratch the itch (I think specifically of the promising opening to Thimbleweed Park), but this one's tone lets you know right off the bat it's going to just do its thing and please don't get in your head about plot threads.From what I've gathered through unfinished sidequests and reading a bit online, I missed a bunch of secrets. I may scour the game a bit or might revisit once guides exist, because I'm so curious where they could be hidden--I'm usually somewhat thorough, so I respect so many well-hidden bonuses.The music is so bizarre and weird and fun. No essential tracks are coming to mind, but you can check a lot of them out on music streaming and get a feel for it.It's fun! Don't overthink it! I always respect high effort levels and this is up there with the most ambitious of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: This game may be one of my favourite games ever. As I'm writing this it's been almost two weeks since I completed the game, on the first days after its release, and it's still haunting me.
