_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Solid RPG with some good tunes, fun characters and fun mini-game based combat. Heard about this game YEARS ago and finally getting to play it is pretty cool. The art & animations feel very colorful and vibrant, which can also be said about the music.In terms of the mini-games (since that's what the combat is based around), they're mostly quick and fun. I actually thought it was going to end up like YIIK where they became annoying and super dull, but the amount of mini-games + each mini-game having 3 difficulty variants freshens things up.Like I said in the TLDR, it's solid. Looks like it'd be one of those "quirky" rpgs and it is, but it doesn't feel like it's trying too hard to be one of those.The game does have some cons though. Your inventory is absolutely the biggest offense. 8 slots for your healing items, status effect items, KEY ITEMS, WEAPONS, AND SKILLS! That's crazy. Its annoying managing it. I'd recommend to the developer to either add 3x that space, or create separate inventories for key items and weapons.The game can be a bit grindy, but that could be either a positive or negative depending on your taste.Once again, it's solid overall. Would recommend to RPG fans that enjoyed stuff like Earthbound, Undertale, LISA, etc. It's not those games, but it's unique like those games.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really happy to say that knuckle sandwich was not a casualty of its decade long development cycle. The amount of time spent on this game shows in the density of novelty, one-off mechanics, visual gags and high effort set pieces, especially in the combat encounters, comparable to that of deltarune chapter 2, a game made by a man with infinite money.Those combat encounters are, in many ways, the highlight of the entire experience. Between the unique mini games given to almost every enemy and definitely every boss, the psychedelic procedural backgrounds that accommodate them, and the regular breaks from format to make a single joke, knuckle sandwich is a breezy experience that rarely overstays its welcome even if you feel as conflicted about other parts of it as I do (more later). I did find the game's maths to be confusing and kind of unpolished, with numerous skills shockingly under tuned, others over tuned, and a really inconsistent approach two enemies health and defence stats that make it very difficult to tell if you're actually doing decent damage for any particular encounter.I'd like to give particular praise to the game's OST, created by a bunch of independent artists who aren't necessarily in games, and God does it show! Swagger and personality oozes out of every track and manages to make even some of the least interesting locations shine through sound. Special props to the standard battle tracks "Handsome Humans" and "Fearsome Freaks" as well as "Nothing Sweeter" and "Brightfang Lash".In broad spoiler free terms, the story and writing writ large is the biggest letdown of the game. Knuckle sandwich has whimsy, much like many indie RPGs of its lineage, but it doesn't have much in the way of emotion. Your party characters barely allow you to endear yourself to them by letting you know basically anything about them (the most i ever got was one character being a former athlete who struggles with chronic health issues, said once in optional dialogue). All characters in general could serve to be A bit more intense and punchy than they are? For the simpler archetypes to land. The strong thematic basis of "being a young person working sucks" doesn't last, and with the story being almost entirely driven by a very simple plot, knuckle sandwich is left feeling like it's about nothing but very, VERY gentle satire for most of its runtime. That's about all I can say without delving into plot details.Ultimately, knuckle sandwich is a very light and breezy time, at a crisp 10-15 hours, full of novelty and virtuosic presentation, but struggles to be a story worth the grandiosity of the JRPG format. In other words, it's a really good Mario and Luigi game.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: good:-banger soundtrack-compelling gameplay-endearing characters-charming story-a good homage to its GBA RPG inspirationsbad:-maybe it's TOO good an homage to its GBA RPG inspirations. item management and some puzzles in some dungeons feel a bit outdated/clunky -the story was engaging but i wish they expanded on it more. i feel like as soon as things got really interesting, it was overonce i got a taste of Knuckle Sandwich i was hooked immediately, but unfortunately left a bit hungry for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I really like Knuckle Sandwich! It's a holistic vision of the world communicated through a medium that the creator(s) clearly know and love, with a consistent perspective on what makes this type of game compelling. It is auteristic in a way that may put some people off, but is the reason why I so regularly reach for indie games. At the time of writing this, I'm roughly halfway through the game and very excited to see the rest of it.I will say, I read through some of the negative reviews on Steam and I don't NECESSARILY disagree with many of the criticisms. The game sure does abandon plot points it sets up early, the humour is front-and-centre (so if the sense of humour is grating to you in any way, you're probably going to have a hard time enjoying it) and the difficulty wavers significantly from section to section. HOWEVER in spite of all this, I've had a fantastic time discovering what the game is doing and saying. It's a layered cake of excellent hand-feel, distinctive art direction, hot tunes, genuine surprises and fun characters. Locations feel deeply considered, the pacing is compelling and I have no idea what the last half of the game is going to look like.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: A solid RPG that plays like a fun mix of something akin to WarioWare and Earthbound. The music, visuals, and story are so cohesive and feels like a living, breathing place.  The minigame combat is neat and has enough variety and challenge to keep it interesting and engaging, and the difficulty is pretty forgiving. I'm not sure if the negative reviews mentioning these minigames played prior to any patches, but I played on version 1.2.3 and the difficulty wasn't overwhelming. I think I had to restart 3 battles in total, and the number of free party heals outside of combat are plentiful enough to not stress about running out of healing items.   I finished the game maybe 5 days ago and I still cannot stop grooving to the soundtrack or thinking about different themes within the storyline. Do yourself a favor and give this game a shot - you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed my time with Knuckle Sandwich.  Had no idea what to expect going in since I avoided most of the demos and trailers but the plot was entertaining and the combat engaging throughout.  Several songs from the OST are seared into my brain.  Really captures the feel of what Warioware would be like as a short form RPG.  Biggest complaint is the inventory system, I don't see why it's so small when there's so many items.  Will recommend this game to people.  It is a strange journey that should be experienced.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game with a fun story and plenty of little secrets hidden around. Artistically it is vibrant with color and humor in its unique style which made me smile every time I got to meet a new character. Be it a random NPC or a recurring main character they all had a lot of heart and stood out as their own person (my favorite being the depressing soup guy on the ship).What makes Knuckle Sandwhich such as good game is not only its visuals but also its combat system which is a beautiful blend of Earthbound's 2-D art turn-based combat and WarioWare's bizarre but charming minigames. Reminds me of the Mario and Luigi series of games by giving you bonuses the more skilled you are in identifying and timing inputs.Definitely worth the buy and highly recommended to anyone who enjoys short RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I been anticipating this game for a long time. This game has all the self aware quirk you expect from an RPG like this. The battle system is so fun you want to keep getting encounters. Just when i think i know where the story is going it goes somewhere else. Every unique character i come across has me asking. "whats their deal" The humor is right up my alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: this review was a joke at first but i actually want to give my serious thoughts on this game. i guess i should put a spoiler warning but i don't really cover anything specific.i think the game overall is REALLY good, i absolutely love the minigame gimmick, it adds so much to the gameplay and makes the game really stand out on its own, i also adore the music and artto me the story was pretty much just alright, it kinda felt secondary to everything else in a way? it starts off with the whole gorilla burger plot but then it just goes in a completely different direction, and it feels like they were trying to do *too* many ideas to the point where everything just felt cluttered and i had no idea what was really going on. the way gorilla burger was brought back into the story near the end felt like it was rushed just for the sake of giving that story some sort of conclusion.the characters on the other hand i really like. a lot of them are pretty simple and one-dimensional to my knowledge but i don't really mind that, they have pretty diverse personalities that got me really attachedalso shoutout to the accessibility features and support. i haven't used any of the accessibility features myself but they definitely are a lot more in depth than a majority of games i've seen. also i made a feature request related to high-dpi monitor weirdness and it got added really quickly, which was super nice :)overall, don't let the "quirky earthbound rpg" bs turn you off from this game, it has some cornball moments for sure but i had a really good time with it, and i think it was absolutely worth the price
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: - Some of the balance feels off, in that often my character does like 3 damage per attack and a single combat takes a long time despite being in a dungeon with 20+ enemies. This leads to me dodging enemies in dungeons, which leads to me fighting less, getting less exp, being under-leveled, doing even less damage relatively.- The very restrictive inventory space does not really add anything to the game for me. It is a holdover from the Earthbound influence, and easily my least favorite part of those games. - The soundtrack is wall-to-wall bangers. The music does a perfect job of conveying the funky, absurd, off-kilter setting of the game. Back Alley Beat by Nelward is such a jam.- The art and character design is fantastic. I love how the art style will randomly change between the default 2d world, jittery 3d scenes, NES-style chunky pixels, etc. A lot of games will use a change in visual style to represent something weird or otherworldly, and it is done here to great effect.- The writing is hilarious, irreverent, and sometimes pretty sweet.- Brightside
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying the game so far. However, the only issue I have is that you can't save before a mini game with an achievement tied to it. It would be a big convenience for anybody who achievement hunts to have a save point or option to save just before the mini game begins. Or optionally, add additional save files so that if it gets to a mini game with an achievement tied to it you can still progress the game on one file while having the another file to retry the mini game for the achievement. If both were implemented it would be a nice quality of life improvement. I also could just be beating a dead horse since I don't know if there is a point later on in which you can retry said mini games.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to come out since the Kickstarter campaign. And I'm glad to say that it didn't disappoint. This feels like a love letter to the GBA era, and I love it for that. The battles are super fun,  and I love the story and  characters. If you like games like Mario and Luigi Super Star Saga, Mother 3, and Warioware you'll enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: fun silly rpg that feels directly taken from someone's brain and laid out on your computer to play.if you like the minigames, the funky music, the wonderful 90s slushie aesthetic and the fun cast of characters you'll probably enjoy it and forgive it for its occasional jank and slightly underwhelming plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the perspective of someone who rarely plays RPGs Knuckle Sandwich found a way to pierce my hesitance with it's unique combat. Classic click fight, choose target, watch attack animation and subsequent appearing numbers, then repeat isn't for me, however this game changed that system around. While the RPG combat bones are still there, many mini-games to master in both your attacks and those directed towards you will demand more skill than simply pressing a button.After playing through the demo its odd story and killer jams sunk their hooks into me as well and prompted a purchase.I thoroughly enjoyed the game for a little over half my total playthrough and then started to get the desire to reach an ending/final chapter. In that later "half" I was intentionally avoiding combat where possible and stopped searching every nook and cranny for hidden treasures. With that change in gameplay necessary combat sections were still beatable and while I wouldn't change the gameplay settings from their defaults there are plenty of options to cater the difficulty to your liking. From difficulty of mini-games, to healing after every combat, and even having the option to skip combat altogether.There's a lot to love in Knuckle Sandwich and that's evident even in its demo. The full game revealed some pain points over time, but their issues didn't linger. Rattling off a few: Try the demo, if you like it you'll like the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I'm happy to have finally played it after years of watching its development, and let me start by saying this game is a trip. I'm sure you knew that already if you've seen any of the promotional content, though. This game is incredibly strong in every department I can think of. A masterpiece, if you will.The story is well thought out and everything feels like it happens for a reason. It does leave a few questions unanswered to keep things interesting, or maybe I'm just missing something. There wasn't a single part that felt like it didn't matter. It goes really hard on the twists near the end, and most everything ties up really nicely.The gameplay is something else. Battles are super interesting with almost every attack and ability hinging on the player's skill. Not to mention the hundreds of microgames across the entire game. Story beats are also broken up with other minigames to keep things interesting outside of enemy encounters. There are a couple that are frustrating (both on purpose and unintentionally), but that's just a consequence of having such a varied collection of gameplay styles.The visuals are incredibly charming and well-made, having a very distinct style even if it changes from time to time, which only adds to the charm. All the different characters are incredibly lively, especially in battles. The transition to 3D every so often are very surreal, giving them an odd sense of importance.Don't even get me started on the music. Every track is a banger, the sound design is phenomenal, and I'm gonna be having a hard time getting it out of my head. Easily the best modern RPG soundtrack, in my opinion.Everything about this game oozes care and charm and is well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming RPG that had a lot of love put into it with a wonderfully weird and surprising story the entire way through. Well worth the asking price, if the demo interests you there's so much more in the full game to keep you delighted, full of little secrets and funny tidbits. Special shout out to the soundtrack, it starts off and keeps being consistently great through the whole experience. Some would find shortcomings in the battle design being mostly focused around the warioware-esque mini-games, thankfully if that ends up being a bother there's accessibility options to get past those for however long you want.For people looking for more of a challenge there's a pretty brutal challenge mode available.Really great experience overall, I was so happy to find this a few days before release.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: While I had a few small problems with the gameplay (and many of these were likely the result of me running an outdated version of the game for like 2/3rds of it) and pacing, Knuckle Sandwich should not be missed for boundless creativity, gorgeous art, groovy soundtrack, and nonstop hilarity. An Earthbound/Undertale inspired game that does more than enough to stand on its own.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game about five years ago on Kickstarter, and out was worth the wait. The unique combat was always something to look forward to in every encounter, where you essentially get a different mini game every time. The characters were very fun, and you could tell that the Andy Brophy enjoyed coming up with silly ways of having them interact with the player. The story I'd say was overall pretty decent, but gets absurd by the end, which I think is on purpose. It's a really fun game, with lots to do, and discover. I really think this will be the next indie hit that many will be talking about for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this one for a while and I like the direction it took, even if I would've loved if the game kept a more grim tone after Chapter 1's end (same moment when the demo ends, for context), but I don't mind the lightheartedness after that, and the tone wrapping back to being more unsettling when nearing the end.Besides that and a few nitpicks with the backtracking, painfully slow movement speed and some of the later battles, I enjoyed the game a lot, and it shows that the creator put his heart and soul into it. Shoutouts to to the amazing soundtrack, by the way.Would go for seconds if a sequel is ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I originally left this review before I had finished the game, because I was really enjoying it and wanted to help boost store visibility, and then slightly updated the review after I finished the game. My feelings haven't changed, but it was a "regular" and "boring" review. Knuckle Sandwich isn't really a "regular" and "boring" game, so I'm going to sum it up with an analogy:Knuckle Sandwich is like a homemade spaghetti sauce. It was a labor of love, and it's chef clearly poured their heart and soul into it. It took quite a while to make, and the sauce came out a little watery in the end. Some ingredients overpowered others, some others may have been a little understated, but damn if it didn't still taste good all the same. Not everybody is going to like this particular sauce recipe, and sure, it could have maybe used a some cornstarch to thicken it up a little, or maybe a little more salt. But at the end of the meal, if you like this kind of sauce, you can't help but still tell the cook "damn, that was good sauce! Thanks for making it!"(p.s. still don't listen to any comparisons, positive or negative, with Undertale. It's a disservice to both games, which took similar inspirations, but had wildly different intentions with their gameplay and storytelling)
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of issues in terms of balancing and inventory management but it also has a ton of heart. It does a lot of creative stuff I've never seen a game do before, and I'm always a sucker for games that constantly shift genre and art style for the sake of story beats and gags. The best of this game reminded me of the very best of the game Mibibli's Quest, which is one of my favs.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: So. This game game is an amazing piece of art and I binge played it. I guess I missed a few things but replay value, ya know.Knuckle Sandwich was long awaited by me and a good friend of mine who even cosplayed the protagonist and Dolus at one point at Gamescom. A few days ago I just got the notification that it's out and we both went and played it. I like that it kinda shadow dropped and I didn't even notice any content in the internet that spoiled me anything. I guess some secrets are gonna be spoiled if I can't find them in time but thats life I guess.This game, just as the creator said, reminds of so many things but in general it seems to be the Mother 4 we all deserved mixed with arcade/wario ware elements and some Pokemon homages. I think with all it's charme and unique caharcters it is good enough to be it's own thing and together with Pizza Tower the best game I played throughout this year actually. Even if I'd stumble over some spoilers for some secret bosses or whatever, I'd definitely like to play it again.Andy Brophy, if you're reading this, WELL DONE on an excellent game!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Played it, and beat it. The game is excellent, on paper. But the narrative structure is painful to experience. its front loaded and back loaded. Everything in between is mostly tepid nothings and 'Well that happened's'. This is a Critical Review. It all seems a bit awkward to just recommend in good faith as the game sells it self as a 'funny' experience yet it feels actively afraid to be jokesy and playful for the majority of the runtime. Its really disappointing in this regard and leaves SO much to be desired. Its not even that there arn't GOOD jokes, there are, but they are so rare as to leave the player confused as to what kind of 'tone' this game is suppose to have. Is it a playful quirky game, or is it a dreary personal meta fable about the relation between game creator and player that also has funny jokes here or there. It feels like it could have had both -easily- but it actively refused to in a sense.Which is REALLY unfortunate because the game is beautiful, the music is probably some of the best 'quirky earthbound like' music one could ever ask for. It gets mostly everything right and on point except for the narrative, which feels anemic, limp, and dry as as a desert for much too long. (outside of the beginning and ending? Those are really good actually, and I usually complain games don't know how to have good endings.)Also the main character keeping the black eye through the whole experience 'in earnest' is really... a strange choice? I don't know why this choice was made, their original stance at the start of the game is actually really good. Even if its some artsy creative choice its not a good or 'worthwhile' one that adds anything to the experience beyond again, sending mixed messages about the 'tone' of the game. Is the game cute and quirky or is it complicated? Both? It can't seem to decide on a tone, so it just actively does not. Which is kind of my main frustration with the game's narrative. It feels like its actively shy to have 'character' in the 'characters' in the cute and quirky colorful game that feels like it should have more -character- and depth to those characters as is.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Combat, Great Music and a weird World. Definitely worth the Price.But the 8 Item limit is AWFUL when 2-3 Slots are always taken up by Equipment, and Key Items also count towards that limit. There is essentially no reason to ever buy things, which makes you less likely to explore the City.And I must adress some issues I have with the Story the Game goes through. So SPOILERS!!I feel like the entire Busdriver Story hinders what could've otherwise been a really unique Story. You murdered someone, and your new collegues are trying to find out the Mystery of why there are Ghosts in the Burger Joint. Your Boss even admits that he was trying to frame you at the End. It still hints over the whole game that that part is important but it really isn't. The Game would go the same Route if you never killed the Guy.  But essentially after the Freezer Dungeon that Plotline gets dropped in favor of the Brightfangs and 1000 Futures, which railroads the Game into a "Save the World" Plot. The Murder was heavily featured in the Trailers and Demo, heck the Game is named after it, so it feels a little bit like false Marketing. It's sad too because your Friends in the Game basically Dissapear completely at the end, and the Busdriver is not a fun enough Character to make up for it.I will not say that I could "fix" the story or anything, but there are some misstped that stopped the Game from reaching its full Potential.Overall though the Character Interactions and Scenarios are still fun and Entertaining, so I can't complain too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Knuckle Sandwich is a bit of a mixed bag.The game's atmosphere, aesthetic, and music are all top notch.  The gameplay is about 50/50.  There are a lot of good ideas in here marred by a few frustrating ones.  Fortunately a few of these can be resolved via changes in the gameplay settings, but there are still some issues holding this game back:  The Earthbound style limited inventory, lack of local map or journal, some odd enemy scaling to name a few.BUT even with those negatives the game is absolutely still worth your time if you got any enjoyment out of Earthbound + Mother3  or the Mario + Luigi RPGs and/or have a taste for weird vaporwavey vibes
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: A warning, do NOT try challenge mode (on your first attempt) like i did. As it is right now, it is way too difficult and the damage scaling is all out of wack, making it a very annoying experience, thankfully i was able to turn it off mid way through the game in the settings. Anyways, this was a fun game. The creator really put a lot of things he enjoy and like about video games, which feel a little messy. Some minigames goes too long, story is a little loose, the goblins and murder at the start are completely dropped after chapter 2, the fishing minigame/side quest is impossible to attempt since fishing baits are nowhere to be found, skills/cds are pretty much useless since you need to hold them but regular attacks can do more damages if well comboed, etc..I think as of right now, wait for some fixes. The devs seems to be updating the game a lot and perhaps in a month or two all of these will be problems of the past but some will definitely remain as they are the core of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I was a backer of this project five years ago after seeing the demo on Vinesauce.At the time of writing this I am about 4 hours in and will update this as I get further.So far, the game is a blend of Paper Mario / Super Mario RPG and Wario Ware - but rightfully its own thing at the same time. The story has kept me interested, the characters are interesting and unique, and sometimes the game feels like I'm on an acid trip. But I am greatly enjoying it. If this holds up I highly recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Played just past chapter 3, but it's been a blast so far and I'm looking forward to playing more. It's zaniness is gonna have you doing double checks every other moment. Dodging attacks is both like timing blocks in paper mario or having to play a minigame specific to the enemy, it might be turn-based but with those mechanics it keeps the game really engaging.The game's pacing of humor definitely keeps in mind that you probably played undertale if you're playing this and it intentionally messes with your head for it. Even if you haven't though the dialogue has a good amount of jokes sprinkled throughout it.Overall really fun combat, really catchy and wonky (in a good way) music and just a funny and zany experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Knuckle sandwich is weird. You shouldn't think of it as a high expectations game well worth your money or some life changing indie RPG like Undertale/Deltarune, LISA or OMORI.Think of it more like a random game you found on itch.io that seemed like good eye candy, and let it do to you what it wants and needs you to do (with some random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thrown in of course). It's a video game where you can heavily see that it's made to please the creator more than the player, like some sort of message that says "hey look what i enjoy isn't this neat :)" and nothing more, really. It's simple, lighthearted and funny, but should be played like an RPGMaker game with random knick knacks, including the jank and annoyances. A lot of it is made to laugh and parody other games' tropes, and not another reason more. The game just does anything possible to try and make you laugh. It can also be pretty annoying and confusing at times, but I don't think you should really ask any questions and try to go with whatever the hell the story throws at you next.I love knuckle sandwich a lot. It's one of my favorite games even, but it really has to be appreciated more for it's presentation, music and as a concept of what would be Andy's ideal game, more than it would be a contender for best indie games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Knuckle Sandwich is an absolute treat of a game. Earthbound meets Warioware with an extra helping of character, charm, weirdness, and personal touches. While the difficulty is a bit surprising in some sections, you can always almost make your way through with a bit of cleverness, and if all else fails there's a huge number of gameplay options that can make KS accessible no matter your play preference.Had a great time bouncing around Bright City, and strongly recommend you take a trip there yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: please whatever you do buy this game and show it to people! i am IN LOVE with itthe writing is super funnythe graphics change from time to time which adds impact to certain scenesi love the funny wario ware style micro games to both avoid and land attacksdo yourself a favour and give this game a try! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Knuckle Sandwich is REALLY close to being an absolutely perfectly uneven game. If it pulled one or two fewer punches near the end I'd totally forgive it for how much the plot meanders from one rushed plot thread to another rushed plot thread, hell I'd even see the game's sometimes clumsy sometimes downright abrasive design as a plus not a minus. It's like, already in the range of simulating the confusing absurd agency-killing sometimes brutal mundanities of service industry life, if it could just take that laaaast stretch over the whole thing would fit like a glove and I'd call it a miracle game whose disparate pieces somehow manage to line up to a whole greater than the sum of its parts. Christ, it's not like the game doesn't deserve it, every bit of it is brimming with this loving attention to detail, all these new and fun and lively bits that just keep winning you back in every time the game feels like it's daring you to lose interest in it outright. I want for nothing else than for Knuckle Sandwich to be the kinda sleeper hit that filters everyone but the Realest Kinosseurs of true Ludonarrative Mastery.... but the future refused to change. I can't say I don't want more games like Knuckle Sandwich to exist, at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute MUST buy if you're a sucker for indie RPG's. From the engaging combat, the characters, the art style, the rich story, and ESPECIALLY the music (keep in mind I only found out about this game last month, so I went into this game completely blind), it quite literally ticks every box there is for what makes an "indie" game "indie". Had an absolute blast playing through this, it's one of the few games I've played where I just couldn't stop grinning throughout. And if you're curious, it is pretty much nothing like Undertale at all, both story-wise and (mostly) gameplay wise. I'd say it's a mix between WarioWare and MOTHER 3, with a dash of it's own creativity in the mix. Honestly a 9/10 game, with the only downside being the weird pacing in some parts of the games story, but it balances out in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: been watching this game's development since i was in like middle school, SO SO glad to see it come out and after having beat it i loved it a lot :)i liked:- the battles, enemy designs were super creative, battle themes range from camp to amazing, the minigames and methods of attack constantly changing made things feel dynamic and prevented staleness imo- the characters are cute WE LOVE DOLUS <3- game is easy to customize, you can adjust things like the amount of damage you take and you can even skip battlesi disliked:- some of the puzzles (esp late game) felt kind of unfair, less like my critical thinking was being challenged and more like my patience- the story and pacing started off strong but towards the later bits it kinda seemed like different elements of different ongoing plots were just interrupting each other, not a big gripe if u value gameplay over narrative but yknow.- some of the boss fights dragged on for a really really long time, i don't know if it was because i was playing on a harder difficulty or something but some of them just took so many hits to kill, even for a hard mode
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: Having now completed this game, I can still say I recommend it. It has a lot of good going for it, very fun gameplay mechanics, excellent music, really charming art and character designs and an overall enjoyable story. However, I do have some minor gripes that I feel are worth mentioning at this point. There are a total of three annoying ice puzzles in this game, and one is already too many. I honestly think the game would be better off without these rooms entirely, or at very least it would be better if they were redesigned so that you have visibility over the entire room. My other complaint is in regards to some enemies that can do damage to you no matter what with their regular attacks. There are only two enemies I can think of that do this outside of bosses, but it's not a very fun mechanic when the rest of the game lets you react to attacks or complete a minigame to avoid damage. Still, despite these annoyances I came away after about 25 hours of playing this with an overall very positive impression. This game is something special, and definitely worth your time to experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Knuckle Sandwich

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a bunch! Some design choices and fight balancing bog down the experience a bit, like inventory slots and enemy surprise attacks (enemies moving first for free). Which is a shame because some of these weren't issues in the games that inspired Knuckle Sandwich, Despite that, I very much loved the music, art, characters, enemy variety, and microgames of course. The passion put into this game is apparent, and that passion really flows chapter to chapter in my opinion.  Watching this project slowly take shape since 2018 has been a blast, I was elated to see my name in the very special thanks! 😊

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: Every patch released from the time I started the game has reduced difficulty of encounters and puzzles, so anything I said about that will probably not be accurate at all.Knuckle Sandwich is a what would happen if you mashed together a classic turn based RPG with Warioware and then multiplied the strange level by about a million. You play as a silent protagonist who just moved to the fictional Bright City in Australia and are looking for a job. You end up working at a burger joint and things quickly escalate from there. You'll meat some friends, cohort with Goblins, and unravel the mystery of why things in Bright City are getting so weird. I truly enjoyed my 12 hour play through of the game. The turn based battles never got too stale because the mini-games for attaching and defending get swapped out fairly frequently. Even your basic attack has three variations associated with it. The music is excellent and varied and you get to look at just plain gorgeous pixel art the whole time!That's not to say the entire experience is flawless. The characters have a very small inventory that needs to be constantly managed, but mercifully item storage is always fairly close by. In the back half of the game starting in chapter 5 the enemies get very spongy and while they're not overly difficult they can take quite a while to defeat. This can be mitigated with the many accessibility options that effect difficulty, but I would guess that the balance will be tweaked over time as well.If you're a fan of turn based RPGs, or want something that's just plain weird then you should take a trip to Bright City.

It's got themes and ideas you don't really see in them there big time rpg's. Its different dimensions, party members, story perspectives, and best of all.... BED ROOM CUSTOMIZATION!!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really  add much to what people already commented on this game cons. In my opinion this game is geniunely good. Yes, there might be some amount of not the best game design and storytelling desicions (especially  towards the end), but it's all just small details that didn't distract me from enjoying the game. I had couple times when I got frustrated by some weird game design choices, but it wasn't a really huge deal, for the most part I was just having fun with this game.  I found out about this game back in 2018-2019  because of the DESKPOP(rip)/STAFFCirc, amazing internet labels/communities that most of the  musical artists for this game originate from. That being said, the audio is top-notch. It's just very appropriate and well-made soundtrack that effortlessly blends with the game's aesthetic and could be listened to on it's own. Especially loved the gyms'es(gym's?) part of it. Same for visuals. Despite going very experimental with them, varying from pixel art to low-poly 3D, everything just perfectly sits in place. Very strong design. Yet again I enjoyed the game and have enormous respect for the Andy Brophy and all people involved. Releasing indie game of this scale that is actually playable and enjoyable is absolutely outstanding and gigantic amount of work that requires a lot of passion and will for such a small dev team. If you are searching for unusual mother-like JRPG that would stand out in that niche, Knuckle Sandwich is definitely your way to go.

detailed_description: Kunio, the beloved hot-blooded renegade, is back to wreak havoc in the world of the Three Kingdoms! Get ready for a whole new and exciting Three Kingdoms experience, with Kunio as the lead! ■Simple controls let you overwhelm the battlefield! Take down enemies with flashy moves! 　Unleash powerful special attacks with the press of a button! 　Save up SP to wipe a crowd of enemies out with an ultimate attack! ■Master a variety of Tactics the Romance of the Three Kingdoms are known for! 　When you think of the Three Kingdoms period, you think of the various military tactics used. 　Master the 10 Tactics available to attack the enemy, generate items, and more, 　and get yourself out of a tough spot! ■Power up your character as you make your way through the story! 　Take down enemies to level up! Get an advantage in battle 　by powering up your character! Items dropped by enemies can have 　powerful Bonus Effects, so try finding the right equipment for you!

_childDocuments_.review: PSA: Controller problems? enable steam controller global override and they go away.there's really something weird about long-time Japanese developers slowly forgetting how to make their own flagship title as programmers retire and new blood get less done with every iteration.Aesthetically, and as a spiritual successor to the Downtown Nekketsu games that involved period piece parody, this Three Kingdoms game is cute and on-point. The retro look is amped up by simple 3D landscapes and the characters have more exaggerated spritework for all the cool new moves they have.Mechanically, though, it's kind of a flop. I'm an hour and some in and the combos are stiff, the spacing in dodges and with certain follow-up attacks is scuffed, and negative edge (hold button to charge) moves are fickle as hell. Sometimes attacks let you scoop floored enemies, sometimes they don't. There's a roman cancel mechanic straight out of guilty gear where you use 50 super meter to slow down time and pushback enemies to reset yourself out of guarding. i don't think arcsys had anything to do with this game on a development angle but it's funny.Day 1, and the peak number of players is 45 around the world. i think everyone knew they were gonna get a half-baked experience just from looking at this, but I still went in because I love the series and wanted something to take it easy with.if you love the MECHANICS of old kunio games: attacking barrels, enemy stacks, combo juggling, etc, don't bother much with this. It's designed inherently more like an action RPG than it is a true beat-em-up.While it has better aesthetics than games like River City Ransom Underground and more visual loyalty than River City Girls, it's become obvious that westerners imitating Kunio games know how to make Kunio games better than the Downtown Nekketsu team do.Kinda like Sonic Mania versus Sonic Team. You want the loyal, full experience? Go to the programmers who grew up loving the games and wanted to fix their favorite series. The original developers either quit decades ago or never kept up.I still recommend it positively because a 6/10 game technically passes anything but a bar exam.
_childDocuments_.name: River City Saga: Three Kingdoms

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved river city ransom and games like it since I was a kid.  I've also loved dynasty warriors.  It strikes a nice balance between the two and I really enjoy it.  If you know nothing about what to expect, its a side scroller beat-em up heavily focused on character customization where you can spend money to buy food power ups and level up to specialize in various fighting styles.(punch, kick, throwing, and weapons).  You also get scrolls to give yourself tons of special moves for every circumstance as well as get tactics and learn ultimate moves through killing enemies with the special moves.  It starts as a fairly standard beat em up but you start seeing some crazy super saiyan like stuff eventually which is always awesome to see in this style of game.  That combined with the fact that it has online co op is a nice recipe for success.Edit:Once you beat the game there are multiple story paths based on your rep and new equipment that gives you stat bonuses to push into the next tier of OP character builds.  It's pretty rewarding and definitely even more fun at that point.
_childDocuments_.name: River City Saga: Three Kingdoms

_childDocuments_.review: The best Kunio game that's come out in a long time (not a high bar). It's Basically a modernized and more story-based take on Downtown Special, but lacking a lot of what you might expect if you'd played that.There's no fun interactions like riding on carts or other players. Local co-op is pretty weak as player 2 is just a clone of player 1 in terms of stats and moves, and can never switch characters... not sure if Online is different. The general gameplay could have felt snappier and more physics-based like the best old Kunios.Anyway it's "fine" overall and if you're big into Kunio and the Three Kingdoms its a lot of fun to see who is playing who. Sticks very close to the actual Three Kingdoms story.
_childDocuments_.name: River City Saga: Three Kingdoms

_childDocuments_.review: Great, fun and addictive. This one starts out kinda slow and the overall gameplay is grindy. However, once you start unlocking the special moves the fun really intensifies. NB: This game is more like the classic NES RCR games and not like River City Girls, so the combat is a little more simplistic but the level designs on this one are amazing, and more complex than the ones on RCG. It's a beautiful game that uses 3d assets and 2d sprites, and the world is very big. Modern combat mechanics would have been really good for this one but the old school NES combat is just fine.  I'll give it a 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: So a buddy of mine got me this game to try out for myself as I just finished this in Let's Play format. I have to say for a series that has underwent so many regional changes in the span of 35 years, it has kept its charm from back in the Famicom days when it under the Technos banner. Story-wise, it's a Kunio version of the retelling of the Sangokushi era or what we know it better as The Romance of the Three Kingdoms. It spans across 6 chapters and goes all around the map as in classic Nekketsu form.  Now I've played my share of games like these and honestly glad to see the old artsyle being brought back like this.  It brings a rustic charm that has been forgotten after all this time.  Music-wise, there are no words to describe this. I mean, most of it had a mystic and true to form Oriental feel to it so most of it felt like a breath of fresh air after listening to it, especially the shop theme from the old game and the Sousetsuken theme from Double Dragon. Combat and control-wise, they were pretty tight for the most part and had little to no problem with. My only issue I felt was there was with certain platform stages, the planes felt really off to me in some spots, I managed mind you but I feel, it should've been done like how the older games were being on a 2D than a 3D one. Threw my perspective in a way but again, I managed.  I liked the Reputation level, kinda wish you had titles to go with them as you go or at least what you got out of it.  The China Heroes side game was fun, I played a bit of it after I was done with the LP and it became an extra video to mainly show it off. Now as a recommend to others? If you're a fan of River City Ransom/Double Dragon..consider it as a love letter to those who grew up with this series. You won't be disappointed for sure. But as always, your taste may vary. Is it worth the time? Sure. It's fun, and that's what a game just needs to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- All characters from Nekketsu series- Best girls are also in the game, Misuzu, Hasebe, Mami, Misako, Kyoko, and Madoka sensei.- Good stories. Funny characters.- Map system is good. Can travel across ancient China on foot. A lot of exploration and challenging side quests.- Beautiful graphics. Very colorful.- The music is really good here. Hopefully Arc System Works will use them in future Kunio games.- Feels like reading/watching Wuxia series.Cons- Very big game. Sometimes its easy to forget the progress after returning from a break.- Only Kunio is playable on solo. The AI allies only show up in story battles.Good job Arc System Works. Please use the same artworks and gameplay from this game and Rival Showdown for future Kunio games.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty big disappointment.  A lot of yapping, very little punching.  Seriously, 1 playable character in story mode...?  At least in 1989 you could get a guy with a different colored shirt.  Pretty much just a re-skin of RC Rival Showdown...which was also not a great game.  They're doing sequels and reboots the wrong way around; to be successful at that, you change the appearance, not the formula.  They've been keeping the aesthetic, but sucking everything out of it that made the original great.  Arc, let the fans handle the remakes like you (begrudgingly) did with Underground...you're no good at this anymore.  Alternatively, check out RC Girls, which actually feels like a proper RC/Old skool brawler.

_childDocuments_.review: As fellow Technōs Japan Corporation enjoyer and a fan, this game was a must-have must-play on my list since it was released. Bought at full price, do not regret. Had solid 50 hours of fun, in nostalgia sauce as well as some modern tweak. Once again, You take the role of Kunio (Alex/Crash, whatever weirdos) and in case of second player Sonokawa, who respectively play role of Guan Yu (God of War) and Zhou Cang. During 6 chapters, You will follow a story in a period between Yellow Turban Rebellion, fall of the Han to the Red Cliffs Battle, also know as Chi Bi. All characters You know from previous games, show up in bigger or lesser role to play too, for example Misuzu, Yamada, (not) Twin Dragon Bothers, etc.Despite being 2022 game, they still hold too much to some mechanics made back in the famicom era, but maybe that's why I... We... love it? If You know this series, You must give in the temptation. I wish Goal 3 would be made like that!Pros:+ Good old Kunio beat-em up we love and share!+ 6 chapters, having 3 different "endings" each+ Familiar skills are back and more!+ Familiar characters put in old-new roles+ ABOBO+ Soundtrack remixed from previous games to match game setting+ Bonus mode with unlockable charactersCons:- Weird and unnecessary platformer segments, even if only few (especially chapter 3)- No crossplay, only few players, so multiplayer is dead. Get a friend or smash them solo- Inventory management- Quests resource gathering- Before battle start, enemies have split second to move and attack, which can result in 1 HKO before You can even move on higher difficulties...- Already saw skills from this game, coming to a new one and being marked as 'brand-new' on a trailer...- Even after 55h of gameplay, I didn't even get close to accumulate enough gold to buying secret armor piece, not saying about entire set On first difficulty, it was about stats and leveling up. On second difficulty, I was often using tactics, on third, I needed to manage gear properly and by this point, have some skill and effective ability combination. Hardest difficulty is literally a test from all above, as one error can get You into a combo, that will finish You off faster than You can open inventory. A game that I will come back gladly to once a while.
_childDocuments_.name: River City Saga: Three Kingdoms

_childDocuments_.review: A blast from the past! Overall, a charming 2D beat-em-up with great music and cool references to past titles and other beat-em-up series like Double Dragon. Early on, the gameplay is a bit repetitive and a lot of grinding is required... but leveling up your character with new moves and combos becomes fun and even addicting.The "Bonus Mode" (China Heroes) is a nice diversion from the main game and lets you select a bunch of different characters, including the heroes from River City Girls and Abobo from Double Dragon. I enjoyed using Kyoko from River City Girls who has an awesome and very hilarious and effective Chun-Li-style stomp combo! :)If you enjoy 2D beat-em-ups with style and charm, this is a great one to add to your collection!

_childDocuments_.review: How did you get yourself here? What are you looking at? What am I doing with my life? This is a NES era Action RPG Beat Em Up. _childDocuments_.review: Great game especially if you grew up with the RCR game for Nintendo. Pure nostalgia with a skill system that reminds of the old skill system with many more skills. Stats are gained through level instead of food. Weapon skills for several weapons and new skills are awesome.The Han dynasty story just adds to the gameplay. Being able to free roam through the chapters has been really nice as its so much bigger than River City.*Warning* The worst part of the game is the platforming. Since now you have a single button jump, they punish the terrible movement from the older game. Up and down in specific SUCK. It is very slow and some ledges are not exactly the shape they appear. There are only a few platform areas that are vertical climbing, but the 2 that I found climb are just painful.Altogether I'd say if you like old school Kunio games like River City Ransom, GET IT. Just be aware of the rage of poor movement on platforming areas.
_childDocuments_.name: River City Saga: Three Kingdoms

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! I've always been a big fan of the Kunio/River City/Downtown Nekketsu series, ever since the NES days. Back in the SNES era, it bothered me how none of those games were ported to the US. Finally, after a long time, the series is getting western releases. I've played all the ones released on 3DS and Steam (even underground, which has nothing to do with the original Japanese plot) so far and I hope they continue to get released. Also played many of the ones we missed in the west for famicom, and so I played my fair share of these.All that is to say, I've played a lot of these Kunio games, and as far as they go, this one is a really good one. If you're a fan of the Three Kingdoms story, you'll appreciate this retelling of it with the cast of the "River City" games. All the familiar Downtown Nekketsu elements make their way into the game as you traverse a two-dimensional China and battle injustice. There is also co-op play, which I can't wait to get into with my people this weekend.I can't recommend this enough.  There are way worse things you can do with 30 dollars.

name: TASOMACHI: Behind the Twilight
detailed_description: Yukumo is a young girl traversing the world in her beloved airship. Upon arriving at a particular Far Eastern town to run some errands, her airship suddenly breaks down. She decides to explore the town to search for parts for repair; however, the town has fallen silent with no trace of the people who live there, the only inhabitants being a strange cat-like species... Tasomachi is an independently developed adventure game that lets you freely explore the beautiful world created by designer nocras. Assuming the role of young female protagonist Yukumo, fix your beloved airship by exploring the mysterious town covered by the Twilight Mist to collect hidden Sources of Earth and help restore the town’s lost brilliance. Enjoy this unique world with an Eastern fantasy twist, complemented perfectly by composer Ujico*’s mystical soundtrack. The Town Wander and explore this mysterious and beautiful town. As time slowly creeps by, the subtle differences in the town between night and day are mesmerizing. The Nezu Tribe – the only remaining inhabitants of the town – just may provide some useful hints regarding the Sources of Earth. Sanctuaries Test your skills in the athletic stage-like “Sanctuaries” located on the edge of town. Your Airship Hop into Yukumo’s trusty airship to explore piers, valleys, and lakes. Gather the Sources of Earth to expand the scope of your adventure even further. Outfit Changes & More Extras Collect money around town to change outfits and decorate your room. Try to complete the entire collection!

It is a chill, very simple, even simplistic, Collect-A-Thon. Some people, like me, will relish that simplicity, others will get bored after 20 minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: Tasomachi is a beautiful short length doujin 3D platformer/exploration that harkens to the old days of collect-a-thons but it's done with such a style and mood that I couldn't help but love it. (The short length helps a lot but, unfortunately, people looking for a meatier experience won't find it here.)What Orbital Express achieved here was a mixture of solitude, exploration, Far Eastern townships with a distinct retro-tech style that are abandoned and you slowly restore to their former glory and a relaxed, chill out feeling that the excellent soundtrack (which has a similar tone to Yasunori Mitsuda's work on Chrono Cross) really elevates. In short, the story is kind of there because it's the journey through that matters as you work to repair your ship and ultimately try to help the situation.A photo mode is also included to take screenshots around and it's indeed very helpful since the game features a night/day cycle that make for a lot of cool shots.My praise goes to the mood and chillout effect achieved through the game. Yes, there are trials, platforming and some challenges ahead (which will eat a few hours of attempts) but the town exploration and overall relaxing feeling is simply great when you are sick of all the visual clutter, noise, gunshots and carnage.That's it on the aesthetics.Mechanics-wise, you slowly acquire different abilities as you progress through the challenge areas but the entirety of these are a bit floaty (especially the dash/double jump) and I think the issues are caused by Unreal Engine itself. Thankfully since you don't have any deaths, your only punishment if you fall off a platform is being sent back to try again almost immediately.You get to drive the airship as well so be prepared for inertia-driven controls rather than arcade precise movement. Again, it's mostly for exploration so luckily you don't need the ship all that much except for one achievement and with enough practice, that last challenge can be done.Once you collect enough key items by clearing quests across the towns or finding them in hidden spots, you can access the final area and by beating that you are free to do one last pass to get all the remaining collectibles, which are not too many (thank heavens) but can take a bit to find since the maps provided are static and have zero indication of where you are at any spot. This is where the airship helps since you can oversee the entire area.Last bit are the graphics, which sport simple polygons on terrain and strong architecture cues which are carried by the global lighting through the previously mentioned day/night cycle. Most things look very pleasing as a whole and, of course, it helps it also runs without any hiccups, at least on my configuration. You may have to tone down a few things in the options however since, being an UE game, it may be temperamental on certain PCs.In short: very recommended if you're looking for Tatsuki-type of relaxed Kemofre-like ambience adventure/exploration of about the right length, without any punishing or harsh difficulty, this is for you. As per usual, when on doubt, pick it on a sale but make sure to get the OST bundle!
_childDocuments_.name: TASOMACHI: Behind the Twilight

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so the good is the setting and the music (for the most part). Cute character and town designs. Somewhat fun flying mechanics (but you only get a taste in the beginning and then at the end after about five hours of regular puzzle platforming).The bad is everything else. The story is just a few screens with about three lines each. Controls are super floaty. Platforming is super basic (you have awful jump, and then you unlock small dash in the air and then double jump). On top of that, some special blocks are glitchy (especially those jump plates with net on top, you'll fall through those quite a few times).The structure of progression basically forces you to clean up each of the three towns thrice, so my advice is to only collect enough earth lamps to progress and leave everything else for the post game. Same goes for shrines, you can see advanced lanterns during your first time there, but you're forced to go through all of them again in post-game when additional platforms are unlocked in the rooms.Money collection is a pointless menial task given to you to extend whatever gameplay time there is by another hour or two. Each time to try to collect a coin, you have to wait for a 5-second animation.Some puzzles are tricky in execution, but some are extremely basic and reduced to simple brute forcing to determine the correct order of execution. Some puzzles are not obvious (there's no interaction indicator and no hint that you must use interaction, but at the same time you can't platform your way in due to super obvious invisible walls, which is super dumb).Puzzles in towns are very uninspired, and what's worse, you have the exact same set of tasks to complete in each of them, down to the number of each task. It all gets very repetitive very quickly.All in all, the concept is interesting, but the execution falls flat. Just get the soundtrack and watch the trailer.
_childDocuments_.name: TASOMACHI: Behind the Twilight

_childDocuments_.review: Take on the role of Yukimo as she explores a deserted town, looking for items to repair her airship after it was damaged by a mysterious force. Along the way, you'll encounter the Nezu tribe - made up only of cats - who will guide you to more items for your airship. There are a number of "sacred tree sanctuaries" at the edges of each area. These are basically platforming challenges for you to complete in order to access the trees at the end, which will dispel the fog and unlock more areas. Tasomachi: Beyond the Twilight (T:BTT) is a platformer that issues you two main tasks: collecting items known as "sources of earth" (in the shape of glowing red lanterns) to help repair your airship. Unlocking further areas requires the collection of a certain amount of lanterns. The core of the gameplay is to run around the towns, collecting. There is no combat and no way of dying. If you fall off a ledge into the water, you'll appear right back where you fell off. It's immediately apparent the instant you start playing T:BTT has floaty controls. Yumiko seems to hang in the air for an inordinate amount of time after every jump. This is an issue, as the platforms that you'll encounter are all at different heights, meaning you'll be overshooting most of them. This quickly gets annoying during the general exploration parts but for the precision platforming sections in the sanctuaries, this is a nightmare. They've tried to compensate for this by having Yumiko's feet stick to the floor whenever she lands, but this just winds up looking absolutely terrible, especially on sections that have moving platforms. The camera doesn't help out either. You can control it using the right analog stick, but the camera will immediately turn in the direction Yumiko is facing. If you want to run in one direction but keep the camera facing another, you'll be fighting the camera the entire time. The gameplay quickly gets very boring. After the first hour you've basically seen and done everything it is going to throw at you over the course of the game. The towns aren't interesting to explore, and the sanctuary challenges are all the same after a few hours. Each new area's appeal wears thin very quickly after you've taken a run through them for the first time. There's also a infuriating thing that happens at the start of every new area where the game plays an intro then fades to black and, as soon as you walk forward a few steps, it fades to black again to play a second intro! And it happens in every single area. On the surface, it's beautiful. They've gone for a real  vibe, and while they haven't cleared that high bar, they've achieved something really special looking. The art style is a curious blend of Fantasy Oriental and rustic charm. Trees and their shed leaves are everywhere and contrast starkly with the lampposts, cardboards boxes and trash bags littering the streets. The water effects, in particular, are stunning. How the light glints off the surface of the water and the reflections are all perfect. The panoramic views you can achieve in this game are serious artworks in themselves: this game was made for photo mode. You can tell the developer has done artwork for games such as  and . Get past these surface impressions, however, and you'll find a game that is unfinished to a shocking degree. The problem is that, ironically for a game that looks this good, there's very little attention to detail. So many of the models get reused that each area just blends into the other leading to you not being able to distinctly remember which is which. Animations are missing from actions like digging, sitting and praying at save shrines. All the interactions are just static poses, apart from picking something up, which is the same animation regardless of there the item is. Lots of the effects look cheap like the flaming barriers that block your path and the swirls at the save points. This lack of detail is crowned by the main character. She looks like a doll because her face never moves. It's stuck with the same grinning face, no matter what is occurring at the time. How a studio can put this much effort into the landscape but not even animate the main character's face is incomprehensible. The background music is good for the most part. They've gone for a real relaxing, ambient feel throughout the game. The issue occurs with the sanctuary sections. The music doesn't suit the artwork they're going for in T:BTT. The pairing of grating, ambient electronic music with the serene, naturist vibe of the artwork just didn't work for me at times. As for the sound, there's not a lot of variety. Often, sound effects don't trigger when they're supposed to. There's also no sounds for speech at all and no character voice. Another issue I had with T:BTT, which I've seen reported in other places, is often the game would go completely silent for no reason, making me check if I'd accidentally muted my speakers or headset. I hadn't but, for some weird reason, there are parts of T:BTRT that are nearly completely silent. The storyline can be summed up with three words: there is none. We don't know anything about the character, where she is from or what she is like. There's no lore about the world outside the areas that we visit. This is a real shame, as the blend of the traditional building styles with the modern technology leads to a lot of interesting questions about this world. The airship and how Yumiko got it are never explained either. This lack of detail in the storyline lead me to a constant series of questions running through my head when I was playing:	• How does Yumiko not know how to fix an airship she pilots on her own?	• Why does an airship run on sources of Earth? How do they also fuel AND repair the ship?	• We don't know what she was doing near the town or why she decided to go there.	• Why are we following the orders of a weird group of cats? Have we seen Nezu before? The lore scattered throughout the game is thin. It's usually just three lines or less on some trivial detail that adds nothing to the game's world. In particular, the Nezu are barely explained at all. There's no substance to go with the style on offer here. This is clearly a game where the vast majority of the effort was poured into the artwork. While beautiful, this seriously feels like an early access game due to the lack of content. It's so unfinished... I just can't recommend it to anyone. A platformer with floaty and imprecise controls was never going to be a good game, no matter how good the graphics are. With boring gameplay, no storyline to speak of and no real clue of what you're supposed to be doing and why, T:BTT has nothing to hold the player past the first hour and nothing to convince them to come back and play again past that.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is far from complete. I could see the potential here.If the devs keep on improving then it will be worth it but at the current state it is not.There are some puzzle rooms that you can skip by paying tokens/currency but the game never mentioned that. _childDocuments_.review: This game is... tough to review, because there are some legitimately good things about it - I found the controls to be generally pretty solid, making the platforming only slightly annoying at times. The atmosphere is nice too; very calming, peaceful villages, etc etc. But I have two major gripes: first, it's just... boring. Somehow, between the dialogue and the gameplay, I only ever felt myself thinking "okay, neat... when will I be done with this?" - and that's a shame, because there were moments where the gameplay clicked, and I was legitimately having fun bouncing around... to collect one thing, and then I was on to other boring collect-a-thon fare stuff: dig up the buried macguffin, grab the macguffin in the portal, get the macguffin in the bush. And normally I wouldn't mind it, but somehow, I just never felt engaged with this game - which might have to do with my second gripe.Second, this game feels unfinished. It feels like a tech demo for an RPG before it's filled with NPCs. There ARE some NPCs, but they seem to use the same three models (or at least, I think they did, I wasn't playing close enough attention to tell any noticeable differences, because the game gave me no REASON to). Grass and other terrain items are generally static - in contrast to the PC's very... anime walk cycle and animations. And, like, she's cute, sure! But her design doesn't feel like it fits with the game in its current state. I feel like I would have almost preferred a stick figure character, or one in shorts and a tshirt so I could spend less being distracted by the floaty, flashy model, and more time looking at the gorgeous scenery. I know that sounds like a dumb gripe, but it's just a part of this sense that the game doesn't really feel like a cohesive product - just a mishmash of a bunch of different ideas.I think the most damning thing about this is that the game sets you up with a goal of 90 macguffins, and once I reached that (in almost exactly 2 hours - this is NOT a long game), it turned around and said "ooh, now get 150!", and I decided I was closing the game rather than backtrack and get 60 more thingamajigs. It's not a BAD game. It controls fine. It's pretty. I just...  recommend it, at least not at its base price of 20 bucks. Wait for a sale of at least 50% off, then get your 2 hours of enjoyment. Maybe you'll like it more than I did.
_childDocuments_.name: TASOMACHI: Behind the Twilight

_childDocuments_.review: The more I played this game, the less I enjoyed it.Which is a shame. Tasomachi looks gorgeous, and has so much potential in the world and controls, but ultimately it boils down to repetitive trinket collection.You go from hub to hub and complete the exact same activities in each to gather the collectables, this wouldn't be so bad if there weren't so many of them. There is no sense of impact, nothing I do stays done upon returning to an area, and the trinkets themselves are just a gate on the next area.Ultimately, Tasomachi is fun collectathon nostalgia bait, for the first few hours. If that appeals to you, definetely get it on sale. But a lack of narrative weight and purpose keep this from ever being a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: TASOMACHI: Behind the Twilight

_childDocuments_.review: The only good things about Tasomachi are its tranquil and vibrantly coloured scenery and its JRPGish, upbeat soundtrack. There are a ton of flaws that make me unable to recommend the game:-The story is advanced by collecting lantern-shaped collectibles called "sources of the earth". Problem is, you need to collect 150 out of about 240 of these to reach the endgame, and there is no substantial gameplay loop besides the collecting;-Money is scattered around the world without any in-universe explanation;-The in-game maps you can buy from vendors (yes, maps don't come free in this game) are not very helpful because they don't show your current position, making the collection quests more frustrating;-The quests you get from the three main areas of the game are EXACTLY the same. You will always get three copies of the same quest, like tearing down protest posters or removing weeds. It's just the designer padding out the playtime;-The platform challenges are bad not because they are actually hard (they are dead easy), but because of the floaty and imprecise movement controls;-The "dash" and "float" abilities do not match what they actually do. The first one is actually a pretty weak sauce forward movement that briefly resets gravity, and the second one is actually a double jump;-The keybindings are very awkward as if the designer had never played a game with a PC keyboard before. The aforementioned double jump is not mapped to space as one may expect, but mapped to R. Also the bindings can't be changed;-The player character, despite having many anime-ish costume to buy, has unchanging and wooden facial expression;-The achievement for finishing the main story is bugged (at least for me) so don't bother if you just want to hunt achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: TASOMACHI: Behind the Twilight

_childDocuments_.review: Yukumo is a girl on a journey, flying an airship and soaring through the clouds when a mysterious shockwave damages her engine and she’s forced to crash-land on an Island covered by fog. Kogara, a stranded member of the Nezu cat tribe, finds her and asks for help in a mutually beneficial relationship. By restoring the Sacred trees, the fog will leave the city and its citizens will gradually return, and by collecting the tree’s lantern fruits – a fuel source – Yukumo can restore her Airship and continue her adventure. Solve puzzles, make friends, and revitalize the land in an experience no one will soon forget!  3-10 hours to complete, TASOMACHI: Behind the Twilight is a puzzle platform object collection game that revolves around collecting lanterns in an abandoned city smothered by fog. As more shrines are completed, citizens – the Nezu Tribe – move back in and the towns become operational again, enabling jump pads and more accessible areas. Puzzles are skippable, you can collect money in the streets and pay 20 coins for a teleporter to the end of a puzzle if it’s too difficult. Gameplay is pretty smooth, and after the story is completed, you get access to airship racing. This profitable mini-game significantly lessens the grind of purchasing all six outfits and furniture for your house should you want it.
_childDocuments_.name: TASOMACHI: Behind the Twilight

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been looking forward to this game as a special treat for when I'm down and too exhausted to really  a game, after all those reviews saying it was boring and you just walk around... Well, there was a lot more gameplay than I would have liked, but I have no regrets. First of all, this is one of the most beautiful games I've played. I wanted to take a screenshot every couple of steps. I absolutely adore the autumn vibes with mellow colours and falling leaves, the traditional Japanese architecture, the lighting during different times of the day/night cycle... Each area goes from foggy and mildly gloomy to bright and clear after you've collected enough items and gone through the platform puzzles (or collected enough money to teleport through them). Unlike other reviewers, I love exploring deserted places without any dangers. The soundtrack in the village areas was nice, relaxing and a bit cheerful.  On the other hand, the hectic electronic music for the tree sanctuaries felt wildly out of place. I mean, it did reflect how stressed I got by the "trials", but I had to turn it off so I wouldn't feel worse... I've read a lot about the game's platforming being either "way too easy" or "fun" and uh thanks, I hate it. As someone who's desperately bad at platforming no matter how hard and long I try, I found some of the puzzles really mean. You can buy your way out of them, but if you do it too often you've got to grind for the money. Some of the collectathon items are also hard to reach without good dexterity, though thankfully you don't need all of them unless you want all achievements. There are frequent checkpoints with a pretty saving animation, but having no autosave is obnoxious imo. As is being teleported to the starting village after loading, and to the current region's starting point after drowning. Which, if you're anywhere near as clumsy with controls as me, you'll do a lot. You're just fine after falling from any height at all, but as soon as you touch water you're instantly gone lol. There's no map and I've got no sense of orientation, so sometimes I'd just jump into the water to get back to the starting point... Speaking of heights, there are spectacular views to be had. On narrow ledges and planks. Which triggered my vertigo something fierce. There's also a photo mode, but you can't use it while sitting on benches? And maybe it's just me, but I was put off by the long row of key commands that popped up, so I noped right out and just took regular screenshots - there's not much UI anyway. So that's quite a lot of negatives, but I still found it worth it for the aesthetic experience. Definitely one of the games I can see myself coming back to and just walking around in when I need some unwinding or cheering up. * * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .
