_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting what I got when I played this.Welcome to Elk is a surreal RPG based around the life of your player character in a town called Elk, and in which the central attraction and mechanic is storytelling. I don't just mean this in the sense of the story of the game, but rather the storytelling itself. Over the duration of the admittedly short, but well-made game, you get to experience a myriad of stories told by others  in fun and innovative ways, and a lot of it is inspired by experiences had in Greenland. Some characters exists directly as a reference to the true stories surrounding them. And stories? They're pretty damn good, and paired with some of the surreal "minigames" that pair themselves with it make for a pretty unique and unforgettable experience, and the fact that a lot of what you see is based on true stories is pretty sobering, which is ironic considering that you drink every day in this game. The artstyle is one I'm a fan of, and often the surreal sequences were musically and visually quite interesting. The ending... was ok. I'm personally not a fan of the type of ending it pulled, but I can see other people enjoying it. It certainly does give a neat-ish conclusion to your experience.Overall, this was a decently enjoyable game. There wasn't an awful lot of content for the price that's attached, but what IS there is pretty great, in spite of the ending which I was lukewarm on. I'd suggest buying this when it's on sale. Rating- 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk feels like being invited into the home of somebody very earnest. You're politely shown around, told of the highs and the lows, and after a solid time together your visit comes to a gentle end. The inclusion of real videos of people telling these stories throughout the game was really touching and kept the game grounded, and the ending made me smile. Welcome to Elk didn't blow my mind or change my life, but it didn't really feel like it set out to do that - even though it's the kind of indie game that may seem like it from the store page alone. It felt like it set out to make a human connection between these stories and players, and it absolutely accomplished that.As far as gameplay and achievements, both were smooth and easy. I paced the game out over several sessions, just because it felt better with each story being told to take a break in between, but it wasn't very long and could be completed in one sitting. I explored enough that by the time I finished, I only had three achievements to go back and get, and it was very quick to mash through the dialogue and reach the points I needed to get them. I struggled a little with the "Look, shrimp!" achievement, but got it after a handful of tries.I'd say this game is an experience worth having. My time with it was pleasant, and I'm glad I got to know Elk and the people who live there.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game with unique art style, great music and full of real stories to share, some touching some dark...but all of them real,  which makes the whole experience so rich and emotional, specially if you find one you can relate too. Honestly, you can see how much love the developers put into this game ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of 'Night in the Woods' will undoubtedly love this. Indie gems like this hit so hard; they lift up a curtain to reveal a glimpse into a world that seems so private, an adolescent's experience in the US - or, as it is in 'Elk' - life on a small island in the unforgiving Northern Hemisphere. These games hit so hard perhaps, because unlike TV or a film (wherein we remain passive) the experience is 'experiential', as in  - happening in real time. We are taken on a journey of sorts where we actively participate. For a while we walk with these characters, can almost smell the icy rain and feel the bitter windy cold. This is made all the more powerful in Elk as video interviews are interspersed into the game play, bringing the characters fully to life. I grew up in a small rough town in the Northern Hemisphere - nowhere as isolated as this - but every bit as real.For 'mature' gamers who appreciate the phenomenal power of a story and how art can truly impact us, never pass up Indie games like this. They stay with you long after, and I'm good with that. I don't think there's a better way to learn about other people than through their stories. Well done developers, for honouring these stories so wonderfully. Very recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cool game! The story follows Frigg, the newest resident of Elk, and how she gets acquainted with the locals. After a couple of days in Elk, however, Frigg starts to feel as though death is following her. Every night, Frigg has different dreams involving a boat, and wakes up to a new bottle on her dining table every morning, each containing a different story with death at its center. There are plenty of interesting mini-games interspersed throughout, but the strength of the game overall comes from the true stories incorporated into the overarching narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game that is carried by its narrative and by the strength and presentation of its stories. Elk presents its stories in many different ways, all of which are worth experiencing.Also, that soundtrack had no right being as good as it was.Thank you Murray for the postcard, it was a thing of beauty.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! It is so clever and interesting and dark and funny and not like any game I've played before. If you liked Night in the Woods you will like this. We finished it in about four hours over two days but I've been thinking about it ever since. An incredible story and such a strange way to tell it. Definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't quite convinced at the very start, but not long into the game (as soon as I helped out Anders!) I was hooked. I just sat and played the entire thing in one go. It has some unique stylistic choices that I really enjoyed, which I won't describe, as I really appreciated the surprise of them. I knew nothing about the game going in (just saw part of the trailer), and I very much appreciated slowing realising what was going on / what the game had been built around. I don't want to say anything too much, so as not to spoil anything. So I'll just say that Welcome to Elk is a fantastic example of how video games can be used to share and interact with stories in new ways. I enjoyed the small glimpses into those lives in Scandinavia, and I'm sure I'll be remembering some of those stories for a very long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Finding gems like this is what makes me loves games as an art form. Truly novel in its approach to storytelling and able to cover difficult themes as respectfully as I've ever seen it done. Counterbalanced with some genuinely fun and well designed mini-games. Its deeply sad but never crushing in its sadness, it revels in the emotional rollercoaster that life can be and the stories we tell from it.There is some true talent here, can't wait to see other work by this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: "There’s salient care for the characters in the game and the real people who inspired them. This is an adventure game like none-other that left me with a single tear running down my cheek as the credits began to roll. It wasn’t because the ending left me upset, I just felt touched by the games final moments in an almost religious sort of way."
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly fabulous. A big thank you to the developers who worked through the bugs I had with this game and got me back to playing this masterpiece. Welcome to Elk is the kind of experience I'm looking for in games: funny, engaging, heartbreaking and impactful. It also has the added appeal of being based on entirely true stories. True to the heart of the game, I've been able to share these stories I've heard and read here with others. This is a huge reccomendation to everyone out there looking for something special.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect game to play on a cold winter's night. While the meta storytelling convention can wear a bit thin at times, it's a rich story driven game filled with viscerally striking moments, beautiful illustrative art direction, quirky characters and charming music. If you're a fan of Night in the Woods you'll certainly appreciate this similar, albeit shorter and delightfully Nordic, effort (although with an antagonist cheekily named 'Leeroy Brown' there's still quite a smack of Americana - turns out the US hasn't cornered the market on post-industrial melancholy).  Have a feeling this one will stay with me for a while with its darkly humorous atmosphere of tragic tales.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Such a unique experience! You will find yourself in so many strong emotions evoking situations. A collage of life changing situations gathered from real human stories and woven together so artistically!Regarding its gameplay, it is actually a relaxing interactive movie, sprinkled with super fun mini games. But, some of those mini games, although mini, will give you ULTRAMAX intense emotions. The use of music for that purpose is also spectacular!Great artwork and great soundtrack. Everyone in the team put their soul in this.A love letter to stories.A piece of art!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Was so excited for this game, as I tried the short demo available. I really appreciated the stories shared. At first, I was shocked by the actual videos from people haha. But understood that method after a while. Loved the minigames - fun, calming, and unique.Emotional storytelling, impactful music, and a powerful narrative to keep you engaged through the story. Can't recommend this enough.The singing minigame is beautiful. Wish I could download it.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome game!Back in 2016/2017 I played a small demo that the team were pitching and god, has the game grown and come along since then.I love the up-close-and-personal gameplay, but it's also handled with such care, even in some of the dark moments.In terms of design and visuals - I love me a pretty game but Triple Toppings balance the style and substance very well, which sometimes is a very difficult balance to strike. The use/lack of colour really helps people figure out what and who they can interactive which I really enjoyed because sometimes I get overwhelmed with point-and-click games.And finally, the music. This for me was the highlight of the game.How the score interacted with the stories, and seeped into some of the level design was where the game was at its strongest.It really helped to create emotional impact towards the characters, but also the scenes that you could predict the out come of, but blanketed you to approach them gently. Could have easily been longer, and maybe some more games but overall - it was very unique and I look forward to more games from this studio!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game, surprisingly dark sometimes, but a nice experience nonetheless. It's a great medium to tell several stories about real people that lived and died on the cold landscapes of the north, these are not happy tales, but they are presented in a charming way, some of them through text, others through video, and they are reflected in this little game, in which cute little people jump from one place of the island to the next, talking and living their lives. This dichotomy makes this a weird experience, but definitely unforgetable.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: From my initial entrance into the game and when they introduced the workshop I felt as though I was getting into a variation of My Time at Portia, or Stardew Valley type but quickly came to realize it wasn't that. The game has been classified by some as an RPG, Adventure and Puzzle game but I feel as though if you go into it with similar games of those genres in mind you'll be disappointed.My best description of my time so far with the game would be that it's like playing out a story, not a choose your own adventure, there's no levelling or XP, no inventory and no real gaming at all and the game relies fully on its ability to tell compelling stories to keep people engaged. The stories are interesting in the very least but I haven't gotten through the entire game and I would say that none of the mini-stories in the game have entirely gripped me and none have completely fallen flat either. You can tell that the developers of this game were trying to keep it relevant with current issues and the theme of death is not only constantly recurring but pretty much at the forefront at all times. It's apparent from the very first scene in the game that this project was more then just a game to the development team, each story is told with weight and respect to the people who were putting it out there and the developers handled it well.The animations are interesting and at first struck me as novel, I honestly thought they were going to bother me but even after a couple hours I was still saying "doot dee doot dee doo" everytime I walked anywhere. The characters in the game were well-written and it was easy for me to come up with voices for them as I read all the dialog aloud on my stream with 1 viewer. I'll likely find the time to finish the game but I also felt that after playing for 3 hours I was exhausted and couldn't possible read anymore. That being said I also didn't want to just skip through to get to the end because every piece of dialog was compelling and I wanted to soak it all in, therefore, I had to stop and wait until I was ready to read again.At one point I found myself thinking that maybe this game should've just been a book, then I started thinking of how that would tell and it wouldn't work. Honestly, the game is one of a kind in the sense that the way the stories come out and are told could only be achieved in this platform and for that alone I would recommend this game.When people say the "mini-games" are compelling they're either generally mobile gamers or they are really easily amused. The "mini-games" could have not existed and the game would've been equally as compelling or more so, just simply based on the fact I find them extremely tedious and pointless.As mentioned, I'll finish the game because I want to hear all the stories and learn more about Elk but after I'm done I can't imagine there's a lot of replayability.Ultimately, I would recommend this game to anyone who's looking for a new style of storytelling that's done really well, I would not recommend this game to anyone who's expecting an RPG style adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Would be a good game if it wasn't so buggy. When you need to make Balloon Faces the "seal of approval" just didn't work so I had to exit the game. After that it did work but from that point on my safe file didn't work anymore. Whenever I reloaded the game it was at the balloon part no matter how much I played afterward. So that is a let down.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: is an amazing amalgamation of insane stories and quirky character that actually have some truth behind them. It's like playing through an episode of  with the incredibly unique art style and the way the characters walk around all jaunty, hopping around like refined stick puppets. The soundtrack is also equally amazing, along with the sound design. There is so much effort put into this game, I hope it receives the recognition it deserves.The story starts out quite innocent and pure and soon turns into a very adult themed game. There are some difficult situation that the main character, Frigg, will experience on the island of Elk. Some of these are told through VERY abstract mini-games, such as seeing a character murdered but told through a theatrical play, bonding over a 'Simon Says' type game of repetition, or playing a few rounds of mini-golf where the golf club and the ball change every hole. I have to praise the developers over their ability to just... make incredibly unique, one-off mini games that the player will only experience for a minute or two. It must have taken a lot of time and patience to pull off when they'll only be seen for just one set piece and never again. is incredibly unique and beautiful and weird and sad and hopeful. It's full of personality and charm, with real life characters and stories that I couldn't believe were true until I learned more about them. It's really quite a special game and one of my favourites ever since I played the demo. If you're looking for a different type of game then I wholeheartedly recommend  with every fibre of my being.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: This "game" has a lot of things that make a good story-driven "game": — pretty hand-drawn art — cool music — idyllic Nordic island setting — getting mulholland'd/David-Lynch'd — 40ºC below zero — booze — alcohol caches —  — breaking the 4th — FMV — Klumben —  — a few "puzzles"The only problem is that the gameplay is too bland for me (it's an inherent genre limitation though, so it gets my thumb up). You must be in a special kind of mood to be able to enjoy this "game", or be the type of person who's attracted to and enjoys games of this particular genre. / 1o.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: I received this product for no cost for the purpose of reviewing. However, this does not affect my views and opinions of the game.Welcome to Elk is a strange little 2D exploration adventure title with very interesting characters and stories. The game revolves a girl named "Frigg" who has recently moved to the island of Elk to work as a carpenter. The game is made up of many individual stories as well as plenty of mini games to keep things fresh.--------The first thing noticeable about Welcome to Elk is the art-style. Everything looks almost hand-drawn and there are very bright and vibrant colours. The game seems to be very colourful even with most of the backgrounds being in black and white. Every so often the game will interrupt itself with live action footage of the people behind the stories, explaining how things came to be.--------The soundtrack of the game is pretty good, and there's a lot of variety when it comes to the music. There seems to be a song for each situation that fits well. The mini games, especially the ones revolving music, are fun and upbeat. The overall sound effects in the game are also decent.--------There really isn't that much too do in the game. Most of the time the player is walking around and talking to the other characters and listening to the stories they tell. There are many things to interact with in the game, and all of those things are "coloured" in, as opposed to being black and white. The game tackles different subject matter, from humorous situations to sensitive subject matter. There are also mini games that keep things fresh.  --------Thanks to the developer for giving me the opportunity to review the title, as well as anyone who took this review into consideration, I hope it helped.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk was not at all what I expected but I think that is truly the appeal of the game. Above all things it’s a collection of stories that highlight the pain, absurdity, and unsavory aspects of living. However, it’s almost as if the game is telling you these often painful tales with a goofy wide eyed grin on its face with all the vibrant colors and bouncy movement. It’s hard to recommend but I’m glad I got to experience Welcome to Elk.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the demo for the game a while ago, and I fell in love with the game and the story about George. And now, playing the full game, it's a really bitter sweet game about making friends and family and how all that can change. Sue and Bobbi are my favorites out of the group because of their dynamics and how they just work. Plus their saying "Out of beer, out of here" is so funny. The way the game is made, and how you get both get a game and a mini movie all in one is something that I've never seen outside the game. It seems that the stories are all true (As far as I can tell) which just adds more to the game with a personal touch. 10/10 wonderful game!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: If possible, go into this game completely blind.  *Especially* do not watch the game trailer, which spoils many of its most hard-hitting moments.I had it recommended it to me on the strength of the story, played it completely blind, and this went approximately nowhere I expected.  It's a meditation on life and death in a small Greenland town, and virtually the entire experience relies on the interplay between its narrative and its metanarrative.  It's basically a walking simulator, although it's got a sprinkling of minigames, so don't expect any gameplay per se.  Just let it take you along its 2-4 hour journey.Do be aware that it's got a number of mature content warnings (largely for themes of death and violence), and some unflinching moments.  Part of the game's is how those hit you from kind of unexpected angles, but it might not be everyone's cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: More art than it is game, but that's never a bad thing. Short, but very impactful. You will feel real discomfort in certain scenes, sometimes cringing at something you must do or feel the anxiety of unwanted advances. The game keeps you on your toes and gives you an insight into a world likely very different than the one you live. But it has a sense of realism while slowly becoming more and more unreal as the game progresses. If you enjoy arty, character driven storytelling you will like this. Just don't expect a ton of "gamey" aspects and enjoy the story and the messages.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk is a beautiful series of stories. That is the heart of the game, about how stories are told and transmitted, how they impact our lives, and what things they have to say. It also leans heavily on the theme of loss and death, and honoring those who have passed. It looms heavy over the entire game.Do not let the style of the art in the game fool you; things get heavy very quickly, and I've written out a small content warning about the game near the end of my review.Primary gameplay is walking around your new home on the island of Elk, talking to npcs, and engaging in small minigames. I would look at Welcome to Elk less as a video game and more as a story, or a piece of art about storytelling, told through the medium of video game mechanics. Clearly a lot of work went into showcasing these themes in this medium, and I am happy to have played this game, but there's also little replay potential; I think having heard these stories I'd rather put them aside.Still, it is an interesting concept, and a well-executed work of art; if such games are things you enjoy (think games like Before Your Eyes), it's definitely worth the purchase; otherwise, perhaps if you find it at a discount, or want to spend some time being reflective. Final Review: A thumbs up, but go into the game knowing you're in for a heavy time!Major Content Warning for this game: Death, Threats of Sexual Assault, Pet Death. While I think they bring up these subjects as a part of storytelling, I felt that, not knowing about them going in really affected me emotionally, and I wasn't prepared. More details behind spoilers Death: Sexual Assault Pet Death:
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Globalisation is incredible, it allows for unknown and small communities to be able to communicate with the world and stories from afar to be shared. And Welcome to Elk is such an attempt, a lone isle somewhere in Greenland, with its small community of colourful characters which you meet as you start your journey and slowly discover their stories and get acquainted with the reality such remote communities entails.Pros1. The walking animation is among the most interesting and janky i have ever seen in any game, really one of a kind.2. The whimsical art adds to the colourful cast and stories to be told and the small touches here and there.3. The stories themselves are the star, its hard to believe that these can be real stories from real people, from funny ones you will never find anywhere else but in such a place and others really horrifying which shows the dark reality in similar out of the way communities.4. Music is good if limited.5. I like that the mini games does nothing, and instead is just a fun part of the overall game, no trying to beat a high score or solve before you can go ahead, frankly its liberating.6. Some parts of the game really hit it off with me, there are aspects which really hit me hard, which i wont spoil it for you.7. I want a real world elk stack cards to play!Cons.1. Its short, you can probably finish it in a few hours.2. The small town has a lot of places which are not accessible and generally filler art, some of it is just eye candy or even when actionable don't do much. This could have been improved to enhance the interaction.3. The breaking of the fourth wall can be jarring at times, and takes getting used to, i believe this may divide some opinions, on the other hand we do get to know the team behind the game and what they are trying to do with the title.4. Generally a walking simulator with links to various story snippets, not that the journey nor stories themselves were poor (they are great in fact) but there is so much more potential perhaps here which were not explored.It's great we get to know a community distinct from ours and so off the ballpark that we realise the world is indeed large, and yet some of the issues and problem still seems familiar wherever we are from. The team that did this really made it as a labour of love and to showcase their culture and part of the world, and perhaps more should do so with this great medium we have in gaming. Give it a try and you may be amazed.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk is a wonderful game relying on telling stories that are beautiful, tragic, and beautifully tragic. Gameplay is short but definitely worth your time. This is 100% a game I will be playing more than once and take something new each time I play. The feelings and experiences you encounter will be held dear in your heart forever. Such an underrated gem everyone should play! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quirky one. Not so much a game, more a series of vignettes with a bunch of mini-games sprinkled in. This is a series of (true?) stories set in Greenland. Some sad, some tragic, some bittersweet. I loved the cute art style and the quirky animation. Not a long game, but worth the experience.Warning: Achievements are bugged for this game, so if that matters to you then rather not buy this. If you're not bothered then I can definitely recommend this!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk was a game I had on my wish list before it was released. With very little information available at the time, I was mainly drawn to.. well, the drawings. This style is so very unique and reminded me a lot of games I used to play as a kid. This game, however pretty and innocent-looking, will raise your neck-hairs from the start, and take you through all emotions possible, and so fast you sometimes have to pause and just... Let the situation sink in. Almost like real life, where something bad happens, but then something good happens, whilst your still trying to deal with the past. Every mini game fits to a character and gives extra depth to their already rich personalities. Rarely have I played a game that made me upset with characters, or straight up disgusted. I appreciate the "life" in this game so much. It's about people, made by people, for people. Isn't being alive wonderful in all it's strangeness?
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: 09/2022 EDIT! Those issues have been fixed for me now, even though I completely missed the devs respoding to this review so I had no part in that. It's a very lovingly crafted story that I very much liked! Definitely give it a try if you have interest in storytelling and/or small local history yourself, even if the artstyle doesn't seem like your cup of tea. Very charming and human experience, I'm very glad I gave it a try again after getting a new laptop.-Well. It does seem like a game with a fun story I would be interested in but the problem is if you buy you most likely won't be able to finish it so I'll never know. I miraculously got thru the bug with mom balloon by closing the game and the game creating a loadable save at the start of the balloon minigame that somehow fixed the issue. Unfortunately, game then proceeded to crash on whatever was supposed to load after  and I haven't been able to get past that OR create a save anytime after the balloon minigame.The story might be good but don't buy it until the devs come out with some bigger bugfixing patch. You're not gonna see much of the story without it.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I was talking to one of the writers of this game on reddit and after a few questions I decided to pick this one up. I had a blast with this one. The storytelling is a lot different than most games and makes you think. I also really enjoy the art style of this one. Glad I was able to talk to them on reddit or I would have probably missed this one. I only missed 3 achievements so now I have to do another quick playthough to grab those.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Friggin' great! Super immersive with a brilliant balance between the bleak and blurry and  the warm and fuzzy. Triple Topping have built an island of imagination which reels you in with authentic and eccentric characters, fast-paced mini-games and remarkable real world stories. The only problem is you may wish you never want to leave!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unlike any other — you'll be taken to a rather bizarre journey through Frigg, a character who comes to Elk as a carpenter, but never seem to manage getting a hand on the carpentry during her stay and instead had to deal with issues like death, sexism, and gelk card (that being my favorite part of the game). The game invites you to be deeply immersed in each story by telling the real stories inspiring it, some through videos.What I adore — the art style, the music, the mini games, and the way the dev made them walk (like puppets!) I also love the pace, and the switch between dark twists and light humors every now and then.What could be developed — the length! I think I like it too much that I want it to be longer, it does feel like it ended too suddenly. One of the characters was just there. No stories, not involved in stories immensely, at one point I almost forgot they exist.Overall — 8.5/10, would recommend getting it, especially when it's on sale. Kudos to the dev, this one is a gem, surely! Hopefully it'll bloom into a bigger project in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I wish this game was longer!  It is done absolutely beautifully, and the stories are incredibly touching. I really appreciate the content warnings as a heads up, because some things that happen in the game are incredibly sad. I admit I cried a few times. I really hope they make more games like this one!The mini games were fun, the music was beautiful, and this is just a lovely game. As someone else mentioned, it's not like a lot of other games in terms of play, but that doesn't make it any less of a brilliant game.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk charmingly weaves a bunch of short stories together in a truly original way, hard to compare it to any other work of art. It's a solid indie game with a great soundtrack, but be aware that the gameplay is very light (failing is impossible), and it's heavy on text. If that doesn't scare you off, do yourself a favor and play it to the end, chances are this game may catch you off guard.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Fantastic artistic approach. Lovely hand drawn black & white graphics with some colors here and there. They have also made some other unique choices as of the aesthetics.- Unique concept. Good story. Don't expect agony and plot twists. Everything is so poetic and simple. It makes you reconsider you approach of life and death.- Cute, well built characters. Each of them with his own personality. You will love them all.- Its atmosphere is something special. It is a combination of mystery and weirdness. You will get immersed in its world.- It is one of the few games that so much repetition and simplicity work well for the concept. Each mini game is so simple and each day looks like the previous one. But it works. After all it speaks about life, which is full more of daily little things than heroic actions.- Nice music.- Animations are simplistic but funny.- The little stories you find in the bottles are well written and interesting.- It has some points with great distinctive humor.The bad- Trying to be so much cute, that some dialogues feel a little bit childish. Sometimes they also speak for way too long with a result of killing the pace and get you bored.- The topics of the mini games feel a little bit random. They could have been more targeted.- Although the music is nice, it plays all the time at the background which gets tiring. I would prefer some moments of silence here and there.- A bit short.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. I knew nothing about it except that it was point and click and I loved the art which reminds me of Bob's Burgers. It's not cutesy or for children at all and it's wonderful.The story deals with characters on a small northern island, and is based on a series of true stories. I loved uncovering the stories of the island, the tragedies, the loves, and the peacefulness that can be found.The game tackles alcoholism, mental illness, grief, and crime. If you enjoy Night in the Woods you'll like this game. Please make more games like this!! Perfect to play over winter break and in one sitting.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I saw some good reviews about this game and thought I would give it a chance. I was completely blown away by how good Welcome to Elk was.The animation reminds me of a children's book, but the themes, language and stories can be really dark and hit on some pretty serious topics. The characters are all well designed and show their personalities throughout the game.I really liked the mini games and only wish there was an option to replay some of them after the game was over. The stories from the real life people mixed in through the game really got to me. You see this children's style animation and fun games and suddenly when a real person comes on and tells you their true serious story, it adds a perfect balance to the game.If you are considering whether or not to give Welcome to Elk a try, I would highly encourage it.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game, but kinda short. I love the design, the characters and the way the game is drawn. I would love to hear more stories and maybe have a little bit of story with the main characters. When I saw it the first time I though it will be a very dark game but it ended up being really fun and intriguing. For me it was a 7/10 :)
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the experience of this game! Its a bit experimental -- but I'm glad I went in blind. The UI and gameplay are polished and crisp. Some parts of the game were surprisingly disturbing, but it was all very interesting. I was glad to get such a unique perspective. Oh, and all the music & sound effects are REALLY good. (Beat the game in about 2.5 hours)
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk is one of those games where you get something else than you expected. The story and mood of the game is absolutely amazing! This is supported by a strong narrative based on true stories, wonderful and quirky visuals and well composed music. On top of that there's a lot of fun and interesting mini-games. I ended feeling empathetic with most of the characters and their stories and I wish that would be able to meet them again another time. Sooo if you like story-based games you should play Welcome to Elk!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough of Welcome to Elk, and I am completely blown away. The nature of storytelling that is presented in the game is amazing, and I love the community of Elk. I found that by the end of the game I was feeling for the characters as if they were my own friends. It also shows the bittersweet schedule of life, where sweet, fun moments are often interspersed with sad ones, but we must make the best of the good moments while they last, and use that to conquer the sad ones. Great work to the team, and I will definitely be looking forward to more Triple Topping in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: *Sometimes all it is is a good story.*It’s been a while since a game has had such an impact on me! This is a mix between a point & click, an adventure game and a collection of stories. It’s fairly short but I’d much rather play shorter games that thrill and wow and touch me at every turn, than any of the AAA ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ being made these days. The ending of this game had me teary. Oh my gosh I’m so curious to see what Triple Topping do next!!
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: This is my review right after playing Welcome to Elk and let me tell you, as the credits came up - my eyes started tearing up and it's not the first time I cried during this game. Welcome to Elk is cathartic. I felt so present and I couldn't stop playing. I played for roughly over 9 hours which is quite a lot for the price I got it for. I heard, watched and read moving stories and I was pleasantly surprised with the way the stories were presented. When I bought Welcome to Elk, I had no idea what I was walking into - I didn't know the plot, or the characters, or the world and going into the game with such a blank canvas really provided so much space to be vulnerable during the game. This is such an emotional response to Welcome to Elk because it took me to a space that is so personal and well-crafted. The art and characters are gorgeous and it really felt like so much went into this game. I take my hat off to the developers and everybody involved.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a perfect example of storytelling as an art form.Welcome to Elk is an amazing game that uses the medium of video games as a tool in order to tell enhanced stories that will be received and understood by players in a deeper and richer way. It portraits individual stories that are, intense.The game gets personal and the various artistic styles blend very nicely.Totally recommend this game to people who like interesting and alternative interactive narratives.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting Welcome to Elk to be a fun indie game based on the cute art and friendly soundtrack. I wasn't expecting it to come at me with some very emotional and existential storytelling. The team behind Welcome to Elk have done a fantastic job balancing fun and drama, I'd highly recommend taking a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game that really sucks you in and plays with your emotions, but done in such a sweet and caring way. The way each story is told through the game then the full spoken story is so well done it literally left me speechless a few times. I could honestly not recommend this game more, from start to finish I was fully immersed into the world of Elk and the tears of happiness and sadness were well worth it!Gorgeous animation, music fantastically written and the way you can interact with everything is so well done it's an adventure from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Was ininitially captivated by the art style and assortment of mini games, but make no mistake, this is about the stories we tell.  As Frigg, you an embark on the island of Elk and embark on a journey that will hook you in seconds.  To say that much more would be a crime on my part.  If you at all care about gaming narratives, you need to check this one out.  It will send you on an emotional roller coaster unlike any other.  Even though it can be completed in one sitting, it's impact is worth revisiting time and time again.  Very meta.  Very cool.  Pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Only about an hour in at this point and I can already say this was 100% worth the price tag. The stories are beautifully told  I won't spoil anything because this game is best gone into blind, but I will say that if you are a fan of This American Life, or are looking for an interesting, well told story with complex, lovable characters along with a healthy dose of dark humor and a story that invokes a roller coaster of emotions, look no further. Welcome to Elk! I hope you enjoy your stay.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk follows a woman named Frigg who has left the city to take up a carpentry apprenticeship in a small town named Elk located on an island. Upon accepting this apprenticeship position, she expects this part of her life to be calm and boring, however this is not the case. It’s not long after she arrives that she learns that this small community has its own problems, colorful characters, and stories to tell. For better or for worse, she gets involved as quickly as she has always lived there. The game has a short and sweet story and the gameplay is pretty straight forward. She soon discovers that the town is a lot more than what it seems. She finds herself in the middle of a mystery, and it's up to her to uncover the truth. The game will have the player exploring the town and interacting with the locals to uncover the secrets of this small community.This is a lovely game with unique art style, great music and full of real stories that are impactful, some touching some dar. Very nice to see that a Danish indie game dev has made such a wonderful game.You may like to watch some of the game play  of this amazing game. If you like it support the dev by buying the game and if you like my channel, you are welcome to support it as well
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the cheery art style contrasted with the unexpectedly dark and thought-provoking story. Just got to chapter 2, and so far I've loved every second of it. The game takes a lot of inspiration in scandinavian tradition and lore, but it's also got the option of playing the game with danish subs and in-game writing. While this won't affect most people, it's an awesome feature for someone who has never played a game with such adult themes in his mother language. It's appreciated!Ultimately it's easy to tell that a lot of love has been put into Welcome To Elk! and it definitely deserves the praise.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Klumben ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wrecked me. This was such a beautiful and unique way to tell people's stories, there's just so much life to them. Definitely makes me want to go out and collect more people's stories. Even the things we might find mundane can have so much to them we don't even realize. Amazing story-telling, interesting mix of art styles, 10/10 walk cycles, definitely made me cry in ways I wasn't expecting to. I wish there were more games/experiences like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Elk is a biographical adventure set on an island like no other, where every character you encounter has a story to tell. From the weird and wonderful to the dark and desperate, all the tales told on Elk are based on true stories of life on the road less traveled.
_childDocuments_.name: Welcome to Elk

name: NERVE
detailed_description: Key Features NERVE is an arcade racing game focused on progression and mastery featuring: Vibrant and intense abstract visuals Original soundtrack by Gustavo Coutinho Over 100 unique handcrafted Zones Gate Keeper Boss battles! Freeplay World Select mode with global leaderboards In NERVE you play as a fragile ball of light racing along an endless cylindrical path. Your journey will take you through portals to different ever more threatening Worlds, whose common defining trait is that they all want you dead. Race through each Zone, dodge and destroy obstacles, learn from mistakes, master every World. Conquer the Campaign Race through 10 alien Worlds, each ending with a battle against a Gate Keeper that blocks your path. Use the unique mechanics you've learned from their World to defeat them. Dominate the Leaderboards Each World has a global leaderboard scoring system so players can see how they fare against their friends and other players around the world.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid Thumper player, this game checks all of my boxes.-dark atmosphere-killer soundtrack, heavy drums-high speed, high intensity-high skill ceilingThe game makes use of all of its mechanics, all of the time. So even though you are encouraged to go fast, there are points where you can't always be turbo-ing. USE THE BRAKES!Solid game, and I'm only on world 4. 10/10EDIT:After completing the game, I have to recommend it even more.And the devs are receptive to feedback and are improving the game! There were several unfun issues with a few objects and hitboxes, which have been patched, making this an even better speed game.
_childDocuments_.name: NERVE

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game! Fast paced with a fantastic soundtrack! The sound design flows fantasically with the stage, adapting to your speed and progression. Levels are challenging and usually not outright unfair.In previous versions, particular levels became an unfortunately memory game. Whilst memory is still important, a lot of the unnecessary gotcha level design has been reworked to a fluid and globally consistant structure. Moving objects clearly marked and particular traps have clear tells to how they now behave (Looking at you level 6 snare traps).It isnt fully without it's flaws, however. Bugs do exist and occasionally disrupt the flow of the game. They are, to my experience however, few and far between enough and only become an issue when dabbling with experimental settings.Some RNG and overall timing can sometimes unfortunatly get in the way also. Some obsticles so not reset on death, meaning moving parts may be in different positions during your nect attempt. With RNG, bosses may use differing numbers of attacks which progress the fight, meaning completion times may be extended. Be aware of this since it could be bothersome if trying to go for leaderboard positions.Overall the experience is fast, intense and a hell of a lot of fun, as of writing this review the game is on sale and worth the price!
_childDocuments_.name: NERVE

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, fast action runner-esque game whit simple, but cool visual and a good soundtrack. Depending on your reaction speed and/or skill this is either gonna be really hard for you or relatively challenging. Has a campaign style world from world mode and what I'm gonna refer to as leaderboard mode, where you compete with other players for a high score of the fastest time.

_childDocuments_.review: Nerve is a classic hidden gem. It's a tragedy that a game this polished somehow lingers in obscurity on Steam. And I don't entirely understand why. (I suspect that the game wasn't sufficiently polished on launch and hence got some suboptimal metacritic scores, but since those launch reviews the game has gotten half a dozen patches.)Anyway, this is a fantastic game in the same overarching genre as Thumper, Bit.Trip Runner, or Super Hexagon. Instead of a rhythm theme, here you can adjust your speed, and the game challenges you to complete zones at a breakneck pace. Judged as an ultra-stylish and eminently enjoyable runner & obstacle-dodger, I found NERVE pretty remarkable.I liked the game's aesthetics, and one can tell how it looks from the trailer. Something that may not be entirely apparent, though, is that this game has handcrafted worlds and zones. So you can master each zone both during the campaign and for speedrunning. And the level design is creative, varied, and just orders of magnitude better than the needless procedural generation many indie games suffer from. Finally, there's just a lot of game here: 10 worlds à 10 zones each, including a boss at the end of each world.I also really liked the design of the controls and game mechanics, and how they impact the game's difficulty.First of all, the variable speed mechanic is really clever: the game scores you only on your speed in each zone, whereas deaths are irrelevant (and you respawn with absolutely zero delay). So for each zone or obstacle, you can always choose between going faster to get a higher score, or going slower in exchange for less risk. To do that, there's a boost button (1.5x speed), a brake button (go slower), and later on a focus button (rotate twice as fast but go half as fast; plus the game clock slows down significantly).Secondly, while the game is presented as difficult, and getting the S-rating in levels certainly is, I think overall this design might allow for a pretty accessible experience: the ability to brake and focus as much or as little as you want essentially gives the game a fantastic dynamical difficulty.Other than that, there's a miscellany of smart design decisions. For instance, each world ends in a boss fight with multiple phases, but crucially there's a checkpoint after each phase. Or: My hands hurt after holding the boost button for hours, so I worried this was one of those games that induce RSI (repetitive strain injury) - but no, there's a setting which allows you to toggle abilities like boost or brake instead. (As a side note, tough, I played the game on a controller and can't really imagine playing it without one.)That's not to say the game is perfect. Occasionally, the collider of a few obstacles felt very slightly too big, i.e. I had a few cases where I figured I could squeak by obstacles, then repeatedly collided with them. The boss fights for worlds 7-9 were way too long for my taste (regular zones take <30 seconds to complete if you don't die; these had ~3 phases à >1 min each). And there's an experimental setting to increase the boost multiplier (speed gain from boosting) from 1.5x to 2x, but this doesn't disable achievements and can be used on the leaderboards, so the optimal choice for competitive play would be to always leave it on, which is rather yikes for something labelled as "experimental". But you can just ignore that setting while playing through the campaign, like I did.Anyway, I'm overall just so very impressed by this game O_o. It's a masterclass in its genre.Highly recommended.

name: West of Dead
detailed_description: Purgatory, Wyoming, 1888. A place of gun smoke and darkness, sin and damnation, wendigos and witches. A shifting, chaotic world that takes its form from the memories, culture or beliefs of the souls who pass through. When a dead man awakens with only the memory of a figure in black, he sets into motion a chain of events that have truly mythic consequences. Step into the boots of the dead man William Mason (voiced by Ron Perlman) and descend into the grim and gritty world of Purgatory in this cover-based shooter which combines the fluidity of twin-stick controls and tactical cover usage. Put your skills to the test - Dodge behind cover as you try to outgun your enemies in the unknown procedurally generated hunting grounds. The Wild West has never been this dark.

_childDocuments_.review: is an action rogue-like that’s set in a dark wild west purgatory that you’ll have to fight through to uncover how your character died. Visually this game is extremely appealing, however, what lurks beneath the darkness is messy gameplay that doesn’t feel satisfying or addicting to play compared to other rogue-likes.• The lighting is a very unique mechanic that plays a key part in combat• Games atmosphere is fantastic• Dark and gloomy graphics set the atmosphere extremely well• Simplistic and dark soundtrack that adds another layer to the gloomy and dark environments• For a rogue-like it lacks variety in every area• Weapons are standard, nothing unique or exciting about them• Unlocking new weapons, items and trinkets is a massive grind• Fixed camera angles lead to not being able to see inside some of the rooms without just running into them• The melee enemies throw the cover and shoot combat out the window• Lacks polish and refinement making it feel like an early access game• Some enemies can hit you even if you’re behind cover• AI can be dumb sometimes• Unbalanced difficulty• NPCs dialogue is practically pointless half the time• Game is clearly designed for a controller rather than a keyboard and mouse• Day 1 DLC (Cut content)• Sometimes when vaulting over cover you might go through it instead of over it• Whenever you pick up your first rifle on a new run you will always get a tutorial about how to use sets itself up to be a cover-based shooter and for the most part, it succeeds at it, the early levels definitely get you into the mindset of having to take cover and wait for the right moment to shoot at enemies. However, this falls apart when the introduction of melee enemies comes into play, these enemies will come running at you and if you're taking cover you are practically forced to retreat out of the room whilst shooting at them. This then becomes a problem when the other enemies start walking towards you and you find yourself in a narrow corridor with no cover.You’ll see a number of different enemies as you explore the different areas of purgatory, however most of them felt like reskins of earlier enemies and some of them are just annoying. For example, you’ll eventually come across healers who constantly run away from you, considering there will be at least another two enemies constantly shooting at you at different times, it's hard to kill the healer without taking damage. The pathing for the AI can be pretty bad as well sometimes if you go into another room with an enemy following you they just try to beeline to you and consequently just walk into the corner of the room they’re in.The most interesting mechanic of  is the way that the lighting affects the combat. Rooms that you enter will be partly pitch black with enemies scattered around, sometimes hiding in the darkness and sometimes just standing in the open. You can light up these areas by interacting with lanterns which will also stun nearby enemies giving you a chance to take cover. Unfortunately, this becomes a problem with the fixed camera angles, if you're running towards the camera going into a room you will have no idea of where the enemies might be or where the lanterns are. You’ll have to blindly run into the room, find the first lantern you see, interact with it and then quickly find cover before you get shot. As with any rogue-like you can expect procedurally generated levels with every new run which is meant to give the player more variety and encouragement to try again after losing. However, with the lack of variety in terms of enemies and the different rooms in areas, every run feels almost the exact same. Even when it comes to weapons, there was always a specific set I was on the lookout for because it was just better than the others. Even the weapons lack variety and you’ll more than likely just pick up the ones that do more damage rather than weapons that do significantly less damage but cause different effects (bleeding, plague etc.). Overall, for a rogue-like, there is just a lack of variety to differentiate one run from another and to encourage the player to try again after losing.Speaking of weapons, unlocking them is a relentless grind that doesn’t feel rewarding. You’ll get roughly 10 - 20 Sin every floor from random enemies you kill (assuming you clear out every room on that floor), considering there are a lot of weapons, trinkets and items to unlock (some of them require over 300 sin to unlock) it's quite a daunting task. Compare this to other rogue-like games like  and you’ll find that you can unlock a bunch of new weapons within the first few hours of that game and it feels satisfying and exciting to unlock them. After a couple hours of playing  I think I only unlocked a handful of cheap weapons that I didn’t even like the sound of but unlocked them just for the sake of having a more variety of weapons.Difficulty is another aspect of a rogue-like that’s important to get right and unfortunately  doesn’t get this right either. The first floor is fine, you're given a lot of space with few enemies to learn the way that the game works. But after this you're greeted with a difficulty spike that doesn’t get any easier, in the second area you’ll find some enemies can kill you in a hit or two, some can hit you even when you're behind cover and with the previously mentioned melee enemies it just completely throws the cover and gun combat out the window. You’ll eventually find other enemy types as you progress like healers, which are a complete pain since they run away from you and cause you to get hit by the other enemies who are shooting at you. I just ran through these rooms without bothering to kill them because it caused more frustration and I wasn’t even guaranteed anything rewarding for my efforts to kill them besides the  of getting 1 - 3 sin.The soundtrack is simplistic and adds a sense of mystery of awareness to every area you explore. Even though there doesn’t seem to be much variety it still provides a rather gloomy and dark atmosphere with the visuals.The one thing this game has going for it is the art style, it definitely fits a dark wild west purgatory from the way that your character is designed to the enemies that you encounter. Every new area you explore is dark and grim which creates this fantastic atmosphere along with the soundtrack.Despite all the negatives I really wanted to enjoy , the art style peaked my curiosity but what followed was a disappointment. The gameplay suffers tremendously and doesn’t feel encouraging or addicting to start a new run after failing the previous one. It feels like an Early Access game with its lack of polish and general balancing issues. There are definitely much better rogue-likes out there than this one, I wouldn’t recommend getting this one unless you're desperate for a new rogue-like.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just give you a short and juicy reviewPros:*This game has an amazing art style! Everything you see just feels new (which is rare to see in video games now) and everything just fits together perfectly *Fun combat. Big variety of guns and they all have their little perks, making it possible to create different "builds" to get through the game and changing up how you approach enemies Cons:*Taking cover is a big part in this game and it works well, but it feels very sticky. When you're fighting a big boss or have a bunch of guys coming at you, you're rolling and dodging all over the place, but your character will just snap to cover and when you try rolling away it just takes you to a different cover spot or a different direction entirely *Progression feels good in this game, but it has some flaws. This isn't really a con, but it sure isn't a pro. once you die you have to restart from the beginning, which isn't a big surprise considering this is a roguelike. But the game can get very repetitive, they're four chapters in this game and once you die you start from chapter one... every time. Chapters one-three take around an hour each, so imagine you're almost done with the game and you die because your camera wasn't showing the enemy shooting at you, so now you have to go through all those chapters again and again until you get good enough rng to get good weapons and beat it. And yes, i know that you're suppose to die so you can make some permanent upgrades to your character, but no one wants to go through the same levels 20+ times to beat a game. *The camera is by far this games biggest flaw, it does have it's moments when you step into a big room full of enemies and you just see an overhead view of your character fighting away and dodging all the bullets, but this usually isn't the case. Your camera will most likely pan around, not revealing the enemy you're shooting at or sometimes you can't even see yourself! All the other cons are just little annoying things or stuff that didn't work well, but no matter how hard you try you can't like a game if you can't see it!Final thoughts: This game is a fun experience, it has some replayability but if you've already beaten the game you're probably already worn out of the levels. I would NOT RECOMMEND to buy this at FULL PRICE, but if you find a good deal on it it can be a lot of fun. This game feels like it has all the building blocks made but just wasn't put together correctly. It has good mechanics, cool gun ideas, bosses and different areas. But I feel like the movement and actually playing it is just a pain. I give this an official Gluurb review of 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I personally love this game, but it's a difficult sell in some regards.It's the kind of game indie games have needed since FTL: something that takes the mechanics of a beloved game genre, encases them in a creative and appealing setting with a killer soundtrack, and provides a familiar but unique experience to players across generations. It's got a great gameplay loop, satisfying kills, and plenty of challenge. However, it's let down by some odd (but rare for me, anyway) bugs, too many useless "dead-end" weapon unlocks, and a bad difficulty curve caused mostly by overinflated health values.West of Dead starts out slowly, since the player is supposed to fight enemies and cash in "sin" (unlock points) for more unlocks (weapons, usable items, passive trinkets, and gameplay features). Players are supposed to fight, acquire and cash in sin, then eventually die. This is all fine and good, until the player starts unlocking more weapons.My first gripe with the game is that the more the player unlocks, the worse the equipment RNG gets for subsequent runs. I remember getting pretty far in the beta and getting used to the gameplay loop to the point where when the game released, I breezed through the first three levels without a second glance. Eventually I died at the Farm for my first death, and cashed in my sin. I was surprised at how many cool-sounding weapons there were that were possibly available to me. For subsequent runs, I wasn't afraid of dying after cashing in a level or three of sin: it was all just a step closer to cooler guns and items to use. Well... that's not how it went. Here are some examples of in-game buyer's remorse that continue to haunt me:This list could  go on, and it annoys me that it could. I've often found myself in this position with games like this, going "yes, not  gun  to be good, but not as bad as this". It goes hand-in-hand with my next gripe: the health (and damage) scaling of opponents is absolutely insane and there aren't enough stat boosts and good weapon drops in the game to keep up. I've gotten to the Church and Churchyard several times with high stats across the board, and it  isn't enough to make it through. What might've been fine in the Town quickly becomes borderline useless. No one I know has been able to actually make it past the Church, and looking at the achievement stats for West of Dead, only 1.4% of the playerbase have beaten the Canyon. 1.3% have been able to beat the Church. Obviously practice makes perfect and I'll probably beat the Church by hitting that level enough and preparing myself for every dumb encounter I could possibly have there, but the investment for doing so is  too much, in my opinion.With the bugs they've had and the gameplay mechanic issues I've outlined, Arcade Fury probably should have taken it into Early Access. However, to their credit, they've just added a lot of good quality of life features and the ability to aim at opponents hidden in the dark manually on July 1st, 2020. I really hope Arcade Fury keeps working at West of Dead so this game can truly shine as a recommendation, but I like the game enough to still recommend buying it. It definitely has the sauce.

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead is one of those typical games that had a rough start, but over time grew to become what the devs have initially planned it to be - from its buggy beginnings, lack of KB & M support and being practically devoid of content, in a period of one year it managed to arrive at the point where I would consider it to be a pretty challenging game with a well-narrated story full of mystery - albeit with its own design-flaws which mare the experience quite a bit.The pros of the game are the setting, visuals, general gameplay and music: the Weird West sort-of otherworldly experience is a perfect match for rogue-lite gameplay, the player traversing the Purgatory over and over again trying to figure who he is and what's he up against. Visuals are well done, evocative of Mignola's style of stark contrasts and deep, pitch-black shadows, and the music is somber, reflects what is happening on the screen, and appropriate for this setting (but it gets quite repetitive after 10 hours or so). Overall, the elements for what I consider to be a "pretty good" game are all there, but...The cons that are the apparent lack of content and insane grind outweigh the good parts - I know this is a roguelite and that the devs want you to play the game over and over again , but what IS in the game content-wise is SEVERELY lacking, and the unlockables are progressing at a snails pace. I managed to finish the entire game in 8-9 hours, and after continuing to pursue grindy achievements to 100% the game (i.e. a full 17 hours (!) later), I can tel you that I cannot recommend this game. First off, the Good Soul achievement relies too much on RNG - you can play through the ENTIRE game and encounter maybe one lost soul (or none at all), which is unacceptable since you need 50 (!?) for the 3rd rank of that achievement. As a matter of fact, getting to those 50 souls took me 17 hours, nearly double the amount I needed to beat the game fully.Next is the weapon unlock system - you basically have to not only have luck in order to make those remnants (which unlock items and weapons) drop at all, but you must then power them up with in-game currency called "sins" that may or may not drop from enemies you kill. And considering that there are quite a few unlock with 30+ cost, and some at 50+ sins requirement (and gaining around 12 sins per map), well.... it is a very lame unlock system, to be frank.Thirdly, the devs could have capitalized big-time on adding more game related achievements that actually make sense and go hand-in-hand with their design logic to extend play time - like "Collect all items in the game" or "Beat the game on Deputy/Gunslinger/Sheriff/Marshal difficulty" or "Beat the game without refilling your HP flask" etc., yet the devs have failed to do so. Having an achievement to drive you to beat the game on harder difficulty (I completed the game on Gunslinger, mind you) would alleviate a LOT of problems with grind I listed above, because in trying to surmount the challenge would the grindy parts balance themselves (as in you would get to those required numbers of saved souls and dead outlaws more naturally, without having to resort to fulfilling them artificially).Since the devs have gone radio-silent since 12 May 2021 (their last game update), I have little hope of them polishing this game to reflect the cons I listed in this review - really sad, since I find that the game could really be something else than just a quick 9-hour affair, the rest being just achievement hunting for completionist sake (and not a pleasant one at that). Getting West of Dead on a deep, DEEP sale would be my final recommendation ($9 or less, to reflect what you actually get for your money). There was never a game that made me feel like I was in real-life Purgatory, doing the same grindy chore over and over until I earned my way to Heaven (or Hell, since I feel like a rotten corpse grinding this achievemenbt stuff).

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start this review by saying WoD could be a really great game. The good things are very good, and the bad things are (to me) confusing choices the devs made, that look like the game was never properly finished / tested. For starters, the game was released full of bugs, and even after a lot of patches, some still make an appearance once in a while.The game's graphics make it look like a comic book, and I personally love that.The voices are also great, and Ron was a great choice for the part.The sounds FX and music have its moments of brilliance - I could do without some of the door breaking samples.The game's most appropriate tag is indeed action roguelike, but don't expect a huge amount of action, and it's a very short rogue to be honest. The game can be finished from chapter 1 to chapter 4, in about 3 hours (once you master the mechanics). That's 2 runs from start to finish, maybe 3 in order to pick up some extra "runes". The game flow is quite balanced, and feels smooth as you go from room to room, taking a few enemies at a time, and exploring a bit more of the map (even if there isn't really much to explore). Some players could find it slow though. This is not a shoot'em'up, and even if you can get weapons that discharge a lot of bullets (like revolvers), it just doesn't pay off when you can have the same damage (or more) with two shots from a shotgun. Unfortunately, after a while it does get a bit repetitive, as it stops being challenging, and here comes the weird part - unlike other roguelike games, where it gets easier the more runs you make and items you unlock, WoD's inventory is mostly made of redundant items. Most of the time, unlocking a new weapon ends up making the game harder for you.The basic weapons that are already unlocked from the start - double barrel shotgun and double barrel pistol - are good enough, and in comparison, better than most of the other stuff you unlock: so once again, unlocking new (worse) items and weapons will make the game harder.My advice is to unlock the health flasks, shield, lantern, stay with the defender charm, and you may discard everything else.To make it "better" (not), in order to unlock these items you use "Sin" - Sin is dropped randomly when killing enemies (but each level has a max sin amount you can pick up). You then spend that Sin gradually to unlock new items. So to make it quick, Sin is scarce, and a lot of items have an excessive Sin cost - meaning, you may accumulate a lot of sin from a lot of runs to unlock a certain weapon, and after getting it realize that the weapon is crap, unbalanced, low damage, or has some other downsides that just make it unworthy, but now it will pop up occasionally on your runs - congrats: you just made it harder on yourself.So, do I still recommend it? Yeah... this is still a good game, but it comes with some disappointments for me. It has some interesting mechanics and ideas that may keep the player entertained for a few hours, but once you understand how the enemies work and finish the game, there just isn't any incentive to continue playing - and I'm stating this after having spent over 100 hours on it (and closely the same amount of the Betas).There's a lot of potential for greatness, but the great things on this game set up the bar at a level the rest of the game just fails to reach.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like the Binding of Isaac? Would you be OK replacing Isaac's bullet hell dungeon with cover-based shooting? Would you be OK replacing Isaac's cartoon purgatory with a wild-west purgatory? Would you be OK replacing Isaac's 45 enemies and 43 bosses with 19 enemies and 3 bosses? Can you tolerate a 2-weapon looter shooter system where you guns get weaker every level if you don't swap them out with other random guns? Can you tolerate a cover-based shooting system that is fundamentally buggy, often simply does not work, and will never be patched? If you answered yes to all of the above, West of Dead may be for you. Buy it on sale for $2.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's setting – Purgatory, a place suspended between hell and heaven presents a great alegory as to where this game sits. It has some very nice qualities such as varied weaponry, distinct visual artstyle and of course Ron Perlman as the game's protagonist. 	Unfortunately, there are numerous issues preventing West of Dead to ascend into the gaming heaven. Numerous bugs and glitches, unengaging storyline, lack of boss variety, day one DLC offering cut content.	This is a good product for 5 – 10 hours playtime. After that the repetitiveness hits and player starts to realise that what seemed to be a sprawling, deep system allowing for various builds is actually very limited. Each run starts to feel similar. In my opinion, that's the biggest flaw of the game.   	My time spent with the game was actually quite fine but I can't recommend this title. In a crowded market of indie roguelikes and rogue-lites West of Dead, while made in a competent way lacks the longevity and staying power. _childDocuments_.review: Another game for which I wish there was a neutral option.I was intrigued by its aesthetic - Old West meets Purgatory - and who better to guide you through it than the great Ron Perlman? So the hook is definitely there. The actual fundamentals, however, are a pretty shaky.All roguelikes, especially procedurally-generated ones, have some combination of grinding and pure luck built into them - you never know if you're going to get decent weapons and items, so the only solution is to play over and over until you do. The best games in the genre come up with ways to keep this loop fresh, but West of Dead can't figure that aspect out after the first few hours and settles into a rather tedious rhythm it never really gets out of. Much of it is down to the basic gameplay - movement and combat walk a fine line between deliberately slow and mechanically clunky but often end up being the latter, particularly the sticky cover system and the uncontrollable camera hampering your ability to aim. I found that favoring rapid-fire guns served me much better than actually taking the time to line up shots, mainly because the aggressive enemies and destructible terrain force you to be in constant motion. There is a decent progression system in that permanent upgrades allow you to access parts of the map you couldn't before, but it caps rather quickly and levels soon become tedious treks back and forth. The devs recognized this and implemented a fast travel system but were undercut by the randomization, which occasionally puts several portals close together and then makes you run for large stretches. And for a game now two years old, I'm a bit dismayed by some of the glitches still present (graphics warping out of proportion, sound cutting out in certain cutscenes).A decent ride at a heavy discount, but not a rodeo I'm keen to revisit.
