_childDocuments_.review: A wild west action, cover based Roguelike game is the best way to summerise this game. With Ron Pearlman voicing the main character. Having the looks of a wild west Ghost rider. What's not to like? Well...The good: First The game has a very unique art style which makes it easier to run on older machines. Second just like Dead cells and other Roguelikes, you can unlock whatever you want when you grind a couple of runs. Third, spamming dodge does not work you need to time the dodge right before the bullet/attack hits you the get max Invulnerabilty (Bad english i know) frames. This way the game will slow down and you can get a moment to take a breath and get the shot you need to kill your enemies. Fourth, the way line of sight works is interesting, if enemies are covered in darkness there are harder to hit and your character can miss, despite how sharp your aim is, but if they are covered in light, even if your aim is not that good the game gives you a little aim assist on those enemies and lands most shots. You'd think this makes the game too easy but once you get to the later levels like the Church, Canyon and so on. Lanterns become more rare and you have to hit them before lighting them up to see your enemies. Alternatively there are shortcuts to help you skip the game, but be aware. Skipping levels can hinder you, as you only get 1 random weapon for using them and forfeit a couple of permanent upgrades on your run. Which could hinder you considering 1 of the upgrades is straight up gun damage, while the other one is Health and melee damage. The story is layed out through bits of memory you collect when slaying enemies or helping NPC's. Thank god they reduced the punishement for helping NPC's to taking more damage, it used to be death in 1 hit... YUP....The bad: Sticky cover can ♥♥♥♥ your momentum sometimes, I've had a couple of bug in the past but it seems that developers might have squashed most of them. The camera can work against you sometimes, focusing on you instead of where you are aiming, preventing you from locating your enemies sometimes, forcing you to go closer.The ugly: The way the controls work for PC compared to consoles. Having to use "C" to skip cut scenes or dialogue makes it very clunky. This is definitely better on console compared to PC if you are talking about controls responsiveness.Overall score: A very solid 7/10A breath of fresh air from Rogue like games, not the best, but not the worst! Worth a try on its own or when on sale!

From what was being shown with some interesting gameplay looked very promising and I wanted to try it out. Then it hit me, looks can be deceiving. What I got was a game that had a ton of issues that makes the game not polished in any way.   The year is 1888.  is brought back to life and awakes in a strange bar, there he meets a barkeeper, who tells him that he is in  and finds out that he has no memories of who he is. So, he sets out to go and find his memories while fighting enemies and getting answers to his past. That is all that I can remember from . The story makes no sense and is entirely forgettable. The characters have nothing special to them in any shape or form and they don’t even speak, all they do is repeat the same textboxes every single time with nothing new to say. They are not even worth interacting with, literally, the only character that actually develops is  himself and he is also completely forgettable as well. Whenever I got a new memory from him, I forgot about it five minutes later and it never made sense in the first place. It’s just that empty with nothing interesting going on and it’s sad to see that as there are some nice ideas that it had going for it.   is a top-down shooter with many gameplay issues. There is a cover mechanic where that protects you from getting shot. The problem here is that some enemies are melee-based, so it’s completely thrown out the window with some enemies, as they will actually go through the wall you are behind, which will result in you getting hit. The gameplay is also very buggy, one time I was hit by an enemy in which  completely disappeared and it resulted in my death, or when you start a new run you will always get a tutorial on how to use the rifles. The rifles are not really useful as the hitboxes on them were small and sometimes did not hit the target. That is also another issue, the weapons are not really worth using, as I always ended up using the same weapons,  and  were the two weapons I went after, no other weapon I came across was worth using. However, getting weapons is a huge grind on its own. To get weapons and abilities, you will need , however, to get that, you will need to kill the enemies that are in the areas, there are two problems with this. The first problem is that the stuff you want to get will cost at least 100, 200, 300, or more  and the second problem is that you will only get a certain amount depending on the area you are in, as there is a limit on how much you can get per level. Games like  will give you many opportunities to get  and the game rewards you for beating the levels in a certain amount of time or killing a certain number of enemies.  Every time I died, I felt a pit in my stomach open, as I did not feel encouraged to do another run. Sometimes you will fight these mini-bosses called  and they are fun to fight when they work. They will either stand still or jump over the cover spots and not fight back. There are also some bosses you will fight and they were ok but not at all memorable and fun. The one thing I have to give the game some credit where credit is due is the lighting mechanic. The rooms you will enter will be all dark and you have to light them up to see them. This will stun the enemies and you will have a chance to kill them more easily.  My favourite thing about  is the art style. I love the dark cartoony atmosphere that the game has going it felt. It shows us how dark and messed up  actually is, something that I enjoyed. I tested the game on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, 16 GB of RAM, and an AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Quad-Core Processor 3.50. The game does run really well at 60 FPS.  Now I have to admit that the soundtrack for this game is awesome. I loved the guitar jiggle that would play after every battle you do; it just feels so fresh. The  theme is my favourite song to listen to, it’s just a shame that they are sometimes buggy to fight against as the theme is just that good. Makes you feel like you really are in a fight with a gunslinger.  I really wanted to like . It had promise and potential to be a unique game out of the  genre. However, what I was presented with was a game that had a forgettable story, broken combat, weapons that are not worth using, pointless grinding, and a feeling of just wanting to quit playing. _childDocuments_.review: What you are reading right now is an update after I finally finishing the game, The 30 minutes - in version can be found down below after this review.Let me start with an apologize first, For a bit "overly positive attitude" I put on the previous review of this game. But you see, I'm quite expecting a lot of this game since the beta. The game has potential. But after finishing the whole game I think I finally deducted more through conclusion than my previous review. I'll try to address them as specific as possible.Mainly, The gameplay and its mechanics1. The game was a twin stick shooter. Most of the time it work very well. Your controlling mechanic encourage you to think more before barging into each room. This is a very reason I love West of Dead in Beta. However, This mechanic will start to burden you down as you progress more into the game. After the Mine. Most of enemy type will force you to move around very quickly and this is where problem start to shown.- Your movement when taking cover (which by the way, is automatically done, no dedicate button) was slow and prone to glue you to the cover. Combine with charging in enemies, Well, I died a lot because of this- The auto lock system really messed the game up so bad, Especially when there are a lot of enemies in one room, Combine with "Shadow mechanic" where you can't properly lock on to enemies hiding in shadow, The game felt very frustrate just because I missed my very last shot on "about to be dead enemies" by this messing up auto lock system or when I use power up projectile, Instead of locking on enemies. The game just locking on another objects in the room instead.2. The game encourage you to replay it over and over with more upgrades to be unlock. But the problem is the setback itself. When you died, You'll get to restart everything over again. No exception, No rare item to assist you or anything, You died you restart EVERYTHING from the scratch again. And since the last part of the game require you to go through whole streak of "Burden" (One shot and you get an insta killed). This system really took away all the fun from the game that dying suppose to get you more excite instead of desperation.3. The unlock items are not at all very synergize or fun to use, They feel "Separate" and very inconsistent to use. The game try to put on an effect on specific weapons and items to be used together. But that's not enough to make you feel confident on your load out at all. The game may allow you to use 2 different type of weapons but its not dual-wield kind. Its like you can only have 2 guns that you can't be using simulteneously and can't be reload separately too. 4. And the boss, That Injustice, Whoever design this fight should be hang. Seriously, This is where every flaws I am mentioned on this game shining so bright it just so infuriated. You have to upgrade exactly so you won't get 1 hit kill, You have to plan specific loadout (good luck with a game base on RGN) and lastly you have to fulfill a specific condition so you won't make a Pikachu face when you realize that you have to find all your old pals before beating the last boss, Or you'll have to start over again from the start.I feel terrible, I really love the look of this game but the gameplay is not very consistent on giving you that much fun. I am still going to recommended it though. If you are a rouge lite junky and want to find a fix. West of Dead was for you. But if you are new or just want to have a thrilled. Don't, Just don't.**************** Here's my old review****************West of Dead was a rogue lite twin stick dungeon shooter. Which at this point, There are so much number of games in this genre out there but what made West of Dead standing out are two things. The Aesthetic and The Voice over.Let's cut the chase and get to the game play first. As you very much already expecting, The game is a twin stick shooter same in a flesh if you are already playing something like Dead cells or Hades. Most of your weapons are guns, Pistol, Shotgun and Rifle each gave you a different stats for you to play the game as you like, Always take cover (which doesn't last that long) and take a shot, Sure. Go full throttle and ballets around enemies, You got it. Mix and match of both, Still got it. And a higher level weapon also give you some effect boost to improve you quality of life as you venture deeper into this dark west of purgatory.And yes the game feel really dark and gritty. Like in the original Mike Mignola's Hellboy....which brought us to the main selling point of this game. The Aesthetic and voice over. The game feel so much straight out of Mignola's artwork, The shadow cover every inches of the dungeon and can only be perish with the lamps (Also help temporary lock stun enemies) combine with that low but charming voice of Ron Pearlman. Well, This is going to be one epic game for you to play through, I can assure you that.As for the cons part... Well here's the lists- No vibration for controller- The voice over volume was so low, It need to be boosting up a bit more.- The enemies AI need a little tweak, They seem to be a bit slower than in the Beta.- This is a bit personal but I think I could use more graphic tweaking options, Just saying.So far so good. The game was the same as you've got on Beta but better. More weapons, More equipment and more fun. As for the DLCs, Well I think adding a little bit more into dev's cookies jar doesn't hurt that much. :)

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to recommend this game, I simply can't. Let's start with some of the positives. There is a lot of charm to this game. Ron Perlman's voice and the soundtrack for this game are amazing, and set up the vibe really well. The guns and tools are also relatively fun to use, even though I would generally gravitate towards a very limited selection. It also features a system similar to dead cells for unlocking new weapons and tools. West of Dead had every tool it needed to succeed but it failed in the most important place: the gameplay. This is where the cons begin, and boy is there a lot of them. To start, movement in this game unfortunately feels absolutely awful. The controls are sticky and really only work on controller, but even then they feel very clunky. The combat is centered around a cover-based system, but your character rarely goes to cover the way you expect. I get what they were going for but it does not play out well. The weapons are also unfortunately a letdown. Even though there is a wide variety of weapons, there are only a few choices that are really good. The rest either all feel similar or are just not good, so the most viable strategy is to just not unlock most of the weapons. This makes the replayability very low compared to other roguelikes, especially considering I got the "true" ending in about 10 hours. Finally, the bugs. By far the most frustrating thing about this game. To just list a few, I frequently encountered a bug where I couldn't get past the witch because I couldn't spend my souls. At some points, my character would just turn invisible. Even though some of these bugs could just be a silly visual thing that didn't matter, quite a fair few literally softlocked my game. I'm not really sure how these issues are still in the game 4 years after launch.Overall, I think this game is not worth the purchase, even on sale. I refunded the game before buying it again to give it another shot, and I really wish I didn't. It will leave you grasping at what could have been and disappointed by its lack of replayability and responsiveness.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is a staple of this game and it's... bad. Game doesn't reward you for any kind of precise shooting, your cowboy can miss 3 consecutive shots in a row at target in 5 meters. Even my grandma shoots better and she's almost blind. _childDocuments_.review: I really would like to love this game for its innovative gunplay with roguelite element and its' narrative. I even buy the DLC after some play though, Though, I sadly admit that the clunky movement control and game breaking bug that cause the player's character model to disappear if you just happens to stand in the same location that the obstacle respawn and some how even cause the character to fall through the ground making it unable to continue the run. _childDocuments_.review: I just can't get into this one.Edit: I've beaten the game (well, I "could" do another run to get the "true" ending, but I've beaten the final boss, which is not at all difficult). I honestly can't think of a reason why I would ever touch this game again. I did get better at the combat, but the game still feels lackluster. I guess, you "could" try out new weapons, but in the end everything is either a pistol, a long range gun or a shotgun, so why? The game's enemy variety and combat flow don't make any of these unlockables interesting, because at the end of the day it's going to be the same over and over again.Played one session basically, reached the Preacher for the 2nd time, almost had him, died, restart from the beginning. Bleah.Yes, it's a rogue-lite that's meant to be played over and over again and is different each time, because you can choose different characters, perks, weapons, bonuses, levels, etc.However, West for Dead doesn't have anything like that really. There's only ever one character with no perks whatsoever, the bonuses are just flat percent increases of health, damage, etc. and are always the same. And the weapons are frankly boring and nothing special, so why would I care about unlocking them if a simple shotgun + pistol combo carried me all this way on my first run?The gameplay itself isn't terrible, but just not engaging enough to warrant me spending more time with this game. The graphics are unique, sound and music is good, voice acting, alright, I guess, there's not much of it anyway, but the clunky mouse and keyboard controls forced me to use a controller, which is better in terms of movement, but worse in terms of shooting. Even at high aim assist, my rifles keep missing almost point blank shots... that's why I stuck with the shot gun ... and a pistol, because that one reliably hits for some reason, while a musket misses 90% of the time. I feel like I'm playing XCOM.The maps themselves are super boring though. Each one is exactly the same. There's destructible cover from which to shoot, which is pointless without a precise shooting mechanic ... or having to light the torches in the room to even SEE and be able to hit enemies...and there's indestructible cover to hide behind. Enemies are so so, ranging from standard and elite shooters, to bomb throwers, attack dogs, bat swarms and for some reason earth elementals. Not sure what else they have in store, but since I'm halfway through the game kinda ... melee weapons feel very weird to use as well, since they're essentially items. The cover system is also kinda atrocious and can really screw you over with the automatic snap to cover. All in all the combat is just not that engaging.So why grind away? I see no reason to, even the boss fights are boring. They try to hit you in melee you dodge away, they attack you from range, hide behind pillars. Not much more you can do with such a simplistic system. There are great rogue lites out there, West for Dead is at best a 6/10.

There's a bunch of bugs, with some that are quite destructive, but its mostly funny stuff. _childDocuments_.review: The combat is very simple but the different timings with the weapons add a little spice to the mix, making each run feel stylistically different. Sometimes you get just the equipment for a run n' gun, other times its more like a hunker down and dodge everything in a well timed manner type of run. The western style is fully utilized here and feels excellent to be in. if you're a fan of westerns and roguelikes then this is the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the core gameplay loop is great and the art style is on point.I really wanted to like the game but as further I've played it the more frustrating it becomes.Typically for a roguelite you have to start over again after every death and you can only unlock new items and weapons which you you can then obtain in the next run. The problem is that you have no shortcuts and every run is basically 90% the same. You don't know what you need for the next boss and can't really influence what you get in a way this game would need it. Another problem is that have to spend the meta currency for new unlocks which forces you to widen the pool of weapons and items you get. If there would be some sort of possibility to ban very bad weapons and items from occurrence and if you can skip a level if you for example win a single tough fight and get a reward equivalent to the ones in the normal level the game would be great. You can expect to spent an hour per run at some point just to test if you are lucky and get the right weapons at the right item level is just frustrating.I would recommend you wait for a sale and you have to be open for repetiveness.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with great future ahead of it. It has great single character voice acting/narration and an intriguing color pallet. I both love and hate the use of darkness in this game. It sets the mood and it sets the scene, the environment is so very cinematic. So far I've only made it as far as the bayou and despite my continuous struggling and death, this game keeps pulling me into another round. The more I learn about our mysterious protagonist, the more and more I want to know. The game has so many more merits, amazing world building an interesting cast of NPCs and villains I can run across on my each and every attempt. I do have my problems with this game, on several occasions the generated world has created dead ends that made me start new runs. The darkness is amazing, but mixed with the wonderful muted color pallet and the lack of the ability to pan the camera for better view I can find myself confused by lack of contrast and in many rooms, even if lit as entirely as possible, the shadows still overpower the screen. The game is hard and often times frustrating, but it gets better. I hope in the future the developers re-balance the reload speeds, of some of the weapons and this is just wishful thinking, but make a free roam First Person RPG based on this art style and character in this setting. I think with this world and art direction, a stylistic Undead old west Wyoming would be more successful than Zelda: Breath of the wild. The art is original and powerful, enemies are well developed and an amazing hero has been born before us. The world is brilliantly twisted, unforgivingly hard, and hauntingly dismal but in a good story telling way. Bravo, and thank-you. 88/100
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: The old West, sixshooters, shootouts, spaghetti western music, the witch, Ron Pearlman narrating. Need I say more? You had me at 'Ron Pearlman'. _childDocuments_.review: Ok.  West Of Dead does several things really well.  Unfortunately it does several things very poorly as well.  Whether this mix makes it a worthwhile purchase will depend on individual taste I suspect.  Lets demonstrate this mix as follows:The core shooting mechanics here are satisfying.  Though gamepad is mandatory as the M/KB controls are borderline totally unplayable and you can't rebind keys.  Lack of key rebinding is totally and completely unacceptable.  Non Qwerty users? Get ♥♥♥♥♥♥.  ESDF peeps like me? ♥♥♥♥ yourself. Lefties? Tough ♥♥♥♥.The levels and enemies are well done and fun to fight.  But it takes time to unlock teleport between rooms so early game will be spent backtracking through totally empty rooms.  Why?  What possible design imperative is there to force players through empty rooms?  It's literally a complete waste of the players time. Early game is easy giving you a chance to get your bearings and not punishing players for unfamiliarity with a relatively interesting and unique gameplay loop.  But those easy early levels become totally and completely infuriating after those early hours.  Five hours in the first two levels are a waste of time that force you spend 15 minutes with literally no chance of even taking damage to say nothing of dying. In a game that's laid out in chapters why wouldn't the early levels become harder after the player has moved on? With a progression system that's almost an afterthought you don't even have the satisfaction of the early levels in Issac.  You'll never luck into the equivalent of Brimstone in the first level of West Of Dead.  Hell you'll get the same 3 things every single time.There are a ton of weapons to unlock and most feel good to use. But the grind to unlock weapons is truly grotesque.  Literally hours upon hours of grind for one weapon. A weapon can cost 300 Sin.  You get like 10 per floor and a floor takes 10 minutes plus. Worse there is almost zero variety on offer.  You will spend hours unlocking a shotgun to find it is almost exactly the same as the other 3 shotguns.  A rogue-lite MUST have interesting builds and unlocks. That's literally the hook that keeps you playing.  West Of Dead has a nice core loop but there's no reason to push on.  There's nothing more deflating than spending a couple of hours unlocking a rifle that does absolutely nothing to change your game-play experience.Finally the upgrades on the floors are just pathetic.  You choose between more gun damage. More health. More tool damage.  This is unbelievably boring.  These games keep you playing with the possibility of OP builds around the corner.  The game would have been better off NOT letting you choose but pushing up the power of the upgrades.  After 3 floors you're choosing between +8% gun damage or +11% health.  What's here is so polished when it comes to game-play, story and art style, but totally incompetent when it comes to the core, crucial systems and mechanics that make a rogue-lite shine.This game would have massively benefited from NOT being a rogue lite and simply crafting a normal linear progression system to go with a linear game path.  When the rogue lite elements are so half baked at best or superflous at worst you end up with something deeply disappointing.Still, all that said, it DOES have that very enjoyable shooting, and a decent enough storytelling style, and great art design.  So....if the price here is low enough that you're ok with eventually saying "Meh, that was fun enough." then sure, buy it.  I don't feel like I've wasted my money.  But when you stack this game up against peers? Dead Cells, Risk Of Rain 2, BOI, Rogue Legacy, Gungeon, Hades, Nuclear Throne? It looks very, very bad next to those titles.  At the end of the day you're left with a near miss.  A game that does enough well to be worth the money to someone in my financial spot, but not good enough to be worth playing over starting a new Risk Of Rain 2 run.More than anything this game needed another year in the hopper. It needed to spend that time really honing in on why their game is a rogue lite. IF you're not going to create an experience that embraces randomness, build crafting, luck and the possibility of explosive ridiculousness than you need to ask yourself if you're using the wrong genre.  People love rogue-lites for a reason and it's not the basic structure.  Developers need to understand the game they are making.  West of Dead is a game that doesn't know why it's a rogue-lite.  In fact its a game that seems to not want to be a rogue lite at all.  Again, decent enough but ultimately disappointing not for what it does but for what it fails to do.

_childDocuments_.review: This game...its good, but it's not quite great. The pace of the game is very slow at times rather than methodical. The guns as diverse as they appear to be, end up feeling like the 4 base guns of the archetype. Busting down barricades is extremely slow and so is the roll. Healing feels very reluctant than gratifying, also why can't you heal behind cover? The cover is especially broken, enemies will stay behind cover and if you try to sneak up on them while they're about to shoot, they snap around and no scope you right as you were about to get a good shot off. Enemies whip around too fast, it always defeats the purpose of the weapons meant to hit enemy backs. Overall it slow. Your character feels slow. Painfully so. The way he moves does not correspond to the way he looks, making it feel like somethings always being held back. I've played this for 7.5 hours and I like the game, I just keep telling myself "maybe I'm not playing it right", but a rouguelite should be adaptable to all play styles. This games has good bones lol, but it needs to be heavily reworked to be considered fun.I hate to compare it to another game; but Dead Cells is a very good example of a roguelite. You gain speed as you kill enemies and you're rewarded for how fast you beat a level. You're rewarded for being methodical and slow when you do so. This game tho... you're always slow. If you try to play more fast and aggressively, you'll find yourself dying more often. This game and Dead Cells have great things in common. The art, concept, and replayability. They also have similar problems. You'll often times find the blue category of equipment and almost completely forget to use it. They'll seem useful but you'll find very few uses for it. I could go on and on about the problems of this game...Really, I do like this game but it just has too many problems to be the best game it could be,

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are great, the style is really unique.There are some minor bugs that happen sometimes but nothing gamebreaking (except for Chapter 4).In its current state it still has some balance flaws like some weapons overperform others look good on paper but suck when put into action.Some of the shortcut levels are near impossible on Marshal difficulty as getting hit twice by a grenade (Battlefield) or once by the plague effect (Churchyard) is certain death.But regardless of that i enjoyed my time with it.In my opinion its fairly priced and well thought out and executed. 7,5/10.Notable unexplained Mechanics or Bugs:Q: Why does the plague effect keep one hitting me?A: When you suffer from the plague effect its the trail that damages you, keep moving and stay out of it until the effect stops, if you stop moving ur most likely dead or now missing 75% of ur health.When you kill an Outlaw without getting hit once they will drop one of their respective weapons.Try not to jump on top of crates or cover when jumping from a ledge as this can get you stuck in place.Sometimes Outlaws are locked into their dialogue or death sequence, thankfully you save everytime u walk over a teleport circle. Unfortunately you have to close and restart the game when that happens.Currently investigating if the righteous soul spawn in Chapter 4 is broken or not or tends to not spawn a soul when it says it spawned one.Sadly can confirm that Chapter 4 in its current state is broken. If you can win the game depends entirely on luck if you get all the souls to spawn or not. Even though they should be Hardcoded to spawn when following the righteous path, they  are not guaranteed even though they should be. Also the Pathmarkers are super buggy and do not display properly.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The voice acting, the music, the gameplay, the enemy design... It has all the right components to make it an addicting roguelite. I was initially concerned about it being a twin-stick shooter (I'm not very good at them), but I found myself improving steadily, alongside a good difficulty curve. I particularly enjoy this game when compared to ones like Binding of Isaac, because there are no bullet hell bits. Very enjoyable!

Years ago, I tried it and found my first one, that alone made me stop playing it. Then I read it had been solved and tried to play it again. When I killed him, the game just froze giving me the only option of ALT-F4.Great game with Big nasty bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game since I enjoyed the beta but there are a lot of issues that prevent me from recommending it. The gameplay is solid but repetitive. Bosses are one time only as far as I know, which is strange for this genre. Progression is slow, think dead cells but weapons were around 5x more expensive. Maps are monotonous and exploration is pretty much nonexistent - 2 upgrade shrines plus maybe a merchant or a weapon stash, then topped off with a normal exit, and an alternate rune-locked exit. Also traversing the map is tedious, as there is no running even after you finish off every enemy.

HOWEVER, the issue is the controls with the cover mechanic is MISERABLE and is so hard to use. The character refuses to disengage with the cover causing serious frustration. This game is so good but controls like you're stuck in glue with metal boots.

I recently picked this up as part of a bundle and wanted to play it again as I have had a reasonable break.  now I am finding it much more fun. _childDocuments_.review: This game is bad because of a few too many little irritations.Combat is decent, but the cover system is too sticky and some enemies are more irritants than challenges. There are too many weird unlockables that pollute the pool of guns you actually want to use. And the camera... it really starts rooting for the other team at the exact moment you're about to die.I hate that so many NPC conversations take twice as long to get through than they need to be (why does the Witch want to ask me the same question 15 hours in?) But if you like Ron Perlman, you might be willing to overlook it. It doesn't help that a flimsy narrative also takes up a lot of time (looking at you again Witch). The straw that broke my camel's back was when I defeated the final boss and nothing seemed to happen. Then I read that the "true ending" only kicks in if you do something the game never tells you to do.There are better roguelikes out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying it; the game is unlike any other ive played before. Ron Perlman is annoying and needs to learn when to shut up though.. overdramatic as hell.After a bit more time Im starting to see the complaints about the controls. Auto locking to cover is choosey. One second im dodging, the next the game wants me to roll to cover.Aiming recticle is a bit choosey as well. I know the "x" is directly in front of an enemy, but I guess my bullet can whiz to the left or the right..? Dont know whats up with that. Animations really interupt fluidity. Also, dont trust the enemies crosshair before you dodge, it likes to switch to where youre dodging to while dodging for whatever reason.also, make sure to put everything down and not go into combat when Ron Perlman is talking. the voice captions get in the way and block 1/4 of your screen. You cant turn them off either. God, I wish Ron Perlman would shut the f*** up...

_childDocuments_.review: Stylised visuals, wild west purgatory, cool music(Run by Cat & Stoic is fantastic) and narrated by Ron Perlman? Sign me the ♥♥♥♥ up!Well no, actually no. The game is a top down roguelite shooter, which took inspiration from Dead Cells(3 main stats), but didn't really nail the execution of the system, as health, weapons and abilities are their separate stats. Those are not affecting a variety of weapons, only red does,  which isn't really that wide here in the first place. No different movesets that actually play differently, just a gun that shoots two bullets at once or some other alterations. Game isn't lacking variety only when it comes to playstyles, but also the maps are all exactly the same, the only difference being a tileset. The encounters play out all the same, as the shootouts are about sitting behind a cover and taking shots at enemies that cause too little damage and pausing only to reload, just sitting there with nothing to do.  This leads to very unengaging and repetitive gameplay.The game is very obviously low budget, though developers clearly did put a lot of care in. It just makes me wonder if putting money for Perlman into prolonged development wouldn't be a better idea. Then again, I am sure a lot of people got the game only for him. Anyway, I can't in good conscience recommend this game, when you can get much better roguelites, namely Hades or Dead Cells for around the same price.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game after playing the open beta. Fairly simple "rogue-like" mechanics with, what I thought was, a really interesting shooting and cover system. It wasn't perfect, but the art direction was unique and interesting, looked liked it was ripped straight out of Mike Mignola's Hellboy. Unfortunately the game seems to have taken a drastic dip in quality since that open beta. I feel like I ran into a lot more technical issues in this version of the game rather then the beta. I would take cover when I didn't mean to or the cover would spawn on me and cause my character to freak out. I also think one of the feedback items was the game felt too easy in the beta, so instead of doing anything interesting to fix this they just added more enemies to a room and called it good. I do enjoy aspects of the cover and shooting but it is not meant for a large number of enemies at a given time. I will constantly shoot enemies that I didn't mean to shoot and take damage because of it. In rogue-likes precision is everything. If I take damage in one I should feel that its my fault and not the games fault and here I constantly felt that.I would love to recommend this game based on my early impressions I thought this was going to be a sleeper hit of the year, but as it is I think there are too many technical and gameplay hindering issues that keep me from fully recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: It's weird to not recommend a game I'm immediately going to keep playing.Twice now I've had runs interrupted by bugs that have just flat out killed my character. Sometimes I'd get late into the game too, and I'd really be getting into the move, only to die to a falling bug or something.There's so much jank and unecessary clutter. I don't care about dialogue with the Witch when I've done it twenty times already. Just let me get my items, skip the dialogue and move onto shooting.The core loop of cover/shoot is amazing. It's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun. But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game is janky and buggy. When that's fixed, and when i can skip the dialogue, I'll be happy to recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks nice and I really want to recommend it to people, but I just can't. The design, the aesthetic, Ron Pearlman voice acting, and the atmosphere. The music really gives the game a good vibe for being Ghost Rider seeking justice. All of this is good, but this game has some bugs and details that don't make it fun. I've been killed through walls and stuck on terrain. There are debuffs that stay on the ground and disappear after a while. The debuff can disappear from the affected area, but you can still end up taking damage because its apparently still there even though the effect is no longer visible. All of this happens very often and its super annoying when you have something good going. These are minor complaints, but the game just isn't that fun. There is not a lot to this rouge-like that makes it stand out like others. I genuinely want this game to be better and I hope the devs keep updating it. As it stand right now, I suggest you get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead is a game I really enjoyed since the beta stage. The combat is incredibly satisfying, this being the main reason I purchased this game. On top of that the games provides a soothing soundtrack, great voice acting and a nice comic book aesthetic, all of these combined create a nice atmosphere. My biggest complaint is that it can be a little grindy to get new weapons and items.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: In the lines of Hades and Dead Cells, but with a western feeling, and a cover based gameplay that makes it different enough to deserve a play through.  Not as polished and not as replayable, I got to the end in 4 hours being a casual player and it didn't feel like there was more to do besides collecting stuff. The narrator is great, the style is good but gets old quite fast, as most areas are too similar. If you already have Hades, Dead Cells and have an itch for another roguelite give it a go, otherwise I'd recommend any of the other two first.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I'm generally a fan of Rogue-lites and this is a great dual stick Western rogue-lite dungeon crawler. The achievements aren't punishingly 'grindy' or tediously difficult; the longest investments are 50 Outlaws and 50 Saved Souls. Pros:~The weapons are fun, diverse, and sound satisfying.~The music is solid, unobtrusive, and fits well to the themed stages.~The art style is very well done feeling like of mix of Darkest Dungeon and top down cell shading.~Saving is frequent so you can stop mid-run and come back to it anytime. ~The voice acting and story (albeit simple) are well done.Cons:~Infrequent game freeze when fighting/killing Outlaws (often when text should pop up). Alt-F4'n will get you out and the last save will still be valid, so although aggravating it is not that bad. ~The camera angle is also occasionally problematic. ~The charms are probably the least diverse and most unbalanced part of the character equipment.~Once you've played a bit, the dialogue and text bubbles become a bit of a nuisance - especially in regards to Bounties, Lost Souls, and Outlaws.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead initially didn't seem like the type of game I'd normally play. However, I was blown away by the gameplay in West of Dead from the very beginning. This game combines elements of rogue-likes with cover-shooters to create a fantastic environment and system to play in.Positives:+Gameplay: Fantastic shooting mechanics. Decent cover mechanics (a bit clunky to move out of) and combat movement. Abilities and charms add another layer to great gunplay.+Environments: Each unique level encourages exploration and adaptation to new enemies and tactics+Story: West of Dead didn't seem to have the most rigid story, but I was instantly enthralled by the story of the protagonistCould do better:-Soundtrack: Music seemed a little light and quiet, I would have preferred more of an "old west gunfighter" sound. This is just personal preference, and a minor one at that.Overall: Excellent game, I was hooked from the start. Highly recommend!Footnote: I got this game as part of a Humble Bundle Choice, but I'd gladly pay full price
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I had good expectations going into this game, but after about an hour or 2 it immediately felt boring & repetitive. My only take a ways that I like are the art style & theme. The combat is very simple & doesn't build on its self or become any more interesting as you play. Besides a difference in colors, all the maps & enemies feel the same. The enemies may have more health, but its nothing you probably haven't fought before. Their's a good sized arsenal of weapons & abilities, but  wont be any better then the few starting weapons you get or the things you can unlock early on. The most upsetting problem over everything else is that theirs a  lack of challenge that doesn't change, even after multiple run throughs. Their isn't  new game+, challenge mode, or even a difficulty setting, so once you've done one run, all the ones afterwards feel no different. At least I got this free off of Humble Bundle, because I would definitely consider a refund if I hadn't

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is great, part horror, part western, and difficult gameplay. Kept running into issues where the game would become unresponsive but not freeze up. _childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one. On one note, it's a good idea on paper and everything looks cool. It's visually good and some design in the mechanics are there but it is over shadowed by a weird clunkiness that I didn't expect. I really wanted to just LOVE this. I even put it on my wishlist. The things about it is that is has several weird mechanics that make it so you feel nearly helpless or stupid. First one is this weird auto aim ♥♥♥♥. This makes the shooting (which should be the most important in a shooter) clunky. There was a time I  was aiming at an enemy but he was near a door so I ended up shooting the door due to auto aim despite aiming at the enemy. I don't like that.There is a reload mechanic that you will either love or hate it.  It reloads automatically for both weapons but you have to stop shooting that gun in order to reload it. However, the issue is that there is a slight hiatus in between shooting and reloading where nothing happens. So when you have two guns that may not be super strong but have massive reloads you are sitting there doing absolutely nothing while they can shoot you or run at you as much as you want. Another thing that I don't like about it as well is that it reloads each bullet individually which would work in a game that warrants that mechanic. But even in games like that, they don't restrict you from reloading and then reload on bullet at a time. In games that are fluid in nature often time have a reload but reload the whole clip / cylinder/ whatever or the flip slide of reloading each bullet but you can do it without a weird gun stun. It makes the game that much more slow.I like the abilities, I like the lantern stun, I like unique guns, I can get down with the style and the enemies but man the things that should be almost integral feels like cottage cheese that you let sit on the counter with the lid off for like a month. Honestly, I wanted to like it and to an extent I did but I'm have to say pass until something changes. I'd give it 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't really hook me.Art style is pretty nice looking, and while I like the gritty comic book style, it is extremely dark, half of the screen is always black or very dark colors.Gameplay is ok for the most part, found it extremely easy. Enter cover, shoot enemies, stay still when they shoot to dodge and recover ammo, dive when the cover breaks, repeat.Managed to get to the final level on my first try, but the game glitched and sent me to the title screen even though it showed "chapter 4".I just have an issue to the way the character magnets to cover, sometimes you are trying to avoid a rushing enemy or just walk around, and if you get too close to a cover, the character will automatically glue to it.Enemies are all basic. Some shoot, some rush you. The worst of them is the big golem that is invincible unless you hit his back, but it has perfect tracking so you have to get close so it can stomp, and then it will stop for a second. Or just abuse their AI by going around cover.The game tries to copy Dead Cells a bit too much. Similar protagonist, same 3 stat upgrade system, same 2 weapon/2 items/1 amulet system, same use cells to unlock more items system, same bosses give transversal upgrades system.Pretty much everything but setting and camera is copied from Dead Cells.Talking about camera, it sucks. The fixed isometric camera makes it hard to see or avoid stuff that comes from the lower part of the screen.And as a very bad look for the devs/publisher, a small part of the game was cut in development in order to be sold as day 1 DLC. The Crow DLC adds very little stuff, was released on the exact same day as the game and costs 1/5 the price extra.Overall is... ok-ish. But I think I've seen everything it has to offer in the 2 hours I played.

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead is a unique, stylish cover-based twin-stick shooter whose "Weird West" vibe, visual design, music and solid gameplay shines through a host of audio bugs and occasionally iffy cover mechanic. I first tried it during a notably rough beta phase and half-forgot about it before receiving a key from from a friend recently, and after digging into it I'm glad I gave it another chance.Purgatory, Wyoming, 1888. A nameless gunslinger spirit awakens with no memory of his former life, and only one goal he can recall: Find the Preacher. He finds himself in a run-down bar at the precipice of a twisting, shadowy maze of rooms and corridors populated by vengeful, gun-toting revenants, both of man and beast, that have lingered a bit longer then they ought to. It's time to earn an afterliving.As mentioned above, West of Dead's combat is largely cover-based. You can carry two guns, and they reload passively when you're not firing them and reload faster in cover. You can safely shoot at enemies from cover even while they're actively shooting at you, and only certain enemies can bypass it, such as fliers or ones tossing AoE explosives, as well as melee enemies that simply walk around the objects to get at you. But cover objects can break and will change visually to alert you when this is a bout to happen. There is a context-sensitive dodge button that will cause you to perform a dodge-roll in the open, slide into cover, or vault over cover as necessary, all of which have invincibility frames. But the cover system is rather sticky and finicky at times. When it works you'll feel like a badass, and it when it doesn't, you won't. It's jank, but its not game-breaking.There is a light and darkness mechanic in WoD: Enemies standing in the dark cannot be targeted normally, though you can still hit them if you're good. Strewn about each combat room are lanterns that the player can light by interacting with them, which not only lights up the area and exposes enemies to being auto-targeted but also briefly stuns them if they were within range. Normally they stay that way, but some regions have bat-like enemies that will prioritize going and extinguishing lanterns over attacking you directly.You will automatically perform a melee attack instead of shooting if an enemy is too close, and certain active items take the form of knives with special effects and give you additional melee options. Other active items include things like thrown axes or dynamite, or temporary buffs such as faster reloads or a damage-absorbing shield. Weapons include revolvers, regular pistols, rifles and shotguns, ranging from flintlocks and muskets not even up the standards of the game's timeframe, to powerful steampunk-esque wonder guns like a full-auto rifle that ramps-up its firerate the longer its fired, a triple-barreled shotgun, weapons with elemental effects, and weapons that guarantee critical hits if certain conditions are met, such as a shotgun that always crits if fired from cover- one of my personal favorites.You will occasionally find said weapons and other new gear just lying around in the levels, but you can also find treasure chests and a wandering trader, either of which will have gear of a higher level then the drops. You can also find shrines that can increase your health and melee damage, gun damage, or active item damage and cooldown for the remainder of that run. I find upgrading each equally is effective, but there's no reason you couldn't hardline one over the other two... You might also find a Lost Soul, which you can relieve of its burden for a large amount of sin currency and usually some gear drops. Taking on the Soul's burden will curse you, requiring you to kill six enemies to lift it, but watch out- you take much more damage while cursed, and taking on multiple burdens will add to the total enemies needed to remove the curse. Most of my failed runs were due to damage taken while carrying said burdens- the game is surprisingly fair for a roguelike otherwise, at least on the default difficulty.Dying kicks you back to the limbo bar and you lose your shrine buffs, iron, unspent sin and gear, but if you complete a level you'll always first have to spend any sin you have towards unlocks- you cannot actually leave the witch's room with unspent sin.There is a bit of a branching level structure to a run, but most of the branches will be restricted to you at first until you obtain special runes from specific bosses in specific regions. You'll always play the Crypt first, which is attached to the bar. From there you have a choice of going to the Hunt or the Bayou, which have their own branching paths (though in the case of the Bayou you'll need the Crow DLC to visit the Battlefield, otherwise you'll always go to the Mines next) before converging at the Farmlands, which split again into the Town or the Churchyard before you converge once more at the Church proper, which leads to the final showdown. which path you take is mostly optional, but you'll probably want to head to whichever one has an outlaw to fight or a specific "Righteous Soul" to save, the latter of which only comes into play after you've defeated the final boss once, as far as I can tell. Doing so allows you to obtain the true ending.The hero is aided in his quest by a mysterious witch that will take sins obtained from slain enemies in exchange for persistent unlocks as well as show you tidbits of the hero and the villain's pasts in exchange for memory fragments, a wandering trader who will take iron fragments dropped from enemies in exchange for new gear, a bartender who will refill his reusable health flask between levels, a bounty hunter will who will point him towards powerful outlaw spirits in the levels that will reward extra Sin and provide "remnant" item and weapon blueprints for the witch, and the ever-helpful Frank the Zombie, who is a fountain of gameplay tips, one of which will encourage you to use the accessibility settings you feel comfortable with: WoD features a difficulty select and and an adjustable aim assist that is extremely powerful when dialed up. Progress, unlocks and achievements ignore these settings entirely, so configure them to your liking.A number of reviewers have commented on the game's heavy aesthetic influence taken from the comics of Mike Mignola such as Hellboy, to the point where WoD's flaming-skull-for-a-head protagonist is voiced by Ron Perlman! Some reviewers find him a bit goofy in the role, but I found his trademark understated growling an appropriate aesthetic touch. Which is good, because he's the only voiced character in the game. This of course gives rise to the usual, and oft warranted complaints about celebrity voice actors in games, and yes, West of Dead is a bit rough around the edges. Perlman's inclusion I think comes down to taste- its a pretty good game regardless.Fans of action roguelikes or rogue-lites, persistent progression, top-down shooters, fantasy westerns and/or Ron Perlman will want to give West of Dead a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem that all rogue-like enthusiasts will most likely love. In this action game you are a dead cowboy kicking butt with a whole arsenal of fun guns and abilities. The gameplay is so fun and satisfying, it really makes you feel like a cowboy. You get behind cover and exchange fire with the enemy while demon dogs run at you, and if your cover is destroyed you have to dodge bullets while sliding to a table to hide behind. You can even shoot explosive barrels! I especially love battling these minibosses called outlaws, it feels like a real duel. Pretty much every gun is fun and unique, switching up your experience each game. The visuals are also amazing for this game. The guns, levels, and enemies all look great. I also really like the soundtrack which is some nice guitar music, which really matches the feel of the game. Now for a few negatives. I like the abilities, but some are kind of bland or not very helpful, and I find myself not using them to much. The game is also has a lot of similarities to Dead Cells, which is an amazing game, but I wish they made it a bit more unique. You unlock stuff exactly the same as dead cell. You get blueprints, collect sin from killing enemies (basically this games version of cells) and use them to unlock stuff in-between levels. The levels are like Dead Cells because its a series of rooms filled with enemies, with portals scattered around, and a portal to one of the next levels. This isn't really a complaint though. The way you become stronger are these alters you find through the level which have three types upgrades you can choose from. Its like the scrolls from Dead Cells, but worse, they are a bit to simple for my tastes. They upgrade health and melee, gun damage, and ability cooldown and damage. I upgrade in the same way every game unlike dead cells where you focus on one or two upgrades every game depending on what you have. I think they should have made upgrading entirely different. This is a minor complaint, but sometimes cover can be a little weird, like I'll try to duck but don't or get stuck on cover, but it's not a big deal. Lastly I think the UI is a bit messy and hard to control, at least on keyboard and mouse.Despite these complaints I still love this game because it exceeds with its gameplay and visuals, which is the most important part for me. Also the complaints I listed are not very major. Overall I would give this game an 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead is a wonderfully grim and gritty western game. It's fast paced and the gameplay is very smooth. What I enjoyed the most was using the light sources to your tactical advance. This also adds a lot to the atmosphere in the game, as well as the gameplay itself. It felt refreshing and gives you the opportunity to think through some strategies, instead of just barging in.The combination of tactics and the fast pacing of the game seems contradicting, but works incredibly well. I also loved the graphics of the game, it's like you jumped right into a very grim western comic, and the music is fantastic.Unfortunately the game does contain some bugs and I encoutered one game breaking bug. It doesn't happen often and can be patched out, but to spawn in complete darkness and losing all your progress because of that, is incredibly frustrating.West of Dead has its challenging moments and can be unforgiving, but once you get the hang of it, it's incredibly fun to play and to anticipate on your enemies.The Wild West has never been this dark.8.5/10Full review (in Dutch) can be found .

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.  A slower paced, more tactical version of the Dead Cells formula.  The control get a little bit of getting used to and you have to learn to respect the light and darkness system and the cover system.  But everything is telegraphed clearly, you can understand exactly what's going on if you pay attention.People will complain about the auto-aim, they will complain about the camera.All of these complaints arise when you try to play this as some more conventional twin-stick horde shooter.  Move too fast, do more than you should, and yeah the helpful systems they created will freak out a bit.But if you play the game they made, instead of trying to play it like the game you think it should be, it becomes a tight, nuanced, thoughtful shooter.  Where each move needs carefully considered and smoothly executed.  Once you let yourself get into it's rhythm (instead of forcing your own rhythm on it) you'll be amazed at how easy it feels to pull truly awesome stunts of dodging, diving, running, gunning etc.There's nothing else like this.  It is phenomenal.But once you start playing the game they made instead of trying

_childDocuments_.review: This review has been updated due to the developer's continuing support for the game. The initial review is left below as a reference, but the game has been improving since launch thanks to the dev's efforts in listening to player feedback.Numerous bugs and issues that had affected the game at launch have been squashed and while the game can still be tough, it feels like a much more fair and most importantly enjoyable experience.The aiming system has seen the most improvement with a greater degree of precision given to the lock-on system. You're now much more likely to aim at the enemy you're pointing at, even if they're hidden in the darkness, without the autoaim constantly trying to steer your shots at the nearest illuminated enemies. Other issues such as locking on through walls have also been fixed. The higher level of control lets you prioritise the targets you want, taking out the most dangerous threats quickly instead of the game inadvertently shielding them with inaccurate lock-ons.The cover system has had similar tweaking which gives a more responsive feel to taking cover and leaving it when you want to, with a greatly reduced chance of standing next to safety and taking a faceful of lead just because your character decided not to bend down. Additional movement options have also been added, allowing you to slide out of cover similarly to how you can slide in to cover, leaving your dodge move ready to use if needed instead of using up your dodge just to leave an especially sticky piece of cover.On the whole, it definitely feels like you are much more in control of your character and runs are more likely to end because you made a mistake instead of unresponsive controls.The game's balance has also been looked at, with shotguns being buffed to have greater range to feel like a much more viable weapon choice. Later level enemies are altered too, so that they don't feel quite as tanky as they did before, but are still a threat if they manage to land a hit. It's a fair change that doesn't punish the player as much if they weren't able to find stronger weapons, but still keeps you on your toes when it comes to avoiding attacks.The only negative that remains is still with some screens of the UI when using mouse & keyboard controls, although it's understandable that it's not as much of a priority at the moment and the current setup is functional, if uncooperative.It's always good to see a developer putting in the work to improve a game after release and taking note of the feedback from players. It shows a real love for their work that the players will hopefully share.If you're looking for a roguelite shooter with a very striking style, this definitely gets my recommendation.==Original Review==Despite having an initially interesting style of gameplay, West of Dead sadly suffers from a multitude of poorly thought through and badly implemented ideas, leading to a experience that's more frustrating than anything else.In-run progression is all to often brought to a halt by a lack of weapon upgrades. The game has you relying on RNG for weapons to appear in levels, but they are competing for space with other types of equipment, too many of which are simply underpowered of outright unusable in their current state.Most notable are shotguns which have a range barely greater than your melee ability, which for a game with such emphasis on using cover is a major issue. This ends up with later level enemies feeling like bullet sponges who are perfectly capable of deleting your own health in a couple of hits.On top of this the game just seems to be at an almost early access level of polish, with unkillable bosses a common bug and the controls fighting the player every step of the way. The main character will stick to cover when you don't want him to, or refuse to take cover when needed.The aiming system is also in need of work, with weapons snapping to enemies who might not even be on the screen instead of who you actually wanted to hit. The UI also seems to be designed for gamepads and trying to navigate the upgrade menus with mouse & keyboard feels like more of a struggle than it has any right to be.Hopefully with time and patches the game can iron out the issues with controls and progression, but for now it's a bit of a mess.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: an enjoyable western-themed twin-stick shooter with bags of atmosphere and fantastic narration from Ron Perlman.Gorgeous art, moody soundtrack, great writing and first class narration from Ron Perlman combine to make this indie punch above its weight in  the genre. It feels polished in a way that a lot of indies do not despite not aiming for the stars from a technical perspective. The narration really sells it as top notch affair.  Gameplay-wise its compelling. The weapons are varied and fun to experiment with, and there are a lot of different tactics to try based on what your loadout looks like.  Each run feels fresh because the weapons you are given at the start are randomised so you have to figure out how to make do. Since most weapons are useful, you rarely feel you've been dealt a short straw.    On the downside the way getting in and out of cover controls can feel a bit wonky and is never as smooth and satisfying as you'd like. Still its perfectly serviceable and doesn't get in the way too much. I also think a difficulty choice should be presented before you get started; the default is easy, and only because I played this on Game Pass and remember getting thoroughly murdered did I check to see what was up. If it feels too easy it's just not satisfying.  Overall, I love it. If you like twin stick shooters and enjoy the wild west this is one to investigate.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent, but for every good idea there's a flaw that holds it back.  The movement is just a bit too stiff to allow it to flow, and eventually a minor glitch will punish you in a major way.  You very quickly get through the original text/dialogue, so future runs are just a bit more tired & boring.  There are progressive unlocks, but you HAVE to spend ALL your unlock points between EVERY level, and you eventually will have to unlock things you don't want, but will appear in future runs anyway.  There's a risk/reward system where your character can take on an extra challenge for some extra loot, but the risk and reward are always the same, so get boring quickly.  The dialogue is a bit too generic and forced, even with Ron Pearlman voicing it.Speaking of dialoge:  The "advance text" button doesn't work.  It advances by itself no matter what you do.  If you want it to go faster, you have to mash Escape to open the menu and close it in order to advance one text box.  The 5th time you have to do this to advance through the same 3 boxes of text you've seen a dozen times before, you get frustrated.Repeated playthroughs seem to be part of the gameplay loop.  Then it's quite a strange oversight to have the same unskippable cutscene for every Outlaw, or only 3 unique lines of dialogue for the first NPC you always see at the beginning of each run.  There are so many things to break the flow without adding anything, it feels like it needs a lot more refining.I could say more, but the bottom line is:  There are enough issues that break the flow of the game that I felt I'd seen everything it had to offer, and was disappointed.  It ALMOST worked, and I feel like could have been so much more, which is a shame.  I feel you can safely miss this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if I've really played enough of West of Dead yet to properly judge it, but I'm also struggling to see myself returning to it, so... here goes. This game is good. It's just... everything this game has to offer, I feel like Enter the Gungeon also offers, but just plain better. Better for me at least. See, I'd describe West of Dead as a slower, more strategic, wild west aesthetic Enter the Gungeon (so, a top-down shooter roguelike). I like them both, but personally I prefer the snappy, reaction-based gameplay of Enter the Gungeon. Plus that game is way more polished...So yeah I hate to be this way, making my entire review a comparison to another game, but that honestly is the whole reason that I have trouble imagining myself really getting into West of Dead. I'd just rather play Enter the Gungeon. Maybe if I give West of Dead another chance and see more of what is has to offer, I'll change my mind, but I dunno... it's sorta the core gameplay elements (which are perfectly good by the way, just not my style) that I have an issue with, so... yeah. _childDocuments_.review: Interesting presentation/art style and premise, Ron Perlman does a good job with the voice (no surprise there), and... that's about all the good I can say about this.Day-one DLC is always insulting.The controls are absolutely terrible , and apparently they've been improved greatly since launch. It's as if the devs have never played PC games.The gameplay itself would be mediocre and uninspired, even if it controlled smoothly. Considering how playing this means constantly fighting against the controls and the UI, though, it just makes the whole experience rather unpleasant.There's an interesting idea behind this game, and it could have been good had it been made better, but... it's just not.I've played through the first chapter, and some masochistic part of me is kind of curious to keep playing a bit and see what else happens, but it's hard to imagine that things get better.Didn't die in what little I played, so I can't comment on how the roguelike/roguelite aspect plays out, but considering how bland and same-y everything has been in what I've experienced, I can't imagine it's very interesting.Maybe you get access to all sorts of cool stuff later on? If that's the case, the interesting stuff is hidden too far into the game to matter; there's nothing to grab you earlier on.Couple of guns that shoot vaguely differently (not enough to really matter), couple of "abilities" on cooldown that also mostly feel the same (throw some dynamite or throw an axe? stab with "knife 1" or stab with "knife 2"?). _childDocuments_.review: The general vibe is "what if dead cells was a top-down shooter?" I've seen some comparisons to enter the gungeon, and while I can't say I've played that one, it seems fair from what I've seen. The good: gameplay loop is great, the metaprogression/unlocks aren't too grindy and you feel very powerful in a glass tank-y kind of way. I did something stupid and kept not unlocking weapons, just getting them to 1 point needed and moving to the next one. But was pleasantly surprised when I finally did a couple and it opened up a huge number of possible unlocks for me. The aesthetic of the game is really nice and atmospheric, and the lore is interesting to collect (and you'll collect all of it in time by playing) The bad: it's a bit unpolished, with some bugs and some questionable QoL design choices. For example I think I broke the final boss in my first fight against him and he never recovered from his stunned state until dying. Another time I just fell out of the map and lost a good chunk of health for no reason. The endgame content (chapter 4) is incredibly difficult and frustrating especially because my major complaint is run length. A full run is over an hour if you're full-clearing each floor, which you want to do to be powerful enough to be viable in later areas. And if you die in the 4th or 6th or whatever area past the first 1 or 2, you've lost a lot of progress. It's also weird that you can only buy the revive once item going into the last area of the game before the final boss.

_childDocuments_.review: Having experienced West of Dead initially during the BETA, I held firmly onto the belief that this was tailor-made for me. First and foremost, it is a rogue-like western; a peculiar amalgamation we do not see very often that exhibits quite an atmospheric feeling with a compelling soundtrack and the voice (and sadly only one) of Ron Perlman. Alas, these non-gameplay related perks as well done as they are, did not rectify my overall negative perception of this game. It feels simply unfinished. Controls are clunky especially when taking cover where one does not know if the character is actually taking cover or not, the camera is perplexing and the game embraces the repetitive nature of rogue-likes entirely, unable to render a varied experience with its meager content. It should not come as a surprise that dying is a common occasion, but what is worse is to know that you have to undergo the exact (emphasis on exact) same routine to get to your previous level. Except for some new weapons one may encounter, there is nothing new to each run, making it borderline boring after a couple of attempts. Atleast West of Dead is somewhat forgiving when it comes to survival as opposed to kindred games such as Enter the Gungeon where gaining health is an extreme rarity, and hence manages to somewhat stretch the time of a potential run. Considering the price tag on this game and the lack of content a player gets to explore, I can not recommend it and have refunded it myself after 2 hours BETA and 1 hour official play time.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so impressed at how slick and well-polished this game is. At about three hours in, I won my first run, but I can already tell I've barely touched the content in the game, especially the story and unlocks. West of Dead takes the equipment structure, permanent progression, and biome pathing of Dead Cells, adds in a good dash of Curse of the Dead gods gameplay feel, and puts a dash of, believe it or not, Rainbow Six Vegas 2-style cover to create its own unique atmosphere and gameplay loop. Despite its clear influences, WoD has its own signature look and feel, especially present during boss battles, where both you and your enemies are scrambling to find safety from each other amidst the destructible cover. The gameplay is a bit slower and methodical, but moments like these really add to the intensity and fun, especially when the game enters bullet-time when you have a perfect, just-missed-it dodge.It's worth mentioning the guns all feel amazing, too. Even the default guns feel punchy and satisfying, and a litany of abilities like thrown axes and assasin's knives add good variation. I also didn't expect to care about the story aspect too much, but Ron Perlman's voice over does incredible work in world-building and atmosphere, and the story actually has quite a bit of intrigue. Any story at all in a roguelite is kind of rare, so I'm glad WoD does a good job, and the themes of redemption and vengeance are interesting and appropriate for the setting.There are a few sore spots. Teleports, while convenient and plentiful, have an awkawardly long animation; so, too, does climbing ladders and talking to NPCs. These can make the game feel slightly sluggish at times, but are ultimately minor blemishes in the grand scheme.All in all, so far a great, very unique game that I'm looking forward to many more hours in. If you're a fan of westerns, shooters, or roguelites, definitely try this out!

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead is a roguelike in which you fight through Purgatory as a gunslinger against hordes of dogs, rifleman, hunters, dynamite-throwing miners, and the most deadly enemy of all- the game's cover mechanics. There's no button to go into cover, your character is simply magnetically attracted to the various bits of respawning cover in each combat room. The window and angles for this entrance are grossly overcompensated, often resulting in you making cover for the box against enemy gunfire rather than the other way around.Beyond this, the weapons are.. paltry. There's maybe three worth picking up among the five or six you can start with, and the roguelike elements of the game involves you building up your arsenal. But a quick look at what that expanded arsenal actually contains is in no way exciting, with many guns offering low base damage but critical hits or status effects under certain conditions when several of the base guns do the very simple thing of just killing your enemy with good base damage.In my very first run I made it past The Farm, something only.. 25.9% of players have done. Admittedly, I'm unsure what qualifies someone as a "player" to Steam. I got the game in the recent Humble Ukraine Bundle, and it's possible that everyone who activated their Steam copy but has yet to play it counts as a "player."

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a game like this before, from the very start I kept saying to myself "It's different". The graphics and sounds/music are incredible. The controls are almost perfect, I'd say 90% so, on rare occasions I make a move I didn't want to, or miss a move I tried to pull off. I find the camera angles to almost meld with my mind, knowing exactly how I want to see the area. I was confused about the constant game saving I saw going on because when you die, that's it, back to the very start with you. It turns out the saves are for if you want to come back to the game later. It could certainly use a better tutorial, there were things I was still learning about after 20+ hours in. Being forced to spend sin sucks as there are a lot of weapons/abilities/charms I never wanted to be available, the variety does have some appeal though. The difficulty ramp up of the Battlefield and Churchyard (aka Graveyard) is too much, it boiled down to blatant luck for me to beat them. _childDocuments_.review: the game is a decent start, but it lacks several things that would be indicative of a complete product.  Firstly, there is no game reset option, which means that as you acquire more items it becomes harder to plan your strategy, and more of a trip guided exclusively by RNGesus.  Secondly there have been multiple play throughs where the blue souls needed to beat the game are not actually present when the totem says that they are.to be clear the difficulty of various endgame contents are great, they are what makes any game challenging and fun, but it is the two sloppy errors of design that make this game difficult to reccomend

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a rating in between positive and negative I would because West of Dead makes me so conflicted. On one hand I absolutely love the art style and the gameplay itself is really solid, I just think the game makes a bunch of boring decisions that prevent the game from flourishing.My biggest issue with the game is that the progression in this game is really subpar compared to other roguelites. The weapons and equipment tend to feel very similar to each other and the upgrades in game are just boring stat upgrades that are the exact same every game.The longer I played and the more runs I went through the more the game started to feel repetitive. However the core gameplay and visuals are a ton of fun. I love the darkness mechanic where you can only attack enemies that are in the light and I love the cover based shooting.So I would recommend this game as long as you know that the roguelite mechanics aren't the strongest and that the game can start feeling a repetitive because the core gameplay is so solid.
