_childDocuments_.review: On the whole I think I would recommend this game, but probably on sale.The game looks great, for the most part. The shadows kind of ruin things. I know there is a light versus dark motif/mechanic going on in the game, but having entire rooms basically shrouded in the dark was just, not fun, and when there were cut scenes, the shadows would often clip body parts or even heads. The levels all have their own unique flavour and design, the shaded cell graphics hold up and look great (except for NPC faces when you zoom in).Overall it sets a really good tone with how it looks, and how it sounds. The ambience and the music are both really good, and the combat music really got me hopping and zipping around. It is especially potent, the music, with boss and mini-boss fights. Purgatory looks and sounds good, but how does it play?Well, you run from room to room on each level, fighting enemies, collecting souls and iron, and slowly increasing your power each run. For a rogue-like, there was not a lot of death on my part after the first one or two in the learning stage. It is not all that difficult of a game, which is nice. You get to have fun, without tearing your hair out, and experience the story which is actually pretty decent. I wasn't really even expecting a story from this game, so I am pleasantly surprised.You run, you dodge, you gun. It is alright. The fact that if you move too close to cover it kind of 'snags' you and has you moving super slow when all you wanted to do was move quickly past it, is really annoying. But that is really my one complaint.. other than enemies who heal other enemies. That literally ruined whole levels for me.Overall I got a good amount of time out of the game. I can see people who really enjoy it putting in a ton of time and effort to unlock and clear everything, but I just couldn't bring myself to go that far. For some games that I really love I do; but this I just liked.I would recommend it, like I said up above, but on sale. It is not very long and I think about $16 CAD or lower would be a more fair price, rather than $26 CAD. If you can catch this game during a sale, go for it, if not, this is something that can wait.

_childDocuments_.review: An isometric "cover shooter" with dodging mechanics that reset your dodge "cooldown" so long as you're dodging or sliding into cover, which basically means that once you learn to play with a mix of momentary safety and pure insane aggression you get some of the most satisfying and slick combat that money can buy. If you've played Dead Cells the structure of the game is very similar to that only with a bit more of a story focus to it but it's that combat that keeps me coming back, it is so much fun to be sliding around and over cover, dodging bullets as you go in slow motion to then set up a shotgun barrage at close range; it'd be nice if the rogue-like elements build up with even more surprises and run variations and modifiers and so on to make things a bit more chaotic and crazy for pure replay value but damn if there isn't an absolutely fine game here already :)

Health, Ability CD, or Damage. There's no reload speed upgrade, no crit chance, no movement speed, no extra dodge, it's just super basic upgrades. The elite 'outlaw' mini-bosses are a joke and just bullet sponge of normal enemies, they're just chores to go through. You  alsodon't feel like you can make a 'build' that's unique or get a god-run as the weapons and abilities are not synergistic enough. _childDocuments_.review: The numbers for unlocking are much more reasonable now. While I wouldn't say the game is complete polish-wise, the core featureset of the title is worth playing through. Positive list: 1. The gunplay is good. I'm often excited to unlock more weapons more than any other unlocks because the guns sound and play well. 2. Ron Perlman sounds great. His voice work is suitable to the tone of the game and often sells the setting well. 3. The artstyle for the game world is good.Negative list: 1. The menu you use to unlock stuff is awful. Probably the least complete feature in the game.  It still contains stuff you've already gotten before and makes you navigate through it even though you can't interact with already unlocked things in the menu. There's no way to quickly navigate down or up(e.g. RT for a page at a time, etc.), it isn't categorized in any useful way e.g by weapon type, alphabet, etc. 2. The VO is mixed way high volume, so voice volume 1 is still Ron Perlman in your room and in your ear. 3. I wish the UI was cleaned up a bit more. Good UI should largely blend seamlessly into the game. The UI in this game is a few steps above implemented wireframes, but only 85% production ready. 4. I wish the reload UI indicators were around where players are often looking and not static in the bottom left. For example in Enter the Gungeon the guns are in the bottom right but the reload animation plays above the character, where the player is often looking. 5. The lantern stun mechanic is antithetical to rifles as a playstyle. You cannot lock onto enemies that are not a majority in the light so to use the rifle on an enemy in the dark (which is usually >50% of the time) you're forced to attempt to either use free aiming which is damn near impossible at range or go in and risk taking damage just to light the lantern and make your way to the nearest cover and shoot from there.6. Outlaws are usually the same guy with less or more health, kinda wish they did more with it to make it feel like a different encounter. I'm sure they have design ideas about this and I'm a programmer not a designer.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn’t know what I was getting into as I only had seen brief gameplay from this, I was pleasantly surprised to find out it was a roguelike. That pleasant feeling however was short-lived. You start by finding yourself in an unknown crypt and a lot of unanswered questions, including who you are and why you keep coming bac after dying, and none of those questions are answered or are answered very briefly, the point here is the story might as well might not have existed and it wouldn’t have added to nor taken away anything from the game. There was minimal voice acting and only the main character, none of the other characters had voice acting. The atmosphere and music were good but it doesn’t evolve beyond that, there’s no climactic music when fighting a boss or the final boss, in fact, there’s no climactic boss fight at all -at least it didn’t feel that way.The greatest perpetrator of all is the graphics and art style. The art seems unique and cool when you first start but it gets old too fast and about 5 minutes in it’s already hurting your eyes and is just too dark and minimalistic, which makes you thing it’s more of a cost-cutting choice rather than an intentional design choice.As for gameplay the majority of guns are boring, you have your revolvers, shotguns, rifles and so on but the way to go is just take more damage, one ranged and one close range is good enough. Damage over time effects are useless as the game isn’t designed for such strategies, and unlike other Roguelikes there is hardly any meta progression except unlocking new guns or abilities which are pretty much all the same, no flavor or variety, overall just….boring. the one good thing I wanted to say about it - which are the waypoints and how they’re perfectly distributed so that it’s not tedious to walk and backtrack - is marred by the fact that it loads every time you teleport, WHY? Why is that? The whole map should be loaded, it’s not like the graphics are demanding or anything, that slows you down so much, 1 hour from my game time is probably me teleporting or just trying to frantically get through the incredibly slow dialogues.- Teleporters are very well placed you don’t feel its tedious going from one part to another.TLDR; I honestly don’t see why anyone would play this when games such as Hades or Warm snow exist.Pros:- Good music- Atmospheric- Cover gameplay done rightCons:- Unimaginative gameplay and progression- Poor Story- Minimal voice acting- Eye-hurting graphics- Slow controlsOverall Score      5/10

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr A good-to-fantastic game held down by bugs and lack of polish.I spent the first two hours of playing this game basically going "yeah okay, that's a bit rough but I suppose it's fine." I vaulted a piece of cover into a boss' molotov, and my character disappeared, meaning my guns stopped working. I could make it through if I just killed the boss with my dumb hatchet, but then the boss fell through the floor and progress-locked me.I don't think that one instance of game breaking bugs cements this no from me, but the fact that I spent an hour using a mouse and keyboard while the game doesn't feel super designed for that. The art direction is cool, but gets in the way of actually seeing enemies, as does the fixed camera perspective. The rooms with verticality to them can have enemies attack you from above if they're ranged, but you can't fire back up at them. The menus feel stiff, and it took me a while to realize the stats were associated with the colors because in the actual level up screen they don't have any coloration.What stiffness and awkwardness is there can sometimes really work for the combat, and Ron Perlman being the only major voice, as well as the internal narrator for your character is rad as hell. This might sound like a dunk, but I honestly really appreciate the ideas copied from Dead Cells, and I think they could really make them work considering all the factors. If you even deigned to read this paragraph after the other bugs I wrote, then I'd honestly suggest trying the game for yourself.In a year from now, I hope at least some of the issues I had get addressed, because this is a game that *could* be good.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering the rather mixed reviews regarding WOD, I felt compelled to throw in.For starters, lets remember this is an Indie Game. Now that we got that out of the way your expectations should be tempered. Let's begin.I hear many knock Ron Perlman as just "phoning it in". Though not a huge fan of the guy, I must admit he provides just the right amount of inflection and tone, giving the player a stronger connection to Mason 's emotional state throughout the game.Many reviewers, most with only hours of gameplay, knock the controls and level design. Make no mistake, there are some legitimate gripes and critiques, but in my experience none of these are game breaking or frustrating enough to ruin the overall experience. Once you get used to the gunplay and creative(somewhat janky) cover system, you'll be upgrading your gear/perks with ease and looking forward to the next encounter. Honestly it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast and nothing quite like it in the genre.While there could have been more depth in the roguelike meta progressions dept and more variance and nuance to the charms, abilities, and power ups, The variety of guns and melee weapons, most of which need to be unlocked as you progress, more then make up for it. Die, start again, rinse and repeat. Saving your new start point after completing each chapter.Games of this ilk will live or die by their gameplay loop, and IMO this is where WOD shines. It's that gritty gunplay in and out of the shadows while dodging bullets and enemies via the roll as you barely escape from cover to cover. The just one more run or just a few more rooms vibe is ever present because the game respects the players time with ample use of the auto save.Make no mistake the last chapter will TEST your RESOLVE as the difficulty Spikes immensely. Don't expect to get 50 hours in this one or 100's like TBOI, considering you can most likely achieve all in about 20-30 hours or so. BUT it's well worth it considering there's nothing comparable in this genre and we need more Indie Games like WOD. Much respect to the Devs for achieving such a high level of success and polish with such a small Indie Team. I did buy the DLC just to have a crow following me around. ♥♥♥♥ it, Brandon Lee style.Buy this game on SALE, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Zero out of 4.West of Dead could have been a good or great game. The bugs are the problem. I've played at most seven runs. In three of those, progress was lost to a bug. One level didn't have an exit spawned. Once, selecting "Continue Run" from the main menu started me at the beginning. And lastly, upon killing a sub-boss the game just froze all controls there.I'm pretty sure I was shot through a wall. It is a certain wall that juts into half a room that spawns rarely. And no, I'm not being confused and talking about the wall-enemies in The Town.If you wish to play with no Aim Assist, it's kinda a bad idea because -- I know it sounds illogical -- the lines... I think they aren't straight in all/certain camera angles (cursor placement vs. where the bullet visually goes vs. where the bullet counts as a hit); And yes, I know you have to aim for the feet area of the enemy.Your character's light-radius isn't actually always on, it only activates when you step in a dark area. This is bad generally, and slows your exploration. An unlit area was either unlit due to this or a "wall" of the room was blocking or casting a shadow -- regardless, what I thought was a walled off region in combat was not. You can remap controls unless you want to remap the buttons to... shoot. Basically due to a bug. So the right-most weapon on your UI will always have to use your left mouse button, and your left-most weapon use your right. This was actually rather difficult to mentally try to correct for. Controller also doesn't let you remap shoot successfully, but left/right default is set correctly.Time waiting on traveling between warp points is too long, and the short "shortcut" version takes even longer. The button to advance dialogue usually doesn't do anything, so you have to wait for it to auto-expire. A certain level objective always has dialogue. To learn game/level structure concepts you can talk to the person in the starting area who has this dialogue issue and is vague. This is the only game knowledge -- no journal/how to. Sub-boss random names are often like Leeroy and Cletus. In one of my first runs I had two with the same first and last names. One run I completed a level and instead of the next area, it loaded the same area, but with only one room which had a sub-boss fight. I assume it didn't correctly put him in the previous level space, but then the game progressed correctly until -- as mentioned before -- the next sub-boss I killed put the game in an unresponsive state.

_childDocuments_.review: Another roguelite shooter, with an undead western theme - which is something I think we need more of!It's mostly okay, with satisfying combat but it doesn't really hold up compared to other games in its genre. Fights take place behind cover and emphasis is given to lining up your shots and slowly reloading. You don't have much in terms of fun abilities or synergies, the pacing is quite slow and the constant backtracking takes time - your character moves relatively slow compared to the size of the levels. Ron Perlman as a VA is technically competent here, but the direction and writing of the voiced over dialogue is pretty miserable and you just have a very bored sounding Perlman on top of a slowly paced game. Its definitely a missed chance to inject some life into the game with some personality.Overall, solid core, but an undercooked game that has a lot of missed potential. Perhaps in a sequel....

_childDocuments_.review: is an arcadey Roguelite shooter with striking art but one that might be stretching the definition of the term "lite" as it's possibly the shortest game I've played in this particular genre. It features Ron Perlman as the voice of the main character and while it's novel that he's doing the VO for such a niche title his performance isn't anything noteworthy really.There's plenty of weapons and items to pick up (and unlock) as you liberate lost souls and defeat outlaws but due to the nature of it being a relative straightforward shooter (without character abilities) there's no reason not to opt for the high damage, fast shooting, pistols & shotguns (which also provide critical damage when shooting from cover). So unlike some of its more popular contemporaries you won't find yourself itching to start a new run as every playthrough basically boils down to the exact same formula. There's no real build variety to speak of, let alone the the kind you might see in power fantasy experiences such as Risk of Rain 2 or Binding of Isaac. Once you've beaten the final boss once or twice you've really seen all the game has to offer. Not that its shorter length is a bad ting per se but just don't go in expecting to "loop" it over and over again. The stylized visuals are definitely the highlight of the show but unfortunately can also provide the occasional instance of bad visibility in certain rooms. That said if you can stomach the somewhat clunky controls (or rather how the game handles the combat & cover mechanics) then  is the perfect side dish to whatever other main Roguelike you're playing. Not bad!

_childDocuments_.review: The only good thing this game has going for it is Ron Perlman (best known for his acting in Hellboy and Sons of Anarchy.) Beyond that the games narrative follows a seemingly dead cowboy as he makes his way through "purgatory" which is literally just several corridors that looks like rundown mines. At first glance, the gunplay looks tactical until you discover how the targeting operates. I played on KBM so it would auto-lock onto anything that reacts to being shot IN THE DIRECTION you're firing (from enemies to breakable doors.) So that means if an enemy just so happens to be standing next to a door, you risk auto-targeting locking on the door! And if they are in the dark, just count on missing every shot. This games targeting system RUINS it for me and if they would allow a toggle option to freely aim, I'd easily give it a go. But that coupled with some of the enemies in this game just pummels the experience for me. I recommend that you try it for yourself if you doubt my comment cause it MIGHT be better on controller. But for all my KBM players out there, take it from me when I say that you should wait a couple more patches and see if this game sorts itself out. It is not worth the price tag.Edit 6/23/19Played a bit longer and found the targeting system becomes more intuitive as you luminate the room. So that's nice. There's no stamina gauge for dodging? There WAY too much automatic function. Like if you go to close to cover when the room is empty, your character forces you to cover. Running up to walls and boxes (meant for opening) are touchy in terms of melee. Even enemies up close sometimes dont get melee'd. Just give us a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ melee key. For people who like to uncover the map, there's CONSTANT checkpoints but no teleporting on these elaborate corridors. At this point, theres just WAY too many negatives that outweigh the positive. Definitely refunding the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, a good entry level rogue-like, I guess you could call it a rouge-lite! Sorry, my bad... TLDR; game goes on sale for $4 with DLC a lot, its a great game, DLC good but the section it adds i avoid like the plague because its hard asf (but it gives you a crow that flies around with you so thats awesome), RON PERLMAN AS THE LEAD VOICE ACTOR. Story is great and keeps you interested, gameplay is fun and intuitive but not overly complicated. Soundtrack is insane and meshes phenomenally with gameplay, graphics are great. I have no ill things to say, buy the game if you like anything ive mentioned This game has ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Ron Perlman as the lead protagonist... i mean come on... what more could a man ask for. Casting aside the great voice acting from hell boy himself for a second, we have the best soundtrack ive ever heard, and the very tasteful cell-shaded graphics as well as the game play and the story, both of which are not too hard to grasp and feel great to engage with.  To go over everything in a little more detail:Voice acting: Ron Perlman.Music: it is so damn good. a different song and guitar riff for each of the 10 levels, the riff will play upon entering, clearing a room, and leaving the level. all of which are absolute BANGERS, my favorite is the bayou personally. The music really plays a phenomenal role in this game and sets a great mood for the "wild west" grunge that the game imbues so well.Graphics: If you like tasteful and more artful style graphics this game delivers very well in that regard. I highly suggest that when youre comfortable with the game you turn the brightness all the way down, the game looks so so good.Story/Gameplay: There's not too much story so I wont bother telling you anything more than you can find in the description, but i will say the story is a great "vengeance for good" trope, not much story but whats there i remember thinking was cool. As for the gameplay its a twin-stick cover shooter (can be played with mouse and keyboard but better on controller) Gameplay is not difficult to grasp but you will notice there is plenty of room to improve but not to a degree where you feel youll never get good at the game. There are also difficulties in the main settings that you can select, ive been playing on the hardest difficulty for a long while now and still loving the game. Only have one achievement left.My only gripes with this game is there are some points where you can feel a bit of unpolishedness, such as the delay between dodging again can be a little unforgiving at times due to circumstances meaning that occasionally you're taking damage regardless, which sucks. But, it can be argued that you should never have put yourself in that situation to begin with. The rifles in this game get out-leveled very quickly as their DPS does not warrant their usage beyond the first couple stages, I wish they were shown more love tbh. The last two achievements take foreverrrrr, 50 lost souls and 50 outlaws with no ingame or steam counter is roughhhh. But the game is fun so i persevere. The life cycle for this game is over so I would not expect any new content or fixes to come. Only really annoying bug I have found is the prospector charm which gives you 2x iron (the currency) also makes everything cost twice as much. Any other bugs I've ran into are too few and too far between to remember off the top of my head.I don't think theres much for me to cover beyond that, but if i did not put enough emphasis on it already, but RON PERLMAN and the soundtrack has to be the best medley of noise ive heard from a game in a long time. I'm probably overplaying it at this point but its honestly great.To finish off, if everything i said here is something you love BUY IT NOW, if youre a broke boy like me or arent totally convinced, wait for the sale, i swear i see this game as $4 more often then i dont. Phenomenal game. And if you have any questions feel free to msg me or comment on this post, I am also live on twitch all time the time and if you hop in with questions more likely than not ill boot the game up just to show you! There's also a Raw Fury (the publisher) discord with a section just for West of Dead.-Lagggin

_childDocuments_.review: Look, it aint bad - yet another Steam 'I wish there was a neutral rating' review - but while playing I constantly wish I was playing Hades instead. The art style is sick, if a bit dark at times, and Ron Perlman's a fine voice actor. But at the end of the day I'm not sure the necessary time was spent polishing up all the elements that make a rogue-lite fun, and gives them those delicate little barbed hooks that insert themselves into your cortex.Repetitive runs where you unlock weapons that you don't want (literally, you don't want the item pool packed with a bunch of new stuff once you've unlocked your favs), no progression with the characters in the 'hub' area, and not a lot of variation between runs... a 'let me re-run this real quick just in case I rng a crazy combo' feeling will not be forthcoming.I actually like the quite stripped back combat, where taking cover makes you reload quicker, and rifles, shotguns, revolvers and magnums all have some very specific pros and cons, Meanwhile the accessory items/weapons are not well defined, and often just add noise. Once again, you'll probably find a favourite that you'll stick with, if you remember to use it. The controls are fine, with a 'auto lock on if the enemy is illuminated' mechanic that adds another tactical layer and doesn't frustrate me like it seems to have frustrated other reviewers. I very much enjoy the moment to moment combat and running through a level, when I'm in the zone.That said, often I'm dying in later areas because some sudden b*llshit area attack has frozen me for a second, everyone else piles in, and that's that. If it was more exciting to check out what I've unlocked or progressed between levels this wouldn't be as much of an issue, but really it just means starting over another trudge through the levels. Not very exciting stuff.What pushes it down to a negative is some quality of life stuff that just tips the scales. To skip dialogue you need to mash the skip button, and it will still take a few seconds to go. You'll only realise how annoying this is when you figure out that most of the dialogue is on repeat, and not needed after the first time. There's pretty much no dialogue, to put it in perspective, but ever since Super Meat Boy spoiled us with that quick reset button, I'm sorry, but there's just no room for that ♥♥♥♥ anymore! The other item that tips it is that the 'crow familiar' in the (very affordable) DLC is literally just a silhouette of a crow flying past every now and again. Yeah new level as well, cool, but Raw Fury, common, even you must have noticed that a actual familiar or pretty much anything at all to add flavour to the progression would have been a dream here.I'll beat this flippin' boss soon, and it will have been a nice time, but I won't be sad to put it down and call it a day either.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10PROS:West of Dead is extremely charming.  It oozes Western Thriller from every little bullet hole in its body.  The gun play is very solid and enjoyable.  And playing around the game's use of lighting will make you feel like a right proper genius.  Since the protagonist doubles as the narrator you'll get to hear his voice very regularly, which is awesome, cause his voice actor has one of the smoothest voices in existence, even the repeated lines are a pleasure to listen too, and seldom get old. Lastly, the enemy design, despite appearing unoriginal and one-note at first glance is surprisingly complex.  While yes, if you've fought one guy with a rifle you've fought them all, many of the monster designs are unique and interesting takes on american horror staples, which really hammers in the feeling that something in the game is very, very wrong.CONS:This isn't Dead Cells, it isn't Rogue Legacy, and it DEFINITELY  isn't Hades.  This game is slow burning, time consuming, and at times, quite sluggish.  Every fight is a spaghetti western shootout, and despite the seemingly generous stats you're given from the upgrades, you cannot afford to get hit. Period.  The game has many, many levels, and isn't afraid to kick you all the way back to square one if you don't take it seriously.  Aside from the much slower pace to other rogue-likes, the game's AI isn't the best.  Something I'm willing to forgive for an indie game, but others might not.   The occasional derpy enemy or exploitable boss is something you'll have to look out for during your runs.Lastly, WoD has a noticable issue with its upgrades.  Namely, it has a TON.  And not all of them are particularly useful.  There's an overwhelming amount of things to sift through, and minimal information about each upgrade given to you at face value.  Meaning the resources you invest to permanently grow stronger (namely Sin) will sometimes feel poorly invested. Or in worst cases, flat up wasted.SUMMARY:+Awesome lighting effects+Unique guns+Good variety of equipment+Awesome music!+Awesome sound effects!+Great atmosphere-Slow and tedious gameplay-Difficulty spikes-Minimal enemy variety-Equipment balancing issues-Hard resetsAs long as you don't go into West of Dead expecting another run-gun-fun Rogue-Lite, I can all but guarantee  you'll enjoy yourself.  Take it slow, take it seriously, and you'll enjoy the ride.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Enter The Gungeon, Gunfire Reborn and Fury Unleashed.This game is harder in then all of those Roguelike/lites combined.But while the above mentioned games just requires more skill, West of Dead is often more about luck and some elements feel unfair or designed to end your run.- Lighting LampsMany rooms are dark and filled with enemies. You have to light the room to see where they are and without the light your guns will rarely hit their intended target. The problem is sometimes the lamps are surrounded by tons of enemies. But if you don't light the lamp, you won't be able kill what's in the shadows. Your enemies can still see and shoot you though. The lack of light doesn't affect them and you will be hit in the dark.- Your Gun Options Range From Great to UselessYou unlock guns over time with points you earn by killing enemies. The requirements for unlocking anything powerful are HIGH and you never know which guns are useful and which aren't. And if you pick a dud, well tough ♥♥♥♥ gotta play a dozen or more runs before you can unlock another. No take backs. This isn't a big deal on lower levels, but as you progress the enemies become more bullet spongy and your gun damage stays roughly the same.- Lots of Enemies Small RoomsRooms will often be dinky and it will be you with 4-6 enemies inside. They'll be almost no room to move without taking damage and little to no cover. This will happen often.- Aiming Works Most of the TimeYou'll get use to it after a while, but aiming will always feel clunky and you will hit walls and things you weren't aiming at occasionally. Some of these aiming mishaps will end your run. And it becomes more frustrating because most successful enemy attacks strip away most of your health. Some attacks kill you in one hit even at full health. Every shot counts.West of Dead does a lot of things right but the game play always feels little bit off. But if you likes Roguelites and a challenge, it doesn't get much harder then this (Maybe Dark Souls is harder?) Just prepare yourself for a heavily flawed experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly kind of surprised this game doesn't seem to have a lot of coverage. There are some comparisons to games like Dead Cells and Hades, but I think those are completely misplaced; this is a totally different game from those. Yes, the game has some similar systems such as a health flask that can be recharged between levels and a currency system that is used to permanently unlock items in the loot pool, but the gameplay is absolutely nothing similar. West of Dead is a slow-paced, tactical, twin-stick-style shooter with a heavy emphasis on cover and making every shot count. If you come to this game expecting to shred through dozens of enemies like you can in Dead Cells, you are setting your expectations wrong. That being said, this is, for the most part, a pretty fun game. Properly positioning yourself and timing your shots to take out your enemies feels satisfying if everything goes right. You even get a nice little "KA-CHING" sound every time an enemy dies, which is cool. I also like the darkness system, which further emphasizes the importance of positioning yourself and knowing when to move out of cover. The only real complaint I have is that some encounters feel legitimately unfair. When you walk into a room with at least four or five enemies in it, it's pretty hard to beat it without getting hit at least once. The boss fights can also be a bit frustrating, as some of the bosses are incredibly nimble and hard to hit. However, I haven't unlocked a lot of items yet, and I'm interested to see if further progression will make the character more powerful later on. Ultimately, if you like slow, tactical shooter games, I think this one is worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game in a bundle, but can't recommend it due to poor console port/bad game design, boring game play loop, bugs and overall blandness. "Welcome to Purgatory" is the first achievement, which shows that of all players who own the game 63% of them have got this - safe to assume 63% of players who own the game have started it. This is not always a good indicator based on timing/priority on backlogs, but is a starting point to understand how many people continue with the game. If we look at "level" achievements, the next most common received for completion is the 3rd Global Achievement "Survived the Mountains" at 41.5% ie 21.5% of players cannot be bothered finishing the second level. Here are the global stats for the next levels:- Farm 25%- Town 18.2%- Bayou 17.3%- Church 11.4%- Canyon 5.5%- Graveyard 2.7%- Battlefield 1.4%So 63% of people who have started the game, but only 1.4% of all people have finished the game. So here's why I think that's the case:- Poor console portThe game suffers from strange design decisions related to using a controller. When you're in the menu, you cannot click on each tab, you must press 1 + 2 to navigate left and right (and not the left + right keys). The potion key (hold shift) and talk/activate teleport (shift) share the same key. The hold mechanic is to prevent you accidentally drinking a potion and sharing the same key is due to limited button space. Both of which are not a problem if you have a keyboard. The mouse attacks are stupidly opposite - left icon is right click, right icon is left click. You cannot scroll down with a mouse on when spending Sin, you can only do it with the keys. You cannot click an item in the Sin shop without buying it, if you want to look at an item you must scroll to it using your keys only. - Bad game designBeyond a bad UX, the game suffers from a crippling cover mechanic where you automatically move to cover when you are next to cover. This is true even when there's no enemies and can get in the way of moving to dodge (since cover movement is so slow). The game feels sluggish and unresponsive as a result.- Boring game play loopThe weapons don't significantly feel different - guns are either long ranged or short ranged. Have lots of bullets or few bullets. And that's about it apart from reload speed and damage. There are a very few that have DoT or more stun, but usually only 1 gun exists for each type. - BugsIn my 4 hour play through I've had camera glitches, AI glitches where enemies don't know whether to shoot or take cover, and as a result just twirl in place out in the open. I've also had a freeze, where when meeting an Outlaw they do not activate their speech and the game locks completely forcing an exit.- BlandnessThe art style is unique and a novelty that wears thin quickly. The palette swaps and small details give some variety (farm has grass, bayou has swamp) but in the end feels really bland. The bland weapon choice matches the bland enemy types as well. Overall the game becomes quite the chore to play, as you grind out Sin to buy items.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I got this from a giveaway, because this was mediocre and extremely disappointing. I never thought I'd say that about a twin-stick rogue-lite voice by Ron Perlman, but go play  instead.Combat feels janky if you aren't playing with a controller. "Builds" don't really exist since running health/guns is far more efficient over items (you can clear entire rooms with guns before an item can cool down and kill someone in two hits). The story is okay, until you get to mid and late game where Mr. Perlman sounds like he's bored out of his skull and the game just... ends. Quality of life in general is just poor, with UI constantly feeling clunky and poorly tested. One of the worst parts is that majority of the equipment is disappointing to unlock from the shop mechanic. You won't unlock most things until completing 3-4 floors, only to be disappointed when they're just <standard flintlock with freezing> or <worse damage rifle, but high damage on fringe condition>. After some point, unlocking more things makes your runs harder as poor equipment clogs your drops and in-level shop.West of Dead isn't a bad game, but it's subpar in boring ways that you can't even laugh at. Unless you're out of all the other rogue-lites and twin-stick-shooters out there, go ahead and skip this one.EDIT: I forgot to mention that 4/5 bosses in the game don't come back after being defeated, and the powers they give you don't influence gameplay outside getting past lame gating mechanics and removing fall damage. I legitimately forgot entirely about them sort of how the game does.

Did they just hate it and wanted to get rid of it? there's not a single thing that works or feels good in it!This is maybe half a game, and half of a bad one at that. _childDocuments_.review: A very cool game but it feels severely unfinished. The games visuals are amazing but the UI is incomplete. The biggest and most obvious example being that the Shrines UI, when you are picking upgrades, looks no different than your "general settings" UI. The map is bland and stale, and with such a banger of a theme for the game, how could you not, at the very least, add an old paper treasure map look instead of this stale black and gray map.Combat is nice, but I hate how much the game just keeps trying to play the game for you. The aim assist is very much not needed for a PC game and makes it feel like the game wants to play itself for you. Additionally, your character jumps too much into cover, and the fact that your "taking cover" and "dodging" abilities are both on the same key hurts you more than it helps. The worst times that this happens is when an enemy is trying to chase you down, and instead of dodging away from their attack, you simply glue yourself to a nearby cover and leave yourself exposed >:(The dialogue feels empty and hollow, while yes, these characters are dead, that is no excuse to not make them interesting. If they are boring in death, then they were no more interesting in life. And if their character isn't interesting, why would I bother talking to them at all?Overall, cannot say that I could recommend this game, as it overall lacks a lot of polish in both gameplay and UI.PS - I think another players description fit this game perfectly "This is just a beautiful exercise in frustration"

_childDocuments_.review: When I first reviewed this game, I thought it was really good but had some annoying bugs. Then the bugs became more and more annoying (ie. doors not breaking when they should have, impeding progress and locking out useful items). Then I got to the final boss and found that my build was completely ill-equipped for it (I used revolvers and shotguns but the boss felt like a battle where rifles and pistols would have worked better), so I stopped playing.During my hiatus from the game, it got a bunch of significant updates that included game rebalancing as well as bug fixes. Today I decided to give it another go to see what had changed.At first it was promising. Everything seemed smoother and more polished, and some of the cosmetic bugs from before had been fixed. There was also a selection of useful and affordable new weapons so I had something to work towards.And then I reached the mines and one of those stone golems appeared. Instead of chasing me (which it needs to do so you can dodge around it and shoot it in the back) it just stood on the spot. I still managed to defeat it but the door it was guarding remained locked, which meant I either couldn't progress or couldn't collect whatever items were down that path. This is a HUGE issue in a roguelike, where not having the best available equipment can make all the difference between life and death.Sorry, but these kinds of issues (doors not unlocking and enemies not moving) have been part of the game for years now. And just like before, I'm now starting to wonder if they'll ever get fixed.It's a shame because everything else about this game- the visuals, sound, game mechanics, level design etc- is fantastic. It's just that the game has some pretty big bugs that have been present since launch and still haven't been fixed. Yes the game has been drastically improved since launch, but IMO it's still not at the point where it's really worth the money (at least from a stability perspective).I wish I could recommend this game, but I just can't anymore... unless you want to get it during a sale and take your chances, but don't say I didn't warn you.

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead is an underrated gem in the genre. It's not Isaac or Gungeon, and people going in expecting another bullet hell dungeon crawler are setting themselves up for disappointment. This is a tactical cover shooter, meaning cover is encouraged, not dodge rolling or weaving through bullets. A cover shooter set in a somber interpretation of purgatory in the American west, riddled with occult nightmare spawn and a healthy variety of guns to dispense underworld brand justice, all complimented perfectly by a forlorn yet brutal acoustic soundtrack and incredibly memorable art direction straight out of a Hellboy comic, It's like what would happen if Mignola was raised on Clint Eastwood movies instead of Dracula.

_childDocuments_.review: "West of Dead" is a console ported 3D rendered isometric twin stick cover shooter (and in case you are wondering, cover shooter + twin stick shooter concepts do not work well together at all).  The idea is that you are Ghost Rider but in the wild west (yeah, Marvel is gonna sue) voiced by TV's Ron Perlman (Beauty and the Beast, 1987).  You run around small procedurally generated levels shooting bad guys and walking between snap-cover objects so you can't get shot as much.  There's a slew of problems here and I feel bad for Ron Perlman having his name attached to such a badly made game.  Before getting into the rest of the problems with this console game on PC, the real killer here is the crappy consolesque camera angles that are thoroughly unpleasant to have to wrestle with as a PC gamer.  One of many limitations that the console heritage of the game brings... and while that's enough to disqualify the game, there's more, and it's worse.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The game features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the 1990s.  There's some cel-shading style attached to it to try hide the low quality game assets, but it doesn't work, the low quality assets are plain to see.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the game (maybe they blew all their budget on Ron?), and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks bad as a result of their decisions, a compromise PC gamers shouldn't have to put up with.The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game."West of Dead" has the almost scam-like price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun roguelike with an original cover based combat mechanic.It has style, it has punch, it has some replayability and a few variation on its combat. There is even little metaprogression to keep you playing. Combat is interesting, and it's what makes or breaks this game. It's basically all about strategic cover switching. The flashy trailers are a bit misleading, imo. West of Dead is a cover shooter first, where you move from cover to cover, avoiding enemy bullets, while shooting at the same few enemy types over and over again. The controls need a few rounds to get completely used to, it was very weird at first that shift was the main interact key. But it works, because this game is all about efficiency. You can only shoot a few times before reloading, so choosing cover for faster reloads is crucial. This type of combat design is probably not for everyone, but a run and gun game would get boring much much faster. There about three different kinds of weapons, the rest are just slight variations of these. This system lasts a few hours, unfortunately the game is just too long. Getting to the final levels simply takes so much time and an ambushed from a dark corner could happen any time. I don't know if this is a bug, but sometimes the room complete sound effect plays before all enemies are dispatched. I took so much unnecessary damage, just because I though the room was safe, just to receive a bullet from a dark corner a second later.There is some jank in the game, but not nearly as much as other reviews seem to suggest. I say try it out for an hour, if the combat clicks with you, you will know it really fast.

A run is around 30 minutes to 2 hours (for completed ones). It can feel a bit repetitive in the end, but I guess completionists can find it amusing to unlock new weapons as they collect souls.The narrative is somewhat clear. I liked the simple yet effective animations/cinematics which looked like a mix of tarot and medecine wheels. Something strange, as all other elements point to "European themes" (the church, priest, purgatory and the colonisation of the West by settlers). _childDocuments_.review: First things first: this game is highly addictive and a lot of fun. There are many positive aspects of the game design, like the soundtrack, graphic design, and gameplay. But there are also other issues that could improve the game. For instance, while the narrator of the player is awesome, it is a shame that all other NPC have no real narrators (and instead we have only subtitles). Also, there is a very steep difficulty increase between levels; if you aren’t luck enough to find a good matching weapons and gear, you will have a very hard time moving forward (you will die). Finally, it seams you need to finish the first run of the game to unlock other aspects of the game, basically requiring you to go for 2 playthroughs; its ok because the game is fun, but at the same time it fells like a bit of cheating, in order to artificially increase the play time of the game; I would rather have more original content…Also, the end of the game (chapter 4) is too abrupt and the story line feels incomplete. Overall, an 8/10, a good purchase on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and stylistically presented isometric rogue-like with a nice snap-to-cover mechanic that surprisingly doesn't get in the way often. The game's kit variety gets good later on, as you are able to take advantage of crit and stun damage as well as timing the lamp-lights for instant stuns. The various perks and abilities allow you to play aggressive or passive in the encounters. I think this build strength could have been extended even further if the game weren't as stingy with its unlock points, or had more perks and abilities unlocked from the beginning. While fairly consistent, the player's dodge roll mechanic could be routinely defeated by some annoying enemy types, who's first shot will miss and second shot will snap onto the player nearly every time as the dodge animation is finished.There is a narrative mystery that is revealed as the player defeats bounties, as well as an over-arching story, but it's all fairly bare-bones and unobtrusive. The main character's VA is well done, but it would have been nice if other NPCs were also given VA. Apart from the VA, the sound design is functional and gives the player good situational awareness Overall it's a fun rogue-like that doesn't ask too much of the player's time or money, considering the game is frequently on sale for 75% off. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun roguelite with great gameplay and nice aesthetics. If you generally enjoying messing around with cowboy combat (finding cover, using pistols vs. muskets vs. shotguns) West of dead is pretty satisfying. The random level design makes every run a new challenge and you can get lucky or unlucky with how hard your run is.I do get the feel like this game isn't quite finished, or it could be a lot more. The story offers intrigue but isn't very responsive and intensive. There's characters to talk to but the dialogue is minimal and doesn't go anywhere (at least not in the first dozen play-throughs which is as far as I've gotten). You unearth memories of your character's life before death but that's also too slow to feel to meaningful. The writing doesn't feel prioritized, which is a downer just because the game is quite good so it makes you imagine what it could be if the writers had more time/money etc.It's very Stephen King's The Gunslinger in the way it takes Western tropes and then pours in American Gothic horror. But it doesn't get very dark or scary. The tone is ominous but nothing particularly bad ever seems to happen.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I'm not gonna start this review with the bugs, since I want to say all the positive things first and why you should still consider buying this game. First of all, the combat is hella fun, it can be frantic or methodical, depending on your style of play and what types of enemies you're facing. I think the devs nailed the twin shooter mechanics and gun variety, altough there are some weapons that can carry a run and some you will likely never use. The different biomes were really well realised and each had a distict feel to it, with a good amount of enemy variety and scaling difficulty. The individual shooting galleries were really fun to maneuver around in and complemeted the combat style perfectly. However, travelling between those arenas can be a bit tedious. The stroy is honestly really captivating and even though there is not a lot of it, I was always excited to pick a memory remnant and bring it to the witch, to learn more about mason and the preacher. Now I have to talk about the bugs. The ones I encountered (in decending order of frequency) were: 1.) the game randomly black-screening for a couple of seconds, which was annoying, especially in hectic firefights, but pausing the game until I could see the screen again was a pretty effective band aid "fix". 2.) the character model dissapearing, which usually came from a collision issue when vaulting over cover and landing iside an enemy, but a quick reload always fixed the issue3.) voice lines and music not playing correctly All in all, some annoying and slightly game breaking bugs, but nothing too egregious. To summarise: A really good indie game, with fun combat, interesting story, some slight bugs and moderately good replay value. If this game is on your whishlist and comes on sale for -50% you should definitely check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: (This is a long review. For the summary, skip to the pros and cons and my Score)If you are feeling the rough and tumble western vibe and want a roguelike that captures that same spirit, then this is the game for you! In this twin stick roguelike you will find your inner Punisher and send evil spirits West using a combination of knives, guns, and explosives. Ron Perlman's voice means you will want to listen to every line (at least the first time through) of the main character. The selection of weapons and abilities and charms was enough to add meaningful variety to each playthrough. While some weapons felt a little samey (Damage Over Time (DOT) weapons like fire and poison effects) they are not prolific. Changing from a rifle to a pistol or a shotgun or a revolver can determine if you survive the level. Equipment and Charms determined how much risk you wanted vs how much reward.Need help surviving? Take a health recouping charm.Need to pull out some more money (called 'iron' in-game)? Prospector charm has you covered.Need some added utility? There are a couple charms for that too.Want a solid finisher move? Take the knife with crit on stun.Need help clearing a bunch of weakling enemies? Mines are the equipment for you!Need to block the bullet coming out of the gun that you just accidentally threw yourself in front of? Shield yourself!Only having 1 charm and 2 equipment slots means you had to decide what you really need to balance your build. If you have ever played dead cells this game will feel very familiar. Better than deadcells though, is the apparent story. It pops up on occasion and helps you get into the protagonist's shoes. The art style is thematically solid and darkly beautiful, but on rare occasions the camera and art style can conflict leading to some moments of character blindness. The game and art is dark more than it is light. and Light actually plays a key game mechanic. Enemies in the dark cannot be targeted with aim assist, Lighting a lamp stuns all enemies that can see the light and helps with the art style. Pretty elegant. The level portal system is like dead cells for quick map navigation which is good because the main character is not fast and going down a spur of a level can be a little tedious but always rewarding (I ALWAYS explore as much as is beneficial.. its part of my gaming style). Completing certain levels will reward you with small Metroidvanic abilities that unlock shortcut paths/levels or get you an additional ability or gun drop. The pace of the game is MUCH slower than most roguelikes and you need all the time that it gives you to strategize against your enemies and capitalize on your environment. Minibosses called 'outlaws' are quite fun to encounter because they used the same weapons and abilities that you have access to as the player character. It felt more like pvp, but highly manageable. For those of your worrying about crunching damage numbers in order to win, it has an intuitive gun damage system. a higher level gun will always have more damage than its lower level counterpart but each shot is labeled as necessary and critical values are all displayed and easy to understand. No hidden math to unmask an op weapon or build. Damage can increase with upgrades but base damage of weapons are all kept at a comparable point. (ie: rifle lvl 2 does 10 damage and rifle lvl 3 does 13 damage even if you have upgraded your gun damage 3 times since you picked up the lvl 2 rifle to the unknown effect of +50%+35%+14% 'is that multiplicative or additive percentage points? what about..." no. stop. all gun damage is increased relative to the base value. play the game how your want and dont worry about the math.) The fact that not everything is displayed in damage per second (DPS) values means you should experiment with everything to fit/maximize your enjoyment and playstyle. This lead me to sometimes not take the higher level gun if I didn't like its play mechanics.The cover system is one that I have not seen matched in a rougelike. You use guns that need to be reloaded. Reloading happens a lot when you shoot a lot of enemies. Cover is both your safe haven and your speedloader, but it is not overpowered. Your enemy can use cover too. It is also destructible so you cant just hide forever. Some enemies punish your for thinking cover will get you through every fight. It won't, and thats ok. It adds to your need to strategize and git gud.Novel to its genre, is a difficulty slider! I ran on normal, not finding the difficulty slider until after I beat the 3rd chapter of the game so if you are finding the game too easy or too hard just give yourself a nudge either way to make it match your skill level. Usually with roguelikes its just 'git gud or die endlessly' but this can help ease that stumbling block for the casual roguelike player.For this twinstick rouguelike western I give a 7.7/10Pros:Fun GunsLots of GunsIntuitive damage system The game rewards your skill and strategy Difficulty sliderRon Perlman's husky and incredibly thematically accurate voiced character.Risk and reward system is rewarding more than it is risky for the careful gamerHelpful tips and explanations about game mechanics.Art StyleCons: Game makes you stop to listen to the protagonist almost every time. _childDocuments_.review: West of Dead is a relatively functional attempt at what on the surface should be slam dunk of a concept; a twin-stick shooter western between an undead lawman and his greatest foe, a demonically empowered preacher. It sometimes works, but fundamental flaws make it a brief, albeit fun distraction rather than a competitive roguelike in the vein of Enter the Gungeon or Dead Cells. StoryRon Perlman as the main character Mason is fun enough to listen to, but his drawl is never used for anything particularly profound or interesting. As I write this, I can't think of any line or phrase that stands out from a general haze of westernisms. No one else has anything particularly interesting to say either, although I was curious enough about the memories you occasionally find. It isn't bad, its just not what'll be playing the game for Gameplay:West of Dead's gunplay is pretty fun at first. There is a decent variety of weapons that you unlock with currency collected in game in the style of Dead Cells. Weapons you find earlier in runs do less damage than ones you find or buy later that run, so you're encourage to switch up your fighting style as you go. Pistols, revolvers, shotguns and rifles make up your primary armaments, supplemented by thrown bombs, axes, knives, and the occasional melee ability. Ammunition capacity is low with relatively long reloads, so good aim, timing, and use of cover is needed to deal damage quickly and safely. You spend most combat rolling between bullets, dodging away from enemies, picking off enemies before ducking away to reload. Its further supplemented by the game's use of light; lanterns can be activated or thrown to light up rooms and briefly stun enemies for more damage. When done correctly, its is a frantic, barroom brawl style of combat as you fire bullets in all directions, knock over explosive barrels, and flashbang someone before diving for cover. And this is all fun. The problem is the game alternates between trivially easy or frustratingly inconsistent. For reference I have played the game for approximately five hours. I finished the game (beat the final boss with the additional criteria needed to get the credits), and managed to do it without ever dying. Enemies are not capable of standing against you except on the final levels of each run. This is partly because of how strong cover is (ranged enemies struggle to fight you behind cover, and most melee enemies are not fast enough/ do not have the initative to close in to flush you out before you can shoot them down), partly because enemies don't do much damage, partly because enemies have the same ammunition restrictions you do, and partly because you game showers you with recovery options. Health pickups are common, your healing ability is easily upgraded, and numerous charms exist to let you recover some lost health. When the game does start hitting hard and faster, you're already equipped to run roughshod over your problems. At that point the only remaining danger are the occasional homing attacks from bosses that are incredibly awkward to dodge. Enemy variety is present, but with one exception I was never forced to learn much of anything about my opponents. My strategy of "bomb and shoot" worked on everything except some golems, which instead required "dodge and bomb and shoot in the back." The game also wastes a good amount of your time by encouraging you to backtrack through long samey hallways to find health pickups or alternative weapons. West of Dead is a functional and fun distraction, but for anyone seeking a roguelike experience with the replayability to match, there are stronger entries across the board.

_childDocuments_.review: This review has been shortened from its original version to fit the Steam character limit. My full review is hosted , and contains my additional thoughts on: Audio Design, Visuals, Narrative+, Gameplay+The Metroidvania elements had my curiosity peaked to search every nook and cranny, the areas seemed to randomly generate randomly enough to make every run-through feel fresh and unique. There were enough enemy designs to keep me on my toes, though there were a couple that I thought should have been different for sure. I was genuinely surprised at times to find the enemies strategically flanking me out of cover which led to some pretty cool western showdowns out in the open, as I dodged bullets and creatures with guns blazing through slow-motion accents across the room to the next cover.I think the most important thing to understand about West of Dead is that it has all of the pieces of success. There are so many mechanics that independently work well, or seem like they should work on paper, but for me as a player who has played countless roguelites, it’s clear that West of Dead doesn’t have the polish it needs for all of its ideas to come together into a satisfying whole. So, keep that in mind as I continue on.The first sin West of Dead makes is that it gives the player auto-aim. The way the devs try to balance this is that your character only locks on to enemies in lit areas of the room you’re trapped in, so there are lanterns you can ignite to get your auto-aim back. There is technically twin-stick shooting you can do here, but it’s often quite frustrating to use, perhaps on purpose of course. I understand how maybe the isometric perspective could be the culprit here, and that’s probably why this particular system is in place, but losing that player engagement from not needing to aim made some of the game a bit easier, but also equally a bit more boring as it is less engaging. This is compounded by the waiting required to reload your weapons… as there’s no active reload, no manual button press, it’s just on a countdown timer (after you run out of shots, or after you stop shooting for a second), which furthers the lack of engagement you have with the game.The second sin is it is counterproductive to expand the item pool. West of Dead takes the Dead Cells approach with its item pool and allows you to unlock more items to play with using a resource (Sin) you gain from killing enemies. The problem is that it doesn’t take long to find that there are two weapons that don’t need unlocking… one, a revolver with 5 shots, the fifth shot doing critical (double) damage, and the other, a shotgun that does critical damage so long as you’re behind cover. Those are the only guns you’ll need to beat the game. You’re always behind some cover, so the shotgun is always double damage. The revolvers shoot and reload quickly and the critical damage on the final shot is too much to ignore. They’re such good weapons, given to you right in the beginning that nothing else matters. Expanding the item pool with more weapons just reduces your chances of getting those guns.This leads to the third and final major sin, the other play styles (damage types) are not effective. There are weapons and items that deal bleed damage. There are weapons and items that deal poison damage. There are weapons and items that deal fire damage. These sound cool conceptually, but they are all the same — they deal damage over time. What’s worse, is that they never deal more damage than guns that deal critical damage. These damage types that do damage over time simply don’t deal enough damage fast enough. You can even see in their descriptions that the DPS of these weapons and items is always second to any other type of gun because of their status effects. For some strange reason, the status effects never deal more damage than any other counterpart. For example, if I can deal 60 damage with the 5-shot critical revolver in a sub-two second burst (10 damage 4 shots, 20 damage one shot), what you find is that any other gun that deals damage over time via status effects will deal 55 damage total. Over 5 seconds or something. The effects also never stack. It just doesn’t make sense. Of course, I’m going to take the near-instant 60 damage over waiting 5 seconds to get similar (but still worse) damage. It might make sense if damage types had an advantage over an enemy type or even all enemies in an area, but it’s, unfortunately, a shallow system that frustratingly doesn’t pay off.Again, important to note, before the previously mentioned sins were discovered, I had a fun time playing the game, and I do think it has all the pieces to succeed - It just needs some tweaking to make it worth playing (at least for players like me).I really thought [the narrative] was well done, it’s probably the best part of the entire game. It’s mysterious, and it doesn’t give you enough answers to ever make you satisfied. Even after I had beaten the game, I kept playing for a bit and I was still getting new threads to the story that continued to build on this overarching narrative. It was very well-paced and very satisfying to put together. I do wish I learned a bit more about the demons and the locations within this purgatory location, but still, excellent system, especially for a roguelite.The voice acting is okay? I think it would have landed even better if they chose a different person voicing the protagonist. We have this ultra metal ghost rider flaming skull cowboy… and the voice actor, bless his soul, is the most deadpan inflection-less dude they could have ever picked. His performance fell really flat for me — everyone else was fine.I played this on my SteamDeck, and I had a solid experience for the entirety of my playtime with no lag or other hiccups.Ultimately, West of Dead is an Off-Brand product, and I can’t say that I recommend it. The three gameplay sins I have mentioned above: lack of player engagement, counterproductive item pool expansion, and ineffective alternate play styles (or damage types) make it a hard recommendation for someone looking for their next roguelite fix. The most concise I can be with this review, is that I had most of my fun up through one full run of the game, and I’m a bit saddened that as a roguelite, it offered more, but the game’s systems are not optimized enough to give me the drive to experience it.If West of Dead had a bit more play testing, a little more time in the oven, and a few good tweaks to iron out those 3 major sins with perhaps a little extra flare on top, this would be a hidden gem of a game. But, I don’t think it will get that as it’s had one DLC already. It’s a bit sad to see it get so close. On another note, I’m really interested in what this developer cooks up next, there’s definitely a possibility for greatness in a sequel or spiritual successor using what the developers learned here, and I am keen on following their progress, and wishing them the best in their future endeavors.I arrived at this conclusion after 11.2 hours of gameplay, and while I thought I might play more to continue to expand the item pool just to see what else was in there, I believe this review will mark the end of my journey with West of Dead, and I will mark it off my backlog. There are just better roguelite options available for me to play. While there is DLC available, I’m not interested in returning for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than I was expecting! A roguelike with stylish graphics and some fun voice acting from Ron Perlman. The whole game oozes with style - from the "ghost rider" main character, to the western weaponry and character designs, to the dark, menacing descriptions of the various levels that instill an epic sense of foreboding. There are demons, undead, witches, and all manner of evil cryptids to undo on your journey out of purgatory. The combat flows smoothly with a decent blend between attacking, moving, and dodging mechanics that create a sense of satisfaction when you outwit or outgun a particularly tricky group of enemies. The game heavily rewards an action-strategy approach to each combat scenario, and makes you feel like a boss with a lovely little "DING" every time you fell an opponent.There are some things that I don't like very much - having played roguelikes like Risk of Rain, I feel like there are not enough upgrade/build options. You have to do a lot of work to get a small collection of upgrades. When you get them, BOY do they help, but it can feel pretty stale on occasion while trying to find them. A positive to this is that the game feels balanced enough that you don't HAVE to have the upgrades to have a good time. But again, I wish there were more, or additional build mechanics to further make each playthrough a little more complex and fun.One complaint is that there are certain character upgrades that stack less and less at a sort of witch's totem, where you can choose from 2 or 3 upgrades at a time. As you level each one of 3 categories, you get less and less of a bonus with each upgrade (e.g. your first weapon damage upgrade is 50% bonus damage. The seventh is like 7-9%). While I can see some of the logic behind this as far as reminding the player to bolster ALL of their attributes and not just one, it makes it harder to get a lot out of dedicated builds, such as a high damage shotgun one-shot build or a high health tank with weapons that deal bleed damage to outlast your foes. Builds that would be viable with a consistent boost to certain stats (e.g. 20% with every level gained), or even having a straight up RPG style leveling system with multiple stats where you can allocate points where you choose would be preferrable in my book.Despite how flowy combat can be, it sometimes feels stiff. It's frustrating to fire your shotgun and have to wait for it to reload before you can fire it for a short time again. This is part of the design of the game, as it is more of a tactical action-strategy one, and for me, it's frustrating all the same. All that being said, I think the game is nonetheless super fun, and well worth the $20 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the first "roguelike" I've played.This game is a top-down shooter, with you aiming in the direction you are facing. Aim assist is available, and even at its default setting of mid it can be very generous. Taking cover behind objects is recommended, as you get a substantial boost to reload speed; very useful when the majority of your guns won't have more than three shots, unless they are pistols.It's not very challenging on its default setting; when writing this review, I beat the final boss in about four hours, and I played very sloppily and died several times. An experienced player in the genre will very likely beat the game even faster.I liked the art direction the game chose; light plays a role in gameplay where igniting a lamp in an area will stun enemies nearby. This is hardly needed, as you can absolutely take shots at them in the dark by looking at their bullet trails, and you are told by a ring around your character where attacks are coming from.Sound is also very nice. Guns have a nice pop evocative of Western films, revolvers get a nice bonus with a spinning of the cylinder when fully reloaded, and all combat ends with a little strum on a guitar.I do not have any of the DLC for this game, and thus am uncertain if the story continues past Chapter 4; if it does not, there's certainly something there that could be built upon.

_childDocuments_.review: FYI I played the beta so I actually have more hours than what this review will indicate at the time of writing. West of Dead is a vaguely difficult Rogue-lite with solid mechanics and level design. Unlike most other rogue type games, it has a story that is much more apparent and doesn't require any digging or extra work on the player's part. The story is somewhat dark and fun to piece together as you play with some well done voice acting by Ron Perlman. First and foremost it is a cover based combat system with many weapons and items being influenced by whether or not you are in cover, this shouldn't be seen as boring or lazy by any means as most enemies have one advantage over the player; being faster, dealing more damage, or the ability to completely destroy cover in one hit. The cover is destructible by the player and enemies but comes back after about 5-10 seconds. with a lighting system that (I at least) have never seen in a game before, some parts of the rooms are automatically lit while other lanterns need to be turned on by the player adding a layer of danger to basically every room as you don't know where all the enemies are, or even what they are, lanterns that need to be turned on at least offer the bonus of stunning all enemies in the light's range. Allowing the player to gain visibility and get some easy hits on enemies. The combat is not super challenging if you are patient or at the very least play smart (keeping a variety of weapons and not just playing long or short range exclusively). the enemies and bosses never feel like they are cheating or broken, its a well balanced game where (personally) you never feel like your death was undeserved. All in all I recommend it to anyone looking to play a fun rogue game that likes cowboy aesthetics. There ares some glitches here and there but in my experience they are minor and fix themselves or can be fixed by destroying some cover.PS fans of dead cells may have a particular interest in this game as it has a VERY similar system in terms of how it adds items to the RNG Pool through currency dropped by enemies that you can only deposit in between stages, among other similarities.PPS USE A CONTROLLER, in case it's not obvious when you look at the control schemes it's supposed to be a controller played game, if you refuse and want to use keyboard go ahead but it's MUCH better on controller, trust me
