_childDocuments_.review: If you would like to see the In the bleak darkness of Purgatory, you assume the role of a lone gunslinger, seeking his memories and a purpose, all the while contending with various groups of enemies and monsters. Purgatory is quite unique, shifting and changing with each run. As you dart between points of cover and inch your way towards the villainous Outlaws to claim their Souls, you will gradually expand your otherwordly arsenal of late 1800's firearms and gadgets.William Mason is the starring character in West of Dead, voiced by actor Ron Perlman, and he has a fair amount of dialogue for most situations, making the journey feel a little more personal. As you begin each run, you will be greeted by a few NPC's in Purgatory's finest bar. These characters don't have much to say, but they can give you direction and hints as to how to proceed. Further in, you'll frequently encounter the Witch, who can awaken the Remnants you collect from enemies and bosses, granting you new unlockable gear and an occasional bit of lore.Your runs begin in the bar, but the Crypt level is only a short walk away. As soon as you pass through the front gates your run truly begins, and each corridor and room will be randomly generated for you to navigate. You can explore rooms to find enemies that drop currency and Remnants, equipment and stat upgrades, Lost Souls, mini-bosses, and exits to other floors that branch out ever so slightly. While some factors on floors remain consistent, the exact layout and contents of each floor will be randomized. As with any other rogue-lite, death is not the end. A run always resets Mason to Lv. 1 in his three primary stats (Health, Gun Damage, and Ability Scaling), and he will lose his equipped gear. From the gates of the Crypt, Mason can outfit himself anew to prepare for his next conquest of Purgatory.Where West of Dead really starts to set itself apart is its interesting combat. Mason can equip a passive buff charm, two guns, and two abilities. Guns each have their own damage, fire rate, chamber size, and stun values, among other more crazy effects on a per gun basis, and abilities are typically thrown (hatchet, etc.) or melee weapons on cooldowns, with a few exceptions for utility. You can and should always stick to cover, which will become obvious as you find yourself strongly magnetized to the different debris in every room. Cover not only makes you practically immune to damage, but it also grants a significant reload buff, and both guns are reloaded simultaneously whenever you aren't shooting. Mason can dodge roll with generous amounts of immunity, but it has a long recovery. The only time you'll want to venture out from cover is to reposition, or to enable a light source. Without illuminating your enemies, your aiming precision feels like anti-aim-assist, as bullets seem to bloom outwards from your firing direction.  a light, your shots are insanely accurate and it will be almost difficult to miss.+ Visual style, voice acting, and music are great and really lend to the atmosphere of the game. The story seems interesting enough, but I personally didn't care about it after a while+ Engaging gunplay with satisfying feedback. It feels very good to go from room to room and trade shots with other enemies, sliding between points of cover while gathering Souls and Remnants in anticipation of something cool to unlock- Unfortunately, as far as unlocking cool things goes, most guns and gear are underwhelming for how random and difficult it is to discover their Remnants. As you unlock more, you dilute the pool of gear to find during a run, with most equipment being different flavors of knives, or guns offering crazy abilites that range from lackluster to straight up useless compared to the standard fare- Once you understand cover, the game is pretty much over on Normal difficulty. Pistols and shotguns dominate most of the game, and more elaborate strategies or weapons have little payoff. That said, trading shots with enemies using the same cover as you feels inconsistent, and perfectly evading certain attacks or group patterns feels unfair, as if to compensate for how shallow the cover system is. Lastly, I think Abilities are poorly thought out, with higher level gear only upgrading cooldowns, and the majority of them being knives you will never want to be close enough to use- Actually navigating levels is dull and slow, as Mason has a low movement speed, and teleporters are often poorly spaced with lengthy animations to sit through. On the other end of things, rather strangely, most enemy encounters can be skipped outright by simply walking past them, though that isn't any fun and the game seems to have trouble processing this sometimes- The game has many bugs and glitches that can end runs or force a restart, such as your character becoming invisible and unable to shoot, or Lost Souls required for the ending being impossible to collect. Then you have level geometry disappearing, achievements being bugged/misleading, attacks that linger long after they've disappeared, etc. - The final boss is very underwhelming, and after defeating them, you'll end up in the same transitional room with healing that's between every floor, even though the run is over. Combined with all the glitches, the weird MS paint splatter all the equipment icons have, the wonky animations and effects... and overall it just feels incomplete~ If you focus on the story, then the game will be over in a few hours. There isn't much reason to play more afterwards, as the remaining content is just a grind that gets worse over time. At least the initial experience is decentWest of Dead offers another fresh take on the rogue-lite experience with its expressive gunplay and setting. However, this experience can quickly sour and there isn't really much meat on its bones. It honestly feels unfinished. If you are looking for a short and sweet experience guided by Ron Perlman, then go ahead and give this one a shot, as it goes on sale quite often. If you are looking for mechanical or narrative depth though, this one is a definite pass, as West of Dead is more trouble than it's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very surprised by this game. I came in not expecting much and came out pleasantly surprised.Let's start off with the visuals and sound. This game looks spectacular. The artstyle here fits perfectly with the dark environments of the game. Character designs are great and are easy to differentiate from one another. Music and sound are good. The voice acting is amazing with Ron Perlman voicing the protagonist, but this also leads to a problem. He is the only voice actor for the game, other characters of any sort of importance are completely silent. This is most likely, because the devs spent all of their budget on getting him to voice for this game, so it could be debated on whether this was a good choice for the game.Next up is gameplay. I really enjoy the gameplay here. This game is of course is a roguelite, so if you have any knowledge of this game genre then you'll know what to expect. Combat is similar to a top-down shooter, but not quite. You see, when you aim into a certain direction, you'll lock on to an enemy in that direction, so there's not much of good aim needed here on your part. The game is primarily played as a cover shooter, because your character hides behind a piece of cover when you walk up to it. Level and enemy variety here is pretty good, but the bosses leave more to be desired. Most bosses are stronger version of existing enemies or is just a reskin of the priest boss which you'll be fighting in the game on multiple occasions. The final boss is fun, but a bit too easy. Weapon variety here is really good. I like how many of them feel very much different from one another. I especially like the one's with unique passives like "Critical hits when bullets ricochet off walls", "Critical hits when hiding behind cover", or "Temporarily increasing speed after being shot". One problem I have with the weapons is that most weapons feel weak and you'll often resort to the less interesting stronger weapons to beat levels. The difficulty of the game is done pretty well. Not too hard, but not too easy. Lastly is story. The story is fine. It's told through memories which you gain through special encounters throughout the game. While these are interesting to listen to and help flesh out some of the mysteries of the game, I unfortunately feel that these are spread out the game a bit too far from one another, so it's often hard to to remember where you currently are in the story when you gain a new one.Before I end this review, I did encounter one glitch in the game which caused me to fail a run in the game, because my character fell through the world to his death.In conclusion, this game is a very fun few hours, but don't expect to be blown away. The game knows what it is and does it well. While I don't like giving games a score rating, I would say that this is a perfect example of a solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tricky one. I personally enjoyed it, but I totally get the negative reviews. I've been craving something a bit different as far as Roguelites go and this game was different enough that its kept me interested. Combat is fairly straight-forward and methodical once you figure out how the cover system works, and you learn how to work around certain weird behaviours. For instance, using the Lasso from cover will remove you from cover, so you quickly need to re-enter it or you'll probably get shot by the thing you just Lassoed. Bosses that freeze in place, and the auto-fire shoots out of the room ... so you have to melee them until they wake back up. General jankiness of movement and controls where you feel like a sluggish molasses compared to some of the best action roguelites. Honestly the weird jankiness and art style feel so similar to Tribes of Midgard, it makes me wonder if both teams used the same underlying code.To make things even more tedious, it forces you to waste a lot of time running between rooms for no real reason; its not like there's timers like in Dead Cells keeping you moving and frantically looking for an exit, or hallways filled with traps to dodge like in Curse of the Dead Gods. You're just running through empty hallways for 10-30 seconds between each battle before you find something worth doing, which is usually just a powerup with a needlessly slow UI, or a side-room you need a special Rune to access, which again just takes a needless amount of time to investigate and get back to the hunt, mostly because Teleporting itself is pointlessly slow, like its going through an entire loading screen just to go back up a ledge you just jumped down. The level designs are basically copy-paste jobs with hallways between rooms, nothing exotic between them like you'd find in a game like Dead Cells which spices things up by creating uniquely-style rooms, or chaining together in interesting ways to create claustrophobic sewers, or cliffsides, or ancient tombs. Just combat rooms, corridors and random powerups. So, suffice to say, massively wasted potential because is has fairly fun combat, just very little else to support it as far as reward systems/permanent upgrades, exploration/secrets, enemy/boss variety, and combat intensity goes. There's few peaks and troughs in intensity depending on what crazy thing you're going to stumble on next, as the game is very even, flat and can get repetitive quickly.Even still, I've been enjoying it, but then I got it dirt cheap in the Summer Sale. Had I paid full price for this, I'd probably have felt cheated, lured in by a pretty art style and Ron Perlman. But, for $6 it's been entertaining enough. The weapons are unique enough, there's a certain strategy to the combat, and the boss fights can be pretty fun, even if they are all generally similar.Give it a try and maybe 10-30 minutes, at which point you've seen enough to know if its for you or not.

_childDocuments_.review: A great rogue-like, situated in a dark, supernatural wild west purgatory. The only thing holding this amazing gem back is the controls.To start off, I don't know if the developers are fans of Dead Cells, but the entire game, for me, felt like 3D Dead Cells in a dark Wild West setting, but maybe that's just me. But I digress...The game creates this fantastic atmosphere, interesting storyline and engaging risk/reward gameplay with features getting unlocked as you progress through the chapters and defeat bosses for path-unlocking powers. The voice, look and feel of everything just hits the visual spot behind a 600 MB download. In this day and age, when people drool over 20K textures and hyperrealistic lighting and god knows what else, this game simply packs up everything it needs in a neat, little package and certainly delivers 100%.For the most part I had a lot of fun playing through this game, even with the uncontrollable camera which some people distinctly hate. The entire aiming control felt like it's lagging behind a fraction of a second. It's no biggy but you'd expect the controls as tight as a drum. But the fatal flaw of the game is it's "sticky" automatic cover system. It's not a deal-breaker as you can learn to play with/around it. But it really leaves a bad taste in my mouth when I try to run towards a stunned enemy next to an object only for the character to stop and glue themselves to the cover while leaving me exposed to the stunned enemy who has now recovered and is about to put a few more unnecessary openings into my body. Or heck, if an unfriendly stick of dynamite comes for a friendly chat over my cover, I try to dodge out of the explosion, but my input gets recognized as vaulting over the cover so I'm on the side, where all of the enemies I was previously taking cover from are.The gameplay you see in the trailer where the player weaves, dodges and dashes around, over cover, punching, shooting and stabbing enemies all over isn't the least bit representative of actual, typical, gameplay due to this "stickyness". If you're caught in a bad spot with this sticky cover, it can put a dent or outright end a run for you, throwing you all the way back to chapter 1. There are a few ways to put in more effort in order to get more rewards or potentially a shortcut, but I'll leave those for you to discover.All in all, if you like the dark wild west and feel like you can put a little effort into adapting yourself to the controls, you'll have a nice time. I'd recommend waiting for a sale if you're not really entirely sold or the idea. At 6 euros or lower, if the style calls to you, you'll probably have some good fun with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really desperately wish there was an option to give a mixed recommendation instead of a solid yes or no on Steam reviews.Regardless, the long and short of my experience with this is that it's a fantastic game in art, sound, and story, but unfortunately falls short in the game department. Ultimately, this plays like a sloppier, slower, more frustrating version of Enter the Gungeon. If you want a twin-stick rogue-like, Gungeon should be your go-to. Here, while there are good ideas and plenty to separate it from others it may be compared to, what's unique about it simply isn't the makings of a good game. The guns aren't fun to use half the time, are wildly inaccurate for no particular reason, and all of the interesting special 'concept guns' are entirely outclassed by just using a basic gun with no frills and competitive damage, especially given the tendency to miss easy shots, which severely cripples a lot of the arsenal.In a lot of ways, the game feels more like they had an infatuation with the concept of purgatory and how that could translate into a rogue-like without having a real solid foundation in pursuing this kind of game, while they dumped all their love and care into the framing of all of it. Makes for a wonderful bit of spectacle, but with such a shaky core, it just doesn't live up to the expectations set by the stellar presentation.Play this for the art, music, and writing. While the story is nothing particularly special, the moment-to-moment narration really sells it all, and if that's what you're here for you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: A promising roguelike that is hampered by a tedious pace and terrible PC controls.West of Dead's combat has a unique rhythm that takes some getting used to, rewarding timing and tactics rather than precision and reflexes. At its best, it makes every gunfight an exciting and unique cross between a tactical puzzle and a wild west action sequence. At its worst, the terrible controls make navigating difficult fights clumsy and frustrating.The pace of the game is glacial. Rooms are too far apart, animations are too slow, levels take too long to get through and there's too many of them. A typical run can take hours, with little variation. Structurally, the game mimics Dead Cells to a T, but the same structure just doesn't feel good with a slower paced, less frantic experienceThe controls are abysmal and can't be remapped. They also seem to be mirrored for some reason (Left mouse fires your right weapon, right mouse fires your left. E activates your right ability, R your left). Space and shift are heavily overloaded, and interacting with cover - a critical mechanic - is a crapshoot. Navigating menus such as the upgrade screen and teleport screen is a nightmare, as the game struggles to parse whether to use the mouse or movement keys for input. The game has clearly been made with very little consideration for how it would be played without a controller.Overall, would not recommend, which is a shame because I haven't seen anything with quite this same combat system or visual style.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and creative addition to the rogue like genre with a western spin that I've been really enjoying recently.West of Dead has a really unique and ambitious art style accompanied by top down shooter gameplay that's slightly slower paced, but still really fun. It is a nice refreshment compared to a lot of other rogue like games released within the past decade. The soundtrack is extremely good at setting the mood for the stages and Ron Pearlman did an absolutely fantastic job voice acting.Again, can't give enough credit to the art style, voice acting and soundtrack of this game. They all set this undead gritty western scene with perfect execution design-wise.Although I have really enjoyed this game, this wouldn't be a helpful review if I was bias.This game does have it's flaws that, in my opinion, are still carried by the positives. Firstly, the camera can get really bad at times, with some players complaining of motion sickness. I personally didn't experience anything too bad other than 1 or 2 shockingly bad camera angles. Second, (other than the churchyard) the game is too easy even on the hardest difficulty setting. And lastly, the UI for the map is buggy which did get a tad annoying once or twice.It's definitely worth picking up on a sale as I've really enjoyed my time on this game. I might go for 100% achievements (which is a rarity for me on steam) but it seems like 50 outlaws and 50 lost souls is going to take way too long. A stat tracker and/or a faster way to get them them would be appreciated. :)Honestly, I think a well polished sequel to this game that fixes a lot of the issues this has and adds more replayability would sell really well ;).Recommend as it's worth the time, but wait to get it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can get past the fact that the game often gets stuck in animation loops on the completion of Outlaw (miniboss) encounters. Every play through is different, as you unlock items small changes in difficulty and enemy behavior unlock. Overall I feel that many of the weapons are worse than what you are given during your first run. The game forces you to unlock items in order to start missions, via purging your sin (enemy souls acquired during missions). The majority of items are worse than the starting set, and by unlocking these items they make it so your likeliness of getting good items decreases. So the more you play the more difficult it gets, each new weapon you unlock has its own special use case, but they are less useful for general use. At time of review I have yet to finish the game on the hardest difficulty without aim assist. On lower difficulties the game is probably much more fun to play. Great concept and looking forward to seeing more.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a soul stuck in purgatory who needs to defeat a force preventing you and other souls from traveling west, along the way you learn more about who you are and gain tools to help you live longer.Great sound design through the voice over and the music. The visuals to me were pleasing, I like the low poly isometric look but the trailer would allow you to make your own opinion. 	I liked the variety of guns and abilities that you can find, and the strategies that you can make using them. The pace of the game is good with the exception of some particularly frustrating enemies. For just about everything in the game it was intuitive and did not need the wiki to guide me.Note this next section is filled with my gripes with the game however I liked the game and these are things that if improved upon would make this a game I might come back to and play againFirst the slanted top down design and the short aiming reticle made it hard to aim for long range guns and often felt inconsistent, I believe this would not be a problem with a controller however I did not use one. Second, the game has way too many dialogues. After the first or second time you read a dialog, it pausing the game for a few seconds was just frustrating. Third, the mechanic of accepting burdens often felt too underwhelming or overwhelming. I like mechanics with a risk and reward system, however burdens felt like they either did nothing or a strong enemy / outlaw would two shot you for reasons almost beyond your control. Them being on lost souls gave that risk reward that I like however making them crucial to the plot through the  in my opinion limited options and made dieing to them feel like something I could not improve on.Fourth, I experienced too many bugs in almost 30 hours. One of them soft locked me in the room with the witch and repeatedly gave me story memories that I did not collect and refused to let me spend my sin. another got me stuck outside of the world after a table respawned on top of me. The other problems I had were mainly visual problems with the red circles around exploding objects while they were pushed and others were with the aforementioned tables glitching me temporarily.However overall I liked the game and think if your on the fence on the game you should get it on a sale or something
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally enjoy rogue likes, but this gets a recommendation because of the very enjoyable gunplay that kept me coming back to it every time I perished. In a game such as this where you're expected to repeat a lot of levels over and over again in your multiple attempts as you master the gameplay, its critical for the gameplay to be inherently fun and rewarding. Fortunately enough for West of Dead, the firefights in this game are relatively basic, yet incredibly satisfying each time you clear a room of baddies. The physics of the shots fired, the sound effects, the wide array of weapons to choose from, and the varying enemy types make each room a unique challenge. Myself, I don't enjoy the repetitious nature of rogue likes, but West of Dead's combat was unique and visceral enough to pull me back.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style, the atmosphere and the concept of the game. The reason I am saying no to this game is the clunky heavy movement that will make your game experience not worth it. The automatic hide to cover is too wonky and when it does work it makes sure to not listen any inputs and sticks you so hard to that one cover while you fight with controls to get out of it. The roll is wonky as well and while it works in the sense of, you'll pass an enemy, it won’t always go where you input it to go. To many times had it roll in place instead of vaulting over a cover.I am guessing the game is trying to make sure you plan/ use cover but when the roll, vault and the controls that are fighting you more than the enemy “work” while you are getting pounded in the bayou by three enemies two of them with guns and instead of vaulting over the cover you were hiding it vaults in place and you die….I think you are seeing where I am going with this.There are small bugs with buying things at the merchant and then not getting them. The dialogue unsyncing  or just scrolling past you and the C button not really doing anything to pass the dialogue faster.The game would be a big recommend if the controls weren’t the biggest obstacle in the game.To praise the game it has good music, enemy design is fun, the story in my three hour experience was really intriguing and I would love to know more!Some nice stuff I noticed are the “witching hour” basically if you played Bayonetta you know what I am talking about. Thought that was really nice! The nice biome designs. The enemies that were clear to see and their attacks that were nicely executes. The bosses also look good and their designs looks neat!

_childDocuments_.review: I recently got this game and I have a few points:What I enjoyed: 1. This game has a great soundtrack and style2. It blends its style of the Wild West with the afterlife well and it gives me a little bit of Jonah Hex vibes3. I am a sucker for roguelikes and the game makes it work so wellWhat I did not enjoy:1. I find the adjustments of settings a little clunky where it isn't very clear that the adjustment of the graphics and audio are to be dragged (this is more on a preference and can be minor)2. There is an input delay when I use the Shift button for healing and for interacting. Additionally, there is also an input delay in many of the controls like "C" for dialogue, and when I click, it takes a while for the next shot to be fired as I have to wait for the animation to finish.Overall, this was an interesting game because it blended one of my favorite genres in gaming with a unique style. Save for a few problems with input, this game is good to recommend to friends!

_childDocuments_.review: a damn fine roguelikeWest of dead feels like a nice mash up of lots of rogue like ideas that work and puts them into a focus more on precision and timing vs raw output and memorization (these still help of course) Theres a huge variety of items and charms and weapons to choose from that you unlock as you play through spending SIN, it takes a while to unlock many items but you'll immediately see their worth.The story and visuals are pretty unique with colorful characters and the way the darkness is utilized makes many areas feel that much more foreboding and grim, the whole purgatory angle gives lots of room for maddening levels and creepy themes.Tying this together is our narrator who is none other than Ron Perlman giving a gritty, harsh reading as he often does.I really like West of Dead not only as a fan of westerns but just games in general, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a nice idea, a roguelike where you traverse through shifting dungeons and shoot your way through enemy rooms. It is in no way a bullet hell, the rooms are not very full.It is kinda fun actually but got a lot of weaknesses like: little not gamebreaking bugs, sluggish controls, outlaws (which I guess are minibosses) that are either too easy or too hard/annoying. The bugs are a little annoying but not espescially worth discussing. The controls though espescially regarding the dodge system will make you get hit a lot of times though. It just feels like the game is too clunky to manage some of its enemies really.By the way, it has a little auto aim feature to help in game, and it is actually saving you a lot of trouble, because the direction looking to be exact to hit enemies is often enough besides your target. That is because of the way the camera looks into the game. This is not a problem if you take that little inbuild aimbot, which fixes this inaccuracy.Depending on your loadout you will struggle against some enemies and sometimes that will just make a boss take long and longer and ♥♥♥♥.As you progress through the game, you will collect new items, which you can buy at a shop. Problem with that, you cannot not spend your Sins, which are used to shop em. So at some point, the items you can purchase aren't really that good. While going through a run you find weapons and accessories and stuff. If this collection gets filled up with filth, your game will actually become harder, which sucks.So it feels like it should get some kind of rework before I could say it is good but it is not that bad either.Just cant really recommend it. I guess it is worth up to 5 Bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Humble bundle monthly never fails to surprise me with hidden gems.if you are a Ron Pearlman fan you will love his narration throughout this game, a nice surprise to have such a talented actor in a video game.The gameplay seems easy at first but ramps up once you hit chapter 2.  The aiming takes getting used to but it's not bad once you get the hang of it and make sure you use cover or you will die fast.The game is a roguelike with perminant upgrades when spending sin to unlock perminant items and also unlocks that add the possible items that you can find during each playthrough.  I recommend the potion first and then the flare gun.  Certain unlocks open up more possible upgrades.  Defeating bosses also give you upgrades that persist through death.  Each time you die the map changes and resets so you never know what you will find.  I also recommend visiting all shrines on map before going to the next because you can't go back unless you die and when you do you lose all those shrine buffs anyway.  It's basically leveling up one of 3 stats hp, gun dmg, or abilities(like dynamite etc). I plan on playing this until I beat it.  Learning bits about your characters life before he died is an interesting twist that keeps me playing to learn more about him.

As other people have noted, the controls need more polish. Many times I found myself dying because I couldn't get into cover, or get out of cover. This happened infrequently, but enough to be an annoyance. All in all, I recommend playing it, as it is unique to it's field and definitely boasts an iconic art-style. The story so far has been limited, but the dialogue sound great, and has a mysterious  overarching plot.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna start by saying that I really like this game, but it does have some a couple of little annoyances that start to add up after a while.-Most of these little annoyances stem from the overall speed of the game. cover feels too... sticky? it feels harder then it should to peel yourself off from cover. On it's own its not that bad, but instances where you're traveling from room to room where cover is right outside the door, or trying to leave cover to hit a lamp feels slow and awkward. -Teleporting and climbing ladders is also really sluggish, which makes more vertical rooms or rooms with big gaps where you have to teleport to get to the other side slow the game to a crawl.-Dialog boxes also feel like they take a long time to leave the screen, which gets really tedious, especially when you get repeat text / VO (I love Ron Perlman but I can only listen to him comment on the stench of the Bayou so many times until i want him to shut up) I wish there was a way to skip dialog faster or have an option that disables repeat lines of text. So with all that said what do I really like about the game?- The art direction NAILS the Mike Mignola comic book art style- Ron Perlman delivers his lines well even though he repeats them a little too much- I think some of the guns feel really good to use (I love getting repeat crits with the deadshot), and the little clink sound that plays when you kill an enemy is so weirdly satisfying every time. - The game also has a good balance as far as difficulty goes, fights are hard enough to feel engaging, but not so hard that they feel unfair.Like I said before, I like this game quite a bit... but I want to LOVE it, and I think I could end up loving it with just a few more little tweaks

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest games I've played in a while. With almost 10 hours at this point I can say I've only encountered one bug where my character got stuck walking slowly, so I can't relate to all of the reviews claiming this game is buggy or not buggy. The controls are a bit different compared to some other games similar to this title, but they are nice and smooth once you know what you're doing. The atmosphere is absolutely beautiful yet haunting, with a really unique story as it's backbone that includes many just down right cool looking characters, sometimes giant bosses, and visually striking yet simple maps. Not to mention, RON PERLMAN voices the main protagonist in this story. That is Ron Perlman, the voice of the narrator for the Fallout series, the man who played Hellboy in Hellboy one and two, and many other great series and movies. There are weapons, power ups and upgrades to be unlocked that make the almost dark souls like death cycle of having to restart feel not so redundant. The procedural generation of the maps helps a lot with that too. The dodge feature causes this great cinematic zoom and slow-mo that make the combat feel so much like a sweet action movie. The combat can be fast or slow paced, depending on what guns you use, with a heavy focus on taking cover on destructible cover placed around the combat areas. For its great atmosphere, story, voice acting, and overall fun gameplay, I give this game an 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: West of Dead

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like Rouge Legacy, Dead Cells, and other rogue likes then you will enjoy this game. Same kind of upgrade system. You collect Sin in the game and at the end of each area you spend it to unlock more weapons. I really enjoy the combat. Taking cover and shooting is most of what the combat entails. Unless you prefer to play using melee. I highly encourage everyone who enjoys Rouge Likes to buy this. Its for sure one of the best. It's not Dead Cells levels amazing, but its darn close.

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead asks the question: "What if Dead Cells were a western themed twin-stick cover shooter?" And the result is actually strangely satisfying right down to the oddly similar flaming skull. But it is its own game with its own narrative which can be pieced together slowly as you struggle to make your way through the various stages.The art style is appealing. A mix of dark and dirty contrasted with bright lights and the occasional pop of color. It fits the game well, as the lights are actually useful for stunning enemies and catching them off guard, and skulking in the dark leaves you open to surprise attacks unless you are incredibly careful. The light also has an added bonus of granting aim assist (if you have it enabled) which makes combat a bit easier.The various mechanics are a mixed bag. The upgrade system feels rewarding initially, granting much needed extra health or power, but the bonuses eventually diminish to the point of almost preferring an even balance of all traits. The weapon variety is interesting: a nice mix of potentially useful gimmicks and outright solid, powerful choices, but a few of the unlocks leave something to be desired, especially given the random nature of finding weapons on any given level. The core gameplay is enjoyable. Navigate the maze of paths to find an exit. Pop in and out of cover during gun fights while facing a variety of enemies with unique weaknesses or attack styles. Collect souls to unlock additional items or improve your basic equipment, and collect iron to purchase from vendors you may find along the way. Rinse and repeat until you die, and then do it all again. On death, you'll lose whatever weapons and currencies you had, but anything unlocked will remain unlocked allowing you to slowly (almost too slowly) gain more of an advantage out of the gate.Overall, West of Dead is an enjoyable game. Its a bit rough around the edges and may not be for everyone, but it is still worth recommending, especially to fans of roguelikes or those who enjoy the visual style.

_childDocuments_.review: This game comes with a cool factor that's hard to deny. From Ron Perlman's narration to it's killer visual style, before you even talk about the game itself you have to tip your hat to the set and setting of a world exposed to you through the noir lens of a nameless, burning gunslinger that refuses to die. You experience most of the game's story through terse bites of dialogue from a rotating cast of the roving undead, and playing just to experience the writing there is well worth the asking price on it's own IMO.Mechanically, this game is also quite satisfying once you understand that the combat is deceptively rhythm and timing centric. There is a "momentum" to every action that punishes mistakes in execution, so button mashing or going in with the idea that you have "perfect response" will get you killed pretty reliably. Rolls do NOT respond instantly, shots will queue if you fire too many times, and actions will not register if your character is doing something else when you attempt them. Positioning, timing, rhythm and strategization are all EXTREMELY important to surviving in this game. Players that go in expecting perfect-response gameplay may be disappointed, but those coming from MMR oriented games will feel quite at home here.The single gigantic major humongous flaw: You can't remap controls on PC, and menus / UI are awful as a result of being controller oriented. Super awful. Bigly awful. What buffoon in their right mind decided Item 1 would be Mouse2 and Item 2 would be Mouse1, and that making that unchangeable was a good idea?The game can also feel very quiet for long stretches of gameplay (aside from combat). The developers are very stingy with both the soundtrack and the narration for some odd reason, and any sound at all beyond combat can be sparse enough to make the world feel quite empty at times. If I had to change one thing about this game I would definitely say that the very decent soundtrack should actually be applied to the game rather than hidden away-- you almost have to play your own music so that you have a sense of ambience while you're playing.And there are bugs. Noticeable ones, regular ones, some game breaking ones. But they don't really take away from the experience.With those caveats out of the way, it's still really hard not to love everything else this game has to offer and I do hope the developers are still tweaking the game to improve those things even now. It's still a highly satisfying game with an undeniable panache. Who doesn't want to carry a fistful of burning lead into the underworld? That's cool as ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: I keep trying to like this game, but outside of the general lack of variance as time goes on, it just seems to have mechanical issues that may or may not have gotten worse from release.1. Sometimes enemies will spawn on top of cover, making dodging awkward and inconsistent as your character attempts to both dodge and take cover2. My very last playthrough I found a rendering error that makes the player character invisible if they land on top of an outlaw after sliding over cover3. You either play on normal or get killed off screen, this was what necessitated OSP I imagine, but as a gameplay element it is dissatisfying even with that protection4. Builds are somewhat inflexible, and there is a very clear meta that you're not allowed to operate around so much as within.5. Random damage occurring when running around hallways? This is not a serious issue, but I find it odd that this somehow was *implemented* after a period of time, as I never experienced it on release.6. Guns have very little mechanical difference between them, and after playing Gungeon, I have come to accept this is simply a flaw of the specific type of shooter-roguelike WOD is a part of.Overall the only thing I can say about this game is that the entire budget must have been blown on Ron Pearlman's inclusion, with very little spent on the actual polishing, bugfixing, and content creation. Certainly the more recent updates added variation that the base game was sorely missing, for FREE no less, but I still cannot recommend this from my own viewpoint. It just has too many core issues and resolves none of the genre's archaic holdbacks. Don't take this as a condemnation of the devs or really anyone involved in this game's creation, I honestly think they tried their best, but whatever constraints were put upon them proved too limiting to make a compelling game.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing, I think this game has a lot of potential, I really do. The artwork is beautiful, the nice lazy western music is pretty neat and the style of rogue-like that the game follows is rootin and quite tootin.Now that being said, most new games upon release will have bugs and such that the developers are trying their best to get figured out for maximum enjoyment for the players and other flaming skull people out there.What should be fixed:1) What in tarnation is up with the aiming? I could be looking and a baddie and it'll completely switch to another enemy  that can be close or far. The depth perception is confused on this biz. 2) Bullets not hitting the targets. It's a little frustrating, I'll be shooting directly at the enemy and the bullet will fly right through them, very strange my friends.3) THE DODGE ROLL. I'm used to playing games like Enter the Gungeon or other fast paced rogue like games that have amazing dodge roll mechanics. However West of Dead seems to fall short just a little. The enemy in the blue uniform has two shots per attack sequence, sorry pal you're only going to be able to dodge one of those bullets because the dodge has a delay in between rolls which is a major bummer when so many other games perfect this. Please fix, PLEASE FIX THIS.4) Weapons not scaling correctly. On the first floor your weapons do alright to get you through, but sheesh when you get to the second area your guns are a badly timed joke. You'll be blasting an enemy that took you maybe 4 shots to beat, but in the next area it takes maaaaaaany shots while the enemy can kill you in seconds. Yikes.5) The bosses are invincible. I've played games with major challenge behind them but it'd very rare that I come across a game with an invincible boss battle. They can aim their attacks at you no problem even when you dodge but when you finally get an attack on one it does little to ZERO damage.6)Reloading takes too long. The reloading takes waaaay too long, it really messes up the flow of the fight you're in with each room because you'll be trying to dodge like a western bad*** and be a cool gunslinger but sorry baby, you gotta reload with a 5 second delay while getting blasted from not being able to dodge correctly AND slow reload speed.Ah gee wiz. My conclusion to this game would be *drum roll* Have faith in the developers, they all work very hard and I doubt they'll let their game drown. I think this game has great potential to be a fun rogue like. Just needs a little work and YES I do recommend this game, it's pretty sweetles

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I am a VERY casual gamer.  If I'm gaming I'm usually just looking for a platformer or roguelike game that I might just play a run or two and then call it a day.  That said, those elements and the western gunfighter theme had me very intrigued during the beta.  The released version is definitely better than the beta. Not being a hardcore gamer,  I'm not one to be able to deconstruct the nuances of all of the gameplay good or bad as some of the other reviews, but I know what I like and I like this game!  It has kept me coming back for runs more than any other game I have played in years.  The mechanics are fun enough that even dying an ungodly amounts times is fun.  I for one like the gunfight dynamics, especially after some practice.  Kicking down a door and taking out a whole room of enemies using a combination of guns, ducking, cover, light, and what ever else is a blast after you get some skills.  I also find the artwork and style wonderful, lots of depth but also good use of negative space and the changing isometric camera angle between runs is cool,  keeps the runs fresh.. I feel like I'm actually in a good graphic novel, not playing a video game.  That being said, I can agree with some of the comments on what a grind it can be to get to different levels.  A save-point or re-weighting a lot of unlocks would definitely help some frustration. Either way though, EASILY $20 worth of fun and I hope the game gets some traction because I already know I want a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: West of Dead is a rogue-lite, top down shooter.  It's pretty damn good to be quite honest!  The voice acting by Ron Perlman is sparse in most areas but enough to be cool that it's him.  The graphics are great for a game of this type which isn't overly demanding the graphical arena as well as total space the game takes up on your hard drive so it's a good game to play for little space on your hard drive.  The controls are great on controller.  I assume they are just as good via keyboard and mouse as well.  Everything in the game is procedurally generated.  From the maps of each level, to the monster count and type as well as weapons, abilities and skills.  You can purchase new weapons and "charms" aka skills in my book, and then they are available to be found or bought in the game from the dead merchant in the maps.  All around fun game to play and not super easy either!  A good amount of fun and time spent for the price of admission so to speak!  I highly recommend this game to anyone that enjoys rogue-lite/like and top down shooters with a bit of unique variety to them!  This game delivers on all of that in spades!  Great title!

_childDocuments_.review: let me first say, everything about west of dead is blisteringly cool. like, that's the only word to describe it, just... cool. i think that's sort of a given considering the protag is voiced by ron perlman, but everything else works towards this goal of coolness, too. the slower, more methodical approach to a twin-stick roguelite? cool. the extremely fun to look at gothic western artstyle and extremely good to listen to gothic western soundtrack? cool. the plot basically just being ghost rider in the wild west? cool. it all just works, and of course, the game feels good to play. i like the way that combat works in this game. i'm not 16 anymore so playing anything exceptionally twitchy makes my hand cartilage turn into dust, so the, again, more methodical gameplay here works out well. but that isn't to say it's like, easy, or anything. it's still a fairly difficult game, as roguelites tend to be, it's just difficult in a different way. i haven't played a ton of stuff exactly like it. buuut, there is one issue that i have. the keyboard and mouse controls are absolute balls. they are not good. they feel bad in just about every way, somehow? when i tried playing this way, my little ghost rider cowboy ron perlman would repeatedly just swing in a random direction and shoot there instead of where i was aiming, and menus are so bad to navigate that they're downright hostile. everything feels good on controller, but i'm also having an issue where my controller either isn't detected at all, or west of dead decides i disconnected it a few minutes in. this kind of limits me to either restarting my game every few minutes, or playing in a way that i think just.. doesn't feel spectacular. still recommending because it's entirely possible this is just an issue on my end, but the fact that my computer and steam both are still detecting my controller and just the game isn't kinda concerns me. so just like, keep that in mind until that gets patched up.EDIT: i have continued to have issues with the controls even after trying different cords and controllers, so i'm pretty sure it's a problem with the game. i'm leaving this recommendation as positive because i like stuff about the game too much to just give it a negative review, but like... that's kind of a big issue lol

name: Unrailed!
detailed_description: Unrailed! is a chaotic online and couch co-op multiplayer railroad construction game where you work together with your friends as a team to build a train track across endless procedurally generated worlds. Master encounters with its inhabitants, upgrade your train and keep it from derailing! BUILD A TRACK FURTHER THAN EVER BEFORE Gather resources and craft tracks to extend your railroad to prevent your train from reaching the end. But watch out - there is only one tool of each type. Co-operation and co-ordination of your team is essential to survive this increasingly challenging journey! PLOUGH YOUR WAY THROUGH THE WORLD Every world is unique! You and your team will have to master ever new challenges to stay on track! ATTACH NEW WAGONS TO MASTER THE UNKNOWN Upgrade your train to be prepared for whatever is about to come. Get an atomic engine, upgrade your crafting wagon, attach a supercharger or choose from a vast range of other options. PLAY WITH OR AGAINST YOUR FRIENDS Play cooperatively with up to four players in a single team or challenge the co-op skills of your friends in a two versus two game. OVERVIEW An intense and chaotic railroad construction experience Online and local couch co-op multiplayer (also mixing both possible) Procedurally generated worlds with 4 different difficulty levels Dynamic weather system & day and night cycle Game modes: Endless, Quick, Sandbox (up to 4 players) and Versus (2 vs 2 players) Distinct biomes (5+) A bunch of upgradable wagons (10+) to modify your train in Endless mode Unlockable characters A replay system Online highscores with replays Simple controls & split keyboard and split controller mode Blocky to the core

name: VirtuaVerse
detailed_description: In a future not too far away, one Artificial Intelligence has prevailed over all other AIs and their governments. Society has migrated to a permanently integrated reality connected to a single neural network that continuously optimizes people's experiences by processing personal data. Nathan, an outsider still refusing to comply with the new system, makes a living off the grid as a smuggler of modded hardware and cracked software. Geared with his custom headset, he is among the few that can still switch AVR off and see reality for what truly is. He shares an apartment in the city with his girlfriend Jay, a talented AVR graffiti writer whose drones have been bit-spraying techno-color all over the augmented space in the city. Waking up one morning, Nathan discovers that Jay disappeared overnight, but not before leaving a cryptic message on their bathroom mirror. Having accidentally broken his custom headset, Nathan is now disconnected and determined to find out what happened to Jay, but he soon finds himself tangled up in an unexpected journey involving Jay's hacker group and a guild of AVR technomancers. Travelling around the world, he'll have to deal with hardware graveyards, digital archeology, tribes of cryptoshamans, and virtual reality debauchery.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a "sort of" option, rather than full yes or no for recommendations..Ultimately, this is a pretty good game, but it comes with a heavy, HEAVY warning.The story? Top shelf.The art? Terrific.The music? Amazing (and what brought me to the game in the first place)But some of the puzzles in the game are absolutely absurd..Yes, they make "logical sense" after you find an answer elsewhere, but they require a really skewed version of logic that is outside reality and common sense.. and there's enough of these puzzles that it really slows down the game, not to mention there's spots where you're forced to run back and forth through transitional areas for no other reason than to advance the puzzle solving by one unit.My playtime to completion was about 11 hours, but I would say of those 11 hours, at least 3 of them total was angrily banging my head against a wall trying to solve a puzzle only to find out that the solution was something ridiculously obscure.There's also an entire section that could be entirely omitted from the game, save you about an hour and a half, and you would lose nothing other than some cool pixel art.Again, all the pieces of the game are fantastic, but the overall gameplay is just more frustrating than enjoyable in a lot of places (and I know this is a throwback to the P&C games of yesteryear that are just like that), but this could have been a shorter, more enjoyable game if there wasn't so many back and forth and gotcha puzzles, and it just relaxed and told the story it wants to tell.
