_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the demo scene of the 80s, retro computing, cyberpunk, old school point and click adventures, and an absolutely awesome soundtrack (seriously, buy the version that comes with it). The bit where one of the characters starts geeking out about how to do something in 68k assembly...I was just grinning to myself.I would love a follow up game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10I really wish I'd like this game. I've been collecting and admiring similar retro cyberpunk graphics on DeviantArt for years.Altough the game starts really well, you will soon find some boring puzzles that are there just to block the story from progressing. There are some great, fun moments, but in the end the game drags on and I could not be bothered to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: VirtuaVerse is probably one of the best modern point n click adventure games I've ever played. While it does go full old school, it has a modern touch that makes it feel refreshing. It has a deep storyline, compared to many other modern point n clicks these days, with a good balance between the serious parts and the funny moments. The artwork is beautiful and it's amazing how they with the pixel art makes it so detailed. I also love how each different area and environment looks so different from eachother. The soundtrack is fitting and the only thing missing is perhaps some voice acting, but even then it doesn't actually need it.With several callbacks to the old school point n click games, old technology and the looming threat of our personal data being sold to company overlords, VirtuaVerse is a game that is worth playing. I genuinly had a great time with the game and I feel like I haven't played anything as good as this in a long while when it comes to the genre of modern point n click games. Heavily recommended many times over and I can't stress enough that I'm hoping for some kind of sequel or a new game in similiar style from the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best adventure game 2020!!Pro:- The Artwork is very beatiful!- The Atmosphere is damn ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ great, and the whole setting is kinda realistic, something similar might be a thing in 20-30 years.- Great Sounddesign! Yes there is no voice acting, but the text dialogues are pretty short but still tell a very deep story. So you wont see wall of texts, but still get the whole construct.- 10-15 hours gametime, and there is not much timewasting like in others games so you are constantly doing new things and discovering stuff- Great Puzzles! Most of them have a good difficulty, and you can solve it almost completely without a solution. However there is one negative point about the game here:Con:- Some puzzles require you to have experience in coding / know how computers work, otherwise some puzzles might seem insanely hard to you. So if you are a programmer you will find your skills very useful in some of these puzzles :)Many people complained about the hard puzzles, but yeh that's due to the fact I just mentioned. However, this also gives the game a very unique touch, and gives the puzzles an extra layer of deepness!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetics are top notch and music is ok - but the story is really bad. Quite a lot of good ideas with poor execution. Point & clicks thrive and fail based on plot above all (considering how puzzle-light the game is), and this one did not rise to the occasion. Quite a lot of heart here, but I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended if you like cyberpunk, pixel art, or synthwave music. Personally, I enjoyed the soundtrack and overall gritty vibe the most.VirtuaVerse is a classic, somewhat challenging, point-and-click adventure game. The game's locations and well-drawn and animated, encouraging you to explore and discover numerous sci-fi tropes, plus a few slightly on-the-nose references to retro technology that some may be too young to appreciate.The story (mostly linear) and dialogue are okay, but sometimes fall flat, with a few awkward plot points and conversations. Gameplay is generally good, and you'll feel clever for solving certain puzzles. There are some occasional frustrations where a solution doesn't quite make sense, like requiring you to backtrack and talk with an earlier character who magically has new dialogue options.Overall, a solid effort from a small team. I can forgive some of the shortcomings, since it's not a high-budget title. Play it for neon-lit, rain-soaked, dystopian atmosphere, and old-school adventure game challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Art and soundtrack are great. Didn't finish the game. Didn't bother.BUT gimme a break, I found Discworld and Woodruff a lot easier (and logic) than this game. While you can see where the riddles are going from miles away, the game always put artificial obstacles in your way without much logic to it. Not only that but sometimes you litterally have relevant items on you that you'd realistically use for some puzzles, but the game doesn't agree.And as unpleasant to say as it is, this game has "wtf" puzzle fix. Like you go find the solution on google and are litterally frozen in awe by what you read (boat riddle anyone ?).The writing is factual, nothing glorious or memorable, pretty relatable tho.On a side note, I found myself quite annoyed with the rain sound, which isn't separate from other sfx. So for next game, please introduce an additional sound channel for atmospheric/ambient sound.Also, no mouse keybind possible for inventory is really frustrating.That said, the RVA glasses bit was interesting within gameplay.At the end I was pumped for this game, waiting in my Todo list for long time. But I guess am better off playing wierd point&click of old. At least I had a laugh here and there to compensate the infuriating puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Very true to the nostalgic point-and-click adventure games, yet entirely feels like a breath of fresh air. Excellent pixel / 8-bit / 16-bit (or however it is called) visuals that are gorgeously immersive and atmospheric, the writing is excellent and makes the player invested in the story, the setting is futuristically dystopian and the sci-fi & cyberpunk topics discussed are earnest yet the entire narrative is sprinkled with genuinely good humour. I found the puzzles and tasks to be a fair challenge. What stands out most without a doubt is the soundtrack, which is beyond awesome. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, and easily recommended to Adventure fans (not just hardcore ones who like sadistic puzzles).Chronologically, if this game had been released in the heydays of Adventures, UX and puzzle wise, it would be somewhat in between "Day of the Tentacle" and "Full Throttle". The Puzzles so far aren't infuriating, and the story is mostly interesting enough.The art and ambience is great too.And the music, oh boy! Great job having MBR onboard.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Decent universe, but the main ideas are very generic cyberpunk tropes, with average writing. There's a lot of gratuitous nostalgia plugged-in, with characters randomly talking about old technology, with little link to the story, feels like fan service.Puzzles are often decent, but many are way too complex and unintuitive, one needing to pay attention to random stuff in a video to be used quite a lot of time later, or requiring general culture far removed from the game theme (constellations). The main character moves slowly with no way to run or skip screens, but the game imposes lots of back and forth across areas.All in all, good general ideas, could have been really fun with tighter writing and more coherent puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this solid pixel-art P&C adventure with really nice visuals and soundtrack. Puzzles are quite fiddely and sometimes frustrating but still tolerable for my taste. However I find the walking mechanics too 'slow': there's no double-click induced running or immediate screen-switch shortcut available, which should be a genre standard imho (or at least the game did not show me).
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I kept telling myself I would come back to this game eventually, but I just don't see it happening. The time that I did spend with it was mediocre, puzzles were not intuitive at all, but the worst part by far was the writing — it is simple and basic at best, and cringy or outright unbearable at worst. Graphics alone are not enough to save this game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game in every aspect, except that some of the puzzles are extremely obscure and impossible to figure out. I had to check on a guide a couple of times, otherwise i would've dropped it pretty fast. Also, some puzzles were super tedious, like for example, there is a point in the game where you know exactly what you have to do, but you don't know how to do it, so the only option now its to check every single screen again (more than 20 different places) and talk with every single character you've come across before (more than 16 characters, with several lines of dialog) until you find the one that says something to you that will advance the story. Just.. Crazy, and annoying. But whatever, the art, the music, the story, the dialog, everything its perfect, and i'm not ashamed to check a guide if i get stuck, or if i don't want to waste my time walking for 5 minutes to see a specific word or clue.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Like Blade Runner? Wish we could go back to 90's internet? Have an irrational love for useless hardware? This game is for you. The poster child for what a modern cyberpunk game should be, it takes classic sensibilities from the point and click games of old, with beautiful artwork by Valenburg, seamless coding by Elder0010, and a beautiful soundtrack and story by Master Boot Record. A must-have for any cyberpunk fan.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS AHEAD: I love Cyberpunk and until September 2020 I have to play mediocre games. The designer of this game wants so hard to invoke/revisit the 90s point-and-click era, but fail in the most parts. The main character is totally unlikeable, he destroys lifes, kills someone, and is an awful boyfriend. He blabbers about oldschool tech nerd topics, that is not funny or in any way important for the plot. Just for the "hey look here nostalgia" and the member berries "member ANSI code?". The main plot is cliche and boring as hell, why is everything bad? Because the main character tells every time about it. The corporation are eviiiil and augmented reality is baaaaaad. Why? How? Because dystopian Cyberpunk! And why trust the AIs with a plan to overthrow an "evil" corporation? Why do you trust them? The soundtrack is boring and plays in a loop. The scene in the club would be the perfect oppurtunity to play at least 3 different chiptunes song. nope. just a loop. The puzzles are all over the place. Some are very good and straight forward, some are dumb and meant to be funny (use a panty to make a torch) and some are ridicolous difficult to solve. Sometimes you are stuck because you must trigger an event in one location and backtrack to another location far away to speak to someone you totally forgot. No hint, no mention you should talk to someone. It is charring. The good is the style and visuals. Love the pixaleted cyberpunk feeling. But that`s it. So no recommendation. 5 EUR max for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: honestly, virtuaverse has one of the best graphics && art design i've seen with the soundtrack equally up to parr . i love how they push the boundaries of what a stereotypical cyberpunk world should be , landscape wise ( as you'll soon find out once you explore different regions in the game ) . the conceptualisation is amazing && clearly very thought out , especially for a point n' click game  . that being said , as a point ' n click game i don't feel like a lot of the choices && things you had to do was very intuitive , && i found myself referring to a guide a lot . furthermore , it doesn't feel like the protagonist has a solid moral code (ie . killing an npc in one route / saving another for no apparent reasoning . )tldr : beautiful graphics , soundtrack  && well thought out concepts : i recommend this if you're more focused on these aspects over storyline .
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice adventure game with gorgeous esthetics. The music is excellent, but I'm a huge fan of chiptunes anyway. The riddles are very manageable. Not too easy but also not impossible to solve. Anyone who's played the LucasArts classics won't have a hard time with this game.The social commentary also reflects the problems we have nowadays with the always-on mentality and social media taking over pretty much everything. The development also clearly know what they're talking about, which becomes apparent with all the references to the demo-scene, chiptunes, BBS etc.It's a great game which I heavily recommend if you're into cyberpunk and/or classic adventure games .
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel art in this game is so well done that I started with really high expectations. Unfortunately, the gameplay and narrative is very poor and I bounced off it very quickly.The game starts you in a two room puzzle, with no obvious clues how to get out besides something generic like "the answer you need is in this room somewhere." honestly had to reach for a walkthrough to figure it out, which is not a great start.Once you reach the second area, the place you're meant to access is barred off, but the person blocking it does not give you any reasons why. Instead you're meant to walk around the world randomly interacting with things? I can't stand this kind of game. Give my player a clear goal, a personality and an obstacle to overcome. Don't just say "no" then expect me to click on everything and use every combination of items until I figure it out.I do not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect nostalgic trip to anyone who enjoyed point-and-click games like Monkey Island, or Zak McKracken. The game can be finished in anywhere between 10-12h for people with 4000IQ or in 14h like me if you get stuck in certain areas for longer than needed. The game gets increasingly more difficult and requires the player to pay close attention to certain details that other characters say early on for future discovery. I have to admit that the ending was frankly rushed and disappointing, and some clues are unintuitive requiring some help from the community (the steam discussion page for the game and the VirtuaVerse discord server are both places where you can find spoilers/hints).Overall, this game is challenging and creative with great atmospheric qualities and a William Gibson-esque feel throughout. The artstyle and colours make me want to screenshot every new location and use it as my wallpaper (great pixel/8bit art). The music is retro and doesn't become annoying even after 14h of listening. I highly recommend this game to anyone who is patient enough to return to previous areas and dialogue with every character methodically. Gameplay 5/5Style 5/5Storyline 4/5 (some reactions were under or over exaggerated depending on the information received)Ending 2/5 (ending was abrupt and seamed rushed compared to rest of the storylines)Music 5/5Logic 3/5 (some clues were unintuitive at times and require aimless item combination to get right)Overall 4/5! Try it out! Congrats to the whole team!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style, setting and the story as well. I especially love the music! Throws me back to the good old point and click adventure games while having a great cyberpunk setting.What I don't like is how the puzzles are sometimes designed. There's always only one solution. Hints are only available when you follow a chain of events. As it was with old games, multiple solutions or at least giving hints based on different approach ideas would be ideal.Another improvement might be to add an option to swap the pixelated fonts with proper ones, as they get a bit hard and tiresome to read on large screens.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: You've finished re-reading Neuromancer and Snow Crash again. You've been watching Amiga demos and listening to a Dubmood track loop from the installer of some pirated game. Deus Ex and Cyberpunk 2077 are on their 14th playthroughs. You've been thinking about re-watching Akira and the Blu-Ray of the Blade Runner sequel is still in the disc drive of your PS4 (can't afford the 5 yet).You have your standard stock of cyberpunk archetypes arranged into a sci-fi plot of techno-ghosts, Augmented Reality graffiti artists, abandoned subway systems, and a tension between old magnetic and analog technologies vs new digitally connected, always-online networks. Sensible puzzles with a minimum of hunt-the-pixel moments, and does not try to trick you to your death. Mostly figuring out where to use an item and selecting dialogue choices at the right moments to trigger something, we're not talking Professor Layton puzzles here, just context clues and hints during conversations.Since this is so steeped in the cyberpunk genre, with all the tropes and synthwave and pixel art and Japanese neon signs, you pretty much already know if this is your thing or not. It will likely come down to how strong or interesting the plot or characters are, so I will say this:1. The plot is excellent if you are a fan of philosophical or moral questions about augmented reality, the relationship between AI and human, and the tension between 80s tech optimism vs modern tech pessimism as once seemingly beneficial technologies are increasingly locked down and turned toward surveillance and control.2. The characters are not particularly memorable on their own. Your character is a faceless (you literally never see his face) mixture of the cynical and alienated cyberpunk protagonist and the self-centered point-and-click protagonist whose need to solve puzzles and progress overrides any and all ethical concerns, so he can come across as a psychopathic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when read in a certain light. Most characters you meet engage you in a single dialogue tree which generally does not change later on and will not come up again once their moment has passed, and this may also be a representation of the character's lack of reflection or concern about those he meets, but that is completely speculative. The only real persistent characters are Nathan, the protagonist, and his girlfriend, Jay, and maybe you could consider Jay's boss a regular supporting character. This is definitely a game fixated on setting and plot.Overall I would rate this: Worthwhile for the Plot, Fairly Easy, and Short (probably because it's easy).
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally the most difficult point & click game I've ever played - and, trust me, I have played a lot of point & click games. The storyline is excellent and it makes you think. Every character is weird and memorable. The puzzles are of a hardcore difficulty. They require a lot of thinking and trial & error. I like the whole message that this game is trying to deliver. Its ending is weird, but quite awesome! I really hope you'll keep on creating games. Great job, developers! Totally worth its money!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: -Amazing artstyle-Insane soundtrack (It's Master boot Record after all)-Interesting storyBut yes the puzzles...The solutions range from "out of the box" to insane(not in a good way), and are especially in the second half of the game so frustrating to solve, you don't even feel accomplished when solving them, you're just happy the puzzle is done.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: In this cool cyberpunk point & click adventure, in a future not too far away, one Artificial Intelligence has prevailed over all other AIs and their governments. Society has migrated to a permanently integrated reality connected to a single neural network that continuously optimizes people's experiences by processing personal data.In VirtuaVerse you play as Nathan, an outsider still refusing to follow the system. Geared with his custom headset, he is among the few that can still switch AVR off and see reality for what truly is. The truth however is not as pretty as it once was.The game claims itself to be a challenging point & click game, but fails to actually make it's puzzles too much of a challenge. The dual layers of reality were fun to play with and explore, but there were too many times where I knew exactly what I needed to do and figured it out quite fast.The story was rather boring and in the end it felt like it had been a long winded road to a very boring and uninteresting ending. It was also quite predictable in some ways, but there was some interesting twists at the end as well, that made me scratch my head a little bit. The soundtrack was very nice in my opinion, but also got very repetitive quite fast when you started to linger in certain areas longer. The pixel artstyle was great and the cyberpunk feel was well implemented in it's design. Some areas were more impressive than others, but overall, it was a very visually nice pixel game.I wouldn't say that I regret the time I spent playing this game, but I definitely would have preferred for it to be shorter in length and less repetitive. There was way too much traversing back and forth between different areas - the quick travel (which is totally not mentioned anywhere - hit M) worked pretty well for the first few sections, but some of the later ones just required crossing several long screens repeatedly, back and forth, back and forth...In the end, I would say that this game might be a great choice for those invested in cyberpunk style and point & click games, but for someone like me who prefers a good story, this was not it. I also don't think it's a game worth 15€, despite the fact that the game takes closer to 10 hours to beat. Take it as you will!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

Also, the soundtrack is second to none if you're a fan of the likes of Perturbator, Carpenter Brut, Lazerhawk, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: For starters it's not cyberpunk.The game starts quite nice, with traditional cyberpunk "small adventure turns into something big" story design, with lots of little detail and worldbuilding. It's clear that the first half of the game is where authors were really inspired and were making something they loved and was fascinated about. It's a bit inconsitent in tech application (for sake of all the demoscene references), but it's more than ok.But then in the middle of the game it comes to "something big" part and the whole game falls apart. Because that something big is not "cyberpunk". It has nothing to do with the world and all the setup they made so far. So, it's all just thrown away - all characters that before were acting in various witty and distrustful ways (in a typical trust-no-one cyberpunk way) suddenly turn into naive idiots taking everything at face value. Main characters, secondary characters, everyone.At this point it's also clear that apparently the message they decided to say wasn't the message they wanted to say. So both the writing and storytelling takes a deep dive and starts infodumping loosely connected nonsense on the player. At some point it degrades to the point they have to resort to cheesy "ahaha, adventure games" jokes like hiding an entire ladder into your pocket with a funny sound, which is fine for comical adventures, but that wasn't setup as one.Oh, and it ends with a "twist" that is foreshadowed so hard that it would be less obvious if they would tell you it directly at the start of the game. But you won't believe that's actually the case until the end, simply because how stupid it is.Gameplay on other hand is going from tolerable to terrible. There is ton of backtracking, going back and forth between locations, sometimes there is zero information you need to do something at another location, hiding information (when you get generic "I won't do it" response when doing something for the first time, but it's actually a valid action when you discover something else), double-dialogs (when you need to click on a character twice), etc. AND all that is not consistent - it happens only sometimes. The biggest problem of adventure games as a genre is that as they aren't systemic you have to guess what exactly the author had in mind, so the art of making them is to establish such a context for the player where it would be possible. This game does everything to the opposite of that.It's not as bad as old adventure games, and it's clearly tries not to be a casual mix of trivial puzzles like those modern adventure games, but it's doing quite bad job at that, so it would actually be better if it would be casual
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game because of the cyberpunk setting, but found out it has a lot more to offer in terms of gameplay. It made me realize how much I miss the classic adventure games like The Longest Journey. It features some head-scratching puzzles that will make you go around and try random things or check out a walkthrough. This seems to be the main thing people are not happy with. I think that's what a good adventure game do so I didn't mind at all. If you prefer to just go through the story there is the option to play more like a visual novel. So it shouldn't be a dealbreaker.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: i really enjoyed Virtuaverse from the beginning to the end.This is a true love letter to the adventure games of the '90s, and has all the cyberpunk vibe of such an age.Maybe it won't be for everyone: it has a clear statement about technology, music, and some 'nerd' sub-culture, but I think this is fine since the makers of this game have such a clear vision.Graphics and music are top-notch, as well as the whole story. Puzzles are just ok, I didn't find too much of a moon logic as I've read somewhere around, nor I suffered from an excessive pixel hunting.Everything - or almost everything - is made clear by dialogues and description. I've got stuck only twice, but because I didn't think enough, or I just skipped something in my reasoning.I'd definitely recommend this game to all the classic adventures lovers out there <3
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game, from beginning to end. A word of warning though, this game has a . As others have said, this is for fans of original point and click adventure games. In addition to that, , it’s also for fans of retro cyberpunk stuff who probably also have real-world knowledge of computers. In addition to that, it’s definitely targeted toward people , enabling turbo mode with a jumper on your 386, etc. While it’s still possible to play and enjoy this game, you might not really fully enjoy all the references to that time, or appreciate some of the subtle (or not so subtle?) digs aimed at the modern era as contrasted with the “good old days” of computing. Don’t let that deter you if the game looks good to you though. Stranger Things might get a similar review, but many people who don’t remember the 80’s still very much enjoy that show. That being said, I am one of those people, and I found the puzzles intuitive, fair, balanced, etc. I needed to look up something one time only, and felt immediately stupid when doing it:  So the thing I got stuck on wasn’t even a puzzle, it was just one of those things you miss and don’t think to come back to the same place ever again and look at it with fresh eyes the next morning.I really do think though, that if you haven’t played a ton of the original point-and-click adventure games, some of the item combination puzzles (where you put two items you have together to make a new item) could be hard. But honestly, the types of things you do with item combo puzzles in this game really are pleasantly typical, to the point of almost being a trope of the genre: for example,  So that particular puzzle is more like: “hey, do you remember all those other games you’ve played? Yeah, that works here too.” than anything.  I think it’s similar for other aspects in this game: if you aren’t exactly the target demographic: you might, I don’t want to say struggle, but perhaps you might not fully appreciate some of the puzzles or plot; that or you might feel the cynicism is laughing at you, rather than with you, as it was intended.&tldr; I love this game, and I’m so very glad I got it. But I played King’s Quest games on a brand new 386 in the 90’s before Pentiums were a thing, then putzed around with the EMS/XMS memory (after realizing “turbo mode” didn’t help) in to get MechWarrior 2: Mercenaries to run, read Neuromancer and loved it, and when asked, said I wanted to be a robot when I grew up, then grew up, and became a software engineer instead. If that kind of describes you too, you’ll probably like this game, and if that doesn’t describe you, you  like it, but you aren’t the exact target audience of this game, and it does have a pretty laser-specific target audience in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the good: The soundtrack is incredible, the graphics are nice, and the mood and theme are integrated well.Both the plot and the gameplay fall flat, however.  Both place no faith in the player.  In the case of the story, the protagonist's constant explanations of technology and philosophical musings both break immersion and make various plot points unsurprising and entirely predictable.  The fact that the protagonist is a colossal jerk to literally everyone he meets does nothing to make me more interested in or invested in the story either.The gameplay, meanwhile, leaves no room for intuition or experimentation.  As a contrived example, if you have a bowl of ice cream and a banana and think that you want to put a banana split somewhere, you likely won't be able to.  Instead, you'll have to travel halfway across the map, talk to an NPC who explicitly talks about a banana split, and then go back to place the banana split where you were before.  This happened more times than I could keep track of throughout the game.The puzzles themselves are very hit and miss.  Some are straightforward.  More than I admit were completely unintuitive or required pixel hunting.  Almost none left me feeling satisfaction when solving them (because most were in the two extremes).  I grew up on point and click SCUMM games and am familiar with the genre.  This game tried to have a throwback feel, but takes nothing from the 30 years of game development we've had since then.  This is in contrast to Thimbleweed Park, a modern point and click with a similar legacy feel which fixes most of the pain points from those old games.Overall, the game is beautiful and I don't regret my purchase, but for large chunks I was being dragged along from one unintuitive "I give up, I'll check a guide" moment to the next, and by the end I was glad for it to be over, so I really can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This game is painful, I'm invested in the story and the art style is very much something I enjoy. But it suffers from so many of the problems that adventure games have moved on from.It swaps genuinely interesting and good puzzle design for the farcical and nonsensical - e.g. distract someone from a computer with a cat chasing a dog. I would only give one puzzle the benefit of being called 'clever', although I wonder if its relying too much on knowledge of the source material (e.g. ascii art) to be able to do it. It also doesn't go out of its way to provide hints and you can find yourself at an impasse due to a single easily-missed part of one screen. One of the cardinal sins is if you are going to stuff your inventory with useless objects and red herrings and especially because this is non-voiced, you have to write better custom text for object interactions. There are times were objects you cannot use (despite working out what to do already) before triggering a certain event will simply have a generic 'these dont work together', making subsequently solving the problem rely on retrying things. It also ends up with nonsense where, as a particular example, using a screwdriver on an item says it has proprietary screws. There is a proprietary screwdriver item in the game, these dont work together ...Its a shame as I'm certain some tuning in the puzzle design and/or a more sensible hint system could have saved this game. At points I just referred to a walkthrough because I just didn't enjoy solving the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Let's see... I love adventure games, I love pixel art, I love cyberpunk inspirations, so of course this had all the ingredients to be the perfect game. Is it perfect? No. Is it damn good? Hell yes.Not sure why so many people are complaining about the difficulty. It's definitely not easy, especially since it allows you to pick up items you will never need and there's plenty of "red herrings", aka items in the world you can interact with and that seem important, but you actually never end up using. However, all of the puzzles are fair and reward careful examining of the environments and paying close attention to what the NPCs have to say.If I have to complain about some things, it would be the writing (the story is pretty run-of-the mill rogue AI dystopia) and far-fetched nature of the final two chapters. Other than that, it's a solid 8.5/10 and I really hope to see more from these developers.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I give it a 7/10. The audio/visual design was phenomenal and the story was very good, with a solid twist ending. There are two big weaknesses: the puzzle design and the protagonist. The puzzles are sometimes innovative and interesting, but many are moon logic and aren't satisfying to complete since they leave you with that 'really?' feeling. A few pixel hunts to be sure. And things that make no sense like an item you can see but cant get until you progress another puzzle so your character 'knows' to look at the thing that already caught your attention. As for the protagonist,.. he isn't an avatar for you as he has a name, a set of interests and a story. But that's pretty much it. There's no real development on him, no face, just some hacker nerd in a hood. I really didn't care about him all that much. And that's a very serious thing in this genre.Still recommending; its worth the experience of playing and there was some very serious talent that went into this. The soundtrack alone is stellar. Geeks will love all the retro hardware/software references. Good walkthroughs exist if you get stuck. Definitely pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others, I discovered this game thru MBR's music.  The game is a huge throwback to the point-and-click era of games like Kings Quest and Tales from Monkey Island but with elements from the scene days on IRC.  There are so many easter eggs from those days that if you were old enough to be a part of it you'll just have nostalgia overload with this game. It seriously makes me want to break out my old floppies and reminisce on whatever the hell I saved on them..  but I digress.  The gameplay is pretty fluid, the story is great, the graphics/animation are legit and the music takes you on a journey while you play. For a 3 man team, this game is very well done!  I got stuck more often than I'd like to admit but that's the whole point.. for you to try different things and to think outside the box. I highly recommend this game and not just when it's on sale.. it's only $15 and 3 dudes put their time, sweat and blood into it for several years.  Support them and play the game! I just nominated this game for best soundtrack! Good luck, MBR!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Great pixel graphics, very good chiptune-style music that evokes the feeling of the era they were going for. The story is pretty good, going well off the rails toward the end in a positive way.The puzzling is--mostly fair, occasionally excruciating. But even this is reminiscent of the old Sierra and LucasArts-type games that this is an homage to. I would expect the overwhelming majority of people to have to consult a walkthrough on at least a couple of occasions (looking at you, crab, and looking at you, cleaner-bot). Top-notch retro point-n-click adventuring.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of hate this game, but I like it even more than that so this gets a positive review. I got stuck on something when this came out and quit because I was too proud to use a guide. But then they released the story mode for people like me, and I felt attacked by  this, so of course I decided I would finish the game properly so people wouldnt call me a normie. I would say that unless you fancy yourself as competent at these kind of games, you should be willing to use a guide every now and then. I enjoyed the game a lot more that way.What I didnt like: Maybe this means im a basic *****, but I had to get over my ego/pride and keep a guide at the ready because I personally dont enjoy missing a small item on screen and then wasting 20 minutes of my life ritually engaging with every single NPC and item I can think of only to check a guide and shake my head at the solution. Maybe some people enjoy that, but when I am reduced to attempting every conceivable permutation of items I can think of I am not having fun anymore. I just dont find that enjoyable, that is tediousWhat I did like:-Master Boot Record -The pixel art is so good it is just stupid. This game hands down has some of the most interesting and fun pixel art I have ever seen-It is fairly humorous when it isnt being dark and depressing-I was really enjoying the game when I wasnt stuck because I didnt notice an obscure detail or item
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Please leave your tribute on the decorative skull table ..thanks}:)point and click adventure tribute accepted!This story has been a truly inspiring source of thought and visual stimulationgreat adventure with some vivid imagery, used at least 2 fold everywhere thanks to the AVR goggles. homage in places, I think to the old lucas arts games, also a good point&click, thought leads your investigation to where you need to be and though it can be picky at times the ideas play out well. the goggles really add an extra dimension of thought to the game, even the walls have secrets!Plot biulds very well throughout, fun interactions and we only had to premeditatedly murder 1 person, hahaha!A plethora of interesting looking chars and places and thought provoking problem solving!If you need a reminder hit the journal button to recap, if your still stuck then there is a great friendly hint in the steam guides.suggestions for improvement.(These are mostly to save time!)>Object from inventory stays until you right click (save time.)>Alot of these puzzles are logical no problem so you know what to do most the time but often there is also a final layer, that logic is sometimes just read the mind of the developer, I tryd this its coded in binary and Amiga cracker demos!!>A true adventurer knows you check everything just in case, I prefer Guybrush's logic.. I dont know what ill use this for but ill take it anyway (into the pant-ventory!) this also save time not double baking and double checking everything!I played this game mostly before bed so time includes the game on providing me some nice white noise for slumber!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic point 'n click throwback. I'm simultaneously happy and sad that I'm old enough to *fully* enjoy the old demo scene references....this made me go find on youtube my old fav from 5th grade, "Amnesia" by Renaissance, but it's just not the same not being in slow motion on my old x386. Amazing that a game can make me want to go source some really old tech so bad....good job, guys.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely magnificent! The art style is stunning, the music is on point and the story is great too! The riddles are kinda hard in some places but absolutely doable if you do some thinking outside of the box and if you pay attention to the whole screen and the dialogues.All in all: 10/10, would and will play again!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but flawed.The graphics, mood, sound and universe are great. There are tons of computer geek references, going as far back as the Amiga 500 good old days.There are some excellent puzzles, which are unfortunately poorly implemented and end up being more frustrating than enjoyable, because of;- too many "Ho you thought you solved the puzzle? Gotcha! Here is some random additional stuff to do to fully solve it, mwahahah!"- too many red herrings- sometimes, puzzles that look like they have a system and structure (like the technomancers riddles) actually end up being pretty random- too many random conditions must be met sometimes to unlock a puzzle next step (like using all dialog options with random NPCs)Despite all this, that are pretty common flaws to the genre, it's an enjoyable ride with great designs, characters, mood and music, and will bring you back some cool memories if you are gaming since the 90s.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant point-and-click cyberpunk adventure absolutely worthy of the hype. Gorgeous pixel artstyle, a consistently slapping chiptune soundtrack, sharp writing, and clever puzzles. VirtuaVerse confidently paints a game world so palpable that I was hooked from the opening scenes.Like the old classics, trying many interactions of your inventory and fully exploring dialogue trees will be needed to solve the puzzles which, for me (6hrs so far) have felt fair and not too frustrating to figure out.It's also clear the developers have intricate knowledge of cracker/demoscene culture and they nailed the tech references. There's maybe even some hidden/ARG content? Fantastic work from a three person team, VirtuaVerse deserves to be considered one of the greats in the point-and-click genre, and is easily a personal favourite release for the year.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, great visual achievement, great music, great story, loved it from start to finish. I totally recommend for Point & Click lovers, Theta division gave us a great one. Kudos guys !One thought, I think that in order to get the full nostalgia effect you have to be born in the 80's with the rise of computer and the demo scene. So much references here.About people finding the puzzle too hard or too obscure, I don't get it. Every single puzzle is explained in some way by a NPC, a document or an interactive object. Every friggin time. You just have to take the time to READ (important point here) and the solution will appear. This Point & Click is on the easy side, play Discworld 2, Noctropolis, Space Quest 6, King Quest 7 or Darkseed, if you want to taste what is hard.To conclude, this game is a gem mixed with a critic of our decaying over-consuming, over-communicating, quantity over quality society. Almost perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Remember point-and-click games? Did you forget getting stuck in them, digging through hints, being humiliated to go back to hints, being exasperated when they didn't work right away? But did you also forget the sheer, unadulterated bliss of warping your mind until it fit the game creators' perverse imagination? Because this brings back more than just the superficial. It's a love letter to all that was great and good and psychotic about those adventures. And if you don't enjoy then seeing spectacular pixel art, clever writing, a true antihero and the devastation he leaves behind, and this brilliant Master Boot Record score, it's possibly you just don't like joy. Sheer artwork. Could have been skin-deep, but gets straight into your brain instead.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The game is unsatisfying to play through because all the puzzles you have to solve to progress frustrate you by badly written extra steps when you thought you completed them. The game does this all throughout and it deprives the player of any sense of achievement and momentum. Also all of the puzzles are unintuitive and bad. The games does a very bad job of both telling you what to do, and how to do it. There isn't even an object highlighting option to show what you can interact with on screen, making you run past important stuff all the time. The developers really have to play more point & click games and take notes how to properly structure and implement puzzles that are entertaining and satisfying. The art and world-building is actually quite good and the story starts of decent enough as well. Humor is below average and the characters are uninspired and underdeveloped. I only finished it becauseI wanted to see how to story ended, and I was somewhat disappointed. It is obvious the developers cared about this game and put effort into it. But what this game needed to be better was more time to flesh out the story and characters, and maybe some previous research on how to make better puzzles. However, I will be keeping an eye on the developers because I see the potential for something better in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Do you love atmospheric detailed pixel art with lots of details to find? Get this game, oh boy, are you in for a treat.Do you love Cyberpunk which does not shy away from showing changes in society and how we could be changed by technology and how the world will progress? Get this game, I love the world-building!Do you love classic adventures? Get this game, I haven't seen a single stupid puzzle so far, everything makes sense and some of the solutions you find are hilarious, I had more than one good laugh.Also, if you love good electronic music, that isn't hiding itself and likes to beat in your face, this alone might be a reason to buy this game. You can get a sneak-listen here:
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is a first impression review for now, i will extend this when I've completed the game to the end.As of now, I'm captivated by the beautiful scenery, the amount of detail in the pixel art department is incredible. And it does an outstanding job at depicting a cyberpunk dystopia, feels like something straight out of Neuromancer. As for the gameplay, it's frying my fragile brain, but I'm having fun trying to puzzle together what to do next.Overall, I'm really enjoying this game so far!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a point-and-click game in... maybe over a decade? I forgot how annoyingly "clever" pixel hunting tasks are. Despite the usual frustration of figuring out what you're supposed to do in a p-a-c, this was a wonderful game to play. I've been a fan of MBR for a few years and love that they made a video game. Lots of funny surprises throughout. Excellent music, of course.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: VirtuaVerse will challenge your grey matter and delight your senses. The aesthetics feature some delightful pixel art sporting a stilysh theme that will both throw you back to the golden age of point-and-click adventures and surprise you with its new ideas.The score is another MBR masterpiece, and the technical aspects connect all the right dots thanks to super-smooth movement, a sleek and no-frills user interface and its pixel-perfect aspect.Gameplay-wise, it is challenging but never punishing and solving puzzles is a rewarding experience. There's plenty of surprises in this game, and it's crammed to the brim with references to hacker and demoscene subcultures that are well placed and neat even if you don't get to catch them all.TL;DR: Totally recommended!!!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Super Duper Awesome Point & Click Adventure Game. MUST HAVE for any 90's adventure game lover.Astonishing graphics, FX, music & atmosphere; smooth gameplay with intuitive controls.The game is long but never boring - quite the opposite. The difficulty is PERFECT.The attention to details - if you can look hard enough - is OUT OF THIS WORLD.WHAT MORE COULD YOU POSSIBLY ASK FOR ?Masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game and liked it a lot. As a cyberpunk, retro pixel, electronic music and point and click fan, this game seemed tailor made for me. I enjoyed the quality of the riddles, the great pixel art, the music by Master Boot Record, the jokes and the vibes in the game. Even more impressive that the game was created only by a team of 3. Great !
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game. The puzzles are by and large challenging enough but not too much (except for very few), the music is amazing, the artwork top notch, and the text pretty funny.I was a bit sad that there was no voice acting, it would have catapulted the game into the hall of fame. But even so, two thumbs up. If you like point and click adventure games, do not miss out on VirtuaVerse.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: It's oldschool in every way, even the bad. That means that the puzzles are obscure, and that you frequently have no idea what to do next. When trying things that seem obvious, you get a reply "I'm wondering what's going on in your head right now" instead of something useful.Try a walkthrough? Well, the puzzles don't sense even when you know what to do next. It only gives you the feeling of "why am I supposed to do that?". Adding to the obscurity is the fact that you unlock new dialog options with certain characters when you do things, without knowing it. So you can talk to a character and deplete all options, go and click on some random things, only to come back to the character and realize that you now have a new dialog option.The solution from the developer's perspective would be an easy one - simply have the main character say things like "I should go talk to X", or "this thing could be helpful for Y", or "I can see the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fruit from here!" (you'll know what I'm talking about when you get there).So... I can't recommend this unless you are one of those people who enjoy frustration.---I like the homage to the demoscene and the Amiga, since that's where I come from myself. It gets pretty fun to compare fact with fiction. In the fiction, we nerds become godlike "Technomancers". In reality, we have regular 9-to-5 office jobs. Game development attracted many of us, and I think this game is evidence of that. :)
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and music are great! The story is interesting. And as an Amiga 500 fan I enjoyed a special segment of the game (you know it if you play :-)) Some puzzles are a bit weird old school but there is a nice low spoiler hint at the "nice game hints" website if you need any help. Would definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a reasonable game, and a fantastic soundtrack, but several unreasonable design compromises along with a narrative that feels progressively sloppy and rushed weigh it down far more than they aught to.  Many bits of foreshadowing are abandoned or fumbled, and the final act seems completely disjointed from the rest of the game.Also, exceedingly poor inventory management for a graphic adventure - arguably the most core gameplay facet for the genre - makes the game more frustrating than it needs to be.Overall, a firm 5/10 which could have easily been polished into a 7.5, but inexplicably wasn't.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an unexpected journey into true old school point and click, graphics are amazing, rich in dialogue, story and characters! The plot develops smoothly, you are never extremely stuck, that's some good game designing and love right there :) I didn't expect it to be as long in gameplay time as it has proven to be, I was pleasantly surprised. This little gem labour-of-love is packed with real-life stories behind the scenes of the game development world, that may be familiar to most developers but I certainly had no clue, being the gamer on the other end of the screen enjoying the end result. Well done, I thoroughly enjoyed this game and I'm really looking forward to more releases from this studio. Excellent job!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this iconic stylised game. The cyberpunk style brings a true homage to the theme with the beautiful area designs and music. Music in all honesty won me over after watching a friend play the game. The puzzles are very much brain teasers, but with me and a friend making it through the game it was a 2 heads better then 1 scenario. If you like a puzzle game with which it encourages you to think of what you need to do and all the possible actions this is for you (kind of a think out of the box kind of game). Like hiding answers in plain sight to crafting stuff you would not believe. I hope any who attempt this enjoy it for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome effort for such an small development team. The visuals do really blend in very well with the music. No moon logic puzzles so far, which is in my opinion an good thing for an point and click adventure. Also outstanding support for a small issue (which is already fixed in the newest update) via Discord
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely excellent atmosphere... the music and art are just fantastic. Great throwback and contribution to the classic p&c genre. The story is solid and has a few nice surprises beyond the initial setup, rich in retro computing glory while being suitably future dystopian. The only things stopping this from being a perfect game is some of the clunky english dialog (Im not sure if this was translated or just needs a bit more refinement) and the difficulties of many of the puzzles - while logical are certainly challenging! However neither of these two things detract majorly from the excellence that this game delivers.(Also go check out Master Boot Record's other albums - they're also excellent)
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game, it has some of the best pixel art ever made and the music is just amazing. I like the story, the politics (red-pills), the philosophy and the numerous retro-computing references.2/3 of the puzzles are unsolvable without a solution, and even then they will be difficult to execute, because the game wants you to do it in a very specific way. Half of the time, I knew what to do to solve the puzzle, but could not do it (because you need to do something so specific, in a specific screen, after triggering a pixel perfect something...). I had to look on the internet 50% of my time with this game and then the other part of the puzzle was actually making it work. You will use the right item on the right object many times, but it won't work and think that was not the solution, but it was. You just need to do it in the only convoluted way the game accept.I don't recommend the game, even if I really like the game because most people will find it frustrating that the only way to play this game is by fallowing a solution step by step on the internet.So if switching constantly between a walktrhough and the game is your definition of fun, this game is for you.18.5 hours to complete with the solution right next to me. Love the ending. But as a game since It is impossible to solve any puzzle to completion, I think it is better to watch a playthrough on youtube.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The early reviews and visual style of this game really drew me in.  But then I quickly ran into the obtuse puzzles and lost the will to play, knowing I'll need a walkthrough.  And I used to beat Lucasarts/Sierra games without walkthroughs back in the day.  Agree with other reviews saying the developer should play-test their puzzles more.  Unless you are an uber level adventure gamer with 30+ years of experience then expect to need a walkthrough from early on.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I'm trying really hard to like this game, but honestly it's very nerve wrecking. The art style and music is cool. The cyberpunk atmosphere is very cool and retro but so far those are the only good points.The gameplay itself so far sucks. It's too heavily puzzle based. I'm usually very good at point and click games like this, but when literally EVERYTHING is a puzzle, it starts to feel more like work and less like a fun game. I can't even get into the storyline really because I'm too focused on how to get from point A to point B, who to talk to, what to buy, etc. I'm not giving up yet, but if it continues like this I wont finish this game until someone posts a guide for it. Overall: Great theme, but if you hate puzzles, don't buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I almost didn't get this because of people complaining about cryptic puzzles and moon logic.I've just finished the game, and I'd say the puzzles all made logical sense besides one late-game head-scratcher that I would never have figured out had I not desperately combined random items.I did consult a walkthrough a few times, but each of those consultations could have been mitigated with more patience and thoroughness.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most brillant classical point and click adventures, I've played in a long time.As I'm getting closer to the end and have already read some reviews, I must say one thing.For me the puzzles are very logical and not too hard, especially, when compared to older games; in earlier times there were mainly two companies for point and click adventures, Lucas Arts and Sierra. While Sierra had puzzles you sometimes couldn't solve without a walkthrough, sometimes even with one, it was hard as hell - for example the Leisure Suite Larry Games -, Lucas Arts games were much more logical and foregiving. For me, this game could have been a Lucas Art Game like Indiana Jones or Monkey Island - and for all of you ranting about the "moon logic", only because one reviewer started this kind of impulse: why don't you play Monkey Island 1 and 2, if haven't done that already? Then you would see, hey, these classics had incredible hard puzzles in them. I sometimes spent hours over one puzzle - an ammount of time, no regular player now would ever spend on a puzzle again - and finally managed to solve it. Here it takes me longer than most of the games, I've played in the past few years, but still, this is what a good adventure game is about, you think about it, you try some stuff, you find the solution and it makes sense. For me every single puzzle so far, made perfect sense and didn't find it difficult . So! Thumbs Up!(One game I was looking for a long time, that in my opinion has nearly unsolvable puzzles - and too many locations, you went around collected stuff over stuff and never used it - and for that was a big disappointment for me, was Timbleweed Park; here, for me, nothing like that, you progress and change the location; and the locations aren't too big.)Finished it; great game, only the ending is a bit disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Can't beat this game without seeing the walkthrough but that's not a problem for me. I'm here just to admire Mr.Valenberg's awesome Pixel works. The story is okay but the Soundtrack really make a great atmosphere for this game! The whole thing in this game just makes me want to play this over and over. I've been beaten this game 3 times now btw. Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: As this was one of my first games, I went in with no expectations. I like puzzle games and pixel art, and the colours of this game looked nice. Now, the visuals were definitely what I expected and I liked that very much. It's been relaxing to play this at night in the dark with Bon Iver playing in the background.However, you are lying if you can say you finished this game without getting any help. Especially in the second half I lived and breathed on the guides, which made the game less relaxing and more confusing. Overall 7.5/10 if you like pixel art and puzzles, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially seduced by the gorgeous pixel art and the kick-ass soundtrack, along with the light-hearted adventuring in the game's first act.Whilst it is a remarkable feat to pull off for a three-man team, the game as a whole, disappoints. It nails cyberpunk's retro-style but nothing of its substance. There is no plot, characters or conflicted humanity in this.The further you push into the story, the more it becomes apparent that it's a horrible mishmash of genre cliches, the worst of 90's obscure-sell-me-a-hintbook adventure game puzzle design and by the time I reached the finale, I was so fed up with the moon logic required to solve many of its puzzles along with the lack of characters or meaningful story, that I finished the game strictly for the sunken cost fallacy of it all. It's easy to love this during the first 3-4 hours but the longer you stay with it, the more it's glamour fades. Old school purists may still find some things to enjoy (the pixel art and music are top notch) but it left a bitter taste in my mouth as the credits rolled.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The game comes in pretty packaging. I adore cyberpunk pixel art, and I adore adventure games, so I was really excited to play this based on the trailer and art direction. Believe me, I wanted to like this game but they made it downright impossible.First of all, the plot was convoluted and the writing was wordy. I agree with another reviewer who called it "sophomoric". For much of the game, the main character pretty much had the subtlety of a boomer spouting "technology bad". He is, for all intents and purposes, a technology hipster who considers floppy disks and dial-up modems the height of culture. The dialogue was also weirdly filled with paragraphs upon paragraphs of unnecessary technical descriptions. Little dialogue was devoted to character development or relationships. And despite all the unnecessary technical descriptions, the sci-fi in the game pretty much devolved into hand-wavey magic nonsense.The core of adventure games are the puzzles, and this game does not do them well. This is one of the few adventure games I actually stopped playing because my sheer frustration turned into boredom. Puzzles are satisfying when they make logical sense, not when half of them amount to the main character going around irritating and screwing people over completely at random, just in case they happen to do something useful that progresses the plot. The character also walks unnecessarily slow considering most adventure games these days offer run options. There are entire screens where you pick up one small item then otherwise ignore....except that you have to walk back and forth through them repeatedly.Another bizarre problem is that the game has several seconds of load times between screens. And I run AAA games in high quality just fine, so the problem isn't on my end. This adds to the tedium even further.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Point&Click isn't my thing, however I bought this game as I've been a big fan of MBR's music for the past while so I played it just as it launched (which among other things means no walkthoughs are available yet). I got stuck at times, but with a few nudges from fellow players I was able to 100% the game. The setting and story is very cyberpunk, and riffs a bit both on that and point&click in general.Overall enjoyable, and certainly better than previous Point&Click games I have attempted.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation is fantastic. The music is excellent, the art is consistently excellent. There is a variety of unique and colorful locations and experiencing the game never becomes boring.The writing is a mixed bag. The first half of the game is basically fine, the story is light (your girlfriend disappeared, go find her), but the characters are interesting and the worldbuilding works. The second half of the game devolves into a pastiche of plot points from various cyberpunk novels and movies, the writing picks up some pseudophilosophical wankery.The gameplay is... ehhhhh. Again, the first half of the game is relatively good. There are some obtuse moments, but it's generally not too hard to figure things out. The second half gets way more backtracking and the puzzles start getting esoteric and at times downright absurd.Overall I like this game and would recommend it - the presentation carries, and the price isn't very high. If you like point-and-clicks and/or cyberpunk, it's a decent pick.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice point & click adventure and definitely worth it for fans of the genre. The graphics and the music are an absolute stand out and the story/writing in general was good. I wish it had a hotspot system though and I'm really glad I had a walkthrough for a lot of the puzzles,  especially when it involved backtracking without hints. The puzzles aren't necessarily moon logic, but there are some solutions I'd never have thought of. Guess it depends on how your brain is wired if you find this game difficult or not, for me it was
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting a long long time for this game, and I was so certain I would love it.Perhaps a long build-up to a game release is a bad idea, it gives people time to build up incredible standards that might be impossible to attain.It goes without saying, it's a very beautiful game. From the art style, to the music, and to the evident effort that went into this game. This is definitely a game to be proud of making.Although like many other people, I found parts of the game very difficult which took me out of the story.  This would be fine if the story was enough to hook me in, to create some sort of pay-off. I felt no sense of reward though.I got about halfway through the game and realised I didn't care about the characters, and I didn't care about the outcome. My only commitment to playing this game at this point was because I really wanted to love it. And after about 6 hours of game play, I just gave up because I just didn't care.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr this is a decent enough adventure game that I could recommend playing it.However if you prefer to read a more longer review, please read on.Virtuaverse is an imperfect game. It's beautiful and scored amazingly, the artists on this were excellent, but there are a number of frustrations that underlay the basics of the game that can make it frustrating at times.So here are a number of criticisms that I can levy at the game. They are relatively small things, but they can ruin the experience for you if you're not used to an older design of adventure games.1) The presentation of text could be made more easy. Scrolling the dialogue tree to see options you have already exhausted is rather clumsy. I feel if you've exhausted conversation with an npc, most of the redundant options should disappear.2) Sign posting of what to do. The journal system is a good idea to help players understand their goals, but the problem, compounded by a lot of backtracking between multiple environments, is it can become easy to forget exactly who or what in the environment needs to be operated on. 3) Item clutter. It's a double edged sword to have so many items for flavour, but most of the items seem to be trash that don't do anything but clutter up the inventory and make it harder to figure out what needs to be used where.4) It would be nice to have the ability to leave scenes by double clicking. Perhaps this is a limitation of the game engine, but since there's a lot of backtracking and moving around, it makes it feel frustrating if you can't move quickly around.With these said, I'm sure the game wears its influences on its sleeve. The story fixates a lot on the past, both in the game and in terms of the references and this makes it rather narratively simple. What I find interesting is that there's never really much in the way of opposition. The megacorp never poses much of a threat to the hero, and at several points, he ruins the lives of many people for seemingly no other reason than progression of the story. This culminates in an ending which is fitting for the story but may feel unsatisfying.I would contrast this game to my other favourite one like it, Technobabylon. Technobabylon is a lot more polished in ways, from the UI, to the puzzle design, to VA and so on. But it's a game that's definitely more post-cyberpunk than it might seem and consequently can go in more interesting directions narratively.Virtuaverse in contrast doesn't stray far from the safe harbour of the foundational elements of cyberpunk. It delivers exceptionally well on it, but that can come off more dated seeming than it first appears. It still is compelling of course, even to someone who is very familiar with the genre, and it was definitely more enjoyable than not. In summary, Virtuaverse is as beautiful and flawed as the genre it evokes so deeply. I look forward to the next game by the studio.

_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This really is a love letter to the old 8-bit adventure games. The music is absolutely fantastic. It sets the stage of the game so well and keeps you immersed. The cyberpunk setting is very welcome, and reminds me a lot of Blade Runner or Altered Carbon, and a lot of the story reminds me of one of my favorite books, Vurt. This is such a refreshing game in a genre that we haven't really seen much of in a long time. It's also very difficult! Which is refreshing in a time where everything takes you buy the hand.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying that this game is great. I just finished it, and it was quite the journey.Almost everything about this game is next to perfect - the environment, the graphics, the music, the writing, the world building, the classic point and click approach to the gameplay. Even the story, despite being extremely generic, is not bad.However, and unfortunately, this game is smaller than the sum of its parts. The reason for that is how frustrating it can get. Sure, difficulty is fun, and tough puzzles are fun - but this game has too many bottlenecks. Too many pixel hunts and EXTREMELY 'out there'  logic puzzles that are so frustrating to get through that it can really drag down your enjoyment. If this game had better clues, or at least some system to help you out when you're stuck at the same point for over an hour, along with a handful of quality of life improvements (fast forward traveling, for example)- it is a contender for one of my absolute favorite games of all time. Unfortunately, and much as I wanted it to be, it isn't.Overall though, it is still a very good game. If you enjoy video games, sci-fi, cyberpunk and puzzles, there are very few better ways for you to spend your money.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo and loved it!  After that, this game suffers from getting too big.  I was carrying like 30 items and and it got really annoying having to try 30 items on everything to see when the game decides some random combination is going to work.  That combined with a map where you might have to walk 10 screens, walk to get on a boat, walk to get on your bike, to then walk 3 more screens to check if something else might work, and I just got really burnt out on it.  This led to me looking stuff up and finding a bunch of steps I'd never have guessed to take, and I just washed my hands of it.
