_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I first learned about Virtuaverse from MBR since I’ve been listening to his music for years. Virtuaverse is an excellent implementation of the classic point-and-click adventure game that could have easily come out in 1993 and fit in along side The Curse of Monkey Island. Of course at that time no one would have known what a smart phone or QR code was but the game does a good job of giving you the details you need if you know to look.The dialogue is full of the humor we loved in those classic games and the clues/puzzles are not too tortuous. The game, soundtrack and art are all well thought out and implemented and this game is an instant classic.If you are a fan of point-and-click adventures, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a nostalgic yet new experience that rubs your Point-and-Click itch VirtuaVerse will be right up your alley!VirtuaVerse fully embraces the core mechanics that made the genre what it is today, pays homage to it roots and offers plenty of throwback jokes while simultaneously making sure you feel your time well spend with a fresh experience.MBR's tunes underlines the retro vibe the game heavily relies on well and the soundtrack is a masterpiece in itself. Speaking of the retro vibe you will be welcomed by a plethora of subtle and at times not so subtle often humorous oldschool cyberpunk references which was a pleasant surprise.While the game won't hold your hand it isn't knee breaking challenging either. It has the right balance to keep you on your toes while still making sure your experience won't be too frustrating. There are a few missable achievements if you aren't thorough adding a minor replay factor.Naturally every good game is bound to have it downsides and unfortunately VirtuaVerse has it's flaws too. While the puzzles are refreshing and the story feels unique enough to keep you interested both the MC and his love interest are fairly bland and some of the actions/justification feel out of the left field and even unfitting at times especially near the end of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Loving this game! Hard puzzles, fantastic atmosphere, somewhat corny humor. Before I picked it up I saw a streamer playing a little bit of the first part while narrating, he was australian but did a fantastic American accent with a deep voice for the main character and that was awesome, could totally see that be in the game too and also gave extra depth for myself when I played it. I found out about this game when I, a while back, first started to listen to Master Boot Record who's a phenomenal artist making fantastic music and the soundtrack to this game might be the best he's done, to my ears.Awesome job! Total throwback to my childhood, playing the cult classics from Sierra, Lucas Arts and to not forget the Blade Runner game that also finally was re-released digitally this year! I hope I'll see more from you in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this for quite some time - not only because I really like old school adventure games, but also because the music of MBR is absolutely awesome. And most of my expectations were met. The visuals and music fit the theme very well, the cyberpunk-feel is captured perfectly and the puzzles are challenging but (usually) not unfair. However, there are some minor things missing that prevent this from being an awesome game (instead of the very good one it is!)First of all, the game story somehow isn't all that engaging. Sure, the mood fits the story's background very well and everything is appropriately bleak. But what is more or less entirely missing is a concrete antagonist. Like the Nazis to Indy or LeChuck to Guybrush. Pretty much everyone is working towards your goal or is neutral, there is never a moment of doubt. There are no plot twists, (almost) no feeling of narrow escape, you just do what everybody tells you to and you are fine. Second, the game is almost completely linear, it feels like you are on rails the entire time. Every puzzle has just one solution and one only. And it's not always the most plausible one. () Sure, you can pick up an enormous amount of non-puzzle related items, but you can do nothing with them. Especially the  would have lent themselves very well to some unrelated but fun mischief!Finally, the protagonist and his motives are not completely credible and/or consistent. Especially when he shows blatant disregard for health, safety and the lives of others, his sudden obsession with freeing humanity from a potentially harmful condition he himself is not even affected by feels a little... far-fetched. And some tiny details kinda ruin the pixellated retro-glory for me: One is Jay's walkcycle. It looks as though her legs are not even attached to her body and her knees bend somewhere they probably shouldn't. And (call me pedantic) the sprite-scaling is not consistent with the pixel-resolution of the background. I know, with modern game engines this is difficult to achieve, but for a game that has obviously been made with such attention to retro-details, this looks just sloppy.Anyway - I had fun playing it and I totally admire the effort and love these few guys have put into making it and I can only hope that they take all the (often very constructive) criticism to heart and make an even better sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: It's an A E S T H E T I C creation with a strong vision, great art, great music, and a fun story. Well, it's a dark cyberpunk story, but I definitely enjoyed it. The creator's voice and opinions seem to shine through pretty strongly at points in a "commentary on how I see the future going" type way, but that's kind of what the cyberpunk genera is all about isn't it?Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. The pixel were drawn by Valenberg (known for a wonderful music video by Perturbator), music is composed by Master Boot Record (pioneer of the Synth Metal genre). But the best part of this game is the puzzles: never boring, never stupid hard, always full of logic. I came to a stop in my progression several times, but I was always able to resume after no more than half an hour searching through the pixels or re-reading the dialogues.If you grew up playing Lucas Arts point and click adventure games, and you liked Mr. Ron Gilbert's return with Thimbleweed Park, you will LOVE VirtuaVerse.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A great classic point and click adventure with a unique soundtrack written by MBR, an alternative, industrial and experimental project. It is nice to get deeper and deeper into the story,there are many scenarios to visit and some tricky parts, but that is the good part of a click and point adventure. The ending is exactly right. I can only suggest playing it, waiting for a sequel sooner or later.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 4 out of 5Awesome! Design, Animations, looks, sounds. Special kind of humor.Few things could have been partly better, writing of story and character.Check out Master Boot Record`s music, if you haven´t already. I`m mindblown and can´t stop listening to it.Also search for Valenberg and Elder0010 (dude, that glove... great, now I want one...)I would love to see more of these creations. Theta Division: Keep on going - and rockin - dudes!The long version: (Probably with typos, not my native language, blah blah)+ is shorter, because it doesn´t need much critique, but it outweights the -- is supposed to be helpful, not bashing() is neutral at the end. About puzzles and violence++++It looks and sounds awesome, animations and everything is as lovely as in the old games, it has a dozens of references for everyone having played the old games, the riddles are mostly great and classic. I love the humor, serously (pun intended).-However there are a few things that could have been done better, so maybe this here helps the devs in any way.Or this try to put things into perspective helps people not to be angry with these things (beeing angry about stuff you can´t change is ultimatly going to fire back to you anyways).It´s kinda short.But well, it´s the first game for Theta, as far as I know (if I´m  wrong, please do correct me, then I´ll play the rest).And if one takes a longer time solving the puzzles... short is a relative term here.The lenght is really something going hand-in-hand with the story, the next point.One of the first reviews which I´ve seen here said "the characters don´t have any development" and "the story is generic". I can´t remember Guybrush Threepwood having much of a character developement either.Also, Theta are coders and acoustic/visiual artists, they´re not writers.Personally, I am just beginning the craft of writing and for everyone thinking, that this or that is shallow or generic: Try it, try writing something, that is neither shallow nor generic. Write something, that has never been there before, be it in a book, comic, game, movie, whatnot. Create a world, that feels real, let characters roam through it, which seem like living people. All you need is the abitlity to write words, right? If you can pull that off and become an author, I salute you, well done, you´ve earned every bit of success. If not, just chill. Creating a lifelike world and characters is harder than it seems. And, in addition, beeing able to sell it. There are far more authors who are able to write well, but not well enough to make a living. Or they don´t get enough distribution.Nonetheless, yes, there is room for improvement to give story and characters more depth. Maybe Theta could get a hobby writer, a fanfiction author or a hardcore character-acting roleplayer in on the next project.Still, these characters and the story have potential and even if Nathan was, well, akward, I liked him. Not sure why, but I did. I was sad in the end. I´m thinking of writing a fanfiction as a part two with... a different outcome (my, writing this while avoiding spoilers is also akward). ()The only people who probably aren´t enjoying it, are those who don´t like point&lick in general. Or those with very high demands or whatnot.It might also be a bit harder to understand if you have absolutly no knowledge about IT - which is hard to imagine for gamers today, I guess. The puzzles... hard to judge. I don´t even want to, if I´m honest. Some were harder, some were easier. Not sure how to feel about the backtracking and the pixel hunting. If I remember correctly, pixelhunting did appear in old point&click as well and sometimes you also had to backtrack. So maybe it only seems more dense, because it´s not the longest of point&click games.About the descibed cartoon violence, which some reviews say "is too dark": well, read some (older) Cyberpunk books, to sty in the gengre of games, try Shadowrun lore, for example. In most Cyberpunk worlds dying and killing is part of day to day life. Many characters in these worlds become or already are indifferent about it. That´s one of the many things that make it a dystopia. Wouldn´t be very dystopian, if everything is just high-tec butterflies, right? Not even Star Trek was all high-tec butterflies, and that was a utopia (at least TNG was based in an utopian world). And yes, I, too, was shocked when it first happend. Came unexpected. So in this respect: nice shocker.

_childDocuments_.review: I never wondered how it feels to play as a dull, obnoxious, immature, entitled creep (and worse), and having to cope with the consequences of his mistakes instead of exploring the huge and not-so dystopian world that he seems to inhabit. Well, now I know, and it was mostly frustrating. I'm still not sure if there was a moral lesson or redemption story hidden in there, or just random writing. If I ever finish the game, and that everything eventually makes sense, I may change the review, but what a drag for the first 4-5 hours (at least).Also: gameplay inconsistencies, as others pointed out. A shame, since the aesthetic is great and some cyberpunk elements were engaging (drone racers, augmented reality graffiti, retrogeist, etc).
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I like pixelated point-and-click adventures, especially in the cyberpunk genre. After playing a masterpiece like Technobabylon, I kept searching for similar games.Virtuaverse looked promising at first. But very soon, it showed its true colours - dull and uninspired.The story doesn't make much impression. It's some sort of alternate future reality, and technology and lore consistency are pretty low. Advanced tech is mixed with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. In fact, it doesn't feel like a cyberpunk game. The MC design is cool, at least.His motives are dumb, and everything proceeds in an irrational direction. It starts with his GF missing in the morning. She is gone from their apartment, and he instantly panics and starts to search for her as if she was a child or smth. He breaks his AVR googles, and we spend a lot of time fixing them, then he goes around and searches for his GF, also finding out from the news that she is a wanted hacker, and it was him using her ID card that gave the law enforcement an excuse to arrest her. It doesn't make sense, really - he even gets involved in a gang war and gets a person killed - for what? His motives are shaky at best. It lacks a sense of urgency even though he allegedly is in a hurry.So he finds her before the police, and coincidentally it is at that time that some sort of AI freedom fighting group leftover from the AI war of the past sends a message to the gang in question. It turns out - implanted AVR chips are being used to control the world and plunge everyone into illusion, like some mega Tsukuyomi from naruto.His GF was secretly a hacker involved with some random street gang who just so happen also to be heroic rebels against AI-controlled AVR tyranny. He instantly jumps on the team, and it feels rushed and unreasonable. Like, "no time to explain - travel around the world on errands cause you are the only unwanted person here". And the mc is like - "ok". Wut? He travels on a flying tour bus with four rock stars who are now jobless (because of him). They somehow don't see a problem with giving a stranger a ride around the globe for shady reasons and otherwise stay in the bus and do nothing.The rest is just a series of convoluted riddles with very lacking foreshadowing. Dialogues are bland, and characters are unremarkable.The worst part is - the whole thing doesn't feel personable. I failed to empathise with the MC; his "adventure" lacks drive and motivation.Since such games are primarily story-driven, I can't recommend such a lacklustre game to other people.

_childDocuments_.review: This entire game and a project is a love letter to the Lucasarts adventure games of yore. If some of your earliest PC memories are learning insult sword fighting or using a rubber chicken with a pulley in the middle (Secret of Monkey Island), then this is 100% for you. I did receive the game for free (as a surprise!) to help with last minute testing but I was absolutely going to purchase anyway. This entire project is a labor of love created by a small handful of talented and passionate human beings. The sound, the visuals - it all serves to create an atmosphere that really sucks you in and adds a fresh coat of paint to a genre of game that could be entirely nostalgia, but it has actual modern play value here. Play this while you wait for Cyberpunk 2077. 10/10, would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Completion Update:It is a true homage to the genre and that is super hard to do with sincerity imo. Many have tried, but this team crushed it! They have all the aesthetics! They do a great job of compartmentalizing the puzzles. You always have access to all the things you need in the zone to progress in that zone. This simplifies the puzzles a bit. However, later on the areas are quite expansive, and I got lost in the pixel hunt, and failed to notice some subtleties. But, the frustration also leads to a greater sense of completion when I figured it out.As far as I could tell, you couldn't accidentally lock yourself out of progressing but accidentally not getting an item or talking to someone. This is HUGE!! And used to be a big problem with this genre back in the day.------------------------------------------Pre-completion review:Its a faithful and fun genre tribute with one of the best soundtracks ever! Never muted it. Usually get tired of repetitive background stuff, but I had zero problem listening to it the whole time. Critical part: Are some of the puzzles tough or wonkey? Yeah, welcome to old school point and click. If you're saying WTF and banging your head against the wall, that means they did it RIGHT!! They all used to be this way. If it was easy and obvious and the UI was smooth and not at least a little clumsy, I'd call BS. This is the way its supposed to be. Please see Kings Quest (one through seventy-two), Monkey Island, Day of the Tentacle, Myst, Space Quest, and Maniac Mansion. Just be glad you can save at anytime and don't have to worry about the power going out and loosing all your progress! 100% love this game!

_childDocuments_.review: VirtuaVerse is a 2D retro pixel Nintendo Switch game that's been dumped on Steam for who knows what reason.  It's a point and click adventure game, basically a ripoff of games like Secret of Monkey Island, which became mostly obsolete last century.  So, you know, if it was 1990, this game might have been considered mediocre.  It's not 1990 anymore. As a text heavy point and click adventure, this is far from the best.  You're confronted with mini-puzzles frequently, which is fine, but they're not positioned well against the flow of the game.  Like, in Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis, you'll hit a puzzle at a momentous position in the game where things are coming to a bit of a climax, which puts a lot of narrative pressure behind the puzzle.  LucasArts knew how to do things right.  Here, you get slapped with a puzzle for trying to open a door so you can go out.  Come on... This also falls down the hole that many amateur point and click developers dive into eagerly... "close enough" is not good enough to solve puzzles.  If you need to get something somewhere, no matter how you do it, that should be okay, but this is one of those games that requires that every switch, dial, inventory interaction and click needs to be done in precise sequence or you can't progress.  This is tiresome.  Repeating the worst mistakes of an obsolete genre is the last thing that will revive it. There's a slew of technical defects as well. A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.  The benchmark for modern Cyberpunk games is the licensed R.Talsorian Cyberpunk 2077.  This game is nowhere close to that in terms of visuals. While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.In an attempt to excuse the low quality of delivery here, the game makes a big point of having a nice soundtrack.  If the business plan for a game is to compete with Spotify, which is free and has effectively unlimited music, all of which is better than the music here, it's failed before it even started. Gamers can listen to the Spotify for free.  A game cannot be seen as recommendable just because it competes badly with listening to the radio or to MP3s.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?VirtuaVerse has the laughable price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $15 asking price for this game could get you games like "Kingdom Come Deliverance", "Doom Eternal" or "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt".  Or a tonne of retro Sierra games or LucasArts point and click adventures in bundles for less than they're charging for this.  That's actually the most cyberpunk thing about the game... the unrealistic portrayal of inflation based on that ridiculous price.

_childDocuments_.review: I was largely attracted to this game for its synthwave music, pixel-based graphics, and cyberpunk story. I enjoyed it for the most part, but I have to admit that I did get bottle-necked at times. I tried to use guides but found them unreliable due to my stupidity at the start of the game. There are two modes to choose from: old school and story. I thought I had chosen the "harder" old school mode at first, when I had actually chosen story mode. Thus, the guides were not accurate. It should be noted that you CANNOT complete all of the achievements on story mode. So, I ended up restarting the game after having gone through 75% of the story mode. The old school mode I found was more interesting.Regarding the story, for a game that came out in 2020, it sure gave a believable look into the near future, if not already now. Being in my mid-40s now, I enjoyed all the references to technology and ideas of the late 80s and 90s. The ending was a little surprising as I couldn't really predict it playing out as it did.My one major gripe about the game was it's point-click mechanic. When you click on something, you will generally get two options: look and action. I constantly had to re-click an object or area to select the action icon. There really was no purpose for the look action. Also, I would recommend using a multi-button mouse and programming the keys that you need. There is no need to use a keyboard for this game.Finally, although I like pixel-based games, this was not worth playing at full-screen. I have an 3440x1440 QD-OLED monitor, but I windowed the game to 1600x900 (Ultra-Wide is not an available option).

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is still hard even with story mode but also I can just use a guide. I wouldn't say it's a visual novel and it still takes parts of the 90s point and click for the mode. All these games can be beaten with a guide and I think there's nothing wrong with that since you already paid for the game. I enjoy the writing and the details in the game but in my opinion there's so little difference when trying all the options there's no real point of trying everything out on everything. Story and difficulty are key and I think it's hard to keep that without sacrificing our time. That being said, I've always played point and click adventures to feel apart of a world and enjoy witty writing with fun characters. That's why they're my favorite compared to all the other game genres that give you so much to do but some of it is just repetitive. Video games are interactive movies with areas that you can go back to have fun again in. Movies suck compared to video games on price and time spent. This game has amazing music and art that reminds me of why I play video games, for good vibes.

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are good but they feel arbitrary most of the time - like making a task harder than necessary to pad the runtime. _childDocuments_.review: Always pleased to see a new PnC on the scene and VirtuaVerse doesn't fail to please. Wonderful aesthetics, good music and a good story. I played it in the "old school" mode and I did find myself stuck on more than one occasion, almost to the point of frustration. I looked up a couple of bits where it turned out I had missed an entire room, or a dialogue had unlocked for no real reason. So plenty of that old school running around trying to work out what to do next, but equally, plenty of decent problems to solve rather than feeling like you are in an interactive movie.With its 8-bit graphics, and multiple references to old school computers and the demo/crack scene - there's plenty here for nostalgia nuts, without falling into the trap of not being original. I only spotted one reference to a Lucasarts PnC and it was very subtle. The interface was clean and easy to use. I was quite surprised to see it come with Steam Controller configuration out of the box, although I did have to tweak it - who on earth uses mouse on the left thumb?

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun. Amazing music and aesthetic. _childDocuments_.review: A grand point and click cyberpunk adventure that starts slow and builds momentum up to the very end. The game is a masterpiece and you will be immersed in its atmosphere of stunning visuals and masterclass of a soundtrack.There are two difficulty modes: old-school hardcore and casual, so players can decide what kind of experience they want out of this. Hardcore was satisfying to play with lots of well thought out puzzles and contextual event-triggered dialogue and inventory progression. The game makes homage to Monkey Island, Beneath a Steel Sky, 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968), Akira (1988), Moon (2009) and throws in some fun hardware and ascii puzzles to boot.All the environments you travel through are picturesque and detailed as well as the cutscenes. Dialogue can get long-winded but never detracts from the pacing and mood of the story it is trying to convey. If you can get past all the puzzles, the ending is quite satisfying with strong messaging on the human condition. Kubrick fans will feel right at home.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A blast to the past!This took me right back to the 90s when I could spend the whole day wandering through wonderful and phantastic worlds and soaking up every last pixel while being mesmerized by the most atmospheric soundtracks. Never thought I'd experience this again. So many things that reminded me of stuff I thought I'd long forgotten.Thanks, Theta Division, for putting so much effort into this time machine. You created a true piece of art. Especially considering you achieved all of this with only three people (!) in your spare time.For reference, I played the game in hardcore mode and don't mind searching pixels or trying out random stuff if I get stuck. It's amazing to see how much fun you can have, once you lean back, relax, enjoy the experience and don't try to finish the game as fast as possible.Had to consult the guide once because I was stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Masterfully written, executed and the soundtrack is top notch. Some of the puzzles are quite hardcore, which came as a very pleasant surprise. I miss the day when you had to actually write down stuff.It also feels like a sweet love letter to old Amiga fans around the world which probably hit my soft spot. For fans of the genre, grab it and enjoy. This is art.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Everything is really well done, from the artwork, to the soundtrack, to the story. You can interact with several components of the environment, even if most of them won't be useful to go on with the game, which is really refreshing compared to other modern titles, and contributes to the immersive atmosphere. The puzzles are tough but solvable, especially if you grew up with adventure games in the 90s: details are always there to point you in the right direction, even if they might not be obvious at a first glance (Monkey Island 2's spit contest-style, which I always remember fondly!). In any event, the developers added a "story mode" to let you focus more on the story and less on solving puzzles. I appreciated a lot the multiple references to old-school computer technology and music. Familiarity with them helps in both solving some puzzles and enjoying the overall story setting.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play the story mode, however with the recent update it's is a major reason I'm giving this a thumbs up as the aesthetic and story here are the real winners. The story takes a while to develop, well past the halfway point but makes a fair and relevant point about the role technology plays in our society and how it influences the course of humanity as a whole. The puzzles in the original game mode are tedious, sometimes with moonlogic solutions, but overall should appeal to veteran Point and Click Adventure gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A great old-style linear point and click with the trappings of cyberpunk dystopia, unfortunately hamstrung by its ending.The game takes you on a grand romp through its world and its different locales with a few twists and turns, with a lead-up to a climatic confrontation only to... sort of fall flat in the very last moments. Despite this it is still a great game and completely worth it, but how it ends prevents it from really reaching its potential. Essentially you get a short spiel about what is  going on and then the game ends with no exploration of the revealed material and no closure.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Always nice to catch a cyberpunk themed game! And this one is done nicely although I'm not a big fan of pixel graphics. You will find yourself as a protagonist who wakes up one morning recognizing your girlfriend has gone. To find answers you will start looking for her. This game focuses on story content and solving riddles. As I have played this game a while ago it appeared to me that parts have slightly changed. Maybe a kind of an update?
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Whether I recommend this game or not is due to personal preferences. This game is a Point & Click Adventure game, similar to the ones from the 1990s. However, it is not charming enough for me. The oppressive background world and the opportunistic protagonist did not buy me over. Sure, the protagonist is a kleptomaniac (as usual in this kind of games) but also an incidental murderer without any remorse. Edna & Harvey 2 introduced all the murder scenes in order for the protagonist to evolve mid game, something I see lacking here. There is little to none comical relief other than mentioning random stuff from the 80s and 90s, like how a demo achieves one of the effects, all in assembly language.Then there are the puzzles. Some of them may seem logical, but others are kind of odd. I am talking about cat moustache levels of moon logic. In order to get physical access to a computer to register yourself to a separe net, you need to trash a car in a repair shop in order to push a cat to the ground, then unleash a dog that follows the cat into the shop where the computer is located where the cat and dog fight and chase away the computer user. I am skipping many steps here. Not sure what the logic here is when you could have waited for a person to leave the computer free - there was no time pressure at this point of time.Music does fit most of the rooms except the jungle town one. And thankfully, no bug that I noticed.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This has got to have the BEST cyberpunk pixel art I've ever seen in a game. The music is very good, and if it is raining outside as you play this game, it becomes outright SURREAL. The story and dialogues are well-written too. Art: 12/10 ---> Genre-defining, magnum opus Music: 11/10 ---> Ethereal, dream-likeStory: 10/10 ---> Amazing, superbP.S. See the game's logo? That's me, nosebleeding out of pure ecstasy everytime I play this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game for everyone who loves classic point n click adventure games, pixel graphics and cyberpunk, blade runner style worlds.The puzzles are challenging enough, never got frustrated trying to solve them.The only minor nitpick would be some long dialogues that get boring and lack humor and ending is something we've seen a million times.But overall it's a great game, and had a lot of fun playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, congratz to the devs. Definetely worth it. I liked the overall cyberpunk setting and the many references to old pc hardware and coding. I'm proud to beat the game without hints, even if it took a little while longer.Just remember to use all Tools at your disposal and basically scan each frame to not miss some subtle crucial items laying around. ;)The only thing i didn't like was the ending, tbh. As Nathan is basically on a quest to rescue his love Jay, (even if it takes everything...and the lives of others), I would have liked some kind of fitting ending (call me a romantic). Perhaps an alternate Ending, if you have had the chance to take a less reckless approach to things, - or boosting your karma. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a tough one to review. There is so much here that I loved and so much that I loathed. From the credits, I see it was only 3 people who did the game design, and for such a small team, they did stunningly well for the most part, but I think particularly the puzzle design suffered a lot from having such a small team of people. The pro's here are that there is gorgeous artwork. The game looks magnificent for the vast majority of it. There are some faces that I thought could do with work, but apart from that, the environments, the items, the people looked really great. I was really immersed in the world. Another pro is the music. I really loved the music. It was the perfect type of music to compliment the game and it contributed heavily to the immersion and feel of the world you are playing in. (I will say though, particularly the first section, the music got really repetitive, annoyingly so.)The con's for me are mostly about the puzzle design, and to a much lesser extent the ending. From some other reviews I saw which suggested that this game is marketed at a younger audience I expected the puzzle design to be more in line with the difficulty of something like The Darkside Detective, (a fantastic game but not very challenging). However, I found that some of the puzzles were ridiculously hard or just completely lacked logic, moon logic for those who play lot's of adventure games. I had to use a walkthrough more than a few times, in fact, so many times to get through this game. One of the puzzles (a riddle puzzle in particular), even the walkthrough wasn't able to explain it, it just gave the answer and said they had no idea how you reached that answer based on the previous logic of the puzzle. When a walkthrough can't explain a puzzle to you, you know it's ridiculous. Another example SPOILER SPOILER SPOILER Is where you purposefully pick up a book about tying knots, but then when it comes to tying a knot, you have to speak to the Captain and he then shows you how. Um what?! Of all the stupid puzzle designs, why? Why even bother putting this dumb 'red herring' in there? The logical choice, especially because you need to use another book you pick up in the same place, for information to solve a puzzle, is to use the knot tying book to tie the knot, but no. I found so many of the puzzles like this. They just made no sense. At least that particular one was easy to solve, but that isn't the case for other puzzles. Lastly, the ending. It wasn't something that I cared for. Now, ending a story is hard, no doubt about it, but this just wasn't for me. It felt a bit flat, and just a bit disappointing to end the whole game on that. I would have much rather enjoyed the more straight forward ending that you are more or less expecting to happen.Overall, I did enjoy my time in this game so I would reccommend it to a certain extent, but get yourself a walkthrough because you WILL need one. It's a 3/5 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I almost gave this game a negative review, but I just couldn't. The storyline is great, the setting and the aesthetic are awesome, and the puzzles... well that's the thing, they're just too difficult. Which apparently is very intentional. I finished the game in 20 hours of playing (never left AFK). However after the first few scenes you'll probably be reaching for the "nice hints guide" from the community page. Once you accept that this is fine (because you will be needing it), then you're good to go.To be honest, some puzzles are doable if you spent a good amount of time on it. Which can be rewarding, as long as you don't get frustrated. That is important!All in all, definitely get this game if you like the genre, the music and the trailer. But keep this review in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome atmosphere, story and puzzles like classic Lucas Arts games. The interface works really well and there's a map you can use to quickly go long distances.Most of the puzzles are not so far stretched as in the classics, but like them, sometimes you miss to pick up a thing and later, sometimes much later, you can't make progress because of it. It can be a bit frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A great classic adventure with a beautiful cyberpunk setting. The music is awesome and atmospheric. Since it was made as an homage to the classics the difficulty level can be frustrating for players who are used to play "modern" adventures. You won't get much help and sometimes you cannot progress because you need to speak with someone first or clicking on specific objects - but that should not scare you from playing this cool game. If you enjoy the music then search the net for Master Boot Record.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Just when I thought it's been ages since a Wadjet game to satiate my thirst for point and click games, out pops VirtuaVerse. I really enjoyed this - as a coder with a lot of friends in the demoscene and having grown up with cracktros and old PCs, this was just amazing for me. I love that it's got a serious story but is consistently funny with a lot of self aware humor, and it really captures the Sierra/Lucasarts vibe of humor, combining it perfectly with intentionally cheesy cyberpunk stuff.I will say at times, especially during the middle section of the game, the puzzles become at times obtuse. I used a walkthrough for a few bits but let's be honest who doesn't with this kind of game - it's basically part of the genre. Anyway, yes, I recommend it wholeheartedly.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ great & use of AR in the universe is unique but believable. People buy AR to cover up how gross the real world is, if they cant afford it they can get a pair of googles financed but they're constantly barraged with gross advertisements that drive them nuts. Plot goes a little wonk towards the end, but not enough to hurt what that was laid down before. Also its pretty w/ a great soundtrack. 100% worth the $ if a dystopian sci-fi point+click is your vibe
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: VirtuaVerse is a delight from start to finish with a fantastic soundtrack. The intro theme is still stuck in my head! I'd recommend VirtuaVerse to fans of old school point 'n' click games, pixel art or fans of the cyberpunk genre.The puzzles are a good challenge and there was a tough one in particular I had trouble with towards the end of the game. The story is interesting and is thought provoking regarding the affects of Virtual Reality in society.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: There are good sides and bad sides of VirtuaVerse.Graphics and artistic design is superb. I understand the choice of music but found it a bit too punchy for what the game actually is, an point and click adventure in old school style. Mellower synth without the highs would be a better synergy. Main character is quite generic and inconsistent. Game suffers a bit from pixel hunting and logical fallacies in the puzzles. Side cast of characters is quite good and could be fleshed out a bit more.I would recommend this game to fans of point and click adventure and cyberpunk themed games (which is an niche in what used to be a niche), for others playing this may turn out as a chore. That's said, this game does nothing better than the classics like Policenauts, System Shock 2 and Bladerunner already did before, although it combines story archs quite well.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I've got some mixed feelings about VirtuaVerse, but in the end I'd come down on the "recommend" side of the house.  It's a competently put-together point-and-click adventure game which takes the LucasArts path of having no failure states, which is always nice for an adventure game.  The UI is sometimes a bit clunky.  Dialog can sometimes get a bit "lost" in the visuals, and it'd be nice to have a way to cancel out of dialogs entirely, without having to choose the conversation-ender.  A mouse hotkey to open inventory (like the middle button perhaps) would've been a nice QOL improvement, but those are minor concerns.The visual presentation is excellent overall, and the sound is quite good as well (though I found some of the backing tracks overly repetetive after awhile).  Unlike some other reveiwers on here, I feel like the puzzles in VirtuaVerse are by and large quite good, and sensical.  I did use some hints a few times throughout the game, but in nearly every case the solution elicited an "of course!" reaction, rather than bogglement.  Even the more obscure puzzles have clues scattered around.  I did have a couple cases where I'd simply not found a very-small area of the screen to click on, and one instance of the ol' "I didn't realize there was another room off the side of this area," but those kinds of problems are hardly unique to VirtuaVerse, so I don't take points off for that.  There's a few times during the game where you might know exactly what you need to do, but your progress is gated by events that shouldn't be, like when you need to upgrade a racing drone but literally won't get the necessary dialog options until you go ahead and lose a race.  In general I think the puzzle design in here is quite good, though, especially compared to the absurd logic you'll find in many early adventure games this draws inspiration from.The main issue for me is one of tone, and characterization.  The game's not funny enough to be satisfying in that regard, nor is it serious enough to swing the other way.  The result is something that often feels very dour and tepid.  Adventure game protagonists are often quite misanthropic but can get away from it with sufficient overall game levity, but the first half of the game especially just throws it into sharp (and uncomfortable) relief.  In one memorable segment, our protagonist (Nathan) purposefully sends a gang member to meet with his companions wearing the identification of their rivals, resulting in that character's death.  It could've been a darkly humorous bit in a game that takes itself less seriously, but it feels pretty ugly in this one.  Fortunately for the game, it does lighten up considerably about halfway through, when the plot takes a completely batsh*** turn into the absurd, and you move beyond the confines of the Cyberpunk city.  The environs become much more varied visually and thematically, and the inherent silliness of the plot provides a nice contrast to Nathan's insistent seriousness.Nathan himself is nearly devoid of characterization (to the point of spending the entire game with his face not visible, underneath a "hey look how cool this looks" hoodie).  When characterization *does* come through, it's to berate concertgoers for not being "real" fans of the band onstage, mock people who don't share his views on technology, or generally spout off diatribes which sound more like angry forum posts than dialog.  One brief segment towards the end has us controlling a different (far more interesting) protagonist for a bit, and I was disappointed to have to go back to this glum, prickly jerk instead.Still, all that said, it's a well put-together game, and the visuals especially lift it into a recommendation from me.  It's bolstered considerably by the much more colorful and silly second half, has some pretty solid puzzles, and uses some augmented-reality mechanics to great effect.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Wow wow wow. I first saw a tweet somewhere about this game and got really excited about its release even though I knew little about it. So when it released and I was able to jump in I was so excited! And let me tell you the game was fun every bit of the way. This was my first sort of modern point and click adventure game and I def needed the help of guides throughout but man was the story and soundtrack great. The visuals and soundtrack alone should be enough to convince a buy for this game. I recommend all to give VirtuaVerse a go.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Being born in '85 in Eastern Bloc of EU I grew up with C64 which itself was maybe a little obsolete in '92 when I got first computer but hey games were gold. My favorite genre was adventures, text ones and also P&C ones as I was never quick enough to play shooters or run and jumpers. After finishing The Cave and Thimbleweed Park I learned about VirtuaVerse and OMG. This game rocks. It's Amiga-grade pixelart with C64 SID grade vaporware-metalish soundtrack. The game itself reminds me a lot of my early days gaming and has everything from that era in terms of game play. Things aren't linear and obvious, actually there are almost no clues and I really enjoy being stuck. Story is very well told and has atmosphere of what can be described as 80s kids dreams about 2020 lol. Thing that I like the most is the never ending chain of jokes and references that might be hard to grasp for those who never used floppy disk, flip phone that lasted three weeks on one charge or never dreamed of having a PowerGlove or never booted Amiga A600.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the game looks nice, the music is really good and goes well with the theme, but there is somethin off and i can't tell what. It just wont make me feel the way, that i felt when i played like Primordia or Whispers of a Machine. It's a good game tho, maybe i just had a bad mood when i played it.So try it, if you like point and click and pixel art!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A work of love by two of my favorite artists, and an amazing demo scene programmer. It is an old school game with a lot of style, and an excellent OST. The story is pretty decent, and the puzzles are good, but some can be a bit obtuse at times. Thankfully, it has a very helpful community on Discord. Feel free to join the server if you need any help! Looking forward to the sequel that is already in the works. Especially since the devs have now listened to a lot of feedback and are making the next one to be even better.Oh, and one more thing: this is a really easy game to get 100% achievements at, if you're a completionist.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great cyberpunk adventure game. The best in a long time if not ever. The story and setting are superb. Puzzles are very hard though, vibe is on point and humor is pretty good. Character is an empty slate really, but I like the fact that he's an anti hero who's actions mostly just screw things up while he's thinking he's doing good
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel art and soundtrack are god tier.There is a background "lore" throughout the game that ahas really cool ideas in it, many carachters will talk about actually interesting stuff.The game requires an insane amount of attention to small details to actually progress without checking solutions, hope u are up for it.GG
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This epic game is a masterpiece. Amazing nostalgic graphics, a really beautiful cyberpunk world to entcounter and a even better soundtrack I even hear outside  the game.The overall athmosphere is impressive.Virtuaverse throws me back into the days of my youth when I played Click & Point Adventures like Monkey Island, Days of the Tentacle or Indiana Jones.The puzzles are really thought through and even if it takes a while it is a joy to solve them. The story begins really strong but for me it flattens to the end. Didn't play to the end of the story yet but look forward to do!I can without any doubt recommend this game to all Point & Click fans or people who like nostalgic games and puzzles. One of the best games I played 2020*Sorry if the english is not that well. German is my native language but used english to reach more people

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:-A unique take on the cyberpunk genre that focuses around virtual reality and augmented reality. -A completely awesome soundtrack by Master Boot Record-Nice art!-Classic point & click adventure. _childDocuments_.review: Great game. Great soundtrack. Great environments. Great art. puzzles are rather obtuse, but most of them are solvable without a walkthrough. Dialogue heavy game. _childDocuments_.review: Music and art is brilliant! MBR being one of my absolute favorite artists, this isn't any surprise. As for the gameplay itself: If you like these kind of adventure games, where you have to click around and match everything with everything, this is the game for you. _childDocuments_.review: The art, world building, and music were really enjoyable. The storyline was decent, but the puzzles were pretty random / problematic to solve. _childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks and sounds gorgeous, I just hate it.The biggest problem is the dialogue, the character you play as is a complete buffoon. _childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for (i) for 1980s adventure nostalgics, for (ii) retro-cyperpunk nerds or (iii) for anyone who just enjoys a good point & click.   The atmosphere is really fantastic and boosted a lot by the awesome soundtrack and the low-res art style.The dialogue is well written features a healthy dose of irony, the game doesn't take itself too serious.
