_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into cyberpunk P&C adventure games and a fan of the film THEY LIVE, then you've hit the jackpot. Be aware though: this game has challenging puzzles with a lot of backtracking and it feels like 2 or 3 games in one  when it comes to length. My biggest gripe with the game though is the several NPCs lives you end up ruining throughout your adventure. Yes, you're trying to save the world but it seems a bit cold to me that they wouldn't mention what happened to these other characters to show any sort of empathy.  With that being said, this is a big adventure with a badass soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of point and click games and Master Boot Reccord's music, so getting this game was a no brainer. It is solid and the amateur of the genra will apreciate it. There are numerous reference to the hacker subculture and demoscene, the soundtrack is also really good, all in all, I recommand this game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The game _oozes_ identity - the music, the pixel art, those are all are great. But the gameplay is a chore.I have played a lot of classic adventure games, but seldom do I encounter puzzles so poorly designed such as I've encountered here. As many others have pointed out here, many of the puzzles don't make much sense. The game provides little context or hints about your goals, and has very linear structures on how they should be solved. Even if you figure it out the general "idea" of what you should be doing, you often need to do things in very rigid sequence defined by the designers, otherwise, the right options will not be open for you to access and solve the puzzle. They also often include a significant amount of backtracking, further disrupting the flow of play.Many adventure games have one or two puzzles which are non-sensical or that might feel unimaginative - but in VirtuaVerse, this is the _norm_.Which is a damn shame, because the game has a lot of positive aspects going for it on other areas - like the aesthetics mentioned earlier, but also, on the effort the designers have made to bring this world to life. You can interact with many things as you travel through the areas, which can really help you immerse in the narrative. Unfortunately, all those options then clash hard with the tightly linear focused quest design - breaking your immersion immediately. Even though you can interact with many objects/people, the game only permits a single solution to its puzzles, in a very particular order, no matter what you might imagine should be possible/feasible using all those options you could interact with.That being the case, unless you're willing to "grind" through the gameplay, VirtuaVerse will not deliver a good adventure game experience. There are many other "cyberpunk options" in this genre of gaming that would be better deserving of your time: "Whispers of a Machine" and "Technobabylon" come first to my mind.I hope the developers get a second chance of creating a game like VirtuaVerse - the universe and feel are spot on, but hopefully, they'll improve their skills enough to give us more solid gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Quick:3/5.  This game is pretty good.  I had fun playing through it.  There were several times that I had to consult a walk-through to make it beyond certain sections.  It can be very ambiguous and frustrating at times, but the story is engaging enough to keep you guessing how to complete the puzzles.  More:VirtuaVerse is a Cyberpunk-ish Point & Click style game.  It is story-focused, with most of the narrative delivered via text in dialogue between characters.  There are very few cutscenes in the game.  They are short, yet interesting and well constructed.  What begins as a search for the protagonists missing girlfriend, ends with a grand plan to shut down an evil AI.  The world portrayed here is great.  I enjoyed the characters that I met along the way.  There are several interactions that really stood out to me, and a few that are very shocking and memorable.  This game depicts a dystopian future in which magnetic data storage has been outlawed, and everything and everyone is connected via a cloud-like information infrastructure.The artwork is pleasing to look at.  Most of the character designs are simple, and the animations are as well.  Yet, they are done well enough to help you maintain immersion in the world, and clear enough to get a good idea of what is going on.This game is hard.  Many of the puzzles are difficult beyond reason.  There is little foreshadowing in certain areas, and not many hints at all on how to solve a lot of the puzzles.  One thought that I kept having was 'How was I supposed to know that?'.  If I did not have access to a walk-through, or was unwilling to consult one to complete this game, I would have never finished it.  I am glad that I did, however, even with the walk-through assists.Overall, I think that this is a unique, and good game.  I am glad that I played it, and look forward to more from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great retro point and click with a great style, and a story that doesn't go off on the usual divisive woke politics and instead focuses mainly on the technocratic dystopian future. The one issue for me is that as per a lot of old school point and click games it is extremely difficult to figure out what you are supposed to do to make the story progress.  There aren't a ton of puzzles, just figuring out wtf to do, thereby making it necessary to have a walkthrough open in the background.  I'm normally pretty decent at knowing how the logic these games work, but this one is frustratingly non-handholding, and don't expect a hint system because there isn't one.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: FINALLY THIS GAME! I was expecting to feel again the shiver of the old school adventures, where one could feel a bit of thrill in discovering the story and not just falling into it as a consequence of time passing. Yes it can be a little bit "hard" sometimes, as I got more and more used to easy games, but in the end it just took few more hours to complete all and that is a good thing! If I remember how long it took to me to locate the wheel chicken in monkey island 1.... with now games every solution literally shines and you only have to go on. FINALLY, i could relax in my mind feeling I was salving an enigma, not just completing an easy kid puzzle. Maybe this is not for all the users, as COD players are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ everywere in the net, but I love chess and mine sweeper and if I buy an old school graphic adventure I want this fun! Moreover I loved the environment, the graphic, the characters, the whole cyberpunk estetic is amazing! Could have been better?  Shure, there are many things that everyone could easily think they would have done differently, but in my opinion only game developers can understand what really can be done differently or not. And as a player I am amazed by the world they created!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I *REALLY* wanted to like this game.  The music is AWESOME! The retro graphics are AMAZING!  The story looks great! But after trying for nearly 30 minutes to get out of the first "level," aka our 2-story apartment, and not being able to, I finally had to lookup a guide online.  Went to the second area and struggled for over an hour to figure out how to get passed it.  Pulled up a browser to search for the answer before realizing that I'm not going to enjoy a game that I have to consult a wiki for every little thing.  Maybe I wasn't in the right headspace for it at the time, but it was just incredibly frustrating.I'm still giving it a positive review, because I think it might just be that I don't like this style of game...I hated Myst and Riven back in the 90s, and this felt like a more frustrating version of those.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Consistently fantastic art, a soundtrack that is amazing when it wants to be and a refreshingly retro approach make this an adventure worth taking for Adventure Game fans willing to put up with some major tone problems and a few less than original scenarios. VirtuaVerse succeeds as a platform to showcase the phenomenal talent behind all of the parties involved in their respective fields while betraying a lack of experience with regards to design and writing.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This just goes to show that you don't need bleeding edge RTX graphics to make an awesome, immersive, story-driven game.  With some of the best retro pixel art and an amazing synthwave / chiptune soundtrack, this game is a throwback to some of the best point-and-click adventures of the late 80's / early 90's and does a fantastic job of capturing the essence of a Cyberpunk future with an interesting twist.Its rare that a game captures my attention so firmly, but once I started playing, I couldn't stop until I had finished.  Be warned though, it contains some brutally difficult puzzles and you will most likely need some help to get all the way through. But this game is definitely worth it.  Kudos to such an amazing team of developers and artists.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: VirtuaVerse flew under my personal radar until release. I only learned about it from the twitter buzz it generated at launch. It was receiving glowing reviews from the gaming community, from Cyberpunk enthusiasts especially. As an enthusiast myself, I decided to give it a try. And I absolutely loved it.I'll start out by noting the most important aspect of the writing. This game was obviously written by those with a passion for computing and it shows, blending modern tech enthusiast themes with a future, dystopian atmosphere. These guys know what they're about. If you're passionate about cyber-security, the future of virtual reality, and retro hacking, you're going to love the references and themes in VirtuaVerse. Secondly, I absolutely love Master Boot Record's soundtrack. It's almost like he was meant to write the music for this game. Makes for good casual listening outside of the game. Thirdly, the art is amazing! It pushes pixel art past what you normally see in games like this. The pixel art rivals Hyper Light Drifter and The Last Night (unreleased).I only had one gripe with the game, and it stemmed from me just needing to git gud, but the path forward to progressing further in the story was muddled in tiny details and things you'd have to have a very, very keen eye for, and some ingenuity to solve. I am neither a detailed oriented person, nor good at puzzles, so I am chalking this up to a personal opinion rather than a critique, as I'm sure there are a lot of players who will enjoy the hunt, but I had to spend the last half of the game with a walkthrough up on my second monitor to get to the end. I did not feel that this was a significant drawback, as the story was so interesting that I didn't mind missing out on the puzzle-solving.Absolutely pick this game up if you're looking for a good story, love cyberpunk, or love point-and-click adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A great game. Art, story, writing, music, concept. All top notch.It does run into some of the classic adventure game problems (obtuse puzzles, pixel hunts) in the later levels, But still solid design overall. I'd argue better than most of its genre.If you like the old adventure games and cyberpunk check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this game. Completed it in about 13 hours. Puzzles were great although I'll admit I did have to look at a walkthrough when I felt really suck. Story was engaging with good humor peppered throughout. Music by Master Boot Record is awesome that fits the world perfectly. Pixel art very reminiscent of older point and click style games. If you like those point and click adventure games, this should definitely be in your library.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully art directed 8-bit point and click adventure. Just what I've been dying to have more of. Beautiful art, engaging puzzles, thoughtfully realized characters and a great storyline. Felt like I was getting to enjoy an old classic for the first time. Haven't finished playing (a little over halfway through I believe) and still no bugs or glitches. Plays like a dream.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I should start off by saying that I liked the art, the music, and the story (except, I agree with others that the ending was poorly done). However, I can't give this game a good review because it isn't fun. It feels like a chore playing it. Some of the "puzzles" have reasonable solutions but many of them are completely illogical and it's simply the game of trying every permutation of every item on all the clickable objects in game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This game defied my expectations. It is dark, but has some comedy to it. The story is good, the locations are different enough to keep it interesting. The puzzles are refreshing and not too difficult that it gets frustrating. Nathan isn't the most exciting protagonist but it does not detract from the experience of playing. One misstep is not having a location map where you can just click and quickly transport somewhere else. Going back and forth from the Blade HQ to other further off locations does get tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it will be worth it.  I keep telling myself that in all point and click games whenever I get stuck.  This was the case in the first couple hours of VirtuaVerse.  There's much to collect and interact with, much inhabitants to have dialogue with. All done in a sick-ass cyberpunk pixelated world.  It's all good stuff.  An easy recommendation to those with interest in these kind of adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere is beautiful, the music is excellent, the puzzles are hard. During my playthrough there were times when I wanted to break everything on my desk out of frustration, but when you figure it out you get a great sense of satisfaction. If point and click adventure games are your thing AND you like solving sometimes difficult puzzles, this is a great buy. Would highly recommend despite my anger while playing.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just beautiful. Not only for fans of oldschool point and click adventures, but also for cyberpunk and synthwave enthusiasts, like me. I am in the last quarter of the game or so, i don't know, since i am avoiding spoilers of any sort, but the riddles in the game are quite hard but fair. you have to pay attention to so many things, but it will be definately rewarded. The dark humour is also a big plus, it is not always so obvious and makes you think a lot about our current situation on this planet. I still have to finish the game, but this is by far the best videogame i have played since the witcher 3, when judging on the capability of sucking me in, so i can flee RL for a short while :) waiting for cyberpunk at first i considered this game to be just a gap fill, but it is so much better than i expected. i would give it a solid 8.5/10 1.5 points missing since it could be improved a bit in controllability, like a double click run for example. i have encountered some movement bugs, making your character just continue to walk after already having clicked on another object than the one that was clicked before, hence the character not cancelling the current route to a new one in some situations, nothing really bad, just a bit annoying sometimes. Also i think it will be a bit too hard on the riddle side for some people, but hey you can't make it right for everyone, so screw that!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool adventure game with great plot, aesthetics, sound design and soundtrack. There isn't really anything not to like apart from some squandered chances for more+better gameplay and an average at best Ending. Not that I didn't enjoy it, but the end of the game seems a little rushed.There are LOTS of eastereggs pointing at 80's popculture and retro-futurism. Some great humor aswell. Definitely worth the money, even more so with a discount. I would really love to see a revamped version of the ending and maybe some additional chapters patched in from time to time. I would definitiely love to see a sequel! Have fun playing!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable classic point-and-click adventure. Graphics and music are excellent. Sometimes the storytelling felt a little smug and heavy-handed—probably because I'm a programmer of just the right age to understand all the tech talk. There were a couple of puzzles where I had to look up the solution, but I don't mind that and it sort of feels par for the course for the genre.Just a small thing, but I appreciated that I could pick models of either gender in the dark room.My first playthrough took about 16 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Classic point & click adventure with aesthetically pleasing cyberpunk-themed pixel art graphic and music. Puzzles are challenging like old games from this genre and really make you think outside of the box. There are guides online but solving it by yourself is still the best feeling in the world. Overall, it is a good brief escape from most of today's mindless button mashing fiesta in gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Hi and welcom to my review of VirtuaVerse! Upon seeing this titles I immediately purchased this game.I think because the game looked fantastic and the soundtrack drew me in.So I started playing and I got sucked in by the story, which starts off really interesting.I wanna talk about a few minor thinks that bugged me while playing (I kept a notebook and wrote it all down)- So in the Inventory there is no magnifying glass to get more info about you items, which is a bit of a shame..- Second, When you use a item from your inventory on a item in the scene you're in it will go back to your inventory if it can't be combine, instead of staying in hand to try and use it on something else.so you have to open your inventory ALOT.-last thing, the journal next and previous buttons (Q & A) do not work with page up and down in the public terminal, eg:  the dating app etc.And in addition to that they do not work in your inventory either, the inventory scroll is done by scrolling mouse. I would have like to see a more coherent use of keys since they are under the how-to-play section and except for the Journal you're not reall make use of them, and journal is not something you actively open and scroll through.Now some very positive things, and I wanna start with the soundtrack. It features a Synthwave score, and boy it sounds really awesome. It is a bit of a shame they did not use Synthwave for every arrea of thegame, but the city does have some interesting tracks!!the quality is unprecedented, and I've never hear such a good quality soundtrack in a point&click adventure game before. that's one of the advantages of playing point&click games in 2020. The graphics arts reminds me of games like flashback, another world, day of tentacles ,sam & max and many more 90's games. You can see the developers loved this genré and stayed true to it!Finally, I think this game totally deserves the price it goes for, were it not for making point&click game in 2020 then more so because everything feels right about this game, the genré the music and a rock sollid story!   7/10 for me, (developers pls let me know when you have done something about the few issues i encounteredso I can change my review to 10/10)
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Have you already seen those reviews that point out that story and dialogues are not top-notch?Well, here is my experience: VirtuaVerse is  for those who can fall in love with excellent pixel art backgrounds, outstanding synthwave/chip music and a sweet technology-heavy story,  the execution of some narrative aspects is not perfect.For some players, the writing might result naive, or it might lack deepness. Others might feel that the "cyber" perspective doesn't match very well with the strong emphasis on retrocomputing, which the developers clearly love.Still, VirtuaVerse is an intriguing, vast, and rich point-and-click adventure game that, in my opinion, can't miss in the library of any old-school adventure game fan.* Immersive cyberpunk atmosphere* Many locations* Awesome pixel-art* Great electronic music* Nice story, but don't expect something too deep* Some beautiful puzzles, especially those involving the virtual reality headset* A few puzzles are not very well designed* I would probably have liked a less explicit and subtler approach to showing the negative political and social aspects of the world* Add "backtracking" here, if walking around and re-admiring pixel-art backgrounds bores you.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, i'm very impressed by the love of detail that the developers put into this game, so many easter eggs and references to older games, i love it!The game is very atmospheric, i don't mind the puzzles to be challenging at times, i played some of the most iconic Adventure games like Monkey Island, Beneath a Steel sky, The Dig, Day of the Tentacle, Simon The Sorcerer 1&2, i like to use my brain and imagination for these sorta things like puzzles.The artstyle is gorgeous, i knew when i first saw pics of this game, back then, that it would be a great game.The music is also great and compiments to the atmosphere of the game very much.I'm in the slums district now.It's a clear recommendation from me! :)
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Point and click cyberpunk pixelart adventure game from 2020.I loved it from the first time I heard about it via the Blood Music FB page and bought it, as soon as it became available on Steam. The soundtrack is more than amazing (I got it from Bandcamp and love to blast certain tracks loudly: Punk Chiptune, Church Of The Old Code and my absolute favorite: Keygen Assault - hell I would even buy merch of that fictional band + Motördrone)The story is great, the art is amazing... Only the last quarter and the ending were a big disappointment and overall, I wish that the game was longer.Edit:Replay late 2020: Still loving it!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I love sci-fi, I love cyberpunk, I love MBR's music. And the pixel art I love too. This is a great game with a great story and really worth every minute to play it. The puzzles aligned to the well recognizable  computer technology of our time are amazing. I'm excited if the story will get a sequel and hope for it.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: It is more than clear that the developers have certainly put in a huge amount of effort and time into making this game as professional and as fun as they possibly could. The game took me about 11 hours to finish so it’s definitely longer than a lot of modern adventure games. It is certainly refreshing to have such challenging but mostly fair puzzles and for anyone who laments the fact that adventure games have become too easy nowadays then I would certainly recommend this game for you. While some of the puzzles could have been integrated better into the game and narrative and the main character could have been more interesting and more likable, overall the game did win me over with its fascinating story, interesting cast of characters, diverse locations ,beautiful pixel-art graphics and intuitive gameplay and I would definitely recommend this to anyone who wants to feel the experience of playing an old school adventure.For my full review check it out here:
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible futuristic adventure where your character is sent, due a series of events, to save the world from a terrible menace.. The gameplay is easy and well done, and the story is absolutely great..Lots of compliments goes to Master Boot Records (who cured the OST and Story) and to the digital illustrator Valenberg for the amazing scenarios we got during the entire adventure..Thanks a lot to the developer and super code hacker Elder0010 who really got the Number Of The Beast to made this jewel reality.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Great point-n-click, reminiscent of the best age of the genre but with a fresh story and feel. Music is obviously great! With the exception of a few times where it was about going pixel-hunting for items to pick up or drawers to open, this was a challenging but always logical trip.If there's going to be a sequel or second work of the team, I'm looking forward to it
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, took me back to my childhood and early teens both on the subject of point and click adventures and my baby steps exploring computer hardware and software development. Great music, abundance of humor and great references to the past. Not to forget the beautiful art. Keep it cyberpunk. Thank you, for me it was worth every cent and more.Edit: After writing this review I have read a few reviews commenting on the story being bad, the protagonist being unlikable, some of the puzzles being ridiculous and the backtracking being unneeded. As for the puzzles being ridiculous and the backtracking point, I have had the same "frustrations" in almost every point and click adventure I played in the 90's and accept it as a part of the genre. Perhaps that is too easy, but it didn't bother me. I remember being stuck in Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis for an hour or so on several occasions and during the playtime of VirtuaVerse I had some flashbacks to this. It just made the experience better ;-)Of course it is not the same as reading Neuromancer for the first time 20 or 30 years ago (I couldn't read yet when it came out, so it was mid 90's for me), but it is not something to give the game a bad rating over. Although I understand people would hope for the game to be more perfect than it is, the goal of this game (as I see it) was not to write a new eye-opening genre-starting culture-shocking story, but to entertain people who can appreciate the mix of old tech, the scene, the cyberpunk pixel art and the "new" synthwave direction that perfectly complements it. Comes together beautifully. ++
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR worth it, buy it.The style is magnificent, the music is banger, and the story is fun. There are plenty of really enjoyable diverse characters and environments to explore. The soundtrack especially is a huge selling point for this game, I personally really enjoyed listening to it while solving puzzles. The story feels really worth investing into as things go from personal vendetta to-...well, I guess you’ll havta see for yourself.It definitely has the occasional point-and-click game’s “oops I skipped a step” syndrome, but it was never anything that made me wanna quit playing. The devs also clearly have opinions on some things (such as cloud tech) and will let you know, so if you don’t like feeling preached at it may be a bit to chew from time to time. Though it stuck out like a bad advertisement segue when it happened, it never made the experience less enjoyable in my opinion (sometimes it was pretty funny).Any mild flaws this game may possess are greatly outweighed by a cyberpunk adventure that keeps you gripped and immersed. The devs were kind enough to give me a copy to stream after I requested it, and it made for absolutely excellent streaming content.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Although the puzzles can be very convoluted, I really enjoyed the cyberpunk atmosphere along with the pixel art. I do think that in future releases, maybe a little more guidance in the opening puzzles, with clear focus on what things you need to pick up and go with could be helpful. Still the challenge and feel of the game overall so far is quite on point!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This hit all of my nostalgia buttons for those old 8-bit adventure games and my love of weird science fiction. Music was fantastic, and story was great. Some points were difficult, due to needing to back track for subtle changes, but was never frustrating. All the information that you need is in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning visuals! Challenging enough to keep you guessing but also wanting more. I'm a big fan of Dark synth and the sound track hits home. Bloodmusic also comes through with amazing content like Perturbator, "the uncanny valley" ablum and Valenbergs's video work with "Sentient". The game is a job well done and i love it, looking forward to many more hours.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: The game is absolutely great. Very nice attention to details, especially appealing for nostalgics and fans of cyberpunk and synthwave. Some of the puzzles can be annoyingly difficult and entirely unintuitive (thankfully there are walkthroughs). It's also rather short. I finished it in 11 hours, it may take even up to 20 depending on how much hassle the puzzles are to each. After a few attempts i can't be bothered to waste more time though, i'm in it for the story. Speaking of - the story is amazing and the dialogue is very well written. It kinda feels like a cyberpunk version of the first two Broken Sword games. If you like PaC adventure games - this is for you right here.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A great addition to the point'n click genre, which happens to be one of my favorites. I wasn't too satisfied with the conclusion though, and that'd have to be the only negative I give the game, I didn't particularly care for the ending. The rest of the game is spot-on, however!Regardless I recommend it for any Point'n click enthusiast out there.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game you'll love until you will most probably hate it and back.So, just to expand: a true to the heart cyberpunk visual galore, Virtuaverse packs all the good stuff expected from the genre in a classy point & click adventure. Visuals are gorgeous and immersive, all the hubs/scenes have a certain cinematographic feel to them and contribute to the world building. Music, as well, amazing if you are a fan. The story I would argue is overall strong and has some nice little subversive moments, but I do get the feeling that it sometimes builds up a lot of anticipation and tends to fall flat / not build upon.Characters... well... are serviceable to the story. And now I am getting to the “love till hate” part... Again, there are moments when how the characters behave and react that really contribute to the immersion and as you're slowly building up anticipation and getting into the flow they do or say something extremely stupid on non-related to the task at hand... Or straight up seem to not care about anything that happens around them or the consequence of their actions.One of the most frustrating negative points for me personally was the loophole logic some quests have. I don't know if it has to do with the inherent way old school point & click adventure games are designed, but there are moments in this game when you will exhaust all possible options and MAYBE then remember a random item/character 2 stages ago that might push the quest forward.  After you manage to finish said task and you look back I often had many "Why would anybody do this in this specific way?" moments. More often than not, there is no cue that the quest progressed and the journal system is there for... something.As a conclusion, I personally love it for the piece of art that it is and, if you manage to live with some of the jaggedness of the quest design I can wholeheartedly recommend this game as a fine addition to your game collections.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: I had the pleasure to accompany the game already in the beta phase. As a fan of classic adventure games like Monkey Island, Day of the Tentacle, Zak McKracken etc. I was very happy to be part of such a game.Of course I could write an extremely long text now and praise the game through the roof.But let me say just one thing:If you ever did a beta test - and I mean a real beta test - for finding bugs, typos, glitches etc.Not the 'Look at me I'm part of the World of Warcraft Beta - but I'm just playing and braggin' on reddit about it, instead of helping the developers!'*cough* where was I?Ah yeah, if you ever did an intensive beta test you will be familiar with the loooong process of testing the same scenes over and over again.And I can say: I enjoyed it! There's so much love for the whole atmosphere, that you can discover new  details every time.You dive into a world that's so diverse and mysterious that you think you're reading one of the many famous cyberpunk novelles that inspired this piece of art.The riddles might get a bit tricky sometimes, but that's the part of an old school adventure.(In case you forgot already)
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: A amazing return to classic PC Point and Click!To those who loved the classic point and clicks of the 90s, you'll love this game. The developers love and passion for old school gaming really shines through in this game. From the classic design, to the many DOS era Easter eggs throughout the game! The beautiful pixel art and synthwave/chiptune soundtrack blend seamlessly to immerse you in the world Theta Division have created!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Fun nostalgic cyberpunky adventure, great soundtrack, good pixel art. I have not yet finished the game, but so far puzzles are pretty difficult and sometimes frustrating, but generally leave me thinking "i shouldve thought of that". We're nowhere near cat-hair-mustache levels here. The cool atmosphere and fun story more than make it worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely perfect, and I say this as a person who doesn't play many adventure games. I've been playing it for a while and I have to say it's such a great game, the story is very compelling and full of details, immersive sound design and the graphics are soo beautiful. The puzzles are sometimes difficult but very rewarding when you understand how to solve them, they never seem too far-fetched. Instant classic.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: Well, here we are. To be honest, I’m too lazy to write a review for each and every game I play, but sometimes, I feels like a I owe it to the developers for their hard works, especially for a just-3-nerds team like Theta Division. I can only imagine the humongous quantity of cruch-time needed to make this beauty. If you are a fan of old school lucasarts-like adventure game, stop reading and just buy the game. No running, sometimes you need to backtrack a little and some puzzle are really hard, but you can always solve it using your logic and lateral thinking. _childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a game that will hold your hand and let you skip dialog just to finish it, then this isn't for you.  The graphics and music are astounding. Reminds me of playing games off floppy disks in school, but with drugs and music. BUY THIS NOW. Don't try to rush through it and whatever you do don't ignore the dialog!
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review: art direction and music are outstanding, imo the music could have a bit more variation, i feel like i am listening to a handful of loops over and over. warning: there is some loopy adventure logic and tough puzzles here. none of them are super absurd or unfair, all solutions can be found inside the game, but if the way of thinking that requires from you puts you off, you should consider going in with a walkthrough or guide. i must say this bothers me much more than it used to back in the day. i see how it is part of the genre, but i am kinda asking myself if it has to be. definitely a great game if you like point and click adventures. if you are missing the old great ones, this is a top title.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

_childDocuments_.review:
In a future not too far away, one Artificial Intelligence has prevailed over all other AIs and their governments. 

Nathan, an outsider still refusing to comply with the new system, makes a living off the grid as a smuggler of modded hardware and cracked software. Geared with his custom headset, he is among the few that can still switch AVR off and see reality for what truly is.

He shares an apartment in the city with his girlfriend Jay, a talented AVR graffiti writer whose drones have been bit-spraying techno-color all over the augmented space in the city.

Waking up one morning, Nathan discovers that Jay disappeared overnight, but not before leaving a cryptic message on their bathroom mirror. 

Having accidentally broken his custom headset, Nathan is now disconnected and determined to find out what happened to Jay, but he soon finds himself tangled up in an unexpected journey involving Jay's hacker group and a guild of AVR technomancers. 

VirtuaVerse is a challenging old school cyberpunk point & click adventure set in a future not so far away narrating tales of technomancers, AVR graffiti writers, hacker groups, tribes of cryptoshamans, digital archeology, epic cyberwars and virtual reality debauchery.
_childDocuments_.name: VirtuaVerse

name: Conglomerate 451
detailed_description: Conglomerate 451 is a grid-based, dungeon crawling first-person RPG with roguelike elements set in a cyberpunk world. You are the CEO of a Special Agency, instructed by the Senate of Conglomerate city to restore the order in sector 451, where corrupted corporations have established their turfs. Thanks to the last constitutional decree, you are allowed to create human clones. Build your own team, manipulate DNA, train your agents, equip them with high-end weapons, choose what cyberlimbs to implant, and send the squad to the field with only one goal: eradicate crime and restore order at any cost. Manage your resources - Make use of your own personal R&D department to research advanced technology, unlocking new features, powers and options for progression More than just body mods - In addition to upgrading weapon and armor proficiencies, augment your body with interchangeable cyber implants that completely change your agent’s skills and utility Pain and Trauma system - Even the smallest wounds can have a lasting impact. By taking damage in combat, agents risk generating permanent Traumas that will follow them between missions Story or Endless Mode - It's your choice. The Story Mode brings you in a world filled by events and a war with corrupted Corporations and their propaganda. In the Endless Mode, the game will create endless content for you Perks and Mutations - Your agents can acquire special skills (Perks) and obtain Mutations Drugs and Disorders - buy synthetic drugs to temporarily empower your agents, with the risk that they develop Mental Disorders Procedural cyber dungeons - Experience the dungeon crawling you love, mixed with future technology as you take on procedurally-generated dungeons and missions If you die in the game... - Each mission could be your last thanks to agent permadeath. Consider every move, because if an agent dies in battle, they will be lost forever Hack the world - Enter cyberspace mid-mission and hack your way ahead of the competition to get crucial intel and give yourself the advantage Collectables and Achievements - find collectibles around the dungeons and bring them to the Collector to discover the truth

In the Endless Mode, the game will create endless content for you Perks and Mutations - Your agents can acquire special skills (Perks) and obtain Mutations Drugs and Disorders - buy synthetic drugs to temporarily empower your agents, with the risk that they develop Mental Disorders Procedural cyber dungeons - Experience the dungeon crawling you love, mixed with future technology as you take on procedurally-generated dungeons and missions If you die in the game... - Each mission could be your last thanks to agent permadeath. Consider every move, because if an agent dies in battle, they will be lost forever Hack the world - Enter cyberspace mid-mission and hack your way ahead of the competition to get crucial intel and give yourself the advantage Collectables and Achievements - find collectibles around the dungeons and bring them to the Collector to discover the truth
short_description: Conglomerate 451 is a grid-based, dungeon crawling first-person RPG with roguelike elements set in a cyberpunk world.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Like I hoped, the first update has addressed some of the issues I mention. That's a good sign that the developers are paying attention to people, and bodes well for the future.The game has been officially released for all of 24 hours as I write this. No doubt patches will make a lot of my gripes obsolete before too long.I think the easiest way to describe Conglomerate 451 would be "What if Bullfrog classic Syndicate Wars, but Grimrock/Star Crawlers exploration and turn based combat, with a little X-Com base management between missions?"You run some government agency which has just set up in the city of Conglomerate, which is wholly owned by corporations and utterly infested with corruption and crime, with the mission to restore order by using massive amounts of firepower, immediately letting us know we're in present-day America and you're basically flinging clones of dangerously unhinged and over-armed police at the problems until they go away.Ok, it's a *little* more nuanced than that, but the game essentially boils down to sending cloned operatives out on missions, securing resources, and using the time between missions to develop your agency's training, research and development departments. Research new technologies, agent skills, weapons, character classes, DNA enhancements, cybernetics, and more. Your clones can develop physical and mental injuries during play, so do you put a valued agent into a healing tank for a week to fix that dislocated shoulder or do you keep them in the field and risk the damage becoming permanent? There's a week of downtime between missions, and you have 75 weeks in total to take down all the main corporations. You get to unlock new areas of the city as you progress, which keeps the environments from getting stale. Missions vary from "find the maguffin" to assassinations requiring a mix of combat and multiple hacking minigames, which can be as simple as a timed button press, or as complicated as a timed word search in a constantly scrolling sea of similar phrases. They break up the exploration and combat quite nicely, and can offer some very nice loot to upgrade your agents' equipment.Combat is a simple turn-based affair, very much like Star Crawlers, but where Star Crawlers cuts away to a separate, static map for each encounter, here it happens in situ, very much like Legend of Grimrock, but turn-based. You can initiate combat at range which is a good idea when attacking melee enemies as you'll get some free shots in. And if you manage to flank the group before starting the fight you can ambush them. Various abilities cause damage, buff and debuff and mess with the initiative order, and some attacks cause bonus damage or effects if the target has one or more status effects active. There's lots of potential for setting up some massive damage moves, but the enemies can do the same. It all works quite nicely, and I've nothing really to complain about.That's not to say the game doesn't have issues, it's definitely a little rough around the edges; the cityscapes look great while some character models can look very uncanny valley or cartoonish in texture; Voice acting varies from good to quite poor; The dialogue and text (for the English, anyway) need more proofreading for typos, general grammar and some really odd mistakes (as a microbiologist I cringed so very hard at the thought of a virus being used as a "bacteriological weapon". Viruses make virological weapons, bacteria make bacteriological ones! They're completely different in almost every way!); The repetitive quips from your little floating robot guide get old very quickly; And there are a couple of small annoyances such as the glitch animations and sounds being rather... unpleasant on the ears. I get that glitches are *supposed* to be unpleasant but perhaps sacrificing realism for the sake of less nails-across-the-blackboard effects would have been a better choice.But.But the game gets a lot more right than wrong. Apart from the above problems, the graphics and sound are excellent. The mechanics are straightforward enough, but offer quite a bit of depth in terms of skill and research trees. The imposed time limit of 75 weeks will keep the story more focused than Star Crawlers' "here's infinity missions you can do between plot sections" approach, while the "Endless" mode does away with the plot and lets you clean up Conglomerate forever in a state of perpetual war, just like US police forces have always dreamed.So. I think it's a good game, and if the studio takes on feedback and sorts out these niggling issues, it can end up being a great game. Whether you want to wait for a patch or two to come out before buying is up to you, but there's a good solid game here, no mistake.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Starcrawlers, but Cyberpunk.And without the charm, the enemy variety, the plot, the character building, the consistent theme...It's kind of a mess because the concept is neat, and the game makes a strong impression at the start. But then it falls off hard when you find there are only six locations and you will see all the enemies you're ever going to see on the first visit. Your agents gain levels, but the bonuses are very minor and don't make the agent much stronger; most of your power comes from your gear and skills. And the skills can be numerically improved but the ones you start the game with are all you get. Since there's so  very little plot (and the plot missions are basically just normal missions) you'll see all the content in the game early....which wouldn't be so bad... except that even if you complete the game's central objective of "kill all the corp bosses", you still have to play out 75 weeks of the game to finish it up. Screw that.It's also got some major balance problems. A lot of the bonuses you can get are irrelevantly small; +2% HP (when your base is 50-ish. Oh boy, one hit point!), or +2% damage, for example. But on the other end of the scale you can, quite easily, push an agent to a 100% crit rate very, very early on in the game, and then just curbstomp everything you come across. If you take the soldier (who can recharge shields), the infiltrator (for damage), and any sort of support character, you're basically invincible and combats are over almost as soon as they begin. And you can ignore all the defensive upgrades and just take the "If you have X% of your battery left, get 50% damage reduction" upgrades to make things even less of a threat.All the game's written lore comes in 20 'echoes' that serve as a money sink and, all added together, make up about one single note's worth of lore from most other games.In summary, great concept, but incredibly disappointing once you get past the beginning.Special mention to the drone that follows you around and makes witty remarks that get old very quickly. It's completely out of place in the tone of an otherwise very serious Cyberpunk game and has a pool of lines way too small for the number of times you'll hear it speak. But the devs must have known, because they gave the drone's voice its very own volume slider.

_childDocuments_.review: Corporations are bad and the future is bleak but hey, at least it’s neon-lit to the point of causing seizures! Sure, we can’t synthesize cyberpunk in a single sentence yet one thing is clear: it took several decades but now we finally have a self-standing genre dedicated to humanity’s slow suicide by technological advancement. Before a certain “2077” will drop on us like Thor’s Hammer, we have an interesting blend of not-so-literal dungeon crawling within a convincing cyberpunk world. Conglomerate 451 is developer’s RuneHeads first foray into Sci-Fi and their 2nd Steam project to date after the more traditional fantasy “crawling” from Fall of Light. So far, so good as I’m always going to encourage indie devs into expanding over multiple settings, themes or topics. Creativity should never be stifled, regardless of perceived popularity or potential risks. Cyberpunk’s inception caused quite a stir and that’s how you gauge proper progress. Stilted minds will never move us forward.Yet I can’t stop asking myself if we’ve reached a point of no return as a species. Luddites will certainly advocate for less or no influence from technology in our daily lives. I don’t think that will ever be possible from now on. At least not in the highly developed and allegedly civilized world. Whether this slow climb will be followed by a sharp decline, it is not for me to predict. I thoroughly enjoyed discovering Conglomerate 451’s intricacies, even as the game is still in Early Access and its dev team has acknowledged that it’s a work in progress which has yet to reveal many of its planned elements. If that 451 has triggered a proverbial lighbulb by chance, you are correct in assuming that it’s a nod to Ray Bradbury, a prolific science fiction author deservering more recognition. His “Fahrenheit 451” is dystopian novel from 1953 which discusses the dangers of censorship and total control over society without necessarily delving into cyborgs or corporations gaining more influence than the national states themselves. Yet this theme still remains true: it’s just one executive branch replacing another in the end, while blind loyalty is to be found in either case.The year is 2099 AD. A megacity which is simply referred to as “Conglomertate” after we presume that it engulfed neighbouring urban centers, stands on the frontline of a civil war between the private sector and whatever’s left of the local authorities. An agency is founded with the sole purpose of removing Conglomerate from corporate control. You are its Director and this crucial task shall hopefully fall into capable hands. The “Ghost Class Agent” is a fancy term for a clone soon to be enhanced into a cyborg. This isn’t an exaggeration at all, since your agency will start off surprisingly lacking in basic resources. The shaky start of every fledgling governmental enterprise, right? In any case, the one field in which you can fully place your faith, is the gene pool of your cloning center. Your agents have quite a few things in common with the “sleeves” from Altered Carbon. They’re expendable and relatively easy to suppress before any risks of getting “sentimental” might arise.This is another title which looks excellent in spite of being powered by the Unity Engine. I didn’t have any performance issues and it scaled perfectly to my native resolution. There weren’t even “small crawling bugs” as the game’s introductory screen explained in its Early Access clause. A single fly to this ointment though: lack of visual diversity. Whether we’re talking of the enemy types, maps or the agents themselves, there isn’t enough random generation or customization at play here. I understand that we’re dealing with a lot of clones, but please don’t take it literally to such an extent, RuneHeads. The loading screens between missions are drawings which could certainly fit in the concept art definition. There are plenty of screenshot opportunities and the dev team has confirmed that they are going to implement an option for temporarily removing the HUD, thus enhancing user generated images taken in-game.A convincingly cyberpunk soundtrack is present within Conglomerate 451, but it cannot compensate for the lack of voice acting. There are several voiced cutscenes such as the intro featuring an android secretary, but the rest of the gameplay seems far too silent for a project of this scope. General sound effects shall not disappoint, so overall I shan’t lower the game’s rating too much simply because it still has plenty of room for improvement and it is labeled as Early Access, afterall.The perfect footsoldiers against all-powerful corporations that shall rely on sheer numbers over troop quality. Your agents will start as weak, standard clones but the situation will change for the better once you’ve gained enough reputation along with the credits and tech points needed for DNA splicing, cybernetic implants and cutting edge weaponry. Be prepared to lose a “batch” or two, their loss still doesn’t have the same impact as in XCOM’s case, for example. The clones have high pain tolerance, but will obviously falter once they start losing limbs. Have multiple teams set up (three members can be dispatched during the active mission types) so that the badly injured might have time to heal in the Regeneration Tanks. It won’t cost you anything to create new clones, but healing them can leave a dent in your budget. Injuries will also become permanent if you neglect them for too long. I like this concept, more games should implement it.I mentioned active missions because there is also a type of “passive” task in which you can send a varying number of agents while you don’t have direct contol over any units. These secondary mission play out off-screen while you’re dealing with primary objectives throughout Sector 451. A gameplay mechanic I’ve seen plenty of times in the Assassin’s Creed series, it’s useful for gathering extra resources which you’ll surely need. In this title we have a surprisingly complex tech tree which branches out in several areas, each focusing on developing the agency’s lethality in one regard or another. I suggest you use the initial tech points in unlocking more agent types and genetic mutations, instead of investing in cybernetics or weaponry, at least initially. The clones themselves are the best weapon in your arsenal, give them an edge and increase their survivability.This may not be XCOM, but that doesn’t mean Conglomerate 451’s difficulty won’t teach you a lesson or two in humility. I’ve had teams clear out almost an entire level only to succumb to a last patrol of deadly drones which specialize in AOE attacks. “Area of effect” is a phrase you encounter in traditional dungeon crawlers and RPGs. It can be a blessing if you use it or an obvious curse which may dispatch your entire party, if the enemy possesses such spells. The autosave system isn’t leaving room for any errors. In case you’re already familiar with the genre, the movement won’t pose any issues. If you haven’t played dungeon crawlers before, get used to a hybrid of turn based movement & combat in which you rotate the camera a lot, while playing from a first person perspective. Vaporum and Legend of Grimrock are two contemporary examples you can also try out, since they’re in 3D and working perfectly on current OS’ and systems. Finally, I want to point out the hacking minigame which I enjoyed in Conglomerate 451 and it reminded me of old school Splinter Cell titles.

_childDocuments_.review: The Story Mode for this game lasts 75 weeks.  You are asked to kill the bosses of four corporations.Each week is a procedurally generated map, with one of three missions.  Kill a guy, Kill all the guys, or find items.After about 20 weeks, you'll have seen as much of this as you would ever want to.You have a base where you can upgrade your technology, agents, etc.  You can get to a point where the difficulty (on hard) becomes pretty trivial around week 40.  Have two agents spec for 100% crit chance and 80+% defense.  Have a third agent that can spam shield healing, and 80+% defense.  Done and done.So by week 40, you'll be ready to finish the game.There are four boss stages.  They aren't much harder than ordinary stages if you have a decent build.Ok, so it's week 45 of 75 and you're done. Pass.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rare beast. Meet an example of Early Access done correctly. The game started off somewhat basic but with a good core concept. A cyberpunk version of Legend of Grimrock but with Turn Based Combat and with stellar music and graphics. That concept then got refined and added to over several months with the introduction of narcotics, with better hacking, with the ability to delve into a mini cyberspace layer, with a timed campaign where you need to complete your objectives within a fixed number of weeks (thankfully Endless mode was retained for people like me who just like farming and blowing stuff up). Polish was layered on, bugs were fixed and new classes were added until eventually the 1.0 version stands before us now. With a solid tutorial and intro that drops you into the game and gives you a thorough idea of how the game works, but not quite so hand-holdy that you feel like you're being spoon fed everything. The game still expects you to do some legwork and learn how to minmax your team, there's still some QoL refinements that could be worked on, but by and large where we've got to now is worlds ahead of where we began. This is a very full blooded dungeon crawler with brilliant surroundings, enemies that will punish you if you get too cocky, and a suite of upgrades that force you to often make tradeoffs as to what kind of build you'll be gunning (literally) for with your teams.Your missions start out in the overworld city level (EDIT: You can optionally skip this now at least in endless mode, but I'd really recommend you do not), where your meat and veg is discovery of transit that takes you to your mission zone as well as accessing randomly generated vendors and dealing with, or avoiding street thugs who act as attrition encounters (as well as sources of credits, tech, and mods). Once through them you enter your target mission zone via elevator, and enter one of several brilliantly detailed and featured areas, the graphics here are genuinely high quality, and the enemies are well designed and in keeping with the theme. Praise really does need to be heaped on the art design team, the level geometry is some of the best I've seen in a dungeon crawler, you're not going to get bored of these environments even after several hours farming the same places over and over.The music, similarly, works well, and the menus in the corp screens where you manage your merry little band of misfits along with the combat beats are solid, well delivered and make sure you're always "in the environment", whilst the sound effects themselves vary a bit in quality this is forgivable on account of the soundtrack being -really- good. Again, it's not something you're going to get tired of even after extensive farming runs.There's a -few- but we're into "Nice to haves", things which probably were limited by the constraints of Early Access. Being able to insert more than one DNA mutation into new clones at an exponentially increasing cost would be useful, since some mutations are strictly more useful and others more situational.  Cyberhacking in combat still needs too many clicks right now, this could be rectified by adding them as additional skills as a second row in the combat skill palette. The Research tree could be cleaned up (It's still very much about passive gains, many of which could be rolled into more important nodes), and one or two of the classes could do with some extra love.That's about it. Everything else is great. Oh, and possibly the ability to have permanent upgrades for the drone. But that one has been on my dream wish list ever since we could tinker with the thing.Do you like dungeon crawlers? If so, this one is an easy win. At this price point, you'd be nuts not to get involved.Do you like the idea of a cyberpunk dungeon crawler? Ditto.This game set out with a very definite design goal. It's pretty much -nailed- that and done quite a bit more on top. For an Early Access triumph, I'm quite happy to see that it turned out pretty much as hoped.Verdict:

_childDocuments_.review: Hey guys,TLDR: If you like dungeon crawlers, especially futuristic (ala Starcrawlers) there is a good chance you will like this game too.Conglomerate 451 is set in and under (water) a cyberpunk style city. Actually my favourite map is the 'entry' cityscape. I love the look and the rain/water effects are pretty nice. Would liked to have had missions based in an offshoot of the outdoor area but currently all missions are enclosed. After the tutorial mission you can skip this part and head straight to the mission, which i do not recommend as buffs and map hacks and shopping can be done in the city and can make the mission itself more rewarding and easier.You as the Director of your corporation are in charge of recruiting agents to perform the main missions of the game. This is done by creating your own clones. They each have a class, four skills to pick out of a small list (which you can swap out later if you wish - losing any advancement in them though) and a select dna trait. You do not start with any but with research you can unlock more. So essentially the clones that come later will have a bit of an advantage in this matter.The initial classes you can pick are the Soldier (DPS/Tank), Infiltrator (Sniper) and drifter (support) but others unlock as you progress. These are the Splicer (healer), the Bodyguard (Tank/support), the Techie (Hacker/support), the Juicer (Nutjob... i mean someone who gets much stronger when abusing drugs but will suffer for it) and finally the Binary (mini DPS/Support).You can go through the game with no problems with just the initial three but i prefer the Soldier/Infiltrator + either Bodyguard/Binary. Credits and tech (Tech essentially a crafting/training resource needed for pretty much everything except unlocking memories (more on that later))  are the resources you need to advance.Aside from the usual shield/hit points you have two smaller bars for Pain (combat damage) and intoxication (drug use and some enemy attacks). As these build up you can end up with negative trauma/disorders which if not treated in healing/detox tanks within a certain amount of weeks these problems become permanent. You are given a percentage chance of how successful treatment for each issue can be resolved per week in the tanks.Between missions you spend time at your Headquarters where you can clone more troops, heal and detox your agents. try to unlock memories, research the various trees (Clone/health/training/Military and Cyber), view the agent graveyard where your failures go, Directors office (overview),  train and manage agent skills and slot mods into weapons, shields, cyberdeck (for hacking - doors, containers and people) and even cyborg parts you can unlock via research. Careful though add too many new body parts in a short time can cause the agent to die of cardiac arrest as i found out :) though you are given a heart rate que which of course ignored first time!There is a background pre-story which i wont spoil and to find out about it you must find and unlock (hack) memories of the past. You find on occasion these pulsing orbs on a level which you can hack and if successful you end up with one of the 20 memories that need decrypting at H.Q. To do so you decide how much money you are going to throw at the problem with a min of 5k. Essentially you are buying a better percentage to unlock but RNG being what it can be i have spent fortunes before finally managing it.The main goal is to take out the Leaders of four rival factions to make allegedly the city district safer. There is no story that runs concurrently with the present.Wow review getting to long (you can probably tell i dont usually write them :) ), so i will sum up in the usual fashion.Pros +Cyberpunk (for me anyway).Stable - not one crash in 87 hours or so.Pretty decent looking for what it is on max settings and fluid gameplay.Decent controller support.Lots of customisation.Good price. I certainly got my moneys worth!Trauma/disorder mechanic that feels Darkest Dungeon esq.Cons -Cannot customise agent other than tattoos with a change of portrait direction.The five biomes (random gen) other than the city could use more variation in my opinion but is ok.Once you take out the 4 bosses which you can do fairly early (20-30 weeks), even on hard you are left with just random content to finish the game at 75 weeks. Some achievements do not unlock till you do this. So if you are an achievement ♥♥♥♥♥ you must grind for it.Endings are to the point but compared to the intro upon starting a new game seems rushed and VERY abrupt, though hints of a sequel maybe in the offing :)Im sure there are more things to say both positive and negative but i do recommend the game, it is addictive and im planning my third replay to get the third ending. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: From Italian indie developer studio Runeheads comes Conglomerate 451, a cyberpunk-themed dungeon crawler currently in Early Access at the time of writing this review.  Having first read about this game from an article published on the internet, I decided that I would pick this one up for a review to ease the long wait I had for Cyberpunk 2077, back before it was announced. In its current state, Conglomerate 451 has one of the strongest introductions to gameplay I've seen in non-mainstream indie dungeon crawlers to date.  The project is admirably ambitious and you're throw headfirst into a sprawling skill tree that looks impactful, meaningful and fitting to the game's overall theme.  It's just a real shame that much of the luxuries I hoped the game would have already had have still not risen to fruition yet.  I did not expect this game to be as grueling and punishing as Darkest Dungeon either, which it most certainly is (to a certain extent).The player begins with three operators which cannot be visually customised. They're also all bald.  These operatives, though they can be cloned, will always begin from level 1 and will stay dead if they die.  A part of me wishes they'd grant some variation and randomisation to these clones when successful dungeon crawlers like Darkest Dungeon grant characters with quirks and specialties, which makes each of them unique, whereas in Conglomerate 451, losing a character is little more than losing the exact same guy that you're immediately going to the lab to clone again, except with overall better base stats.  They are the same three roles that are necessary for the player to traverse the map, so after some experimentation I found that any attempted creativity with my roster resulted in immediate failure of the mission without proper grinding.  Moreover, I had half expected to be able to customise my operators to a certain degree, so I ended up being quite disappointed in this regard.I won't speak much about the turn-based combat because frankly, a lot of Conglomerate 451's mechanics for its actual combat is quite standard and not exactly much to talk about.  I must admit that I personally don't play dungeon crawlers that often, but while I can definitely say that I have played better, and more fun games that use turn-based combat and innovate upon pre-existing cookie-cutter mechanics, I definitely cannot say that I did not enjoy the combat in this game.  The graphics powered by the Unreal Engine make this game good-looking overall which gives the developers a lot of leeway for satisfying displays and animations to facilitate my enjoyment of the game.The hacking minigame is the best I've ever seen, in any game to be honest.  It's not tedious at all like the ones you see in Warframe, nor do they serve as a roadblock for player progression.  Rather, they are an optional task in a terminal which the player finds in the map.  Essentially, the player must find the current prompt listed on the right hand side within a rapidly scrolling wall of text on the left.  It may seem overwhelming and confusing at first, but once completed, the player is given the option of a few rewards such as unlocking all doors on the next floor (which confused me at first...why not the first one i.e. the one I'm on right now?), or granting you extra rewards when you pass the level.In its current state, however, this is where the game hits a massive roadblock and rather disappointed me.  Firstly, the more complex branches of skill tree are so insurmountably difficult to access because it requires such a tedious amount of grinding the same levels over and over again, the game feels like a more boring version of Diablo at launch wherein people would spend hours repeating the same story mission, except with far less action.  I soon found it nearly impossible for me to get anywhere on the skill tree without carefully grinding my way through base-level enemies which I could easily one-shot.  This leads me on to my second point: there are skills which are clearly imbalanced.  The soldier class has a rocket launcher that deals an incredibly high amount of damage.  So much damage, in fact, that it renders the sniper class' "deadly shot" skill a gimmick that in itself deals far less damage anyway.  There is also such a sudden spike in difficulty between the second and third mission that I had to take multiple runs of the first two missions just to get my characters even close to skilled enough to compete.  I feel as though a dialing down on the difficulty on the first two levels would do the game far more good in the long run.Lastly, the map design is filled with a copious amount of vast and empty space that I wish they had used.  There are also idle NPCs sitting or standing around that you can't currently interact with at all, but I'd imagine Runehead is planning to develop these a bit more.It's clear that there are some games that don't truly understand the depths of 'cyberpunk' style.  Conglomerate 451 appears to land in between Sci-Fi and true 'cyberpunk'.  The menu is oddly (traditional, tommorowland-like) Sci-Fi, or even kind of similar to Star Citizen. However, the streets are a gritty, neon-lit basin that the genre has become a staple for the genre.  This division in style, although is meant to separate the upper class--the player, from the lower class--the soldiers you send to do the conglomerate's dirty work, kind of falls flat in my opinion because of how much the overall style changes from what *should* be armoured up mech suits and visible cybernetics (like Deus Ex) into neon jumpsuits.  Hopefully the team plans on addressing this in a later release.The visuals are great and deliver the standard package one would expect from the unreal engine, especially on the streets.  However, this leads to a point I would like to address: a division between the game's complexity and the game's visual fidelity.  The unreal engine is normally seen in FPS games, or TPS games where the player is afforded more freedom of movement.  As it stands, this makes the game, at times, play like an animated slideshow because of how restricted the players' movements are.  Though I would have preferred a more simplistic, but more heavily stylised map design in favour of a barebones cyberpunk one, though it *does* look quite nice, I must admit.Conglomerate 451 is a cut above average in quality when compared to many other tile-based dungeon crawlers out there.  This game doesn't seem like a desperate cash grab and is even more so not an indie game attempting to catapult credibility off of the use of Unreal Engine.  Though fresh, the novelty which sets Conglomerate 451 apart from its peers is quickly washed away by sharp difficulty spikes, tedium and inherent design flaws.  That said, I believe that Runehead still deserves credit for the recent headway, pushing out newer, much-needed content which the game, in its current Early Access state, needs to take a positive turn.  I vouch.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game.Pros-Neat atmosphere, randomly generated dungeons, interesting combat systemCons-Feels a little unpolished, Confusing disorder/ trauma system, repetitive enemiesIt has really nice atmosphere and feels thoroughly cyberpunk environmentally, however the animations sometimes feel a little janky and the models feel a little low res compared to the lighting and environments. Sometimes an enemy wont even move for their turn despite their actions happening mechanically.The story is simple, pretty standard for a cyberpunk setting. Some of the dialogue writing is a little confusing and feels like an odd translation, but this is more for a select few lines through the game rather than a massive problem. It's not a dialogue heavy game so overall this isn't super important.The mechanics are neat where you need to treat your agents sometimes after a mission, but it felt somewhat unexplained so I had to figure it out on my own leaving some of my agents with a laundry list of disorders I didn't realize.Once you've seen every enemy they start to feel a little repetitive, with the only special "new" enemies being late game bosses you fight only once. Harder levels only change the stats of the enemies instead of adding new ones.Overall it's a game worth getting on sale and if you're craving something to mindlessly play to sate a cyberpunk craving, but it overall feels like it needs a little more polish. I feel like the system could be expanded upon and turned into something really cool if given the chance. It's nothing to write home about, but nothing to avoid either.

Exploration is a bit janky, there didn't appear to be any mechanic to heal while in a dungeon outside of combat, and the aiming mechanic felt really clunky. There are mechanics at play to make the game more difficult, but they aren't difficulty swings that provide any satisfaction to the game.
