_childDocuments_.review: I'm very disappointed with Sniper Elite 5. Compared to the SE3 and especially SE4, this feels like a huge downgrade in so many ways. Just to name a few of my grievances, the game's maps all feel worse than those from SE3 and SE4, all are both far to large yet also too linear. The former might seem like a weird complaint, but the maps in this game feel disjointed, having a few areas surrounded by lots of open space with nothing happening. The first, second and sixth missions are especially bad, having vast flat field with little verticality, and a few very tall positions that turn the mission into a cake-walk. Several improvement from SE4 were also removed, like the ability to sprint while crouched or the small hub areas at the start of each mission, and whats new in SE5, like the ability to look down the sights of any weapon or the useless sniper vision I never used, aren't good. Sniper Elite 5 just feels like a massive downgrade from Sniper Elite 4, having worse maps, less tactical depth and poorly implemented mechanics. If your looking to get into the Sniper Elite series, go play Sniper elite 4 instead. As a fan of the series since Sniper Elite 3, I'm not impressed with rebellion's latest showing. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: if you liked the other sniper elite games, you will like this one too.there are some aspects of the game that i dont like as much (whats the point of a heightened vertical movement system if you cant climb a small fence?) all around it is a good gamesomething i do love that i have seen people complain about is the new "axis invasion" modebasically think of it as invasions in dark souls gamesyou queue up in this mode and will be placed into a another player's campaign game and you try and hunt them down and kill them before they kill youtagging german soldiers will have the campaign player marked on you map if they see him but other than that you are given no indication as to where the heck they are, which makes for a really cool experience (granted that you know the map well enough to not get instantly lost)the campaign player though is given a near constant reminder of where you are using either the focus mode (by pressing alt) or by using one of the many phones placed around the map. this allows the campaign player to always be one step ahead, as long as they dont alert the german soldiers you have taggedall around a very cool, fun, and rewarding experience as you hunt down your prey, or set traps for your hunter.long story short, all around a good sniping game. some of its new features are a bit poorly implemented, but other new features really add to the experience

_childDocuments_.review: 3 days after launch, 1/3 of the sniper rifles in the game are unobtainable or heavily bugged.K98 is unobtainable, which the devs have said they're investigating since launch but still haven't patched. As for the 2nd, it took literally 4 tries to get the achievement to pop for the french rifle. It's a game literally called SNIPER Elite 5, but since the K98 is bugged, theres only one bolt action in the game thats ideal for very long range. It's a shame. It's basically more of SE4 but with a more generic and familiar ww2 france setting, and a somewhat interesting nazi superweapon plot. Levels are a mix of pretty good, and borderline filler. Overall, level design seems to offer much less in the way of longer range engagements, and offers a lot more winding tunnels and trenches and bunkers. You can either sneak through or run and gun thanks to the far less recoil and far better accuracy of SMG's in this game. The ideal strategy if you actually want to be a SNIPER is to use the M1 Carbine or Gewehr with shorter range sights to one or two shot enemies in firefights. I'd say its not necessarily a downgrade, more like an alternate version of stealth action gameplay compared to SE4. If you like focusing on sniping, se4 is a lot better. If you like stealth and/or firefights with a decent big of sniping on top, se5 is better. I almost wish this game had the SE4 maps, it seems like the perfect combination. Music is overall much worse than SE4. Protip: if you keep crashing or even bluescreening, start up the game launcher, go into the settings, and switch from DirectX to Vulkan. I've only had one crash since I switched.Edit: day 3/4 patch fixed a small number of bugs and crashes. Still no fixes for K98.

It's very unclear what walls you can scale and not, or what rocks and slopes you can walk over, which makes moving around incredibly jarring at times. _childDocuments_.review: It never gets old. I've been playing Sniper Elite since its first installment back on the PS2 and I love the franchise. Is Rebellion becoming more and more a money-grubbing shameless company? Totally! Just got the game on sale and I'm pretty happy with it and with the DLCs I bought, based on reviews. I laughed a lot when I saw a DLC that adds a silenced .22 pistol and it just showed what's wrong with companies these days: they do have a good product and can make millions with it, but they need to milk that cow to near exhaustion before getting their creative team back in the room and work on something new and original and focus on COOP instead of the ridiculous multiplayer. Again, great game with a solid fan base, but most people want to enjoy it solo or with a friend. Last but not least: if you're selling one weapon with a couple of customizable parts and some ridiculous camouflage, it doesn't make it a weapon pack, it makes it a money grubbing scheme. Bottom line, the game is great,

Invasion is a good feature. You don't like it ? Turn it off. I don't get why people are frustrated to get less XP while you are shutting off a feature that puts more challenge and unlocks weap customization. 2. _childDocuments_.review: Ladies and gentlemen, gather 'round as we dive headfirst into the mesmerizing black hole of pointlessness that is Sniper Elite 5. If you've ever wondered what it would be like to play a game that defies every expectation, where boredom is the main attraction, then congratulations, you've stumbled upon gaming's magnum opus of nihilistic irony.Sniper Elite 5's brilliance lies in its ability to take everything you've come to expect from a game and turn it on its head. The game opens with all the enthusiasm of a sloth in a sedative-induced coma, introducing you to Karl Fairburne, the protagonist who probably questions the meaning of life more than you do. His mission? Well, it doesn't really matter, because nothing in this game does.The gameplay is a masterpiece of absurdity. It revolves around the concept of hiding behind cover, waiting for enemies who seem just as clueless about their existence as you are about yours, and then engaging in a slow-motion ballet of monotony as you line up your shots. Each kill is punctuated by an X-ray kill cam, which serves as a stark reminder of the sheer absurdity of it all. It's as if the game is saying, "Look at this! Isn't it ridiculous?"The AI, or lack thereof, is a work of art in itself. Enemies saunter around like they're on a leisurely stroll through a warzone, and they hardly react when their comrades mysteriously drop dead around them. It's almost as if they've given up on life, just like you while playing this game.As for the story, it's a narrative rollercoaster that somehow manages to go in a straight line. Characters deliver their lines with all the enthusiasm of someone reading the phone book. You'll find yourself chuckling at the sheer absurdity of trying to care about a plot that seems more interested in mocking you than engaging you.Graphically, Sniper Elite 5 pushes the boundaries of mediocrity. The environments are as exciting as watching paint dry, which, ironically, might actually be more engaging. Character models look like they were rendered by a bored intern, and the animations are so stiff that you'll wonder if everyone in this game is secretly made of cardboard.Sound design is another exercise in ironic indifference. The soundtrack seems to be on a never-ending loop of monotony, while the voice acting delivers lines with all the emotion of a malfunctioning robot. It's as if the game is laughing at you for even bothering to listen.In conclusion, Sniper Elite 5 is a nihilistic and ironic masterpiece of tedium. It revels in its own absurdity, inviting you to join in on the joke. If you're in the mood for a game that not only embraces boredom but turns it into an art form, then Sniper Elite 5 is your ticket to a hilariously pointless gaming experience. Just remember, in the grand scheme of things, nothing really matters, and neither does this game. Enjoy! Or don't. It doesn't matter, anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: ***Another update*** I wont be buying the new season pass. Most of the issues bellow haven't changed. Rebellion have killed the SE franchise for me. This is now a dip in game for me at best. ***After playing several hundred hours on this game, as wells after several  40-50gb updates, I stand by my original overall opinion. This is one of the worse coded games I've ever played, and they had the cheek to declare it GOLD before release. It has lots of potential, however as it stands now i would only just pass as a beta version.- Invisible walls all over the map. and Ironically, places where you can shoot through walls and tanks etc. - Inconsistant landscapes ie: you can jump over railings in certain maps and not in others, even tho they appear to be the same type/height etc. Same with shooting through wood. - Glitches galore including Mines don't go off or go off without making a sound. Or they go off when you are no where near them.  Enemy snipers and tanks track you through walls. - Grenades don't throw properly. They will randomly end up anywhere but where you throw them. - Wind and Bullet drop are a joke. - Melee system is retarded. You cant melee from the front unless you have a bayonet, and you can melee people before they are even anywhere near you. - Survival is far too easy even on Authentic. Abundance of supplies, gormless enemies, highlighting enemies when you get 5 left. white boxes and exclamation marks appearing over their head so you know where they are. - Ridiculous features such as Focus - basically a built in wall hack. At least give us the option to turn it off in multiplayer. - No dedicated servers leading to toxic noobs who will kick you for shooting them.- Annonymous votes so people will just keep spamming the vote button with no accountability. Lots of potential. There are some good ideas in the game but Overall a let down over the previous SE series and has clearly been dumbed down for the next generation of gamers. Ive paid for it now so i will keep playing it but don't buy it unless it is on sale. ***A massive let down. SE4 is basically all I play so I was looking forward to SE5. I don't mind bugs in this stage of release. It is to be expected (however how thoroughly was it tested given that bugs appear in the first few minutes)Graphically it is excellent. I like the weapon customisation feature. Shoulder aim has been eliminated and there are different aim options. But that's where the good ends. As well as small but very annoying features being removed, this is basically a watered down, overly simplified SE game clearly aimed at the younger generation. The Sniper Elite veterans have been forgotten.- Movement and interaction feels clunky and not smooth and fast like SE4. Almost like everything is microscopically slowed down. - Authentic mode is a joke. Enemies are highlighted (on survival), You get red exclamation marks over enemies in campaign so you can then see them.  No wind until later missions in campaign (why?! just why?!)   If i wanted an easy game I would choose an easier mode. Bring back the standard of Authentic plus in SE4!!!- They have removed unlimited stones (which in reality would be readily available) and replaced it with limited supply of glass bottles! How bizzare and random is that! Why would a sniper carry bulky bottles that clunk around rather than using stones? An idiotically bizzare feature.  - Multiplayer movement and game play looks and feels like fortnight, its lost the speed and atmosphere of SE4. - Also they removed the option to see the game rules, ie: when you enter a server to see what they have turned on or off. Useful feature that is no longer there. Overall, despite the excellent graphics, this game is just feeling dull and lifeless compared to the others.I don't mind the fact that many people say its a copy of SE4. That would have been excellent. In fact I would have welcomed new SE4 maps rather than this SE5. And its not nostalgia, I was ready for a whole new challenge. This has been a major let down. Especially for the cost. I hope further updates change some of these features.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. Pretty fun, but also sometimes pretty ♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. Sniper Elite? More like Silenced Pistol Elite. Like bruh. Anytime you fire a rifle, or even anything other than the silenced 1911 enemies will swarm you, and not just a few, legitimately about 50 all at once. Another thing to note - Why are SMG's completely useless outside of 2.3 centimeters away? the recoil / accuracy is completely out of control. You cannot hit a thing unless you shoot one tap at a time. Also why can you hit an enemy straight through the heart 3 times and they just flinch and move on like it was nothing? This has been a problem in the last 2 sniper elite games as well but it definietyl still happens here too. Next gripe - the maps are so big that it's completely overwhelming in my opinion. I enjoy branching paths, and different options for stealth, but the maps are so large it almost feels like a chore. Think of a hit man level but 3x as big. Of course this is my opinion, but I preferred the map design on sniper elite 4 much better.Another thing - Enemies will legit spawn near you after you clear an area, and the WILL kill you. So basically - not enough "sniping" sidearms are almost completely useless outside of headshots or pointblank, gigantic overwhelming maps. and in a lot of ways this is a re hash of the same game we've played since sniper elite 3 and 4.  Even with my complaints, I do think this is a great game. and I had a fun time with it. I finished in about 9 hours. While it was frustrating at times, the exploration is vast and you might need to play a few times through to see everything in a certain level -This is more of a splinter cell meets ww2 type of game, and less of a sniper game. If that's what you are looking for though, I think you will love this. Oh, also the graphics are quite good.  Might replay in a year or two.Cheers

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of the series and sniper / stealth games in general. However the last one was a little bit on the clunky side. SE5 however is absolutely fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 5 offers expansive maps and diverse environments, maintaining the series' signature sniping mechanics. However, the AI of enemy soldiers feels lacking, diminishing the challenge and immersion. Basically, you can kill half a squad and after a while the enemy will continue to go back to their daily tasks while standing in a literal killing field. Despite the vast landscapes, I often find myself engaged in close-quarter combat; while this is necessary, its detracts just a little from the core experience of long-range sniping. While the game delivers decent and satisfying shooting mechanics, the discrepancy between the expansive maps and the frequent close-range encounters detracts from the depth expected from a Sniper Elite title. It's a good bit of shooting fun. but it's nothing taxing.

_childDocuments_.review: Soooo, Sniper Elite 5.Steam says I have played 30 hours. But it does not count first two or three missions, because I started playing them while in Microsoft Game Pass, that is add about 10 hours more. And that'll be time required to play the base game from start through the end (9 missions, actually 9th is very short), while in general one mission took me 4-5 hours o complete. Yes, I know, it is long time, but I like to explore everything and find what is there to find.So what's new since Sniper Elite 4?Workbenches in every map (3 per map), where you can unlock/modify your weapons while in mission.Various weapons (usually slightly better in first missions) lying around to pick up and use while they has ammo. That is modified general weapons you can unlock by progressing thtough the game - silenced versions, stronger versions or with larger magazines etc. Plus there are weapons falling from every dead enemy, you can pick these weapons and use while they has ammo, or simply take ammo from them (need to unlock certain skill for that)."Parkour". Yes, some climbing elements from Tomb Raider - ledges, ladders, vines, sliding down the slopes, ziplines. Interesting, useful.I'm not sure if it is new since 4th game, but there are crowbars and bolt cutters in every map as well as locked doors, crates, walled with planks holes that needs these tools to open new paths.Also the game still has safes with secret materials or secondary objectives. Safes can be opened with found keys or explosives.As 4th game it has beautiful graphics and sound, retain hiding in tall grass, sound mask options where player can create them by himself where applicable or use those in the world (fight sounds, plane sounds etc)One little personal disappointment I have to notice. Even with most difficult custom setting set to lowest amount of ammo found/dropped, there are still plenty of ammo to use. One minor bug I found where killed vehicles retained working engine sounds. And that is it from negative things.In summary, if you liked 4th game, you'll also like the 5th one. Plus there are additional DLC missions, weapons and skins to unlock.Oh, and now you can slow down or fast forward the flying bullet scene, I think it is also new feature.So yeah, thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a 4/5. I really enjoyed the realism of SE 4. The Sniper Elite series seems to strive for authenticity. It's hardest mode is called "Authentic", and honestly I'll be damned if it's not the most authentic shooter experience in a game I've had; wind/bullet drop, smart AI etc. But there are basic flaws in the game that make the authentic mode inauthentic and a lot harder, it's terribly frustrating to be killed be inauthenticities when that's the whole point.1. When searching an enemy for loot, lives enemies can come upon you and shoot and it takes way too long for our character to disengage searching and engage in fighting. 2. Can't shoot all lights out in SE 5. In SE4 not only could you shoot out basically every light to provide cover of darkness, you could through rocks and do it silently. That was SO COOL.3. Authentic provides no indication of health, but wouldn't we have some idea how close we were to death if we'd been shot? I guess it's all out the window since we can continuously patch ourselves with bandages and med kits but still. 4. Melee should be instant kill. We are a super elite bad ass, and yet some of these German foot soldiers can block us again and again and again. One soldier I even shot first, then tried to melee, and he was still able to block me indefinitely. C'mon. Still love the game. Recommend.

_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to write a new review after I got a new laptop (Acer Nitro 5) which allows me to play the game with the highest settings. It's clear that the better visual details are not just eye candy but also improve the overall gameplay experience.Also I now have played more than 100 hours of the game, so I felt I have new things to say about the game.A disclaimer: I love the previous Sniper Elite 4 and I've played it a lot.I was a bit annoyed in the beginning that Sniper Elite 5 changed a lot of things including most of the action keys for example. So you have to re-learn many things that you took for granted in SE4.It took me quite a while to get used to SE5 because of these changes specifically.Also, while the first mission is good, it's not a great mission to open the game with because it takes place at night and it adds an unnecessary level of difficulty when you're already struggling with so many new concepts in the game.So if you find the first mission frustrating, don't lose hope ;)It's clear they tried to make the game more grounded in reality, so for example you don't have an infinite number of satchel charges but instead you have to find each one in order to use it. Also you have to press a button to collect an item, not just bump into it. And you can't destroy every vehicle with a single shot except when they carry explosives. The enemies can activate alarms to call reinforcements which only makes sense. I like these changes.It's also clear they put a lot of effort into improving the existing UI. For example, I love the larger permanent crosshair in the middle of the screen and now I really miss it when I go back to play SE4.I have to say, the more I play SE5, the more I like it.It takes a while to get used to the new game mechanics and the new action keys but I like them better.Some people complained there's far less sniping in this game and much more stealth. I don't think so. It may seem so at first but as I was replaying the missions again and again, I discovered many opportunities for sniping when you take the time and explore the environment.So overall, despite some initial frustration, I grew really fond of this game over time and now I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by saying that I love this game. I have played and replayed both release 4 and 5 many times, admiring the gorgeous scenery, the diversity and freedom in planning out your levels and the weapon options. I also specifically LOVE playing the Jäger in invasion mode. There is that special 'je ne sais quois' about hunting real players, especially when it's a duo.But the sharp reader will not have missed this being in sharp contrast to my present opinion of this title. Now, I've purchased SE4 with all the trimmings. No complaint there. I purchased SE5 with almost all content... bar the 'Season Pass 2' expansion because, going by all the negativity about it in other reviews, the devs seemed to have put as much work into that expansion as their morning bowel movement after a gallon of coffee.So, just keep playing the rest of the game, right? Well.... not only does the game still crash to desktop like it has always done, they will now minimize my game on EVERY start-up to show me a webpage informing me that I have yet to purchase said expansion. Sorry guys, but I'm saving that money for other, more useful purposes, like assisting a local crowdfund to support my neighbour's cat getting trans surgery. But to add insult to injury, Invasion mode will also proceed to MATCH ME WITH PEOPLE PLAYING THAT SPECIFIC DLC AND THEN KICKING ME OUT AGAIN STATING THAT I'M MISSING THAT PARTICULAR DLC IN MY COLLECTION. Seriously? From a programming perspective, this is so hard to ♥♥♥♥ up that I cannot but conclude they are doing this on purpose. So, currently, I'm entertaining the following possibilities:- the rebellion team have hit their head on a sharp toilet bowl edge after a night of binging- the team has collectively contracted a brain-eating bacteria- they were secretly bought by EA or Ubisoft- all of the aboveSo in short, dear people of Rebellion:Get your face out of the toilet, sober up, get your heads checked and then have a good long think about your life's choices. Contrary to what some game companies think, making a product that sucks hard doesn't magically create a vacuum that pulls the money from our pockets if you market it enough. Be the honest and game-loving development company we all want you to be. Fix your DLC, fix your season pass and stop shoving it in my face until you do.- edit -The game, when playing invasion mode, is STILL matching me with people playing a map I do not own. This is downright idiotic and would be so easy to fix... this is just them pressuring me into buying it (hint: I won't, not this way).

_childDocuments_.review: Still good but not so much of a sniper. I'll try to keep it short as nobody likes lectures. Love the maps, really extended, with plenty of corners to explore, great addition of the different starting points once you unlock them. Great graphics, hats off to the artists as usual. Really liked roaming the old buildings, forts, castles and so. Workbenches - very good concept - you can tweak your weapons according to your play style. Invasion was pretty much good at start but the continuous tweaking / nerfing is not so good. Now apart from the bugs, which am not gonna pretend doesn't exist, but am sure will be fixed (most of them been fixed at this time I'm writing), my biggest no-no of the game is the kinda lack of sniping, if I may say so. In most maps you really no need to snipe / use the rifle. Long story short SE5 is indeed a 5. Yup there are only 5 mandatory snipes in the whole main game. Snipe 1 & 2 - the 2 search lights at the start of the game Snipe 3 - not really mandatory but a must for any elite sniper bio, the almost 2k m long shot in Spy Academy Snipe 4 - end of Rubble and Ruins Snipe 5 - Möller - you are locked on a stamp size location with no option to whack the mole other than by rifle. The second no-no is the difficulty - all, including Authentic, is easier than Sniper Elite 4. We really need some higher difficulty like A++. Other than that, hoping that more mp and survival maps gonna be added, I enjoyed playing the game. I can still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game. It is beautiful and the sniping is fun, but there are a lot of "buts"* The game feels very arcadey, meaning it have tons of invisible walls, small rocks and hedges that you just cannot pass. It feels far less open world than SE4. You are very much stuck to one or two paths.* The fluffing ladders from SE4 is still in. You just automatically grab a ladder when you don't want it and you can never climb one when you want to.* Very often you have to stand up to pick something up and you frequently pick up things you don't want to pick up (at least you don't drop your stuff at random like in SE4).* Even if you kill all the winesses in your vicinity the marker for "last seen location" is still on you and 15 new ai is coming your way. This makes it more of a combat-oriented shooter than a sneaky sniper game.* Very often the notification that you are about to be discovered is never there. From nowhere you are just suddenly shot. It is also a lot harder to discover ai than SE4 (not necessarily bad) and the minimap is very imprecise  - sometimes it looks like ai is extremely close and then you realize they are far away.* Some of the objectives are very unclear and the markers does not help.* SE4 was a better game overall than SE5, but SE5 have very much content (you spend hours on each mission).
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: As the fifth big installment of the Sniper Elite Series, this game does not contain many surprises. As every Sniper Elite has a bit of an identity crisis, this one is no different. The gameplay of Sniper Elite 5 is probably the most hybrid third person shooter gameplay of the whole series. The sniper rifle is still a trusted tool (also the only weapon with optional aim assist) but submachine gun and pistol work almost equally well - and I like that. I like variety in my shooter gameplay and this game gives me enough choices to fill that want. The levels of the campaign are beautifully crafted and offer very different combat arenas/sandboxes/sneaking challenges. I've read the critique that many maps don't offer that long shooting distances as in previous installments and while that is certainly true, I don't think it takes away much. You're still able to fight at ranges of 100-200 meters very often and it isnt like you would hit much beyond that without the aim assist. The story is nothing to write home about but that is also not the point of the game. It is written well enough to justify the mission sandboxes you're getting dropped into and for me that is very much sufficient. Also, the invasion mode: Before buying the game, I apparently dodged all the announcements about this gamemode and was pleasantly surprised upon discovering it. In this gamemode, you can join the campaign games of other players. You play as an enemy sniper and have to stop the other player. A simple concept that makes each mission way more thrilling for me. I absolutely love getting invaded in a mission and suddenly having to adapt to the new circumstances, because NOW I am facing not only the AI but also a human player that can do almost everything I can do - and can also kill me in one shot. It is really something else and even if you get killed by an invader, you don't really lose progress. You can still save. And you can turn it off. You can turn the invasion mode completely off and be done with it. I don't get the negative reviews where the major critique is this gamemode. Just turn it off. You can also kick an invading player from your game session since you are the host (yes, really. I also don't get why you can do this).

_childDocuments_.review: It's been pretty obvious that Rebellion has been on a cash grab spree since Sniper Elite 4 was released, but this truly takes the cake as the magnum opus to their greed. I went in with hardly any expectations, and would've been less disappointed if they went with another reskin of a previous game. There are many issues I have with the game, but the worst offenders are as follows:- Overpriced DLC for very little content that is still locked behind silly requirements- Lazily tacked on features and game modes that are unbalanced and generally unfun (mainly Invasion) to supplement very little base game content- Braindead easy to predict AI even on the hardest difficulties- Unsatifying "loud" gameplay with most secondary weapons feeling very samey-  "Open World" maps with very bizarre and nonsensical invisible wallsThere are many more issues, but much like Rebellion, I would rather not put more effort into this than necessary. The game looks and feels much less complete than it's predecessors and is a testament to how far Rebellion has fallen as a company, as it seems to be much more of a cash grab than a genuine attempt at a game. I can only hope that the game gets much more base game content and has many of it's issues fixed within the coming months, but as Rebellion seems to be a lot more interested in adding more and more overpriced DLC, such as a $15 DLC for a whopping two guns and a weapon skin that's uglier than cat barf, I sincerely doubt it will happen any time soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Loses a lot of its knack very quickly. The Kill Cams are so unsatisfying. Also wish dismemberment was a thing. Shot someone in the head with a anti-tank rifle and the kill cam showed a bullet the size of a 9mm and it barely did anything to the guy. Big maps are a plus and I didn't notice too much repetition with the missions.Stealth system doesn't feel to great. I feel almost like im playing a COD game. They rarely give you an opportunity to shoot someone from over 100 meters. I found myself never even changing my zeroing because of how almost all engagements were close range.Another feature i'm not a fan of is the enemy spotting system. Say you shoot someone in the head and it hits the helmet, If you get a follow up shot and it kills him within a second or two everyone in the vicinity will know exactly where you were even when you are suppressed simply because that one guy by himself saw you for about a milisecond.PvP Can be fun when it works. Most times the Host will die before you even get close. Or they disconnect you not sure how that works but that happens quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Many other reviews share pretty much all of my problems: too much emphasis on CQC, lots of small ledges you can't walk over, level design is just generally lacking, there are only 6 rifles, 6 SMGs, and 6 pistols (but don't worry, there are already 2 weapon packs announced coming as DLC!), the weapon customization is bland, boring, and nonsensical, lots of bugs (can vault through the map, collectibles that can't be collected, problems with the AI etc.), coupled with day one DLC and a Season Pass One (implying more), mark this as a purchase not worth making.EDIT: I've been playing a bit more, and OH MY GOD are there so many bugs. _childDocuments_.review: What I write for this review is the experience I had with the game, everybody will experience things differently. This is my honest review if you don't like it well tough. Also no game is safe from a review whether its early access or full release now onto the review.Sniper Elite 5 is a great sniping video game. You playing as the famous Karl Fairburne in finding out a secret German nazi weapon in 1944. This game is absolutely amazing-ish. The campaign is pretty slandered from the other Sniper Elite games. Find a main nazi bad guy, snipe them & done. You can pick different difficulties from I link lowest is civilian to authentic but they now added more customization options to suit a players comfort when playing. Graphics looks amazing even on the lowest setting possible it just amazing. There wasn't a lot wrong with the graphics except for when you join in on other players missions you sometimes will have bad graphic quality for a few seconds. Weapon sounds were okay but if I am being 100% honest they all sounded the same to me except the anti-tank rife. I am not sure its just my bad hearing or I wasn't paying enough attention to the weapon sounds but they just sounded the same to me. The rifles sounded the same to each other, the SMGs founded the same to each other & the pistols as well.Game-play was okay, movement wasn't bad except for the auto cover messing a few things up. Aim movement was actually okay for my default, normally I have to adjust it higher but this was okay. Another thing I had an issue was the buttons being the same for so many different things. Throwing stuff sometimes bugged out to where Karl would just be stuck in the throw animation for a long time. There was the re-load loop issue where you select an ammo type & Karl would just infinitely reload the weapon until you re-select another ammo type. Weapons were okay but I didn't like how they were locked through challenges or finding workbenches. Skill leveling would have been nice to do for the weapons & attachments should have been challenges (& some are). Attachments are good I guess, I didn't see any issue with them except for the pistol scopes & the pistol suppressors not showing on the gun sometimes. Axsi Invasions is where a player is an enemy sniper trying to kill you or your partners if your in a joined match. I turned this feature off in my game but some players I joined has this on & I don't think its a bad idea since it gives a slight more exp reward. The only issue I had was helping a player in his mission & we defeated an invader (damn sounds like Elden Ring & Dark Souls over here) 5/6 times. I would like to see a system where you defeat an invader you can't get invaded again until the next mission. Survival is how it sounds, you survive waves of nazi's. I can't remember is this was in Sniper Elite 3 but I know it was in Sniper Elite 4. Multiplayer is blank for me meaning I don't know how it is due to never trying it. I my first SE multiplayer was in SE4 & first game there was a hacker which put off multiplayer for SE forever.Accessories were okay, there were some changes from SE4 to SE5 like no trip wires anymore. The only issue I had with the accessories was the satchel charges unlock requirements were never explained better. It only said complete the campaign to unlock which I did on the easiest difficulty & never unlocked them come to find out it has to be hardest (authentic) difficulty to unlock them since I did easiest to hard & still didn't unlock the satchel charges.  With all said & done I felt SE5 is nothing new really. Its just the same the previous games. Only thing new (from what I can tell) is the Axi Invasions & thats it. The DLC is the ame & the campaign is just repeat. I would love see Rebellion take a bold move & try something else like a different time era. Don't get me wrong Rebellion does amazing work I think better then Underdog Studio. So Sniper Elite 5 gets 5/10 score from me making just average but I still recommend buying this game also the other Sniper Elite games as well.That's the Pony review for Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: Within the first few hours, I noticed that the AI is weak/flawed along with sub-par graphics. The main issue with AI is that 90% of the time when a grenade is thrown near one or more NPCs, they'll cower where they are and die. They could be standing, walking, running or in a truck. The search pattern the AI uses is questionable as the NPCs will only go so far while when here a noise. Half of the time when I whistle and I'm close, they don't hear me..sometimes they do but they go in a different direction than towards me.The graphics are fine but I've seen better. My PC has run many AAA games at max settings with no problem with Ray-tracing/DLSS but this game mimics them to a far lesser extend.  The serious weakness with the map is that they don't allow true freedom to roam. There are artificial walls and scrubs that force you down predetermined paths which I hate! The story feels good and the UI is easy to understand.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, but, significant caveats and/or warnings:#1 - This isn't about sniping much of the time. Thus far, most kills are probably under 100m, and a large number are even under 50m. Scoped rifles almost seem like a liability in some missions... the first mission, rounding corners constantly and going through narrow bunkers, I used a Thompson and a MG-42 most of the mission. Soooo.... more like SMG-Elite 5, especially compared to the previous game, SE 4, where a number of missions did have larger open areas to snipe from.#2 - I read reviews about invisible walls, but that's not really it. The problem is the clipping is wildly chaotic. Sometimes, I can walk right up to a hedge... other times, I'm colliding with it despite the graphics showing another 6-8 feet of space before I should be touching it at all. This makes sniping over hedges and low walls a pain. Not so much an issue of navigation (mini-map tells you basically what can be moved across), but more an issue of sloppy clipping design around some areas of terrain.#3 - Invasions aren't my thing. Played with them off the whole time so far, so one of the major changes of the game I am not even really experiencing. I don't want to play MP, so, that's a change that is lost on me I guess.#4 - Movement feels worse than SE 4. I'm either running too fast, walking to slow, or crouch-walking about right. Karl will just freak out at full speed trying to find the angle to open a door sometimes, so hitting the Z key to walk or Ctrl to crouch is how I slow down when I need to, but it's too slow for advancing forward all that far. Speed of movement is a little off.Overall, though, it's a fun game if you approach it as a combo of Wolfenstein and Hitman. It feels a lot like another universe where Wolfenstein is less dark and Hitman is less stealthy. I really enjoy blasting away with the SMGs and throwing grenades and using traps... but I'm not sure that's what players were expecting, especially since SE 4 had much more open maps. SE 5 still has those sniping mechanics, but after a fun little practice with the 1,000 meter target in the training area, I've since been making most shots, often with SMGs, at a distance under 100m, which is a bit odd. But that's how the map design pushes the player to play. Even the DLC maps sometimes feel not that open, with buildings and corners to clear more often than large open horizons.Again, really fun, but not that much sniping despite the name.

Story is whatever, its nothing special or memorable, but it does the job.Fun game, but the DLC prices are obscene imo.

_childDocuments_.review: The Sniper Elite series continues to improve over time. Not all the maps offer the same level of detail as the best ones, but Sniper Elite 5 is a great example of "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" while at the same time having more stuff to do than its predecessor.I don't care much for the non-lethal options (we are killing Nazis after all, so why bother knocking them out?) but I appreciate that the option is there for anyone who wishes to use it. Otherwise, we can still happily dispose of Hitler with a well placed nutshot, and that alone is well worth the price of entry for me.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/4 of the game is not functional. The multiplayer part is almost non existent. You can't connect to other people.The support for the game is non existent.The official support page replies with automatic messages and nothing happens.The official discord is useless since nobody replies to your issues.If you want a nice game with just 9 missions for 50 EUR then you got a good deal.For me the game is just too sort for this amount of money.Without the multiplayer part this game has about 50 hours of game play.If you have plans to play this game with your friends go find another game because this is not for you.Pro: -it can be played with any stile, stealth or guns blazing or any combination.-has plenty of multiplayer game modes to keep you busy WHEN multiplayer worksCon: -plenty of glitches and bugs (bodies clipping through the map visible to enemies but cannot be grabbed by the player, falling through the map in various places, bullets hitting invisible walls/weapon shooting blanks, enemies spotting player through boxes when they should not, getting combat prompt while knocking out enemies from behind or from behind a wall causing the score modify, etc.)-technical support is non existent (no answer to tickets after more than a week besides one automatic reply)Edit:After months still no answer to the ticket.Multiple requests about this issue over discord where me and my friends offered various data requested remain unanswered.The error 12011 (regarding poor connection) is still the issue and no multiplayer sessions are possible even though we were able to play for a week before the error started showing up.Me and my friends found some temporary fixes with flushing DNS and resetting internet connections but this is not something anyone should do.The game just doesn't manage connections well.Without the multiplayer section this game has no future.I feel I did not get my money's worth of this game.This is the only reason i kept asking for a fix.Signed,an angry customer

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't breaking any new Sniper Elite ground, and I'm totally here for it. The 'sniper porn' is still gloriously graphic, the gunplay is what you'd expect from a game from this series. I'm really enjoying it. That said, unless you're a big fan of the series I'd maybe wait for a sale. It's not really innovating or moving forward, and SE4 and even SE3 were equally as satisfying and entertaining. Also, find a friend for the co-op! The co-op campaign is really where this game shines.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 5 is a meaningful improvement over past games, with far better stealth systems and more set-piece focused map design. While the range of engagement has been reduced, there are a handful of good opportunities in each level to engage in extremely long range shoot-outs, which are unsurprisingly the highlight of the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: For a sniping game, there are just way too many close quarter encounters. I don't feel like a lone wolf - carefully planning out my routes and taking my shots carefully as I once did from V2 to SE4. Instead I'm joined by my merry band of diversity hire "allies", while I run and gun down brain dead, lifeless A.I.  It's a shame too, because the graphics are stunning but, the game just feels phoned in.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: All in all a large step down from Sniper Elite 4. Even with much larger levels, it manages to feel comparatively lacking in content. Some very good features such as crouch-running were removed as well, which is a bit irksome. You'll find plenty of more detailed complaints in the negative reviews.But that said, it's not all worse. There are still interesting new ideas and features, such as iron sights/scopes for secondaries, a weapon customization system that allows you to tune weapons for specific situations and playstyles, and what was eventually perhaps my favorite, an overhaul of player noise. Low-level noise masking footsteps and suppressed gunshots, and individual noise levels for each gun, forcing you to modify weapons, choose ammo types, and carefully decide when and what weapons you can use for a given situation, and even making the Welrod relevant again for when you need ultra-quiet shots.All in all, I'd say Sniper Elite 5 is 2 steps forward, 3 steps back. A lot of good changes, a handful more negative changes, but overall still a good game, and one I'd still recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Sniper Elite game, If you enjoyed the last few you'll enjoy this. It looks great, it shoots great and the locations are great. I have a few small ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that I'll address and those are the character movement feels a little rough. Didn't feel particularly smooth moving player around on controller or m&k.The only other issue i have is with the 'camping' status in Axis Invasion. It's a game about snipers and you kill either player during an axis invasion for camping. In a game about snipers. I understand wanting to keep the game flowing but this seems like a really weird mechanic to have in a game that focuses heavily on sniping. I joined someones game and set up a great position overlooking one entry point into a house in the first mission. Killed me for camping, reloaded then the player themselves got killed for camping because they were scoping around the map from a bunker vantage point. Makes no sense. It's sniping. They camp. There should be an option to switch that off unless i've missed it somewhere??Otherwise though the game is great. It's Sniper Elite so it's great stealth, great shooting and a really enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit torn on this game tbh guys, I don't know if I should be recommending it, but for now I will give it a thumbs up!The graphics are great, the guns and ammo make it a good game, it's ALMOST like an open world, but you are still guided, but this is not a problem in the Sniper Elite games, as you can still get around to most places, it just takes longer as you can't traverse the hills and even in the first level, there are so many places you want to jump over railing and can't, you have to walk the long way around. Trivial I know, but gamers want shortcuts, we want to be able to hide everywhere, shoot out lights (which you can), and creep up on unsuspecting baddies and break their necks (yes, you can) oh yeah and talking of shooting lights, you can't do that in Far Cry 6 and in SE5, the mirrors work too, awesome :)  again in FC6, mirrors do not work; for shame UbiSoft, for shame! :) Ok, so the bad points, let's get them out of the way:The music is crap, or at least on the first level it is, it's nice at first but it's the same loop over and over and over...... Collecting items, especially in a safe is an absolute nightmare if you don;t require the other items (bullets, mines etc), there were two instances where I could not collect the documents because I could not collect the other items, this needs fixing urgently, I must have wasted about 5 minutes at both locations just moving around as slight as I could to get the Y to highlight, well annoying! Lastly, (for now) the AI is crap in most parts, I shot soldiers next to other soldiers and they never responded, I had a guy tonight who was looking right at me and never saw me, well, until I shot him in the leg, then his marker went yellow, yes yellow, not RED, but chuffing yellow, even though I was stood right in front of him and I shot him  -wth???Anyway, that's all for now, I'm only 8 hours in so I'll update this as I find good and bad in the game :) If you're going to buy it, do like I did and get it on sale, then it's not too bad if the AI are idiots :)I've finished the game, I think this will be the last one I buy tbh! We need the world to be more like an open world, where we can climb and jump walls, too many times I try to jump a fence and it won't let me, it's painful tbh! Oh yeah, the music is crap, even in the DLC , it's terrible!

_childDocuments_.review: Eonymia suggestion to use the Vulkan engine instead of DirectX seem a solid resolution to solve the constant crashing under DirectX. So, if you are also experiencing often crashes, try switching to the Vulkan engine. I have now played the game for 25 hours and now the game seems stable I actually got to enjoy the game. I like the Axis invasion element where basically a multi-player enemy is inserted into your solo campaign.The chevron (^) arrow makes it easier to pickup the element you want. I did had some issues pickup letters or elements when I was taking a knee, not to protest some social injustice, but to silently move unseen and unheard to the area. However some items a very hard to pickup that way. Often I have to actually stand erect to pickup the item. Most secondary actions like carry you're victims to a hiding spot, requires you to hold the 'c' key for a second. The 'e' key to kill or pickup items is instantly. When you have enhanced yourself you become finger fast in searching bodies when you perform a melee style attach. But some reason when you shoot a enemy and than search it, it takes forever to complete the search. In my opinion this is a bug because the time it takes to search a body for items should be determined based on the attach style. The environment is very beautifully created and the typical French small urban street style requires a lot of close combat. The eagles are still in the game, but are much better hidden, but in order to improve from weapon arsenal you need to also find the workbenches in each level as they unlock options.I also love the kill list element where you have to eliminate a specific bad actor. So far, I have not participated in online multiplayer part of the game other than that some other multiplayer has joined my solo mission in the form of the axis challenge. Once I have completed my first run of the solo missions, I'll checkout other axis- and multiplayer options...

_childDocuments_.review: Another great addition to the Sniper Elite franchise with some great new additions, including ballistics that aren't highly unrealistic (like in SE4). The most exciting addition is the Axis Invasion mode, which works mostly like invasions in the Dark Souls franchise. It makes for exciting and tense gameplay moments - I would advise leaving it off for your first playthrough, however. There are some significant bugs to work out, but I trust that Rebellion will be working on those in the coming weeks. In a month or two, this game will be in prime shape, but even as it is, I would highly recommend this game for anyone who likes slow and methodical shooters with sniping elements.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Sniper Elite Series you'll love this game. I have played 2,3,4. I love 4 it is really relaxing and no timed elements which I really hate. This allows me to explore the surrounds for the hidden eagles. The weapons menu is designed to be basic and authentic so that you can spend more time playing the game. I did prefer the x-ray cam better on Sniper Elite 4.  The soldiers are more aggressive in this game and come after you very quickly compared to number 4. A few draw backs is the clunky sniper rifle movement on the joystick which I am still fiddling around with in the settings. I was hoping that there might be a little bit more of an effort to make the enemy snipers more competitive and have secrets or bonus items on them. This game does not have the different variety of mines as version 4 also the map could be a little more detailed in where items are located. but I absolultely love this version since starting to play it. Yes  would recommend it and Rebellion have stuck to their traditional design and layout of the play and the simplification makes the game so great!

_childDocuments_.review: So for starters, yes the game is fun and lot more with co-op with a friend.However, the game is clunky, interacting with objects is not good/very finicky. There is an invisible wall in the DLC which you get stuck into and you have to panic run around until you find the right path to get out. The co-op disconnects a lot. A lot of items don't unlock after completing game-specific milestones/achievements; mainly the satchel charge item.The biggest complaint I'm seeing with the game is the XP drop when you turn off invades which I haven't encountered yet. I got all the skill points maxed out.Overall it is fun but there is some fine-tuning that needs to be done and until that is fixed I can't in good faith recommend this even though I am a huge fan of the series. This one feels a rather rushed clone of an MGS game since half the game is close encounters and not a sniper elite game similar to 3 & 4.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 5 plays really well on my PC.  The scenery is beautiful and the game feels more fluid.  I prefer single-player campaign and have no opinion on the invasion or the multiplayer mode.  Having played this for 4+ hours at the first review time and 24+ hours for the second review, I have overall enjoyed the game's smoothness, graphics, and I like the improvements over the previous installments.  The game feels even more modern, but still retains the original Sniper Elite characteristics, such as x-ray cameras, bullet ballistics, difficulty levels, and traditional stealth or loud options with multiple ways to progress through each mission, which makes this an all too familiar game and genre.  I have not encountered any crashes, frame rate issues, or errors.Pros:- Beautiful scenery and graphics- Massive levels with multiple approach and tactics- Different ammo types- Rifle iron sights and first person view for all weapons- X-ray camera for all weaponsCons:- No crouch-and-run mode (this was a great ability in SE 4)- No Shooting Range to practice with weapons and earn medals- Too many invisible walls and inaccessible terrain- No customization for Karl (no different outfits, jackets, etc., which was great in SE 4)- No AP or tripwire mines- Limited distraction objects (SE 4 had unlimited rocks, while SE 5 has limited bottles)Neutral:- Silenced weapons are not truly silent, but this keeps the game interesting.- There is not enough weapons to choose from, and weapon modifications do not make up for this.  SE 4 had more rifles, pistols, and SMG's to select from.Thank you, Rebellion, for delivering such a great game, but some improvements are definitely worth including in SE 5, especially the crouch-and-run option for stealthy approach.  Perhaps, these will arrive in the future updates or DLCs.Current PC Specs:Intel Core i5-9600K, 5.2 GHzEVGA RTX 2060 Super XC Ultra, 8 GBCorsair Vengeance 32 GB RAM, 3200 MHzSamsung 970 EVO NVMe M.2 SSD, 1 TB

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun and I would recommend it to fans of previous Sniper Elite games and also to new players who are fans of games like Splinter Cell (and to some extent Hitman), as they have definitely changed things to be more appealing to a wider audience. While I understand why some people are saying it doesn't feel like a SE game, I would like to clarify that you have many opportunities to climb up to an elevated position and snipe from far distances if you choose, but there is now the option to essentially skip all sniping (except for the last mission) if you would like. I am glad they did this as it is obvious they want to bring in new fans rather than just catering to the core audience from the previous 3 games, which is great for the health of the series in the future. My only real complaint about the gameplay/missions is that there are essentially no "Snipe/Kill this Target" main objectives, although there are "Kill-List" optional targets in every mission so it doesn't bother me too much.I do not understand what people are talking about when they say these maps are not as open/big as SE4. Yes, there are invisible walls/barriers that push you towards one of a few different entrances to certain objectives but it is never just "you must enter from this one point." There are always options on how to approach objectives/areas but I guess if you can't just walk to it from any direction that means it's now more linear (?). The maps are also very big and most have huge open areas with no invisible walls, but I guess having any wall that isnt a cliff like in SE4 is the issue.Another big complaint I keep seeing is complaining about the invasions from players during your campaign. I don't really understand this as you can turn off invasions with no repercussions except that you can't gain the xp from killing invaders. In my opinion I am a big fan of the invasions as I find both hunting a player down as invader and hiding/ambushing the invader to be very fun.The graphics are fine. I don't think they're exceptional or great in anyway but definitely a slight increase from SE4 and definitely not as awful and "dated" as I've seen some others complain about. I haven't played multi-player at all so can't comment, but I will admit that if there is no sniper-focused/sniper only playlist then they definitely need to change that. There is invasion but obviously the core fan-base comes back to these games for the sniping so not having a multi-player focused section for sniping would be a huge misstep by Rebellion.My main complaints would be that I find the weapon options to be very limited and the plot is basically pointless. There are only 2 bolt-action snipers which is immensely disappointing (at least give me a mosin-nagant, I know Russia isn't close to France at this point but who cares) and there are only like 4 or 5 pistols/machine guns for secondaries. You can customize each individual weapon which I really enjoyed but that needs to be built upon further to be truly satisfying. As far as plot goes they just randomly toss in cutscenes of Nazi's complaining about Karl and saying "how can one man do this" alongside your "allies" giving you some intel on the next mission or complaining about something random before disappearing. Just stop with the plots at this point and go back to Karl doing narration between missions, no one would be upset. All in all I think this one is more fun than SE4 due to the replay-ability of invasions and being able to complete missions in different ways, but obviously fans of previous games looking for just sniping gameplay will be slightly dissapointed.7.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of stealthy, tactical shooters, I found Sniper Elite 5 to be a satisfying and engaging experience. The game's emphasis on precision and planning appealed to my strategic side, while the open-ended levels and diverse objectives provided ample opportunities for creativity and experimentation.I particularly enjoyed the game's detailed and immersive environments, which allowed me to feel like a true sniper operating behind enemy lines. The bullet-cam sequences, while gruesome, were undeniably satisfying, adding an extra layer of visceral thrill to each kill.Sniper Elite 5 isn't without its flaws. The AI can be a bit inconsistent, and the game's pacing can feel a bit slow at times. However, these issues are outweighed by the game's strengths, which include its rewarding gameplay loop, engaging story, and stunning visuals.Overall, I would recommend Sniper Elite 5 to fans of stealth shooters and World War II action games. It's a well-crafted and enjoyable title that delivers a satisfying blend of challenge and satisfaction.

_childDocuments_.review: Well now the entire story is out i can say definitively that SE5 is worse is almost every way than 4. Fewer weapons, Worse customisations. Waaaaay too many challenge or gimmick guns. The kill challenges borrowed from hitman are more annoying and harder to get than the ones in 4 and sometimes essential parts are locked behind them. For a game set in France there are only 2, maybe 3 French guns. They even tortuously contrive a reason for Japanese weapons and troops to be in France and do nothing with it. A handful of officers to kill and two guns (three with dlc) from Japan and what did they pick? The Type 100 submachine gun that can't be fitted with a suppressor and the Nambu (the worst production gun of ww2). The DLC adds the Terra rifle some weird low power paratrooper rifle that can only be fitted with  a handful of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ scopes. Woo! I guess the Japanese forgot to bring the Arisaka rifles, the actually decent rifle with real sniper variants. And i guess the germans forgot all their P38s so every officer has a Luger and every soldier has an obscure french pistol. Sorry got on a tear there. Can't swap your gun for enemy guns in the field anymore, no more S-mines or trip-mines. Enemy AI seems somehow smarter and dumber. Better at tactics under fire but brain-dead pathfinding. Every tank in the game is now a King Tiger but don't worry armour-piecing rounds will kill one in three hits from the back. Oh but the driver is now invincible. Look this game is perfectly fine, hell i played it for 89 damn hours. But having played 4 i can't help but see how in basically every way this instalment is inferior. And as far as i can see they stripped out a whole bunch of stuff for no reason, put in a heap of BS that would only appeal to streamers and even with the overpriced dlc still haven't restored the missing content. If you want a Sniper Elite game get 4, its cheaper, longer and better than this. So very disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 4 was an overall wonderful game. The maps had dozens of spots where you can set up a sound mask to conceal your shots, grab some cover and wait for the perfect shot. Despite not being an open world game the maps felt large and full enough to give you a lot of freedom. When I read that Rebellion was bring open world to Sniper Elite 5 I thought this might just be the master piece game of the Sniper Elite series. Instead this open world game is somehow more closed off than it's non-open world counterparts. There are only 1-2 to paths you can take just like in 4. However, they offer much more limited opportunities for sniping. In 4 Rebellion would set up sniper nets with sound masking, long field of views, and multiple enemies visible that could be spotted if you were patient. In short, they encouraged you to play like a sniper move quietly and slowly to a good vantage point. Observe the enemy, conceal your shots, and wait patiently for the perfect shot. In 5 Rebellion will either give you cover or a sound masker almost never both and never a place that offers a good view of multiple enemies at a time with sound masking and cover. Instead, you will be funneled into trenches and buildings where enemies are too far for CQC but in perfect pistol range. Rebellion has replaced the Welrod pistol of the previous games with an overpowered 1911 equipped with a modern style suppressor. The pistol is way overpowered and in the cramped quarters of Sniper Elite 5 is way more useful than the rifle. If you try to play as a sniper and not a pistol toting cowboy the game will become much more difficult. Since the sound masked locations really only give a god view of one or two enemies and little cover you will find yourself taking one shot and running away quickly. Many enemies can’t even be seen from logical sniping locations. So you’ll be forced to fire one shot which will be detected by enemies and runaway from all the return fire. You’ll soon give up on snipping for most of the game as it becomes an exercise in frustration brought on by poor level design. If you are a Sniper Elite fan this game is an easy miss. I wish I missed it and I am sad that I missed the return window hoping that his game would get better. Rest assured it does not.

_childDocuments_.review: This one's a weird kind of "recommend" for me. I've played Sniper Elite since V2 and enjoyed all of them, including 5; however, I feel at this point that the formula is starting to get a bit tired and that Rebellion has nearly exhausted Karl and this franchise as a whole. Basically, if you like Sniper Elite and want more of it, 5 will definitely give you that. If you're expecting much new mechanically or design-wise from it, though, you'll be left wanting.SE5 continues the trends from the previous game with how SE looks, feels, and plays. The spotting, sneaking, and shooting mechanics haven't changed at all outside of the continued reduction of natural soundmasks in favor of suppressed weapons and precisely placed generators just waiting to be sabotaged. The games have leaned into a more Hitman-esque murder-puzzle loop with each entry, and SE5 is the latest there--for better or worse.As has been the case for a while now, half of the arsenal is locked behind DLC paywalls, but there's enough variety in the vanilla arsenal to get you through the game. Although it doesn't matter so much as you won't even recognize half of your guns once you're through customizing them, as SE5 has been infected by the Modern-Warfare-reboots-and-Tarkov-sourced "granular weapon customization" pathogen. I actually enjoy that feature in other games, but in a WWII shooter attempting to brand itself as "authentic" for the whole series--including in its hardest difficulty--it feels odd and against that vision. To be fair, it's not as bad as COD Vanguard, but something about putting a Russian PU scope, shoulder stock, foregrip, and bulky suppressor on a WWII-era M1911 doesn't feel right to me. It's a minor complaint, since that's just how many modern mainstream games are--chase the trends whether it clashes with the identity of your game or not.The story is also pretty mediocre, as you'd expect from Sniper Elite--you're not here for it anyway, and I think Rebellion knows that. There's a short intro and outro to each mission narrated by Karl and/or a British SOE handler of sorts, as well as intro cutscenes featuring the game's "characters"--if you can really call them that. They're only present to provide Karl and the player with the thinnest thread of context for each mission, as well as linking them to the larger war as a whole. I'm impressed they resisted a full-on D-Day mission, to be honest, since this game skips over the week the landings took place. I'm glad Karl got a bit of a break.As a more serious issue, however, Sniper Elite 5 is buggy--and I mean it's infested with them. The detection system frequently bugs out, leaving enemies frozen behind a single piece of cover as they "Investigate" the gunshot they heard. Enemies hear sounds that they shouldn't or don't hear whistles and distraction devices when you're ten feet away. Some enemies will randomly become untagged--as far as I know there's no limit to tags and they're the regular guards as opposed to the trucks that sometimes drive through the map and despawn on the other end. Sometimes dropping a body will send them into the Earth's core, never to be seen again. If you want to guarantee that happening, quicksaves often result in that exact behavior--or them falling through floors or off ledges rather than where you left them. And I promise you will want to use quicksaves, given that SE5's missions are long (my pace of play is admittedly slow and methodical on the Hard difficulty, and I try to complete most if not all of the side objectives, so all in all I'm spending 2-3 hours on each level). If you're not careful you will get set back 20-30 minutes if you decide to reload and forget the all-important F5 key. Surfaces that should be easily shot through, like some leaves on a bush, sometimes aren't when the game randomly decides they're actually those rare rolled-steel bushes the Germans farm all of their tank armor from.While nothing is totally game-breaking, it's a lot of minorly frustrating things that add up; some to the point where I've had to put down the game for a few hours or a day and come back later. Nothing like losing 30 minutes of progress where the game had a dozen opportunities for a fine, safe autosave to get you to take a break for a while.I will admit I didn't touch the multiplayer or the Axis Invasion modes at all. Going through the first time I didn't really want some fanatical sniper spawning in and doming me midway through a mission--if anyone even still plays this game at all--so I turned it off. I remember watching some gameplay years back, and it looked fun and like an interesting twist for those into that sort of disruption, but it wasn't for me and not what I'm playing Sniper Elite to experience. I also tried one round of Survival and found it incredibly tedious. I ended up quitting on Wave 3 when I realized the five waves were going to take almost an hour. I'm sure it's more fun in a group but so is everything so it's not much of a feature-add for me.Regardless though, it's still...fine. The game looks decent even a couple years out, runs well, doesn't crash or hitch outside of a mildly frequent (and more annoying than anything) crash-to-desktop immediately after hitting "Play" in the launcher, and is overall fun despite the shortcomings I mentioned. Would I recommend it to someone looking to get into Sniper Elite? I guess; I'd prefer you tried V2 or 3 first but there's nothing wrong with 4 or 5 besides how tired they feel at this point. It's clear that there's not many places they can or want to push the franchise to, and are risking stretching Karl's continuity to the breaking point. I think a time period change and return to the more sniper-focused gameplay would do this game well--although I imagine Rebellion is very comfortable inside the relatively low-nuance and "safe" setting of WWII. Killing Nazis is only going to make weirdos upset, whereas you might raise some eyebrows with, say, a Vietnam, Gulf War, or GWOT setting--where you don't have the broad cultural consensus of a "just and good war" as you do with WWII.As I said at the top, I softly recommend Sniper Elite 5. It's more "modern" Sniper Elite, so if you liked SE4 you'll absolutely love this since it's more of the exact same. If you liked V2 and 3, you'll probably find it alright. If you're not into Sniper Elite at all...well, your mileage may vary but you'll probably have a decent time.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game. I was a MASSIVE fan of Sniper Elite 4, and despite a few new features, the developers have made one single catastrophic mistake. Bigger doesn't always mean better.What I loved most about Sniper Elite 4 was that the opening level was replayable. Grindy. You could predict where everyone was, complete the level in about 15 minutes when you knew it, and just have some fun... but Sniper Elite 5 has completely lost that.It took almost an hour and a half to complete the first level, the same on the second, the third I got an hour into before I gave up, and (as much as it's a good game), I just don't have time for that. I need a game that I think "hey, I've got an hour spare, I'll play that and snipe some people"... but every level so far, keeping in mind I've tried 3 of the original 9, have been in depth large maps with a LOT of enemies, and this game compared to its predecessor has totally lost what made it "fun". It's become more of a simulator which really doesn't suit it at all.In SE5 they've gone for "Hey, let's make massive maps because everyone is craving huge open worlds" without stopping to think if it actually suited the game, and it doesn't which is a massive shame. Partly because it's made SE5 almost unplayable for me, but mainly because I can see the level of work that they've put in to actually creating these huge levels, and that work has been the reason they've made me go back to Sniper Elite 4 again. A real pity.Would I recommend it? Tough call. I prefered the weapons unlock system in SE4, I preferred the system where suppressors would gradually wear out (which is missing in SE5), and I preferred the smaller levels in SE4.It's not a bad game, but you need to be thinking that you'll be spending at LEAST 90 minutes per level which is something that really doesn't fit in with the genre for me hence the negative review.If you want a couple of hours of intricate luring and stealth killing 100 enemies, you might think the opposite.

But the story feels like it's been recycled from the bargain bin, and the gameplay lacks that "oomph" factor that makes you want to keep coming back for more.  The level design feels a bit uninspired, and the AI can be frustratingly predictable at times. Overall, it's a middle-of-the-road experience that might scratch your itch for stealth action, but don't expect it to leave a lasting impression. It's not a bad game by any means, but it doesn't quite reach the heights of its predecessors. If you're a fan of the series, you'll probably enjoy it enough to give it a go, but don't expect anything groundbreaking here. Overall, it's just... meh.

_childDocuments_.review: TL; DR: I would not recommend buying this game to anyone. Not in this state, not with this price. It is priced as AAA game, but it is AAA game only in glitches and bugs. First, graphics. You would expect at least cutscenes to be believable. But we get plastic dolls, with unbelievable movement and awful shadowing. During game you wont feel it that much, as it runs quite smoothly. The assets though feel like from indy game, with either no clipping, or blocking your movement randomly.Thats comes to second part, mapping and traversing. They have some wall traversing, but only in specific palces, and only if they allow you to. Most simple shrubs are blocking your way. The map is big, but you get only few chokepoints to move between areas, making it realy annoying when you have to run by the "wall" looking for some entrance, when you objective is somewhere behind it. You can see it, but you cant shoot or get close to it, due to invisible wall, called hedge.That comes to third part, invasions. If you are invader, you feel practically god. It is so badly balanced, that you want to cry for the person you invaded. Playing invader feels toxic most of the time, how easy it is to find and kill the guy. He needs to do a lot of preparations and wait for you in some sort of chokepoint, to catch you. And then, he might get kicked for camping. While you have all the time in the world, using all npcs to your advantage as additional scouts. You know where he is most of the time, unless he is so good, that he does not trigger anything. But thats hard, cause the AI is glichy and dumb. They can be stuck underground and trigger your presence. But of course, you can allways kick the invader. Wtf with that? You can spend good 15 min looking for the guy, and then he kicks you. I could not believe it myself untill I tried on my campaign. Guy joins, you kick him, and continue with you quests like nothing happened.That comes to fourth part, AI. Omg you would expect some sort of clever behavior form stealth/ranged combat AI. It is just not here. Its way easier to just trigger alarm, and shoot guys running at you from the chokepoint. _childDocuments_.review: The game is boring but invasion mode is awesome.     This game's story takes itself too serious and the gameplay is lacking. There are very little good sniping positions, sight lines, and sniper possibilities. It has specific positions which encourage sniping by providing an obvious vantage point and scoped rifles......OVERLOOKING TRASH and like 5 AI. Because of the "realistic map design," the game forces you into their bad stealth.....CLOSE RANGE combat, in a SNIPING GAME, because the maps are near claustrophobic. A few maps are a bit more open and include a few open fields with bushes at every angle blocking your views. To top it all off, DLC suck as of the time of this review...so I either didn't buy them or returned them.     The new DLC maps they added have the same problem as all the base game maps with much of it being indoors or narrow tunnels. And the gun and skin packs are just a waste of money for dumb looking skins and useless weaker reused guns from the other games which you need to unlock the attachments for through challenges.     The invasion mode however, is golden. The only reason I would recommend buying this game is if you're interested in hunting down players. The invasion mode is the only thing I play on this game anymore. Using your map knowledge to track down the Allied sniper with the AI's locations, the completed objectives, and the sound cues which the sniper might cause is extremely fun and satisfying. Then once you find them you get to land the classic Sniper Elite cinematic X-Ray kill or get into a sniper battle with you flanking to a new position. It's thrilling.... but has some flaws. Many games end with the Allied sniper getting killed by the AI before you get close and ending the match as a victory (witch doesn't count as a kill for you in order to unlock items) or, they finish the level as soon as you spawn. The Victories and losses aren't tracked at all actually; only your direct kills on the sniper are counted and tracked. But you get nothing past the 100 ghillie suit other than a number going up. Even still, the invasion mode is FUN and by far the best part of this game. If this game mode were to be split off into its own game somehow, I'd only buy that and ignore the rest of this game.     Unfortunately, even the standard multiplayer modes are kind of lacking. It's exactly what you'd expect from a third person perspective game based around sniping.... people camping in one spot for much of the match and using third person to peep over walls. I know some people like it but I find it boring.      That's all I've got to say about this game, hope it helps you....

_childDocuments_.review: Basically, as a stealth shooter and general SE (or Hitman) fan - you can buy Sniper Elite 5 (in the sale), but overall the sequel falls short of its predecessor.
