But I have to say that I usually play either solo or co-op campaign/max. co-op survival, otherwise I completely ignore the MP area.BTW. of course the invasion mode is a welcome addition that would have suited the predecessor well, but beyond that SE5 seems in some places to have been quickly put together with the most necessary set pieces. At this point it should be mentioned that the controls have improved for Pc, but in my opinion the controller has deteriorated significantly.Well, maybe the developers ran out of steam after creating the medieval island fortress (2nd mission) :D Because it's quite impressive, just like the rest of the maps, which look pretty nice when you compare them to real photos, and are also fun to play, but still have that typical Unreal look from the basic construction kit...or, as in the case of some cutscenes (or patrolling torpedo boats, for example), just look lovelessly thrown in. When has ''unfortunately'' probably worked according to schedule and didn't have the time to design it lovinglyAs long as you don't want to carry over the demands from the predecessors and want something to shoot with your friend(s) with sniper or SE vibes, you'll get your money's worth here.Sniper Elite 5 is definitely fun. My wish for the next SE would be that you put more time into stories and the game again, then I'm optimistic that it will be something xd

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend playing Authentic difficulty because the other options just make it feel like an Ubisoft handhold-trip with X-ray markings, hud indicators out the wazzo. Added mechanics of Non-Lethal allows for (mostly) pacificst runs and easier setups on the complicated "kill X with Y weapon or Z item" by allowing you to move the body before ending the digital heartbeat. Also Coop with friendly fire on is great fun. Invasion is a wonderfully fun time, a good game of Cat-and-Mouse, but the problem is most people don't really know how to actually play the game like a sniper and just run around like its a run-n-gun shooter, so they usually ragequit instead of hunting, and it leads to idiots who don't read the instructions complaining about what an "annoying feature it is" and not turning it off for some reason or how having it disabled "reduces the XP gain". XP gain really is not an issue in this game. Since unlocks are tied to in-level objectives, and Multiplayer and Singleplayer are separate XP trees completely, it does not matter.Coop and Cross platform function work great, although they should make it clear to players that engaging in a sniper duel Mouse vs Controller is NOT recommended for most people.Story: Who cares its a damn sniping game. Works well, didn't question the settings or locations.Guns sound fantastic, as does the masking SFX and localized voice positioning. The headshot SFX is satisfying. Footsteps are muddled, and the low-health state where everything echos and they add a white balance filter should be removed. Don't think it should be replaced with jelly or anything, just remove the low-hp UI state as its incredibly annoying. As usual, I play with music off in multiplayer modes, and since I play with invasion on that means I have music completely off.I see people complaining about confusion on "climbing, vaulting" etc. Some of it is 100% valid. Some environmental and level designs are done for a reason, but the coverup and justification to the player is presented as a 2m tall bush that they cant jump over sometimes. Personally I never had an issue, might because I played the previous games and am familiar with the level design style already. The problem is the game LOOKS like a modern open-world style level design, but it is still DESIGNED in a somewhat linear nature. People might just assume they can go anywhere and do anything based on how it looks.Invasions: This could be the perfect defining addition to sniper elite, however it does need some tweaks, as it is INCREDIBLY skewed towards the invader. In addion, the spawns need to be reworked as I sometimes spawn DIRECTLY FACING the enemy player, meaning I have an easy kill.  The designs should make it hard for the INVADER, not the other way around.By default, Invasions should be turned off and players should have to make a choice and effort to enable them. Most people are casual players and due to the incredibly unbalanced design for the Invader, will easily get hunted with no actual cat-mouse fight occuring. Its also incredibly enligtening to see just how bad some people are, not even hunting them just watching them fight NPCs and realzing that they literally have zero chance against an invader even on a 2-v-1 and probably just skipped through all the prompts about invasions.When an enemy invades, the host player should KNOW the area the sniper deployed in and not have to mess around with the stop-gap mechanic of "invasion phones". It really feels like they couldn't figure out a way to inform invaders of host activity without just TELLING them the position. All the NPC invasion spot mechanics should be the only thing needed for a hunter to narrow down the location of their prey. Also, being able to invade people on their FIRST TIME THROUGH a level really is not that fair. Invasions should be an optional thing that can be enabled for re-visits of a campaign level, not as the first experience.Horde mode and Multiplayer are fine, could just a bit of adjustment for each but honestly co-op and invasions are why I got the game. As for the whole "waaahh you are humanizing nazis by allowing non-lethals" childrens section. Its a video game. Who cares? You being bothered by it says more about you than it does about the developers adding in a new playstyle method. Its an OPTION, don't wanna use it, don't have to use it, never ever had to use it unless you are going for the 100% achievements, and even after you pacify the enemies, you can still kill them to sate your digital bloodlust.TDLR: A smooth and polished launch with good campaign coop, fun atypical gametypes, and a relatively low base-price purchase make this well worth the cost imo.

_childDocuments_.review: The following are my thoughts and impressions after completing version 1.22 of Sniper Elite 5.Early reviewers have been critical that the 5th instalment hasn’t introduced enough new elements, but I think that Rebellion knows exactly what they want to accomplish with their franchise.  For me there are ample new elements to get excited about.  Much larger maps (with fantastic levels of details), more ways to approach an objective, unlocking optional objectives in mission, ability to customize you weapons through discovered workbenches.  None of these are game changing in their own right but the way it was implemented was done in a way to enhance the core Sniper Elite franchise.  I’ve enjoyed the game so much that that it is the first ever season pass I bought.Added bonus:  Even though the game has always had a multiplayer option, the invasion mode is what I’m more excited about.  Now that I’ve finished all the missions at least once, I can attempt them again but this time with invasion mode, to play cat and mouse with a real person.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't the game you think it is. It's not bad, but it's not a game about being a sniper.There are precious few sniping spots in the missions, and very few objectives that demand usage of your sniper skills. The levels are quite constrained compared to the previous game, and there's a LOT of space that isn't traversable or usable.Player movement is worse than previous games - the environment is much more visually 'noisy' now, and mantle/jump is less consistent. There are often knee-high obstacles you can't step over, but can't mantle either. There are also lots and lots of places where you can't jump/hang, but it seems like you should be able to. The cover system is improved, but still prone to nasty bouts of stickiness at the worst possible times.I can't speak to the invasion system - maybe it's the secret sauce that makes this a 9/10 - but I can't see how it improves the base gameplay. There's already very little sniping, having another player trying to hunt you down is only going to make it more tedious to peel the onion on these levels.The upgrade system, previously only tied to objectives, is now ALSO tied to finding hidden objects in levels, which makes it even more likely that you'll go through most of the game without seeing a lot of the content than previous games.The 'special target' system is good - giving specific kill requirements adds the thimbleful of extra thought to their deaths that makes it more than just another speedbump in the missions.The 'targets of opportunity' that show up as optional objectives are nice, but I found only one mission where it wasn't guaranteed that you'd be given those objectives through normal play.Adding multiple spawn points to each mission is a wierd extra system to spend time on - there's basically no variation in how the missions play out, I'm not sure why Rebellion thought anyone would want to play them more than once. If you've gotten all the objectives, you've seen everything the mission has to offer.In conclusion - This feels like Rebellion wanted to make a Hitman game with asymmetric multiplayer. It's not that, it's about 30-40% of that, and in the process they lost most of what made Sniper Elite 4 a good game. I'd have gladly paid 60$ for "Sniper Elite 4: 10 more missions edition," but this isn't even close.It's... fine for 10$, but it clearly cost way too much to make to sell it for 10$.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a step back from Sniper elite 4, and shows severe signs of being rushed after SE VR's failure. Gone now is the fun sandbox design of sniper elite 4 with huge massive maps that may contain outposts that exist solely to be eye candy and world building, or target practice, instead we now have dark souls invasions. Metal gear solid 2 Non lethal ammo, with the same fatal flaw as metal gear solid 2. And XP nerfs that encourage charging in with a maxed out SMG and rifle with non lethal ammo to get that sweet chunk of XP you used to get for farting in time with an ambient sound. The long versions: Map design: The maps are HUGE, EASILY some of the biggest of the series that aren't called "San Celini Island" and "Aquaduct". But the problem lies in the fact that every map is so JAM packed with side objectives that if you see a Nazi walking around somewhere you can bet your ass there is an objective there. Alternate paths have been SEVERELY limited based on this fact, likely due to the dark souls invasion mechanic which can be opted out of, (more on that later).   You get about 2 alternate paths to each objective which consists of climbing walls that are poorly indicated by white objects such as dead vines, smears of white paint, or French resistance graffiti tags that the Nazis don't seem to give a ♥♥♥♥ are plastered all over the place, or you can just run across the fields and you MIGHT find some broken fence somewhere you can crawl under or a waist high fence that CAN be vaulted over, as opposed to the 30 feet of the exact same fence beside it that you CAN'T vault over. Weapon selection (Warning: gun collectors and sniper elite veteran's rant ahead): Remember the Mosin? The gun in almost every sniper elite game since the first game? Rebellion doesn't, or more accurately cut it to package it into a DLC (this was written prior to the DLC all being released If I'm wrong, I'm wrong, but I am willing to bet steam points I'm not). You have a narrow selection of about 4 weapons per category suited to the french theater, kinda. Instead of things like the liberator or M3 grease gun that were air dropped for french resistance fighters prior to Operation overlord (D-day for the non historically inclined) You have an american selection, a German selection, a couple british guns, and a French RSC from 1918. A gun that barely saw production and was, had WWI not been declared, planned to be the first ever Semi-auto rifle. The m1 Garand from sniper elite 3 (and 4's DLC), the king of ping, has been replaced by the M1a1 Carbine.    The Thompson is obscenely powerful when maxed out and I often found myself, instead of sniping, running around like an idiot with a rapid fire Thompson with a suppressor and a 100 round drum cutting down entire patrols before they can raise an alarm like scenes out of a gangster movie instead of a WWII sniper game (more on why later).    The 1911a1 also makes a return and honestly, except the welrod from the prior games and the Mark 6 Webley revolver, the pistols all feel no different from each other, so I'm not going to go too in-depth on them, the first example I've cited of a rushed game.   The German list isn't really worth going into too much detail in. A Kar98, a G43, a walther P.08 an STG44, and an MP40 that I can think of off the top of my head. All fairly unremarkable and standard for the series at this point.   Silencers are more accurate to reality, they are SUPPRESSORS, not SILENCERS. Hollywood silence is only achieveable using ammo that doesn't break the sound barrier, IN conjunction with a suppressor. And even then only on certain calibers. For example the .22 long rifle. Suppressing an m1911 and still using supersonic ammunition still results in the sound being about as loud as a lawnmower.  Honestly I could, and SHOULD go on, but I'm not getting paid for this and I have limited space that I have somehow managed to hit. Weapon unlocks: THANK GOD THE WEAPON CHALLENGES ARE GONE! Oh God, now you have to unlock weapons by beating missions, you can't just pick them up anymore due to how small the weapon pool is. And here we have the second example of a rushed game -- arbitrary limitations that were lifted in the prior game in the series (not including SE VR). The kar98, which is POSSIBLY one of the better guns in the game tied with previous installments variants of the mosin, isn't unlocked until almost the final mission -- assuming you even get the record for completing it which I'll cover later in bugs.   In order to unlock upgrades for the weapons you have to go on an easter egg hunt for the weapon workbenches in each level, I'm not sure how to feel about this as I like the idea of having to scavenge the equipment and not having SOE resupply you like in SE4, and it gives incentives to find intel documents and officers with the keys to FIND said workbenches. This illusion however, is then destroyed by you walking within 20 feet of the workbenches location, and it being marked on the map. Then you can either find the key or, since half the map is likely aimbotting your location at that point anyway unless you are carrying non lethal ammo with a silenced weapon, just throw a satchel charge on it and go in. I have mixed feelings on this. But I DO lean towards it being a pro since I had to farm liver shots to max out the mosin in SE4. And the horrid "high heart rate challenge" massacres that consisted of setting the game to cadet, sprinting everywhere and emptying a mag into people's heads.Story: Let's face it, we are all here to shoot Hitler in the balls, listen to Karl crack one liners (Which he doesn't do very often in this game) and kill Nazis. It's a standard sniper elite story. Nazi has secret project, Karl finds info on it, you go to win the war single-handedly. Moving on.Bugs: Todd Howard called. The rental of bethesda's QA team is up.  Where do I START? You go to open a door, hit whatever button you have bound to interact, and Karl stands there admiring the French architecture for about 30 seconds before he opens it. In the meantime some Jerry from the other side of the map has spotted you because apparently EVERY German in 1944 decided that carrots were their ONLY food, called reinforcements from Fallschirmjäger, and now the entire base is emptying bullets into your dome. You get into the door with ONE bar of health, maybe less, pull out your trusty WAY OVERPOWERED maxed out thompson, and it seems Karl has retained EVERY SINGLE EMPTY MAGAZINE EVER AND WILL RELOAD INFINITELY UNTIL YOU CHANGE AMMO TYPES. You change ammo types, Nail the active reload taken from gears of war (A nice addition, by the way) to reload faster, go to a wall that you climbed up before and hurl yourself over the side to escape the swarms of fire coming your way, And because you have to hold space to vault, Karl immediately pulls himself BACK up the ledge, and dies. You reload, fix the reload bug, and just decide to execute everyone before they become a problem, then proceed to admire the door for 30 seconds again. Remember how I said I often ended up just gunning down entire squads with the Thompson? Yeah this is why. I'm sure -- Actually I'm HOPEFUL these bugs will get fixed. Especially the infinite reload as it means that if you get this bug on ANY gun and you are OUT of alternate ammo, the gun is now broken entirely. I've had pistols do it, I've had rifles do it, I usually end up seeing it on the SMG's because they end up being my most used weapon.  I don't know if the AI's eagle eyes are a bug or intentional so I'm putting it here, because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ these guys can spot you at a range and hit you with irons that would make Simo Häyhä, Francis Pegahmagabow, and Carlos Hathcock, jealous. Forget the war, Hitler should have invested in a trick shooting team to push his ideology.In summary:  Since I'm at the character limit: wait for a sale. Use non lethal at all times you can because it gives more XP.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is terrific. Don't be fooled by the title. While it does include various rifles and plenty of open areas for shooting, this isn't really just a sniper game. Karl is a commando, through and through. You'll be sneaking around hostile territory conducting guerrilla warfare against the Germans, sabotaging enemy equipment (coastal gun batteries, AA guns, comm equipment, etc), gathering intelligence and assassinating officers. There are a bunch of different ways to complete each mission, including both ends of the spectrum. It is a lot like Splinter Cell in that way. You can sneak around without touching anyone, you can just knock them out (why not kill those nazis?) or you can ventilate them with your blade. Naturally, you can also engage at all ranges with various firearms. If sniping isn't your thing, there are submachine guns and pistols that are perfectly viable in combat, especially now that you can aim down the sights. CQB with a Thompson is definitely a treat. A lot of care was put into making Karl shoot and scoot in a realistic and period accurate way, including his usage of the fighting knife melee kills and the way he reloads his weapons. It's a cool game, and definitely nails that espionage vibe. The Axis Invasion mode is a lot of fun, too. Definitely give this game a shot. If not here on steam, then try Gamepass. Also, set your AA to medium and increase the render scale instead of just maxing out the graphics. You'll thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently playing and trying to enjoy this game as much as I did SE4. I'm not a massive fan of the franchise, but 4 was pretty good fun on medium difficulty and it felt like you could sneak around until you cleared the map and the world was a happy place. SE4 made it clear what you could do with the environment and you could plan around it. SE5 on the other hand, is very ambiguous.There was one section where I thought I would walk upstream to the waypoint. Upsteam had an invisible wall in it so a pretty glaring break from immersion as my character moonwalks in the water against a glass case of emotion. The game also doesn't really reward you for playing clever. It just descends into run and gun like a third person shooter where you're flailing around murdering waves of Ze Germans who teleport out of the woodwork screeching Achtung! All the cool trip mines and ambush stuff is pretty much missing. It is a little confusing because I'm not really understanding how the game should be played. Maybe it doesn't know either. AI also is pretty woeful. I was standing in a stairway while Jerry is moonwalking against my character model, until I mercifully kill him in melee and put him out of his digitised misery.Oh and if you're into playing games for the story, please be aware that WW2 is very progressive now. "The Message" features heavily.I read the negative reviews previously and just wanted everyone to be wrong. I waited til it was $20 AUD on sale.  I wanted to like it. I tried turning a blind eye to its faults. Logically, you'd think each iteration of the game would be an improvement. This one doesn't seem to be it, Chief.Life is too short to be playing badly designed and implemented games.OH - and non-lethal ammo and on-lethal mines feature in a game about murder from afar. _childDocuments_.review: The game is ok. Can be entertaining for a few hours.  Multiplayer is a bit frustrating, sometimes maybe good, sometimes maybe ♥♥♥♥. Hacking can be frequent. And obvious. And the balance is non-existent. Peer 2 Peer Hosting is the worst idea ever, with the match just ending if a hosts leave mid-match. Happens so frequently... that you just get used to it. Luckily XP earned is instant, only xp loss would be a possible match win bonus.  Single player campaign is quite lengthy. The maps are a mixed batch. Some are good, some are not.  I would say more good than bad maps. But only a few that encourage Sniping. Then again, I don't see this as a sniping game, as much as a Stealth game.  Difficulty customization are very detailed, and allow for great personal customization. Only miss is a Authentic Plus Mode, seen in Sniper Elite 4.   Survival, it's not as hard as previous games, but still quite fun overal. Higher difficulties can become a challenge, as are playing anything but solo. Invasion mode is a nice welcome, albeit the huge nerf to the invader since release. It adds a little challenge. However once you're quite skilled at invasions. Matches can be completely crap, frustrating and boring. Or Amazing. Not really anything in between. Due to the fact, you'll get matched against players playing for their first time. And players who've spend the past 8 hours on a single map, gathering every single explosive they could find to make it a guaranteed deathtrap. And they'll just be camping in some cuboard, waiting for you to step on a mine.  But once a match is good, youll be guaranteed to rematch multiple times.  Weapon customization. Ok, so the most unrealistic part if you ask me. But then again, Not an unwelcome part. Unlocking of new weapons, or weapon modifications are done through challenges ingame, encouraging replaying levels. And compared to the 4 challenges per weapon that would "upgrade" it in previous games. This allows for more persoinalized equipment. Very noticable when picking up someone else their rifle or SMG in multi-player modes. Often, you'll just not like the feel of a weapon.  And allows for a more wide style of gameplay, from full assault to stealth purist.  But honestly, The game is not bad. Could be better, but have seen worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I could just copy and paste my review for Sniper Elite 4, because that's essentially what the makers of this game did. It's 4 with new maps. Although the maps are big, they are riddled with invisible walls, which gets pretty infuriating after a while. One great addition is the unlocking of two more infiltration points on each map, which definitely adds to the replay value.I've played it through twice now, mainly because I didn't take the achievements - especially the weapon related ones - into account on my first playthrough. So now I'm just farming kills. For a game about snipers, there are surprisingly few long shots to be made. Most are mid-range (<100m). It's not that it's difficult to score headshots for the rifle mastery medals - Nazis heads are like bullet sponges - it's that a lot of enemies are too close for the 100+ m requirement. It's says quite a lot that in order to get a rifle gold medal you need 50 kills, but for a secondary gold medal you need 150 (!) kills. The game is telling you that sniping is secondary. So anyway I started blasting.One thing which has remained constant however, is the main character. He's a supposedly elite soldier who is in worse shape than I am, panting and wheezing after a five meter sprint. But at least the running animation is better than in the previous games. And there is something peculiar about a game released in 2022 where there isn't a jump button. Time and time again super soldier gets stumped if a curb happens to be more than two inches high. Clearly they blew their load on the kill cam function, but it's still strange how they seemingly disregarded just about everything else.I bought it on sale and the DLC is only worth it for the maps. I personally don't care about skins, but the ones they give you are absolutely horrendous. It's like they were designed by a five year old on crack.OK if you can find it on sale, but not worth getting a full price.

_childDocuments_.review: While I will give a thumbs down for this game review, I *do* like the game, fun to mess around in and nothing else. This review will only be for single-player, non-axis invasion. - Weapon Customization. It's very fun to fiddle around with different types of weapon accessories, even if most don't really need to exist.- Weapon x-rays. It's cool to see where you end up hitting a target with a pistol, or any secondary, really.- First person aiming on non-rifle weapons. This helps GREATLY when trying to be accurate and even sometimes discreet when doing stealth.- Multiple starting points in every map. These are fun to change up how you play the given mission greatly. All starting points should be unlocked after completing the mission instead of finding them.-Being able to bodyshot enemies in authentic mode. Semi-auto rifles still suffer greatly with a lack of power, however.- Lack of scope marking customization. The T-post tactical of SE4 make authentic (plus) mode a far more enjoyable experience. Sure, there is the bullet drop indicator when you have a scope, but it's too far off to the right to be of any use.- Reinforcement phone boxes are a waste of time. The enemy become easy pickings as you keep killing them trying beeline to it. Rigging, or creating a loud noise area is never worth it, non of the boxes are in a hidden location to make it worthwhile.- Gun cycling/reloading sounds. They sound like hollow tin cans being clinked together.- Nonlethal fighting. There's no real reason to do non-lethal other than to offset killing officers/soldier in a pure stealth run.- Animations and model detail. Cut-scene animations and characters suffer this the most, they look really, really bad. The weapons look/are animated nice however.- DLC/Skins. Too much money for what it is worth. If you want to buy a DLC, get the one with the DeLisle in it and don't buy anything else. - Bottles instead of rocks. I don't use bottles at all because of the max 6 bottles you can carry. Whistling is far more effective. Also why is it that you start every mission with 4 instead of 6 even when you unlock the perk to maximize the number of bottles you can carry?- Lack of better stealth hiding places. Long grass is fine, but it would be interesting to hide inside boxes or crates. Would also be nice to have it so soldier get curious when they see a gun sticking out from a corner or grass.- Big maps that only really have sniping action in small areas. Best you can do is snipe out some sentrys  and use that as your way in if the body doesn't get discovered.-Decoys. They are useless. I have yet to see effective use with them that doesn't immediately cause them to find out that it's a decoy and now they are enclosing on your position. Decoys also have a big time to set up to be effective so it's not worth having.All-in-all my view is still negative despite it being a game  that I am still sinking time into since I have bought a few DLCs and whatnot. An OK game to get on a heavily discounted sale, and never full-price.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes - with caveats - read on.First off let me provide context. I'm most certain an 'older' gamer, and a casual gamer. I have played and completed all the Snipe Elite series, as well as played many other sniper style games.Did I enjoy this? Yes, Was it worth the money; not sure.I know many are waxing lyrical about how good this is, but I'll be honest ... I was 'meh'.On my older rig I'm probably not running at full detail, so can't comment on exactly how good the graphics can be; for me I'm not seeing a massive improvement over SE4.In terms of game play, there are a few new elements, but overall it is very much more of the same with some tweaks. I didn't feel the game play was markedly different to SE4, to be honest.I still felt frustrated that my supposedly 'elite' sniper who has years of experience, is still unable to clamber over rocks, move through bushes or step over small walls. In fact, in one map I 'swapped cover' from one side of an open gateway to the other side and promptly got stuck behind a knee-high hedge garden and had to re-load a save. A well known issue for snipers the world over, I'm sure :-|The enemy AI also doesn't appear to be that much better than before either. I can shoot a guy in the head, right beside his mate, and there might be a bit of 'searching' but not the panic and calling all troops into a search that, I'm sure might happen in real life. Be 'concerned' for a couple of minutes and then "ah well, no bother, back to guard duty, nothing to see here after all". Really?I'd also like to see more missions of having to sneak in and make a kill and extract without any other conflict. One shot, one kill.Would I buy this game if I knew all the above in advance? Well, probably, because I like tactical stealth sniper style of games. But I'm not altogether convinced it is worth the asking price. If you don't have it already and are curious and not a hard-out fan, then I'd probably wait for a sale. If you are a hrd-out fan, well, then you likely have it already! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 5 presents a bit of a mixed bag when compared to its predecessor, SE4. While it brings in some new tricks like non-lethal approaches and weapon customization, it also holds back on certain aspects, such as fewer options for enemy engagements like grenade explosions. The maps, though visually stunning, feel somewhat more constrained and linear. As for the story, it's rather forgettable, with a villain that's about as menacing as a kitten. Nevertheless, it still delivers that quintessential Sniper Elite experience of chaos and destruction.The gameplay has received a commendable polish, with smoother movement and improved AI, making it a thoroughly satisfying experience for aficionados of the series. Invasion Mode adds an extra dash of excitement, and the inclusion of non-lethal options injects a bit of novelty, even if it does come across as somewhat gimmicky. The narrative takes a back seat to the action, akin to the ethos of a John Wick flick, while the multiplayer component adds another layer of enjoyment.The killcams have undergone a notable upgrade, providing a more cinematic spectacle, though some may bemoan the absence of destruction physics for character models. All in all, Sniper Elite 5 emerges as a robust addition to the franchise, appealing to both seasoned veterans and fresh-faced recruits.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Buy the game on sale, do some coop, have a good time. Otherwise I wouldn't buy at full priceSniper Elite 5 brings some interesting ideas to the table, but ultimately feels like a downgrade for the series. A lot of the ideas felt like the developers played Hitman and thought, "Hey, that'd be neat!" There's different starting locations, limited climbing mechanics, and the targets have patterns and 'kill methods' like the new Hitman games. The problem is, a lot of these features don't feel very polished. The starting locations are unlocked only if you stumble upon them across the map, you can only climb a very limited amount of walls and surfaces, and the targets usually bug out and prevent their special 'kill method' from being used.Speaking of the bugs, there are a lot of bugs in this game. I've had targets spawn below ground, instances where enemies across the entire map are alerted after a steath event that was unrelated, enemies stuck in walls, and more. I know the developers are working on fixing these issues, but it's a huge issue when you're playing a level and have to restart because targets or events just don't trigger. There are also big optimization issues. Any level with rain tanks my FPS.Another new feature is the invasion mechanic. Basically it's like Dark Souls or Deathloop, where someone can invade your game or you can invade theirs. I actually really like it (but you can turn it off if you don't). However, the time between invasions needs to be drastically increased. Getting 3+ invasions per level is tiring, since they all pretty much function the same way. My final note is on the soundtrack, setting, and level design. I felt like the soundtrack for SE4 was far superior than this game. This game has no recognizable theme, and the soundtrack didn't really stand out to me. I also wasn't as keen on the setting as I was for 4. It could be because just about every WW2 game is set in France, but I found it stale and overused. There wasn't much variety in the locations either, but most of them looked the same. Level design wise, a lot of levels felt very linear and there were very limited approaches for many locations. It's just arbitrary barriers too, like certain fences you can't climb over, or hills you can't go up. That makes it all the more annoying.Overall, it was still an enjoyable time, especially doing coop. In any future games though, I hope they refine these mechanics to be more polished and workable. I think they have great potential, but in their current state they can cause more issues than enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just wrapped up the base game with the goal of killing every soldier in every level. Took about 47 hours and lots of patience. Out of SE3, SE4, and SE5, this was my favorite, and I thoroughly enjoyed the other games. I took a firm stealth approach to the entire game, which worked out very well. If you like that sort of playstyle, you will enjoy this. If analyzing troop movements and finding short strike windows is your thing, this game has it in spades. What I liked...- The weapon customization is detailed enough to be fun, although a few of the items are a little silly. I'm looking at you, weirdly-crossed grip tape.- The visuals are fantastic.- Soldier bios - This was a nice touch. It allows you to get to know your quarry before you put a bullet through its skull. Not sure why they added this feature, but it was kind of funny.- The suppressed rifle sounds actually sound fairly realistic. As someone who spends a good deal of time on the range and spent seven years in the Army, it's nice to hear a game get this right.What I didn't like...- I'm not a fan of "weapon/item unlock" mechanics in games. I'm not even sure why developers put these in games any more. It would be great if you started with the ability to build your loadout however you wanted. The pros and cons of each weapon/item should be enough on their own to prevent any particular loadout from being overpowered.- I'm not a fan of the way the player icon displays on the map. I know, it's a small thing, but when you are trying to orient yourself on maps this size, the direction of the character icon should reflect the way the camera is facing instead of the character's body. This is a minor annoyance when you are in cover, which is a lot of the time. - Constant kill cams get old. Look, I loved this game. Thought it was great, but if I smoke 150+ dudes on one map, I have to watch 150 kill cams. Each one runs about seven seconds. That's 17+ minutes of kill cams. Bruh, that's a bit much. I know you can turn them off completely, but what about a happy medium or some way to modify the kill cam frequency? This is just one bald dude's opinion.Overall, this was a great game. Definitely took top spot for me for the SE series of games. I'll be buying the DLC so I can go smoke the dude with the bad haircut and the toothbrush mustache next. Have fun dropping bodies. I certainly did.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: + One of the few games which supports crossplay PC - Xbox One/Series, for me it was a key point since my partner has only Xbox SX at his disposal+ Cooperative and invading are fun as hell. It’s not just a tactical stealth action, but can be also highly dynamic: no one forces you to be silent all the time, even on hard difficulty.+ AI is surprisingly smart and creative.+ The locations design: these meadows, lakes and castles are very pleasing for eyes.+ Except a few glitches, this game works quite stable and does not irritate you with crashes/endless bugs/syncing problems.Cons:- Visual shimmering and ugly distant aliasing, it hurts my eyes and makes precision aiming/spotting enemies more challenging, especially if the screen resolution is 1080p or below (VRS/DSR doesn't help). DLSS/FFX 2.0 could solve a problem, but this engine doesn't support it - only outdated and terrible Fidelity FX 1.0- Game design sometimes forces you to wander around the map for some nonsense. Why can't I crack the lock with bazooka or mine, but need a damn satchel which could be very difficult to find? Or in one mission I was looking for a valve for 15 mins.- Clunky controls. For example, there are no keys to use medicine or grenade, you have to choose the thing and then use F, so in some instances you accidentally explode yourself instead of healing.- Lackluster story - it is NOT a dealbreaker here. Thanks for the developer all cutscenes can be skipped.I would give this game a solid 8 out of 10: strongly recommend it for walkthrough with your friends, especially considering the fact that there are not many cool options for crossplay. _childDocuments_.review: It's that solid 7/10 action game; nothing is quite as interactive as an immersive sim, or as freewheeling as an open world. Sometimes it can feel confining or arbitrary - why do I have to walk 200m down a shin-high stone wall to enter a field, or only climb perfectly things with perfectly flat edges? The flip side of that is that it gives Rebellion a chance to control the experience, to funnel you this way or that, and give you the limited-yet-fun options they've dictated for a given encounter.There's solid, satisfying action here, and once it starts to click, the limitations are liberating, unlike what I find can happen in open worlds or even immersive sims where I'm always wondering if I "played it wrong." Though there's lots of weapon variety, relatively lean set of overall options - loud, quiet, distant, close, traps - make what's there gratifying. A little more disappointing is some general jankiness - world objects that are extremely particular about where you are in space to interact with them, enemies that get stuck in alert-investigating-cancelled-alert loops. This last is especially bothersome because despite a huge, rich set of accesibility and difficulty controls, the HUD options are terribly limited. You get quest markers and enemy tagging and status updates (alert, investigating, etc) and tool tips and etc etc or you get nothing - no option just to have, say, a few essentials on the screen and leave the rest of it up to the thrill of the hunt. I might remember wrongly but I'm pretty sure that this is a regression from SE4. The menus are also a terrible modern design paradigm where everything is tiles, and there's no simple way to just resume your campaign. It's not a touch interface; I don't need 5cm x 5cm block of screen to resume my campaign. I wish it leaned more into the eponymous sniping - it's so rewarding, especially as you dial down assists. This game seems less confident than SE4, though, and does have habit of clearly blocking lines of sight, or tucking enemies into places that you can't engage except at close range. Speaking of things to lean *out* of, Carl talks too much and this game doesn't need (or at least do well with) the cutscenes, in writing or execution. If you want soulful Nazi-hunting, go play the new Wolfensteins. SE5 I think has aspirations but can't meet them.It's all still worth it though, and so refreshing that, even if a bit less confident than the one before, is still proudly what it is; a schlocky, shooty power fantasy that is fun to play. Turning off all the assists, sitting 800m out from a target and nailing that shot is something that no other game does or has replicated.Edit 26 July to add: Rebellion has implemented the Shooting Range feature, which is so so helpful to learn to place your shots. Glad to have it back for SE5, thanks Rebellion!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this late, but I've played through the campaign twice, once on medium and once on hard. It's pretty simple really:- In a vacuum, sniper elite 5 is a "decent" game.- Compared to Sniper Elite 4, it's a bad game.Why?- Map's are prettier but not open world. Way too many invisible walls or things you cant't jump over, each map really only offers two or maybe 3 direct paths to follow. This makes the best part of the game (Sniping from long distance) naturally harder because you can't get on that hill over there that you want to, no you have to climb this specific building they put right here. SE 4 gave you WAY more freedom and options for long distance sniping.- Weapon upgrades are a cool idea, but don't make a big enough difference really, I always end up just going for muzzle velocity, and as quiet as possible. Even then most of the rifles are just too loud. Now this would be fine if the maps were like SE4 because you can almost always go over 100-200m away from the enemies but in SE5 you are semi guided on a path, there is FAR less room for long distance sniping. This felt more like Splinter Cell where the majority of kills were either stealth take downs or pistol shots. Why not call it Pistol Elite 1 instead.Main Point : Sniper Elite 4 was awesome because you could CHOOSE to be a up close pistol man, or that guy that finds the furthest possible point and then sits there and takes out 1/4th of the map, then moves to another great natural spot. SE5 does not give you that same freedom. It has a tiny bit of it, but it's just way more forced and ultimately that's the complete wrong direction they should have gone in. I still enjoyed the game, I like the B movie campaigns they are silly. I didn't personally find this game woke, I think adding non lethal options is good. Choice is good. Unfortunately overall SE4 had more choice than SE5, and ultimately that's why you should buy that one and play that one instead.I really hope SE6 goes back to the more open world design. It's the difference between a just okay game and a great one.

_childDocuments_.review: The best game in Sniper Elite series! Period.Built on Sniper Elite 4 formula (which is a good thing, that formula was already great...no need to change), SE5 will take you further into the enemy's den. - The levels are great, the French buildings are depicted perfectly (the team has certainly done their research)- The enemies behave similarly like in SE4 but sometimes a bit smarter (one map has 3 different paths to approach and once the enemies became aware, they came from different directions at my location!).- Everyone's favourite bullet kill cam is slightly improved. Now pistols and SMGs will also trigger these cams!- There is a new Invasion mode which adds another great dimension to the game, where you can play as German officer and disrupt Sniper player's operation. Or alternatively, you as Karl, can team up with another player to stop the person invading your game.This is optional and can be turned OFF if you want to experience the campaign the first time without any invasion.One thing to note is these kind of games are to be played patiently, using tactics and strategies. They are usually not designed for going in directly without thinking, and just firing everywhere a.k.a. speedrun. In real life also, snipers take considerable amount of time to become familiar with their surroundings and enemy positions. Then why would it be different in such a realistic game?The bad reviews you see may be from Fortnite players, or Call of Duty players...they really don't know how to play this game skilfully. They just go in and try to gun down everyone / do speedruns which is a failed strategy for such games.Also note that this is NOT a AAA game but even then the devs have delivered an excellent Sniper Elite game to their fans.Go for it if you enjoyed previous SE games, or just want to experience what it's like to be a great sniper!

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 5 is a fun game, especially with the enhanced kill cams. Every bone, every muscle is incredibly detailed and makes it even more fun to see it triggered with every weapon. The ragdolls are pretty funny too, especially with explosives. Below I'll be giving a summary for each subject.Graphics: These look good and performance wise work well. FXAA looks a little bit off though. But there's certainly more detailed graphics than in SE4. However I've noticed a slight issue. Cutscenes are prone to freeze the game. This happens consistently in multiplayer (campagne coop. ) Even freezes during the end-results screen.Story: The story is pretty good, albeit a bit short. The missions are interesting, debriefing is well animated, voice acting is fine too. It's a bit short, but done well. The DLC missions are a nice addition to the storyline. It does get a bit repetitive from time though. Character models: Very detailed, the clothing especially well detailed. Ragdolls are fun and often realistic. Facial expressions are a bit wonky. Combat & parkour: The combat mechanic works great, enemies react realisticly to gunfire and may stumble around when wounded. Not much a fan of the current parkour system, Karl moves around a bit sluggish/not as responsively. Weapon customisation: The customisation menu is great, there's a good selection of attachments to pick from with different effects. Some look weird to me, such as the blue tape and some buttstocks and grips. I mostly keep the weapons stock. Weapon selection: A problem that I have with the weapons in SE5: there's not enough of them. It feels there's too little amount of weapons to pick from, most of them are very similar to each other & don't bring much different to the table. The MP40 is much better than the Welgun SMG, then the Thompson beats all SMGs by a long shot. Same with rifles, the M1903 cannot compete with the Kar 98. I'm happy to see some Japanese weapons in the game, most games don't feature them. There's no Soviet or Italian weapons yet, which feels weird. I hope the DLCs add some fun, unique, interesting weapons, because I had a lot of fun with the arsenal in SE4. They were diverse and suitable for every occasion. It's just weird not to have a Garand, Mosin-Nagant or MAB38 to pick from. Also even worse: THERE IS NO SHOTGUN. I miss the shotgun the most. It was an absolute blast (pun intended) to run around enemy bases, CQC with the pump-action. Unrivaled damage, quick to aim, ragdolls everywhere. Tools and equipment: Most of the equipment has been left the same, which is a good thing. It worked well before, so I didn't require a change. Few have been added or removed though. Added: decoy, shu-mine,limited amount of throwing bottles. Removed: tripwire, unlimited rock throwing. Not gonna lie, I kinda miss the tripwire. It was a fun tool to use, very entertaining in survival mode too. Maps: The world is well designed, lots of open & closed spaces to explore, from islands, cities and bunkers. A lot of propaganda posters placed around the map make for realistic scenery. I like that. Makes also a lot of sense in historical context. Map design is one of the best parts of the game, next to the killcam. Mission variarity: Most of it is kinda similar and repetitive. Shoot a guy, stealth kill here and there, sabotage generators. It makes sense that the resistence would do these on a regular basis. Personally, I don't mind it, but it can get a bit boring after a while. The most interesting mission I have seen so far was in mission 3: where you have to stealth kill a target. Infiltrate the meeting, wait for the meeting to be over, then follow the target until he's isolated. Very challenging, but also very rewarding & fun. (Might take a few tries to get it done, but when it's executed well, you feel like you've beaten the entire game)In summary. Pros: Great map design, amazing killcam, lots of weapon customisations, good graphics. Tools and equipment work well with your weapons and the maps. Cons: Mission variarity can get boring after a while, occasional freezing/crashing, little amount of weapons to pick from. Also, because the game is very recent, there's the occasional technical issue, such as stuck in mid-air, falling through the map, overall game stability.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, right off the bat I feel like mentioning that I'm only covering the base game in this review, because most of the DLC's deserve their own review entirely, so please keep that in mind.Sniper Elite 5 has it's flaws and drawbacks, don't get me wrong. Yes, the map design is on average subpar to that in Sniper Elite 4, with some of the levels being particularly frustrating to get through (*Cough* Level 6 *Cough*). Yes, it was odd for Rebellion to remove the trip mine and S-mine from the main game, and yet keep them inside Multiplayer. And yes, this game doesn't give you as much of an opportunity to snipe as much as the previous games, which is a little weird. But with that said, it's still a pretty good game in my mind.1. StoryFirst things first, this game has much better characters, and a better story compared to anything that came before. Karl is a little bit more interesting than he was in Sniper Elite 4, and actually has pretty decent chemistry with all the main characters. Speaking of them, Charlie is a decent enough buddy for Karl, but be warned because she might have the single most aggressive Scottish accent in any character from anything ever.Other than them, Marie is a pretty good character who ties them to the resistance and sometimes helps provide transport, although not being super interesting. And Moller is a good villain who bears a likeness to the douche bags in charge of the Nazi Regime.For the story, Operation Kraken might just seem like another evil Nazi super weapon, and it is. But what really sets it apart from what has come before is just how insane the actual plan is. I wont spoil anything, but the whole game is worth playing through just to find out the awesome conclusion of exactly what it is.2. GameplaySniper Elite 5 might not have as good levels as Sniper Elite 4, but it does make up for it in the new things it added. For one thing, this game added Invasion mode, which is a wonderful way to play through the game if you don't feel challenged enough. The game adds plenty of new weapons like the SREM-1, Welgun, and RSC 1918. I for one think that it's an interesting idea to add non-lethal kill methods, since it's a really good way to get XP. Some of the levels are pretty well designed, such as levels #2 and #7. \There are several different ammo types, all of which are useful for different situations. And of course, weapon customization might not be realistic to the period but it is a really cool factor. 3. ConclusionSo, in the end Sniper Elite 5 might not be an amazing game, but I do believe that it has many strong parts. I would recommend to get it on sale, since I'm not sure that it's worth the $50 (but to be fair, I'm not sure that Sniper Elite 4 is worth $60).8.2/10I hope that if they make Sniper Elite 6 it will take all the good stuff from this game, and the good stuff from the last few games, and put it all together to make the perfect game.Until then, stay safe, drink water, hug your loved ones, play this game, and have a nice day. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a really fun game, and a worthy addition to the Sniper Elite franchise. Unfortunately I ran into several bugs while playing, and I had a few frustrating experiences with invisible walls and barriers, etc. But they have been working on patching them.The overall level concepts and designs were really fun. The WW2 France setting was done really well, it reminded me a lot of old Medal of Honor and Call of Duty Games set in France. It had everything from rural farmsteads to ruined cities to fortified beaches., And in my opinion level 3 was particularly great.The levels are more linear than Sniper Elite 4, and featured a lot more close quarters situations. This lead to less sniping and long distance sniping opportunities, and having to rely more on stealth and traps. But nevertheless I enjoyed it and had fun infiltrating Nazi bases by using distractions, traps, and stealth.The story was a pretty standard Sniper Elite story. The Nazi's are working on a super weapon project, and you must find out what it is and destroy it. Nothing special but not terrible either, but I found myself invested at least.There are also new game modes, such as Axis invasions, where you can invade someones campaign, or have your campaign invaded by a counter sniper. It can be turned on and off optionally, but not using it gets you less XP, and it's also required to unlock single player items (like guns and cosmetics) which I didn't care for. But overall the mode is fun.There's also Survival Mode where you can survive against waves of AI invaders, single player and Co-op. There's also Co-op in the campaign mode, and regular multiplayer battles.So overall it's not my favorite Sniper Elite games, and it's not perfect, but nevertheless I had fun playing it and I feel like I got my money's worth. I would give it a 7.5/10 and recommend it (after they release more patches if you can wait, but it's still fun right now)

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome sequel to the great Sniper Elite franchise, just as expected. The maps are downright huge, reminded me of some Commandos maps back from the old days. Even the entry paths are much simpler and lead to either very early aggression which turns into a map wipe or weird hiding behind a crate for 3 minutes until that one guard finally turns around. The movement feels wooden and choppy.SE5 is visually gorgeous. The challenges and achievements are very interesting and invasions are exhilirating. There is so much to explore and see. Saving often is also smart as you can just load if you die. _childDocuments_.review: Even though the graphics haven't had an update in quality, Sniper Elite 5 lives up to it expectations for great gameplay, excitement and outstanding maps. The building interiors, the towns, the fields, they all look believable and reflect the WW2 period. The format is the same as before: Karl Fairburne goes from mission to mission, aided by the resistance to foil the next Nazi plan. On his way he kills nazi soldiers, captains and leaders by stealth, melee kills, explosions or dropping things on them. Meanwhile he collects mementos and destroys the odd stone eagle.Changes since Sniper Elite 4 are the skills system and a more elaborate gun upgrade system using workbenches in-game. The rocks have made way for bottles and there are zip-lines now as well.There is more emphasis on multiplayer gameplay, but you can ignore it if you want. There is also a new game Defence game mode where you have to defend a position against waves of enemies.If you loved Sniper Elite 4, you cannot miss Sniper Elite 5. You will feel right at home.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: This is more Sniper Elite, with graphical improvements and some minor gameplay additions, the killcams seem downgraded somehow compared to SE4, there seems to be something wrong with the VRAM allocation as the game during a 1 hour play session takes up the whole 10GB VRAM on my GPU which doesn't seem normal as the game recommends a 6gb GPU, also the AA setting is still a mystery, on 1080p low AA looks better than high which isn't right, would love for them to implement a good TAA solution into the engine. Overall it's a good time sink, I've enjoyed these games ever since they transitioned into the HITMAN (2016) style level design, but it's not going to change your mind if you thought the previous entries were boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: This is the SE I always wanted after SE1 ;-)This is the sequel I've always expected in modern times and now I finally got it with a FOV slider. The FOV in SE2/3/4 made these games almost unplayable for me, there was no mod and Rebellion refused to address this issue for so long. But now we finally have it, an SE that really gives you all the freedom you've ever wanted and it's just a great game. I especially love these extremely large and detailed maps, made with so much attention to detail and hidden things. Depending on your playstyle, you can waste hours on a single mission. I personally prefer to play stealth with a bit of action here and there. Well, let's face it, the action happens when I do a stupid thing and all hell breaks loose, and that's where this game shines in my opinion. If that happens, it doesn't mess up the whole mission. It's always like having a small battlefield, on the larger battlefield. It's not realistic, but it's still fun. Nobody wants to lose their mission because of a mistake or reload afterwards. At least I personally like to live with my mistakes in this game and the game is perfectly designed for that. I have to mention it again, the maps are insanely cool, there is so much to discover, even beyond the side objectives. I can't imagine how much work it was to finish all these maps and make them work with everything on them. I haven't beaten the game yet, but now, after about 15 hours, I'm already giving it a 4/5 considering I had it on sale for only $17(Please no more SE without FOV slider)Peace ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: I had to retract my old review, this game is great. There are small details that need work. I doubted this game, even pre-ordered with that doubt, but this game is good. Really. I said that "open world" didn't work, but you only stick to a certain part of the map really, and it works well. You have out done yourselves with including all playstyles. I feel there only needs to be 2 ammo types, subsonic and regular. And I also feel the customization of weapons is a bit weird. Im a gun-nut, and the customization isn't bad, but its weird. Anyways, after starting mission 2, I feel like this game *is* good. The banter between the enemies is great. The graphics on medium are great, but it does run hot, and i mean *hot*. And the story feels a little forced, but still interesting. And yes, yes, yes! Karl finally has emotion. And the audio is great. I need to edit my review so much bc its all great. The first person experience is great as well, feels clean to pop grapes in first person. Rebellion still has some work to do, but they have proven that they are a good company.

_childDocuments_.review: I was kind of on the fence with this one. On one hand, I did enjoy it. On the other hand, some of the criticism in the other reviews are fair: it is a downgrade from SE4, and that's not what you would expect from a sequel. The un-reloadable, un-holsterable picked up weapons are arbitrary and annoying, and while the levels are still large, intricate and picturesque, *some* of them seem less open/more linear than they used to be, with less opportunities for actual sniping. I also feel like there's just overall less enemies in the game, or at least they are more sparsely placed around the maps - it's rare to find more than two germans within sight of each other, which makes clearing an entire level without firing a single shot almost trivial.With all this being said, it still feels and plays like Sniper Elite, so if you liked the previous games and craving for more, you should probably check this one out too. May wanna wait for a sale though.

The amount of bugs I have experienced is astonishing from kill list objectives not spawning or not completing despite doing what the game requires to animations not working correctly has made me just uninstall the game.Tiresome that developers think it's okay to release games riddled with bugs and don't seem to QA their games anymore before releasing it to the public for us to beta test for them so they can fix it in a patch later down the line.Sad because I have always enjoyed the Sniper Elite series.

The weapons are better than in previous games, the sounds are better, there is more customization and while it can be egregious with many made up and ugly options I appreciate many of the historical options.Something I found weird was how the vehicles were done. There are less different vehicles than in previous games and for some reason they decided that their only tank would be one of the heaviest the Germans fielded and also that all vehicles including this heavy tank could be destroyed with a SMG and a magazine with armour-piercing bullets.

A game brought to a dead stop by file size updates. The message boards and responses were huge to stop it, but they ignored everyone until the player base left, then went into panic mode and now literally broke the game completely for most of the players that were left.REbellion was my favorite developer, ZA,SE3,4, Strange brigade ect.. But ZA4 left a bad taste in my mouth and this disaster is one of those so huge that I'll likely ignore their future releases completely. That partially depends on if this is ever playable I guess, 100 bucks for a game I never even got to finish ,cant play and barely came with any content and they want me to purchase what they did release? . Rebellion still has some weird, confusing issues though that are a nuisance .First the good, some, not all the maps are amazing. The replay value will be great. The 3rd map "spy academy" my favorite . I won't go into tons of detail but generally quite fun.Not necessarily "bad" but more like "why? what is going on"Odd "open but not really open" world with very confusing barriers to stopping you. _childDocuments_.review: Initially I was debating on whether or not to refund the game. But after an hour and a half I decided to stick with it. Sniper Elite 5 is a more slow paced game for sure, contrary to its predecessors. Overall movement is more of an actual methodical pace of a sniper. Some will say that this game is a few steps back compared to Sniper Elite 4. In some ways it is. In other ways its better. Here is a quick Pro/Con.Pro:- Better Bullet Cam/X-Ray- Better Bullet Penetration and Bullet Origination (Meaning from Barrel and not HUD Crosshair)- Better Weapon Customization- Better Weapon Statistics- Better Ammo Stripping and Variety Ammo Types- Disposable Weapon Pickup- AI Ability to CQC Counter Melee Based on Training (Basic Officers and Infantry can't counter. Only Special Trained.)- Multi-platform Cross-play (When it works. I have, on a couple occasions, had a disconnect or two.)Con:- Missing Weapons (i.e. Mosin Nagant, M1 Garand, PPSH-41, m1897 Trench gun etc.)- 9 Base Game Mission Campaign (10 with Wolf Mountain DLC. Overall the game is short, though it does not lack detail.)- Only 3 Base Game Survival Maps- Movement While OTS Aiming is Really Slow (Specifically for SMG and Pistol, Sniper is alright.)- High CPU Usage If You Are a Mid/Low-end Content Creator/Streamer (Tweaking stream settings can help mitigate some of this.)- Rebellions Heavy Reliance on Adding Content as DLC (Specifically Weapons that would actually be in region), as well as Separate Season Passes  That is just a quick summary. Knowing Rebellion, they will most likely add some of the mentioned weapons as DLC. But the weapon variety for Snipers feels lacking. There are only 6 Rifles, 6 SMG's, and 6 Pistols (That's excluding the p.38 pre-order bonus). An interesting choice of numbers, but that is only for weapons you can choose for a load-out. However, they did add in the MG42 and PzB 38 Anti-Tank rifle and still have the Panzerfaust. I know this may sound ridiculous but I wish they could have added them into load-out customization to further broaden play-style aspects as well as open up an avenue for ambush operation tactics for both Campaign and Survival. The MG42 could function almost exactly as the Thompson since the Thompson has a 100rnd Drum mag and you could only carry 150rnd's of regular ammo total (Including Magazine) only differences are the obvious. Overall customization is nice, from variety of Scopes, Barrel Extensions and Muzzle Attachments to Magazine, Receiver and Grip Modifications. Each weapon features unique customization options. I like the addition of Bayonets as a muzzle attachment for snipers making CQC more of an option since it increases melee range. Cosmetics such as the Desert and Mastery paint-jobs feel uninteresting. And what I mean by that is, its better to keep your SMG and Pistol as default paint-job in that regard (Personally I don't care about flashy cosmetics like the gold Mastery skins from SE4, but more variety in cosmetics like the Cloth wrap or Ghillie wrap that help you blend in I'll take anytime). Character customization however is a yikes. With only being able to choose preset characters for Campaign, Survival and MP as well as only being able to choose a hat as a cosmetic is a bit of a letdown. Now I was not expecting to be able to customize like its an RPG. But being able to choose/edit your Uniform, Vest, Boots or whether or not you wanted a Ghillie suit for Campaign, especially since Axis Invaders get to use a Ghillie or try to blend in as an AI, would definitely add in an interesting or little more intense Cat and Mouse experience. When I think Character customizing, I think Rainbow Six Vegas 2. Axis Invasion certainly is an interesting new twist for Sniper Elite. It can definitely be jokingly compared to Dark Souls. But I still need a better understanding on how the invasion occurs. Whether it is just something that can happen at any moment, or is based on if an alarm is triggered. I would err on the side of caution and assume that it is something that can happen any moment while enabled. But what I do know is that you can gain more XP with the risk than without it. And no XP is not throttled if you choose to disable it because you can reach max level quite easily with it disabled. From what I have also seen the game-mode seems to penalize you for camping while being invaded. For balancing reasons I can understand intel-gathering for both the Target player and the Invading player. But if the AI are completely unaware and not alerted then there should be no information relayed to the Invader about the Target player until they do something to make themselves known. It would be a good idea if the invasion mode was based on your play style. Meaning if you were to be stealthy and never trigger alarms or get into prolonged active combat, you would be less likely to get invaded. And for doing so you would be rewarded even more XP for being a True Shadow, at least as an idea that would be great if they did it that way. Overall I enjoy the game-play. The new areas give me more variety of environment, and if I ever feel like a change of scenery I won't have to go back to previous titles unless I felt like it. I will say that most of your 1000 hours (I doubt many will spend over 500 hours, but there are those that will) will encompass collecting and completing the challenge medals for campaign if you are a completionist or perfectionist. But everyone is different when it comes to personal preference. I would recommend that if you are on the fence and not sure if it would be worth the regular price to get this, then wait for it to go on sale.Edit: Aldo would be proud though.Edit2: Another thing I have noticed is complaints about Wind having little to no affect on Trajectory until you get later in the game with long distance. I would like to point out that More Muzzle Velocity = Less Wind Deflection. Which makes sense that anything within a 500meter or 546.8yards distance will have some to no effect on trajectory if the Weapon Power is maxed out. The trade off would be more recoil, so overall weapons seem to handle more realistically (Despite missing other varying factors like temp and moisture). And Sniper Elite, while sniping is part of the entree, has been more of a Tactical Espionage Assassination Sniping game rather than Modern Based Long Distance Sniping game like Sniper Ghost Warrior series (Good game btw, Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 1&2 Redeemed the series a bit).

_childDocuments_.review: It’s Sniper Elite. There’s some new additions here as with every new addition to the series. But it’s more or less the same visceral, satisfying action game you remember.The biggest change is the idea of invasions -- other players busting down your door mid-game, usually as you’re carefully infiltrating a nazi mansion, or gunning down a blockade. Always a little inopportunely. Always a little too frequently. And always a serious monkey wrench in your machinery.I love it. It fits the rest of the ethos perfectly. These games have always been about embracing a bit of chaos. Sure, it disturbs the otherwise meticulous and predictable gameplay. But it’s all about being allowed to play and improvise. It’s not really a puzzle, even if you can treat it as one. But you can throw caution to the wind too. You’re allowed to bring out the big guns one moment, and recede into the darkness the next. No one makes you feel bad, or lectures you about how to play. In fact, the game implores you to explore both its world and all the mechanisms and systems.Invasions embrace that, turning games into heart-throbbing cat-and-mouse rounds. Both parties with itchy trigger fingers; knowing full-well that every missed shot, unnatural movement, or revealing glare from your scope gives you away. It’s tense. It’s fun. But it’s also a serious distraction and padding to your overall play time -- for better or for worse.Recommended, if you enjoy Sniper Elite.

_childDocuments_.review: By comparison with the last offering (SE4), this game is a disappointment.  If you can start the game at all (lots of reports that people can't), and if you play without crashing (lots of people complaining about crashes), and if you can put up with bugs that are being "looked into" for months, and if you can run the game long enough for memory leaks not to send you crashing, then you can play.Survival mode is a disappointment, lacks the luster SE4 had for replayability, and has coding issues where sometimes poor spawns or out-of-bounds vehicles end your game.  Also too few maps.The maps are beautiful in most cases, but there is repetition (designer laziness) in some of them and you are not as free as you'd like to be.Wind effects do not compare with SE4 unfortunately, and also there is no authentic plus mode, both of which make the game less challenging than most would welcome.Weapon modifications are too complex and silly, too overdone.  And some weapons that should appear do not.The game is geared towards console warriors, and the game is cross-platform.  PC Steam users do not get the attention of the developers in the forums.  The most you will get is some lame acknowledgement (sometimes, not the majority of time either) that they read the issue, then you get told to contact support, who does nothing in most cases.Updates are still 40 GB and up, all the time.  "We are working on it"Most maps are not sniper-generous.I enjoyed the single player campaign, but replayability is not as good as SE4.  It is replayable, but not as good.  If you play multiplayer, be prepared for a host of cheaters and disappointments there, IMO mostly because of all the console action that is now in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall while it can be fun and engaging, it feels like the soul of the game with the long-range shots has severely degraded. Worth picking up if on sale, but definitely not worth full price. Reasons below: This edition of the series could far more accurately be called PISTOL Elite 5. Mostly thanks to the weapon customization list being larger than ever, and expanded to include the secondary weapon and sidearms. That very customization is what nearly kills the primary weapon of the sniper rifle. The vast majority of engagements here in 5 tend to max out at only 100m, and thanks to even more ledges, vines and pipes than ever before, you can very easily close to under 20m from nearly every hostile with very little effort. Additionally maps are much, much smaller than previous titles, many of the achievement "Long Shots" struggle to break 500m, conversely many shots in Sniper Elite 4 that were normal (not achievement specific) could easily break 800m without even trying; so the maps are roughly 50% the size of SE4.Overall difficulty was tuned down. Playing on "Authentic difficulty" is much closer to Sniper Elite 4's Hard, while SE4's Authentic and Authentic Plus are far more challenging than anything available as yet on 5. Additionally there was another low difficulty added, which could better be described as "Games Journalist", which is even easier than Recruit. So all the difficulties in SE5 are on average 1-2 steps lower than previous titles.On the plus side:-enhanced graphics, gorgeous views if you stop and just look out over the terrain-voice acting was pretty good and the scripts didn't quite feel as cheesy as previous titles.-The Big Bad Nazi Officer in charge is also the smartest one in any Sniper Elite title yet. He genuinely understands he's in trouble and tries to run rather than take Karl on in a 1v1. Every prior title they fight to the last man, trying to stop us and acting like they won, so kudos to FINALLY having an intelligent foe.-As mentioned the customization is both very bad (too much emphasis on secondary/pistol) but the primary modifications are great too so its a double-edged sword.-Invasion mode: wasn't very fun at launch when any random schmuck could join and hunt you, and hackers were very quick to make it very much not fun to play with Invasion mode enabled. But the Devs eventually added the ability to set it to friends-only, which makes this title extremely fun for playing with and against friends.

_childDocuments_.review: "Let me start by saying that Karl Fairburne is one of the coolest characters in video games. He doesn't use cringe-worthy or awkward dialogue that makes me cringe and drop the game. He's pretty cool, and I also like his attire. So, the main character gets a solid 9/10 from me.I appreciate that there isn't a lengthy and complicated tutorial in the game. Instead, you have a short and straightforward tutorial before diving into the game. I give this aspect an 8/10 because overly complex and long tutorials can make a first-person shooter boring. However, I had a slight issue with not knowing how to heal initially. It might have been my mistake for missing it, but it would be helpful if the game explained which button to press for healing.The variety of guns in the game is fantastic, and I like that the game explains their historical usage in a simple and concise manner. It's impressive, and I've learned about guns I never knew were used. The fact that guns can make different noises depending on their loudness adds depth to gameplay. So, this aspect gets a perfect 10/10.I admire that Sniper Elite 5 includes elements that many other AAA games wouldn't dare to touch, unlike titles like Call of Duty. The game provides an authentic World War II experience, and even using terms like 'Nazi' and featuring the Nazi flag was surprising to me, as many games have avoided them since 2005. I appreciate that the game uses accurate terms like 'Fritz,' 'Heinies,' or 'Kraut.' It feels more genuine than generic labels like 'bad guys' or 'evil people.' This aspect deserves a 10/10 for its boldness and respect for historical accuracy.Thank you for giving German voice actors a chance. It makes the characters feel genuinely German, unlike Ubisoft, who didn't use Swedish actors for Assassin's Creed Valhalla. This approach often results in incorrect pronunciations and disconnects from the culture. Kudos to Sniper Elite 5 for giving voice actors from the respective countries a chance, and I appreciate that effort. It makes me happy to see this attention to detail.I also love how the soldiers' dialogue feels like it's meant for them, making the game feel more real and immersive. It's a subtle but important touch that adds to the overall experience.Moreover, when you press 'B' to use your binoculars for scouting, and you can see their names and some personal information, it adds a layer of complexity to the game. Sometimes, it can make you feel conflicted about taking a shot, depending on what you've learned about them. It adds an emotional dimension to the gameplay that can be both engaging and thought-provoking.Regarding bugs or lag, I purchased the game a bit late, so I can't comment on its early state. However, I didn't encounter any major bugs, just some minor issues like soldiers occasionally bunny hopping or having creepy, open mouths. So, I'd rate it 8/10 for the relatively smooth experience.I like the game's map and how it creates an immersive environment that isn't empty. It's great that you can find items scattered around. However, I did notice that some areas are inexplicably blocked, which was a bit confusing. So, I'd give this aspect a 7/10.The menu design is good; gray and blue colors work well, and it's simple and visually appealing. While it's not a big deal, it could be interesting to see different menu designs for various locations in the game. So, the menu gets an 8/10.Overall, Sniper Elite 5 offers a solid gaming experience with a few minor quirks, making it an enjoyable addition to the series. Its historical accuracy, including the use of the Nazi flag, adds an extra layer of authenticity to the game. The immersive dialogue of the soldiers adds to the realism, making the game truly engaging. The personal details you discover about enemies while using binoculars adds an emotional dimension that deepens the gameplay experience."
