_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a hardcore sniper player so the criticisms from more expert players don't apply to me. I spent I think 67 hours to complete the game at mid-level and I thought it was great. Perhaps some areas were a bit too sparsely guarded but you just need to up the expertise level. I thought it was just as good as SE4 (maybe better, if you exclude the DLC) and well worth it if you buy on sale. And much better value than a cinema ticket. I also read ALL the credits at the end -a truly international piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: Might be my favorite Sniper Elite. The maps are more beautiful than ever, and are worth exploring not so much for story lore, but for items and, regrettably, some item unlocks.As usual, the guns are sold separately, but guns in the SE games aren't really the focus for me. The quality and the depth of the gameplay is what matters, and frankly I like the idea of the base game being a somewhat smaller sandbox. It feels old-school game-y. On Authentic, the challenge is really strong but never overwhelming.Fighting as a commando with french resistance just feels so right. The story is better written and acted than past Sniper Elite games. I probably won't rewatch these story cutscenes after 1st playthrough, because SE stories are always *IN A DEEP VOICE* I'm a sniper. "Oh you are?" YES. "Huh, here's what I think about that. Go blow this thing up now. Thanks."The level design is the real highlight. Gameplay flows into setpieces and the updated movement system brings the stealth gameplay up to Last of Us 2 levels, but in open levels. Obviously the animation system within the game, for Karl and the AI, still looks stiff and somewhat outdated in comparison, but Last of Us 2 cost $220 million. SE5 cost less, and needed to make money back via DLC, but the base game is already very strong. Put on a better soundtrack and it's a near-perfect WW2 stealth shooter. Overall rating, 4/5. Loses points just for the movement still feeling jank in areas. Rebellion can't seem to figure out a perfect non-floaty movement system. My hope for the next Sniper Elite is to have a true next-gen movement system. Karl still feels a bit like a robot with a rifle, but that doesn't stop the level design from shining through.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: I may just have spend as much time in the first mission than in all 3 (three!) real ones of Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 together. No joke, that might about be realistic.  With about as many enemies in that first level alone as in all of SGWC2 . And there are 8 bigger and vastly more complex missions in SE5 (and a small one). Also SE5 doesn't have SGWC2's 20+launch Weapon and Skin DLC.  So instantly a better look and less exploitative feel.  But of course SE5 was just begging for a (completely avoidable) ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ by gating the usual kill-Hitler DLC behind pre-ordering. Will they ever learn?Issues like the still very limited movement and object interaction systems. Like(no)  jumping or moving gas canisters (aka bombs) to strategic locations. Or using doors...  Instead still concrete canisters and some impenetrable obstacles that don't feel like they should be. A clear and completely unnecessary change for the worse is the new, very limited weapon pickup system. I absolutely don't understand why they did that and what was wrong wth just swapping your weapons.  That makes no sense.You can still pick them up as 4th, temporary weapon but they are just dropped when switching to your loadout ones that you can only change at workbenches to very few unlocked other ones Those are at least nicely customisable.I don't care much for the new online "Axis invasion" feature. I guess it's a nice option to have if it works and doesn't get annoying. Can't judge, have it off. Only annyoing that some items are locked behind that feature. On that topic a big bonus point for just having a simple checkbox option to disable the the Easy Anti Cheat spyware*. Instead of needing launch parameters, file renames or no way at all. Forcing EAC down your throat (unnecessarily!) has become a absolute pest in recent (mostly) single player games*Only the privileges people give willingly to EAC in their windows are a wet dream for any spyware.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, just like Sniper Elite 4 was to 3, Sniper Elite 5 is basically just more Sniper Elite 4. If you enjoyed 4, you'll enjoy 5, and the much larger environments and generally more content is worth the price of entry.What I especially like, that I don't remember being the case in the earlier entries, is that the game actually shoves the DLC away in its own menu instead of being front-and-center in every menu option you see. From the inventory to the bonus stages, unless you actively go to seek out the DLC you're not going to see a bunch of locked-off options in your menu. After coming from Zombie Army 4, where 90% of the content was all DLC and just taunted you with how little content you owned for buying the game, Sniper Elite 5 gives you a healthy amount of stuff to unlock, and your inventory isn't cluttered with things you don't own just for buying the base game.Dumb reason to give it a positive review, I know, but it was refreshing.What I really don't like is the return of the ability to see enemy backstories by zooming in on them. For a game that markets itself as the game where you get to shoot Hitler in the balls, not only is that feature DLC (like it always is), but it takes the fun out of shooting Nazis in brutal ways when more then half of them are given sympathetic backstory text blurbs.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: I noticed a lot of reviews mentioning glitches. I personally have not had an issue with the game play, so I guess they have fixed the problems other players were having.  I have played every Sniper Elite game since the beginning and have enjoyed this as much as the the others. There is a axis attack mode that you can allow in your game play, I didn't even know what that was until a player requested a rematch.  Basically other players can enter your game while your playing and try to take you out, kind of a cool idea.  9 maps with lots of enemies and challenges along the way,  each map has 19 items you need to find and some are in very odd places. I have only found all 19 on 1 map so there is a challenge in that aspect of the game. I found the game to be fun and entertaining and the graphics have come a long way, much better than some of the games coming out today.  If you like FPS games where you only depend on yourself I highly recommend Sniper Elite 5.

_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: For once I find myself in amazement at the Steam reviews for this. I bought it because I enjoyed SE4, and the reviews were mostly positive. Could not disagree more.Note: This game needs a LOT of work, and Rebellion needs to seriously consider getting back to the basics and listening to their players. They always used to be responsive to player input and prompt with support tickets in SE3 & 4, now there are rampant reports of them being completely ignored.This game is just not fun to play, and I'm on PC, while half the bugs are on console. Didn't even make it through the first level before I quit.Karl pops out of cover for no reason. In a stealth sniping game.Noise radius of rifles is grossly inaccurate. Got heard by enemies 300-400 meters away with a rifle rated for 96 meters.Vehicles, especially gunboats, are now bullet sponges.When trying to hide an enemy body, Karl strolls along like he *wants* to get spotted. Why would I hide a body and stand up straight as possible and make a huge *THUD* noise when hiding it?Sound masks are few and far between and now must now be created purely through sabotaging equipment. As a result a common complaint is that their pistol and knife get used often when the rifle hasn't even left its sling.SE4 basically eased you into the game, making gradually harder and harder missions. The first map is damn near impossible not to get spotted. Constant invisible walls often force you to walk on roads with frequent traffic if you want to get to the vantage point early. with absolutely nowhere to hide. Speaking of hiding, apparently the only place to do it is tall grass, which Karl repeats ad nauseum "this will be good to hide in" but crouching in a bush does absolutely nothing, if you can even walk through the bush."Play your way" is one of the first things said about this game, and it's less true than ever. It's no coincidence that all the featured images for this game are open combat or with a pistol/SMG in your hand except one. The game forces you into choke points, half the map is not usable, and generally makes trying to remain in stealth such a pain that the SMG comes out more often than your sniper rifle.Apparently non-lethal takedowns of Nazis gives you more XP than lethal ones. In a war. That the Allies are desperately trying to put to an end. Against Nazis (I know not all of them are Nazis). The game takes it further by making a point to humanize the enemies much, much more than it did in the past with their backstories. If there is a game that should encourage taking out as many enemies as possible, this is it. This isn't Hitman where the ideal goal is to make it look like nothing ever happened and the only death is the target which happened by accident. It's to leave a silent trail of death in your wake without being seen.Many other bugs reported such as getting stuck in walls, stuck in reload animations, guns getting stuck in the ground, bullet drops and travel that often have you aiming 4 inches away and below the enemy (on the first level). Zeroing your rifle isn't even mentioned unless you go looking for it.TL;DR: I'd give this a 3/10. It's playable, the graphics are good, and they put some effort to make it not SE4 DLC, but not much, and it did more harm than good. I feel bad for the console players. If I was on console it would be a 2 at best.

_childDocuments_.review: The ability to get in to a players campaign and hunt them is incredible265 hours in. I am a casual older gamer. Hell, I played World of Warships for hundreds of hours. It got too toxic. I get off work around midnight, I might do a few beers after work, I may come right home. Either way, I get immersed in the game. Before I know it, it's 4:00 am. The graphics are nice, the sound as well. It's enjoyable. I've purchased all the missions as far as I know. I just finished the Kraken awakes. By far that has been my favorite. A critical review? I'll say not being able to climb over a lot things is ridiculous. There are things you can do in some places but not others. I know there are limits the programmers have to include but it would be nice if you could climb over a lot of things. A box in front of front of a stairway after I just climbed up a vine trellis or scaled some crates? I should be able to get over the box. The enemy AI, yeah, not consistent. I know they wanted unique experiences and give you weapons options, but I do not agree with all the damage the weapons provide. Regardless, the game is pretty, the world is large, the tidbits about enemy soldiers you watch with binoculars is a treat. Rebellion, thank you for a good game and I look forward to your next download. I have to say, I enjoyed the Hell out of "The Kraken Awakes"!

_childDocuments_.review: I actually was hesitant to play Sniper Elite 5 based on the reviews being left. Particularly complaints about the game attempting to be "Woke" by putting Characters of Color or females as resistance fighters throughout france. But this is actually decently accurate to how things were at the time. With the French Governement offering citizenship to people willing to fight, this still continues with the French Foreign Legon today. The Shooting Mechanics of the game are just as satisfying as players of previous games would remember. My only complaint is some lack of polish of some of the buildings. Where I might melee an enemy from a doorway and pull them through the doorframe because of the animation, or be standing inside of a nearby wall. I also have occasionally ran across areas where I might see between textures and seen the sky where I clearly shouldn't.  Still overall the game is a satisfying experience and the Survival mission (When playing with friends) is fantastic. Can't say I'm a fan of intrusions by other players, but the setting to turn those off is easy enough to find in the settings.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. However since I am a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, here are some complaints:-Climbing over stuff is very inconsistent. Some barriers and walls which you should totally able to climb aren't and some are. You can't jump over a lot of tiny obstacles-The map Saint Denis is awful. It looks stunning but the design sucks. You gotta work your way up the city, which is overly hard because you never got any high ground. Every building looks kinda the same aswell.-Despite great graphics, the antialiasing is still awful. This has been an issue since the last game and they didn't fix it. Even at high resolutions and upscaling, the whole screen flickers from the lack of proper antialiasing.-In some points of maps, there is literally zero cover. I got stuck near the beach and there was literally only one way out with 0 bushes and 0 walls or rocks. Each time I loaded the save I got overrun by enemies and there was only one path out of there. There are multiple location where this can happen. Again, I think this is kind of a map design flaw.-There are less sound masking options for the sniper rifle than in SE4. Generators are rare and the occasional plane and artillery fire also don't occur very often. I ended up using a rifle with a built in suppressor, which as a downside has a terrible range.-A.I. can be very unfair at times. They can track you through walls even when you're not spotted.-The DLC's, as already mentioned by other players, are way too expensive. Most of them are not worth it anyways (a ♥♥♥♥♥ skin and a gun for 10 bucks).Overall I enjoyed Sniper Elite 4 and 5 the most. The map design of both games is comparable I'd say. It has its flaws and I wish you had even more options to kill enemies, like in other stealth titles such as Hitman.

_childDocuments_.review: ProsVariable Difficulty. True sniper aim is now separate from the enemy difficulty. I'm not a fan of the bullet drift mechanic and I am not looking for a realistic sniping experience. I want my bullet to go where I aim. But that doesn't mean I want the enemies to always be easy either. In SE4, in order to disable true aim, you were forced to run in easy mode. Difficulty settings have been split up so you can choose easy aim with difficult enemies.Non-lethal ammo and take-downs. When I first saw these, I passed them by as useless. Boy was I wrong. Knocking out enemies causes nearby soldiers to investigate rather than freak out when they see their comrades being killed. Extremely useful in an area filled with enemy soldiers.4th weapon. Yep, keep your perfect load-out and when you see that tank buster, you can pick it up in addition to your 3 custom weapons.Melee attacks. In higher difficulties, if an enemy knows where you are, your melee attack will not always work! They can break your attack wasting your time while reinforcements arrive. ConsNo more unlimited satchel charges. You have to search for them.No more unlimited rocks to throw to cause distractions. Now you have to find and collect bottles.Vehicle destruction is now very difficult. Gone are the single shot destruction of trucks and cars.The maps are large and interesting...but imho, not as interesting as in SE4. Some areas the enemies are feast or famine. There are large areas with no enemies and small areas with many enemies.Harder to spot enemies. You will be relying on your radar far more in this game. Enemies show up as a large circle on your radar before they are tagged. Once tagged, the circle disappears. Sometime the large circle makes it easier to spot an enemy than when they are tagged.

_childDocuments_.review: The Campaign may be pretty bland, but Sniper Elite 5 is very much an iterative sequel that builds upon what players already enjoy about the series without focusing too much on the innovation. That being said, x-ray vision headshots and invading players who just want to have a good time are both well worth the price of admission for a sniper tour of France.Pros-------- Axis Invasions are addictive Dark Souls-esque PVP invasions- Each map is a unique miniature sandbox- Cross-play and Cross-Platform- The return of the internal x-ray gunshot killcams- Freely tweakable difficulty settings including health regeneration, wind, and bullet drop- Only 9 campaign missions (10 with the Wolf Mountain DLC) makes it short but sweetCons-------- Separate unlock progression across Campaign, Multiplayer, and Axis Invasions- Most weapon and attachments are locked behind either collectibles or kill counts, depending on mode- Assassinating Hitler is locked behind DLC- Large amounts of downtime and sprinting around oversized maps to find your next target or objectiveWhile going back to World War II might not be on the top of players' minds when it comes to a new shooter, the new Axis Invasion mode brings Dark Souls competitive PVP to a stealth series in a way that might be impossible to top.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: As a baseline the game is conceptually nice, however it needs a solid round of patching and QOL improvements.Graphics haven't changed much, rendering is mostly same. Assets have been upgraded through use of photogrammetry which greatly improves look of everything except foliage, shading is bit outdated and antialiasing is non existant. Performance is also mostly okay although much like SE4, lack of benchmark on game launch makes synthetic testing and fine-tuning harder.Gameplay is about as good as SE4 is, couple of things got streamlined for better or worse. My biggest issues are with how clunky player handling is as every interaction seems to have a hefty delay before it's actually executed, turn radius is huge and causes issues indoors.Level design seems to be sidestep from SE4, levels are slightly bigger than in previous game and more detailed (especially urban parts) but they also rely on having a lot of areas that aren't technically accessible to the player, very often you cannot travel from point A to point B in a straight line as you'll encounter large patches of inaccessible areas in the middle, sometimes they make sense and sometimes they don't, like patch of farmland fenced off with hip high rocks and bushes.AI i don't particularly mind, it's also an improvement from SE4, stealth is even more viable although enemies are easy to pick off outside actual combat and even if combat breaks out it's easy and way more preferable to run away and come back once they settle down. As far as actual combat is, they are way more deadlier than in previous games.Audio is also a genuine improvement, it doesn't blow competition out of the water but there are now way more distinct weapon sounds, for up close and distance shots plus some nice reverbs which are sometimes used in interiors.The new featured gamemode of axis invasions is a mixed bag which sounds great on paper but doesn't play out half as fun in practice. Majority of the time people either are ignorant of the fact that they're invaded and you can pick them off with ease while at another end of the spectrum people will stop dead in their tracks and entrench in one position for as long as they can or outright commit suicide or kick you out of their session. In general the mode has very, very little to do with sniping duels as majority of kills will be in close quarters range.This also leads into topic of netcode for peer to peer modes like Invasions and Survival/Coop, which is atrocious (and has been for many entries in the series now). It flat out doesn't work, there's a huge delay on everything and players/enemies teleport every now and then. In coop modes this is perhaps a minor annoyance but in invasions it means difference between victory and defeat.In terms of bugs - there are several, none of them gamebreaking but they can prevent you from completing achievements and getting weapon rewards. On my machine performance and stability is OK.Perhaps biggest and "wonkiest" change in my eyes are new ragdolls which seem to die in very similar but also very unlikely gymnasitc positions like frog squats, heads between legs, trying to suck themselves off and so on and so forth. The frequency of how often each of those repeats is so consistent i consider it a deliberate feature at this point.In general the game isn't a necessarily a huge evolutional step for the franchise, it has a potential to be a much refined version of SE4. Provided the develoers sit down on it and implement several much needed features and fixes to further polish the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: With Sniper Elite 5 completed, I have now all SE Games (except Part #1 - it is just too old/clunky) completed and am now able to say the last one is the best of them. The levels are great designed and there are always a lot of ways to solve the instructions. A few optional tasks are added to each mission, as well as a new kind of task: Kill a named guy within the area using as specific way. This can be via an explicit gun type or to e.g. throw somebody in wet concrete. I have completed each mission with all side missions, which took me 21 hrs - whereby this includes the sneaky gameplay. If SE is played like a shooter it will be most likely way shorter.Graphics are, as well as the Music/FX, good and the story is also better as in the previous parts - even though most of the parts are not historical correct.SE5 is also the first part in the series which came 100% uncut to Germany, which increased the immersion a bit, too.I would recommend this SE part to everyone who is interested in this kind of games and to everybody who had fun with the previous parts!

seen. etc etc etc. why am i walking around with weapons silenced into the dirt if im getting seen doing things that shouldnt get me caught (minus .5 stealth). bit of a minor gripe i suppose but _childDocuments_.review: I love the Sniper Elite series, but they certainly messed up this time around.For starters, the game plays like a generic action-stealth MGS V  clone, instead of a Sniper Elite game. 99% of all combat takes played within 50 meters, making rifles pretty useless compared to a pistol. The maps are also lacking in verticality, which is bizarre for a sniping game.Also, in the past you could take a shot on Hard difficulty and the enemy would only be alerted. Take a few shots, and they would pinpoint your location. Only on Authentic difficulty would the enemy immediattely pinpoint your position and run towards you en masse. In Sniper Elite 5, now a single shot will immediately alert the enemy of your exact position, making sniper kills only viable from a few pre-orchastrated locations (the ones with a soundmasking generator). This means that apart from a few pre-orchastrated locations, you’ll be using the silenced pistol for the entire game.They’ve also removed S-mines and Trip Mines from the game, to “streamline” the experience for new plyers. In previous Sniper Elites, you could cover your sniping location by laying those mines in doorways/stairs/etc and could make some really awesome traps that way.Now the opportunity of trap laying is gone since you only have 2 teller mines at your disposal. What makes this even worse is that they’ve convoluted the game with all kinds of new ammo types, all of them having no de-facto advantage over the normal and subsonic ammo. They’ve also added the Shu-mine, a non-lethal mine.However, playing non-lethal has no advantage whatsoever, since the total XP you get from that playstyle is always lower than playing lethal. You can also no longer replace your weapons with enemy weapons. Enemy weapons now function as disposable items; You can finish off the magazine and than they’ll disappear, Use your own weapon or item and the character will drop the enemy weapon. What makes matters worse is that there are a ton or rifles, smg’s and pistols in the game, but the player has only a handful of them in the load-out screen! Why create so many types of rifles, smg’s and pistols if the player can’t use them? The new weapon customization sounds great in theory, but the difference in stats are so little that it basically has zero use. What makes it worse is that they’ve removed all the different reticles you could select in previous SE games. Why would you do that? Why would you remove the Sniper out of Sniper Elite, and replace it with generic MGS/CoD stuff?Also, the new X-ray vision looks graphically great, but all the added veins and muscles make it impossible to discern the organs and bones from it, so the X-ray vision is less conveying in damage and gore than the X-ray vision in Sniper Elite 3 and 4.There is also an issue with enemy bodies disappearing. To unlock a new weapon, you must kill a high-ranking officer in a specific way. My tactic of preference is to pacify the officer and kill all other enemies in the area so the killing of the officer by explosion/falling objects/etc makes no sound.However, bodies disappear very quickly after pacifying or killing them, so that officer you pacified is disappeared by the time you come back to him. You can also no longer wait to loot the body of an enemy, since the body will disappear ASAP.What is strange is that this was an issue in Sniper Elite 3 as well, and fixed in Sniper Elite 4. Why did they revert back to a known game problem?If you love generic action games, buy this game for a few bucks after all the DLC’s have come out.If you love Sniper Elite, stay clear of this entry.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played Sniper Elite 4, 3 and 2 (in that order), and I was a big fan of 3 and 4. Sniper Elite 5 is quite similar in many aspects, and it keeps the game loop where you probably want to be stealthy, as well as taking advantage of opportunities (such as noisy places) to snipe. But it also adds nice progression elements, such as useful skills you can unlock, as well as weapons and weapon parts.As on the others, sniping can be trivial or a bit hard, depending on the difficulty you pick. There are also extra difficulty options.Graphics are much better (although cutscenes still look sub-par), and there are a few extra modes, including multiplayer.Problems were minor - sometimes FPS will drop (using a 3070 at 4k) to 20s for a few seconds (mostly always at 60FPS with VSYNC), I get a weird flicker on movement, and the pre game setup is slightly broken with large fonts.So far it seems like a major advance, and a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same and the same is good.If you have never played this series, you could try the fourth as it is very similar and much cheaper but you cant go wrong with this game. A forgiving balance of stealth/sniper and combat, even if it is designed for stealth. Think Hitman but WWII.AI is easier than hard, maybe kind of dumb sometimes, but I was playing on sharpshooter setting (medium), because I want to have fun, not play darksouls so higher difficulties might address some of those issues (stuff like finding a body or getting shot at and then 30 seconds later, oh welp, guess we are good).Map design is good, allowing lots of approaches. It really rewards full exploration as many secondary objectives are hidden around the map. Graphic are pretty much the same as the fourth, including the death animations this game is so famous for, though I cant help but think they are a little less impressive this time around. A few changes like no longer having the ability to shoot grenades on a soldier's belt and they removed a few of the one shot kill spots on vehicles, don't really reduce the enjoyment. Not a run and gun game but pretty forgiving if you do end up in a fire fight. Enemies don't respawn per sey but there are areas where it seems like vehicles keep coming along a certain route until you get to a certain point in the mission. The invasion feature, similar to Deathloop's, is fine and doesn't seem to mess with your overall progress in the mission. It happens at least once and sometimes more per mission. It is a little irritating if you are focused and enjoying the mission and suddenly you have to drop everything and go hide/hunt for this sniper and you know the only people who do the invasions are cheap sweat boys who have all the time in the world. You can disable it but there is an XP bonus if you don't.An easy buy if you liked the previous games or anything in the hitman series.
_childDocuments_.name: Sniper Elite 5

_childDocuments_.review: This series has evolved and grown a lot. I honestly didn't like the first 3. 4 was ok, but this is actually pretty good. Secondary missions appear and evolve as the primary mission happens, just like real time warfare targets of 'opportunity' are found and become things you can do or not do. I like this format a lot, it feels organic. The sniper cam is cool, but just like previous titles only the first 10 or 12 times you get it. After awhile it's clear regardless of how you shoot there are only a handful of headshot sequences you're going to get. My biggest issue with this game, remains my biggest issue with the series. Except for headshots, guns don't do proper damage. I cannot count how many times I've nailed an enemy center of the chest and they are stunned, but re-compose themselves and remain combat effective. This is World War 2. There was no body armor or bullet proof vests, if a Kar98 hits you in the chest, you're dead. Sometimes helmets deflect bullets and I'll buy that, it did happen. But he game has some broken math, for instance the .45 pistol, if not a headshot, takes roughly 3 shots to kill and enemy in the chest. The .45 thompson sub machine gun, firing the SAME bullets but faster, takes 5+ shots to kill the same enemy. That's not how weapons work, firing faster doesn't mean less dangerous. Finally, and this is trivial, I was super heart broken to see the anti-tank rifle A) fires a tiny round instead of a big proper sized bullet, someone messed up on that and B) does NOT make people explode on impact, the bullets hit with the same force as the normal rifles which is entirely incorrect, you hit someone with a round made for a tank and they pop. 5 games into the series and it still feels like there is room to grow and some basic things should be understood about how firearms work. BUT, at the end it actually is a fun game even if the maps are a bit tediously large and laid out.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the Sniper Elite series, then you cant go wrong with this newest entry in the franchise. Some mechanics have changed, but still stays true to its roots. If you jump in to a game that has been almost completed and has 2 other players, the axis player gets killed almost every time. Fun for now but i suspect will get long in the tooth down the road. Still all in all, a very good entry into the franchise!!

_childDocuments_.review: I like it, despite its many, many flaws. Sure, the whole game ought to be a better game than it is. But the essence: unhurried sneaking around and head-shotting a finite number of bad guys from a safe distance is something I really enjoy. And it's fun too, when you miss too often and are forced to fight. The two co-op modes are campaign and survival. I’ve played a lot of survival with my brother, and with only 2 players on 4-player maps, it’s challenging enough to be fun – we get wiped out often enough :-) There are five survival maps to choose from. Each asks the players to repel (usually) 3 waves of Germans at a series of 4 command/ammo-resupply posts. Each map has a choice of 3-5 operations, that put the command posts in different places, so the survival games can feel quite different even on the same maps. Sadly, in SE5, no maps allow a long-ranged sniping game.(And FYI, the steadiest way to join a friend's co-op game is for him to set up a lobby (For example: Play, Survival, Host) then for him to click on his own name in the top right to reveal an invite code. You click on your own name, see a form where you can type in his invite code, and you can now join your friend, even in a private game, even if you suffer a disconnect later...so long as you still have the code written down.)The graphics are improved from SE4. Lots of green. Better faces. The settings are much more beautiful than say, L4D2 or Killing Zone, or most maps of World War Z. The voice-acting is good. The story, well...Sniper Elite stories are terrible :-)And the user interface is still crap. It is adapted from a console layout. One example: stand/crouch/prone is controlled by one key instead of three. A second example: you select an item with one key, on a radial menu, then apply/use/deploy the item with a different shared key. Why a different key? Worse, the game won't let you select an empty item slot, and if you run out of an item, it auto-switches you to another item you still have in stock. So, many times I've selected a bandage, not realised I had no bandage, or had just run out of bandages, and instead of healing myself, I lobbed the explosive which had popped into my never-allowed-to-be-empty hand. Another example, but this is avoidable: the default hold breath key is the space bar. (Try assigning Breath-hold to shift.) With default settings, you often press space when NOT yet in scope, and when not in scope, space means hop over the cover in front of you...so you jump over a railing or wall in front of you and hang from it in full view of the enemy. Shared function keys.(Just played some SE4. The F key isn’t so over-used. There are different keys for searching a corspe, using equipment, defusing a mine, or picking up a discarded weapon. Ammo is automatically picked up.)Oh! I forgot. When your chosen cover is a bit too tall, you can observe over it, look downrange through your gun's scope, but cannot shoot. I simply had to stand before shooting, but there was NO indication of why I could not shoot. Similarly, my brother ran out of special ammo once and thought his main rifle was glitched - he had plenty of regular ammo but the game would not let him fire that weapon again until he switched ammo-type manually.YouTube reviews are ambivalent about the new maps. They are more closely based on real environments than SE4, so there aren't as many long sniping opportunities. The new maps do feel more real. And that's nice. But the SE5 maps also feel more cramped. At distances under 100 meters, wind and bullet drop are somewhat insignificant, so the biggest skill in SE4, aiming your rifle over 100m, taking bullet drop and wind into your estimate, rarely becomes necessary.In SE5, the combat distances are so short that aim-assist is turned on by default, except at the hardest difficulty, since aim-assist doesn't make much difference most of the time. Happily, one can customise the difficulties fairly finely, and turn off the aim-assist if one prefers to play that way. I think it's MUCH better. (With no aim assist, it feels GREAT when you get a head-shot over a 150m in a strong cross wind.) Unhappily, the fine difficulty management is really uneven. For example, in SE5 you can tune the mine defusal distance to about either 5, 6, or 7 feet. But you the HUD can only be adjusted by turning it off completely, or keeping it completely on, including its sixth-sense warning that the enemy is looking at you, and from which direction.Yes, I finished on authentic difficulty, but no, I won't play authentic again. I like either lots of ammo, or the ability to conserve unused parts of my magazine when I reload. In authentic, I particularly don't like checking my health by trying to apply bandages (at full health, you get a message that you can't bandage yourself anymore.)Gun modifications are a big, big thing in SE5. There are very detailed stats for each gun that you can examine while setting up your loadout. Vertical, horizontal recoil. Shot grouping. Damage. Audible range. Audible range is what I look at most. It can vary from about 4m to over 160m. Even with a quiet gun, eventually, the enemy will spot you, if you keep shooting. But a very quiet gun lets you shoot much more often without moving between shots.Most of the mods and many of the guns only unlock after discovering particular workbenches, located in enemy territory on the campaign maps. (You do NOT have to return to the same workbenches to re-apply the mods after they are unlocked.) Some of the mods unlock after certain feats, like total headshots with the weapon, or kills within or beyond a certain distance. In my second playthrough of the campaign, I used the D.L. (De Lisle) Carbine, a highly suppressed rifle - only easily audible within 17m. It's a DLC gun. Well...the game is old now, so if you want to play, wait for a deep sale and get the DLC too - how else will you get a chance to kill Hitler in a dozen different ways?In my first playthrough of SE5, I was pleased that tanks were realistically hard to kill. In SE4, it was always presumed that tank drivers and gunners had had their vision blocks damaged, and hence had removed them, and hence could be sniped through their small vision ports. Not in SE5. I used panzerfausts and TNT and teller mines to disable tank tracks and had to leave the tanks damaged but dangerous behind me; sometimes they'd burn out over the next 10 minutes or so. Unhappily, I later learned that SE5 simply has different weak points than SE4. Armoured cars have engine port covers that can be destroyed with bullets, after which the armored car can be blown up by shooting a couple of bullets into the engine. Tanks? Yeah, tanks too. With bullets, one can (not simply pierce a hole through, but instead) blow a big chunk of armor off the back of a King Tiger, between its exhaust ports, then blow up the tank completely by shooting its exposed engine. Bullets. A full-health King Tiger. Sigh. It can also feel a bit disappointing that even on the highest difficulty level, the enemy often stands still and peers about after a near miss, or when an explosive goes off nearby. The highest difficulty should feature bad guys that keep their heads down, or move a few feet behind cover before exposing themselves again. (Checked: SE4 enemies don't keep their heads nearly as still as enemies in SE5.)And of course, even on authentic difficulty, there were plenty of magic healing kits to restore you to 100% health, and enemy snipers continued to reveal their position with lens flare on their scope that shows up like a search light.Did I mention that when you crouch and concentrate ("focus"), you can see through walls out to a distance of about 50 feet? But you can turn that off in the the fine difficulty settings if you want.And yet, I enjoyed the game. I really did. And I'm going to try SE4 again too, now that I've forgotten most of its maps.

_childDocuments_.review: Snagged this game on a 70% off sale, and let me tell you, even at that discount, it felt like I overpaid. Sniper Elite 5 takes you on a nostalgic journey back to the first Medal of Honor, except without the charm of it being 1999. You're funneled down the same unimaginative, rigid paths that could bore even the most ardent history buffs to tears.On 'Sniper Elite' difficulty it's like playing on 'toddler mode.' Make a blunder so colossal it should have you ousted from the brotherhood of snipers? No problem! This game forgives like your grandma, letting even the worst mistakes slide with barely a slap on the wrist.The graphics? Oh, they've got high-quality textures, alright. People and objects sometimes look so sharp you’d swear they could cut glass. Too bad that’s where the innovation ends. The first cutscene? It's like a B-movie zombie apocalypse minus the suspense and horror, complete with characters sporting the dead-eyed stare of a department store mannequin and movements as fluid as a robot dance from a 1980s pop video.In conclusion, if you’re looking for a game that manages to simultaneously bore and annoy, Sniper Elite 5 might just be your perfect match. It's a lackluster parade of missed opportunities wrapped in the thin veneer of modern graphics, proving once again that not all upgrades are for the better. So, buckle up for this snooze-fest; you’ll need the sniper’s focus just to stay awake.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished my first playthrough (Normal) and wanted to share my first impressions. I enjoyed the game and would recommend it if you enjoyed previous Sniper Elite and Zombie Army games. Dropped down to Normal on my first playthrough because for some reason I couldn't shoot straight at first. Only played the campaign, haven't played any Season Pass content yet. The main campaign was shorter than I expected but the missions and side objectives were what you'd expect from a Sniper Elite game. AA guns, lots of them. Nazis too.Sniper Elite 5 reintroduces armour piercing ammo which makes dealing with armoured vehicles a lot quicker. There's also non-lethal, subsonic and match grade ammo. Can't say much about the new ammo types as I haven't really used them enough. Takedowns now offer a lethal or non-lethal option. Each map has 3 different starting locations, the default locations and two other locations that you have to find and unlock. A nice feature that allows you to mix things up a bit.Rocks are replaced with empty bottles. No longer an infinite supply but you can find empty bottles all over the map. Throwing a bottle at an enemy's head will knock them unconscious which is handy and neat.Truck engines can now also be used for sound cover, just like generators. Alarms are also new-ish. Once the alarm is triggered, sirens will call for reinforcements. Alarms can be disabled and booby trapped as well, so that's fun.Zip lines to travel across larger distances relatively fast. I suppose they're handy but I'm not sure if they really add anything. A crowbar and bolt cutters are new tools. They can be used to open doors and supply crates, some can be opened by picking the lock or brute force, others only by brute force. You can also use them to cut holes in fences or sabotage mission objectives. The Kill List is a nice addition. Every mission has an optional objective to kill the target in a specific way. Some are easy, others are a bit trickier but they were fun to do and I'm sure I'll have fun with them in the next few playthroughs. I do have some issues with the game, though. Nothing that made me regret buying this game but I still want to mention them.First of all, it is set in France. Not one French person to be shot, though. Not even civilians. In Italy we got to shoot Italians on both sides but in France the best we get are NPCs slipping in and out of their stupid French accents. Very disappointing.The graphics are really nice, the fabric of Karl's sweater looks pretty realistic but at the same time the player models look a bit more plasticky. The facial animations are more detailed but look off, especially in the cut scenes. Corpses often have wide open, contorted mouths  which is more comical than anything else.I always found the Zombie Army games to a bit a jankier than the Sniper Elite games when it comes to the controls in general. Weapon handling was the most noticeable difference to me and  Sniper Elite 5 feels more in line with Zombie Army 4 than Sniper Elite 4.Gun handling feels different, more Zombie Army than Sniper Elite but I can't quite explain what that means. The balancing of weapons and other decisions don't make sense to me. They added the Drilling shotgun but it doesn't have a rifle barrel, which is the defining feature of the Drilling. Also, Mosin, poor thing. Maps are big just like in SE4 but feel emptier, first few maps have a lot of open fields and hedges. Villages and military structures are smaller. Feels a bit more open world compared to SE4, if that makes sense. Maybe it's the difference in design, I think SE4 had better level design with elevation differences and pathing. Traversing the terrain in 5 is a lot jankier. Lots of invisible walls, hills you can't climb, obstacles you can't mount or vault.Getting interaction prompts to appear can be a pain. Especially picking up items from safes was quite iffy. I point directly at the documents but no prompt, have to do a little dance to get the prompt and then I still have to pick up the TNT or ammo or whatever before the documents even register. Don't know why that is but it is annoying. Enemies are spread thin,  I first thought that was due to Normal difficulty but apparently it's no different on higher difficulties. Will find out for myself soon enough.Not a big fan of locating work benches to unlock weapon upgrades. I suppose it's nice to change or upgrade your rifle on the go but adding three, one for pistol, SMG and rifle each is a bit much. I very much would have prefered individual weapon challenges like in SE4 to upgrade instead of unlocking them across the board.And last, but not least, there sadly is no Overwatch mode. I'm sure Invasion can be fun but Overwatch was really good in SE4. A huge improvement on SE3 and I would've loved some DLC missions for Overwatch. I prefer co-op, don't really touch multiplayer so the removal of co-op Overwatch means a game with less content.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I know I'm late to this one, but its a game i've put a few hours into now and it deserves a review.Rebellion as a studio went through a big change from SE4 to this new iteration. Most of the leads moved on to different challenges in other studios. The Head of Art, Head of Design, and Assc Head of Code ALL LEFT after SE4.So, we expect SE5 to be a drop in quality right?Absolutely not. Testament to Rebellions ability to elevate staff from within, the new Head of Design was a previous lead designer, and he nailed it. Not straying too far from a winning formula, but taking out some of the bloat of SE4 and focusing on slightly less options, but much more considered paths and routes.At times in SE4 you felt a little lost, thats so far gone in SE5.Rebellion are not reinventing the wheel here, im sure their new project 'Atomfall' will have some great new ideas, but we really dont want them to.If you live this series, you'll love this game. _childDocuments_.review: Being German myself, I'd like to comment on the design of the Germans in the game.The first thing is the language and voice acting. It's great that German soldiers speak native German, but the actual acting is horrible. Everyone sounds vaguely comical, as if not taking the situation he's in seriously. I have not heard any voice that I could reasonably believe to belong to a real soldier in a serious scenario. There are also literal translations from English expressions in their lines, that aren't proper German, as well as smaller details, like grammar errors in Propaganda Posters.I know the game had expert advisors on weapons and such, why couldn't they have also had just one or two German people to check for this kind of thing? They would have spotted all of it immediately.The level design goes for oversimplified Pseudo-German set pieces, like a large sign that just says "Achtung!" in the middle of a camp. I get that this is useful for being recognizable by Non-Germans, but that sign makes no sense. "Achtung!" for what? There needs to be some explanation on what that sign is a warning against. Especially since German is famous for being very detailed and specific.I don't want to make this too long, so I'll say this in conclusion. In order for me to enjoy fighting enemies in a game, I have to be able to take them seriously and have respect for them. That is what is lacking here. Even though my complaints may be less problematic for Non-Germans, I'm certain that a more authentic depiction of them would make for a much better game for everyone.So please, pay more attention ("Achtung!") to detail when designing villains, antagonists and enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 4 was a great sniper game.Zombie Army 4 was a great zombie/close combat game.Sniper Elite 5 is awful, because it uses mostly the close combat mechanics of ZA4 in a sniper game.  Close combat should be very difficult and dangerous, like it was in SE4.  Instead, it is the best way to handle most of SE5, you can leave your rifle at home.  When critical sniper shots are required, the game kindly provides you with one of several very powerful sniper rifles.  Once that's done, feel free to return to using SMGs and pistols.Swing and a miss.  Rename this as something else, don't call it Sniper anything.The fact that the latest DLC pack is called "Up Close and Personal" ironically underlines the problem with the overall design of the game.  Not a "sniper" game, it's an "up close and personal" fighting game.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I don't know quite what some negative reviewers have been playing, but this is by far the best of the Sniper Elite games to date by a country mile.  Don't be put off at the start - the first ten, fifteen minutes of the first mission seem rather restrictive in where you can actually go to achieve the set goals, but after that, freedom to move around a vast world gets somewhat better.  This world in Sniper Elite 5 is simply beautiful.  Campaign Italy in Sniper Elite 4 was good, but this is even better.  The detail is simply incredible - a huge variety of scenic battlegrounds combined with close quarter town elements provide a breathtaking experience.  It is simply beautiful.Game play is far more challenging.  It takes a few missions to develop a style of play that you find works.  There are multi objectives in each of the main missions bar the very last one whcih is a bit of an add-on compared to the other missions.  There are far more enemies around - you simply cannot go in guns blazing with a hope of blasting everyone in sight and surviving.  Strategy is needed - a space to bail out to if things get tough - and boy are things easier if alarms are not triggered.  Added to that - weapon tactics are much more realistic in this game.  In SE4, you could pick up a weapon, keep it, and add copious amounts of ammo to it as you progressed each mission.  Here, you pick up a weapon, and can only use the ammo left in it before either going back to your own weapon, or finding another similar weapon to use.  Far more challenging and realistic.The sniping element has changed the least in my view.  Depending on what level of difficulty you play, the sniping mechanics are pure Snipe Elite as it always has been.  Unlike Ghost Warrior Contracts, sniping distances are not that extreme.  However, the cut scenes are pretty brutal and weapon sounds are a huge step forward.Afraid the voice acting is just as bad as it ever was, but there we go....you won't be buying this game for the cut scenes which are still somewhat predicable and hackneyed.  I like to play each level to the full - if you want to, you can take a good two hours game play for each of the major levels in this game.  And each mission has such wonderfully created environments.  Most compelling and enjoyable.Tanks and vehicles are more difficult to destroy - this is one part of the game play thatis nothing like previous SE episodes.  You will need Panzershreks or armour piercing weaponry and ammunition to destroy tanks and such like in SE5.  Much more of a challenge than sniping gunners and drivers as experienced in SE4.There aren't many games that I'd justify not waiting for a sale price - this is one of them.  Buy it.  It is a load better than SE4 and that is saying something.At the time of writing, there are two major issues that need sorting - one is the lack of zoom functionality on the middle mouse when in sniping mode.  It's designed to work, but doesn't for me.  Secondly, the zip wire bizz has a bad habit of freezing up which stalls the game play badly.  Save before zip wiring, and it's ok.

_childDocuments_.review: The guiding design philosophy for this seems to have been "let's take what worked in 4 and find ways to make them more annoying to use and less fun". A thumbs up seems a bit too nice at this point but it's not necessarily a *bad* game either.The maps I've played so far are good, especially mission 3, (only up through mission 6), the shooting is still good, weapon customization is cool (ask me about my 1911 suppressed sniper pistol) but the mechanics changes are baffling to me. And even though I've tuned down all the settings to get a consistent 60fps (be warned, the game is a huge step up hardware wise, can play 4 on ultra hitting 90+ fps but I'm dropping back to high, shadows on medium to get 60 *max* with 1660ti) there seems to be like a half second of lag before the game registers input, on both kb/m and controller. Also right now the game has a huge amount of bugs, including some major gameplay related stuff like challenges failing when you complete them, just check out the discord if you want proof of that. The x-ray view tanks my fps to like 30, and it may just be me but it feels like they toned down the bone and organ explosions in it too?List of weird changes they made that I've encountered so far-you have to manually pick up all items now?-removed crouch sprint-active reloads-radar doesn't show enemies you can hear anymore-altered binoculars tagging so you're forced to hover over an enemy for multiple seconds-some enemies now block your melee attacks-bleeding damage-can't permanently change weapons in mission, you can only pick one up, use what's in the magazine and then drop it-removed open gas tanks from vehicles, making multiple ap rounds to engine the only way to shoot and explode them

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. I'm a massive fan of the Sniper Elite series and in my opinion Sniper Elite 5 lives up to the series, though it is not a substantial leap in quality over Sniper Elite 4 in the same way Sniper Elite 4 was over 2 and 3. It's more of a side step, with certain areas improved, others worse, and others changed. There's been a ton of negativity surrounding this game, and while certainly it lacks the polish of 4, I think it has enough alterations to the formula over 4 that it can stand alongside 4 as a great Sniper game. While I don't think it is as well realized of a game as 4 (all of the components of that game worked together perfectly to make a game greater than the sum of its parts), I love the increased complexity of the game. I found the levels were larger in scope and more varied than 4, not just in terms of visual design but also in layout, approach, and gameplay. Along with the complete weapon customizability and non-lethal ammo types, there is far more player agency in the levels. While it doesn't have much positive gameplay function, I found the non-lethal options were a fun player-imposed challenge, and its honestly also fun to be a complete bastard and play judge, jury, and executioner based on what it says on the individual enemies bios. I also appreciated the fact that you get updates on the games missions/side missions by exploring the level itself and reading documents/overhearing conversations. I found the game generally easier and the sniping more forgiving than 4, but its still plenty challenging if you want it to be. Being able to unlock different starting locations for missions is a great touch as well. The biggest negative for me is that it is reasonably buggy, particularly with AI and animations, though this has improved quite a bit since launch. I really like the music as well. Different themes for the different levels is an awesome touch, and I really appreciate the more organic way the music changes based on the alert state of the enemies, over 4 which was often far too explicit in its music an audio cues. Sniper Elite 5 is not Sniper Elite 4, and I think in accepting that you'll come to find that 5 is a very good game indeed. I was pretty disappointed by this game after launch (probably in large part due to its super buggy state), but have come around to love it. It's refreshing to play a game that's super straightforward and gameplay focused without the fat and nonsense, though I still don't see that a skill tree is necessary in this game. There is a TON of content in the base game too, especially in considering the reduced MSRP. The single player levels are more expansive than they have ever been, you have multiplayer (which I am not much of a fan of in general but IMO the multiplayer in 5 is an undeniable improvement over 4), survival (a personal favorite game mode of mine) and invasion, which is an awesome, awesome addition. Don't buy the season pass though. It's an absolute rip off, particularly when its price is compared to the price of the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 5 is a welcome addition to the Sniper Elite franchise, offering a satisfying stealth experience with its slow-paced gameplay and realistic environments. The game's core mechanics remain unchanged from previous installments, but the new maps and missions provide a refreshing challenge for seasoned players.The game's stealth mechanics are top-notch, encouraging players to carefully plan their approach and take out enemies silently. The X-ray kill cam remains a highlight, providing a gruesome yet satisfying reward for well-placed shots.What I particularly enjoyed about Sniper Elite 5 is its relaxing pace. Unlike many action-packed shooters, Sniper Elite 5 allows players to take their time, carefully scouting out enemy positions and planning their next move. This makes for a more immersive and enjoyable experience.However, the game isn't without its flaws. I initially experienced some motion sickness, but this was easily remedied by lowering the controller sensitivity settings. Additionally, there seems to be a disconnect between the gameplay and the cinematics. My character Karl was wearing a ghillie suit in the game, but he appeared in his default uniform during cutscenes. This created a jarring disconnect and felt like a programming oversight, especially for a game with a premium price tag.Despite these minor issues, Sniper Elite 5 remains a solid stealth game with plenty to offer fans of the genre. The slow-paced gameplay, realistic environments, and satisfying stealth mechanics make it a worthwhile addition to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game doesn't play as well as its predecessors and really needs polishing in order for it to feel better. A strange downgrade with this installment compared to the rest of the franchise. But definitely try out Sniper Elite 4 if you're looking to play a smoother, less janky and well paced version of this game.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Compared to Sniper Elite 4, this game doesn't play well at all. I don't know what happened, but this feels like a downgrade to the franchise. It's hard to explain, but there were a lot of little things about the game that killed my experience playing it. Player movement was janky at times, and often wouldn't allow you to perform the action you wanted. Stealth could be ruined because of a glitched texture or object you thought you were safely hidden behind. And sometimes the enemies would just.. break ...and not move anymore, especially when you raised suspicion. These sorts of things were very smooth and well executed in SE4 but for some reason it's terrible in this game and it really killed my enjoyment of it. Things felt less intuitive and more forced and there were times where I thought I could get creative in my approach, but the game basically said I couldn't for no real reason. On top of that there were new mechanics implemented that felt unnecessary. Gun customizations instead of simple upgrades, non-lethal options for bullets and explosives that do nothing for overall gameplay or story, and character upgrades that didn't really change much in how you performed, and were too easy to level up.The story was also all over the place. Without giving away too much, the game starts with you stuck behind enemy lines for the longest time, all by yourself aside from a few french revolutionists. And all of a sudden, after 3 or 4 of the levels going like that, you're then back with the allies invading Normandy?? There was no real flow to it after that because it felt like we skipped 3 or 4 chapters in a book. In the past, Sniper Elite games have had stories but it never really focused on them aside from providing backstory to the mission you were doing  and setting up the big bosses and their evil scheme that was supposed to turn the tide of war for Germany. It never needed to go further than that, but for some reason it's starting to and it's almost to Sniper Elite's detriment.Overall while I really wanted to like this game, it just has too many issues for it to be worthwhile. It really felt like I was forcing myself to finish the game towards the end because I was fed up with it. If you've read this far, GO PLAY SNIPER ELITE 4!! I promise you that game is much more polished and very satisfying to play. I hope that future installments of Sniper Elite really try and smooth over these issues. Very disappointed to say "no" in my recommendation of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a strange one, I haven't spent much time with the game and I don't really intend on finishing it. It comes down to in what essence this game is. Despite its name of sniper Elite, It focuses more on special operations like sabotage. With this instalment of the series this is essentially a stealth infiltration game. Clearing levels is in some way more alike to Farcry where you sneak around, silently killing enemies and disabling alarms. Now if that's what your after you will enjoy this game It does those things very well. My issue is it actually presents few opportunities to actually engage in sniping as a sniper would. Most enemies are engaged at CQ or within 50-100M.  You will rarely ever need to adjust the dialled in range of your rifle at those ranges. absent too is information on the weapons bullet trajectory/drop and Windage info. The other issue when you actually fire off the sniper rifle is the noise it creates. (i'm aware guns create noise i'm speaking purely from a game mechanics perspective) Being that this is a stealth game that means any large noise will attract mindless droves of NPCS on your position. To counter this the game creates opportunity for you to sneak around camps, sabotaging vehicles and other objects to create noise so you can get a round off without triggering a mass NPC rush to your position. Once again to engage such targets at 50-100m max,To reiterate if that seems interesting to you then by all means hop in here. As far as an actual Sniper game or simulator yeah its just not there. It would have been more interesting to me if they had created levels where you could actually be deployed how a sniper would have. The depiction here is more akin to a one man army Rambo or commando operations. Anyways thx for reading I just wanted to give clarity to what this game is all about. I had bought it with different expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Sniper Elite 4, I really liked this game. If you are new to the Sniper Elite series, I'd recommend playing Sniper Elite 4 first, I feel the level design in the 4th is better (more places to snipe long-range from, along with more clear navigation options) And I, debatably, feel the progression is better in the 4th (linear skill tree with fewer, more meaningful options, that I feel make choosing new skills far easier, and a more simple, casual weapon upgrade system)However, if you played Sniper Elite 4 and really liked it, this game will certainly appeal to you. The difficulty options are greatly expanded, along with accessibility options, allowing for more variance on not just how difficult the game is but how it's difficult, whether you want the sniping to be harder, or the close quarters combat to be harderStealth is more viable in levels crowded with enemies due to the weapons customization system, being able to add stealth attachments to your weapons and then seeing how they affect the bullet simulation, instead of needing rare "stealth" ammo, that isn't clear on how much they reduce the noise (unless you have them make the gun fully silentOverall I'd say this game is a sidestep compared to Sniper Elite 4 right now, with some upgrades and some downgrades. This is an easy recommendation for any fan of Sniper Elite 4, but I'd be more hesitant to recommend it to someone new to the series

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I love it. With that said though, this should've been released with a little "Early Access" tag on it. There are bugs and glitches. Bodies you can't search, non existant doors that you can walk right through and open, or not open, the choice is yours, the doors don't exist, but you can open them. The way the enemy soldiers aggro is a bit off, you can have a marker that shows "Here's where the sound came from" and as soon as they have investigated that area, they'll beeline it right for the position you are at. And I really really really wanted more out of the DLC where you get to kill Hitler in more and more imaginative ways. In Sniper Elite 4 the DLC came with several maps. Weapon and mod unlocks, this is one that is probably liked a lot by people, but, with that said, there's not enough challenges per map. And I want to be able to see what I am missing in a collection while I'm actually playing that map, is it a personal letter? Is it a hidden item? What's my stone eagle count?Rebellion, as per usual, delivers a very enjoyable game. But you will sink HOURS and HOURS into it. You will run around a map for countless hours to find all the collectibles, unless you find a guide online, that will limit the time you spend to a mere hour or two per map, just for the collectibles.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the game from sniper elite 1 on 2005. I have played all the games so far except nazi zomie 4.If I was not that big fan I would not recommend the game. It is actually like they took the code from previous sniper elite games and just kept some of the features without adding a lot and created a game.  Over all I am kind of dissapointed. If someone is not a fan can play Sniper Ghost Warrior has much better gameplay and environment interaction. This game is mostly for fans that they liked sniper elite but it is not improved. I do not mean to completelly change the game and make it like SGW but they could add a few stuff. Here is like playing a new level in a mix of SE v2, 3 and 4, a bad mix though not a cool one.What I do not like: - They removed cool features prev games had, like talk to allies or the rock we used to throw :'(  or some cinematic kills when you reach the enemy etc- The environment is not fully interactive, you can just touch very spesific objects. An are the same objects all the time. I got tired seeing this yellow box with the white line. You could at least have it in many colors...- Even if a grass is tall you can not hide unless it is the ONE.. ONLY 1 grass TEXTURE that you can hide... It's 2022. At least in SE 1 released on 2005 you could hide on shadows.. Here you can not ! I would like to be able to hide in more grass types, dark places or bushes.. - To many doors are closed and you can not open them- Very guided enviroment you can pass only on the path they choose so it's not an open world map experience.- Very similar levels with previous editions. That's not a negative that much but since you did not spend time to design new maps and you copied the old ones. Could not you improve the gameplay ?- Hostile soldiers can be very stupid but very clever in the same time. An officer killed me with a small weapon from 50meters while a soldier came next to me, did not shot me, stoped looked me shot me and could not kill me...- I would like more collectibles and in a little more obvious positions, there are too many empty rooms.- Sometimes too many solidiers pop out of nowhere sometimes.What I liked.- Yeaaaah an other Sniper Elite !- Nice new mood the Axis Invation- Nice challenges to kill with mouse or poison etc- Nice decoy and other traps. I would like the bottle to be something like a molotov though- Story line and videos where as always nice- Alarm and the way to stop itThe game has lots of bugs also but these will be solved soon and it's normal.Ideas for the next make it in Balcans :) I would like a mission to Acropolis :P or Instabul I will update, I can not remember everything now :P

_childDocuments_.review: This review is purely focused on the singleplayer aspect of the game, I never touched any part of the online part.I don't understand all the people in here complaining about how they do more sniping in <enter non-sniping game here> than in SE5. If you chose to go in guns blazing, mow down everything with the MG42 and chuck some nades you can hardly moan about the lack of sniping opportunities.If you don't make use of the custom difficulty options and then go on about how there's too much UI clutter and how the aim assist is literal cheating you can't expect people to take your opinion seriously.SE5 surely does a lot of things worse than SE4, especially when it comes to terrain interaction (vaulting, invisible walls, crap like that), but level design isn't one of them. The maps are huge, allow for a range or even mix of approaches, open things up for replayability, can be punishing, but never unfair and are generally not as CQC excessive as is often claimed. Also, they look amazing. Seriously, Beaumont-Saint-Denis and Saint Nezaire are probably among the most atmospheric levels I have ever seen.You can and will snipe a whole bunch - IF you care to find and secure suitable locations to set up in. If you don't, well..The AI is still pretty braindead, no point in sugar-coating it, but if you're looking for a challenge you can still Sam Fisher this on Authentic (or Custom) and have a hell of a time regardless.SE5 is a respectable successor to SE4 with a lot of improvements and a few downgrades here and there. I very much enjoyed my 45ish hours so far and will continue to do so, hopping into the DLC mission.Addendum: gun modeling and textures are superb (with a few tiny exceptions), same for accessories (minus suppressors). Gun behavior as well as animations such as reloading, bolt manipulation and handling are top notch. If you care for gun play and the details surrounding it then this game will deliver on that front.

There will be times when sniping is just not possible (its never taken away directly) and stealth is better. Or you mess up and need to  light some ♥♥♥♥ up. Fun game though. Similar to the Witcher 2, this may be the game that gives these devs confidence and the income to produce something super good. Needs to be something besides this though. 5 Is a lot of sequels with not a ton of core gameplay/genre innovation.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased the game somewhat reluctantly as I previously played the games in the franchise.  I am also awaiting other titles to be released.  I read some reviews and thought....okay, it would fill the void.  However, now that I am comfortably in the game I realize that this franchise is past its due date and needs an overhaul.The game suffers from multiple limitations as well as being a bit buggy: Enemies showing up, looking away for a second, then looking back but they are not there?  Walking up to pillage a body, but if you stand too close, or at the wrong angle, you lose some menu options.  Very limited in movement as you have to follow very distinct paths, and cannot open many doors or leap barriers right in front of you.  The menu wheel is buggy as you have to almost double check your selection before you continue as it sometimes selects wrong.  Movement is terrible, unless you are perfectly aligned to a track you get stuck behind poles, etc....really fun when you are trying escape......not!  Upside?....GREAT graphics as I am using a 2080 RTX Ti, and the map is "nice".  Would really prefer it to be more open....but again the limited pathways.All in all this game lacks...well...a lot!  If purchased discounted...very maybe.  I won't be buying the next in the series....that's all I know.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 5 has been released for many months now, and in my own opinion, it's one of the best games of the franchise.  However, it does have its flaws.  Despite being released as a sniping game, it is fairly easy to complete each mission with an assault style playthrough, utilizing unscoped rifles and the various secondary weapons.  If its a more realistic take you desire, a pure stealth sniping route could easily land you 60+ hours of gameplay, and it is worth just about every hour.  Observing patrol routes, calculating the trajectories, pacifying or killing lone sentries, every action demands your utmost attention and ability to plan out the next move.  For example, it takes me about 6 to 7 hours of gameplay just to complete each mission undetected.  The option for just simple run-and-gun DOOM style fighting can also work if that's more your speed.Moving on from basic gameplay, the visuals are stunning, the levels are large and feature various zones to either blitz or sneak through, and the ability to pick up weapons from fallen enemies and supply crates is a plus, in my mind.  Each level has a hidden cache with at least one MG42 and a belt of 100 rounds to neutralize large groups of soldiers, while Panzerfausts and Panzerbusche anti-tank rifles can deliver stand-off attacks on armored vehicles and troop transports.  Every encounter can be dealt with in a variety of ways, and while that's not a new feature in the series, it's the best implementation of it so far.The AI can be rather smart at times, but is still rather easy to fool.  Soldiers will take cover when shot at, and if you're using a suppressor on your rifle, this can lead to them actually retreating and falling farther and farther back, but this only works if you are outside of their detection range, which is another very well-implemented gameplay mechanic.  I've played way too many games that feature the Hollywood-esque suppressor where your weapon is silent at all ranges.  The suppressors in this game though work exactly as they should, and while they significantly reduce the range at which your shots can be heard, they don't completely remove them either.The various types of ammunition you can unlock during the game is another great feature, although the less said about the nonlethal rounds, the better.  Subsonic ammunition though is a game changer, and combine that with a customised Welrod, and you can complete missions with just that sidearm.  And speaking of unlocks, it just feels reminiscent of Call of Duty and Battlefield, where you have to meet the prerequisites to obtain them, from attachments to weapons and gear.  I did enjoy having to find the workbenches to mount the new attachments or utilize the new kit, but it does get a bit ridiculous.  Have you seen a Tarkov-inspired Luger?  Some of the attachments just don't work like that at all.Moving on to weapons, the selection was pretty decent, but I wish there was more!  The SREM-1 is a nifty little rifle that I actually did not know anything about.  I'd never even heard of it, and thought Rebellion was pulling my leg, until I watched Saint Jonathon at the Royal Armouries actually talk about it and show off the only surviving example.  Speaking of which, Rebellion, would you please complete it's model, it's missing a scope ring, and the point where that can be attached is easily seen on the handguard.  Moving on from that, for a game based in France, there's not a lot of French weapons available.  I was expecting to see a Lebel or a Berthier, maybe even a MAS-36, but maybe that's for a later DLC package, I'm not sure.  I wasn't expecting to see Japanese weapons and equipment, so that was a little weird despite being central to the campaign.And that leads to a new issue, the campaign is basically the same: the Nazis have a new superweapon, you have to follow all the leads to find said superweapon, then you blow it up and kill the man in charge.  That was V2 with a V2 rocket loaded with Tabun gas, that was 3 with the P.1000 Ratte superheavy tank, that was 4 with an upgraded radio-guided rocket, and now we have stealth-plated submarines with V2 rockets.  The formula is getting tired at this point.  Same for the Hitler assassination missions.  Don't get me wrong, there is nothing wrong with killing Hitler.  It's just, when are we going to be able to target other senior Nazi officials?  I've shot Hitler's testicle off in four separate games now.  I no longer have that juvenile chuckle.And now we get to the major issue I've been having.  Sniper Elite 5 is still acting like its out of Alpha and into Beta.  I'm having game-crashing bugs practically every level, more often 2 to 3 times per level.  I don't know if that's because the code is still a little iffy or if it's because my hard drive isn't capable of running it, all I do know is that this issue still needs worked on.  If you've read this far, good for you, make sure your PC is up to the minimum requirements, but I highly recommend going as far beyond that as you financially can.  Maybe it's just me, but I don't have the money to throw at it right now.  I will say that it is very frustrating having to restart my PC multiple times just to finish a single mission.Well, that's all I've got.  Make sure you get your free DLC downloads when they come out, because hey, they're free even if they don't do much of anything gameplay wise.  I can't say much for the rest of the DLC, I don't have them yet.  Sniper Elite 5 is another solid addition to the franchise, but what's next?  We've gone to Berlin, to North Africa, to Italy, and now France.  There's only so much more Karl Fairburne can do before V2 begins, so will we see him again in the Netherlands as part of Market Garden, or maybe in Belgium for the Battle of the Bulge?  All I know is, his story is almost done, if not done already.  That's up to Rebellion, but I think they might still have one more installment before calling it quits.This is a good game to play if you've got time to kill, and if you can handle the game-ending bugs and hope they get patched, then this game could be a good entry into your library.  If you want to snipe, look no further.  If you want to run-and-gun, you can do that here.  If you want to be the SOE-equivalent of James Bond, that's here too.  If you have the previous entries, then you know Karl's story so far, but now you have to help him liberate France.  The war is in it's final act, the Western Allies have landed in Normandy, the Soviet Union is moving in from the East, and the Third Reich has less than a year to live.  What insane wonder weapon will they come up next, and who's the next officer to assassinate?  Hopefully, we'll find out next time.  Take care, everybody, and remember: 'Vive la France!'
