_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played Sniper Elite but enjoy games like MGS:V or the Splinter Cell series, you will probably like Sniper Elite 5. There is a focus on stealth-action/espionage gameplay, but unfortunately the actual stealth isn't as good as either of those games. Instead there are sniping elements like bullet drop, wind speed, and 'sound masking', with a bit of a focus on things like managing your heart rate - e.g if you sprint for a while, your increased heart rate will make your sniper scope unsteady until you catch your breath, and if you are bleeding from a wound then your heart rate will not decrease until you use a bandage or medkit. You can also customise elements of difficulty like turning the minimap, and enemy marking on or off. After going through the game once I found going through a second time without a map or markers was an excellent challenge, because you really need to make some of those shots count.Be aware that the game is a bit janky. There are invisible walls around the edges of missions, and there is no jump button, so sometimes you can't climb over really simple barriers like chest high walls or small rocky slopes (instead you get a button prompt to climb things like walls and fences if it is possible). It makes just a couple of parts of the game seem weird and confusing. But when it is good, it is REALLY good and you can have some seriously fun and very tense moments moving through very detailed European castles and cities. Trying to do a no kill run can be very difficult.The most fun comes from the co-op and invasion modes, which add extra layers to the experience and allow you to come back and approach missions in entirely new ways. Invasions especially require players to keep moving and always be alert to their surroundings. At the time of writing there is one frustrating issue where the player character will narrate information to himself out loud for the benefit of the player (e.g "I see the enemy bunker up ahead, looks like the intel was correct.") and the invading player can hear him speaking to himself. The defending player cannot currently turn these narrations or control their speaking volume when being invaded, which means they might unintentionally give themselves away just by walking into a new area. With enough feedback the developers should be able to patch something like this. EDIT: they fixed this issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the negative reviews ruin it for you.I've played 3 and 4 and loved them both, and almost didn't buy this because of the bad reviews. It's really not a big deal. Like, at all.Other Cons: The invisible borders can be annoying, especially for a stealth game, let me hide in the bushes! Controls can be a bit wonky at time. Sometimes it's difficult to grab items, but just use the 'arrow' on the screen, hover it over the item you want, and it will let you select it most of the time. Can't think of much else I didn't like about the game.Pros: You can adjust the difficulty a lot more than you can in the other ones. For example I like turning off the mini map, making the enemy search long and hard for me, and making them a good shot. But, I also left detection on, and kept loot turned on high so I could find a lot of mines because I love booby traps.All-in-all it's a great game and it had a lot of the same magic the older ones. I loved the attention to detail with all of scenery.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I've completely erased my previous review to a write a new one, because frankly there are enough reviews going into the nitty details of what this game did good or did badly. Instead, here are my thoughts about some of the baffling design decisions instead:- Why does Karl have to get a new crowbar and new set of bolt-cutters in every mission, when he can easily carry 3 sets of mines, tnt, shoeboxes, hand-grenades, over 200 rounds of ammunition and 3 full sized firearms.- Why did Karl after 2 brutal campaigns in Africa and Italy suddenly decide that being non-lethal is a priority in this WW2 setting while simultaneously generalising all german soldiers as "Nazi bastards!" (actual quote).- Why can Karl climb a straight 90 degrees walls covered in thin lichen like a mountain climber, but can't step over a small bush up to his knee.- Why has the germans gone to such lengths as to manifacture 5 different types of ammo for every single type of gun and spread them all over occupied France. Including WOODEN BULLETS!?- Why do german soldiers get alerted by the sound of a bottle shattering 30 meters away, but when Karl breaks someone's neck and lets the body hit the floor 5 centimetres away, the other guy doesn't hear a thing.Good game, worth giving the benefit of the doubt. But some of the newly implemented mechanics are really nonsensical and it takes some effort to try and overlook them so you can get to the good parts. Ultimately, playing this game only served to highlight how good Sniper Elite 4 was.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the myriad of game-breaking bugs that people seem to be having with this particular title so soon after launch, I have not encountered anything seriously game-breaking. A few minor visual glitches here and there, and I fell through the floor into null space a grand total of one time in over 50 hours of play, but nothing a quick re-load of a recent save could not fix. I also encountered the body-hiding bug in which the game auto-saves while hiding a body in a crate, then subsequent re-loads of that savegame show me as still holding the body (despite not actually holding one). Reload of a previous save fixed it.Many people seem to be complaining about the visual quality of the game being terrible and literally worse than SE4. This could not be further from the truth. The visuals in this game are absolutely stunning, and the views in Wolf Mountain are especially breathtaking. Mission 8, Rubble and Ruin, also has some extremely good visuals with respect to level design. It really hits home just how absolutely devastating the effects of WWII were on once-beautiful places like France. HDR is supported, which makes the daytime maps really pop, but there is a disappointing lack of raytracing and DLSS support. AMD's FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 is supported.Explosions in particular have had a substantial upgrade from SE4, visually speaking. I actually prefer the realtime non-xray explosion visuals. Extremely realistic.The attention to detail, both visual and audible, of each of the weapons is absolutely impeccable. They really did their research here, and even recorded many hours of real-world audio produced by each weapon in the game. A high-end audio system is HIGHLY recommended!X-ray cams are now available for SMG and pistol kills, a very nice addition. I also like that you can adjust the speed of the x-ray cam faster or slower in realitme, although I would like to have seen more range in the adjustment.As for traversing around the various maps... Well, especially (but not limited to) the very first map, there are far too many obstacles that SHOULD easily be hurdled by Karl, but are absolutely impassable. Short bushes less than waist-high? Impassable. A pile of rocks no taller than Karl's ankle? Impassable. Various knee- or waist-height rock walls? Impassable. This particular aspect is a downgrade from SE4. In that game, anything that seemed logically passable in fact was.Weapon mastering has had a complete makeover compared to SE4. It's much simpler and easier to master each weapon instead of having bonkers requirements like "get 100 ricochet kills in the nuts while hanging upside down from the library's chandelier and reciting I'm Henry The 8th I Am". However, mastering a weapon only unlocks a skin for that weapon (either some super-fugly yellow/green camo for pistols and SMGs, or a ghillie wrap for rifles). No stats buffs are applied. These are only accomplished via the myriad of customizable attachment options, which get unlocked by finding the various pistol/SMG/rifle workbenches throughout the game, 1 of each type for a total of 3 per map, giving the game 24 benches in total.Expanded weapon stats are actually presented numerically now instead of just arbitrary-length bars, and this is especially helpful with the various suppressors you can attach to most (not all) weapons, including SMGs. I absolutely welcome the ability to see just how many meters away an enemy will be able to hear your suppressed gunfire. Further to this, a black exclamation mark will appear over a tagged enemy's head while aiming any weapon at them, if they're going to hear the gunshot. Very handy.The P.1938 pistol available only to those who pre-ordered the game is kind of a letdown. It's not a significant step up from the other pistols in the game. IF that happened to be a deciding factor for your game pre-order, you are likely very disappointed with it. I know I am. However, it was not a deciding factor for me, personally.S-mines and trip-mines are no longer present in campaign mode, only in multiplayer modes, and have been replaced with the schu-mine, which is non-lethal. This is a big thumbs-down from me, as now the only lethal mine option is the teller mine, and you can only carry 3 of them (2 before you've unlocked the extra carry ability). One may put forth the counter argument that you can now booby-trap bodies with TNT and grenades (you couldn't do this in previous games), but it's still not as effective as a trip-mine for area denial. I've seen enemies run right over bodies and not trip the trap. They must actually inspect the body to set it off. Big big big thumbs-down.The minimap has also fundamentally changed compared to previous games. In SE4, if an enemy was nearby, it would show up as a discrete dot on the minimap, regardless if he was tagged or not. Now, enemies only show up as large nebulous clouds denoting their general area, and only show as discrete dots once they are tagged via binoculars or a scope. Scope tags wear off after a few moments but binocular tags are permanent, at least in non-Authentic difficulty modes. While some may dislike this new operational mode, I find it a more feasible solution to what basically amounts to a superpower.All in all, I would still recommend the game. I am thoroughly enjoying it, and if my hours logged in SE4 is any indication, I'll be playing this for a long, long time to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Sniper Elite 5 ReviewControls, movement & traversal mechanics:Sniper Elite is first and foremost a tactical game, which implies the player's ability to observe the map, plan ways to approach and then execute the plan with fluidity. For that appropriate level design, movement animations and controls are a requirement. When the player can’t predict whether or not they will be able to climb this wall or vault over that group of crates or hide themselves behind that corner all the tactical elements that give Sniper Elite games their unique identity are removed leaving only generic 3rd person action with clunky controls, glitchy animations and weird AI.Animations blending is missing resulting in disconnected animations. The main default speed feels like you are in a manga, too speedy to me for a jog and the torso of the character is inclined too much. It’s a tactical shooter. Also the transition between climbing a stair and then resuming the default speed is obviously not proper: seems like the math behind is wrong and the speed is miscalculated because of the slope - happens too often in nowadays games. Slow crouch feels unnecessary as you can still approach enemies with a normal crouch (which looks very similar to the one from Splinter Cell Blacklist). At the same time the fast crouch was removed, so the player can only rely on jogging animation which is too fast and clunky to control. Sniper Elite 4 had the same set of animations but used differently with slow crouch being the default one and fast (running) crouch being an option, jog, walk and sprint all working properly and transitions being smooth. Why keep those animations and then change the movement system completely to speed everything up, so it becomes broken?Traversal is incoherent: you don’t really know what you can climb and where. Sometimes you can climb a wall and other times you can’t. Same with vaulting: you can’t vault over wider but still small enough walls, tree trunks or crates which is absurd. It breaks the immersion and reduces the tactical options. And it was possible in SE4! Fluidity is missing from player movements. An important thing - fluid vaulting over and jumping down from high walls when sprinting (like in SE4 … almost and Splinter Cell Blacklist) was removed. Instead you’re constantly interrupted by your character hanging down the wall and need to press the jump down button to continue which breaks the continuity, feels clunky and can be deadly in combat.To resume, people are usually saying that with Ubisoft games you are not in control of your character, but honestly I can legitimately claim that by Splinter Cell Blacklist I was for once in full control.If the developers tried to mimic Elden Ring (not because it was “a said” good one but because it was a successful one on sales*), they reached their goal by successfully reproducing both clunky controls and the invasion system. * I bet my hand FromSoft won’t reproduce that success in their next title if they stick with the same mechanics. I did like, however, the difficulty and the non-handheld approach to the exploration side.Other parts:Binoculars are high tech ones. Did devs try to copy-paste Watch Dogs smartphones this time? Because you feel yourself always connected to a satellite database which is giving you precise information about every German soldier personality and lives. Also that wonderful device comes equipped with a powerful long-range microphone you can use to listen to all their conversations (only tested the Hard difficulty level so I assume the “Authentic” removes that superb feature).Same with markers and UI: Rebellion (the new team) decided to follow Watch Dogs and not Elden Ring (which would have been more appropriate here).A mechanic to hide dead bodies comes straight from Blacklist, Hitman and Metal Gear Solid 5 games (my preference goes to the last one). Zip lines are … no they are not from Death Stranding.Gunplay is … meh. Recoil is almost nonexistent from what I’ve seen. It’s becoming a very “popcorn action game” oriented and no longer a Sniper “Elite”. And yes, some people did say it truly on forums here, I’m starting to be much more interested in Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts games from Underdog Studio, it’s just a shame they did not add a co-op feature to those!And what this animated gif is suggesting to potential buyers, future players, about what you can expect from the game? I’m interested in your answers.Here is mine and also suggestions from my friends: we will be able to drive all those vehicles in the game.Also for the very first time in a game I turned the music off after listening to it for 5 mins. What an idea and a strange one to loop a sound ended with cymbals (drum set) when not in combat?… could continue talking about clunky and broken mechanics compared to Sniper Elite 4, overabundance of silenced guns, strange way to manage your equipment, alert being irrelevant, AI inconsistencies … but it’s enough said already.A conclusion:Don’t get it wrong: I am comparing SE5 to other games not to favor those studios, but to point at nowadays developers copy/pasting existing mechanics and mixing them inappropriately which leads to their own game losing its identity as a result. From my personal point of view it’s not a game made with even a bit of passion, it’s a release rushed to generate funds for the next Rebellion game (by the main team this time and let’s hope that one will justify those sacrifices).

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played any of the previous Sniper Elite games, you already know what you're in for. You play Karl Fairburne, lone wolf American sniper and infiltrator marching through 1944 France and single handedly investigating and ultimately sabotaging a new Nazi weapon system over the course of 9 chapters (well, 8 chapters and some change). As with Sniper Elite 4 the maps continue to be amazing. The third chapter in particular (Spy Academy) takes place at a fictional Beaumont-Saint-Denis which is loosely based on the real life Mont-Saint-Michel in northern France. It's perhaps the most amazing FPS map I've experienced. After I thoroughly cleared the place of Nazis I seriously pondered setting up a virtual coffee shop in one of the courtyards. Unfortunately after that map (and one that proceeded it, Occupied Residence) the remaining maps felt just kinda... meh (Until the final map which was pretty good but involves a lot more close combat than, you know, sniping). The AI is... fine. Ish. I played on the middle setting and while it was a challenge, there were choke points on some maps where the AI soldiers just didn't behave logically. On one map in particular there was a small bridge that soldiers just kept crossing even after watching their comrades getting picked off by Fairburne. It made for an easy culling of the herd, but it felt a little bit like cheating.All in all though it's a very fun game. The maps are sprawling and challenging and I appreciate that they put a LOT of work into a long and varied single player campaign. Looking forward to Sniper Elite 6!

In sniper 5 you always have the silencer so you have to jump back to the weapon ammo screen to see what ammo you are using to know if it will be silenced or not. This SUCKS!!See a nice weapon you want to use just take it....no you might as well not take it. In sniper 4, you can pickup a new weapon and you have it for the rest of the game or match. In sniper 5 this is not the case. If you pickup a weapon, like a cool rifle that is better than yours, and then decide you need your silenced pistol to take a bad guy out, you drop the rifle you had previously picked up that you wanted to keep using. What the HELL! Sometimes you can pick it back up, and sometimes you CAN'T pick it back up. So unless you are going to pick a weapon up and use it right then on the spot, don't bother picking up weapons you will just drop them when you change to another weapon. Stupid!Plant a bomb on a dead body, sure just like sniper 4, only thing is, I have seen bad guys come and kneel next to the body with the bomb in it and it NEVER explodes!!!. They only way I can get them to explode is to plant a bomb away from dead bodies.The weapon upgrades is a complete and unmitigated disaster and an insult to all of us that have any knowledge of firearms. I put a leather cheek pad on my rifle stock and now it takes longer to reload!! What???!!! ARE YOU NUTS!!!! Who had the bright idea to create this system where everything you add to your weapon has an equal or worse negative effect, you are NOT UPGRADING ANYTHING! You are SWAPPING CAPABILITIES! In most cases you are better off just playing with the standard weapon unless you want to TRADE a capability.WOKE GAME? I have seen many comment on this about Sniper Elite 5, and I have to ask the question: Why did they put  NON-LETHAL AMMO in this game??!! This is supposed to be a sniper game not a game of tag! Why don't they just take the weapons and bullets out and give us the option to throw beanbags at the bad guys and really make them afraid. HEY REBELLION: As others have mentioned and I can concur: The MAP execution SUCKS compared to sniper 4. Did you fire the sniper 4 map team and hire a new one with no experience??? How can you muck this up so badly after making such great maps in sniper 4?? A 3 foot fence or a 2 foot bush can stop you from leaving the road or field but hell you can climb a wall or house like spiderman. I can't walk up a 3 foot dirt bank that is nearly flat!!! Constant dead ends in the map to again funnel you back to moving from point A to point B in the manner you designed we would all have to follow in order to play. Just a complete failure when compared to sniper 4. This one point is the reason why a year from now, there will be a lot of people still playing sniper 4 and not a lot will still be playing sniper 5. You took a semi open world map in sniper 4 and made sniper 5 a closed map with pathways. Here is an idea for the future....have 50 or 100 veteran players of the last version of sniper and put them on the concept team to give input into what you are going to build so you don't work on something for years only to find out your new game is not very well liked by your die hard base of customers.My rating on this game so far compared to sniper elite 4: 4 stars out of 10. Sniper elite 4 I would give 8 stars out of 10.Let's hope they fix the bugs, build some open world maps and scrap the weapon trade offs for real upgrades. I would drag this version out behind the barn and bury it. If you don't have sniper elite 4 go buy that one. Skip Sniper Elite 5 for now.

_childDocuments_.review: As part of a covert US Rangers operation to weaken the Atlantikwall fortifications along the coast of Brittany, Karl makes contact with the French Resistance. Soon they uncover a secret Nazi project that threatens to end the war before the Allies can even invade Europe: Operation Kraken. It's Karl's mission to take out the high-ranking Nazi officers and end Operation Kraken once and for all. Based upon real world locations from France in 1944, the new game maps are the largest and most immersive in the franchise's history with the new traversal system offering players an even greater sandbox of options when it comes to taking out their targets. You can even invite a friend to help you on your mission with enhanced cooperative gameplay options.

name: Seed of Life
detailed_description: Seed of Life is an action-adventure puzzle game that will take you to a beautiful yet toxic world where almost all life has disappeared. There's only one way to survive: help Cora find The Seed , an alien device capable of generating the essence of life, and save your planet from annihilation. Find your way through a labyrinth like world full of mysteries, dangers and beauty. Search for capsules and learn special abilities. Face off against alien creatures and solve challenging puzzles. As the sun is dying, the world is fading into chaos. Invaders appeared out of nowhere and took us by surprise... There was nothing we could do! They took our most precious treasure: the planet's life force, leaving us to certain death. Alien creatures were left on the land to absorb what's left alive. To save your home you need to find the source of life and activate the ancient machine. Let the light guide you! features: AN EMOTIONAL JOURNEY - A dramatic, engaging story full of mysteries to be revealed. Face up to your fears and find a way to bring life back to Lumia. TRIPLE-A QUALITY GRAPHICS - A breathtaking sci-fi setting in a dystopian future. A fascinating fading world, where bright colors meet utter darkness. DYNAMIC GAMEPLAY - A story-driven adventure packed with puzzles to solve and dangerous shadows. Learn unique abilities and try to survive in a hostile environment. SEMI OPEN-WORLD - Freely explore a beautiful and vast world where secrets are hidden in every corner and environmental challenges will test your skills.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to be able to enjoy this game - but overall my experience wasn't a fun one. I received a copy of the game for free, via the devs through Keymailer. The game looked really interesting and promising - and overall the game  very beautiful. The music and sfx are also quite good. Now let me tell you about the things I did not enjoy.  - the main character, Cora's voice. While I appreciate the effort of going through and having a voiced game, I feel like the main character's voice was... emotionless. She felt very flat, she sounded almost bored with everything going on.  Coming from a background in theatre and audio dramas and the like, I think this is... kind of a buzzkill -  on a main protagonist. The voice actor seemed as though they were handed a script with very little direction, and they just went monotone and emotionless, and that really takes away from the character. I ended up lowering the speech volume down to zero so I didn't have to listen to her anymore. - There were some small collision issues I kept coming across. Small ledges that a character should be able to just step up on, were huge hindrances and would stop Cora dead in her tracks. When you're running on a timer, these little hiccups cost you precious moments at the cost of your health and power. - There was very little. While I think that there's merit to not holding a player's hand that much, there was very little in the way of guidance even at the very beginning of the story campaign. You were shown cut scenes, but no real markers to point you which way you should be headed to complete your objectives. You were just given an objective and the rest was left to you to figure it out. In the early stage of this game, that's not much of a problem. However in the next zone, it is a HUGE problem. You find out that outside of the way points you unlock, the air is toxic and you will steadily lose health while you're not in one of the waypoints. When attempting to find your next location that you've got to head off to, this health timer is a big detriment on top of not having any guidance as to where to go. You unlock a very simple compass fairly early, but it's not much help with pathing your way to the points you want to go to.: The color coding on the arrow markers was a bit confusing. I initially thought that the colored arrows meant that: green would be the closest and easiest to access of the waypoints, and red would be the hardest and farthest. What it ended up being, however, was that the colored arrows corresponded to the color of the power that you unlock at that particular waypoint. I think that the more intuitive way to have that set up would have been the former rather than the latter. It's not a huge deal breaker, but it was a point of confusion for me. I suppose that this is somewhat true, it is a semi-open world, but it's not one that you get to explore and enjoy at your leisure. You have a severe limit in your health while traversing outside of the waypoints, which means you can't do very much exploring of the beautiful game without risking losing anything you find because you can't figure out where the next waypoint is, or get back to the previous one in time to save your things.My suggestions: -  In other games where there's timed zones for whatever reason, like oxygen capacity in swimming levels, there are typically spots through out the map in those games where you'll be able to top off your oxygen in order to continue to your objective. In this the waypoints are both your objectives and your safety bubbles - but getting to them can result in a lot of dying in between. To counteract that, perhaps the Lumina plants could also be small safe zones where you can slowly regenerate your lumin and health. It would allow the player a chance to get their bearings and to figure out the best route to take to get to the objective, instead of having to blindly leap out into the unkonw and die repeatedly until they figure out the path they have to take.-  Even minimal suggestions or small arrows pointing out paths or telling you that you should wait to go a certain way would be helpful. Right now there is very little in the way of guidance for the game, and I spent about 30-40 minutes attempting to figure out where I was supposed to go in one of the areas. This could be easily fixed with some small  hints of which way you should generally go. If you want people to not have their hand held, or if people don't want to have these tips and hints, make it so that they can be turned off in the settings. I think that this alone would alleviate a great deal of frustration - at least on my part.I'm not sure how to go about implementing such changes, or even if it's a feasible thing. I'm not sure what can and cannot be adjusted or changed within the game or even if the Devs would want to do something like that. I was very excited about getting to play the game, but in the first twenty minutes I was ready to shut it off. I held out for just over two hours before I said that I was done and couldn't keep going. I really,  wanted to love this game. I could absolutely still see a lot of people enjoying the struggle of it. But for me, it was like I was bashing my head against a wall and hoping the wall would break before my skull did, and that made the least enjoyable experience I could have probably had. If there were some significant changes and updates to the game that would adjust a few things, I might give it another go. As it stands right now at release? I doubt that I'll be playing any further.

_childDocuments_.review: Seed of Life is third person adventure game with platforming elements.Aliens have raped the planet Lumia of resources and left with all the vital life source, Lumium.Lumium maintains the balance and holds the universe together; Without it life ceases to exist and the Sun is dying.Cora, an inhabitant of Lumia finds an old book describing her grandfather’s heroic mission to find the seed of life. The seed will reignite life into the planet and return order to the universe, but he has not returned and no word has been heard from him.Having not lost hope, she decides to follow in her grandfather’s footsteps and sets out to find him and save the planet.  The planet is in decay and the water and air has become polluted. The darkness fills the land and slowly kills anything it touches. Every second spent in the darkness drains your energy until you die. Your only chance is to run through the darkness and find pedestals where you are safe and can recover your health and lumium levels.Technology is gained by finding the Talisman, an ancient artifact that seems to bond with you. It becomes part of you and is able to house capsules with special abilities. It lets you know how much lumium and health you have and acts as a crude direction finder by pointing in the direction of your goal.The capsules can be gathered at special pedestals where you need to decipher a picture puzzle by turning three wheels. Once the pedestal is unlocked you can purchase a capsule in exchange for petals.There are six capsules to collect and they introduced in order as you progress.This is very useful for finding places of interest and revealing hidden objects. Using this ability highlights sources of lumium, health waypoints and petals among other things.Health Waypoints can be accessed if you have enough lumium and grant you a plus ten health bonus.The vision ability also reveals hidden paths in midair.Using the light capsule will light the way, or at least give you some extra visibility in darker areas. This is useful when avoiding chasms or navigating thin ledges in the dark.This capsule recovers your health, allowing you to travel further without seeking refuge. Once activated, a shield surrounds your body and slowly regenerates your health. The sprint capsule will boost your running speed and allow you to jump much further distances. Once this is equipped you will be able to interact with magnetized items, flying through the air and sticking to them.This capsule allows you to manipulate special objects and move them around. Once you have collected a capsule it gives more detail about its use and gives instructions on how to use it in the glossary.Seed of Life is a game of two halves. I hated the first half due to its forced feeling of hurriedness. Navigating the dark and watching your health depleting wasn’t fun or challenging, it just felt frustrating and annoying. I wanted to freely explore the environment but this time penalty placed on me made me feel rushed. This was made even worse by the fact that the sprint capsule is only introduced later in the game.You will be running a lot in this game and Cora moves too slowly. I don’t think they should have made sprinting an ability. It should have been included from the start as a default and it shouldn’t have cost lumium to use.The darkness seems to disappear in the second half and is replaced by environmental dangers like acid pools and lava rivers. This was much more fun without the pressure of finding safety constantly to recharge. Unfortunately, platforming issues made this less enjoyable than it should have been.The character movements are very inharmonious which can be seen at its worst when walking slowly. Movement is jolting and cumbersome and feels unsatisfying. This makes traversing thin areas like planks more difficult than it should be. The camera angles when in tight areas seems to go a bit aloof. This can be seen in caves and climbing ivy on walls. The controls are extremely loose and I had countless deaths from platforming that I didn’t feel was my fault. For example, jumping on to platforms in midair was a challenge because the character can stop in mid jump. I wasn’t very good at science but I thought it was impossible to just stop like that. Isn’t there a thing called inertia? This meant I had to over compensate and often I would shoot over the platform. There were other anomalies that made platforming a chore and annoying.It was only towards the end that I sort of realized how everything fitted together. There seemed to be a little bit of confusion caused by lack of instructions. I would advise reading the glossary after obtaining an ability capsule as this tells you much more information which is needed. There are lots of things left out which will make you feel puzzled. The game play is quite tedious. There are no puzzles as such. Progress is determined by finding the right path. It becomes a little repetitive after a while. Enemies are very weak and provide no challenge.The story was uninteresting and the only real information was given at the start and end of the game. There was no character development or plot. It isn’t much of an adventure. It gave me no incentive to drive on and I felt like quitting the game on numerous occasions due to the above mentioned criticisms.The game world is nice to look at and the special effects sounds are good, apart from the awful grunt every time you jump.It takes around ten hours to complete and you should obtain all the achievements if you get to the end. The visuals are very nice and look colorful and bright. The aesthetics are probably the highlight of the game. The sprinting mechanic is especially pleasing to watch.Sound effects are quite nice with science-fiction like ambient noises and harsh environmental sounds. The voice acting is cartoon like in quality and doesn’t sound human. It therefore lacks emotion and takes a while to get used to.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game 100%, I'd like to give a review that will hopefully be beneficial to both the game devs and the potential buyers. First and foremost, I give the game a 6/10 and here's why.1. The game is lacking. While some of the later sections have some decent puzzle mechanics, most of the game doesn't have much in the way of puzzles. The platforming has some potential, but lacks the polish to make it a notable indie game. As of now, I barely see a reason as to why it is considered action.2. The game's visual and auditory assets are above average. As such, there are a few minor cosmetic glitches that can happen to the main character at various times (though most people won't encounter them). The Sound Effects are also reasonably well-made. They are fitting and decently impressive. These 2 aspects are the saving grace of the game.3. This game has potential that unfortunately doesn't seem used. I can see some very interesting puzzles that the devs could implement using the , but unfortunately the main focus of the game seems to be the sprint mechanic. After completing the first area and acquiring the first 3 abilities, the game tends to lean on the sprint feature throughout the rest of the game (which isn't a problem), but seeing as you have several other skills available later on, I feel like they could have done much more with this game in the way of puzzles.4. Voice acting: where to begin.... It isn't bad at first, but then the monotone voice that stays the same throughout the rest of the game feels very lackluster. I don't want to spoil anything, but none of the characters seem to exhibit any emotion throughout the majority of the game.5. Sprinting: the not game-breaking mechanic that kind of breaks the game. Walls and ledges tend to interact very weirdly when sprinting, for you see, apparently Cora can fly up walls or slide down them when sprinting. Also, you can essentially get out of bounds on nearly area by just sprinting and jumping on a wall. (you have to learn the technique, but once you do it is fairly simple)The devs don't hold your hand in this game and usually don't give much in the way of directions which is fine for the most part (personally, I think this is a bold move, but a fairly good one relating to the story). Seeing as Cora is on her own, and doesn't have any real teacher.)  I paid full price for this game, unfortunately, like I said before, this feels liked missed potential. I played this on stream and didn't have a very fun time with it. The one time I played it, I actually changed games mid stream. As a word to the devs, polish. Polish one feature and let the player master it before giving them another or just work them into a more complete "level" of some sort. There just seems to be a lack of build up in the way of learning the usefulness of your abilities. Each item's glossary is essentially the same as the dialogue line you get. IDK, I feel like it just a little more useful information then that. Feel free to contact with any questions. I hope this hasn't discouraged you. I will come back to this game if they ever do like a major update (maybe even some minor ones) just because I see potential for this game to be something. Best wishes to the devs, and I hope you continue to update this game, but right now I unfortunately wouldn't recommend this game, at least at full price. I don't feel ripped off, because I know that in supporting them, it will encourage them to make the game better and better. This is something I hope they do. Cheers!P.S. If there is going to be any more chapters tell me, and I will be glad to give it another go!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game on my stream, and while I recognize there are a lot of really neat aspects and concepts behind it, along with beautiful visuals, the gameplay itself is quite lacking and frustrating. The physics in the game were a constant frustration, with POV and FOV problems making it difficult to judge platforming positions, especially on platforming where sprinting was required. There are also times when the environment is too open where you lose a sense of what it is you are supposed to be working toward or how you should get there. I had to consult walkthroughs several times after getting stuck, something I do not do on my streams. I also encountered some glitches that made me think I was doing something wrong, only to find out that restarting the game fixed the glitch. The game has a lot of heart and work put into it, but it's simply not enjoyable and has been the source of some of my strongest frustrations in gaming in a long time. It has so much potential, but in its current state, I don't recommend spending the time on this.

I made a video to show the way to the last capsule, which you can find , but no other guides available yet. 2 on Astats No No No No No No No No, you can play on the easiest difficulty (Story) NoI find making the review of this game a bit challenging. The game has a lot of potential and the start of the game is fun, but later on in the game I mostly struggled with the controls, which sucked out some of the enjoyment. I played the game with a gamepad as I'm used to that, but I hear it plays better with a keyboard and mouse. The ability I struggled most with in combination with the controls is the running ability.  Since you have to push down the left control stick to use it, which in my opinion is a horrible way, I would personally swap that to R2 but at this moment the game doesn't allow you to change controls. I hope they will implement that option in the future. The story of this puzzle adventure game is quite interesting, and I enjoyed it and loved that Cora wouldn't want to harm the planet she is living on even more. There feels a disconnect between the story and the voice acting of Cora. She didn't show much emotion in her voice. What also doesn't help is that Cora walks slowly when she starts talking, so if in the middle of something she starts explaining some of her thoughts you feel she is holding you up. On at least one occasion she ends her thoughts with "I should hurry", yeah please let me walk normally then even when you talk and we would hurry :PWhile I have all this critique, I want to also point out that the 2 developers are very responsive. On the steam forums, discord, and by e-mail. They implemented already some of the improvements and tips from players into updates, and that while the game is only out for 2 days. So I have high hopes that most of the raw edges will be patches out. I think this game would have benefitted a lot from more playtesting or maybe even releasing in Easly Access. The achievements for this game are very straight forward and you can't lock yourself out of any of them. Try to find as many plants as possible to make the game easier for yourself and you don't have to backtrack much at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzling adventure with a handful of small flaws for my personal taste..This is one of those occasions where I wish the review system wasn't simply yes/no. A "maybe" button would definitely be in order for this one.I really enjoyed the premise of Seed of Life as well as the art, but a few things just spoiled the experience for me personally. The delivery of voice acting from the playable character felt a little stale, flat, and even emotionless at points. This is a shame because of the over arcing story of the game itself was very intriguing and I genuinely wanted to learn more about what was going on.Exploration was fun, and gradually getting new abilities as you go and encounter more of the world felt rewarding. Sadly, for me, this was also somewhat ruined by the fact that you have a constant ticking clock, in the form of your health bar constantly emptying as you go, which means getting from point to point becomes a race against time and you can't simply stop and smell the roses, nor take in the vistas as you go. For these reasons, it's a no from me, but, others may enjoy the things that I found myself disliking. Who knows? Perhaps future updates will change my mind.

_childDocuments_.review: And here comes the giant NOPE. Don't buy this game.- Physics is broken- The camera is sometimes drunk (shaking when I'm swimming for absolutely no reason, for example)- Some textures are just ugly (on a rock, in a lava lake that is supposed to be in motion, it feels like I'm on a giant lava treadmill, everything is static)- The animation is terrible (jumping, swimming, climbing, falling, nothing looks natural)- Falling, by the way, is random. Sometimes you take a bit of damage, sometimes you die. - Walking in a bit of water makes the grass steps sound, no water sound.- No splash animation or sound when you jump in the water- The controls don't feel nice at all- The main character we play talks. God, that acting is flat. I don't believe in any emotions she is trying to play. If she is trying.- The interface is not clear at all.- The transitions in the music are absent. It's literally: Music 1 on. Stop music 1. Play music 2. No fade, no transition, nothing. I even managed to get the character right at the transition zone, the game didn't know which song to play, so it was getting from song 1 to song 2, than song 1, than song 2, etc... Without any transition, of course. Horrible. I think you got it.I'm really sorry for the team who did the game, maybe there was not enough time, not enough budget, I don't know, but that's not done correctly at all. The final product doesn't worth £20 at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Seed of Life is all about rewarding exploration.  Explanation on where you need to go is bare minimum, which comes across like a breath of fresh air.  Even control tutorials are left for you to figure out, for the most part.  I enjoyed it!  Hand holding is fine most times, but trial and error brings it own triumph as well. All in all, Seed of Life is a great time for secret hunters and explorer buffs.  Jump on in, ma dudes!

_childDocuments_.review: ^^I purchased this game, with my very own monies^^Seed of Life is an action adventure puzzle game. I found that the story and worldbuilding drew me right in. An alien world that has been desolated and is falling apart. A Protagonist that is one of only two people that we know of. The voice of Cora was very intriguing. To start with her voice is very emotionless, worn down ready to give up. I get the feeling that we don’t know how long she has been alone, or how long the planet has been falling apart. As the game progresses along you can hear more emotion come into her voice, as she regains hope, and starts to believe that the planet can be saved. Point being I believe that this was an artistic choice by the game developers to have her acted in this way.The puzzles in the game had some challenge to them, but most of them could be solved quickly. This ramped up well as I got stuck on two puzzles later in the game. One was a platformer puzzle over lava, and the other was a bunch of the shadow enemies patrolling. This game does not hold your hand as far as where to go or what to do, you’ll have to figure it out, and carve your own path. This can be frustrating when you know you need to use a new capsule ability, but don’t know how to use it. I hated the checkpoint system at first. I felt totally tethered to them, and all exploration was closed off. As you unlock the abilities you gain more and more range. By the time you get to the final zone you won’t even notice the checkpoints anymore.The length of the game felt short for $20, I completed the story with 3.4 hours of playtime. I am missing 3 achievements, and those could probably be finished in another hour. The ending also leaves more questions, and a feeling that the game hasn’t really ended. I would give it a rating of 3/5 I think the worldbuilding, style, and voice acting is worth checking out. Loss of points for a low hours to price ratio, puzzle challenge, and lackluster ending. If you enjoy story driven puzzle games it is worth checking out. I also have a Let’s Play on my youtube channel, all episodes are out now.

_childDocuments_.review: Seed of Life is an enjoyable, yet decent adventure game as you take on the character of Cora on the dying planet of Lumia, which has been overtaken by an alien invasion. Cora must journey through the realms of this planet in hopes to activate the Seed of Life and restore the planet. While the description says that the light conquers the darkness, I have mixed feelings about this game. On the one hand, it definitely meant this game is for those that want to relax and wind down. The gorgeous environment visuals and peaceful, yet ambient nature of the landscape of Lumia definitely provide this. This game suffers from generic-level designs that should have been more innovative. The game’s story keeps to a simple K.I.S.S formula and that works wonders for introducing the world and showing how this world is illustrated by the backdrop of an alien invasion. The story, however, did not achieve the deep potential connection that it was striving to go for, as I did not feel enough of an emotional connection to Cora in the first half, but during the latter half of the story, I did. This game is definitely more family-friendly, and I think they created the story in a way that it did not become ambitious, and it did not reflect the extreme potential it had in making Cora stand out as a character, as she should have.The story of the gameplay of Seed of Life is quite simple, and it does a good job of introducing Cora to this world. As Cora, you leave your house and navigate through a myriad of complex canyons and volcanic lands to enter the Seed of Life. Once you pass through these levels, you collect Lumium, which helps with energy. You also have to go to Pedestals to make sure that you recharge your health and Lumium and collect petals. This I felt was the strongest aspect of gameplay because it is giving you directions on how you survive in this world. Another powerful aspect of the game is that when Cora reaches areas, you can feel earthquakes, wood dropping to the deep caves of this world. These moments definitely make the world alive, but it doesn’t add enough immersion. There are no murals, no illustrations written in the caves depicting the fall. Even if Lumia fell to the alien invasion, there would have been survivors that wrote or depicted the event. I think there would have been enough space within the budget to add small touches like this here and there.Once you do this, you can unlock abilities from the Pedestals that will help you in regeneration, increasing your Luium supply, and allow you to recharge often. One of the best parts is the sprinting ability, which I absolutely love, but hate when you have to cross bridges because the minute you fall is when you have to respawn once again when crossing a level. This, I felt, was the strongest aspect of gameplay. One thing that disappointed me about this game was collecting petals. To collect Petals, they are your life force in a way to unlock new abilities once you reach a pedestal and solve a puzzle thereby unlocking that new ability. You must navigate crooks, nannies, and whatnot to collect a petal by going to a purple gate and pressing E. This then activates the shield guarding it to disperse.This sort of focal chokepoints sure adds mystery, but they don’t add enough sense of adventure for me in the game. I didn’t like how you had to climb certain areas when I would have just wanted to climb everywhere, to be honest. Cora doesn’t run quickly enough. I believe that with a bigger budget, the story should and could have been more. I should have had Cora narrating her personal moments to me when she enters parts of a canyon, maybe some more forgotten ruins here and there. For a world that is medieval, from what I saw, I would have wanted to see more medieval ruins dotted around the map here and there. What I felt Seed of Life was essentially a game that was the foundation. Introduce the world, and make the world as simplistic as possible, which is a good thing. The game lacked combat in pretty much most of my gameplay, and in fact, solving the puzzles is an enjoyable challenge. But they are not as good as they should be. As I went from checkpoint to checkpoint, pedestal to pedestal, I came upon these puzzles to solve. Outstanding, you might say. What disappointed me the most was how easy they were to solve. I wanted more mystery. Yes, you talk to a robot named Nar that explains why they destroyed Lumia, but that it was inevitable, yet not a choice of their own choosing. This was quite a weak moment for me, as I would want either free content updates or DLC to expand the story and a better explanation of why the invasion actually occurred. I think the game followed the K.I.S.S formula a little too much. To get to further elements of the story, the Robot advisor Nar does a good job of motivating your character. To unlock further secrets of the story, you need to gain around 2000 Lumium, where you go to these other checkpoints or landmarks in order to deplete your points and listen. I didn’t think this element added much fun to the gameplay.Seed of Life is a game that promises adventure, and where it delivers on the adventure aspect are the environments and the tasks that you need to do to survive. Where it doesn’t fulfill this aspect is by not having challenging puzzles to solve, by having very basic level designs for crossing bridges or going from one end to the other, and it doesn’t have many medieval ruins nor does the story introduce some nuanced, deeper gameplay mechanics that could also be simplified in a way. Seed of Life is begging for more content.Seed of Life is a fun, family-friendly game that has decent voice acting, a story that follows the K.I.S.S formula to a great degree, but at the expense of sacrificing deeper lore for more basic gameplay level design and gorgeous environment visuals. However, good visuals cannot disguise the weaknesses of Seed of Life’s major story. For a game like Seed of Life, it needs a strong story, and the story in this game is serviceable, but not deep enough that it got me emotional at the end because it feels like the setup for new content to be added, some DLC or maybe a Seed of Life 2. It lacks much in the innovation department for solving puzzles because the puzzles could have been better designed. It should have motivated me more than often. Yet I often fell from bridges many times, and it made me so frustrated that I almost didn’t like it. Seed of Life should be more engaging with its lore, allowing us to get immersed in the world. It does this at the beginning, but the game then becomes this: Explore the fantastic environment of this world, gain a lot of Luiumn to discover secrets, but not enough content is there yet to immerse the player. However, this game is definitely worth trying out because it is a game that is relaxing and the lack of combat in this game is a prominent feature. I want more puzzles, more content, and more story updates. I believe this will make the game better.You can find the full review here at Sassy : You can also find my review on youtube here:

_childDocuments_.review: Seed of Life, by developer MadLight and publisher Leonardo Interactive, is a fun story driven adventure game that is a bit rough around the edges. You play as a young girl named Cora who is the last known survivor of the dying planet called Lumia. The only way to save Lumia is to activate the seed of life so that the world can be restored. You must venture out and explore the perilous dying planet, overcoming many obstacles and puzzles along the way to restore your world, for you are its last hope. In the beginning of the game, you go through a long cutscene where the main character tells you about the world and what has happened to it. After the cutscene is over you start in a house where you ultimately decide that you have to go find the seed, thus starting your adventure in this dying world.The story of Seed of Life is very interesting and compelling, and has some pretty good pacing as well. It gives you gradual information without completely telling you the full story in the beginning. The graphics of the game are also very nice, it is a little dark, but not so much in a bad way as it makes the lights of the plants all the more vibrant. They give off a good dark and mysterious vibe, along with the cutscenes that give you a nice look at the surroundings and where you are going. Another aspect of the atmosphere is the music and sound effects; they keep up the mysterious atmosphere as well as the adventurous state of the game. All in all, Seed of Life sets up a really good atmosphere and while it did make me want to continue playing I had quite a few issues along the way Most of the movement is alright if a bit touchy; the main problem I have with it is the collision. There were areas that you could crouch under at one point but then couldn’t at another point, as well as ledges that should be easily climbable, but keep making you slide off. It made navigating through areas difficult at times especially in the areas that took away your health the longer you were in them. Not only was the navigation through the world difficult, but so was the actual progression of the game. There was some, but very little guidance on where to go and I often got lost along the way. It didn’t help that there were areas that I thought I could go through or around only to be stopped because the collision was so touchy. Another issue I had was the voice acting. The main character’s voice was very monotone and didn’t match the situations she was in at all, taking away from the story telling a lot in the beginning. I will say, though, you do kind of get used to it later on. Overall, I loved the atmosphere the game created, but there were also quite a few issues that could use some work.Seed of Life is a fun action adventure style puzzle game that has an interesting story, but has quite a few problems as well. The developers do set up an amazing atmosphere with the graphics and story, but there are many issues with the gameplay itself that make the game harder to play. The navigation and collision along with the monotone voice acting take away from the game and the potential it has. All that being said, however, Seed of Life is not a terrible game, it is a bit frustrating at times but isn't impossible to get through and is still fun to play. The developers just have some polishing and updating to do and this game could be a lot better in the long run. I’m giving Seed of Life a 6 out of 10 rating because even though it has many issues, it's not a bad game and can certainly be fixed in the future.

name: Torchlight III
detailed_description: It’s been a century since the events of Torchlight II, and the Ember Empire is in decline. In Torchlight III, Novastraia is again under threat of invasion and it’s up to you to defend against the Netherim and its allies. Gather your wits and brave the frontier to find fame, glory, and new adventures! Travel the Frontier Brave the vast wilderness of Novastraia and all of its dangers either alone or with a group of friends!  Collect Epic Gear Whether it’s armor, weapons, or even new pets...there’s always more to find as you battle through dungeons and take on dangerous foes. Build Your Hero With four unique classes to choose from and five available Relic subclasses, there are many different ways to build your hero and maximize your damage. You’ll also gather epic gear along your journey that you can customize to work with your hero’s unique make-up. Build & Upgrade Your Fort It’s time to rebuild – and that includes you! Enjoy your very own fort, where you can upgrade gear and renovate your fort to show off to your friends and the world. Pets Are Back Fight your way to fame and glory with your loyal companion! Add skills and equip them with gear to make them stronger. Each species comes in a myriad of colors and styles, so make sure to collect them all!

_childDocuments_.review: Torchlight III fully detailed reviewSPOILERS MAY ACCOUR - Updated with bug fixes and patches (15 of April 2021)This review is based on my knowledge from both Torchlight 1 and 2.I’ve completed both games with 100% of the achievements and with 44.7 in game hours from TL1 and 153.9 hours from TL2.I will mainly compared TL3 to TL2 since it’s the most complete game and my favorite so far.!!! EVERYTHING CAN CHANGE IN THE GAME !!!This is just my opinions and view on the game from early access to the date of this post.Conclusion (Keep in mind, this is my opinion):This game is without doubt pretty good, but it really does feel empty and repetitive. I know it’s a dungeon crawler, but why not go do something completely different and think outside the box a little?It’s a solid game experience, but I would recommend you play online with your friends as you’ll get more out of the game.Player single player gets a little boring with time and having some social moments will for sure lighten it up.You can’t play single player characters in multiplayer and vice versa, so have some single player characters to test things out and then go for multiplayer with your main characters.The game is not yet complete, it still updates and their Discord is filled with devs and helpful players who can guide you on the game and updates.It's pretty similar to TL2, TL3 is just not there… Yet.As the player base grows, guides and help on the WiKi will expand and things will be clearer to new players.XP System:The XP system is a little confusing. It scales in a weird way.The amount you need for leveling up depends on your level like any other game, but as you level up, you still need the same amount of XP for  some time.Potions:Potions are interesting in some ways and then not at all.In TL2, your potions scaled with you. You also had mana potions and other potions that did everything from boosting you to instantly kill you.I like that the potions have an effect when you use them instead of just healing you, nice touch.Items:There are a lot of cool items in the game with unique passives just like any other game.The items also have cool looks and you can even customize your weapons and armor.A thing that makes me sad is that all prices are fixed in the shop and the legendary weapons you’ll find throughout the game is worth no more than 100 gold coins and doesn't scale with enchantments or alike.In TL2 and similar games, the legendary and enchanted items are worth a lot more and this seems to be left out.Bossing:Bossing was something I looked forward to a lot in TL3.I really liked the bosses from TL2, but in TL3 it’s a little different story…I did enjoy the longer boss fights, but with that said, it feels like they just gave the bosses more health points so it would take you longer to kill them.I wouldn’t mind if that meant that the bosses had different stages and different abilities throughout the fight, but only a small handful has that and some only does one or two things.I would love to see the bosses be more hardcore and have different stuff that would make the fights harder and more unpredictable.So far I also found that the Act 2 boss is WAY easier than the Act 1 boss.The Act 3 boss is not only a familiar one, it’s also a more interesting and aggressive version.Creeps/Mobs:The thing I really like is that many enemies are similar if not the same in TL3 as in TL2, but I only enjoyed that upon encounter.After thinking about it a little more, it just felt like they reused the old enemies as they struggled to come up with new ideas.I do like how the different enemies fit their environments, but I would have loved to see a little more variation and a lot of new enemies so you’d encounter the same enemy less often, but kept founding new enemies. Trading:Trading is non-existing in multiplayer.I played a fair amount with a good friend of mine and several times we came across some nice loot that would fit the other player better than ourselves, but we just couldn’t trade it. The trading feature is simply not there.Maybe some sort of an auction house where all players could sell/buy and trade weapons and gear would be a cool thing.Enchantments:So for some reason enchanting is an end game feature which I'm not a fan of.I really like the idea of combining and figuring out the best options early on so you don’t waste money on expensive gear, but yet again, the enchantments are not necessary in early game as you’ll do just fine.However, the entire enchantment concept is all about breaking down items into essence and then spending that on recipes you'll find throughout the game, so don’t expect your favorite items to be enchanted right away.Fort:The Fort is a nice little feature, but honestly nothing too special.You had no such thing in TL2 and you did not need to.It’s pretty cool to have a place you can show off to your friends.You can fully customize it and do as you please, but only a few things actually serves a purpose for you character.I’m sure there will be much more to it in the future, but as of now, not that interesting.Skills:There are a lot of cool and unique abilities for each character, but compared to similar games, it’s barely anything.You have your different relic powers which are pretty cool, but in similar games, you can combine skills and abilities and do as you please, but in TL3 and TL in general it’s more fixed and you have to be creative with what you have.The limited choices the players have are a little sad, but you’ll quickly figure out what works the best for your play style. Pets: Pets haven’t really had a change and I don’t think it needs that.In TL2 you could go fishing and give your pets a buff, but in TL3 you can’t do that and there’s no fishing.When fighting bosses, there are often pet cages you can open after the fight to receive a pet with a unique passive.In TL2, you also had 3 different modes you could set your pet to.Passive, neutral and aggressive, in TL3, there’s nothing.Quests:Quests seems the same to me, a little killing here and a little gathering there, nothing too major, but I do think it would be more interesting with some special quests or tasks like “Robot Parts” in TL2.The end game:So I must admit that I liked the end game in TL2, different maps at the Clockwork Core, but yet again it got pretty repetitive.In the TL3 there’s a little different spin on it.You meet your good old friend, Dun’djinn.Although I like how this puts up different challenges and puts a new perspective to the game, it seems like the only purpose is now to grind your way to level up and enchant stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: After seeing all the disappointed reviews, I didn't want to try this game. I love the Torchlight series and didn't want this third instalment to ruin that for me. I waited until the sale was on and thought I'd take a bite.I regret not buying this game when it first came out because it deserves what it costs. What you need to know is that I have clocked many many hours on Hack and Slash / ARPG style games so neither is this my first nor do I review this with any particular bias.TL:DR=====Torchlight 3 is an excellent game. It is fun, addictive and satisfying and it does all of that in perfect Torchlight style.Everything from the fighting, the bosses frequency, the inventory management, the loot vs level, the forge (you set out your own forge - brilliant!) the game style, well done. I'm hooked.I highly recommend it!Some More Detail==============Looking at the sheer number of negative reviews on this game does not make sense to me at all. This game isn't meant to be a competitor to Diablo, I don't think it even cares to do that. It is a completely different style of game and I think that's what makes it shine the most.Torchlight stands out among other ARPG games in being beginner-friendly, family-friendly and beautifully made. It moves away from the dark style art and horror-feel and has never been like that. The art team must have had so much fun designing this game because I think they have nailed the trademark Torchlight style. It has a sort of Dota 2 style smooth, easy-on-the-eyes design and I am absolutely in love with it.I couldn't put the controller down and clocked over an hour of play from the first try. That may not be much for some people but I don't have that sort of time anymore. This game is addictive and fun.Is it perfect? No. I wish the game ran a little faster. I wish there were different, more innovative, classes.There also seems to be some minor glitches that don't affect the playing AT ALL I did notice them.Other than that, I can't fault the game as of yet. I love it and I know that you will too.Get this game. It will be worth it.What other Games have I played in the genre?Diablo 3, Path of Exile, Hades, Torchlight 1, Torchlight 2, The Incredible Adventures of Van HelsingWhich classes have I tried in Torchlight 3?SharpshooterWhich pets have I had?Llama, Fox, Bulldog (you get more as you progress. It's hilarious and brilliant)

_childDocuments_.review: "Why is this so poorly rated compared to Torchlight II."So, two of the key devs left Runic Games, the company behind Torchlight I and II, to return to making smaller games. Echtra, the developer of Torchlight III, is the remaining key dev and a handful of the remaining team from Runic before they shut down.It's no surprise this is not the same type of game as the first two; it's not  a sequel so much as it just skinned Torchlight and wore its skin.My personal hangups with the game involve accessibility issues; No subtitles during cutscenes, and the inability to rebind the loot key to something more ergonomic than the alt key. I'm mangling my hand just to play the game optimally.There are some cool ideas present to try and streamline the experience but so much is executed poorly, it gets hard to overlook.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, BUT ..... only if its super cheap and on sale.  Its still a decent game to play through, as leveling is fun, and it is a Torchlight game and all.  But DO NOT PAY FULL PRICE FOR THIS GAME.  If they finally fix this game, I'll come and change my comments, but since its been a couple years, I doubt we'll ever see the game we wanted to see in Torchlight 3.  Torchlight games have a lot of cool ideas that they bring to the table.  Torchlight 2 was a nearly perfect game and was fun through multiple playthroughs.  However, Torchlight 3 feels completely unfinished, even after it has been out for years.  They have some really cool innovative ideas that would be SOO FUN to play with if only they were properly finished.  It feels like they got a rough outline built out in the game (for a lot of things) and then forgot to finish them or decided not to.  And in many areas, they seem to have forgotten that Torchlight is known for creating cool new features and ideas for RPG games and in this game they feel like they regressed back into childhood and don't understand RPGs anymore.  Here are some examples:-- Vendors: really, the last city in the story line in the game has vendors that sell the same exact things as the first city.  They don't even have a vendor that sells higher quality gear than whites.  Yeah, they have a gambler, but you don't find much gold so not many people are going to waste  their gold on gambling.  I tried a couple of times and again, all I got were whites.-- Map Overlay Glitch: The minimap and map overlay are nearly broken all the time.  When you first log in you'll be able to use the map overlay, but if you play for about 5-10 minutes, this will break and become unavailable and you can only get it back by leaving the game and coming back in. Navigation around a map is incredibly hard without this.  Yes, there is the actual map screen you can still pull up, but you can't use that and fight at the same time.- Party Members on map:  You have a really short range to see where your party members are.  If you literally walk half a screen away, you cannot see each other on the map.  This is SOOO frustrating trying to play with people because you lose track of each other and it just increases the frustration 1000% and is also primarily the main reason my daughter doesn't play this game for more than 30min before she gets too frustrated and gives up on this game for another one.-- And the MOST ANNOYING (feature?) in the game is the loot dropping.  As with many RPGs, you run through till you find a boss or miniboss, kill them and grab loot, and run along.  SOOO MANY times I have killed a guy, walked away, then hear loot dropping from his corpse.  So I run back pick up the loot then run away and then all the gold starts dropping off of his corpse.  This game on purpose makes you sit around a boss you killed for at minimum 10 seconds while you stand around waiting for your loot.  This happens on EVERYTHING.  So there really is no such thing as a farming runs in this game because its more of a "hurry up and wait" run.-- Endgame:  All they did was take a slightly different approach to the end game concepts from TL1 and TL2 and then called it good.  It could have been amazing with just a little bit more thought though.  Your basecamp for instance could have been expanded.  There is a tower you cannot go into.  I was sure that would unlock when you beat the game, but no.  It would also be cool to maybe expand into another section, but no.  I thought there would be more crafting available at end game, but all you get is enchanting.  The only crafting you get is doodads for your fort.  Common, most every RPG has some way to even craft crappy weapons yourself.  They could have easily put plans into the game that you could farm for to make weapons and armor in, maybe even with custom stats.It makes me wonder if it were just rushed for release, but after it being out for a couple years and still these problems exist, to me if feels like they have abandoned this game, which is sad, but Torchlight 2 was nearly perfect in my eyes and WAYYYY more fun to play than this game.  My two kids both agree as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Release + 1st patch edit: changed review to negative.That's it. Several updates big and small and a full release later, I can't recommend this game in good conscience. The same massive bugs are listed as fixed in patch after patch (portal problems, pets disappearing, missing quest items, missing bosses, sticky monsters, etc.), but they are still there and new ones are included every time. I'm beginning to suspect they actually don't know how to fix it. With the full release there was nothing added to the game (except new and exciting bugs), there is still a glaring lack of actual content both in the campaign and the endgame, and lots of things which are very basic and simple staples of arpg's still doesn't work like they should. How does one even begin to mess up the idea of how force move should work? It boggles the mind.Relic Update edit: Still no animation cancelling. Input lag is still bad. Still rubberbanding. Monster stickiness returned. Quest tracking is all over the place again. Calling a miniboss 'Bruce Killis' still isn't funny. Plenty of interesting new small UI bugs. Getting increasingly harder to recommend this.TLIII got off to a rocky start, nonfunctional servers and everything, but that was to be expected like pretty much every single game ever released in early access before.But the amount of changes, fixes and updates in a very short time is simply amazing. Other developers who doesn't listen to their players and do less in a year than has been done for TLIII in three weeks should take notice.The bad things remaining, apart from minor bugs here and there:Input lag on skills is pretty bad right now and animation cancelling can't be implemented fast enough. Dying repeatedly to otherwise well-telegraphed attacks because you're stuck in a long animation is simply killing the fun.Item levels and resistance types being linked to areas is a terrible idea and should just be scrapped. Switching gear just to go back to earlier areas is a chore or being totally nuked by the weakest monsters in the game after having killed Ordrak just feels wrong. If the endgame is the mapworks, why even the need for changing the area/player stats at all?Depth in character building. There's two skill trees, a relic "skill tree" (really just one skill and some passive modifiers and you get them all) and some pet and legendary passives. So actually just two real skill trees. And most of the skills have cooldowns and you only have six slots, so character diversity is almost non-existant. Another skill tree, removal of cooldowns (and some skill adjustments for balance of course) on many skills could do wonders here.But all in all I have high hopes for TLIII and I'm sure it will be a great game and worthy of the Torchlight name when it's finally finished and everything is implemented. As it is now, it's still worth playing, I had good fun on my first complete playthrough.PS. ... and on a a more personal note:I guess the railmasters train is someone's beloved baby, but... it's pretty much the worst idea for a skillset in any arpg ever made. As it is now, there's three real classes in the game and one retarded half-class sitting at the back eating glue.Rename the class, throw away that whole skill tree and make another. There's plenty of skills from the engineer and/or alchemist in the previous games that could be made to fit in.Dixi.
