_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr If you're desperate for an ARPG like Diablo or Path of Exile then Torchlight III will probably entertain you for a short while, but it doesn't offer much beyond that.Disappointing. As someone who put a lot of time into both Torchlight I and II, I can say that it feels like the gameplay hasn't improved at all and the systems have gotten worse over time. Trying to play a ranged class is tedium because every other click sends your character rushing into melee range. Trying to use skills from range, for example, triggers the global cooldown, which in turn disables your attack, which means when you try to attack (usually because you never even stopped pressing the attack button) your character will just kamikaze run into the enemy for a second. This is an issue other games is the genre solved before Torchlight I even came out. And that's just one example of clumsy gameplay.The systems themselves are disappointing. The game seems to favor Borderlands 2's atrocious "every level is such a steep upgrade" design that if you don't start swapping out low rarity items with skills and stats you don't want, your defense and hp will lag behind to the point that you'll be getting consistently 1-shot by some elite enemies. Especially in Phase Portals, which kick you out and disappear when you die but also throw leveled-up enemies at you.The game also bizarrely throws only a small handful of the possible rare and legendary items at you. You may never, ever use Plunderbus on your Ghostly Captain but you'll get some version of the item with the affix that boosts Plunderbus every 5 levels. Guaranteed. You may not use Black Spot or Double Cross or Powder Keg either but you'll also get one of each of those about every 5 levels. And it'll be the same legendary every time. Just leveled to your current level. By the time you're halfway through the story you'll have seen most of the legendaries you will ever see before the endgame grind.And the endgame grind is terrible. It's a simple random dungeon generator that lets you choose between a set of one positive and one negative modifier for your run. The runs are in arbitrary sets, like levels 3-7 all being a set. If you fail any run between levels 3 and 7 you'll get kicked back down to level 3. Which is absurd. One bad wombo combo from the AI or similar bad luck can get you 1-shot and cost you 3 levels of progress. And from what I saw, there was no benefit to this grind. The gear was leveling up with me but most of it was so bad that it wasn't worth replacing my gear from the end of the story mode.Another flawed system is the skill system. It's horribly tedious to use respectacles to revert one single skill point at a time, and even the action bar is pure garbage. By default you use keys 1-7 for skills, but 90% of players can't reach past key 5 or maybe 6 comfortably. And again, if you want to experiment or move skills around, you have to use a rare item drop (or buy it for 2500g each) to remove points from skills so you can spend them elsewhere.And that's not counting the absurd relic system. You're forced to pick a relic at the start of the game and that's your third skill tree. You cannot change it. It might turn out that you end up really liking using bleeds or poison damage in your builds but you chose the frost or fire relic and you're just stuck with that.Overall, the game feels like it belongs circa 2001 in terms of gameplay and systems. The graphics are ok but nothing beyond what Torchlight I and II offered. Bugs also abound. I repeatedly would exit a phase portal and find myself stuck in terrain. Or I'd portal back to town to sell items and when I tried to return my entire map would be reset and my portal erased, so I'd have to start the area over.

_childDocuments_.review: I played TL3 in beta and decided no way in hell am I ever buying this game.  In every aspect, it was terrible.  And boring.  Time passes.  Rumbles that at half off, it might be worth it.  Sure, I can go for half off and if after 1 hour and 58 minutes it's still a boring piece of doodoo, I can refund.  15 hours later, I'm completely surprised by how enjoyable I'm finding the game.  Are you expecting Path of Exile?  This ain't it.  Are you hoping for The Last Epoch or Wolcen?  This ain't it either.   In other words, this is not a hardcore RPG (although there is a hardcore mode).   Rather, this is a fun, light, enjoyable and relaxing game to amble through smashing items and whacking mobs.  If you're really tired of games that expect you to go 110% most of the time, need a outside app to figure damage and gearing, then Torchlight 3 may be for you.  There are boss fights and they do require attention.  You may have to sit up for these and use a few healing potions.  There isn't a lot to worry about when choosing skills.  You'll soon enough settle on a handful that work for you.  And respecs drop or can be purchased.   You do have to be careful when choosing your relic at character creation, as that is a big determination of how you'll get along.  I'm all for defense, so I chose Blood Drinker for my Railmaster and am pleased with the survivability it gives.  Railmaster is pretty tanky and Blood Drinker just makes her very hard to kill.  Fort building is another nice surprise.  During beta, doing anything in the fort was an off-putting grind.  They've lightened up considerably on building requirements and the fort building aspect is now readily available for even the most disinterested players.   Is T3 for you?  I think that depends on what you're looking for.  If you want a challenging, nerve-racking ARPG experience with insta-twitch combat mechanics, well, T3 will not satisfy.  But if you're looking for a fun game, where you don't have to worry too much about min/maxing your gear, where you can make mistakes and still get on, and where you can progress at a decent clip, then I'd suggest giving Torchlight 3 a try and not be put off by negative reviews or comments.

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie- 3 and a half hours in and I already regret buying this game. Despite the negative reviews, I decided to give Torchlight III a shot because I've got a real soft spot for the previous game in the franchise. After running into some really nasty visual bugs, had to force quit the game because the menus weren't working.That aside, here are my thoughts as a fan of Torchlight II:[The Good]- The pets system feels pretty good overall, albeit a little shallow. - Player housing is a fun addition that looks like it could offer a fun way to keep investing time in the game across characters.- The Legendarium is a good addition that adds an extra layer to builds outside of gear.- The artifacts system introduces some interesting skill trees that can add new ideas and build variety to each class.[The Bad] - Mechanically the game feels really flat, and the abilities across the two classes I tried (Railmaster & Dusk Mage) lack any kind of punch or appeal- The UI is really needlessly complicated and unintuitive and feels really weirdly scaled.- Movement is weird and buggy, character pathing and spell targeting isn't always accurate.- The respect(acles) system really holds back experimentation when it comes to playing a new class. If you decide you're not feeling a build or set of abilities a few hours into playing, you don't have much choice to revert this (nothing new from TL II, but this still feels really bad)- The variety of legendaries is really slim. I looted the same piece of legendary gear 3 times with a single character over 2 and a half hoursLike with past games in the franchise, the story feels irrelevant, but this time around, I don't feel hooked enough by the gameplay to carry on playing. Guess it's time to reinstall Torchlight II and get back to the fun. This was a big miss! Listen to the reviews :)

_childDocuments_.review: While Torchlight III looks like the first two Torchlight titles, that pretty much where the similarities end. Much like Diablo 3 felt lesser than D1 and D2, T3 is going the same route with a slimmed down system that feels like it would more at home on mobile formats than as a PC game. The lack of customization in character builds compared to the previous titles is only the tip of the iceberg. Soulbound items (Items that disappear when you die) is a terrible mechanic, and one that requires very rare items to get rid of. The maps all feel similar. The items dropped don't feel varied enough either, leaving you stuck with the same gear for levels on end. All of this leads to a feeling on boredom that can only be remedied by shutting off T3 can playing a good ARPG like Grim Dawn or Torchlight II. I'm hoping that much of this will change as time goes on and much like D3, I hope that T3 will become a fun game. As it stands right now, this isn't worth anything close to $30 and should be avoided.UPDATE: I'm updating this review as I beat the game and then uninstalled. While the graphics and gameplay are solid, and it can be fun for a little while there's just not enough here to keep me coming back. I still hope that the game will continue to receive continual improvements so that it can eventually become a more fun game for those that feel like they may eventually get the $30-40 value they laid out for this game. _childDocuments_.review: This is just freaking bad.But you won't even get that before 2 hours for refund run out.- Sharpshooter is a joke of cooldowns. Bored of cooldowns? So you constantly jump in or out of dungeons when kiting monsters around the exit.- Piles of debries everyfreakingwhere: 1 box is not enough! Just a fixed cooldown, until you get a cooldown to cool that down cool.- Difficulty is pumped up by multiplying monster HP like crazy and almost not giving them any threat. You get surrounded - no damage on you, you may be killed (theoretically) by some stupid boss attacks, but bosses lag so far behind you, the only way you get caught is you're already so damn bored of this gameplay, you're looking in your window.- Trash mobs lag behind you and then they get a little more HP they stop dying from 1 hit, so you have to stop here and there just to keep up with experience. _childDocuments_.review: Well here we have it. We are not even a month into release and the game has 500 players on at peak times. If you were a fan of TL1 and TL2 this is NOT the game for you.  Zone and Maps: There are four elemental maps with different areas you can go into. Each one is identical to the previous with the exact same assets used for every zone. Same monster assets. Bosses all use same basic abilities with a couple of individuals but its basically just charge attacks across the boss rooms (which are all a circle room). It gets really bad when you realize the entire 2nd arch is just the first archs maps but with some green shlog here and there. Characters: The abilities do not mix well together like the previous games. Builds seem linear and cookie cutter to almost forecefull in their design. They removed attribute points.... Skills them selves have cast issues and your movement ability will not activate half of the time. Your party members will look like they are firing in the wrong direction. The weapon system allows you to use any weapon you want no matter of the class, neat right? If it was implemented  correctly. If you are a ranger you shoot arrows out of you no matter what weapon you are holding. if you have a bow with a 100 attk and 146 attk sword drops, you equip it and forget about your auto attks completely at you spam spells. They have no direction of the basics of their game. New studio Loot: Old school Runescape has more enticing loot. You constantly get the same loot drops over and over and over .... even playing on Ridiculous mode does not bring any enjoyment from the lack luster loot. On top of it, in my opinion it is the silliest looking armor of the whole series. They added a interesting fort system, that could have been a lot of fun if you didnt max out all the donation buffs in the first night of gameplay, leaving it to be no more than an annoyance to have to go to use storage, doing respecs. NO FISHING! I will end this with a childish remark to the female Dev who was doing a discord appearance before launch. I tried to open a conversation about your game and why it was heading in such a odd direction. You chose to insult me and turbo charge a bunch of nerds to your defense and the banned me from the discord for literally asking me why this game was so far off from the previous games. Enjoy your 500 players :D

No character depth still since TL1 to now - I have played all 4 of the classes felt like i played similar before.3.) character builds are limited! Great for beginners but bad for long time players of ARPG's.4.) lacks verity - with weapons skills and classes! _childDocuments_.review: Somewhat stating the obvious but whether or not you like the game will come down to whether you like the classes/skills.  Are they limited, yes but in D2 everybody more or less had 1 skill per character and we loved the game because we enjoyed spamming the skill.  Look up videos/guides to find out what classes offer what so you can get a good idea of whether or not they appeal to you.  For me I like having a non-animal custom pet w/ various active skills so I've been enjoying playing Rail.*edited for after game completion*After completing the game the positives remained unchanged as the class was fun to play but that remains it for the positives.  The game design however shows they wanted to be creative but the ideas are either incompletely or just not properly hashed out. Lets start off w/ the issue w/ of your gear/defense designs.  Gear has too few stat lines which they balanced by high amounts of each stat.  Elemental defense in particularly is excessively high causing you to end up w/ generally all around poor gear w/ each one having the highest elemental defense you have had drop for that slot.  Ignoring that stat or not making it priority will typically result in death because each Act will be spamming that element constantly.Continuing that though, what is with the concept of element per act?  Random unique/legendary enemies contain passives effects that do damage and aren't based on the act and they you only provide gear in the act for one element leaving you mostly defenseless at times.  Also each time you start an act your defense is a joke because your gear is the wrong element.  To worsen it further, the random phase missions ignore your act and will throw you in boss fights/dungeons that you may have no defense against and they can drop items w/ wrong defense stat that you are essentially useless to you.Biggest threats enemy threats are siege trait (drop large telegraphed aoe on ground) followed by blazing trait  which is high damage ground effect that can bypass your acts 2 & 3 elemental defense types, lastly by ranged mobs spamming aoe damage zones.  In short, you spend your game running around dodging deadly ground aoe.  This actually fits Rail's playstyle so it didn't matter to me, but that is still a poor design.  Lastly at higher levels there are so many effects all over the screen you start to lose the ability to even see the ground which will inevitably lead you to the occasional instant death to the siege trait.To counter these ground effects damage you get just potions because life leech doesn't exist on gear and HP regen on gear is too low.  You have 25% potions w/ weak bonus effect (dropped by mobs) and 60% potions from vendor w/ a aoe knockback to avoid further damage.  Potions options is a good idea, but why offer options when the vendor sells infinite amounts of a significantly better one at a low price.Last point since this rant is going on too long is basic attack.  Maybe at a low difficulty it might do something but on highest difficulty it isn't even worth attacking.   The skills get damage multipliers on top of passive boosts to make them hit literally multiple times faster and for more damage each hit than your basic attacks.  As a Cold Rail I had to focus on positioning my aoe freeze while getting shotgun car in good spots to maximize its aoe and wouldn't have been attacking anyways, but that still doesn't give a good reason for basic attacks being so useless.So again, if you think the class(es) look enjoyable to you then you may very well enjoy the game.  The game itself though is not doing itself any favors so if nothing seems really interesting to you then it would be best to stay away.  Lastly have others have noted, wait for a sale.  It takes less than 20 hours to clear the game per character so unless you like a whole lot of classes or enjoy post game grinding you aren't going to get your $40s worth.

_childDocuments_.review: TL3 is ok, but not worth the $30 price tag it currently has.Originally TL3 was going to be a freemium title, and there are some mechanics in the game that remain from its freemium days.Example: The game has 2 skill trees per character, Each level you obtain gives you 1 skill point. Once you allocate a skill point it's set unless you obtain a rare item off bosses (roughly 15%-25% droprate) called a Respectacle. Respectacles will allow you to take ONE skill point from a skill and allow you to place it somewhere else.So, unless you know how you are going to build your character from the start (via reading forums or joining TL3's Discord), a considerable portion of your playtime will be spent farming these Respectacles to move skill points from 1 skill to another.Now, I didn't play Torchlight 3 when it was called Torchlight Frontiers, but I can see how these Respectacles could have appeared in a cash shop to help speed along your trial and error testing out the skills for yourself playstyle (as I have been doing).TL3 has 4 classes, but it seems to be balanced around 1, the Sharpshooter. You will have a MUCH easier time playing as the Sharpshooter than any other class. The game is also MUCH easier if you play a ranged focused spec, which all of the classes allow for, to some degree: The Sharpshooter and Dusk Mage are heavily ranged focused, while the Forged and Railmaster can do either or, but you'll have more fun at ranged than in melee as the itemization for this game is extremely wonky.Weapons are ok. They all have damage numbers, maybe a proc, maybe some crit, etc. Armor on the other hand doesn't always provide you with a defense stat. Sometimes you'll get a piece that provides no defense, just HPs and/or other bonuses. Also, the acts in TL3, which there are currently 2 with a 3rd being released in a future patch, all require a different defensive stat.Items can provide 1 or 2 different types of defense to 4 different elements. The first type of defense is just generic defense. This helps with everything. The other 3 types of defense are elemental: fire, poison, and shock (lightning). Each act requires a different type of defense. Act 1 is all about fire, act 2 is poison, and act 3 is shock. So, when you go from act 1 to 2, you need to shed all of your fire resist gear for poison resist, and I guess just pray you never have to go back to act 1.I know what you might be thinking, "Once I get to act 2 and 3, I'll be a higher level than I was in act 1, I should just be able to steamroll everything." Not exactly. Your level, and thus damage and defense scale with whatever area you are in. So, while you might have beaten act 2 at level 30, once you go back to the start of act 1, you'll be level 1-3 again, although with all of your skills and scaled down gear.Why would you try to stack the elemental defense gear and not just try to stack the generic defense then? Because the elemental defense values are sometimes 2 to 3 times more than the generic value. A torso armor item could have 100 defense, but then 200-300 poison defense on it.It's late and I've gone on a little rant. Good night.Update: Aug 10th 2020:Taken directly from the store page:Will there be a wipe?Yes. At the end of Early Access there will be a wipe so that we can continue to aggressively test new features and bug fixes. Players who purchase the Early Access version will retain their copy of the game - this will be an account/character wipe only.”It says there will be a wipe at the end of EA, but I'm no longer playing this game because the developers decided an unscheduled wipe was necessary.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a review bomb...But this game can't be recommended currently.First of all, Lifebound gear is awful. The lifebound mechanic boosts gear past its normal level and stats (superior in every way) but will be destroyed on death. ??? Terrible idea. There are items you can farm from bosses to remove Lifebound which is also bad because every time you find an LB upgrade, and you will find them MUCH TOO OFTEN, you might want to farm an early boss just to get a scroll, just to save the gear. And then do that again and again. Or you can just keep a full set of inferior gear in storage so that when you die because a skill didn't fire off properly, your potion didn't work, or a boss or elite mob just rubberbanded around the room and killed you with something you couldn't see, you don't lose your entire arsenal. It's a bad idea to start with, and it is implemented poorly as well. About half of the drops I've found were Lifebound so very quickly your entire set of gear is at risk of disappearing if you die. It just isn't a fun mechanic in a game purely centered around Loot. It is buggier than any other early access game I've played. Some skills don't work as intended (don't trigger associated buffs, pull enemies inside of the character model and trap you, etc..) The servers are doing better now than launch but there's still TONS of rubberbanding and enemies teleporting around the screen.The loot just isn't exciting or satisfying. Very bland stats and unique affixes. There's a couple good ideas like the relic system and being able to break down legendary items to keep their unique abilities as passive buffs. Stolen straight from D3's Cube system. But you never really feel more powerful after picking up an ugrade.There are too few skills available on the bar. 6. That's it, just 6. Each character has 2 skill trees with about 10 skills each, and you get to use just 6. Boring. None of the skills I've used felt good either. There's often too much delay between using a skill and being able to move and attack or just use another skill. You feel slow, clunky and weak. You don't feel that spike in power when you upgrade a skill or get a new one from a higher tier. The level design is incredibly boring. It's nothing but hallways with medium sized square areas breaking it up. No more large open maps from TL2 that were worth exploring. The game was originally meant to be Free to Play and changed pretty late in development and you can clearly see they haven't been able to get far enough away from that style of game. Doubtful that this game will ever be more than just something to casually enjoy for a couple hours here and there and forgetting about in between.Right now it just isn't worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Fate.  I played Mythos.  I played Torchlight and still play Torchlight 2 occasionally.  This...isn't the same.  It may look the same-ish, it may sound the same-ish, but a lot of the things I like about the previous incarnations are gone.  Random enchanters?  Haven't seen any, can't enchant at all.  Sockets on items?  No.  Fishing?  Well, you can break nearly infinite buckets of fish...with small amounts of gold in them.  The skill tree for the sharpshooter and the fire relic are rather nondescript. There's no way to access a lot of your menus by clicking on the screen, you have to use keyboard.  I went to pick up a nice item from a phase level (thank you for keeping those, even if it's just "random boss level" now) and went through the portal home because there's no way to tell what I was hovering over.  There's no quest log, and the story is so thin that you have no idea why you're going someplace to do something.  Your quest on screen is literally "go to X place" with no explanation.  To top it off, you can't pause, and leaving to go to your fort seems to often forget where your portal connects to so you get dumped at the beginning of the area and have to hack and slash your way back through to the entrance to the area you want.  I started making a portal at the beginning of every area and dumping inventory then so I wouldn't lose progress.  Did I mention YOU CAN'T PAUSE even in single player???  So many annoyances and not enough payoff.  I hope the devs take a look back and bring elements back into the Torchlight series, or even take a page from excellent games like Grim Dawn that do skill trees and perks far better.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state I do not recommend it. Servers are causing issues frequently and you won't be able to play the game. If you do happen to login and actually play, the game play itself is pretty simplistic and down to the bare bones. While I do believe the game being in early access is completely fine with all the issues running around, I unfortunately do not feel like the game is anywhere near quality like previous titles TL1 and TL2... SO FAR. It is not fair to compare TL3 to TL1 and TL2 since both of those games were full games upon release and not put into early access. Hopefully with this being in early access, it only means that the game is a base to build upon and not what we'll see in the final release. Lots of work is needed from the developers to make this worthy of a sequel. Their discord has consistent communication with the developer team and they are working hard to fix all these bugs and glitches with the servers. I still enjoy the game for how simple it is, but like I said before, it doesn't nearly have any steam compared to TL1 and TL2. I personally enjoy the game, but I know a lot of people will think otherwise. And even though I enjoy it, I do not recommend it in its current state. Hopefully I will be able update this later down the road as the game progresses.***3 days later***After a few days of server issues, most of these issues for me have gone away. Developers are still consistently updating us on Discord and are consistently providing information as to whats going on. Highly glad to see developers working towards getting stability on servers. Only issue I have is when I party with someone. The game seems to desync between my friend and me and the enemies start to float until they die off. Seems the only fix is to do a solo game and those issues disappear almost entirely.**6/30/20**New update, hurray! Rushed content to completely honest. A lot of the bugs posted from the previous build are lingering still over on this update. Server issues are still there, unable to load, desyncing issues with parties, etc.... I'm starting to worry that the only reason the servers worked on my prior review was only because the amount of players dwindled making the server handling more tolerable... It makes me wonder if the servers are ever going to get better. When the developer said that there should be no downtime when the patch rolled over, it made me worried as to if the servers were even touched or capable of handling the load. Usually when someone tells me there is no server down time, usually its because of a hotfix. Rolling out a completely new area and not have some sort of server work to do?.... Right now the games performance totally shows. Its a shame that there was so much put into the patch notes, but in the long end the amount of it that was relative to what the players are experiencing? Little to none. The Last act is all this game has for content. They are adding small things like bounty boards and such, but that will only go so far.... Unfortunately I've defended the developers for the outstanding work they've done, but so far it starting to look more and more like a quick cash grab than a sequel. Its such a shame... but I'll give it one more patch before I ditch ship and try to grab a refund.. And before someone says its my hardware, I'm currently running on a i9-10900k, RTX 2080ti, with 16gb of Ram.**07/24/20**Time to jump ship.. Month has gone by and nothing is getting me excited to return to TL3, the amount of players have dwindled down to about 600 at peak. Servers are still being worked on a month later, and I'm honestly tired of hearing "We have worked on servers, but it is not entirely gone away but please report issues". This should not be an issue a month later. And how do we know its been fixed when almost 80% of the player base is no longer loading the servers? Sad to say that this game should be scrapped and a proper sequel should be made. Its sad when Torchlight II has almost double the amount of players playing right now than TL3. Character wipes are in August which is fine, but seems a little soon since a lot of people were expecting at launch... Game breaking bugs are fine, but a month later and we're already wiping characters? Pets still haven't been attacking.... How is this still a bug? The game is starting to chalk up like a game made by 5 year olds. Early Access? Gotcha, but a month later and you can't fix the biggest issues that players are experiencing? Then it becomes a problem. This is starting to become more and more of a cash grab and its showing. They took a chance by calling this TL3, grabbed peoples money and are making this game look like a child made it. Sad, I was hoping for more but this is pretty much all to expect from TL3.

_childDocuments_.review: Torchlight III is a fun game with a lot of problems, but could grow into something better with the right time and support.The Good ---- Gameplay is fun and fast paced, with a difficulty curve you choose. I prefer Painful.- The world is bright, colorful, and full of plenty of baddies to squish.- The classes have great personality, and the Relic system lets you put your own spin on your favorite class.The Bad ---- There are a lot of bugs, even after a handful of patches. The client itself is stable, but there are a ton of "why the hell is this happening" moments that frustrate you.- The end game feels tacked on and keeps you away from the social world. I honestly don't enjoy it, but it is challenging.- Loot feels unrewarding at end game, despite ongoing tweaks to the formula.Compared to the Alpha of Frontiers, and especially the release on Early Access, Torchlight III has come a very long way in its development time. The decision to go live in its current state is a strange one, but at its core is an enjoyable dungeon crawler. I look forward to this game maturing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very similar to Torchlight 1, so if you have enjoyed that you'll be fine with this as well. The key differences (aside from the upgraded visuals) are that TL3 seems very linear and won't really let you progress or explore on your own. You generally need to accept quests to enter the next location and some side locations. It's not really interesting if the game patronizes you like that, but I hope that it opens up later on or having some sort of infinite generated dungeon.The variety of skills is okay, not great, but okay. You get a relic weapon later on that basically adds a new skill tree, as well as being able to add 3 significant skills from a dozen in a list. The feedback you get from fighting also feels good enough for me.The most infuriating issue the game has right now is the pathfinding and auto-targetting of spells and attacks. If there's an interactable nearby and you click somewhere near that, instead of walking to where you clicked it will prioritize opening the chest. If you want to walk past an enemy, eventhough there seems to be a path through them, your character will just stand still and do nothing. Not even walk against the enemy. It happens every few minutes and it's super annoying.They've also added forts as a mechanic. It's basically the hideout from path of exile where you can customize your little space with decorations and functional objects. It's great and the fact that you naturally come across these owned by other players is fun too.As for the online interaction: I have no idea how it works. It's almost Dark Souls levels of obscure. Outside of towns you randomly come across other players who kill mobs with you, but then disappear a little while after. Considering it's early access, it's already enjoyable for me, but I hope they're making it less linear and provide some mechanic like rifts and maybe a better skill customization system.

_childDocuments_.review: I've requested a refund. The lack of ability to distribute my stats was a huge red flag, but it went on from there. The classes are very hard-set aesthetically and otherwise. All "stats" are from the randomly dropped gear, so you don't even get to start messing with any kind of build until way, way late. It even lacks the juvenile synergy guidance of Diablo 3. You're just completely at the mercy of RNG.They got rid of dual-wielding. In 36 hours I haven't seen any spells to learn or teach my pet. No fishing. No cool pet forms aside from what you might possibly eventually randomly find from some box somewhere, maybe. The "fort" is a joke. There is some junk you put in it and farm stuff for to get minor, arbitrary percentage boosts to loot drops and a couple of resistances.The story is set way, way after the first two, so forget familiar faces. Some new enemy is invented for nothing and invalidates the efforts of previous heroes.I could just go on. Oh, the "ridiculous" mode is the only one to really play on. _childDocuments_.review: Torchlight III is the spiritual successor to Torchlight II, but in no way as good as its predecessor.It is an ARPG, which means you kill monsters to get better equipment to get better at killing monsters. And you gather XP to level up skills to get better at killing monsters. That is all there is to it. The game is good if it does these things well. Torchlight II does them very well. Torchlight III is just mediocre in this regard.My four main criticisms are:(1) There is no real penalty for dying in this game, which takes the tension out of combat. You pay something like 5% of your gold to get resurrected on the spot, but since gold is pretty much of no use in this game, when you die you shrug and continue. (2) The controls are unresponsive. All the boss fights follow the same pattern: the boss telegraphs where it is going to do the next big attack, and you move out of the way, preferably not into the environmental damage that the boss put down. That's it. So you'd think that there is no reason to die, but unfortunately the game tends to be unresponsive to the controls, so often when you think you should be moving, you appear to be stuck (even if there is no obvious reason why you should be stuck). Which means that I am actually glad that dying in this game is meaningless, because I mostly died not due to my own mistakes but due to the game not reacting to my inputs.(3) There are quite a few bugs in the game. Notably, your pet often does not follow you through portals, which means that you have to return to your fort to get your pet back again. Unfortunately, there are a lot of areas which you are not allowed to leave without the area disappearing, so you have to do those without pet support. This is particularly annoying in the post-game content, where your leveling resets if you dare to leave an area or die in one.(4) And perhaps the biggest sin in a game like this: the loot is uninteresting. The most interesting items are the legendary ones, and you get something like 50 of those during a regular playthrough, but the same ones repeat constantly at different levels. For instance, during one sharpshooter playthrough I got no less than 9 legendary bows: 6 of one type and 3 of another type. Anything good about this game? I liked the graphics, though those are an acquired taste. For the rest, if you are in any way interested in ARPGs, play Torchlight II. It is superior by far.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been testing this game since close alpha.  Some of the choices they made going from close beta to this early access have me guessing who made some of the decisions.  For those looking for Torchlight made by the people that made the previous ones just go play the other 2 because this isn't that.  This was going to be an ARPG-MMO but all the parts that made it MMO where horrible to be honest.  As a tester I asked for them to remove them over and over because they didn't add anything to the game at all.  They had server issues from the start, don't think they have a good framework for an MMO game.  All this game ever needed was to have offline and local multiplayer to be honest to draw in a good faithful crowd.Now with that said the game isn't a bad game.  The 4 archetypes are different enough.  They do have 2 different skill lines, a little low though on that end if you ask me.  They sped the combat up a good bit after changing over from Frontiers to 3.  Used to feel really, really slow sometimes.  They streamlined the story though and it doesn't really feel like it flows to great now.  The fort is a nice feature that they left in place, but you can level up everything way to fast in it.  Also I don't know why they turned off the fame system for the EA it was working great in the beta and gave you something to look forward to while leveling up. The fame system was the main way to get stuff to put into your fort.Overall I would say it is a decent ARPG, but if it doesn't add modding support for the full release it would be a real blow to the game.  Modding is what made both of the other games what they are to be honest.  Hopefully they will learn from this blunder of an EA launch and fix some of the things people are saying.  Would I recommend the game?  Yeah I would, but with some very stern warnings about what to expect.  Think you could get 40 or 50 hours out of it the way it is now, at least for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I only say "No" as a placeholder.I like what they're doing, I'm a long-time Torchlight fan. BUTThere are issues. I understand it is in Early Access, but it is probably still a bit early to have released it in this state. At it's core, the pieces are there, but they don't fit well enough yet. The classes need more fleshing out, the story is underwhelming, and there isn't much in the way of item variety. I could accept server issues - stress testing is a part of multiplayer game development - but the infrastructure to support a game of this magnitude isn't there. It feels like the "infrastructure" is a bunch of hamsters running on wheels, connected by cables made from recycled Halloween wigs they found in a closed down costume store. Ignoring this, not enough of the game is there. Like people are saying, it feels like a jump off platform for a free-to-play recurring revenue model (Battle Pass). If this is indicative of the direction they plan on taking the game, it will be a hard pass, and the "No" will stay. If it is not, then the developers should have stayed their hand a little and released to Early Access something with more meat ($30 worth) on its bones. There are no microtransactions or other pocket money graveyards. Through the 5 difficulty levels I feel permanently challenged even as a "veteran". Boss fights are equipped with stronger phases and in general the game has not skimped on facets. Of course, a comparison with such insane titles like Path of Exile is not possible. But this appeals to a broader spectrum of players. Looting and leveling, figuring out new builds in conjunction with different armor sets and passive bonuses..... Lots to do in this "B" game. And there are so many people playing Diablo Immortal, I can only laugh. I caught Torchlight 3 on sale, but even full price is absolutely fine for at least 50 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: As i am writing this review. My Torchlight 3 game is running. It was loading as i teleport to My Fort. It has been loading for 15 minutes and i think i will need to force shut it down soon. What a shame. Reason i was using teleport was because my inventory was full and i need to grab one legendary shield. Devs ! you owe me one legendary shield ! That being said, I've seen a lot of polished between Early Access and the official launching. What i don't understand is, what's the rush ? The game are still buggy as hell, there is no denying that. But all things consider, i think the gameplay was fun and let me break it down in Arpg kind of way:1. Theory Crafting.Basically you can build wide range variety of character to suit you gameplay. All the rules of the skills etc are written in good explanation. What i don't understand is that why we can't duel wield in TL3 ? It was fun to dual wield in TL1 and TL2 although i am not dual wield type but i would surely would prefer having that choice instead of not. What if i want to use pistol akimbo style ? Should i just be happy with pistol and shield or focus now ? However Torchlight as always still deliver the mix and match skill that is fun to be experimenting with. I just thought it could be done better. I get it not all Arpg will suit our preferred play style but this just seems a little bit more to have happier player.2. Story Story was abysmal to say the least. New player that wasn't attached to TL series will probably think this game was written by amateur sci-fi writer. Sorry Devs. 3. GameplayThis is by far the strongest point of any TL series. This 3rd actually feels better in the gameplay itself despite the least environment setting compared to the previous two. The swing of the two handed sword feels ever so satisfying and the trigger of pistol also feels like shooting actual gun. Bravo Devs. However, The enemy is quite repetitive and I've been slaying phase beast over and over again, sometimes got 2 of em in the same area just to fight the same boss over and over again with very very disappointing winning loot. Which bring me to the next thing.4. Loot I am on level 20 now, the loot starting to get good, i think. Before that, it was just meh. sometimes it looks like a pile of coins which when we actually received it, it was only 2 coins. Seriously, it feels like charity instead of loot. But never mind, gradually i think it's getting better. I saw 2 legendary item between my run from level 1 until 17 but suddenly between 17 to 20 i already saw 3. i expect it to get better (which remind me again, the game just crashed while i am typing this review and i lost opportunity to take legendary shield, you owe me Devs).5. Character SelectionSure, at least Torchlight always trying not to fall into the same cliche of rogue, fighter, archer and mage. This is something i appreciate. Also i play as range character that wield sword and it still works fine (i played in hard mode) so yeah, i like the character selection  being offered with opportunities to mix and match. I do want to complaint a bit about appearances though. Does anyone else think that the armor, etc looks a bit girly if you using male character ? I feel like my sword wielding sharpshooter looks more like a bard or a dancer. (which nothing wrong with that, it just doesn't feel like it look the part for me).6. The New StuffWithout being so much spoiler, now you own your own space which you can decorate etc, This is a breath of fresh air, but i think it is more gimmicky although really appreciate the effort of trying something new. It was okay, probably for some player who is ready to dump hours and hours into this game will sometimes take a inside game break and just decorating stuff. Again, i don't want to spoiler but it does kinda annoying to see your place in every junction of the different map like it suddenly appear there. Well, welcome to magical and creative thinking of the Devs mind, i guess.  7. GrindingYes it is very possible to grind in TL3. It is not necessary though. With the right build and your controlling skill, you gonna do just fine following the stories. At least that is what i feel now. In conclusion, i will still recommend this game. I am attached emotionally to TL series and i still do until now. Do i think TL 3 is the best TL so far ? Far from it. But again, i already saw improvement from time to time probably someday it will be something really solid. The gameplay still satifying albeit with lack of variation for me so far. I still remember how i was a bit disappointed with TL 2 because in TL 1 i was playing kick ass summoner build and it just seems to be impossible to build the same character in TL 2. Only to be blown away later when i played as the berserker (ah good old days). My game just frozen and i need to force quit it. But definitely i will come back to play it again. Damn you TL !

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Wait till full release and on sale. Also: limits, limits everywhere.UPD: It's a slog and a very slow grind.I don't understand why this game. _childDocuments_.review: Game release comments:The first 24 hours of the release of this game, it was full of disconnects and bugs - which is to expect with any game release. No developer can expect their volume to double/triple/quadruple. The developers have been very active in their Discord providing minute by minute updates on the changes and bug fixes they have been implementing.I completed Act 1 & 2 under 6 hours of gameplay. A few bugs that need to be hashed out.Gameplay:If you are looking for a filler ARPG in between leagues in Diablo or Path of Exile or just a fresh take on the genre, give it try. The skills are fun to play with, they do not need a calculator or a talent builder to complete the content (unlike Path of Exile & Wolcen). You try the builds you like, you can respec (at a grindy cost) or just make a new character like in Diablo 2.Relics & Legendary items have a completely different take on how you can customise your character and who doesn't want to play a sentient robot and smash zombies?Closing comments:I am looking forward to what direction they take and all the updates they will implement over the next year. The developers have done a great job with this game, they have been openly communicating with everyone and they take feedback to heart. People need to understand that this game was released under Early Access, manage your expectations, don't go in thinking this is a Triple A game that have had years of development and support.

_childDocuments_.review: I assume that the game has left the beta phase and is now live.I have played for about 20 hours now. Two different classes.I am not going to compare TL3 with Path of Exile, but maybe with TL1 and TL2.The game feels very unfinished in terms of character customisation. The stat system is poorly designed. Relics have very low synergy with the characters identities and active skills. I personally miss some passive skills. There are fewer item slots than in TL2. Overall it feels like a poor refactoring attempt with about 1/10th of the quality of TL1/2. I have enjoyed TL2 a lot, and TL3 is nothing like it. The misc. content such as forts and materials feels like extra steps with no real purpose. Yes, hideouts are cool, but they don't really fit into the current TL universe. You can as well have a garden / crafting bench in town.The navigation/quest UI feels unfinished and is not self-explaining. Mobs/Bosses all use similar skills. Overall the game feels very generic and monotone. The items are boring and don't have much variety in terms of stat types.In the current state the game has way to many severe bugs. A few examples:- Certain skills stop dealing damage once you upgrade them to a new Tier (<- bad user experience, especially if you build your char around this active skill and invest many points just to brick it upon reaching a cool milestone)- Tooltips of skills don't correspond the essential mechanics (such as reverse knockback direction)What I dislike about TL in general (also in the previous parts) is that you are forced to use the default attack. In TL3 this intensifies further, since you gain charges, relic energy etc. from it.Verdict:- Was hoping for a cooler version of TL2.- Did not get, what I have expected (even if I don't consider the bugs)

_childDocuments_.review: First, a little bit of background about my experience with ARPGs and hack/slash titles so that you have confidence that I know what i'm talking about:Diablo 2: 10,000 hours+ (currently playing the ladder reset!)Diablo 3: 500+ hours (and I was there near a FutureStore getting my hands on the earliest copy just to be greeted with the infamous ♥♥♥♥♥♥ launch). Own Diablo 3 on the Nintendo Switch as well as PC.Grim Dawn: 200+ hours (and still play on LAN with my wife)PoE: 50 hoursLast Epoch: currently playing every updateWolcen: played in beta, still playing even after a terrible launchA bunch of assorted ARPGs such as Viktor Vran, etc: a couple hours each. I try out every ARPG in the hopes that it can match Diablo 2's magic.As you can see, I play a lot of these types of games.  That said, there are some fixable gripes I currently have with the game:The loot system seems on par with the previous titles. Any of the "bad loot" commentary seems to be unfounded imo.The overall verdict is that for an Early Access Title, this is a great game for some co-op play. I feel like the future of this game will have it be on the Nintendo Switch as well. The overall negative reviews seem to only be based on the server instability experienced during the weekend launch of this title. But seriously, Diablo 3 launch, Wolcen Launch... like it's kind of expected at this point and shouldn't be the deciding factor in your decision to buy this game. As a rule, please wait at least a week after a launch of the game to buy it so that the servers remain relatively stable if you want to enjoy the experience to its full potential. This amount of negative reviews is extremely unwarranted and strikes me of a bandwagon, which is what prompted me to write this review in the first place.I greatly enjoyed playing this game. You can do cool customization options when building your Fort; the color palette is flavourful. The loot is great and the bosses are unique. Overall, it's a 7.5/10 as it has some room for improvement but is overall an enjoyable experience as an ARPG veteran.

_childDocuments_.review: /** Oct. 15, 2020 Update **/Since my original early access review, I've invested another 30 hours into the game (thank you Steam for tracking that info).  This game is still a 'no' recommendation for me.  Here's the breakout:-> Price increased from early access 29.99 to launch of 39.99 (33% increase for what now?)-> Price to awesomeness ratio, Diablo 3 and other clones have much more in terms of content.-> The game still lacks polish and balance; relic choices matter, and let's hope you don't pick a bad one.-> Game play is very linear and on rails.  End game content is terri-bad.  Replaying the same bosses over and over again with limited modifiers.  In contrast to my early access review, playing on harder difficulties now adds additional benefits; such as drop % chance.  So that's a good change. This is still a no for me; however, if you want to support the franchise - don't let me stop you.  It just isn't a content rich game.  A full play through beginning to end can be done in 1 day (2-3 if you're more casual)./** Original Early Access Review **/The latest update was pretty much the nail in the coffin on this title for me.  Maybe it'll get better, but meh; not sure.  The game has various difficulty modes with very little drive to play on the easiest vs hardest setting... oh, other than you get a better % drop chance of potions...  riiiight, not much of a motivator there.  Doesn't really fall in line with other Torchlight games (1 & 2) and just seems to miss the mark.  If you do buy into early access, be forewarned they'll be doing another character wipe before launch; so pay to test, if desired.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that has tested the original TL series, I wanted to give this a well fleshed out review for those that are hesitant to buy into Early Access, and perhaps after release as well. The game needs players willing to test out it's content and the development team has been spacing out the wipes patches and content updates in larger gaps to see how stable the game itself is with higher population. A lot of these negative reviews aren't even close to honest in regards to the game play, the features of the game itself, or it's content and community. No, Runic isn't developing this one, and that's fine. Echtra has a good handle on this, and they are not ruining the series. In fact, they are adding a lot of content that was most commonly used by the TL2 community for enhancing game play, improving balancing, and added new classes and pets to the game to play with.  If the thought of losing a character you spent hours on leveling, and playing through quest chains bothers you, then don't buy it right now. Wait until it hits release and buy it then. But for now, only game play mode available is multiplayer, so you'll run into other players doing their quests in the hubs and cities across the game world. You could chat with them, but most don't even use chat, for whatever reason. (I do, I love chatting with people in games and making new friends.) For what it lacks in keeping characters at the moment, it's stable enough to play and you can join parties with others to run through more challenging content, mapworks, or just do quests as a team. You can always solo as well, but me...I prefer teaming up.

_childDocuments_.review: So I read plenty of bad reviews about the game before buying, but also saw good reviews and, well, being a huge fan of Torchlight, clearly saw only what I wanted to see.  I really really wanted to love this game.--PRE GAMEPLAY--Before even getting into gameplay, the cracks started showing.  $40 is VERY steep for a Torchlight game, with the first 2 games running $15 and $20.  Getting into the game, the main menu music was pretty off-putting.  I know I'm nit picking, but it's just a jolt that continues to feel like warning signs that I just refused to see.  Luckily the music does get better right after that screen.So I went to character creation and wow, those character faces look just...BAD.  Thinking about it, as a phone game, with your screen being about 1/15th the size of your monitor, you might not notice.Each class has 2 skill trees and then a 3rd tree based on a relic.  I later found out that the relic trees are the exact same for every class.  There are 5 relics to choose from, but at 4 classes and 5 relics, ehh I can't knock them for lack of effort.  Pets also have a handful of abilities that can be learned throughout the game as you find more pets (only one pet ability can be active at a time).--GAMEPLAY --Jump in and I was actually okay with the graphics (granted, I was playing the robot) and after giving it some time, the skills.  I didn't feel like skills were as big of a complaint as other reviewers, but a point I will make is that I was disappointed to see the removal of the spell scroll abilities from the previous games.Monsters aren't standing out in the open like normal.  Every single combat encounter is groups of monsters jumping out of whatever hidey hole they were in.EVERY.  SINGLE.  ENCOUNTER.It gets old pretty quick.  I started to find myself playing strictly for this knowledge --  shotgonne blast until full heat, vortex explode the entire group killing 90% of them, finish off the rest with rapid fire.  If the group is very large, I might use charge a couple times to get them grouped better.Over.  And over.  And over.I played for 3 hours and here are the monsters I ran into:Skeletons/Zombies.  Melee only.Spiders.  Melee only.Goblins.  90% melee, very rarely a goblin with a gun that takes forever to shoot at you.Purple guys.  Melee only.See a trend?  It is beyond easy to avoid getting hit by attacks because every attack takes the monster time to charge up.  I didn't use my first potion until around level 7, when I was just pulling massive groups to try to change SOMETHING up.Speaking of which, difficulty.  I played on the second to highest difficulty.  I think there were 5 difficulties:Easy, Medium, Hard, Very Hard, and Insane.  The game suggests that Hard is for people that are experienced with ARPG's and that Insane is just... no point to playing.  I went for Very Hard and about fell asleep.  The only difficulty in the game was what difficulty I added by pulling huge groups of monsters to change things up for myself.  Monster attacks are so slow and easily avoidable that it's a joke.One of the big things you'll have is your own camp.  In theory, it sounds great.  In practice, look at any phone game with a town and that's what you're looking at.Make a building for converting rocks into masoned stone.Make a building to turn logs into planks.Make a building to turn metal into bars.When you choose to convert one of these items into the usable form, there's a timer to do so.  48 wood into planks will slap a timer on the building for 1 minute, because why not?--FINAL THOUGHTS--I was willing to look past a LOT for this game: double the price of the old games, terrible character faces, smaller skill trees, loss of spell scrolls..  But I couldn't get past the same, "walk up, wait for monsters to jump out, kill the same all melee group of monsters that are too easy to avoid taking damage from, loot, repeat"I gave the game 3 hours really only because I was hoping it would change.  It didn't.  I'm hoping my steam refund will accept even though I've put in the extra hour.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not hopping onto review bomb train but rather writing a review in hopes that some things will change and that i'll change some day this review to recommend. Ever since shutdown of marvel heroes I've been looking for a arpg that isn't set in dark fantasy. There are a plenty of those on the market. Some good, some bad but the tone is unchanged and therefore the arpg market has gotten monotonous. I've been following this game since it's first announcement with one thought in mind: "Here's something different, and they have two fantastic games behind them, this is bound to be awesome". And different it truly is, the tone is lighter, the graphics are gorgeous and ideas behind characters are on point, and really made me smile. However, unfortunately, those are the only ups at it's current state. Even though characters are beyond interesting, skills and builds are lacking to say the least. I understand that you wanted to simplify this compared to path of exile, but i think you went a bit overboard with simplification. Along with that, my biggest concern is that there are only 6 active skills if you include auto-shot which is way to little to engage players over longer periods of time, and will ultimately lead to "flavor of the month" endgame. Don't get me wrong, each arpg has that "problem" but with multiple skills present, there will be some diversity or even other combinations of skills which will lead to new builds. Considering this is an early access a lot of things are subjected to change and therefore i will not ask for a refund but rather believe that you'll take the feedback that you're getting and make this game stand shoulder to shoulder next to Torchilght 2 as one of the gems of the genre.Best of luck in further development and i truly hope that i'll change this review to recommended status by the time you reach release stage.Edit 1: Yeah, lost cause... _childDocuments_.review: Pros- Feels/plays the same as Torchlight 2. Some people are claiming it plays like a mobile game and I am unsure if they ever played anything like Diablo or Path of Exile. If it's "too zoomed in" zoom out. V is the default or scroll wheel. Buttons too big? Play with the UI scale.- Skill Trees - They feel simplistic at first as there are only 2 per class, but add in the Relic and Legendarium and it adds a new level of customization without overly complicating builds.- Loot - Loot seems to drop less often, but it seems to be more useful items when they drop. I don't seem to get many low quality items and plenty of green/blue quality while I have been leveling.- Fort Building - similar to building a hideout in Path of Exile (if anyone has played the season that gave that) and provides some perks as far as improving resistances, gold find and item find. As well as some crafting it seems. Haven't made it far through the available decorations/functional items but definitely good potential.Mixed- Always Online - it's nice to see other players rather than just disembodied voices in chat. However, with current issues this means server instability makes it rough to play for long periods at the moment. Always Online is being removed by full release per the Dev Team.Cons- Respectacles - I haven't figured out how common these are, if they are farmable at end game, what have you. But by level 10 I had earned 1. It allows you to unlearn 1 rank of a skill. If these are rare, this can be frustrating to try and play new builds or if the meta changes, nerfs/buffs to skills etc. Similar mechanic in Path of Exile and it makes unlocking skills very unforgiving.

_childDocuments_.review: It still feels like the crappy phone game they were making. I'm hoping they update it thoroughly, but its clear that the old charm of the first two isn't there anymore. The art direction for example isn't bad, the world around you is pretty dope, but that is in vast contrast to the character models. The Sharpshooter's model (male or female) looks like someone held a candle too close to a Barbie\Ken doll, the Duskmage looks like they went into Maya and scaled the Sharpshooter alongY-axis and the Railmaster looks like Joe Rogan stopped half way through turning into a chimp. The Forged class however is pretty cool, I like sentient machine vibe, makes it feel a bit more unique.Combat isn't as fun as before, with the normal melee attack animations, most classes have two swings in one combo. It quickly starts to feel like your character isn't swing a club as much as their just spazzing out a bit. The combat overall also doesn't feel very impactful, next to no visual feedback or weight to how your character moves during combat. There are some pretty cool spells though, Joe Rogan's little train comes to mind.I mentioned it feeling like a phone game and it shows in the menus especially, like on the map, all the inputs\buttons are positioned on the side of the screen in a way that feels like it was designed for optimal reach for your thumbs, don't know if I'm right on that but that's the feeling I got. Also the inventory size is kinda poor, especially for this type of game, even with the extra pet space I kept having to either stop to empty my inventory or portal back to town to sell off what i had which means at some point the game starts to make you worry more about logistics than playing the game...Also you can't drop items from your inventory, you can only destroy it or transfer it to your pet, which again, fits the M.O. of most of those crappy phone games.Some things it did right though...When I started in the first town I didn't have turn off some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ multiplayer chat log in the bottom left corner full of Brazilians trying to sell you a fake sword for real money.The FOV is good, has a nice balance between range and angle, so I can see the enemies and still have time to plan the best offensive or defensive response. I'm surprised to how many modern ARPGs ♥♥♥♥ that up.The fort building is an interesting concept and I'm excited to see where they take it, just hoping it becomes more than just another hub with a customisation option.All in all it's OK but I kinda wish they just made an Expansion campaign for Torchlight 2 instead, maybe even an additional class? Or hopefully this turns into the new No Man's Sky and they make it worthwhile. I refunded it, but I kind of regret it. The developer at least deserves praise for not keeping in Free-to-Play or Pay-to-win mechanics and I'll buy it it again when they've taken development farther.TL,DR : a Mediocre experience where even the option to play as an autistic Joe Rogan clone and his favourite toy train does little to hold back nostalgia for the previous entries into the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it, but it just isn't a well designed game. I think most of the failings have been well documented, so I'll just give you my "highlights".There is a bug that makes your pet disappear after you leave your fort. This would be just a medium-level annoyance if it weren't for the fact that the entire endgame content is started from your fort, so you have a pretty good chance of not being able to take your pet with you each time you start a dungeon from there. You can't leave these once you start them, so you will just have to do the whole thing without your pet.There really isn't much variation in skill choices. There's only two skill categories per character, with a third that is common among all character types and is chosen from (I think) five different options. There aren't many individual skills in each category, so you don't have a lot in the way of customization.You can't turn off the audio error messages. This is the most annoying thing of all for me, and I'm amazed that this game was designed by veterans in this genre. You'll constantly get bombarded by stupid messages telling you your health is low and whatnot. The worst thing about this, though, is that you get messages for your pet's health as well, but the pet health bar doesn't ever change. Also, I don't know if there is actually anyway to heal your pet in this game, so you're basically getting spammed with error messages for something you have no control over. I got the game on sale for $10. I guess if you have to feel a sense of completeness in having all three games, it's worth picking up at that price. Still, it might be better to wait and see if it goes down to $5 at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would recommend this game BUT it does still have some bugs that need to be worked out. First off, it's a Torchlight game; if you don't know what that means then first off, welcome to the series! This is not a special game. I don't say that to be mean, I say that because there is nothing groundbreaking in this ARPG game. It's the same thing over and over: go kill monsters, pick up loot, maybe upgrade an item, sell or dismantle the rest of said loot, repeat. However, with this being such a simple game, it's nice to not have to worry about theorycrafting a build. The Devs this time kind of made your builds for you in a sense that you have limited skill points and the more points you put into a skill the better it becomes, not really leaving a lot of room for nine skills to be on your hotkeys. its NICE!!! Sometimes I feel like devs go nuts with skills and it takes me longer to think of a build and analyze every skill than it takes me to play the game. I love Torchlight for the simplicity of the game play and builds. This one is no different. With that being said, at the time of writing this, there are some bugs that make me frustrated. When I fill my pets inventory and click the "send to town" button, if I exit out of my menu too quickly, the game will tell me my pet has returned but it actually doesn't. I can still send things to it's inventory but I can't send it to town because it's actually not there. The only way to reset the bug is to exit the game to desk top and then reload. This is frustrating, especially when in the middle of a long quest. There is an audio bug that I have experienced twice now where one of the sound effects from any monster will play on repeat and will not stop. Again, the only way to get rid of it is to exit the game to desktop and reload the game. the third and final bug I have seen is the map not loading entirely and therefore you cannot complete the map, you again, have to exit the game and reload it. These are simple bugs that should have been worked out in early release as I experienced them then as well. I did put them on the official bug report forum and yet here we are. As I said, overall, if you are looking for a simplistic ARPG looter game, this is the game for you. I'm a big fan of of the TL series and have played expensively over the years and will continue to play this one. Happy hunting and may your gear luck be ever in your favor!

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately it falls far short in terms of expected character progression and general UX design compared to the first two torchlight games.The new classes are less diverse than the normal torchlight classes with more overlap. The classes each also have a much smaller variety of skills and playstyles available than previously, the descriptions on several skills are missing and often lack useful information such as duration of summons. The relics using accumulated damage instead of mana may have been nice gimmick for a single class skill tree but as a replacement for every classes' 3rd tree they're just disappoint lacking the impact to justify the point investment in their tree compared to your regular tree skill which have less usage restrictions. The UI is generally more obscured than it's predecessor and is missing a lot of quality of life features of character/skill/inventory management from the previous games. Using skills and more around the world is on par but terrain objects i.e. tents often have much large collision boxes than their visually representation. The mini-map is offer less options for viewing the area and the colour scheme + revealing mechanics often require you to stop and open the map full screen to determine were you haven't explored yet. The game recycles mini-bosses very frequent compared to previously I've had to the same 1 in at least 2 separate overworld locations already...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for people who enjoy dungeon crawlers like Diablo or Victor Vran. The developers respond quickly to player feedback and use it to frequently improve the game. The game has great visuals that you can take advantage of with a customizable home base that you can show off to other players. Customization is where this game really shines.Combining two skill trees per class across four classes with one of five elemental relics each with their own skill tree (all with benchmark passives that can synergize with other abilities) allows for deep customization. In addition to those you also have legendary skills, pet abilities, and a deep gear system to make each character feel unique.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm a huge fan of ARPG games, and Torchlight 2 is one of my favorite game of all time.Would I recommend people to buy Torchlight 3? Absolutely NOT and here is why:Yes, Torchlight 3 was originally build as a F2P "mobile" game with microtransactions, then they decided to make it a Buy-to-play game, but the core of the game is still a mobile game.I like the artstyle, the pet loot and the map system, but everything else is basically a downscaled version of Torchlight 2. Everything in Torchlight 3 is simple, too simple : the skill tree is extremely basic, items don't need to be identified like in the previous games, you can use teleport as often as you want... I don't mind playing simple games, Torchlight 2 wasn't really complex either, but this just feel like playing a mobile game, a game that is made to be played with one finger while you're waiting for your bus. Even the character movement/animations are more simple. Also, there is no skill customisation like in any RPG, you can't assign skill points to, for ex, Health or Magic skills, to make your character rely more on Magic or stronger for close attacks. And the worst part: YOU CANT FISH ANYMORE! :( The OST is uninspired, it's a million mile years from the amazing OST in Torchlight 2.  And don't get me started on Torchlight 3's "story", they didn't even try (like in Torchlight 2). The game isn't awful nor bad, it's "ok".I understand when people say "this is a small studio, we should understand them, we should support them", but come on, at the end, this is your money, and Torchlight 3 is absolutely NOT worth the 40 euros they ask for. That's insane. The game is worth maybe 20 euros max.Playing Torchlight 3 feels like a waste of my time, so much that I decided that I should enjoy some music in the background.  Also, playing this game gives me a really weird sad feeling, maybe because I love Torchlight 2 so much and it makes me sad to see what Torchlight 3 could have been instead...  I think the 2 biggest problems with this game are: 1/ it kept the "Torchlight" name but ditched lot of stuffs that made Torchlight serie such a great choice for ARPG fans.   2/ the 40€ price.   If the game was called, I dunno VikingStörm", made by an independant studio  and costed 30 euros, it would be decent. But having the name "Torchlight 3" and asking 40 euros for it is basically like a spit inside the mouth of Torchlight fans :(   The game get much better after the second act, but the lack of essential RPG features and the price tag still make it a no-buy. Again it is not a terrible game, but it's not really good either.There are good ideas here and there, but they were ruined by ♥♥♥♥♥♥ management decisions. Even Max Schaefer (who I have nothing but respect for) doesn't seem to believe in this game  :( The final word: Get Torchlight 3 only when it is on sale for 10-15 euros (probably really soon). Meanwhile go buy (or play again) Torchlight 2 (it's available for cheap on Fanatical), which is a masterpiece.  Or maybe try FATE by WildTangent, it's THE game that inspired Torchlight I and II. And on contrary to Torchlight 3, in Fate you can fish and customize your character :)   ------------------------------------------------REVIEW EDITED to give more details about how the game is too simple and to mention its "2 biggest problem".
