_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough of the release version. The game is still fun and still buggy. Between the classes, the relics and the legendary system there are quite a lot of builds in the game and although it might seem shallow in the beginning it is definitely not.Early access review below:OK, first thing first - Torchlight 3 is not an upgraded version of Torchlight 2 like TL2 was to 1. It is a completely new game with different mechanics some are similar to those in TL2 and some are not. At this time it is also not finished so if you are expecting a finished and polished product then don't buy it. If you do not want to have your characters wiped at some point - do not buy it as well. The game is buggy and it is laggy and there are large chunks of content missing even when compared to the beta version that was running before the early-access. It also has a lot of potential.Torchlight 3 currently features 4 classes each having 14 class skills. Those are somewhat arbitrary separated into two skill trees but you don't have to have invested in any skill in a skill tree to get any other skill in the same tree effectively rendering the tree grouping thematic rather than mechanical.  Each skill has 10 levels and the skill morphs 2 times - once at level 3 and once at level 10. The morphs are mechanical changes o the way the skill works and sometimes they interact with the class-specific mechanics and sometimes they are just situational bonuses or additional elements of the skill. When you reach level 6 in each skill a passive unlocks that often does not have anything to do with the skill. That passive will be active even if you do not have the skill on your hotbar so effectively you have 14 active and 14 passive skills kind of rolled up into one and you would get some skills for the passive exclusively and some for the active exclusively and sometimes you would be happy that the two are tied to the same skill.Additionally early in the game you get to pick one of 5 relics for your character. Those relics are shared across all classes and level up independently. Each relic kind of has 2 active and 3 passive skills and these are tied to a specific damage type and its procs(poison, burning, bleeding, shock, freeze). The relic is usually a support to your build but it is possible to build your entire character around a certain relic.Next, you have the pet system. It is kind of under developed. You basically collect pet skins and abilities from special chests near boss fights and the pet skills offer some basic auras and periodical buffs for your character and some attacks(my favourite is the pet farting and poisoning the enemies around it).Itemization is kind of standard fair for the genre with items of four rarities dropping with different number of random affixes. White or normal items don't have any additional affixes but only the basic item stats - damage for weapons and resistances or health for the armor-type. Green Magic items have 1 additional affix, Blue Rare items have 2 additional affixes and Yellow Legendary items have 3 additional affixes and a set legendary affix. The affixes matter but everything below Legendary item is basically a simple stat-stick. Still the legendary items and their Mayhem Affixes offer mechanics that morph existing character skills or provide additional mechanics on actions like basic attacks, potion consumption, relic activation, skill casts, getting hit, etc. Those effects are pretty powerful and most builds would be build around those items. Additionally those items usually come in sets. The set does not provide a stat or effect bonus like they do in other games but instead if you have 3 items of the same set equipped the mayhem affixes of the individual items get enhanced. There are about 150 legendary items all with unique mayhem affixes currently in the game.The last part of the character building process is the legendarium. Basically you can choose to disassemble a legendary item and gain it's legendary affix in the legendarium and you can have 3 of those affixes active as passive skills without having the items equipped. Those would get buffs from set bonuses but do not count as an equipped item when counting the number of set items equipped.There is also an enchantment system that is kind of an reimagining of the standard socket system. Basically some items drop with enchantment slots and you can put enchantments in those slots. The enchantment you put in provides a random stat bonus chosen from a set for that enchantment type. Additional enchantment types drop as recipes along with other loot.There are also some other minor mechanics such as sacrificing items to permanently increase your loot and collecting account-wide defense bonuses the more you fight against certain enemies as well as a housing mechanic but those do not affect the gameplay significantly.What are the problems with the game?Well, first off - there are only 14 active class skills. They do provide variety but more are obviously welcome. The devs have said in the past that they do not plan to add more in the future but with the recent massively negative feedback over the lack of active skills that might change.Same goes for the amount of relics - only 5 at the moment. No word if they are going to add more but one can only hope.The pet skill system is also underdeveloped and would benefit from more variety. Again - no word on what is going to be happening here.The lag makes the combat really not responsive at times.The resistances mechanic is kind of pointless because you would generally encounter only one element that the enemies are using per act. That might change with the endgame mechanics that are coming at a later date but it is not really a certainty and the game would benefit if any element can be used by enemies anywhere.The UI is huge and kind of ugly when you are in the menus. It is functional but it was also meant to be easily accessible with a controller on a TV and it kind of shows. The devs said that UI scaling is coming in the future.There is no stat-distribution system or anything to substitute it. As this is a massively requested feature in a recent post the devs have said that they are going to implement a system to address this issue.The levels are randomly generated but are also pretty linear so most of the times you are running through a long weirdly shaped corridor rather than exploring a maze or an overworld zone.The visual variety is not great. There are a few enemy types and a few world tile-sets and because of that everything looks kind of the same in each act. The first one with the goblins is probably the worst as even different goblin types kind of look the same and are hard to distinguish.Overall I would say that the game does have a solid core but needs more content and variety in everything. The devs are competent and are listening to player feedback - every single system in the game has been reworked multiple times since the initial alpha release of the game due to player feedack. Unfortunately that did not leave a lot of time for the developers to work on content and variety and the game has suffered because of that. This game is not ready for release in its current form and while I would recommend it I would do so only to people who want to actively provide feedback on a developing product and not to people who just want to play an aRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "Maybe" option for recommending, because honestly, at the core, the gameplay itself is decent hack & slash dungeon crawling that I find relaxing. But on the whole, I am very disappointed in this installment of the series. I tend to take it with a grain of salt when folks complain that a game is "unfinished," but even over a year after its release and months after its last major update, Torchlight III is *riddled* with bugs, and many of them are pretty disruptive.Playing through the main storyline and a little of the endgame dungeon, about 25 hours in the past few days, I encountered ALL THIS:• The constant tendency for my pet to stop following me when I port somewhere, requiring me to return to my fort and swap pets to fix. Especially disruptive for the endgame dungeon because you have to restart the level you're on if you leave.• 2+ times where the entrance to an area I needed to go for a story quest was not highlighted or even usable until I restarted the game.• Equipped a staff which bugged the game sound pretty badly once I started using its attack, and had to replace the weapon and restart the game to fix.• Equipped a collar to my pet that... kept killing it... for some reason. Had to replace with another item, and mysterious out-of-combat pet deaths stopped.• Got stuck in place each time I exited a particular mini rabbit hole dungeon area, had to portal out and back to move again.• During a special portal boss encounter (I can't recall if it was a Phase Beast portal or a reward map), the boss just wasn't there. Had to portal out, empty-handed, and the opportunity was wasted.And these are just the particularly disruptive bugs. There are minor ones of varying annoyance, and frankly, it's just a lot.My second biggest gripe is the lack of subtitles/captions for speech in cutscenes etc. Otherwise, I feel some things are lacking in comparison to Torchlight II, which may unfortunately result from its troubled development and changing hands.I don't regret getting it on sale or playing, all the same. I liked a few of the additions that it made. I just hope that one day it'll get the TLC it needs to fix up the bugs and flesh out the experience a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: Torchlight 3 is an amazing game, and will keep you hooked for hours. Torchlight 3 is a 3D, Third Person, Top Down Perspective Dungeon Crawler Game. In the game there are 3 Campaigns, or what Torchlight 3 calls them, acts. Each act has it's own storyline/lore, while still being connected throughout the game. In this review I will tell new players, or people interested in Torchlight 3 about the game, but I will also compare Torchlight 3 with the previous game in the series, Torchlight 2.For longtime fans of the other games in the Torchlight Franchise, Is Torchlight 3 better than Torchlight 1 and Torchlight 2? Well, It's very hard to say, and one of those reasons being I didn't play the first Torchlight as of writing this review. Torchlight 3 did so many things well, but the problems it does have makes it hard for me to decide if Torchlight 2 or 3 is better. They both aren't perfect, but both are very good games.The First thing Torchlight 3 does better than Torchlight 2 is the graphics. The graphics in this game are just amazing. Torchlight 2's graphics were good, but not near this game's. I also feel like the game takes longer to complete the story, which is a good thing! I played 20 hours in one playthrough of Torchlight 3, whereas Torchlight 2 takes probably 10 hours to complete a playthrough. Another part of this game I liked was the Pets. In Torchlight 3 you get a new pet every boss fight, being able to choose whether you keep it, release it or swap. I love this aspect of the game, as  Sure Torchlight 2 had the ability to transform pets, but I like Torchlight 3's version better. Yet another part of this game I liked was the difficulty of it. I played on Normal difficulty, and it actually still got pretty tough towards the end of the game. Torchlight 3 has a new feature to the game called your Fort. Your fort is your base where you have your storage, training targets, crafting stations, displays and more. Displays can be either displaying your equipment or pets, which I find super cool. Torchlght 3 also introduces Crafting within your fort. I never used crafting much in my playthrough, but I like that it's there. Crafting is used to make things in your fort like displays and other stations. One station in the fort that I find cool is the dyeing station. You can dye/reskin your armor and weapons, giving your armor and weapons different colors, and being able to totally reskin your items. This paragraph is me complaining about some issues in Torchlight 3, but the issues are fixable by the player pretty easily. If your new to Torchlight Or just thinking about getting the game, I would skip this paragraph. I know that was a decent amount of complaints, but those issues didn't stop me from absolutely loving this game, as they were easily fixable. In the end, I highly recommend Torchlight 3, you'll be playing for hours. I for one still have many hours to play as I'd like to 100% this game's achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not reviewing this on latency issues or bugs, because this is early access. I'm only reviewing this based on my grind through out twenty hours. I'm also reviewing this to inform you that you should pass on this game for the reasons listed below, until the developers address some fundamental issues:First, life bound items aren't bad due to the rare drops of unbind scrolls, it's a terrible idea over all and should be stripped from the game. Never have I seen an ARG do something as punishing. Make the weapons and armor damaged and require a trip back to town to repair. How did the developers think it was a good idea to destroy something a player had to grind for?Secondly is respec. The drops to change points are rare. What was wrong with the previous systems where a person in town can do it? It is almost easier to start over from the beginning than it is to undo a skill from your tree. Again, dumb idea and what were the developers thinking!Thirdly, fix the issues with traveling and the map. The scrollbar on the map is so thin that its unnoticable. There is a ux law I can't remember off the top of my head that states that users expect your application to work like others. Even now, I try to scroll that map using a drag operation.It also can be confusing to some people that they can click on an in between passage, hear a notification sound, but not travel there unless they are standing on a portal. Those should appear disabled, or why even allow a user to bring up that World Map at all?You know I watched people in chat constantly complain about not understanding how that works, as well as having to grind to a save point or they will have to rediscover the entire area again. This is an obvious pain point for many and its apparent the developers didn't do any journey maps with gamers actually "playing" the game.Lastly, the dungeons are linear, the npc attacks are predictable and the same, and the classes and skills aren't even that interesting.I don't see how they can fix all of this.

_childDocuments_.review: is a fun, but  ARPG not unlike its predecessor  which fans have come to love over the years. If you're looking for the complexity provided by  or  the simplicity here may be a turn off for veterans. I believe most of the negative reviews stemmed from launch day server issues, and this is an unfair critique of an otherwise enjoyable experience. Below I'll list some pros and cons from my early impressions that will hopefully give you the potential buyer some insight before you decide to spend your hard earned gold!- aesthetically the game is beautiful (environments, NPC's, characters, etc.)- game-play is fast, addictive, and user friendly- skills are varied, characters feel unique, and build variety is possible (more on that in a bit)- loot is exciting, drops are frequent, and inventory management is made simple thanks to the "pet" system- the "Fort", a new personalized hub for your character is expansive with a fair amount of customization- sound and music are adequate and compliment the game-play, especially the "Forged" skills audio- always online, server stability at the time of writing remains inconsistent (disconnects are frequent)- stat management is gone, attributes are distributed automatically (hurting overall "build" variety)-  maps can take a long time to load thus pulling you out of the experienceAs you can see, my overall impression of the game is a positive one. Besides a few shortcomings this is a solid experience that has a ton of potential and room to grow. If you're looking for an ARPG besides the titular  (Diablo, POE, Grim Dawn) that you can pick up and play you should look no further. If you're on the fence here the highly rated and objectively superior  is more or less the best entry point into the series and notably cheaper!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game right now, definitely early access material with some bugs and such. I'm only voting this a No right now b/c the developers don't understand that the whole point of an ARPG is to get gear so you don't feel weak.I spent 5 hours playing the game the past couple of days... from hour 2-5 I kept saying to myself "I'm getting all this gear but literally nothing is dying any faster". I was level 11 in a level 7 zone, on the second hardest difficulty. All of my gear was level 9-10 but there was no difference in how long it took me to kill anything when I swapped from my lower level pistol/rifle to my level 10.... then I noticed the level said "7/10"... They scale your gear down for the zone you're in.In their Frontier FAQ , they go on about how leveling is more than just about gear, how they want it to be rewarding... well, I don't think any of them have ever played an ARPG b/c that's some of the most ignorant crap I've ever read coming from a game that's supposed to be one. There is NOTHING rewarding about being 4 levels higher than the zone you're in and not stomping through it b/c your gear has been sync'd to match the zone level. -NOTHING-.It's for that simple fact I can't recommend the game right now... if you want level scaling, go play a game that isn't quite as gear dependent as an ARPG is.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit - bug made a late game quest unfinishable. Recommending again as the bug was fixed within one day of providing feedback. In addition I'm finding the simplicity of the game actually adds to my enjoyment, especially when inebriated. The simplicity + fort upgrades also helps relieve the potential tediousness of the Hardcore playing game loop.What I like best in an action RPG is a hardcore mode, great build diversity, and some randomization of the levels/encounters on future runs. I want a great pieces of equipment to make my build around. Maybe even make me re-imagine what is possible for my toon. That gives you an idea of my preferences and where I’m coming from.Does TL3 deliver for me? So far it checks the boxes, but at a very superficial level. TL3 is basically a free to play peg jammed to fit into a premium game sized hole, and it definitely feels it.With all that said, I’m having quite a bit of fun. It’s light, breezy, and it keeps much of the stylistic charms of its predecessors… despite its lack of depth. It is a great pick up and play game. I think it could be less expensive for what has been delivered, but its price certainly isn’t outrageous.Solo players… especially hardcore players… especially mature players trying to escape the grind…. You need to know that this game has NO PAUSE FUNCTION, even for solo play. This makes no sense and can be pretty frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: In a few words: what an awesome gaming experience that TL3 has been so far!So, i was really skeptical to buy this game or not, mostly because i have said that i will not pay for an early access game ever again, and in one hand i am a fun of the previous 2 games and have been excited for this title since they announced it (not so excited for the Frontiers version of it), but on the other, reading all the bad reviews, watching various streams calling it a damped down version of an arpg and a few gamers in youtube saying "don't buy", i got the impression that it is not worth it. But since i did like what i saw in the streams, and waited for the first days hiccups to go away, i said to myself that i should try it by myself. And boy am i glad that i did.- Graphics: awesome. Not to offend others, but guys if you compare this game with a mobile game, you seriously need to have your eyes checked. Now if you don't like the artstyle, thats subjective, but for me, i simply love it.- Sound: it sounds pretty good. The music doesn't bother you, you hear clear sounds everywhere and the world feels alive. At least in the one class i have started playing, the skill sounds feel realistic.- Animations: just perfect. Not too flashy to fill the screen, so at some point you have no idea whats going on, not too poor. To my eyes, they are balanced.- Skills: pretty interesting skills and far from boring. Combining the main skills, relic skills, and passive pet skills, i think you got enough to work with, and play an interesting build. For me, that i don't play games all day long, i don't stream games, i don't enjoy spending my time and my life "theory crafting builds", a simplified skill tree is a plus not a minus, like many "hardcore" gamers say. If you are looking for a hardcore niche type of gameplay, maybe then this game isn't for you, don't try to turn this into one. There are other arpgs out there doing exactly that.- Gameplay: i like to take my time in video games, whenever i have the free time to play. I loved previous torchlight games because of their simplicity and providing me the opportunity to take my time with them and i love TL3 for that too. The world is responsive, the gameplay is fluid, the combat feels awesome and i am having a blast. The fort is a nice touch, that keeps me from having to return "to a town" all the time, while i can customize it to my liking.- The world: looks and feels fantastic. Gathering mats for the fort is fun, the locations are looking cool, the mobs are funny, and if you don't rush through the zones just to reach "the endgame" (which is not implemented yet btw), they don't feel small at all, like others have said.Overall trying this early access version has been a really fun experience. I am leveling slowly, i am enjoying exploring every corner of the well designed world, i am not rushing to level cap and the "endgame", i am having a good time. There is definitely room for improvement, but hopefully it won't turn into a over complicated mess until the full release, for the shake of "niche" complication. Jump in, kill mobs, find loot, get a little stronger, rinse and repeat. Got bored? go make another class, until the next content patch hits or whatever. Want a challenge? play harder difficulty (i played "hard"), or hardcore.Definitely worth playing!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, Simplistic, fun action loop, light hearted fun graphics, OMG BESTEST BOI PET, base building mechanics! Slotable unique upgrades for when you find those legendary equipments. This means you can slot that special effect and then use another green or blue item that stat wise is much better but still gain the benefit, this is a FANTASTIC upgrade. Shared stash/base tabs! Contracts that give you 3 different types of rewards,  resources, gear or window dressings for the base. WoW meets Diablo. Torchlight three delivers on a lot of aspects for the hack n slash casual gamer.DownsidesGambling for all loot. There are no vendors that spawn loot just a gambler merchant.gold cap of 20k when I have to spend 5k at the gambler for a random blue this sucks.Reskinned bosses. Some bosses were reskinned for later levels leaving me rather disappointed.Later level bosses depend on 1 shot kill mechanics step at the wrong time? BOOM your dead even with 60% resist.Not really a fan of the way gear scales as no matter what your either capped at 60% or end up with really low resistance.No depth, the game is pretty shallow there really isn't a lot of optimization to be had and the loot is pretty bog standard.You cant craft till you beat the game which REALLY hurts gear customization. craftable equipment stuff doesn't drop til almost level 50. End game seems to be some sort of card based modifier dungeon which would be cool if it didn't crash every time i tried to go into it. The random crashed REALLY hurt and usually happen between zone transitions which can suck when you try to go to the boss encounter then have to reload and redo the ENTIRE previous level to clear to boss.pet's are bugged to auto run away for 2 min when you get hit by a trap and when you just had full inventory UGH!The relic skill tree is hard to synergize with a lot of your set powers so you really have to rely on specific weapon types to make things pop or legendary equipment. A lot of relic powers require things to bleed,burn,freeze or be poisoned but almost none of the set character classes have the ability to do so this can be rather hard to work around unless you have the right legendary slots so it forces you to take specific relics that kind of synergize with each character making the whole "choose your hero archetype thing" moot because X+Y = best synergy.

Been playing on hard difficulty and having a good time.  15 hours in and it was definitely worth the $8 summer sale price.  No bugs or glitches encountered. _childDocuments_.review: A bit different than Torchlight II game but so far I really like this 3rd installment. I played with my mom all the time but this newer game doesn't play the same. Now it's either a single player or an online co-op - no multiplayer LAN parties!  We had a bit of a hiccup when we first started which was we couldn't see each other in the game. No matter what we did, it took us almost 40 minutes before we were able to actually see each other in multiplayer. Then it was another 20 minutes of inviting and kicking each other before one of us could join the other in a party.  We were getting pretty pissed, but once we were able to get past that, the game has been fun to play.We have experienced the same issues a couple more times but it's not taken as long to get it corrected. Sometimes going thru a portal will correct and we don't even have to log off.  Needs fixed for sure, but hasn't deterred us from playing. Unfortunately, Torchlight III is missing some of the things I loved about Torchlight II.  For example, you can't trade with anyone.  It's not uncommon to find more gear for all the other types of characters other than the one you're playing so it's nice to be able to trade with your team if you want. Worse yet, you can't even throw stuff on the ground - not to get rid of or to allow someone else to pick up. Granted, with an online co-op multiplayer game, you wouldn't want to throw stuff down and some stranger snatch it.  But there should be an option to trade with other players! There are some cool upgrades though. Torchlight III graphics are much better and comes with your own fort - a place for you to have storage for your items you want to save and can share among all your characters. However, you can also decorate it with various items. Some items allow you to get protection bonuses, luck bonuses, you can transmog your weapons, you can build and place crafting stations to produce things you want/need to build/create.  If you played Torchlight II you will see and hear references to some of the characters/bosses in this 3rd game. There are still phase portals but are much more common than in the first two games. A lot of stuff can be busted for loot and coin - and a lot more coin than in the previous version. The character builds are a little different but I think an improvement over Torchlight II. This new Torchlight is a mix of Torchlight II, World of Warcraft and maybe a little Diablo/Grim Dawn. My 73 year old mom and I have played a couple hours each day and are having a good time. I think Torchlight III is worth checking out!

_childDocuments_.review: I played the previous two games for hours and hours, and Torchlight II still is my favorite ARPG (action RPG). There are still a few bugs, as with any new release, but the mechanics have the same feel as the previous games, with a few changes. I still don't see the point of the fort-building mechanic, but perhaps that will make more sense as I continue playing.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:Never had a crash (maybe all the kinks previous reviews mentioned were all worked out by 2023).Fluid and fast movement. Easy to get into, all cutscenes are skippable.Unusual character classes to experiment with (if you're tired of being a wizard/warrier/healer class).The Bad:Unusual character classes to experiment with (a newcomer to the genre shouldn't start with this game).Plot/storyline is demotivating and not compelling - I didn't get any sense of progression through the game.Complex interactions due to added mechanics. You're not just keeping an eye on your life+mana, because "mana" is replaced by a complex interaction between 3 other things. TL2 had the separate recharge bar and its effect quite obvious. In TL3 it is never obvious what these extra "things" do.The Ugly:Completely breaks the existing TL1/TL2/D1/D2 (the "other" ARPGs I refer to below) user interface. How do you bring up quests? Other games use had 'q'. How do I assign potions to a slot (still haven't figured this out, just keep using 'q' for health and damn the rest!). How do you bring up your character sheet? Other games used 'a' or 'c'. How do you show your pets(mercs) inventory next to your inventory, like ARPGs have been doing since 2001? Shift-clicking on an inventory item does nothing.The UI completely ignores the existing conventions for how lots of things work.If you are a newcomer then this isn't so bad, but then if you are a newcomer, the complicated interactions between all the replacements for "mana" means this game probably isn't for you either.I see there's legendarium points, ammo points (replacement for mana?) and skill points (for skills), relics (dunno what the quantum is for that) and (IIRC) some sort of recharge thing for continuous attacks.This system is definitely not for newcomers.Another ugly is the focus on irrelevant stuff. You're trying to save the world, but you want to do some interior redecorating? C'mon! That adds literally nothing to the A or the RP of ARPG. I wasted a bit of time trying to figure out what the fort is primarily for, before I realised it's for those people who miss farmville!This game is not for people who want to role-play a character, because the character doesn't meaningfully progress, the focus is on collectibles more than character attributes.Conclusion:I think you will enjoy this game if and only if:a) You haven't actually played any other ARPG (like D2/D2Remastered, or TL1/TL2, etc),andb) You play hyper-casually on mobile (i.e. something you play for a short period while in a docs waiting room or on the train)andc) Role-Playing is secondary to Action for you.This game *can* work for you if all of the 3 points above is true. If not you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: (Early Access) Yes I have 0.7hrs here on Steam. It doesn't mean there are not more hours accrued during other testing phases. Dusk Mage abilities don't weave, and the animation for ability 2 (light ball at range) just        feels bad. (2) Combat feels sluggish and not fun.      - I reached level 5, and in that time at no point did it feel good to me. At no point did I go,        "WOW! I want to keep going". It felt sluggish, the first two abilities didn't mesh together at        all.  (3) Balance does not feel like it is there.       - Enemies felt they took longer than they should to kill; enemies being level 2 vs player         being level 5. During Enchanted or Boss fights, at no point did it feel fun. Spam 1 or 2         abilities, potion, and run around until it is dead. More abilities unlock later, sure, but the         first 2 abilities didn't feel good and left me concerned for future ones.(4) It just wasn't fun at all, I'd rather play Wolcen or Diablo 3.       - Wolcen is a game I backed, and did not like at the end of their production. I'd rather play         that, I won't, but that is how I felt. That is how much I didn't like my experience. T3 is by         name only, T2 is far superior right now. (5) Feels like mobile F2P game ported to PC.      - Yes this was Frontier, which was going to be a very different game. They started to redo         it, but there is a lot here that exists from that point of the games history. It doesn't         justify the cost point on entry, and it doesn't feel like $30 (to be raised on release). Grim         Dawn? Victor Vran? Cheaper, and better. To all the people who are aggressive towards people whom have a different opinion than you; maybe try to realize they have a different opinion than you and be constructive rather than hateful. _childDocuments_.review: (I've finished the game, tried out the end-game challenges. I played offline on steam and it didn't record my hours. Took me around 20 hours.)It's fine, but I wouldn't recommend it to a friend to play. If you got nothing better to play, sure, have at it. I hit a few bugs, the worst being where it seemed like the level didn't load properly. The most annoying one was the pet kept disappearing (wasn't dead), and I'd have to return to fort and swap a pet to get them back. Minor stuff.My two biggest complaints: No Pause in single-player and No Subtitles. That was very surprising. I can't remember the last time I played a game that didn't have those two features. It shouldn't have left early access without those, in my opinion. These are a big deal to me.So because of that I have no idea what the story was, because everything is told in audio format. There's no way to replay them later either. I couldn't spoil the story even if I wanted to.That aside, in regards to gameplay, to me is the game is boring and repetitive. All the areas feel the same, loot was lacking which caused me to just start running past mobs, and the monsters lacked variety, and monster mechanics were repeated regularly across different monsters in different zones. I got sick of the grubs and the floating balls of poison.Another issue is the pet variety. I got the impression at the start of the game that I would unlock DIFFERENT pets, not re-skins of the starting pets. I had at least 3 dogs, 3 cats, and 4 birds. I was very excited about that idea at the start, so that was very disappointing.I also disliked the respec system. Every game I've played, an item like that wipes your skill tree entirely. This game, one respec item = 1 point returned.The cosmetic forts felt very lacking. I like the ideas of all the fort & functional items, but I got very few fun decorative items to place in my fort. Without lots of neat items, I didn't want to bother changing my fort around much. The game should be really showering you in cosmetics so you have reasons to play with the customization. Upgrades to gear just seemed much more rare than it should have been, and the item variety also felt lacking. I got 2 different duplicate legionaries (which of course were not for my class). And lastly, enchanting is only post-game. That's a terrible idea.Positives?I did like the pet abilities, I unlocked a few of those and that was fun. By end of game I think I had around half of them unlocked.I liked the 3 talent trees. I think there were too many abilities in the trees, because you can only have a set number of them. But the variety felt good. I would have experimented more if not for the respec system.I played the sharpshooter, and that class felt good to play. I had a good variety of abilities for different situations, and they felt well balanced.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is resoundingly "meh," which is kind of a bummer. TL1 and TL2 were a bit dated but still relaxing fun, and TL2 especially was an enjoyable and chill co-op experience with friends. Lots of good memories there. But TL3 just feels so ... empty, half-realized, and frustrating. You can see the bones of the F2P skeleton it was originally developed on, and there are tons of quality of life issues here that boggle the mind. You can't trade with other players; instances will often reset themselves and re-populate with enemies during the same live session; you can only see fellow party members on the mini-map when they're very close to you, the game doesn't show you quest indicators until you're quite close to the objective, so you're forced to spend a lot of time wandering blindly (and especially if your instance and its fog of war were just reset), zones are weirdly corridor-like and samey, there's very limited enemy variety and poor AI; and pretty simplistic skill trees, although the devs seem to be trying to improve this at least. For example, the Forged update seems pretty good.But itemization is very poor, which is a serious issue when the core gameplay loop revolves around getting better, shinier, more powerful stuff. There are far fewer item types, quality gradations, and affixes than you'd expect, and the whole setup feels weirdly simplistic. You can find "upgraded" versions of the same legendaries throughout the game, which I don't mine, and the ability to select "Legendarium affixes" (kinda like the cubed abilities in Diablo 3) adds some variety to the mix, but there are just very few notable or fun items of any sort. Hopefully the devs will be adding in far more interesting and build-altering items in the coming months, but currently it doesn't take long to see most of the loot pool. There's also a quaint but weirdly half-baked personal fort mechanic, which (while pretty) has very few functional benefits. Even its crafting station doesn't become available until you've completed the main campaign, and by the time I had invested the 20-22(ish) hours to get there on Painful difficulty, I was mostly burned out. It seems like the only "end game" right now is running those mapworks levels and doing the endless dungeon stuff, so I'll check back in a year and see if things have improved enough to warrant changing this review. The art style and soundtrack are nice, the graphics are simple but good, art direction as a whole and some of the boss models and animations are great, and the "feel" (mostly targeting and responsiveness) is solid. But the net code or some other element of the multiplayer infrastructure here is pretty rough. I would sometimes desync from my co-op partner and be unable to resurrect him, or we'd rubberband weirdly and vanish temporarily from each other's screens. The ability to teleport to each other is pretty nice, though, and the town portal and related traversal is solid all around. The game is also weirdly stingy with waypoints, and it often felt like our sessions were artificially extended by how long it would take us to find the next WP and really "lock in" our progress.The story is ... mostly trite and nonsensical, delivered with minimal context and seemingly not even taken that seriously by the game itself. I enjoy the narrative garnish in ARPGs like this, even if it's only to set the stage and provide a rationale for the loot-hunting romp, but a story this bland and poorly delivered may as well be missing entirely. I finished the campaign today with a Dusk Mage approaching level 50, and aside from something about Ordrak's Heart I didn't really have any idea what was going on. It makes me kind of sad to say this, since I've got a soft spot for TL2 especially, but I'd suggest passing on this one unless there are substantial content updates and other QOL changes made in 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put 4 hours into this game upon review, but those are 4 straight hours where I couldn't put it down. Yes, it has bugs. Have they been game breaking for me? No. Sometimes mobs will appear frozen, running in place, but no big deal. Some of the UI features need to be reworked and organized so they are in a more appropriate location and size, but again...no big deal. I get some lag with melee attacks, but hasn't bothered me. I think the concept of lifebound items is great and a fun challenge. Integrating them in a different way is a good idea, but I hope they do it right. Maybe lifebound items go into a building in your fort where you have to do certain challenges and/or collect materials to unlock. Maybe able to upgrade lifebound items through various quests, i.e. killing a boss, etc.The bosses have been a fun challenge. Kiting a boss all over the map to stay alive is exciting; even on normal mode.  The pet features have been great.  Allowing you to swap pets whenever you want in your fort and after bosses. I love the big boss chests as it feels really rewarding and one of the reasons I wanted to keep playing. Gathering materials for your fort is going to be a grind, but to be expected. _childDocuments_.review: I've had my heart broken several times in my life. Once, on Christmas Day 1989, I eagerly ran downstairs and gasped at the sight of what was clearly a crudely but lovingly wrapped skateboard. A skateboard that I had wanted ever since I had seen Marty McFly cruise through the streets of Hill Valley as a stowaway behind an unsuspecting SUV driver. A skateboard with a custom deck, with artwork that would cause my fellow skaters to shout "rad". A skateboard whose wheels would send me gliding across the streets as I headed for the nearest half-pipe. A skateboard of majestical proportions.I grabbed it, and with shaking hands and a heart beating against my chest, I tore that festive wrapping as hard as I could. Through an intricate web of sticky tape, ribbon and ever expanding wrapping paper, I dug through. Years later, I wondered that this is what Andy in The Shawshank Redemption must have felt like as he dragged himself through the tunnels. My own redemption was in sight. My prize was near. Finally, the last shred of packaging fell away to the floor. And there it was... a plastic skateboard from the local store. With stiff plastic wheels. And a picture of a clown on the deck.That's what playing Torchlight III felt like.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a short early access where you can get about 15 hours of gameplay going through the first 2 acts in Painful or Ridiculous difficulty, on a lower setting the game time will be less of course. As for build diversity you have 2 talent tress for each class and 15 Legendary's items for each class as well that can drop and level cap is 40, you are limited on respeccing your talent points as they are tied behind a very rare respectable currency where at lvl 34 I have gotten 10 most which is a random drop from bosses I believe.The game is a good idea and foundation of it but the ugly truth is its been in the same state for the last year, meaning no updates or optimizations, act 1 plays fairly well, but act 2 is a mess with sound bugs and lag spikes and rubberbanding of your character which makes it almost unplayable, act 2 is just incomplete , coupled with server issues you get DC'ed and magically old quests appear on your log sending you on a duck hunt with no end in site until you figure out its bugged and you already completed that quest a while ago.I would say if you would like the game to succeed and want to support its development via financially or with your thoughts pick it up and play it and provide feedback or just invest on it, but as a selfless purchase to have fun, I believe you will be disappointed.I had fun with it and can see the vision and potential and like the Torchlight series, but from what I experienced 8 months ago in beta to now during the early access Id say the game will be ready for full release with end game replayable  content around 2022. You can get more hours of content playing all the classes as well, 15 hours is one class only.my advise to the Dev team is add more content fast, replayable content, do not scale down player power and zones, but scale it up, the constant power flux between high and low as you change zones is really demoralizing, no one likes to feel weak after they have gotten strong, maybe its a instancing system bugging or intended I dont know, and multiplayer scaling and xp sharing is a mess if someone of higher level joins you they receive no xp for helping or the reduction is 99%.Please take your time and create more diversity and for testing purposes remove the cost to respec so you get more feedback on all skills and talent tree.I am giving the game a positive review because I always want every game to be successful and I believe Torchlight has a solid foundation and very good potential in the future  as well as 2 previous titles already,so please invest responsibly, after all its your money on the line.Goodluck.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not finished the game and this is my early impressions.Visually the game looks really good compared to the previous games. Everything just has a more solid look to it.  It has some familiar mechanics but they they quickly pass into the new direction. Given the game was originally planned as a MMO-like the corner stones of the design still remains and it affects the rest of the games design.You still get a pet but they are interchangable and your pets now have their own skills with skills being unlocked as you rescue more pet classes.Your skill trees (although no skill is required to unlock another, just your level) are visible at the start of character creation allowing you to have an idea of what you want to play and how you will play. You have 2 skill trees per class and then you select 1 of 5 relics as your 3rd tree. This dramatically reduces the actual amount of skills you will use in the game however you still get skill points to invest like in the old format and every skill invested strengthens and changes how the skill works (eg holy bolt lvl3 gets buffed damage on a 3rd attack).Weapons have their own attacks such as greatswords have an arc attack that does 350% weapon damage as your basic attack while a pistol would do 80% weapon damage on a single target etc.The game has seemingly done away with character stats and resources spending will regen over time with skills having cooldowns for use.A remnant of the mmo build is that you have a fortress where you store gear in a shared stash, build and use structures like a luck tree to increase gear and quality drops by sacrificing items to it, crafting structures which I have no looked into yet, upgrade your pet stables to keep more pets and just decorate your fort the way you want. You have a gold cap in the game and it won't take you too long to hit it so feel free to spend money when you have it. The game also allows you to use skills from legendary items as legendary enhancements just like Diablos Kunai cube with the exception you dont need to destroy the item and its accessable from your character menus. Ultimately its a rather big departure from the previous entries. The game is different but so far it isn't all that bad. I do give my recommendation but I feel the game is a lot more shallow than its predicessors and a Diablo 3 beater I don't think this is.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good Torchlight?- kinda of, 6/10It is a good RPG?- could be more customizable, 5/10Have good action?- loved this part, the pace and flow are really nice, 9/10Good players interaction?- worst of most RPGs out there, you cant trade, shared instances are bugged as hell, 1/10Enjoyable mechanics?- it is simplified af. but is pretty good actually, 7/10Good difficulty and balance?- I only played the Ridiculous diff, and it is really Ridiculous with some classes and at some points in the game, 8/10The lore makes you want to see what is to come?- no, pretty unexistent, they just trashed the lore and style of the antagonists, the lore is VERY shallow and bad written. 1/10Is it stable?- almost, there are a few bugs but, until now, nothing that renders the game unplayable for me. 6/10What about the equipments? Drops? Leveling?- the leveling is really balanced imho, I could feel my character getting stronger and the equipments drops followed up correctly, could be much more variety of legendary and set items, but the drop rate (in Ridiculous diff) are OK, the bad part is that you cant trade. 8/10Can you make a unique/smart build?- not really, every skill are balanced to the point where you dont need much combo, the combos are not much worth it, you can just spam your main AoE skill and you are good to go, a few skills colaborate with each other but not too much relevant and single targeted frenzyed builds are useless, and you cant customize your attributes/talents either, just skills and equipments, the Legendarium system are OK, but dont contribute against the overall system's simplicity. 4/10Overall rating- tl;dr: 6/10It is good and fun to play if you just want to pass time and dont give a sht about what torchlight was like, neither story-wise nor mechanics. Previous torchlight games was very slow paced and boring at some points, where Torchlight 3 excels imho, because the gameplay is very fluid and fast, I like it. You can finish the game quick, but you also die quick so thats a plus for me, specially because I love hardcore diff in any ARPG. Still they could improve it a lot, the game could be much more customizable, I love weirdo builds I can make in Path of Exile, Grim Dawn, Titan Quests, even at Diablo 2 I could fiddle with a mix or two of different exotic builds, but TL 3 character progression are so simplistic that you have basically the same gameplay with a range of classes and builds, but the current system gives you a bit of freedom for combining equipments with certain skills.Well thats my personal review, this game have TOO MUCH potential, but I dont think the current devs would make any effort on it. The Torchlight title may be dead on the second iteration, and TL 3 just started something based on that, but far different. _childDocuments_.review: Level 23 conductor max difficulty, experience so far.This review is a recommendation but a tentative one. There are some serious quality of life fixes that need to be looked at. Tutorials are far and few in-between and when u do get one they are still pretty meh. The skill points system is possibly the biggest let down, partly because it has a fun little twist which makes it kind of interesting as well. It wants you to explore the talents but then has a really bogged down system of doing so. It hovers somewhere between POE and Diablo. With the leveling being a real grind. You can't reroll like in poe and you can't spec around like Diablo. I think they know this is an issue because you can get respecticles, which are respec points. However they don't drop often enough to spec around and get a feel for the talents. I still think this is a decent game, it has a real charm about it and in terms of game play. Its fluid and has a great feel.  I have been playing a lot and plan on continuing to do so. In spite of its many flaws, its fun. This game like torchlight 1 and 2. Will be make or break on its mod support. For roughly 20 quid its a good deal, at 30 which is what the price will be a few weeks. Not so much. There is a lot polish that needs to be done and systems need to be looked at. However I think they have a great little niche for them selves and provided they invest the time into this game. At 30 it could be a real contender for that 2nd place spot behind POE.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - The final product aspired by Torchlight 3 wouldn't be impressive in 2010, let alone 2020. Save your money and stick to Torchlight 2.As a big fan of Torchlight 1 & 2, I am disappointed to say I don't see this game ever coming together to be a good product. This isn't a "It's in Early Access and it's not *currently* fun!" This is a "Looking at what's laid out to be the final product, the final product is severely lacking."There are only 4 classes, which is an increase from previous games, but the skills laid out in the game are extremely sparse. The gear on offer isn't class locked, which is good, but there's not a lot of different types of equipment. The builds diversities just aren't going to be healthy and interesting in a year. The weapons and movement skills are varied but there isn't enough room to try new things after two or three builds with each class. If you compare it to a product like Path of Exile, you have more diversity there right now, and will have even more diversity in the future because PoE is simply more flexible than Torchlight 3 is. Torchlight 3 has a set plan and it isn't going to be able to be grown easily from the plan.And that's... sad. I had high hopes. I guess the switch from MMO to traditional hacknslash looter wasted their development time and development dollars, and this is the best they've got.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the worst RPG's I ever played.And saying that about Torchlight really hurts, because Torchlight 2 is my favorite RPG ever.I know the game has switched hands, and had a troubled launch being focused as a MMORPG, and now that model is still cursing the game because it was entirely built upon, but you can't make a game this bad by mistake.Believe on all the negative reviews, because as I said, Torchlight is my favorite RPG, and I'm disappointed and disgusted by this game.So I'm gonna list all the sh!t the game has, so you can avoid it right away:- Level cap is 60, that means you can barely max out some of the skills. I remember reaching level 100 on Torchlight 2 and feeling powerful. Now that sense of completion in this game is gone.- So, when you reach the endgame, what's there for you? Nothing.Just some stupid maps that goes I don't know how long because I only had the patience to reach 40.- You like being one-shot killed by enemies? Because some maps have elites that will insta kill you if they crit, even at full health. And if you are in one of those endgame maps, that means your progress will reset  some maps, and you gotta do all over again.- So you think it's just like the other games, and some random maps are fun?No! Because some of the maps are BUGGED/GLITCHED. Some maps requires you to collect some items, but you kill all the mobs and still missing the items to complete the mission. And this happens when you have to kill mobs too, because some of them just never appear. And once I had a boss not showing up, and a boss chest glitching up so I had to open a portal or I couldn't leave the stage.- Your pet bugs ALL THE F#$KING TIME.You enter a map, your pet is not there with you, so you have to go back to your fort, swap to another pet, and then back to the one you were using. This bug has been adressed looong ago, and they say it has been even fixed on a earlier patch, but that is a LIE!- Quests are all the same: Go to that place > Kill This guy > Repeat.I never seen a so meaningless RPG like this one, so short and with a boring story. Three cities, with something like 10 NPC's total, not a single one have something good to say.- Talking about NPC's, you can't buy things like we used to, because you can only buy common pets, potions, and random items that never give a rare drop. So your money is wasted to, since you have nothing to buy.- And the thing that annoys me the most: Characters are tied to singleplayer or multiplayer only.That means the character you play on singleplayer CANNOT be use in multiplayer, and vice versa. I never seen this before, NEVER. If I want to play my level 60 character on both modes, well it's my fu#$ing business. But they say it was to avoid exploit on multiplayer, where you would be overpowered. You know why? Because it's how MMORPG's are built and that was what they intended since the beginning. It's like Shadow of War, when you reach the endgame and it's you agains't hordes of orcs that kill your captains, so you would have to BUY more from the cash shop.Resuming, this is NOT Torchlight.This would be a cashgrab, but the negative feedback they received during the public test have they changing their minds, but too late to erase all the bad decisions that were implemented into the game already.I rather play Torchlight 2 a 1000 times more than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I would rather not give it a recommended/not recommended but since I had to choose, I'm going with: [Not Recommended]. Someone asked why people don't like this game and I think my response to that question will serve quite well as a review for this game, so it is as follows:------------------------TL3 was originally developed under the name "TorchLight Frontiers" and was intended to be a F2P loot-grinder ARPG in the space of Path of Exile but from the very beginning, it was fairly clear that they had no actual idea how to make this work and eventually claimed the community had demanded they make TL-F into TL-3 and sell it as a B2P, a claim I am skeptical of. They tried to retool what there was of TL-F into a marketable product, and rebranded it TL3 and sold it with a $40 price-tag while it was still far from a complete game.It's fun for what it is in my opinion but I bought it knowing what I was walking into since I'd been following it for a long time but it's an unfinished F2P loot-grinder retooled into an attempt at a sequel to TL2 which I think was more out of a desire to get some returns on their mistakes and when that obviously did not work, they washed their hands of it and abandoned it.It's not hard to see why this disaster has left a lot of angry people in it's wake who were hoping either for a really fun, long-lasting seasonal online TorchLight or people who believed (somehow) that it was going to be a successor worthy of TL2.The confusion comes from not knowing what happened from it's initial announcement to it being a"finished product".More than anything else, I'm just disappointed.But worst of all is that with the devs having abandoned it, none of the bugs or issues with this game will ever be corrected, some of which make enjoying it fairly difficult (if you experience them, not everyone does).------------------------For what it's worth, I'm fine with the endgame mode it offers. It's nothing amazing but it's not bad, either. If you see this game on sale for like $10 or something and have read and understand what I said here about what it is, then I would say it's worth getting it at that price.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought torchlight 3 despite the reviews, I figured it might just be the super hardcore fan base a bit disappointed in a sequel that didn't live up to the crazy high bar it's predecessor set, I thought it might be a bit more scaled back but ultimately still a fun arpg, I was wrong. Not terrible but certainly very lacking, torchlight 3 isn't just a bad follow up, it's a bad arpg. On the surface it seems pretty good, it has good graphics and what seem like good systems on top of some interesting classes, you get pets by default and all in all it seems it could be a winner.What follows is a painfully shallow experience which has remnants of what this game was meant to be, an mmorpg. The devs listened to fan backlash at that premise and morphed what they had as an mmorpg into what we know as torchlight 3 and the damage shows.The issues go further than that though. It's short, had a bad campaign with very few interesting areas or enemies. Skills are too simple and gear isn't varied enough. Endgame is there but it's so uninteresting I couldn't force myself to engage with it much.I can see some merit in this game however, I got it for £6 and if you're desperate for some arpg content it'll do for a day as you blast through it but this isn't your 1000 hour time sink, that would be torchlight 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I have played only a little bit of TL2 so i'm not really sure how exactly this installment compares to the others.The character progression in this game seems to be lacking quite a bit. Although i'm only level 12, I can be in a level 9 area and it will still take me 2 actual minutes to kill a unique or legendary monster. Yes, i'm on "Ridiculous" difficulty, but the only thing ridiculous about it is that no matter what gear you get, you see very little improvement in damage. This difficulty isn't difficult. Some people may think "well if it's taking you longer to kill enemies doesn't that technically make it more difficult?" Well, yes, and no. Yes being that it is difficult to want to keep playing. No being that the enemies you fight aren't difficult to fight, their health pools are just massive. It seems to be that the character progression scaling is far too linear and doesn't feel impactful at all. It almost feels like you're playing the game for no reason. I suppose there is a reason if you're heavily into lore and whatnot, but to me I like feeling my character become more powerful, and I don't mean like end-game Path of Exile powerful, but just powerful in the sense that I can kill enemies with a little bit more ease, and with some challenge (again, a massive health pool is not a challenge).The only reason why I would recommend this game is if you genuinely just enjoy ARPGs in general. I didn't really mind the rough launch, I'm just hoping that they change this game a bit when it comes out of EA (or even while it's still in EA since games tend to stay in EA for 3+ years).

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so this is less of a review and more of a preview because this is written during early access. I love the Torchlight games! The graphics are cute, the upgrades small but constant, the powers are fun, and the core gameplay is satisfying. It's an isometric game like Diablo, and the setting is pretty neat too. (They do a good job of mixing traditional fantasy tropes with more modern ones like a clockwork robot and shotgunnes.) The story? I think it will be good when it comes out, and this sequel includes a neat personal "fort" where you can decorate and build upgrades. That's a nice touch because it's so different from the typical gameplay. Combat is good with one notable exception: The clicking. If you click on an enemy, you attack it. But if you click just outside the enemy (which happens all the time given their tiny size), you MOVE there instead of attacking. I've lost a few fights because, instead of snipping from a distance, my character casually walked through the firefight to stand next to the enemy. Still, that's a minor quibble because you can hold down the SHIFT key to stay put no matter what. And again, all the little details like goblin noises really make the game shine. One other problem that I believe will be fixed by the time it's released: The area maps reset whenever you log off. If you explored the entire level yesterday, all of that is gone by today and you have to explore again. Overall, I have a great feeling about this game and I'm excited to see the final version!

_childDocuments_.review: as of 06.01.2021 - Main story Quests STILL bugged making you unable to progress same with the Endgame Maps. Bosses dont spawn, you cant complete, you wasted 15-30 min in the game. Severe piece of Trash of a game. This game is so far behind in the standards of 2021 ARPGs aswell. You're better off with TL 1 or 2. TL:DRvery bad compared to Torchlight 1 + 2. feels like a mobile game at best. the current price should be lowered to 10,00 usd at MOST.Gameplay and Mechanics: Game feels extremely clunky, unpolished and full of bugs. I started my adventure as a Sharpshooter, and quickly realized how BAD the hitboxes are. When a monster is spawning like jumping out from a house/hut, Coming out of the ground etc, you'll quickly realize you'll need to wait for the whole animation.. then wait another second.. or two.. before you can actually hit the monsters, otherwise your damage is being ignored. I've tried/played with the Explosive Arrow skill as the sharpshooter, worked 25% of the time. <--- THIS is the general experience I've had with this game. Experienced it on all characters, with different skills. Forget about cancelling your animations, it's not possible. So if you decide to do a big volley of arrows at the boss and he decides to charge you.. well ♥♥♥♥.. for you. Takes away the fluent gameplay and that great feeling with control over your character. Some skills even sometimes activate 1 second AFTER you press the button, meaning if you're fighting and you EXPECT the skill to hit where you had your pointer, it might end elsewhere. this is not intended. Im on a 1000/1000 connection with 2 MS to my central. and a 5000 USD PC. so doubt its on my end. Loot, Gear and Customization: loot - Same boring ♥♥♥♥ will drop. Same legendaries. SAME SAME SAME. 30 hours almost in the game, finding same legendaries I found at level 7. Gear/Gearing - kinda answered with the same crap dropping. Customization: Nope. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to tackle this subject first! I think this is important for anyone and everyone who plays ARPG. I cannot understand how can this happen 2020. There's lots of comparison among PoE, Diablo etc. I'm here to give my review just for the game as it is, not biased towards any other but played those other ARPGames. So.. There is no trading. With no trading I mean: No trading among website, no trading in 2h after drop, no trading with friends who have been on your list more than 7 days, no trading among party members. No trading any type of form. This was the real killer. We started to play co-op with friend and you choose this relic in beginning. It's locked and gives active and passive skills. With locked = you cannot respec and choose other relic. Relic is part of your class. My friend got sword that gives stuff for fire relic. He was playing with poison relic and cannot respec so it was just plain useless for him. I actually had fire relic. We couldn't find the trade option so I googled and it turns out that there is no trading of any sort. The game is out of Early Access now... its supposed to be finished product. And no trading even among party members? YIKES! So my friend vendored it as useless item.I did only play 1,4h but I can still say something. The character creation is there. I play dusk mage and the options were small and quite horrifying, some of the faces. Imo 2/4 female faces looked like male. They should've given more details. Don't need to be many options but details!You can see legendaries from the list of legendarium. So basically you can browse legendaries suited for you that are in the game. Imo it was quite straightline and basic. Also quite few legendaries. We also kept getting the same legendary drops constantly with my friend. Same helmet etc. I think the legendary library can grow in time but it's fully released game, not early access.. and costs 34€. Yikes!All and all it felt like 15€ arcade game. From reviews online I understood its not even that long and endgame variety is very minimal. It should be 15€ arcade game and I could recommend it. Place it in same category as Gauntlet for example. With all the knowledge I know about the endgame, checking now the game a bit by myself... the trading killed it for me. I was one of those "maybe this could be worth the money and something small fun and change" but nah.. it's definitely not worth the 34€. With friend especially not because you cannot trade so it kinda kills the interaction on loot part (you still get your own loot and other players cannot see the loot in ground). So yes, it's refund from me.If you really really want to play this game, wait for sale at least. Feels still like Early Access but I guess live service is 2020 for early access but not really.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is impossibly buggy, Multiplayer feels like it was thrown in as an afterthought and had next to no time put into its development. Map and levels do not load properly, and connection to your party is spotty at best.Features its predecessor had have been removed from the game, Dual Wielding for example. How do you have less features in a game that came out years after the original?In Torchlight 2, I was able to use the same character for multiplayer as I did in singleplayer. That is not possible here. If you wanted to grind a single player character and then hop over and play that character with some friends, you would be unable to do so. I will still give credit where it is due, the pet system seems drastically overhauled. Before you could give your pet a potion or something and it would morph into a different creature. But in T3 you unlock new pets as you adventure and they have different abilities that you can mix and match to make a truly unique companion. Props for that. If you haven't played T2 this game will probably give you some enjoyment. My wife has not played T2 and is enjoying our playthrough so far. If you have played a previous version however, you may be a little upset at the changes between the two games. Seriously, what's the reason for using a pistol if you can't dual wield? "uSe A sHiElD" Look if I wanted a subpar Captain America experience I'd play the Avengers game.I read a Dev response to someone who asked about the dual wielding, and they just said it took time to make all the animations for the attacks. But you did it in the last game, so there's really no excuse. TLDR Game is subpar but if you're new to the series you'll probably enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: In 2020 many are looking for a pleasant distraction to get them through the onslaught of meme worthy events that seem to have no end. An ARPG is a perfect fit and Torchlight III appeared at a great time. Unfortunately, this is a poorly slapped together, and incomplete game that still suffers from many issues that were present back in June 2020 when this game hit early access. Despite continued patching efforts over the last 4 months, lag and disconnects are still present during multiplayer. Skills that once worked are now broken due to patching. Basic things like damage over time do not work correctly in some cases. Then there is the endgame loop, which comes in the flavors of Contracts, Forts and Frazeer’s Dun’Djinn. This sounds like a lot, however, Contracts simply level up and unlock various rewards by playing the game like normal. There isn’t anything you’re actively doing. The passive event that it is makes it bland even when getting a great reward you’ve been looking forward to. I thoroughly enjoy building and designing in game and Forts would seem like the perfect distraction that would elevate this game, but sadly, it doesn’t. Like many aspects of Torchlight III, it feels like an afterthought or more like a remnant of an idea that was left in because is was “neat”. The Dun’Djinn is a 251 floor challenge dungeon that is essentially Mapworks from previous games, but with a twist. You can pick modifiers that can make the level you’re about to enter more difficult. The levels and bosses are from the campaign and the loot drop chance is tuned (currently) lower than in the campaign, which is simply poor design. On top of that, there is literally no reward system for completing any part of Dun’Djinn and for me, simply having bragging rights is not enough. I joined Early Access on day 1 and joined the Discord community immediately. It was refreshing to see the devs working so hard on the game and seemingly listening to what the community was saying. The devs did make some good changes, but like I said earlier, every patch would break things that were working and since it was early access, that was largely OK. But then they rushed to release, ham fisting a broken game into 1.0 status without the stability you’d expect from a game with the name Torchlight. Single player has suffered from losing characters and character progress. The devs are largely absent now only to occasionally pop in to say “something great is coming” but I just don’t believe them anymore. I had hope for this game, and it may turn out good as time goes on. Right now, this is still playing like an early access game that is broken and lacks the endgame loop that is needed to keep an ARPG floating.

_childDocuments_.review: Limited review, I played through the campaign on 1 character. Apparently only 16% of players make it that far so make of this what you will.On the plus side, the class design is rather good. I played as the Forged, a steam powered robot with a minigun in its chest. Has a resource system where you use an attack to build heat, use an ability to convert heat to steam, use an ability to spend steam. I used my minigun to build heat, an aoe explosion to convert to steam and a sniper shot to spend steam. As you can see I primarily used the Forged's ranged tree but there was another tree that was melee focused.Each class has two trees, not necessarily ranged vs melee for example the Dusk Mage has a light vs shadow tree. There are also relics that each class can choose as a third tree that they share. I chose the Electrode for some shock/attack speed abilities but there's also a fire, blood, poison and frost relic. You gain relic energy using the class' native abilities and once you spend relic energy on relic abilities there's a sort of ultimate relic ability available. With the electrode it was a huge attack speed buff.If attached to a better game, I'd have been interested in trying the Railmaster who has a traincar of turrets follow him about and the Cursed Captain who has a cursed pirate crew at her command and lots of gunpowder abilities. These are cool, unique arpg classes that have a lot of design flourishes to them. Now the downsides.-First this has little to do with Torchlight. Yes there are a few terms namedropped for flavour but were they not used you'd have no clue this was a Torchlight game.-The story is barebones and not very well written. Story may not be a deal breaker for you, it's not like the prior Torchlights were vastly intricate yarns. The plot is either delivered through quest descriptions, audio logs or cutscenes. The latter are just dialogue over drawn panels, some of which aren't even coloured which adds a sense of either laziness or minuscule budget. The last cutscene just has the narrator describe what's happening since there's no dialogue and it'd just be a slideshow of uncoloured sketches otherwise. As for badly written one of the act finales is to stop a minion of the big bad getting their hands on a (namedrop) ember, you defeat the minion and the cutscene has another minion stroll up and take the ember anyway; apparently we either forgot to take the ember with us when we left or conveniently ignored an easily defeatable minion walk up to the macguffin crucial to their plans take it and walk off.-The sound design was rather underwhelming. I remind you that I played a minigun robot, having a local kid make a 'Kchh' gun sound would have more impact that the TL3 sound. The sniper shot was comparable to the sound you make trying to blow a hair off your tongue. The music was ok.-This only occurred once but I had one dungeon that was the same map piece repeated 4 times. It was a short dungeon so it became apparent quickly. Entry, path leading to a circle with a path leading to a circle with a path leading to a circle with a path leading to a circle with a path to the exit.For it's own section here are some of the bugs of Torchlight 3. Is it unplayable? No, however there are enough to make it unpleasant. -Loot will drop through the floor or shoot through the ceiling to unreachability.-You will need to use the Force Move command as characters will stubbornly attack the air where an enemy/destructable item was long after it dies. -The world will 'reset' constantly, there seem to be fixed open world maps with several attached dungeons that the story missions take you into. Frequently after completing the dungeon the open map will repopulate the enemy closets (most enemies are spawned from monster closets) and the map will reshroud meaning that unless you memorised it you need to re-explore the same map over again for your next objective. -There are audiologs found in the world to give some extra story. These are frequently cut off for no reason. Some of these logs are found at fixed points which can be made available again by reloading the area, some are found in chests at random that have no such easy workaround.-Frequently my discovered waypoints became unavailable to teleport to when reloading the game.-The map showing the waypoints repeatedly had an issue where the icons would flicker frenziedly, they weren't 'un-discovered' as above just the icon was unclickable.-The pet's resistances seemed to be bugged, there are pet items that grant invulnerability to the area's element yet my pet would get oneshot frequently. Maybe a bug due to said item also have +resistance to the same element (yay rng) but that's a guess.If you absolutely must play every Torchlight game, if you are tempted by the admittedly cool classes, if you can ignore irritating but not gamebreaking bugs pick it up on sale. If you're looking for a polished arpg perhaps with a good story, shop elsewhere.
