_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - if you want an ARPG that makes you appreciate Diablo 3 and Blizzard's QA, then look no further.The game has bugs, lots of them still. Some are game-breaking, while most of the ones I've encountered are merely annoying, requiring restarting the game. If the game was better, I could forgive them. This needs work before I could recommend.The basic gameplay and level-design is very samey and boring, with a few of the TL spices thrown in for at least SOMEthing interesting. Phase beast portals come to mind, and the pet thing is cute. They at least did something good with Fame this time around (Contracts). Base-building is also surprisingly kind of fun, and probably better than PoE. Having said that, it's ridiculously easy to max out the 4 things that make building the base fun, and there's seemingly little depth to the other structures.Soundtrack is much more forgettable than past instalments of the franchise.Based on other reviews, it sounds like class design was at some point worse than it is now, which is a little bit sad to hear. There are some good ideas here - each class feels different in play, and each has a different mechanic to master, and they're all fun.I particularly enjoy the forged class heat-vent-steam cycle. Was much less thrilled by the dusk mage mechanics in play, but the concept is cool, and admittedly better as you level. The railmaster sounded completely stupid to me, but in play, it was actually a pretty fun and novel take on a "pet" class, though the tracks are a bit awkward, visually. The sharpshooter feels probably the least-polished of the bunch, with minimal depth to the ammo mechanic, but that could be appealing to some. My main issue with it is that the skills will only animate with a bow, and not use alternate animations if you've got a pistol or rifle, which seems like a huge oversight.As to the relic idea, where each class has two trees, but they all have a third choice to make from the same pool of options, I like the idea, but it too needs more work. Some of the choices just don't seem to integrate well with some of the classes, and the skill choices, at least in my play experience so far, seem only to waste points you could be spending on core class abilities, which seem more powerful, or at least synergistic. I think that's something that still needs to be worked on.The game is also kind of short, with only three acts of mostly-samey environments. This is something the other two games in the franchise did a MUCH better job of. Likewise, the NPCs are basically cardboard cutouts with nothing to make you care about them or their struggles at all. The plot is nothing new or special, but honestly, that's not why I would play an ARPG. The lore is much less exposed in this game than others in the series, so that feels weak as well.It's not a bad game overall, but there's nothing here that any number of other ARPGs don't do better, and it's just not worth the asking price in its current state (Dec 2020, Jan 2021). I will plow through the rest of the campaign, and probably call it quits until they make some major revisions, then try again and see. I will adjust my review accordingly.

With three skill trees (two per class + 1 for a chosen relic) per character. There are some meaningful skill choices you can make as you level up, to lean into the gameplay style you're wanting.Played Torchlight II a lot before this, and of the two, this one has more overall polish, albeit having some odd bugs here and there but nothing that's not resolved itself. I'd suggest playing it on hard difficulty the first time around as I've done. That way the threat level seems on par or at least similar to Diablo 3's default difficulty. If everything is a cakewalk as I expect normal and lower difficulties to be, I imagine it would be less interesting to play.The two games feel a little different. TL II has the workshop which is a huge plus, fingers crossed that eventually makes it to this release to. And seems more "open".While this one is more linear, which story so far, while not amazing or anything. Has been interesting enough to keep me engaged in between slaying hordes of enemies. With some interesting boss fights. Everything so far has been voice acted which is fun.ps. Keep an eye out for hidden recordings in the game world. Like a message in a bottle, books on stone pedestals etc.Overall, if you're looking for some casual fun, with a little story to relax over after a day of work. Interesting and unique character skills. Then this game might just be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Unplayable. Controls are confused, cause confusion, and make the experience unnecessarily frustrating. It feels like a mobile game slapped onto the PC platform. It's co-op in name only. There's virtually no way to interact with your fellow player and no in-game advantage even if it were possible. You may as well play separate sessions of the game. You can travel to new areas without your teammate. Each player must activate quests to progress to locked areas; otherwise, the player who doesn't cannot progress, while the player who does can progress, leaving the other player in the dust. You can't exchange gear. Powers are dumb and numerous with no tangible advantage for creatively combining them. It's a mind-numbing click-fest.Oh, and it's glitchy as hell. There is severe lag between host and co-op player, and the image of the co-op player is often very slow to update, not showing new gear or proper current location or action. It's such a mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of Torchlight 2, however Torchlight 3 really felt like a letdown. I will try to be constructive here. The game runs well, at least for me. There are some cool, truly unique classes and improvements upon TL2 such as a better skill refund system, as well as the Relics and the Legendary skills. They did away with the (subjectively) poorly designed gem system and permanent attribute system. I like that you can see other players in town. It's nice that you can adopt new exotic looking pets. But... they also removed... FISHING?? :( I was disappointed to find out that the game was a breeze on nightmare difficulty from start to finish, with boss fights that had the most basic mechanics and were over too soon. Unfortunately the enemies you face are not interesting at all. You are always overleveled and there are no secret areas, interactives, collectibles or side quests, so there is no reason to explore a zone (you're just going from A to B and back). The story felt like an uninspired recycle of the previous games. There are some issues with multiplayer too, such as loot taking 5-10 seconds to appear, and not being able to visit your own fort sometimes when you're not the party leader.

_childDocuments_.review: Torchlight 3 has some good ideas, but suffers from two immense flaws:1) Its base frame is that of a mobile game, as it was intended to be one in the first place;2) It is half-finished and many areas remain either unimplemented, or poorly done.Those two massive flaws overshadow all the good little bits you might find here and there. Honestly, the core gameplay could have been very fun and enjoyable if not for that.Those two flaws come from the fact the game was originally designed like a mobile game. Upon presenting the early versions of the game, the devs received a huge backlash (who'd have seen that coming?) and did a 180°, trying to fix that mess with the time and budget they had left, which wasn't much.So you now have a half-finished game, quickly hacked together, handicapped from the start by its mobile-game frame, with the quality you can expect from that.The main offenders being:* No modding support; a multiplayer character is stored on the servers. So the modding community was left at the door.* There was no story planned initially; one has been quickly hacked together after the 180° on the design, so there's basically nothing.* Maps turn repetitive very quickly - you're able to quickly identify the "base building tiles" of maps because there are so few of them. You'll be passing through the exact same area multiple times throughout the same map.* Combat is dull. There is no strategy outside of nuking the same packs of the same enemies over the same map tiles while avoiding the occasional one-shotting effects.* There is no endgame. There is no New Game+. You're stuck farming an endless dungeon, with repetitive maps and dull combat, for very, very low drop rates. From the end game at Lv46 to several dungeon checkpoints after Lv60 (which was easily as long as the main game), I changed 3 pieces of equipment, and saw less legendaries than through a single chapter of the main game.In other words, it's a boring repetitive slog, that tries to hook you in at the start by showing you plenty of loot, then turning the faucet down to a tiny drip once you reach the endgame. Who would have expected that from a mobile game ...As I'm writing this, the next "Torchlight" installment, Torchlight Infinite, has been announced, and the new IP owners have apparently learned from the lesson of Torchlight III because they're planning ... a full-on mobile game.Torchlight III can be an enjoyable small game, but the Torchlight license ended with Torchlight II. Anything after that just bears the name as an attempt to sell more units, but has long departed from the original ideas and design that had made Torchlight a jewel of its own.

_childDocuments_.review: You can see from my hours played that I gave TL3 more than a fair chance, and it has some good elements, but, unfortunately, for me, the bad outweighs the good.  The levels are dreary and claustrophobic.  The inability to map to M4 and M5 is inexcusable.  Mechanics that are annoying in MMOs (like watching a two-minute progress bar to craft basic items) are even more annoying in a single-player game.  Only the tiniest shred of TL2's charm can be found here.  The world is lifeless. Mobs respawn when you leave and return to a map (which isn't necessarily a bad thing) but the fog of war resets as well, which is a bad, stupid thing.  Levelling is painfully slow.  Levelling up has been dumbed down; there are no stats, only skill trees.  There's barely a story.  The game plays like a F2P MMO-lite cash-grab that changed horses midstream to be singleplayer/multiplayer, but kept all the MMO crud a gamer like me hates.  I encountered numerous bugs.  With ARPGs like Grim Dawn, Titan Quest, Path of Exile and others available, there is zero reason to play TL3.  I bought this game cheap on sale.  I don't feel I wasted my money, but it's certainly been a joyless waste of precious time.  The only good thing it did was inspire me to reinstall Torchlight 2.  I'd forgotten how much fun Torchlight 2 can be.

_childDocuments_.review: EA-Review:After playing through all 3 maps and 30 hours in. I am still having fun in this game. This arpg feels like a Diablo 3 contender. Its awesome that we get our own personal Fort to customize. I like the different pets you can find and bring on your adventures. Developers hit the nailed just perfect with the overall progression and stories pacing. Economy feels good too. Ember cores and respectables need a boost in drop rate or should be sold in stores for gold you collect in game. I always love when games have difficulty options to cater a wider player base. Bad Stuff: Been playing as a Dusk mage and the Digitus Grip is bugged. When you teleport to a new area of the map. This weapons does not trigger. Some areas need to be smooth out. Player characters sometimes get stuck on invisible floors. There are other bugs and glitches that need to be iron out. I manage to finish game in the state of EA. Servers sometime lags and disconnects player, this is a big problem. Adding peer to peer play would help ease up Torchlight server problems. Please developers and publishers don't add microtransaction to the game. This would ruin the game. Instead make expansion packs and/or add-ons.Add Stuff: We need side quest badly, maybe devs can add npcs that would move to your forts and give you daily side quest to do. We need one additional character in the full game and 1 more skill per character. So we can make versatile builds. We need a mini game in this game. Fishing would be cool. We could sell our catch or cook them for buffs that last 1hr or 2hr. You could also add to the maps. Dig spots that our friendly pets find for us. When we dig we could find from rare to legendary loot.Other than this Torchlight 3 is heading in the right direction and could be fully price at 40-50 bucks when game releases from Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: *edit* so after 40 hours and completing the 2 acts available. I really only have 2 things I did not enjoy about the game, first thing was your stats go down as you advance (alot) from start of act 2 to the last last zone/map you lose over 50% so it felt like you were being punished for advancing, this same factor goes with raising the difficulty. This brings me to the second thing. Playing on ridiculous (which I complete the game on) was challenging, however, I feel like the burst of damage from trash and elites needs to be toned down a bit, or the damage of the player need to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. My autoattacks in normal are 1500-3000 in ridiculous mode they are at time 1-5 or 10-30 at some points i did see it around 100-200 but even so I dont think for a mode where your one shot most of the time, you pretty much lose all your items every time you die cause not enough scrolls of unbinding drop. I guess the 3rd thing would be why have melee builds in your game, melee builds cant go any higher than normal mode cause of the damage output vs intake, not to mention there is no life on hit or anything like that and most of the survival abilities still in harder modes dont stop you from being 1 hit or burning to death in a second.My opinion so farThe game is alright, I am enjoying it. I havent had the serious issues others have had (knock on wood) I expected servers to be wonky so it doesnt bother me. The game plays smooth though, skills pop off when you press the button. I would advise playing on the hardest difficulty if you want to see more loot, however, the harder difficulties can be unforgiving when you die, what I mean by that is you lose alot of gear whether its equiped or in your inventory. if you dont have a movement ability dont try and pile the mobs up, sometimes you will get stuck in them and then burn to death cause you cant move (had this happen a few times) GFX are torchlight, cartoony but nice. The skill trees are small, hopefully they add more later. you get a legendary passive, there are some for all classes and then some that are locked to each class. There is the relic thing too which also comes with its own skill tree and it lvls while equiped. With that being said there is not a whole lot of diversity to builds but to me its enough. (this isnt POE) I would like to see more items, there are a bunch but more is always better. Forts are basically your housing, you can build stuff some of it is functional and some of it is just for looks. you feed the luck tree items to lvl it up and you get more luck for item drops, you can build a goblin statue which you feed embers that goblins drop and it give you fire resist. you can enchant items and dismantle items for mats, pretty much all the things. Overall for EA its fun and kills time, to me its just another ARPG that in time it will get better. Is it worth 30 bucks? idk I have paid more for less so its all personal preference. If you like torchlight or ARPG's in general its worth a go if you got 30 bucks.

This game is a disgrace to the series and the price is a straight money grab before people catch on. I tried to enjoy the game. I forced the most boring ARPG I've probably ever played. I just can't do it.The game loop along with many mechanics are bugged not working or I'll fitting to the game. Abilities aren't cohesive with each other and make little sense. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fun ARPG with a decent amount of variety in the gameplay and classes and, as a loot grinder style of ARPG, it's been a blast for me to play through it.  I'm on my first playthrough now as a Sharpshooter with just under 22 hours in it, and I'm about 2/3rds of the way through the campaign (hey, I take my time).  I suspect I'll play through a couple more times, which might bring my hours total on this to around 100 hours.  It depends on how different and yet fun the other classes are, which is TBD.  If you like ARPGs and have enjoyed Torchlight, FATE, PoE, or Diablo then I think this is an easy decision.

_childDocuments_.review: I played a Dusk Mage in Normal difficulty. My character is now level 14 and Im at the very end of the first of 3 'maps'. My biggest problem is that respec'ing a skill is to difficult. I spent points on skills just to try them out, to see how they worked and how they felt. Huge mistake. I only got 3 respec points so far in the game. My second complaint is about the absurd difficulty. The boss I am on right now, Braal, launches these pools of slowness, which also launch projectiles at you, all over the combat area. I got hit more by these pools than her. These battles last SOOOOO long. Like 10 minutes or longer and usually end because you run out of healing pots. That wouldnt be so bad if you were in a party, but forming a party is not a simple task. There is no way to set yourself up as LFG and get added to a group. You have to beg in chat and usually no one responds. I did get help once. They need to automate party making badly. I would have loved to have run around with a group of people doing content, but its just not a thing, even though you are forced to play in multiplayer mode because single player mode isnt ready yet. I have read about the fact that relics now share the same skill point pool. I didnt hit a problem with that as I quit playing before that was a problem, but its there and would have been a problem. Many videos I have watched about builds after the relic change show how much of an impact it has on builds. There is a SERIOUS balancing problem in that regard.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 6/21/21They have fixed most of the bugs. The map still resets and randomizes every time I go to town/ phase portal and come back so that's annoying. But most of the other issues have been addressed. I'm still disappointed that they would leave so many bugs way after release. I can now say that I recommend the game. But honestly I'd wait until it's on sale. 3/1/2021 DO NOT BUY IF YOU HAVE ANY INTEREST IN PLAYING THE COMPLETED VERSION - because this game is NOT complete!!! I've never played a game SOOOO BUGGY. And from what I've been reading online, these bugs have been there since the game was in early access. SHAME on the company and how lazy and greedy they are to sell a game for $40 knowing it is incomplete. So many bugs... Empty boss chests, animations and sounds that don't stop (like after chopping down a tree) even after the action is completed, weapons that don't work or work intermittently, making a portal out of an area and when you use it to get back the entire map is reset, waypoints that reset themselves...and the list goes on.  The most annoying bug is the one that doesn't complete a tutorial quest that leads to being able to build an enchanting station. So 5hrs in I discovered this bug and couldn't get a refund because it'd been more than 2hrs. Can you just make a new character? NO it doesn't fix the bug. The bug exists in every single character preventing me from EVER being able to build an enchanting station on any character. I can't believe (A) with a game ruining bug like that I can't get my money back and (B) Steam would even sell a game with so many bugs. I continue to play because I spent $40 and I'm not letting that go to waste and I'm HOPING that they fix the bug one day.My husband who plays on his own computer has experienced all these same bugs so I know it's not just me. Torchlight 2 was an amazing game but Torchlight 3 sucks. Don't be like me and buy 3 just because 2 was so awesome. You have been warned!

_childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS REVIEW: Disclaimer, everything I am saying now is subject to change as development on this game progresses.Update (6/26 - 50 hours played): I wanted to update my review to be a little more timely and also now that there is more time played under my belt. I'm leaving my original review below as it still holds true.First of all, I still recommend this game to anyone who is okay with bumps and glitches as part of the normal Early Access experience. If you want a finished game that plays smoothly DO NOT BUY THIS GAME NOW. Wait. A frustratingly high number of negative reviews address things that are just part of the Early Access experience. Over the past few weeks, I've spent a large amount of time reading the Discord and interacting with developers and honestly a lot of things people are unhappy with are being fixed/removed/adjusted as a result of player feedback.Again, this is how Early Access is ideally supposed to work. The game is unfinished, but player feedback helps shape the game through development. As far as Early Access titles I have seen on Steam go, the developers have been incredibly responsive and the game plays solidly well. Yes there are bugs, but the majority of my 50 hours played at this point have been fun and free of issue. The game is enjoyable and the roadmap and the changes we've seen already just say it's going to get better.The disconnects that led to rating bombing in the first 36 hours have largely ended. Offline play is still on the way for launch, and won't be an issue at that time.I cannot state this enough, the game is in development. While I feel it plays like more of a complete game than most Early Access titles, if you buy this expecting it to be perfect and finished and get frustrated when you run into bugs, do not buy this game now.But if you can handle playing for several hours, running into a bug, and then reporting it to the developers rather than leaving a negative review and refunding the game, then this is a very fun game for your money. I can tell you that if you have read a lot of the negative reviews here, you'll be surprised when you actually play it how little those things come up. We're going to be getting a big patch in a few days to address many of the issues people are still having and we'll also be seeing the addition of Act III to the game.If you're interested in this game, try it. I've been enjoying it tremendously over the past few weeks since it launched and it just keeps getting better.Original Review:Normally, when I see that a game is "Mostly Negative" I skip over it. Or at the very least, decide to wait and see how things go further down the road. However, giving my history of enjoying Torchlight games and the long wait and hype I felt for this one, I decided to give it a try.Off the bat I want to address two things that I am seeing in a LOT of negative reviews:1. "The servers won't connect!" - Yes, at the time of this writing (one day after release on early access) server issues are very much a thing. I was able to connect and play for a good chunk of time, only the be disconnected again. I've played enough online games though to say I know this isn't going to persist. These kinds of connection issues plague EVERY new game that launches. I'm not at all worried that these will continue beyond a few days. For those worried this will persist in the long run, I want to also point out that offline single player is coming soon. Since this is early access, only multiplayer is available at the moment.2. "It plays like a mobile game" - I don't get this at all. It plays like Torchlight. Have you played Torchlight? It plays like that. The only thing I can imagine sparks this criticism is that people are upset that it lacks the depth of Path of Exile (it does, but to be fair, so does everything) and it lacks the polish of full releases (Again, it's Early Access). But considering it's in Early access, the game plays very well.My recommendation comes down to this:Do you want to play Torchlight III? Are you ok with Early Access hiccups in exchange for getting to play the game as it develops? Then this is worth your money. The game is there and it's a lot of fun.Do you want a polished, finished game that works 100% of the time and has everything out of the box? Then maybe wait on this one. Early Access has a flag on it for a reason. This is not a finished game. This is not a perfect game. But the bones are there, and the potential is there. Come back in a few months or a year and I'm sure you'll like what you see.All in all, I recommend this game. I suggest deciding which of the two players you are that I mentioned above before buying. It's bumpy right now a day after release. But don't fall for the rating bombing. The game has potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Torchlight 3 in early access is great to find out.  Writing this and finding out that this game is being developed/fixed.  This is a must buy.  If you played Torchlight 1 and 2.  Torchlight 3 will bring a lot of new things for this genre.  You get relics that act like a skill, but it has a lot of passives once activated.  There are 5 different relic elements that will adjust your gameplay experience.  There is a new thing called legendarium, when you disenchant a legendary you can use the passive on that legendary in 3 different legendarium slots.  You get a fort that you can customize.  Get extra buffs from the fort buildings, such as gold find, gear luck %, and stat defence against certain elements.  Plus the new kinds of characters that they offer are all unique in their own way.Before purchasing you should only think about if you want to support this game in the long run.  It is in early access and is in the processes of fixing bugs/server issues/missing cutscenes.  But whatever the company had planned in the past is in the past and it is great that this game is going back to the roots of how it got itself in the ARPG.To add what I mentioned.  I replayed Torchlight 2 and found more differences / similarities / changes.-You won't see are added stat points where we had to choose where to place our stats for Torchlight 3.-Fishing isn't a thing in Torchlight 3, but I'm ok with that.  It was only a cosmetic / skill for the pet.-Torchlight 3 feels like it has more macroing than in Torchlight 2.-Torchlight 2 monsters feel like a sponge.  Torchlight 3 has that sponge feeling but is a little more challenging if you have to dodge their attacks.-Torchlight 3 offers challenging bosses with different boss stages based on the health and macroing of your character.-Skills are totally different.  Torchlight 2 has 3 different trees with a total of 20 skills and 10 passives.  Torchlight 3 brings in a new taste of skills and relic combinations.That is all for now.  I would still suggest Torchlight 3.I would suggest changing all the skills and keys around WASD(movement keys).  It really changes the experience of the game for me.  I use the mouse to aim and the space bar to attack.  The skill buttons i use is q, e, f, z, x, c, v, and i moved the skills to g.  My potion is now 2 and my portal is now 3.  1 is still my primary skill but probably i'll shift the keys around till i find a happy medium.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright congratulations, you have annoyed me enough to get my first steam review.This game is so buggy for such a big name title. I don't really know if I want to keep playing at this rate.- I almost never see the real time position of my party member, even though I know he should be right there in front of me.- Sometimes on my screen he's standing in a corner, when mobs are dying on the other side of the screen where he is actually fighting- One time he's standing besides me on my screen before the boss portal when I could also see the boss fight below has already started- Loot appears in locations not where the mobs die - another clear sign the game doesn't properly recognize where we are- My luck tree loses the last level and reverts back to beginning of level 4 whenever I refresh my fort (I've just stopped feeding it, what's the point?)- I randomly die in fights from full health to 0 when there are no apparent attacks, circles or fire on the ground etc.  (I assume there is something there but I just can't see it.)- After the game crashed once, I logged in supposedly in town but the entire screen is a light blue cloud. I couldn't move and restarting the game did not help. It's like stuck falling off the map. Luckily I was still able to teleport to my fort, then it returned to normal.- In one of the challenge maps, we literally cleared the entire map twice and it did not trigger the boss zone. First time, the game crashed just as the map was mostly cleared (leading to the above blue screen). Second time, after killing everything we ran around for a while thinking we missed something, but after circling through the empty map multiple times, it became clear it was bugged.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's preface this by saying I am a huge fan of the original Mafia 2. I've played the story countless times. So when the remaster rolled in, i had to relive Vito's inconveniences once again.I had a blast playing; the jokes in the game are top notch, driving is fun and damn, even the random deaths you get on hard difficulty made me giggle. But did anything actually change from the 2010 game we know? Original game came out a little bit rushed and gutted. In my opinion, it's an insult to call this a "remaster", since so much content was ditched for sake of faster release date, and all we get 10 years later is a glorified graphics mod, with the same bugs still in place. They had the opportunity to make this great game even better; half of the work was already done anyways. but they've chosen to go the greedy path once again, patting themselves for a great job while doing a work comparable to a Skyrim mod. So yes, I did enjoy this game, but that's because it was already great. Hangar 13 makes me very worried about the future of the Mafia series; and based on their work on this, and the botched third game; oh boy, it looks fairly grim.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 2 a game I hold near and dear to my heart, I personally hail it as one of the best narrative driven stories, while linear it is still a game that holds up to this day and is much better than the mess that is Mafia 3, now that I am done tooting the horn of Mafia 2 I will talk about the changes to the game from it's classic edition to now. Mafia 2 Definitive Edition definitely has some problems, more so on console to my knowledge but this isn't about the console port this is about the PC version.The remaster problem: The graphics on some characters look gorgeous, Joe, Henry, Vito and the other big players within Empire Bay look nothing short of amazing as with some of the set pieces as well looking beautiful however there is a drawback with this in which not everyone in Empire Bay got the special treatment and thus they still look about the same as they do in Mafia 2, for a remaster this isn't a very good thing however as someone who has played through Mafia 2 many times it was a slight annoyance to see a bunch of NPC's look like they do and have Vito look great. A lot of Empire Bay also is very beautiful to look at you can tell there was definitely some passion put behind remastering the game however sadly some of the passion was put into one area and ignored in another.The story: Mafia 2 follows the story of Vittorio Antonio "Vito" Scaletta born in Sicily in 1925, his parents moved him and his sister to America to start a new life, in 1943 he was arrested during a heist with his buddy Joe and given a choice, go to prison or fight in World War 2, after returning from the war in 1945 he meets back up with Joe who gets him out of the service and working with him, Vito after finding out the debt his family has sets out for a life of crime with Joe in order to pay back his family and himself so as to never make the same mistakes his father did. This is just a basic synopsis I wrote up for the start of the game's plot, the story of Mafia 2 while a bit cliche holds up extraordinarily well telling an emotional story of a man who originally set out to help his own family ended up becoming deeply involved in the Mafia life.The gameplay: Mafia 2 Definitive Edtion's gameplay is the same as it is in Mafia 2, some people call it outdated which is true as it's still the same as it was in 2010, a little clunky but I think it holds up quite well. Each gun brings something a little different, the 1911 is the perfect all rounder handgun to use, the .38 is the weakest of the bunch but fires quite fast, the c96 boasts the most bullets out of all of them and the magnum is the strongest, the shotgun is one of the best weapons for close to medium levels of combat and the Thompson M1A1 is a great all rounder machine gun only rivalled by it's big brother the Thompson 1928, there are other guns that can fill in different roles for each scenario so it is fun to experiment and see which one will suit you best, however keep in mind that some of these guns you won't be able to come by very early on in the game with the exception of Chapter 1 when you are fighting in World War 2. The driving hasn't seen much change either, don't speed around the city otherwise you will be chased by cops unless you know the car you are using will outrun the any day.Glitches that I know of: currently with Mafia 2 Definitive Edition I know of a few glitches in the game, one of them being a texture glitch with some litter on the ground having broken textures and I believe I am the only one who has encountered  this glitch so far but in the cutscenes for the end of Chapter 10 and part of the cutscenes in Chapter 11 would abruptly end before they were supposed to, these don't affect me too much as I have already finished the game many times however these can be a massive problem for players who are just starting out in the game, if this was just something that happened to me then it is okay but hopefully if it does happen to others it will be patched out soon, the last glitch is just a goofy one in which during cutscenes Vito's head would clip through his hat or his hat would clip through his head, it was funny to see that happen from time to time but it should be patched out somewhat soon so as not to take anyone out of the cutscenes. The only other problem I noticed with the game is that during the main story pretty much every coat that should have physics with it would just stick to Vito, there appears to be a mod that patches this out already so use that if you want while we wait for it to be patched out, this problem does not occur in the DLC though for some reason.In conclusion Mafia 2 Definitive Edition is what many would consider a true remaster, it updates the games visuals and makes it playable on next gen consoles, this is a pretty good PC remaster but a horrendous one on console according to the problems it has, my advice would be to pick this game up if you are interested in an old school Mafia story or get the bundle to get them all, however you need to make your voice be heard if you are encountering glitches to 2k or through reviews to get them patched out.

_childDocuments_.review: Tricky review but I'll keep it short and to the point.Pros:- AMAZING and memorable main character and side character.- BEAUTIFUL music if there was a soundtrack it would be worth every penny. - Artwork and game setting/time periods are BREATH TAKING.- Remastered graphics are GORGEOUS from a wide shot view.- GREAT and somewhat "realistic" driving experience (police will tag you for hitting cars/speeding). - Story is good (Game is told in chapters which is INTERESTING).- Ending will leave you with your mouth open and wanting more.Cons:- A LOT of driving (like seriously. A LOT).- Save points are via chapter beginnings and hidden playboy magazine pickups (if you die you may start from the beginning of the chapter).- A LOT of names you may have to keep up with to fully understand the story.- Zoomed in faces during cut scenes have terrible eyes o_O.- Combat is simple, repetitive and dated (think of a less polished and simple cover shooter).Finished the game on the hardest difficulty. I would still recommend Mafia 2 100% but remind them it is a game from 2010 and the remastered edition are just graphical improvements NOT gameplay improvements. All in all this is the perfect game for people who are fans of GTA but prefer a smaller city landscape without the overwhelming side missions and is strictly story focused on it's characters.

_childDocuments_.review: After reading up all of the negative press this remaster got, I was expecting a smelly, hot piece of garbage to be delivered to my library on the silver plate. However, after actually playing it myself, it seems that most of the stuff people are bashing this game for is not entirely true. I encountered few bugs, sure, such as weird light flickering on the skyscrapers at night, a glitchy grass near Joe's place, and during the  , one of the characters had a particularly bad case of the Mondays (his face was smudged around the whole screen for like a second or two, which was really funny I might add). Oh, and Leo had a weird eyes fixated to his left  Other than that, no bugs and no issues.Graphics is really good and improved: characters, details, roads, cars everything (well, almost) had a facelift. I played classic mafia 2 after that just to compare and it was really evident how blurry classic mafia 2 is. DE version is much cleaner and also gets rid of the annoying yellowish piss filters the classic version has, game really looks better without it. I don't see why people hate this remaster so much, maybe they need to take off their nostalgia goggles sometimes. The only really negative side of this version compared to the classic is the file size. OH MY GOD, 44 GB?! I know that most of it is 4K textures but still, its quite big if you consider that the original Mafia 2 (classic) is like 8 GB or so. Well thank  Pappalardo this game did not get the Warzone syndrom. If you don't have the disk space, I suggest you get the classic Mafia 2, which is included in this purchase anyway, and play it to your heart's content. But since you get both versions, give them each a try and see what you prefer more.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II holds a special place in my heart and is my favourite in the series. I absolutely loved the story, and the characters are so memorable that even now, years later, I still randomly recall their dialogues. I first played the game during my school days, and it made such an impact that I often think back on it.For fans of single-player story-driven games, Mafia II is a must-play. You’ll have an amazing time with it. The music is wonderfully nostalgic—some of the tracks still linger in my memory even today. The atmosphere of this game is also breathtaking. Without a doubt, this game ranks among my top 3 games of all time.A Bit of Backstory (Feel free to skip)Back when I was in school, my computer wasn’t powerful enough to run Mafia II. I remember when it was released, my friend and I would talk about nothing else. While my friend had a decent PC and was able to play the game. He would come over and describe scenes and gameplay elements (thankfully, without spoilers), and to me, it all felt like a fairy tale.Eventually, I got a better PC and finally got the chance to play it myself. Those were truly unforgettable days, and it’s one of the reasons this game remains so close to my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard the Mafia trilogy is being remade, remastered and repackaged will all its DLCs, I couldn’t have been more happier. The quite disappointing third entry in the series left a sour taste in mouths of many players so it seems only right to go back to the roots. The first Mafia is getting a full remake and while we wait for it, why not kill some time with the remastered version of Mafia II.The following review will be cut into two parts. First, I will talk about the remaster itself and the differences from the original. This is intended for players who are already well familiar with Mafia II. The other parts are for newcomers. I will be talking about the story (spoiler-free) and core gameplay. Without further ado, let’s dive into this gangster classic.Mafia II: Definitive Edition wasn’t remastered by Hangar 13 or 2K Czech, the work was outsourced to a third-party studio called d3t. If you previously never heard of them, join the club. Their most recent work, apart from remastering Mafia II, was porting Shenmue I and II to modern platforms. I have to give credit where it’s due. Porting a 20 years old game is certainly a feat. Although, from what I‘ve heard and seen, not a lot of work has gone into texture quality, character models and geometry, making the ports still look outdated in comparison. So, how did they do with Mafia II: Definitive Edition?Let’s start by saying you will be disappointed if you expect a huge upgrade to the visuals. It’s a remaster after all, not a remake. However, in terms of remasters, I have certainly seen better. While Definitive Edition did fix well-known bugs from the original, it brought bugs of its own like some character’s eyes not moving, game randomly going to slow motion, an achievement not popping up, coats not reacting to physics etc. A recent patch was meant to fix most of these problems, however, the patch notes do not even specify what has been fixed and not. After coming back to the game, I can confirm stuff like stiff eyes is still present.While the overall look of Definitive Edition isn’t a giant leap compared to its predecessor, the graphical upgrades are more noticable during the summer section. Higher contrast makes the entire city a joy to revisit with greater detail on cars, passers-by, billboards, shop signs etc. The city also feels more livelier with more NPCs and cars roaming the streets. Important story characters have also undergone a makeover with Vito getting the spotlight. Vito’s hair looks much more realistic, his scars and wrinkles are more detailed and new facial expressions bring his character to life. However, the same can’t be said about some minor characters you get to interact with. It’s particularly distracting when Vito‘s 2020 look speaks to a character from a PS3 era.Sadly to say, Definitive Edition doesn’t provide any new gameplay options either, apart from adding 30 new collectible wanted posters. If you own Mafia III: Definitive Edition, you get Lincoln’s Samson Drifter and combat jacket. If you pre-ordered Definitive Edition of the first Mafia, you will get Tommy’s taxi as well as a new outfit. Unfortunately, the list of changes ends here so if you were expecting new side quests and free time activities in Empire Bay, you will be disappointed.The Mafia franchise has always been known for its gripping story with many twists and turns, not afraid to show brutal, unfiltered imagery. In Mafia II, you are Vito Scaletta, a young sicilian who emigrated with his family to the US. With no money to spare and lack of english, Vito soon finds himself working for the Italian mob. After a botched job, Vito enlists in the army to avoid prison and goes to fight Nazis in Italy. When he’s send back, Vito and his best friend Joe Barbaro work their way up to achieve the ultimate American dream. Although, not everything will be as smooth as they think it’s gonna be.Mafia II’s crime thriller takes inspiration from many famous mob movies including Goodfellas or The Godfather. Mafia II does a much better job at portraying the inner workings of Italian mobsters than Mafia III which focused more on racism and injustice of 1960’s America. The story is set in Empire Bay, 2K Czech’s interpretation of New York.  Empire Bay is easily one of the best open worlds to explore. Perhaps the city’s beauty came at a price of a lack of interesting side activities. While Empire Bay is undeniably pretty, it’s also eerily empty, devoid of any engaging stuff to do. In fact, you can hardly call Mafia II an open world game, since every chapter takes you on a linear journey from objective to objective.That is not to say that there is nothing to do besides main missions. Vito can get dressed in a number of period-apropriate suits, customise cars, buy weapons or hunt for collectibles. Mafia II suffers from a similiar problem early Assassin’s Creed games do – money is meaningless. You earn money from high risk jobs, so you go spend it on weapons, ammo and car repairs, so you can go on more jobs, so you get even more money, you get the picture. I wish Vito was able to buy safehouses, invest in stock, open his own pizzerias, bars, car dealerships and manage them. By the end of the game, I was flushed with money I didn’t know what to do with.Don’t expect a GTA mafia clone. Mafia II is kind of its own genre that doesn’t follow typical open world structures. What Mafia II lacks in gameplay opportunities, makes up in attention to detail.+ story+ setting+ attention to detail+ satisfying driving- weak remaster- empty open worldWhile it’s not a perfect remaster by any means, it’s hard not to consider purchase when you get the original Mafia II (now titled Mafia II Classic) + all DLCs and other bonus content for free.

_childDocuments_.review: Hold on ... the game is not bad.The game has an amazing story (excluding the end). Mission writing is equally good to the first mafia game. Gun-play is equally good, while the world's atmosphere albait a little stale, feels nice. The problem with this game, is it's gameplay. The way the story is laid out, makes you feel more like a taxi driver rather than mafia guy. From the 15-20 hours you are gonna need to finish the game, more than half of them you will spend them inside a car of yours, going from point A to point B. At this point, I think i can go to Joe's place with my eyes closed, from any point of the map. The game unfortunately doesn't offer a "teleport" option (like in Mafia I) either, in order to skip a few known and boring rides.And if that wasn't enough, the game has awful checkpoints as well. The developers have put very few checkpoints during missions, which is not necessarily bad, but they have put those few checkpoints at very awkward places as well. Meaning that if you die, you might need to re-drive back to the mission's location, re-watch (thankfully skippable) cut-scenes, and sit back during scripted portions of the missions. In general if you die during a heated mission, you usually have to waste a few minutes to go back to where you were.Additionally, I would like to talk about the game's "remastered" aspects. The game has a bunch of glitches, some of them that seem to have been transfered straight from Mafia II classic as well. Additionally, character graphic glitches are prevalent from time to time as well, breaking any immersion that you might had at the moment. In general, it's not a good "remastered" game. The developers treated this remaster as a cash-grab, since they just did a reshade, repacked the game with zero changes, and shipped it back as something new, which is totally a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lie.Finally, what the hell did they do to my boy ? The ending was pretty bad and inconclusive, leaving you with a cliff hanger, which is implied, but never going to be clearly laid out. Everybody can think for themselves what's gonna happen to both   and  . It's a linear game, therefore I would have liked a linear and straightforward ending as well.To conclude, playing this game is not going to be a very happy journey. Especially after the second half of the game, in which you are going to start getting frustrated more and more with some of the stupid game mechanics. Nevertheless, if you really really want some mafia dose in your system, make sure you have played Mafia I first, and then buy this (ON A SALE) as well.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 cannoli out of 5, honestly i'd rather fuggedaboutit! Cosmetically it looks great, it's been seriously overhauled in those terms. It might not be on par with other 2020 releases but overall its a vast improvement on the original. It honestly feels like all the effort (if any) that was put into this 'remaster' was cosmetic. From a technical stand point this game feels more dated than the classic.Mechanically it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, there are so many bugs and a few proper game breaking ones; twice I had to restart a whole chapter because I literally couldn't progress as a result of either guys not spawning in that I 'had' to kill or because NPC's dialogue wouldn't trigger.The AI is simultaneously the smartest and dumbest in existence. Enemies can blind fire from cover but you cant. They know when you are aiming at them so if you try and hold the angle till they peek they never will, that is if they don't kill you when you are about to peek. The peek animation for you is so slow that (combined with them clearly knowing you're about to peek) means they will literally peek out of cover like the road runner on speed while you are still in the middle of the animation and gun you down. Rather than duck behind cover while being shot at they will literally tank your bullets and shoot back at you which usually results in your death before theirs. Other times they will literally just rush you and 1. You can't shoot from cover without peeking, so in order to shoot the guy thats now broken past the defence line you need to stand up/out of cover in order to shoot him thus exposing your back to any other enemies 2. Shooting them a second time can sometimes interrupt their stagger animation so thus they can snap back to shooting you like they had a brief moment of alzheimers and forgot they were in a fire fight, except they remembered they were some sort of sniper elite James McAvoy type in war and shoot you with ridiculous accuracy even though their gun is facing the opposite direction.There is also a little Sam Fisher in them as you will often walk into a room with 0 indication that there are enemies hiding, walk past a box and get shot in the back by the guy hiding behind it, im not sure if they were already there or if the game is literally spawning enemies behind me. The destruction of cover is really cool looking with tiny little fragments of the wall you are hiding behind getting blown towards the camera, makes me feel like I'm saving private Ryan. It also means you become exposed to bullets the longer you hide behind cover. This would be cooler if the same thing applied to the AI. On several occasions I had blown their cover to ♥♥♥♥, can quite clearly see their head through it but shooting at it just sparks off like they are iron men!Playing on hard was more about repetition than anything, playing the time loop game of triggered sequences i.e. when a grenade will be thrown and counting how many enemies are in a room so i dont run into the issues above. In terms of story it's ok, not as great as i remember. Its very linear and most chapters are 1 'mission'. It gives the illusion of open world but really there is almost nothing else to do other than the story, the only time i every really explored the open world was to get collectables/other achievements. The characters are pretty flat in terms of personality, it seems like the are all rehearsing for the same background role in goodfellas 'Angry Italian American #2', I found myself constantly forgetting who any of the people were the main character kept referring to outside of Joe & Leo. Overall its ruined any nostalgia I had for Mafia 2 classic. Mostly becuase the mechanics feel dated which suggests they've just taken the coding from the original slapped some flex tape on it and called it a day. Although I could be wrong the original might be every bit as great as I remember but honestly I'm too lazy to find out. I think i got this free for owning the classic version, which is the way it should be. Buy the classic and get this puttanata free!TL;DR buy this if you enjoyed the original and it's going for somewhere around 5 bucks. Otherwise get the original its probably better

_childDocuments_.review: The creators were clearly intent on recreating the era’s details. Magazines strewn across tables, posters tacked to walls, the interiors of cramped apartments, the knock of police on a neighbor’s door. The music, the vintage car models—it’s all done with real care. But while the world is technically open, it feels flat, uninspired, and devoid of any true sense of discovery.The cinematic references to  and  are a cinephile’s delight. Vito and Joe are archetypal mafia movie characters, their personalities fitting neatly into established screen tropes. The narrative is fragmented, with each part following classic beats that aim for resonance.As for the missions, they’re rather dull and unoriginal, burdened by a sense of “development hell.” In one particular scene, during a bar shootout, I noticed a severe drop in fps—a shame, because that moment felt like the most authentic in the gameplay, only to be marred by optimization issues.For its time, it was a solid game, the kind of success a remaster is trying to revive. If you can get it on sale, it’s worth revisiting, if only to relive a period when we were less demanding of game mechanics, and more easily swept up by atmosphere and story.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I played Mafia Definitive Edition some time last year and had a good time. I had some time to burn and figured I may as well give Mafia II Definitive Edition a go too.I'm happy to announce that I'm enjoying it about as much as I enjoyed Mafia Definitive Edition. One of the reasons I generally dislike definitive/remastered versions of games is it is never apparent what was actually changed. I never played the original Mafia II so I've no idea how this stacks up to that, but from what I understand they mostly added bugs. I have, however, only stumbled upon one of these bugs so far and all I had to do to get around it was to backtrack a couple of steps to shoot some dudes in order to progress. Not too bad. A lot of reviewers also criticize the game for not utilizing the open world elements a lot, but to me this is not really an issue. It just means that the creators had focus and they knew where they wanted to spend their time. In this case, they had spent their time on making the story and the gameplay around it feel as fleshed out as possible. I think more open-world games should follow this approach. Having an open world is great, but do we really need the open world tower grind that were popularized by games like Assassin's Creed? Mafia II proves to me that you really don't. Focus on what makes the game good and spend less time on content for the sake of more content and I'll be a happy camper.Anyway, that's it from me. I can definitely recommend this game and I fully intend to finish the main story at least before putting it down.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mafia Trilogy has always been one of my favorites of all time in the open world genre, I was playing Mafia 1 before any other GTA, I've played through Mafia II countless times, the classic cars, the atmosphere, the cities, everything is beautiful, and in Mafia II's case the story is *chef’s kiss*, it  like you're on a Scorsese movie, the graphics while not the best, haven't aged badly, and this "Definitive Edition" gives them a little boost, for a great price though. Gameplay I'd say can get a bit stale compared to more modern shooters/third person games, but it is a 2010 game so that's to be expected.As I said before I've played Mafia II several times before and the story is as intense as always. I've read a few times on the internet that the DLC were supposed to be part of the main game, with several side quests you could do between chapters, and boy am I glad they cut that, it makes the game pacing a perfect ride jam packed with action, car chases and intense shootouts. Side missions would've ruined that and it wouldn't be held in such high regard as it is.Graphics still look pretty good, sadly this version of the game is riddled with bugs and performance issues, in my case the solution was to reduce the PhysX setting, such a disappointment for an almost 15 year old game to still run badly on modern computers. Yet, it is a great game that everyone should experience. And I definitely recommend getting the Trilogy.

_childDocuments_.review: The short and sweet of it is that i think it's a good game overall. Although while not as likable in tone, characters as the first game there's a lot more going on here with the amount of details and things you can do brings the city of Empire Bay to life. The game stands well on its own and doesn't really require you to play the first game, but there is a brief portion of the game that let's you view the end of the first game from another point of view.Oh and the soundtrack is just amazing. If you're into 50's music with things like John Lee Hooker, Screamin' Jay Hawkings etc. then you'll just love zipping through the radio channels and cruising around to some sweet tunes :)My gripes comes with the technical and marketing sides of the game. Calling it the "definitive edition" is, at the time of writing, a bit of a slap in the face of the player. You see, the game runs well and looks good for such an old timer. And it's not like the game is full of bugs left and right. But the bugs that are there are just disappointing to see.For example on more than a couple occasions the dialogue would repeat at least once, which could make the scenes very hard to decipher without subtitles. Another more serious bug occurs during one of the end-game missions which hinders your progression through the mission and the only remedy seems to be a restart of the game and back-tracking half a level.Like I mentioned, no game comes without its bugs but getting your horse stuck on a roof that you can fix on your own without exiting the game  is one thing and being forced to leave the game to keep playing just stings a bit.Some may feel compelled to compare this game to GTA but I'd say they are two different beasts with a lot of the same looking fur. For example, the obvious: You play in a open city that you can explore and you drive your cars around in it and it's about organized crime and you shoot stuff.However I feel that the comparison ends on the generic level. GTA is much more designed to allow for more fun and games so to speak while Mafia II is more about presenting a story. The tools you get to play around with in M2 are mainly those that were necessary for the developer to include to tell their story rather than added for the sake of having it in the game so that players can mess around with it.There's not that much more that can be said about this game, I feel. But that's not necessarily a bad thing - It sticks to its points and does them well rather than sticking its neck out to try something vastly different that might feel tacked on or such.So if you like a 50's gangster game with solid driving and cover-based shooter mechanics that also features a rockin' soundtrack - Then look no further than Mafia II!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Mafia II: Definitive Edition tells a story that is gripping and while it may not be largely unique in the span of Mafia lore, it’s one of the best available in video game form. I genuinely cared about Vito and the terrifying criminals that surrounded him. I grew to love their antics and laugh at their quirks, and feel sorry for the situations that they found themselves in. I think it’s a little unfair to class Mafia 2 as an open-world game, because the city does nothing but offer the setting for the story to g from point a to point b. If you’re looking for a city that is brimming with side quests and random activities, you won’t find them here. What you will find is a bittersweet, interesting period piece that looks at time that is not often explored in video games, and it’s a pretty damn memorable one at that.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright look .. If you own Mafia 2 classic and got this upgrade free you have no right to complain because its free on 2Ks bit . I wont really say the game looks any noticeably different to the original except certain lighting and weather effects . Would recommend you to purchase the original game key from a 3rd party at a lower price to get the upgrade for free for just the Mafia II experience, even better to purchase the trilogy to have access to all three games if you have the money!! :)Improvements and Additions - Higher resolution HD texture pack  (Obviously)- All additional content for free for those owning the classic- You get the classic if you purchase the definitive edition to avoid bugs and technical issues- Access to new outfits, cars from the Mafia III - Better quality player models Graphical / Game Issues:- Glitches such as aissing debris/particles from objects and buildings- Where is the Apex PhysX option?- Random stuttering issues - Audio issues with distancing at certain areas- Removed DLC outfits and vehicles - Low resolution subtitles - Why didnt they  include the content that was cut from the original game- Very unreliable benchmarking tool that detects your system but sets a low graphical preset - Default 30 fps ? which can be tweaked with its launcher- Crosshair appears at the top of the screen - Cutscenes have blacked out textures- Broken Physics with NPCS , you can cause them to glitch into buildings ( Fix Below ) - Sometimes the eyes of NPCS just appear bugged or dont appear at all- Frozen police NPCS who remain stationary after giving up the pursuit- 4k HUD elements are stretched- This game will take 50gb which is 38gb bigger then the classic editionIts the most common of the bugs in remasters so its no doubt they will affect game play hence you have the classic game option , but just take note as mentioned before its a free upgrade for you to re experience the game before the Mafia 2002 remake set to release August 28th 2020.Personally Mafia 2002 has aged tremendously so its a obviously provide a nostalgic release  hence it deserves a remake. Don't understand the reason behind people expect this game to be remade as well when it clearly still holds expectations graphically and story wise.How to enable PhysX on Mafia II Mafia II: Definitive Edition1. Go to Documents\My Games\Mafia II Definitive Edition\Data\profiles\<ProfileID>2. Open " settings.xml "3. Edit <Apex>0</Apex> to 1 or 2 (0=OFF 1=Med 2=High)4. Save5. Can enter the game to shoot the ground or glass Dude.

_childDocuments_.review: The story and characters are great, however the definitive edition does not add enough value to justify the game and if you own the main game and whatever goes with it, I would say stick to the original. The game relies heavily on driving and the game has notoriously bad driving mechanics. There is no feeling of being in control of the vehicles and the closest feeling is oil on an icy surface and cars made out of cardboard. There is no sense of control or weight or anything that would allow the player to feel a sense of control. The cars do not respond in a way you would expect and in a game where you need to drive a lot, it's too much to bear.For this reason despite loving the mafia games, I have promptly uninstalled the game because of failing in missions has nothing to do with my gaming abilities and more to do with random physics and game AI causing extreme frustration all the time. Imagine driving on a straight road but your car spins 360 for no apparent reason due to the game physics and car handling. Add to that police who will start to ram into you when they see you spinning and hitting bystanders beyond any vehicle control and opposing gang members, you will start to see the mayhem this game's broken mechanics will inflict you with. Graphical and other glitches abound as well and the DE does not really address existing issues with the original game.This was an opportunity to give salute to a great gaming premise, but instead turned into a lazy cash grab by not fixing the things that marred the original flawed but albeit good game in it's core. Also the game systems should have been updated as control of your character definitely feels very decade old and not refined at all. Essentially you feel like you are playing the original game with slightly improved textures but everything else feels even slightly worse than in the original. That may be caused by golden memories, but this is evidently a very lazy DE as they sadly tend to be.

_childDocuments_.review: A Timeless Masterpiece - Mafia II: Definitive EditionI've just finished playing Mafia II: Definitive Edition and I'm thrilled to say that it's been an unforgettable journey that completely exceeded my expectations. This edition takes a classic game and masterfully revamps it, taking full advantage of current generation hardware to truly make this title shine.From the onset, you're immersed into the post-war world of Empire Bay, a city brimming with life, diversity, and period-accurate details. It's a setting that is both intoxicating and unforgiving, perfectly capturing the romantic yet brutal essence of the 1940s and '50s.The game's narrative is its biggest strength, showcasing a captivating and deeply personal story of survival, ambition, and the undeniable allure of the Mafia lifestyle. The protagonist, Vito Scaletta, is a character who's realistically flawed and relatable, bringing depth to his journey from being a war veteran to an ambitious gangster. The supporting characters are just as compelling, each one contributing to the intricate, morally complex tapestry of Mafia II.In terms of gameplay, Mafia II: Definitive Edition manages to find a good balance between driving, gunfights, stealth sequences, and narrative sections. The gunplay is tight and responsive, with a cover system that feels intuitive and keeps firefights engaging. The driving mechanics have also been refined, providing a good sense of weight and momentum to the various period-appropriate vehicles.Graphically, the Definitive Edition shines with its impressive visual overhaul. From the detailed character models to the atmospheric lighting, this game is a visual treat. Empire Bay looks stunning in all its glory, with beautiful day-night cycles and weather effects adding a sense of realism to the world.Perhaps my only gripe would be that some of the original game's flaws still persist, such as the occasional AI mishap and the lack of variety in side activities. However, these minor flaws are easily overlooked in light of the game's strengths.The original soundtrack and exceptional voice acting also deserve a special mention. The developers have curated an atmospheric soundtrack that perfectly complements the era, while the voice actors deliver convincing performances that breathe life into the characters.In conclusion, Mafia II: Definitive Edition is an exemplary remaster, staying true to the spirit of the original while enhancing every aspect of the game to meet contemporary standards. It's a testament to the timeless appeal of a well-told crime story, coupled with engaging gameplay and stunning visuals. This game deserves to be in the library of anyone who appreciates narrative-driven games and the noir charm of the Mafia setting.A must-play classic, definitively.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II: Definitive Edition: Godfather Part IIIt was a bit of an interesting choice by 2K to make this sorta deal. You remake the entirety of Mafia I from scratch, putting Hangar 13 on the deal to do so. You do a slight spit shine to Mafia III, unlock all the DLC and such and add your lovely DRM that works so well that you grenaded your own game and then you did this. You took a game from 2011 that looked pretty alright, gave it the world's most VAGUE spitshine of a remaster and called it a day. Oh and the DLC's no mortal man bought.You are lucky I love this game 2K, because I will still give this game a positive review. ONLY because you allow people to play the Classic Edition through this. Take this new review as more of a talk about Mafia II (Classic) than the DE, because beyond a few hundred bugs, it's still the same game.Mafia II is the game that got swept over in the fanfare about GTA IV back in the day, and most people just sorta shrugged at it as a result. Mafia as a franchise has been perpetually stuck playing second fiddle to GTA and being judged for it. The ol' Crowshaw meme of "CRIME DOES NOT PAY" does fit this game like a glove, but in comparison to the 19 other games that tried to do that, Mafia II actually decides to make that concept work and matter by giving you actual stakes to lose.You play as Vito Scaletta, a slightly DIFFERENT first generation Italian immigrant to America who initially falls in line with his best friend Joe Barbaro into the seedy underworld of crime in the city of Empire Bay. Through a world war and back again, you follow the pair as they attempt to pay for Vito's fathers debts by any means necessary. Quick, simple and with enough points for the plot to throw wrenches in it. And with a fun 1950's world to explore, various old cars to steal and destroy and a very fun and basic gameplay system to it, Mafia II is a modern classic. Like the original, it's simple in regards to most of it's actual parts, but that simplicity works in delivering the story. Are the plot points super deep? No. Do I care? No. I still remember most of this game and I can't remember like 95% of GTA IV so who's winning here, Rockstar?

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Mafia I: Definitive Edition, expectations were high for Mafia 2: Definitive Edition, especially with both remasters released in the same year. Unfortunately, this edition didn't quite live up to the revolution we saw with the first game.Graphically, there’s no significant improvement over the base edition (which came out in 2010). Visuals feel largely the same, which is disappointing given the progress made with Mafia 1: Definitive Edition.That said, the Definitive Edition includes all the DLCs, offering a more complete experience, and makes some minor gameplay improvements, including better controls and bug fixes. The cutscenes have also been slightly reworked for a smoother experience.The game is structured over 15 chapters, but by the 9th or 10th, the gameplay becomes repetitive and tedious. While the missions feel monotonous, it’s worth pushing through, as the final chapters (13–15) provide a much stronger and satisfying conclusion.Though the gameplay has aged, the game is still important to play for the culture, its story and lore. Despite some slow moments, the narrative makes it worth finishing.

_childDocuments_.review: Shorter than I remember but still a great game.I've just completed Mafia 2 Definitive Edition in around 11 hours, which makes it a relatively short game, although I didn't do anything other than plough through the story missions; not that there's a great deal else to do, besides selling cars, robbing the odd shop or looking for collectables. Mafia 2 was criticised at the time for having an open world without much to do in it but I see it as simply the setting for a good story. While part of me wishes that the experience was longer, and that I could have played out a couple of the cut-scenes, rather than simply watching a montage of my criminal activities, I think this would have impacted on the flow of the game and the story.At first glance the graphics seem the same as I remember but take off those rose-tinted glasses and you realise that they have actually been nicely updated. Cars look the part and handle well and everything fits the period, providing a great atmosphere; the soundtrack too is also really good. Shooting and brawling obviously play a large part in the game, with gunplay being of the "press button to hide behind cover, hold aim to pop out" variety; again, it works well and I have no complaints here.There has been a lot of talk of this being a poor remaster, so let me just say this:if you have the original already on Steam, then you have this in your library right now, for free, which is how I got it, and it is definitely worth another play through.if you have the original on another platform, is it worth buying this? Probably not, not for the current price. It's the same game (albeit with all of the DLC included) with some nicer textures and the occasional sound glitch or "eyes stuck looking to one side in cut-scenes" glitch thrown in for good measure.if you don't have the original is it worth getting this? I would say so. Maybe it's showing it's age in some areas but hey, forget about it. Now get outta here!

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for free, which I sure do appreciate.  That's a good thing too, because I am disappointed.  It looks like this was quickly ported over from DX9 to DX11 API with a few general enhancements (textures, lighting, etc.) by D3T.  Unfortunately, there are many technical bugs present right now in this port.  It seems that QA testing was either slim or non-existent.Here's a quick list of bugs I have personally seen happen and/or confirmed from multiple reports from others:-Physx API is broken.  It's really bad.  Physx is always on, with no option to turn it off, and it's extremely buggy.  Vito (your character) has 0 physx applied to coats, leaving them looking like old PS2 style graphics with the bottom sticking to Vito's legs.  This can be worked around though, by deleting the physx files which enables the back-up physics engine (much simpler cloth physics, comparable to 360 version of classic edition)-Audio is bugged and cutscenes only go through the left speaker.  You can work around this by setting audio to high and to stereo, although that is a poor workaround for people with surround sound setups.-Hitching is pretty bad, but I remember the Classic version had similar hitching.  This is likely due to the old engine being overly conservative back in the day.  The engine loads chunks of the world frequently when traveling through the world, causing the hitching(even installing on an SSD didn't help).  This adds to my suspicion of quick port of the Classic version.  I ran Special K and used it's more advanced framerate limiter, in order to normalize frametimes and minimize some loading hitching.-Smoke and other alpha effects flicker now.  I have seen reports that limiting to 60 FPS corrects this, however this is a bad workaround in the days of Gsync/Freesync monitors.  I personally limit to 60 in single player controller games anyways, but this seems like yet another oversight from the port job.-There a plenty more, but these are the most frequent I have seen or have experienced myself.  Just look at the other reviews, and you'll probably see many more bugs like special characters causing save issues (Silent, creator the the GTA SilentPatch's, is creating a patch for this as I speak, he knows far more about the issue than me).I would really avoid buying this RIGHT NOW.  Keep your eyes out for a patch though, if D3T can continue supporting it then it will be even better than the original Mafia 2, which holds a special place in my heart.D3T, if you see this, you're up to bat!!!  This is your chance to redeem yourself, until then I simply cannot recommend buying this version as it is fundamentally broken.  If this changes and you patch it, I will adjust my review :)

_childDocuments_.review: A Second Chance to experience this truly immersive 1950's Mafia open world action-adventure game!Story 9/10: You play as Vito Scaletta, a wannabe gangster and aid and get aid from and to your best friend Joe Barbaro who has been there for you for your whole life. You will experience so much together. So much indeed. The city is Empire Bay. Real life New York. So many opportunities, the American dream as they say. Will you accomplish that dream and so many other dreams that Vito has? How will Vito's story end?Graphics 7/10: Not that much improvement overall. Some of the textures were upgraded. Better lighting and facial structures of the main and sub-characters. Mostly, it's the same look from the Classic version. But of course there are bugs, glitches and lower fps and game performance with this game. 30 fps near many areas, even on strong rigs. The developers might fix these issues sometime in the future.Gameplay 8/10: The driving mechanics are so realistic! You won't find the GTA driving style here. The driving style here is a more brutal and realistic one, I would say. You get penalties from driving fast or not driving carefully from the cops. The shooting gameplay is rather simple. The weapons are rather impressive. I Like their design and sounds. As I stated above, the gameplay is open word so you can kinda explore and collect collectibles, only this can you do though. The game has achievements also, always a plus in my book, just like the classic version. Sadly, no more stuff beyond the main story missions and collectibles were added.Soundtrack 6/10: I wouldn't say that I am intrigued or surprised by the soundtrack, only the main theme puts me on chills. Some scenes have a powerful track out on them while others don't. Kinda a miss or hit or done by purpose.DLC (3 in total) 5/10: Filler in my opinion. With the DE you get all of the DLC with the main game of course, so no losing here, you can play them or not, if you are an achievements hunter like myself you need to complete these and miscellaneous achievements that you can only obtain by playing the DLC's. All the DLC's have a timer on every mini-mission and you have a limited time given in order to complete the missions and do some extra work for the achievements (e.g Drifting daddy 'o', millionaire etc). The best one is Joe's s Adventures which covers the time gap on what joe did after a crucial point in Vito's life.In Jimmy's Vendetta, well you guessed it: Jimmy's Vendetta!And The Betrayal of Jimmy: Betrayal. In addition to these, you get various car and outfit themed DLC's and exclusive outfits from past mafia games to the most recent ones. (E.g. The Mafia III protagonist can wear Mafia II's protagonist's clothes and drive his car and so on)Overall 9/10: This is a nice addition to your Steam Library in general especially if you are a Mafia fan, have already completed the Classic Mafia 2 game, the story, the achievements etc or even a newcomer who wants to try a Mafia game and also get all the dlc included in the price and not independently. Then this game is for you. 100 %Thank you hangar 13 for giving us another chance at completing the game again from the start, obtaining all the achievements, enjoying the game with a fresh look and of course giving it for free to the Mafia 2 Classic owners like myself!P.S:*The achievement "Enforcer" was fixed a long time ago. You will be able to gain it no problemo.*I got the DE for free because I had already had the Classic Mafia II game. You will get the Classic Mafia 2 game for free if you buy the Mafia 2 DE. And vice verca.
