_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II Definitive Edition is not the best example of how to do a remaster yet is still an experience worth playing even if its bring some flaws and old bugs that should not be there is still a great game.The Immersive Storytelling:At the heart of this experience it's a storytelling triumph. Vito Scaletta's journey from a war-torn soldier to a rising figure in the Mafia is a nuanced exploration of loyalty, ambition, and the consequences of life-altering decisions. The narrative spans years, allowing players to witness the evolution of characters and the transformation of the city itself.Timeless Setting, Modernized:Mafia II Definitive Edition flawlessly recreates the post-World War II era, presenting a meticulously detailed world that feels both authentic and evocative. From the classic cars to the carefully curated soundtrack, every element contributes to the immersive atmosphere. The Definitive Edition enhances this setting with updated graphics a bit here and there yet don't have high hopes to see something next get on that regard.Character Depth and Emotional Resonance:One of the defining strengths of Mafia II has always been its well-developed characters. Vito Scaletta's journey is more than a rise through criminal ranks; it's a deeply personal exploration of his motivations, friendships, and the moral quandaries that define his choices. The supporting cast is equally rich in detail, contributing to a narrative that evokes genuine emotional investment.The Nostalgia Reimagined:For those returning to Mafia II, the Definitive Edition is a nostalgic journey made fresh. The familiar beats of the original story resonate, but the enhanced visuals that even if they are not much is decent, refined gameplay, and quality-of-life improvements make it an experience that transcends mere nostalgia. It's a reunion with an old friend, albeit one who has undergone a thoughtful makeover.In Conclusion:Mafia II Definitive Edition is more than a game; it's an immersive cinematic experience that stands the test of time. With a narrative that remains as compelling as it was a decade ago, visuals that bring Empire Bay to new life, and characters whose stories resonate on a deeply human level, this edition is a triumph of revitalization. Whether you're revisiting Vito's world or stepping into it for the first time, Mafia II Definitive Edition is an invitation to a world where crime, loyalty, and consequence collide in a masterfully crafted symphony of storytelling. Welcome back to Empire Bay; the streets await, and the story is as potent as ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II: Definitive Edition brings the classic crime saga back to life with updated visuals and all previously released DLCs, offering a nostalgic yet fresh experience for both newcomers and long-time fans of the series. Set in the 1940s and '50s, the game follows Vito Scaletta, a young man drawn into the world of organized crime as he navigates betrayal, loyalty, and the pursuit of wealth in the gritty streets of Empire Bay, a city inspired by New York.The story in Mafia II is compelling, with a strong narrative that captures the essence of classic mob tales. Vito's journey from small-time crook to major player in the Mafia feels authentic and emotional, and the well-developed characters contribute to the story's impact. The voice acting and cinematic presentation are excellent, making it feel like you're playing through a classic mob film.Gameplay-wise, the title features a mix of driving, third-person shooting, and story-driven missions. The shooting mechanics are solid, though a bit dated compared to modern shooters, but the focus is more on storytelling than innovation in gameplay. The open-world environment is rich in detail, with vintage cars, radios playing classic tunes, and an atmosphere that perfectly captures the post-war era.The Definitive Edition brings some visual upgrades, including higher-quality textures and better lighting, though the game still feels a bit limited by its original design in terms of world interactivity. Despite this, Mafia II remains an enjoyable experience for its captivating story, immersive setting, and memorable characters. It's a must-play for fans of narrative-driven action games and those who enjoy a slice of Mafia history in video game form.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review is about Mafia 2 as a whole, since i haven't played it before)The only memory i have of this game is when i played the DEMO on my crappy Acer laptop. I love the way that you never really get to spend your blood money, cause some ♥♥♥♥ happens, and that's just a clever lecture of how the Mafia life really is. I love the characters, i love the voice acting.Things i don't love: This definitive edition has some bugged smoke FX, and i fixed that simply by turning off PhysX. The save spots are a tad bit too long, if you make a tiny mistake, you get sent wayyy back, and have to do that 2 minute work over again. Theres a little too much driving. Still a classic, a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR The only thing you need to know is that my favourite new feature of this mess of a remaster is a borderless fullscreen option.A very lazy crash prone 'remaster' whose only reason I can see for its existence as far as 2K is concerned is being able to up the price.While it looks better, it isn't by much. And as someone who plays this game for freeride mods, I have no idea what to feel after I discovered that basic freeride mods work on this thing, meaning that they simply upped the textures and that's it.Oh and locked the dlc behind story progress, which only makes the classic version a more appealing prospect to a sandboxer like me.It crashed a fair few times for me too, however take this part with a pinch of salt because I'm not sure if the reason behind this is because of said mods.If you own the original and got this for free I would still recommend the older version, and you get all the dlc for free as a bonus for that one! I'll put it this way: The only reason why I will continue to play this version is because of better rain effects, the fact that I disliked the cloth physics (another black mark against this atrocity, the effect was disabled because reasons) and the fact that it has a borderless fullscreen mode)If you're a new player, play the original because see above.Shame on you, Hangar 13. If you think I'll be preordering Mafia 1 "Definitive" this "remaster" will keep me away until the reviews for that one pop up.Still recommending it because Mafia 2 is one of my favourite games, but only with the caveat that the old one should be played, and not this one.10/10 for the version that matters, 1/10 for the lazy remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the top, I received this game for owning the original on Steam, so I give points for not making me buy it again. That is a consumer friendly practice that must be commended in my mind. However, this game was a mixed bag for me. It was the most linear, open world game I have ever played. And even though the game is open world, I never felt compelled to explore it. I never felt the need to go the various stores, and never felt the need to take in this really cool retro city. This is a shame because so much love went into it and the mechanics of the world. It was a missed opportunity the whole way through. I had fun with the game and it’s characters and setting, but I never really felt like I was role playing Vito. Also amusingly, money seemed useless in a mafia game. At a couple of points, I lost all of it, and nothing changed for me, gameplay wise. I still had all the weapons and ammo I needed, and I never had to worry about paying to hide from the police, so who cared how much I had?Technically, the game ran fine for me. I only had one cut scene with wonky character models and some serious T posing from dead bodies, but nothing game breaking or infuriating. I didn’t play the original enough to have a comparison to improvements to know the difference, so I can’t compare the two in good faith. Overall, I had fun with it, but a serious heads up for people on this game, GTA or Saints Row this ain’t.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember how many times I finished Mafia 2. 10 times maybe... So after playing Mafia Definitive for the 2nd time I decided to give this edition a try. Grabbed it for 7,49 EUR. Was it worth it? HELL NO! I have never experienced as many bugs in M2 like I did during my first approx. 4-5 hours in Definitive Edition. It's a freaking disaster. Graphical glitches, environment (flashing objects during cutscenes) and character (deformed head while wearing specific outfits), sound issues (volume level is a mess, it's jumping during dialogues no matter how you set it up in the settings, sometimes it's screaming from the speakers just to not hear the dialogue 30 seconds later) and frame drops... Man, RTX4070 + i5 13600KF with 3440x1440 resolution and I have constant frame drops while driving around the city. Mad frame drops. During every other crossroad... This is a huge BS and I recommend to avoid it at all times. I don't know if there are some graphic mods for M2. If there are, just use them, it won't be worse than official "remaster", I promise. I don't see an improvement to be honest. Yes, I can do Ultrawide QHD, but that's it. But for what? For the issues I described? No, this mess is not worth it! And this is coming from a Czech gamer who loved this game despite all the hate the game received in my country. I always stood for M2. Sure, was not perfect as M1. But still an enjoyable experience. And the "Definitive" Edition is killing me. I will finish it, because I want to see how much the "remaster" can break the original. 0/10, stick with the original!

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 2: DE. A game developed by Hanger 13 and D3T Studios and Published by 2K Games.If you're familiar with my Mafia: DE review, you know basically what i'm gonna say here. The Mafia trilogy are up there amongst my favourite of this genre, The grit and violence means they are a cut above the rest, And debatable whether Mafia 2 or 3 reigns as the best of the series in my opinion. I would like to mention here, that i don't quite recall quite what  was available in the original rendition of Mafia 2, So i will be trying to review this as its own title entirely.Story: 8/10Having already played Mafia 2, and knowing the ins and outs of the story, the twists and turns in it still captivated me this time around. You play as Vito Scaletta an up and coming criminal in 1940's "Empire Bay" which is essentially just a soft rework of New York of the period. You are busted for some low end crimes and begin the game in service of the army. Upon leaving service you meet up with long time friend Joe Barbaro and your first steps toward becoming a "Made Man" begins. I rated this story so highly not because it isn't a cliche mafia story full of betrayal and intrigue.but because of how fleshed out Vito is as a character. His background, his interests and his personality are all almost readily apparent and begin to develop as the game progresses. I would also like to mention that this game pulls no punches. It's filled to the brim with racism, violence and sex. This adds to the realism of the era's grit and immerses you but its by no means for the faint of heart.Gameplay: 8/10+ Movement: A slight increase in mobility from the first game, Vito moves fairly smoothly around the world, his ability to vault short obstacles and that's position on the controller (I play 3PS games with a controller because it allows you to move slower in stealth) makes alot more sense and is far less clunky than it was in the first game. This doesn't mean its without flaws though, Vito still has a hard time navigating tight areas and often will "take cover" against completely irrelevant surfaces and get shot in the face because of it.+ Gunplay: The gunplay here is hard to argue with, the guns feel effective and powerful and sound completely immersive, When you heart people belting out full mags of a tommy gun into the cover you're hiding behind and you hug it hard because you know peaking will clean your clock.+ NPC/World Interactions: While the world isn't exactly ALIVE. Because the game takes place in Episodes across a 10 or so year gap, the world changes quite rapidly. But even so, each individual experience is full so to speak with people to talk to, and people living their lives, and you can really feel that as you run and drive Empire Bay's streets. My only qualm is that police seem completely disinterested with the NPC's breaking laws and only focus on you. It would add to the experience if police pulled people over occasionally.+ Driving: While NOT as immersive as the completely remastered Mafia DE, Mafia 2 DE is still quite a solid driving experience, the cars react like you would imagine they would to the certain environmental effects, rain and snow. But also smashing the rear of you car, leaves quite a significant dent in that spot which was a nice touch.+/- Fist Fighting: I couldn't decide if this was a positive or negative. Perhaps its both, perhaps its neither, But seeming it takes up a large portion of the game time, I have to mention it. It's great to see the mechanic where you get locked into fist fights with groups, shakes things up from the whole run and gun gameplay, But its not done particularly well here. Its pretty hard to monitor what your opponent is going to do and because Vito isn't particularly agile, he seems to get smacked in the face quite frequently.- Difficulty: This game is easy. Far too easy even on the hardest difficulty, I don't recall it being so easy the first time i played it through but this time it was a breeze, i wish there was a realistic difficulty where gun shots actually took their effect on you, slowed you down, made your aim weaker etc. But unfortunately the overall difficulty was mild.- Mission Diversity: One of the things that makes these kinds of games captivating is taking part in a lot of different experiences, The first game pulled this off amazingly. The 2nd..Not so much. There isn't a lot happening here, beyond driving from here to there and fight off waves of enemies until you reach your objective. A strong dynamic for sure, but it gets boring by the 10+ hour mark.Visuals: 5/10I was hoping for more, from the definitive edition, the touch ups weren't enough to warrant replaying the game. The game still suffers from what it always has, graphical glitches to make your character and the characters your talking to look completely broken or animations completely broken, breaking the total immersion as a whole. The remaster was almost completely irrelevant. The game is extremely graphically glitchy, in fact the first mission i played i jumped out of the cinematic car, and a woman was half way through the concrete of the footpath. Not a great experience. Surely without a doubt though on a mid to high end PC this game ran flawlessly high frames, Which i would expect no less because much of the world is still geometrical.Audio: 7/10Its hard to rate the audio bad here, apart from a few audio glitches that occurred frequently at the start of the game, completely loss of sound in 1 ear on my headphones or crackling as people talk, or completely cutting out entirely. But the soundtrack and audio here was expertly done back in the day, and were made to seem aged even then, It doesn't suffer in the slightest, if nothing else i feel as though it might have helped the immersion.Overall: 8/10Mafia 2 was a trophy winner of its time, perhaps the best Mafia game ever made (Up for debate with 3) but the Definitive Edition didn't bring much to the table, the game suffers from what it always suffered from, graphically and gameplay wise, But now suffers from its aged graphics and a new slew of audio concerns. I received this game as a freebie as many who owned the original did, But its really not any different from its original experience. Other than a very limited assortment of face touch ups to make it not seem as old as it is. A worth while experience for the sake of the trilogy but if you are after the same dedication here as the first games Remaster was, you're going to be sorely mistaken. For the price of $70 AUD for the DE trilogy though, i would warrant that price seemingly it included a full remaster, a rework and all the DLC's.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game while it was one sale, around the time when Grand Theft Auto Definitive Edition was being released to great fanfare. Initially I treated it with a lot of caution: having played GTA over the last 17 years, I was afraid I had grown too accustomed to its universe and that I might therefore become unable to enjoy comparable games.My fears were overcome after I gave Mafia 2 a few tries. It is a strong title with a very good storyline and characters as well as great graphics. When you drive around you absolutely do feel as though you are in an East Coast American city of the 1940-50s, 2K Games and Hangar 13 deserve great credit for how they recreated this kind of urban environment.Their attention to detail is further evidenced by the level of detail of the vehicles. The player can find out various information such as the vehicle's top speed and power when it comes to vehicles that have been stored in the lockup. Also unlike GTA, vehicles kept in the garage remain in the player's possession; you don't have to fear about losing them in random missions.I played the main story on Medium difficulty and felt it was just right: not so hard to the point of making it impossible to enjoy yet challenging enough to keep it interesting. The combat and shooting modes are impressively realistic. You won't see stuff such as heads exploding when you shoot at targets. Also depending on where you aimed you may need more than one shot to finish off an enemy, which brings added realism. There are not many missions, however this is offset by the complexity of the missions and the time required to complete them.Vehicle handling is a lot like in Grand Theft Auto IV: the vehicles feel heavy and therefore convey the feeling of being behind the wheel. Car crashes have been replicated quite well: they won't suddenly turn into trash or catch fire as in some of the GTA games.A common criticism I have read of this game is that it is not truly open world: you have to follow a specific sequence in completing the missions and do not have total freedom to explore Empire Bay. I did not find this to be detrimental to my enjoyment of the game and I certainly do not think it should prevent others from enjoying it for all its other aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: This game used to be really good, but unfortunately it has been updated and now comes with malware known as the "2K Launcher" with no easy way to disable it. There is an option ingame called "disable launcher", but that does literally nothing and keeps resetting to default if you change it. If you start the game, you will be greeted by a the 2K privacy policy, there's no way you'd ever hit "accept" if you read and understood all of it. You don't have to accept the privacy policy to play the game, but if you refuse it, you will get nagged by it every time you start the game. The game also keeps nagging you to create a 2K account, which again you don't have to do to play the game, but if you don't do it, the game will keep annoying you with it every time you start it.If you buy Mafia II Definitive Edition, you will also receive Mafia II Classic, which is the superior version as it has neither of these anti-features added later. There is no way to buy the original version individually on Steam anymore, so you'll still be paying $30 for an 11 year old game. If you really want to play this game, get the original version via retail or whatever, but don't buy the Definitive Edition.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend overall as a solid game however it is ultimately frustrating as:1) Areas where Mafia 2 could have improved over its predecessor; it ultimately did not i.e lack of free roaming variety, side missions. 2) Where Mafia (2002) excelled; Mafia 2 is somewhat of a downgrade i.e the AI is more clunky, cops don't immediately chase you if you cut corners or speed a little and NPCs seem to rush in front of your car. Also to my great dismay there is no real time public transport system :(The story is great, the characters are generally good, the car radio is excellent and the city and environment design is awesome. The game has amusing collectables in the form of vintage playboy magazines as well as 'wanted posters' spread throughout the city although the latter is a hassle.The 3 different DLCs provide the player with something as close to 'GTA' that this game can get but its not that refined, with recycled assets, areas and most missions feeling like busy work. 'Joe's Adventures' is arguably the best of the 3 as it contains key stone missions that provide new indoor areas as well as story driven cut-scenes associated with those missions.

What I mean is that: Mafia 2 is a great game, but ultimately the Definitive edition feels kind of pointless.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, this game fails to live up to the standard set by Mafia 1. The story is just okay—nothing groundbreaking or particularly memorable. However, where it truly falls short is in the remaster itself. It's riddled with bugs, making the experience frustrating rather than enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: The main story of Mafia II is undoubtedly the game's strongest point. Vito’s rise through the ranks, his friendships, and his dangerous dealings make for an engaging narrative. The setting of post-war Empire Bay is crafted beautifully, and the game does a fantastic job of immersing you in the mid-20th century aesthetic. The voice acting and character interactions pull you right into the world, and you can’t help but get invested in Vito’s journey.One of the things that made the original Mafia games so special was the attention to realism, and unfortunately, Mafia II loses some of that charm. Certain features from the original have been cut or toned down, and the overall gameplay has shifted towards a more arcade-like experience. For instance, the point system in the DLCs feels out of place and can take away from the immersion. Instead of adding to the story, the point-based challenges make the game feel more "gamey" and less like a realistic crime drama. Fans of the first Mafia may miss the more grounded mechanics that made the experience feel authentic.The additional content in the form of DLCs falls a bit short. With the odd point system and lack of strong narrative focus, the DLCs feel more like side activities than meaningful expansions of the main story. Instead of diving deeper into character backstories or adding rich new plotlines, the DLCs offer more of an arcade experience, which may feel jarring in contrast to the main story. It would have been great to see the DLCs enhance the immersion and realism instead of taking players out of it.While the journey through Mafia II: Definitive Edition is exciting, the ending is a real letdown. Without giving away spoilers, there’s an off-screen resolution for a key character that feels rushed and unsatisfying. After investing hours in Vito’s story, the final scenes don’t deliver the payoff that fans might hope for. Killing off an important character off-screen feels like a missed opportunity, leaving a sour note on an otherwise thrilling experience.Mafia II is a worthwhile revisit for fans who want to experience Vito's story in enhanced visuals and improved performance. The game has an engaging narrative, with a main story that’s hard to put down and a beautifully designed world. However, the removal of some of the original’s realism, the somewhat disappointing DLCs, and an unsatisfying ending leave this edition a little short of greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: ** Major Spoilers Ahead! You Have Been Warned, So No B*tch*ng! **I got this game as a free upgrade so my review will be less harsh than if I had of spent money on it. Billed as an "ultra HD remaster" but it's barely noticeable IMO. Sure the city looks better, the sunlight and such is lovely, the music and the old time vibe is spot on, the faces up close look better, but this game still looks, and plays like it's hella old! Shame it wasn't built from the ground up like Mafia: Definitive Edition.There's a lot of issues with cut scenes starting early, or cutting out midway though. All the door's should open automatically because there's a lot of pissing about having to stand in the correct position to trigger them to open, and it's gets annoying real fast! There was a point in the game where I couldn't pick up a Playboy mag because a NPC was laying in the way of it and that annoyed the tits offa' me because I don't think that I can go back to the hotel roof to get it at a later date!The information about the city or people on the loading screen flashes by way too fast, I get to read two or three words before the game loads, so really what's the point of them? The game feels rushed and unfinished but I still enjoyed it for the most part, but I would only recommend the game if you buy it for about £5! (Sorry but I wouldn't even spend a tenner on this game because there's just too many issues, bugs and annoying things about it) The story is bare bones basic and doesn't make a lot of sense, but the voice acting is amazing! I also find it quite unrealistic that it was always Vito having to start over when all his $hit got jacked up, how come Joe flourished through it all?! The top annoying thing for me was always having to always re-set my weapon when I'd set them seconds ago, it always reverted back to the fist so lots of times in gun battles I was bunching me fricking fists, all the while getting my nuts blown off! The same thing with the radio, I always set it to Delta, yet every-time I got back into my car it would be revert back to dry ol' Empire.Was there really that much traffic back in the day? Even if there was, I doubt that the drivers were as dumb as a bag of spanners like the A.I in this game. These dude's were meant to be wise guys but they come off as two bit Muppetbutts, nearly every job went tits up, and even when they didn't, it was only a matter of time before you lost everything once again and had to start over, things like that make the game a bore to play, you never really get to revel in your wealth. When you're in between home's you're forced to buy clothes from the shops when the police are hunting you down, because you can't just go to Joe's whenever you want. Silly little thing's no doubt, but it breaks the immersion of the game, as these things would not happen in reality. Too many boring filler missions, there's nothing to really get your teeth sunk into. I'd give Mafia II a broken thumb in a splint, thumbs up, but wait for a sale to get this game because it's definitely not worth full price at this stage. Maybe if the bugs, glitches and texture clips are ironed out, but I can't see that happening anytime soon. I will say that the Marlon Brando from "The Wild One" outfit did appeased me quite a bit! Damn, Vito looked hella sexy in that one!The ending was absolutely terrible and senseless, because if Leo thought that Vito wasn't going to avenge Joe's death then he's sadly mistaken. After all that Vito risked for him too! (In my mind,  Joe doesn't get whacked, he just wasn't invited to the cat house, that's more realistic in my mind, it just doesn't make any sense to take him out when Vito did 90% of his work with him!) The whole storyline was hella sloppy and rushed, so in that view, I guess the ending did fit right in!

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, i got the game for free because i already had Mafia II.I can understand all the other comments saying its a bad remake because of the amount of bugs occuring now ingame wich aren't present in the old game, but i'm positive the Dev's will fix themPositive Things / What i like about the remake:- Better lightning, reflections, volumetrics- Street lamps have a really great lightning it looks very nice too see the city at night- Shadows are more saturated and softer- Way more detailed charakter skins- Faces are more detailed, you can even see every freckle, scratch- Beards better visible- Hair looks now more like the gelled hair young folks had in the 40's- The environment feels more reflected on the vehicles- Objects that were actually round, but were rather angular due to the technology at that time, are now round- More options to adjust the graphics and behavior of the game- A "Launcher" gives you the chance to adjust the settings before you start the game and can also be turned off in the settings- Cutscene movies are remade to fit the 1080p optic- Film grain was removed in many occasions (never understand why it's a thing in games, same as motion blur)- New arrangment of the Main menu- Story is still the same (yeah i think this is a valid good point because many remakes do changes on it's stories)- Xbox Controller work better now- Even the remake can run easily with 60+FPS on most machines on highest settingsNegative things /What i don't like:- Main menu now show an Ad for the "Definitiv Edition Collection"- Why should i create an 2k account? And why the game needs to remind me about this everytime?*Answer* You will get 2 new Cloth pieces ingame wich are both ugly in my opinion.- Ingame cutscenes sometimes have problems with buggy characters, sometimes the eyes don't move, don't blink or just look somewhere else- Smoke, Steam flickers sometimes and are a little "too much" and are not constant- Some lights especially in the tunnels are way too bright and dazzling- PhysX. Do i need to say more? Well, it "work" but only after you delete the "Cloth" folder in the game folder- PhysX again - after fixing it, it will work, but your clothes start to wobble some time after your character stops moving and some other world objects will also begin to wobble too as soon as they move- PhysX once again? Well not exactly but its still PhysX fault: DLC Clothes (Greasers, etc.) will not show up in your wardrobe if you don't delete the "Cloth" folder- If you kill a NPC near objects like chairs, it will most likely happen that the object will spin away- If you stealth-kill a NPC like a cop sitting on a chair, the NPC will stand up regulary because he see you, but then act like getting strangled and get unconcious without alerting anyone else- Combat System is untouched and ducking is still a little clunky- Movement with Controller is sometimes a bit loose- They really could have reworked the tuning system, you can only make your car better, but you can't downgrade your car if you don't like the highest tuning because the engine goes through the hood which looks ugly on some cars- Some objects still have their original graphics wich look out of place- sometimes the characters glitch a little in cutscenesThere are sure many more things to mention but i think those are the most notable. Summary- Do i enjoy the game? Yes of course- Do i ♥♥♥♥♥ about some bugs? No, because they are minor, yes i think they shouldn't exists in the game but well, here we are- Do i recommend the game? Yes and No-- If you loved the original and want to see the game polished in 1080p then yes, buy it or if you're lucky, you already have it for free anyway. --No, because some of the bugs can breake the immersion and fun for many people especially since the gaming community became very ♥♥♥♥♥♥ about anything what isn't 100% perfect (nothing can be)All in all, in my mind, the bugs and everything negative i mentioned is somewhat minor and can be easily ignored, because Mafia II Definitive Edition is still a good game and a worthy successor of the original game and i really have fun playing it

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say much on the remaster of Mafia II as I, following the steps of every gamer, bought the game and never played it. However, with the release of Mafia II: Definitive Edition, I decided to hop into the world of Vito Scaletta and the Italian Mob during the 1950's. And I have to say, I was thoroughly impressed.Mafia II: DE tells the story of Vito Scaletta, the son of an immigrant dock worker, trying to find his way in life and make a mark on the world. He begins by befriending Joe and committing thievery, which eventually gets him enlisted in the war effort and shipped off to Sicily. Coming back from the fight, he joins up with Joe once more and begins his involvement in the Mafia of Empire Bay. The narrative doesn't have a "plot" but rather just a look at the life of Vito, and despite the lack of a fully cohesive story it manages to hold up very well. You see Vito go from getting involved in massive gang fights to learning more about the Mafia in prison, and the various connections he makes and the people he stays loyal to prove to twist his jobs for the mob and consistently put him in uncomfortable situations. It's a well written narrative with dialogue that mimics the time, providing for a great experience.The gameplay is your standard third-person shooter, but done in a way where there's more emphasis on storytelling than just gunfights. Between sneaking around and stealthily killing enemies, getting into cop chases and committing pretty much any crime you can think of, simply labelling it as a third-person shooter does Mafia II: DE no justice - it feels more like Grand Theft Auto with the clock spun backwards. The game's graphics and audio have definitely been revamped, and that's my guess given the time between the original release and this remaster. There are quite a few pesky bugs that need dealing with regarding graphics and gameplay, but nothing that hinders game or collectible progression.All in all, I believe that old-school games set in the 1900's are absolute gems, and Mafia II: DE certainly lives on the top shelf of that list. A game with great atmosphere, wonderful licensed music, great gameplay mechanics and a story that's both unconventional and refreshing, this is a definite must-buy from me, capiche?

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 2 is a bit different than other open world games, instead of throwing side content at you they keep you on the linear path. Is it a bad thing? No not really. Who says you can't have a linear game set in a open world? Sure you can buy suits, upgrade your cars, crush cars to earn money and stuff like that but those are minor diversions and doesn't really take up much of your time.- The combat is standard third person cover shooter but a bit more difficult than other open world third person shooters. - Story is really good and the big reason I don't mind the linearity, it doesn't get boring at all.- It's super immersive, there's multiple seasons throughout the game so it doesn't feel like your stuck in a time loop like other open world games. NPC's act properly, if it's winter people slip on the sidewalk. There's a lot of little detail in the game that you probably won't notice, stuff happening that isn't related to what your current task is.- As I wrote earlier there's shops around but I didn't pay much attention to them besides the auto shop, you can go buy guns and stuff but they usually give you one if you don't have any and you're going into a mission that has combat.The upgrades made by the Definitive edition however are minor, there are some modern graphic options added on top of the game, some better texture on character models that kinda stuff and you get almost all the original DLC's (you have to make a 2k account if you wanna get the Made Man suit pack or whatever it's called). It performs well enough, didn't crash so it's way better than the BioShock 2 Remaster which is also published by 2k. But eh I don't know, the Definitive Edition or the Classic Edition? It's up to you, the Classic Edition has stutter that I couldn't fix, the Definitive Edition also has stutter but way less severe so you probably won't notice it that much. It also features a framerate limiter but it only works during gameplay, so I'd cap it with some form of vsync or external framelimiter. I encountered a few bugs, minor character face stuff, one which had characters repeating everything they said during a whole chapter and a missing conversation during a drive to an objective. Conclusion: If you haven't played it before I'd recommend it, on sale though.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 2 was a pretty good game. The story is quite solid with plenty of little twists and turns. Lasted maybe 15 hours and didn't feel repetitive at any point. Voice acting is good. Gunplay is pretty good. It pushes the player to use cover rather than running and gunning, and the enemy AI behaves the same way. Enemy AI is quite impressive for the game's age, though they will occasionally get stuck in place. Only saw this a few times, so no biggie. The game has a shocking amount of environment damage, like tables, pillars, etc. all visibly losing chunks of material when shot. It's a cool effect when in a gunfight. The driving in this game is better than pretty much every new game. The cars feel truly heavy, and not many games pull that off. I'm very impressed. Graphics are well, 10 years old. They hold up well, but don't expect to have your mind blown there. My biggest issue is that stuff that forms as a result of large gunfights like debris and casings do not despawn when they hit a certain count. As a result of this, I've had my frames drop from a stable 60 down to 15, which is not fun in a fight. I looked briefly at the DLC in the game, and it seems kinda bland.All in all, would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II Definitive Edition is definitely a blast and easily recommendable. The story is great. The mission structure is also much more diverse than the original Mafia's, making the whole plot more unpredictable and thrilling. The narrative can be both extremely deep and surprisingly shallow at times (for example, the ending feels very abrupt, and there are some plot holes here and there). Also, the atmosphere is pretty great, and it stays true to the historical setting.The warning about "sensitive cultural content" at the beginning of the game is no joke: this is perhaps one of the most overtly racist () game I've played so far. Nonetheless, I do appreciate that they chose not to censor the game. It was definitely interesting to play it like this. It fits in with the overall narrative Mafia II is meant to portray.The shooting is far more pleasant and diverse than in the original, as you get more weapons and you are no longer restricted to holding just two at the same time. I do feel that they could have toned down the driving sequences somewhat; the story sometimes loses momentum as you drive from one part of the town to the other. I don't think I'm exaggerating if I say that at least 5 hours of my 20 hours spent in the game were solely driving.The open world definitely feels somewhat lively, as the money mechanic adds a lot of depth to the gameplay, making your actions within the game much more impactful. Sadly, the world itself feels rather empty; collectibles are very few and of little interest, and to my knowledge, there aren't any side quests or too many secret activities. Chances are that once you complete the story (which is roughly 15-18 hours long, depending on how long you take to explore the city), you won't have much left to do.Now, the remaster is somewhat of an odd job. Some textures are clearly upscaled and look much crisper and more detailed (the facial details are the greatest improvement by far, along with the use of ambient occlusion and higher-resolution shadows), while others seem completely untouched. This might also just be my impression, but it seems that some of the longer cutscenes still use the old facial models, so there will be a discrepancy between how Vito looks during gameplay and in those cutscenes. Additionally, there are some NPCs in the DLCs that were not touched at all, so there is a huge contrast between their very outdated models and the crisper look of their main characters. Nonetheless, since I encountered extremely few glitches overall (some characters not moving, some weird animations, etc.), I would definitely recommend the Definitive Edition. This edition also lists "Full controller support" among the features and has some other minor additions as well, so why not, I would say you can go with this one.I haven't played much of the DLCs, but they don't really seem that interesting. Their arcade aspect really ruins the atmosphere for me. Still, since they're included in the Definitive Edition, they do offer some extra shooting/driving sequences and some minor lore and side stories. Joe's Adventures seems like the most interesting one by far, as it expands upon the story a bit.TL;DR: Definitely recommended, even if the Definitive Edition has some quirks. I would give it a 9/10 for the shooting, great story, and overall awesome atmosphere.

This is a pain, because it means that if I wan't to play the game, I need to keep my anti-virus turned off (which I really don't like to do).Another thing I noticed which really annoyed me, was the fact that when I exited the game, the game continues to run the executable in the background, and when I go to turn off the exe in the task manager, it tells me I can't. The only way for me to fully close the game is to restart my computer entirely.I was really looking forward to this remaster too, but until these problems are dealt with, I won't be playing the game, and I can't recommend buying it if you didn't get it for free. Honestly, I'd just play the classic version, it may not be graphically better, but it is the same game, and at least you can play that without having to disable your entire anti-virus software.If these problems get fixed, then I'll be able to continue with the game, and my review will be changed.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are only slightly better than the original, so it's not a big upgrade like the Mafia 1 remaster. I also found bugs, like characters repeating everything twice or glitchy textures. In some areas, my FPS dropped significantly (this only happened twice).The NPCs were really annoying. This never happened to me in the Mafia 1 remaster, but in this game, I had to restart missions more than five times because they spotted me and I died instantly. Sometimes, the NPCs would just stand behind me or behave oddly (and sometimes they didn't show up on the map either). Plus, the checkpoints were usually right before a cutscene, so I had to watch them over and over again.The game was still good, but I can imagine people who bought it at full price on release day would be pretty upset (at that time, the game had too many bugs as well). I got it for 6 dollars, and for that price, it was a nice upgrade, so I'm satisfied. The game was really good, especially with the story staying true to Mafia 2.If you buy it on sale, I definitely recommend it, it's an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II as a game itself is fantastically good an immersive affair with engaging story and interesting characters with incredible atmosphere and jaw dropping attention to detail but you probably already knew that. However this Definitive edition manages to introduce a host of new visual glitches (such as character models clipping through clothes, eyes of npcs as well as player character sometimes get locked in a certain position starring into abyss, textures exude a stretching effect and more noticeable pop ins of objects) none of which were present in the Classic edition on top of that frame rate seems to be about as stable as a skateboard in a canoe. Support for 4k resolution and sharper textures are a welcome edition however there are mods that provide that for free and do a better job at that. It is difficult to tell what has been changed without having a side by side comparison sometimes.Major positive for this however is that the owners of the original copy of Mafia II got the "Definitive" edition for free for if I had to pay for this i would have refunded it by now. Heres hoping that these issues will be ironed out through patchwork, however this botched job of Mafia II has me somewhat worried for the original Mafia remaster as its the same company Hangar 13 who are working on it. Heres hoping they dont screw that up.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the story will always be my favorite Mafia story. *chef kiss* BUT this game on pc is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmare. The controls are janky as hell, the AI for joe? TERRIBLE especially in the gun fight. There was hella times he ran into someones face just to shoot em and back off. He doesnt really defend you in the big gun fight and he will let the person come around and shoot you in the back. Joe AI literally pissed me off for most of this gameplay. His little comments when you are speeding or just driving, the comments about your aim when he barley kills anything lol. The controls barley worked during fighting. I might replay this but the classic one just to see if the comments ive seen was true. 10/10 for the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Ahhh, Mafia II Definitive Edition! Is it a perfect game? No. But very good and well worth the bit I spent to get all three Mafia games in the Definitive, including DLC's. Hours and hours of satisfying gameplay. I'd played these all in the past, but it was so long ago, I can't even remember if I had a controller for the driving function. I have a midrange setup with an RTX 2070 video card. The game looks nice. My monitor is 60hz, so I'm not trying to push anything crazy and I wonder if that's where some people are having issues. Asking an old game to do too much, graphic-wise? My settings are 2560X1080@60hz and most everything else is maxed out. The glitches I've seen are not graphic errors. They are glitches that either prevent you from doing an action or as some people have previously mentioned, there's a map glitch that will always show your best friend's house as a mission item where you are supposed to go sleep on the couch. If you try it, it won't let you after a certain point, so it's an annoyance that you live with. My recommendation would be in the first chapter, when it tells you to go to bed, don't go exploring, just go to bed, lol. This game is well worth the little bit it costs nowadays. The few glitches are usually remedied by restarting the game, with the exception of the one mentioned above for the map.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people say this definitive edition for Mafia II was done poorly, especially in comparison to the treatment Mafia I Definitive Edition got. I agree with them, there are some gameplay/graphic upgrades, but I barely notice much of a difference between the original Mafia II and this Definitive Edition. However, for some god forsaken reason, the classic version of this game is unplayable for me, it always crashes 5-10 minutes into playtime. Doesn’t matter what fixes I try, nothing works. The classic edition is scuffed for me for some reason. Thankfully, at the very least, there is this playable "definitive edition" of Mafia II.Most Mafia fans say that classic Mafia II is one of the best out of all the Mafia games, but personally, coming from someone who has never really played the classic Mafia I and Mafia II games, I would prefer and recommend Mafia I Definitive Edition over this game. However, for this game, narratively, the story is solid and entertaining, the environment and open world are well thought out and immersive, and the gameplay feels crisp to a T. I still enjoyed my time with this game, and, to a lesser extent, recommend it to Mafia virgins/noobs coming form the Mafia I Definitive Edition like me. Wait, no Steam Cloud saving so 0/10 worst Mafia game. Utter trash and garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. I gave it 3 chapters to draw me in, so far I don't care about anyone or anything in the slightest. The game's just boring. And I don't like how the game tried to lean more into the GTA elements instead of playing to its own strrengths with a good story and mission design. Instead, the missions are boring, and the main character and his friend are annoying
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This game is....amazing.Just finished playing Mafia 2 for the first time and I'm in awe.I played the remake of Mafia 1 a couple years ago and it was fantastic, my first entry into the Mafia series, heck my first time even really hearing about this series was when I checked steam and saw "Mafia 1 Definitive Edition", I had no idea what I was in for.The ending of Mafia 1 left me wanting so much more even though It was very sad.Enter, Mafia 2 with Vito and Joe.A game from 2009 with a remaster that doesn't do it justice. While Mafia 1 got a needed ground up remake, 2 got some graphical improvements but at the cost of missing content in the main story.The graphical improvements are noticeable however for such a legendary game it not getting a ground up remake is disappointing.Nonetheless the game still holds up pretty well in 2023 for a 2009 game. The movement, car mechanics, and other things do feel clunky at times but it never makes you want to stop playing or enjoy the game less.The story is amazing. Taking place in two different settings where one has snow and more retro cars, outfits, and radio songs while the other is the spring and more modernised in many different ways. The characters, voice acting, and dialog/writing is top notch. A story that has all the moments you'd want in one.Characters play off of each other well, Joe and Vito especially, the main theme of the game is one of the best in gaming, and the ending like Mafia 1 is extremely sad.My only big complaint with the game is how many missions there were where you have to drive across the entire map while watching out for cops and not killing yourself by crashing just to do something small that plays a little part in the story and then to drive all the way back to your home, go to sleep, and continue the story usually by doing that over and over again. It got repetitive and annoying due to how many of those types of missions there were.Aside from that this game is amazing.The music, graphics, voice acting, characters, sound design, story, dialog, and city all come together to make a fantastic game that still holds up well in 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Decent upgrade for a great game. Im not complaining since it was free. The new textures that are there are definitely nicer than before. Plus i always had issues with the original port, for instance my characters head would be missing and blacked out, so having a copy now with no issues for me is great as well. I have an i7-4790k and RTX 2080 black, have been playing at 4k everything turned max except msaa at 4, and been getting 60fps.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This game was bad.After playing through Mafia 1 Definitive I went into this game with super high expectations, however, from the get-go it was obvious that this game was a steaming pile of garbage.It's NOT the graphics, because I understand more work went into mafia 1 than this.The ENTIRE game is boring as hell. Drive Joe, go to the bar, drive here, drive there. The story was meh.BUT THE BUGS ARE WHAT KILL THIS GAME.Constant clipping, dialouge and character failures, t-posing enemies who will stand still and then one shot you immediatley once you get close. The AI is the worst I've seen in a video game in a long time. Cars will TRY to run you off the road and the cop "speeding" feature is so stupid.I could not WAIT for this game to be over so I could delete if forever. What a joke.Compared to Mafia 1, this game was a joke. Really dissapointed with Hangar 13.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: You should definitely play Mafia 1 before this. The graphics are a big disappointment when coming from the Mafia 1 Definitive Edition, it's just not on par. What's lacking on the graphical side is easily compensated by the game's beautiful and entertaining story. Something that slowly begins and gets more intense towards it's end eventually leaving you on a big cliffhanger. My biggest issue, besides the major lack in graphics are the bugs of which you will encounter quite a few. Some of them might force you to replay whole levels several times. Followed by the bugs, the DLCs included with this game are mostly lackluster missions on a time limit and a sometimes ridiculous difficulty enhanced by bugs.-7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The story of the game is amazing, nothing wrong to say about it, but there are some things that aren't okay. Starting with the graphics, if you do a masterpiece work with the first one definitive edition, i don't understand why you have to be lazy on the second one and just fix some lightining. The game has bugs, sometimes for no reason it has fps drops, sometimes Vito doesn't steal a car and just stands in front of it, other times Vito restart his dialogues and end up speaking above Joe's or other people who are talking, it happened only one time but Joe textures completely disappeared during a cutscene and it looked like Vito was talking with a ghost.  There are other things that didn't work for me, but it's my personal taste, so i'm not going to write it down.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game way back when it got released for the first time on PS Plus. I never played the full game, so I saw this as a good opportunity to buy the definitive version.First of all, this game is not 'definitive'. The player movement still feels like it hasn't changed since 2011.The driving in this game is ruthless. Sometimes I'll have some sick drifts, other times I'll be fixing up my engine...The gun battles in this game almost gave me a heart attack. The enemies can take a whole mag, meanwhile they are aimbotting my *ss while wildfiring above their head whilst throwing a grenade. Getting oneshotted by a man a shotgun or those sneezers running with their Tommies straight into my face. It really frustrated me and almost took away the pleasure out of this game.Luckily, the story is one of the best I've played. Vito and Joe, they are good people. From beginning to end, I wanted to know what would happen to them. And then, probably the thing I loved the most. The scenery and timeperiod. Seeing all those classic cars drive by, the first chapters in the snow. There's nothing better than cruisin around Empire Bay while blastin' Chuck Berry or Dean Martin. I'm really dissapointed there was no free roam after the last chapter. There was still so much things to explore. I guess I will have to do another run when I've got the time.Joe and Eddie singing along with Dean Martin is my most favourite thing in a game, ever.

_childDocuments_.review: All you idiots talking ♥♥♥♥ about the remaster yes they could have done a better job but be thankful that these guys have took the time to spruce up the game Mafia 2 is a perfect game and people just down voting it for the glitches are moronsVito Scaletta a war hero returns to Empire Bay after taking a bullet he and his best friend Joe Barbaro get involved with the three main crime family's in Empire Bay starting from small jobs to jobs that get more risky and harder as the years go by and the war ends the atmosphere and writing is the number one thing i love about mafia 2 the voice acting is one of the best i heard mainly Joe Barbaro's actor Robert Costanzo and Vito Scaletta's actor Rick Pasqualone the soundtrack is full of classic 40s and 50s which is my era of music and modern day gamer's wont even notice because there music taste is like ♥♥♥♥ on a shoe from Dean Martin to Bing Crosby some of Franks songs where meant to be there too but got cut you can hear some of them with the ''Friends for life mod' which can be only played on the ''classic version'' of Mafia 2the story always keeps you engaged there is never a single time where it drags at all most characters are memorable just as the missions are the city breaths life from diners full of people people fixing cars stuff like that i give Mafia 2 8/10 if it didn't have most of the content cut i would give it a solid 9

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, Mafia 2 is a great game. This remaster does look a fair amount better than the original that is 10 years old. However, within the first 10 minutes of playing i have experienced npc's getting stuck and falling through the floor and faces not loading causing npc's to look like zombies. This game is 10 years old so it is understandable that it will feel a bit dated, but why not fix a few of the bugs while upping the resolution? You can slap on a new coat of paint on a car, but if it doesn't run well then what's the point? This is basically a re-release and just isn't worth $30. I would wait for a sale, maybe around $15 before i would recommend this to someone. I still love Mafia 2, but they could have done more with this remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: So mafia 2 is a very good game and I do recommend playing it but I wouldn't recommend playing the "definitive edition" its honestly just riddled with bugs, for example during my 42 hours playtime I encountered bugs where dialogue would repeat itself or if I was given money it would give it me like 2 or 3 times and there's also times where I would just start to fall through the map and cut scenes can be very buggy to the point where the main characters head is literally showing twice in it, so if you decide to buy this because you wanna play mafia 2 just play the classic version that comes with it and stay away from the so called definitive edition you'll have a much better time playing that one and I'm sure you could find mods to make it look better if you wanted toalso the dlc sucks just don't bother playing it unless you care about getting 100% for the achievements theres literally no cut scenes for it and its just like an arcade mode where you drive from point a to b kill a few dudes drive away repeat with a bad time system and point system per level it doesn't offer anything to the main story reallyTLDR Play the classic version not the definitive edition and the dlc sucks

_childDocuments_.review: This is kinda a case of good game, bad remake. To clarify, I bought this game as part of the trilogy bundle that was on sale and still I can confidently say I paid too much for this game to be included in said bundle. I really, REALLY loved the old game as while the graphics are admittedly poor the gameplay was at least not constantly interrupted by framerate drops. I also remember from a while ago that there was an interview with the old devs going on about how the original game was originally going to be much larger with things like rackets, gambling etc. So maybe for the final edition of a classic staple of games there could've been a way to integrate said systems into the game or add certain things to make the world actually worth exploring, as it's always been a beautifully made city.TL;DR: game had a solid foundation because of the original game, however the lacking "remaster" should be taken out back and given the Tommy Angelo treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: What 2K and Hangar 13 has accomplished here is nothing short of revolutionary! They've somehow managed to transform an 8 GB classic into a massive 44 GB masterpiece, all while preserving every single detail exactly as it was. The sheer dedication to achieving a perfectly indistinguishable visual experience compared to the original is truly admirable! This 'Definitive Edition' is an essential purchase, if only because the original, tragically, just won’t cooperate with Windows 11. A truly stunning feat of modern gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: In my humble opinion Mafia II aged pretty well and it didn't need to be remastered but on the other hand it was a good excuse to play it again :D Graphics looks prettier (especially faces and lights) but difference isn't as huge as required disk space would suggest :) There are some minor bugs but nothing serious and the game runs pretty smooth (I got stable 60 fps on RX 570 for most of the time).It's worth to mention that Definitive Edition comes with all DLCs and it was given for free to original Mafia 2 owners which is pretty rare nowadays. Mafia II DE is good but to be honest I'm more excited about Mafia 1 remake :)

_childDocuments_.review: I might change this in the future; I don't know just what is going on at 2K.  I own the Linux version of Mafia II: Definitive Edition, and it is only the classic version with a ton of overhead from 2K (namely their launcher!)  If you run Linux, don't buy this version at any price!  2K has written off the Linux version.  Steam requires that all games run in Linux by the launch of the Steam Deck, so all 2K did was a quick hot fix for M2DE.  There have been not one single announcement saying that they are working the issues with the game.  They simply did a FU fix to a very popular game!  Now, let's take stock of what 2k has done so far.  They have DEs of Mafia, Mafia 3, Bioshock, and Bioshock 2.  There might even be more.  There are the games that I own.  They've done all of this, and Mafia and Bioshock are simply breathtaking! In stead, we're greeted with the old version at twice the price!  It's a Fracken insult!

_childDocuments_.review: I've not finished the story for the definitive edition yet, but the mixed reviews so far are 100% right. It's a great game story wise, the graphics and sound are pretty decent, overall the game play is mostly great, just occasional clunky stuff you expect from games from the generation this originally came from.The big draw back to this game is simply the bugs, they're super common and completely ruin what could be on of the greatest games. You can't go 10mins without seeing minor graphical bugs, half the cut scenes just sometimes don't play any sound at all, randomly my characters head shrinks right down where there should be a hat, but instead i get a mini head.... Tbh it's mostly amusing because i know the story inside out, but to anyone knew experiencing the game, it'd be awful. Thankfully i've not had any hard crashes or anything, it's just minor weird stuff tbh.I'd recommend this game for anyone that has played the original, or someone that really (and i mean really) enjoyed the first mafia definitive edition and wants to experience more of what is a great story (although you might have to keep replying a mission for the sound to work etc to experience it), it's a headache because of the bugs, but i'd still recommend it to them certain people. Everyone else should give it a hard pass.6/10 overall because of the bugs, if it wasn't for them it'd be a 9/10. What a shame.I'd recommend waiting for a sale or buying it cheap if you can, to avoid buyers regret.Edit, i've managed to fix a handful of the bugs by using headphones which solved most of the audio related bugs, none the less, it shouldn't need headphones to play the game. All the visual bugs are still there but thankfully they don't effect the actual game other than being funny then they do happen. I'll bump it up to 7/10 because it seems like you can work around the bugs with trial and error.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 2 is a game that slipped my radar forever and I finally got around to playing it. The story and characters are great and it manages to tell a compelling story that will have its action packed moments and its more somber character focused periods. The combat is fine and while its nothing special, it's at least serviceable. The 1950s atmosphere is great with its array of licensed music being played in the period appropriate vehicles. However, issues arise on the technical aspects. There are various visual bugs and glitches such as flickering smoke, weird physics etc that still haven't been fixed. Something that I haven't seen mentioned is how immersion breaking the open world activities can be. For example, for some reason every single person has a gun in every single store throughout the city and robbing the store at gunpoint will mean that everyone will whip out their guns to shoot at you. The police system is also a bit weird as the police will only stop you for speeding or crashing into people at full speed and will turn a blind eye for running red lights or driving on the wrong side. Overall Mafia 2 is a great experience that delivers a great story and atmosphere but is held back by some technical bugs and some nitpick immersion breaking issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 2: Definitive Edition. Just like the Mafia remake prior to it, I was excited to get into this one. The impetus of revisiting this story, actually completing it for once following a couple of prior attempts on the PS3 and the original PC version in the past, with some enhancements to make up for the passage of time to boot, was surely an offer I couldn't refuse... in hindsight. Having finally completed it on my Twitch.TV broadcast in October 2020, and experienced it for all that I personally feel it is worth, It only seemed appropriate that I share my thoughts. And broken down in the paragraphs below, here they are: While a fairly short experience by some of today's standards, it's still every bit as good as I remembered from the original Mafia 2. It's not a dyed in the wool classic like Mafia: The City of Lost Heaven, or even the Mafia: Definitive Edition remake. But it's also not an unmitigated disaster of epic proportions that shouldn't have  made, either. Thankfully, for better or worse, there have been no changes in that regard, and it's been preserved in all of its original quality. Nothing watered down, or sugared up for today's overly sensitive Z generation who have to cry to Twitter every time somebody looks at them cross-eyed. For probably 2/3 of the time I played it, it's been pretty good. However, I have noticed a fair amount of moments in the story where background noise would just be vaporized out of the cutscenes, leaving only the voice acting (which is awkward), or lines of dialog repeating more than once (which can overlap in some instances). This is a bad oversight which has broken the immersion, and affected the overall experience - especially towards the end of the game - and something that I would have to dock points over. Finally, while I understand that licensing issues become a thing after a certain period of time, legalistically speaking, I was nonetheless disappointed in the amount of cut music from the games radio stations. There are remedies for this, but none that I will publicly provide. Dated, and cumbersome. We're not talking PS1 or N64 era, but it's significant enough where I would've considered them an oversight in the remastering process. Had I been in charge of them, there would at least be two options: one for more modern controls similar to GTA, and one for the classic setup. Unfortunately, I can only judge these from the perspective of playing this with an X-Box One controller hooked to my PC, though. So, while I won't dock a  of points, I will still be making concessions here for what it is. The hardest ride of them all. The AI can be straight up broken in some instances, and rudimentary actions or events sometimes don't register as they should (like the objective for crashing on Joe's couch never going away throughout the entire playthrough). And these are just a couple examples of the various bugs, big or small, that you will encounter throughout your experience with this "remastered" title. While they CAN look better than the original game, there's a lot of things here in duality that throw a wrench into the cogwheel. Hats clipping through the player model, eyes not properly tracking, faces literally morphing off of peoples bodies, and various other things of that nature. Play it long enough, and you will discover something to hate. Guaranteed. ...and while we're at it, a side-note concerning the PhysX: I should  have to go into the game's root folder, and delete files, in order for rudimentary clothing physics to work properly, either. While not game-breaking, or even a buyer beware-grade issue, it is still annoying. It was just there, baked into the code of the original release, and should've been considered here as more than an afterthought by the developers all the same. Rant over.Anyone familiar with my past reviews knows I rate games on a scale of 1 to 5. Here's a description of how that system works: 3 out of 5. It wasn't totally void of fun, and I was happy to have finally seen this game through to the end. Playing the classic, if you can get your hands on a copy (or happen to already have it in your Steam library), I can see where that would be at least a 4 out of 5 experience - one that I recommend you dive into first-hand, wholly, above anything else. However, if your only option IS the "definitive edition", it is almost guaranteed that you will experience the same level of bugs and glitches that I've endeavored (as well as others), and I urge you to factor that into how much you're willing to spend - if you're willing to spend. Personally, I can only recommend it in good conscience at a deep (if not reasonable) sale price across both the PC, and console editions (replacing the latter entirely with a full on rental, if you're one of the lucky few who still has an operational video store nearby). The developers (or management) refused to commit to full-priced quality control with this product, opting to release it in a semi-broken state, and this level of effort should not be rewarded as such. It sets a bad precedent, and only ensures that we get more products like this in the future - an existing trend that I'm honestly sick of at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Could be a great game if it either got a better story or better free roam / open world elements. The player gets forced to deal with the typical twitchy third person cover shooter mechanics everybody is doing these days (Tomb Raider, Hitman, GTA, ...). Its bland, it requires no skill whatsoever when using mouse and keyboard. Get hit by twitchy AI opponents which either do nothing or pepper your face aimbot style. What you get is a bunch of highly constricted cover filled shooting galleries full of one dimensional AI. Hop into cover...wait for the AI to do their peek, headshot, rinse and repeat. Got hit? Bloody screen, pumping sound, automatic HP recharge. The rest is driving from A to B with nothing to do and cutscenes in between to push the story.  The story feels meh at best and suffers from atrocious pacing... everything you do could've been condensed into a shorter experience with better highs and lows (see Mafia 1 which is excellent in that regard). There are barely any likable characters, and there is no real feeling of belonging to a Mafia family. The main character basically betrays everybody but his sidekick at some point and nothing really has weight to it. Sure there is a nice Police mechanic (the player and the car he sits in can individually be tagged as wanted, so you are forced to change clothes or get a new car) but starting fights with the police is fun 2-3 times, then becomes a nuisance one runs into in the worst moments. Especially cops shooting from cars are laser accurate and just kill you in one unlucky burst over 2 blocks distance, while the player cannot even fire out of the car. Since the game is stingy when it comes to saving your progress, you end up getting whacked when daring to experience some free roaming while driving to the next mission, just to respawn on the other side of the city. The driving model is somewhat arcady but still clunky. Maybe its not optimized for keyboard input. Mafia 1 felt much more realistic with fitting clunkyness, while Mafia 3 goes full arcade. Both feel better to me than this. I keep crashing against cars, trees, poles which does a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of damage to the player. Combine that with the laser drive-by policemen and car chases become a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Especially retarded is the camera system: You can move the camera freely using the mouse, but when stopping the mouse it goes back to the standard camera angle behind the car. Gives me a headache and prevents me from getting nice city views while doing my boring A to B driving. Just give me a checkbox to turn that off.Revisiting this after the "Remaster", I cannot tell the difference from the original. Still looks great and sadly plays the same. Bugged out around chapter 14 (paying back the depth -> stuck in loading screen) and could not be bothered to try the, now included for free, DLC.Revisiting this after player Mafia 3, a disgusting hamster wheel of a "game", didn't help the game since now I can see the first iterations of many bad ideas they later brought into Mafia 3.I don't like it, but I still recommend it for everybody who likes boring console cover shooter mechanics and wants to drive nice post WWII cars through a semi interesting american mafia backdrop. Just don't expect anything special.Giving it a thumbs down since steam cannot be bothered to implement a better rating system than this binary nonsense.
