_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II: Definitive Edition is an updated release, a HD remaster, of an already HD game that features enhanced models, textures, changes to lighting and the sound engine of the game. The game does look nicer at in motion. Some changes, like the greasy hair and the somewhat shinier eyes do look a bit strange, and I have noticed a few interesting artifacts with the Ambient Occlusion implementation, but generally, the game does look nicer. The nicer graphics don't necessarily explain the fact the download size of the game is nearly 5 times larger than the original, or the performance hit, but generally, the game does look nicer. As an owner of the original PC version of Mafia II on Steam, I received this version for free, while still keeping the old version in my library, which is a big plus (unlike Rockstar and the 'Complete' Edition of GTA IV that replaced the originals completely).BUT, there are some issues with this re-release, starting with the first thing you see when you launch the game; the launcher is pointless. When I adjusted my settings so it would run in 1080p Borderless, when the game loaded up, it was rendering out at 480p full screen, but in a 1080p frame, so the game was in a tiny corner of my screen, and I had to navigate and change the options through the in-game options menu to get it running in the correct resolution. After getting the game to run 1080p, Borderless, Maximum settings (minus MSAA, which I ran at 4X and Vignette and Chromatic Aberration off because those effects are bad on a good day), I immediately saw they had re-done the pre-rendered cutscenes. Not just an upscaling, but they had re-done from scratch. The pre-rendered scenes look quite a bit better and might run at a higher framerate as well (which might explain the file size increase somewhat). Then the game crashed. After re-launching, Borderless Windowed Mode no longer worked, and when I tried running it through the options menu, the game threw up a load of messages about Nvidia Apex/PhysX, which is still in this version, but significantly gimped, and with no clear option to enable or disable the effects. Also, despite setting it to skip the launcher, every time I restarted, the launcher would load up first.Once I got back onto the game, now in Fullscreen instead of Borderless, it loaded the in-game cutscene, and the audio was only going through my left ear on my headset. In-game cutscenes are mono on my setup, not pre-rendered, not actual gameplay, but the in-game scenes are. The shooty shooty bang bang part ran just fine, and audio was normal. The next in-game cutscene also ran in mono. Then the train station cutscene ran normally, then the in-game drive down the hill ran normally, and then the bar cutscene ran in mono. I was able to fix this by changing the in-game audio option to stereo and restarting the game.Once I got to run around, I saw that the cloth physics were removed. This is disappointing, I have a Nvidia GPU so I was hoping these physics extensions would still work, considering that some PhysX particles are clearly still present, but they are not. Consequently, because some PhysX effects seem to be forced on, there may be a performance hit on AMD GPU's but I do not know for certain so take this statement with a grain of salt. Lacking the full PhysX effect experience has no impact on the actual gameplay, but it is a visual feature that is missing from the Definitive Edition that belies the idea this is the Definitive Edition for some players. Also, note that I did not run the game at an unlocked frame rate, so I can't comment on whether or not they fixed the bugs caused by running at over 100 FPS, such as the slow-motion glitch. Reading around suggests they have fixed them, but I cannot confirm that right now.Graphically, as mentioned, the remaster is a mixed bag. Faces have benefited the most, but the eyes and hair look a little strange sometimes, appearing far shinier than they did originally. Artwork is generally of a higher resolution, pre-rendered cutscenes are completely rebuilt from scratch to use higher quality assets and run at a higher resolution and framerate. Lighting changes, such as sun effects and shadows have changed, with a stronger Ambient Occlusion process (with mixed results), higher quality shadows, including better actor self-shadowing, and a draw distance that seems to be further pushed back than it was before. The game generally looks better, although some of the artistic changes might throw you off.Audio-wise, the soundtrack is apparently equal to what was in the base game in 2016, down 16 music tracks from the original release, some of which are on the better known side of soundtrack as well. It's far from what could be a definitive release, not quite on the same level as GTA IV, or the current state of the original Mafia if you buy it on Steam now, but that's little comfort. You are not getting the full original soundtrack experience. Apparently, some further tracks are also missing from the Joe's Adventures DLC pack, but I can't verify that myself, as I don't really want to play this version of Mafia II any further due to those technical issues. There is a mod to re-add the missing music, but you shouldn't have to mod a game to get the original intended experience. Audio mixing, by my ear, sounds a bit off in some places. Some sound effects have been replaced with higher quality assets that again I think work quite well but sound mixing seems off, even after I fixed the mono sound in some of the cutscenes, something still seemed off compared to what I was expecting to hear, as though the sound mixing in-game was wrong, with loud effects playing too quietly, something that does not occur in cutscenes, where instead it seems to lean a lot on my left speaker channel.Overall, I can't recommend playing this version over the original. It does look nicer, but there are too many issues that make the Definitive Edition an inferior edition to the original version, which is still in your library and included in this versions purchase (or on GoG). Play the classic version instead. It doesn't look far worse (Mafia II still looks quite good) and suffers from far fewer bugs. Because this is a remastered compilation, it doesn't add anything, so you aren't missing out on any additional content unless you want to play the DLC mission packs (which aren't very good to be honest), and the original might not crash as often either.Mafia II is a great game; the remaster is not the best way to play if you just want to play the game. The new version does not make a good game bad by any means (granted, I stopped playing before the end of hour two because I had enough of having to stop, drop out, tweak and come back to get the damn thing to work), but it is a sub-par re-release. Fortunately, unlike Rockstar, 2K aren't forcing you to use this version if you don't want to and unlike Rockstar's 'Complete Edition' mess, there are actual improvements that can be mentioned. The original release still works perfectly as long as you keep under 100 FPS on modern operating systems, it's also a HD game with a far smaller install size. There are too many drawbacks to truly call this game a definitive release. The classic release is included in this package, unlike GTA IV now, so I would recommend playing that version instead if you've never played Mafia II before.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II: Definitive Edition takes you back to the lively streets of Empire Bay in the 1950s, and it really brings the world to life.One of the cool things is how NPCs act. You’ll see them slip on ice or spill their coffee, making the world feel real and full of surprises. Random events, like cars breaking down, keep things interesting and engaging.The driving mechanics are fantastic. Cars handle really well, and you can see the wheels moving and the body swaying as you drive. In winter, snow falls off the roof, and the paint gets dirty just like in real life. It’s these little details that make driving enjoyable.You can also rob stores, and the chaos that follows is a blast. When you use your tommy gun, you can shatter displays and create mayhem. Plus, when you honk your horn, NPC cars actually move out of the way, which is a nice touch.The environment is packed with details. You can open windows in your house, grab food from the fridge, and watch life happening outside. The streets are filled with little things that make the world feel alive.The story of Vito Scaletta is gripping, and it kept me hooked for hours. The characters are well-written, and the voice acting really draws you in.The soundtrack is also a highlight, featuring great music from the 1950s that fits perfectly with the game’s vibe.In short, Mafia II: Definitive Edition is a fantastic revival of a classic. With its detailed world, fun gameplay, and great story, it’s definitely worth checking out for both longtime fans and newcomers.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute master piece of a game and by far the best story line in any game I have played (far better than gta or rd2 or any other mafia) with perfect characters and perfect setting. Some may say the graphics or logistics of the game aren't very good but that's just how it was styled and it suits it (it is also an 'older game'). The only part I disliked was how all the things that u would use in a 'free roam' were available during the chapters/missions which when I was playing it was focused on completing the missions, not driving round taking up all the offer. The story line was a bit repetitive on how we just entered families got connections then lost it all the money (which was pointless because where were you spending it during mission?). But this was all made up for in the masterpiece of a plot of switching between 1945 and 51. Also adding Vito's prison punishment was a good addition although a lot of people died (including his mother which I felt were slightly unneeded which let to a slightly brutal overall story line). When Vito and Joe were separated I felt a bit of discomfort and that this wasn't really needed (It was implied Joe was killed) which gave a slight backlash on my opinions on Vito not stopping to save his friend who gave up a lot for each other. I also thought it wasn't long enough but that may have been my fault because I only played it on two separate occasions for even amounts of time (roughly 7 hours each). All in all the realism in the game to say it really was just a chapter game (I know you can load into the DLC and replay chapters but its not the same) was incredible I just wish when you point your gun at 'irenic' NPCs you could rob them, but that's a very picky problem. All in all this is my number 1 game I have every played even though I won't often visit, just the sheer genius of the story line will do it for me. I tried mafia 3 a while back a was extremely underwhelmed at how lazy and repetitive it was but I have heard with the recent DLCs it was 'ok' but I thought it was utter crap, so maybe I shall try it again but mafia 2 definitive edition will always be number 1. Cars were also liked as I am a big fan of classic cars especially Americans, which brings me back to how perfect the setting was for this game. I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND to anyone who is considering a piece of the mafia trilogy, this is the one to go for. I just wish there was more!EDIT: The voice over was also a bonus It made it feel real.

_childDocuments_.review: They should have called it 'Special Edition'Here original Vitto is happy to see Joe's gal pal and in the remaster its like he came back from the war castrated or something.Over here we have Vitto visiting Joe at his place for the first time and we can tell right away original Joe is making eye contact and happy to see the idiot he got to take the rap for him a few years back but in the remake he forgot to put his dentures on and got some crappy face surgery work.Original Joe going in for a warm embrace of his pal while Remaster Joe looks like hes in a bad state and is about to puke his guts all over Vitto. The super sharp pockmarks make it all worth it though.It's not all bad though in game around the city the sharper material textures are a noticeable improvement but there's all kinds of visual glitches and the performance hit relative to the original is huge for an overall not too impressive improvement in graphical fidelity that's obviously gone awry when it comes to the character cutscenes.But hey at least its free (for mafia 2 owners) and we still got the original in full working order. I'd suggest just playing the original over this remake if its your first time playing the game. The cutscenes are clearly better in the original and the story usually is considered the main draw of the mafia series.For vets that want to drive around a nicer looking city you can dive right in or wait for a patch or two that might truly make this version a remaster over the original.Oh also you might as well see it for yourself in action side by sideHave a nice day and a prosperous tomorrow.

_childDocuments_.review: GRAND THEFT MEATBALL: OLIVE GARDEN EDITIONMafia II is a game I’m so slowly becoming obsessed with. I only have five hours on it so far, but the original release is pretty good! However, it’s very much a game from 2010 with jagged anti-aliasing and Xbox 360 vibes. So out of curiosity, I wanted to check out the remaster to see if it ran better and looked a little more clean…But remember, kids: Most remasters are slimy, cynical cash-grabs that ruin everything we love about old games. Mafia II: Definitive Edition is a mistake born out of laziness and piss poor optimization. All the care and love that went into the remake for the first Mafia is lost here. Just slather some hi-res textures and bad saturation and call it definitive. What a mudda fwuckin’ joke! First of all, it’s a major downgrade visually. Yeah, the original wasn’t much of a looker even by 2010 standards, but this issue was remedied by great retro filtering, the level of detail found in the streets of Empire City, and the utilization of physx particle effects. The remaster has all of that, but the aesthetic is completely ruined by over-saturation and the loss of graphical nuances (fabric physx and character animations). Yet, textures are overhauled significantly with some improvements, but they are so insignificant to the overall experience. Secondly, the game is a glitchy mess. Like more so than the original game! Flickering effects and performance issues are still prevalent 2 years later. The original Mafia II had fps drop, but the fact that it wasn’t patched for a modern release is the pinnacle of laziness. Those 50GB didn’t do  nothin’!This game is a literal waste of space. Even though I got it for free, I would trade it in for a refund. Keep playing the original.

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr: This game is worth playing but the remaster is very half-assed and it's overpriced at $30, since Steam forces me to make a binary choice I would say NOT RECOMMENDED... AT FULL PRICE. Wait for a sale.Let's be clear about what Mafia II Definitive Edition is: it's a very lazy graphical remaster with no other meaningful enhancements made to the original game from a decade ago. You can watch side-by-side comparison videos and see how little noticeable difference there is. Vito has blue eyes now and looks a little more tan? Maybe the textures on cars are a little sharper? Basically this looks like the original game with a reshade mod enabled. Apparently they've fixed some bugs which affected the original game on high refresh rate monitors (I was still a 60hz pleb back when I played the original so I can't say), but in exchange they've removed the PhysX elements for some reason? If you were hoping for, say, some of the additional content notoriously cut during the Mafia II's development to be restored here, fuhgeddaboutit.  Since I got Mafia II Definitive Edition for free for owning the "classic" version of the game, I guess I can't complain too much, but if I paid for this, I'd be upset. Underwhelming graphical upgrades and cut content "might have beens" aside, Mafia II is still a game worth playing, and didn't get as much respect as it deserved because people expected it to be GTA with fedoras, which it just isn't. However, while it's an enjoyable experience, it's also quite a short one. If you're wanting to play the game for the first time you're looking at paying thirty bucks for 10-15 hours of gameplay, which is a bit dear. If they still sold the "classic" edition of the game at a lower price I would say just buy that - buuuut, they don't. That being the case: If you haven't played the game before, get it, but get it on sale. If you've played it before, there is no reason to play the "Definitive Edition" apart from nostalgia, it plays and even looks (almost) exactly the same as the game you remember.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the main game and IMO this re-release is great. I got this as I own the original release of Mafia II, and unbelievably, all the DLC came with it free as well, which I never owned before, so I'll be enjoying them soon.Sure, its got some strange bugs, glitchy facial expressions and some of the achievements don't work (note how I've completed the game but somehow didn't get the achievements for completing certain chapters) but overall the presentation is very good. A lot of hate for the new lighting system, but I personally think Empire Bay at night looks much, much better.Gunplay is the same, simple, straightforward and satisfying. Driving is fun and varied, and incredibly unforgiving.Mafia II is short, but the attention to detail throughout the game is insane - from hubcaps rolling off your car when driving erratically, your car getting dirtier the more you drive in the snow, to the way the citizens of the city start the game not knowing who you are, to them knowing exactly who you are. Memorable levels, memorable chapters, memorable characters.Still one of all time favourite game endings.

_childDocuments_.review: The main game has a very good story. Maybe it could be longer, but I'm fine with it. You will visit many interesting places in Empire Bay city. You will play as Vito Scaletta who came to the USA with his parents and sister to start a new life. You will want to be a real gangster, but later you will see it isn't as easy as it looks. I play it in the Czech language and I must say dubbing is perfect. There are many funny buzzwords and smile situations.DLC pack will double your playtime. It's not like the main story. There are arcade missions where you go destroy stuff, hijack cars and kill some guys. What I miss in DLCs are cutscenes. Before nearly every mission you have only text without dubbing. Joe's Adventures has 4 story missions but Jimmy's Betrayal and Vendetta have fewer missions with cutscenes. I would appreciate it when mission descriptions have dubbing at least. Overall DLCs are fun to play. You have free-roam where you can do anything that you want.The game has very good music. You can listen to the radio in a car with many nice old songs from the 40s and 50s that make you feel you are really in the 40s or 50s years of the 20th century. Also, the cars list offers pretty cars and the game has awesome car handling. Not awesome, it's one of the best car handlings in open-world games. When you choose simulation in options you will need to drive really carefully if you don't want to end in a tree or wall. Mafia 2 offers a good selection of weapons. You can find here classic Thompson 1928 or Colt 1911, German rifle Karabiner 98k or Italian submachine gun Beretta Model 38. There are a lot of toys to play with.The graphic is better than in the original game. There is no that a quite strong bloom effect. In the 2010s it was fine but nowadays I'm happy it's not here. Textures are better and the whole Empire Bay looks updated.Both the main game and DLCs have quite a lot of bugs. Sometimes face is bugged in a cutscene, people are doing stupid on street things like jumping over a fence without reason. Another bad thing is optimization. There are some FPS drops if you have NVIDIA PhysX enabled. Also, the game crashed a few times during my playthrough. And there is one thing that is not a problem of remaster but Mafia 2. Devs should make more missions in the 40s in snow. In the main story, there are only a few missions in snow and in DLCs, there is only one in Joe's Adventures. Snow is well made here and fun to drive. Cars feel like they are driving on snow. The devs didn't use the potential of snow.

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard about the Mafia Trilogy being remasterd, Mafia 2 wasn't my first thought, I thought about the wonderful and underrated Mafia: The City of Lost Heaven, then I heard we were getting Mafia 2 remastered three months before the first one, so why not go back to it again ?In all honesty, the original game has aged well, even 10 years later it still looks pretty good considering the technology. Mafia II : Definitive Edition keeps things fresh thanks to newer texture and shadows. But that's pretty much all you'll get from this edition.The game is still infected with bugs all over the place, from weird AI to visual glitches. Outside of that, the game feels like the original, meaning you'll still get this great campaign with this underlying feeling that they cut so much content out of this wonderful game. Should you play it again ? Of course, but don't expect it to be the Mafia II we were supposed to get years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game with decent atmosphere. Very story-driven. The open-world is kind of just scenery filler. Once you've seen it, there's not much point in it other than your progression through the story, meaning there's not much to do in this game outside of the story, sadly. Some clunky gameplay, which becomes particularly relevant in combat situations or when you get caught by the police, who will fire on you non-stop for merely chipping someone's vehicle or even when you're the victim of NPCs attacking you (at least, as far as they know) lol. Examples of clunky gameplay are:1. Sometimes your guy might switch to the wrong side of cover when you're trying to aim the opposite way2. There may be times where your guy doesn't switch to his weapon on time in the heat of the moment, getting you killed.3. NPCs may take cover in front of you before you do. In this situation, it can be difficult to get them off on time, and you can get lit up by gunfire as a result of this.4. When you pull someone out of their car, the game won't automatically put you in the car, but instead force you to press the action button again to get in it. Might be a personal choice of theirs, but seems counterproductive to the idea of stealing people's cars and can negatively affect you in a heated situation, especially if you forget how it works.5. Molotovs will sometimes hurt you when their effects are physically nowhere near you, which can get you killed, obviously.The game design is quite outdated in those ways and can be quite frustrating.Also, be mindful that the checkpoint system can be quite bad too, and set you some ways back if you happen to die at a certain point (this can be especially frustrating if you played on Hard difficulty like me).Overall, these gripes are annoying but fairly minor for the most part. There are only a few situations where it might impact you greatly, unless you play like an absolute madman. Otherwise, the game is a reasonably fun, atmospheric story that will take you through a variety of interesting scenarios. I think it's worth experiencing once. Not much replayability though, unless you like collecting magazines and cars but hadn't done so already in your first playthrough. It's a reasonably short game if you just go through the story the whole time.Keep in mind I have not played any of the DLCs as of the writing of this review.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Mafia games back when they first came out and I have really enjoyed the definitive editions of Mafia and mafia II. While I think that Mafia is the best of the three games. Mafia II offers a charm that is difficult to come by with games that are released today. I especially enjoyed the time jump to 1951 and getting to hear music that I grew up listening to through movies set in the 50's or my grandmother or my mother playing rock n' roll from the 50's. With innovative mechanics for its time, and a map small but one that doesn't feel like it is small. A decent enough story with memorable characters, especially Joe. The variety of cars was nice too. The game isn't too long either, which is a nice change of pace in an industry that is over-saturated with games that can easily span for hundreds of hours, unless you basically rush the experience.Some issues that I had was that the gameplay does feel dated. The shooting mechanics are simple but feel rather stiff and there is a lot of shooting in this game. Driving feels dated but is actually a lot of fun! I felt that the sound design was pretty good! The cars, the music, VOs... the only thing to really suffer sound wise was the guns. Of which for a game like there was a good variety, but would have liked to see some more rifles. One issue that I had is that the M1 Garand doesn't make its famous PING sound when the enbloc clip ejects. My biggest disappointment with Mafia II is that it didn't get the same make over as Mafia Definitive Edition. Overall a fun experience for Mafia fans and those who have never played Mafia (I do recommend starting with Mafia)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of problems. First off, it is barely any different from the original release a decade ago. It went from looking like a game that was published in 2010 to one that was published in 2012. It's very clear they only re-released this game as a gimmick to advertise for the original Mafia remaster. This game does not come close to meeting the standards of a game released in 2020. The animations are very minimalistic, choppy, not fluid, and unpolished. There are several visual and audio glitches and bugs, none of them game breaking, but annoyance nevertheless. They did fix one game breaking bug from the original release in the second to last mission where you could not progress, which is good. All this being said, the game is still worth playing. The story is one of the best narratives from this genre, even if it may not hold up in places. I'm glad 2k made the decision to give everyone that owned the original versions of Mafia 2 and 3 the definitive editions for free. There would have been even more backlash otherwise. It was also a nice gesture to include the DLC expansions with the definitive edition, as I never would have played them otherwise. They shouldnt have released the definitive edition for this game however. They should have waited until Mafia 1 remastered was finished, and then gave Mafia 2 the same treatment. Yeah, it would have been resource heavy and they might have other projects they want to focus on, but it's a missed opportunity with a game that deserves a remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Downtown (north of the docks) there is a clothes shop that is bigger than the usual ones, whith some more exlusive clothing.The police can recognize you based on you appearance, you car, or both. So even if you change your clothes, the cops will still give chase if you drive a stolen car. You can get rid of your wanted level by changing the licence plates of your car, getting a new outfit or using a telephone kiosk to call a contact and bribe the police. The wanted logo will give you a hint (i.e. if it's a license plate, you need a different car; a wanted poster, change your clothes)Shops and gas stations can be robbed (owners of gun shops will fire back at you!) and cars can be sold at the junkyard and the docks. There's really not much to spend your money on (getting your shoes shined!), though, and you will lose all your savings several times throughout the story (around every 5 chapters or so).Two people you meet in the story, Guiseppe and that military guy, own stores with some unique weaponry.Cars do not become "surrogate health bars" in this game; crashing your car at high speeds (or being crashed into, for that matter) does damage and can kill you!When driving, cops only really notice car collisions they see, collisions with their vehicles and speeding. You can run stop signs and red lights at your leisure (so long as you aren't breaking one of those three "rules").There are only a couple missions with branches in them (usually "Do/don't do X, get more money"); seeing as money is only temporary, don't bother going back to replay them for a better outcome. The branches don't change anything; issues that arise should you fail an "optional objective" are the same as if you succeed.Vito is a good brother!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game from a time when writers weren't afraid to tell a story.+/- Light remaster. This is not a complete remaster. Its only upgraded textures and additional post processing. Sometimes certain PP effects don't work well.+/- Semi open world. There is no free roam at all. Any time you are alone without a timed objective you are free to explore the city. There isn't much to do besides grab collectables. Much like the Mafia 1 it just facilitates the story.+ Great story with memorable characters.+ Voice Acting is very good.+ Immersive world design+ Vehicles are well designed unlicensed recreations.+ Driving physics are interesting on simulation. Attention to detail with effective transmission modelling and tire compression under these heavy vehicles using old tire technology. Descent damage modelling.+ Combat is well made with focus on realism. All weapons are one shots to the head. Just consider magazine size and dispersion for the best results. Hand to hand combat is okay. It takes a little getting used to. Particularly on hard difficulty.+ Music selection is descent and adds to immersion.+ GPU accelerated physics/PHYSX. Works wonders for this game(and most other games its implemented in). A surprising amount of deformation and particles breaking off of objects makes environments more believable and interesting.+ Collectables. For once they are contextual and relate to the games world rather than being random meaningless objects(granted they still don't actually do anything). Real images from early playboys and wanted posters are the exploration collectables. The others are progress based.- Post Processing. Some of the new effects don't work correctly. Such as blinding lens flares/bloom in certain lighting scenarios.- Particles. Some physics particles accumulate without being deleted until going out of range causing massive lag spikes in a few specific scenarios.

_childDocuments_.review: "You know something, Carlo? For the last 10 years, all I done was kill. I killed for my country, I killed for my family, I killed anybody that got in my way. But this one? This one's for me" (Vito Scaletta).  An action-adventure game and a sequel to Mafia game, Mafia 2 Definitive Edition is the remake of the 2010 Mafia 2 game.  While worse than Mafia 1 Definitive Edition (that had a great story, great gameplay and better graphics), Mafia 2 Definitive Edition may be a choice for the fans of the series, provided they did not play the original game. Good-buy if on sale.- This review is a personal opinion. Try the game for yourself.- Game was played on max graphics setting and ultrawide resolution.- This is the definitive, remastered edition of the game and includes all 3 DLCs.- I did not play the original 2010 game.- The plot takes place a decade after the Mafia game setting, in the fictional city of Empire Bay during the 1940s–early 1950s and follows the life of the Sicilian immigrant Vito Scaletta and his story of climbing the Mafia family ladder, with both larger reward and consequence.- You can steal and drive any vehicle (including trucks), you can kill anyone (except companions).- Visit body shops to repair, personalize cars and enhance their performance.- In comparison with Mafia 1, this game uses a handbrake to help car make tight turns at high speeds.- You can make use of cash to bribe police and you can use phone booths to call-in a bribe and lose your red wanted status.- Make use of cover very often (press CTRL near walls or obstacles), it is an essential mechanic of shooting gameplay in this game.- Obviously, the proper order to play the games is Mafia, Mafia 2, Mafia 3, not the release order (Mafia Definitive was released after Mafia 2 Definitive and Mafia 3 Definitive Editions). Mafia  Definitive Edition remains by far the best game of the remastered series.- An open-world design of a large city with parts modeled on New York City, Boston, Detroit, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Chicago, along 19 story chapters plus prologue (15 chapters from base game and 4 more story chapters from DLC), featuring remastered graphics and real-time generated cutscenes. A narrative about family, loyalty, betrayal and greed, a decent story about Mafia.- The story starts quite slow-paced and you may say even uninteresting, but it gets a lot better at the end of Chapter 5.- Nice atmosphere and design, a beautiful city and around 50 famous drivable and upgradable epoch vehicles.- Good soundtrack (and car radio music from the era).- Good optimization, high fps count.- Some collectibles (Playboy magazines and Wanted posters) for completionists.- Partial ultrawide support (although real-time generated not pre-rendered, cutscenes are pillarboxed).- The story ends abruptly and very unsatisfying.- The lack of manual save (the game saves only at the beginning of story missions and at certain checkpoints) may create problems when you and exit the game without starting a new story mission (unless you managed to reach a checkpoint, everything will be gone when you restart the game).- The remastered graphics do not look quite 2020, some textures and the cutscenes still look old and face animations are not the best around, not much of an improvement over the 2010 original game. Mafia 1 Definitive Edition looks a lot better than this one.- No side missions available.- The DLCs are not much of a content. The first 2 DLCs deal with a guy named Jimmy, without any connection with the main story. The third DLC (Joey's Adventures) is about Vito's friend Joe and should have been either part of the base game or deleted.- Very few bugs, but they are still a thing.- Cars get damage extremely easy. The fact that you have to repair cars very often (and refuel them), along with feeding your character to recover health is too old style and just a gameplay filler.- Map directions can be confusing when showing inside doors or building entrances.- You must dress again every single time you get up from bed (and you must go to bed to progress to the next chapter).- Gameplay is a bit boring, around 60% of the time you will be driving in traffic (and compared to Mafia 1 Definitive Edition, here you cannot skip driving). Some of the missions are just a waste of time, you must drive around town to sell stamps or cigarettes or whatever. The gameplay also combines too many styles and requirements (shooting, brawling, stealth action, racing, adventure, cars management, evading police, etc.) resulting a GTA kind of mix with Yakuza-like character management (health, weapons, ammo and money). This inconsistency in gameplay actions can become annoying for some players.- The lock-picking feature is also just a gameplay filler (most of the time I used Q to smash car's windows). You can make good use of it only to lock-pick a few of building doors and cars and one safe-box in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: "Mafia II: Definitive Edition" falls disappointingly short of expectations, particularly when compared to its predecessor. The graphics are a glaring disappointment, resembling a parody when juxtaposed with the visual excellence of the first game. Character movement further compounds the letdown, awkwardly reminiscent of the clunky animation seen in "Alan Wake" before its much-needed remaster. Adding to the dismay, the characters in "Mafia II: Definitive Edition" appear cartoonish, their movements unnatural and detached from any semblance of realism. This departure from the lifelike portrayals seen in the first installment only serves to diminish the immersive quality of the game.So far, equally disheartening is the plot, which fails to measure up to the compelling narrative of "Mafia I: Definitive Edition." The story lacks the excitement and intrigue that captivated me in the original game, leaving a void where the anticipation for a gripping tale once stood. Nevertheless, I will continue playing the game with the expectation that my perspective might undergo a positive shift.Either way, to compound the frustration, the controls have undergone alterations from the first game, introducing a level of inconvenience and discomfort for players familiar with the intuitive setup of the initial installment. Overall, "Mafia II: Definitive Edition" pales in comparison to its predecessor, marred by lackluster graphics, unnatural character animations, a lackluster plot, and questionable control changes that contribute to an overall unsatisfactory gaming experience. The intention behind the remastered version is supposed to give the game the appearance of a 2020 release rather than one from 2012.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 2: Definitive Edition is at best an okay remaster of an otherwise great game. Some benefits of getting the Definitive Edition is the ability to experience Mafia 2 with a more modern flare. However with this edition comes new issues - First, aspects of the original game have been censored which takes away from the true experience of the game as it was intended back in 2010. Furthermore new glitches appear at cutscenes now, whether characters are missing half their head, models missing eyes, or looking elsewhere completely, there are issues. Finally the crashing issues that experienced while playing the DLC's that weren't issues found with the original game. Despite these aforementioned issues I DO recommend the Definitive Edition, Mafia 2 will always be a fun and classic experience and I appreciate the attention it deserves. Being able to experience each story with it's enhanced look is worth it in all regards. I do suggest buying this game if it's on a sale though.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry Vito, a remaster wasn't a part of the deal.Mafia is a series of games that followed me throughout the decades. Mafia II in particular was a very important game to me. And with a heavy heart, I have to tell you all to save your cash and stay away from this re-bastardisation. Graphically, you might not notice any difference, but while having a 2080ti and a 3900x, this game still stutters like a snitch at gunpoint. Suits look like 2d textures, and small details have a faint reminiscence of low-quality JPEGs. Most annoying and immersion breaking bug is Vito's head popping through the brim of the hats.Gameplay is mostly the same, however AI is much glitchier than it used to be in the original release. Cover doesn't work sometimes, and NPCs will act out of character, ruining missions and wasting your time. It all just seems off.The saddest thing is, it seems like this game that was important to me and many of my friends got a botched re-shade mod. It seems like a very brutal fate for a game of this caliber, and it wasn't taken out with a .45 or 9 mil -- it was killed because no one cared.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is good but there's a big problem. The game is:* ~50% - driving (extremely boring)* ~10% - boxing (extremely boring)* ~25% - shooting (not bad but not very good either)* ~15% - cutscenesSo, ~60% of the game is just a waste of time; the story is basically locked behind a "drive wall". if you didn't have to drive from one part of the completely dead city to another several times per chapter and if not for the dumb fights, you could complete it in ~5-7 hours depending on the difficulty setting. Dead open worlds not only kill the replayability of a game but also make the first playthrough hardly bearable.There's another issue but I think it's specific to only the Definitive Edition. But what's really bad is the performance, 70-100 FPS on RTX3080TI is unacceptable, game stutters all the time, in some locations the FPS counter drops to ~20 for no reason. _childDocuments_.review: This game's a borrower, and nothing original or groundbreaking ever comes from it. Were it just for the main character being named after one of the Marlon Brandon's more iconic roles or, hell, flat out looking like a young Marlon Brandon, the game wouldn't be half as bad. Yet, aside from fairly impressive car physics or AI, there's nothing to praise it for. Mediocre story that ends nowhere, it's awkward pacing filled with pointless and cliche side stories, somewhat poor writing with it's edgy world view, at times hideous voice acting and sound mixing are the silent killers of this game. Furthermore, the barren open world feels only as means to pad out the play time as there's nothing to do in it, save it for collecting useless collectibles or money that, in the end, has no worth in this game. Anyone jonesing for some deep gangster stuff after watching flicks such as Godfather or Scarface ought to look elsewhere.There's heart in this game, but good intentions count for nothing if it amounts to nothing.

Here we have a remastered version labeled as “Definitive Edition” where the developers put little effort in it. Basically we do not have much more than HD graphics, cool snow and some tweaks here and there. In the end, the game feels buggy with NPC’s, and even our own character, do not move their lips in some cutscenes and in some others they are invisible. And on top of all the bugs the game feels laggy and I was not playing with the same graphic card that I had when the original game released in 2011 I was playing it on a 3060 Ti. It is a mess how a game Mafia 2 can be destroyed with a “remaster” job like this.Imagine how funny it would be if one day they decide to remake it. Since this is already the “Definitive Edition” what would they call the new version? “Definitive Definitive Edition”, “Real Definitive Edition” or “This time the Definitive Edition”Anyway, as I said before I do not recommend this to anyone. It is sad because I did like the game, I like the trilogy but this is not the way. Surely for many players that never played Mafia 2, this will be unnoticed and you may like it despite the many issues of the game’s version. After all, now, you cannot buy the classic version anymore, when you buy this you get the classic version for free and surprise surprise what do you gonna try to play? (Big mistake).

Let's not forget there are also typos on main mission brief/art screens - embarrassing.I almost forgot, there are multiple times throughout the story where the unknowing player will rage and/or decide to load a previous save wasting a few hours of story progression when certain story events happen - trust me, its better than taking the major Ls when they drop those bombs on you. One time in particular is quite damaging if you aren't an impulse spender. I can't say much else without spoilers. This is the worst game of the trilogy. The only good thing about this 2nd installment in the Mafia franchise, is the voice acting - mainly Joe. Other than that, ♥♥♥♥ game in an amazing series. I tried to push through, and managed to get through the main story. The DLCs are cancer. Joe's adventure is decent, but about 50% though you want to put holes in your monitor. I bought the trilogy, while already having mafia 3, thinking I could gift the extra Mafia 3 or get a discount for already having it. Nope.It's unfortunate considering how great 1 and 3 are.I have 28 hours logged on Mafia 1 DE, I rate it 4.5/5.I have 95 hours logged on Mafia 3 DE, I rate it 5/5.After 27 hours of Mafia 2 DE, I rate it a 2/5. Garbage. Don't waste your time unless you, like me, need(ed) to finish the trilogy. It saddens me that my first review after 50+ games and countless hours of enjoyment has to be a negative one. I will be forced to go and write the deserving positive reviews for all those games I didn't give kudos to.Thanks for that.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Mafia 2 veteran with probably well over 4k hours(in a non-Steam version of it) I have to say that this remaster is really underwhelming in some respects. Yes, I got the Definitive edition for free, and I am grateful for that, what I am NOT OK with on the other hand is that other people who have not purchased the classic version of this game have to pay for a rushed, buggy and non-optimised remaster. 9 hours in this game and I have already noticed many props that haven't received a texture enhancement, then there's the mystery surrounding the clothing physics, the glitchy debris, flickering smoke and steam particles, FPS drops that seemingly have no source, which I'm not okay with either. Some people play for the visuals too, don't they? SO if you're gonna charge me 25GBP for this, at least give me something good? Not an unfinished product? In some cutscenes the NPC's view target is really off, even in the action game.They added new sounds, which again, is really nice, but even with this there's some bugs. Taunt voice lines missing, in chapter Time Well Spent, when you get to the part where you go to the showers, you can't hear the prisoner who's singing anymore, but you can still hear the others throwing tantrum at him for his supposed terrible singing. Why though? Veterans know what I'm talking about here.They done some touch ups to the game's radio soundtrack too, replaced some segments of news bulletins with newly recorded lines, but what for? They sound terrible, I know very well how the old bulletins used to sound like, the sound mix/effects were far more immersive and resembled the sound of an old 40's car radio far more accurately than the new ones, it just seems pointless to me. 2K, you had 10 years at your disposal to make this right, 10 years to think about the cut content. Please, if any of you from 2K read this review, please get your ♥♥♥♥ together and give us updates to this remaster, listen to your community. Do it right, what the hell.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the original Mafia 2 game since it was first published back in 2010. I loved it to the point I still play it no matter what.Of course it has a lot of dust on the code now. However, there are few TRICKS you can use to FIX this underperforming new version:Issue #1 Vito's CLOTH physics are not workingCloth APEX PhysX fix workaround:APEX PhysX effects work properly except the cloth physics in the main game. APEX PhysX works well in the DLCs and with DLC clothing.Solution: Delete CLOTH folder. The game will run on APEX PhysX particles and standard cloth physics (which are still in the game files so no worries)Go to the in-game video settings.Set global settings to "high".Close the game.Go to <path-to-game>\EDIT\APEX folder.Back up the CLOTH folder.Delete the CLOTH folder.You can now change other video settings to your liking. This will change the preset to "custom". If you change the preset to "low", it will disable APEX PhysX.NOTE: You should add it back when you want to play the DLCs.Issue #2 Flickering FOGSet Vsync to FAST or ADAPTIVE in Nvidia Control PanelIssue #3 APEX PhysX DEBRIS doesn't last as long as in Mafia II: ClassicCopy Effects folder from Mafia 2 Classic Version (download and install this version of the game and copy the Effect folder from it).Replace the Effect folder in <path-to-game>\EDIT\APEX.NOTE: Makes PhysX more demanding.#4 Irritating INTRO videos<path-to-game>\pc\sds\videoFrom the video folder, delete or rename the following files:d3t.bikLogos.bikI hope these quick fixes help you enjoy this old lady. Let me know if you need more support. I will look into it.Salute!

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia II is an exceptional game that deserves a 9/10 rating for its compelling storyline, authentic atmosphere, and well-crafted gameplay.Set in the 1940s and 1950s, Mafia II follows the story of Vito Scaletta, a young Italian-American who becomes involved in organized crime. With a narrative that spans several years, Mafia II offers an immersive and engaging story that keeps players on the edge of their seats.The game's world is meticulously designed, with an accurate representation of the time period that includes everything from the cars and clothing to the music and architecture. The attention to detail is impressive, and it creates an authentic and immersive atmosphere that is rarely seen in video games.The gameplay in Mafia II is also well-crafted, with a perfect balance of action, exploration, and driving mechanics. The shooting and cover mechanics are responsive and satisfying, while the driving feels smooth and intuitive.

_childDocuments_.review: 10 Years of appreciation and love for this game only to be given an unexpected remaster of the original for free, I was down.So I will add, this game is brilliant, the graphics were ahead of their time and to this day still hold up, now with the definitive edition even more so than before. Mafia II is set in a fictionalised version of New York city from the 1940s through the 1950s in what can only be described as a gritty yet realistic time period sandbox. As Vito, you work your way up through the ranks (so to speak) as a member of, you guessed it, the Mafia and it's told through a well written story of family and betrayal.I did not get my chance to play the original Mafia, but despite that I fell in love with Mafia II and to this day I will recommend this game well before it's follow up, Mafia III which frankly let me down in so many ways, be it graphically inferior in many ways to its predecessor and a story that does not hold up to the name that is 'Mafia'. So I beg you, play Mafia II, you'll be doing yourself a favour and perhaps adding yet another game to your ever growing list of timeless classics.

_childDocuments_.review: I was optimistic when I started the game: Slightly better graphics, improved gun sounds, slight changes here and there, lots of particles (for example when you shoot up the bar and all those tiny wooden pieces drop everywhere is cool), but it eats your PC on that specific mission. My PC isn't the strongest in the world, but it isn't a bad one either. Normally, the game went smoothly at max graphics, 900p, 60 fps, but when you have to shoot up the bar, or in another mission some particles starting to spawn in huge quantities, then all hell brakes loose. My PC dropped to 18 fps, it was horrible until I got out that specific location on the mission, The Wild Ones. I had to get away from that location ASAP, had to travel hundreds of meters until my PC regained it's energy. It looks good when those particles fall everywhere, but was it necessary? It puts heavy weight to the CPU, it's a very CPU intense feature, and almost unnecessary. I'm glad for the Mafia 3 extras, like the Samson Drifter (my favourite car in the Mafia series), Lincoln's outfit etc., but compared to new things and small graphical update there are lots of bugs. Bugs, bugs, glitches everywhere. Some funny things happened to me, and I was optimistic about them at first sight, but later it just became annoying. If you're really desperate for the Definitive Edition, don't buy it for 29,99EUR, instead buy the old (2010) edition, and you'll get the DE with it. I owned/own the basic Mafia 2 with DLCs and Mafia 3 + SP and I automatically received the DE for both of them.

_childDocuments_.review: After taking a bullet during World War II and returning home to Empire Bay on leave, Sicilian immigrant Vito Scaletta discovers that his late father was indebted to a loan shark. He needs to make a lot of money fast, and thanks to his career criminal best friend Joe, soon becomes entangled with the mob. As Vito, you need to prove yourself by committing crimes of escalating reward, status, and consequence. But what happens when your motivations become less about necessity and more about greed? When having it all is not enough? For the first time ever, Mafia II: Definitive Edition packs the entire Mafia II crime drama into one HD package. HDR and 4K resolution are supported on PC as well as on PlayStation®4 Pro and Xbox One X consoles. Mafia II: Definitive Edition also benefits from improved facial animations to give cutscenes an even more cinematic feel. While technological and graphical improvements have given Empire Bay and its inhabitants a visual overhaul, Vito's timeless story is unchanged.

detailed_description: Mafia: Trilogy - Complete Your Collection Includes main games and DLC releases. Mafia: Definitive Edition Re-made from the ground up, rise through the ranks of the mafia during the Prohibition-era. After an inadvertent brush with the mob, Tommy Angelo is reluctantly thrust into the world of organized crime. Initially uneasy about falling in with the Salieri family, the rewards become too big to ignore. Mafia II: Definitive Edition Remastered in HD, live the life of a gangster during the Golden-era of organized crime. War hero Vito Scaletta becomes entangled with the mob in hopes of paying his father’s debts. Alongside his buddy Joe, Vito works to prove himself, climbing the family ladder with crimes of larger reward, status and consequence. Mafia III: Definitive Edition After years of combat in Vietnam, Lincoln Clay’s surrogate family, the black mob, is betrayed and killed by the Italian Mafia. Lincoln builds a new family on the ashes of the old, blazing a path of revenge through the Mafioso responsible. About the Game Part one of the Mafia crime saga - 1930s, Lost Heaven, IL Re-made from the ground up, rise through the ranks of the Mafia during the Prohibition era of organized crime. After a run-in with the mob, cab driver Tommy Angelo is thrust into a deadly underworld. Initially uneasy about falling in with the Salieri crime family, Tommy soon finds that the rewards are too big to ignore. Play a Mob Movie: Live the life of a Prohibition-era gangster and rise through the ranks of the Mafia. Lost Heaven, IL: Recreated 1930's cityscape, filled with interwar architecture, cars and culture to see, hear and interact with. Re-Made Classic: Faithfully recreated, with expanded story, gameplay and original score. This is the Mafia you remembered and much more. Own Mafia: Definitive Edition to unlock Tommy’s Suit and Cab in both Mafia II and Mafia III Definitive Editions .

_childDocuments_.review: First, I will say the story is fantastic, probably one of the best story I have ever seen in a video game. This should tell you how bad the game-play were to justify a not-recommend.Before you started typing on your keyboard, I am not one of those Nintendo fanboys that's like "story is pointless, game-play is everything". In contrast, I consider myself to be very tolerant to annoying mechanics if the game delivers a good story. But, Mafia DE had gone too far.I chose the "simulation" difficulties when starting the game, I have hundreds of hours in milsims like Arma, so I didn't see how a open-world RPG could hinder me; I could not be more wrong. The word "simulation" should be replaced by "ultra hard" or "hell", since it did not add any realism or satisfaction in the game, but only made it almost unbeatable.Let's start with shooting, my "simulated" Tommy Gun now takes 8 shot to kill an enemy, and can't hit anything beyond 20 metres, I feel like even my pistol is more accurate than it. The enemies often do more damage than myself AND outnumber me 20 to 1. The aiming mechanism is also extremely clunky, I ended up  lowering my mouse dpi to 200 in order to vaguely hit anything - but obviously this meant say goodbye to target transition.If shooting missions can at least be completed by dying a few times so that I memorised enemy spawn-points, the driving is just worse. Yes, I am talking about Fair Play - THAT racing mission in case you didn't know - it took me literally 8 hours to beat the mission. My driving is not bad for a casual gamer, but unless you have a few thousands hours in some serious racing game, and have a controller/wheel, don't even attempt to beat it within 3 hours.In conclusion, if you want to play the game without smashing your keyboard, just set it to all easy to enjoy the story. Or better yet, just watch a walk-through online, trust me, you are not missing anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon its original release in 2002, Mafia was a groundbreaking achievemnt. Full of surprises. A vast open world city. Superb attention to period detail And a stirring story that revolved around realized characters. I'd go so far as to call it the "Half-Life" of the GTA genre. It also was hugely unexpected, hailing from a relatively unknown developer at the time.20 years later, the world of the remake may seem small by today's open-world standards, but it still manages to pack a punch, namely in the lovely attention to every detail and the winning story. Sure there's a lot of long cutscenes, but the vibe and execution in those too is spot on. Also of note, there's really nothing extra in terms of side quests or optional tasks so the focus remains squarely on the main story arc.The gameplay itself is about evenly split between driving elements and cover-based third-person shooting elements. The driving has held up admirably, but the shooting is relentlessy brutal even on modest difficulty settings (unless you really enjoy reloading to checkpoints A LOT). In hindsight, that's a characteristic of the original that definitely remains intact. For maximum enjoyment, I suggest setting the shooting difficuly to "Easy" or "Medium" while ratcheting up the driving and police response difficulty to "Simulation."The biggest disappointment is the lack of the entire original soundtrack, which included many period-specific recordings that were popular at the time. It really immersed me in the original game and I truly miss it here. But even that oversight shouldn't stop you from playing, or replaying, this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Being honest... that's awful.I'm 100% sure that positive reviews are given mostly by those people, who haven't played the original game.Of course, I'm not going to talk about graphics, animations and game mechanics, those are nice for today, but THE SOUL of the game was murdered.Thomas used to be a naive, pure guy who was involved in dirty business and there were some conflicts between his conscience and job. "Remade Thomas" is kinda bad guy who is sick of being a taxi driver, he's glad to use an opportunity to become a gangster and about the inner conflicts of his: NONE OF'EM, just making exceptions.Dazzling number of Hollywood cliche made me mad during playing the remake. I agree that the original game was predictable sometimes, but everything was in harmony and that Hollywood part of it was about pushing the story, but not showing tough guys like in remake.To cut a long story short: please, play the original game and then, when remake costs a half of its today's price, buy and play. After that you will understand why Daniel Vavra(the original Mafia's script writer and director) and me can do nothing more than a facepalm looking at the remake. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly faithful remake to the original - it hits all the major points of the plot (that I have encountered so far), but I cannot recommend it due to a number of problems:1. As I progressed through the story, I began to encounter long freezes (they lasted for 2-5 minutes) during gameplay, mostly around when the game autosaved.  The further I got, the more frequent they became.  None of the fixes I found on the internet worked in my case.  Because of this, I could not complete this game.2. The walk toggle could only be turned on while pressing W, and then would also shut itself off every time I let go of W, making it difficult to walk around rather than run around.3. On Normal difficulty, enemies would sometimes show up on the minimap and sometimes they wouldn't, leading me to think an area was clear (and thus get blasted in the face point blank by a guy with a sawn-off who was hiding right around the corner) when it wasn't.4. Melee combat was awkward.  Enemies have long wind ups before they attack and you'd think Tommy could get a quick hit in to interrupt them instead of dodging, but nope, you HAVE TO dodge.5. The music would randomly cut out when playing in borderless windowed mode.6. Also, in borderless windowed mode, the Windows taskbar remained visible and active, meaning I could cause pop-ups to appear over the game screen if my mouse cursor hovered over the taskbar in specific spots.  I had to hide the taskbar in Windows settings to prevent this.

_childDocuments_.review: 18 years ago I played the original and to this day it remains one of my favorites. The story, the setting, all the iconic missions, characters, music, it all felt ahead of other games in the early 2000s.Definitive edition is all that the original was plus a ton of positive enhancements like slightly redesigned (and improved) missions, reworked story details to better fit the narrative, modernised combat and driving (still feels appropriately heavy) and of course all the technical details. The world and the story built in the original have been heavily praised so I'm not gonna discuss them much, let's just say they've aged gracefully and they've mostly been left intact for a reason.The original featured a ton of driving to missions and back. That has been cut down by about half and while many disagree with the change, I'm personally tired of using driving to pad game length. What I'm not happy about being cut are all the freeride extreme missions, which was a mode unlocked after finishing the original which gave you some weird and often hilarious tasks to complete in exchange for unique cars. It gave you extra 6-8 hours of gameplay which was a welcome boost for a game that lasts about 15 hours and doesn't have an insane amount of replay value. The characters looks and voices are completely changed, it's a fairly subjective topic but I prefer the new ones.Everything in this game is at a premium quality except one big thing - gameplay. I suspect you won't be thrilled by the very basic cover shooter combat system and less varied game mechanics (by today's standards). Not that they're bad, they're serviceable, it's just that the bar has been raised quite a bit since 2002 for what games can do and what makes an interesting experience. There's only 2 things you really do in this game and that's driving and shooting. It would be unacceptable for anything other than a remake of an old game to do this in 2020. Of course, if you played the original like me, nostalgia helps quite a bit, or if you played mafia 2 and 3 and liked those, I'm sure you'll like this one as well. For everyone else, I'd say it's definitely worth to play at least once for the story and atmosphere, just keep in mind you probably won't be blown away by the barebones gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia: Definitive Edition isn’t just a game; it’s an elegy to a bygone era, a tapestry woven with ambition, betrayal, and the inescapable weight of consequence. The story it tells may be set in the 1930s, but its themes are timeless, cutting deep into the heart of what it means to chase the American Dream, and the moral decay that often festers beneath.From the moment I stepped into Tommy Angelo’s worn-out shoes, I felt an unmistakable sense of immersion. Lost Heaven isn't just a backdrop, it's a living, breathing entity, an urban sprawl that pulses with the relentless pursuit of survival. Every streetlight, every shadow on the pavement, whispers the stories of those who’ve thrived, fallen, and been forgotten in the cracks of history.The game asks us an unflinching question: What are you willing to sacrifice for power? As I worked my way up through the Salieri crime family, I found myself constantly in moral conflict. Every job I took, every man I silenced, chipped away at Tommy’s soul and at mine. You want to believe you’re doing it for something greater: family, loyalty, self-preservation. But deep down, you know it’s just self-destruction disguised as success.

I don't write reviews because I honestly don't care to waste the time, but if I can save even one poor soul from wasting money on this, then I will be happy.The race mission is unbeatable for the majority of players. There is zero excuse in 2020 to not add a Skip Mission option. If you manage to find a save from someone who by now surely has bloody hands and went through an entire bottle of Excedrin to get it, and you attempt to finally enjoy this dumpster fire you just wasted $40 on, then your reward is the very next mission being a giant glitch fest. Walking next to a certain character, you start to slowly tilt sideways until you fall through the map. Then, after what feels like walking through sludge because these characters move at a snails pace, you get to the part where you have to beat up a bunch of thugs, and since the melee is absolute sh!t, you will have a horrible time repeating the mission over and over. Finally, you manage to get past it, and then you get to fight a bigger thug, and guess what? Yep! ALSO GLITCHED. You'll break your keyboard trying to take him down because he won't go down. He will, however, drift through a fence, turn transparent, or freeze in place. Now bear in mind, this is all only going to happen if you even get past the freezing and the crashing. So, I ask you: Do you enjoy throwing money in the trash? Then sure, buy the game for aesthetic alone because that is the ONLY positive part of this dumpster fire. The people enjoying this and lying in their reviews are the 2002 fanboys wearing rose colored glasses, on their knees giving Hangar 13 the time of their life, OR the neckbeards wanting to be a part of something. If anyone says this is GOTY material, have them committed to a mental institution, ASAP. Thank you to the wonderful Steam rep who heard my cries and refunded my money. He is the hero we all need.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic remake of the OG Mafia. The devs really did put a lot of effort into the visual overhaul of the cities' ambience and graphics, as well as the gameplay in general. Only the cars still handle like they do in all the Mafia games - steering and braking like you're driving a truck, but this makes the pursuit missions and especially the notorious race mission challenging and engaging. Don't expect too much gameplay, though - it took me rougly 14 hours to finish the campaign, without huntig for remaining achievements. You'll also watch a ton of cutscenes, but the characters and the voice acting are pretty good, so it's not like you want to skip all that, since it really is an interactive Mafia movie. If you're looking for a story driven 3rd person shooter with all the beloved cliches of chainsmoking gangsters in the 30s, get this game if it's on a 50% or more sale. It looks and feels fantastic, but is too short for the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Mafia: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I try to avoid posting negative reviews but as someone who went into this seeing the "very positive" rating and having played almost all of 2 around launch and a lot of 3, I expected a lot more. This game isn't "bad" per se but it is very very boring. It's a very by-the-numbers mafia story. I have absolutely no point of reference for the original PS2 release of this game so I tried not to hold that against it but compared to the 2 games that followed this one, I just don't feel motivated to play this to the end.I'll give it the positive points where I'll say that the game is absolutely gorgeous. It really looks like it knows its setting. The voice acting is well performed and the music is very in line with the aesthetics. I appreciate that the game let me skip over unnecessary driving from one objective to another and I also appreciate that I don't have to drive to specific spots in an open world to initiate the next mission if I just want the story...Unfortunately, I don't have much more I can say I enjoyed. The character models are very nice but still slip into that uncanny valley of janky animations periodically that make me feel like I'm looking at a wax museum. The cars control awfully which I chalked up to the time period. Cars in the 1930s would control vastly different than ones from even the 60s. This excuse fell apart when I started controlling the character. The character has the worst turn and most sluggish feeling controls I've experienced since RDR2. It feels like there's input lag in the controller. On top of that the shooting feels horrendous which is odd because I recall Mafia 3 being a very fun shooter upon release. This game's shooting feels like a more polished Sinking City which controls like an awful version of Resident Evil 4. The story is dull, it feels like a "greatest hits" of mobster movies and is pretty predictable.If you read all that and have major nostalgia for this game and want to see it with a fresh coat of paint, then I say go for it but as someone who's played the 2 sequels, you're much better served by those. Mafia 2 is a more well-rounded package and Mafia 3 had an intriguing story and fun shooting. Both games also suffer from the fact they don't have a lot to do other than shooting people and maybe racing but this feels like the same thing focused down to a fine point. This game is absolutely not for me but I feel people who don't have attached nostalgia for the original release will walk away from this disappointed and bored. I wish I liked this as much as 2 and 3 but I can't even be bothered to finish it from boredom. If I revisit this and fine my opinion changed, I'll revise this review. I just feel Hangar 13 is capable of so much more than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I never finished the original Mafia game when it came out so when Mafia Definitive Edition was announced I was excited but even with the upgraded and fine-looking visuals some things have not aged well. 👍 +Great visuals and a stunning recreation of the original Mafia game. +The characters, the story still feels good to experience even to this day.👎-Even with a modern touch the gameplay is below average.-The race is abysmal.If you haven't played or finished the original Mafia game, then The Definitive edition is your must-play version. You play as Tommy Angelo, a cab driver who finds himself caught in a long and ongoing war between two mobsters. You eventually have no choice but to join one of them and thus your new life begins. It's a classic mobster story, with revenge, family, twists, and whatnots, and at that time, it was a huge thing to play, and even in Todays's standards I personally think it holds quite well. It's a short story but you will certainly get attached to certain characters, including Tommy. I can't talk much more about it without getting into spoilers since I'm certain a lot of people have no clue what to expect of it. All I can say is, don't go in expecting Oscar-worthy storytelling, hell I will even go as far as say Mafia 2 had a better story but without a doubt, Mafia Definitive Edition is something we needed in these woke times. A classic story of what it is to live as a mobster, simple as that. Story rating: 8/10Now while the story holds up quite well, the gameplay sadly does not. It was obviously remade for modern times just like everything else but it's only, the year 2010 type of modern gameplay. Shooting and driving are obviously the main aspects of the game, with everything else such as stealth and melee combat being second. Shooting is janky but works fine most of the times, with a barely functional and outdated cover system that will annoy you in a lot of scenarios. The AI is not very smart when it comes to shooting you back, they just have the classic auto-aiming the head with a shotgun from 10 miles type of programming and will rush your position blindly most of the time. The driving if you're playing on classic difficulty as I did is locked to simulation levels and the cars without a doubt feel exactly like old cars did back then, sluggish, and heavy as hell. Taking corners is a pain in the ass and you will fail repeatedly in certain timed missions if you dare play the game as it should be played.Sadly the infamous race makes a return and it's absolute sh#t. If you plan on playing on classic difficulty, you will be severely punished for it, for it's heavily scripted and unfair and I tested it for hours. The race has 3 rounds however if you're not in at least third place by the end of the first round it is impossible to win. I am unsure if lower difficulties are the same in this regard but on classic, the race is incredibly scripted. Why do you need to be at least in third place? Because each car in front of you will crash in the same spot, every single time. It's complete bullsh*t because taking corners in the game requires abusing the ram feature which bugs your car a bit and makes you take turns a bit easier. Overall it's a sh#t show and I almost gave up on the game. Melee is just as bad and it felt like I was playing a 2003 game whenever I was punching someone and stealth mechanics are as simple as you can imagine. Don't bother exploring the city, there's nothing to do. Overall the gameplay has not aged well nor has it been remade well, at all. What a shame. Gameplay rating: 6/10I'll start with what everyone wants to know, how are the new voices? I vaguely remember the old ones so there was no nostalgia factor involved in my opinion but with a few exceptions, they all do a great job at voicing the characters. Yes, I know Paulie sounds annoying a lot of times but it'll grow on you, hopefully. The soundtrack is great just as you'd expect though I'm not sure if all the songs in the original are back or not. Still, it fits well with the atmosphere and even the newer songs do a good job of immersing you in the game. As for everything else sound related, it's all good as well, cars sound surprisingly realistic. Audio rating: 8.5/10Visually the game looks great and it's quite an impressive task the devs managed to do, remaking the classic. The cars, the city, the actors, all look great and while the open-world aspect of it lacks many details, the set pieces you are thrown in are nice to look at, especially when it's night and raining. This would've looked even more incredible with some ray-tracing effects.As for performance, no complaints here, the game runs at 70+ frames per second most of the time at 1440p on a 2080 and there are never any hiccups or stutters whatsoever at least not if you're running it on an SSD. There are a few bugs, some quite annoying that may require a restart but they hardly ruined the playthrough. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score:  8.5/10So aside from terrible and outdated gameplay, there's no reason not to get Mafia Definitive Edition at any price, regardless if you're new to the franchise or just want to re-experience the classic in new clothes.
