_childDocuments_.review: Nowadays, going back to a classic is quite the difficult task. Over time, video games just can't hold up the way a cinematic masterpiece or a bestseller can. What  have achieved in recreating the original  is a phenomenal feat.  The rise of Tommy Angelo from a small-time cab driver, living off table scraps, to a caporegime in the Salieri crime family. Action, drama, betrayal and the inevitable demise that, sooner or later, befalls all characters in these stories. Pulp. But it's good pulp.   Visually,  is stunning. If Lost Heaven merely existed before, confined within a green screen, here - it's truly alive. Life goes on, even after the player has turned off the game. Intense third-person combat. Every bullet counts, every bullet can be fatal. Satisfying driving mechanics. Your palms begin to sweat, as your ride wobbles down the bustling street, doing 80 on a 30.  When it comes to the , everyone knows that the story is the main draw. There are rarely any side activities and what little there is, begs the question, “Who was this made for?”. It's either a collectathon or arcadey challenges, that plummet the overall quality. Pick your poison. Tedium.  is a great game even if repetitive, because the loop revolves around a strong foundation of exciting combat and sim-esque driving, that once mastered, makes you feel like an action hero, as you skirt around tight corners to the rhythm of 60s psychedelia.  takes everything that worked, but condenses it into a tight narrative experience, barring all filler.

Playing through the story really gives you no reason to explore around the city like in other open world games. There literally nothing to do, except get into a shootout with the cops. It's best to just cruise through the story and then hit up free roam mode to explore afterwards. Still, this is a great story driven game with decent action set pieces and it's beautiful. The cars also handle great and the car physics are off the charts.  Remember to switch to simulation style driving in the options. It's far more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid remake - very faithful to the original, to the extent that there are zero surprises when it comes to the plot. Too bad they had to change the likenesses of the characters, but I guess Andy Garcia is less likely to sue you than Mel Gibson.. Performs/looks excellent. Driving is solid. Shooting sections can be a little slow paced, the enemies hunker down into their cover and it can take you multiple minutes to clear small areas if you play it "properly" - though more often than not you can just sprint passed a lot of the enemies. Melee system works but is a bit too easy to be very satisfying (press triangle once, then mash circle). But all-in-all, a great port and game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 1 (2002) is one of my favourite games of all time, so this remake has a lot to live up to for me.Played the first hour and even though I can't review the entire experience yet, if you were in the fence go for it.So far it didn't disappoint. It runs flawlessly, looks absolutely gorgeous and still feels very familiar to old fansSurprisingly, some classic tracks (at least one) still in the game. As a hardcore fan of the original, I'm still getting over the new faces and voices, but I'm having a blast. Lots of minor details people were so worried about thankfully was kept authentic to the original. Play in Classic difficulty mode.The writing and dialog is hugely improved and expanded.. making every story cutscene far more believable and natural.

_childDocuments_.review: If only all remasters were like that... The original game was already fantastic but now it's even better in pretty much every single aspect, there is even a classic mode available if you want, which offers the same level of difficulty of the original game. In terms of graphic the game looks gorgeous, reflections are probably the best ever made (if we exclude hardware accelerated ray tracing) and the OST has been re-recorded. The story is overall the same but it has been enriched with new dialogues and cutscenes which further develop characters like Sarah who were barely seen in the original game. I really couldn't recommend this game more, it's a must play for everyone who loves the genre, kudos to Hangar 13 for respecting the original material and making a wonderful definitive edition.One not about Free Ride, I see a lot of people angry because Free Ride Extreme is not available, actually it is, they just mixed together the two modes. You will find notes scattered around Lost Heaven in Free Ride which will point you to phone cabins where you will be able to start out secret missions.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original, but i have played 2 and 3.I had fun and enjoyed it, so yeah i recommend it, but not for $40.I beat the game playing at what feels like a medium pace, without skipping any drives or cut scenes, in about 13 hours. This was including a little bit of free roam gameplay, which unfortunately is terribly empty and boring. It seems the only thing to do is drive around, murder random civilians, and run from/ shoot the police.The game itself is just okay. The story really is its strongest feature, but unfortunately i think there are missing cut scenes/ missions? For instance one night i walked this girl named Sarah home and then quite soon after that she's mad when i get home late for dinner, I find it hard to believe it was left so vague on purpose, it does seem there is some stuff missing there.While overall some action scenes are pretty fun, and overall i didn't care too much about the old style shooter with all its quirks, I do have to say the shooting is lackluster. Weapon choices are limited. The tommy gun feels nearly worthless, its pretty inaccurate, does little damage, and you can never seem to find enough ammo to comfortably use it. I always preferred the shotgun or bolt action rifle. Also death animations take away any rag doll physics or hit registry, so you plug a guy twice, but you wanna send a message and empty the gun? You'll shoot the concrete beneath him. MY IMMERSION!! NOOOOO!!!!Driving is meh. I've never driven a car from the 1930's but i bet it was harder than in this game. It does seem the elongated turns and slow roll of your car is meant for a sense of immersion, not high speed action impact. Still most missions i was able to get from point A to point B with some slick wheel work, and playing in manual transmission was fun.All things considered i don't think this is worth $40 at all. If you've played the original you will get some nice pretty graphics but be let down by the lack of anything which impacts your fun or replayability, and even worse changed content which does not seem to be for the better. Honestly i do kind of regret buying this for $40, even 30 is too much. $20 sounds more reasonable. Save your money unless its on a heavy sale!

Gameplay is more similar to the gameplay of Mafia 2, than the third one, which in my opinion is a good thing.The game also received voiceover for Czech Language, which is awesome and hearing Tommy, Sam, Frank and other characters voiced by their original actors was something totally unexpected and heart pleasing.Anyone, who played the whole game till the end must have dropped a tear. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I didn't play any of the original titles and a friend recommended this to me based on his opinion of the old games.That being said, I actually enjoyed this.The gameplay isn't anything groundbreaking, graphics aren't mindblowing (although very good and absolutely time appropriate), and the story is pretty cliché, so why do I recommend the game?Because it's refreshingly old school and it feels nice to play.It's a linear "open world" game that wants to tell a story, and that is exactly what it does. The story, while not being great by itself, is told in a compelling way in my opinion, that even justifies the linear nature of the game.Also, and this is a big one for me, the game doesn't feel like the classic ubisoft/social media type open world where they have to constantly hit you with some random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nobody cares about to keep you playing for 300 hours so you can feel justified in spending your money on it. If you expect any side missions or random events you will be disappointed, but I really feel like this is one of the reasons why I liked the game so much. It didn't bother me, it's not annoying, there's no "whacky" archetypical comedic relieve characters. Basically, it doesn't treat you like a toddler with an attention span of about 8 seconds, like Watch_Dogs 2, or Assassin's Creed and the likes.Another reason for me to recommend it is that it doesn't overstay its welcome, which I feel a lot of games do nowadays. It's a relatively short game at about 12 hours, but I'd gladly take a 12 hour finely crafted bare bones experiences over a game that tries to just fill as much time as it can.If that sounds like something you'd say, you may wanna get this.If you think the Watch_Dogs titles are good games, it's probably a hard pass for you.

_childDocuments_.review: If like me you have strong nostalgic memories of the original game, this is a fantastic experience: remade from the ground up with modern graphics, motion capture and gently modernised game-play, it feels like playing Mafia as you remember it rather than the clunky, blocky mess that it was. The plot remains essentially unchanged, but with some welcome additions and tweaks to flesh out the characters and provide clearer foreshadowing. I haven't played the original in years I have to admit, but in this version Salieri is much more clearly a villain - sometimes charming, sometimes suave, but clearly and emphatically a mob boss, as a result it's much clearer in this version that there isn't really much difference between him and Morello and . Conversely, Sam feels more human and likeable all the way through, and Paulie is more clearly a loudmouth out of his depth, which really helps the story. Unfortunately the devotion to the original plot means that it is still a fairly run-of-the-mill gangster story, hitting familiar beats, and some plot holes still remain (. It's also worth noting that it (still) miserably fails the Bechdel test and the 'sexy lamp' test. Yes, it's a story set in 1930s USA, but apart from a single comment about women's suffrage (from one of only 2 named female characters), it doesn't provide much critical engagement with the social norms of the era or women's place in it. It also largely sidesteps the issues of race and racism by barely touching on them - despite the fact that the USA had segregation at the time, and that the main characters are all Italian Americans, who were themselves often victims of prejudice, and that this is in a large part how real mafias operate (i.e. providing a community 'police' when the regular ones cant be trusted).  These are flaws present in the original game, but while they were par for the course 20 years ago, they feel really glaring today.As mentioned, the game-play has been gently modernised. The biggest change is to level design - every mission has been overhauled and while the layout of buildings will be familiar to you if you played the original, it simply plays much better, and the set-pieces have been drastically improved. Working closely with the new level design is a cover system which makes the extended gunfights more about patience and skill than reaction speed which was a real problem in the original game. Driving has been greatly improved (although optionally you can play with more realistically sluggish vehicles), and the addition of a "Skip Drive" option is greatly appreciated for the many missions where there is an extended drive from A to B with no actual content in between.  Best of all, the dreaded race mission is now significantly easier!One puzzling change is the removal of the Lucas Bertone side missions. It's quite surprising that they focused the game down on the core story rather than building out more side content to give you more reason to explore the city of Lost Heaven in Story mode. It's especially odd to keep Lucas' dialogue telling you to come see him for side hustles, when he never offers you any.  I would have appreciated more free-form parts of the game punctuating the story and giving me more reason to collect cars. It would also have provided space for additional side missions where the game could have explored some of the social issues that the main plot glosses over, without drastically altering the story.Overall this is a great game for anyone who played and enjoyed the original (for all its flaws). However, if you're coming in cold, having no connection to the original game, you'll probably find this a mediocre FPS with an entertaining but hackneyed plot.

_childDocuments_.review: As the best game of the Trilogy, the original Mafia from 2002 still lingers somewhere near the bottom of my personal Top-50-games-of-all-time list. It has an exceptionally well written story, tense gunfights and gripping atmosphere and for that I always liked it a lot more than GTA III, which came out around the same time. I was really looking forward to play the Definitive Edition now to revisit this awesome classic with modern grafics and some much-needed quality-of-life improvements, but one big bummer almost completely ruined it for me: Its is piss-poorly optimized.Even though it runs on a slightly improved version of the engine used in Mafia III (that game runs flawlessly on my rig when maxed out) and my laptop (i7 7700 quadcore, 16 GB Ram, GTX 1060) just barely misses the recommended specs only in case of the GPU, I had to lower the grafics settings to medium quality to maintain a decent framerate and make additional use of an undervolting tool as well as an external cooling unit to stop my CPU from overheating. Still the game was stuttering heavily at times, especially during night missions when the game is heavy on its lighting and shadow effects, and even had a couple of minor grafics glitches. Needless to say that the highest resolutions were out of the question for me and i had to settle for 1920 x 1080. For such a demanding game, Mafia DE doesn't even look that spectacular, except maybe for the smooth and realistic facial animations. The technical problems don't stop there, as I found a couple of the new controls slightly confusing. For example, you select your melee weapon from the weapon wheel and equip it as your primary weapon exactly like every other gun, but if you want to swing you baseball bat, you have to press the designated melee button instead of just clicking left mouse like you would do to shoot your guns. WTF?Gameplaywise however, it is still pretty close to the original, while not feeling as "stiff" and outdated, due to some very welcome improvements. The only thing that bothers me is because of the modern mechanics and improved gunplay the gunfights are still fun, but much easier and don't feel as tense, challenging and realistic as in the original anymore. Furthermore, even though the modernized driving mechanics feel a lot more comfortable and less annoying, it takes some of the more realistic and historically accurate feeling of the original away.The cutscenes and dialogue have been reworked, but not so much that it feels too unfaithful to the old version. Nevertheless I have to say that i think that some cutscenes from the original are still better written and have a lot more weight and emotion.Lastly, some content was cut in favor of the pacing of the story, namely all the Lucas Bertone-missions, but since I wasn't too fond of them in the original anyway, i can perfectly live without them. As f*cked-up as this thing might be for some people (including me) on the technical side, the gameplay, story and atmosphere mostly remain as excellent as 20 years ago.If you got the proper hardware to run this thing smoothly, Mafia DE is a great remake of an outstanding game. Unfortunately the technical condition ruined it for me to some extend. Due to the absolutely miserable framerate I experienced until I finally came near the sweet spot between visual fidelity and performance for my system, the game wasn't half as fun and immersive as it definitely would have been if only it would run properly, and this brings it down considerably. For the reason of Mafia DE being not very well optimized plus the tons of nostalgia I have, I personally still prefer the original. Nevertheless, Mafia DE is objectively a very good game and a faithful, modern retelling of one of the best and most gripping and believable stories in videogame history.    _________________________________________________________________________________MAFIA (Definitive Edition)Genre: Open-World Sandbox, Third-Person-ShooterRelease: Q3 2020( ) 0/8 Simply one of the worst games ever made. Don't waste any money on this.( ) 1/8 Bad. Seriously flawed with barely any redeeming qualities. Worth a couple of Cents at best, if at all.( ) 2/8 Sub-par. Only for hardcore-fans of respective genre / series. Don't pay more than 5 bucks.( ) 3/8 Meh-diocre. It‘s okay. Don't pay more than 10 bucks.( ) 4/8 Decent, but not for everybody. Don't pay more than 15 bucks.( ) 5/8 Good game, Must-play for genre- / series-fans. Worth 20 to 25 bucks max, if you are not a fan.(X) 6/8 Great game, universal recommendation. 30 bucks would be a steal for this.( ) 7/8 Outstanding game, a milestone of it‘s respective genre. _childDocuments_.review: Mafia: Definitive Edition, developed by Hangar 13 and published by 2K Games, is a stunning remake that breathes new life into the classic crime drama of the 2002 original. This reimagined edition retains the essence of the original while introducing modern enhancements that elevate the experience to new heights.From the moment players step into the shoes of Tommy Angelo, a cab driver turned mafioso, they are transported to the roaring 1930s of Lost Heaven, a fictional city inspired by Prohibition-era Chicago. The developers' meticulous attention to detail in the world-building is evident, with authentic architecture, period-appropriate cars, and a soundtrack that perfectly complements the game's atmosphere.The narrative of Mafia: Definitive Edition remains as engaging and gripping as its predecessor. The story follows Tommy Angelo's journey from an unwitting bystander to a key player in the Salieri crime family. The reimagined script and top-notch voice acting breathe new life into the characters, making them feel more nuanced and relatable. The emotional depth of the characters and the twists and turns in the plot keep players invested in the story from start to finish.Gameplay in Mafia: Definitive Edition is a blend of action, driving, and open-world exploration. The gunplay and combat mechanics have been reworked to offer a smoother and more satisfying experience. Gunfights are intense, and the cover system allows for strategic maneuvering during shootouts. The driving mechanics have also been improved, making car chases and getaways feel authentic and exhilarating.The city of Lost Heaven is an open-world playground for players to explore. From its bustling streets to its seedy back alleys, the city feels alive and reactive to the player's actions. Whether it's participating in thrilling car races or completing side missions, there's always something to do, enriching the overall gameplay experience.One of the standout features of Mafia: Definitive Edition is its jaw-dropping visuals. The game boasts stunning graphics, character models, and meticulously recreated environments that rival some of the best in the industry. The enhanced lighting and attention to detail breathe new life into Lost Heaven, making it a joy to explore and experience.However, it's essential to note that while the game is a faithful recreation, some elements of the original, such as mission structure and certain gameplay mechanics, might feel a tad dated to players accustomed to more modern open-world titles.In conclusion, Mafia: Definitive Edition is an outstanding remake that pays homage to the classic while delivering a fresh and immersive experience. With its compelling narrative, refined gameplay mechanics, and jaw-dropping visuals, the game captures the essence of a classic crime drama while providing a modern gaming experience. Whether you're a longtime fan of the original or a newcomer to the world of organized crime, Mafia: Definitive Edition is a must-play title that offers an unforgettable journey into the dark underbelly of a bygone era.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia 2 is one of my favourite games but I'd never actually played the original Mafia, so a modern remake seemed a good opportunity to experience the story.I'm only a few hours in but so far I'm having a great time. The world is gorgeous and vibrant, driving is weighty, characters are expressive and the limited combat I've experienced so far has been fun. If you are thinking of buying this game it is important to know what to expect. It is not an open world with lots to do like GTA. It is a linear game with an open world to allow for car chases, world building etc. Just don't expect hours worth of mini-games and side quests and you'll enjoy it. There are some challenges you can complete in the separate "free ride" mode that unlock a few cars and cosmetics but that's it.I've only experienced minor bugs so far such as character animations not quite lining up with an object they're interacting with and my character model standing at a 45 degree angle during one fight, purely visual. Performance seems good and I haven't had any significant issues.My only major complaint is shooting while driving. You can't actually aim and try to shoot out the tires or the driver, rather you kind of just lock onto the car you want to shoot at and click to generally 'deal damage' to it. This is especially disappointing as when you're on foot you actually can shoot out drivers and tires.So far the game is great. I was disappointed with Mafia 3 so having a new, modern Mafia game to play through is a joy. I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia the City of Lost Heaven is one of my top 5 games of all time. What Definitive Edition did was suck the soul out of an incredible game 19 years later, leaving behind a console-fied, dumbed down, version. Where to begin? The voice acting is the first thing you notice. Paulie, Sam, and Tommy all went from sounding like Italian mob guys who aren't caricatures to NNNYEEEEH SEE, FUGHETABOUTIT. Paulie keeps his character more or less, but his voice actor is horrible and obnoxious. Sam sort of retains his voice, but his persona goes from the "straight man" that Tommy would confide in, to a cocky jerk. Tommy's voice actor was okay, but his personality got assassinated. Whereas originally he was a mellow but confident man and definitely not bloodthirsty, he went to being a cocky greaser type who happily kills scores of men and then hesitates to kill one more. Inconsistent character delivery and inconsistent motivations all around. The car and gun features have been greatly reduced. Vinny the gun guy and Ralphie the car guy were super fun to listen to ORIGINALLY where they would tell you about the cars, the new technological improvements and how to steal them. Or the various guns and what was special about them. These characters now say a few words to you and largely exist in short cutscenes. Vehicle deformation is almost NONEXISTENT. Can't shoot tires off cars, can't break windows, knock off mirrors or cause grievous damage to them anymore. Cars just boringly smoke and stop running. This is such a disappointment from the original where car damage (in 2002) was exceptional. Which brings us to gameplay. They removed free aim in car chases, the ability to end any chase mission early. Now they all end in pre-determined scripted paths. You chase people or get chased until they crash at which point the game says YOU DID IT. And not a moment sooner. No more skillfully nailing the driver or popping their tires, or anything creative. Some of the slower paced missions were redone and rearranged to have gunfights, like "Happy Birthday" where a dumb gunfight was shoehorned in. Other missions like "Lucky Bastard" were re-done to remove any tension and slow parts and instead threw in more extended scripted chases. The cover based shooting is okay. It doesn't detract TOO much from the game but the guns feel inaccurate and unsatisfying. Going for headshots is annoying, and enemies will frequently play whack-a-mole with you popping in and out of cover. Cars are also only accessible when the game wants you to, so in certain missions where there might be cars, you're not allowed to use them for no other reason than "we said so". Lastly the story, while on the surface the story remains the same, its changed for the worse. The ending is entirely butchered, getting rid of Tommy's impactful speech and his confrontation with Sam. Tommy's character doesn't feel like a man going in too deep, and the twist at the end doesn't come as a surprise OR that the characters had decent motivation. Detective Norman speaking to Tommy in the diner to frame the story isn't written nearly as well and feels like it's taken from a bad mob movie instead. Overall playing this game is like looking at your highschool sweetheart 20 years later only to see her with ugly plastic surgery and sagging boobs. Go play the original, don't waste your time here. Don't waste your time on the pointless collectibles or the lifeless free-ride mode. The remake didn't add anything to a great game, they only made it worse.

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster was a mixed bag for me, I ultimately enjoyed it but I feel like they messed up in quite a few important areas:-It appears you can't use public transport, major let down-I had to launch the game from the mafia exe directly as the launcher crashes-There's some discrepancies between the remaster and the original I don't like, such as removing driving to and from objectives in a few missions. Driving around the city is really pleasant so I wouldn't have minded more of that-I encountered an ultimately harmless but weird bug in creme de la creme where after the last cutscene in the mission it said I died (wtf lol?) and pressing "load last checkpoint" fixed it-First mission feels too unrealistic compared to the original version-I can't confirm this as I haven't tried it myself but apparently the alternative Morello death is gone, if this is true then that's pretty sad-The music was better in some areas and not in others, it was really bad in combat. Felt much more tense in the originalBut there's also a lot of things I like:+Throwables are actually used in the remaster, they were barely used in the original+Several sections have been expanded in meaningful ways compared to the original+Graphics are gorgeous+The new character models are really nice looking and most stay true to the original+More scenes with Sarah makes the story make more sense+Customizable difficulty, I played on hard all the way through except in that damn racing mission+Collectibles of various kinds+There is some level of the city feeling alive, unsure how it compares to the original as it's been ages since I played the original. In one mission you can see a bunch of protesters and in another the bridge is closed due to a car accident. +The audio is much better compared to the original I feel likeThose are my thoughts, others maye disagree.

_childDocuments_.review: I got mafia Og for free tried it, loved it then decided to buy the definitive edition, Never regretted the decision of buying it, The 1930s Chicago vibe is extremely immersive with great lighting, the story feels organic and grounded, the characters are a treat, and the shooting levels are actually super fun. Honestly just setting the speed limiter on and driving to a mission with jazz on the radio is so relaxing and enjoyable, more so than any other game I've played of late.Okay, so most of the main gameplay loop is basically driving around and cover shooting, with small stealth-ish sections. But the game does this really well, and is very convincing as a period piece. With a good plot that moves along briskly in just 20 missions including some really action-packed set pieces, the game doesn't last long enough to feel too repetitive. It's also a fairly accessible game that most people could easily finish on Easy/Medium i completed on Classic (Most difficult setting)If you'd love a good ol' shoot-em-up with a solid gangster story, without any complicated gameplay mechanics and a million side quests, this is the game for you. I just finished the game today and I'm pretty sure I'll replay it at some point.P.S : Don't judge by playime, (I played almost double the hours on Offline mode)

_childDocuments_.review: As a HUGE fan of the original game, I was beyond hyped to hear that not only were they going to release a remaster, but as a remake of one of perhaps the most enjoyed games of my youth.Going into the Definitive edition, I had made sure to steer well clear of any reviews which may impact my judgement on the game, and so I experienced it with an open mind.The Graphics - Absolutely gorgeous! Although I often found myself a bit confused at the old characters suddenly having definition to their features, I think the team did a stellar job in re-imagining the world of Mafia in a modern day engine. Some of the effects in gunplay/grenades was interesting, but overall very impressive!The Story - As based on the original ,the story took me through a whole rollercoaster as life as a mobster in the 1930s. Very captivating, extremely well voice acted and animated, it's definitely a classic. Gameplay - Now this is where the game begins to fall short in my opinion. A lot of the gunplay with it's cover system felt very generic, and from my limited experience with Mafia 3 it seemed almost identical to the system in that game. A generic cover and shoot system didn't feel at place in this game, and often I found myself in long sequences where i'd hide in cover until the bad guys stopped shooting, kill them all, and then rise-wash-repeat.The driving mechanics were vastly improved. vehicles actually feeling responsive and infuriating in equal measure. It created a very immersive experience drifting round the streets of Lost Heaven in a saloon car guns ablaze!That being said, there were certain sequences were I felt cheated of a true 'chase' experience, the game automatically taking over with a short cutscene to illustrate the getaway.Overall - Mafia : Definitive Edition is a good game. I wouldn't stretch as far as saying it'll be remembered with as much fondness and joy as it's original form, but it's a solid shooter with a fantastic story. Recommend picking this one up on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10TL;DR: The first half is driving simulator with a mafia story, then it turns into mafia hitman, then the story gets interesting.I really enjoyed Mafia. I had always wanted to play these games, but I wasn't sure if I wanted to put up with the dated graphics of the first one. Then they announced the remake and I was all in.Overall, the graphics are really good here. Lighting is great, frame rate is solid, and the rain/puddle reflections really impressed me. I'm a little mixed about the facial animations. At times they looked good, at other times they looked clunky. Motion capture has really ruined any other form of facial animation for me.I liked the story here. The game is kind of a driving simulator with a mafia story for the first few hours, then you start doing hit jobs for the mafia, and then the story really starts to pick up. The characters were also interesting enough that I wanted to keep seeing how they grew throughout the story. It took me 11 hours to beat this, and I thought that was perfect. Not every game has to be an open world, 30-40 hour story + side quests. This is nice and short and enjoyable.This is an open world game, kind of. You will be driving through the city to mission locations, but there won't be any side quests to grab along the way, just the main story. There is a free roam mode in the menu in case you want to explore the city, but I never did that. If there aren't any quests, I didn't see the point. But if you think you're getting GTA: Mobster Edition, this isn't really that.It plays at a solid 60 fps, although it did occasionally lag for a couple seconds for me. The pause menu was also really laggy.I played on medium difficulty because I just wanted to sit back and enjoy the story, and it may have been a bit too easy. You can also adjust how aggressive the cops are. I turned them way down, because of how much you are driving I did not want to put up with them getting mad every time I drove crazy. The pedestrians are also really stupid, often running into the streets in front of my oncoming vehicle.Overall, this is another example of a great remake, bringing an older game to a newer generation for them to experience it. Unlike older movies, which can just be watched and it requires no extra effort of the viewer, older video games can be difficult to play, not just because of being visually dated, but also because of dated controls or mechanics that can be frustrating nowadays. Remakes like this, Demon Soul's, and Shadow of the Colossus do a good job of bringing these games into a more playable state today. I recommend playing this one, especially if you like movies like Goodfellas or The Godfather.

_childDocuments_.review: Wasted potential.Well this rewiev is kinda painfull to me, but for me, its hard to recommend that game. Dont misunderstand me, it's a great game after all, but compared to the original Mafia, it is, on almost every aspect(except graphics and shooting mechanics) worse. At first i have no idea why story was that much changed, and EVERY single changed bit of it that is changed, is a change to worse. The characters are now just 100% mediocre, Paulie is a typical funny-psyco archetype tough-guy gangster, same with others. In original all characters felt believable, in this game they're feel like caricature copy from any gangster movie from the 90'. The story feels plain and rushed, it's just going way to fast. The slow pace of the original was, i guess, the point here. You were just getting used to the all characters, the city, you cared about them. In the remake it's all going too fast IMO. Story jumps from event to event, without any chance for player to chatch the breath, and IMHO its a really, really bad thing. Even driving through the city was limited as much as possible, no idea why, because driving is the best part of this game. Driving feels belivable, it's challenging, enjoyable and it just feels good. But, there's no point in sandbox, actually there's no sandbox at all(free roam mode is there, and i tried it, no worry, but here im talking about the story mode), and it feels like it was planned but, cut out of the game. The game says that you can store the vehicles in garage, but there's no option to put them there, because when you're getting out from Salierie's bar there's no way to get back to the yard with the garage, and you cannot enter the garage. Just getting in to any vehicle saves it in garage. That feels weird IMO.Side mission for Lucas Bertone from the original are also cut. There is no additional content in the main story, nothing(except some collectibles, but it doesnt count). Sure, you can play Free roam mode but it has no purpouse, you can collect the cars there, but what for? You cannot use them in story mode when you finished it... In Free roam mode there's almost nothing to do. There are some missions that were originally in Free ride extreme(these are horrible balanced anyway - some are really really hard, some of them are too easy) mode but that's it, no point to play that mode :/ No economy, no collecting money to buy guns, and things like that. You can just drive,  and play some taxi missions(no point in them, you're getting nothing for playing them...).Actually game has content for max 30 hours - done everything on highest difficulty(including free ride missions).And the another thing that i don't like here is the in game "music", it's just trash, nothing more to say. Original score was perfect, and was making really really great atmosphere. In the remake there is not even single track that is rememberable(except main theme from original game xD), it just feels like AI generated "nothing to remember" music score. Such a shame, i guess developers had copyright problems with getting orignal game score, because there's no chance that anyone thouht that the mediocre rubbish they gave us is better than the score from the original game. The linearity is another thing that i wanna point out here, there's only one way to finish every mission, and that's it, no different approaches like in original, it's all scripted, and in every playthrough just the same. Going back to the game content, there are much less cars in the game, i played original few years ago, and i remeber many cars that are not there. Well actually i got back to the original game and checked that, there are many many cars missing in remake(there, cars had few version like coupe, convertible, fourdoor and twodoor, in remake most of them has only one version...). Developers gave us few new cars but thery're mostly trucks, and utility vehicles that nobody really wanted, but cut out many good normal personal vehicles. Shame. There are also things that are really really good here, i have to admit that, the graphics are just amazing. Game looks great, and its really, really nicely optimized. The city looks beutifull, and alive, same with car models and characters. Graphicwise the game is 10/10, but that, with quite solid gunplay(original game gunplay is outdated and cluncky, didn't aged well) is the only thing that is better than the original. In almost every aspect is a huge step backward, game is much more liniear, and simplier, there's much less content, and music is a horrible "placeholder-like" :/As a game as it is, it can be a solid 8/10 but as a Mafia: The City of Lost Heaven remake it's no more than 6/10. As a gamer, well maybe i cound recommend that game, but as a big fan of the originall i just cannot :/If you're not alergic to old games - play original instead, if not, well this game is a good game as it is, but still i prefere the original one, and its a worst thing that you can say about remake, right? :(

_childDocuments_.review: A preface: I played Mafia 2 first, back on the 360, then 3, years later, and have only gotten around to playing 1 now, so it it worth noting that this is from the perspective of someone whose primary connection to the series is Mafia 2.Mafia: Definitive Edition is a pretty good game, all things considered! I'm fresh out of the incredibly long end credits, and I would say this game is worth a play! There's not enough games set during the Great Depression and Prohibition Era, and this has some fun exploring the city of  Lost Haven (not-Chicago) during the opening era of the North American Italian-American Mafia, going from a guy on the streets to a made man. There's great stuff on the origins of things like Big Break Whites, and Swift Cola. The driving in this game hands pretty well, and I think, in simulation mode, a fair number of driving game aficinados may have some fun exploring old jalopies in their element.The game does suffer some issues, and it seems like a fair number probably stem from what is, ostensibly, a good idea: being faithful to the original. Top of the list is that this game is hard as nails! I tried playing this game on normal, but about midway through, I gave up on any sense of optional difficulty. Most enemies take a fair number of rounds to put down, unless vital areas are precisely aimed for, which the game's primary weapons are less than ideal for. More than once I'd emptied a full, 7 bullet magazine from a pistol, only for him to gun me down. Certain sections  are absolute meat grinders, and looking for advice on some of them will come up with "Reduce difficult to minimum, maximize aim assist, and repeat until accomplished". I can't imagine playing this on Hard, much less Classic Mode.The game is, compared to 2 and even 3, not focused on realism, except maybe on the cars. Major weapons and free cars wouldn't be invented for years if not decades, and several characters sound much closer to cartoons than real people. While this can be disappointing, and slightly distracting early on in the game, once you embrace this is going to be a fun, if not realistic, romp, you can get over it. While sometimes sounding a little silly, most of the characters are engaging enough that you grow to care for a fair number of them.While this game has some issues, I still feel like I can recommend this game to others, especially if you love Mafia 2. It's replaced some of the setting's charm with bone-grinding difficulty, but it still feels like a great fit with the other games, and is worth a play-through.-A Note about Definitive Edition vs The Original- So, if you're expecting the original game and this Definitive Edition to be the exact same game, don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember this little game called Mafia III? Of course you do, it was famous for its mixed reception. Lots of content that was put together in such a lousy and grindy way it put off many of potential players. Now imagine if most of the issues that plagued Mafia III were suddenly gone - and you will get Mafia Definitive Edition.Mafia DE, being a remake of one of the most influential games of early 2000's did a really good job at bringer one of the best mafian stories inspired by Goodfellas to audience that did not want to put themselves through all the struggles of playing almost two decades old game. It, being on the same engine as Mafia III, kept everything that made third Mafia a great game and removed all of the stupidities that plagued it. While slowly wandering through Mafia DE, a thought crossed my mind about what it would be like, if Mafia III was linear, well polished game that did not need to put us through that racket hell. Well, that's what you get her - perfect cutscenes and voice acting, engaging gunplay, polished graphical coat and fun driving model.Of course, some of the issues that annoyed us at Mafia 3 still plague us in DE - certain cutscenes being locked at 60/30fps, the fact that, even though they specifically said that Tommy is not a trained soldier like Lincoln, they literally kept the same short and swift reload animations and aim as well as many other animations such as ladder climing, vaulting and more. The only real change was in melee combat, but that was about it. After this, there are of course many bugs and glitches, many of which I am sure the devs will remove ( although I must say I am really happy that the launch of Mafia DE was infinitely smoother than that of M3).I can easily recommend Mafia Definitive Edition to both fans of the original Mafia as well as to those of Mafia III. Pros:+ Graphics and details+ Weather effects+ Gunplay+ Masterful cutscenes and voice acting+ Soundtrack+ Driving+ StorylineCons:- Some bugs and physics issues- Some sentences and phrases from the original that are changed/omitted feel like they should be there just as they were as they made sense in the context of the game- Many animations are same as Lincoln's from M3 despite being completely different characters

_childDocuments_.review: At it's core it's a very well made story driven game that recreates the original very faithfully... Almost too much so.I have been a Mafia fan for a very long time, but what has always disappointed me the most about the franchise is that it gets the core mechanics (for the most part) so right that the potential for a GTA killer is everywhere but is never realised.The car handling? almost perfect. Bonus points for having an optional simulation mode and manual transmission.Soundrack? Tick. Atmosphere? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ yes. Graphics? Most of the time in this title, the game will look breathtaking.The gunplay? Not perfect, but feels faithful to the setting and is competent enough to be satisfying sometimes.Story and character performances? Exactly what you'd want from a game about the mafia.So what's missing???The sandbox.Yes the game is open world.. but unfortunately there's just very little to do in between missions, in fact there aren't really any missions, it's just story beat after story beat with no breathing room in between unless you want to ignore the mission you are on and explore, but that's about it. If you have played LA NOIRE, think of that, except with even less to do. There are no random events, no side activities, no shops to buy things, no properties to purchase, such little car customization it's barely even worth mentioning.Yes there is a free mode, but it's honestly about as feature rich as the free mode in Driver 1 from 20 years ago.This game has reinstated a lot of my faith in Hanger 13 as a capable developer for the series, but for the next game I really want to see them deliver on having an interesting world full of things to do, stuff to buy and events that bring the world to life as well has having a good campaign.In my opinion, Mafia 2 is the best game in the series that gets closer than any of the others to achieveing this balance, so I highly recommend picking that up first, and then playing this one if you want more story.This one is a 7/10 from me. Has so much potential that isn't realised, but what's here plays well, has a solid story and is graphically beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia: Definitive Edition is an action-adventure title and a remake of Mafia from 2002. As was the case in the original, the game is set in the fictional city of Lost Heaven, Illinois, during the 1930s and follows Tommy Angelo, a Sicilian American cab driver who quickly finds himself sucked into the dirty world of the mob within the Salieri Crime Family. It features enhanced mission dynamics, the introduction of motorcycles to the series and an original score was also created for the game. While some of the veteran Czech voice cast from the original have returned, the English voices have been recast.+ Lead protagonist Tommy Angelo is someone who will have you emotionally invested in their journey from beginning to end. From a humble cab driver to a loyal soldier for the Salieri Crime Family, you experience the rise and fall and there is never a dull moment. The rest of the cast give strong performances in turn. There are plenty of plot twists and all the characters are well-developed with a suitable blend of action, drama and a touch of nostalgia. The story has been expanded but missions and arcs from the original have carried over.+ There is a 'classic difficulty' option for those that wish to play through the game on it's most challenging setting. This changes some gameplay mechanics such as ammunition and how police respond to crimes. Selecting this will bring you closer to the feel of the 2002 title.+ As you would expect, the entire setting of the game has been completely redesigned. Meticulously crafted, I sometimes had to stop and take in just how drop-dead stunning and beautiful Lost Heaven looks. The city feels super authentic and the 1930s atmosphere couldn't be more perfect if it tried.+ ​The Free Ride mode offers substantial replay value once you are finished with the main story. There are numerous collectibles to obtain, side missions to complete, outfits, vehicles, easter eggs and you are free to explore Lost Heaven at your leisure without having to follow mandatory objectives. Expect to invest in a considerable amount of time if you wish to hit 100% as there are a ton of collectibles.- One infamous mission stands out in the story and that is the race mission. If you're not going through the game on classic difficulty, then it shouldn't cause you any issues but if you are, then you should prepare yourselves for a lot of frustration. Thankfully, the rest of the game is nowhere near as painful on classic difficulty. Completing the race on classic was one of the most nightmare fuelled periods I've ever had in gaming but hey, you might actually enjoy having to work for it. I'm only giving you a helpful warning in advance!- Driving in this game can take some getting used to. Don't get me wrong, it's definitely better than it was in the original game. The fact that you have to watch your speed otherwise the cops will come after you (at least when you're on the simulation settings) may annoy some players or you could find it a refreshing change compared to other games. This one is subjective.- During my time with the game, I had some bad bugs such as cutscenes freezing while the audio was still playing, falling through the map in free ride and radio stations continuing to play even when I was far away from my car. -It's a small nitpick but the lack of a theatre mode to watch cutscenes from the story is kind of a shame. Revitalised and rebuilt from the ground up, Mafia: Definitive Edition takes the best story in the series and injects new life and polish into it. Along with excellent performances from the new cast, an enthralling reimagining of 1930s Chicago and the added Free Ride mode, there's never been a greater game to experience the life of a mobster. Some clunky combat/melee mechanics aside and bugs here and there, this is still, in my eyes, the finest game in the Mafia series to date and definitely an entry that doesn't deserve to go and sleep with the fishes.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia is a decent game, with a well crafted story, but is sadly short on content.First of all, the game is beautiful. The city looks great, and it is filled with quality cars, people, and environments. The billboards, posters, and architecture are a wonderful created in that "could exist in our universe" fashion. The city may not be as big as other games, but that's not an issue (more on that later).The story is the best part about the game. The characters, dialog, and animations all sell the player on a fun prohibition era crime simulation experience.Unfortunately, that's where my praise for the game ends.My biggest gripe with the game is that it is light on content. I completed the main story in about 10 hours, and there isn't anything more to the game except collectible chasing filler. The city, while beautiful rendered, is only a boring backdrop devoid of player activities or reasons to go anywhere besides completing the main story. The sad thing is that developers know this, because they included a button to skip driving through the city even on story missions!Law enforcement in the game is also pitifully easy to evade. Smash through police cars with ease and then park for a minute on a walkway. That's all that's required to escape capture.Overall, the game is a quick, fun, one time experience through an excellent story that ultimately fated to gather dust on the digital shelf after completed.I would recommend a buy but only on a deep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Mafia: Definitive Edition is one of the best remakes ever. Hangar 13 has brought the 2002 classic back to life, delivering a hard-hitting wave of nostalgia that reminds us why the original was so beloved.  The upgraded graphics are stunning, enhancing the atmosphere and immersing players deeper into the story of Tommy Angelo and the Salieri crime family. Every detail—from the city streets to the character expressions—captures the gritty charm of 1930s America and amplifies the impact of the narrative.  The gameplay feels both familiar and fresh, retaining the essence of the original while introducing modern refinements that make each mission more engaging. Whether you’re revisiting old memories or discovering the story for the first time, this remake is a must-play.

Even if you didn't like other Mafia games, you should give this a shot. One of the best crime games out there, none of the GTA games I have played are even closely fighting in a same ring.Then fast bullet points what I have noticed so far-I have yet to be experiencing bugs.-Audio is really good. Music selection is good and foot steps have a good sound and everything sounds good from directional perspect and only thing I would change is the weapon sounds. They would deserve bit more oompf, even though they are not nearly as bad as in BFV. My Laptop is quite decent (i7-6700, 16GB RAM, Nvidia GTX 960 4GB, 1TB HDD + 256 SSD) and to run it smoothly, with FPS stable around only 25, I need to setup all Graphic Levels to Medium only.I have to give a thumbs up, despite my slight disappointment, because it is a good game overall and because undoubtedly my review is biased by having played the original game.Definitely a must have for all young players and for who never played the original Mafia. The city is fairly big, but the different districts only serve as different backdrops to the missions in the game. There are no real side activities to do, and the game is broken up into various missions, which never lets the player feel like they can take the time to explore the city for the sake of it.The game is fairly short by modern standards, the time I've put into it at the time of writing (8 hours) is roughly how long it'll take you to finish the story. _childDocuments_.review: A (nearly) perfect remaster of the classic. Mafia was the first open-world RPG I had ever played as a kid. Some folks wrote it off as a jumped-up GTA clone, but it was very unique, leagues ahead of most other games at the time, and featured wild mechanics that really pulled you in. It's probably one of the few driving games in existence where it's actually MORE beneficial to drive the speed limit than it is to break it.The original was as close as you could get to a fully-interactive film, and this is a very faithful remaster.It was really cool seeing such a ground-breaking game get the upgrade treatment, and the additional story beats and quests they added in are so seamless that I actually had to go back and reach which chapters were new and which I had just forgotten. The graphics are good, the story's incredible, the controls are JUST tight enough that they're good, but loose enough that things still feel a little haphazard. Which makes sense: You're not an army sniper; you're a mafioso in a pinstripe suit. PLUS the Free Ride game mode is back, and it's even better now that the map is bigger, and they've added missions and achievements. In short, everything in this edition is bigger, better, and more visually stunning, AND it lets them incorporate some of the overlap between Mafia and Mafia II in a fun easter egg.The cons: The graphics - are still a little loopy in some spots. The mo-capped faces work like 80% of the time, but occasionally they'll look real weird. The difficulty - actually feels a little less punishing than the original. Maybe it's just because I was a kid when I first encountered this game, but I remember the church and parking garage shootouts being a LOT harder in the original than they were in this edition. I played on normal difficulty and blasted through the main campaign pretty fast.The mechanics - It's using the same engine as Mafia II, and they use the same mechanics, for good or ill, and that means the ground-breaking destructible environments and reactive car-damage from the original is all gone. Buildings only break when they're supposed to, and the cars themselves, just like Mafia II, will express damage in the exact same, pre-scripted way every single time, regardless of where and how they were hit. In the original, you could punch your vehicle, and see that specific part dent or break. In this one, you can click a pole with the driver-side fender, but your passenger side will always droop first. A really minor gripe? Absolutely. But I genuinely missed that.The music - Some of the songs from the original soundtrack are conspicuously absent or really-underplayed in this edition, mostly because it doesn't change with the neighborhoods anymore. Not really a bad thing, and some, like the chinatown music, was probably overhauled for "modern audiences," but I miss the period-specific clarinet music that was all over the place in the OG.Gripes aside, it's worth your money, even at full price. If you like gangster films, noir media, anything mob-related, or even if you just like GTA and Saints Row style running and gunning, this game is going to hold your attention.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely more straight-forward than more open world games. No, there isn't a lot of freedom to roam around in the world, the game is mostly story driven. No, the game doesn't have intricate skill trees and customization. No, the game doesn't have side quests. No, the game does not have the most realism I've ever seen in a video game, and if you're looking for something like that then expect to be disappointed. Fortunately for me, I like simple and straight forward. I find that it's hard to get invested in a story if the game is sending me on 5 different side quests just to progress the story, which luckily this game doesn't do. You won't feel the element of choice in this game, as there is only one story line and you can't make descisions. If you try to deviate the game will just tell you to restart from the last checkpoint. I also find that the mechanics aren't really that realistic. For example, the stealth: you can strangle an enemy while trying to sneak around and the neighboring guards won't really notice. Or the police chases, pretty much a carbon copy of GTA, if you get out of the line of sight of the cops you'll be clear. These aren't criticisms, because these make the game overall more enjoyable for me personally, especially for a remake of a game that was made in 2002. However, if these seem like things that would turn you away from the game than I would advise against buying it. Overall I really enjoyed the game, there really isn't much to do after completing the story so I'd recommend buying on sale.

I recommend playing on legacy mode, it will give you that old school vibe of dying and retrying, but not to the point where it frustrates you. Shooting feels good, although sometimes I found the pistols to be underpowered. It can take 4 shots to the body to kill someone. Cars handle great. There's a lot of under- and oversteering but that's the fun of it. Driving feels very authentic. Graphics are amazing. I could run it in 1080p on the highest settings with 90fps with a RTX 2060, and I have played it on my TV in 4k, also on the highest settings, with 60fps with a RTX 3070. There is alot of detail in the world and it feels very much alive. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I bounced off the original Mafia back in the early 2000's because of the driving and the race car level. While still not the best (everything pretty much handles like a washing machine on wheels), it has been greatly improved, enough to let me play this all the way through. The character acting and motion capture in this game are stunning, it is a cinematic experience from start to finish. The Definitive Edition is no longer an open world game in the vein of GTA, but instead has been turned into a fairly linear story driven cover shooter with some driving and stealth missions. While I miss the motivation to go an explore this wonderfully detailed city, what has been presented is a 10 hour experience that never overstays it's welcome. It is a trimmed, well put together story. I highly recommend to anyone willing to struggle past the driving sections and the loss of side missions, it is well worth a play-through.

_childDocuments_.review: A great attempt at a remake of an absolutely outstanding game. When I saw the first few trailers and heard the new voice actor for Tommy I cringed, and became a little worried that they'd butchered some of the characters. I wasn't wrong - some feel the same/similar, others are completely different.Tommy himself doesn't act anything like the Tommy from the original game. Paulie was absolutely butchered by the modeling team, Sam is just a lifeless goon until he's needed, and Don Salieri looks like he's 10 years younger and acts nothing like his original self.Playing in classic mode was entertaining and overall I enjoyed the game, despite the glaring flaws with some of the creative liberties taken by the writers/developers. It's very clear the game is running on the Mafia 3 engine - the launcher is a giveaway by itself - and this is a travesty as it completely removes the original gunplay and extreme attention to detail within the game world and the way the player interacts with it. And good lord, don't even get me started on the stealth mechanics that shouldn't even exist.Also, what happened to the music? I was so disappointed when the radio turned on and none of the original music was there, and this applies to all areas of the game, including the Main Menu of the game itself. They should have kept the original score, it's beautiful.This feels like some kind of Netflix reboot of a series that ended up getting 50% on RT. I'm still leaving a positive review since I enjoyed playing it, but it left a slightly sour taste in my mouth due to so many unnecessary and often obnoxious changes.Also, please, for the love of god and all that's holy, don't force me to watch 15 minutes of credit with no way to skip them. Seriously. I paid for the game, I shouldn't be held captive for 15 minutes at the end of it.

_childDocuments_.review: With this review I want to show some negatives of Mafia: Definitive edition and why I wouldnt really recommend it.If we were looking at Mafia as its own thing, the game would be good. But the issue is that it isnt its own thing. There is competition that does much better for the similar price tag.I bought this game because of its "open world" tag, thinking that it would be similar to gta 5, but in a different setting. Of course I was hoping for the game to have its own unique spin on the open world genre, but what happend really disappointed me. (Just a heads up; this review will have some comparisons between gta 5 and mafia)The game IS open world, but you cant do a whole lot with this world. Instead of having a open world game with a story, this is a story set in the open world, meaning that instead of having a lot to do in the open world, the only thing you actually do is missions. But those arent the main issues I have with the game. In a single mission I encountered TWO bugs, not even 30 minutes into the playthrough. For those wondering, its the second chapter. The game instructs me to sprint, and I see the valley that I decide to run towards. Only to be blocked by some magical wall (??) causing me to lose the mission. No big deal, I restart from last checkpoint and manage to run through the valley. Now Im told to vault over the fence. I do it. I continue to run and now I have to vault onto some crates (??) and now I fall through the world and die.... That all happend in the span of couple of minutes. Right there and then I though of quitting the game, but part of me tought that the odds of this happening are low so I kept on playing.The driving camera feels odd to say the least. The gun gameplay feels ok, but it lacks that oomph. In gta for example the whole screen greys out and zooms in for a short period while showing the little x, which feels awesome. The controls for anything that isnt gun related are weird though.... Why cant I press m1 to smack someone with the bat? Instead I have to spam q for whatever reason.And finally the language. I really love when a character in 1930s says "stop bustin my balls". The game isnt bad and I can see why the game has so many positive reviews, but it isnt my cup of tea. I dont think its worth 40€ especially when gta 5 which costs 50% more offers MUCH more. Not to mention that gta 5 often goes on sale meaning you can get it for even less than 60€. I would recommend buying this game only if its on sale, and only then.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it once before on console and had an enjoyable experience so I decided to play it again on PC and I'm quite surprised how bad it is.From what i can remember about the story and all that it's pretty good but the gameplay is just awful.I don't need to go on about the racing mission because It's been done but the driving in general in this game is really bad.The controls are unresponsive and very slow.The AI is awful.The movement on foot in the game feels choppy and weird. Melee combat is a joke. Shooting is fine but standard.Overall I would give this remake like a 3/10 on PC.Console version wasn't as broken so I could at least get through the game so it would get like a 5-6/10. Mainly because of the story.

name: The Flower Collectors
detailed_description: A detective mystery set in the political powder-keg of Barcelona in 1977. You play Jorge, a retired policeman who uses a wheelchair, struggling with a difficult past. Alone on your balcony, you watch the world pass by through binoculars. One stormy night, you witness a murder. Determined to uncover the truth, you form an unlikely alliance with young ambitious journalist Melinda and start your investigation. Together, you’ll solve a complex mystery by unravelling the secrets of unsuspecting neighbours. Inspired by classic crime noir films and games like Campo Santo's Firewatch, The Flower Collectors is a detective story with a whole lot of heart. Solve a captivating murder mystery with an unusual storyline Meet a host of colourful anthropomorphic characters in a lush, atmospheric world Investigate using your binoculars, camera and transmitter to uncover neighborhood secrets from your balcony Create a crime chronology to figure out whodunnit Interrogate priests, beggars, club singers and nosy old ladies alike Dive into the unique setting of post-Franco Barcelona in the 70ies Emphasizes characters, world building and narrative over skill challenges

short_description: Barcelona, 1977. An ex-cop in a wheelchair witnesses a murder, and teams up with a young ambitious journalist to bring the truth to light. With camera, binoculars and transmitter in hand, uncover the town’s secrets from your balcony in this soul-searching detective mystery.

_childDocuments_.review: The flower collectors is first person investigation that takes place in Barcelona in 1977 two years after death of Franco and in the weeks coming up to the first elections that signalled Spains' transition into democracy. Your character is Jorge a former member of the infamous Policia Armada who was retired to a wheelchair following a savage revenge beating. The game takes place mostly in Jorges apartment, on his balcony overlooking the central plaza he lives on. Whiling away his days drinking, stoned on painkillers and spying on his neighbours, he witnesses a murder and decides to piece together the evidence and solve the crime. He's aided in this by a rebel freelance journalist, Melinda, who was to meet the victim for a story she was about to break. The game wears it's influences on it's sleeve, most notably the Hitchcock movie "Rear Window". Much like the movie, the entire game is from the point of view of a character confined to a wheelchair, observing everyone around him. The murder even takes place during a thunderstorm, just like in the movie. After the murder, upon seeing the polices' lack of protocol and urgency surrounding the crime, Jorge becomes convinced there is something up. Enter Mel, who reveals herself as a journalist who had scheduled the meet with the victim for information on atrocities committed by the Policia Armada and the Guardia Civil.Over the course of the game you will piece together the stories of the people you have been spying on, solve the murder and help Jorge reconcile himself with his past. For the most part the game looks fine. The slightly cell-shaded look to the graphics works for the scenery. The issue with the graphics comes to the character models. They're designed well enough, it's just that none of them have proper eyes. They all have this eerie blank stare like you've wound up on the set of the Children of the Corn or some other horror movie. It just destroys a lot of the relatability of a character when you're constantly looking at them thinking "Did they mean to use searing comets for their eyes or was it a mistake?"The model movements aren't properly done either. They all move with a real artificial style and really make it seem like they are completely separate from the ground or any other objects they're interacting with. The movements don't always sync up with what they're saying either in the dialogue scenes. Some times they're giving off nonchalant body movements when giving a really serious or important line, other times I was looking at a character go full Calculon while describing a mundane activity. This is a particular bugbear as there areso many dialogue scenes that it results in the lack of proper mo-cap becoming a really glaring issue. The lip-sync is terrible too also. There's a chance that's it's synced to the original Spanish and the English voice-over is just a dub but there's no option to play with Spanish Voice-overs so I've no idea. Blasphemous had a similar problem in that, while it was developed by a Spanish studio staffed almost entirely by Spanish speakers, it was released with only English Audio to try to give it as wide an appeal as possible. In fact, it only recently, as of this videos release, got a Spanish Audio release years after the game launch. The dialogue is decent. It progresses the story but it's not going to blow you away. The best I could say about it, is that it's functional. Most of the characters just outright say what they feel, like they've all been to the same support group or something. I suppose this is a result of the limitation of the graphics. Without the ability to convey anything through facial expressions, you're relying on the script and the voice actor to do the emotional and tonal heavy lifting. Unfortunately, it falls downs on both counts. The voice actors efforts are completely undermined by some really poor editing that leaves huge gaps in-between each line. It really takes the immersion from a scene involving two people in a room when it's abundantly clear that the voice actors aren't.The use of animals as characters mirrors the similar use of them in the comic series MAUS which uses the cutesy animals as a sort of fluffy counterpoint to the Nazi atrocities it depicts. The flower collectors uses them as a counterpoint to the horrors of Francos Spain. However, unlike MAUS, flower collectors never really goes into any real detail. For all the story you're told, the police were a nasty group of people just beat up and imprisoned a load of artists, poets and gays. A few died and that's what fuels the story but it goes nowhere near the reality that, at one point, around 250 people a day were being shot dead by the police forces in Barcelona alone. In Madrid the number was closer to 400.I suppose my main issue with this is that the developers could've gone into some real depth here about a topic that isn't very well known. Spain under Franco was basically a War-Crime factory for over thirty years and almost no-one outside of Spain knows a huge amount about it. Even less when you venture outside Europe. So there was a huge vein of historical material that could've been mined to give the story some real bite and traction. Instead the mass deaths are pared down to a handful and the White Terror isn't even mentioned. They even cop out on Jorge by having him state he can't remember what he got up to during his time in the Flower collectors, in an act of ultimate fence-sitting. It would've given the scenes so much more impetus if he'd actually been a witness or even responsible for some deaths. We're given a hand waivey "I was drunk and I can't remember" excuse. I found this odd as it almost seemed as if the writers didn't want to discuss the very events that underpinned the game. This running away from the source material undermined the story and the characters in a big way. With such an interesting angle, I can't see why the devs didn't completely go all in on it.As for the story itself, it's passible. The series of events that lead from the murder to the resolution never get too far fetched and the mini-stories of all the minor characters are quite good, in particular the one of Carmen the singer. I was confused by the dream sequences being dropped so suddenly. We get one almost every chapter end and they seem to be building to a crest regarding how Jorge came to be in his wheelchair but then we never get another one. Then we're just told bluntly how he got injured. It seemed like such wasted opportunity. The gameplay is good.  Given the nature of the main character, the style of investigation is entirely observation based and it's done quite well. The mechanic is repeated throughout the game so, if it has you bored in the first twenty minutes, I'd quit the game and get the refund because it doesn't get any better as the game goes on. My main issue with the gameplay is that it's quite repetitive in that most of what you're doing is just scanning for an item or person, finding them and clicking.In conclusion, The flower collectors is an interesting little game (2.5 hours) with a decent story and some OK artwork. It's  a game with some good points all offset by some poor design and/or execution. It has good artwork but its' simplicity  has all the characters look like they've been hypnotised. The voice-acting is good but is offset by the terrible mo-cap. The dialogue and story work well but there's so much more that could've been put in to really enhance it and give some impact but it falls short in the scant playtime. This is a bit ironic as more game time would've really highlighted the repetitive nature of the gameplay even more and ruined the game. I'd like to recommend Flower collectors as a game with a unique play angle and a decent storyline but I can't for full price. There's just not enough here, both in content and effort, to justify it. But on sale, I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: It was a shame that the game was so easy. You won’t get stuck or struggle to find clues to solve the case. The game is designed to keep you moving so don’t expect a murder mystery in the vain of Sherlock Holmes for example. This is purely a nice and interesting way to spend five hours watching a story unfold. There is a slice of political history thrown in to the mixture which is entwined with the main characters. The story was well told but was interesting rather than exciting or dramatic. Similar to Blacksad, there are anthropomorphic characters playing the main roles and although not to the standard of its counterpart, I thought the characters looked quite realistic and pleasing. The environment is small. There are only two locations;  Inside Jorge’s apartment where certain characters visit and conversations are had, and outside where Jorge moves up and down his balcony observing events in the Plaza. There is a café, nightclub, garage and church along with a handful of characters to watch. Jorge uses a set of binoculars which can zoom in and watch events unfold and he can also take photos with his camera for vital clues and evidence. The game is quite linear in that sense. You can take as many photos as you like but you’ll only be able to use photos that the game dictates, indicated by your camera view turning red. Once you have collected enough evidence you can visit the pinboard and place the clues and photos in the right place. It isn’t that difficult and if you get it wrong you aren’t penalized; you just try again until you get it right.  The story briefly explains how Spain has struggled politically with democracy and certain freedoms most of Europe takes for granted. The scene is set in Barcelona in the late seventies and revolves around a retired police detective called Jorge and a journalist called Melinda. Together they try and solve a murder that the police do not seem interested to investigate. As they uncover more clues and evidence, they realise that their pasts have a big role to play in the mystery.  Jorge is wheelchair bound and cannot leave his apartment. He can move around outside where he has a wrap around balcony. He can see all events that happen in the plaza by using his binoculars, which can zoom in to observe more closely, and a camera which takes photos. He also has a walkie talkie where he can relay instructions to Melinda. For example, he can ask her to talk to characters or eaves drop on conversations. It isn’t as open world as this sounds however. It is linear and he will only be able to ask Melinda to carry out these instructions when the game allows. Mostly, you will be reading and listening to dialogues between the handful of characters in the game. This will reveal clues and set up the next scene. I was very impressed with the voice acting. It sounded very professional and was full of emotion and character. At the end of these dialogues you might be tasked to observe certain people in the square and try and get more information. You can ask Melinda to listen in to conversations occasionally or you can take photos of suspects. Any evidence gathered is then placed on the pinboard where you have to arrange the correct bit of evidence with the question asked. For example, how did we identify the Victim? You soon learn that there is no penalty for getting this wrong so it doesn’t feel like you are a detective, rather it’s just another mechanic to forward the story and feel more interactive.Other than observing and listening, occasionally you are asked to perform certain chores in a timed manner. You will have between three and five minutes to carry out tasks like finding certain objects hidden in the square or helping somebody gain safe passage from the prying eyes of the Police. These are mainly achievement based and if you fail the story still continues. There’s a slim chance you will get stuck trying to gather evidence but because the environments are so small eventually you will find that piece of evidence you are after. Sometimes you will be given a choice of answers in a dialogue exchange but again these are mainly achievement based and don’t have much bearing on the story. The achievements are fun to get and will offer you scope to play the game again. Once completed the game can be played from any of the ten chapters making it easier to mop up any you missed on your first playthrough.  I loved the graphics and I was frequently marveling at little things I noticed throughout my playtime. The characters are quite animated and portray their emotions quite well. There are loads of nice touches like weather conditions, the way life just seems so real in the square and the way characters interact with each other. I particularly liked the way characters could be seen entering rooms and talking to characters whilst you watched through your binoculars. It just kept the immersion levels very high and made you feel like you were actually spying on people. The sound was used perfectly to create drama and tension. Apart from the superb voice acting there was a nice sound track playing throughout which changed appropriately with each scene. Curator Info: This game was received for free
