_childDocuments_.review: Calling The Flower Collectors a detective mystery game is like calling cheesecake a health food; the components that make it means you’re correct but mostly on a technicality. This isn’t to say the game fails on its premise, but it feels more like a visual novel played out at a distance (pun partially intended). Sharp writing, good voice acting and an intriguing story kept me hooked to complete the game in one sitting, but I walked away from it feeling less like a sleuth and more of an inquisitive spectator.Since this is a story-driven game, discussing its plot in detail would lead to spoilers, so I’ll only touch on themes and what’s known in the marketing. With the game taking place in Barcelona in 1977, how much is reflected of our real world is beyond my historical/social knowledge, but it certainly addresses subjects that are very real and still encountered in our modern time. Playing as Jorge, a wheelchair-bound ex-cop, a murder occurs in the plaza outside his home. Through morbid curiosity, and with the local police not making progress, he falls in cahoots with a journalist named Melinda, teaming up to lead their own investigation. While player control is with Jorge, being a wheelchair user means he can’t wander about to question people or examine scenes; Melinda acts on his behalf this way. Either through binoculars or a camera, Jorge can scope the surrounding neighbourhood and indicate what Melinda should investigate or who she should talk to via receiver radios. It’s seldom for Jorge to speak to others directly (excluding Melinda), so after directing Melinda, there’s downtime as she chats up a person or examines a scene. You’re not left twiddling idle thumbs for very long, usually long enough to give the area another scan or think on possibilities for the case while she does her thing.Thanks to solid writing, information that’s reported back is succinct, to the point and lacks useless fluff (red herrings excluded) that also gets recorded in Jorge’s journal for later reflection. After significant events or the end of that chapter, registered info, clues and testimony must be placed on a timeline to uncover motives, occurrences and eventually, solve the murder. Unsurprisingly things aren’t that simple story-wise as the investigation unfolds, but unfortunately it is that simple gameplay-wise. It boils down to plunking puzzle pieces into place then moving right along to the next chapter. As the player, you aren’t investigating per se; Jorge and Melinda are doing most if not all of the vocalization and thinking - You just slap their findings on a corkboard and call it a day. There didn’t appear to be any fail states for placing the wrong clues to the wrong place either, just a quick ‘no, that’s not right’ and have you try again. This would’ve gotten in my way of enjoying the game if not for the script, concept and actors pulling me in and keeping my interest. Where choices really become your own is in the limited order versus chaos dilemma the game poses. Considering the year, location and political climate the game communicates, I can’t help but feel your moral alignment with these choices are merely black and white. Order is intrinsically evil as it favours corruption and brushing things under the rug to retain balance, while chaos isn’t pretty, but it means letting the truth be known and taking the ‘system’ down a peg*. The lack of finger-wagging (there’s no saving you from Melinda’s incensed wrath at times, though) by the game makes it a story to experience and not having any titanic weight of ‘the big moral lesson’ hanging above your head. For the heavy subjects the game addresses, it’s all played seriously but with sensitivity to avoid portraying the villains as cartoonish in their evil intent, or portraying the locals as cardboard cutouts whose fates are easily disposable. This treatment also extends to Jorge’s disability and using a wheelchair, a concept that’s not lofted to push an agenda or try to garner empty sympathy; it’s a part of him as a character/person, the game works with and around it. Admittedly, this concept was what garnered my interest in the game in the first place. As someone with disabilities of my own, it’s not often to see such characters portrayed without being treated as a punchline or used for the aforementioned empty sympathy.Despite its genre, The Flower Collectors favours solid, full colours instead of hard noir comic stylings. Ignoring the awful occurrences nearby, the game is warm to the eyes, which avoids strain when scoping around for clues. While it’s only one location and with the limited sight of it, Jorge’s neighbourhood is a nice place to look at. The warmth of the visuals does mean that when there’s an action to trigger, it may not immediately be apparent since there’s no evident highlights or markers, the HUD itself being very limited. I only had this occur twice in my three and a half hour playthrough, and anything time-sensitive generally has a generous window to work with. While the gameplay is limited to looking around, putting clues on a board to get a yes or no response and a handful of dialogue options, The Flower Collectors does just enough with its story, interactions and concept to keep it from being flimsy and dull. There’s some replayability with side plots that can be missed, though they don’t seem critical to the game’s completion, more of wrapping up all the optional loose ends. You can find better if you want a mystery game that asks more of you as a player, but on the other hand, if you want an interactive mystery to solve and not have the stress of various webs of intrigue to sift through, The Flower Collectors gets a definite recommendation from me.*My own moral alignment may be influencing this view, so I can’t call this a criticism in fairness.
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: This unique game got me hooked. I loved the new detective style. It speaks about fighting for equality in the '70s and how the community looks at 'different' people as something that should be wiped off the earth. You play Jorge, a retired cop who is prisoned in his wheelchair after an incident in the past. One day he witnessed a murder from his balcony, then a young journalist sought his help to hide in his small apartment. Armed only with his binoculars and camera, Jorge decided to help her and watch the townspeople from his balcony, taking photos of evidence to help the young journalist to uncover the secret behind the murder.There are ten chapters (You'll be able to jump to any of them once you finish the game) the puzzles are only on the detective board, none of them are difficult to figure out. I liked the idea of controlling two people, helping the other characters to sneak around by observing their surroundings. everything the game did is good and enjoyable, although your character is stuck in one place, they made it very interesting.You can choose how your character responds to some of the conversations, and it does affect your relationship and outcome with the other characters. There are multiple characters to observe and learn their full story, this will change the ending of the game. The voiceovers are very good, I liked all of them as well as the soundtracks. In the beginning, I didn't like the first-person aspect, but I'm glad it didn't give me any motion sickness as you are most of the time sitting and zooming in and out. I liked the character's design, they are portraying them with animals, they did a good job showing their personalities through their facial expressions. Pros:+Interesting well-written story.+Unique gameplay.+Good voiceovers.+Interesting characters.+Good soundtracks.+Good puzzles.+Multiple endings and characters stories.+Good game length.+Chapters select.+Steam achievements.Cons:-No manual save.Very enjoyable and well-written game with a good pace, I highly recommend it to people with an open mind who enjoys murder mystery, Noir detective games.

_childDocuments_.review: Game received for free as part of the Average Achievement Hunter Curator. Thank you to the developers.To quote the game description, "...a detective story with a whole lot of heart", and more than that. The Flower Collectors puts you in the shoes, or wheels in this case, of a grizzled, cranky, retired policeman with a lot on his mind and even more on his soul trying to cope with the changes knocking on Spain's door after the end of Franco's regime.The game is set in an anthropomorphic version of Barcelona in 1977 and your entire world view is from your balcony. As one reviewer already mentioned, the idea immediately reminded me of Alfred Hitchcock's Rear Window. And I quite like how it's implemented here. Being bound to a wheelchair, you watch your neighbourhood through your binoculars, following people's lives while reminiscing about yours. The neighbourhood itself is very well done. The art style is lovely and fits the game. Limiting the play area left the developers with a small sized world that could be fleshed out and they did a good job. Colorful characters, a giant graffiti, small details in the environment like posters and pamphlets, very nicely modelled cars (and I do mean very nicely, special kudos for that), different weather as the days pass (giant fan of rain and the droplets striking the balcony), some great lighting at night and it all adds up to a living, breathing neighbourhood. A small, but understandable flaw, there are no characters populating the neighbourhood that would bring more life to it apart from the story ones.The audio is nicely done, music fits the story and the voices (you can practically hear the enthusiasm in them) are particulary good for a small indie game.The story is not afraid to throw punches and take a side dealing wih oppressive regimes, something you'll almost never see in the AAA industry (or at least they'll never admit to taking a side). Without getting overly political, the game follows a murder mystery with a historical context you witness from your balcony and leads to you taking a stand with a young journalist all the while reevaluating your past and your actions. During the investigation, you are eyes for your colleague on the ground, communicating through a walkie-talkie (Firewatch vibes) and guiding her actions and in the process somewhat influencing the lives of your neighbours. And the story flows smoothly, building momentum for the end which comes somewhat abruptly, but is still satisfying and not a deal breaker in any way.The technical side has some slight issues in the animations department. They're a little bit janky overall. Characters would sometimes just slide instead of walk, there's no animations for taking things, talking on a telephone or for characters entering cars. There were no other bugs, glitches or crashes and the animations don't detract that much from the game and can easily be overlooked for the narrative and the charm the game offers.The game's message and the historical context is very timely for the world we live in and it's an interesting choice for an Austrian based studio (or maybe not, considering Austria's history). In essence, this could be everyone's story. A story about "...a line that separates the place where everyone begins from the place where too many bring themselves, no matter their age, nation or circumstances. A line that separates the reasonably just from the mere functionary." If you're at all interested what that line might be, give The Flower Collectors a spin. It's sometimes too on the nose with it's views, but it doesn't require much of your time and will leave you thinking about the line.Take a peek inside the newly opened  if you like to walk off the beaten path and only sometimes return to the main roads. You might find something worth exploring. And if you do, thank you for the visit.: The game doesn't count for any statistics, for now at least. After finishing it once, I had 7/13 achievements. It seems some achievements are tied to you spotting scenes and character interactions at certain times in the story. There is chapter select after finishing it once and I've cleared the missing achievements by using it, so it makes getting them easier.

_childDocuments_.review: - It is a game set in Spain, in the post-Franco era, a very original setting and very rare in the medium.- The starting point is extraordinary, outlining a very interesting plot.- The game is very reminiscent of the ‘Blacksad’ comic, adapting our world to an anthropomorphic one where the personality of each character is a nod to the animal it represents.- The music accompanies really well, even without having any memorable theme.- The dubbing is in English, mixing some words in a strange way in Spanish (like ‘policías’, or ‘señor J’), happening the same with some written documents.- The game takes place in only one scenario: the protagonist's small flat and the square and surroundings that he can see from his balcony; this is not necessarily a negative point, especially if we take into account that it tries to adopt films like ‘Rear Window’, ‘The Cabin’ or ‘Last Call’ to the videogame genre.- Its animations are really poor.- The gameplay elements are reduced to three sections: puzzle elements (where we must place photographs and drawings in the correct order on a nautical chart as appropriate at the end of the day), stealth moments (literally three moments, where we must guide two characters to get from one point to another on the stage without being detected by other characters: something really simple to achieve and not challenging at all) and moments where we must observe our neighbours to get plot details or different clues.- The story is quite interesting, but the further we get into it and the more we tie up loose ends, the less interesting it becomes.- It's only 2.5-3 hours long, so buying this game off sale is not an option.The Flower Collectors is a videogame in which unfortunately the low budget is noticeable, a kind of failed videogame; it is an interactive adventure that starts from a great idea and that a priori is interesting, but it falls halfway. Why do I recommend it, despite all its negative points? Because the game managed to hook me from the beginning to the end: it is a very slow-paced and somewhat predictable game, but I played through it straight through, without pausing, and that is something I value very positively. Besides, I really liked the two main characters, although I regret that it didn't go deeper into them or the neighbours in the neighbourhood. 5,5/10.It's a pity that The Flower Collectors didn't have a bigger budget. If it had, it is certain that this work would have achieved a more rounded result. As a videogame, it has a lot of potential, but it's a pity that only the two main characters are so developed, or that it doesn't have better character animations to convey something more than awkwardness and intentions to the player.
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Nope, it is a little detective story about a political (?) murder in Spain after Franco's death.A grumpy ex-policeman, bound to a wheelchair after an accident, spends his time rolling around in his little flat (2 rooms, balcony), smoking, watching the neighbours with his binoculars, drawing little pictures, taking pills against his pain... but mostly sleeping and being bored. This flat is his world, and this is where the game takes place. Suddenly a gunshot in the night, and a dead corpse in the middle of the plaza under his flat. A young, terrified girl knocks on the door, breaking into his little world. And so the story begins...From your balcony you can see only a few houses, a plaza and 3 streets leading into the plaza. A cabaret, a mechanic shop, a church, a cafe, some rooms in other houses... this is where the action happens. There are around 15 characters populating the scenery, this seems to be a quite part of the city. The characters all have their little stories, though.The gameplay consists of rolling around the flat, mostly the blacony, in your wheelchair, and observing the souroundings with a binocular or camera. You see people move around, discover their secrets, and your new-found friend, the young lady that fled into your apartment, is down in the streets. You talk to her via transmitter and tell her where to go and sometimes what to do... and she does the groundwork. The game seems to advance only when you discover the required clues, so it is not possible to watch one point and oversee something happen elsewhere. Actually, you are guided as what to find out next with kind of quest markers. There are timed sequences where you have to observe certain locations, but either I always discovered everything or at least the story continues if you do not see everything. After some chapters you have to piece the collected clues together to reconstruct what you found out so far.The game is divided into chapters and it saves only at the end of a chapter. Can be easily played via controller, but works also fine with m+kb.Unique adventure, but quite scripted and not overly challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: The promise of a Rear Window esque detective story game is a very compelling premise. But between its short 2 hour runtime, its underwhelming presentation, and little gameplay beyond waiting and pixelhunting, this is a hard game to recommend. But ultimately even its story is a rather rote, heavy-handed detective mystery that's isn't very engaging. Perhaps at $5 during a steam sale it might be worth a play.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the weaker detective game I've played. Very rough around the edges. Severe animation issues. And all around boring. Considering it only took me 3 hours to finish and it still felt like a bit of a drag, it seems half bakes at best. Shame, was excited for it too. At least it's somewhat pretty when the characters aren't turning by sliding or moving through walls.The narrative was ok. But not good enough to carry the games weight (or so to say the rest of its flaws) on its own. I wish they would've focused on their strengths or developed the further on to iron out the very blatant issues with it. Currently the games issues are truly to its detriment. Talking about police brutality as the police characters play a stock stomping animation and the other character playing a stock prone animation just throws out any and all weight we might feel to a funny occurrence instead. Considering you are bound to a single position with a camera or binoculars, you could've just put both those characters behind a wall we can't see through and play a fall animation on the victim to leave the rest to our imagination instead of doing something so clumsy.The game does take it self super seriously and I would say with these flaws this would make it a great comedic experience but rest of it is so slow and tedious the main mood stays as boredom instead. I say don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: 4h+ 3/10 1, but you might end up with at least one more No Not yet. I tried to write one, but it isn't easy for this game. I hope somebody else will be able to make a good guide. 3 on Astats No Yes, mostly the side quests No No No No No difficulty option NoThis game is amazing! It is a story-driven detective adventure game. It doesn't waste much time before the story gets really interesting. You play as Jorge, an ex-police officer who got hurt and ended up in a wheelchair. You're stuck in your apartment with only your sketchbook and a binocular, watching your neighborhood. You'll never leave your apartment during the whole story, which may sound weird, but you can see a lot of things from your balcony and you get a "partner in crime" who can investigate things for you. This game has so much charm. The voice acting is amazing, and the artwork has so many small details. The game has a political theme, which might not be for everybody. It is also based in a time where freedom of speaking up and freedom of being sexually attracted to the same sex isn't accepted by the authorities. At the beginning of the story, the main character is very short-minded but during the story you'll see that his opinion changed when he sees how unfair certain people get treated. A big downside to this game and that is that it doesn't have a manual save system. It saves automatically at the end of every chapter (there are 10 chapters). If you quit during a chapter, you'll be back at the beginning of that chapter when you start the game. Most chapters aren't that long, but some might feel long and it sucks that you can't quit the game during a chapter to come back to it where you left off. Another small downside was that some sections have a countdown timer in which you have to do something, or find something. Those sections gave me a bit of stress while I think the game didn't need that. In my opinion the game could easily not have times sections and still tell the same impressive story. I would highly recommend playing this game the first time without any guide or help. It is worth it to fully experience the game the first time. It took me around 3 to 4 hours to beat it without a guide. After you beat the game you get chapter selection so you can easily get the achievements in which you had to make a different choice. There are quite a few missable achievements, for the side stories. Try to focus on all the main characters during your first playthrough. Then in a second playthrough you can focus on the ones you're missing. There is an achievement for completing all the side quests, but you don't have to do that in 1 playthrough. The achievement will check if you got all the side quests achievements and the beginning of the credits.

_childDocuments_.review: The previous game from these developers - "The Lion's Song", was an incredible little discovery for me. I can talk about it a lot, but the most important thing for me was the incredible courage of the original idea. I really hoped that this courage would not disappear in the developers in the following projects, and I was not mistaken in my expectations. The concept of their new game is again beyond praise, while avoiding unnecessary complexity. Here we have such a Hitchcock's «Rear Window», crossed with Spain, still seething after Franco left. A lone and middle-aged former investigator, moving around the apartment in a wheelchair, periodically watching the streets through his binoculars, suddenly becomes a witness to the murder, and someone is knocking insistently on his door. And now he will have to investigate this murder, without leaving his balcony, observing and using the help of other people, collecting new evidence and unraveling the entire web of crimes.Someone may call this game a “walking simulator” and will probably be right. But the crux of the matter is that it is a masterfully directed walking simulator in which there are no voids and boredom. Scriptwriters are constantly throwing new leads to you that support your interest. The characters that the investigator observes are very lively and worked out, there are a large number of secondary storylines that the player may not notice for the first time. Some small plot moments seemed completely unnecessary for me in 1977, and they existed here solely for the sake of modern trends, but overall I was pleased with the plot. Visually, the game does not look as impressive as The Lion's Song, everything is much simpler and more angular, but how does the game sound ... The voice acting of the characters (especially Jorge) is incredible, the jazz Spanish musical accompaniment is simply unearthly, I forgot about the game several times and just Listened to music, it is so beautiful.“The Flower Collectors” fully met expectations, we have a very strong game, focused on the plot and immersion of the player in the surrounding world. It sounds incredible, it plays nicely, we are waiting for a new meeting (as you promised in the credits)

_childDocuments_.review: At a time where democracies all over the world seem to be sliding back into authoritarian regimes, when dictators like Orban in Hungary have amassed power to promote skewed traditional values at the expense of others that don't fit within their idealized visions of the nation, narratives like The Flower Collectors remind us of the dangers authoritarian strongmen pose, and how precious democracy really is.Set in Barcelona, Spain during the tail end (no pun intended) of Franco's regime, you play an ex-cop named Jorge whose daily monotony gets overturned when he witnesses a murder in the town plaza one stormy night. Together with Melinda, a journalist for a leftist publication, they seek to uncover the mystery behind this murder and find the deep ties that strangle everyone in this small town. From the cabaret that serves as a reprieve for artists and poets seen as degenerates against the regime, to the church that enforces strict values for the sake of maintaining power within this system, everyone is involved and connected somehow through six degrees of separation. All this ties with the general elections coming up, and the future of Spanish democracy with it.The historical backdrop reeks into the everyday lives of these characters; after all, life itself is political as Melinda notes, and it seeps into the most minute details of the town's denizens and their lives. The game does well in discussing how police authority can be used and abused in authoritarian environments, as well questions whether those often deemed as 'degenerate' against a government's traditional values really deserve to be labeled as such in the first place.While the narrative and world building is engaging, areas in terms of gameplay need to be more polished; as Jorge is disabled and bound to a wheelchair, you conduct most of your investigations and searches seated from the balcony, with Melinda serving as your feet on the ground. You relay to her instructions through your transmitters, while watching from above through binoculars and camera lenses. At the end of the day, you take the clues you amassed and pin them up on a board, searching for connections and answers in the process. As most of your tasks often leave you to watch the action taking place, you're often left feeling like an observer most of the time. This may have some narrative use, as Jorge's arc is one that transforms him from passive observation to taking on a more active role and responsibility, but it does leave one to wonder what details they're missing that could help expand upon the situation of each character and how they tie to the greater dangers of the world as a whole. Sometimes, the instructions on the left-hand corner of the screen are too vague, and I've spent quite an amount of time searching in frustration for clues in a heavily detailed environment with little to no direction, unsure of what I should be looking for in the first place.The animation can appear jarring and odd at times, lacking a polish as characters sometimes slide across the ground; which is a shame, because overall the art style does contain some charm to it. The world outside Jorge's balcony is no doubt alive, and the details do make one feel they are in some small Spanish town, but areas in the rigging could be improved upon to avoid yanking the player out from the immersive experience of the world.Overall, The Flower Collectors is a charming game with a lot to talk about. While areas in the gameplay and animation could be improved upon, its message feels relevant and timely.
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: What I love about Mi'pu'mi Games is that the time and place their games take place is very important to the story. It's not just set dressing. This one takes places as Spain is making the transition to democracy, which not everyone is happy about. As a retired police officer, you team up with a journalist to solve a murder that took place on your street. It's like a combination of Rear Window, in that you're observing and photographing, as opposed to doing the investigating yourself. Your partner goes and searches for clues and talks to people while you direct and look out for her. Overall, I thought it was quite good. Nice writing and voice acting, great pacing. At around 3 hours it was the perfect length. The story was very engaging, and though there wasn't a ton to the gameplay it was satisfying in a voyeuristic sort of way.

_childDocuments_.review: TFC has an interesting plot, but the gameplay and actual meat of the story was a bit lackluster to me. as previous reviews mentioned, there is a lot of potential that could've been dived into for this game, and I do agree that it felt disappointing to have the main character say he didn't remember what he did, etc etc. but all the same, I did feel like the way the topic was introduced was pretty good. my other disappointment with this game is that it's less actually solving the mystery and more following along. yes, there is information presented that isn't truly relevant to what happened, but there's no real consequence to getting your theories wrong. If you are wanting a much more stressful, heightened detective game (where you're not actually a detective & your mistakes cost you) I would wholeheartedly recommend Night Call. overall I enjoyed it, it was an interesting story to follow along to for a few hours, just think the plot could have been enhanced more with more details & connections.

_childDocuments_.review: I longed for a game like this and I'm glad I bought it. I'm a huge fan of Firewatch and this was familiar. Nice music, setting, decent storytelling and good voice acting. Some silly, off-putting character animations. I don't get these strange choices to have them be animals? It could have done without the "surreal" element (the story here is not Sam & Max). They way the character interacted with each other was also strangely similar to characters from the Sims. Except the two protagonists, the other characters are not really developed or interesting.   Still, these flaws don't really take anything away from the enjoyment. The "puzzles" are not challenging at all, but I'm fine with the exploration and story-driven focus. _childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games I've played thus far this year. Very enjoyable to play with some surprisingly incredible voice acting. I wasn't expecting that when coming into it. I recommend using a controller over a mouse, as the mouse moves the screen so fast it's disorienting. Nice to play with someone else and pass the controller back and forth too. Very good story, especially for a fellow young leftist (who admittedly knows nothing about Spanish politics). Looking forward to what this studio does next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: The setup is certainly intriguing and the developers have certainly done their research on the time period and the setting. Politics played a big part back then and even though the dictatorship was over, there was still a lot of tension in the air. Furthermore violent police raids were still common if you were believed to be on the wrong side of the “family values” according to the far right wing government and Catholic Church. This is demonstrated throughout the game and it’s easy to follow even if you don’t have a lot of knowledge of 1970’s Spain. This conflict is also shown through the characters as Jorge is a conservative older male and the other character he meets is a more liberal young woman who writes for, as Jorge puts it, “one of the few leftie rags in the country”. Despite their differences they agree to team up and investigate the murder to find out exactly what happened.What’s most impressive is how well the game works for the most part especially considering how these are indie developers. At times though, your partner asks you to let her know when a certain character is out side even though she can clearly see them and once or twice she does run out in front of the police but they somehow don’t see her. Still though these are very minor issues and the gameplay works remarkably well throughout overall. One thing I would like have liked to see however is for characters to use their animal traits more, such as a dog sniffing out clues but instead the characters are all basically human in animal form which is a bit of a missed opportunity.The graphics are in 3D which in this case was a necessity considering the way the game plays out and  they look very impressive as well. The characters all have proper facial expressions and the plaza looks lively and vibrant. The sound effects also certainly help with birds chirping, rain coming down and people talking and singing in the cabaret next door. That said, the lip syncing isn’t always exact and the characters’ reactions at times look like people from The Sims which can sometimes slightly detract from more intense scenes. The game is helped by truly superb voice acting. Thankfully there are no forced Spanish accents as the only Spanish we hear are a few words such as “Si”, “Senor” and “Dona”. Instead the characters have American accents which suit the characters well. Jorge has a gruff grizzled voice and the young woman he meets has a more youthful energetic voice. The game also has a nice jazz soundtrack in the background which is never intrusive and pleasant to listen to.If there are any drawbacks then it would be the lack of a manual save system. The game is composed of ten chapters which save automatically at the end of each chapter. While each chapter is only 20 - 30 minutes long it isn’t a huge issue but I believe the game would be enhanced greatly if a manual save was was added to the game to allow the player to save at any time. This would help ensure that the player would not need to replay large sections of the game if they had to quit playing in the middle of the chapter.At 3 hours long the game isn’t the longest but the length felt just right. The story kept me gripped throughout, with some beautiful graphics, fantastic voice acting and some memorable characters as well as a unique setting and time period this is a game I can highly recommend if you want to get your teeth into a well written murder mystery with a political twist. Here’s hoping we’ll see more from this world in future!For a more comprehensive review and more reviews check out
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this game is worth a play. It's story is really what carries it completely as it's so very passionate about the source material. The game is presented to you through the eyes of a man in a wheelchair looking off his balcony, he is powerless to interact with the world around him. He also is someone that starts almost entirely opposed to the message the game is telling, he is a grumpy annoyed old cop who wants to be left alone and judge people from up above. Even still, with enough evidence and observation he begins to understand and see the world around him. He doesn't fully get everything by the end and has his reservations, but I personally like that part as it shows that maybe for us to spark societal or political change we need to get some people we don't really like onto our side, something I think our current society struggles with understanding as we often like to take the nuclear polarizing option. That is what I liked about the game/story, I would go as far as to say this is the kind of material I'd like to see used to educate children in school. Now what isn't so great is the visual presentation. The character portraits of the townsfolk are pretty ugly, very polygonal but not quite achieving the low-poly look of something like "For the King", the waiter or rabbit character being the worst offenders. The animations and pathfinding are pretty bad, they look like The Sims moving around in the early games. The gameplay is pretty uninspired, just click on the interact points. There are a couple of puzzle-like parts matching evidence but they aren't really puzzles as you have no time limit, no limited tries, and the game tells you if you got any part wrong instantly. Nevertheless, they should be included as-is because they do make sure the player understands the events of the day. It's was good to play, not mind blowing but still very interesting and with many moving parts.
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: It was an enjoyable game. The story is nice, voice acting is top notch, gameplay is pleasant, artsyle is pleasing, music was pretty good. It feels more like indirect point-n-click than, say, walking sim. The only nitpick I have is animation, it is pretty inconsistent. But it doesn't prevent from enjoying the game!

_childDocuments_.review: is a detective noir, murder-mystery in which the player takes on the role of a wheelchair-bound, ex-Policía Jorge as he tries to solve a crime from his balcony with the help of a young journalist. Set in Barcelona in 1977, the game’s narrative is intertwined with the complexities of a post-Francoist Spain just before its first free election in four decades.Overall, this game was an enjoyable experience with a familiar but intriguing narrative and fascinating social setting. _childDocuments_.review: Boring game to say the least. It turns out to be political too early in the game which is why I did not find solving the murder mystery at all. Also, the game is too dark and there is no option to tune up the brightness, which was extremely annoying. _childDocuments_.review: The Flower Collectors is a game from small austrian studio called Mi'pu'mi. In this game we play as Jorge - an anthropomorphic bear, who (as we know from retrospections) lost senstion in his legs due to an accident on a boat few years ealier. Now as retired cop on wheelchair he have a slow-paced, calm life, until one day. When our protagonist is trying to handle with leak on a roof, someone near his house gets shot. Due to other circumstances, we try to figure out who killed this guy and why. Gameplay is mostly adventure game mixed with walking simulator (that should i call move simulator cuz Jorge can't walk), where as a "work-from-home" detectective we are making an invastigation. Movement is well made, you can feel wight of that wheelchair and thats not the only plus. Audio is well made as well, that's the most important thing in game like this and devs knew about it so dialogues feel natural and voice actors sounds like they tried to give soul to these characters. I really liked this graphics thats looks really much like made from clay and thats really cool. It really matches with not only noir style but with furry characters in general! Only thing that looked average was some of the animations. Dont get me wrong most of them is really well made but this moment when catgirl (i didnt finished the game at the moment of review) is going to lay down on the bed looks poorly made. But overall its a really impressive game that i can recommend to everyone who likes anthro or noir climates and imo its really cool to see games like this one after great BlackSad!
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: The Flower Collectors is a breath of fresh air in the Detective/Puzzle video game genre with a lot of drawbacks.The game relies a lot on how enthralling the story is, it kinda succeeds a it. The story is interesting but one of the first things I noticed is that character arcs are not well executed, everything seems a little bit rushed and sometimes contradictory, but that doesn't necessarily make the story worst. You can definitely nitpick some things like the constant and sometimes exhausting “progressive” talk throughout the game but the story is very political so it is expected. I didn't enjoy that some things are left unexplained by the end of the game, it doesn't make sense to make a sequel out of the story so I don't know the purpose of leaving details out.Gameplay could be better, I played on keyboard and mouse and it was rough. Moving was a little bit awkward and slow. Selecting dialogue was also kinda rough but not a major issue. The game does support controller play and I think that may be the way to go. Animations are good for an Indie game, the art style is very interesting and overall great. Voice acting is not very good, it feels awkward at its best and empty at its worst, but it is passable for an Indie game. Some of the animations are kinda janky but not a huge deal, the main thing is that sometimes you have to wait for animations to complete to continue the story and that can be good or bad. The game doesn't require you to do something every single second of gameplay, it makes you observe a lot and that's the point of it. I would describe the whole gameplay as a big cutscene with some actual gameplay in between. Puzzles and problem solving are not challenging but are definitely entertaining.Now let's address the two huge elephants in the room, the inspiration from “Rear Window” and the fact that the characters are anthropomorphic animals. The inspiration is clear, a man bound to a wheelchair who likes to watch the neighborhood tries to solve a mystery from afar. Do the devs credit Hitchcock? From what I can tell, no. The characters being anthropomorphic animals is something kinda shocking at first but you get over it quickly. Does it take away from the actual story? Kinda, it doesn't make the game worse but the main theme of the game is a very heavy and real subject, it makes it seem less serious. If you believe this game is “furry trash” just because of the anthropomorphic animals, grow up it is a clear stylization decision and nothing else.Achievement hunting is not very good, you can't 100% this game on your first gameplay. You have to go back and make different decisions to get some achievements and that is definitely boring. The game has little to no replay value and lacks extra content in general.Overall I would not recommend this game to the casual player even though I really enjoyed it. I think it takes someone to really like story heavy games and be open to some unpolished aspects to enjoy this game. If the game is on sale and you are willing to look over some details and like story driven games, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting is very promising, but the game mechanics and dialogues are not up to the task, in my opinion. This is a detective game inspired by Firewatch. So I was hoping for something similar to Her Story (investigation), Firewatch or other narrative games. However, the investigation aspect is very frustrating because of limiting game mechanics. It's incredibly railroady. Every tiny action has to be undertaken in a pre-decided order. Dialogue starts at decided times, and does not merge with action smoothly as in Firewatch. You can't take a picture while chatting : you go through conversation, then take a required picture when the game prompts you to. Initiatives are not rewarded, and you are not free to go through investigation in the order you would like. The invisible hand of the developer is always here, in the form of a constant to-do list on the screen... which breaks immersion for me. (deviations from the to-do list, in nature or order, are not allowed). Some tasks are also on a timer for no apparent reason, although the rest of the game is not in real time. More immersion-breaking. For an investigative game, it also assumes its players are dumb. Assembling the evidence and coming to conclusions is guided to the point you do not need to think whatsoever. Assembling evidence is done on a big board. There are empty slots, labelled with easy questions, for example "what does the victim look like ?". The player has to pick a picture of the victim and stick it there, that's it. If the wrong photograph is chosen, the game will not let you stick it, so the player can win by trial and error and basic reading ability. Finally, the narrative aspect is not here either, in my opinion... Dialogues are a bit cliché and not very believable. I did not finish the game, but from what I've seen on videos, the ending is generic. I find it disappointing for such an ambitious setting. The good parts are : - interesting premise- beautiful graphics- good voice acting

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of the game is nothing new in movies but it seemed like an interesting idea for a game. Unfortunately it ended up being closer to a point and click. The story is simple and straight forward. Given the subject matter, it leaves a lot to be desired. This game is meant to be serious and address serious issues, I was having an incredibly hard time taking it seriously solely because of the animations. The animations, out of everything, are what left the worst impression. The animations come across as lazy and unpolished, frequently not matching the situation that’s currently playing out before your eyes. (Ex: the police “punch” a character but the animation is of them stomping. The character getting “punched” just lays down on the ground like Apu spills his tendies)I would argue that animations are just as important as story and worth the time and money to make them look clean, polished, and at the very least convincing. Clearly, all the animations were taken from Mixamo because I recognize a bunch of them. There were no in-betweens so characters would snap, slide, blend into their next animation. The fingers frequently don’t animate correctly. (Ex: hands go into an “ok” position and they bend back like hot dogs) The devs did not spend enough time on the character movements as the characters are often sliding around during walk and run animations. All of this just really took me out of the experience. It’s hard to connect with what’s happening when you’ve got characters that are over the top animating like the Sims. (Ex: Main big bad villain waving at the bouncer with one leg up like a schoolgirl)Unfortunately the story and the game play are just ok and are not enough to make me look past the, honestly, comedic animations. I feel like the making of this game was a bit rushed. With more time and dedication to all aspects of development (particularly animation), this could have been a better game.

_childDocuments_.review: In the shadow of Facist General Franco’s death, the nation of Spain began an uneasy transition into democracy. It is the mid 70s and Spain faces its first free election in 40 years. It is during this period that our protagonist, Jorge, lives above a sleepy town square. Jorge is a wheelchair-using, former police officer who spends most days watching and sketching the world around him. ‘The Flower Collectors’ is a narrative heavy detective story with a ‘whodunnit?’ theme. You spend the majority of your time observing the residents around you and trying to piece together what happened, when a man is shot dead in the square below your apartment. It is brought to you by Mipuni Games, the same studio that released the well received ‘The Lion’s Song’ in 2016. Graphically, The Flower Collectors is fine. The colour palette used is evocative of the setting, the warm oranges dominate and really give you a sense of the Spanish locale. The use of a smaller environment is a nice idea, but it is often let down by the lifelessness of it. NPCs within the square feel static and inanimate, with no real ‘awareness’ of what is happening around them. This is compounded by poor animations that feel almost ‘stock’ and are very exaggerated, bringing to mind the cartoonish animations of The Sims or even Lionhead’s ‘The Movies’. The game’s characters are anthropomorphic cats, dogs, foxes etc. which suits the cartoon style the game has gone for, but much like the scenery around them, they are fairly basic models; with no emotion conveyed. This isn’t helped by the dialogue system in place, whilst the voice acting stands out as well acted, the game’s delivery of it is lacking. The omission of auto scroll dialogue makes sentences feel disjointed from one another and serves only to break immersion. The switch between English and Spanish pronunciations is strange too; an option to experience this in the native tongue would have been welcome. These issues with characters really undermine the game’s greatest asset, its story. Whilst this is no game changing tale, and at times almost excruitantly generic, it is mostly a well delivered and interesting affair. The game handles exposition well enough, with the usual trope of investigating items and objects. These fill in tidbits of information and the characters you meet/observe are likable enough; although sometimes it feels like the emotional connection to them was born from how you expect them to react to situations rather than how they are actually reacting within the game itself. Sadly the themes of oppression and history of the era are largely an unexplored backdrop to the game’s events and whilst they help set up the narrative, it feels like a missed opportunity to learn more about this important part of Spain’s modern history. The main villain of this piece is not a well crafted antagonist. but the game mechanics themselves. Often the slow and boring sequences eliminate any pacing or tension the story has built. Game play sequences amount to little more than point cursor at X, for an arbitrary amount of time. You are tasked with investigating the world’s characters by the means of sketches, and later photography. These mechanics are woefully thin, and could have been expanded upon to give you a feeling of being more involved. These are brought together at the end of chapters on a noticeboard, where you have to piece together your findings. These sequences serve as a good way to recap events and keep you on track with the story. The chapters themselves are handled poorly however. Often ending with a ‘oh I’m tired’ sequence, followed by a fade to black. This feels lazy and frustrating; especially when it happens around a story revelation that has you motivated to learn more.This is a theme that runs through the game unfortunately. How the story is presented is often at odds with how you want to play. You may notice something in the environment that is interesting, but there is no reward for doing so. A broken window springs to mind, which stands out and could have been interesting, considering the mystery aspect of the game, but it isn’t even given a line of dialogue and is never explored later on. You often find yourself having to guide a character into a building, avoiding security. There are no choices or player freedom as to how to do this and the glaringly obvious distraction technique is not used until later on when the story decides it should be used; it feels restrictive. Timed sequences also feel arbitrary with little feedback as to how failure (almost impossible) might be handled, with poorly used music cues used to inject a little slice of contrived tension.The lack of incidental happenings in the environment and lifeless characters, make these sequences dull and forgettable; with little to no challenge. For a game based around observing people, observing them simply isn’t very fun. The story progresses and wraps up in a satisfying manner, it is pleasing to see how things turn out for characters and there is scope to have further lines of dialogue depending on information/evidence gathered throughout the game. Annoyingly some of the story beats are helped along by frankly ridiculous realisations from characters, however. A character’s identification is clearly featured on a newspaper a fair while before the character notices, and the game’s later macguffin is handled very poorly are two stand outs. It is frustrating to realise things far sooner than the characters do, with no reasonable explanation as to why. One of these realisations is the main character’s past history, a huge part of the story itself, with absolutely no explanation as to why he wouldn’t have remembered it sooner or even need to remember it at all. Maybe if the game’s POV character had been explored in greater detail, perhaps to explain this strange omission from his memory, you could look past this; but it’s not. Sadly Jorge amounts to little more than a nihilistic ex-cop cliché. The Flower Collectors is an interesting enough detective adventure game that makes frustrating design choices.  A curious little world, let down by poor mechanics, an often stiff and lifeless world filled with immersion breaking audio and visual design. There is a good game to be found here, but it requires a lot of patience to navigate the simplistic and dull gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of many noir detective games featuring anthropomorphic animals in my Steam library, which is not a sentence I ever thought I'd type. If that's your extremely niche favorite genre, then you'll love The Flower Collectors. A -inspired voyeur mystery set in 1970s Barcelona, this short and sweet little video game will take you through the conflict and emotions of a retired, now-disabled cop who is forced to look at his own history through a new lens after witnessing a murder from his balcony. With the aid of a cunning left-wing journalist, you may be the only hope for uncovering the truth.All things considered, I still really liked this mini-adventure game. I'd love to see this concept even more fleshed out in the future; it felt a little more like a short story than a full novel.

_childDocuments_.review: The Flower Collectors is an entertaining adventure game that revolves around Spain's road to Democracy in the 1970's.StoryThe Flower Collectors puts you in the role of a former Policia named Jorge who is in a wheelchair after a past accident. Jorge witnesses the murder of a man outside his apartment. He is quickly pulled into a case to solve who the murdered person was and why they were killed.The story progresses over the course of 10 chapters and largely revolves around spying on the people in your vicinity using binoculars or a camera. Jorge teams up with a reporter named Melinda who is on the side of democracy in the strife between the old ways and the fledgling democracy. With Mel's help Jorge learns more about the people around the game world and is ultimately able to solve the murder. The story is quite entertaining and there's some great character development as well. GameplayAs I mentioned, much of the gameplay in this game revolves around spying on your neighbors. You do this by finding important points in the game world, usually revolving around a character, and either watch them, guide mel to eavesdrop on conversations, or take incriminating photos as clues.At the end of each chapter, you'll need to utilize the case board and line up the clues with the correct information. The only chapters where you didn't need to do this was between chapters 8 and 9 because the ending closes in pretty quickly at this point.There are also times when you'll need to choose answers during a conversation which seem to have some impact on the overall story. This also changes which achievements you'll acquire as well so in order to get all the achievements you'll need to replay some chapters and choose a different answer.VerdictOverall, I enjoyed The Flower Collectors quite a bit. It's an intriguing story revolving around an event that I wasn't too familiar with. It was interesting seeing the case unfold and I actually didn't expect the murderer to be who it was, though, thinking back, I should have seen it coming but hindsight is always 20/20, as they say. I managed to complete the game in 3.1 hours but I wouldn't let the shortness of the game dissuade you from giving it a shot. It's still well worth experiencing if you enjoy adventure games like myself. I gladly give this one my recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

Look forward to what this developer does next.

_childDocuments_.review: The Flower Collectors is a game that's unafraid. It presents a story that is proudly anti-fascist and only possible through the representation of many different kinds of people (well, animals in this case). It casts you as a protagonist (Jorge) that is pretty repulsive in some ways and doesn't goad you to celebrate that. It is a game that revolves around non-violent game play while presenting a story often about violence. The Flower Collectors takes a lot of big swings, and for me most of them land.The Flower Collectors takes place on one street corner. One balcony really. The primary gameplay involves taking pictures of different events on a street corner and helping a journalist, Melinda, uncover a murder. This may sound simple,but this gameplay works for the run time (about 3-4 hours) and the situations you observe keep it interesting. There is also quite a bit of dialog and some story choices you make that help give the story some stakes. What I appreciate about this gameplay loop is that you don't just move from one set piece to another, but get to be an actual actor in the story. I am not sure if you can fail any sequence, but the game does put time limits on certain sections which adds just enough tension to keep it from feeling too relaxed. I thought this was a smart system for a game and I think The Flower Collectors did a good job with it. The Flower Collector suffers a bit in polish though. Many of the animations are stilted, which can be a bit distracting in the middle of a scene or dialog. But, this is made up for by the voice acting. It's quite good. Specifically, Jorge has a range that I was really impressed by. Jorge was able to ride the line between being a sympathetic character while also a jerk well and in a way that did not feel too forced. I'm not sure I would have bought the character otherwise. I am overall impressed with this game and recommend anyone who wants to play more games that are unashamed of taking a political stance to pick it up. It goes for it in a way that many games don't and for the most part succeeds.
_childDocuments_.name: The Flower Collectors

_childDocuments_.review: This really immersive game can be thought as a mix between Hitchcock's classic "Rear Window" and Firewatch game. The game has a nice, interesting noir story, very well narrated and voice-acted. It can also be conceived as a theater piece since all ten episodes take place in your apartment (and balcony). Although there is little to no real puzzles, The Flower Collectors is very enjoyable since the story advances by means of your voyeaurish investigations (in a few situations, you will also guide characters down in the street –radio in hand- by directing them in order to keep them safe from patrols).It all begins with a murder down in the plaza below, and you, riding your wheelchair and armed with binoculars/camera, have to resolve it in the following days. There are characters that will help you on this quest, and your apartment will also be the scenery where people and situations take place. The game is very well crafted since the isolation inside your home is not a limit, but a very well squeezed resource.If you liked Firewatch, this is a short game that very much resembles its unique perfume.Note: all characters are anthropomorphic animals –not humans. There is really no need or explanation of that, and I could not find any proper usefulness in this choice. Anyway, it is something forgettable as soon as one is hooked with the story and events.

name: Best Friend Forever
detailed_description: Step off the bus at Rainbow Bay and start a new life with your furever friend! Adopt a dog, find true love and experience all the wacky hijinks this colourful city has to offer. Best Friend Forever is the world’s first simulation game to combine pet care and dating (just not necessarily at the same time). Train, pat and play with your very own dog to form a bond that will last the ages. With your four-legged companion by your side, meet, woo and cherish the many cuties of Rainbow Bay’s thriving singles scene. Choose between four adoptable shelter pups to take on your journey through laughter, love and existential crises - a Maltese, a Shiba Inu, a Mutt and a Staffordshire Terrier! Each pup has their own backstory, personality, strengths and weaknesses, just like any other shelter pup in need of love and a good home. Encounter and develop relationships with six residents of Rainbow Bay! From a family lawyer to a youth counselor; from a Pomeranian lover to an ice-skating Samoyed owner, there's someone for anyone looking for love in this city. All you have to do is load up your Woofr - the app for people who love dogs who love people who love dogs - and get going. Take your adopted pup on their own journey through Paws Academy, Rainbow Bay Vet Clinic's own puppy school. Make sure you keep up their training, as well as look after their wellbeing to excel and raise a healthy, happy pal for life.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, REALLY wanted to be in love with this game. I love the idea of raising a dog, and the idea of dating sims, but this game just feels so unfinished. The dog raising aspect is well implemented, but it's not long enough to get an idea of what you need to do and really feel like you're doing a good job. I managed to romance Anders and pass the dog school, but it just feels like it was way too rushed. Another thing that got me was no CGs, or even a CG menu. I play a lot of otome games and dating sims for the CGs, the fact there were none, not even an ending CG for the route, felt very lazy to me. The romance, like many other things in this game, felt very rushed. I barely got to know the characters, only the outwards facade everyone portrays, not the inner them. There were little hintings of sexual content, and even that felt rushed in the relationship. One route lasted just over 2 hours, and for the price of the game, it's too short. I really didn't feel like I got my money's worth. And like I said, I was SO EXCITED for this game and purchased it the moment it released. But I got a buggy game, with typos related to the chosen pronouns, characters not appearing when they were meant to. I didn't know what stats it wanted me to focus on more in training my dog, I was trying to keep them balanced and was then getting lectured by the vet for certain stats being too low, which just irritated me more. Over all, I'm just disappointed. If you want a rushed experience with cute dogs and kinda okay characters, then you'll probably like this game. But compared to other visual novels that are even cheaper, I'd say look elsewhere. They focused primarily on the dog animations and dog raising, and barely any on the dating. At least that's how it felt to me. I hope this helps you in deciding whether to purchase the game or not.

_childDocuments_.review: I was more excited to play this game than I now know I should have been. It starts off with so much promise!! And then it fails it almost every way possible. -While I appreciate how inclusive this game tries to be, it feels like it's infantilizing the protag every time the NPCs have to thoroughly describe/explain their circumstances. -Why did we have to go through and create a dating profile if the protag had a set personality to begin with??? And why would you give the protag a set personality if that said personality is going to be awful??? It is truly and completely unbelievable that the protag was able to get everyone to fall in love with them so easily when they act like that. Especially Anders!!!-This game has no replayability even if you enjoyed your first playthrough. Going through it more than once has you skipping through essentially every event other than the dates with your new interest. Everything with the dog feels like a clicker game that you need to tap through as quickly as possible.-I understand the story spans out over 15 weeks technically, but the stories with the love interests just feel so rush in some places that it really ruins the entire interaction. They add in some random conflict/solution towards the end and assume that's what makes a full-fledged story. With the dating part feeling more like a side quest, you would think the dog events and interacts would hold more weight, but no. I can't recommend anyone buy this game for anything less than 50% off.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember when you’d log into Facebook and boot up one of those little cute pet games where you’d take care of an animal of your choice and get little rewards? That’s what this game feels like, only without the rewards, and someone figured they’d just slap a dating sim somewhere in it. There’s just so much done wrong that I’m not even sure where to start.                                                                           • • • •The characters are honestly the only thing I like about this game, art aside. The diversity is amazing, from size to race it was a breath of fresh air. I respect the developers for being bold enough to place in a trans man, who’d probably be my favorite if not for Anders. The respectful use of pronouns was interesting as well as how they handled delicate topics in general. I was probably impressed most by Felix.  There are a number of cliché ways I expected that to play out, and yet they went a completely different route, I couldn’t have been more pleasantly surprised. The ages have a nice range as well, no more high school drama. Just a bunch of confident adults who know what they want and aren’t afraid to acknowledge their shortcomings. Unfortunately, this is where my praise ends.The story is nonexistent, but I’ll give you a rundown. Your character moved to Rainbow Bay after a nasty breakup, looking for a fresh start and a change in careers. Of course, you learn this all at once during a truth or dare session about midway through the game, but I digress. You came here with the intention of being a well-known photographer, now whether you’ve always had this passion, or it was simply a heat of the moment thing, we have no idea. But the only real-time this comes into play is briefly at a fair, in which you happened to immediately get some big-time offer and gig. I just couldn’t care to be honest, because the game doesn’t have enough to make you care. Your character’s personal life appears to revolve around who your pursuing’s personal life and your dog. BFF just severely lacked enough depth needed to make a lasting connection or leave an impression.This is probably why I have mixed feelings about the romance. It’s not bad by a long shot, but there’s not enough to it. Due to so much focus being put into the dog element of the game it almost feels forgotten about, or like a last-minute addition. Your character pretty much kisses everyone on the first date, and while the kiss is sweet and well written when you consider your interactions with them throughout the game it all moves so quickly. Seriously, what happened to romantic tension!? It’s hard to even know where you stand with some characters because the word friend keeps getting thrown around despite you having kissed or slept with them multiple times. It could’ve possibly come together a bit more smoothly with CGs, however, there are none. At all! Not a single one! I’m so heartbroken. How can you deny me an Anders kiss CG? Or Astrid! It’s just too cruel. On top of that, it bothered me that some characters still openly flirted with characters you were pursuing and neither party said anything or reacted in a way to suggest being uncomfortable. There were a few times where your character expressed disappointment at the word “friend”, but the lack of conviction behind it and the going with the flow was quite irritating, to say the least.                                                                           • • • •Now, I’m not going to pretend that I like stat raisers, but I can often look beyond them if the story and romance are good enough because it’s usually worth the effort, albeit extremely frustrating. The irony here is that the stat raising element was not frustrating at all, rather it was just boring, and I didn’t understand the reason for it. There’s no reward for raising your dogs’ stats outside of getting the valedictorian achievement. I didn’t see an improvement in the dog’s behavior, nor did it seem like having higher stats changed the outcome of specific situations. On top of that, I found that the constant dog events were more annoying than anything and killed any type of potential romantic tension, not to mention it just personally made things awkward at times. It’s honestly quite amusing to me, that the part of the game it felt most if not all, their efforts went into is quite possibly the worst part. Somehow, rather than making me a dog lover, I’m quite glad to own a cat instead. Don’t get me wrong, I love dogs, but this game made me absolutely fed up with them.Finally, BFF lacks basic VN features. You cannot skip, only click super-fast, but not too fast or you risk the game-breaking and having it freeze up for a moment. Not having the ability to skip read text in a visual novel should be considered a crime, and a game sin. I also found that the method of fast clicking sometimes leads to sprites not loading in. There are also a few typos here and there but given all that I’ve mentioned so far, this is simply nitpicking at this rate as there wasn’t an insane amount, just enough for me to notice and make mention of. Nothing another proofread couldn’t fix. My final complaint is that if you like to save before choices, like me, and then go back and try other options, even that’s a hassle. The game doesn’t save at the spot you pick, rather it saves at the beginning of an event itself. To clarify, essentially, it’s like starting a scene all over again if you want to reload and try for other options. When you reload, you have to click back up to the point you saved at which almost ruins the whole purpose of saving in general.                                                                           • • • •Words cannot accurately describe how painful it was to get through Best Friend Forever, nor how completely disappointed I am. Never have I fallen so hard for characters within a game I hate. There’s just so much wasted potential here and I feel like they pushed the dog part so hard that it comes across as cheap and lackluster, rather than cute, adorable, and funny. Originally, I was leaning more towards a neutral rating but after a few more run-throughs, I just have to say no. It’s cute, love the characters and the art, but everything else is just… bad. If the devs released a dating sim without stat raising elements and a fully fleshed out story, I think it has the potential to be mind-blowing.

_childDocuments_.review: Although this is a cute game with a fun dog-sim gimmick, I believe it overall falls flat as a visual novel. The story and writing are linear and your choices do not really affect anything aside from who you may or may not be dating & if your dog is going to get some gold medals for the week. The characters are very poorly written with no realism/organic feeling to any of them. I feel like they could be fleshed out more with gradual looks into their lives, however I believe they feel so fake/rushed because of how quickly the gameplay goes. A session takes about 3 hours to get through. I think it's a great idea and start to something good, but should be given proper care and more time into developing the core of the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: [Update 05/21/2022]I want to preface this with the fact that I do enjoy this game and will casually boot it up when I want something low stress and cutesy. However I don't particularly recommend it at the current price tag in comparison to other dating sims.-The romance scenes (albeit short) feel genuine, funny, and enjoyable.-The characters are likable! Come from all walks of life and seem to have been specifically written in order to give as much representation as possible which, for me, is something I actively seek out in dating sims.-The fact that there is a solid lock in for romances is helpful and lets you know a good point in time to save and when to be aware of going back and trying out other romances without having to play a whole new game if you don't want to.- The art is great. Colorful, thematic, and expressive. I sometimes like to sit for a few seconds and just admire some of the background art as well as the character designs.-Pet events. The overlay issue  fixed for which I am very grateful. However, I can still see the timer being a bit too quick for someone with accessibility issues. I also don't like the timer simply because it makes me stop in the middle of reading in order to deal with what is basically QTE. I suppose personal preference.-Because there was only 3 dates available with each romance, it left the last 3 weeks of the game feeling...empty. There was nothing to do except slam through a couple of encounters each day and then work on your dog's stats while you waited for the final check in.-No matter what I do, my dog comes up as 'mediocre' during evaluations. I tried very hard to keep my (lovingly named) Tiramisu well rounded but each time I was given bronze in each category. When I switched it up and attempted to only level a couple of stats instead, I was scolded for not working on the others. Then got bronze again all across the board.[As of updating this, this is still an issue. Most guides explicitly state the only way to receive valedictorian is to choose a specific dog and literally spam 1-2 different training options at the end of each week. This...really saps the fun out of being able to enjoy the cute art for each training and 'bond' with your chosen dog.]-The romances are short. They are very sweet but they do not flesh out the characters enough imo. The same goes for the characters you don't romance. This makes the game very one note. You should be able to explore the other characters in a non-romantic way. The narrative is pushed that the main character is good friends with all of these people but we get very very little interaction unless we use our 'energy' on the one minute interactions which makes it so we can't do all the dog encounters or the romantic encounters. I understand the need to balance this but it inevitably makes the game feel too rushed. I would do away with the energy mechanic all together.- No full art of any of the characters in game. Maybe I'm being a bit critical but most dating sims will offer at least one full art for the romance option when completing their path.All in all, it's a good game. I like it. I'll probably attempt to play it to see all the romances slowly but surely. However, I do feel that there are other dating sims on the market that surpass this one and have a smaller price tag and less struggles. The idea is creative and the design of having to juggle a pet as well as romance and friendship is a very fun one but there are some design issues that leave me wanting more. If you have money to spare I wouldn't tell you not to buy it but I would definitely do a little research to see if this game meets the criteria you might personally want in a dating sim.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could recommend this game, but at the end of the day it falls short of that mark. Overall I think this game has a great concept and a lot of heart, but it falls short in execution. The dating sim part of the game is great, but each route is fairly short. I'm not bothered by the presence of the common route major events, but I wish there was a skip function to get through the text I've already seen faster. Most of the playtime is spent on dog training, the mechanics of which just aren't fun. The "feels" meters seem completely arbitrary. I was constantly doing the same three things every week to increase my dog's energy, while her hydration and hygiene never dropped. The traits make sense in theory, until you discover that the standards for improvement at Paws Academy are impossibly high. Even using a guide to get the most out of the weekly activities isn't enough to get a gold medal at check ups. The most recent update seems to have made the valedictorian achievement more attainable (which I can confirm is possible), but this seems like a band-aid on a gaping wound. I was excited to play this game, but was ultimately let down. 6/10+ Fun and diverse cast+ Beautiful art+ Engaging writing- Dog training system- Dates feel secondary- No way to skip repeated events

_childDocuments_.review: Much like others have said, I had been following the development of this game for some time and was so excited for its release. I downloaded the demo when it was available and finished that experience feeling like this had so much promise and was going to be a real gem. I still feel that way in a few ways, but at the end of the day, the cons are outweighing the pros for me after my first play through of the full release.Pros: 1) BFF really surprised me with its level of representation. LGBT+, disability, body types of all kinds - this particular aspect of the game honestly blew me away. 2) Another positive is the entire dog companion and mechanics concept as well as interesting story concepts that start to pull you in. It’s such a brilliant and promising base! However...Cons: 1) There aren’t really clear instructions when it comes to navigating those dog mechanics. From how to take care of your dog (e.g: pet by clicking a lot on their head NOT by holding the mouse button and dragging it around), to deciding exactly what you should be focusing on when training (I originally aimed to train all skills equally but became confused when my evaluations would come back negatively. Even after trying to correct my approach  and do what was recommended I still couldn’t seem to produce good  enough results.) 2) The dialogue has some great moments but ultimately just feels disjointed and rushed. The vignettes with the characters start to feel more like...well...tiny stand alone vignettes...rather than an interwoven story that ebbs and flows with your experiences and choices. And this is especially exacerbated by —3) The glitches and lack of proofreading. An instance or two of a misspelling or rogue letter is fine- sometimes even the best editors miss one or two- but it happened so often in just one play through that I started to wonder if they bothered to proof it at all. Not only that, but more than once a character would “repeat” themselves, like the conversation had suddenly reset itself momentarily. Once I even had a full conversation with a character after a major event they were a part of, only for them to suddenly “reset” themselves while we were talking and have the same conversation with me again from the beginning but as though they hadn’t been there for the event. I also encountered a few audio glitches. At the end of the day, I left with an overwhelming feeling of BFF being unfinished. Had this been an early access release I wouldn’t have batted an eyelash because there IS so much great potential there, but as a finished product that is being sold for $20 I am incredibly disappointed. I don’t feel like the game in its current state is worth what it’s being sold for. And that honestly breaks my heart because I was so ready to love this! If the dev team pushes through some major updates that correct the issues above then this opinion will likely change, but right now I just cannot recommend it at full cost.
