_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this game. But after the first route it's...a struggle to finish. It's definitely polished, the art is nice and it's well done for what it is. That being said, in terms of being a visual novel it really falls short. My biggest issue is that you could take out the dogs and it's the same game more or less. The training of your dog and the stats mini games mean absolutely nothing. They don't influence who you can date, but then again neither do the choices you make with those people.By far the worst part is that the replayability is awful. Because it's so linear and there is no skipping, you have to sit through the same options that mean nothing and the same dialogue over and over. Story wise it tries to be...relatable? But it feels forced. Especially because sometimes it sets up concepts then just doesn't do anything with them. Like the whole ending story ultimately leads to nowhere, it's this big deal until literally everyone, including the main character just...stops caring and doesn't mention it again. I want the achievements, so I'm going to finish this. But I wouldn't recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with a positive.  The game is cute.  The art looks nice, the dogs are adorable, and the music is chipper.  I am glad that I was able to have they/them as my pronouns. More games should have that, as well as the other LGBTQ+ content in the game.  The characters are diverse in race, body, gender, etc.  Good, good stuff.However, this is a visual NOVEL, which means the writing is an essential part of this game.  And, sadly, the writing isn't great.  A lot of the game's story feels strangely disjointed and the primary conflict that randomly crops up towards the middle of the game is really random and seemingly arbitrary.  Nothing ever really comes from it and the problem is miraculously solved, leaving me to wonder why it exists in the first place.There's characters you can date, sure, but I'm *shocked* at the speed of things.  You talk to someone three times and suddenly, they're pulling you into a dark corner to make out.  Is that...normal? Do people do that?  The character building feels shallow and,  again, disjointed from everything else that's going on.There are also a bunch of bugs, from characters not appearing to random choice boxes popping up that have nothing to do with what's going on.Even the real big hook of this dating sim, the dog raising, is more clicking icons in a window and watching a bar go up.  The words for those actions never change.  Taking care of the dog is just as tedious; look at bars, choose actions based on bars, wiggle the mouse so the bar can go up.I sincerely regret having bought this game instead of watching someone just play it online.  That sounds harsh, but it needed more soul put into it.  The cast is diverse, but there's no development within themselves or with me.  And my relationship with my dog feels just as shallow.
_childDocuments_.name: Best Friend Forever

_childDocuments_.review: I reallly,  wanted to like this game, and in a way I kind of do. It is SO close to being really good. But in the end it was so disappointing that it pushed me to write my first review in years. The ideas and concepts are amazing, but it seems underdeveloped. The characters are great. They feel very real (and the VA's did amazing work), and they're likable. But there's no real depth to them, just concepts. Nothing is especially fleshed out. I personally went with Anders.  And that's hardly a summary, because the game makes each one of those issues that quick and short. As much as I like those characters, with the drive-by story telling, it was hard to really get emotionally invested.It is . The way this is set up is you get 15 weeks. Each week you can spend however you want, but there are three big events that propel the MC's story, every other week is just filler.  Again, hardly a summary. The story sometimes brings up MC's past, as if it's gonna be expanded on, but then it gets swept right back under. The little events you can spend MP on. They're drabbles. Very short, with maybe a choice you can make to better your relationship with whoever's in that event, and they don't really give any substance. You find out trivial knowledge, and get some fun dialogue. They go nowhere. And when the main story isn't giving you much, and the fillers also give nothing, it makes the padding even more obvious. Then the biggest part. Taking care of the dogs, very cute, and it seems like that's where they put all their time. But your dog is just...there, which is sometimes all you really need, but in a game that advertises combining taking care of the dog while finding love, I kinda expected it to intersect a little more. We have instances where you can choose to be with your dog other than have an encounter with one of the people, and your dog occasionally borks at the people you're around. Other than that it seems like these two games could exist separately. And the whole doggy academy thing and the stats, I get the idea, but I'm not sure where it was going. To find out if you're capable of raising and keeping your dog of choice after you adopt them, you have to do this academy program, which checks your dog's stats, and it shows how you do compared to the other dogs in your class. I'm not sure if I was supposed to level up a certain stat more than the others, or level them up in tandem, or try to get gold medal improvement. It wasn't even sure if it even mattered in the game if I improved poorly. It really seemed that nothing you did would have an impact in any way. Depending on what you want out of a dating sim, I can see the appeal of this game. I really can. It is nice to have an LQBTQIA+ game, and it is nice to see a diverse cast. The characters are likable and I had a very hard time choosing just one to go with. The art style is very pleasing to look at. The dogs, my god, are so cute. I just can't recommend it because it feels very shallow and quick. If this were a more fleshed out dog-sitting sim or a more fleshed out dating sim, I would absolutely recommend it. As is, it's just kind of riding the middle fence, not really having either in a satisfactory way.

_childDocuments_.review: ok listen. i've just fully completed the game and i have Thoughts.-i thought literally all of the love interests were very charming and fun to engage with, which is a rarer experience than you'd think in dating sims (for me, at least)-the artwork was, for the most part, really charming and pleasant to look at-all the dogs? amazing. more dogs. please-loved the diversity and inclusion! having one of the love interests have a guide dog seems so obvious now but it's a really nice touch. would have loved to see a service/working dog too!-SUPER appreciated that you couldn't really "fail" an encounter or date, because that stresses me out SO bad-kind of loved how the dog breeds corresponded with their owners. like robin had a working dog because she's, you know, very busy and smart always on-the-move. astrid had a samoyed because she's an ice skater so naturally she'd have a dog made for that kind of climate, and also a dog made to work and pull sleds and help hunt. felix had a german shepherd because he was into true crime  like those were nice touches i appreciated that-feels like a demo still? like it's only really three dates with your love interest and i can tell they were trying to do the whole "so-and-so is actually more than whatever-stereotype" and like, yeah, but also a character introduction and three dates are absolutely NOT enough time to pull that off. sometimes they would reference the intended stereotype and i would have no idea what they were talking about, lol. also i got little to no backstory for really any of them except sacha? which yes, isn't really necessary to liking the character but?? i'd like to know more about them????-not often, but there were still some grammar mistakes and pronoun mix-ups, which is disappointing considering it seems that those have been things that were brought up since the game released-your choices never really felt like they mattered? which can be a good thing but i don't know. honestly i wish that choosing a dog mattered more, especially if you only get four dogs to choose from. like if the dogs don't really add any unique interactions with characters just... add more dogs?-story was a bit messy, to be honest. like,  ugh whatever moving on-maybe i'm not a good reviewer for this since the only dating sims i've really played are like, doki doki literature club and monster prom but those two work to me because they're like, on opposite sides of the same spectrum. like DDLC is long and your choices don't matter too much but it does give you a skip button and even will stop skipping once you encounter dialogue you've never seen before (which i would have LOVED in this game omg too much clicking!!! especially since the dialogue is the same like 99% of the time!!!!). and monster prom doesn't have skip buttons but it's very short and your choices matter and even then there is SO much to do? it really encourages replaying the game to see everything, which i feel like should be sort of expected from a dating sim where the whole draw is to pick characters and romance them? like at least add a few notable changes based on choice because it got so exhausting to restart your game to romance a new character because you just clicked through sooooo much of the same thing over and over again.-and this is a problem for like, me and only me, but there was NO bernese mountain dog i am SO devastated!! give me my boy!!!anyways overall i did enjoy the time i spent on this game but i would not recommend you buy it at full price. if it's on sale and it sounds like something you'd enjoy then go for it, or if someone else wants to buy you something then put this on your birthday wishlist or whatever, but i can't say i recommend it at full price. maybe if they update the game or release a sequel i'll check it out (both are really unlikely, considering they haven't updated since 2020 and i'm not sure if there's even any market for a sequel because as of right now there are only ~150 ish reviews on here and from what i've seen, even people who really liked it aren't completely satisfied with their purchase), but as of right now i think i'm done with the game and i'm not super happy with my experience. i understand that this is the first game from this developer, though, so maybe they'll make something else i'll enjoy more? hopefully this is at least a learning experience for them ^_^

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to say that this developer has done more than I have ever done, and this VN is still really ambitious and I think accomplishes some of the interesting goals it set for itself. (A dating VN with a dog-caring component IS really cool!)However.I personally am really tired of "lol sploot dog cute random over the top silliness"-style VNs. Half of this story and dialogue contains puns, that's not a joke, it's CONSTANT. The other half of the story and dialogue is extremely irreverent and doesn't take ANYTHING seriously. It's very mildly hinted at that your character has a bit of a dark or tragic reason for moving, but when you find out what it is like an hour into the game, it ends up being ruined by that same lol dog rando cute silliness. Your character found a random dog during a really sad time, and it mysteriously led them to a bus stop, and now your character refers to it as the Dog Wizard.Because of all of that, the narrative is extremely shallow. "You're definitely just a person playing a VN so we're going to do the bare minimum to actually try to immerse you in our world." Seriously, the game does VERY little to pretend that you are a "real" character in a "real" world that it wants you to engage with on that level. No, instead, it mostly just says "Here's your dating app, you can see where people are at any given time, here's a lampshade where we acknowledge that that's really weird for privacy and safety reasons but then we blow that off because hey you're playing a dating VN with dog training, you're not here for real immersion, are you? Anyway, you only have 5 motivation points to do things, some events cost more than others! Also here's a bunch of spam in your inbox that we, the company in the game that created the dating app, could totally clean up for you, but we won't, because the developers want to shove puns in your face and be silly constantly. We're also going to constantly say that everything that happens is extremely "serendipitous" instead of trying to actually think of ways for things to happen to and around your character more organically."In that same vein, your character is nothing. They are a cardboard cutout. They make constant jokes about never unpacking, they sleep on the floor of their apartment, they have no personality except being a stone-cold idiot. They don't know how to cook. They only like burgers, apparently. They let Anders just walk ALL over them. And they apparently have to be nosy and/or oblivious about/to people's private lives (which is what made me just quit the game and finally write this review, it'll be detailed at the end of this review). Why do VN authors insist on making your character a tactless dumbass? You get NO input as to how your character actually acts, you get hardly any dialogue or narrative choices. You get your name, and a choice of one of.. three or four character portraits.You can apparently ♥♥♥♥ Anders on the first date, but it cut that date off so quickly I genuinely couldn't tell if I had ♥♥♥♥♥♥ him or not. Also he absolutely dictated the hell out of everything, my character did NOT get a say in ♥♥♥♥ even when they TRIED to be the one to decide where to go for dinner. Anders even said, "I still get to pick dinner but you can pick what you get for dessert" which was SO disgustingly controlling, and the sad thing is, I'm not even sure the developers realized that that was actually a real red flag of a thing to say in conjunction with how Anders has interacted with the character up to that point (and how your character thought of Anders in their head), I bet they just thought it was a silly joke. It's possible that Anders' controlling tendencies get touched on and resolved later in the game, but first, lol, no, not with this type of game, I have no trust that they would actually try to tackle character flaws like that in a serious and satisfying manner; and second, I am not playing any more of this game to find out.The dates do NOT mingle into the rest of the game at all. I went on several rapid-fire first and second dates with three different characters and their was no narration whatsoever of those things happening and possibly conflicting with each other. Like, I get not having it actually cause complications, it IS a dating sim and you do want your player to be able to test the waters with different characters, but there wasn't even a thought of any other character in your character's head between events.You do not get to pet the other characters' dogs.Fox is the worst character, she's insufferable, extremely not funny, and very mean.Actually Felix might give her a run for her money on all accounts, except that Fox is omnipresent and Felix is not.At least the art is nice, and the game tries to be inclusive. I like the music well enough.What finally made me quit was when I went on a first date with Sacha and one of his friends mentioned him transitioning. I (the human being playing the game, NOT the character) had already suspected that he was a trans man, but I didn't need to know for sure, he was cute and nice no matter what. However, your character is given a set of questions to ask, and one of them was "Transitioning?" Like they didn't know what that meant, or didn't realize, hey, maybe now is not the time to pry? And that would actually be okay, if it was part of a roleplaying choice you could make.. but it was not. You HAD to ask ALL of the questions for the game to move on. You were not allowed to NOT ask any question.So yeah. Do not recommend. The characters are prop caricatures and are written all the same way (that doesn't mean they all act the same, just that you can tell they were all written with the exact same ideas of characterization and stereotypes), the story does not exist on any more than a superficial level, and your character is an empty-headed milquetoast bore.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface by saying I am mainly a VN/dating/stat-raising sim gamer. Some of these points might not bother you unless you know the genre well. I knew I had to lower my expectations but I didn't realise how low they had to go.Pros:- Cute art- Funny writing- Dogotachi is an interesting concept- Implies an interesting argument about how dating sims objectify love interests by making your presence crucial to their character development (very poorly executed and might be a happy coincidence)Cons:- Inconsistent art. The dogs you can adopt are more detailed than the love interests' dogs. The humans' faces are so much more detailed than some of their clothing.- Seems to think being funny = puns and jokes 24/7. There is no interest in pacing or timing of jokes. It's like someone saw Dream Daddy and thought it could work even with a much shorter script and less mini-games to pad things out.- Writing not proofread. This game lists 3 writers yet they don't have time to get all the typos out.- No replay value. The endings for all characters are the same no matter who you choose or what you do. Oh, you didn't interact with this character at all outside of the compulsory events? Don't worry. The game will tell you all about them and their future in the ending, even if you don't know anything about them. Your dog's stats don't matter at all outside of potentially being valedictorian (that gets you 1 line about it). The only thing that changes is the pre-epilogue scene where you get a glimpse into daily life with your love interest (lasts less than 5 minutes). Their future? Eh, you're not mentioned in it at all.- a lot of minor bugs and glitches- Not made with a VN game engine.So, a button to speed past already-read dialogue, something essential to VNs? Non-existent. Devs' ability to patch out minor bugs without taking a lot of time? Nada. The current bugs are all things that could be easily corrected with a few words if it were a VN game engine. Instead, the bugs still exist, even after being patched out.Not one I recommend paying for full price unless you just want a short, cute 2D version of Nintendogs.

_childDocuments_.review: I am gonna start out that this game IS very enjoyable but it is not worth 20 bucks (not even 15 which is what I paid for it).The representation is very nice. It scratched an itch I haven't had scratched since I was 10, playing Nintendogs in the back of a car.Sadly all of this is outweighed by the rushed dialog and programming, There's a bunch of grammatic errors (coming from a non native speaker this should be a red flag), characters don't appear on screen when they're supposed to, Dialog options that aren't supposed to show up, pronouns being mixed up and I got a bug where no matter how hard I tried one of the dog events just wasn't win-able.Not to mention that raising my dog was just super unclear? _childDocuments_.review: The game does not live up to expectations. I was extremely excited for this game, but I was disappointed. The functions with the dogs are repetitive and boring. You do not really get a sense of the dog’s personality or bonding with them at all. All the events feel like you could have them with the dog or without them. They have little to no effect on events. I tried to train my dog in a well-rounded manner and ended up getting punished for not doing more? Or not doing enough in one area even though it was almost even with all the other states.       The story is bland, weird, and rushed. There is little to no depth to find in your fellow residence. Your background story is simply weird to say the least. It is like the game wanted to have a mystery but could not figure out how to implement it. By the end of my first run I knew nothing more about it and honestly could not care less to know more. The romance route was rushed and held absolutely no depth. It was like reading a half-done script. As a LGBTQ myself I enjoyed the inclusiveness and diversity. That said you get little to no choice on your personality which makes it very hard to believe you fit in with many of the main characters who seem to fall in love with you in half a second. Overall, the game needs a lot of work. Amazing concept failed execution. Would be willing to look into it again if there were some major fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited to play this game, and while I'm still glad that I bought it, I have to admit that the experience was a little frustrating. In the end, I was mostly focused on just the dog raising aspect as that was the part I found most enjoyable.As other reviewers have noted, the game feels a bit rushed and unfinished, leading to both the dating mechanics and the dog raising mechanics to feel underdeveloped and leaving you wishing for something more.The main issue I had with this game was the writing, though. I don't mind the cheesiness and over the top cliches of otome games, but the characters here were so over the top that it had me rolling my eyes. I never thought that I'd feel preached at by a dating game, but this was super on the nose. This aspect also made pretty much every character shallow and insufferable, and in the end I was struggling to pick who to romance because I honestly didn't connect with any of them. I even disliked some of them. I ended up finishing Maribel's route, but by the end I still felt like I had hardly learned about her as a person and the relationship hadn't really progressed. It felt like a first chapter or prologue, and was lacking any conflict or tension at all. Maribel and the reader char still felt like nothing but friends at the end, and not even friends who care for each other very much. Also, for a game that purports itself as LGBT+ friendly, I didn't feel represented as a lesbian at all by this game, and if anything it was so over the top with convincing you how gay friendly it was that I just felt icked out, like my sexuality was a spectacle. The female characters were all very feminine and not relatable for us gnc lesbians. This also meant no romance options if butches are your type.

_childDocuments_.review: ok so it's more complicated than me just not liking the game, i actually do like this game [mostly the dog care elements] but the dating elements need some work, despite the fact that the games markets itself on "letting you be who you want to be" it doesn't even consider that the player might be ace and didn't give me an option to say no when one of the npcs started nsfw stuff with my character, this honestly made me uncomfortable and it was really disappointing because the game is tagged as LGBTQ+ so i thought that ace identities would be more acknowledged, also despite selecting they/them pronouns for my character at the beginning of the game my character being nonbinary and therefore trans isn't something that was ever really acknowledged either, i had to select a dialog option about not knowing what transitioning is to progress the game instead of just being stuck on that one screen and then i had to skip through npcs explaining to me, a nonbinary person, that normally it's a bad idea to out trans people and it was only ok this time bc the npc knew that his friend [the trans guy being outed] would be ok with it, i understand that this would require changing the dialog so i'm less annoyed at this but despite the game being tagged as LGBTQ+ and saying that you can be who you want to be i didn't feel very represented and it fact i felt more like my gender identity was an afterthought and my sexuality wasn't even thought about at all, also sometimes even ppl who aren't ace just don't want to have their character do nsfw stuff with the npc they are dating so this isn't even just an "acknowledging ace identities" thing it's more of a "understanding that not everyone wants to see stuff that suggests their character doing nsfw stuff with and npc they are dating and just because they are dating them doesn't make it an automatic yes" thing, usually i wouldn't be this disappointed especially when it's a dating sim but let me remind you again that it's tagged as LGBTQ+ AND it is selling itself off the idea that you can just be yourself and this game will accept you and it lowkey feels like false advertising when the dialog and the dating elements in the game doesn't even take into consideration that the player might be trans and that the player might be ace especially when the game then has an npc that you can date who's entire backstory is about how difficult being LGBTQ+ can be for some people because of a lack of understanding and acceptance there is for the LGBTQ+ community, it's honestly kind of jarring having the game talk about how awful it is that this guy got kicked out of his parent's house for being a trans guy and bisexual and yet in the same breath it doesn't acknowledge me being ace and nonbinary, just be aware if you are thinking about getting this game that just because the game says you can be who you want and it's tagged as LGBTQ+ doesn't mean that it acknowledges us outside of npcs and a "they/them" pronouns option, granted those are both good things to have in a game but it's not the same as acceptance of the player or "letting you be yourself"

They've got a disabled character, plus size, trans (i think, didn't play their route), heck you even got a stronk lady. I love that!2. Art style and concept are beautifully done. Music is also amazing, had the pause menu up while i had to do something else and i didn't want to close the game and it was *chef's kiss*Cons:Literally everything else.The game just feels too short, and while short games aren't necessarily a bad thing, it doesn't help that the game feels empty. Seems like a missed story point to me.Raising your dog is pointless. _childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed the game and I think it is worth its money regarding playtime, but I have a few things to say about this dating sim.Sometimes the relationships feel a bit rushed and there are also plot points that don't have a conclusion (example: the stolen camera). I love the general concept of his character. However, he tries to pull me into his lifestyle, lets me experience it without asking me first - if I recall right, but then reacts negatively when I mention I just want a burger? As someone with ADHD, who struggles with texture and taste and relies on safe foods, that made him very unlikeable. I need to go with what he wants for a positive outcome, but I cannot like stuff he doesn't or he will disapprove? Considering he is disabled, it makes me even more confused that out of all the characters he is the one to not consider the other person's needs and wants. _childDocuments_.review: Best Friend Forever is a really cute dating sim centered around dogs and their owners. I was surprised at how much I loved the characters of this game, and I enjoyed seeing each of their character arcs. The romances felt realistic and didn't shy from the not-so-great things about relationships, which I haven't seen many dating sims do before. There was so much queer-friendly content in this game that extended even beyond the dating sim aspect, and I really appreciated that. The dog-care elements seemed overshadowed by the dating elements, and I wish the dogs played a bigger part in the story, but overall, I really enjoyed this sweet game, and I recommend it to anyone who wants a cute dating sim with lovable characters and cute dogs.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:This goes without saying but the dogs in this game are just so lovely. Best Friend Forever does a great job of combining the dating sim/visual novel elements with caring and training your dog. Having them be on screen at all times for you to interact with while out and about in the city is one of the standout features in the game, and makes me very thankful to be playing on a touchscreen laptop as the patting mini-feature translates really well to touchscreen input. The art for the dogs and the date options are a lovely soft 2D style. And the cast of characters includes tonnes of diversity, so hopefully there will be a love interest for everyone.What could be improved: The dog events mid-conversation add a level of anxiety to the game I'm not necessarily looking for in a cute game about dogs and dates. There were a couple of reasons for this: one was that I often didn't seem to notice they were happening because I was busy reading the dialogue, and the second reason is that I found it difficult to know what the mini games wanted me to actually do. It took quite a bit of trial and error to get each one right, even though the actions themselves are actually really simple. Apart from that issue, I at times found the tone of the game's humour to feel a bit jarring and out of place (especially the opening quiz) but this wasn't a major negative.Overall Best Friend Forever is a fun combination of Nintendogs meets Dating Sim, which definitely leans more towards visual novel than it does pet management sim.

_childDocuments_.review: I love dogs more than people and I think many others would say the same thing.You head off to a city where basically everyone has a dog and you are not going to be an exception. Best Friend Forever is a simulation/visual novel that’s all about looking after your dog but also finding yourself a lover. After you adopt your new buddy, your pup will randomly need assistance throughout the game. Sometimes, he’s scared and needs a pat. Other times, he’s pooped and you need to toss out the bag. I enjoyed the management element of this at first, having to balance reading each conversation with caring for my dog.Each week you’ll choose certain events to go to, or people to socialise with, from a map. You have five different options to pick out of a whole bunch. These can range from simply bumping into people while you’re out with your dog, to more serious outings, like going on dates.Dating Rainbow Bay residents means exploring the city together, hopping around the local joints to read their stories as they unfold. There’s back-and-forth dialogue to choose from, but I didn’t feel my choices made much of a difference on how things played out. Once you’ve hung out with a person enough, you can progress the relationship to going steady.With that said, I also have some dislikes.Lack of dog breeds. It always gives you the same 4 dogs.It sometimes bugs the characters' image, for example:.There's  skip option and if you save before a choice to see both reactions after you load in the menu, you will have to .Those errors make this game (after some routes) a .In my opinion it's a really little pricey for its content, 12 would fit better. But as I said that's my opinion and It's not a big bother (idc)

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played two hours, but I honestly love this game a lot already. My first route was with Anders, and lemme just say, *chef's kiss*. Emotionally unavailable? Just my type.PROS:1. Cute dogs! And the mini things you can do with them are super cute; I like taking care of them. Having to stop your dog from taking a fat dump everywhere is hilarious. 2. Very intriguing characters! I like how they all have very distinct personalities. No one is the exact same. I can't say anything on backstories yet since I've only done Anders, but if he's anything to go by, I think they're all really, really great. 3. GORGEOUS art. This art style has always been one of my favorites. Every character just looks so beautiful and pleasing. It's what attracted me to the game in the first place!4. The dialogue and humor feels super natural. It isn't cringe-y or forced, all conversations feel like real ones you could have. 5. Small social media part -- it's not super prevalent, but it's cute, and I like how you can choose your personality through it.6. Pronouns! I love seeing they/them in there. It's very queer friendly (it made me so happy seeing a trans character btw). 7. SUPER DIVERSE! 8. Sacha, Anders, and Maribel exist.CONS:1. Not much character customization. I'm a huge fan of being able to choose exactly how my character looks. You have to choose from three people, all who are just the same person but like masculine, feminine, androgynous, etc. 2. The routes are kind of short. I wish they were longer! The game is still very fulfilling and satisfying, but I get attached easily, so I'm a fan of longer story lines/routes. 3. You can't romance Quincy or Jade ): What am I supposed to do without my himbo and pretty girlboss? 4. Some things aren't as fleshed out as I wish they were (our job situation, the Dog Wizard, the statue everyone keeps mentioning, etc). These things are mentioned quite often that you'd think we'd get more of an elaboration on them all. It doesn't ruin the game, but it was a con for me. 5. The dog medal system thing. It's a little difficult to get gold medals. Because if you focus on one trait, Jade mentions the ones you didn't focus on, and when you focus on those, she mentions others, and it's back and forth. I tried doing everything evenly but I still ended up with all bronze in the end. This part was a little frustrating. Is it worth the price? Depends on what you find most important in a game. I personally think you should go for this if it's on sale only, unless you have money to spend, of course. I don't regret spending the amount I did though! TL;DR - Cute game with cute dogs and cute people. Worth it to play, 8/10, would play some more.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Friend Forever is a visual novel dating sim coupled with dogs, sound like a winner right? Unfortunately what looks good on paper is executed poorly here. The gameplay of Best Friend Forever is a very generic point and click dating story where you take of dogs in between. The characters are dull and the dialouges downright cringeworthy sometimes.The romances are also not given time to build up and feels extremely rushed. It took me around 2 hours to complete a selected route while taking care of the dog activities. Speaking ofdog activities, the dog part of the game feels tacked on just to appeal to more people.The care you take of your dogs does not effect the game in any significant way and its purely added for the sake of it. Since the characters are mostly bland, the short journey you take through the game is also farily bland. There is no spark between characters or a real feeling releatonship between you and your dog and it ends before it starts so the gameplay here is not good. Visually Best Friend Forever, in my opinion, is not good. It goes for a cutesy artstyle but most of the characters and animations come off as jarring to say the least. The only thing I liked about the visuals here are the backgrounds and they are usually covered off by some bad looking characters. Some people might like this kind of visual style, it simply does not look good to me.Like the rest of the game, fairly generic. It does its job but you won’t remember it after the game is over.For this price tag, you can do far better than Best Friend Forever. It is short, generic, characters are bland and the story is incredibly rushed. It’s better to look for something else as there are far superior dating sims available for the same price. _childDocuments_.review: I have complex feelings on this game. I'm gonna start with the negative to get it out of my system.I wish more was done with the dog ownership component of this game. As it is it feels like more of a gimmick then anything. They're cute, and you can improve their stats, but that's about it. If this is gonna be how you market your game do something more with it. As it is the dog ownership parts of the game and the romance parts of the game are very disconnected. Maybe have one of the dates with each character be a doggy play date, where you have to make sure your dog is on its best behavior. Maybe give the romancable characters' dogs more personality. Like you love one character, but man they're dog is so yappy! Or maybe how cute their dog is becomes a reason you want to be with them lol. Asides from just the dog gimmick, I think another thing this game struggles from is how short it is. This can cause character arcs to feel rushed and stop you from being able to form a really strong connection with the romance options. One last nitpick is I don't like the 'pick one of these options and if you pick the wrong one the date doesn't start'. It's annoying, especially when you forgot to save. The difficult part should be the date, not starting the date.Okay, onto the positive. It's so damn charming. I love my dog in this game, it's so cute. I love the other dogs in this game, they're so cute (especially Marshmallow). There's a variety of romance options for people with different types and I appreciate that. I like that each has issues which makes it feel realistic but also they still work on those and they have other things which are positive to offer. Anders step on me. Also good disability rep in a dating game? So rare! Really love that. I like this game, but I wanted to love it. Congrats to team behind it still, it has some really good elements.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is very cute, well-designed, and I like the structure of the game. Having weekly choices to nurture your relationship with your pup is really nice. The dog and PC relationship building is by far the best and most unique part of the game. However, my biggest gripe with the game that makes it very hard for me to play is the lack of choices for building my character and creating relationships with the love interests. Most dating sims allow you to have choices on what you do and don't like in order to get a feel for who you are and which love interest you would be most compatible with. For example, one love interest asks if you like Opera. Most dating sims would allow you to chose if you like it, don't like it, are meh on it, or just say an off-hand joke or something. This game just makes you insult the love interest by saying you are under the age of 50. I like opera! I think this love interest is hot! Let me woo! This game offers very little character customization and very few dialog choices. It's like they already made an established character and want you to just be that. Final thoughts; As a dog ownership sim, I would recommend this game. As a dating sim, I would not.

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5/10Completed Sacha's route. I usually go for the 100%, but I can't make myself replay this one.- Generally wholesome and pleasant art style, aesthetics, and atmosphere.- The backgrounds are pretty, particularly the apartment interiors. Was a big fan of the home your protagonist has with the fairy lights and the details like their collection of souvenir mugs.- The variety in dogs is cool, with four to choose from, each of a different breed, personality, boosted stat, and backstory.- The main focus is on the dog care rather than the romance for sure, so YMMV on whether that's a good or bad thing. I'm personally playing dating sims for the relationships and characters rather than the 'management sim'-esque aspect this has, so it wasn't the way I'd have preferred.- The humour reminded me of Dream Daddy. Whether that's a plus or minus is subjective. For me, it was a minus; that kind of relentless, in-your-face goofiness that gets overplayed fast and makes it hard to take the game's attempts at heavier subject matter seriously.- Why. Why. Why.  isn't there a 'skip read text' button? Not only is that a mainstay feature of visual novels for a reason, I'd go as far as to say it's an  one. The lack of one is the major reason behind why I'm not continuing with the other routes - I am absolutely not sitting here manually clicking through the entire story over again for the minute-long scenes you get with specific characters every so often.- Dog events happen way too often. Like, within the span of about twenty seconds, I had to continuously stop progressing the story to comfort my cowering dog, then to pull it back from running away, then to pull it back from digging in the ground, then to pick up its poop. Begging you to let me read the damn dialogue.- Continuing from the above, the randomised factor of when dog events trigger completely messes with the dating sim/emotional story beat aspect of the game. You'll be having your first kiss with your love interest or discussing their childhood trauma and your dog will be farting and taking sh*ts that you have to stop to pick up. Is it funny to mention when you're not actively having it happen to you? Yes. Does it completely ruin it? Yes.- Typos and spelling mistakes are littered throughout the game; not frequently at all, but I noticed a fair few like "and" instead of "a", "through" instead of "throw", etc.- When you're texting characters on your phone, the text speed of your replies is agonisingly slow and non-adjustable. With the main dialogue speed being adjustable in the settings menu, I don't know why this wasn't also affected by that toggle; no one wants to sit there and watch responses get typed out at less than one word per second for a whole conversation.- Randomly tone shifts from cute slice-of-life in a utopia-esque town where everything is perfect to you getting violently robbed and knocked unconscious in the street out of nowhere. Huh? Huh???? Pick a vibe.- The first scene on the bus leads you to think that the game is fully voice-acted, but as soon as the intro's over it shifts into only random noises and catchphrases being said out loud. They're incredibly repetitive and sometimes out-of-place, so I ended up just turning voice acting off.Another negative point that is exclusive to Sacha's route is the handling of the trans themes. During his route, you meet his roommate who mentions Sacha's transition in front of you, and then the entire game grinds to a halt to force you to have a discussion about it. It was already obvious to me that Sacha was trans and I didn't really feel the need to question him about what his roommate meant by 'transition', because... I knew what he meant. So when given the dialogue options "Transition?" and something unrelated, I went with the unrelated one to progress the conversation, only for it to loop back around and force me to pick "Transition?" anyway. Sacha then acts shocked because "I thought you knew!" (I did), you ask him if his roommate was allowed to disclose that, and then all three of you sit down to have a PSA meeting about how you should never out someone without their consent but that it was okay for the roommate to do it in this instance because he had pre-received permission and Sacha isn't stealth but that in any other circumstance this would be bad and you should learn from this information. Later, you're also forced to confront Sacha's transphobic family and discuss his gender there too.Throughout all of this, there is no option to say that you/your character is also transgender, despite the fact that you can choose a 'gender-nonconforming' (read: still feminine, but with a stereotypical 'nonbinary person' hairstyle) appearance and use they/them pronouns. You just have to stand there asking what a "transition" is like an idiot and have these characters explain surface-level facts about being trans to you.I understand why it was put there - as a way to educate cis people - but it was clumsy and ground the whole game to a halt, and when you already know these things, it feels incredibly patronising to have to get 'taught' them by this game, especially with the sort of "You should never ever give away anyone's personal information without their permission!" tone it uses like you're a child at an internet safety lecture.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Friend Forever is a delightful romp through the joy of new love and companionship. Taking on the responsibility of moving to a new town and not knowing anyone, you are soon whisked through the charms of both pet adoption and dating - and BFF does a smashing job of integrating both into a cohesive experience. The dog adoption aspects are wholesome and put a lot of emphasis on proper dog care encouraging the player to maintain good health, exercise, and education for their furry friend. Regular check ups from the Vet nudge the player towards investing in their canine-friend, and players are rewarded for doing well on periodic dog training exams. On the dating front, BFF does an excellent job of making you believe that everyone in Rainbow Bay is legitimately all about their pets and almost every aspect of the narrative swirls around how the player interacts with other potential romantic partners, and more specifically, their dogs. All the characters feel well thought out and it's easy to imagine the lives they live outside the core narrative. Scratching the surface on a couple of the residents of Rainbow Bay it's immediately clear that without following their storylines to fruition, much of their persona is hidden behind believable layers of vulnerability adding a much needed human element to this otherwise dog filled game. There are many extra layers of fluff and flair as well that should not go without notice - the witty and charming writing comes through with every interaction, and emails you receive daily add an extra dash of humor that umbrellas the general narrative. The world feels well thought out and beautifully rendered in a wholesome aesthetic, and locations all have their own charm that adds to the overall vibe of Rainbow Bay. I enjoyed the main plot line and felt that it had a nice progression and believable story; a classic rags to riches bent towards a millennial ideal of fulfilment and meaningful work, it left me feeling good about life. My main critique would be I wish the game was longer and I had more opportunities to learn about other characters before having to commit to a single one. Best Friend Forever has a lot going on, and without repeated playthroughs there is plenty to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on where I stand on this game.  As a Kickstarter backer, I've been waiting for this for quite some time.  I played the prologues, which in hindsight I wouldn't recommend if you're going to play this.  I only say that because at least one of the earlier prologues(I forget which) contain a bit of the main game, so you'll be playing through it twice.I think if you were a fan of the first game you'll likely find this one an entertaining followup.  Otherwise I'm not sure you're going to get what you're expecting to find.  The game has a great look to it if you're a fan of Giger's work(Aliens, Xenomorph, etc.), and like the works of HP Lovecraft.  While not directly tied into Lovecraft, it has lots of elements that feel like part of his world.  I'll be honest, the artwork for the world is really what made me interested and I'm not disappointed in the slightest.  Character models are better than the last game, and if you picked this up for the erotic stuff... Well, there's quite a bit of sexual events that you'll witness or partake in.The music and sound are well done.  Voice acting isn't perfect, but it's pretty well done for 90% of the characters.Level design is really hit or miss.  Some areas of the game feel really well made, and others seem obtrusive just to make them last longer.  There aren't many puzzles that you'll run into during your playthrough, but you might find them somewhat disappointing.  They're often rather simple, so you can figure them out with trial & error instead of finding the clues throughout the game.  Other times it might not be completely apparent that there's an actual puzzle for you to complete.  I'm not a huge fan of puzzles, so I'm not going to complain about the lack of complexity here.Combat is...  Well, it's horrible.  Combat is the least compelling portion of the game and is actively encouraged to avoid by the game itself.  Unfortunately towards the end of the game you're going to have to use combat to survive, and it's still not entertaining.  But at least the final boss fight(s) are more enjoyable than the latest Doom Eternal DLC.One thing that's difficult to address, is the forced sexual acts that occur in the game.  While it fits into the story from a narrative aspect, I wasn't quite a fan of it.  And there's a few moments in the game where this occurs.  Being performed by you, or it happens to you.  To avoid any ambiguity, I'll be blunt; there's some rape in the game.  Again, from a narrative aspect it makes all the sense in the world as to why these things are happening.  Your character never seems to address this, or have much in the way of thoughts about it.  But you might deal with that sort of thing differently, and should have an idea of it.  Spoilers below.

The eroticism feels campy and forced instead of having that horrific pull of say, Clive Barker's work. Speaking of horror authors, there are those that practice not in  jump-scares or gore, but in trepidation, suspense, and putting one step in front of the other because it felt you had to. Lovecraft (a professed influence for this game) springs to mind. Unfortunately, the parts of Lust For Darkness that really made me interested fell short in the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this kind of story-driven games with strong cinematographic flavor, where mechanics are built around story and characters and not the contrary. As consequence, mechanics are various, depending on the narrative situation; gameplay is not repetitive as in usual games. There are very few challenges for challenges sake, very few puzzles for puzzles sake; combats are not the pivot of the experience; everything pivots around the plot. You're immersed and live the story in first person view, as you were the protagonist of an interactive movie. Speaking of cinema, it reminds me of Eyes Wide Shut! Speaking of games, it reminds me of another cinematographic and story-driven game, The Beast Inside; the latter is better in my opinion, however Lust from Beyond is still a good game. It dares to propose adult contents that are usually considered taboo. Sex and lust are mixed with serious thoughts about society, humanity, love, feelings, relationships, pleasure, sorrow, etc. Well, the result is weird and funny, too many sex toys in my opinion! Like to say: sex is a game, just like the one you're playing, don't take it seriously. That's ok, but it's weird! However it's not porn, at most refined and soft erotism. And no, it's not exciting from a sexual point of view. Story is aimed at mature people, it's not a voyeuristic work for perverted and excited people! Despite the content, it's quite a serious work, even if it's difficult to take it seriously because of the weirdness! The best added value of the title is the beautiful aesthetics inspired by the art of H.R. Giger, who everyone knows for the design of Alien, the xenomorph. LFB is a weird mix of Lovecraft's mythos and Giger's visionary paintings! Graphics are not the best, but very good indeed. Animation of characters could be better. Actors and dialogues are very good. All in all, I appreciate such weird unusual experiment! 73/100 could be the right rating. I suggest developers to focus on better and more serious stories and contents, with less weirdness! Their narrative gaming art is promising!

_childDocuments_.review: Giving a positive simply because it exists. It is not a good game mind you but I'm sure most are here to get a taste of some horror.The story revolves around Victor who seems to have an addiction and is genuinely trying to solve it now that he has a fiance. His journey to overcome this addiction leads him through quite a struggle against Lovecraftian horrors that influence many others, for better or worse. They present with two options at the end, either spread the addiction or leave it so just a select few go through this problem hoping time will fix it. It is a strong narrative exploring how some believe lust should be considered above all but it alone doesn't lead to any growth or progression. During the game, we often run through a world that is consumed by the game description of lust with most inhabitants frozen in a constant state, and we decide on should this fate befall Earth.Apart from the story, the game sucks. It seems to face plant so often that every time it tries to do something new, I get scared it is going to pollute the experience. The prologue version was promising and generally  pretty good. Animation and Dialogue deliveries were so stiff, that reading from collectibles made it more intriguing. I was laughing sometimes because the voice actors probably had no idea about the emotional state of the character.The game doesn't have to make itself be so long, while I was mostly walking in the first few hours later I got fed up and just kept running because there was so much ground to cover. They try chase sequences, stealth, and some straight-out combat but it just doesn't seem to work. And I don't understand why do I even have to click two buttons to pick an item, often they strip me of everything I've collected put it in a box, and ask me to pick it up again one at a time. This game will work just fine if it is kept short to 3 or 4 hours. Why should I even use the aim button to slash with a knife that I'm already holding up or reload manually when empty otherwise you click empty shells. That is also the reason for infinite ammo, a safety net because they can't risk you screwing it up and have to start from the beginning. _childDocuments_.review: Horror fans have impatiently been waiting for Lust from Beyond more than any other title. After its appealing Prologue and Scarlet “demos”, it was clear whatever the main dish was going to be, it was set to be the most delicious erotic horror experience ever conceived. Surprise surprise, it’s finally out and guess what? It’s grotesquely perfect!Without spreading many spoilers, we’ll be playing as Victor Holloway, a man whose life will forever change as soon as he joins the Cult of Ecstasy. A cult that it’s quite far from your traditional gentleman country club. This secret society is in touch with a very unique realm, a dimension of pain, pleasure and peculiar sensations.Lust from Beyond will have you deep diving into a fascinating world, emphasizing on exploration in a somewhat linear gameplay, but still very open to details and tribulating encounters. The story and narrative are exquisitely well placed, and captivating, and I’m sure it will hook you up as much as it did for me. The design makes this game stand out from many other horror games out there, in a unique and fashionable way. Its inspiration from Giger and Beksiński are very noticeable, but as if both were mixed, depicting the dimension of Lusst'gha through organic pulsating membranes of living tissue all over the place.Through a demonic style, creatures, and characters show a massive stylized influence of this mysterious world, and even little details aren’t left aside. The game explores human reactions to sexuality both in a gore explicit way, as much as it does in a psychological manner. This ultimately reflects on the main character, and despite his wild reactions, we keep traversing in an adventure that honestly surprised me at every turn. One of the major surprises were the puzzles. I wasn’t expecting to even find any, but they are more and more common in horror games.Puzzles in Lust from Beyond are basically fillers, requiring players to find and utilize objects to unlock doors or a way to collect specific items. I personally don’t have any issue with this, but some players may find this mondaine. Thankfully, they are easy and are a good reason to motivate investigation across the world.Another surprise was the gameplay mechanics, having players to approach a more stealthy attitude, and allowing a choice between play styles. There are some nasty encounters, but there are also some really hot ones, so I’d say they are quite level headed. This is an erotic horror experience after all. If you can’t handle the worst, why would you deserve the sweet pleasures of Lusst'gha?Lust from Beyond had a major update before release date, which improved drastically the optimization. It falls very well under the recommended and advised hardware requirements, so you know exactly what to expect. I’d say is fairly good optimized, considering it runs on Unity.With a fascinating world to explore, and intense moments to live, Lust from Beyond is more than we wanted, and it’s exactly what our most deep, secret desires hoped it would be. It’s alive, it’s evil, it’s sinfully, but it’s ours to be. A masterpiece crafted in blood and flesh.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an adult only game you should buy if you're looking for something "sexy." This is a pretty legitimate horror game that uses sex as a theme, as your character is entrapped in a rivalry between two depraved Lovecraftian sex cults. My immediate worry was that this was going to be a repeat of "Agony Unrated", but I was pleasantly surprised. The game doesn't rely on shock factor only, and doesn't go so overboard with it when they do use it.The weakest part of the game is probably in the combat/stealth as both are probably too easy and amount to either tanking a hit in order to kill an adversary, putting a pistol point blank in someone's face and pulling the trigger, or just running a short distance so that the AI resets. There is also a sanity system that didn't really have much of an effect on gameplay, and didn't feel like was actually a risk to ending my run at any given time. Boss fights amount to some simple puzzles on timing when and where to shoot, nothing too memorable about them.Overall the game shines due to its level design, aesthetic, and a story that grabbed me and kept me interested until the end. There seem to be at least two endings that unfortunately seem to require two full playthroughs to see (as far as I could tell, the last auto save occured after the big choice was made, and I didn't see a way to replay chapters or manual save.) It's one of those things where while I'm not going to go through again right now, but I definitely will revisit this at a later spooky season to see the other ending.I recommend this to those looking to immerse themselves in a well crafted horror world, not necessarily those who are looking for a very engaging gameplay experience.I can also highly recommend this to anyone who is a big fan of H.R. Giger artwork, as there are some very obviously heavy influences in the other world you'll be visiting during the game, and it's probably the best Giger tribute we'll see until Scorn releases (if it ever does.)

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this by first saying that both of the Teaser Demos Lust From Beyond: Scarlet, and Lust from Beyond: Prologue were both fantastic, and the first game, Lust for Darkness, while rocky at first, ended strongly.As for my review:Lust from Beyond is a game that isn't sure quite what it wants to be.  It tries to be dramatic, and story driven, and tries to be survival horror, but falls flat on both.  The plot itself is only mildly engaging with an onslaught of exposition.  It does too much of telling, instead of showing.  The characters are simple and boring, and only really serve as a means of spewing exposition.  A few things are very predictable and uninspired.  The game attempts to use graphic sexuality for disturbing imagery, however, what little of it there is, isn't particularly disturbing.  Being a sequel to Lust for Darkness, one would expect them to ramp it up to 11, however, it falls short of that, and what few scenes of sexuality there are are just a mild curiosity before moving on to advanced the plot.As for the story itself, it feels like it really takes forever for it to take off, it doesn't really start to get interesting or even scary until about chapter 12, and since there's only 15 chapters and an epilogue, means you have to go through a lot before it starts to get interesting.As far as survival horror is concerned, there is no real fear of danger from the enemies in the game, they are easily kited and killed via knife.  Once you go into Lusst'ghaa and have to face multiple enemies, you have a gun with infinite ammo, and they die easily.  So it feels to me, that the enemies are more of a minor inconvenience than anything else.  In fact the only point in the game where the enemies felt even a little threatening was during the rooftop chase sequence.The game had so much potential, but just falls flat.  If you're looking for something to kill about 12 hours, then this game is for you.  If, however, if you're just looking for something that is creepy or more horrifying, stick with the Demos, and the original game, Lust for Darkness.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, Lust from Beyond is definitely a title to talk about. I want to point out firstly that my playtime stat is inflated, I did leave the game on accident several times throughout my playthrough. The true length is probably more like 10+ hours including puzzle and exploration time along with several dozen game overs. In this review I will try to not give away spoilers as I want this to be a good representation for people that haven't played. (Just be warned I may slip up as its difficult to explain some things without spoilers) First Ill talk about  As far as modern games go the game looks pretty good as a indie title goes better than expected. Where the game truly shines is environment, the color schemes, the attention to detail is extremely rich. I was far more struck with the levels than any other graphical feature. The character models are nicely detailed in clothing (when there is any lol) and simple not trying to draw too much attention. Though I do say there is quite a bit lacking in the actual models themselves faces are dull and boring and the nudity does what it needs to but oddly isn't a distraction in a erotic horror game. Both of these points a feel a partially intentional as this is not a porn game, and the Masks most characters wear are beautiful. Along with objects I found myself looking at the masks and object models alot as they were very well done and detailed. Enemies were decently varied, Human enemies took the cake in variation while the eldritch enemies from another plane of existence were surprisingly kinda monotonous after while, wish there were a little bit more unique looking enemies in different parts and stages of the game while in Lusst'gha. , what can I say this game did a great job with everything from voice acting, to music, to ambiance. Developers knew what they were doing with sound. I cant think of anything it lacked or needed more of, it did what it needed to do and the most important part is increase tension and getting me ready to be scared. The enemy audio cues are wonderful by the way.Now onto the meat of the game, I went into this playing the prologue like the day before. And while I didn't follow the whole thing through it still made sense and was contextually satisfying. I kinda liked not really knowing what happened in Lust for Darkness or LFB: Scarlet. It made a sense of mystery to me that made the horror a bit better even. The characters felt unique while not extremely complicated as to their motivations, personality, and sense of how they fit into the story. The entire story felt pretty good overall, I love the themes and controversy involved. Although the section where Victor went through a temporary visual change was confusing and felt to amount to nothing really, so its unclear to me as to why it was in the game at all. I liked this story far more than most other titles of similarity that were popular in the past, like Amnesia for instance. Though the bulk of info in the Book of Secrets the background info about that plane of existence I mostly ignored for my own reasoning. They did a great job with what I had decided to read but to understand cosmic horror seems counter intuitive.Lastly Id like to add the pacing was a bit unusual as the last couple of hours towards the ending seemed like it was under developed, but that's what timeskips usually do to me. Its also difficult to close a very Lovecraftian style story like this I feel.Lastly but certainly not least the potatoes of the game, Walking around and interacting with stuff for the whole game was simple, done well, and decently intuitive. Sometimes however I found myself interacting with a swinging object like a door or lever that had inverted its swing direction for whatever reason. I don't know if these were glitches or a peculiarity with my own system and/or peripherals. I also would've liked to see some hitbox sliding or model smoothing, basically when you hit another object with a hitbox that stops you it made you stuck for a split second. Instead of moving around the object kinda slower than walking, it messed me up in combat situations with obstacles in the room. Wish there was variation in enemy tactics they all just sorta ran at you and attacked. Upgrades felt like little secret rewards. Stealth was also simple which they could've done more but honestly for what it is I think they did just fine with the implemented stealth features. Achievements will certainly give it fair replay value.Graphics: 8.5/10 reduction for base model blandness (half point) and though locations in Lusst'gha were stunning to look at they were reused for a few of them (full point). Audio: 10/10Story:  9/10 reduction for a few parts not making sense and the Book of Secrets info being a bit too much for me to want to know though it is optional I unlocked them anyway fearing Id miss out on a secret bonus thing which didn't happen anyway. Also for a pacing breakup near the ending.Mechanics: 7/10 Decent but with enemies attacking the same, upgrades being under utilized, and puzzles being ok but not really difficult, this and few other things brought this to the lowest scoring.Game length: Long 8+ hrs about for a game like this is a fair amount of content and that doe even include replay.Overall Score: 8/10Spoiler Warning ( For those that have finished it, here is my sectional in-depth review)

_childDocuments_.review: Out of a YES or a NO, It's a yes, but if I am honest with you, only just.  [7/10]This Review CONTAINS MILD SPOILERS.As someone who is an avid fan of the Lust Series, Lust from Beyond was WAY too long. I was told that the game was between 6-10hrs of game play. I have just completed it at over 16hrs. This caused some major drag factor for me. There were times that I pushed myself forward in the first half of the game just because I agreed to review the game for the Devs.The game actually felt like 2 separate games pushed together. I honestly thought that if you removed 60-70% of the first half of the game, the game as a whole would have been a solid 9 or 10 /10, but there was so much of that first half that seems shoe-horned in for shock value that I really lost interest. There was one point -- MILD SPOILER ALERT -- with a completely Pointless rape scene that nearly ruined the game for me. Had I bought the game myself, I would have stopped playing it there and not picked it up again. The previous games had edged around the topic with threat and that had me on the edge of my seat with discomfort, but having it thrust in my face like that just made me angry and i know for a fact will ruin the whole game for others. -- SPOILER OVER -- I felt the majority of the first half dragged and seemed to add random bits for the purpose of shock, and discomfort. This was doubly annoying cause it failed. All it did was make me bored, frustrated, and extremely angry.All of this could not be MORE infuriating cause the second half is PHENOMENAL, The Lore, the Intrigue, the interweaving story line, the twist of fate and the choices... Honestly mind blowing. It kept hinting back at aspects from the previous games that had my adrenaline pumping with excitement. And the Lore!! The History of Lusst'ghaa, How Lusst'ghaa was connected to our realm of existence, and the purpose and reason for the Seeing ones.... Sensational!The Game play additions also really added to the game. The addition of the inventory game was amazing. And the way that the game incorporated a sort of "levelling up" system was inspired to say the least. Really enjoyed the variety of collectable that were available (even if i did think the design was lacking in comparison to the 2 prologues). There was also a really nice evolution around the protagonist's abilities that I absolutely loved, even if i did think that came a little late in the game. There were a couple of annoying aspects of the game. For a computer as powerful as mine, the loading screens took a laboriously long time. And much like the previous games, there were still some audio balance issues, The despite the Voice levels being at 10 and the other audios being at 3, there were still occasions where the voices were only understandable cause of the closed captions.The Character of Victor was actually really identifiable. Throughout the game you really felt what he felt and was with him every step of the way. This being said, there were some plot points that seemed really illogical and backwards, I got that there were certain plot points that needed to happen, but it was really janky at times.The Aesthetics though were phenomenally beautiful, Really drawing from HR Giger and the City really felt like a new age Lovecraftian town.Overall opinion - Too long. Too much added for shock value that ended up actually detracting from the game in my opinion. Aesthetically beautiful, and the core story (Specifically in the second half of the game) combined with the intricate Lore was sensational.

_childDocuments_.review: A huge improvement from its predecessor, Lust For Darkness, this game combines beautiful and horrific settings with a reasonably well-told plot. It has great atmosphere, and far fewer useless clickables when compared to the first game. The controls are more refined, if not perfect, and it has a much better balance of exploration, puzzles, character interaction, and action. Best of all, it has some great jump-scares and lurking terror, without inundating the player with this material.The game has some weaknesses that distracted me from the story, though. Facial animations and lip sync were very primitive, and in some of the sexual encounter scenes, it's very uncanny valley to see animatronic-style eye-rolling and weirdly lit teeth in a clenching jaw. Not sexy at all.  One character I noticed had no lip-sync at all, and moved his mouth open and closed like a Muppet! This is was unfortunate, but at least most of the time they use the well-designed masquerade masks to hide characters' features. Voice acting is hit and miss. Many of the secondary characters are quite passable, but then you get the bellhop with the head wound whose weirdly European accent has a New Orleans drawl to it. In Massachusetts? Probably the hardest to listen to is the protagonist, who flip flops between pathos and rage far too quickly. The writing doesn't help, because for a book-learned antiquarian, he sure likes to call everyone "****-heads." I received the "Lust From Beyond M Edition" with a Humble Bundle purchase, and I can't really recommend it. While it does tone down the excessive sex and gore, that version doesn't do enough to replace it with content that makes sense. I played it first, and there were lots of scenes where the game cut-to-black and skipped over meaningful dialogue or exposition that should have made the plot more engaging. The M edition went too far, in my opinion, by removing too much of the erotic material. This game is about lust, after all, and you can still get an "M" rating while including things like nudity in the artwork around the mansions. This original is the version to get, and you can always enable a censorship mode to pixel-mosaic the nudity.It's hard to know who to recommend this game to. It's not a porn game, but it's much too explicit to be called simply "risque". It's a game of Lovecraftian, Gigeresque horror and gothic romance that strays very far into exploitation territory. This game needs trigger warnings on its trigger warnings.A last comment about the characters and themes-- don't look here if you like role models and positive examples. I'd almost call the game misogynistic because of its portrayal of wicked, sadistic Delilah tropes and violence against females. Only the game is full of bad men, too, and murders and tortures them in equal amounts. Count yourself warned.If you're just looking for your next game to play, you could skip this. You really need to be in the mood for great atmosphere, bad voice-acting and facial animation, great surrealist horror, awkward and repulsive explicit sex, fascinating Lovecraftian themes, over-used Gigeresque bone-and-organs hallways. The best predictor of if this will be up your alley is if you play the two excellent prologue chapers (more than demos). Lust From Beyond Prologue, and Lust From Beyond Scarlet do a fantastic job of showing off this game's best qualities. If you can't stand those, you won't want to pay for this.

_childDocuments_.review: NO! I do not usually play NSFW games. This was recommended to me by a friend ☹. I mean, it was First Person Perspective…..has shooting…..and is horror…so, some of the stuff I like. These reasons made me try it. But no, it’s not a game that can turn someone on as it’s very grotesque & gory. Everyone’s fantasies morphed into a living nightmare.      A horrifying fantasy is the best way to describe this game. The plot is filled with love, lust & horror. So, the basic plotline goes something like this:    The plotline is a bit unique as I have never played a game that falls under this genre. It was really engaging & kept me hooked until the very end.   Oh, and yes, Lust from Beyond is the sequel to Lust for Darkness. I mean, I didn’t play the prequel but still understood the plot of Lust from Beyond. If you want to get a thorough 100% understanding of the story, I recommend playing Lust for Darkness first.    Horror games aren’t only about the spooks & thrills. You need to be able to play the game properly. Here, I will be mentioning a few of the core mechanics of Lust From Beyond.    This game is filled with puzzles. Let me first talk about the “Inspect Object” feature. So, you can pick up most of the items around you & inspect them by turning them around. So, this made me think that whatever object I could pick must have a clue for some puzzle on it or something. Well, the game proved me wrong. There was literally no use for this feature unless you are inspecting the lore stones that make you rotate an object to a certain position to solve the puzzle. _childDocuments_.review: Lust from Beyond masterfully blends psychological horror with dark eroticism, creating a uniquely unsettling experience that only deepens the more you play. What might seem like fan service in other games is instead grotesque and twisted, fitting the game’s disturbing atmosphere perfectly.You play as Victor Halloway, a man haunted by terrifying nightmares that lead him to the eerie town of Bleakmoor. There, he embarks on a nightmarish journey filled with lust, death, and revelations that turn his reality inside out. The game’s narrative takes inspiration from Lovecraft, with design elements heavily influenced by Giger and Beksinski, and it shows in the nightmarish landscapes of Lusst'ghaa—a world shaped by twisted desires.The game's environments, especially in Lusst’ghaa, feel alive. The walls breathe, pulse, and seem intent on devouring you, creating a constant sense of dread. The unsettling visual style amplifies the horror, though the option to censor nudity can disrupt immersion when pixelated bodies suddenly appear in scenes designed to unsettle. Exploration and puzzle-solving are central to the game, though the puzzles themselves are rather straightforward. Early on, the solutions are practically handed to you via notes, but toward the end, the game presents more challenging, satisfying puzzles that require actual thought. I only wish this design had been consistent throughout.The “essence” mechanic, introduced later in the game, feels like an afterthought. Its potential is underutilized, serving only to create paths or distract enemies, leaving much to be desired in terms of its impact on gameplay.Combat is initially a last resort, with running and hiding being the primary means of survival. However, once you acquire weapons—particularly the pistol—the tension fades. Running past enemies becomes almost too easy, and later battles, including boss fights, lack the punch you’d expect from a game with such a strong atmosphere.Despite its flaws, Lust from Beyond offers a truly unique horror experience with its grotesque visuals, compelling world, and unsettling atmosphere. While the journey is more engaging than the destination, it’s still a game worth playing if you enjoy atmospheric horror with psychological depth.Check out more of my game reviews on my curator page:
