_childDocuments_.review: It's not a sex game with horror elements, but horror game with sex elements. It's an indie game and the dev clearly wanted the game to be more resident evil-like, it's just not that scary nor hard. Even in the hardest difficulty the game is more or less a breeze, The game features health, psyche and another bar down the line, and you technically can "upgrade" them, but upgrade them only make your game easier, and the game is already really easy. You can sprint indefinitely, so getting past most enemies beside one is a breeze. You have 2 means of defending yourself and the best method of fighting enemies 'cept for the end is running away. Now the puzzle parts are fun. It's like a little collect-a-thon. It's for bonus content but you can obtain a better weapon with it. And the puzzles are easy but fun, if a bit bland.The lust part are more or less well done, but it's more of a narrative device to the Eldritch cultist overarching theme, which is actually pretty good. It's not breaking any ground but it's sensible. You get to choose dialogues sometimes and choosing some options that will affect the ending slices (except some which maybe inconsequential? I may have to play more to know, but then playing a horror game is pretty draining). I finished only one of the two main endings, and the other ending is potentially more rewarding, because none of the characters in this game are happy. They're all deranged with multiple problems before coming into the cult part. There's not enough "lust" in Lust from Beyond. Yea sure there are some in the game but you'd think you can do way more with how much prop they make and the things they portrayed, I recommend the game if you like Resident Evil and want more feisty stuff and gore. My mind is scarred forever and it'll never go away.

_childDocuments_.review: In many ways a throwback to the early till mid-2000s when titles like "Manhunt" or "Condemned" were at least possible to produce, "Lust from Beyond" reminds of a wild time in gaming's long gone past. Of something in the medium's "youth" so to speak, when transgressive content was - if you will - not an exception but rather the norm: yes there are a few sex scenes and sexual displays in the bonus section, but what really stands out is the amount of violence and how a contextualized story unfolds not with but despite of it.  Although most violent content present in here is somehow also sexualized, what differs from today's mainstream games is that violence does not fit a certain purpose: it's not there to "make a point" nor "proof" something but rather to disturb and "put off".So in today's world it's much more important how a game is perceived than what's actually in it: public opinion matters more than any fiction.In "God of War" (2018) for example, its message of parenthood is clearly more important than anything else. It's also praised for its gameplay alright, but that cannot possibly be the case: it plays perfectly, yes, but still rather dull in comparison to the original idea of "God of War" as a video game. It just plays out as streamlined as any other AAA title nowadays.Even still more or less grotesque content like "Mortal Kombat 11" now feels rather abstract because representation comes first, creative freedom second: it may be "consumed" without a problem but not actually mindfully received.Ok, from a limited technical standpoint, "Lust from Beyond" (2021) is not a good game and even not a great step up from its tame predecessor, the also Kickstarter-funded "Lust for Darkness" (2018) which later on got a much more explicit re-release in VR. Further more, if you already played its two demos there is not much new content in the full release: you only get a rather empty town environment in one chapter that's totally new. That's it. Most of the shocking value was also released for free somewhere inside those two demos.And "Lust from Beyond" is a classic adventure at heart: nothing spectacular and very formalistic. There are some simple puzzles and a rudimentary stealth mechanic at present, to accompany the first-person view.  Later on it turns into a shooter that's definitely not very good. Like many hotspots to activate something in the adventure part, even one and a half years after release the reload function of your weapon does not necessarily work properly and the default gamepad control scheme constantly asks you to turn everything on with the trigger button.Yet the worst thing of these damned and stupid gameplay decisions certainly lies in the fundamental save system: there's only one checkpoint that constantly gets overwritten and you always have to manually back it up somewhere in case you missed one of the many collectibles.All that said you can easily spend way over twenty hours with this game and still find something new to explore. For a linear title that has rather reduced production values (videos and screenshots of the game look as if there's much more here than what's actually there because everything is repeating itself constantly) this is rather astounding: in some ways "Lust from Beyond" is not what it seems.As a pornographic endeavour it's not erotic at all, then you meet colorful characters not shy of any stereotypes that throw in some scatological humour, and finally there is this rather complex mythology of the "Lust" universe: even the libertine character of the narrative is just a pose because there are cleary good guys and bad guys in this world. Not unlike "Manhunt" the game is therefore much more moral than you might think: it's a fun video game about desire and betrayal that dares to ask difficult questions. It's Gigeresque alternative world is not nearly as satisfying as the one of the blown-up "Scorn" (2022) but you have to kill pityful creatures in it and therefore won't forget anything about it. So it's even whimsical at times and makes you think about what you actually like in this world - something today's AAA titles mostly forgot how to communicate with all of their identity politics.Some of the designs are really exceptional: there is one creature that resembles the Navigator from Dino de Laurentii's "Dune" (you already encounter it in one demo), then there are sex toys that seem to come straight out of Boro's famous 1973 short film "Une collection particulière" for which he may have invented a sexual "history" in form of an early mockumentary. Well, there are certain limitations to all those things: it may be good that because of Unity all of the corpses in this game look like mannequins.While the true tasteless stuff does not lie in monstrous sex scenes but a Bosch triptych or this famous painting of Goethe on his Italian journey in the salon: why the heck is this stuff in a suppsoed to be libertine mansion? Are those people Catholics after all?As puzzling as those items are, they just look like mindless copy and paste out of image libraries - because they look good and are in the public domain.Anyways, like "Agony Unrated" and "Succubus", 50 years after the departure of filmmakers like Polanski, Boro and Zulawski, the "Lust" games as truly Polish(ed - no pun intended) artworks certainly echo and respond to a repressed Catholic environment and society in popular culture. Just like what Viennesse Actionism did with my country in Austrian fine art. It - to a certain degree - transformed it. And certainly for the better because unlike both aforementioned titles, the "Lust" titles are no provocations for the provocation's sake. They may not be technically marvelous, but what they lack in finesse they more than enough make up with character. And they are all produced with good will at heart.Just don't listen to what deplorable journalists will tell you about them: even in 2009 someone like Adam Sessler condemned my favourite video game franchise of all time during its initial western release, the Onechanbara franchise. Their clear goal is to make video games all the same and everyone who does not want that just has to support titles like this: they tried to release a toned-down "M Edition" but even that seems to have difficulties finding a home on consoles. At least the quite similar "The Beast Inside" could recently been released but there's nothing to ridicule or "wrong" with "Lust from Beyond". It's neither "sick stuff", nor to ignore in its unusuality. Just hateful and intolerant bigots might articulate those insults.

_childDocuments_.review: I agonised about weather to recommend this or not. I bought it for about NZD $20 and I think that was fair for my casually paced 14 hour playthrough. A lot of love has gone into this game.tries to build a compelling universe with rich lore but is sidetracked by a lot of other things; Combat, Puzzles, QTEs, consequential dialogue choices, Sanity meter, a magic system, sex scenes … I feel like it tried to do too much and has left the story and storytelling behind, which is a bit of a shame since it does such a good job of atmosphere, sound and voice acting. It doesn’t know if it is an atmospheric puzzle game or an action-horror game. In either case there is plenty of gore, a few jump scares and a dash of cosmic horror, worth buying especially if you like Giger’s work. Because of the effort that's gone into this title I also feel like a future game by  would be worth attention.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a really solid opening, some really imaginative and creative ideas, presents itself well, and is leagues above the typical schlock you find in most horror games. So if you're looking for a good horror game, or at least a horror game that is better than the oceans of mediocre garbage that pollutes steam, you'll find it here. But as much as I want to like this game and recommend it, after beating it and letting it settle in my mind for a while, I just can't.As I said, the game has a really strong opening, and the story tackles some really uncomfortable but important topics regarding the human condition. At first I thought the game was pacing itself pretty well, and that it was going to have a gradual descent into madness. But then all at once a bunch of nutty cultists show up to try and kill you and things go sideways rather fast. It's a bit disappointing, especially since the cult comes off as rather over the top, but the story was still intriguing enough that I wanted to know what was going to happen next. The eldritch other world that you explore on and off throughout the game is incredibly eerie, both beautiful and creepy at the same time, and it's a visual marvel. And I liked the mansion that the main character ends up staying at, as both the location and the characters you find there are very memorable and interesting.Unfortunately the antagonistic cult is so messed up that it ends up being hard to take seriously. The moment that lost me was in the bloodhouse. It's supposed to be a place where high ranking members of the cult go to fulfill their primal desires, no matter how dark or twisted they are, and it's meant to be disturbing. But the sheer number of dead bodies in that area just made me laugh, and it came off as cartoonish rather than disturbing, as it makes no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sense. I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ how much they're bribing the police, if the cult is kidnapping and killing that many people, there's no way in hell they would be able to remain in operation for longer than a week without being discovered and shut down. Plus, even if you're a total psychopath with no regard for your fellow human beings I still have to believe that the overpowering smell of those dead bodies would be a massive turn off that would make it impossible to enjoy anything down there.But while these flaws did bug me, ultimately they were forgivable and were outweighed by the things the game did right, and if the game had ended at chapter 11 with part of chapter 12 serving as the epilogue I would have liked the game, and would be recommending it right now. But unfortunately the game kept going, and the story ended up ruining any goodwill it had built up.The first major issue is that the game overexplains the lore of its otherworld. The key to good horror, especially lovecraftian horror, is fear of the unknown. Lusst’ghaa is an intriguing setting, but having the characters exposition dump who made it and how it works sucks the mystery and fun out of things. It would have been better if the characters were just speculating, and didn't actually know or understand much of anything about Lusst’ghaa beyond the basics, as it would leave more room for the player's imagination to fill in the blanks.The original Silent Hill games did this so much better. While the games did offer a little bit of explanation for the mysterious dark power behind the supernatural stuff going on in the town, it was always clear that the cultists were dabbling with forces that they did not understand and could not control, and this frequently backfired on them. So it's rather underwhelming when in this game the characters seem to be not only be quite knowledgeable about the eldritch other world, but also have some degree of control over it, which further takes away the fear and mystery.But the real deal breaker is how the game unravels toward the end. I'll try to avoid any explicit spoilers, but I'm not going to be disguising my critiques too much, so be aware of that. Near the end it's revealed that a character who had appeared to be a nuanced, flawed, but ultimately still sympathetic person was actually a deranged psychopath all along. Because I guess the game decided it needed a villain, and couldn't be bothered to properly establish one sooner. We already dealt with a deranged psychopath earlier in the game, could they not have done better for the climax of the game?And the ending sucks, because while there is some variation in the ending depending on the player's decisions throughout the game, broadly speaking there are only two possible endings, and both are terrible. In one ending the main character sides with the villain and agrees to basically destroy the world, which is just awful. What makes it almost worse is that based on the descriptions in the epilogue it sounds like despite the villain's grand vision their plan didn't actually affect the entire world, just the nearby region, which is pretty underwhelming. If you say that there's going to be an apocalypse then at least follow through on it.In the other ending the main character rejects the villains plan, and after leaving and spending a few months trying to rebuild their old life ends up committing suicide. Now, I think I get what the game was going for. The game is very lovecraftian inspired, and the whole game the characters are interacting with eldritch forces beyond mortal understanding, and dabbling with otherworldly forces can drive you mad, which is why even after surviving and living on the main character is still haunted and that's why he commits suicide. But unfortunately the game ends up sending a rather dangerous message. From the beginning it's established that the main character is a sex addict, which is why he's drawn to Lusst’ghaa in the first place and gets caught up in all the cult stuff. Throughout the entire game he wants to get over his addiction, stop the visions he has of Lusst’ghaa and just live a normal life. By making it so that the only two endings are one in which he gives in to the eldritch nightmare, and one in which he commits suicide, the game seems to be implying that anybody with a sex addiction (or any kind of addiction or mental health illness for that matter) is incapable of living a normal life, is incapable of overcoming or managing their condition, and that the only way for them to be free is to die.Now, I don't think this is the message the game was trying to send, but it's the one that it's sending whether it realizes it or not. And as someone with a mental health illness this is an incredibly damaging and incorrect message.For a good example of how to handle this sort of thing right, we turn back to Silent Hill, more specifically Silent Hill 2. In that game James Sunderland spends his whole journey dealing with his trauma, and the various endings are him coming to terms with what happened. In one of the endings he commits suicide, but in another ending he's able to move on and live his life. The multiple endings clearly demonstrate that sometimes trauma does run too deep, but that sometimes it can be overcome, even if the scars will always remain. It doesn't just present one outcome as the only way.And that's really the key problem with Lust from Beyond. It's not the fact that the game has an ending where the main character commits suicide, it's the fact that it's the only non bizarre ending, which presents it as the only way. And that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up.The game isn't terrible, and there were a lot of things about it that I really liked. But unfortunately the missteps the story made toward the end were bad enough to poison my overall feelings toward the game, and I can't in good conscience recommend this game. The developers are clearly talented, and hopefully if they make another horror game they'll have addressed and fixed these issues and will end up making something truly great. But for now, I'm left feeling rather disappointed.

Pros-Story and Lore-Most of the voice acting-Visuals are very good, especially in the Land of Eternal Ecstasy -Just when you think the game is going to end, nope! Still a good deal more to go! -Upgrade system for the character can get rid of small annoyances like Stealth Mechanics being slow, or QTEs. Cons-Game length (Clocked in at 8 hours on my first play-through)-Combat (Its not the worst, but it isn't the best either. Playable for sure, but as combat isn't a heavy focus? This really isn't a problem)-Control settings (There is no camera smoothing, and the sensitivity settings vary greatly from 1 to 2, let alone the rest. Takes some getting used to) Overall? 8/10. Worth the price they have set and I very much hope to see more games from this world, or what other worlds these devs will craft.

In my opinion, this game went way too heavy with the gore and torture porn aspect, which took up the bulk of the game, but I was more interested in the sex cult stuff. Then again, that's entirely subjective to me, and for what its worth, the first game (Lust for Darkness) delivered on the sex cult stuff much more, even if that game was really short.Anyway, where the game shines best is the atmosphere. The town and the other dimension you explore are super creepy, but jump scares are predictable when the lighting is suddenly non existent. The game play was kind of clunky, especially combat, but for the most part you're not doing much more than sneaking around and solving puzzles. The one part I found particularly annoying was the boss fight with Tim, because you have to let him get super close and time everything perfectly, and I had a problem with hurting myself with the steam.Over all I'd say if you can stomach gory visuals and like lovecraftian horror combined with erotic themes, give it a try. _childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rating of "ehh". It does some things well. The H. R. Geiger inspired world looks great, there's a fleshed out story, and it has enough gameplay variety to stay interesting. However there are things that really drag the game down in terms of quality, most of which are related to the gaming aspect, and some to the execution of the story.The problem with gameplay aspect is that just about every mechanic in the game has been done much better in other games. Stealth for example is very barebones. You basically stay out of sight of enemies that have very limited visibility cones, and that's it. That's the whole stealth mechanic; you're outmaneuvering partially blind enemies.The fighting mechanics are very limited as well. I know this isn't a fightning game, but once again this sort of limited survival horror fighting has been done way better in other games, and it feels utterly unsatisfying as a result when you do use it. It actually reminds me the look and feel of fighting mechanics from 20 years ago because all the modern innovations like ragdoll physics and enemies that physically react to the impact of your attacks (stagger animations and the likes) and parry mechanics for melee fighting are all either absent or really primitive. When you stab someone to death you just get close to them, left click really fast, and they fall down with some generic animation. It's just not up to par with today's standard.The puzzles are easy and mostly obvious after a while I just felt like I didn't want to go through the motions anymore and just get on with the story.With regards to the story, it's disappointing to me that a game that is called "Lust From Beyond" that is about a sex cult and a world of sexual ecstasy can be so unsexy. It's actually way more focused one gore and violance aspect of horror, than on gratuitous sexual thrills. A game like Agony (unrated) has way more sexual thrills than this game. I feel like it's a wasted opportunity. I wanted to play this game for the fantasy of dark sexual indulgence, yet I spent most of my time in slaughterhouse like scenery, or in an alien looking scenery, and the sexual content is actually pretty scarce. It's almost as if they were too busy making sure the game can be preceived as a "serious" game, and completely forgot what the concept is advertising.The reading material from the other world is just a bunch of mumbo-jumbo nonesence, and I didn't feel liek the reading material in the human world added much to the story.With regards to the technical aspect of the game, the anti-aliasing is really poor.Strangely enough I'm not disappointed I played the game. It's OK. It's just not what it was supposed to be, and there are better games, but if you don't have anything else to play, it's an alright kind of novelty. But nonetheless, it's a thumbs down for me, just because the game should've been different, and could've been much better.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a full-length high quality mix of a horror game and an adventure game game featuring pornographic elements. You should support it just because of its bravery and artistic integrity in the face of mass media censorship. It is not a cheap cash-grab like the vast majority of erotic games. It is a proper game with sex in it. I massively enjoyed it and heavily recommend it. That out of the way, here's some praises and some nitpicking:Pros:- Delightfully perverse. If you've ever wanted to take part in a ritualistic orgy, but not in real life because of the crazy people or the STDs, this game is for you.- The game mixes body horror with cosmic horror and while it is rarely scary it is heavily atmospheric with some impressive environments.- I loved the blood house bit (except the smiley face puzzle). That section was the one section I found scary.- I loved that room with the desk and all the curtains. Compliments to the voice actor's performance in there. That must be one of my favourite moments in the game.- I loved the last puzzle in Lusst'ghaa with the three crystals and the three tumours. That was some enjoyable puzzle-solving and good level design.- The game features a little bit of (avoidable) combat. It's not the greatest but it gives you a bit of variety when you replay.- The story is great. There's twists. There's choices to make. There's even a deep philosophical question about the meaning of life if you dig deep enough. There is one bit which I found a little jarring but other than that it was excellent.- Level design is simple yet effective (except the first open level).- The game is very speed-runnable. Almost all of the dialogues and cinematics are skippable though you need to mash spacebar (maybe an option for auto-skip is in order?).- There are some amusing instances of humour both in the game and in the achievements.Cons (nitpicking):- The first open level has a couple of things you can easily miss and also a couple of places you can get stuck. Accessing the common room relies on luckily picking the right thing to say in a dialogue you can easily miss. The note on the bar's door appears after you've done something else so you might have been there and assumed you're done with that area when you're actually supposed to return for a second look.- That puzzle with the smiley faces. Maybe I would have gotten it if I wasn't being chased by maniacs. Who knows. I had to use a walkthrough.- Replaying the bit where Amanda shows you around is quite slow as you need to wait for her.- There are a couple of things in the house you can interact with that are not obvious at all. Yes, they are for an optional thing but still.- There's a weird camera feature where the camera kind of "follows" the terrain as you walk over it. You do get used to it but it's quite annoying especially in Lusst'ghaa where the floor is super uneven and the camera just bounces around all the time as you walk over stuff.- That one achievement which requires low sanity. It is very luck-based and if you don't know for sure exactly how it works it can be a pain to get.- The Lust for Life achievement. It's based on two obvious choices, one not obvious choice and one choice you can easily miss because the optional objective to help the person doesn't appear until you talk to another person you might have already talked to in that section and assumed you're done with them.- To get achievements you've missed you need to start from the beginning because there is no save system. It's all auto-saves.- When you're at 0 sanity horizontal (strafe left/strafe right) controls periodically invert. Same for vertical (forward/back) controls. It's extremely annoying. I didn't know how exactly to get the low sanity achievement so I beat most of the game (including the final boss) at 0 sanity and it was pretty aggravating. Also I didn't get the achievement from that.- The enemy encounters are extremely scripted and not scary at all after the first walkthrough.- The enemy AI is easily exploitable.- The fight with Tim. I assumed I am supposed to conserve ammo so I used the knife when he was vulnerable. It took WAAAAAAAAAAAAY too long.

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains spoilers. Also, sorry that it goes on for so long. TL:DR at the bottom.I've got a lot to critique about this game so I'm going to get the things I liked out of the way right off the bat. The game is gorgeous. I can't overstate this part. The textures on some of the outfits are gorgeous, most notably on Amanda's leather jacket. Most of the environments are well done, especially in Bleakmoor, and the sound design is honestly phenomenal. At one point while walking through the empty streets of Bleakmoor I noticed that I could hear the hum of the electrical boxes on the wall which I think is an impressive amount of detail from the audio team.The whole sequence in Bleakmoor before you enter the Hotel is well done. It's well paced and has one somewhat unnerving moment when you enter the upstairs of the bar and see one of the Scarlet Lodge stilt women standing in the road staring at you. As you head downstairs, and back out into the street, she vanishes. This was well done and very enjoyable. The sequence near the end of the game after you've retrieved the mask of Ughro'ecna is good too. Everyone is dead, the mansion that has been so lively and colorful is completely dark and Amanda's baby monster is running around murdering people. The occasional scream from some unknown source helps to really drive home how suddenly alone you are in this once safe bastion. Loved that bit. ----------Ok, now let’s talk about the rest of the game. It seems like the game's notion of horror comes from the same school as Dead Space 2-3 i.e. "Show the player the things that are supposed to be scary as often as possible, fully lit,  and with as much detail as you can." Every chapter of the game that takes place in the Eden theatre feels like a constant stream of bloody boobs, eviscerated corpses, and mutated rape monsters that feel more at home in an exploitation slasher where the gore, nudity, and sexual acts are so over the top that they fail to be horrifying and instead jump the fence into being laughable. A few examples of this: -Being crucified naked to cross that's suspended over a theatre stage while getting sucked off by a middle aged guy. -Having sex with something that was probably human at one time? But now more closely resembles a slug with a few functionless limbs and a gapping butt hole. -Getting jacked off with a very fleshy looking crab claw by what was once Amanda but is now a facially flayed mutant.-Everything in the underground of the theatre (the bodies hanging from the ceiling, the iron maidens, the dismembered bodies strapped to varies torture equipment)All of the characters in the Scarlet lodge have a similar problem with how abusive and sexual they're supposed to be. Rhea especially got on my nerves specifically in the part where I had to "set up the stage" for the next "star". Nothing about her constant moaning and cooing was scary or arousing and more than once I found myself wishing she would just shut up so I could light my damned candles or remove the body parts. Side note. What is up with the Scarlet lodge stilt walkers? They make some sense when you're out on the street since everything to do with the Lodge has a kind of... dark carnival feel to it, but why are they on stilts in the underground. There's definitely no doors or anything down there that would allow them to get in with their stilts on which means that they'd have to take them off, go through, and then mount up again afterwards. Why are stilt walkers in the basement? I imagine a conversation between two stilt walkers as something like that following: "Oh man you know what would be really freaky?""What?""If we went downstairs to wait for the Seeing One.""What, like the rest of the people down there?""No, no, we go down there on our stilts, he'll be all like 'whoa oh no, stilt ladies' "But won't we hit our heads on the low ceilings on every connecting passageway?""Ugh, stop ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ over thinking it Patricia."Anyways, let's talk about the Mansion.I really don’t have a lot to say about the segments of the game that take place in the mansion. The puzzles were generally pretty fun even if they weren’t super difficult, and most of the people were interesting to talk to.Lusst’ghaa feels lacking. Don’t get me wrong, as I said above it looks fine. In a few places I had to stop and admire the landscape because it really was a beautiful alien world and I commend the team on that. But it feels empty. Static. And yes, I understand that that’s because it’s supposed to be stagnant or whatever by nature (yes, I went through and read all of perspective puzzle lore dumps) but we’re shown glimpses of what it could have been. The chambers with the giant upside down thing that we get a buff from? Those were amazing. I absolutely loved those and 100% I feel that they captured some of Beksinski’s style. So why couldn’t we have more of that? Everywhere else just feels so generic. Speaking of generic. Let’s briefly talk about sex. While there is a lot in this game, none of it feels like it belongs in the sex cult that we’re a part of. Much of it, especially in the orgy scenes in the mansion, feels subdued, with all of the participants showing as much sexual creativity as a teenager whose only sexual experience comes from porn. I just… I expect more from a sex cult. This is running longer than I would like it so I’ll try to wrap up by talking about the actual story by first saying that I saw the “Lily is part of the Scarlet Lodge” twist coming from twenty miles away. Outside of that, the story is… OK. I didn’t find it overly compelling, nor did I think it was bad. A lot of individual bits of dialogue were cringy. One thing I will say is that the worldbuilding was interesting enough that I wanted to learn more about the Omniscients, about Lauv’abrarc, Ac'mlale, and Ughro'ecna, and about Lusst’ghaa as a whole, as well as the Cult of Ecstasy. TL:DR, Lust from Beyond has a lot of good ideas that unfortunately flopped in execution. It failed to be scary or erotic and at best had me laughing at the absurdity of some of the situations. It is beautiful, but empty. Scary in the second that something jumps out at you, but then immediately forgettable. I won’t be having nightmares or checking dark corners of my home because of anything in this game.I know this review is negative, but I would like to say that I respect Movie Games Lunarium for having made it.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game about sex .... it's not very sexy.Having played "Lust for Darkness" when it was released a couple years ago, I didn't have super high expectations.  It played like a janky Amnesia clone with some occasional nudity thrown in.  The biggest difference here seems to be that this time you play as two different characters  - A female sex cult leader , and an abusive jackass who beats his girlfriend and embarks on a quest to find therapy (while chiding his abused girlfriend for having made him do it).  Nice. All of this will lead him to encounter a sex cult that worships a dark god who simultaneously seems to encourage people to have sex all the time *and* punishes them for doing it.  If you're confused by this, don't worry, the game seems to be as well.    You are frequently coming across references to the "pleasure realm" , and in a few instances you will actually find your character teleported to a Giger-esque land of vulva walls and ♥♥♥♥ shaped rocks.  I'm not the kinkiest guy in the world, but my concept of a "pleasure realm" sure as heck wouldn't look like an abandoned Alien Hive with the occasional puzzle that involves putting orbs into doors, or sneaking past angry monsters.On the bright side, the gameplay here is vastly improved from "Lust for Darkness" with a rudimentary combat, stealth, and character progression system implemented.  None of it is very meaningful, but I'll applaud the developers for trying.  The pacing is also pretty good, and it avoids relying on jump scares too much.   There are still a couple, but it's more of a slow burn type atmospheric horror than in your face stuff. I'm torn here.  I'm having some fun with this game, and I do think the developers have done a commendable job of improving it since Lust for Darkness launched. On the other hand, I'm bored by their recycling of Giger art,  Lovecraft themes, and their bizarre attitudes toward sex.   They seem to simultaneously want to scare you, shock you, and turn you on.  And it .... just doesn't quite work. I'll give this a thumbs up for the simple reason that they stuck with their vision and made some genuine improvements over the years, which at this point is all you can really ask for in a platform that is drowning in lazy asset flips and meme games.Good luck Movie Games Lunarium,may your next game be a little kinkier.

_childDocuments_.review: It started out very promising, but ended in a disappointment.To start by pointing out the good stuff: the visuals of this game are simply phenomenal and will on many occasions make you stop exploring simply to stand still and look around. It is a beauty whose form shines through its horrific content. If you ever wanted to walk around in a HR Giger oil painting, here's your chance. The only point of critique on the graphics is that animations and facial expressions are are lacking behind contemporary triple-A games, but the stunning art-work in the spooky Gothic mansions, and the phantasmagorical environments of the nightmarish otherworld more than make up for it.The psychological horror bits are, for the most part, well executed. LFB makes very limited use of jump-scares (praise Cthulhu!) but instead skill-fully builds up tension with just the right amount of scary sounds, foreshadowing letters and phone calls, changes in the scenery, or the occasional monster roaming around. The nightmarish explorations also come with a story and plot, and the human element behind the grotesque scenes add to the ever-present sense of dread that this game evokes. Though it's somewhat of a cliché, LFB is just as much concerned with confronting the monster within as it is with slaying the monster out there.And that monster may well turn out to be a sexy, sexy beast. In an absolute Freudian cluster**** of a sex-and-death nightmare, LFB rapidly alternates between (and eventually blends together) the erotic and the grotesque. Pain and pleasure are one and the same in this nihilistic universe, and you will learn all about that as you travel in and out of portals leading you to the hellish otherworld of Lust'ghaa and the real-life places where perverted and murderous cult-members have set up shop.What then, is the deathblow to this otherwise good game?Two major short-comings: the combination of a game-breaking bug and a very rigid saving system. You have no control over when you save your progress: the game automatically saves at check-points and to make matters worse, there's no chapter select or even the option to restart a level.And that's where the aforementioned bug becomes a problem. At about two-thirds into the game there is a section featuring an enemy that is (at that point in the story) unbeatable: your only option when he spots you is to run and hide. Unfortunately, there's a bug that overrides his AI pattern of returning to his standard patrol route after a short chase, and he becomes an unstoppable juggernaut that has an infallible lock-on on your position no matter how much distance you create.And that, sadly, killed the game for me. After many frustrating and futile attempts to circumvent this unintentional challenge, I gave in to the rage-quit and uninstalled the game. Until that point,  was good, but not so good that I would go over six hours of progress just for a chance to be able to continue.

Character expressions are an expectation if you plan on doing any 3D work these days.  Expect to take about ten hours to complete the game. _childDocuments_.review: Intriguing and interesting game completely ruined by a game breaking bug midway through (No Spoilers).  This is my first review ever after joining steam in 2004.As you can see, I've spent quite a bit of time playing this game.  The last few hours I was alt-tabbing, restarting, and troubleshooting trying just about anything to find a solution to where I got stuck.  I'm a guy who likes to smell the roses when playing games, this one no exception.  The main problem is this game only has an autosave feature.  There are no manual saves and you cannot load anything, you can only continue.  I got to a certain point in Chapter 8 and decided to backtrack  looking for a story collectible.  The absolutely crazy thing that happened is that by going backwards through this linear level, the game autosaved at an earlier checkpoint, and when I died I spawned at this earlier checkpoint and the game completely broke.  Gone was my companion who was leading me through the level.  Gone was my ability to interact with the object that would allow my progression.  At this point, I could no longer even backtrack through the level even more to see if I could get a new checkpoint- I was sandwiched between a broken area I couldn't interact with and a corridor that essentially is a death trap.This is so frustrating, more so because I was eminently enjoying the game up until I encountered this game-breaking bug.  I thought about restarting the game, but if something like this could happen because of game design... well then I'd be a fool if I restarted after 10 hours of playing and encountered something similar.  I've posted about this specific issue on the discussion page, and that has minor spoilers.  If the developers can remedy this situation I will change my review to positive, because before encountering this catastrophic bug, I was completely immersed and very much enjoying my experience.A word of caution to anyone attempting to play this game.  In chapter 8, follow a straight line in this linear level and don't even think about taking a step back, or you just may find yourself in the same spot as I am.  Other people have gotten stuck in the same part- don't be one of them because of bad coding/game design.  It's still unbelievable to me that the game will erase your forward progression if you walk back far enough and happen to accidentally die like me.Edit: the game was good enough to go back and play from the beginning, so based on that I need to change my review to positive.  It was quite the experience: Erotic Horror.

The puzzles range from complex to meh and the creativity in getting around Lusst'ghaa is fun, if a bit slow. The item usage could have been better but again they are simple enough to ignore.!! StoryHere is where it goes south. The story isn't good. The ideas are there but the execution is bad. It feels like someone wrote much of the dialog and lore while using a thesaurus to sound smarter. It just feels like they need someone else to write dialog and another to flesh out the world description. It's not that you can't follow what is going on it's just that it feels like a high school theater.! LengthThat's what she said. The game is short, far too short. You spend far too much time in the town and while I understand much of this is to learn the game mechanics, it gets boring and then you get to Lusst'ghaa, annnd it's gone. The most interesting area of the entire game is usually over after a couple puzzles and you don't have any time to experience it unless you fall asleep with the game running like I did. Your S.O. will not appreciate such terrible performance in bed so we should not accept it in game.Speaking of bed we can now discuss the Adult aspect of the game. The horror is both too much and not enough. It's too much shock so after some time it just becomes expected. Like Judge Jean Claude Frollo said in Disney's The Hunchback of Notre-Dame, "Ease up! Wait between lashes. Otherwise, the old sting will dull him to the new". We barely get to see what the creatures can do. If you are especially good at games you only ever really see what the humans do, which has been done before and better. So then onto the naughty bits, out of three possible X's this one gets a single X. For whatever reason this seemed tame compared to what was teased in the demos/prologues. Agony was far and away more adult in that aspect in both execution and ideas.Would I recommend it? Sure. At the asking price you can get at least 2 playthroughs. I want to see what the other choices will do but if you only play once and go through all the lore and puzzles you can probably hit a dollar per hour which isn't bad.Overall I knew the parts I would like and I did. I appreciate it was playable but disappointed in its personality and stamina. In the end I will have some more fun with the game, then we can go on our separate ways.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my first entry into the series and I will certainly be exploring the others in the series for prologues etc.The art, atmosphere and sound design really is first class in this game as is the story from what I have experienced so far.First off, I will say that this review is coming from a massive fan of  HP Lovecraft stories, HR Giger, and also Clive Barker's Hellraiser universe and by extension any of the inspired art or concepts found in each.So it goes without saying that any references I find in the game related to these would score extra points in a sense and pleasingly there are a fair few of them.I would say these are more obvious than merely a few easter eggs, there are certainly inspirations in some areas.However, they are not there just for the sake of being there, simply to give the game a layer of cosmic horror, an ornate masquerade mask to hide it's true nature, or merely to score points with fans of the genre - they do contribute to the experience certainly but even if you are unfamiliar with HR Giger, HP Lovecraft, or Clive Barker I would still say that the overall experience in that sense will be a delight for the senses.This is one game that really does benefit from wearing headphones and playing in a darkened room, the developers mention use of Binaural sound recording as some other game I have also use - but here it is just implemented so beautifully and really helps to draw you in. My first proper visit to the "lust realm" gave me bigger HP Lovecraft vibes than some of the so called "lovecraft" themed games themselves.I can't quite put my finger on it, but something I perceive as seemingly beyond the visuals and sound in these alien environments creates "feeling of being in an alien environment, some kind of interloper to their realm, and so insignificant to their environment"Many games can conjure amazing or other worldy vistas, create immersive sounscapes and evoke emotions of varying levels, but few in my experience can really nail the sensation of "being" short of using VR.Somehow this is one of those precious games that seems to nail a really acute sense of "being" and the "sense of place" -  more so than many other (often excellent) game experiences seem able to.A certain "Je Ne Sais Quoi" makes itself felt and yet what exactly that is, I cannot express.It is something beyond the visuals and sound, maybe lightning in a bottle or it exists in the spaces between the stars....What it is exactly beyond a heightened sense of being in a seemingly more believable game world I can't say, the description does not do my experience justice.But it there, and is in my experience a rare and beautiful thing when artists, musicians etc collaborate to create such experiences in games. This game has that magic.And likewise in the "mortal realms" the people we play as seem to have character and not whilst not strictly speaking empathic (toward video game characters at least lol) ...... I genuinely feel these people and their roles as though I am in their shoes, it all adds to the experience.It is hard to explain but I felt it from the start even though I knew nothing of the woman who's room the game starts in initially...Bar the initial confusion of "where am I etc" when starting any game, it felt like I gradually became them somehow - more so than most other games where you semi identify with your avatar on a basic level.And I guess perhaps partly that, partly the small details and sound etc, it draws you in deeper than some games and so the responses felt to the various themes are possibly that much stronger because there is a connection, as opposed to just watching some video play out passively.I also kind of expected lovecraftian themes going into the game based on the store page descriptions and some of the screen shots.But it was strange - as I started playing - leaving the first portal into that cultist like house, what came to mind was one of the Lovecraft tales that involved swapping minds with an alien race and vice versa, experiencing a strange environment from a perspective of some other alien entity, and yet in the back of your mind there is a small voice saying "this is not right.."It feels like I am the person experiencing the alien mind transfer as I had read and imagined in my minds eye in those stories. Oddly albeit into these game avatars experiences, which by extension, I am so strongly identifying with makes a refreshingly curious experience.From the Lovecraft stories I know of, the game grows organically and kind of feeds off of those expectations from that initial expectation in a way...Kind of as if experiencing the worlds via the characters in the game - as mentioned earlier with Lovecraft stories - in the back of your mind, and there are subtle little things pointing out little prompts and reminders of such stories in a way just reinforces those already well engineered feelings as they develop in the game - if that makes any sense.It is an amazingly well crafted experience in it's own right but if you enjoy the macabre imagination of HP Lovecraft, that will certainly add to your enjoyment.This game surely deserves a tag of "Lovecraftian" but that in itself, while meant as a compliment to the developers does not and should not define it as a whole, and neither should it limit any expectations even if you were to have any.It is at the end of the day it's own unique experience when you look deeper, beyond   any similar and possibly common game play mechanics that may be found in other games.I genuinely mean that in a positive way, at least for the feelings it evokes.The sound, visuals, and yes the story itself but in some ways it really does feel more than the sum of it's parts and in my mind is surely worth playing if you have even the faintest passing interest in any of the elements of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good combination of thriller and horror, and the unique story line makes it very interesting. When I see games that have nudity or sex as a key component, I usually assume the developers or fan-base are weird. This game, however, was so out of pocket that I ended up enjoying it quite a bit.The game is short — I'm 6 hours in and over halfway complete with the game. If you wanted to, you could grind it out over a weekend. There is no combat, you'll be solving puzzles while staying out of sight from cultists or demons. The puzzles aren't particularly hard, but many of them are "timed" and the stress makes them more enjoyable. The story revolves around sex, but it's in a sex cult way and not in an erotic way. The main character has an unhealthy relationship with sexual intimacy and that puts a lot of strain on his spouse. The sexual elements of the game give insight to why the unhealthy relationship exists, and they are very abnormal. In terms of horror, I probably screamed about 15 times but the game was never so overwhelming that I could only play it in short intervals. Outlast 2, for example, I could only sit down and play in ~15 minute intervals before I was drippping in sweat. There is a lot of moments where anticipation is nerve-racking but the characters and environments are more demented than horrifying, and they're actually very interesting to encounter. Overall I would give the game an 8/10. It won't be one of my favorites, but it was a unique experience. If you often get bored of story-rich games, this one might be an exception.

_childDocuments_.review: The thing this game does best:Creating a creepy, disturbing, and yet intriguing atmosphere and presenting some strangely beautiful landscapes and visuals. It's not a simple trashgame, luring you with sex and violence, but sets up a nice stage for exploration.Sometimes the puzzles are interesting, sometimes they are annoying. The AI is really dumb, and some animations seem like they are from the year 2000. But mostly it's okay.What this game does best is using sexual content in a way we are usually used to with violent content, which got me thinking a bit. To me this is an... artsy game. You don't play it for great gameplay (even though it is okay. Not overwhelming, not awesome, but okay), but for an unusual story. You play it to feel uncomfortable, and to discover visually interesting stuff and "enjoy" grotesque perversion.If you like occult stuff, sexual themes in non-sexual context, exploring a story and some shock value... this is for you. It's not a masterpiece, but it's clearly exotic and interesting in many ways.If you have played Agony, which purely relies on shock value... this is what Agony promised to be, but better. It has a story, it's entertaining, and not as repetetetive and annoying as Agony.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite unnerving, very good. It's shockingly polished for a relatively indie horror title, looks spectacular and runs incredibly well. This game takes me back to some of the weirder horror movies of past decades, like Cronenberg's Crash or Naked Lunch, or Hellraiser.If you want a horror experience that'll make you feel very uncomfortable and take you places that you've never been before, while being less frustrating than titles like Alien: Isolation or Resident Evil 7, give this one a try. It does not disappoint, and I'm rooting hard for the developers to continue providing such great experiences. You sure wouldn't find this on any other platform, like console, EGS or the Microsoft Store. Kudos to Steam for allowing a game whose trailer was banned from Youtube and The Hub, ha, and kudos to the devs in the first place for making it.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing my first run of Lust From Beyond, I can say I'm a fan! A fine addition to the colletion! Just around Janurary, I discovered the game and that it would come out soon. I played the Prologue and it hooked me from the start, wanting to play more and here we are!LFB is a fantastic game! I immersed myself fully into the story as we play our protagonist Victor, who at first may seem like a scummy douche but later he learns to adapt his role as the Seeing One. The story is a rollercoaster ride and I enjoyed it. Lusst'ghaa!, the Land of Eternal Ecstacy! A land I would love to visit honestly. For a horror fan, this fills the spot. The violence, the gore, and the themes all blend and make a giant mix of Love Craftian horror orgy! The amount of suspense is immese as making a wrong move can end your life. LFB makes moments that are suppose to be scary actually be scary which is hard to pull off for spook games when you involve a way to fight back.The action aspect of the game was well paired with the flow of the game. Not only can you sneak your way around but you can also fight your way through! You won't always be fighting though, as in certain situations, you must rely on your surviving skills. And yes, you do get a gun. The flow, again, feels right when you first get a gun in hand. Aiming is janky af sure but it works and you soon learn how to use it well and getting headshots is like popping balloons. And what I loved is that you won't always have a gun. I say it's rather OP when all the enemies are melee based as you can carefully take your shots from a distance. Now the true horror aspect of the game is on your way leading up to when you fight your first enemy. The enviroment, the ambient, and the level design all fit the setting of what one would imagine what another world would look like. Making you sneak around corners hoping theres no monster creeping around because your uncertain what may lay ahead.Voice acting was great! I was rather taken away by how great the voice acting is! You can hear they had the passion to make a voice for their game feel natural. And the level design was amazing! I found myself looking at the curious architecture of the level design as you triverse the game in both Lusst' ghaa, and in the normal world. But honestly, there was nothing normal in the normal world.My only disappointment is that you don't get to see the all mighty god Lauv'abrarc in the flesh with your own eyes. Sure you can see statues of him but imagine seeing him! Heres to hoping we see more of this mystical land in future games!Lust from Beyond is a passion project made by passionate people who posses twisted imaginations to create a wonderful series that has not yet been a let down. Depending on your choices you may get one of two endings. The newscast reports were a great touch and something I wish we could see. Sometime soon, I hope to get around to having another run to see the other end and get the rest of the achievements! Both Lust titles have been a special experience to discover myself and go in blindly and to discover this world. I truely hope we see more games from Lust as there can be many more branching stories to be told! I shall await the return of Lusst'ghaa!

Some NSFW content nudity, sexual themes. (I will revisit this in cons in more detail)         Horror survival?         Ocasional nice detail and artistic concepts. Not content, specifically just the artists ability to render it. Cons:           Awful game mechanics. Doors, drawrs, windows, furniture and basically any object that should be a           one button press becomes an awkward hold and drag. So, sometimes you open a door sometimes you           close a door sometimes you half open/close it. One direction isnt universal. ie left to open, right to           close. On pretty much every task that takes a "hit the button at this time" prompt, its never in the           same place, never the same speed, never the same time span. I understand that if it were, it might           become too easy and just boring, but this just becomes frustrating after about the 1,000 time you           have to do it with a limitied amout of "resources" to do it in.            There is No Jump button and no way to defend yourself with your hands.           You are basically running around trying not to die while also trying to figure out where you are            suposed to go and what you are suposed to be doing or looking for.           The "hints" in game are "dont fight bigger enemies just run" Everyone in the game including the ones            who "need you for salvation" try to kill you.           You WILL die about 3 to 30 times till you finaly figure out what you are looking for, how to use it or            where it is, before you can put them all together in one run where you dont die.           There is No storline just ♥♥♥♥ you learn as you go, that never adds up or makes sense why.The nudity and sexual content, and why its under cons.           ALL the nudity is dead bodies in different states of decay, dismemberment.           The only "segg scenes" are basically you trying to do the "hit the button now" gimmic to get you into            the next realm. Which lasts a few seconds till you get it 4 times in a row w/o missing.           While doing this you are surrounded by dismemberd boddies, ppl ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on each other, literally.I thought after a few chapters of relentless hiding and running aimlessly to unlock each random "puzzel" there would be a "reward". Larger enemies will either kill you in one hit or take it all away but one and finish you before you can             run. This can be refilled by finding medkits. Very few and far between. _childDocuments_.review: Lust from Beyond is an incredibly fun and entertaining experience, given you're comfortable with heavy amounts of Nudity and Gore. These elements are a prominent part of the game, and neither of them feel misplaced or unnecessary, as they serve to tell the story that is being told. Essentially, you're walking through a story. You get to collect items, solve puzzles, sneak and hide to avoid detection, and get assaulted a lot. There aren't really many decisions that feel at all important, and as far as I was able to tell, most dialogue options have the same outcome. Combat was fine, though you aren't encouraged to take part in it, and you'll find that sneaking is usually easier. You get to explore most settings openly, and can find bits and pieces of Lore here and there. The most glaring flaw, for me, was the Insanity mechanic, which completely randomises your controls. This at first felt fitting, but it in turns becomes almost impossible to escape enemies, especially in chase sequences. Dying doesn't reset your Insanity, and you don't have enough health to withstand more than 3 enemy hits. Altogether, Lust from Beyond gave me a laugh, and I enjoyed most of its aspects. I'd suggest playing it with friends you can joke around with, as it is definitely a game that'll elicit a response. The story isn't particularly complex, but I still thought it was interesting to learn and I grew to like certain of the characters you meet. Victor, the Protagonist, isn't particularly likeable, though. I definitely recommend the game, although I'll repeat that the game isn't at all shy about nudity, violence and gore. There's a lot of very very graphic stuff, but the game does give you the option to play the game in censored mode. Just something to keep in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: this game was suggested to me on the steam store page. to be honest, i was skeptical at first as i have never played anything like this. time for pros and cons.(possible spoilers ahead)pros:1. the mechanics. running away from enemies and the door you need to go through is closed? have fun trying to open the door for 30 seconds. in my opinion, it really adds to the horror AND the immersion. though, opening drawers on downtime can become tedious. 2. length. i really thought that the game was going to be much shorter than it was. there were many instances where i thought the game was almost finished, and i was very happy when i found the game wasn't actually over yet. my first playthrough took me 10hrs, mind you i was enjoying the scenery and opening every door and drawer i could. 3. collectables and notes. this game has four endings i believe, and those change based on who you save and who you kill. but the game is long, and to be honest playing it four times just to see all of the endings on its own doesn't really make sense. the fact that there are collectables and notes is enough the make me want to replay the game, just so i can find every single one and read every single note. therefore they really add to the replay value. 4. areas. or environments. or whatever. i very much liked the design of the areas in the game. i liked the colour palette, especially in areas like the Scarlet Lodge. i didn't think the game was too dark or too bright. just enough where i sometimes needed my lantern and i sometimes didn't. what i really liked was Lusst'ghaa. the design of the area was very visually appealing and unappealing at the same time. the walls and floors, have round fleshy texture to them, like the human breast. hostile phallic objects. i thought it was really cool. very much grotesque, mutated body horror. (yes, i know this was the point)cons:1. writing/voice acting/story(?). its hard for me to tell if it was the writing or the voice acting that ruined the story for me, or if it was actually the story itself that was lacking. i did like the concept of the story, though there were plot holes. why is Vincent so comfortable with killing? why was Vincent so eager to . those are just a few of the plot holes i noticed. now, the voice acting was mediocre at best. I thought Jonathan's voice acting was really well done, but Vincent seemed like... well he seemed like a bland video game protagonist. Like Ethan Winters from 'Resident Evil 7'. not great, but not terrible. some of the other side characters had decent voice acting. the writing was also mediocre. some of the things Vincent said just didn't make sense. 2. not enough lust. yep. i said it. the game really needed more 'lust'. and to fit with the theme, something more grotesque? i don't know. like i said this is my first time playing something like this. and i still felt like it was, in some instances, a lot tamer than i expected. but there is only so much "lust" you can put into a game before it becomes something else. so i can cope.3. graphics. now this isn't  a con, i thought most of the graphics were decent. but the character models were kind of lacking in my opinion. some clothing and hair clipping through the characters bodies. but hey, it is a video game. what motivated me to put this as a con is those god awful sheets that are on every single bed in The Cult of Ecstasy. it made me feel like i was 11 again, playing pirated 'Nancy Drew' games on a laptop that could barely run Chrome. 4. the loading screens. i have a pretty good pc to my knowledge, and each loading screen took about 2-5 minutes to load the next chapter. it felt like i was waiting forever just to see what crazy thing Vincent would get himself into next. i hope on replay the loading screens aren't as long. the pros outweigh the cons for sure. but the game could use a little work. i did get stuck on a "plant" while i was in Lusst'ghaa, but i reloaded the game and didn't lose as much progress as i thought i was going to.at the time of writing this, i have only played the game once and i plan on replaying it to get all the achievements, collectables, and endings. i will update my review if i feel the need to.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I have only played for just over an hour. This has me starting Chapter 3. I can give some insights about the game here.The Pros:Graphics are pretty good. They definitely do the job. Some are better than others. Only a few things had me cocking my head looking at them like they were strange. For the most part, I liked what they did visually.Movement feels good. I like the way the game 'feels'. Opening doors can be a little wonky but once I got used to it, that was fine. I'm intrigued by the story. I don't feel like it's treading any sort of new ground. Adding sexiness to it doesn't make it new. It's just a new element to a familiar style of game. Still, what's happening is interesting.The Cons:The voice acting. By far, this is the most jarring part of the game. It's pulled me out of the immersion. What would've been a REALLY scary experience is made less so by disjointed acting. Like...I'd volunteer to do the lead lines for free. I'm that convinced I'd do a better job.Some of the writing is that cringe worthy cliche. It's just a little too obvious and in a way that made me groan.Directions aren't entirely clear. Great example, early on you're told to examine the back of the shop. I took that to mean I needed to go outside. Which made sense because there was a purple flash and it seemed to come from out there. But no, it was meant to draw me to another objective. Which would've been fine, but I think the instructions could've been better.All around, the game so far is fun. I'm glad I bought it and the price I got it for was fantastic. I'll definitely finish it and I think that for around the 20 dollar mark, you won't be disappointed.EDIT: Well, I've finished the game. All around, I stand by the thumb's up. It's far more deranged than I anticipated. Some of the stuff that happened really surprised me. My biggest criticism involved the fact that this is not an action game. So the gunfire doesn't always register. It's kind of painful when you're trying to shoot a bad guy and they're point blank and it doesn't register. _childDocuments_.review: How to write a horror and erotic game and fail at both. Summary.Boring, predictable, lacking in substance, poorly acted, structured, modelled, and the highlights appear to have been directly plagiarised from actually good horror games.Lust from Beyond had potential, potential which they squandered at every turn. There is little redeemable about this game. At the start of the game, you play a woman who is in another realm. You leave the realm and have to collect items and people to progress. To do so, you start exploring a Victorian manor with no indication where you are meant to be going. Upon getting to a door or two, I got my first sense the game was going to be problematic, and this was because of the control system. It is, at best, clunky, dragging you out of any chance at immersion. Opening anything is difficult. Like the main character is trying to use their head. To open a door, you have to hold the action key down and move the controller, which shifts your entire camera. This get’s tiring very quickly. What’s worse is that the direction you need to drag the door or cabinet is related to what angle you grab the thing from. For simple things, it’s annoying. For things you don’t know how they are meant to hinge or move, you just have to try everything. This sense of frustration continued as I randomly picked up items to rotate them around in my hand for no reason before returning them to where I picked them up. Yay.Upon meeting some of the people I was meant to talk to, I was surprised to find them bug-eyed and jerky in their motions. I shrugged this off as being deliberate. Later I came to the conclusion it wasn’t.The models in the game are poorly fashioned and disjointed. The love interest moves like a mannequin and has the Innsmouth look. Bugg-eyed as well, like most the other models. Early on, you find yourself in an antique store with a laptop, a mobile phone and a fridge from the 1940s. The lighting felt weird but again, I shrugged that off. Again I was wrong to do so as later on, I found a spot that had an eerie purple light. Nothing was casting the light, no mystical thing, no fungus, no lamp. It appears the makers of the game realised this spot was too dark and so added light. This is indicative of the amount of thought that they put into the construction of the game. More on that later. As you go through the Antique store, you have to find some random items, it feels like this is meant to teach you the clunky mechanics, but it doesn’t. It just annoys you. You have to open a dozen cabinets to find what you need, and by then, you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ off. The whole time the scene is eerily silent. There’s no reason for it, it just is. This isn’t the case for further on in the game, but honestly, it is the highlight of their usage of sound, none. Oh, and don’t forget to pick up the fleshlight. There’s no reason to do so, and it disappears in the next scene, but hey, titillation.  Sex scenes appear at times for no apparent reason other than titillation, but if they think the clunky modelling and porno style dialogue is titillating, they are woefully mistaken. It is crass, blunt and is again the highlight of their eroticism.  After you rape your girlfriend, yes, that happens, there is no clear rationale as to why that happens at the time, but in a later scene, they try and illude to the idea that you have a problem, what that is other than being an arsehole I don’t know.But after that horrible and pointless scene. You end up in the ‘other realm,’ which literally climaxes as you flee down a vagina, again yes, this literally happens.At this point, the game descended from bad to the only genuinely horrifying thing I encountered. You wander around the other realm with literally no objective and no guidance. You find things. What they are, or do you have very little if any indication of. And when you have finished your third hidden object game in half an hour, you get presented with the first horror. And it is laughable. Vaguely female and overtly sexual without being sexy, it makes you cringe. Not only that, the music changes before you even see the creature, becoming tense music which gives away that something unsettling is going on. This continues for as much of the game as I could tolerate.  But the creature is apparently blind as it doesn’t notice you standing in the open and just starts to roam around like a drunkard. If you aren’t sure where you are supposed to go, don’t worry. Go for a run, get killed and restart moments before you died to try a different direction. It is the same mechanic you get in puzzle games where you do the wrong thing, and it tells you you lost, try again. But there is no cost to loosing. So who ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cares.The game presents itself as a horror game with no horror. Another example; a little later, you are in a town where there is an apparent carnival, the character comments on this multiple times until you are sick of hearing it. You also notice erotic posters, and the name of the local inn is not so much suggestive as it is blatantly sexual, not seductive, just crass. As you progress, you suddenly see a topless woman on stilts outside a window and lose one-quarter of your mind. Apparently, tits are too much for your character. They aren’t creepy, dripping in blood or anything. They are just a topless stilts walker.At this same point, your main objective is to find a phone number and call a particular person because your phone has run out of charge. You can see pamphlets about the person, including their number, on the other side of a gate that has no handle, and you have a rare Chinese coin just sitting in the boot (trunk) of your car. Not in a case, just rolling around in the back, so you figure you will somehow pass the gate, get the number and then use a coin which is worth a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fortune in a payphone (cause that works) to call the person in question. So instead of going to the local hotel and asking to use their phone, you wander about for a while, randomly trying things and picking things up until you find a screwdriver, which happens to work on the gate. Why I don’t know, they never tell you, and it makes no sense. But I was progressing, so again, I shrugged it off and continued. I shouldn’t’ have.Finally, I get the pamphlet with the phone number. And moments later, the character I am meant to be playing says “Uuhh, did I say it was too empty in here. I take that back.” What happened? I don’t know. And even if something did happen, who ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ says that? It is indicative of the terrible scriptwriting. What’s worse is that after you phone the number (which your character doesn’t actually dial, just hits a random sequence), you finally talk to the person you spent twenty minutes wandering around to call only to have them tell you to stay in the hotel tonight and meet tomorrow. In the hotel, you decide to phone your girlfriend, so obviously, this was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ option. You could have just done that in the first place. But no, you had to have a ham-fisted puzzle that did not progress the story and did not provide enjoyment just to get them to the same point you could have reached in a one minute video. Then the game goes downhill.You enter a hotel with a suspicious person on the front counter. Go up to your room, with a blatantly big lock on the inside of the door, and in the middle of the night, one of the locals comes banging on the door trying to get in, screaming that they are going to kill you.Your solution, run out the window to try and escape by going to an adjoining room.Now, I don’t know what games you have played, but if you are after a good horror game, try Bethesda’s 2001 Dark Corners of the Earth. And be amazed when you get to the scene that you need to lock the door to your hotel room and flee out the window as a local comes screaming about how they are going to kill you. Lust from beyond is truly a horrific game. It just isn't a horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre H.R. Giger/H.P. Lovecraft horror-sex game, but since there are not too many of those in the market, it is welcomed. It definitely has more going on than 'Lust For Darkness', the voice acting is decent, the characters are compelling and the story is a bit more complex. At the same time, I think the experience is not as good as the first game, for many many reasons:  - The story is more complex yes, but at the same time it is extremely predictable, the start is a lot more interesting than the end, and feels like some kind of lore is missing. - All the bizarre sex scenes and the whole 'alternative reality' is a lot less impactful once you've already played the first game. I don't remember most of the scenarios because I've played 'Lust For Darkness' a couple years ago, but I think some assets might have been reused. - The gameplay itself is boring and the fighting mechanic is unnecessary, it takes more than it gives. Once you realize you can stab everyone to death easily the tense atmosphere of the game is over, then you get the gun and it goes to limbo. The bosses are pointless and unfun. Also, the puzzles are too easy, there's even one puzzle box that a character claims is 'too difficult and no one managed to solve', turns out it is a stupid easy puzzle that a 5 year old kid could solve. A simple walking simulator would be so much better. - The characters are well designed, but the interactions are lackluster. There's a choice to save or kill a few characters but you don't really see how this impacts the game until the very ending which is just a bunch of basic texts telling what happened to them. There's this girl that appears in the last 2 hours of the game, Natalya I think, which could have interesting dialogues, but you barely talk to her.  - It's very bad optimized, I've had a lot of stutters, lag, and a few bugs.Overall, this game is almost only worth it to play for the visuals, there are some cool details, nice graphics and the design of every environment is captivating. The whole sound mixing is also pretty fleshed out, it creates decent immersion although it won't scare you, even with cheap jumpscares. I don't regret buying it on discount, but I'm not sure I recommend full price. It's a very niche genre and contains major flaws, but I don't feel like I've wasted my time.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the bundle where you can buy the original and the M rated/censored version. If you want stuff covered up, the original offers a censored experience anyway. I got this on sale where buying both versions cost less than buying one of the game so, if you have that choice it's up to you. In the game you mainly play as this guy named Victor, who is seeking help for his vapid sexual nightmares that causes him to lash out at his girlfriend one night. He ends up being hunted down by a sexual cult, and yeah things go haywire fast. You kinda get the sense that sex would be the drive of the game, and it is, but at some points it seems the weird atmosphere and plot takes over it, so when sex does happen it becomes...out of place? Idk, in the beginning I was enjoying it all, and I even forgot it was a horror game till it started it's 'Outlast' chase sequences, but in the later half it really tries to be horror, and there are choices that doesn't seem to make sense from both Victor and the rest of the characters. Like when everything is said and done, you can pick whatever you like, but Victor stays at the Cult of Ecstasy for 6 months and your like..."what? why would he do that?" There are two twists that I saw coming, even when not playing the previous game, and by the end the game it angered me, confused me, and I just wanted to be done with it. And sex had become desensitizing, Mainly due to the story and where it went, as well as there not being a chapter select, so I couldn't go back for collectibles or change my choices. Oh, and you only have sex really to go into another dimension (what Victor sees in his nightmares). So sex is really used a tool than anything else and every just treats sex as something normal to do in front of each other, which is cool. If you like a puzzle game with horror elements (Outlast) with sex sprinkled in, I would recommend this game. I will say, you should be warned there are no shortages of kinks in this, and you may see things that will and WILL NOT flatter you. Proceed with caution, and play with your door locked if you don't live alone, lol.
