_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me after playing LFB: Scarlet. While the sexual content was still there, I feel that it wasn't as In-Your-Face as the preview. Which is perfect. Those elements are still there, but spread over the entire story makes them a more pleasant experience. The story is very engaging. I am an old and jaded gamer, plagued by the sense that everything is cliche. Even if I can predict the path a story will take, I am not deterred by a well-told story. That is what you have here. The premise is rough to take at first, but I'm going to say this; At the end, it makes much better sense turning an 'I wanna see boobies' start into a finish with satisfying but unexpected closure. It does not end the way you want, and I feel that leads to a much better story (see Clerks argument about Empire Strikes Back). The puzzle solving is priority over combat, which I love, and the puzzles aren't overcomplicated, being solved by careful observation of your environment. Environs, especially Lhust'gaa, makes the feel of the game. I really felt like I was in an organic environment that was very hard to mesh with my 'normal world' expectation of asthetics.Overall 4 out of 5, and don't make a sequel, since you hit it on this one, and trying to play the same would only be wallowing in the tasteless.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly, from how you expect a game that looks like this to go, from the outside, it’s actually incredibly well done. I’m talking AA to AAA voice acting, an actually really well written story, incredible level design, actual mystery. And not only that, but they clearly understand Lovecraft’s works, and did something incredibly brave, that no one else has yet dared to do, which is tackle his disgust and fear of sex head on. The sanitisation of adult games and the internet in general is a crime. Sex is a part of life, and by god, it can also be used in horror to incredibly great effect. And yet it’s ignored. Every game developer is happy making games where you maim your enemies and burn them alive, but BOOBS?!?! OH GOD A WEENUS?!?! Nope, can’t do that, shut it down. It’s a genuine disservice to those of us that are actually adults, and understand that sex is an inextricable part of being human, and pretending that it doesn’t exist makes all media poorer for it. The last time I felt a game tackled themes like this properly were Outlast and its sequel. The only other current(ish) games brave enough, and willing enough to take on this thorny subject. I’m so glad the makers of Lust did, because this game is fantastic. If I'd know about it in it's Kickstarter days, I would have 1000% paid to have my name immortalised in game beneath a cultist mask, without a doubt.The dialogue, for the kind of subject that can quickly transform into the ridiculous or corny, is actually really well written, like, surprisingly so. In fact, the story was great, I'd highly recommend it. Just don't play it with anyone... Squeamish or underage in the room. That would be a bad plan. This is definitely adults only. The main antagonist is dramatic, theatrical, and just all round great.Very honest, takes its theme and source material seriously and does them justice, which is rare in a game like this. I can actually genuinely recommed this to a friend that enjoys horror, like me, and isn't weird about sex too and really mean the recommendation. I'm very pleasantly surprised. TL;DR If you're an adult that likes horror and isn't a damn prude, you'll love it. Go buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... I believe this is the best horror/puzzle/erotic game I have ever played.I've always found the world of H. R. Giger and H. P. Lovecraft fascinating and finding a game that explores this style, mixed with an erotic theme, it's just amazing!After playing and replaying the entire storyline, I believe I can contribute with some comments here:Pros:- Storyline: Very interesting and with a good job with audio dialogs. It's worth following up.- Boldness: Yes, exactly that. Finding a game with such a theme and that spares no effort to show many spicy moments, combined with an engaging narrative, in itself is a huge advantage.- Immersion: The ambiance throughout the game is very good! You can notice special care in the game, especially with details during the in-game progression, such as the detail when reloading the weapon, something fantastic to notice.- Sound: And about the sound, all the care taken here is also a differential, from the most spicy scenes to details such as the type of floor the protagonist is standing on. The sound work is very good, as is the soundtrack in general.Cons:- The gameplay has some issues, mostly during scenario interactions, like picking objects.- I have a problem with the text stories inside the Book of Secrets, where some of them I'm not able to read the final lines because it's cropped and don't have an scroll option to navigate over it. I believe it's related with my monitor resolution, an ultra-wide in 2560x1080, but it would be very nice if there was a scroll here.- The boss fight in chapter XI appears to be unbalanced. After playing it a few times I couldn't identify a pattern to defeat him, even though the method is basically one. It would be interesting to review this item as I read about several people who simply gave up on continuing the game simply because they couldn't get past this part.- As you make the path to the in-game progression, a few details gives the perception of some kind of rush to finish the game, not in the in-game, but it conveys the feeling that the game suffered with some deadline deploy that affected the same care with details during the initial stages. I could be wrong here, but it is my feeling so I want to expose it here.Suggestions of improvements:- There is no option to access or return to past dialogs;- It could also have an option in the Start Menu to be able to play a specific chapter of the game (this option could be released only after the game is finished);- Allthough the tematic is, in an overall way, very well explored, it could have more sexual elements exposed around the places, mostly in the erotic world created here. Could have more images, forms, walls, things like that, providing a much more immersive experience.- Honestly I was expecting a more richier end, not only about the storyline and with the characters, but some better cinematics also. I loved the intro cinematic of the game, and that said, I was expecting something like that at the end of the game.Achievements :- I had no problems conquering achievements, all are very objective and were achieved with precision, including the hidden ones, which gives a certain incentive during the gameplay. Good job on that.- There could be achievements related to the additional content parts, such as Chambers of Pleasure;- Here we can again comment on the issue of being able to play the chapters individually, without necessarily having to restart the whole game again to reach missing achievements.Overall, the game is fantastic, it has a unique theme that I've never seen in a game style like this, a good storyline that keeps you interested, and for many moments, especially the most intense ones, it reminded me a lot of the movie Eyes Wide Shut from Stanley Kubrick, so congratulations to the entire production and development team of the game. If I had to rate it, it would be 9/10 just because the issues that I mentioned above.Let the light of lauv'abrarc guide you.Yv'h lauv'abrarc. Yv'h Lusst'ghaa!

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS AHEAD! I'm reviewing mostly from a plot standpoint, so they're kind of unavoidable. For me, the lore, backstory, setting, and plot are what really drive this game.FINAL SPOILER WARNING.The  series is a Lovecraftian-esque series. Here, instead of cosmic horror gods, we have cosmic lust gods. There’s an alien dimension called Lusst’ghaa, in which its denizens experience constant, eternal orgasms. How this is possible is beyond me – they must operate on completely different neurobiology, since the human brain is wired to tamp down pleasure after extended exposure to it. And recent studies have shown that…Uhh…where was I? Ah yes. In the first game, , you begin play as Amanda Moon, who has just been kidnapped and thrown into the base for a sex cult devoted to Lusst’ghaa. This cult, the Cult of Ecstasy, wants to travel to Lusst’ghaa to experience that eternal, constant orgasm. The leader of the Cult begins the game by raping Amanda.Right off the bat this is incredibly disturbing. One might think, as I did, “what the hell is with starting a game like that or even having this in your game?” One might also think, as I did, “how many games have the daring to start a game like that or touch this sort of topic?” The rest of  takes place a year afterward. Amanda’s still missing and her husband, Jonathan, receives a letter from her telling him where she is – the base of the Cult of Ecstasy – and asking him to go save her. You play as Jonathan, infiltrate the base, and free Amanda. But a year later, she reveals that her year-long stay at the Cult of Ecstasy has indoctrinated her in the ways of the Cult – she’s now hyper-sexualized and wants to go to Lusst’ghaa. Okay, well that’s also unsettling. is the sequel to . Amanda is now the leader of the Cult of Ecstasy. Between the first and second games, Amanda ends up understanding the alien dimension better than anyone else does. Long story short: a long time ago, Lusst’ghaa was a normal world with normal people. The king decided that the best thing for his people was to transform into beings that had no consciousness and only experienced lust and orgasm. From here he became known as the Lustful God. Some higher-up gods didn’t like that, so they imprisoned him in Lusst’ghaa. The Lustful God responded by psychically projecting “HELP ME” messages across the dimensions. In particular, some people on Earth heard the call, but they didn’t understand it – all they knew was they were getting visions of some alien, incomprehensible world. These people are the Seeing. As you can probably guess, Amanda is a Seeing.In , you play as a guy named Victor, who is also a Seeing. He struggles with his visions and the game follows him as he learns about Lusst’ghaa. I’ll skip a lot of details, but Victor is the only one who can actually open the Lustful God’s prison, so Amanda tries to manipulate him into doing so. Freeing the Lustful God would then turn Earth into another land of eternal ecstasy, with all humans becoming mindless and horny and constantly orgasming.Okay. Let’s stop here for a bit. The first thing that really horrifies me is Amanda’s plot. This poor woman had Seeing visions ever since she was born, and Amanda is the most powerful Seeing in the world, so her visions are especially intense. This is why she was kidnapped and brought into the Cult in the first place. She didn’t deserve this. She didn’t ask for this.And in the end, she became just like her abductors. The guy who raped her and forcefully aborted her child and made her give birth to  child. That doesn’t sit well with me . Because this part of her story arc isn’t some result of fiction. This sort of thing could happen in reality. And the idea horrifies me.If Amanda frees the Lustful God, she’s destroying all of humanity. Our consciousness. Our ability to think. Our ability to feel. Our accomplishments. Our potential. All of that, gone, washed away in lust. And if she doesn’t? The Lustful God will just continue projecting his SOS message, ensuring some other Seeing in the future inherits Amanda’s fate.So this entire plot. This entire, , is meaningless. The Lustful God is apathetically using humans to get out of jail. And he will eventually succeed. What we see – broken marriages and relationships, ruined lives, death, violation – they’re nothing in the grand scheme of what this guy wants and does. It's…well, it’s very Lovecraftian. Lovecraftian stories rarely have happy endings. They’re usually like, “this guy learns of eldritch horrors and goes insane, the end.” They revolve around the idea that at the cosmic scale, humanity means nothing. But I just…I feel really, really sorry for Amanda.That said…the developers did something . Really, how many games/developers make a game with this sort of setting? A setting steeped in eroticism? Where I am, America, is terrified of sex. You can make a game here with violent gore and it’ll get a softer rating compared to if your game has sexual content. Oh, and if somehow my description sounds like the game’s just a porn simulator, it’s not, oh, not by a long shot…which drives home the point that this game is so unique – a game whose central theme involves lust, but  just a porno in game form. And though I wrote at length about how disturbing the plot was to me, . The game’s erotic . It’s purposefully disturbing on multiple levels. So as much as I wanted to cry and throw up…the game did exactly what it set out to do.I give this game and its indie developer team an A for bold, unflinching courage; for visceral, disturbing horror; and for true, creative uniqueness. Congratulations on release, MG Lunarium.

_childDocuments_.review: (Also known as In the Hall of the Vagina God and Debbie Does Devils.)(Joke.)(Just.)More pervy madness from the fine, family-friendly folk who gave us Lust for Darkness.Not only does this game teach children that people have naked body parts, which they sometimes use to interact with one another...it also preaches that mind-altering pills are a viable alternative to living a pure, pious life without psychological trauma. And that having an orgasm can quite  transport a person to another dimension...Beyond that...Oh yeah: this is a HORROR game, too! Actually, the (H.R.) Giger meets (H.P.) Lovecraft vibes are stronger than ever this time (there's even a "Sanity" meter, as is tradition with games riffing off the latter). Did I mention this is a sequel to 2018's madcap Lust for Darkness? And, I'm pleased to say, a marginally superior one. The potential showed there is improved upon , if not by an astronomical amount (the graphics have certainly improved; not least of all the sequences in the land of "Lusst'ghaa", which truly do feel like you're visiting an alien world this time).Don't get me wrong: the story's still pretty silly and the dialogue even sillier...but it all makes a delirious kind of "sense", if you're willing to buy into the aesthetic and atmosphere (though it  benefit from a thorough rewrite by Clive Barker, who's another clear influence on proceedings)! There's a lot of creepy stuff here - some "bits" that border on the positively sublime, in fact - filtered through a constant "lens" of perversion and degradation. Though if you're prudish, there  the option to play a "censored" mode (quite why you'd buy this then bother to do so, I have no idea...but whatever floats your boat)!There's puzzles as well as danger - there's even, erm, sex "mini-games" (honestly, you'll have to find out for yourself!) - but I won't argue that this is one of the very best "stealth-horror" games on the market (expect awkwardness, with a wee bit of clumsy, absurdly bullet-sponge-y combat thrown in for good measure). But for a combination of a very offbeat story and mostly satisfying gameplay elements...this is an easy recommend. Those who love their horror games, but find them all a bit "same-ish", might especially appreciate the effort to create something with a more..."unique" identity.In short: anyone who enjoyed Lust for Darkness is destined to enjoy what's here; and even those who  played it could just as easily skip to this game, as it's a faintly more "definitive" (and slightly easier) iteration of some very similar ideas (and not so much a direct "sequel", with the same protagonist, as a different tale told in the same universe).Verdict: 9/10.(PS You know the stealth-horror cliché of hiding in lockers or closets? This time, it's IRON MAIDENS. And no, I don't mean the classic New Wave of British Heavy Metal band: I mean those Ancient Egyptian contraptions full of nasty . The sense of humour on these devs, I tell ya...or is it just a complete dismissal of the laws of physics?! Hmmm...some days, ya gotta wonder...)(PPS If you enjoyed this review, feel free to check out my two Curator pages: Cheers!)

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This game features the choice of a Censored and Uncensored mode upon startup: the former censoring through pixelation.Lust from Beyond is an impressive and memorable cosmic horror experience that will leave a lasting impression long after the game is completed.  In contrast to its two predecessors, Lust for Darkness and Lust from Beyond: Scarlet, this title is, without a doubt, one of the best horror games ever made, with a captivating narrative, immersive atmosphere, and beautiful artistic direction as its crowning achievements.  This game went well beyond my expectations after playing Scarlet, and I look forward to future projects from these passionate and talented developers.  Even at full price, the game is well worth it thanks to its high quality and 12 hour playthrough time.You play as Victor Holloway, an antiquarian in the modern day who suffers from a troubled relationship, a stagnant life, and visions of an alternate dimension which overwhelm him when he’s aroused (obviously).  After a traumatic incident with his girlfriend Lily, Victor promises to fix his relationship by visiting a certain Dr. Austerlitz at her suggestion, and travels to a remote town named Bleakmoor to meet him.  In order to avoid spoilers, I won't delve any further into the plot.The plot is the game’s greatest strength, and is the main reason why it will remain a memorable experience for anyone who’s played it.  Kudos to the writers, because they've made a more compelling story than the writers of SOMA.  Whether it’s speaking with the characters (though more control over dialogue responses would have been nice), making choices, discovering clues and secrets, or taking it a step further, the characters with whom you interact are all interesting and well-written (with the exception of a few cheesy lines), and will have you saying “just one more chapter”.  This absolutely could have been a book and sold well.The choices you make in the game will influence its ending, so choose wisely.If there’s one thing we’ve learned about cosmic horror games, it’s that most of them are really just “walking simulators” with puzzles and horror elements: that is, they focus more on immersion and your imagination than actual gameplay.  Not so with Lust from Beyond.  While you’ll still experience plenty of atmospheric treks, this game plays more like a proper horror game, while still clinging on to enticing (and gritty) puzzles and an interactive environment.Like any Lovecraftian game, you will have to keep an eye on your character’s mental trauma lest he become overwhelmed.  Thankfully there are plenty of sedatives around to ensure Victor’s sanity, and as the game progresses, he becomes increasingly desensitized to disturbing scenes.  Health can be preserved by avoiding conflict with enemies, or eliminating them as quickly as possible, preferably when their guard is down.  The combat is rather simple and janky, but it mostly occurs toward the game’s late stage.  As far as the stealth goes, enemies will notice your lamp or become alert if you step on noisy objects such as broken glass, or close a door or drawer too quickly.  You’re also unlikely to get them off your back once they notice you, unless you’re quick with your wits.  The game has plenty of puzzles whose completion allows the player to progress, and they are both rewarding and enticing.  A new feature called “Essence” has been added, which allows the use of magic in Lusst’ghaa to repair bridges or light beacons.  Unfortunately, the magic cannot be utilized in combat.  Aside from the puzzles, you can collect certain figurines which pertain to the various stages in the game, and using them all, you can unlock upgrades to your gear, such as an improved knife.My main complaint is that the game saves manually through checkpoints, and sometimes these are few and far between, meaning you will find yourself repeating somewhat long sequences due to death or having to quit the game.  Thankfully the checkpoints are more common since Scarlet.Another one of the game’s strengths is its art direction.  Look at any of the screenshots of the mansion, Bloodhouse, or Lusst’ghaa itself, and you will see that the artists ensured that the game would remain atmospheric and immersive while also alien and dreadful.  Lusst’ghaa, especially, is splendidly portrayed through its environments and aliens, having been heavily inspired by Giger and Beksinski.  For anyone who has long awaited the game Scorn, I think it’s safe to say they found something even better in Lust from Beyond.It’s not all praise in the visual department, however.  While the graphical fidelity of the game is good for an indie game of its time, it suffers from some issues with lighting from a distance, as well as a failure to properly display anti-aliasing (though this was slightly remedied with one of their recent updates, though not entirely).  The facial animations in the game are clunky and static, but I suppose not too much should be expected in that department.  While some animations are good, such as the crawl of the Enthralled or the patrol of the Stilt Cultist, others, like the reloading of the revolver, the use of the knife, or death animations, could use some more work.  Overall, the game is rather janky, but not enough to be offputting.  The music in the game isn’t really memorable, but functions well as background noise to the game’s atmosphere, as it should.  There’s a good reason for this, too: the sounds you hear around you matter, just like in the game SOMA.  It’s not just that the footsteps and coughing of hostiles are crucial cues allowing for you to track patrol movements, since they can spot you rather well, but the player must also keep in mind the noise they create.  The ambient noises in Lusst’ghaa may drown out the music, but they help add to the deep atmosphere and remind you that you are walking through a living world (and you’ll be reminded with every slippery footstep you make).  The combat sounds, such as thudding, cutting, and shooting, are subpar, but combat doesn’t feature enough for this to matter that much.The voice acting is yet another strength of this game, though it isn’t without its shortcomings.  Each of the voice actors does a splendid job with their characters, especially Dr. Austerlitz, Amanda, Mabel, the twins, and Jonathan; however, there are several instances where the dialogue feels robotic or out of place, especially with Victor.  That’s not to say that Victor’s voice actor did a poor job, because he did splendidly, but sometimes the execution of the dialogue in the game and abrupt change of tone is unconvincing.  The controls have been improved since Scarlet, and I’m glad the issue of having different buttons for a flashlight and lamp has been fixed; also, I could finally bind certain commands to the extra buttons on my mouse.  For the most part, you will be using your main mouse button to interact with the environment, and sometimes this can be a hassle with doors where they will open or close in the opposite direction you are pulling or pushing.  I like that they added the ability to skip quick-time events, because it can be rather awkward and offputting “gameplay” to repeatedly click during a sex scene.  Other than this, it’s all smooth in this department.Running an Intel Core i7 10th Gen and NVIDIA RTX2070 Super, the game ran smoothly for me at max settings.  The only issue I encountered was with long loading times for each chapter, and upon dying, the player must again go through the loading screen to try again.  My computer remained relatively cool except in foggier environments like Bleakmoor.I experienced no bugs, glitches, freezes, or crashes.  The game is stable.

_childDocuments_.review: An updated version of "Lust for Darkness". And if anyone doesnt know what that is, here's the breakdown.This is a horror adventure game with a erotic Lovecraftian leaning.For off, its an indie game. Just so you understand that there are limitations to this game based on the subject matter, so dont compare it to bigger budget titles.Graphics look quite nice, it tries to use lighting effects to the maximum potential. Runs on the Unity engine.Voice acting is pretty good. Sound effects in general were quite well done. I played with headphones and I had to take them off several times to make sure the sound was in game and not outside, was that believable. Gameplay wise its an improvement over the previous game. You now have health and sanity indicators, as well as an inventory. You also get to use weapons, a knife and a pistol.Big note, this games' main premise is the story, so the gameplay elements are exclusively to enhance it. So dont expect too much from them. Particularly the combat. While I am glad that its there, some parts of it were ... tedious. Keep in mind that the previous game was more a walking simulator by design. There are also some stealth segments, chases and puzzle solving. Most of the game you will be talking to other characters or reading up some material to better understand the story.Now, how can I say this properly. The puzzles in the free demo versions ("Prologue" and "Scarlet") were better than in the main game. I guess I can consider them all a cumulative product, but still, something to note.You can also inspect some items to check them out. Its been toned down from "Lust for Darkness", where you could pick up most items, which was excessive from my point of view. Quite a few items reference the previous game.The story is pretty good. You dont need to know the characters from previous games, "Lust for Darkness" or the two free ones, but it helps a lot to understand things and be invested. There are notes scattered around in the game that help fill in some of the blanks, but you might not find them all. I missed some things, even though I was trying to be thorough. There were also some characters that I think were underutilized.In the game you can also make certain decisions that will effect the story ending.What I didnt like though, is the weaker feeling of "fear". Dont get me wrong, some segments scared me quite well and some places were pretty disturbing. But compared to its predecessor, this game had a much greater feeling of "Im in control of the situation" than the previous one. And it takes away from the experience.While I do like addition of some mechanics, their implementation is somewhat questionable. Makes me wonder if the game were not better off without them.While the game is longer than its predecessor, I wonder if that really works towards its advantage or not.Another gripe that I have here, is that you cant select chapters. So if I want to investigate a place a new to find information that I missed, I cant.Despite some shortcomings, I enjoyed this game and would recommend it to all who enjoy horror and a good story. You will get a good 7-8 hours worth of entertainment and for the offered price.6/10P.S.Oh, I almost forgot! The sex. I cant say there is a lot of it, to be honest. Either around you or you participating in. And I know that there doesnt have to be, since this is a horror game where sex is just the theme. But I dont feel its impact that much. There are sex scenes, but somehow they dont really pack a punch. There seems to be more emphasis on grotesqueness than perversions. And even some of the grotesqueness seems to have been slimed down compared to the first game. Im pretty sure more could have been done with it. Nevertheless, my general verdict still stands.

_childDocuments_.review: My review is purely based on a game design perspective and not the story since I did not finish the story. Hell, I never got the chance to finish given how horribly designed this game is. Let's start with the pure technical aspect: Optimisation. To say this game is poorly optimised is a gross understatement. Terrible performance on my machine. When high demanding games like games like KSP2 and Horizon:ZD can play at 60fps at 2k, this game gives horrible stutters and lags even on 1080p. Then there's the issue of resource management. Do you really have to unload every asset and resources everytime the player dies and reload it again? Is that actually that bad? I am no computer engineer and even I can think of better ways to handle that. Maybe I am wrong about this and they must be doing something else. But all I know is that I must've spent more time on loading screens than actual cutscenes in this game.The gameplay issues: No manual savepoint. It reminds me of the old DarkSouls games where you travel for solid three minutes only to die to a boss and then travel again for another three minutes because that is where the save point was. Seriously. This game was released in 2021. Not 2012. How ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ difficult is it to let the player save? That brings me to the implementation of the AI.The unkillable enemy: Movie Games tried to pull off the Alien from Alien:Isolation where it can home in on your location by some path and localisation algorithms. Emphasis on the word "tried". Because that big unkillable brute enemies do not have any kind of approximation of any kind. They just home in one your ass like a sidewinder. All these issues compiled is what makes me quit this game. To be fair, the story was actually getting interesting. But alas, I can never know who it goes since The horrible implementations block me from enjoying it. I draw the line when a game is more frustrating than enjoying. And this one definitely is. Unless the developer fixed these underlying issues, I would strongly not recommend this game. Or you have more patience than I do, or if you have no life, please go ahead and buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is just not a good game at all. It starts off well enough with good graphics and a premise that sounds good; You're playing as Victor, an antiquarian and you have a certain problem when it comes to your sexual urges, a problem that is hurting your relationship and results in him seeking help from a therapist who lives in a creepy town in the middle of nowhere. You arrive and things only get weirder from there... classic, right?Unfortunately the game starts to fall apart after that. The actual game-play, which mostly consists of hide-and seek mechanics is very lackluster and buggy. I can't count the number of times that enemies could see me when they really shouldn't have been able to or got stuck on some piece of the map, giving me total freedom. The player character also can get stuck quite easily in places by opening doors which "slide you" into walls, resulting in many frustrating restarts.Speaking of restarts, the game really drops the ball here as certain segments will likely result in a lot of these (the Bloodhouse f.ex) and for some reason, despite having a good machine to run the game, loading times are quite horrible. For a game that is clearly focusing on the narrative and immersion, this is quite horrible.As for the main attraction of the game, the story, I can't say I'm impressed at all. There's definitely an entire world in here, a Cosmology involving the supernatural world of Lusst'ghaa which could be used as a stage for interesting tales but it all becomes so uninteresting and so quickly. This may be especially true as almost all the voice cast of the game sounds like they're half asleep or bored by the world in which they live. There is an upgrade system in the game that allows the player to get more health, sanity or magic power to deal with the world around them but this system feels wholly unnecessary. Having a low sanity does next to nothing apart from the Amnesia-style wobbles and jitters and magic power (essence) is really only used for one function in the game (building bridges). This could have been expanded with more abilities but this game doesn't have time for that. That leaves health as the only real upgrade worth getting which might save you in a pinch. Oh wait, there was also a stealth option upgrade at some point but it felt like it never came into play.Near the end of the game, it decides to give you infinite ammo and a revolver as if to compensate for its lack of game design. This was the last immersion-breaking straw for me and I completely lost interest in what was going on.This is a narrative experience that's pretending to be a survival horror game. It however accomplishes neither very well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is made to invoke a multitude of emotions and is more WAY more than a horror sex simulator. I suppose if you are an avid horror fan a lot of this content wont surprise you all that much, the sex scenes are done well, and is what you would expect from 2 lust god worshiping sex cults although if you play, you will find one of them is WAY preferable than the other. On that note the story overall is pretty interesting and depending on who you are even a bit silly. The environmental graphics are top notch and the music is good as well, creating a creepy and wonderfully detailed atmosphere. I was not a huge fan of the ending or final boss, and to me at least, it is not scary in the sense that your doom is impending, like outlast or amnesia, more of a jump scare game once the shock of the environment and scenes wear off. Enemies are very intimidating at first but they're patterns are easy to recognize and combat frankly sucks a bit due to bad gun play, HOWEVER this is not a combat focused game and the puzzles are really detailed and interesting but not terribly challenging. It was not what i expected in a good way and bad way.  Overall it is really cool and atmospheric and hopefully they will do another to continue the world of lust'ghaa and cults, as well as fix some of the scare and combat issues. This is def not for everybody and has its flaws to be sure, the sky is the limit on how far it can go with sequels, will recommend especially if its on sale. It is worth it for the atmosphere, environment graphics, interesting story, and puzzles, were it possible i would give this a 3 out of 5 as it is more disturbing than scary, with uninspired combat, yet very creative and atmospheric.

_childDocuments_.review: There are two aspects that I felt really made this game stand out.1. The story was very interesting.  You don't have to play the first game to enjoy it, but doing so does give you background about two of the important characters in the story. I recommend picking up and playing Lust for Darkness if you want to immerse yourself in the story.There were plenty of plot twists and turns.  I didn't know who to trust in this game.  Each chapter drew me in deeper.  I wanted to know how it was going to end.  I lost track of time playing this game simply because the the narrative was so captivating.2. The environments that were created for this game fit the narrative well.  It was great to explore the creepy areas of this game to look for secrets and progress the story.  The old mansion really does feel like an old mansion.  The Scarlet Lodge really does feel like a brutal meat locker.  The alien areas really do feel like a creepy alien planet.  They always kept me on my toes.  I recommend this game.  Generally, I didn't feel it was too scary.  It was mostly suspenseful...like when you turn around and find Big Tim right behind you in one part of the game.  The environments are eerie and make for great exploration.  The story and environments complement each other well.  For the best experience, complete Lust for Darkness first and do not read a guide.  Enjoy exploring all of the areas and the plot twists at your own pace!

_childDocuments_.review: It always cracks me up that games can show you murdering thousands of people and that's fine, but if you show anything sexual, it's ADULTS ONLY.  If no one on earth was shot in the head for the rest of time, humanity would continue, however if you remove sex, no one can survive...but headshots are fine.With Lovecraft and Clive Barker being two of my favorite authors, I was honor-bound to buy this game, and I was not disappointed.  With this game featuring both incomprehensible beings from other space-times, as well as horror/fantasy straight out of a Barker book, I was pleased.Next, lets discuss the sex of the game.  While sex does play a large role in the game, I never really found myself rolling my eyes at it.  Really, with the exception of one scene, some slight camera angle changes could have made this game pretty tame and suitable for most audiences.  I feel with sexuality being such a major role in life, it's a disservice to never bring it into horror except as some clunky plot device to show that a bad guy is bad.The gameplay is broken out into 3 parts: walking sim with some hidden stuff (my favorite parts), somewhat clunky stealth, and light shooting.  The walking sim parts were great, well designed locations with lots of secrets and hidden items to find.  You're not in any danger, but the places you're in are always give you a sense of disquiet.  The stealth was ok and thankful not too frequent.  You crouch to stay out of invisible cones of vision and run for a minute if you're seen.  Those sections tend to stink because you can't really enjoy any of the world.  The shooting sections were great as you tended to have infinite bullets.  I'd much rather move super slow and kill the bad guys THEN cruise around taking in the scenery.The lore in the game was surprisingly well developed, if not executed perfectly.  The monsters didn't really strike me as creatures that would lurk in a world of infinite pleasure.  The story was ok, if a bit too long.  Lots of characters, most of which have their own personalities which was surprising.All and all, 8.5/10.  If you're into Barker, you'll probably enjoy this.

name: Struggling
detailed_description: Struggling is a physics-based co-op platformer with a twisted spin on teamwork. Control the arms of a squishy abomination and guide it through a deranged world where anything goes. Outrun ravenous rats, joyride a dirt bike, and vault over pools of unmentionable waste. One thing’s certain: you will struggle. Two hideous heads are better than one Inventive co-op will test the firmest of friendships. Grab a partner and work together by controlling one arm each. When even walking takes a combined effort, communication is key to keeping your cool. Crawl, swing, clamber, and slide to victory Manipulate each arm independently and latch onto literally anything you see, from suspicious levers to dangling eyeballs. Triumph over physics-based challenges, or get your arms ripped off in the process (don’t worry, they grow back).

_childDocuments_.review: This surprisingly lengthy Heave-Ho-like co-op adventure had my friend and I in stitches. It takes a bit of time to build up level design-wise, and if you've played Heave-Ho it might take a bit of adjusting to get used to the difference in physics, but once you and the game get into the groove it's a blast, and there's a lot of creativity in the levels to enjoy along the way. That said, a lot of the fun definitely comes from trying to coordinate between each other so I'd hesitate to recommend it for single player. Oh, and I still haven't mentioned the art style somehow; It delivers on being just incredibly weird throughout which vibes really well with the gameplay. The art definitely shines most in the guts themed areas. We haven't gotten all the way through yet, and I'm really looking forward to playing more.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A masterpiece, everyone should have this game in their library, and play it with a good friend when the timing's right. I played 2 times with different friends via Steam Remote Play, each time starting from the beginning and playing for about 30 minutes. Yesterday, another friend came to my place and I only wanted to show him this game... we ended up playing all night! We had a blast, seriously I don't remember the last time I had that much fun playing a game. I have many co-op games, I like couch gaming with friends, and usually we can play up to 10 different games in a gaming session.  Most of these games can get repetitive and, as much fun as they are, we rarely stick to only one game in an evening. Struggling managed to do that and here's why: -it's tough, but not too much, and it feels REALLY rewarding when you get to the next checkpoint-every level is unique, there are plenty of REALLY great ideas and the game keeps surprising you with funny moments-the sounds! Even after 3 or 4 hours, we kept mashing the B button because those sounds are REALLY funny-sometimes your arm can get stuck, or simply stop functioning properly, but you can always cut it and grow a new one! To me, this game is a 10/10. It's a work of art. Thanks Chasing Rats Games.

_childDocuments_.review: People call this a Getting Over It clone but it's really not that much like it, it's way more like Heave Ho. It's a similar concept to Heave Ho with a story. It's a good/bad mixture as a result. I played this almost exclusively in co-op with a friend so I'm not sure how it really is as a single player game.Comparing this to Heave Ho, I thought Heave Ho had better controls. There were a good amount of times where arms would get twisted. Sometimes you're just taking time trying to get one arm untwisted or just suiciding because you can't get your arms into good position. I don't remember that happening in Heave Ho. It's a game about physics and frustrating controls to make things difficult. It can obviously be frustrating at times by game design but I thought the fun parts made up for it .It had a pretty funny/gross story. The boss battles were really fun and certain sections like riding a dirt bike to outrun a crashing plane was good fun. It just felt a bit long for the kind of game it is. It took me and my friend about 8 hours to beat it and at times we were just worn out of it. Even with it feeling like it overstays its welcome at times, it was still an enjoyable experience with some good humor in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Struggling is a great game but I can see how the art can turn people away. Personally though, I thought it was funny and unique and only made the game more interesting. The gameplay is mostly revolved around your partner and you fumbling to get to the next area. You each control an arm on this abomination and have to use it to pull/climb/jump places. There's a little bit of puzzle aspect in it but not really. We got stumped a few times, some being we couldn't figure out what to do, while others were us having difficulty with the jump(s). It's pretty difficult, especially if you guys don't have good coordination. If you and your partner aren't on the same page I can see how the game can be frustrating. The game keeps it interesting by introducing new mechanics such as detachable arms and time slow abilities. The new areas you reach also kept me intrigued as I really didn't know what they were going throw in our face next. Some notable parts that caught me off guard were  The boss levels were really fun and unique. Either Agamemnus or Amadeus are my favorite. Art and music were great. Music during boss fights was even better. I don't remember there being much story in the game. Only bugs we encountered was the occasional arm stuck in wall/floor.Scattered around the levels are secret hats you both can wear. We didn't get all of them but there is a decent amount to collect. Biggest negatives of this game is that it's only local co-op and has no online feature. Had to Parsec to play. Overall, it's a really amazing game. Pretty difficult so if you can't with these kind of games then maybe wait for a sale. Kinda short, only took us about 6-7 hours to beat it. Still worth full price though.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept seems  very fun and i'm sure the game would be a wonderful time if it wasn't for the unbelievable laziness in implementing any ability to play this game online. As many will know you have two main trains of thought for most games, dedicated servers provided for the players by the devs or local hosting. Somehow the developers of this game just didn't bother with either and opted to have the host player use steam streaming to stream the game over steams (awful) service rather than anything native to the game. This caused huge amounts of lag between myself and my partner making the game all but unplayable because we couldn't coordinate. Hell even without the lag the steam remote play online option took us about 25 minutes to get to connect properly and recognise our controllers.Was totally unplayable because of this glaring oversight. I understand aiming for the game to be couch co-op but this released in 2020. There's no excuse for a co-op experience that claims to be playable online with friends to be this lazily done in this day and age, particularly in a year with a pandemic that means i simply can't play the game in the same room as my friend.Feel like i absolutely wasted my money on getting this and its a crying shame because it looked like it would have been so much fun.For the record my upload speed averages about 30mbps, so not a broadband speed issue, it's insane that steam streaming service/this game somehow lagged this hard and completely shut down my twitch stream to the point my viewers said it was basically a slideshow. My friend said the experience on his end was that the game looked like he was watching a video in 360p.(edit - forgot to mention the above issue was not in any way resolved by closing my stream. That got closed first....then the game 30 minutes later when we still couldn't play it)

_childDocuments_.review: After an hour played for my coverage of the Humble Choice December 2020:Struggling.  So many potential jokes, but truthfully, I don’t like this game.  The concept of a physic basic platformer where you control both hands has been done before.  In fact, we got Heave Ho this year and that was too short but had great controls.  Struggling does not have great controls, nor a good feeling for the game’s physics when you play.  I constantly fought against the control scheme and found my character was annoying to control.  The movements required were usually not too bad though some timed sections really increased my dislike of the game. The real killer, though, is this game looks hideous, and I know this is an art style someone will enjoy but for me, I disliked the look, disliked the control, disliked the screams the character makes, disliked the level design, I’m just not a fan of this one.  Thirty minutes in I gave up.  I could play for an hour but it would only make me hate this game with a white-hot passion, but currently, I just don’t like it, even though I’m sure some people might.  I even went back and played Heave Ho and realized how much I enjoyed that control scheme. Check out this game if you like the look of this.  This is a very stylistic game.  I’ve heard some people think it’s better in co-op, others think it’s easier in single-player, so maybe if you have someone you want to play with, but personally I wouldn’t recommend this to anyone.If you want to see more from me or my coverage of the Humble Choice:

_childDocuments_.review: The final boss that people have been calling buggy and rage inducing is being reworked sometime in the next week to make it much "less random and less punishing" [EDIT: It is fixed now]. You can chat with the devs and other players on the Struggling discord, and they're really responsive to player criticism.Literally every part of the game apart from that boss is incredible: the gameplay, the visuals, the music, the hats, the other bosses, everything. You can play singleplayer or local multiplayer (remote multiplayer with Parsec), and the controls are weirdly intuitive. It takes about 6-8 hours to complete for the first time, but there are so many great bossfights and paradigm shifts that you'll wanna play again. The game is very replayable since are about 50 hats to collect in secret areas, and each challenge has many ways to be beaten.I bought this day a few hours after release, and beat it twice within the first two days. It's an amazing game. It doesn't take itself seriously at all, and surprises you every step of the way. A great use of $15.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit that I only made it halfway through this game, but I really didn't like this game.I can tell that a lot of love was put into this game and theoretically I think it's a good game. It's got a polished art style and sound track and a lot of the concepts are good. However, in practice I found the gameplay to be really lacking a lot of the time.I played through remote play together which was probably me and my friend's first mistake, but honestly I'm not really a big fan of local CO-OP only games, especially during a time where people are just not hanging out in person (dating my review, i know i know). The latency we could deal with more or less, though.My biggest issue with this game is that I felt that the physics was never consistent. There were a lot of times where we would just lose momentum for no reason even though we had tried the exact same thing before and it had worked. Nothing ever felt consistent. Combine that with how sometimes during the pinball sections especially that your arms would literally clip through the boundaries of the wall and get stuck and force you to lose and start the section over, made a lot of sections of this game literally unbearable. There were a couple times where the latency issues from remote play forced me to just play on the save single player to get past a section which I don't blame on the game, but I will say that I did not find the game any more fun singleplayer than I did multiplayer with a ton of lag.Overall, unless you've got someone to do local CO-OP with and like rage games I would pass this game over.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like Struggling, it's a clever idea with cool art and an interesting control scheme, but ultimately those controls aren't up to the task. It feels like something I'd play on Kongregate a million years ago.Most of the challenges require you to be fast or precise, and the controls don't lend themselves very well to either. When you die you get sent back to awkwardly placed checkpoints and have to drag yourself back to the challenge.I'm never gonna have the patience for that kind of nonsense.The humor is almost good too. There's a lot of absurdity in being a scientific abomination trying to make it in the big world with only two arms, two heads and a dream, but the comedy is constantly undermined by how hard it tries.It's just not a very good game.

_childDocuments_.review: is one of those games I wanted to try purely due to its  preview picture, which reminded me of  cartoons. A weird abomination with two heads, funny face, and massy arms? Sign me in! Well, after finally playing the game, I was in the so-called love-hate relationship with it. Why? Find out by reading my thoughts below!You play as , who consists of two characters,  and . Each has one head, arm, and maybe their own thoughts. However, our heroes are locked in a large laboratory with other abominations, as they are just a result of scientific experiments. Fortunately for , scientists decided to celebrate on one day, and one of them vomited on a control panel of  cell. This uncommon situation was enough for  chance for an escape. Where will  path lead, though? Does the story have some hidden meaning? That is something you have to find out on your own!Do not expect from  to have a comprehensible plot from start to finish. This game focuses primarily on the gameplay, so cutscenes and dialogues are very rare, but believe me, they are hilarious, totally worth the wait, and I had a good laugh during them.The gameplay is quite simple. You have to simultaneously control both of  arms to move forward in the levels. Apart from moving with your arms into any direction, you can also grab onto anything. So, you move forward by latching onto things, crawling, climbing, and even swinging. And that is everything you need to know! Once you get the hang of it and start making the first steps with your weirdly looking abomination, you might get the same feeling as if you see your child walking for the first time. At least I think so. I do not know. I do not have kids, okay? So, leave me alone with this proud moment of mine!However, just walking or swinging around without any challenge would be a bit boring, so there are numerous deadly obstacles and aggressive enemies. Fields of spikes and cactuses, poisonous pools and spouts, as well as rats, you will never be completely safe here. And, of course, truly varied boss fights. I have nothing but praise for bosses, as I enjoyed my time with them very much. An important thing to keep in mind is that everything that touches your face will kill you in one hit. That does not apply to your arms, as you can lose them infinitely because they always grow up back, so you can use them as a temporary shield.  is not very happy when you do that, though, and also screams a lot. Well, not like  opinion matters. Fortunately, checkpoints are present pretty often, so you never have to worry about losing much of a progress.As the game is about six hours long, it tries to change the gameplay’s pace by adding a few abilities. For example, you can disarm your own arms and move with them on their own. Why would you do that? You can grab your arm to create a longer one. Slowing the time is also an option, but it slows down  movement, as well. There are a lot of puzzles that require to use the abilities often, even their combination. Time plays an important role, so you have to be fast, or you will end up dead. There are also a few additional paths that lead to collectible hats you can wear.Admittedly,  has proven to be a pretty hard experience for me. That is because of  movement, as you need to be fast and precise, but its arms sometimes unpredictably swing around. A bit of luck will help you too. I had several moments where I was stuck for a few minutes, as I just kept dying. And a few rage quits occurred too. However, the game is definitely not unfair.If you enjoy sharing the pain with your friends, then you might try playing  together. In co-op, each player controls one of  arm. So, you should communicate a lot with your partner, or you are doomed, just like in real life. Unfortunately, the game offers co-op only via  so far. Meaning, one of you has to play it on the keyboard. And believe me, you do not want to play this game on the keyboard. So, while I was struggling with performing simple tasks, my partner’s patience was struggling with staying calm.Apart from the keyboard’s control problem in co-op, there are two other shortcomings. Firstly, the  does not work for me. That makes me quite sad, as even with the hardships I had with finishing the game, I still wanted to try it out in this mode again. Secondly,  arms might sometimes twist itself in a very weird way, so you cannot use them anymore and have to regrow them. Luckily, that only happened a few times, so it is not a common issue, and even with these abovementioned problems, I can still easily recommend this game, as my time with it was pleasant. Painfully pleasant.As I already mentioned in the beginning, I love the game’s visuals. There are so many locations to admire! Mysterious labs, dark caves, ancient temples, wild west, and much more. The designs of abominations and bosses are unique and of high quality too. However, what the game really shines in are its sound effects, which are truly amusing sometimes, like  screams and grunts. And the soundtrack is even better, which was the biggest surprise for me. It is cleverly made, especially during some boss fights.As for the performance, the game was tested with an , , and , running at the highest settings at , at , without any problems. is an enjoyable platformer with the right amount of craziness. _childDocuments_.review: My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. _childDocuments_.review: I didn't originally activate Struggling (SG) because it looked absolutely disgusting, and despite the positive reviews, didn't seem like it'd make for a fun experience. However, a new female friend I made through Steam expressed interest in doing a coop run of it. Without checking the store page, since I assumed that wanting to coop the game meant it had online coop built into it, I activated it from Humble Bundle monthly. It turns out that it doesn't have online coop built into it though, so I ultimately did coop through remote play. Meaning I hadn't needed to add the game to my account when I never wanted it to begin with. The lesson of this story is: Never trust a woman, you will only be betrayed in the end.  For some reason, somebody thought that playing as a moaning abomination with two heads grafted onto a torso awkwardly would make for a great protagonist, because that's what you play as. Obviously something barely able to live also STRUGGLES (Oh, I get it now!) to even move, which becomes the main obstacle of the game. Transferring your grotesque body from one strange place to the next, starting off where you were made, a lab mid-party and... carnival, I guess? You'll then work through a subway system, old Western mine shaft, and just keep trucking through one oddball location to the next. There are hats to get along the way, but aside from overcoming a variety of obstructions and hazards, it's merely an awkward to control “platforming” kind of game. Occasionally there will be something different to mix up the gameplay, but they always end too soon before you have to play the normal segments again.  Joking aside about how I got dragged into SG kicking and screaming, that's almost a summary of the game's controls. The main difference is that you thrash your arms about in order to try and move, but there actually is a button just to make the character moan and wail. I'd use it more often but I had reason enough to scream from playing the game, and a lot of it has to do with trying to get the character to move how you want. Once you get some momentum going, cartwheeling across a ceiling or floor is pretty easy, but if there's some uneven terrain or gaps, that can get thrown off rather easily as the arms struggle to push and heft the body forward.  Oddly enough, the game opens with a somewhat rambling story about extraordinary humans performing mighty deeds that helped the people of the time live better lives. That is, until corrupt dictators banished them and took all of the glory for themselves, somehow becoming titans or gods or something? I was confused by that point, and how the especially strong humans were thrown out so easily in the first place. Then someone prophesied that new champions would come to overthrow the wicked, but they were wrong and nothing changed. Oops. Except maybe they were just off by a few hundred years, and then the game starts. Honestly, I feel sorry for the people who drew the images of these events because it was all irrelevant clap trap. Peeking forward, there's a point when the main characters utter pretentious nonsense about men playing god and people controlling them for sheer entertainment. Pardon the eye roll, but a jank platformer held up by duct tape and a prayer shouldn't act so high and mighty.  Even though the subjects in the game are already grotesque and ugly, that alone isn't why SG isn't a great looking game. For instance, when escaping from the lab, there's plenty of human scientists around, but they aren't particularly good looking or well made models. If you look at them at Dave's party, what's supposed to pass for dancing demonstrates an inability to make these figures move fluidly or remotely human like. This serves as an example of why the game is likely designed and functions as it does, not as an avant garde look at the abominable, but because it'd have looked all the worse if you were platforming as a human. “Oh no, why are the legs spasming so much... that doesn't look right at all. Not to mention what the arms keep doing. But if we weren't using a human for the protagonist, and they look horrific already, this could work.”  In a similar style to the game's visuals, there's an emphasis on the surreal and unpleasant side of humanity. For instance, the music includes sounds like gargling, warbling, and other noises you can make with your mouth that wouldn't be used for musical purposes. It's not as ghastly or gruesome as it could have been, but it can still be a bit off-putting. What's odd about SG is that much of the game is silent, except for any sound effects your character or other on-screen threats might be making, such as the squeaking rats. Only at certain points will the corresponding song come in. That's alright to an extent, but I think that some tunes should have played all throughout the game so it wouldn't be silent so often.  🌟 The few times where the gameplay is different was kind of fun. For instance, moving the metallic refuse to fill gaps felt kind of rewarding, and the body part pinball wasn't punishing like most of the game. 🌟 Later on the game starts adding new mechanics, such as detaching your arms from the body.🌟 You've probably never seen a game quite like this before, thank God.   ❌ Like almost all of these games built around jank controls, it takes simple obstacles for other platforming games, and makes those mole hills into mountains. ❌ SG is somehow boring, tedious, and frustrating all at once. 🔍 It may not be useful often, but sometimes you will need to respawn an arm to get it into a better position. 🔍 Learning how to build momentum and maintain consistent movement will make the game much easier.  Despite thinking SG could be more enjoyable if played with someone else, obnoxious controls only means that you share the pain with somebody else instead of suffering through them alone. Sort of like the main character's very existence, as it's never alone, but never happy. Maybe we're related somehow. Either way, my coop partner was far less annoyed by the game than I, seeing the shortcomings as intentional and an inclusion to the silly, goofy game. Honestly, I can't think about it that way, because I see these matters as inherent flaws that make SG less enjoyable. From my perspective, another game like this, Mushroom 11, wasn't made into a better puzzle game because the odd controls made some of its sections really difficult to pull off. It just meant the developers were sadistic nut jobs who came up with gameplay and stage design ill suited to their own bizarre mechanics. No matter what other people think, something made poorly on purpose (or because it's the best anybody could do) doesn't magically turn it into something of quality. If so, my YouTube channel would be gold, and I know it isn't. Call a turd a turd and stop trying to polish it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, struggling is exactly what it seems to be. An unbelievably unnecessarily difficult coop platformer. I want to make one thing clear. I have nothing against difficult platformers. On the contrary, I'm a big fan of them. But this game is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow and boring.It all starts with an already super weird story. It only gets worse from there. You play a strange creature that only consists of 2 arms and a head. With it, you must move through the levels. Each player (2 player coop) plays one of the arms. You hold on, pull yourself over, let go and so on. In the end, that's the whole gameplay. That's pretty much the only mechanic in the game, which makes it just incredibly boring. On top of that, you move quite slowly, even if you want to catapult yourself forward with minor tricks.Already after a good 30-60 minutes, the game is made unnecessarily hardcore by having to escape a swarm of rats in ultra speed. According to Steam, only 27% of all owners of the game have managed to pass this level. That says a lot. Why put something like this at the beginning? Especially if you can't skip the level. You don't have to do that. I myself experienced fewer complications while playing. I found it easy to control the arm, but my friend, with whom I played, couldn't handle it at all. For him, everything was very difficult, which is why the rat level was pure torture and we needed 15 attempts to get through it. Maybe it's because I play with a controller while he had to use the keyboard (especially since he doesn't have a controller) or it’s just missing skill. I don’t know. I haven't tested it out. But if that should be the difficulty, I recommend everyone to play with a controller. If it’s really that hard with keyboard and mouse, the developers did something wrong.Visually, the game is okay. The level designs are not bad either. However, it was not fun at all. For this reason, I cannot recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Story: It's brilliant.  I played it couch-coop with a friend and its amazing. Longer Story: I bought this game simply because of the art, its so disturbing. I had to try it out. Usually I don't really enjoy each hand is a joystick + button to hold as its usually half baked and gimmicky and ultimately doesn't deliver.  I was sure this game is going to be a funny-game so to speak, not great, just an experience. Boy, was I wrong. Everything in this game ties together. The art style fits the mechanics like a glove (especially later on). The physics of the hand feels slightly-sluggish-creepy (its so well tuned to be annoying and grotesque but reasonable controls, purposely hard). The game continuously challenges you to get better and soon enough you are gliding over areas until the catastrophic and hilarious crash. Just clumsily falling down an area to progress is so silly and amazing. What surprised me the most - is the level-design/progression/game-design. You can tell an ungodly amount of work went into progression/pacing. A new 'mechanic' (ie power) is only introduced like 2 hours in. Meaning, the game relies purely on new content/level design to remain interesting. The devs took the whole concept of hand-thing-controls to the next level. Explored all the little things you can do with it.  With every new area I couldn't stop laughing at the audacity of the devs.  They are flat out insane in the best possible way. Honestly can't remember the last time I was so impressed with a game. Amazing art, killer game design, eerie sounds, hilarious level design - its just.. wow. :) Get it!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This has become one of my favorite games to play basically ever. I love every part of it and cannot wait for more people to enjoy it now that it is making its way to all the consoles/platforms. You can read my original, now outdated (for myself) review below. And would you believe it that even after 100+ I still don't have a single deathless run. Sad day.ORIGINAL REVIEW: Yes, the controls are frustrating (at first), but that's what makes the game so much fun to me. It reminds me a little bit of Octodad in the fact that the hilarity and the challenge comes in the form of your arms not quite doing what you want them to all the time, but still feeling like you totally could make them do exactly what you want them to with a little bit of finesse. I've played through the entire game/story I think 4 or 5 times now and it still hasn't gotten old. Every run through I find myself getting better at the controls, and I find another cool hat! (seriously, the hats are great)There are times where I feel like the hands don't grab onto walls, etc. when I feel like they really should, but I think that would be my only gripe.I have also played this game using Remote Play Together and while the lag definitely made things a bit of a struggle it seemed to work just fine for us and we had a great time with it. I will say that for me personally it is a much more enjoyable experience to play alone, only because it is very hard to navigate some of the sections with a partner and it can get super frustrating trying to do a simple movement sometimes (this may be different if we had been playing local co-op though). That being said, commiseration through video games is always a positive in my book.If you are somebody that wants smooth controls and easy gameplay from the start, you may want to pass this one up. But if you are somebody that enjoys a slightly different way to help your character get from start to finish, definitely check this one out. The art and music are also both fantastic, in my opinion, and the story is fairly entertaining, though the whole meta aspect of the story I'm kind of neutral on still. I've enjoyed my time playing this game and still get a kick/laugh out of some parts of it even though I've seen them now more than a few times.

name: Shadow Warrior 3: Definitive Edition
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Spice up your experience with the Digital Deluxe Edition. Shadow Warrior 3 Digital Deluxe Edition includes: Shadow Warrior 3 base game. Digital Shadow Warrior 3 OST. Exclusive 'Dragonblood' weapon skins for your trusted SMG 'Sidekicks' and the Dragontail katana Official digital artbook. About the Game Experience the Definitive Edition of Shadow Warrior 3, an ultraviolent blend of fast-paced gunplay, razor-sharp melee combat, and a spectacular free-running movement through a mythical Japanese realm. Test your skills in Survival Mode, New Game Plus, and Hardcore Mode, and WATCH OUT FOR THAT DRAGON! Fallen corporate shogun Lo Wang and his former nemesis Orochi Zilla return in Shadow Warrior 3, the latest entry in the gore-soaked, wisecracking FPS series. Embark on an improbable mission to recapture an ancient dragon Lo Wang unwittingly unleashed from its eternal prison, tearing your way through a fractured land infested with demons using a dynamic arsenal of blades and bullets. NEW FEATURES include; NEW GAME PLUS, bringing with it additional challenges, weapons skins, and rewards; SURVIVAL MODE, allowing you to put your skills to the test against waves of incoming enemies, a new HERO MODE game modifier offering an even greater challenge; CHAPTER SELECT for rapid replayability; and finally, HARDCORE DIFFICULTY - the most intensely punishing version of Shadow Warrior yet! Bring a Katana to a Gunfight Conduct a symphony of death with each encounter by mixing overwhelming firepower with devastatingly precise katana strikes as you dash in and around the demonic hordes. Fancy Footwork Flow between nimble movement techniques, including air dashes, wall running, and double jumps, and the fancy new grappling hook busts your combat and movement options wide open in every battle. Execute Then Annihilate Execute spectacular finishing moves to claim a piece of your conquered foe and unleash its powers back on the horde in a burst of unstoppable fury and powerful magic. Dynamic Combat Arenas Each environment is lined with hazardous structures and devices that can be activated to add another layer of creative choice to the offensive strategy. Neo Feudal Japan Trek across a mythic Asian land infused with the magic and technology of ancient samurai, now overrun by the demonic yokai from Japanese folklore. Funny Business Brace for expertly delivered one-liners from Lo Wang, pointed banter with Zilla, and an intense thrill ride of absurd predicaments on the way to turning doomsday into a new day. Step up your Lo-Wang game! Survival Mode is a completely new game mode allowing you to play in 3 new battle arenas providing hours of new gameplay! 3 new weapon skins will be up for grabs for those who can complete the challenge! Survival Mode becomes available after finishing the game! Relive magical moments! The Chapter Select menu lets you go back and collect missing upgrade points and relive some of your favorite moments that defined your adventure with Lo-Wang in whichever order your heart desires! Give Lo-Wang’s mojo some additional pazzazz! New Game Plus gives you a new way to play the game. Enjoy additional challenges, rewards, and skins to give Lo-Wang that much-needed confidence boost! GO VULGAR, OR GO HOME! The new Hardcore Difficulty lets you experience the most intensely punishing version of Shadow Warrior yet! Not for the faint-hearted. LOSE A LIFE, LOSE A SAVE Put your skills to the test in the brand-new Hero Mode, a challenging modifier allowing you to play with a limited number of lives and earn more of them by performing spectacular Finishers. Run out, and your progress is lost forever.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★☆ - Great  8 hours  Hard  Keyboard + Mouse  	- FPS Arena Shooter similar to Doom (2016) and Doom Eternal.	- Fluid combat mechanics that allow for satisfying combos and strategic play.	- Variety of weapons and ability upgrades to choose from.	- Every enemy has a strategy and gun to quickly defeat them, adding depth to the combat.	- Mission structure keeps gameplay engaging with diverse objectives and challenges.  	- Simple yet effective storyline set in post-apocalyptic feudal Japan, blending historical events with fictional elements.	- Well-written dialogue that both keeps to story going and gives character and humour to each scene\transition to the next arena.  	- Visually stunning environments and character designs.	- Smooth animations enhance the fluidity of combat	- During combat, both the UI and level of detail in the characters and environment can seem somewhat jarring.  	- Game is better played in 2 hour max stints so as not to overwhelm you.	- Normal difficulty you can get away without strategy and is the best to play for casual players. Hard is better for people that can get easy bored by this as it requires strategy and skill with each weapon, enemy and movement on the arena.	- Familiarize yourself with each enemy, how to defeat them and their upgrades.	- Make special use of your chi to push enemies into spikes and the swords heavy attack (once upgraded) to gain resources from weaker enemies.

Developers, if you read these, you did an awesome job and I apologize for letting the reviews sway me on buying it until now! Yea, it could be longer, but the game play loop here is really good. _childDocuments_.review: Not sure what the hate is about with this game.Shadow Warrior 1 and 2 was annoying as imo..Kill some enemies, pick up the loot then stand around for 10 minutes trying to figure out which guns to use, compare the stats, add the mods or what ever.Shadow Warrior 3 seems to have gone down the path of Doom and Serious Sam games.I prefer Shadow Warrior 3 compared to the others as 3 is straight forward, simple mechanics, simple upgrades and you unlock new weapons each time you go to like a new area or progress further.Story wise is alright, characters and enemy designs are pretty cool, skins are awesome and the dialogues pretty funny most times.The graphics are quite nice actually even though I am still playing at 1080p and all settings are maxed out with my old rig which consists of an i7 4790k, DDR3 2133mhz and an RTX 2080 and I get between 100-165fps due to my monitor being 165hz.The only time it lags is when a cutscene starts as the fps drops to like 30 or less for a few moments, then boom it goes to over 1300fps.. Once the cutscene is over then it goes back to 100-165fps so I think it is either a CPU or GPU bottleneck because the fps goes super high out of no where and my system seems to chug for that moment.Bought the game for the special price of $30AUD in which I am happy to spend that amount rather than the full price but overall, I am enjoying the game without any complaints.
