_childDocuments_.review: Soooooo Shadow Warrior 3, huh?I was on marathon of old shooters in my library and noticed that I never really completed Shadow Warrior from 2013. So I played it and I enjoyed it. Pretty cool game which has some flaws, but decent FPS with some original features. Straight to SW2 (which I also played couple of years ago) -> game made a switch to a looter shooter with central hub and missions, where you obtain varied weapons, trinkets and stuff. Same maps over and over again. Questionable, yet still fun.And lucky me - right after that Steam has the trilogy on sale, so I'm getting SW3 for like 3 bucks or something. Yes, I've heard that the game was short and it had some rough launch and that players didn't like it much. Oh, now I know why. It took me half an hour to understand that I will never be launching it again. Why?So here's the deal - take everything that was good in SW1 & SW2 and... put it to trash. Add some nice looking cinematics, a grappling hook and bland enemies - here you go, folks. This is appealing, this will sell well. Not. Short list of disappointments: 1. Controls. Yes, I am having problems with shooting stuff. Why? I have no idea. I bought a brand new mouse recently and played previous two games on it - like a charm. In third game, and I have no idea why - each third or fourth click actually makes the revolver to shoot. Shotgun works fine, doubles uzi's - same as revolver. What? Why? Movement is still okay, thanks for that. 2. Weapons. Compared to SW2 - you get just a pinch of necessities to cover your needs. Can't change, defined set + the consumable ones you pull from enemies on finishers. Okay. Old school. But even comparing to SW1 it's just depressing. First game had more guns and gadgets. This is a downgrade. But I'm not mad, no.What grinds my gears, as folks in reviews stated before - each gun is 30% shooting time, 70% reload animations. Guns have extremely low ammo and that's by design. It's not a "First Person Shooter game", It's "First Person Run To that blue thing to pick up your 10 bullets" game.3. Now something about level design and how combat arenas work. So far all levels are sets of multiple "arena rooms" mixed with parkour sections. You don't get no exploration, you don't get tactics or variety. Run there, Kill everyone in that room. Chop that yellow seaweed to open the door - repeat until you get old and share the frustration with your grand kids.4. Back to those "blue things that replenish ammo". Well, I can definitely feel some latest DOOM vibes here, but stripped of any fun by design. The game utilizes the same mechanics, where each arena contains a Health Source and an Ammo Source. Due to limited initial ammo and it's cap - you are supposed to run around like your head is on fire and cross those spots to heal and be able to shoot back. It's just not fun. Yeah, you can confront the mob crowd with your sword to get some ammo from kills, but that's straight suicide. You can use surrounding hazards to freeze, burn and pummel. But if that's what this game is about I'd rather stick with  Divinity: Original Sin, lol. You can't retreat and pick up ammo that you left just behind this slope, you are supposed to play this as designers made it, even though you've expected a different game, based on previous parts. 5. What made the reboot of SW standout? Crude humor, nice gunplay and character progression. Well, we have just humor left (and I will not bother to check if it's still funny or not). But, yes - they kinda shrinked the best part of SW2: the skill system. In SW1 you had a bunch of skill trees and abilities to level up (aside from weapons). SW2 made a step up and introduced card system which was just awesome - there were dozens and dozens of skills/perks/ utilities you could level up. Here you get... Eh... 25% of that? 30? Ok, I get that you want the weapon system from the first game to cut the cost and not the overloaded customization of the guns from part 2. I accept that. You also got rid of money system and elemental system, so the number goes down drastically. Hard but acceptable, But why did all the fun stuff went away? Long story short - character progression is a bleak shadow of itself. Even compared to the first game. What I expected: level up from first two games, making it more complex, more fun, more guns, more everythingWhat I got: some boring arena shooter that supposes I'll have fun by listening to dialogues and watching nice cinematics. Thanks, but no, thanks. Maybe you'll like it, as something to play while you watch some video in background, but if new Shadow Warrior will be ever release - I'll think twice before checking it out. Cheers!P.S. Oh and cookies.... RIP Fortune Cookies.

_childDocuments_.review: Only buy on a sale. I don't regret buying it at launch for full price, but I am disappointed a bit.Yes, it's short, and in some places comes off very unfinished and rushed, but it's compressed quality time, nothing wasted. If you were expecting a looter shooter like the 2nd game, you're outa luck. Shadow Warrior 3 borrows a lot from Doom Eternal. Too much in fact. SW (2013) was unique and its own thing, SW2 was an experiment, but SW3 just feels like it lost its identity. It's a chinese knock-off version of Doom Eternal - in every meaning of those words.Here's another franchise that switched to Unreal Engine 4 and once again I must say the cons outweigh the benefits. Lots of low resolution textures everywhere. The particle effects look sometimes surprisingly worse. Although you can blast actual holes into the bigger enemies, overall the dismemberment isn't as detailed as in SW2 (or even SW1). The game overall straight up looks and runs worse than SW2.That's not to say the game's art style is bad. I actually enjoy the art direction of this game a lot! It's the best it's ever been! All the maps are super colorful, all the plants and trees are moving creating a map that looks alive! The enemies look straight out of a Chinese circus! A mesmerizing amount of creativity went into their design. I only really dislike the ketchup blood, looks too weird.On the other hand, level design is a disaster (worse than SW2). It's often not clear what is the intended play area. While looking for secrets (as you usually do in a SW game), you'll find it's easier to die instantly in an area you weren't even supposed to be able to reach, than to find any secrets. Everything is extremely messy and busy, I often die without even knowing what killed me, although that happened often in previous games as well. The game could use a large "spoonful" of visual clarity. E.g. the projectiles of the icicle guys are hardly ever visible in the middle of all the mayhem.I miss Lo Wang's old voice actor. I don't hate the new one, but it's simply not Wang. Zilla sounds cool, Wang is a bit hit&miss - so objectively worse, yes, but only a tiny little bit. Not sure why the devs felt like recasting was necessary.By far my biggest complaint - and I hate that this is becoming a trend - is that the OST is incomplete. I'm losing my diamonds over this, because Maciej Kulesza did a fenomenal job! The OST is chinese lo-fi techno house, a total vibe, but SO MANY TRACKS ARE MISSING!!! None of the fighting BGMs are included. So definitely don't buy the Deluxe Edition for the OST (unless you want FLACs I guess?). Buy the base game and then pirate the unreleased, unofficial OST or rip the music straight out of the game files using FMOD Tools. Their own fault for not selling what we want, my wallet was ready.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the series but don't recommend this game unless you get it for cheap. I finished it in less than 7 hours (including cutscenes) and it's not really that interesting. The gameplay is very linear with some platforming between battle arenas and some cutscenes as filler. I don't find myself replaying the game ever.There are only two boss battles and they are basically impossible to finish on any difficulty other than easy because the bosses have attacks you can't dodge dishing out more damage than you can tank even if you beeline towards the health pickups. Meanwhile I finished both the previous games on their hardest difficulties and found those experiences enjoyable. Remember to disable motion blur if you choose to buy the game. It's unplayable with motion blur on because it's just a mess trying to see anything in such a fast paced game. For such a short game it seems a bit rushed because it has some glaring flaws with things like motions blur and boss battle mechanics. The combat itself was fine even though it's different from the previous games in the series. If you want a game you can finish in one long session or over a weekend then this game might be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: **Edit**So I finally convinced myself to finish the game.  The last portion of the game was okay, the dragon was cool but still the game just couldn't recover, even with a setting like fighting on the back of a dragon or in it's body.  I was plagued through the whole game with an issue where I'd press my fire button and literally nothing would happen; this is unforgivable in a game that requires quick response and a quick trigger finger.  They had a serious opportunity to do something AMAZING here...and they failed and went for the easy money grab.  5 hours...5 hours is all you get...I'm missing 5 achievements and you know what...I don't even care to try and get them.  Don't waste your money on this very obvious money grab.**Original Review**I am trying very much to love this game.  I have loved shadow warrior ever since the original build engine game, all of those years ago.  I loved the first remake, I loved the second...the third....the third doesn't know what it wants to be.  Does it want to be Doom....does it want to be Serious Sam....does it want to be Shadow Warrior....unfortunately it doesn't do any of them good; at best it does them just mediocre.  The gun play is meh, I have been having this seriously irritating issue where I push my mouse button to fire...and nothing happens...it just doesn't register the click.  It's not my mouse, I have tested it...other games and programs work just fine, no issues.  It only happens in this game.  The sword play, what made the remakes so awesome...is...watered down and lack luster.  The comedy is far from witty and more slap stick then anything, I'm fully expecting for them to make fart and poop jokes soon.The game has lost focus, if they just kept it the way Shadow Warrior 2 was, with a new story...I think everyone would be happy...it wouldn't have won any awards for innovation but we'd have loved it.  Updated graphics and the same game play we already loved...with maybe a few Quality of Life improvements.  This one, however...feels like they sat in a board room and went "What do people like?  Doom, they loved Doom...I hear they like Serious Sam too, the kids this day and age seem to love stupid comedy...you know what...lets just put it all together and hope it works."  No...No it does not.  I hate to say it...I really really do...but if like the other two remakes....you're going to completely dislike this one...Avoid buying, or at least wait till it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: What a disappointment. I really liked the two prior Shadow Warrior games, so I wanted to give Flying Wild Hog a chance on this one, but it's just not fun or enjoyable.Listen, I'm not some Shadow warrior purist, but  fundamentally misunderstands the series appeal at best and is actively trying to sanitize the IP to be more mass-market friendly at worst. The result is an unfunny, miserably linear game of combat arenas filled with the same few boring enemies and atrociously long unskippable execution animations. The first two games  good to play, but 3 feels floaty and generic, and the environments feel cheap and boring.Worse, the writing has taken a significant drop in quality, which is embarrassing in a series about a man named 'Lo Wang'. The dialogue is painful and unfunny. You'd be better playing this game with the dialogue off and subtitles disabled except the gameplay is bland and awful. Just an entire flub from top to bottom.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the other Shadow Warrior games, so I think my opinion is quite valid since I didn't automatically dislike the game because of it's delineation from the original story. I played it like I would any game I was interested in and that was it. The first 2 stages are really immersive and awesome. You're on a dragon and everything is new! But, once you start the journey with the mask and stuff, it's so one dimensional. It's just "fight these waves" then "navigate to the next place to fight these next waves". Another huge one is the fact that you kill the newly introduces boss-ish enemies instantly because they give you your execute for them the moment they are introduced. I imagine they wanted you to understand the weapon the new enemy provides but it just ended up tearing me out of the immersion as it took the enemy's "scaryness" away completely. There were a couple wave killing stages where I was so taken aback by the fact that this became a "wave killing game", that I thought I broke the game progression somehow. I was like "I'm really just on this platform killing enemies in waves over and over? What am I missing here? How do I progress through this level?" Overall the game is beautiful graphic-wise and the gameplay feels utterly smooth and fun, but the story, game progression, game design, etc just don't = me playing this game to completion.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3, oh boy, where do I even begin? If I could give this abomination of a game zero stars out of five, I'd still be too generous. This travesty makes Shadow Warrior 1 and 2 look like gaming masterpieces. How did this disaster manage to get the green light for release? It's a slap in the face to the loyal fanbase who cherished the first two games.They've taken everything we loved about the series and tossed it out the window, replacing it with a never-ending stream of poorly animated, mind-numbing cutscenes. The weapons are pitiful, the storyline is laughably bad, and they've stripped away the multiplayer component entirely.But that's just the tip of the iceberg. Prepare to rage as you randomly die from a jump that's shorter than a toddler's leap, while miraculously surviving falls from skyscraper heights. The game's logic is a maddening rollercoaster ride that leaves you questioning the developers' sanity.Don't even get me started on the voice acting! The main character Wang and his buddy Hoji sound like they've been plucked from the bargain bin of voice talent. It's excruciating to listen to.The level design is lazy at best, with trees sway in the wind and go through buildings and mountains and water that defies the laws of physics. Exploration is a joke, and the game's a measly 5 hours long, a complete cakewalk. It's like the developers deliberately set out to destroy everything that made Shadow Warrior great.The numbers speak volumes. Shadow Warrior 3 is a ghost town with a paltry 26 active players at the time of writing. Compare that to Shadow Warrior 1 and 2, which still boast thriving player bases. The developers have utterly butchered the franchise, and it's crystal clear that nobody wants any part of this monstrosity.I can't fathom what the developers were thinking. Shadow Warrior 3 is a disgrace, a stain on the legacy of a beloved series that dates back to the '90s. It offers absolutely nothing of value, and the fact that the developers were content with this abomination hitting the shelves is beyond comprehension.I love the Shadow Warrior series, but this game? It's the worst thing I've had the misfortune of playing this year, hands down. I paid 6 bucks for this dumpster fire, and I can't shake the feeling that I've been swindled. Avoid this game like the plague.I payed 6 bucks for this awful game and I feel like I got ripped off.

_childDocuments_.review: In comparison to Doom, which has been around since 1996 and is arguably the most well-known game of 2016, I have seen acclaim for its fighting system. When a company decides to mimic the success of a formula brilliantly implemented by the exceptional team behind Doom, a full six years before the release of Shadow Warrior 3, expectations naturally plummet. The 2016 edition of Doom typically costs $6–8. I do not see any reason to shell out a ridiculous sum for Shadow Warrior 3 to get a subpar take on the fighting from Doom 2016.The game is serviceable but nothing special. Is it fantastic? Absolutely not, and by no means is it good; it is merely adequate. Even if this game were to become free on Epic Games or another platform, I would still need help recommending it due to its numerous problems.Every aspect of the game is inferior to its predecessor, Shadow Warrior 2. You could not make the maps more linear and confining than they already are. In Shadow Warrior 2, you had a lot of leeway and choice in dealing with challenges. That feeling of independence and agency has stuck with you. Whatever something was in the last game, it does not exist here.For those who played back in the day, you may recall an upgrade system in which you could customize your equipment to better suit your play preferences. Okay, throw that out the window, too. Do you recall the game's humorous and carefree dialogue? In such a case, just put it all out of your mind. The gameplay lasts an embarrassingly short amount of time, and the conversation is excruciatingly bad. It is clear that no humans were involved in making it or that the designers relied largely on data about what they thought would be popular, like a company's attempt to use social media to sound human.The pitiful husk of its former existence; it was bad enough that many grumbled about Shadow Warrior 2 not living up to their hopes for the sequel, so think of how much worse it must be now.Gamers' willingness to pay eight to ten times as much for a game that does only a mediocre job of what DOOM has perfected is a sad reflection of their declining moral fibre and a key reason why they are so easily exploited by publishers and developers.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect game to buy on sale; I got it half off.  It's definitely a quality over quantity type game.  It's very action packed, has great graphics, and quite good performance as well.  Game play is similar to Doom Eternal, with a dash of Serious Sam.  To increase the longevity of the game, I would play through a level for fun the first time on hard difficulty, then go back and replay it on an easier difficulty to make sure I got all the orbs I may have missed the first time to upgrade my abilities and weapons.  You could say I 100%[ed] this game.To the people beating this game in 4-5 hours, I say to you you're not playing on a hard enough difficulty (of which there are now four).  Breezing through this on Easy or Normal is a waste.  Now, my game time says I've played 17 hours, but it's probably more like 12 (it counts being afk or looking at a Youtube video on my second monitor to find that  secret orb I didn't get the first time around).  The game is a blast to play, and I've played the whole trilogy.  I agree with other reviewers that it is a little bit too short for full price.  It's a wild ride though, and there are times when I was in awe of the sheer amount of animations and particles happening on screen at once.  Now comparing it to its predecessors isn't apples to apples, but if you could only compare (for example) six hours of game play from Shadow Warrior 1,2, and 3- the third would win.  Definitely recommended, albeit on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, let me start by saying this game is decent. Combat is still the same classic Shadow Warrior with quick gunplay and with satisfying melee combat. Problem was everything around it. Let me start with the biggest elephant in the room, or in this game's case, a petite one, the game's like 5 hours long and, at the time of writing, has major stuttering issues and is lacking some pretty obvious features that should have been here in the first place for a game releasing in 2022 - like a Level Select for one. Like I said previously, combat is satisfying, they took the Doom Eternal approach to this game and just give you a decent arsenal of guns while the katana serves as a ammo refill option at the start, but does become much more powerful later on once you gain the ability to add Crowd Control elements to it. Finishers are pretty satisfying too both giving you a health recovery and in some cases, very powerful tools to clear out waves of enemies quickly. So with all this praise, why exactly am I not recommending it? Honestly, the 5 hour game time is not a big deal to me as I value short and sweet games more than the 100 hour epic nowadays - the problem really stem from the game itself. Enemy variety is rather low and even though the combat is satisfying, it can get old and repetitive VERY quickly to the point where it being 5 hours ensures the game doesn't overstay it's welcome.  The game has a grappling hook that barely functions half the time and is mostly used in on-rails and linear platforming sections. I had a LOT of problems with these sections, sometimes the cursor for it would not appear even though I'm staring at it and against enemy encounters I found it nigh unusable because it had an annoying tendency to put me above the enemy itself. A lot of my gripes against the game really is just how forgettable the entire experience is, cool visuals aside. I know this review is written haphazardly and I apologize for the lack of structure, I saw a lot of peeps eyeing this game and honestly, I quite expected better than this, especially after the excellent Shadow Warrior 2. This game feels like a huge step back in every regard, it had some funny moments for me with the meta jokes, but the godawful platforming, repetitive enemy wave based encounters with admittedly great combat and the pretty bare bones story sadly means I won't be revisiting this game for a long time. If you're reading this wondering if you should play it as a fan of these Boomer Shooter titles - it's worth playing at least once, but I would wait for a deep sale unless you believe $50 is worth 5 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Like how the 1997 original Shadow Warrior was an Asian inspired Duke Nukem 3D, the 2013 Reboot was an Asian inspired Painkiller, and Shadow Warrior 2 was an Asian inspired Destiny, this installment to the semi-famous FPS IP in Shadow Warrior 3 is an Asian inspired Doom Eternal. It's finishers with the enemies are clearly inspired by Doom 2016/Eternal's glory kills. Like Doom Eternal SW3 has some frustrating platforming sessions which they often go poorly while in a first person prospective yet for me personally SW3's platforming mechanics had stronger accessibility than either Doom Eternal's or the orginal Turok's platform elements combined! Back to the glory kill inspired finishers most of the enemies if you do finishers on you can use part of them temporarily as a weapon. What makes this game better to wait for a cheaper deal while on sale is the fact that for a fully published AA title that has been delayed several of times the game is short as hell! After I realized that they added a patch that included a Chapter Select Mode which was absent when I had it given to me as a birthday present I work and played hard to 100% the playthrough's challenges as well as general achievement hunting I missed one upgrade orb to complete all upgrades to get my last achievement for a month and a half but thanks to the patch with the Chapter Select Mode added I went to the level where I missed the one orb five or six weeks back and got the orb I missed, did the final upgrade and 100%ed Shadow Warrior 3's achievements making it my fifteenth game on Steam to join my Perfect Games list. Lo Wang this time around is as if Duke Nukem and No More Heroes's Travis Touchdown were a thing and they adopted an Asian child in the Shadow Warrior Reboot trilogy's Lo Wang. One of the enemies you fight towards the later levels in the game are clearly inspired by Doom's Mancubus! There's also a kamikaze suicide type enemy reminiscent of the headless bomb dudes from Serious Sam which are easier to deal with in groups than a single ♥♥♥♥♥♥ from the 1997 original was to deal with! If you're a die hard fan of Shadow Warrior as an IP like me give the game a go if more casual with it and games in general but still want to play it, play the first two installments of the current iteration and wait for part three to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, the game is too short and straightforward. No multiplayer, no random level creation like in part 2. Only 7 weapons and a few upgradable abilities. That's it. The game focuses on fast-paced combat from the first-person perspective. We play Lo Wang, who can handle his sword like no other. When he can't reach opponents, he uses various handguns, but his most important weapon is the katana, a Japanese longsword. With it he cuts his opponents to pieces without ever getting tired. And opponents stand in his way a lot! Lo Wang also uses the environment to defeat his opponents and between the fights there is a bit of parkour running.The whole production is lavishly presented, the story is told through short cutscenes with mostly funny conversations. Mostly, however, action is the order of the day, and there is hardly a quiet second here. The levels are divided into chapters, in which we advance through smaller stages to large open battle arenas, which only open again when all enemies have been eliminated. We can (double) jump, dash, run along (marked) walls, fight with a sword or a firearm, and swing around (or pull enemies towards us) in (marked) places with the help of a grappling hook. With the execution bar filled up, we can execute enemies in a particularly brutal way, which replenishes our health and also gives us a special weapon (made from the remains of the destroyed enemy). The environment is full of deadly dangers that you can stumble into yourself, but it's much more fun to push your opponents into a wall full of (long) spikes, for example. Or into the vicinity of a barrel full of ammunition, which explodes to great effect after a hit. In addition, we also have a kind of spell to push opponents away from us. In some scenes there are also dangerous machines that can be activated. It's fun to set off a deadly machine that shreds overpowered enemies into tiny pieces.If you like fast and action-packed, exceedingly brutal first person slashers, and don't mind to see the end after a few hours, this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the general consensus of Shadow Warriors 3, it still holds up in my mind as an insanely fast paced and fun as hell run and gunner. Yes its short, and no it doesn't seem to have as much going for it as 1 and 2, in fact feeling very stripped down and bare bones in terms of actual content whilst also having its main ingredients changed that made the series so great to begin with, but if you can look past those infractions then you will find a pretty decent game to fill a few hours of your time.Where SW1 set the standard, and SW2 improved on that formula with its crazy customisation and weapon system, SW3 took a different approach by taking a step back and simplifying every facet, which rightfully so, pissed a lot of people of, while at the same time creating a lot of inconsistencies. It seems their biggest focus for this game was to bring a close to the story by rushing you through linear, fast paced parkour maps where you run from one arena to the next to dispatch hordes of enemies. The game also has a grand total of 2 boss fights, it ends up feeling like you just popped some money into an arcade machine for 5 minutes of fun rather than settling into a 20-30 hour adventure.Combat is still fun but not as fleshed out, instead opting for a simplified system of right click been entirely tied to the sword and left click operating your currently selected ranged weapon so you're ready for any situation on the fly. There are several weapons that all function very differently and can be upgraded to perform slightly differently than their base but no longer have a secondary fire option, instead the upgrades just add more such as elemental effects, wider explosive radius or piercing capabilities to name a few.The soundtrack, as usual in the series is top notch as well, some real feel good vibes that get you motivated to kill demons!Unfortunately it doesn't have the same edgy humour that its predecessors had that had me laughing from start to finish, instead feeling more PG and a bit cringey, whenever they dropped a swear word it felt like a cardinal sin. I loved Hoji in the first game too but he was unbearably annoying in this one, feel like they did my boy dirty.But even through all the bad...I can't help but say that it was still a lot of fun, it was a good game and I still would recommend it, it has its own charm that works in its own way. Sometimes you just need a short game to blow off some steam, it doesn't overstay its welcome, it feels like your constantly going somewhere instead of feeling static and stale, it isn't pretentious, it isn't TOO obnoxious and the combat is still a heckin' good time!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to try addressing the majority of people's problems with this game in a way that doesn't downplay them but still explain why they don't bother me and you can decide how you feel about it.1) Short game: yes, and it is definitely overpriced for it. Its a 4-6 hour game and while I don't believe that a game's value should be deeply connected to its playtime, especially if it has some replayability, this is not a game that has purposefully designed replayability beyond multiple difficulties and a new game + which came post launch. I replayed the game because I liked the game. But even I don't think that it should have been $50 at launch and $40 at the time of this review is still rough.2) Its nothing like the previous games: and Shadow Warrior 2 (which I really liked) was nothing like the first game (which I really liked). And none of these games have been anything like the original Shadow Warrior game made on the Build Engine. I liked Shadow Warrior 2 and I wouldn't mind a sequel to that kind of game but bear in mind this is a series that has shaken things up with every entry.3) Its a rip off of DOOM Eternal: the more things change the more they stay the same. In 1993 when the original Doom game came out every FPS game for years after it was called a Doom clone, including the original Shadow Warrior. Something can take a formula and do its own thing with it and still be a good game. Everything you've ever seen, heard or played is in some way iterative of at least one other thing; that's why we have genres. Shadow Warrior 3 definitely takes a lot from DOOM Eternal but I think it differentiates itself enough through a melee weapon, a unique art style, and by just being simpler than DOOM Eternal. If someone wanted to play DOOM Eternal for the first time they could play this first and be eased into this kind of game better than DOOM Eternal does.4) No RPG mechanics: there are character perks and weapon upgrades. You may not consider those RPG mechanics but that's about what the first Shadow Warrior remake game had.5) The story, acting and writing are bad: ♥♥♥♥ yeah it is, this might be one of the most pointless stories I've ever seen in a game. I think there are jokes but its honestly hard to tell, and one of the characters is very annoying and never shuts up... wait which game in this series am I talking about, I don't even know anymore. Flying Wild Hog can't do story, at least not with this series.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat wise If you liked Shadow Warrior 2 (like I did, 110 hours of playtime) and wanted more then this ain't it. This game feels like a well made mod for DOOM 2016 and that's not necessarily a bad thing. DOOM's a fun game. Can't go wrong with copying its gameplay. I said in my Shadow Warrior 2 review that it also felt like DOOM but with Katanas. SW3 is more of the same. Would've been nicer if it was longer. I generally subscribe to the $1 = 1 hour of playtime when judging if I liked a game or if it was money well spent, which is not the case here. My fault for not waiting on a sale I suppose but I've spent $10 on worse things.Parkour segments are a bit hit and miss first time around, you barely get any time to look around and see what you have to do before falling to your death. Thankfully fast respawn timers that put you right back at the start of the segment means it's not a big deal.Music is a banger as always. I don't know what it is about chinese oriental music that makes it go so well with hiphop but it works. Main Menu theme is once again so good it makes me not want to load into the game immediately.Humour is the same as SW2, lots of ♥♥♥♥ jokes, lots of Lo Wang being immature and getting on everyone's nerves, which I don't mind but I know some do. Also there's a lot more movie references in this game. I didn't realise I was playing Borderlands 2. I get it, game devs are mostly boomers and boomers like their old movies, but can we tone down the references just a little? The most annoying thing about this was those enemies that burrow underground. You get a very small window to hurt them when they pop up before they go back underground and can't be damaged, yet can damage you. Very frustrating. Those jack-in-the-box enemies are also annoying with how fast they move and those  flying enemies were hard to hit with melee. Definitely a skill issue on my part but It's my review and I didn't like them. All the other demons were fine though.Lastly there's the matter of general combat strategy. Mobs spawn infinitely until you take out the elite enemies. Theoretically this is good game design, as you can melee kill them as much as you want until you have enough ammo and finisher gauge to deal with the bigger boys but in practice, I found myself completely ignoring them and focusing on the higher priority targets. The game kills all the little guys once the main threats are dealt with and there's enough AOE damage going around that a bunch of smaller guys will die from collateral damage. Enough that I rarely needed to farm them for ammo. Overall I enjoyed the experience. when my biggest complaint of the game is that there's not enough of it (it really is a short game) then that's a good thing. Always leave them wanting more. I also want to point out that SW2 is also a short game once you take out all the upgrades. If you got a high level Lo Wang with upgraded weapons, you can beat the story in less than 4 hours. Most of the length of that game is doing sidequests and farming for upgrades. Take out all that farming and you get SW3

_childDocuments_.review: The original  from 1997 is still the best entry. That said, I had a pretty good time with this one, though I have my words of criticism.I would argue the game draws as much from its '97 ancestor as it does ; the Riot Gun can be upgraded to fire in four-round bursts, there's a river segment reminiscent of an easier E2M1, and the bosses are sparse. There are, of course, valid comparisons to make to , such as the inclusion of a grappling hook, executions, environmental hazards activated with attacks, and an emphasis on resource management. As Civvie 11 once said, "if you're gonna steal something, steal something good." What caught me by surprise, of course, was the ability to knock enemies into spike walls like in . With some upgrades to Wang and his arsenal, the combat becomes just a bit more fun, though not so engaging as . Where the game truly lacks is in its story. I didn't try to pay attention to it very strongly; the plot is basic, which isn't that bad, but certain characters get underused between the beginning and end of the campaign, and the jokes aren't consistently well-delivered until towards the end; some jokes are even groan-inducing, like the off-handed, meta jabs at modern gaming. I refuse to say Flying Wild Hog didn't put as much effort into  as id Software did , because it's plain to see that they did; the environmental art direction, animations, and parkour segments are proof of this. Some fine-tuning to the combat could be done to make it faster and more engaging, but that's just because  spoiled me and countless others for FPS combat.Take an afternoon to try this if you liked previous  reboot entries. It's short and sweet... sometimes sour, but hey. That's Asian stuff, for ya.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let me say that I'm trying to keep this review as objectively as I possibly can, meaning that I won't criticize the game for any (in my opinion) mostly subjective issues. This includes the protagonist being voiced by a different voice actor then in the previous games as well as criticising the game for something it is not trying to be (e.g. a "looter-shooter-light" like Shadow Warrior 2 was).Instead I will focus this review on a few aspects that can be properly evaluated:With that out of way, let's get into it.Unlike its predecessors, Shadow Warrior 3 is instead built on the Unreal Engine 4 foundation (with all it's pros & cons). The result is mostly great: Impressive vistas, high quality effectswork, detailed models & environments and - for the most part - high framerates.There are some rather low-res textures here and there, and some environments don't look quite as detailed as one would like, but overall, I'd say this is a pretty good looking game, keeping in mind it's no AAA-production.There's a distinctive art-direction in place here as well, and although it's maybe a bit too "cartoony", I think it overall fits the franchise rather well. High color saturation & contrast, creative enemy design, beautiful landscapes. However, I have to say that environment variety is lacking; there's basically just three different types of environments.Last but not least, loading times in this game are extremely short, which surely is nice!In my opinion, the core gameplay loop in SW3 is pretty good. It's the classic Arena - Hallway - Arena concept we've come to know & love (or not).Arenas manage to create really tense battle scenarios; there's quite some variety here when it comes to movement options, pathways, and even some environmental traps to take care of your opponents. Although I have to admit that often times I felt like arenas are just a little too small, and I've found myself a few times in combat just falling off a platform or stuck at a wall.The "Hallways" (figuratively, they’re not literal hallways) mostly involve some platforming. You're wall-running, jumping, graple-hooking - just the usual good stuff. These sections are a pretty good contrast to the very chaotic fighting arenas and allow for some time to breath.Speaking of wall-running: Movement in this game is great, which is key for fast-paced shooters like this. You have a lot of mobility not just in the platforming parts, but also during combat. You can double jump, dash to avoid incoming attacks or travel larger distances in short time, use the grapple-hook to fly around the arena (or use it offensively to get up close & personal with the enemy), slide through little passages to escape an otherwise overwhelming force of foes. I can not stress enough that this is really good stuff, and this, combined with the really good shooting mechanics in this game make this experience really fun.Other than SW2, this game only has a handful of weapons (including the melee Katana, there's only a total of 7 different weapons). However, and this is important, these weapons are all vastly different from one another and each one serves a meaningful purpose during the combat sections of the game. You have your starting weapon (a Revolver) to make precise head-shots at larger range and get rid of smaller enemies quickly. There's the Shotgun ("Riot Gun" in that case; a homage to the 1997 original ;) ) that kills stuff good in close combat situation. There's the rapid-firing Uzis for crowd control, the railgun for larger enemies, and so on. You get the idea. I'll take this over the 300 samey weapons in SW2 all day!It is no secret that this game is heavily inspired by Doom Eternal in regards to it’s core gameplay and mechanics. There’s some sort of glory-kill mechanic that allows an instant kill on any enemy (provided you do have your glory-kill-meter full), plus, as a nice bonus, you get full health and ammo back by doing so. Additionally, you’ll also get some sort of super weapon for a short amount of time. This weapon depends on the enemy you just glory killed; for example, a small enemy provides you with a frost grenade that temporarily freezes all enemies hit by the blast radius. Another example would be a large, bloated demon (very similar to Doom’s Mancubus) that provides you with a twin gatling gun upon glory-killing him. Small enemies take only one bar of your glory-kill-meter, larger enemies take up to three bars.There’s also Doom Eternal-like resource management, all be it to a lesser extend. Killing enemies with the Katana drops ammo, killing enemies with guns drops health. Additionally, killing stuff also fills your glory-kill-meter. However, there are also respawning pickups within the combat arenas, so you don’t have to rely on this mechanic all the time – you just have to be mobile and run around a lot to get refills.I’ll make this one short: The story is mostly forgettable. There’s a small returning cast of characters from previous games, but the whole plot is rather… I don’t know, serviceable? It keeps you motivated for your main objective at least.There’s also quite a lot of (short) cutscenes throughout the campaign, mostly at the beginning and the end of a level, or when a new enemy gets introduced. I don’t find these distracting or anything like that; they are mostly well-made and keep the story somewhat stiched together.I don’t think any of this is particularly bad, it’s just not very good either. Personally though, I don’t need a lot of story in this kind of FPS anyway, since I  think the gameplay is ultimately what makes for a good experience here.What else is there to say? I do understand some of the criticism surrounding the game. Yes, SW3 is extremely linear, and very short (my playthrough took me a little over 4 hours on the medium skill). Yes, I do think that there’s a valid point in saying that 45€ (or whatever it’s in your region) is quite a lot of money for such a short experience. For me personally though, it’s not about the game time; it’s about how much fun I had during that time. A 3 hour movie is not automatically better then say, you know, a 1,5 hour movie, right?Other than that, I’d like to mention that I’ve encountered a few irritating bugs. Nothing major or even game-breaking, but there was just some weirdness going on from time to time (“jank” like sometimes when I got hit I was flying around the arena like a baseball). Oh and there are some technical twerks to keep in mind (e.g. the “typical” UE4 stuttering, most likely due to some sort of on-the-fly shader compilation; cutscenes are just video files that only fill up 16:9 space which leads to some odd visual glitches on ultrawides).So, would I recommend Shadow Warrior 3? Yeah, I guess… but you have to keep expectations in check. The game is very short, there’s no denying that. The gameplay can get somehow repetitive, true. The story is blant, Lo Wang’s jokes are immature as ever and there is some cringe here and there, sure. But, all in all, I had a very enjoable time. The gameplay is just really good, it’s fun blasting through a horde of weird looking demon-things, moving through the environments at high-speed, quick-swapping weapons and slicing a few fodder enemies on the way. Is it worth the assigned price tag? For me, that’s hard to judge. As mentioned above, I think it’s just wrong to define a game’s value by its playtime. For me personally it was worth the money, but I do understand that some people may have different opinions on that.All in all, Shadow Warrior 3 doesn’t do anything new or special, but what’s there (gameplay-wise) makes for a good, fast-paced FPS that’s just fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game. I loved it a lot. Takes a lot from Doom Eternal, but I think they have a fresh take on some things. Played on hardest difficulty, but do note that I came from Doom Eternal (Nightmare)  and Ultrakill (Violent) so I am quite experienced.The glory kill is changed to a meter that fills up so you can insta-kill any enemy you want, as well as granting you an OP weapon for a limited time. The great thing about this is that you make decisions on what enemy to glory-kill based on the perks they give when you kill them, almost like a more fleshed out version of the chainsaw in Doom 2016 or crucible in Eternal.The "chainsaw" is your katana: with an inexpensive upgrade, you can use it to gain ammo from fodder enemies quickly, and instead does not put you into an animation like in Eternal. This can be a good thing as some people may not like watching a cutscene every 15 seconds to regain ammo. Health and Ammo are more scarce: they are given to you in smaller amounts and you tend to be running low on weapons much more quickly, forcing quick-swapping and constantly rotating weapons to be more ammo efficient till you find the next fodder enemy. The enemy and level design in this game is amazing. There are super unique enemies with some have certain weak spots that are very intuitive and easy to figure out. My personal favorite is the Slinky Jakku because it looks so goofy, and the glory kill weapon is pretty strong. The levels and backdrops are fantastic and super scenic. You can tell there is a lot of care and detail put into the levels and it shows. I am torn on the grapple hook. One one hand, yay! grapple hook! It's always a fun addition to have. On the other, It's pretty lackluster. The grapple hook has a strange swinging animation where you kind of just float around, as well as not being able to grapple to heavy enemies. So i barely used it for combat other than getting out of tough situations using the grapple points. Just didn't feel that good to use. Maybe one day I'll return to the game and force myself to use grapple hooks on the fodder enemies for more health, ammo, etc. The levels are difficult but fun, fair, and challenging. It's rare for a game nowadays to tune difficulty in a tight way but they managed to do it here. My only problem with the levels is the platforming segments could have been a tad more challenging: ghostrunner and titanfall both had wallrunning challenges (moreso the former) which were very engaging to me. SW3 comes close, but doesn't quite land the mark with some areas just being "run, then shoot yellow thing". Some bullet hell segments would have been interesting, not unlike the last level in ghostrunner. Additionally, sometimes the terrain can be a bit buggy and refuse to clamber, especially during arena fights. About the length - playing this on hardcore difficulty, each combat encounter was super exhausting and i frequently had to take breaks to breathe. That being said, I still completed the game within 7ish hours. Pretty short. But Titanfall 2's campaign is about this length too, and I don't see anyone complaining. Additionally, many of these players don't stick around for the multiplayer either - I've seen the server count. It does not lie. I'd honestly rather have this quality and polish in a game, at the cost of understaying its welcome. For those who have felt the game was too short and played on med-low difficulty, I implore you to try a harder difficulty. It'll be just as fresh and exciting watching yourself get more skilled at the game. All that being said, I got this game pretty late into release. On sale, dirt cheap. Maybe it was much worse back then, but now it's more than worth it's (on sale) asking price, having a survival mode and even a NG+, several difficulty options, yada yada. Buy the game if you like shooters (especially Doom Eternal, Ultrakill, Metal: Hellsinger, etc), because that review score is not indicative of its quality. One thing to note for ultrawide users, is that the game is Vert-, meaning it's not properly implemented and WILL mess up the FOV. I hope the devs fix this and implement proper ultrawide support.

_childDocuments_.review: On grounds of "cultural appropriation" (which the concept itself is ridiculous bullcrap and doesn't even exist anyway), Devolver Digital / Flying Wild Hog decided that it was fit to change a voice actor who had been doing his job perfectly. On this review, I'm going to go on several points to dissect and analyze the absolute idiocy and hypocrisy of this development decision.1) They decided that it was "cultural appropriation" (again, the concept itself already doesn't exist, but I'm dissecting it for the proof of their own lack of knowledge about their own headcanon) for a white dude to voice act a fictional asian character. But, their reasoning doesn't even fit the "definition" of cultural appropriation that's been presented on the internet. "Cultural appropriation[1][2] is the inappropriate or unacknowledged adoption of an element or elements of one culture or identity by members of another culture or identity". Voice acting a fictitious character doesn't fall under this umbrella. This is not someone who is being a ♥♥♥♥ and imitating an asian voice to ridicule an asian person in real life, this is fiction and the art of voice acting for f's sake. People who had this train of thought seriously need to touch grass and return to reality.2) We've set aside the cultural appropriation fallacy. We come to the point that, they terminated the contract of a voice actor who had been doing a good job, and not because of the virtue of his voice acting skill, but purely because of his skin color. Yes, they've let go of him just because he was a white dude, and how do I know you'd ask, because the best part is that they've said this exact thing themselves!This is blatant racism and the best part is that nobody is batting an eye for it. If it was an asian person who was voice acting a white character, or an african american person voice acting character of whatever other ethnicity, and they got changed for the exact same reason, people would burn the globe to get justice for it, and the best part is that it wouldn't even happen in the first place. But because the voice actor is a white dude, it's somehow okay? And it's somehow not considered racism? I'll go on a leg to say that if the opposite was true, valve would sack the game off off Steam, and it would count as a crime in certain parts of the world (LIKE U S FREAKING A), but somehow what we have on our hands doesn't count as a crime. Good equality, good "progressiveness".3) We're over the point that they fired a dude because he was white. The person who they hired to voice act in place of him? He's an american with "korean" ethnicity, voice acting a character of "chinese" origin. So, let me get this straight. They thought they were doing wrong by "cultural appropriation on fictitious person", so they decided to fix that by confusing two completely different asian nationalities/cultures, because in their point of view it probably "looks or sounds the same"? This is akin to some person confusing Nelson Mandela with Kony, or Jackie Chan with Kim Jong Un. To all the people whose feelings were hurt by "cultural appropriation" or whatever, I dare ask; is this not your actual TEXTBOOK racism? It actually is! Imagine being so stupid, the people who actually thought this was a good idea and decided to do this; in order to fix a non-existent virtual problem, they've committed actual racism on two different cases. It's ironic on so many levels. And yeah, again, this is somehow still allowed.I've given it the extra leeway and played this game from start to finish. As a player who've played every shadow warrior game from it's classical roots until today, I have to say this has been objectively the weakest of the franchise ever. The gameplay consists of boring corridor shooter separated by segments of awkward on-rails platforming. It's just arena after arena after arena, the locations are uninspiring, the dialogue and the plot have taken an all-time low nosedive into negative quality. And the game is pissingly short. IT'S ACTUALLY SHORTER THAN SHADOW WARRIOR CLASSIC, and this is no lie nor exaggeration. Also less fun / interesting too, on today's tech and budget. Just check HowLongToBeat to see for yourself if you even doubt. So the big money bros at the top of the hierarchy, looked at Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal and thought to themselves "look, that game has that cacodemon, and that character has a hook that he can shoot to do parkouring, obviously those are what makes a game good, so let's just copy the same thing, it'll definitely make our own game automatically good!" So they just decided to add an enemy called Laser Shogun (which is so similar to cacodemon down to the "glory kill" animation), and give Lo Wang a swinging hook, and thought that their game would turn out alright in the end.And in reality, the game has even less customization value / upgrades than Shadow Warrior 1. Tbh people who thought "looter shooter bad herp derp" about the previous game are left with nothing to play. There is nothing here, no replay value, no good story nor one-liners, no precious character interactions, no nothing.At the end section of Shadow Warrior 2, Lo Wang teaming up with Zilla resulted in hilarious conversations where I chuckled every time no matter how many times I played, and so you would have thought that the same synergy would continue in Shadow Warrior 3 since they are in teamwork there. I haven't cracked a single smile the whole time I was playing through it. Not one. The game is completely devoid of humor and soul. I don't understand what's happening, but people who don't even completely understand what PC is or what it means, is somehow brought up to make decisions, and they ruin and suck the soul out of everything 100% of the time. tl;dr / final verdict: The developers are involved in racism, the game is somehow accepted by Valve; the gameplay is sickeningly and objectively boring and short. It's the worst shooter I've played in the decade, it's actually worse than Duke Nukem Forever. I've wasted my precious time playing it. Why does this game even exist? No money to Devolver Digital from me, from this point on.

_childDocuments_.review: A good twist on the new generation of FPS combat that DOOM Eternal created.The movement, weapons, and resource management are all really well done with a new knockback move similar in usage to the blood punch from DOOM Eternal for creating space. A new way of gaining ammo via sword slicing rather than a chainsaw allows for some satisfying melee kills along with its upgrade to add elemental effects to your slices; as a trade off however, it lacks the breathing room and full resupply the chainsaw provided.Enemies are rather spammy compared to Eternal (played only on hardest difficulty so maybe not as much on lower) melee enemies are fast and can catch a player rapid dashing around an arena, lots of AOE attacks and area denial making it difficult for the player to casually circle strafe enemies without thinking. Only enemy that doesn't add a good flow to combat is a drill monkey demon that for 75% of its time being alive is underground with no way to damage it, meaning you have to wait for them to pop up to damage them at all unlike Marauders who can still have splash damage dealt to them and can be dealt with pretty quickly.A new glory kill system thats less about healing and more about utilising an enemies organs as a weapon. You fill up a resource bar through killing enemies that eventually allows you to glory kill any enemy and use their unique "gore tool". There is some balance issues since some gore tools are better more often than others (especially the 3 that provide AOE damage) but nonetheless they all have their uses and quirks and add a unique dynamic to combat encounters.The campaign length is short with a story thats not really interesting besides the spectacle of taking down a giant dragon, the voice lines for Wang are absolutely awful with an amateur voice actor that has a terrible range, the lines he says are far too frequent and unfunny (think of the most obvious joke for anything and thats what will be said), the supporting cast is forgettable and bland.The new survival mode and chapter select adds a lot of replayability to a rather short game if you care about the whole "git gud" side of games but if not theres no real reason to replay.I've encountered some bugs with only 1 gamebreaking bug on survival that just crashes the game, forfeiting your run but besides that a lot of them are just aesthetic rather than interrupting gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Very short, super fun, but very short. 6.7 hours in, I've completed the game, finished every in-game challenge, and gotten all but one achievement (collecting upgrade orbs, which is more tedious than fun unless you like collectable hunting). I think the story length is fine, but it would've been nice to have some obscure achievements to go after, maybe more weapon upgrades unlocked through something other than collectables, or actual side missions.As for what is here, story is dumb fun, combat feels pretty great (it's a Doom clone rather than a Borderlands clone this time, but it works), graphics are beautiful, and regardless of whether or not you think a voice actor change was needed, I think Lo Wang's new VA does a great job and comfortably carries the role.If you want more Shadow Warrior and are okay with the short duration, I can recommend picking this up (maybe on sale).If you're new to the series, I *highly* recommend playing 1 and 2 first, they more than hold up today.

_childDocuments_.review: So...Shadow Warrior 3...Let me address the major complaints I've seen causing it to have mixed reviews:-More like Shadow Warrior 1 than 2Yeah...Shadow Warrior 2 was an experiment, and one that might have worked well...but there's nothing wrong with going back to your roots then expanding on thoseIf you want more Shadow Warrior 2, then you're gonna be upsetIf you want more Shadow Warrior 1, you'll likely to have a good time-the lengthYeah, it's pretty damn shortI beat it in one session on the lowest difficulty...but frankly, the time I spent in it was a blastAnd I'd rather have a small time that is a hell of a thrill than 100 hours that are a sloughQuality over quantity, every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ timeIt's why I STILL recommend DOOM 2016 and Titanfall 2 campaignsAs for how that quality is:The guns feel good to use, the shotgun especiallyI found myself quick swapping oftenThe sword is a nice filler pieceI found the fact that the guns automatically reload after swapping away from them an amazing bit to keep the flow goingThe one thing I absolutely hated was the execution animationsWhile I appreciate the fact that it is less a finisher and more of a "build it up, knock them down and then get a boost for doing so" they lacked the visceral feel to go along with the visuals, and frankly, I genuinely hate the ones that are on the earlier enemiesSome of the ones later on are better, but still not greatAll in all, I much preferred this over Shadow Warrior 2, tbhThis game was a thrill ride from beginning to end, despite how short it wasNot as good as Shadow Warrior 1 though, but still REALLY damn good

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few points that I will like to discuss before you make a decision to buy the game.PROS :Gameplay is the star of the show. Its fluid and The game is basically an arena-based shooter greatly inspired by games like Doom Eternal and Quake combined with humor, katanas, and guns, well all sorts of guns. The visuals are impressive. The animation during the cutscenes and the lip-syncing is pretty good as well.There is quite a good number of enemy varieties that you will find in the game.CONS:Newcomers to the series may overlook this but the replacement of the Original voice actor to a new one was maybe uncalled for. The long-time followers of the series loved Jason Liebrecht, the voice actor for Lo Wang has been replaced by Mike Moh, and the reason being that Devolver wanted to "correct their mistake" of not casting Asian actors.The game is optimized but there are some concerns on the PC. I experienced hard crashes multiple times during my playthrough. I was able to fix this though by verifying the Integrity of the local files via steam. The reason why I mentioned this is because this is not some development fault but something that you need to be aware of if you're buying the game. Now, I played the game locked at 60 FPS since my game recorder was set to 60 FPS too, however, when the game transcends to a cutscene from live gameplay this is quite a bit of stutter witnessed a lot of times. Also, on some combat-heavy sequences where there was quite a bit of enemy on the screen, you can witness some FPS drops but it's not game-breaking.This is an arena-based shooter which means you need to keep moving around. But there were times when I felt I was being restricted. Your grappling hook and the wall run mechanics are not something you can use at your free will. There are certain points when you need to aim at, or cling to while executing these moves. In the heat of the battle, failing to land on these surfaces will result in some unwarranted deaths.These arenas may look fun to spend time in but then the element of drag kicks in. Sometimes these segments can drag for more than 10 minutes and towards the latter part of the game you tend to try and deal damage against bullet sponge enemies.Circling back to the voice actor and the dialogue choices can be a bit cringy. Trust me when I compared the game to Deadpool because you will see similarities here. But the issue is, in Deadpool where Ryan Reynolds has the element of spark coupled with some well-placed humor that will genuinely make you smile, here the humor is a culmination of some cheesy punchlines and some segment of Karaoke.The entire narrative is revealed to you in the first 5-10 minutes of the game. There is nothing really special in terms of any plot twists that we witnessed in the previous games. So, personally, I stopped caring about the story and was more engrossed in gameplay.The game is pretty short. You can actually complete the game in like 4-5 hours and then that's it. There is no New Game Plus mode.Another thing that I need to point out is sometimes when the game transitions itself into a cutscene - Subtitles get activated without any notification and even though I had them turned off.VERDICT :Well, when I consider the game as an overall package in terms of its fun factor, and when I question myself, Did I have fun playing Shadow Warrior 3? The answer is a resounding Yes ! The cutscenes are well placed and explain the narrative pretty well. This is topped off by some good lip-syncing too. The dialogs,could have been better though. The gameplay like I said is the star of the show and the place where the game shines. Even though the movement can be a bit restrained but you can sense which point of interaction you need to grapple to, or where to land for a wall run. The graphics are just beautiful to look at even though initially, I had witnessed some choppy segments and FPS issues. Overall the game is good but it's also short with no reason to replay the game again as there is no New Game Plus.Considering all these factors, I will still recommend this game but will suggest that on Steam you add it to your Wish list and buy once there is a price drop because the game is overall a good, fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the combat arenas in the game crashes every single time for me on a windows 11 rig with a 5800x and rtx 2080, and 32 GB RAM. Game is, unfortunately, literally unplayable for me until a patch releases so it isn't recommended for that reason alone.The game is also rife with typical UE4 stutter. I'd also like to say that it's generally disappointing to me that they ditched their internal engine in favor of UE4. I get why they did it, I'm sure it makes perfect business sense, but it's frustrating to see the increasing homogenization of tools in the industry. In some ways, I think Shadow Warrior 2 is a better looking game, at least in terms of being artistically consistent. This could be caused by a number of things though, so the blame isn't exclusively on the tools used.First impressions otherwise: moderate disappointment. I really liked Shadow Warrior 2013. I thought Shadow Warrior 2 was surprisingly decent considering how much it was trend chasing. Shadow Warrior 3 so far just...doesn't feel refined enough, while simultaneously feeling like some mechanics are too refined for the sake of handholding. Seriously, why even bother putting a grappling hook in a game if it basically plays itself when you use it? Why have these parkour segments if wallrunning is completely autonomous? Why are choices like these increasingly common in modern games? Jank is tolerable, hell even preferred, if there is mechanical freedom behind it. Shadow Warrior 3 feels like it was designed in a way where only obscene levels of polish would make it better...so like a lot of modern games. Executions fall flat and they all take  too long for the flow of the game, Enemies run largely in straight lines at you and are incredibly easy to dodge, hazards lack a punchy feel both visually and in audio that makes them more boring to use than anticipated. The systems in the game do not meld well together and in many cases don't stand up on their own. It feels like this needed more time in the oven. I think a good game is in here, and who knows, maybe these criticisms only stand up in the first couple hours of the game.Because of my forced low playtime, I will leave the criticisms at that. I hope to see this game patched up, and I'm so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tired of saying this about almost every new release.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 is just Shadow Warriors 1 trying to be Doom Eternal. Shadow Warriors 2 is a decent game and a decent enough sequel to Shadow Warriors 1 done in the span of 3 years with new mechanics and systems in place. And honestly it should had just stayed in the direction 2 was going.  The fact that people say 3 is better than 2 is ridiculous cause at the very least I don't get pre-rendered cutscenes that seem to crap out every start and end during the middle of a level or the start of every level. And it just feels kind of jarring.I get the feeling that the past 6 years this sequel had been in development they couldn't figure out what kind of direction the game should go in with considering  they were probably looking at how well Doom Eternal sold and wanted to follow the trend. So whatever work they probably have already done before the initial teaser trailer got scrapped to appeal to the audience that got hooked on Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal and became the diet boomer shooter audience. Despite the fact that Shadow Warrior 1 came before Doom 2016 and carries many of the elements that late 90s early 2000s shooters so bangin in the first place. The decision  for this change probably was also fueled by the uneccessarily unfair comparisons drawn between the titles. And that is why I make it a habit never to read review articles from gaming journos because they do this all the time.SW3 also has more directors than it honestly needed, and the director Michał Szustak has done a pretty decent work on his own with the past three games he's worked on alongside Pawel. But there probably should had been a point where Pawel's decision with 3 wasn't made with more foresight in mind of the audience they had already achieved with SW1 and 2. SW3's identity has been cemented as the Doom Eternal Clone rather than taking what was good about 1 and 2 and putting them together.  Shadow Warrior 1 and 2 were also about style and combat efficiency. 3 lacks this component just to focus on the action. Which while there is some decent action, you find yourself relying less on the sword than you do in 1 and 2. At least with 1 and 2 it was not only a practical weapon for when you ran out of ammo, but it was a powerful weapon in of itself. Regardless, SW3 found itself with a pacing has found itself sliced up like dragon sashimi, with a story as half-baked as you can expect as it tries to follow the established canon of 1 and 2 with little of the substance and zero of the context. We don't even get much information about the dragon outside of the tibids of its origin in 1 and 2 without having it explicitly known until the end of 2. Overall: Flying Wild Hog needs to go back and retrace their steps because they missed something along the way. If there ever would be a Shadow Warrior 4, it should probably do the same thing Postal 4 did and ignore 3 entirely, or made it some sort of fever dream ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up by Lo-Wang whose probably still in the dragon's stomach from SW2's ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 is exactly the kind of traditional shooter we all need and love. It takes a lot of inspiration from recent Doom games, but it takes the recipe and make it even better. It's been a long time since I had this much fun in a game.Everything in the game absolutely nails it. The combat gameplay is similar to latest Doom games, however the platforming gameplay is much better, not breaking the pace of the rest of the game (unlike Doom Eternal for example). The scenarios are gorgeous, the enemy designs are unique and very good-looking. Even the weapon designs stand out. The writing and presentation is something else. It's the silly over-the-top tone you'd expect from Shadow Warrior, but done better. The characters are charismatic, the game has personality, and the absurdity mixes in the action perfectly. Even the gore has been given a lot of detail, with demons losing pieces of themselves as they're shot.The game is flawless as long as it lasts, however that's its single major flaw: it doesn't last long. You can easily finish the campaign in a couple hours, and after that there's nothing. No arcade or "score-attack" modes, no multiplayer, nothing. It's not ideal but still ok for a game to be this short when there's other, more replayable content to go with it. In this case there isn't. This game would benefit a lot from an arena-like multiplayer mode, some kind of arcade mode or even better user mod/map support to give it more replayability. Because the short duration of the campaign screams for replayability.All in all, quality-wise I couldn't recommend it more. As far as no-nonsense shooters go, this game ticks all the boxes and goes above and beyond it. Solid recommendation from me. Quantity-wise though, you should go into it expecting to finish it in an afternoon or so.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:- Great gameplay that takes strong inspiration from DOOM- Great level design and arenas- A small but focused arsenal- Movement that flows so well- 6 hour length- No additional modes or difficulties upon completion- 2 solid boss fights but only 2While I strongly recommend this game I don't think it's worth the hefty price tag of 49.99 usd. Unless you are just a big fan that can't wait like I am then by all means go for it! The game is a large amount of fun and a vast improvement from Shadow Warrior 2. For one, the levels are fully made and filled with insanely fun arenas that reminded me of Doom Eternal (which I oddly enough found this game way more fun than that game), and no more elemental weakness/strengths. There are only 6 weapons in the game (if you don't count the gore weapons) which sounds bad on paper, but it helps keep everything nice and focused. It's sort of like the first one in that sense where you had a limited arsenal compared to part 2 where there was an insane amount. My one big complaint is that the game is only about 6 hours long which is incredibly short. Considering the wait I wish it was longer but the gameplay itself more than made up for it. Unfortunately there is no new game+ or new difficulty mode unlocked upon completion. So once you're done you are done. Hopefully the devs make some DLC.Storywise it's super simplistic and you don't really need to pay attention. If you're also used to the original VA for Lo Wang like I was it will take some time to get used to his new voice. It's fine but I still prefer his original.That's about it. I recommend waiting for the price to drop or for a sale. This game would have been perfect at 30 bucks or 40 at most.

I personally prefer less content but with a lot of affort put in it so I love this game.Also important improvement: no more HUGELY bullet-sponge enemies on high difficulty like it was in SW1 and Hard Reset,However it's replayability is like a pretty decent movie: you definitely will rewatch|replay it but on a long term.Long story short — give it a try.Read this if you are fan of SW1 and/or SW2:Aside from plot, voice actor, secrets and some cut katana features from previous games this one does everything A LOT better then SW1 and SW2:- No borderlands;- On highest difficulty you actually get fair difficulty: no bullet-sponge enemies like in SW1 and Hard Reset;- Katana is usefull if you play smart but not over-the-top like it was in SW1: almost every weapon aside katana were useless on high difficulty. In SW3 it actually feels like katana from SW Classic but put into the action if you put upgrade points to it;- Modern-DOOM-stuff like ammo and health regen after killing enemies are optional by putting them in upgrade section;- No hour-long bosses like in SW1;- You can ACTUALLY use traps and explosives;- Lots of arenas are smart;- No ♥♥♥♥♥ up secrets like it was in SW1 where you can die IMMEDIATLY after touching water;- No ♥♥♥♥♥ up IMMEDIATLY-one-shotting enemies like green abominations of SW1 and yellow cockroaches of SW2. Even "kamikadzes" just damage you and not one-shot-kill;- Simple but cool platforming that gives SW vibe of... you know... ninja with no lose of pacing;- Soundtrack is a blast like before;- A lot of real-time cool events with stunning destructions; Call-of-Duty-scripted but why is that SUDDENLY became problem?- Stunning views like before;- No boring locations. No swamps, no sewage. Game tries to change atmosphere as fast as it can and it's awesome;- Minimum fart jokes like it was in SW2.That's what I can remember for now. Devs put a lot of work affort to correct old mistakes. Even the plot is not so cringe like it was in SW2. If Devolver was not forcing 'em to change voice actor this game possibly had better appreciation.

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Absolutely beautiful scenes, character/enemy design, cinematography in cut scenes, and more. The game consists of arenas that get set up in different enviorments. I really like this concept and I think it really works for the shadow warrior style of combat, however I do wish there was more than just that. You do maneuver from arena to arena with some "parkour" but its very very basic. Honestly, you could do that parkour with your eyes closed. It's fun, but it could've been better. For example, when you wall run or grapple, you gain a ton of speed. But once you stop wall running or stop grappling, you just sort of float through the air at a fairly slow speed. It makes wall running and grappling feel less rewarding. That being said, everything good in the game is enough for me to look past this.Flying Wild Hog replaced the voice actor for Lo Wang for this installment of the series. I was a bit disappointed when I heard this but gave the new voice actor the benefit of the doubt. I got used to them really quickly - honestly, I don't think the old voice actor would have fit Shadow Warrior 3 very well at this point. I think the new voice actor did great. The game was also pretty short too. I heard about it being short so I savored the game over a few weeks and took my time with it. I ended up getting a good 9.4 hours of game time. This isn't bad, but I do wish it was longer. I also really,  hope that there is some kind of arena mode that adds replayability. I  to be able to play more of this game but without having to just replay the story mode. Similarly, I think some DLC would be amazing. Flying Wild Hog created absolutely stunning environments in the world of Shadow Warrior 3 and I'd like to see more of it (such as cities or more nature inspired areas). The cast of characters is really cool too and I hope this isn't the last time we get to see them.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Tight combat, similar to Doom Eternal. Weapons are fun to use.- While I don't mind the non-linear maps in Shadow Warrior 2, going back to the linear design makes SW3 a more focused experience. It's shorter than SW1 but I like this better since it's always clear where to go.Cons:- While the character and weapon upgrades seem interesting, you don't level up by killing enemies. You just have to scour the levels and do challenges for upgrade orbs. The game tells you how many orbs left in each level, but not the locations. Not a fan of that. - New Game+ forces you to play harder difficulty. Also not a fan of that.- Check points are too far apart in the levels with insta-fail sequences that can be obtuse sometimes. Definitely not a fan of that.All in all, not a bad game but it's a one-and-done experience for me.
