_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, love everything about it.If you liked the previous games and like the gun play of DOOM Eternal its perfect. The story is also good, developing Lo Wang as a character, not just being an assassin that does missions without thought. Some reviews say that Lo Wang's race changed which is false, he's still Asian and the change of voice actor is either because Flying Wild Hog said ♥♥♥♥ it, or Lo Wang's personality changed so they wanted to show that with a new voice. The game is funny sometimes, making me smile or chuckle a few times. Platforming is very fun and it isn't even a platformer? I love the movement, much faster than the previous games, I like how Lo Wang doesn't say "BOOM GOES THE BOOM STICK" every second like the 2nd game. The 7 weapons are enough, and actually have useful uses, like the SMG's are for shredding, the Outlaw is for fast heavy damage. Reloads are beautiful, and also can auto-reload when switching guns. I see the negative reviews as misleading and stupid like people saying the game is racist for voice actors changing, or that it's terrible without any other back up information. I don't like the 2nd game because it is so slow and how it tried to be Borderlands, but this game fixes it. This has the same upgrade system as the first game which is a nice addition. I don't like how Hoji doesn't turn into the mask and fly back to you like in the first game, but that's a minor nit-pick, also he does become mortal so that may be why. Animations are clunky at times also the voice acting is good but lips are not synced properly sometimes. Voice lines that Wang says are cut off during cut scenes or are interrupted by other lines, which is minor again but makes it hard to tell what he was going to say. The only big negative is how short the game is, it's honestly sad, I wish for a DLC or the game just being longer.Overall I'd say it's a 9/10 or maybe even a 10 just from how fun it truly is.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 turns back to its roots, removes unnecessary additions made to the second game, becomes linear again and steps out of being a looter shooter. It focuses much more on the action, platforming and its story which works out perfectly in its favor.I highly believe everything this game represents and does is so much better than its predecessors. It is rated unfairly mostly due to how short it is which is ridiculous since the second games story was also around the same playtime. The second reason is for some reason people liked the overcrowded mechanics of the second game. It was just a generic, very mediocre looter shooter yet people believe it is the better game.While i believe changes made to Shadow Warrior 3 is for the better. They took everything good from their earlier games and made them better.Gameplay is phenomenal. Kick-ass weapons, finishers and surprisingly fun platforming sections all add up to how enjoyable the game is. Guns are much more important now and they feel great to use.Story is much more well written, memorable and feels closer to an action movie.And for me the most important part is the lack of fillers. Every second is full of action. Sure, the developers could've stretched the game a bit more but Shadow Warrior 3 wouldn't have been what it is right now which is a throughoutly great game.If you really think the length of a game is more important than its content, skip this game. However i highly suggest anyone who enjoys linear retro shooters to give it a shot. It is an excellent little gem and is worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game in just under 8 hours on hard and I loved (almost) every second of it.Its really simple folks. Its not SW2+ If you expected another looter shooter with bullet sponge enemies that never quite got its act together you are going to be disappointed with SW3. Shadow warrior as a franchise never was a looter shooter to me and in that way I always considered SW2 to be the odd one out. SW3 to me is a return to form.Shadow warrior 3 is a glorious action FPS. Yes its clearly took some inspiration from Doom Eternal but honestly just calling it a DE clone is doing it a disservice. There are enough new components in this game to make it stand on its own. The enemies are brilliant and memorable. The weapons each fulfill a unique role, fitting certain scenarios and certain enemies better. The arena's are really fun with all the traps and attachment points for your grappling hook.The finisher system is actually an upgrade compared to DE. Enemies don't just flash when they get to low health, instead you get a finisher bar with different levels. Enemy health does not play a role, you can finish enemies at full health when its full. Small enemies require one charge while the biggest ones require three charges. This is where things get interesting since there are different pay offs for different enemy finishers. Finishing a small enemy will just take one charge and only give you health. Finishing a slightly bigger one will give you a one of item you can throw (like an ice bomb) and finishing a big enemy will give you a special weapon for a limited duration.This brings a whole different level of strategy to the game where you may want to dispose of a dangerous enemy quickly and save your finisher specifically for it. Or perhaps you prefer the icebomb for crowd control. Or maybe you are really low health so you are forced to finish a low level mob to restore health instead. It is really fun to play with this system.People shout murder because this game seems less complex. To me SW2 was a messy pile of stuff that never quite worked together. Shadow warrior 3 is streamlined and its so, so much better for it. The combat is fantastic. You have weapon combos, finisher combos, environment combos. Easy to learn hard to master fully applies here. The game is not helped by the fact it starts out way too easy (even on hard) so it really only gets to full swing about halfway into the game but when it does, oh boy. :)With that said there are definitely some rough edges.I think they are pretty well known by now. It needs additional difficulty levels. It needs a level select. It kinda needs something to make the first half of the game fun to replay. Some of the traversal sections are completely devoid of enemies, very long and therefore boring. There is a section where you slide on a piece of ice (i.e. a "vehicle" section) which is awful. Not only is it boring, its also extremely buggy. The game would be so much better if that was cut entirely. There are a lot (and I mean a lot, the beginning section is constantly interrupted with them) cut scenes that always stutter when they start playing cause the game preloads in the background at the same time. However Flying Wild Hog has been pretty great with patches and DLC's in the past so I am pretty confident some if not most of those issues will be taken care of.I love this game. If you like Action FPS give this one a whirl. Approach it with an open mind, don't expect SW2+, and you will have a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this one's a bit conflicted for sure.I'll start off with the elephant in the room: the price. The game took me about 4 hours or so to beat, and as far as I can tell, there isn't really any incentive to replay any of the game's content. So, in terms of price per hour, this game is hot garbage for sure.That being said, the game itself is excellent. It's very comparable to Doom Eternal -- fast-paced, multi-weapon arsenal, glory kills, pick-ups, pure arena-to-arena fights, etc -- and it's probably about just as good as Doom Eternal in terms of raw gameplay, so if you liked that game then you'll feel right at home with Shadow Warrior 3. All of the guns feel impactful and distinct, enemy variety is pretty good, platforming feels surprisingly satisfying, and the upgrade system is decent. And outside of the cutscenes, it's pretty much all action with no downtime which is great.Visually, the game looks pretty nice. Nothing mind-blowing in terms of the tech, but the environments are really well-made and the game never feels same-y with the zones you enter. Performance was pretty smooth on my end as well, although I would recommend using DLSS just to make sure the frames don't drop too hard when there's a lot going on (particularly towards the end of the game).Don't really have much to say about the story to be honest. It's pretty much just an excuse for the gameplay, with some hit or miss wise-cracking as you would come to expect from the Shadow Warrior games. Definitely much weaker than Shadow Warrior 1's story, but at least it doesn't have annoying Kamiko from the second game speaking every two seconds.Final verdict: an excellent game that is only really recommended from me during a deeper sale (like, 50% at least). I'm hoping they add new modes or something in future updates as well, but I would imagine if they did offer anything substantial, it will be in the form of DLC given how little content there is to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 delivers its signature humor in a fast-paced, action-packed adventure, although the game's length leaves you wanting more. In comparison to its predecessors, Shadow Warrior 2 and Shadow Warrior 1, the humor remains a consistent and enjoyable aspect of the series.The humor in Shadow Warrior 3 is infused throughout the game, with witty one-liners, hilarious banter between characters, and over-the-top comedic moments. From Lo Wang's snarky remarks to the absurd situations he finds himself in, the game doesn't shy away from embracing its tongue-in-cheek style. The humor adds a lightheartedness to the intense action and helps create a unique and memorable atmosphere.However, one downside of Shadow Warrior 3 is its relatively short duration. The game's brevity leaves you craving more of the humor and the world it creates. While the levels are well-designed and offer a mix of exploration and combat, the overall playtime might feel somewhat limited, especially for players who want a longer and more in-depth experience.When comparing Shadow Warrior 3 to its predecessors, Shadow Warrior 2 and Shadow Warrior 1, the humor remains a consistent thread across the series. Each installment successfully injects comedy into the gameplay, and fans of the previous games will find familiar elements in Shadow Warrior 3. However, it's worth noting that the earlier titles, particularly Shadow Warrior 2, had a more expansive scope with open-world elements and a greater emphasis on side quests and exploration. In contrast, Shadow Warrior 3 focuses more on hand-crafted levels and a tighter narrative, sacrificing some of the open-world aspects found in its predecessor.Despite its shorter duration, Shadow Warrior 3 manages to deliver a satisfying dose of humor that fans of the series will appreciate. The game retains the comedic charm of its predecessors, even if it doesn't provide the same level of content. Ultimately, while the brevity of the game may leave you wanting more, the humor in Shadow Warrior 3 adds an entertaining and enjoyable layer to the intense action-packed gameplay.Truly enjoyed the series and would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all 3 Shadow Warrior games and this is what I think -Seen lots of sentimental fanboys who complain that this game is not like Shadow Warrior 2. Devolver Digital and Flying Wild Hog tried a different approach and I'm OK with that.BUT WHY IS THIS GAME GOOD?- This game takes 6-8 hours to beat (10 hours at best). It's short, action packed, super fun to play. Like a roller coaster ride, get in, enjoy, then get off. If you don't wanna invest too much time in games this is your mojo.- Shadow Warrior 2 had lots of repetitive side missions which seldom had any story or value tbh. You literally had to go to same areas and kill same enemies over and over again. Dunno why some fans love these repetitive tasks so much but for me they were boring as hell.In Shadow Warrior 3, The devs completely removed side missions and that's a good thing.- The traversal in Shadow Warrior 3 is the best in all of the franchise. You have a grappling hook which you can use for both combat and movement. You can swing from valley to valley and various floating platforms, wall run through mountains without the risk of falling to your death and so on. Also, Wang walks faster, jumps higher. The overall pacing is faster than two previous titles.- The devs have introduced another fun gameplay mechanic called 'GORE WEAPONS'. You have a finisher meter in this game, when it fills (it fills very fast, don't worry) you can execute any foe and use their body parts as powerful weapons (for a certain period).For example, some foes have a hammer for a hand, if your finisher meter is full, you can break their hand and use the hammer to kill other foes.Some foes have an icy brain. After executing them with a finisher move you can use their brains as ice bombs and freeze even the strongest wave of enemies at ease. Sounds fun? It should, cuz it really is fun.- The jokes and memes carry over to this game from it's previous title, so don't worry. Fan favorite loud mouth ninja Lo Wang is still the same, plus another returning character from Shadow Warrior 1.- Many people are complaining about adding fewer weapons from the previous 2 titles. But hear me out first. Are 70+ weapons really necessary in a game which in only 6-8 hours long? It's a short game, so there are few weapons, simple. There are other fun factors which I have stated above.So that's all folks.

_childDocuments_.review: The ONLY reason(s) I would not recommend this game is mainly from the amount of time it takes to complete the game, on normal it took me FOUR, yes only FOUR, HOURS to beat, there are only 11 levels (chapters) in the game and they're all relatively short. I know making a game is HARD and to live up to the name Shadow Warrior in the sense of humor, and content SW3 hits a few nails and misses others.    The new VA's for Lo-Wang and Zilla are alright, not too bad, there actually a few times where I got an honest laugh out of their lines, I would honestly ignore anyone who put #NotMyWang in their review, I know that FWH was just trying to have a better image (even though SW is NOWHERE near a PC game series, and changing the VA's was kinda dumb) but the VA change can be honestly overlooked. The mix of gun to sword play is really enjoyable, the game has a few systems in play to make you switch between your sword and guns, which isn't all that bad, I honestly feel as though that the gun system is a thing they got right. The gore weapons were a nice touch as well,  my only gripe about them is that they're timed and there's no upgrade that extends the time (I'll get to the upgrade system), other than that the gore weapons are nice enough, they're all unique, and all do something different (instead of being carbon copies that just look different).   The upgrade system is a missed nail, the upgrade system in SW2 was nice, but SW2 feels like a completely different game, the upgrade system in SW3 is more attuned to the original reboot title, minus the money, the upgrade system is done completely in points, both Character and Weapons. The only thing is each weapon and tree on the character tree only has 3 upgrades per item, totaling 30 upgrades (12 character and 18 weapon ). Character tree has 4 different skills to go down, none of which include anything for gore weapons, either to allow the player to hold onto them or to extend use time. Instead the tree has environmental damage boosts, pickup boosts, base character boosts (25 more health, health regen, and I honestly can't remember the other upgrade in this tree, I'm sorry). It feels as though the upgrade system was a last minute addition or a last minute cut, which could very well be the situation. The weapon upgrades are okay, but there are no alternate firing mode upgrades, which I liked, but just because I liked it doesn't mean it has to be in every title, so I can let it slide.   The game has nice visuals, music is good (which is always a big thing in my book) but the story feels rushed and it cuts from one place to the next almost randomly, my best example is the opening, it almost feels like it was supposed to be longer instead of just the one mission, but it just cuts to Lo-Wang and Zilla walking up to the sanctuary with Hoji's mask. I like the Shadow Warrior series, but this game feels a little rushed, but my only HUMONGOUS gripe is the amount of time it takes to play through it once, other than that the game is REALLY fun; a good old fashioned momentum shooter like Doom, Blood, and Duke Nukem' just to name a few, and that may of been FWH plan for SW3, back to the roots, hopefully the game will have story DLC to expand it, to give the game some replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Shadow Warrior game yet. It took everything SW 2013 and SW 2 did wrong, and fixed it, and doubled down on everything those two games did right (mixed in a little DOOM Eternal) perfecting the formula. This game's combat is great, the best it's been in the series. It's incredibly faced paced and chaotic, but also thoughtful and well designed. To address some common complaints:-The new voice actors for Lo Wang and Zilla are great. Mike Moh sounds almost exactly like Jason Liebrecht, and if Flying Wild Hog hadn't said anything, I wouldn't have noticed. I understand having preferences, but the controversy surrounding the voice acting has been overblown.-The lack of looter shooter elements is a good thing. Shadow Warrior is a boomer shooter franchise. They felt out of place in Shadow Warrior 2. It made Shadow Warrior 2 unfocused, and there was so much loot I honestly didn't care about it. It was overwhelming. And the open ended, procedurally generated levels felt random, with tedious side quests. This game is an improvement over SW 2 in every way. -Go back and play Shadow Warrior 2013. That game suffered from bullet sponge tank enemies, a lack of resources, procedurally generated item pickups, and an overuse on sword and magic (the sword really wasn't that prominent in Shadow Warrior 1997, remember. It was basically there for when you ran out of ammo. The core of the game was till a first person SHOOTER). The guns felt useless. The enemies took FOREVER to kill enemies. And you were constantly running out of ammo. It was impossible to max your upgrades on a single playthrough. Bosses especially were just mindlessly strafing around an arena shooting for 5-10 minutes and healing until they died. Shadow Warrior 3 actually made every gun viable, and have a purpose, while keeping the sword viable as well with its own purpose. It encourages you to use every weapon available. -Length of a game does not determine the quality of a game. Yes, this game is only 5-6 hours long. But it doesn't need to be longer. Its a fast, fun, chaotic FPS. That's all it needs to be. Not every game needs to be this 15, 30, 60 hour epic. It comes, does its thing, doesn't overstay its welcome, and leaves. And its GOOD. There are so many 15, 30, 60 hour games that I play that I NEVER even finish because they are boring, or drawn out, or flat our aren't good. I don't worry about that with Shadow Warrior 3. I get a great 6 hour experience, that I will feel inclined to playthrough again.  Play through it twice, now I get 12 hours out out. DOOM Eternal is only a 15 or so hour game, but I like that game so much I've logged over 210 hours in it. Length has no bearing on quality. Though it could be improved in the replayibilty aspect. My only negatives is that some of the challenges seem bugged, making completing some challenges needlessly difficult. And it NEEDS a level select like DOOM has. Being able to go back and play certain levels and arenas again will do a lot for its replayability, especially once you fully max yourself out. A lot of the fun from DOOM Eternal comes from going back and replaying arenas and challenges with a maxed out Doomguy, and Shadow Warrior 3 needs that too.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 is an enjoyable experience. The combat loop flows incredibly well and the platforming sections do not overshadow the entire game. It is more or less glitch free, with only a couple things that could potentially make the game seem buggy.It does however have many stutters which may be related to loading issues.The lack of a mission select, NG+ mode, or difficulty higher than Hard is something to be wary of though. There is little in the way of keeping the player around after their first playthrough.In addition to this, some levels are very poorly constructed, leaving lots of open space, but having that open space blocked off by invisible walls and kill planes, which is not enjoyable.If you liked Shadow Warrior 1, you will enjoy this game. Hoping there is more substance added to this in the future, because no mission select really hurts.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shadow Warrior franchise is weird. Each game that comes out is not a direct gameplay sequel, but something entirely different each time.As a fan of the series with over 100 hours spent playing Shadow Warrior 2 I would say this game is not as replayable. But as a Doom clone I would say it was good. This game is very short, but its constant combat kept me in. For the price, it is probably not worth it unless you are a big fan. Wait for a sale to justify the length of the game.I played Doom Eternal, but I never finished it. I finished this game however. They are both very similar but the action in this one kept me in more. The Katana felt very badass to play with, and they actually made guns viable in this one. Switching to melee and gunplay was seamless and effective all the way through.My only complaint would be the story and the length. They completely don't talk about the characters in Shadow Warrior 2. Where is Kamiko? She and a bunch of other characters were integral to the story. This game felt like they wanted to reboot the entire story. The new voice actor honestly, did a good job. I was barely reminded in game that they changed the voice actor because the new one did a pretty good job. Lo Wang has a lot of more lines in this game and talks constantly. Which is a welcome change, I always like more unique dialogue in games.Overall a 7/10, a good game overall but just lacks in the replayability and length department. Wait for a sale to justify the games length.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't had this much fun with a video game in a long time. In the meantime I've played through the campaign several times on Playstation and now started on PC and it just doesn't get boring, which is why I really like going back to the game.I love that Shadow Warrior humor. The game also features well-written characters and a well-directed story. Setting and atmosphere are great, levels and enemies are visually impressive and both the gunplay and the occasional parkour passages are a lot of fun. Above all, I cannot praise the soundtrack enough, it fits perfectly and is really fantastic.It's all the more a pity that you can't upgrade to the deluxe version afterwards. I bought the Shadow Warrior Trilogy Bundle for Steam and unfortunately it only contains the Standard Edition. Hopefully the upgrade will be possible later.If you don't mind the shorter game length and prefer a well staged, consistently entertaining, action-packed experience rather than an open world filled with never-ending boring checklist content, I can highly recommend Shadow Warrior 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Great addition to the series. Overall, solid game that plays a little like doom. But, the game definitely has some downsides. Reviews mentioned 8-10 hours of gameplay for the campaign, but honestly it took about 5 total on the hardest setting. There is some choppy bits and stuttering during cut scenes, but that is over shadowed by the outstanding core game play (you'll need to have updated drivers or the game stutters as well). Story is a continuation of SW2 so those who haven't played the series will be a little lost.  That being said, I really enjoyed this game and look forward to any future updates FWH bring to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: If you liked DOOM Eternal and don't mind a game that imitates it, but watered down and don't mind cringy humour, get this game, have an open mind and enjoy it.I got this game on a sale. Though after completing it, I would have paid full price, against my expectations. More than two years later, I doubt many will care (there are just too many games out there), but still:I personally loved my time with this game, despite it's many flaws. I personally see it as a sort of "diamond in the roughs" product. I have one playthrough only, and that is on hard. What I 'think' turns most people away from this game:- The juvenile-cringy humour (though I personally feel that being the case with all the SW games, yes, including the DOS-Originals on the build engine).- It being a DOOM-eternal rip-off- It still being a bit buggy, even after two years.- The afternoon-cartoon story, that is predictable from 10 miles away.I agree with all of these points. Still, I loved almost every minute. Here's why:- Despite SW3 being an inferior copy of DOOM Eternal (having played through DOOM Eternal including the DLCs), I felt like it demanded less strategy than DOOM, while still giving comparable adrenaline-rushes. That is fine with me, since I am not a hardcore DOOM Eternal player. You don't have weakpoints nor are you forced to use certain weapons (let alone weapon mods, you den't get that in SW3) for certain enemies. Regardless, you benefit from using certain weapons, against certain enemies.- The envirmonments I found gorgeous. Imo the art-direction and the enemy-design deserves a lot of credit. Especially considering, that everything is so fast, you barely get to look at things for more than a second before it's gone.- The jump 'n' run segments were repetitive, but a lot of fun and broke up the shooting nicely.- I felt the short lenght to be  positive. Just when I felt like "Ok, I think this is gonna become stale..." I had two more arenas to blast through and then, the game threw the endboss at me.- The way the weapons and the movement feel is very stylish and feels cool to pull off. Despite, again, being inferior to DOOM Eternal. Regarding the identity crisis the SW-reboots had:I played the other two reboot games and understand the problems with a series reboot that does not know what it wants to be / just chases trends. But, I personally just enjoyed SW 1 + 2 for what they were. I did the same with SW 3. But I understand, that many people are angry and / or disapointed, especially those that started on SW 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Take this one with a grain of salt. I mostly take issue with the visuals and gunplay, and I haven't finished the game out of sheer disgust for those. If you happen to be more tolerant of these subjective flaws or just have a different taste to mine, Shadow Warrior 3 might appeal to you. I can see how someone could have fun with its, at times, excellent pacing and... okay, nothing else, I suppose.Shadow Warrior 3 is bad and I don't respect Flying Hog or Devolver. Devolver pretends to belong, putting on their best pro-consumer mask while quietly selling out to Epic. Not in this case, just wanted to point out how disingenuous their friendly act is. Hogs couldn't remaster classic Shadow Warrior properly. These outsourcers outsourced it, it seems. As for Shadow Warrior 3, it's a shamelessly derivative slop that that made me warm up to its dumbass looter shooter of a predecessor, which is quite a feat. There's plenty of stuff one can dislike this thing for, starting with the stuttering, the voice acting scandal, or the fact that my hours include most of the game. Besides, the muffled sounds weapons and explosions make here are akin to farting in a cake, which is already debilitating for a shooter, but its physically repulsive appearance takes said cake, plants its face in it, and blows bubbles. What they did to the visuals used to be a form of humiliating punishment called "tarring and feathering".You all know about it from cartoons. And the cartoon aesthetic looks cool from afar, it could be appropriate if, like before, at least a modicum of restraint was exercised. The graphics seems to be appealing on stills and the backdrops are fine, but the rest of the syrup gave me diabetes. The sugary broth is too damn rich! This game is vomiting its insides on the screen and barely anything is discernible. It produces a garish mess that doesn't contain a single thing that isn't smudged or overdesigned. I can't even think about local weapons, levels, or enemies... full stop. They are unimaginable. The gratuitous cartoon gore is a bucket of red paint thrown in a cistern of diarrhea. So abundant that it blends everything together into one giant rainbow Shoop Da Whoop during the action sequences that soon become a blur. I can't even tell you what the enemies are and what they do. Hell, I couldn't tell you what was my role in all of this! I was mashing keys until I got tired of this rancid clown parade, I guess.My curator  (I ultimately decided not to add this there for the lack of hours invested, but it doesn't hurt to self-promote, I suppose)

_childDocuments_.review: For 50 bucks I'm not sure you could get away with selling people on the idea of this game. While it is an incredibly high quality and fun experience ultimately it's only 5 hours long and disappointing in a few regards. Primarily being the last minute change in voice actors. While I came for the gameplay usually, the humor was always what I stayed for and a large part of that is how cheesy it was. Cheesy dialogue does not work without perfect delivery and the change in voice actor for lo wang falls flat. All credit to him, it's an okay sound-alike of the previous VA but he loses almost all the charm and it makes the character feel completely different. In the end I didn't dislike the new VA's job, but it was absolutely a downgrade. Everyone else was okay, they barely have 20 minutes of dialogue compared to lo wang talking the entire time.As for the game itself? They really went balls to the wall with the changes. Each enemy past the 2 small unites are all distinct and fun to fight. Their unique mechanics lend itself well to the increased focus on environmental effects and comboing your weapons to achive quick kills. This is further reinforced by your max ammo being quite limited. This on top of the new "finishers" will make people think about doom eternal. But I would say it's a bit closer to bullet storm since the finishers are less about using them to constantly stay in the fight and more giving you consumable tools to help take out enemies faster since every last enemy in the game gives you SOMETHING to work with.That said this concept does kind of fall off a bit halfway through where the majority of your time is spent fighting enemies you can't really push around or manipulate so you're stuck with just throwing barrels at them which can be jank.The story is another thing that's kind of just... there. The goal really doesn't change, it just feels like a straight line with some mild bends that ultimately don't actually change the course of your objective at all.And to top it all off, the environments and music are all incredible. Despite it being 5 hours long they take you through so many different locales that it never got boring to look at. Ultimately still a really fun time, it could have been amazing if they never changed the VA for Lo Wang but it is what it is and hopefully if they make a shadow warrior 4 they can bring him back. But again 50 dollars for a 5 hour long game... It's a tough sell for a lot of people. Though I personally left satisfied, even after a 6 year long wait since 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I suppose it was a short game as many others have said. A lot shorter than the other ones, at least. Not the best one in the Shadow Warrior series nor do I think it could be the 2nd best but because I'm a sucker for these run n gun games, I would actually recommend it because I did have fun with it and ended up beating it in a day and a half. A lot simpler it seems to the last ones and I like how you just start out shooting at the beginning of the game. The challenges weren't hard at all to complete due to the never ending enemies you have to kill in a variety of ways to beat the challenges. The 'lesser' enemies don't stop coming until AFTER you beat the bigger monsters. There are bugs in the game. I noticed most of the bugs came after I cleared the area and so sometimes it wouldn't open up the gate for me to enter the next area, so I had to restart and beat the enemies again. Not that I hated it. It was satisfying killing monsters and it doesn't get boring until AFTER you beat the game and decide to replay the missions over again. I just feel like the game needs a little more content to feel 'alive' and get you motivated to keep playing it. Graphics are cool looking, the game wants to be DOOM so bad right now, it's alright. It's okay. I might play it again but only until after I get dementia. 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could pick options other than "Yes" and "No."  This is a game to buy when it goes on sale.   It is not worth paying full-price.  Overall, I enjoyed SW3.  SW2 was a mess due to the ridiculously complex weapons system, not to mention the hub design that had the player visiting and revisiting levels multiple times.  SW3 did away with both in favor of the more linear design of SW1.  But - SW3 did it wrong.  While SW1 had some interesting characters and a plot, SW3 had virtually no plot, no interesting characters, and was utterly devoid of anything specifically memorable.  When you complete the game, the post-boss closing cutscene is as banal and dull as you could possibly imagine.Also, the game is short.  I'm not a gamer-extraordinaire.  I completed the game in 9.8 hours on medium difficulty, without rushing.Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed those 9.8 hours, but it doesn't compare with SW1.

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but sweet! Shadow Warrior 3 does what it knows best and that's shooty shooty bang bang against some AMAZINGLY designed demons (seriously these guys look really fantastic and ooze with creativity, personal favorites being the Kugutsu and Slinky Jakku) same can be said about the games visuals and landscapes, bright, colorful, and you'll probably catch yourself just gazing out into levels at a few points. Gameplay is where Shadow Warrior 3 shines, fast chaotic arena style combat similar to DOOM 2016/Eternal offering the player to use traps and or grapple/wall run around the arena to stay alive, your movement and use of the games 7 weapons. (which is a huge plus for me as some games over-bloat the weapon selection making some practically useless halfway through the game) not here all weapons remain pretty useful especially against certain enemy types. Shadow Warrior 3 also allows for you to upgrade your abilities and weapons by using orbs obtained by completing challenges or finding hidden ones around each level, 3 upgrades per ability and weapon. Shadow Warrior 3 breaks up these combat arenas by having these really fun parkour sections that take you between each cutscene/level/arena. you'll find yourself running,sliding,grappling and wall running during these sections which I found to be a nice change of pace in-between all the chaotic fights. My only complaints would of course be the length and the lack of anything else to do once you've beaten the main story. what I would like to see is maybe a wave/horde mode or some dlc levels in the future. but what is here is fantastic and I really don't think all the negativity is warranted. All in all if you love fast arena combat like DOOM but not nearly as difficult, with some silly ass humor and all a game that doesn't take itself all to seriously I would highly recommend Shadow Warrior 3 it was a blast, maybe wait for a price drop if your on the fence but I promise you its a great time and a fantastic shooter! (PS the music is pretty damn dope to)

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the last two games in the Shadow Warrior reboot series, this is a bit of a mixed bag.It continues the evolution of the shooting mechanics and feel - Doom Eternal borrowed some of its feel from SW2, and SW3 returns the favor and borrows a lot from Doom Eternal.  An excellent progression from Shadow Warrior 2 in terms of handling and controls, everything is intuitive, and unusually for a game built on UE, it feels extremely snappy to play.The feel and handling is good enough that I was able to start out at the highest difficulty and feel like I had the control I needed to survive, and deaths were my own fault.  As I said, this is unusual for a UE game - even the best examples of shooters built on UE (Amid Evil is top-tier example) still have a slushy, sloppy feel to them.  Shadow Warrior 3 plays almost as well as an idTech shooter.The voice actor change for Lo Wang is a non-issue.  Neither is memorable or distinct.  If it makes a few people happy that the role is no longer whitewashed, fine.  It would be debatable if the previous actor brought something interesting and unique to the role, but that wasn't the case.Graphically, the game is spectacular.  Thanks to DLSS being available, the performance is excellent on nVidia cards.  The game lacks HDR support, which is almost inexcusable for a 2022 release.  Although, that's probably better than the abominable HDR implementation in Shadow Warrior 2.I've only put a bit over an hour in, but based on story progress, I'm going to anticipate that the complaints about the length of the game are on point.I don't miss the looter-shooter aspect of the previous game.  I don't miss the hub-based pseudo open-world.  The linear arena format lifted right from Doom Eternal works extremely well here, and many of the enemy gimmicks are fun to learn and play around.All in all, if this were a full $60 new release?  Hell no.  It's worth the $40 launch if you're the kind of person who pays launch prices.  I'd say that anywhere in the $10-$25 range, it's a solid buy for any modern/retro hybrid shooter fan.Overall, 6/10.  Above average, saved in large part by excellent responsiveness and gorgeous graphics.  Not a ton of substance, but still worth it at a reduced price.It also says a lot about my thoughts of 2022 game releases that I nominated this game - a solidly mediocre 6/10 game - for GOTY.

_childDocuments_.review: People moan about the short length of only 5 hours, meanwhile there is a NG+ and Challenge mode to unlock weapon skins.It's a bit of Doom Eternal but watered down, Bethesda Zenimax is simply the much bigger company and Doom comes with a guaranteed sale-quota allowing them to go with a bigger budget. The id Engine is much more tailored towards the specific game, precise and faster making it a much more hardcore FPS experience than what they cooked up with the Unreal Engine for this game. The previous installments used the developers Flying Wild Hog own engine Road Hog and were published by Devolver Digital while this is published by Focus Entertainment and they switched to the Unreal Engine. Reworking the engine for all platforms and getting it ready for the next-gen consoles was probably too much for the budget. Meanwhile Embracer Group (previously THQ Nordic previously Nordic Games who purchased the rights to the trademark THQ from the bankrupt THQ in 2013) bought Flying Wild Hog and they apparently only care to purchase as many Studios and IPs as they can but not to invest into their existing studios and talents, they haven't yet developed any engine of their own, from Biomutant to Destroy All Humans! to Spongebob their own productions use the UE because it is easier and cheaper - which generally is okay but for what is basically becoming an Investment Holding behemoth that sucked up pillars of game development decades old such as Gearbox, Eidos, Saber that is very poor - therefor that is probably not going to change for SW in the future. Nontheless Shadow Warrior 3 boasts beautiful graphics and creative artwork rivaling that of Nioh in the chinese/japanese folklore and a large number of high quality cinematics.And then it's 'Want some Wang?' Sushi humor, you may like it or not but sometimes it'll wring off a laugh off you.Personally I really enjoyed it, given the price you can get it in external stores meanwhile, and I might play the NG+ for 100% completion because the short length can really leave you thirsty for more, but then if they had just continued without adding new mechanics it would have really become repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 is a single player FPS that has arena battles and fun high octane platforming.The story picks up from the disaster that was Shadow Warrior 2. Basically forget everything that happened in that game except for the ending. It brings back familiar elements from the first game but not the tone. Instead the game opts for a very light and humorous tone. There's plenty of mid game cut scenes with goofy action and bits of humor here and there. It's very consistent if nothing else, I wish we got something more akin to the first game, but it works well for what the game is going for, which is a short and fun ride.There aren't many characters, but all of them have quite a bit of wit and charm to make them stand out. The plot is really simple, take out the dragon. Stuff happens, it becomes harder to take out the dragon. The game's length really not allowing much else in the way of it's simple premise. It's a good and bad thing, the game doesn't waste your time and just keeps on going. But, I feel like there's a lot more that the characters could've said to each other if they had more time.One can say it's a Doom Eternal clone and call it a day and they'd be half right. For one, it's a lot more simple to learn and play compared to Doom E. There's far fewer weapons and less options to fiddle with, which some may consider a bad thing, but I'm all for it. It just means it's far easier to manage your weapons. Speaking of, they're really satisfying to use.A powerful accurate revolver, a REALLY powerful shotgun, DUAL smgs with a large magazine, a grenade launcher, a railgun and lastly a buzzsaw launcher thing. And a sword. All of them (Except the Buzzsaw thing and the sword) excel at their roles, and you'll be heavily relying on all of them throughout your run. It's a great selection imo. Chi Techniques have been slimmed down to just the Chi Blast sadly, but once it's upgraded it's a really good skill.Wang can also do Gore Kills. This is a really fun mechanic as well, aside from the bonus of taking out a tough opponent for a certain amount of the finisher gauge, it also grants much needed health and a strong weapon to turn the tides. (Or a buff to gain bonus health or have a eyeball passively destroying enemies.) Wang still retains his quick dashes, he even got a double jump now. These 2 skills allow Wang to quickly zip around the battlefield. In addition, his new hook shot allows him to reposition quickly from different spots in the Arena. As well as being a crucial tool in the various "Platforming" sections. I call them platforming, but they are more like "chase" sections. The game has areas where Wang is quickly trying to reach a certain destination while he has to jump, slide, wall run and hook shot his way through. These are really fun! Not only do these usually take place in wide open areas, with a great view and beautiful scenery, the sense of thrill from performing these super human acts is really something that needs to be experienced.Look the game's short, but it's honestly a joy from start to finish. I played on Hard difficulty for 90% of the game. Started on normal, felt I could push it and kept on going with Hard. There's only 2 bosses but I'll take 2 really, well designed bosses over how many generic bosses were in the first and second game. They were challenging and kinda fun. It's a shame the game is getting hammered for it's quantity where the quality more than makes up for it. Purchased it on a sale, but I feel like it was probably worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: For the record, this is a fun game. Despite what a lot of nostalgic people will say about it "not being a Shadow Warrior game", it's still worth your time, but worth the price tag? That's a different story.The game obviously takes a lot of inspiration from DOOM Eternal's release in order to make a very VERY fast game with lots of gun switching action, which some people might like or dislike. Unlike previous games, the Katana is no longer a single weapon, and is instead used as a swift finisher against weak enemies in order to get ammo back, which is a fun twist on Eternal's chainsaw mechanic. Also unlike previous games in my opinion, guns are far more satisfying to use, and I think it's done to compensate for the Katana's downfall. Every gun feels like an actual addition to your arsenal and compliments eachother quite nicely for different purposes, and if you run out of ammo you'll never be in a situation where you go "Ah, damn, I'm stuck with this weapon now?" (except the sawblade launcher which I feel is way too gimmicky for my liking).Additionally, the addition of a cool finisher bar that allows you to INSTANTLY KILL ANY ENEMY, on top of giving you an extremely overpowered weapon depending on which enemy you kill, is a very interesting idea that I wish they did more with. Every enemy in the game has ONE unique animation, and they all reward you their own weapon. What I dislike about this is that most weapons you get from the enemies aren't as good as others, and the animation of you killing the enemy, although gruesome and satisfying at first, can get tiring quickly after playing for a long time. HOWEVER, at the time of writing this they're pricing this game at 54CDN$ (~40USD$), which, according to a lot of people, is far too high for a game with far too little replayability value, which I frankly agree with. The story is quite short and there's no other game mode to make up for it, unlike DOOM Eternal which has an already lengthy story mode, but on top of that launched with Battlemode, followed with 2 DLC campaigns each lasting about 2 hours and a new game mode called Horde Mode which may last you around 40 minutes to an hour per run.Case in point, until they launch new game modes or different difficulties worth a damn that actually make this game fun to replay, I think the only complaint most people will have about this game is that it's "not a Shadow Warrior game" (which consists of like 80% of the negative reviews). Until then, wait for a sale. Or price reduction.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 executes well on its two main pillars: Shooting & Movement.To elaborate:It's immediately recognizable (compared to industry favorites like DOOM & Prodeus), but does a good enough job of feeling unique (especially when it it comes to enemy design). It's true that the game initially feels like DOOM 2019, but after a few hours the game settles into its own unique sense of "style"...and violence. The grappling hook and wall running mechanics are essential tools to surviving enemy ambushes and making the most out of every encounter.The level design is the most repetitive aspect of the game, and that may bother certain types of players. Every environment settles into the same pattern of running puzzle followed by a combat arena. Rinse. Repeat. The combat moments (and they are plenty) are the main draw. There's no "aiming down sites" or any other quasi military mechanics. This is all arena shooting, all the time. Mix in the wild & weird weapons you can steal from enemies, and it makes each encounter quite enjoyable.Game ran surprisingly solid on my gaming laptop (mix of medium & high settings). At the time of this review, I completed the game (8 hours) on an intel 9300 and GTX 1660Ti MaxQ. It held 60 fps most of the time with some occasional drops (at 1080p).

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely on the short side, but the game was fun while it lasted.  The combat is fast paced, following Doom 2016 design elements with finishers and limited ammo.  It's much looser and the swordplay is reduced greatly, but the gore weapons received from finishers are a neat feature.  The game is graphically impressive and the enemies are imaginative and varied. Unfortunately, the story is pretty weak.  The voice actors do the best with what they got, but the writing is bad.  People are critical of the new actor for Lo Wang, but Jason would not have made these lines much better.  Some of the platforming was janky and caused some frustrating reloads, but checkpoints are decent.Since it's so short, I might replay it with the new modes being added and try to get all the achievements.  That'll add a bit more value, but I'm already happy after finishing it once.  Overall, it's a step down from the previous games, but still enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to write my review for this game because I'm getting really annoyed reading the negative reviews for this game about how it's nothing like Shadow Warrior 2. Yeah, it's nothing like Shadow Warrior 2, and it wasn't advertised to be. It was shown to be an arena shooter, and it delivered on that brilliantly. If you don't like that, then don't buy a game that's marketing itself as an arena shooter. It's really that simple. The overwhelming negative reviews that try to relate it to the previous game is like trying to compare Star Wars to Harry Potter movies and rate them based off that. Just to get this out of the way now, but if you came into the series from SW2 and think that game is amazing, don't purchase this game. You will be disappointed. If anything, it was more geared towards SW1 fans.Here's my take on the game. Much like how many others have stated, it takes the formula of Doom Eternal with it's own twist and mashes it into the Shadow Warrior franchise. It does and overall good job at that. The combat is satisfying, clean, sharp, intuitive, and makes for an extremely fun learning experience. The katana, the staple weapon of our protagonist across this series, is also a satisfying and well incorporated tool with it's own usages as a combat powerhouse. The enemy variety is really enjoyable, with each playing distinct roles and having extremely unique and visually interesting appearances, which also makes them easy to pick out from the crowd to direct your focus. The dynamic arenas support various playstyles with all your tools that you can use as you see fit. Personally, I wish more enemies could be grappled onto to enable a more aggressively mobile playstyle, but it's fine as it is. The soundtrack for this game feels really cinematic. I think it sets a great tone for the game is very enjoyable to listen to while slashing demons or running across the back of a dragon. The platforming sections are simple fun and relatively easy thanks to the very clear direction the game gives as indirect hints. However, since most of the upgrade points are hidden around these sections, I wish some platforming parts had a little less hand-holding, such as the grapple sections, but they are overall enjoyable. I found myself constantly keeping an eye out for hidden spots to grab an upgrade point. This kept it engaging despite the linearity. Also, the visuals in this game are some of the best I've ever seen. Sometimes I fell off just staring at the beautiful landscape, but it was well worth it. It's absolute eye-candy.Sadly, the ugly parts of this game are obvious. There is no level select. When you reach the final boss you're basically stuck there unless you delete your save. There is only 3 difficulty settings, and even the hardest is not that difficult. There is no un-lockable difficulties or super hard challenges to overcome, although this isn't all necessarily a bad thing, but I would love for this game to have a hardcore challenge; it's short enough to make it an enjoyable thing, which is what I'll get into in a bit. Unlike Shadow Warrior 1 and 2, there is no new-game+, which is very sad because it made those games replayable. The weapons, while they have upgrades, they typically only have one main usage with no alternative mode. They can get a bit stale to use after a while. There is also only one chi power in this game, unlock the various ones the other two games had. This is easily the most disappointing aspect as a Shadow Warrior series fan. The chi powers made the game feel extremely unique. To see most of them gone is just disappointing. There was so much potential to be explored, but sadly it was missed.The biggest draw for this game, however, is the length. This game is very short. It's only about 5-6 hours for an average playthrough. It all depends on how you choose to play the game of course, but those numbers are about how long it will take. Coupled on top of the lack of any post-game un-lockable content and a level select, this is very noticable. The completionist route isn't that long either due to the lack of anything hidden beyond the upgrade orbs. The thing that makes it somewhat difficult is that you have to get all the orbs on one playthrough or you have to restart the game from the beginning to collect any missed orbs. In other words, if this game had a level select completionist would be even easier. Personally speaking, if this game had increased replayability the lack of content would be far more easily bearable. Hopefully, since an update is said to come soon, that this main issue will be fixed, and maybe a new difficulty will greatly enhance the experience.As I said before, this game is NOT like either Shadow Warrior 1 or 2. It plays completely differently and easily has the least focus on story compared to the other two. There is a total of merely 4 characters in the entire game (6 if you stretch the definition) and they have very unequal screentime so it often feels like even less. However, it's clear the intention was a focus on gameplay, and I think they did a great job at that. It's a fun game to just play because of the extremely satisfying combat system and the constant resource management that goes on throughout combat. The gunplay is easily the cleanest and easiest to use in the series compared to the rather clunky nature in the first two games. And the visuals are simply amazing. If you like fun, fast gameplay that forces near constant engagement and thinking, as well as also being a fan of Doom Eternal or a similar shooter, then pick this game up and give it a try. If you don't like what I just said, then I would avoid this game. Maybe wait for a sale if you're really curious. You really need to like it if you want to spend this kind of money on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 1 (from 2013) was a nice concept for establishing the revival of the old-school shooter, more modern though. We saw Wolfenstein: The New Order a year later and DOOM 2016 confirmed that with its brutal combat and incredible pacing. Shadow Warrior 2 took the looter-shooter approach and killed any sort of "progress" you could feel from attacking enemies. What's the point of carrying so many guns if most of them are gonna be futile along with the elemental system that only serve as passive buffs or debuffs?Shadow Warrior 3, thankfully, does away with the looter-shooter approach by somewhat going back to what was good about the 2013 title yet stumbles across a bit of an identity crisis. Does it want to be DOOM-like or Titanfall-like? I don't know... but the game doesn't seem to know either.I won't talk about the non-troversy involving the voice acting since Lo Wang never really was an incredible protagonist to begin with. Yet I'll agree that the delivery felt more forced. Even sound clips from the original voice actor can be heard (grunts) so it really is weird. That being said, on my machine, I've had to endure some serious performance issues and the overall presentation and wonky physics do not warrant such high specs. Be careful if you intent on purchasing the title even after the drivers' update.In around 5 hours, I was done with the campaign... on Hard Difficulty. While Hard was the highest available difficulty setting, I believe the challenge wasn't up to par. In fact, I probably died between 15-20 times which isn't too bad. I couldn't find all the upgrades or optimise my gameplay to beat every challenge yet I don't feel like I needed to push myself since... there's no way to replay missions or earn an extra difficulty setting: there are no unlockables. There's not even a menu to check past saves and see if you could have done better, found more secrets if there are.The combat, at its core, is far... FAR better than it has any right to be. Yes, the weapon choice is limited but each serves a purpose: attack aerials with the Basilisk, use the Revolver or Uzi to kill the fodders, use Chi Blast and the Full-Auto Shotgun against mid-to-large enemies... it's up to you in how you handle these situations. The Katana is certainly taking a stepback... but refilling ammo WHILE in combat with the katana is excellent as the game can keep up the pace. The off-screen reloading is excellent because it allows quick-swapping based on enemy encounters and decision-making. In general, the combat isn't AS GOOD as DOOM Eternal... but it's pretty close. I just am not a fan of the Basilisk in how you HAVE to hold the button to fire. The Grapple isn't certainly no Meathoot and offers a little less compared to Halo Infinite. It's more Ghostrunner, but without the platforming genius.What is definitely not pleasing to me is the parkour-style level design that leave very little for the player to explore. I do not need a game to be open-world to be "explorable": I just wish for alternate paths for secrets, easter eggs or maybe a special reward like a hidden weapon or something... There's no true incentive to go off the path and find the little things. So much could have been done for the Grapple besides parkour-platforming.While there are two bosses, they should have brought their all-out game here and that isn't the case. The first was good yet the second felt wonky to say the least. Both of them have a similar finishing moment and it feels unearned.Shadow Warrior 3 is worth it at a discount.. but at MSRP, I cannot recommend it. If you're going to play on Normal, you'll be in for a walk in the park... Even then, it's average. There's a good foundation, yet it's not mastered. It's fun and I can't deny it, yet it's not quite there...

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 plays less like it's predecessors and is more akin to Doom Eternal. This comes with both pros and cons. The game is a more refined and direct experience. They've done away with many of Shadow Warrior 2's systems and have given us a more on-rails game. Personally I prefer this style, though I understand why you may dislike the changes. For example no Co-op can be a massive deal-breaker for some folks, but I just don't think it'd work in this game with how many linear platforming segments and cutscenes there are.Your weapons have low ammunition counts, but there's always ammo pickups on the field waiting for you. It encourages to constantly swap weapons and to be aware of your surroundings. This results in a fast-paced, engaging gameplay loop. Every firearm feels great to work with, my favourites are the Riot Gun and Basilisk. Both of them have a heavy punch with each shot fired making them my go-to weapons for finishing off a weakened enemy. Enemies will gib when you finish them off, you can blow off legs and rip open chest cavities. Very fun! The enemies all serve a purpose on the battlefield and are very diverse. You've got the fodder which serve to distract you from the main threats. You've got artillery-spouting flying demons. You've got the Serious Sam AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA explodey boys. You've got the tanky melee monsters that force you to keep moving. You've got Mole Men and Slinkey Thingys which both focus on Area Denial. You've got a enemies that resist certain attacks which encourage you to fight them in less conventional ways. The Yokai all complement each other quite nicely and force you to think about which targets you'll focus first.The upgrade system is alright. It may depend on your playstyle, but at first glance some upgrades are definitely better than others. For example you'll want enemies to be dropping pickups when you shoot/slash them, that's a no-brainer.One thing this game does better than Doom Eternal is the melee combat. You've got two reliable melee attacks here: your Katana and your Chi Blast. You can use both of these as much as you want, and are encouraged to do so. Your Katana is quite freaking strong, by the way! Lo Wang is as hilarious and cringey as ever. The game is fully self-aware about how obnoxious he is and completely embraces it. All of the characters in the story are absolutely sick of dealing with him, I love it. Some people are upset about the new voice actor but I think he did an excellent job.The music is lovely, I've caught myself bopping my head and tapping my feet to the rhythm on more than one occasion. Many of the tracks are very Oriental, however there is the odd Heavy Metal track thrown in here and there. Visually the game is outstanding. I've been spending a lot of time just looking at the environments. Bamboo forests, mountain mesas complete with waterfalls, ancient worn-down temples, it all looks great.Apparently the game is quite short, at the time of writing this review I'd guess I'm about one third of the way through the game. It's been an incredible experience and I've been smiling the whole time. It's up to you whether it's worth it at full price or not, but when it goes on sale you should definitely check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I hadn't write the review for some time since I finished the game. Partly because I didn't know how to rate it, partly because I hoped to see some improvements with the updates. Now, when the developers finally added something new - a Hardcore mode in this case - I decided the time has come. First things first, the game looks and plays great. If you are a fan of fast-paced shooters and liked the Shadow Warrior series because it has always tried something new, the new title will certainly entertain you. The weapons and enemies are balanced and if you learn to play correctly you can feel yourself a badass ninja tearing through enemies like an unstoppable force. The level design is kinda lazy, consisting of either straight tunnel sections for parkour or arenas for fighting. It's also very unfriendly for the explorers as every area you are not supposed to be in is a deathpit or blocked by an invisible wall, so finding few secrets that are in the game becomes a pain. The arenas themselves, however, have a decent potential for movement, as well as a number of traps and explosives scattered around, which makes the combat more diverse. The graphics are great and provide very stunning sceneries which you will totally admire as you rush through the environments. The game also has challenges which give you access to additional skill points. Though most of them are simple "do *name of the action* N times", this still expands the gameplay and encourages you to plan your actions.  Nevertheless, everything else about Shadow Warrior 3 is... mediocre at least. To begin with, the series has seemingly lost it's identity by copying Doom Eternal mechanics too much. Sure both SW1 and SW2 were not totally original games but they had it's own distinguishable features. If you dug up you noticed that SW1 took inspiration from The Darkness 2 and SW2 followed Borderlands and Destiny but the games were not direct parodies. Unlike that, when you look at SW3 you instantly see Doom Eternal behind it. Moreover, the story and characters became a kind of mess. Sure, the other titles' plots were not the main features but you could enjoy them, plus, the protagonist had some character. Here, Lo Wang became a kind of crazy cringe idiot obsessed with the death of his friend from the first game (even though he did not care about it at all in the second title) and most of his jokes make you facepalm rather than laugh. Finally, the main problem of the game - its duration. I do not usually consider this factor as if a game is good I do not really care if it's 10 or 100 hours long but here... it's just unacceptable. I finished the whole SW3 on 100% on Hard difficulty in under 6 hours, and I'm sure if you play it on normal or easy without hunting for challenges and achievements this time can drop to 2-3 hours. And this is not bad itself, provided that the game has the potential for replayability... but it doesn't... at all! There is no cooperative, NG+ or heroic mode. Sure, they've recently added a hardcore difficulty but I played it for some time and can say it is not that much hardcore. Yes, it makes you care more about your resources and plan your actions but the thing is that you are already able to do this if you finished the game on hard at least once. Yeah, maybe if you play further there will be brand new experience with boss battles and last levels but why the hell I should go through all the game again to feel the hardcore difficulty? Moreover, the price for mistake is relatively low, as you will simply respawn on the last checkpoint, in comparison to Heroic difficutly of the first title, which kept you in tense for the most of the level, and even Doom Eternal's Ultra Nightmare, which keeps you in tense for all of the campaign! Furthermore, there is even no option to replay the levels, so if you missed an upgrade or just want to revisit your favourite level - hell no, you can't, restart the entire game! All in all, I can only come to a sad conclusion. If the game was at least 30$ I might have thought about the rate but for 50$ 3-5 hours of content is simply not enough. You can buy Shadow Warrior 2 for 40$ and get trice as much content with the ability to play the game with your friends. Besides, you can buy the pack of SWCR, SW1, and SW2 on any sale for about 30$ and get at least 10 hours of gameplay from each of them. If the developers add NG+ or release free story addons I might reconsider my review but for now, unless there is at least a 50% discount or you really want to play this game and have spare 50$, there is no real reason to buy Shadow Warrior 3. Hell, you can buy the original Doom Eternal for 10$ less and get much more gameplay and content and a multiplayer mode on top of that!

_childDocuments_.review: As previous Shadow Warrior games are this one has great combat, weapons and just an overall nice smooth design. Definitely very fun and entertaining however this one falls short in a lot of places compared to the other two.First of all its extremely short, I was able to beat the whole thing on hard difficulty in 6 hours and I only missed 1 achievement. For the price its at I definitely do not recommend buying it, maybe at 50% off. The graphics are very nice though and the whole thing plays out like a movie, the levels all seamlessly transition from one to the next. The weapons are cool and the enemies are cool although the AI isn't that great. Also feels like they're trying too hard to copy Doom with most of the enemy encounters being in little arenas.The game itself runs reasonably well although some parts have lot of frame drops when there's lots of enemies. The upgrade system compared to the previous games has been extremely dumbed down, you just have to collect orbs and you can upgrade your weapons and your character, there's maybe like 8 of each and they can all be upgraded 3 times so yeah very very basic compared to previous games and this one also doesn't have any secrets or anything aside from hidden upgrade orbs there's no real reason to replay a level in fact I'm not sure there's even a level select.So yeah extremely bare bones feeling game, feels rushed in my opinion especially the way cutscenes just feel like they progress too fast and end abruptly, just seems way too short. There's like 5 characters in the whole game and two of them barely do or say anything. But yeah overall feels like a huge step back in many areas compared to the first two games. I do like the gameplay and the graphics and the nice levels and the way every level just plays back to back like a movie but otherwise its just a bit disappointing. 6/10 only buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh. Boy.The third installment of the completely insane Shadow Warrior series and what a wild game it is. Continuing with it's standard insanity, the game is a roller coaster of high flying monster murder, pistol whipping & brutally sh*t one-liners.Having played through the previous two games (mostly due to Lo Wang's... *charm*) the story continues from the end of the second game where our Hero unleashed a big ass dragon that wrecks the planet. The story is about as cookie cutter as it gets which really doesn't matter, this is a game about terrible puns, daemon killing and lots of gore.  Basically if The Slayer had a really sh***y sense of humour. The graphics have been kicked up a notch and Lo Wang does indeed have very fabulous hair. The environments are beautifully detailed with some really nice level design,  the way you need to go is clear and it flows, I'm pretty sure you could play the entire game without stopping at all unless it's scripted.  The platforming is simple and quite seamless with some clever hiding spots for all the hidden upgrade tokens so keep your eyes peeled. It also serves as a brief respite from the crazy combat which lead me to... The combat. It's fast and completely insane.  Fireballs, lasers, blades, moles, traps, fireworks... There's just so much crap flying at you sometimes it's hard to keep track. Flying Hog definitely took some notes from DOOM by having your enemies being essentially walking ammo & health packs when you kill them especially with melee.  But unlike DOOM you get to pull off some gruesome finishers by building up meter rather than damage. The upgrade system for Wang and his weapons is simple and clear, no giant trees of skills and minute % increases in damage for the min-maxers to go ham. Everything has 3 upgrades and that's that. On the flip side the game does have some problems. Annoying ones.  I frequently got stuck when in a particularly furry hairball.  If you get surrounded the enemies they are a wall. You can't jump over or dash through them, they will pound you into a wet mass if you aren't careful (That could also be just me being sh*t). The bugs though were frustrating, a common issue I ran into was being in a long ass fight only for the game to not realise I've killed everything. Side note: you need to kill all the elites, the ads will keep spawning until you do as they provide bullets and health. I'd kill all the elites and the ads would just keep spawning to no end resulting in reloading to the previous checkpoint.  Another bug was during some platform stages a platform or object wouldn't spawn or move as they should resulting in needing to reload the checkpoint or level entirely.  Other than those minor gripes the game is short, violent and full of garbage puns and trash talk, all the things one would love the game for already. It tickled me in all the right places and I played it until 100%. It didn't overstay it's welcome and scratched my itch for gratuitous violence. I give it a big ol' recommendation  and a solid 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really good, but it feels incredibly rushed and isn't worth $50 at the moment in my opinion. It took me 5.7 hours to beat the game (and I got 34/38 achievements, so it's not like I rushed through), there isn't any sort of side content and (as far as I can tell at least) there is no NG+ option. Also the game is somewhat buggy, occasionally there would be enemies floating in midair just sitting there and sometimes the mouse cursor would appear on screen, forcing me to pause & unpause to get rid of it.As for the core gameplay, it's really fast paced and you have a ton of movement options at your disposal so you can run around and do lots of cool ♥♥♥♥. Unfortunately some of the arenas are very small and the enemy counts are very high, making it difficult to use the environment without running into enemies in those areas. When the game gives you appropriately sized arenas it's an absolute blast and one of the most fun shooters I've ever played. The other main issue with the gameplay is the platforming. For the most part the platforming is decent, however given how short the game is already, the platforming sections take up way too much of it and are totally linear so you don't really get any opportunity to be creative in how you use your movement options. It's just jump, airdash, grapple hook between platforms. Of the 5.7 hours I spent playing the game, I'd estimate that around 2 of those hours were spent in the platforming sections. That combined with some of the cramped arenas meant that the super fun part of the game was probably only about 1/3rd of the total time I spent playing it.Comparing it to the other 2 games, the game is far more linear than the 2nd and even the 1st Shadow Warrior games, with no collectables outside of a couple of skill point orbs that are about 10 seconds off the main path and are the only examples of branching paths in the game. The game certainly has the best combat, but SW2 has really good combat as well (as long as you ignore the whole gem system), and SW1 has pretty good combat outside of the mini-bosses which are annoying as hell. The level design is honestly the worst of the 3 because of how linear it is. Outside of the arena fights, 95% of the game is just walking or jumping or grapple hooking in a straight line. There aren't even any open areas to give the illusion that you have options on where to go. It's just forwards or backwards. As for the writing, it's great, but so is the writing in the first 2 games.With all that said, I enjoyed the game a lot. At it's peak this game is amazing, but the peak is so short that it's definitely not worth $50 in it's current state. Currently I'd say $10-$15 is a fair price given how short it is. Maybe that will eventually go up if there is new content added.If you're new to the series, I'd get the first 2 Shadow Warrior games before touching this one. The first 2 games routinely go on sale for ~$10-20 and are definitely worth it at that price. If you've already played the first 2 games, then it really depends on how much you value $50. If you loved the first 2 games you'll definitely get a lot of enjoyment out of it, but it really depends on whether or not 5-6 hours of that enjoyment is worth $50 to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 yearns to return to the simplistic linear corridor run and gun style of the early 2010's. Indeed this game had me reminiscing on the first "Shadow Warrior" Reboot in the early 2010's while playing the third instalment.The Bad: Either through lack of time, funding, previous commercial failure of Shadow Warrior 2. The team obviously want to return to the single player shooters of last decade that made them successful. However, the moment I began to warm up to a blast from the past, the game ended. I finished this game on Hard difficulty clocking in at around 5 - 6 hours playtime and a handful more hours of completion hunting had this game ready for the shelf never to see life again in under 12 hours playtime.While very flashy the game play mechanics are mostly outdated and uninteresting when comparing to many similar FPS titles of the 2020's, the lazy parkour and wall running mechanics leave something to be desired in engagement. Many campaign shooters could be described as linear corridors and arenas that a player blasts their way through, Shadow Warrior 3 makes this far to obvious and detracts from the already short experience.This project is blatantly half finished and pushed out the door to be deliberately forgotten. No further support outside of a weak attempt at a new game+ has been provided. Performance issues and bugs while infrequent, were still in the "Definitive Edition" that were reported in base game launch. I cannot recommend purchasing this game full price or on sale. Instead pick up "Shadow Warrior" for a better experience with more content. The Good: The made me member 2013 Wang.Conclusion: Don't Buy this game, hopefully Flying Wild Hog managed to test some concepts and Idea's in this game and will give the next entry a serious attempt.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 ProsVoice actor killed it, I wasn’t happy about the change at first, but Mike did a good job.Voice actors did a good job of bringing their respected characters to life.Story isn’t gonna win an academy award, but it’s engaging and intiseing to the end.Dialogue is written well, it’s less in your face than SW2. I like SW2’s just not constant or that much low brow comedy.Characters are likable, though it is brief characters do get developed to an extent.Soundtrack is kickassSound design is amazing.Environments are gorgeous and large in scope.Cinematicas are well done and engaging, to help the story progress.Moveset makes it fun and exciting to travel within the levels.Weapons look nice, sound nice, and play nice.Skills do have an impact on encounters.Fast paced combat or leisure stroll depending on how you approach it.Levels are well constructed, vast and easy to traverse.Arena combat is delightful.Bosses are unique, but pretty simple when you understand how they operate.UI is simple and easy to understand.Graphics wise it is a very pretty game.ConsGame is too short.Game is a bit too easy, it won’t challenge you like the previous titles did.No New game + or level select.A little too linear.Not a lot of exploration like in past titles.AI get stuck sometimes.Few bugs, nothing that breaks the game, just ragdoll physics go wacky sometimes.Game is a bit unoptimized with Dllss, mainly in cutscenes; but it will quickly fix itself.Frames can dip when a lot of combat is going on, lowest I saw was 40fps that was with vsync on.The game may leave some people dissatisfied, but in my personal opinion I was quite satisfied with the overall experience. I do hope for a few changes like New game + or level select, but mainly more content to satisfy my appetite. Overall it is a great entry into the series, hope to see more in the future.
