_childDocuments_.review: Is that it?!I'm a self-admitted Shadow Warrior (2013 remake) fanboy, and found restricted enjoyment in the sequel. After playing this game however, SW2 feels like a pretty great game in retrospect.The first point everyone seems to bring up is that this game is short- super short. You barely have enough time to establish the story before it's finished. On normal difficulty you will finish in about 5 hours, on hard maybe 6. Talking of difficulties- there is only three. No legendary, no heroic, and no NG+. You can't even level select once you have beaten the game, and I don't particularly feel like replaying to try and scrounge up the last few achievements.The gameplay here is.... alright I suppose. The combat is a lot more barebones than the previous two games, and due to streamlining, Lo Wang is reduced to a knucklehead with no chi bar or chi powers activated using key combos. No spike generation or self-heal anymore, or anything chi related beyond a push move- which is a shame as chi moves were a staple of the two previous games. Talking of missing content- there arent any directional sword attacks either. No iconic divider of heavens or spinny blade attack. SW2013 had melee combat be a focus of it, and so did SW2, here the katana is relegated to being a glorified *punch enemy when close* attack which you have in any other game. There are 7 guns, all of which only have one firemode so are actually significantly less interesting than those in the remaster or even the procedurally generated weapons in 2.I complained that SW2 felt too much like the devs wanted to recreate borderlands, but here the comparison is DOOM, which I'm not going to complain about because everyone else has already brought this up.The gameplay loop is as follows- Lo Wang runs and jumps over floaty land towards a square arena, has to kill a handful of big demons while small ones constantly spawn, he leaves, a cutscene (with poor dubbing) plays and then he runs and jumps again. Very tiring. The combat plays like the Orbs of Masume challenges from SW2- a dodge fest and bullet hell spam. SW2013 was grounded to a setting that made sense, the maps got a bit bland but keeping it real made the game that much more impactful, here its so absurd and far out its hard to feel any investment in the plot. Yet it still somehow ends up being more shallow and simple to follow than even a childrens book.  Everything is vague and  and Wang working with Zilla is just something that is happening now, I guess, funny epic chill marvel avengers style.Flying Wild Hog seem to be about 90% level designers and 10% everything else because as usual the game is gorgeous. But, there is no photo mode. Alright then. Performance wise its alright, with tiny bit of stuttering, really strange looking cutscenes that either stuttered or had low frames- not sure, and dialogue has the classic issue of characters cutting each other off when a new topic starts.The sound design of enemies gets grating very quickly, repeating 2 second noises until you kill them, or being borderline broken like the suicide bombers who scream till you jump somewhere they have to think about how to get to, stop screaming and then immediately start again. The voice acting by Wang's new (yeah dumb) actor is worse than the previous, and half the jokes feel forced and safe. They seem slightly more self aware than SW2 (remember that infamous fart joke?) but they have basically turned Lo Wang into Deadpool, constantly referencing popculture and breaking the 4th wall.The menus and upgrades just feel very low budget or rushed, which is a shame, and overall the game is lacking any attention to detail or passion the previous two had. No secrets, no easter eggs, no visual changes when you upgrade weapons or Wang's skills. They got rid of the dynamic gore from the previous game but kept the floaty deaths, making everything feel weightless. And also corpses despawn in about 3 seconds for some reason.Overall this just feels like a formulaic and soulless game. It's just a straight up downgrade. If it goes on sale for atleast half price and you buy it expecting to play a lower budget copycat version of DOOM, go ahead. But don't expect Shadow Warrior. The original, remake OR two. Its absurd how small scope this one is. It feels like a game that could have come out as a proof of concept between the remaster and 2 honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a SW veteran. Still have yet to play the PC optimized version of the first game. However, I first got into Shadow Warrior when I saw an awesome clip on YouTube of SW2. Once I built my PC, SW2 was one of the first games I bought and played. Long story short, I LOVED it! Had an absolute blast with the fast-paced combat, enjoyed the funny humor from the voice actor, and liked the free-roaming along with a decent sized arsenal of weapons to play around with and upgrade. I was excited to learn that there was a third game coming out, and the teaser clips of SW3 certainly caught my interest.Overall, if you think SW3 is going to be ANYTHING like SW2 - throw those expectations away. SW3 is supposedly a lot more like SW1 with a linear campaign (I have yet to play the game), but at the time of writing this, I was able to beat the campaign in 5 HOURS. And that's it. No replayability except starting a whole new game. No leveling up, a limited arsenal of weapons, a bland and short story as well as shallow characters that don't live up to the game's predecessor. Cutscenes are pre-rendered (somebody else mentioned that as well in these reviews) and so don't be fooled by the release trailer on it's store page - same exact scene in the game, but nowhere near as smooth (I've got a beefy rig with a 3080). There are also a lot of cutscenes that feel disruptive to the gameplay. For example, you'll be doing a little bit of parkour on some of the levels and then WHAM - cut scene. Kinda killed the mood.On that technical note, I experienced a lot of stuttering and framerate drops but those were mainly during cut scene transitions. The gameplay itself was fun, but not as great as SW2. Everything felt rougher and slower paced. For me, coming straight from SW2, the combat in SW3 kinda felt like I was walking through mud. Of course the game is hopping on the Doom Eternal train with a grapple hook, "glory kills", etc. It just doesn't do it as smooth like Eternal or even SW2. SW3 certainly looked good! I'm a little more impressed with SW2, but in my opinion SW3 looked fantastic. I didn't mind fighting a demonic circus too much lol, it was just different for me, but not necessarily a negative. Like I said before, I had fun with the combat, but if you really liked SW2 and you have expectations that this game will have many of the awesome stuff SW2 had, then it might not be for you, at least not for almost $60. Would probably buy it on a sale.Overall, I understand that SW1 was more linear and such, but at least it had a WAY better story (as well as SW2) and even though SW2 deviated quite a bit, I think it was very well done and Devolver Digital was on to something really good there. SW3 is unfortunately a bit of a let down.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Huge step back from Shadow Warrior 2. I purchased without looking at any media, previews, or material related to the game because I wanted to avoid any spoilers whatsoever and because I enjoyed the original game and the previous 2 in the rebooted series. Experience is totally linear, any sense of having a character build has been stripped out, it plays like the new Doom games... in a bad way. Everything that's wrong with the new Doom is here in force. I beat the game with 6 hours played, and that includes stepping away and spending 2 hours making/eating dinner. Bland, repetitive level design. After the first level you'll basically be sticking to a strategy of finding a route you can loop through each arena to kite enemies along, using ranged weapons if you need to recover health or melee if you need to recover ammo. No strategy required. Hard mode actually makes this strategy easier because the enemies are "more aggressive," which means they mindlessly zero in on your location. No co-op, no revisiting levels to find secrets or collectibles, no fortune cookies, poorly optimised despite several patches and game-ready drivers available from nvidia. The best part about this game is that the traversal at least feels pretty decent (but you will probably have at least one death where you were CERTAIN you should have been able to start wall running, or where you grapple up to something and end up landing below it and falling to your death).Really disappointed to not be able to recommend this game after enjoying the last one so much. Worth getting if it goes on sale for 60% off or more, or if they add more content to the game (somehow), but that doesn't seem likely.

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the game, I feel like I can write a review on it in good confidence, even with only the 6 hours that I played (I took my time and that's STILL all that was required to beat the game). The game has extremely fun combat with nice unique weapons that are useful in their own way. You've got the classic grenade launcher, slice-y disk spewer, machine guns, fancy sword, etc. What you would expect from a Shadow Warrior game but on the most basic level. However, as someone that came from Shadow Warrior 2, words can't describe how disappointed I was with this "sequel" for MANY reasons. Let me explain.After reading some other reviews (after already beating the game), I found that a lot of people disliked the game for a few of the same reasons as each other, like they thought Wong was annoying or that the characters were poorly fleshed out. While I can agree with the latter point, Wong is MEANT to be an idiot. That's supposed to be part of his charm. I personally found his jokes funny in a 3rd-grader-humor kind of way. You just kind of turn your brain off while killing demons and chuckle at the dumb a** remarks he makes. For me, Wong nor any of the other characters were the breaking point in this game. I actually quite enjoyed the dynamic between the characters, for what little time it existed, and that brings me to my main gripes.The game is  underwhelming in content.The content it gives you? Fun! Enjoyable, but by the end of the game when the credits started rolling, I thought it was a joke given how little content there was compared to it's predecessor. What kind of content is it lacking you might ask? Well, honestly everything.The linear level path was uninspired and felt like an ATTEMPT at providing a similar experience to that of the Doom franchise, but without the same unique flair provided by it. While each level/arena area LOOKS slightly different, it all felt very similar in the end and had the same process. - Grapple to an area- Do relatively easy parkour- Kill enemies in area- RepeatEVEN THEN, I feel that the game was digestible and fun, to put it kindly. Although what really turned me off was the removal of all of the previous games RPG elements, rather than the continuation of building upon them and structuring around them. Things like getting mountains of new weapons, upgrading them, whole skill trees devoted to Wong's individual types of talents and gear usage, ALL gone. Instead you're given around 5 weapons ONLY, that you cannot change out at all and that you can only upgrade (each) 3 times. As far as your own character (Wongs) skills,  it's about just as egregious, whereas you only get a similar small amount of rather lack-luster level up abilities too. Like,  ? Really? While the 5 or 6 weapons you get are each unique, it is  compared to the amount of cool weapons you could get in the previous game. If you're someone who liked the loot aspect from the previous games,  .Regardless of the insane lack of loot (literally no loot at all. Your inventory exists solely to upgrade your existing weapons a very small amount of times) and the insane lack of talents/talent tree perks, AS WELL as having no shop/home area hub to buy items, the game continued to disappoint me by the lack of content. I (again) played for around 6 hours, and beat the game. I wasn't rushing or grinding or speed running or anything of the sort. I was playing casually and taking my time, and still beat the game extremely quickly. When it was over and the credits started rolling, I genuinely thought it was a joke. I was thinking, "Oh haha good one. Nice prologue, maybe I get to buy more weapons and access a shop and a skill tree that matters now etc etc." but no. It wasn't a joke nor was what I played an opening prologue, The short, extremely linear. 6 hour experience was the entire game. Now listen. In closing, I had a decent time. However, the main thing that allowed me that decent time was the thought in the back of my mind that the game had more content it was holding out on me, like the things I mentioned previously, but it didn't. If I had been wise enough to read reviews and watch game play of this game before buying it, I probably never would have. Compared to the previous game, the INSANE lack of content overall like extensive weapon choices and talent trees made me regret my purchase and feel sad that I trusted the developers to have made a game like SW2 but better.I'll take this as a lesson going forward to do more research before buying a game, instead of getting excited that a sequel to a game I previously enjoyed just came out, and buying it immediately. If you're looking for a cheap-short arcade-esque feeling game to play and finish in an afternoon when you're bored, then sure, buy this when it's on sale. It might live up to that expectation, but if you're looking for a true Shadow Warrior 3, then I'm sorry  .

_childDocuments_.review: If you're interested in SW3, you've probably heard this a hundred times already, so I'm gonna focus on the individual things I like about this game. Please keep in mind that I haven't played SW1 or 2 and only bought this game because people drew Arena Shooter comparisons:The enemies are interesting and varied, the hitboxes feel fairThe guns are also varied, unique and feel , especially the shotgun with all its upgradesThe game is beautiful and runs at 80fps on high settings and 160fps on low settings on my 1660 superThe gore and the finishers look good, although some finisher animations are a bit too long for my tasteI didn't really like the grappling hook at first and felt it to be a little clunky. I still feel like it could've been smoother, but I got used to it and kinda like it now, especially for pulling yourself towards enemies and pulling barrels towards youThe arena designs are fine, nothing too noteworthy hereThe gore weapons are a great idea! Although i find myself to always use the same two or three, and often I don't use them at all because of the amazing weaponsThe humour is fine, mostly. Some oneliners actually made me laugh and I like the popculture referencesMovement feels great! The slide and dash mechanic feel fluid and mastering them gives you a lot of mobility in the arenas, although I kinda wish you could slide sidewards and backwardsI also like the 1hp system, where a fatal hit sets you to one hp and gives you a last chance to recover. Doom Eternal also had this, but it's more clearly communicated here and it mostly prevents "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths" in my experience and does not take away difficultyThe sword feels amazing and I find regaining ammo to be really fun and fluid here!Some of the things I didn't like:The platforming. In Doom Eternal it wasn't amazing either, but at least you could fly by or even "skip" most of it after you mastered the movement (and speedrunner strats hehe, thank you Raitro). In SW3 everything feels very "scripted" and by the end of the campaign it gets really staleThe boss fights, especially the first one, are kinda lameThe bugs. I played through the "Dragon Nest Village" Survival Map three times on Hard difficutly, and every time it didn't finish although I played through all rounds and waves. Very frustrating. Also a lot of platform edges feel kinda ♥♥♥♥ and you just fall off the map where you expected to climb. In arenas with multiple vertical layers, large enemies often get stuck in between themThe sensitivity settings. I have to go down to 800 dpi (usually 1600) and use the lowest possible sens, and that's already ~22cm/360 on 130 FOV (30cm on 90 FOV). What the ♥♥♥♥? A lot of shooters don't have up-to-date sens scales, and this is on of themI can't map multiple keys to the same action. With all the walking and platforming in the campaign, I like to also bind the slide to the mouse so my pinky can chill a bit. Not possible hereI didn't care for the story at all, which isn't really a valid critique as I don't know the other games. Cut scenes look good though.Overall a great game if you like the genre. As a Doom, Quake and Devil Daggers/Hyper Demon player I felt like I "mastered" it pretty quickly. Played through the campaign twice, once on Hard and once on Hardcore (which is actually gonna kick your ass!) and basically only play the survival mode now to focus on the combat loop. I wish it had more than three maps, but it's gonna last another 10-15 hours for me probably. I recommend buying it on sale7.5-8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It’s very disappointing to see so many negative reviews piling in for this game, mostly because of its length and differences from previous entries. My experience thus far has actually been pretty damn good. I’ll just let you know right off the bat, this game is nothing like Shadow Warrior 2 (I never played #1), and in my opinion, it changed for the better.I guess I’ll start off with the pros. The world design is literally gorgeous, and has a truly massive scale to it. The game will sometimes set you up with a nice view to just look at the graphics and world they created, I love it. The enemies are really cool, unique, and have a new spin on glory kills that you would see in DOOM. Arena’s are set up with great platforming opportunities, trap kills, explosive barrels, all of the above. Basically, all around design is amazing.But the real pro is just the gameplay man. The movement is FAST, the gunplay is TIGHT, and the gore is SUPREME. The different options you have for entering each fight are pretty big, you could make use of your grappling hook onto enemies, traps, whatever it is, same goes for weapons, you can basically use whatever you prefer. The solution for getting materials such as ammo or health back is super fun and easy too. All you have to do is shoot, slash, kill. Easy. Shoot enemies to death, and they drop health. Katana them, you get ammo. And everything is upgradable too. Not just any slight number adjustments either, big weapon changes that can really help you and benefit the fast pace. It feels reminiscent of Ghostrunner with that fast katana action, and feels a lot like DOOM with the guns and arena gameplay. But I think it’s certainly different enough to avoid being called a knock off.The audio design will be my shift from good things to say about the game, to bad things. I’ll start off by saying that the weapon and kill audio design is just FLAWLESS. Beautiful, meaty, chunky, heavy, just truly perfect. It’s as satisfying watching a 12 gauge enter a demon's chest as it is to hear it. Then the music, some of it is pretty great, some is generic. The switch between good and bad music playing in the background is really odd. On one hand you have original unique vocals tied with great immersing world fits, and on the other hand you have super generic, bad, distracting, rock tracks (and I love rock). It’s weird. It feels like they struggle to pick a theme with the music. Now for voice acting, A much bigger topic than it should be. A lot of fans are acting up that the voice actor for Wang changed, but in reality it was because the original Wang was a white dude imitating an Asian voice, so they decided to get an actual Asian actor for an Asian character role. I see no issue here, what's the big deal? Why are people mad? This is a perfectly reasonable decision on FWH’s part. Besides, this is an action game, not a story game, who REALLY cares? Anyway, I’m getting distracted by this- The voice acting. Kinda lackluster. Nobody really shined, and only that one annoying ass dude in the mask stood out for the wrong reasons. Everything else was normal or forgettable, whatever.Now I’ll talk about just the rest of the cons real quick. The optimization is kind of ass. I’m using an RX 5500 XT, which should fit right in the middle of spec recommendations according to the steam page, and yet I’m averaging 40-60 frames with medium to low settings. Like what is that? (EDIT: I have found that the shadows are a huge performance dropper, so if you put it down to low, it should improve frames quite a bit.) To be honest it doesn’t hugely bother me, but that is not going to be good for other people. Next, the game is short, which isn’t inherently a bad thing because this game goes quality over quantity, but again, people are gonna be all pissy that a $50 game is so short in length. Understandable to an extent. Next, the story is your usual forgettable action game story, nobody likes it, but nobody is mad, because we are here for the action. I think that’s probably about it for the bad things.VERDICT- Good game? Maybe. Fun game? Certainly! This is some of the most fun arena action I have had with a game since ULTRAKILL. It feels marvelous, looks marvelous, sounds marvelous, and most importantly is fast as all hell. Although I am poor, I don’t regret buying this game, I won’t be refunding it, and I will definitely play it again when I'm done with it. Although it might not be a bad idea to release a DLC to justify this price tag a bit better. Sure, Shadow Warrior 3 has a good amount of cons to it, but the pros just knock it out of the ballpark. If you are here for some reeeaaalll, fun, fast, and blistering gameplay, I can surely recommend it, just don’t expect too much aside from all the shooting.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well that was a complete waste of time and money.Two games with engaging combat, passable storylines and fun stupid time. That's what I expected from Shadow Warrior 3 as well, but unfortunately it's just plain stupid all the way through. The whole game is just mind numbing enemy arenas connected with lackluster wall running and quicktime hookshotting. Weapons are boring, slow, and they lack both punch and power. They are also constantly out of ammo, because combat design was lifted straight from Doom 2016 so that enemy kills spawn ammo and health. There are also glory kills, but the prompt for them feels like it pops up at random, and often with enemies that don't offer anything good in return. Powers have been cut down to just chi blast and even that does nothing.Enemies are just demons this time around, no more robots or humans. Ugly, uninteresting and sometimes really annoying. The arenas are usually chock full of them and their AI is mostly just trying to swarm you.There was a story I guess, but I started skipping cutscenes towards the end because of the forced "bumbling idiots" comedy, all-around abysmal writing and acting, and the fact I just wanted to get rid of this game as fast possible. Lo Wang's new voice-over does an absolutely terrible job and the dialogue is just f-ing bad. Not campy and edgy bad like SW1 and 2, but I mean REALLY bad.Soundtrack is nice in itself, but doesn't fit this game at all. Could've worked nicely in Cyberpunk 2077 though.As a fan of the original and the first two remakes, this whole ordeal makes me really sad. I honestly expected better, but I guess Flying Wild Hog just wanted to get rid of this franchise and came up with this full priced, yet only 4 hour long wet fart. So yeah, thanks. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, combat is fun, but it feels way more like a copy of Doom Eternal that removed a lot of the stuff I enjoyed about Shadow Warrior 2. Pros:- Beautiful scenery and graphics- Fast paced combat- It's fairly challenging playing on Hard- Weapons are cool and feel good- Grapple hook is fun and parkour works very well- Upgrades for both character and guns feel impactful in gameplay- The finishers are both hilarious and satisfying, and do add a pretty fun component to the gameplay. - Enemies no longer have RNG weakness/strengths, like toxic/electric etc. That RNG bullcrap was annoying in a shooter.Cons:- No coop- Very short campaign- Environments are tight closed arenas that are very easy to fall off...you can't explore or move very far in any direction, making it feel very closed off. Shadow Warrior 2 I loved exploring and seeing the environments but here you can't dash more than a few times in any direction without falling off the map. - Enemies feel less diverse. In practice, the combat is so fast paced most enemies are blurs. I often can't tell one smaller enemy from another. Most of the larger enemies are elaborate spinning goofy enemies, I missed the huge dragon lizard (serpentaurs) and other stuff from SW2.- It could just be me but the gore feels far less present, in SW2 I recall enemies actually getting visible holes in them from gunfire, burns, and slices where you hit with the sword. In SW3 it seems like they just insta-gib and vanish. - Much less weaponry. I loved the different weapons you could sort of pick and choose what you liked in SW2. The RNG upgrade system was weird but it was a cool system to upgrade what you liked. - Sword play is dumbed down heavily. No spin moves, no stab moves, etc. - I preferred the original voice actor for Lo Wang, but the new guy is fine. - You don't see rabbits making love!?!?- Lo Wang doesn't flip off the enemies.- No central hub or places to explore.- Reload animations in SW2 were really unique and you could actually get different ones randomly. Here, reloads are basically completely negated by them autoreloading when you use the sword. Which is nice from a gameplay perspective, but I still miss it. TLDR I'd rate it 6/10, a half way thumb, would much rather they didn't cut all the features of SW2 out. Still, it runs well, is pretty, and fun, just not what I'd like to see in a SW sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 is a great game. The current review average is sadly lower than deserved due to comparisons to its predecessors and its primary influence, as well as the playtime to cost ratio.Game series with numbered entries (Dark Souls, Battlefield, CoD, Half-Life, Portal, Dead Space, etc) are often similar to each other, and are rightfully compared to their earlier entries. However, those comparisons should be valued second to what each individual entry attempts to do and whether it succeeds at that.I've played SW1's campaign multiple times, played SW2, and have finished Doom and Doom Eternal with the DLC. SW1 was a modernized reimagining of an old IP with a dark, gritty, gore-filled aesthetic, involved skilltree, and denser level design filled with pickups akin to older FPS's. SW2 was a multiplayer looter shooter. SW3 is a vibrant movement shooter, with default grappling hook and wallrunning mechanics, with resource management based on kills. Each entry has been wildly different from each other. I enjoyed SW1's campaign, but disliked SW2's mechanics and gameplay. My expectations for SW3 were based on the information presented by the developer and publisher. From them I could tell that SW3 would be different from the previous games.The game runs exceedingly well. When skipping cutscenes I could barely tell when an entirely new level loaded. Aesthetically the levels are wonderful. The parkour sections between arenas add an excellent sense of scale and speed. The vibrant style carries over to the enemy designs. In video games I enjoy killing humanoid enemies the most, but the designs of the enemies in SW3 were a refreshing departure from killing generic man-with-gun. The combat is fast, with melee bound to RMB, and although guns need to be reloaded, that can be bypassed by swapping. The cinematic executions are infrequent, acting as a temporary powerup. Ripping out a piece of an enemy and using it as a means to kill their friends always feels better than using one's regular arsenal.SW3 launched at 50 USD. 2 months after launch, the game has been on sale at 40% off, for 30 USD. Some may consider that still too high of a price for the length of the experience, but I found this experience to be unique, colorful, and energetic.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's what I think of Doom Oriental. It's a short and sweet game with a whole lot of style. Sure the story is pretty basic, the humour is hit or miss, and there's only a few dramatic scenes that make the story more interesting—but we all know what we're here for: THE GAMEPLAY.Which is a nice streamlined cousin of Doom Eternal's. I like that you can switch between a gun and your sword from left clicking and right clicking respectively. Slicing up demons with your sword will grant you ammo while killing them with guns or "Finishers" (this game's version of Glory Kills) will grant you health. The enemy variety is varied enough with your canon fodder enemies used for resource replenishment, and then you got your mid size and huge sized enemies that take more firepower to take down. A whole lot of weapon switching is encouraged here, along with learning which enemies to prioritize first. I'm kind of torn by the enemies in that while I like that they each have their own strategies to defeat and it's all about enemy prioritization, some enemies are just downright annoying flying around and burrowing into the ground...Anyways. The music is a pretty good blend of hip-hop and cinematic with touches of traditional sounding oriental elements from the instruments to the melodies. This soundtrack will definitely deserve a listen outside of gaming time for me.Final thoughts: a lot of people complain that this game is too short, but I personally think that five hours is plenty for a game like this. It is relentlessly non-stop action, overstimulating, and ALMOST overstays its welcome near the end with a long gauntlet of enemies to kill leading up to the final boss. If you measure a game's worth based by playtime then you're an idiot. D'AH I MEAN...then you should wait for this to go on sale. Otherwise, I personally do not mind having paid full price for this short, sweet, and concise adventure. Cinematics have high production value (too bad the writing couldn't match it), the levels are sprawling with nice long platforming sections and a few light puzzles, and of course, the gameplay is frenetic and intense. Definitely recommend. In my opinion, length of a game doesn't matter because I've had fun for most the past five hours compared to say 30-100 hour games where it's just a lot of endless traveling before you do something fun. Those kinds of games TRICK you into thinking they're fun, when really you're just chasing your next dopamine hit while you do a whole lot of nothing before you do the actual fun stuff.This game cuts to the chase. I would just reduce the enemy count in the final level because Jesus...my fingers hurt.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it is rather short for full price, so definitely get it on sale.I'm actually quite amazed by how many people claim the developers should have stuck with what made Shadow Warrior great instead of becoming a Doom Eternal clone, while referring to SW2 as the pinnacle of the series. I distinctly remember when SW2 released how many criticized it for how much it deviated from the oh-so-great SW1, and had instead become a Borderlands clone. Changing up the formula with every new entry is exactly what I like about the series. I didn't like SW1, I loved SW2, and I enjoyed SW3.In my honest opinion, SW3 does of course not live up to Doom Eternal's rather complex and incredibly satisfying gameplay loop, but it doesn't have to. In general, what they borrowed from the Doom reboots are that combat is now more vertical than ever, that it is a bit more strategic in how to engage what enemy, all fights are now arena-based, and they added finishers that actually grant you new abilities, which is an interesting take on the Doom formula.You can upgrade your weapons and character, but far more linearly than in SW2 or Doom Eternal, and with a lot less variety. This means that the gameplay loop is much more narrowly predefined, take it or leave it. I can therefore understand why some decry the lack of player creativity and customization, but I would draw a line at the "dumbed down" accusations. Playing this made me feel much more tactical than playing SW2. Let's be honest, all you did in SW2 was bunching up demons and then unloading on them with the biggest, most AOE-upgraded grenade launcher you had, and for any bigger enemy, you glanced at the elemental weaknesses, chose the respective weapon, and went to town while walking backwards or in circles, it didn't exactly require tactical ingenuity.The story of SW3 is meaningless, the jokes are on Deadpool level, but that's what you buy into with Shadow Warrior. The handcrafted levels are stunning, the fights I found very engaging, with great enemy variety, particularly compared to the previous entries, where most enemies start to feel the same.All in all, I'd recommend it if you enjoyed the Doom reboots, just don't expect the same level of polish. Pun intended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserved a much better reception than it got.For those who just scroll past reviews:I'll get it out of the way, yes, the game is very short and you’d best not buy it full price – which is the actually fair part of the criticism it got. However, when I see reviews claiming that “Shadow Warrior 2 was better :(”, that’s when I really feel compelled to throw in my two cents.Shadow Warrior 2 is a game I was deeply disappointed with. It’s everything a Shadow Warrior game shouldn’t be. It wasn't aimed at people who love the series and the genre its in. It's quite puzzling who its target audience even was because it was poor as a Shadow Warrior game and it was equally as lame as a looter shooter in its own right.Level design was non-existent. Combat was boring and monotonous. BS loot galore with insignificant stat changes. Enemies with random resistances, weaknesses, health pools and damage output. Quantity over quality approach with quests that are so shamelessly repetitive and low-effort it borders on insanity.It feels like a game that was randomly generated by an AI. Shadow Warrior 2 was a poor man’s Borderlands.It was unfunny in ways that are painful to listen to and it was a buggy slog.That isn’t to say that Shadow Warrior 3 is the perfect followup to the very flawed but solid 2013 reboot, I have my issues with the approach it took when it comes to gameplay (will get to that), but I respect that it made a very clear decision on what it wants to be – in contrast to Shadow Warrior 2 which tried to be many things at once and failed at every single one.The gameplay is surprisingly well-balanced and fast paced.No more 70+ guns which all feel the same to shoot. No more enemies of the same tier that are either dying in one shot or are randomly tanking 500 shots because they have some ooga-booga resistance from the RNG gods.It’s very much arena-based. And each weapon has its own role in the combat loop. You have to cleverly manage your resources while staying on the move through the arenas and identifying the situation and take what you need.Sounds very familiar, doesn’t it? Doom Eternal is one of my favorite games of all time and the best shooter I’ve played in a long time. It's a godtier game, and I’m glad that games take inspiration from it. I can’t help but feel it’s a bit of a shame that Shadow Warrior 3 took to this seemingly derivative approach rather than build on what worked about SW2013 and fix what didn't. Thus make a much more tightly balanced version of the 2013 reboot’s style.Shadow Warrior 3 has secret areas here and there but the bulk of the game is either platforming your way to the next arena or walking through a linear hallway to the next arena. As opposed to 2013’s level design which was something of a middle ground between arena encounters that lock you in a room and bigger areas that can be thoroughly explored, with occasional backtracking. Something of a very basic version of the original SW’s design. Shadow Warrior 3 taking an entirely different approach yet again further emphasizes the reboot trilogy’s identity crisis.I appreciate that something different is offered rather than doing the same thing again, but it feels like there’s nothing tying these 3 games together other than the Shadow Warrior name.The writing has been… okay. Sits somewhere between 2013’s and SW2's.2013 being mostly well-written with a good balance of hit-or-miss humor and seriousness.SW2 being the painfully obnoxious type of writing, with Lo Wang being reduced to a discount Deadpool and everyone constantly making unfunny jokes. It’s basically like Borderlands’ writing after the first game but with a lot of penis jokes.SW3 does make a lot of jokes, not all of which land all that well but it’s a lot less in your face and painful to listen to. It’s mostly benevolent... mostly.Now, it’s not that a story matters that much to me in a game like Shadow Warrior, which is very gameplay focused, but when the writing gets as bad as it does in SW2, it becomes increasingly hard to ignore, so I’m glad they toned it down a bit for SW3.The voice of Lo Wang from the previous two games has sadly been replaced, and while initially I was thinking it was really going to bother me and distract me, the new voice ended up growing on me.He gets the job done alright but he’s not on the same level as the original. It’s a damn shame the og voice wasn’t used here for whatever reason, whether it’s a dumb reason or a legitimate one – this is not what will determine whether I give SW3 a thumbs up or a thumbs down.All of that being said, I can get past these gripes because in the end of the day, Shadow Warrior 3 is the most fun game in the reboot trilogy, by far.The shooting has never been good in the reboot games until SW3 came along. It’s challenging but without being unfair in BS ways. The awesome gameplay make it actually worth replaying on higher difficulties.It’s downright sad that a mediocre game like Shadow Warrior 2 (and I’m being very generous when I call it mediocre) gets to get away with its overwhelming shortcomings and net a “very positive” status on Steam. All while a properly designed game like Shadow Warrior 3 gets buried in “Mixed” reviews.Just because Shadow Warrior 2 offered 20+ hours of content, doesn’t mean those 20+ hours were well-spent and worthy of the player’s time.The real black sheep of the series should and in my opinion IS, without a doubt - Shadow Warrior 2, and whoever enjoyed that one more, I'm happy for you, but I'm even happier that Flying Wild Hog didn't take you into account when making this game. SW2 was a wrong turn.Shadow Warrior 3 is the definition of quality over quantity. Don’t be put off by the reviews and give it the chance it deserves when you see it in a price you deem worthy.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, first and foremost: if you were a big fan of Shadow Warrior 2 in particular and are expecting another looter shooter with co-op, this game ain't for you.However, if you are a fan of the more recent wave of "retro throwback/Boomer" shooters, this may be up your alley.  The game this takes the most cues from is (obviously) Doom Eternal.  The level structure, the arena designs, and the core game play loop are very much aped from Doom Eternal.  The health and ammo regeneration system is very much a "take your resources from your enemies approach and the AI and weapon designs are very much in that game's vein.It is, for all intents and purposes, a "Doom clone."  That's not necessarily a bad thing, though.  A great many a game is but a clone of another, earlier game; Halo 1 was basically a slowed-down Quake 3 clone and Call of Duty was internally called "MOH (Medal of Honor) Killer", just to name a couple.  What matters is "does the game present it's mechanics without flaws?"  And in the case of Shadow Warrior 3, yes it does...mostly.First thing's first: the good.  Shadow Warrior 3 is fun as hell.  It's movement is snappy and tight, it's guns feel meaty and powerful, the sound design is great - all of the guns and enemies have very distinct, readable, sound cues and no sound felt out of place.  The arenas all feel hand crafted and like a lot of care went into platform placement as well as what enemies are placed in the arena.  The platforming sections flow smoothly (mostly) and give you a nice reprieve from the onslaught of carnage that awaits in the arena sections.  The visuals are also stunning with brilliant colors, complex geometry, and tons of variety along with technically running quite well.Now, for the bad.  First thing first is, while it's definitely not important to the game play, the story kinda sucks.  It's cheesy and convoluted and feels more like excuses to take you to the really well-designed levels (which it probably is) and the writing is sub-par at best.  Lo Wang's new voice actor (Mike Moh in replacement of Jason Liebrecht because, let's face it, a white guy doing a Chinese accent ain't really gonna fly anymore) does a fine job at voicing the protagonist, but god does his dialogue suck.  Hoji doesn't fare much better somehow being even more obnoxious than he was in SW 2013.  The inability to replay previous levels to complete missed challenges is an obvious problem and feels like it really should be in there.  Unfortunately, once the credits roll, when you replay your save file, it just immediately loads you into the final boss.The mixed.  Well, it's short.  I finished my play through in about 6-7 hours on Hard, but I don't necessarily view that as a negative.  I get that it's a $50 game, but I'm kinda getting sick and tired of these giant, sprawling 60+ hour games that have very little content but extra busywork beyond the main game; like a giant plate of spaghetti with only three or four meatballs.  A 6-hour game that's mostly killer, very little filler that respects my time as a working adult I find very much appreciative.  That said, it's also rather easy.  Compared to Doom Eternal, Shadow Warrior 3 on hard, at the absolute hardest the game ever gets, it's closest to the mid-point of Super Gore Nest on Ultra Violence.  If you found Doom Eternal to be way too frustrating on even "Hurt Me Plenty", you may find comfort in this game's relative ease.  If you're looking for a challenge, however... just load up the World Spear Master Level on Nightmare and let your huevos get crushed under the weight of 6 Tyrants and 5 Archviles.  The soundtrack, while fun, I find unfortunately unmemorable, and I believe a lot of that is just because the default mix has the OST too quiet compared to the sound effects (if you want to remedy this, go into the sound options and turn the sound effects down to between 60-70%).Overall, if you want a quick, bite-sized boomer shooter with tight controls and punchy weapons, I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 is this year's RAGE 2.While this may be taken as a bad thing, seeing how nobody liked RAGE 2, I mean it in the best way possible, because RAGE 2 is my jam and so is Shadow Warrior 3. I love this game: I think it's the best game Flying Wild Hog has ever put out, it's the best game in the franchise and it's in my top three of the best shooters in the last five years. I find it really satisfying to take a chance on a game that has a "Mixed" rating on Steam (which on this platform translates to committing a few war crimes / 10, thanks zoomers) and coming away from it really satisfied, and the reverse often happens with games that have the "Overwhelmingly Positive" rating, because it's an Early Access pixelart crafting indiegame about depression or being a minority. So yes, the campaign is very short, and yes, it has very little replayability aside from the difficulty settings and the achievements. Yet I still prefer SW3 over any current open world / RPG hybrid game (which SW2 was) because it knows exactly what it is and it doesn't waste the player's time with side quests for meaningless characters, loot, enemy levels or repetitive tasks. I will never replay The Division but I'll replay SW3 at least once a year.I want more developers to have the balls to cut out the fat from their games and give players shorter, more satisfying experiences. Surely this is a financially logical move as well? However, while I will die on the hill that is shorter campaigns in games, what I do ask in return is that this supposed freed up development time should be spent in making the game be as optimized and as dense as humanly possible, with as much variety and options for the player as possible. And there were a number of things that I found lacking: 1. Something that sold me on the game were traps that can be activated to quickly get rid of an overwhelming number of enemies, but these are barely in there. I think I count on one hand the amount of arena's that feature traps. 2. I also found the arena's to be a little bland, they needed more variety, where it's not just a circle with health- and armor pickups. FWH copied DOOM Eternal a little too much in that regard, and they needed to stand out more to make SW3 more unique compared to Eternal. I was hoping that the arena's could be these dynamic battlegrounds where, in comparison to the Slayer, Lo Wang shouldn't be powerful enough to tackle ALL of the enemies at once, and first had to thin the horde by outmaneuvering the enemy. You can use your imagination here: you have more regular traps but you could have external influences like a wonky arena over a chasm, an arena where you slide down a mountain and have to use the level itself to not die, a meteor storm that smashes into enemies, a sand worm tearing bits the arena apart, strong weather where you sometimes have to find cover or other elements like a neutral creature that steps on the enemies. You could have vertical arena's where you have climb a tower while enemies chase you around... While I really enjoyed the fights, they could have been these huge, unique, glorious spectacles. 3. The cinematic kills take a little too long and lack variety. After the first time you watch a unique cinematic kill, the game should play these a little faster starting from the second time you watch it. In Shadow Warrior 2 you had like a thousand animations for almost a hundred different weapons and here you get one single animation per enemy or weapon.4. It is quite heartwarming to see that Flying Wild Hog is continuing it's trend of inclusivity by letting the mentally handicapped write the stories and dialogue for their Shadow Warrior games. While the dialogue isn't quite the Joss Whedon cancer levels as the previous two games, even getting a surprised chuckle from me here and there, five funny jokes in comparison to a hundred forced jokes isn't a good ratio.5. I missed the fortune cookies, we get orbs instead. Maybe FWH could've combined the two where the cookies function as upgrade points while giving you a cute one-liner?6. The sound mixing is a little off? I found the volume of the music to be way quieter than it should be, and I had to fiddle around a lot of make it so that it played at the right volume.7. Inability to change certain keybindings, which is embarassing for any game, especially on PC.8. For a game as beautiful as this, the lack of a photo mode is quite puzzling.9. Changing the game speed should be a thing. I replayed the game on the Hardcore difficulty setting at 120% speed, which makes the game feel totally different, and way more fun.What you have here is a really good combat engine that sounds and looks like God, but lacks variety and polish in a few places. It could've used a little more enemy variety, arena variety, animation variety, ... a little bit more everything, really. Either...a. Devolver needed to launch this game at 30 or 40USD, or...b. They needed to delay the game in order to flesh it out more to justify the price. I have a feeling that, since the developers are like working on three (or four?) different games at once, Devolver pushed them to finish this project up as soon as possible so that the team could work on the other projects they have lined up, which in academic circles is known as "doing a Square Enix".I honestly really do love what FWH have created here. Not even this most recent game, but the franchise in general. They are all very different games, and not all of them are good, but they are all certainly unique. I'm excited to see what comes next. An expansion pack or a sequel that takes everything of this game and improves it even more.It made my weekend, and I am very satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on this one. I'll recommend it, because what's there is good, even if it’s a very short-lived experience.The Good: Levels look great. There are some visually stunning levels in there and they are all laid out in a way that works well with the great movement mechanics this game has. Which is another big plus. Run, Dodge, Wallrun, Slide and Grappling Hook all work very smooth and make for a fast paced action. Even though the action is frantic I never found myself lost, and you can always easily distinguish the enemies from the surroundings. Enemies are varied enough. Weapons feel impactful. Sound design is also great. Special Take-Downs add a layer of complexity to it. Do you use the take-down on the smaller enemies to get health or freezing bombs frequently or do you wait for the big boys to grab some amazing time limited special weapons. Slashing enemies with the katana drops ammo, shooting enemies drops health so you need to balance that. Killed enemies drop yellow balls to fill your take-down meter. Works like a charm. The traversal sections in between the arenas are neat and give you some breathing space in between. They are used to deliver many of the games dialogues that aren’t part of cutscenes. The menu and skill trees are very simplified but do the job well. Mostly polished experience.The Bad: No CoOp. Very short. Took me 7h to get through, and from what I hear most people beat it in less time. No New Game+ so you can’t replay the game and keep your Skills or Weapons, which is a shame really. The game tries to be funny, but didn’t pull it off for me. Sure there are some fun moments to be had, but very often it’s cringy. I’ve had two bugs during my first playthrough.1) Arena sections end or progress, when you kill all ‘elite’ enemies. One time I had to look a very long time to find an enemy floating around beneath the actual level in the deathzone. Another time I didn’t find it at all and head to restart the section.2) The traversal section where you slide down the mountain on a disc ends with you having to wallrun/hook a bit before rejoining the disc. However I’ve tried several times and couldn’t get on the disc, not for the life of me. The disc was gone to quick and the grappling hook wasn’t enough to get me on. I always landed behind the disc and died. Quit in frustration and retried later where it worked first time. Can’t say for sure if it really was the games fault, or just me, but it felt like a bug nevertheless.The Different: Shadow Warrior 2 had very open levels, that where actually not all too bad for generated levels, but they where still rather bland. Here the levels are rather linear, but also more focused and crafted with intent. There are no side quests/missions/maps here either. You’re not gonna like it if you’re into open worlds. I personally favour the hand made level design though.Shadow Warrior 2 had a bunch more weapons, but the loot shooter aspect of it was annoying. Looking through pages of meaningless RNG weapon upgrades was very cumbersome and I’m happy that’s gone, even if it means we’re down to 6 Guns + Katana.Speaking of which, the katana serves a much more utilitarian purpose this time around. Gone are all the special moves (except hold to charge) and it’s mainly there to deliver ammo drops for the guns. It’s not it’s own weapon slot either, as it’s bound to the second mouse button, while all the guns are shot with first mouse button. Shadow Warrior 3 is a much more shooting focused game than SW2 was.What I’m hoping for:* New Game+ to restart the game with all your character and weapons upgrades intact. I’m fine with having to collection the weapons again, as long as their upgrades remain.* Chapter selection, or maybe even arena selection.Based on Build ID: 8289111 updated on 1st March, 2022

_childDocuments_.review: This game cost me £35 and I finished it in under five hours.That just about says it all right there. But there's more. They tried to make DOOM and wrap it in a Shadow Warrior skin. It doesn't work very well. The combat is... there, I suppose. It is very DOOM-y, but that's not really much to recommend it. Shadow Warrior isn't DOOM, it was never supposed to be.The combat detracts from everything else. The visuals are amazing, the world beautiful, but it's VERY linear, as different from the second game as that was from the first and not in a good way. Gone are all but the barest customisation options. The weapons have no alternate fire mode. Chi powers are reduced to the one, using the sword is punished, though I like that you seamlessly switch from gun to sword without trouble.The writing is... alright. This just isn't as much fun as the ones that came before and FAR less value for money. Five hours? For that much money?This is such a shame, because the parts not involving combat are terrific, the graphics, the characters, what few of them there are, are fun, but with so little meat on the bones, it's just not what it should have been.When they can make a game like Shadow Warrior 2, which was fun, interesting and replayable... this is just a let-down. There is no world here like there was in previous games. Just one combat zone after another, no people to fight for, no real antagonist except for a dragon that doesn't speak. There's nothing to invest in, no stakes to fight for. It's not terrible, just exceedingly meh.4/10, and only because the few landscapes they have are lovely to look at.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending Shadow Warrior 3 is hard since, while it's decent, it's worse that SW1 and SW2 in almost every way. I did enjoy my time with it, but seeing as the campaign is 4-5 hours long I only recommend SW3 if you can get if for $10 or less. There is a New Game+ mode, but I don't really feel compelled to go back to playing through the game again.- Graphics/art style. It looks pretty.- Performance. It runs really well.- Level design. The levels all look good and feel nice traversing. The running sections of the game really make you feel like a badass with all the parkour. It's extremely linear though, which has pros and cons.- Length. 4 hours is almost insulting for a game with a base price of $40. - Story. The story was never an important part of the SW series, but there's still something that feels off about it in SW3. It's like they had plans for a much more grand story but for whatever reason they where unable to realize it, leaving us with a barely-held-together cliff notes version of what it was meant to be. I suppose you could say that it wraps up Lo Wangs character arc after 3 games.- Glory kills. Similar do the new DOOM games, SW3 has a glory kill system. While not conceptually bad, I'm still putting it under "The bad" because the execution (heh) of the mechanic is lacking. For one, the executions take far too long. DOOM did it right, with extremely quick executions that didn't interrupt the flow of combat. SW3 went in the other direction, with some of the executions triggering animations that can last for up to 5 seconds. A unique aspect of the executions is that you get a temporary weapon based on what enemy you killed, but almost all these weapons didn't feel great to use.- Gunplay/swordplay. I haven't played SW1 or SW2 in a while, but I'm pretty sure that the combat used to feel better in the older games. At least it did in SW2. The guns in SW3 are mostly fine (if uninspired) but the sword combat just feels off. I loved using the sword in SW2 since it felt great slicing enemies apart with various maneuvers, but in SW3 you get far less variety and using the sword just doesn't feel good. There's no impact, you just swing it around and if there's something in front of you it'll take damage and eventually die, but there's little visual feedback that you're actually hitting something.- Enemy design. I'll give them credit for variety, but several enemies just end up being more annoying than threatening.- Linear levels. While the design of individual levels is pretty solid, there's no getting around that the overall level design follows a very set standard: enemy arenas held together by linear paths of of parkour-ing. There are no real cohesive areas, just paths that lead to yet another enemy arena. SW1 was a fairly linear game, but the levels where expansive with lots of hidden secrets and the levels themselves where distinct. SW2 used procedural level generation which made the levels less unique and crafted, but they were at least expansive. SW3 has none of that, it's just a series of straight lines punctuated by the occasional enemy arena. Noting stood out, and while I strongly remember several levels of SW1 I highly doubt it I'll remember much of SW3 aside from the general aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: Hanging from his belt is a sheath smeared with dirt, all scratched up. It's hard not to heed the katana's dull, reflectionless surface as he draws it. He once had a sharp blade and a sharp tongue to match it, but it seems he isn't concerned with either anymore. Other tools along his belt, however, are shiny and oiled up, twinkling in the light. Lo Wang has given his arsenal enough oomph in his latest journey, but he has lost his touch. His soul and identity, too.You're wondering what happened to him, aren't you? Let's back it up to where it started, then. When Duke Nukem was popping steroids to kick alien butt, and Doomguy was on a "Rip & Tear" frenzy without making a peep, a warrior emerged from their shadows. Lo Wang is essentially a gun-toting, katana-wielding, walking d*ck joke that in no way was the funniest man ever brought to video games, but pulled off a few iconic one-liners which made him hard to forget. From boomer shooter to looter shooter to bargain-basement , Wang himself has been having an identity crisis, just like his games. Things that made him stand out among the sea of shooters have been lost, like a fart in the wind. Wang! Haha! Get it? The same exact joke squeezed dry for about two decades, now with eye-glazing puns that he self-consciously defends and trite pop culture references like singing "Another One Bites the Dust”, except he says douchebag in it. His quips are past their prime, and he doesn't try in the slightest to retain the irreverent sense of humor he was known for. The result is dirty, tasteless, one-note gags that spoil a rather sweet blood 'n' guts smoothie. picks up where the second game ended, more or less. A colossal, world-devouring dragon that Wang unleashed turned out to be a real bastard to kill. The epic failure on Wang's part has left him feeling washed up and depressed. Fortunately, his former employer/nemesis shows up with a truce offer and a way to put the dragon down for good. What follows is Wang tirelessly swinging (giggity) from one arena to another, cutting through Yokai—or demons, if you prefer—to get to the dragon.It is an exceedingly one-dimensional story with hollow characters, and that’s about as deep as it gets. It explores a new low compared to its predecessors. Significant betrayals and deceptions are passed over in a manner of moments, and its character relationships are changed with throwaway lines of dialogue. I wouldn't be having many quarrels if some of the old charms were still present: real villains, intriguing plot twists, or light-hearted banter among the cast. Nope... nothing at all.Comedic chafing aside, the combat can be chaotically fun for a one-and-done, seven-hour romp. Crazy-fast gunplay, free-flowing movement, switching between different flavors of carnage, and tracking a constantly dwindling ammo count, this is what Wang excels at. His arsenal ranges from standards like a revolver to more unconventional additions like a shuriken-shooting crossbow. He likes to keep a shotgun, grenade launcher, and railgun in his back pocket for when things get hot, too. Each feels beefy in your hands. These are the guns that put demon b*tches on their back. A bunch of new toys, on the other hand, give the enemies a taste of their own medicine. Nabbing yellow droplets from defeated Yokai fill the meter of finisher moves, then with a single press of a button, Wang rips their insides out to grab a devastating but temporary gore tool to break out complete mayhem. came closer to its roots. And I liked that.One last trick up his sleeve is the grappling hook. It's a mechanic that boils down to hitting a key within a considerably long window and watching the same animation as he flings around each time. A neat gimmick to spice up the predetermined parkour points, though it is functionally useless during combat. Hardly ever did I find myself at death's door to use the hook as an escape... not even on the highest difficulty, which is a joke in and of itself; many second chances, a large room for error, combined with brain-dead, bullet-sponge enemies. Being unstoppable is fun for a while, but it gets stale if a single strategy is the solution to every problem. This is why the shadow warrior never gets the black belt.Oh, it seems I forgot to talk about the katana—not that it's much of a potent weapon anymore. Reduced to trivial button mashing, all of the special moves from previous entries are now replaced with simple light and heavy attacks. It now has no use other than replenishing ammo from the fallen foes, given that if you've upgraded it already. Although these upgrades, whether in the form of orbs littered about or rewards for completing challenges, don't allow for varied playstyles. Extra ammo reserves, more frequent health drops, or a few minor weapon buffs that seem to have a petty impact on your survival.All that said,  still finds more ways to ruin however much fun you had mushing enemies to a pulpy juice. Signs of stagnation appear too early on, due to every gun and demon type being dumped at your feet within the opening hours. It will hurl you from a prolonged fight in a flat arena, right into a mind-numbingly scripted platforming section, and back into another brawl. As thrilling as both can often be, not providing respite from the linear rush damages the loop beyond repair; a little breathing room or a sprinkle of exploration is nowhere to be found. Even tiny extras—like a challenge mode, coop, NG+, or anything of that ilk—to give it a sense of replayability are missing. It Doomed itself by trying to capture 's lightning in a bottle, without realizing a mere bottle can't hold such greatness.For what it lacks in most aspects, it makes up for in audio and visual composition. Sure, it's not as gritty as heavy-hitters of the genre, but I'll be damned if I say it isn't a spectacle, at most times. Neo-feudal Japanese aesthetics nestled in gorgeous panoramas of mountain pillars make for salubrious eye candy. Unless you're capturing the moment, none would stick with you, as you're probably too busy blazing through everything. The music, however, complements the sonic chariot you're riding right into the dragon's maw. Even though the absence of Stan Bush will hurt long-time fans, East Asian traditional tunes fused into hip-hop and electronic beats leave nothing else to be desired.Slicing and dicing on a mix of medium and high settings, my  maintained a steady 60 FPS at 1080p. There were no noteworthy issues... other than whenever Wang opened his mouth.It never takes its foot off the gas... or out of your ass. A dreadful combination, squeezing the life out of it. Painfully linear and limited. Lacking, but not in the number of lame jokes.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: don't buy it right now, give it some time, it's still fun, just not like the previous games.i want to like this game but for what it offers at the moment it's not worth the 49.99, which is sad as i loved the first game, the second game was a admittedly buggy mess, but i loved it too, but i felt the problem is that the game lacks some thingspros--it looks gorgeous and while the cinematic (at the time of writing this review) were stuttering, they still looked lovely-the gameplay has a nice solid gameplay loop, guns give health, melee gives ammo, as well as adding in some features that are quite entertaining-the design for enemies is very interesting, and they offer a challenge on medium (which is what i played on till the end)-the characters are the same as previous games, and wang makes a return as the same old loser we lovecons--while i hate to say it, the game features no level replay function, nor does it offer a new game plus, once you beat the game, you can only continue at the last boss battle-fully upgrading weapons is not hinted at being possible your first time through, as the weapon and character upgrades are earned through challenges and found in the level, thus you will need to keep a good eye open if you want to upgrade everything (if possible)-the story is somewhat lack luster, now while revenge stories are fun and SW1 did it, it also had a very nice emotional beat where the characters grew and you also grew to like them, in SW2 the story revolved around wang helping the woman stuck in his head get back out, as well as get back at zilla and some other side stories, thus, fun, but not quite the same emotional beat. here, in SW3, the story revolves around killing a giant dragon and nothing else, characters barely grow, and overall you'll feel as if some characters were tacked on.-the gameplay loop, while fun will get repetitive given the nature of the combat arenas, where you enter, shoot, kill, shoot ,kill, and you may die occasionally, as the enemies are actually very aggressive, but this will be how every arena will go, you enter, perhaps do a finisher on a special enemy, get the new "gore tool" use it to kill a few enemies in spectacular fashion, toss it away after a bit, then move on to use your (up to) 6 weapons to kill enemies, maybe slice some up, and repeat this process over and over and over for every arena. they took doom eternal and tried to do what they did, but without the same punch, as many large enemies make up the bulk of the enemy roster and you will have a hard time chewing through them quickly (i recommend freezing enemies and shooting them with either the grenade launcher or shotgun)overall, im kinda sad about this, but it only came out today, so it is subject to change, but for now, im not quite impressed, i do hope they fix it later on, making things a little more fluid, and perhaps adding a new game plus feature, but for now, im going to refund, but if it does get fixed up, i will happily buy the game again.that said, feel free to buy it any support the devs, but of course use your money wisely and be aware of hat you are buying here, this is a good game that needs some work.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow we are still struggling with ultra-wide and even REGULAR resolution support in 2022? excuse me? - No adjusting of windowed borderless resolution.- gave me only TWO windowed resolution choices, the highest being 1280x720 for some reason only god knows.- Using an ultra wide monitor and want to set the game to run at 16:9,  1920x1080 for streaming or recording purposes (even with your desktop resolution set as such)? Too bad. You get 1920x1080 stretched out over your whole 21:9 monitor instead of the 16:9 it should be using.- The game uses vertical fov instead of horizontal fov so if you DO use an ultra-wide resolution, you have the top and bottoms of the screen cut out because the screen scales vertically instead of horizontally.I have games decades older than this that have no problems with resolution options and they can even scale up to modern resolutions NATIVELY. But a UE4 game released in 2022? apparently not. I am nowhere NEAR close to being any kind of graphics snob (indeed the game does actually look very pretty, barring some jarringly stiff character and facial animation), but holy jesus this is unnacceptable. And this is coming from someone who loved the previous 2 FWH Shadow Warrior titles.TL;DRIf you have an ultra-wide monitor, don't even bother with this game until they patch in proper support. it will only cause you headaches.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything, movement mechanics, how the combat levels are structured, weapons, even some enemies, floating giant samurai heads that are totally not cacodemons and a fat monster with gatling guns strapped to its both hands that's totally not mancubus'es reeks of Doom Eternal's influence. _childDocuments_.review: Clunky, buggy, extremely frustrating Doom Eternal-like. Finished it on hard so that's where this review is coming from. You don't get any iframes while grapple hooking and wall running so enemies just drain your health while the animation plays out. Running away in some arenas you have to grapple and Lo Wang has to position to the beginning of the animation where you take damage. Grapple hooking to enemies I died multiple times because a demon killed me during the animation. Same is true of wall running, which is also funny because that's where health regen items are sometimes.Health regen mechanics are frustrating. You get ONE chi ability this time, which is push, and even that is bugged. Fully upgraded push, I pushed enemies into pits for them to just walk back on air to pound me into dust. Climbing animations bugs got me stuck in a perpetual climbing loop, during the on-rails segments sometimes red crystals didn't break because I triggered the event too early, and plenty of other bugs.Lo Wang's personality and quips was the only thing I loved about this game.Took me 8 hour to finish it on hard and it was a frustrating experience in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing about this game is that at 11 hours long, the pain of playing it is too short to truly hurt.  The misery I felt playing this was in direct proportion to the sheer joy of playing Shadow Warrior 2 (which is easily in my top 5 FPS games).  If you are near my age, you may remember watching Highlander at the cinema  and loving it, then 5 years later watching Highlander 2 and coming out feeling soiled like a hooker after her first john.  This is how Shadow Warrior 3 made me feel.First of all, this is not a FPS, it is a platform game with FPS highlights (imagine Doom 2, but with 85% platforming and only 15% FPS, minus everything that made doom 2 so much fun).  The times in between the platforming are spent in small arenas, most with death drops taking up much of what little space the arena provides, so that 90% of your deaths will be dropping down these.Second, there are only 6 under-powered weapons in the whole game, many with small capacity so you are always running out of ammunition.  Compare this to the huge amount of weapons in Shadow Warrior 2, each better than the last.Third, the enemies are clowns, literally clowns (OK, they are "demons" dressed as clowns to be precise).  If you suffer from coulrophobia, then this is the game for you as by the end of it, clowns will annoy you more than scare you.So are there any good aspects to the game?  Well, they copied the glory kills from Doom 2 and added a twist where performing one gives you a short temporary boost (a special weapon or health boost).  that was OK.  The graphics were good (in my opinion) and watching the main enemy dragon flying around was fun.  But I can honestly say that the only time I truly smiled during the game was uninstalling it after completing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Turn off the dialogue and skip all the cutscenes for the optimal experience. Trust me, the only thing you'll miss out on is some dated Marvel-esque dialogue. Yeah, sounds great, right?As for the game itself, it is by no means a must-play, but it's a fairly entertaining Doom Eternal-style shooter, albeit way too short and a significant downgrade when compared to the previous two. While I am relieved that it isn't a semi-open-world looter-shooter like Shadow Warrior 2, I'm disappointed by the small arsenal and overly-linear level design--the latter contributing to the game's anemic length. The melee has also been gutted; the combo system is gone, and the katana is no longer a separate weapon, instead being reduced to a quick attack. It's no longer an essential part of your arsenal, and I only used it for the achievements and then let it sit in my inventory for the rest of the game. The gunplay, on the other hand, is delightfully punchy and is bolstered by the meaty sound design and over-the-top gore. This could've easily been the best entry in the series if they had nailed the level design and narrative tone. Still, I do recommend it, and you'll probably enjoy it more if you haven't played the other games. So, pick it up on a deep sale, play through it in an afternoon, and then never think about it again. That's what I did, anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3: Definitive Edition is an absolute blast! At first, I felt a bit lost because the game had taken a different direction from its predecessors and resembled more of a Doom Eternal clone. However, once I got used to the changes, I found myself having a lot of fun.The visuals in Shadow Warrior 3: Definitive Edition are absolutely stunning. The detailed environments and jaw-dropping graphics create a dark yet vibrant world that immerses you completely. Although it's a shame that they didn't utilize their own engine and switched to Unreal Engine, I understand it was likely a decision driven by development costs. Nonetheless, the game manages to look and run great even on my mediocre machine (Ryzen 3600 and RTX 2060 Super).But where the game truly shines is in its gameplay. It flawlessly blends first-person shooting with badass melee combat. Armed with a wide array of devastating weapons, you'll execute flashy moves that allow you to annihilate your enemies in style. The combat mechanics are exhilarating and satisfying, ensuring that every encounter is a thrilling experience.The Definitive Edition of Shadow Warrior 3 offers the complete package, including all the DLC, along with graphical enhancements and performance optimizations that elevate the game to new heights. While the storytelling in the game exists, it's not necessarily the main focus in this action-packed FPS experience. The priority lies in the adrenaline-fueled gameplay and intense combat sequences that keep you engaged throughout. So, even if the story may not make complete sense, it doesn't hinder the overall enjoyment of this action-packed FPS adventure.While Shadow Warrior 3 delivers sheer fun and excitement, it's worth mentioning that there are occasional technical hiccups that can momentarily disrupt the experience. One notable bug I encountered was the inability to shoot until restarting the game. Unfortunately, this issue arose during a crucial moment in the game, specifically when shooting the hook location for rope jumping, resulting in a game-breaking situation.Furthermore, another frustrating bug I encountered was the inability to use chi to stun enemies, which posed a significant challenge, especially when dealing with the formidable "Laser Shogun" enemies. Not being able to utilize this essential ability seriously hindered my progress and caused moments of frustration.Despite these issues, it's important to note that these bugs were not pervasive throughout the entire game, and they didn't completely overshadow the overall enjoyment provided by the intense gameplay and thrilling action sequences.In conclusion, Shadow Warrior 3: Definitive Edition is an adrenaline-pumping gem that'll grip you tighter than a wrestler in a headlock. With visuals so stunning, they'll make your eyes pop out like a Looney Tunes character. The gameplay is more electrifying than a power surge in a lightning factory, leaving you with a surge of excitement that'll make your heart race faster than a cheetah on roller skates.So, strap on your big-boy pants, unleash your inner warrior, and get ready for a thrill ride that'll make your adrenaline glands explode with joy. Shadow Warrior 3: Definitive Edition is a wild, hilarious, and action-packed adventure that'll leave you shouting, "Hail to the king, baby!"

_childDocuments_.review: So this is an interesting title for me and it sort of makes me wish I taken the "try it before you buy it" approach.Gameplay is solid, fun and fast paced. Movement is smooth and not frustrating. The jokes are cheesy and groan inducing, albeit maybe a bit more of the latter than previous entries. The levels are well designed and the  cinematics are well placed and not too long. If Shadow Warrior 2013 was the Duke Nukem Forever of the series and Shadow Warrior 2 is the Borderlands of the series then Shadow Warrior 3 is the Serious Sam of the series. Run and gun, constantly outnumbered and a variety of foes and weapons. Overall I thoroughly enjoyed the game from start to finish and found closure to the cliffhanger that was Shadow Warrior 2's ending.All that said, from start to finish, the game took me six hours. As many likely know I am about as far from a skilled gamer. The difficulty curve on normal was fine for me but is likely too easy for many. Regardless of difficulty, the length of the game is hard to argue for. I have heard the argument of going to the cinema and sitting down for a 90 minute film being easily 10-20 USD if you get snacks/go during the film's premiere. This is true and would put this game right at that price point. Thinking about it, I would say I received about as much fun as I might from three or four films in theater. Still, 60 USD for six hours? Seems a bit excessive.Edit: Major bonuses are warranted; the game plays seemlessly with a trackball mouse and runs with regular old Proton. GEProton7-4 does seem to improve fps a slight bit but overall it runs flawlessly on Linux in my experience. Given that I did enjoy the six hours and the rest of the franchise, as well as Flying Hog's other work, I will not try to seek a refund at this point in hopes that NG+ mode or free DLC will happen.
