_childDocuments_.review: I love Flying Wild Hog and have loved their games since Hard Reset. They do not make bad games however I believe with the talented studio being stretched between three projects at the same time and all being scheduled to release this year, this game sadly has suffered even if it is not a bade game overall.TLDR: Good visuals, progression system from SW2 has been simplified, most similar to the first game, guns feel good with great gore kills that provide useful and creative weaponry, good but seems to be short for the price tag, overall gameplay feels satisfying and addictive, if you are a fan of Serious Sam, Doom, Prodeus, or classic arena shooters you will have a good time. If you have the spare cash grab it, if you can only get one game in this stacked month of releases maybe wait for a sale since there isn't much replay value. So I finally beat the game at about 6 hours. this was including basically one hundred percenting and getting all achievements except two that were glitched. My opinion stand that the game is a good time but for the price I don't know that the short play time is justified when there is no replay ability.__________________________________________________________________________I have played both of the previous Shadow Warrior games as well as the original classic. I am not finished with the game, I am on chapter 5 currently and honestly I am having a hard time putting it down. It is very different from Shadow Warrior 2 but I don't think that is a bad thing. It goes for more of the arcade style arena shooter game play of something like Doom or Serious Sam. Nice cut scenes even if a little too prevalent in the beginning of the game. I thoroughly enjoy the gun play and audio design as both sound and feel very satisfying. If you enjoy the first game or the serious sam games I think you will enjoy this game quite a bit. The "gore" kills if the game are super satisfying as well and I love the creativity of the weapons you receive when killing them (anything from a sword that teleports you, an eyeball minion that slashes through enemies, and even a firework launcher among others) I am progressing through the story very fast (5 chapters at 2.6 hours played, that's with taking time to try and find secrets) and I don't know how many chapters there are, but I feel like I will be done with the game soon and if that is the case I think 50 may be a tad high but I got my key from  and for the 43.59 I think that is much closer to the overall value given what I have played so far.UPDATE: I beat the game and it took me about 6 hours and that was with getting every unlock in the game as well. Overall I really like the game and think if you are a fan of this style of game you will have a good time, granted you don't run in to glitches in the way I have heard some people have. I have not run into any lagging or crashes but my machine is also a little overkill being a 3080, 128GB RAM, and Ryzen Threadripper 3960X 24-Cores, 12TB of NVME gen 4 storage.Rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the essence of "short but sweet". The gameplay loop is extremely engaging and fun. I won't deny the comparison: they almost certainly took inspiration from Doom Eternal's recipe, then home-brewed their own version with an amplified focus on the fun factor. It is far, far less difficult, but the reallocation of combat flow (use gun to get health, use melee to get ammo, use environment to get both, do finishers for temporary buffs/weapons) and uniquely-overpowered nature of your whole arsenal is  for elevating your own ego to the same level as Mr. Wang. Game also ran like butter on my rig, and looked legitimately sublime. I'm a bit of a sucker of landscapes and the like, so I spent a considerable amount of time just looking at the environments in awe (the skyboxes especially look like shan sui paintings in gorgeous colors). The music is not quite anything I've heard before for a game soundtrack, being a collection of  eastern-themed electronic bangers. I legitimately wish for an official soundtrack release.I won't sugarcoat it. If you are looking for a 20-30 hour experience, you will very likely be disappointed. I have no complaints regarding the price point versus playtime calculation, the wildly different gameplay experience compared to SW2013/SW2, or the voice recast (Mike Moh does just fine), but if you have reservations about those, the game simply might not be for you. This experience is all substance and no filler; It feels like Flying Wild Hog set marks for what they wanted to make and then far exceeded each and every one of them. *there originally was a complaint about a lack of level select, but they added one sometime in May 2022 on top of a ng+ and a higher difficulty. very cool, thank you guys :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is the third game in the Shadow Warrior series, and it's probably the weakest, as others have mentioned. However, if you consider the environmental setting, the enemies, and the weapons, then it offers a decent shooting experience, to say the least.     In terms of gameplay mechanics, it follows a similar principle to Doom Eternal for ammo management (melee kills replenish ammo). Unfortunately, one of the major drawbacks is the story. I understand that Shadow Warrior isn't renowned for its "amazing storytelling," but this time it feels rushed, likely because the game revolves around a mere 4-5 hours of gameplay. These hours mainly consist of shooting and platforming, with minimal story-building moments, aside from the looming ancient dragon floating through the sky and the radio chatter with other characters.     Throughout the entire game, you'll hear Lo Wang's quirky dialogue/monologue, which isn't necessarily a drawback if you're already familiar with the character's backstory, but it might become annoying for some players. Some are upset about the replacement of Lo Wang's voice actor, but personally, I believe Wang's "spirit" remains intact, it doesn't feel too foreign to me.     Another significant drawback is the limited number of power-ups/moves, which can't even be compared to the ones from the previous games. The only special moves that are all of the time available are a "chi-blast" that pushes enemies back and the sword stances carried over from previous games, allowing you to infuse your sword with elements. The "other" special moves you can perform are only possible by inheriting elite enemies' tools, but they're only available after executing a finisher on said elite enemies. This feels like a lazy approach by the developers and a lack of creativity, especially considering that even the first Shadow Warrior had more special moves.     The game is decent if you can get it on sale, as the shooting mechanics are solid and provide that dopamine rush to keep you engaged as you slash through everything in your path. However, I wouldn't recommend it at full price. Much of its core gameplay feels shallow compared to its predecessors, as if the series itself has lost its "mojo". I just hope this won't be the last entry in the series, as it would be a very disappointing end for Lo Wang.

Working together to take down hordes of enemies and bosses is immensely satisfying and enhances the overall experience. 👫🎮 The storyline in Shadow Warrior 3 is engaging and well-written. It balances humor and action perfectly, with witty dialogue and interesting plot twists that keep you invested in the characters' journey. The narrative is a significant step up from its predecessors, providing more depth and emotional moments. 📖🌟  Despite its many strengths, the game can become repetitive over time. The mission structure tends to follow a similar pattern, and some of the objectives feel a bit too familiar after a while. More variety in mission design would help keep the gameplay fresh and exciting. 📉🔄 I feel that the character development could be deeper. While the main characters are interesting, their backstories and motivations are not explored as thoroughly as they could be. More character-focused moments would add greater depth to the story. 📚🤔  Personally, I've encountered occasional technical issues and bugs that can disrupt the gameplay. These issues can range from minor glitches to more significant problems that require restarting the game. Regular updates and patches would help improve overall stability. ⚠️🔧 Another drawback is the lack of replayability. Once you've completed the main campaign and experienced the story, there isn't much to keep you coming back for more. Adding more post-game content or additional modes would greatly enhance the game's longevity. 📉🔄 The game can have noticeable difficulty spikes that might frustrate some players. Certain sections can feel disproportionately challenging compared to the rest of the game, leading to potential frustration. A more balanced difficulty curve would improve the overall experience. 📈🕹️ Shadow Warrior 3: Definitive Edition is an outstanding game that offers a thrilling and visually stunning experience. The intense and fluid combat, combined with beautiful graphics and exceptional sound design, makes it a joy to play. The engaging storyline adds depth and keeps you invested in the characters' journey.However, the game does have its flaws. The repetitive gameplay can become a bit monotonous, and the character development could be deeper. Additionally, the occasional technical issues and lack of replayability are notable drawbacks. The difficulty spikes can also be frustrating for some players.Despite these issues, Shadow Warrior 3: Definitive Edition is a fantastic game that is well worth playing. Its strengths far outweigh its weaknesses, and it provides an exhilarating experience from start to finish. Addressing the cons and adding more content would make it even better, but as it stands, it is a highly enjoyable and memorable game.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this with this statement, Shadow Warrior 3 isn't a bad game. It's just a terrible Shadow Warrior and spits on the work the previous two games built. If you want an ok doom clone then this is one of those that looks somewhat pretty. Keep scrolling if you want my real opinion.I bought the entire SW franchise in a bundle shortly after this game dropped and just recently got through them. I beat the first one on Xbox a while ago and decided to do a playthrough to get back in the mood for SW. Then I played through SW 2 deluxe edition. It was a rocky start but turned out to be an amazing adventure with decent characters, and a story that while not perfect, shone a new light on Lo Wang and the collision's affects on the world.I was on a roll, and I have to say I was ready to experience the final chapter in Lo Wang's story. I heard the combat was "doom like", but I didn't really care so long as the story is good, and Lo Wang is Wang. Just hope they don't mess with Hoji or his legacy.Story: The story is short. No getting around it, I beat the game in less than six hours. However brevity isn't necessarily a flaw, especially with how bad it is, and how much changed in an hour. I will cover a few with as few spoilers as reasonable. Wang in the now defunct wang cave explains how "he ended the world", without explaining how it is no longer on dragon mountain. Nor does wang once mention anyone from the mountain in his list of friends, even in the wangpedia. The dragon being loosed is now solely his fault. Retconning the involvement of Zilla, Xing, Mezu, Wang, Kamiko, Anemone, and countless cultists in the ending of the world. Kamiko just is retconned out of existence now, now he just talks to hoji's mask. Despite wang literally being an unstoppable dumba$$ with an amazing mastery of chi, smithing, and the Wang, he is shown as weak and incompetent throughout the game. The writing is a mess, coherent enough that you understand, but a mess none the less.Lo Wang: Lo Wang had been given decent character development over the previous games and made into a strong and interesting character who actually cares about what he's doing. In this game he's a bumbling moron who can't go 5 seconds without getting messed up. Oh they also changed his speech manerisims, accents, design and philosophy, in such a jarring way it's not even funny. This is not Lo Wang, "Mr 2 million dollars", this is Jim (Lo) Wong. HOJI: In the first game the best character was obviously Hoji, and as you progress through the game you learn that Hoji is deeply responsible for nearly everything that led to the collision. Not out of malice, but out of pity, desperation, and love, he causes the goddess Anemone to enter a death like state at his own expense, and screwing Enra. In that game he takes responsibility for the pain he caused everyone and revives Anemone at the cost of his life. In SW 2 he is further painted as someone who was selfish, but ultimately deciding that he'd stand against the realm of chaos.Anyways they made him a cowardly a$$hole who has nearly no redeeming qualities. Oh he also forgot how to transform into his mask, that he actually had the least chi of his brothers, and was actually f##king PERMANENTLY DEAD according to Kamiko who could be compared to Anemone.Other bad changes from the last two:Sword feels weightless, and swordplay feels simultaneously floaty and stiff.Guns have a very limited ammo pool, even when upgraded.Lo Wang has hair now and it looks bad. Writers also try to justify it poorly.There are now 3rd person cutscenes throughout the game, and a lot at that.The demons. Too hard to explain well.All of your powers & perks are either removed or significantly downgraded.Demons are no longer called demons, instead being yokai. Not a great change.All elusion to chi, it's usage, and tech made using it are pretty much scrubbed; being replaced by the blanket term "Magic"All in all I don't like to think of this game as a SW, at least not one that takes place after 2 anyways. It feels like they wanted to soft reboot the franchise because either new writers stepped in or different team was made to adapt the rest of the SW draft to the tune of what's popular. This wasn't a pleasant change of pace, this was a soulless meld of popular ideas painted to look like shadow warrior.Sincerely a SW 1 & 2 fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has received all sorts of flak for multiple reasons and while I can see why, I still think it's a good game. The gameplay has changed greatly from the last two games to be more of a fast-paced arena shooter like those we have seen over the past several years, but too many people have taken this as an excuse to dismiss it as a Doom Eternal clone. _childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered Shadow Warrior 3.  The first game was fantastic, the second game stumbled a bit with the new systems that weren't needed, but the gameplay was fantastic, and the open world took a bit of getting used to and the story was solid, it had a lot to do.  The gem and elemental stuff was fiddly and unnecessary.  I thought Shadow Warrior 3 was going to be a return to form, to the first game, lot's of weapons and upgrade systems, a more focused story with glorious arena's.  It is none of these things.Before I begin the review, if things change, or the game is magically better at some point I will add onto the review and change my stance.  But as it stands…Shadow Warrior 3 is an utter failure.  It is short, the story is suffering from tonal whiplash, the gun's while fun to use there aren't a lot of, and they went with ammo shortages to encourage weapon swapping.  The gore weapons are fun but are limited and often times you save it for a 'worth it' weapon.The game itself is arena's linked by short on rail platform sections, or the required involvement is so minimal it may as well be on rails.  You run along the green paths (even when things are frozen or on fire, or not applicable.) and hit the grapple button when time slows down and you see a ring, and sometimes you have to shoot things off your path.  In a few of the chase sequences this is broken so you can't really grapple what you need to, there are also no checkpoints in these 'chase' sections so if you mess up it's all the way to the start to do the whole buggy mess again and pray to whatever digital gods might be listening it works this time, or glitches to allow you to progress.The Arena's are well made but very open and very linked, the arena's of the first game were very well designed and linked even better, it felt organic like you were moving through real area's.  The second game's open world nature worked because things were out to get you, here… it's just run to arena, have a choreographed fight in arena, and move to the next arena.There are Six weapons, seven if you include the sword excluding the gore weapons.  The weapons feel good, only one is unique and a ton of fun to use.  It really seems like the first two shadow warrior games influenced doom and doom eternal and Shadow Warrior 3 went "Doom's popular lets do that."  So weapons don't have a lot of ammo, it encourages switching and there is an ample supply of 'lesser fodder' oni you can kill to get ammo and health back in a hurry.  The Gore weapons are unique and feel good for gameplay, just wish you could get them longer or make them an actual part of the arsenal.  The way the game wants you to play is to always have gore weapons and looking to finish an enemy (Each enemy only has ONE finisher animation).  However there are better gore weapons than others, so you're going to be saving your finishing meter, hunting the arena looking for the enemy with the weapon you want, which is likely going to be the last major enemy introduced.Lo Wang's witty as always, the story would be good if it was longer and not so rushed and feel like a fitting end to the trilogy.  The game is about Lo Wang having lost his mojo and his journey to get it back in the face of an apocalypse, however once you have control of Lo Wang he is instantly a badass with a shallow upgrade pool (The first games upgrades were way more robust.)  So what Lo Wang says is disconnected from the gameplay, the story is at a breakneck pace and all over the place due to the criminally short story.  Lo Wang can go from cracking wise, to moping, to getting angry and running off and shooting someone in the span of moments.  Everything just feels so rushed.Also the game is made with unreal and like most unreal games it crashes quite a lot.  I thought for the size it was well optimized, I was wrongSo, I pre-ordered the game for $60 in good faith on Devolver Digital and Flying Wild Hog and their stellar record for making games.  $20 would be asking too much for this game.  The game we got feels like the third act of a third part of a trilogy.  So Imagine someone handing you the ending third of a game and calling it a day.  Also the game feels like Doom and Doom Eternal took from the earlier Shadow Warrior games to make themselves better and Shadow Warrior 3 went "Doom eternal is popular lets do what they did."  When they established the formula it is using, It really feels like they lacked confidence all around on this one.Personally I don't know what it would take to fix this game, it needs more, more story, more weapons, more enemies, more upgrade trees, more actual gameplay that's not on rails, the kind of fixes it needs would require just, remaking it from the ground up.  I know the world has been changing, and people have been working from home and I am sympathetic to that, but this game shouldn't have been released in this state, it feels rushed.  It feels like they said "Here is a deadline, get it playable and ship it."  Near the end I was actually dreading the next arena and just wanted it to end.  The game has two bosses where it feels like really fun shadow warrior for a few minutes, the last boss is dragged out to try and squeeze more… time?  Gameplay?  It just feels like a slog, a chore, for a rushed game.  Also it NEEDS a new game + where you can carry over your upgrades and what not.  The other games had that from the start and encouraged more play through's to upgrade everything, this one lacks it entirely, like it wants you to not play it.I can only recommend this with heavy reworks or it's on sale for like, ten bucks tops.

_childDocuments_.review: As of now, I've done everything the game has to offer. I am going to do another playthrough, but I don't expect my views to change.I am not a Shadow Warrior fan and I can say that if you brush aside the need to compare (both to Doom Eternal and previous SW entries) you'll have a time the likes of which you have never really experienced before - especially in the SW franchise. The gunplay is smooth, accessible, detailed and easy to master. So are the controls and the quickswitching, which finally is done right in this series. Every weapon feels amazing to shoot and the impact of the shots is so meaty that demons literaly fall apart. The game also looks amazing and the work that went into the demon, environmental and character design is insane. The story feels really rushed, but it was, in my opinion, what it needed to be to drive the game forward. At least what you get in exchange is constant action with little interruption. The game also has nearly no loading screens, because they are replaced by cinematics - what an amazing idea! Please we need more companies to do this, because it really makes the games feel like a movie instead of a soap opera being interrupted by constant ads of loading screens. The optimization is also really good and I have never seen huge dips in fps, but I would be much happier if the game ran about 15-20% better, because it just doesn't really reach stable 100+ fps. Sure g-sync can fix that, but not everyone has a g-sync or g-sync compatible monitor. However stable 60 fps or mid tier rigs is perfectly doable. I applaud Flying Wild Hog for the work they have done here, because it truly looks and feels like a AAA experience for 3/4 of the price.But my compliments end here. Shadow Warrior 3 is a AA game with a pricetag of 45 dollars/euros, which sits uncomfortably close to the AAA price of 60 for what it has to offer. The game is simply too short. There is only 5-6 hours of gameplay. There are two ways that Flying Wild Hog can resolve this pricing issue. Number one: cut the the price by 15% and p*ss everyone who bought it before off, but atract more people to the product. Number two: release a bunch more content to justify the pricetag - Comunity hub to share content, user made arenas, free dlcs (like they did with SW2) and other content.Why should they bother?BECAUSE THE GAME IS INCREDIBLE. What they have created is a gameloop and gameplay so fun and engaging that it needs to be taken advantage of and used in more creative ways to really fulfill it's true potential. And the best thing? It's not a Doom Eternal copycat like many have said. It is its own thing. Sure there was a lot of inspiration taken from both Doom and also the first SW, but it is unlike both of them.This however crates a different question. Where does Shadow Warrior 3 stand then? It doesn't really fit into the SW franchise (but to be fair, every SW game tries to experiment and reinvent itself). The visuals are different, the voiceactor for Wang is different, the arenas are unlike anything in previous SWs and the demons are almost like from a different universe. All of this is mostly the reason why the fans of the series feel so disconnected from this game. They simply wanted another SW game in the spirit of the first one that came out in 2013. This is deffinitely not that.For who is this game then?I'll answer this question very briefly:For everyone that wants to have fast paced fun, but doesn't want to get a stroke while playing it.I'd recommend this game to basicly all fps fans, but only if they are fine with overpaying a little or if they are fine with waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are coming from Shadow Warrior 2 for its looter-shooter grind style of game, it isn't present hereBut what is here is one of the best story based retro FPS games i have enjoyed in years.A wonderful blend of fast paced Doom shooting where you violently circle the map swapping weapons every few seconds to find different ways to explode and tear enemies limbs apart. The shooting, weapons and overall writing seems more influenced by the Serious Sam series with lead protagonist spitting out cheesy one liners like Sam and Duke-Nukem.The game took me (and plenty of others) around 5 hours to complete the title with a very casual style of play, searching for secrets here and there with the occasional death. I was able to squeeze Shadow Warrior 2 for about 50 hours by grinding its RNG loot system and hunting down all of the unique weapons, but even with the shorter experience id argue its a better title overall. If you are wanting a game to distract you for a few days of gaming through grinding and open map exploration, id suggest sticking with number 2... But regardless of what the reviews sayTHE GAME IS GOODBosses are great, characters only borderline annoy you, The guns are great, the finishers are cool and overall map design is flawless.Each level is built rather similar to one another, but they do fit combat well and you will find yourself sliding under ledges and wall running around rather second nature without former knowledge of the map because of the easily recognisable colours, grappling hook spots and trap locations.There are a few weapon upgrades here and there but id say you could finish the game without using a single skill point and are really only there to allow you to find favourite weapons and boost them further to better suit your own style of shooting ♥♥♥♥.Only negative i have is about the story itself, by the end of the game you can understand whats going on and what your motives are, as well as having only a few name characters you have to keep track of, but when you start out it really does feel like you missed a lecture and felt as if i needed to play the previous games to get caught up. Honestly, i don't believe its too important as every level explains more and more to you as you progress, but that's just me and i could understand this turns you off originally.I hate to see a game like this hit mixed reviews so quickly, but most of the negatives are mainly people upset with 0 resemblance from the previous title, and i get that. Honestly i was hoping for a few of those mechanics myself, but if i had to bother swapping around weapons and perfectly crafting weapons, it would distract me from fun and engaging game itself. The price tag might be harsh for the playtime included in the title, but for new games nowadays normally costing 100$ as the cheapest edition, i find it welcome to see a game this price with this level of polish. If you have grown up playing games like Duke Nukem, Doom and especially Serious Sam. THIS IS A MUST HAVE

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually throw in reviews, but I'll make an exception here as I do think this game deserves a better rep than what it's been getting. Shadow Warrior 3 is understandably divisive after the previous entry. The core gameplay is arguably closer to its '97 roots than the looter-shooter sub genre that SW2 tried to join. Those that call this a new-Doom clone are not wrong - it feels in many ways like an indie take on the Doom (2016) and Doom Eternal formula while adding its own charm. You know exactly what to expect if you have played other fast-paced arena shooters. There's a great sense of mobility with your dash, double-jump and grappling hook. Wang's arsenal also feels mostly satisfying with a few exceptions. My biggest complaint as far as gameplay goes is that the beautiful environments end up feeling a bit shallow; definitely would have been nice to have more exploration.The overall aesthetics feel like a deliberate mash-up of different Asian cultures which may also be divisive. Personally, I think it fits the theme of the series. Lo Wang is a Chinese ninja with a giant Qin Dynasty statue in his Wang cave, fighting enemies that mostly consist of Japanese-themed demons. Visually the game looks great and the soundtrack is an outstanding hodgepodge of East Asian instruments and hip-hop beats. The voice acting is not bad, but if you never enjoyed Lo Wang's humor before, the material here is not going to change that. I won't comment on the controversy behind the voice actor change, though I will say the guy who does Zilla would have actually been great voicing Lo Wang. SungWon Cho's performance has the same tone and gruffness to it that John William Galt's original Lo Wang had. If Doom Eternal is an action blockbuster that has to be seen in IMAX, this is the epitome of a Saturday night Blockbuster rental plus your favorite Chinese takeout. Is it repetitive? Yes. It's also relatively short (with modest replayability). At the end of the day, this is guilty pleasure entertainment, not a refined experience. Definitely worth grabbing on sale. It's also worth noting that the devs responded well to feedback. Early complaints such as lack of a new game + mode and inability to select levels are all features that were eventually added in.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 is a game that I've found myself enjoying a great deal. Keep in mind, I got the game on a $30 dollar sale, and after several updates. However, as it currently stands, I think Shadow Warrior 3 is really, really good. Sometimes great. The arena combat is fluid, the guns are responsive and deadly, and the mechanics are sound. The graphics are great as well. I think if you are a man of the fast-paced arena shooter (ex. Doom Eternal), you'll really enjoy this game. This game can be buggy, though. For how fluid movement often is, the physics feel underwhelming, and sometimes frustrating. On my second playthrough I think I died more to physics jank than to enemies. A constant one is that the forward input wouldn't register after a finisher, or when restarting an arena after death. Very frustrating. I had one hard crash as well. Saved my progress though, so take that as you will. All in all, I recommend Shadow Warrior 3. In the short time it's been out, the developers have shown nothing but willingness to listen to the community and keep updating the game as needed. It's fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Warrior 3 is the final entry in the Shadow Warrior reboot trilogy. It follows the events of SW2, where Lo Wang unleashed a giant dragon. Now, he must team up with his former nemesis Zilla to stop it from destroying the world. Gameplay-wise, its more similar to SW1 than SW2, having linear levels with a single mission rather than a hub world and many features such as side quests and crafting. After beating the story, there's also a survival arena you can play.Compared to previous titles, I think the combat is more satisfying here, you can finish off enemies with gory moves and use their weapons for a bit. I also like pushing enemies off cliffs with the Chi Blast. The boss fights are also better and not too tedious. I also noticed that there's quite a fair amount of parkour-platforming than before, like in some sections you'll have to be fast to reach the next wallrun or grapple point.My main issue with this game is its length, its even shorter than SW1. With the story being super straightforward, there's also not many characters or events going on other than "chase big dragon and kill it". No human enemies, only enemies you fight are demons. The levels, even though they look kinda good, feel very corridor-like and there's not too much variation. SW3 also disguises their loading screens with cutscenes, and in some machines like mine it causes some of them to lag and stutter. Shadow Warrior 3 is still a pretty fun one-man-army videogame to end the trilogy, and if you like the other SW titles you'll still enjoy this one. If they're gonna make more SW games, I hope its more of a mix between 1 and 2, having well-designed, kinda linear levels while still having a hub area you can explore and upgrade. Keep the combat like in 3 though, it's super fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from someone who hasn't played any of the previous games but at least thinks they have a basic understanding of them, this game rocks. I totally understand why people were so disappointed by it when it released, with the length being the biggest offender. The game just isn't that long, I beat it in around 5 and half hours which is a deal breaker for a lot of people given its $40 price tag. But besides that, Shadow Warrior 3's gameplay is amazingly satisfying and while the visuals may look a bit janky from time to time, I LOVE its art direction. I'll even admit the dialogue got me a few times. As I've said before, I understand why this game has a lower than average rating, but I think 60%'s a little egregious. As long as you keep its length into account, I'd highly recommend picking this up while its still on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of these games that really make me wish that there was a third reccomendation option. Because there simply isn't enough here to justify the pricetag.Overall I enjoyed my first playthrough. The movement feels smooth for the most part, and the gunplay harmonises really well with it. Then again having played the previous two installments, that was not so surprising. Then again the chi system was so non impactful, that I forgot to use it even once until most way through the campaign.Story wise Shadow Warrior 3 pales in comparison to what I remember 1s being like. The plot is generic and not fleshed out in the slightest. Sure coming into a game that is more or less a s***post on a highschoo level I shouldn't expect anything in that department, but anything more then "Stop thing that destroys world by killing thing" would have been nice.Of course this leads me to the BY FAR biggest issue with SW3. It's too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ short. None of the new shadow warrior installments have been particularly long games, I remember  finishing 1 in a singular sitting, but 4 hours for one playthrough... ... ... WHAT?!Sure the game looks great and you can tell a lot of effort went into it, but it definitly wasn't towards the lenght of the game.Don't get me wrong, a short game can make for a far more intense experience, where storybeats don't have to be dragged out forever and be watered down, just for the sake of making a 40 hour long title, but again, there is no real story to speak of.It's a crying shame that it does not provide more of it's, and I have to stress this, EXTREMELY fun gameplay. If what you are looking for is a fun shooter with good gunplay just to blow off some steam from a hard days work, SW3 will provide you with a shorth but good time. But as it stands, with the short campaign and the high pricetag, there is no way for me to reccomend it over previous installments. If you want a better Singleplayer experience, play the first. If you need CO-OP, play the second I guess, don't know, don't have any friends to try that mode with.Overall, wait for it to be cheap... like really cheap, like 20 bucks cheap, then get it and you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's short, but it's an absolute joy to play - snappy gunplay, precise, high-speed mobility, and wild arenas full of inventive enemies.  It's been a while since a game put a grin on my face the way the mechanical deathtraps in some of this game's arenas do.  It may not stick around for long (something like 5 hours' gameplay on normal difficulty, hard to say for sure because I was afk with the game running for a while) but it's a quality game clearly made by people who care, and I'll likely replay it a number of times in the future just to revisit its combat.When it comes down to writing, though, the unexpected emotional resonance of the first game's story is a tough act to follow, and Shadow Warrior 3 can't manage it, though not for lack of trying.  At least it's substantially better written than 2, whose characters were the videogame equivalent of a prolonged grimace.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is... fine. I guess. The problem is that it is, essentially, a skin for Doom Eternal. Thus the game loop is a mix of kill rooms with a combat puzzle and 3d Super Mario. Which is precisely what I didn't like about DE. Just about any infuriating game system from DE is here as well. Limited ammo: check. Silly Parkour: check. Kill rooms: Check. Super Mario: Check. Upgrades: Check.The game is pretty, well executed and artistically pleasing. A touch overdesigned. However, it is not anything like previous two games in the series gameplay wise. For that I cannot recommend it to anyone who liked them.I have about 3 hours at the moment of writing of this review and I haven;t picked up since mid august 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the criticisms of this game is that you can clear it in 2~3 hours... but I couldn't even be bothered to stick with it for that long. If this had been a sequel to ... well it still would have been poorly received due to its bad writing and uninspired enemy design... but at least then it would have been in the same genre as previous games in the same franchise.This game is NOT a shooter. It's about falling off of the edge of the world over and over again while running out of ammo for your useless tickle-guns. I actually thought the gameplay in Shadow Warrior 2 was very good. (It was the terrible writing and middle-finger of an ending that earned that game a negative review.)If you liked that game, you probably won't like this because it's not a good shooter/melee game; it's a bad parkour game with some haphazardly implemented combat thrown in.  Who cares what you like?! Certainly not the devs who made the ending of Shadow Warrior 2 a deliberate middle finger to people who invested the time and effort needed to reach it... and then made this game begin on an even BIGGER middle finger to people who finished Shadow Warrior 2.Who cares what you like?! Certainly not the devs who decided to completley remove the one thing that might have made such a lackluster game worth playing.Who cares what you like? Certainly NOT the people who made a three-hour, linear game where you just have to use the stuff the game gives you and learn to like it. Who care what you want?! Don't you get it? Nothing that was in the last game should be expected in this one! Just swallow your minimum-viable-product and quit yer whinin'!Hey devs! Do you have NO interest in making your content-poor, overpriced game actually worth the money but want people to think you are doing exactly that? Add a completely pointless perma-death mode... and then lock some cosmetics behind it. Now people who have Stockholm syndrome will waste dozens of hours trying to complete a game about jumping across chasms without dying and if they are REALLY stupid, they won't even notice how short and utterly lacking in content your game was without this time-waster of having to restart the entire game over and over again.If you are wondering why the devs cut away so much... well I am too but I suspect it may have been to do with the fact that they switched engines. Usually, it's fairly easy to have all the stuff the last game in a series had and maybe add a bit more but when you switch engines, that often forces you to throw out EVERYTHING with the result that you can end up with a new game that actually has a lot less than the old one. I regret to say that I am deeply suspicious that the same was done with this title. _childDocuments_.review: It's a third-rate knockoff of Doom Eternal/Titanfall with none of the carefully-balanced mechanics or regard to how movement affects event triggers, bulked out by Serious Sam-style bullet sponges.For context:Shadow Warrior '97, I got the demo on a demo disc and then played over and over until I knew everything back to front. Shadow Wariror 2013 was a great game, I loved every moment of that. The ending was wonderful.Shadow Warrior 2 was less-good, but I do love me a fast-talking protagonist, but the ending was crap and I still want to know what happened to Kamiko.But this game is just a lot of flailing around with ideas stolen from other games with no regard for how it all gets put together. As someone who used the katana far more than the guns in the previous two games, I especially do not appreciate the marginalization of the katana in this game. But mostly I am aggravated by the copying of Titanfall 2 movement without regard for if you move too quickly and hit multiple voice line triggers before the previous one has finished playing out. Or cutscenes, for that matter. In short, the game wants you to barrel around at high speed, except when it doesn't, then you need to stop and stand still, and that feels really bad.Sayonara, Lo Wang. I'll watch the Let's Play instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this, I was really into Shadow warrior I and & II, but this one falls flat, the humor is dull and sounds forced, the combat is boring and the levels, even the ones set in wide open outdoor areas feel incredibly claustrophobic and restrictive and the movement puzzles do nothing but annoy me and slow down the already awkward pace. The worst offender though is the upgrade system, I should not have to unlock basic moves like power-slash in the third game of the series, I should just unlock cool and awesome crap that expands on a solid core of moves. One quick look at a story summary also revealed that there were no cheeky plot twist or the story going off the rails in an unexpected direction, it really is "we need to go kill dragon" and that is what they do, given the wily plots of the first two games, this straightforward plot is not what I expected or wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game. Finished it in 20 hours on hard level , (dunno why it took me so long honestly, given that I have destroyed every DOOM Eternal master level on Nightmare -  got stuck on the ancient ♥♥♥♥ and missed some weapon upgrades which made me struggle on some arenas, anyway). Love the verticality and traversal with grapple hook (although the hook animation slows down the  combat, feels like it's lagging).  I also would like to grapple hook on EVERY demon, not some of them. I love the in-between-arenas rollercoaster sections, specially towards the end, such a shame these sections don't  give you the opportunity to fight demons as you push through the environment  ( well you can shoot some Kugutsus on balloons but that's just an appetizer) . Now for the downsides : Like everybody is saying, no replayability value. After I finished the game , I would like to revisit some levels but there's no way to do it unless I initialize a  new save slot. I clicked on continue and was brought back to the Heart Guardian fight, WTF?  Last, I think in busy arenas , there's TOO MUCH going on , sometimes my view is a blur. I have played the hardest content on DOOM Eternal , and there's  A LOT happening on the screen most of the times, but I always know what's happening, doesn't feel the same with SW3. For example , the Laser Shogun gore weapon, tha purple beam explosion is a sure epilepsy trigger, they need to tone down some visual effects , it's too much for the eye to handle. Other than that, it's a SOLID gameplay and congratulations to FWH for this amazing game. I am  supporting because we need more games like this, just straight up first person shooters with fast action, and not pointless open world walking simulators.MARCH 2023 DEFINITIVE EDITION UPDATEThe Definitive edition update brings Survival Mode which poses the challenge of surviving as many waves (rounds) of demons as you can. I absolutely loved survival mode, even though I ran on some bugs , like you clear the 6th round on the second arena and the game does not proceed to the next round. You can try many difficulties, the hardest being Hard Core, which lives up to it's name: Really tough. Reached round 15 on normal difficulty, so much fun, can't get past 3rd rounds on Hard Core as the slightest hit from any demon will eat away most of your HP. Great.

_childDocuments_.review: Scourgebringer is a superb real time tactical slash and shoot roguelite, Controls are super fast and fluent, It requires catlike reflexes and everything from the game to the UI looks just amazing.The story is about a thing that came from the sky and burns everything, Nobody knows why but they call it the Scourgebringer, Many people tried to go in, but no one came back out. You play as Kyhra, The last Light. It is your turn to try and stop the Scourgebringer. You are the only hope, the final chance. The story plays out as a slideshow in the beginning, There is not much to it in the game, But there is a backstory and a goal, I think some lore would greatly benefit the story But the game certainly doesn't let the story get in the way of the gameplay.There is just the single player game, You start at the skill tree and when you go into the portal you start a run, When you die you are at the skill tree again. It surely would benefit from some customization and different gamemodesThe gameplay is amazing, It is fast, you can use your gun your sword you can dash you can do a heavy hit which reflects projectiles, Kyhra does exactly what you tell her to do, There are 2 different types of currency, Blood and eye/coin type thingies. Blood will be lost when you die and the eye coins will remain you can use these to unlock upgrades on the skill tree, These unlocks will remain unlocked, It doesn't matter how often you die. All items you pick up or buy in the runs are lost when you die, They can offer some nice boosts, But many feel a bit underwhelming, They also drop very rarely but are pretty cheap at the shop.The game starts in the first biome, Every Biome has a bunch of normal rooms, and 1 of each of the following rooms, A starter, Shop, Altar, Mini Boss and a Boss. The Starter room is where you start, Where it is and where the other rooms are is completely random generated as far as I know. You can buy 3 items at the shop if you have enough blood. You can get 1 out of 3 random upgrades at the Altar and You need to kill the mini boos before you can enter the final boss room. If you kill the boss a portal will appear to go to the next biome. You can go back to clean up things you might have missed, So it doesn't hurt to kill the boss if you get the chance.The game has several attacking mechanics, You must use the room to your advantage, You can shoot but you need to get melee hits to reload, Enemies flash a little exclamation mark to signal they are about to attack, In this timeframe you can hit them with a heavy melee attack which will stun them. While enemies are stunned they are easy targets. You can deflect most attacks and push around enemies with the heavy melee attack, It gets tactical finding out the fastest way to clear a room without taking damage, Because health is scarce, You can get lucky at an altar, But this sacrifices a nice upgrade opportunity.The game looks just amazing, The colorschemes in each biome, The enemies, NPCs, It is all very coherent, The animation is perfect, especially if you take a closer look at Kyhra, You can even slow down the game to really appreciate the animations. The soundtrack is good too but it lacks a bit in variation at this point, I do think each biome has a very nice and distinct soundtrack.I saw a few bugs here and there, Nothing major, At the press any button to start screen it takes a while before it registers any input, This is new since version 1.03, I did not have this before, I also had a boss glitching out of the screen in the middle of the battle, I could still kill him with a special ability And I am sure these issues will be ironed out, The game runs at a solid 2000+ fps, There is Vsync support if you like to give your GPU a break.With a bit of luck you can complete the game in 5 minutes in its current state. So it is very short for now, But even in this state it is very enjoyable, The rooms are not random generated, But the map is, So you might see some familiar rooms after a while, but you will never know where the bosses are. The bosses will remain the same in each biome and the monster placement is the same in rooms that are the same. There is a lot that can be improved here but I am sure it will improve with every major update.Ofcourse I would love to see more Biomes, Maybe even in a random order (or choice from 2 random biomes) where it keeps getting harder with different difficulity levels for each biome depending on which stage it is for you.I feel with a controller it is hard to aim with the gun because it shoots directly when you want to aim, It is even so sensitive that you shoot the other way if you let go of your joystick when aiming the other wayI would also love to see a lot more items with much variation in what they do, A bigger skill tree, and maybe mod support? It could also benefit from more gamemodes, Daily runs? Custom Seeds? Custom runs? Boss Rush mode?The game is still in Early Access, It just released actually, It only has 3 biomes, 3 bosses and only 4 branches on the skill tree, The Roadmap has not been published yet, But I can see this becoming a masterpiece. I will update the review when I feel a lot has changed or when it leaves EA.People say it is a mix between Celeste and Dead Cells, But It is not a platformer nor a metroidvania, I can still see where they are coming from, The single screen action and dashing from Celeste, the fast combat and perma death from Dead Cells. For now it is obvious that it is not a finished game, But it already gives a sneak peak of what it will become. If you like fast paced action and like the idea of a mix between the 2 mentioned games It is certainly worth picking up right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels great at first, game is beaten within the first 2 or 3 hours. (at least for now)But when it comes to a roguelike, it fails terribly in the sense that every run I've played is the same.You dash around, smash around a little bit to interrupt enemies... and sometimes you unload all those gun munitions for bursts of damage on bosses. Annnnd that's it. That's all there is. You approach all enemies the same. And interupt them all the same. The perks you gain does not change the way you play, it's just some upsides you add along the way. (except that one perk that makes you reflect bullets)Then you find some shrines that presents you 3 choices (Now we're talking roguelike!) But there's so little interesting picks to take. And so few that you've seen them all in the first hour. And again, not affecting your gameplay.I think the problem lies with the basic controls. It's the core thing and it's not there to change. You can change guns (And i think it's the most game altering thing there is), but you can stick with the starting gun since it's really good. And changing feels most of the time less efficient.The other big problem I've noticed is.. that the perks you get to upgrade into at the start of the run? Well, they should be stuff you acquire during the run. Right now it's: ''you died, now it's slightly easier.'' Probably to enhance that progression kind of feel which I find unnecessary in that genre.TLDR: Game is the same every run, short and progression is not within the run itself. 4.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: will keep your heart racing as you struggle to keep up with its frantic pace. However, once you manage to, you'll be addicted. It’s unforgiving; each area has its own learning curve, and the tolerance for error is minor, resulting in a satisfying experience. Unfortunately, there’s a lack of variety, reducing the replay value, an important aspect of a rogue-lite. With that said, I enjoyed the game, and I would recommend it - just keep your expectations in check. Rogue-lites are the talk of the town currently. This year, we’ve seen more of them release than any other. However, this spike of popularity has resulted in an abundance of games belonging to the genre. , developed by , is one of the newer additions. Can it manage to stand out in an oversaturated market? is fast. Assuming the role of a warrior named Kyhra, you’ll dash and slash through interconnected chambers filled with monstrous creatures, high-tech robots and fiendish devils. The combat is gratifying, but expect to die a lot. With a steep learning curve, it can be hard to keep up with the rapid pace. Being quick is the goal. When you’re up against multiple enemies, all of which demand your attention, it can get hectic. Luckily, Kyhra is agile and fierce. Her swift dashes allow her to dodge incoming attacks while also moving closer to enemies. With a concise set of maneuvers, each inclusion has its purpose. Your quick attack can dispose of foes efficiently. Each enemy has a stronger attack, indicated by a flashing exclamation point above their head. By smashing them with a heavy attack beforehand, you can stun them. If you don’t like getting up close and personal, you’re armed with a ranged weapon. There are many to choose from; grenade launchers, shotguns and so on.To complete the game, you have to overcome the challenges of five locales. The first two are similar in function, while the others modify the rules. In one area, as an example, walls won’t protect you; projectiles will fly right through, forcing you to face your foes head-on. I liked this aspect of the level design, as it encourages you to approach the game differently, while keeping the core intact. That being said, this isn’t a game that’s easy to approach. With a low tolerance for error, it’s brutally punishing. Kyhra starts out with only 8 health points, and the struggle to stay alive will make it hard to keep your nerves in check. Each area comes with its own learning curve; once you complete one, another will be waiting to test your skills. Unfortunately, the game lacks variety. Whereas other rogue-lites offer heaps of items, tools and weapons to choose from, ’s selection is limited, with a single melee weapon and a limited collection of firearms. Instead of trying out new tactics, I would retrace my steps. Why, you ask? Because it worked. The combat doesn’t encourage creativity, and the lack of variation abolished my incentive to replay the game. It’s not that the game doesn’t advocate this; upon finishing the game, you’ll unlock modifiers that acclimate the difficulty, and there are also additional endings to witness. In between runs, you’ll find yourself at the . Here, you can acquire skills by investing . Aside from a bestiary, this is the only progression that carries over from run to run. At first, I liked the concept of acquiring new moves and upgrades, but I was disappointed when I unlocked them all early on. It meant that, for the remaining 40 hours or so, I had no option of permanently improving my character. It also resulted in the aforementioned currency becoming useless, as it has no other purpose.As you annihilate hordes of enemies, you earn . These are used to purchase items from , an acquisitive merchant whose name is self-explanatory. You can increase the amount obtained by building up your combo meter. The more times you hit a creature, the higher it goes. Should you take damage, it resets. Whereas the frantic pace encourages you to be quick, this system functions as a reminder that you are, indeed, not invincible. Each area requires you to beat a  before proceeding. To face them, you must first defeat a number of . In the first two areas, you need only defeat one, but the number rises as you progress. I enjoyed fighting the bosses; however, I couldn’t help but feel like they were easier than the conventional enemies once I got used to their movesets. Nonetheless, they’re enjoyable and bring a nice change of pace to the action.Right from the beginning, it’s clear that lore and world-building isn’t the focal point. You can find logs of text which provide insight into the world you’re exploring, but none of the coherent themes are explored enough to result in an intriguing story. The game’s setting is nothing out of the ordinary, serving as a backdrop for the exciting gameplay loop. When the combat is excellent, which is the case here, that’s not a problem.The visuals are simple yet effective. ’s pixel art style can be hard to comprehend at first, but once you get used to it, it’s charming to glance at. Its lack of detail combined with sharp textures produce a unique appearance. As for the soundtrack, it’s a nice mix of heavy metal and occasional 8-bit tunes. Although not particularly memorable, it’s nice listening to while you slay the monstrosities you encounter on your journey.  | 1440p

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I have much to say about Scourgebringer, and that's the big issue here.The gameplay is fast and stylized, but feels very messy and unfulfilling for some reason, maybe because nothing has weight to it, and the game is super punishing for even slight mistakes. In ScourgeBringer you zip around a 2d arena with equipped with a double jump, wall cling, a dash attack, a melee attack, a stunning attack and a recharging gun. Enemies have colliding attacks, shoot projectiles and all the usual jazz. The game pushes you to be very aggressive by rewarding more shop currency for flawless rooms and fast kill chains.It's blindingly fast, and therein lies my gripe, as the game is just super messy. White flashes everywhere and with the protagonist teleporting with the dash, it's very easy to get lost in the mess. It doesn't help that the crosshair can get lost in the jumble too, and you can't really alter the colour scheme. You attacks also don't really feel weighty, the bullet reflect with the smash feels extra bad (enemies shoot chains of bullets, but you have no invulnerability when smashing and the hitbox doesn't last long enough for it to matter, unless against single projectiles). I don't really feel for the bosses either, since they react even less to your hits. Playing with a controller feels extra bad to boot, since either you use autoaim or forget about the gun, and I don't like either option.It feels like it wants to be a 2d Devil May Cry/Bayonetta-esque character action game in a roguelite shell but to me it comes across as a migraine-inducing cavalcade of fast clicking and hollow action sequences. The game doesn't feel unfair or too hard, but there's nothing here that really makes me want to keep coming back. I honestly forgot that I had purchased this, and that's kinda sad.

_childDocuments_.review: At the very beginning loved it, but the feeling quickly waned and I was left bored.+ mobility and the sense of flow - you are constantly flying through each level (as long as there are monsters to hit)+ it is certainly possible to get good and not get hit at all, especially on boss fights+ fast paced+ good controls+/- adaptive system of difficulty - it's an option but can be turned off (which I did immediately)- even though it's a good platformer it fails as a roguelike - each run is the same, the only upgrades you get are minor, with little choice. The biggest customization is on the gun and its mods, but that's not even your main weapon- because of that it quickly gets repetitive- drops are not interesting and rare- life-based difficulty - nothing else matters in the game as much as life. Every single point you lose will follow you for the entire game as it's unlikely you will get ever back to full  after losing a couple of points. So you are left with praying on every drop that it heals you- max life upgrades are inconsistent - the one that gives +2 doesn't increase current life, while the one that gives +1 does...I don't want do cautiously repeat the same early game again and again to slowly learn how to efficiently (without losing life) combat new enemies/bosses later on, so I am done.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for those who enjoy a challenge and are OK with dying. In this Rogue-lite, you can build skills for the main character and the skills are carried through your runs. At first, I struggled a lot and almost gave up, but I found it amazingly rewarding to keep playing. The runs are relatively short so you do not lose massive amounts of progress for dying. Now, I play the game to wind down and it is relaxing after work and I really enjoy the hard-modes released in the full release.The games controls feel great. Watching the videos I had worried about how the controls would work, but they have been implemented very well that movement feels very natural. The game assists the player some automatically and this results in a consistently good experience. The controls also allow you to pull off trick-shots and near-misses that feel really good when you can do them successfully.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to fall in love with this game. The movement is so fast and unrestricted and snappy, and it feels great as long as the enemies have massively telegraphed attacks and die in 1-3 hits. But as the game becomes more demanding, you start realizing that the movement is not precise, and the game doesn't respect the inputs you are giving it. Dashing magnetizes towards enemies, which is nice at first, but later on, it just gets you killed. Attacking enemies also magnetizes you towards them, and that has the same issue because it also yanks your character around whatever you're attacking, and that is out of your control. Sometimes when you're on a wall and try to dash in some direction, it will just dash straight down for no reason.It's also hardly a roguelike, because every run is exactly the same. The only upgrades to be found are max HP and damage boosts. The only "real" upgrade is the one that makes your stun attack have a bigger area, and a handful of secondary weapons. So it feels more like a permadeath game where you just have to start from the beginning each time, except the game slowly gets easier due to a simple progression system.This game looks like a masterpiece on the surface, but once you sink your teeth in, it's clunky and repetitive. I think it's trying to deliver on a power fantasy with all the unrestricted movement, the aim and movement assist (which cannot be turned off), while trying to challenge your dexterity at the same time by being highly precision demanding. Those two ideas are clashing, resulting in a mediocre experience where the challenge comes not from the enemy designs, but from trying to outsmart the game's controls, which are trying to help you way too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, not yet, it is still in Early Access. Is it good? Is it fun? YEEEESSS to both questions!It is another roguelike action platformer. Enter a room, the doors close and enemies spawn. Kill them all, and the doors open. Go to the next room and repeat. Until you reach a merchant. Or a boss. Sometimes you find upgrades on the way. When you die, you respawn in a hub and have to start again.What I really love about the game is it's fluid, fast, stay-off-the-ground combat. As long as you keep hitting enemies you stay in the air, and if you combine it with the all-direction, indefinitely available dash you can stay in the air until every foe is vanquished. You can also run up walls. And shoot, as long as you have ammo. Really cool!You are not invincible during a dash, otherwise the game would be too easy. There are permanent upgrades to unlock in the hub, random dungeons, and the game comes with perfect gamepad support.Promising, fast paced roguelike platformer with tons of enemies to slash.PS: The game is now out of Early Access and even better than before!

_childDocuments_.review: is a super fluid roguelite 2D action platformer that happens to be very polished at this time for what is available (Beta v1.04 as of writing, 3 fully developed zones out of 6 planned). More importantly, it is just a lot of fun to play. Despite that it's in Early Access, the combat mechanics feel so seasoned and well-done that you would be hard pressed to point out any problems with it.My experience is limited to my short amount of time spent so far (2.5 hours) and I have not yet cleared the 3rd available area. I see someone wrote that they cleared the whole game after 5 tries. I guess my skills are just much lacking in comparison. I have played probably 20 times so far and only managed to get into the 3rd zone once. has a story, though that's limited currently to a few well-drawn artwork pages when you start into your save. I enjoy games that have a nice story or rich lore, but this game really doesn't need it. Without a doubt, the platforming will remind many players of  with its fast-paced movement and tight jumping. Everything flows so well, both in and out of combat.Aerial combat in 2D platforming is often neglected, and perhaps it becomes difficult to get the progressively unrealistic mechanics to feel natural and right in the hands of the player. This game has perhaps one of the best aerial combat mechanics I have seen in recent years. You can, at times, maim a whole roomful of enemies (usually 1-2 waves) without touching the ground. There is just something really satisfying and fun about it.Another thing to note is that you always have a ranged/gun weapon equipped aside from your sword. And combat on ground or in air using melee with intermittent gun fire transition between themselves seamlessly. So not only is aerial combat done well and feels right in the melee aspect, you can spice up your attacks with some bullets too!For many players, it's inevitable that you will compare  to this game in terms of combat flow. This game may not have as much content and as much variety, but the combat does not feel inferior to  in anyway. And its aerial combat mechanics is really nonpareil--to me anyway.Relying on reflexes is important in this game, but so is an additional knowledge about the game through repetitive motions of playing and replaying. This gets down to the replay value of such a game, which seems to me to be pretty good. The rooms are pre-made although the way that the zones spawn their rooms are randomized, thus making it important for the player to explore each game. The other aspect of the game that increases the replay value is the skill/passive tree that you can unlock progressively by playing and beating mini and main bosses. Sure, the game has its flaws, mostly in the variety category. You can expect 1 of each special room to show up in each zone, shop, altar/pillar for the Gift of Blood (choice of 3 upgrades for that run), mini boss, and main boss (room can only be opened after the mini boss is destroyed). The individual rooms are pre-made so you do start getting used to them over time. In addition, the shop items and Gift of Blood choices seem to repeat and cycle through a fairly small number of selections.All in all, I am very much looking forward to seeing where this game will go from here. I think the developers really did a great job at hammering out undesirable details before releasing it into Early Access. I have, so far, found absolutely no problems or bugs so far.Plays great with a gamepad, as I prefer to play almost all of my 2D platforming games. Kudos to the developers for giving the players functional movement with boy D-Pad and Joystick.The 2D pixelated artwork is rather well done, the game is quite beautiful to behold. V-sync option available.The soundtrack sounds awesome, with the right pacing to accompany the rapid movement and action.For people who enjoy a good 2D action platformer,  you will not be disappointed with $14.99 launching into Early Access is perhaps a bit high for some people. But I am telling you right here and now that these developers did their homework, and the game plays beautifully and is really fun. There will be more content to come, so expect the price to go up a little with additional updates. (Early Access page indicates plans to keep it below $20 overall.)There is a launch week 10% discount and additional 10% for folks who own  that is still going on. So I encourage anyone thinking about it to jump in on the action! Worth the price I say!+A combat system that stands out as being very well polished and super tight+Interesting platforming mechanics that feel right+Progressive unlockable skill/passive tree to change the way you play as you get more or more used to the game+Excellent music+Fantastic 2D pixel art+Nice in-game seamless feedback system+Accessible to people who may not wish to play the game at the intended pace with speed-adjustment options+Most importantly, this game is just so much fun=Current content has 3 zones, which is enough for me, but can feel really short to some people. There are a few more planned, so this is just part of the growing pains of a game in Early Access.-Variety of items found in shop is a little lacking (I saw the same items over and over again)-Similar to above, Gift of Blood choices could use some more variety-Very limited trap design and use in the individual rooms brings quite another nice addition for people who enjoy action platformers. While it may be in Early Access, the game already has excellent movement and combat systems in place to make the action platforming feel oh-so-good. If you are on the fence, definitely take a look at this game, for you will not be disappointed.With such a solid foundation,  will surely realize a brighter future.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought that this game would be really cool, but I ultimately felt exhausted just from playing a run or two nowadays.ScourgeBringer sort of plays like a traditional roguelite, complete with heavy metal vibes (reminds me of Doom 2016 but with more synths) and a Metroidvania level structure. You can double jump, dash, smash, fire from a rechargeable gun, and use a Fury super move. Your gravity-defying, infinite sword-swinging melee combat is already a neat setup for some intense combat, but that's it. That's your whole kit. If you expected this game to have alternate playstyles to experiment with, then you'd be sorely mistaken. THAT really sucks.This game is more of a roguelite because you can access a skill tree (actually, a LITERAL one that's known as the Chiming Tree) and spend Boss Blood on them to further enhance your experience with passive upgrades that can be toggled upon unlock. The skill tree upgrades do encourage you to keep playing the game, but when you eventually unlock everything on the tree, you're going to wonder what the hell you're supposed to do with all of that spare Boss Blood.The combat and supplementary mechanics encourages you to get fast and get aggressive, which can get messy very quickly. The combo system is the greatest offender because it motivates this behavior, especially when your combo gauge decreases every time you take a hit. It doesn’t help that your Smash attack cannot protect you from an extremely long stream of projectiles hurtling towards you, or that the enemies are almost always in large packs, or that the Dash attack can NEVER protect you from projectiles at all. You're not only encouraged to get fast & aggressive, but you're also expected to navigate your way around environmental hazards or enemy projectiles. It's hard to maintain safe positioning as you hack away on one enemy at a time because you always jitter around an enemy with every sword swing that you land. Bosses are not any better, because it feels like you’re just chipping away on a damage sponge as they go about their business. You can stun them, but sometimes those moments can be easy to miss.Also, I find it really easy to run a pattern against EVERY enemy. Dash towards them, hack away at them with sword swipes, use your slow & heavy Smash if somebody attacks, rinse & repeat. An engaging offensive kit would allow you to mix up your attacks, but it feels like your attacks in this game can get really boring most of the time.Oh yea, you'll get a gun, but you'll either forget about it or you'll wish that you had some spare shots to fire at something. To be fair, the gunplay is not the emphasis of the overall combat.What also doesn’t help with this aggressive mentality is the music. The heavy metal rock tracks absolutely slap, but it BARELY gives me a chance to relax in-between battles because EVERY combat track goes absolutely hard, and then moments of respite MAINTAIN that momentum instead of calming down. This choice of tempo is prevalent in practically every world after the first world (At least the first world invokes a sense of wonder and mystery between battles). The only calmest moments in-run are the shops or secret rooms, where you hear nothing but funny alien ambient noises.So the gameplay is exhausting, the enemies are annoying in droves, and the bosses don’t feel that fulfilling. If all else fails, then maybe I can get a kick out of the narrative? Nah man, not in ScourgeBringer. It’s awfully apparent that this game focused on gameplay over narrative, because the narrative does not feel that interesting or intriguing at ALL. The only characters that you can talk to are scarce, and the expedition logs and message pillars that you can find are extremely limited in unique content. I get that this could be a form of environmental storytelling, but it feels like an incomplete narrative was just ham-fisted into the game and left behind. The narrative may not matter if the gameplay is strong and you are there for it, but I don’t have faith in the game’s gameplay because of how dizzying it can get.There ARE accessibility options that allow you to apply a healing assist, toggle your sword attack to a press & hold function, or slow down the gameplay and projectile speed. So the game is definitely hard, but not impossible. You can also enable Chaos Roots which makes your runs even harder, but I’d only go for that if I can play this game extremely well and efficiently.But despite everything this game has going for it, ScourgeBringer ultimately feels like a bombastic display of aggression, and it does it all in a colorful pixel art style. It legit feels like this game could be trying to be edgy purely for the sake of BEING edgy rather than capitalizing on that energy into something meaningful or recognizable.TL;DR:- Roguelite Metroidvania with some edgy heavy metal vibes- No alternate playstyles for primary melee attacks- Skill Tree & Chaos Roots are the only motivation for replayability- Combat is 2fast2quick, but incredibly exhausting- Dashes have no i-frames (smh)- Smash can reflect projectiles, but doesn't always work twice in rapid succession- You'll get a gun! But you'll prolly forget about it while hacking away your foes- Bosses are boring, sometimes annoying- The music slaps, but it NEVER slows down- Narrative sucks, gameplay is given more emphasis instead- The game ultimately feels bombastic and meaningless
