_childDocuments_.review: For those with no time or attention span,TL;DR: THERE IS A DEDICATED BONK BUTTON! (but don't get this game; you'll be sorry)This game will make you suffer for the first 10hrs and only let up a bit for the subsequent 20hrs.I only managed to beat this game at the 30hr mark, and when I say "beat", I mean get the true ending.From this point onward I very quickly 100% the game - turns out the game was going easy on you, and the  really puts into perspective how ludicrously difficult the game can be.So now you wonder how this game could possibly be a fun experience if all it does is hit back harder with every step of progress you make; it's quite simple.• What at first may seem like an uncertain and tricky set of tools to wield - that being Kyrha's dash, flotation, double-jump and wall-run - threaten to overwhelm the player with the sheer number of movement of options at their disposal.• Kyrha's speed and need to get close to her enemies to deal damage, makes it very easy for the player to play recklessly or accidentally collide with projectiles or traps. • Kyrha's parry (or smash) is quick and slightly lunges you in the direction of your influence, meaning if you miss the little window meant to counteract enemy action, you're gonna get punished.• Finally the levels themselves are a set of combat encounters that encourage chaos and very quickly will overwhelm the player if they are not able to surgically eliminate each threat. All of this is punctuated by boss fights, that without prior knowledge of their moveset, will most likely kill the player, or leave them at death's door for the next stage.It is the initial struggle to overcome and master each of these systems readily available to the player, to become a god of war. Quick and calculated movement, as well as clever use of the dash, will render your enemies unable to track your movements and leave the main threats of any room naked, once the smaller ones have been dealt with in the blink of an eye. Being able to juggle the refresh of your jump and/or dash and your ability to float while you slice and dice the air will give you ample time and space to very consistently parry all incoming attacks that you were not able to stop at the source. The parry itself is  very easy to underestimate, when all it serves to do in the early game is risk you taking further damage, but mastering the timing and spacing required for a parry isn't just satisfying, it's very powerful. Once these systems are mastered, it's up to the player to come up with creative solutions to each encounter, or at least a playstyle they enjoy and find reliable. Finding places to fit in a dragon-dash, ground-pound or bullet barrage feels great and allow for awesome skill expression - which, mind, is only available through practice; no one will beat the game on their 9th or even 10th try.Each stage (or realm) tests different aspects of combat and encourage the player to develop different muscle memory for different situations, and anyone resistant to this learning curve will be quickly sent back to the Chiming Tree. During each playthrough, the player will encounter shops that offer buffs, healing and weaponry; these are essential if you want to grow more powerful, but will only be accessible to the player if the player has been performing well. The better you play the more blood you will have, and thus the more shopping you can do. On the topic of blood and power. Every single drop of blood of your enemies serves to make you more powerful, especially in conjunction with the blood altars. Many blessings are hard to make use of, but some are just flat damage buffs or modifications, which only serve to make you more powerful, however, going into detail about these will make this review longer than it already is.In short, the steep learning curve and plethora of combat systems readily available to the player serve as the brutal training required to beat the game, but most people will not be able to endure it, nor have the aspiration to master the combat. I only stuck around because dashing around like an anime character and becoming a tornado of blades and bullets was appealing to me.If you like difficult games that reward the player for being adaptive (and later on aggressive) in their gameplay, then this game is for you. If you're , don't touch this game, you'll get burned.The only reason I'm recommending this game, is for the select few that will indeed master this game's systems and overcome its challenges - to be rewarded with a combat experience and power-trip unobtainable elsewhere.9/10 because the OST isn't perfect, make your own playlist or use mine:A Long Way Down - Le Castle Vania,Furi - Enraged,Hate or Glory - Gesaffelstein,Murder on my Mind - Kordhell,Neon Blade - MoonDeity,One Winged Angel - GeoffPlaysGuitar,Outer Spheres - On Interrupt,Return to Spacetime Six - On Interrupt,The Man Who Made a Monster - Dance with the Dead,Undefeatable - Little V.Why Not - Ghostface Playa,

_childDocuments_.review: Very hard, unrelenting rogue-lite spectacle fighter with free-form combat that, for better or worse, doesn't overstay its welcome (took me 22 hours to clear all achievements, with many... TOO MANY tries, palms so sweaty my mouse started slipping from my grip). The aesthetics consist of crisp pixel art with smooth animations and discernable enemies/projectiles, so you can say that every time you take damage it is purely your fault and not the game's. I wasn't a big fan of environmental hazards (spikes on Level 1 were ok, but the toxic fumes on Level 2 and barely visible wall goo on Level 6 are atrocious and slow down the gameplay to a crawl), so count that as one of the few cons of ScourgeBringer.

_childDocuments_.review: Scourgebringer is a game i really wanted to like and one i can see many people falling in love with but it just couldn’t hold my attention for it,+ + +The core combat system and the upgrades make the moment to moment gameplay feel fantastic and stylish. The soundtrack, art, and sound design are all superb that keep the aesthetics of the game impressive.\ \ \The difficulty can be either a turn off or an incentivising factor of this game which will definitely leave a wide spectrum of opinions on. Shops and Upgrades do a bit to spice up the game but not nearly enough to not make every run feel the same. The same feeling in combat isn’t the worst in the world because the combat feels great so many can still have a blast.- - -Despite whatever issues I have with the game that I try to overlook, I just can't bring myself to play anymore. The difficulty mixed with the lack of enemy variety and lack of build crafting make every single run feel insanely repetitive. I am aware this may be a skill issue as repetition hits less hard if you can beat the game in fewer attempts or make more steady progress but I do not feel compelled to try any more.: : :If you don’t mind the sisyphean aspects of some games this might be right up your alley but for me I have to just take it out of my roguelite/likes rotation for my own sanity

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game, but deceptive at face value. From early access footage I thought it would be a lot more similar to katana zero, but it isn't. This is meant to be played as a very fast paced game, and if you don't play it that way you might as well not pick it up. Early on you'll find that mashing attack and dash is a pretty good strategy, which somewhat turned me off the game, but this is because later on it continues to stack on mechanics and attack patterns that layer onto the strategies you need to use. The game gets very tough, and there's only one way to beat it. There's some leeway in what weapons you prefer, but for the most part there is no other option besides getting better at the intended mechanics. This is hampered somewhat by the fact that the more you progress the more it is required that you improve at fighting enemies you may only see a hand full of times before you die. Personally, it felt quite cheep to reach a new level only to be completely unable to fight any of the enemies as they have entirely new attack patterns to the previous level. As you progress there are certain patterns to the mob variations that makes it easier, but early on progression has some major road blocks. Over time it got more fun to improve my strategies and skill, but even then there are some glaring issues. My main gripe is that half of your attacks will auto aim to the nearest enemy, including your only movement ability. This often leads to situations where I can recognize an incoming attack, but fail to avoid it because a dash locks onto an enemy or because a basic attack glues me to the enemy I'm fighting. This issue wouldn't be so bad if the dash didn't insist on dragging enemies along with you, making it so certain attacks can only be avoided by letting go of the controls and falling away. It certainly looks nice to play, but the combination of auto aim and the optimal strategy make playing it feel a lot more like steering train  than controlling a responsive character. Often times it feels like I'm just along for the ride in any given situation, and I personally prefer games with more control. It's ok, buy it full price if it looks fun, but if not get it on sale. Worth a try, but not for everyone.

This game is Difficult :")Cons - you aren't playing it right now. Go fix this!

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful early access roguelite. This game is way better than I expected it to be. The platforming and combat mechanics are smooth as butter, there's a bit of strategy in how you choose upgrades (not enough yet, but it is early access), the music slaps, and the difficulty is just right. Took me about 18 hours to get all achievements, so it's definitely worth it imo, even though it is still maybe only 70% feature complete or so. Can't wait to come back and play this game some more once it's out of EA. There's no feeling quite like narrowly evading all the enemies and bullets in a room that you lost control over, but still somehow making it out without taking damage.A few early access notes for the devs:- The guns probably need to be tuned/tweaked. As it is, they're not very useful for anything other than bosses, because usually just using the sword is more than sufficient for common mob rooms. I think ammo needs to feel like a more valuable/rare resource. Maybe also add a skill to stay in the air while firing the gun. Doesn't feel as fleshed out as the sword in that regard.- The translation on certain parts of the game, especially lore, leaves something to be desired. Furthermore, I basically couldn't have been less interested in the lore of the game, which is basically fine, because I played it exclusively for the gameplay; but, something to note.- The dash + smash (dragon something?) skill felt unreliable and too situational. I rarely used it, even though it looks cool, because dashing and smashing independently was safer and more predictable.- I had many runs where altar blessings were basically worthless. I think these could be made just a little more powerful and/or synergistic. It was only occasionally where I felt like I was making a "build" in the roguelite sense; otherwise, there were many times where all 3 blessings felt pretty lackluster.- More variety in the biome rooms would be appreciated. After quite a few runs, I felt that I had memorized most layouts, and nothing caught me by suprise or forced me to improvise anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: While it looked fun at first glance and all the player characters own twitchy movement is it's biggest downfall. You will unadvertantly end up in situations where simply hitting the enemy will twitch you into harms way or where the automatic aim overrides your desired dash direction and will get you hit or killed. Given that one of the difficulties is the very low health pool and few recovery items losing health due to an imprecise control scheme feels really bad. Combine this with some very questionable mini boss and level design and you get a result of "hey this COULD have been REALLY fun but it's not"

_childDocuments_.review: Controls and gameplay are extremely tight. The pixel-art-style and animations are beautiful. During this stage in early access the only problem is that it seems a bit lacking in content. After 5 or so hours you sort of feel done with it. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend but with a few reserves and frustrations.The game's action feels very good for what it tries to accomplish! One of the best-feeling platforming and action and the game's beautiful. The basics are covered and super competent!However, everything about the combat is designed towards a very fast-paced, frantic and empowering beat-em-up platformer. I see that as a problem in the context of a hard rogue-like where health is very scarce and precious. Because the game entices me so much to focus on relentlessly pummeling enemies, defensive thinking gets the can. I am reckless because the game urgently tells me to. I must also play carefully because each hit is a big deal but the recklessness makes me take a hit every couple of rooms, slowly churning life away in a "whatever" kind of way, but also my doom is slowly but surely coming. Both aggressiveness and carefulness are cranked way up there and this makes for a conflictual game experience IMO.Also it happened so many times that I get hurt because of the sword attack randomly nudging me into a bullet I specifically wanted to avoid. Still in the context that health is super precious and all that, this is VERY frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy hell, I am absolutely shocked at how fun this game is. It's like a crazy mixture of Devil May Cry, Celeste, and Hyper Light Drifter all processed through Rogue Legacy into a hyper-speed, combat-focused roguelite. Character movement is incredibly free and satisfying; even "rudimentary" combat will have you weaving a flurry of sword strikes and gun blasts together as you dash between enemies, deflecting bullets with your sword and laying down rapid combos in mid-air over a djenty metalcore soundtrack. Permanent unlocks through the game's skill tree will help you grow stronger, and, even then, since it's a roguelite, it's always challenging. You'll find yourself doing just one more run to see if you can make it a little farther than the last one as you sharpen your skills. Buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Scourgebringer is a quick as hell roguelike that takes some getting used to but once you do, its awesome!Gameplay wise everything is backwards, the start of the game is the least fun and the end is the most, the difficulty is somewhat of a bell curve too, mostly due to a few reasons, obviously with any roguelike and action game you have to experiment to find out what works and doesn't, once you learn everything its very easy to be tempted into using accessibility options since it feels like you get really beat up a lot, however i strongly advise against it, because once you start to use advanced moves and learn the hidden mechanics the game really quickly unfolds into a game that's insanely fun to blitz through, the dragon punch, the hp restore on fury ability, the spawn patterns, everything adds up to make you a better player, but the game does a absolutely terrible job at teaching this, infact without certain youtube tutorials i'd argue this game is nigh unplayable, it REALLY needed extra advanced tutorials.Graphics wise the game is stunning, im a sucker for pixel style and this game is no exception, there is a massive clash with friendly bullets and enemy bullets since its only indicated by a tiny sparkle that might as well not exist, they need a solid different color for your own bullets and friendly ones from smashing enemies, regardless the graphics are still very pretty.Music wise i wasn't overly keen, too much rock on rock, no variance between tracks, but sound design wise its easy on the easy, responsive and freakishly well mapped to the enemies, especially world 4's insect enemies sounds creeps me out in a way that's done well.Overall its a solid game, it lacks several layers of polish, the tutorials are lacking deeply and there's visual clutter at times, but when you're able to look past it, you can enjoy a very quick hack and slash roguelike, where you'll quickly see your own skills improve in quick periods of time, the achievements are seriously hard though, i did do the harder ones without accessibility options and it WILL put you to the test, so you've been warned if you want to clear this game purist style.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, very dynamic with a very good game feel. Slashing and dashing across rooms, stunning enemies before they can attack is very rewarding. _childDocuments_.review: Feels very shallow for a rogue-lite/like/whatever you want to call it. Not a whole lot going on other than clearing rooms with random enemies spawning. I think the worst part about this game is that the controls just feel absolutely awful. Here's a breakdown what makes this game miserable to play:- The RNG drops are hardly RNG, its always some useless pick up to reload your gun or +5% to some damage type. Because of this every run plays nearly the same.- Very shallow rogue-liteness. Random dungeon layouts barely change the game. Random pick-ups barely change the game. Locking out extremely basic and useful mechanics exploring rewards feels sloppy. (ex: heavy swing reflects, combo meter, etc.)- This game is designed to around you commiting to attacking and going all-in. Smashing light and dash attacks, then the eventually heavy to stun.  - One major problem is that once you start attacking there's an auto-aim and "stickiness" that basically glues your character to the enemy. If you want to dash out at a distance? Your dash drags along the enemy with you.- Your movements feel like they have no momentum or control. While attacking in the air, you'll float in the same spot. Hold a movement direction, you don't move. But the moment an enemy gets near you your character starts moving to them like a magnet. This seems like it would be great, but it ends up ****ing things up more often because this game focuses on spawning like 8+ mobs on top of you with your character floating around all over the place.- Combat is just a bunch of chaos happening every room, but the cycle of how you fight rarely seems to change unless the enemy type has some gimmick to them.- Guns feel tacked on, a bit randomly in this game. It would have been nice to reload without having to commit to all-in-attacking. Otherwise, it just feels like a mechanic where you dump your ammo while attacking and forget about it.- Enemies feels like they have a ton of health, and this game really likes making you mashing buttons over and over again. You don't really get a break from any of it.Overall, this game feels like it misses the point of what makes a lot of many other successful rogue-lites fun to play. This game is just tedious for the sake of being tedious.What I think would make this game better:- Reduce spawns. Way too many enemies in rooms. Stop spawning 2 rounds of enemies every room. It gets old very quickly.- Fix the floaty/stickyness/auto-aimness of air combat. It feels terrible. Give players control of the momentum.- Make combat less repetitive feeling. ie: Stun should be possible from lights on weaker enemies.- Make guns more interesting.- Make RNG more interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could stand among the action roguelike greats like Hades and Dead Cells! It just needs a few tweaks. I sincerely hope the devs take some of this critique to heart, since it has a lot of potential, and could possibly turn into a breakout sleeper hit if fine tuned in further updates.THE GOOD:- The action is hard hitting, and is based on bashing as much stuff as quick as possible. Feels satisfying to kill stuff. - Crunchy, visceral sfx.- A skill tree like the one they use here is infinitely more intuitive than dead cells' menus.- Distractions (story, character intros, menus) are quickly dismissable. definitely feels like they know they're catering to twitchy gamers here. THE BAD:- There are no real upgrades or replacements for the main weapon. This makes me feel that the amount of fun i can have is limited. You can replace and/or upgrade your side weapon, but since its ammo is limted, i mainly save it for the boss and don't discover its abilities very often. being able to replace / power it up is far less fun than being able to power up / replace a main weapon.- The game is more focused on atmosphere than on story. I would like a bit more story here. doesn't need to be elaborate or time consuming; just needs to have some heart. After four hours of play, I only have a vague sense of why I am doing what I'm doing, and that's a shame. During my playthroughs, I've come across very few bits of story scattered around the rooms. i get a story fragment maybe 1 in every 7 runs. By comparison, Dead Cells had lore rooms in every area of every run. Hades had a Gardenscapes-like system in its homebase. These systems made you feel like you were coming back to something new (even if you couldn't unlock anything during your run).- The skill tree is somewhat limited. It's one screen of maybe 30 powerups overall. Compare this to dead cells' hundreds of unlockables. This makes me feel like it'll only be a couple days before i 'get' everything. - The rarer of the two currencies is given away every time you play the game. This allows you to spam low-effort runs to unlock every powerup in the game.  Compare this to Hades, which rewards you with the rare currency only when doing something new (like trailblazing the game at a new difficulty for the first time).- You start off with way too many abilities: double dump, dash, wall jump, wall climb, and melee while in the air. I get that they probably wanted to give you an immersive first-time experience, but there has to be a better balance in terms of making you earn your abilities while still being immersive the first time around. I would like to have earned some of those before they drop you right into the action because the difficulty curve is too steep this way.- Areas are free to explore, but don't feel like they necessarily need to be. The game loop could have been tightened up by preventing backtracking (Hades style) and i don't think much would feel missing from it. - The music sucks. None of it goes anywhere; it's all very standard and short. The music changes in what seems like every 15 seconds, whenever you go from exploring to fighting and back. The change is very jarring since the exploring music is very ambient, and the fighting music is very heavy metal. This cuts down on the overall ambience because it prevents you from getting into neither 'mood' very effectively. Compare this to dead cells, which has a unique music track throughout each of the areas. - Every room's monsters spawn exactly the same. Enemies always spawn in two waves, one after the other once the first is completely cleared from the room. Hades' spawning was a lot more creative: some rooms spawn in discrete waves like in this game, other rooms spawn monsters continuously after they are defeated, one at a time. Other rooms have special spawn patterns.- There really aren't any secrets to find (or at least none that i have come across). By comparison, Dead cells was littered with hidden areas that you were constantly tempted to try and reach, Hades was filled with different room types and exit types (chaos' warp, thanatos' challenges, olympian gods' decision challenges, bonus rooms of sysiphus, etc) - map is "too" open. Every single room opens to its adjacent (if one exists). This makes things very accessible. However, cuts down on the amount of labyrinthine feel usually found in this kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: ScourgeBringer gives me strong vibes of various games. The artstyle reminds me of Hyper Light Drfiter, the moveset reminds me of Celeste, the combat reminds me of a easier version of Sundered. As a roguelike dungeon crawler, the flow is fast and fluent. The enemies are easy to handle if you can find the rhythmn that suits you well. Overall, the experience is pleasant and quite fun.Speed, fluency, and reflex are the core elements of ScourgeBringer. At first everything might seem too fast to handle, but once you get a hand of how the game is designed to be played it's really satisfying to pull it off. Fast sword slashes allow you to shatter foes within seconds. Dash is not only your evasive maneuver but also an offensive tool to dispatch weaker enemies. Gun Turret provides huge fire power to burst down stronger enemies. Smash is the most useful of all. This special attack offers several ways to help you prevail in battles. It's a strong attack which can knock foes away from you or stun them when they perform attacks. You can also use Smash to reflect projectiles back to their owners. Utilizing all of the above to their full potential yields a great combat experience.I adore this feature. It rewards players like me who enjoy clearing every room before confronting the level boss. The amount of currency you earn during the trial is enough to buy everything in the shop in each level. What`s more, when you complete the whole map excluding boss, the last room you complete will guaranteed-drop  healing items and buffs for your sword or gun. If you are not confident with your reflexes, I recommend clear the room one by one, slowly and steadily. The rewards you can get allow you to survive longer and make combats faster.Aside from general health and damage buff, the Chiming Tree provides some interesting skills to encourage you to adjust your playstyle. Striking Smash rewards you to reflect projectiles instead of running away from them; Combo meter encourages you to switch up attack sequence and rewards you with more currency; Fury is a powerful skill that allows you strike down multiple foes at the same time. These are the three major combat variant you may purchase. I am looking forward to see more ways to amplify the battle in the future.Again, I am a sucker for pixel art.I am not listing "too short" as a con since the game just released its early access. I complete the game within five try. Roughly judged, the total playthrough falls around 15 to 30 minutes depending on ones skill and exploration.The three bosses so far feel quite balanced. The pattern for each other can be fully understood within two rotations. My only complaint would be the randomness of Judge Bileranha's green bubble mass. Otherwise, every attack has an opportunity for you to dodge out. It all boils down to ones reflex and situational awareness. If you have trouble dodging, the Smash attack is your best bet for destroying projectile, or even better, deflecting them back.I am hereby appending some thoughts for the game, depending how it will develop in the future. I will revisit this review once there`s more things added in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent 2 hours with this game, but I already know mechanics-wise it's become one of my favorites. There's some things I wish could be improved (which I list below), but none of them take away from my enjoyment of the game. The jumping feels very precise (like Celeste) and it is incredibly easy to feel badass. If you watch gameplay videos it looks cool, but actually playing it feels great once you've gone through your 5th room taking no damage, dash attacking, deflecting bullets, and shooting an enemy across the room. There's something wonderful as well about combo-ing on a difficult enemy and having an enemy try to sneak a shot at you, and you time it perfectly to send it right back at them. The game oozes with style and the mechanics are simple but extremely fun.It's not a perfect game, but what's there is an amazing foundation that I think could put it up there with some indie favorites like Dead Cells, Hollow Knight, Celeste (the latter being the easiest comparison). Some of the gripes I do have with the game:-Knowing when you have you dash or slam/heavy attacks isn't as clear as I'd like at times. The time between each is fairly short, so this is by no means a huge issue, and if nothing were to get changed about this, it wouldn't detract any enjoyment from the game whatsoever.-Mobility is huge in this game, particularly with your double jump, and sometimes it's just hard to tell when you have a double jump available. Making the comparison to Celeste again, but when her dash was used up, her hair went back to being red. Something visual on the character would definitely help me, but it's also incredibly easy to get a jump back, and the dash is on a short cool down. So with how long you can spend combo-ing enemies, you'll certainly have a jump and dash ready to go.-The heavy/impact attack's deflect ability has some weird frames that really throws me off sometimes. There are sometimes where I've been in fights (notably the first judge fight) where I used it, but in the last couple frames of the move, the enemy's shot went through. I don't know what it is, but visually it throws me off and I sometimes get caught making this mistae. Nine times out of ten it's fine and I can time it right, but for moves where it's a stream of bullets (3-4 in a row, I find the attack lets the last one going through. So, if anything, if you get the game, just be wary of how those attacks are coming at you.Overall, this game is just super fun and feels extremely satisfying. My hand was legitimately hurting because of all the precise movements I was trying to pull off (so maybe checking the box for holding the attack button in Accessibility settings isn't a bad idea at all lol). I'm still struggling to get past the second boss, but the mechanics are fun enough that I enjoy fighting similar enemies. It's still early access, but for only $12 on sale, I can already see myself getting my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRFast paced? - Check. High skill ceiling? - Check. Roguelite? - Check. Competitive price-point? - Check. Satisfying? - cHeck Yeah!Coming into this game off the back of Rogue Legacy and Celeste i felt like i was meeting the angsty child of  two old friends, it has a lot of qualities of the aforementioned games, but the aesthetic is grungier; the sound track intense, the movement fluid, the enemies punishing... this game is beautiful.The gameplay is honestly some of the most satisfying content i've consumed this century, whether you be forcing your way through rooms with brute force, maybe getting tagged here and there or planning your route of attack and executing it flawlessly, sending your enemies projectiles back at them and maxing out your combo multiplier.The 'progression' system so far seems really balanced, adding neat little bonuses without massively impacting the overall difficulty of the game, it also acts as a guiding hand, giving you hints at what you should be doing to delve deeper into the machine.As much as i've fallen for this game and could just heaping on the praise, there are some issues, not huge issues, but issues none the less.As it stands you can unload a magazine (from some guns) into a 'Judge' - essentially a Biome's mini-boss and kill it instantly, or take away half of the actual boss's health. Hopefully they tune them down in the future (maybe have ranged attack weak spots so it takes some skill, rather than dumping ammo?) The current length of the game is the biggest issue, only having 3 Biomes, each consisting of roughly 15 rooms, this might sound like it's a decent size but with the pace of the game it only takes a few seconds to clear a room. - Being Early Access this is obviously going to be extended and is only an issue at the time of writing.Lack of variety - This one is pretty tied in to the above, but even through the current areas the enemies don't really change that much, they all mindlessly come for you, they have very similar attack patterns, and they're all stun-lockable.I'll close this off with a more positive tone, because i really really do enjoy and completely recommend this game. Once development gets to a point where the game is ready for an official release, i'm sure it will take it's place in my top 10 games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Final verdict: f*cking awesome!I played ScourgeBringer in Alpha state, and EA pretty much follows it. Dead Cells is one of my all-time favorites, and the comparisons are inevitable (heck, the devs even say so), so imagine Dead Cells with a dedicated Dash button, and there you have it, ScourgeBringer. Where Dead Cells IS better:1. The gotta-catch'em-all-blueprints mechanics ensured a long lasting appeal for Dead Cells;2. Much, much more weapons, skills, traps, and so on, to choose from.Where ScourgeBringer CAN be better:1. The Dash and stay-off-the-ground combat. A game like this lives and dies (eh!) with its battle system, and in that regard ScourgeBringer seems to be even better than Dead Cells. The Dash can be maneuvered in any direction and it will strike the opponents upon hit, which makes it quite the versatile weapon of choice. As long as you keep striking enemies the avatar will remain flying, and pairing it with the all-directional Dash means full rooms of enemies can be cleared without ever touching the ground.

_childDocuments_.review: This game screams quality. Everything good about it is obvious as soon as you you boot up the game. The vibe, art and sound direction are all top notch. On paper, this would be a very good game. But some gameplay issues make it a very frustrating experience. The sad thing is, these could have been avoided probably, but someone decided not to.Most of the time, I don't feel in control of my character's movement. The character usually doesn't go in the direction I intend it to. When you attack with your sword, the game makes you fly towards the center of the enemy. And enemy projectiles can hit you because of this. Or when you dash, and there is an enemy in the general direction of your dash, game will make you dash directly at the enemy. And if enemy happens to be firing at you at that moment, disaster happens.And game is full of this kind of issues. I assume some of the little mechanics were intended to help the player, but they have the inverse effect. For example, your character will automatically wall-run/slide when you are near the wall, but that can make you hit by enemy projectiles. Another example is that when new enemies are spawning, enemies closer to you will spawn slower. This was probably done with good intention so that player is not surprised by sudden spawning enemies, but it also means enemies far away can come closer and gang up on you while you wait for closer enemies to spawn.I would say the game is too greedy with its mechanics. The game would be better with less and simpler mechanics. For example, the wall-run/slide/jump could be excluded, and honestly nothing would feel missing. There is already too many buttons you should press frequently. The default control scheme (of gamepad) is also not good. My performance improved so much after remapping some buttons so that controls are like other similar games.When I say it like this, it sounds like a bad game, but it is not. I just wish I had played this in the early alpha, so that my feedback could maybe have more impact. Nevertheless I will be looking forward to the next game from these devs.

_childDocuments_.review: This games' strongest suit is also its weakest. The movement makes and brakes this game. On one hand it has fantastically fast paced combat with lots of dashes and slashes, lots of mid-air combat, but on the other hand the movement is too floaty and a bit clumsy sometimes. This makes it pretty hard to escape massive amounts of projectiles (which this game provides with massive amount of generosity). Even if you unlock the ability to reflect enemy projectiles - they spew much more of them than your weapon swing can reflect. Then you take unnecessary damage and your run comes closer to an end.Art style and music fits the game very well. But the gameplay is too frustrating to be thoroughly enjoyable most of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: After Dusk, Doom Eternal, and Nightmare Reaper, this is the first game with Andrew Hulshult's music in it that I dislike to the point of leaving a negative review. Unfortunately, the music can't carry all of this on its own.The game is a repetitive roguelite that tries too hard to be challenging. Many game mechanics, like mixing gun power-ups, are lost due to poor balancing, with the starting pistol being extremely underpowered and unable to equip upgrades. If you wanted to buy another weapon and/or upgrades, you'd be facing extremely high costs.You'll also be crawling across the first 1-2 levels for hours simply because you need meta-progression upgrades to make your runs a little less miserable.Difficulty is not the main issue here, as there is a nice option to tune the experience based on your skill in the Settings, but the fact that every run feels so repetitive and that meta-progression upgrades are necessary to make it through, while at the same time feeling insignificant and adding almost nothing to the actual gameplay. They also take a lot to unlock; you'll be bored before you get to them.Overall a 4/10, could have been a lot better if it focused on being VARIED and HARD rather than just HARD.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, but understand what you are getting into.I'm not bad at games, I'm not the best but i'd certainly say that I know how to play effectively and learn quickly, ESPECIALLY with rogue-likes. Some titles I could mention are: Hades, Skul the hero slayer, Death must die, Picayune dreams, Vampire Survivors, and recently Against great darkness and Boneraiser minions. In all of these games I either felt like I as a player was becoming more skilled, or at the very least my character was getting stronger so I could make it further each run.That being made clear: I have been humbled beyond belief by this game. I thought to myself when searching for a game to buy: "I want a challenge,  a game that can actually test my skill." and oh boy did I get it. When the game boots up, it says "Adaptive game difficulty is enabled by default, and can be disabled", and my first thought was, "don't worry, im not a game journalist! give me the intended experience =)" now 4 and a half hours later, I am slapping myself, angry that I am dwelling over the thought of turning it on again, or choosing the option to increase health drops. Before going into spoiler territory I can sum it up like this: this game is the rogue-like version of "Hyperlight drifter", where you have a sword that can regenerate a gun after striking enemies. If what you want is to have TIGHT combat, and dedicate time to memorizing enemy attack patterns and developing full-proof strategies, this is the game for you. But if you think that with your fast movement you can just spam buttons, and by buttons I mean ANY button, even the movement buttons, you WILL lose.Ok "spoilers" if you want to understand what I mean without being cryptic, idk if they count as spoilers though im just being safe:

_childDocuments_.review: Initially getting ScourgeBringer at its release, I was allured by the aesthetic of the game. I found it to be difficult but I loved the approach to the game, it reminds me of Monolith but instead of a ship with blasters, you're a person who melees all their enemies. There's a few way to damage enemies, however, you often have to play in VERY close proximity, so reacting well to any enemy attacks is key to success.Despite being one of the more unforgiving roguelikes I've played, this one has adaptive difficulty as a setting as well as multiple accessibility options. So even if its too frustrating, the game can be tweaked a bit to still feel rewarding without feeling like you're cheating.With flexibility of options, a GREAT atmosphere and satisfying combat I give this a strong recommendation to any roguelike fans, a light recommendation to those who are a bit familiar with the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: ScourgeBringer is a 2D pixel action, roguelite with minor platforming elements, centered around fast, arena-style combat. You are Kyrha, strongest of your tribe sent to challenge the dreaded ScourgeBringer, a monolithic construct that has brought ruin to the world. By entering it, you undergo the Ordeal, and struggle against the murder gauntlet of foes and uncertain allies in a realm of non-permanent death.The overall gameplay favors high-speed combat, with Kyrha zipping around the screen, performing simple multi-hit combos while utilizing secondary abilities, such as her floating gun drone. Each part is simple and straightforward, but when combined with each other and the speed of combat, it can create some intense split-second decision making. That said, you can play slower and more methodically, so that is always an option. The game, however, does go out of its way to specifically reward speed and efficiency over everything else.A range of accessibility options help to onboard people, with options of changing the difficulty to special considerations for those with trouble on its pixel art or gameplay. Progression options offer modifiers toward gameplay itself, with post-completion runs having access to hardmode modifiers to push even further. I'm reasonably satisfied with the array of options offered, and feel particular care was given in this regard.The story of ScourgeBringer can be charitably called barebones, told more through its environment and snippets of recovered logs than anything else. While the creative vision of the game is clearly conveyed, the lack of real meat to chew on for the narrative is a downside to me. There is something you can piece together, but the story as a whole could probably fit on a couple printed pages and be done. As a writer, I would've preferred more, but I can understand why there is not.The art and music are very good, and particular care was paid to the art's pixel style. Background and foreground come together seamlessly, and all the game elements are clear, evocative, and carry a unique visual flavor. The music suits the high tension, high speed gameplay, combining various forms of rock, electronic, and bass together. While no one track stood out to my untrained ear, none of it took me out of the mood, either.I rather like ScourgeBringer, it carries itself with a clear vision of purpose and clear polish toward its goals. If I had to complain, it feels like a game ripe for having 'more', especially in a post-Hades world which has redefined roguelites. If nothing else, a bolstered narrative element could've done much to enrich the experience.I would wager a good 5-10 hours on ScourgeBringer can deliver most, if not all, its content before repetition. If you're concerned if it's a good pick up, the 2 hour refund window is more than enough to see what the game has to offer without worrying about missing out.

_childDocuments_.review: It gets compared to Celeste, which is a joke, because it doesnt have what is the core of Celeste: precise and frameexact control and movement. In Celeste, your movement resources are meaningfull and should be used wisely. This game however is just a floaty, buttonmash slasher with exhausting controls. Of course this game is meant to be played fast and not as a puzzle plattformer, but it would benefit heavily from a higher gravity and perhaps more momentum from moving, rather than putting all the emphasis on your dash. The movement is way too floaty and the fast gameplay stems from dashing alone, rather than from regular movement. So youre either almost standing still midair, because autoattacking kills off every momentum, or your speed is at 100% when you dash - theres no inbetween.The combat is also extremely simplistic. The main autoattack is just a very close ranged dps tool without any complexity. You dodge projectiles, dash in, bash autoattack, combine it with a heavystun attack and repeat. There are some gimmicks like reflecting projectiles with the heavy attack or a ranged special attack, but it has ammo and thus isnt something you can use permanent inbetween the dodge-attack cycle.Honestly, better check out 20XX or 30XX. They have more or less the same premise, but go way beyond the simplistic design of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Scourgebringer is a chaotically fast, exceptionally fluid, dungeon crawling roguelight w/ a killer metal soundtrack.  Not only does this game offer an extremely high skill ceiling, but it also has some of the coolest pixel art of any game that I have ever played.  To have success in this game, you will need to memorize every enemy pattern, learn where all of the secrets are located, use the environment to your advantage, and know how to prioritize enemies.  This is one of my favorite games that I have played this year.What's Good:-The learning curve is very steep.  This is one of the tougher roguelights out there, but it is also very skill based w/ an exceptionally high skill ceiling.  It took me about 12 hrs to have my first winning run.  My winning run was dependent upon me learning every enemy attack telegraph and mastering the games mechanics.  The meta progression does offer some cool permanent upgrades, and there will be some runs that are more favorable for bonus upgrades, but it is extremely unlikely that you will ever have a winning run due to favorable RNG.-In order for this game to really work, it had to have really fast and fluid movement.  The movement and platforming is absolutely top notch.  It will take some time to get used to it, but once you do, you will feel like a complete badass ninja.  I started to feel like I was playing a different game once I mastered all of the movement, attack, and deflection mechanics.  This game has some of the best moment to moment combat of any dungeon crawler out there.-I'm a complete sucker for pixel art, so this was a no brainer for me from a visual standpoint.  I think Scourgebringer has some of the best pixel art in gaming today.  It may be quite as good as Blasphemous, Dandara, or Iconoclasts, but I'd be hard pressed to think of many other games that have cooler pixel art.  My favorite visual moments are the terrifying bosses, the way projectiles or acid look as it moves across screen, and especially how the later biomes look.  Everything looks awesome imo.-I've heard some ppl say that this game feels like Dead Cells had a baby w/ Doom.  I think that is a decent comparison.  The music definitely reminds me of Doom.  I love the fast, hardcore, metal music that blasts your eardrums as you slash and dash around screen.  This game has a top notch soundtrack.-The meta progression and in game upgrades are simple and effective.  Scourgebringer was never meant to be a game that played like Risk of Rain 2 or Binding of Isaac.  In those games, you expect to have a ridiculously overpowered build at some point.  That's not going to happen here.  The meta progression does offer a few really important and super fun upgrades, but most of the in game pickups are very small but effective boosts.  You must master the games basic mechanics in order to be successful, plain and simple.Could Use Some Changes:-This barrier of entry is extremely high for this game.  I would not recommend this game to those new to the genre.  This game is tough, and will beat you up for the first few hrs.  However, I guarantee that if you willing to put in enough time and make some adjustments, you will see progress.  There are some accessibility options which is nice, but I have a feeling that even w/ those, this is still not the most beginner friendly game.-If you have really bad hand-eye-coordination, then you will probably always struggle w/ this game.  There is nothing special about my HEC so you don't need to be a superhero to play this game, but if you struggle w/ fast acting games, you will struggle w/ Scourgebringer.-There isn't nearly as much variety in runs as there are from some of the other top roguelights out there.  I think that's fine.  Spelunky and Vagante are games that I immediately think of when comparing to this game.  Those are both awesome games, but both are very tough, skill based games that don't have a ton of variety in runs.Consensus:-Excellent Game (Tier 2 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  This game is awesome and I'm so glad I finally got the time to play it.  I'm not sure why I've waited this long, but it was very much worth the wait.  This is my favorite dungeon crawler that I've played in 2022.  It's fast, looks amazing visually, has a killer soundtrack, and is so exhilarating.  It will challenge you every step of the way in just the right way.  Very few games that I've played have struck the perfect balance between tension and reward the way that Scourgebringer has.  It isn't for everyone, so keep that in mind going in.

_childDocuments_.review: ScourgeBringer is a roguelite that delivers difficulty in an often frustrating way, especially in later levels where tight spaces and relentless enemy fire push you to your limits. While it has the potential to be a game you'd sink hours into, the cumbersome controls and lack of precision in combat mechanics lead to player fatigue and even physical discomfort after short sessions. Fortunately, the developers included accessibility options like an immunity mode, which was crucial for allowing me to experience all the levels, enemy designs, and endings without giving up.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat, in mid-air works with the shift button. You use momentum and air-attacks to throw the enemies down on their weight. -You collect blood, as the currency to use in the shops-Hardcore Keyboard and Mouse review; 1x 10HP Playthrough before work- had to let you know  ::)You are a very very fluid ninja, chosen by the tribe to rescue their world. I read reviews before purchase. But let me inform you that the controls are magnificent. How magnificent? Super meat boy magnificent.  But with a keyboard and mouse. Your main keys WASD< E , left and right click and left shift- floating cross-hair on screen - indicates your directions of attack/looking/movement.E - Grab/Pull an enemy / Nice to hit larger enemies around the screen - then you dash in the direction to continue attacking themThe Right click is for your limited magazines Ranged weapon. Think- Desert Eagle - but accurate -Wherever you aim, it will go there.The schema is wall gripping - slow descent.Double Jump -standard ninja - But Dash as well - so essentially, it's super sprint double jump, or triple jump - double jump + dash at the apex of the  second jump.Your katana swings at the slice of every click. It's instant, and while attacking enemies in air, you remain hovering above them, slicing, and dashing as you go. Each level is your playground, There are items dropping for permanent boosts, but it's your highest priority not to get hit.You will need to learn enemies power up times, or throw other enemies in to attack There are puzzle elements, like moving through the level-grids, looking for bosses.You collect blood from your kills to buy things from the travelling merchant within the levels.Death of 10hp- STARTS From the beginning of the entire level again.  You have lost any permanent upgrades/ There are big enemies - pretty cool to fight wave, sometimes you face that one and two waves of an enemy, enemies respawn in a level, just to make sure if you think losing the -1 HP last time was EASY< lets do it again for you hahaha,But that's good, I think blood remains..[will confirm in further reviews}Also. Kudos to dev's. The art style is breath-taking. The captivation and response times to watch an art show in anime-esque PC-gaming; is immersive, and the upgrading feels great.The EULA had an Italian pizza recipe, and a jam recipe, lol  It's to actually informative to read. All works out immaculately with this purchase. Worthy investment into Roguelike :)IF you enjoyed the messenger, you will enjoy this even more. Better Alternative to Kunai -same release day;The Recipe: Title end to finishThis game gave me an italian pizza recipe I shall try- Flying Oak's specialThe dough:Put 500 grams of fine wheat flour in a bowl with a pinch of salt (or baking soda)Put about 20 grams of fresh baking yeast in a glass with one table spoon of sugar and fill it with mineral water at room temperature, mix the whole thing and let it sit for a couple minutesAdd the yeast started to the flour and start mixing your bare handsMix the whole thing and add small quantities of water until all the flour is mixed and stop when it doesn't stick to your hands anymoreLet it sit in a warm place for at least 2 hoursThe fig jam (using premade jam is fine too):Extract the flesh of about 6 to 8 fresh figsCook the flesh in a pan on low heat with some neutral oilOnce it's finely mixed and cooked, add a huge table spoon of honeyCook some more for a few minutesThe pizza:Pre heat the oven at 430°F (220°C)Lay down the dough on your biggest plateCover it generously with your favorite tomato coulis (pasta sauce works quite well)Add some fresh mozzarella all over itPour some fig jam in between the mozzarellaCook that bad boy for about 20 minutesThe finish:Spread some oregano and fresh basilAdd some Italian ham on top of it if you're into itDrizzle some honey all over itServe!

_childDocuments_.review: And there I was, starting to ask myself if I was getting over roguelikes.  Then ScourgeBringer comes my way and reminds me why I fell in love with the genre in first place.  This fast action platformer is everything I could ask for.  Bright and colorful pixel art, a rockin' soundtrack, and gameplay mechanics that feel oh so damn smooth.  It definitely takes some getting used to, and certain enemy and boss types put me in my place more often than I care to admit, but once you get it down, oh baby.  Clearing a room with combos consisting of sword, gun, and dashes is one of the most satisfying feelings I've had in gaming in quite some time.  It's a damn rush that I couldn't get enough of. An easy pickup and without question one of the best games of the year.WINNER: MOST INNOVATIVE GAMEPLAY 2020

_childDocuments_.review: Another rogue-like that combines melee and gun combat, and is focused on very fast gameplay by dashing in the air. By exploring the levels and defeating enemies, you'll collect blood that you can use to buy perks or upgrade your weapons. While the game looked very promising to me, I never managed to master the controls. While dashing, I often ended up in another location than I expected, which resulted in many frustrating deaths. Because of this, I wasn't able to defeat the boss of the first world, despite many tries.It's hard for me to say if this is a good game or not, but it's definitely not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, I must point that I am awfull in this kind of games. Give me more than two buttons on action platform games and my brain overloads. But never had so much fun getting my ### kicked! At first my moves, attacks where random, I could hardly use more than the dash and normal strike moves. Jumping was confusing me, and running straight into enemy attacks was all I could do. Some hours later... on the first two worlds at least, I have learned the enemy patterns, and almost flawless them, even the bosses. When the movement options sink into your muscle memory, everything feels so natural, satisfying! The awesome soundtrack does an excellent job intensifying the frantic rythm of the game! I love the controls of the game, and movement, and attack options are so alien and unique (to me at least) and at the same time so tight, and when given time you will see how billiant (in my opinion) of a game Scourgebringer is! Excellent roguelike, design-wise, also. If you think you would like an action roguelike, a tough one, give this game a try. I think it is amazing, and unique! Amazing job devs!And special thanks to Esty for introducing me to this little gem! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Good game for sure. It is far tougher than it seems. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of fast-paced action games and I really love platformers which allow freedom of movement so this game should be an obvious recommend, but no.The game centers in dungeon crawling exploration in small, usually square, rooms, each of these filled with, be it enemies, shops, "blessings" which range from passive buffs to slightly altering game mechanics, or loot. Although this is not the selling point; which in this case is the fast-paced action platforming gameplay this game sells itself as, which it is.. if you count "clicking your mouse as quick as you can" fast paced action.The game lacks weight in it's action and variation in it's roguelite elements. Enemies range from one-hit-why-do-you-even-exist kills to *clicking intensifies*, and enemy projectiles are annoying as it is! Sure you can stop them by using your smash attack before they use a projectile, but that's not always the case, sometimes they just shoot without warning, and since rooms are very small you will end up going for cover more than once since, even if using the Smash attack destroy bullets, it might not destroy ALL the bullets coming your way,; It's suppoused to be a parry, but you have to go out of your way to use it, thankfully you can dodge bullets while dashing so that's the saving gra- JUST KIDDING YOU CAN'T DODGE, JUST "BLOCK" AND "PARRY".it.. it's just not fun. You basically fly arround while attacking, you don't dash to be "fast", you dash because it's your only option to be effective at all. The game's idea of "roguelike" is giving you items to buff your stats, not change gameplay in any meaningful way. Infact, it's more fun to kill the enemies that die in one shot because you can ATLEAST feel like you did massive damage in one strike. the gameplay goes like this: Jump, dash to enemy, *click*, enemy dies, dash to next enemy, repeat until room is clean", And you might be saying "but ain't that basically every action game ever?" yes, it is, but unlike most other games, that's not basically, it's LITERALLY all you do.Also you have a gun, which.. why? it's only useful against big enemies with lots of HP as a quick burst but otherwise.. why? you might as well keep clicking.am angy, imma go sip my hap juice

_childDocuments_.review: After getting pretty far in this game with multiple attempts, I can easily say this game is more frustrating than it is fun. Taking damage here feels less like a stupid mistake I made, and more of an unavoidable instance. The fast paced dashing and slashing makes the game very fun to move around and destroy multiple enemies, but it falls apart when fighting bosses and in certain areas. Pretty much every upgrade is needed to actually enjoy the experience, leading to early frustration when you feel as if you don’t know what to do.  The many accessibility options, while helpful, can’t help problems inherently baked into the game.-The slight but very noticeable delay in your Smash which makes reflecting bullets seem much more difficult than it should be. Compare to Enter the Gungeon, where your blanks are instant because it’s built around a bullet hell, or Spiritfall, where your reactive actions are slower because the gameplay is slower. -Your bullets are tied to your floating robot which could decide for whatever stupid reason to aim at another enemy or just a random wall.  Because it also flys around Blood Altars and lock onto shop items, you can’t aim in those rooms when looking for secret rooms.-A late game area has floating hazards that make it difficult (if not downright impossible) to actually use the movement that makes the game fun. It is much more viable to sit on the floor and shoot bullets and only dash at enemies when you are out.I want to say I enjoyed the OST but I barely noticed the difference between levels except for minor parts here and there.  Winning didn’t feel rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Great core concept mired in frustrating design choices. The platforming in this game is quick and intuitive, but the focus on quick moving melee combat really doesn't gel with the bullet hell style of enemy attacks.This is compounded with increasing enemy health. If an enemy takes 3-5 seconds of prolonged slashing to take out, you find yourself needing to laboriously clear each room focusing on avoidance and survival more so than the fast combat the game sells you.This is further exacerbated by a lacklustre progression tree and upgrades, offering little in the way of demonstrable power. All in all, there's great design here, but very little that actually realises the fun, fast-paced hack and slash combat the game sells.

_childDocuments_.review: 4.5 hours in and feeling like I'm about half way. Done 4/7 skill tree branches.As far as core mechanics go, Scourgebringer seems very well crafted so far, and I'm interested to see what it looks like when it's fully polished and ready for release. Assuming you have moderate success, you'll have access to all the controller mapped abilities in the first 2-3 hours, which is a good move for a challenging platformer/roguelite; you want to be able to start mastering those controls early on.The art style is solid. Nothing outstanding, but it's got a good aesthetic and the enemy animations are clear as day. It never feels frustrating, as though you can't see attacks coming, and a lot of good design choices have to go in to making that the case.My biggest complaint as far as mechanics go is the dash ability. It works fine when you're flying about, but it interacts with walls very poorly and in a way that is not intuitive. If you're climbing a wall and you try and dash upward, if you aim your dash even slightly toward the direction of the wall, it seems to pretty consistently just launch you down the wall. It's the only part of the platforming that doesn't feel tight and has multiple times resulted in what I think to be unnecessary damage. Considering the game that is marketed as Dead Cells style with Celeste platforming, I'm surprised they dash functions this way in comparison to Celeste where dashing into a wall just moves you nowhere and diagonal dashing into a wall sends you up/down the wall with reduced momentum of a normal dash. This may seem like a small gripe, but it is very frustrating and feels counter-intuitive. Everything else about the platforming is super tight, and changing this could make its platforming top-tier in my opinion.As for style, it's hard to tell what kind of ethos Scourgebringer is going for. At times it feels like it wants to be Enter the Gungeon with goofy boss names like Bodyboulder, and other times it feels like it wants to be dark and edgy like Dead Cells or Sundered with that feeling of being lost or hopeless. Interestingly Dead Cells pulls off dark and humorous very well, and from what I can tell watching old footage, even very early in development it had that kind of ethos. Not saying it's easy to pull off that kind of tone, but Scourgebringer kind of feels like it's reaching beyond its station when it comes to writing. It's also pretty apparent that there is a language barrier and that the writer/s' first language isn't English, and it seems to stand in the way of whatever tone the game is trying to get across. Hopefully in a full release there will be some better localization and maybe the tone will become better established, but currently the writing and tone are definitely the roughest part of this game.Definitely still recommend it to any lovers of platforming and roguelites, but perhaps purchase and wait till full release to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially enjoyed this game but found myself getting more and more frustrated as I continued to play. ScrougeBringer leaves a lot to be desired. On one hand this game has a great artstyle, good music, and a pretty intriguing storyline with some good bits of subtle comedy. However, on the other hand the combat is flimsy and frustrating to control, the floor layouts and bosses get very repetitive, and the game is far too difficult to enjoy without turning on accessibility features. _childDocuments_.review: Wonderfully fast paced, tight and punchy action platforming gameplay, fine-tuned rougelike elements that add just enough replay value to get the player to the finish line without slowing down the experience, and all on top of an immediately exciting world. If that wonderfully animated woeful chaos in the trailers has you excited, you're in for a riot. The newly added adaptive difficulty opens this game up to a much wider audience, especially to those that just want to see the unique world built here, along with beautiful art in motion on display along the way.DO:-expect a challenge still, along the lines of Fury or Hyper-light drifter, with added 'chaos mods' to bump things up to 11 if you're interested.-remember this is mostly an action/adventure platformer, using rougelite elements to flesh out the game loop. You'll be spending much more time learning enemy patterns and how to best use your abilities than deciding which stat block you want on your gun.-check out the soundtrack, which generally sticks to frenetic, ever-shifting synths oozing with atmospheric flavor driven by skittering drum lines. These tracks are then infused with a hearty dose of ultrviolence, a mixture of riffs that RIP  and toned up percussion to help your TEAR through enemy waves and minibosses, with each end-of-stage boss getting their own destructive track.-sit back and soak in the atmosphere. The game's narrative is centered on the central cataclysm and the world around the disaster, with characters serving more to be the player's perspective into the world rather than take center stage and advance the scene. The pull of the mystery still hit me, but you probably already know whether or not that kind of story works for you.DON'T:-Expect a lengthy, endlessly growing dungeon crawler as some other titles offer. This is a tightly woven, compact experience in which the depth of both the game's mechanics and world can be seen within a few winning runs. A few wins make take 20+ hours to achieve for ... some of us, on the default difficulty, but I digress. This was a positive for me, all comes down to taste and free time.-Tunnel vision on the 'rougelike' tag on this game. It's there, but it isn't the center of the experience. The core dash n' slash gameplay is more or less a static element through each run, with upgrades being most noticeable and your secondary ranged weapon. Again don't buy this game hoping to squeeze  a 40+ hour experience out of what is essentially a shifting five floor dungeon crawl.-miss out on this title just because the difficulty curve was rough for some on release. The adaptive difficulty makes the limited life bar much more manageable, and opens the game up to anybody more interested in the aesthetic appeal of the game than it's white-knuckle aggressive game play loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Its description: punishing but rewarding.Its best feature: satisfying movement.Its presentation: beautiful art.The first thing that attracted me into making an instinctive purchase was the art. The colors are attractive and work well to distinguish bullet from foe. As soon as I saw our silver hair protagonist jumping wall to wall to samurai slash baddies I was hooked and couldn't be more excited to play.After installing it, the next thing that got my attention was the movement. It is buttery smooth (at times so smooth, you lose the plot with all the enemies and bullets flying around) and super responsive. If you run head on into a bullet, it's because you weren't quick enough or made an error rather than the limitations of the games itself (like clunky movement) preventing you from playing at your best. In a fast-paced action platformer, movement will make or break the game and this game excels in this area.At the end of the day, when you hear the words "roguelite" and "platformer" you know you in for a masochistic treat. You will die... a lot. But fear not, for there is a nifty progression tree, a series of bosses and a greedy (get it?) merchant waiting for you in and after every level to give reason and respite to every death.May your sword be true and your jumps inspired!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! The gameplay is smooth, fast, and skillful. A hefty learning curve with a fire soundtrack to slice devils to. This is due mainly because of a mid run upgrade which provides A TON of meta currency. If this upgrade was removed I think the progression curve would have a much nicer curve to it.The only other things I would change are minor UI things. Opening the map you use tab and you can use tab OR your mouse to teleport to a different room (Once unlocked). So a lot of the time I end up trying to close the map and end up teleporting to a room that I didn't want to be in. The other UI change I would suggest is just a little x or checkmark on the unlock tree for enabled/disabled upgrades. I frequently wouldn't realize that I had turned an upgrade off until late into a run.Otherwise a fantastic game that may just need a couple of balance changes here and there.Feels like Monolith and Enter The Gungeon and Hyper Light Drifter all had parental rights on raising this game. _childDocuments_.review: this game is really giving me a headache. Its virtually perfect, it feels good, fast-paced, enemy design is where it needs to be, its basically a flawless final project except for one very offensive design choice; the difficulty. I normally do NOT care about difficulty in games at all, in fact I think the game should have some level of difficulty as part of the experience because games are fun when they're challenging, however this games difficulty just feels cheap. It's really difficult to see when things hit you, and some enemies have certain attacks that have hit boxes that are just poorly built and seem to hit me despite my own ability to dodge and time it well. This game has quite the learning curve I'll give it that, and it is in fact an amazing game and a true gem hidden on the Steam market, but I am unsure I can recommend it with the way the difficulty is designed. The game warns you of this difficulty, but for once I felt that the difficulty is in fact not meant to be the way it is for the kind of game it is. There needs to be something done to the regular rate at which health items spawn, how long your invulnerability lasts between hits, and having health return at the end of a stage because there was not a single run in my near 3 hours of gameplay where I reached the 2nd stage with more than 3 hp, and while normally I would chalk that up to my own inability to not get hit, this game gives basically zero opportunity's to recover upon losing hp, both in the sense of regaining lost hp and prevent yourself from being hit again by the same attack that just hit you. Parrying projectiles needs a rework as well, I feel that if you are able to parry a projectile back at an enemy it should also stun them, not just parrying the enemy itself as enemies that should long streams of projectiles will just keep shooting you despite you having parried one of those projectiles, which just totally defeats the purpose of letting me parry the projectiles in the first place. You gave me the ability to keep myself from getting hit by projectiles by parrying projectiles, yet almost every enemy that shoots a projectile shoots more than one in quick succession, so if I parry one of them I am guaranteed to be hit by another shortly after successfully parrying the previous bullet. Instead, I think parrying a projectile that flies back and hits the target shooting the projectiles should stun that enemy, interrupting their current attack (making them stop shooting) and gives the player some invulnerability upon a successful parry of a projectile as to not defeat the purpose of the parry in the first place. And don't get me started on the ranged weapon. What a useless weapon, I barely found openings to use it at all and when I did use it, it was almost guaranteed to get me hit because controlling the aim while moving your character just seemed ridiculously difficult. All in all, its a great game but I wouldn't recommend it with the difficulty as is. Scourgebringer 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is categorized as a roguelite/roguelike, and it has nothing of what makes this genre fun. The short of the problem is that it has no variety of ANYTHING, and so no run feels different, unique, or memorable. TLDR: If you're interested in this game due to the roguelite/roguelike tag, I would highly recommend against getting this. I've played for an hour and a half, and after the first time clearing a floor, you will have seen every enemy variety that that level has to offer, and that's not saying much. The first boss has been the same every time. I have only been to the second level twice, and the bestiary says that I've ALREADY seen almost a third of the enemies there are in the total game. There is only one way to play: spam the slash key until the enemy has an exclamation, do the bash button, and then keep spamming while the enemy is stunned. With the game's difficulty, I've been seeing the first level quite a bit. And when there is no variety in that first level, my motivation to continue with the game has come to a screeching halt. The upgrades within the run don't add to any fun either. I have not encountered an item that adds to any uniqueness or build strategy. It's only been "increase sword damage 5%" or "increase gun damage 10%". Additionally, you pretty much need to clear the stage to get enough currently to buy a single item at the shop, and when the choices are between a different flavor of gun or a +5% increase in damage, there is not a whole lot of incentive. Just think of any other title in this genre; Hades, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, Dead Cells, RoboQuest, Risk of Rain. Each one of these has some form of character, class, or weapon selection at the beginning of the game so that, if you are feeling bored with the runs, there is something immediately to add some variety.My other biggest gripe is that there is only ONE primary weapon. There is a variety of guns, but this is sort of secondary. It's like Hyper Light Drifter, where the guns can deal more damage per second, but they have to be refilled by using the sword. That means that for 80-90% of the game, you're using the sword. And again, there is no other option of weapon. Just the sword that you spam while locked onto an enemy. Lastly, there are just some design decisions that are unfun. The recommended way to play with the gun is NOT to manual aim, but instead using the auto-aim so the game can remain fast. How I THINK this works is that it targets onto the enemy that is closest to you, even if they are behind a platform. I've had plenty of bullets wasted because the auto aim locks onto a target behind a wall rather than one that is above me but a little further away. Also, it aims directly onto the space where the enemy is in that point in time, so it is all but useless against enemies that are moving too quickly, as the bullets will trail behind them. I think this is the quickest that I've become interested in a roguelike title, and if you searching for a game from that genre, I would recommend looking elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Onces again in a post-apocalyptic world we need to save the future of humanity and discover why an alien gargantuan monolith did this whole mess to begin with.To my understanding you had been chosen to save the world, and rightfully so. If I could dash, wall run, literally jump everywhere in the air, I would also want this honor. Kyhra is a badass and makes you love controlling her. "ScourgeBringer" is a roguelike action platformer. You kill everything in a room and continue exploring the next ones. We had seen it before, but here is very stylish.   In your first attempts you will feel a little lost trying to manage all the available moves you have from the start. Eventually in time you will fly from room to room and dash your way through your enemies without even touching the floor. Feels good. The core gameplay is pure gold, but it has its hiccups. The guns don't feel so useful and taking into the account that their ammunition ends very fast, I was never a fan. This also meant the merchants who wanted to sell me guns and updates for them were pointless. Finally, and I will contradict a little what I said earlier, even if the gameplay is an excellent example of how chaotic fun can work, it is also its downfall. You need to be extra careful of how you play because you are VERY fragile. But at the same time you want to go ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and do some cool moves…only a boss beat you to a pulp, like, 34 times. Plus traps, mini bosses and even normal enemies. Maybe in a different timeline "ScourgeBringer" was a more casual action platformer game. But I digress, you will still have a great time like this as well.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for February 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before March 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A rogue-lite with a little Celeste in it. Scourgebringer is intense.  Players will get the ability to dash through the area, shoot, smash, and slash enemies over and over, and then do it again and again while fighting their way through a dangerous maze.  This is a fast-paced rogue-lite, where players have to survive to discover more about an alien artifact.  With the ability to stay airborne nearly forever, and dash up walls this feels unique, and the combat is intense but requires a lot of practice as multiple useful skills need to be combined. Sourgebringer’s one main issue is that it's rather hard, and becomes extremely so.  Of course, some players will be able to overcome almost anything that the game throws at them.  There’s also the ability to use accessibility settings to make the game easier.  Also with this being a brutal rogue-lite, it’s sometimes hard to feel that any real progress is being made, but even still it has a great opening hour and while I have struggled, it’s not put me off just yet. Pick this up if you like a real challenge, and the rogue-lite formula or you just want to play something interesting for a couple of hours.  Scourgebringer feels great for a while, but that difficulty rears its head quickly and players are going to have to master a lot of different abilities all at once to make significant progress, but I’m probably going to return and try to get farther either way. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:
