_childDocuments_.review: Put simply, this is a fast paced combat game with an emphasis on using your dash to get around. The gun is secondary to your sword, but can still be quite powerful in itself. That said, as the time of writing there are a couple problems with the movement and combat, most of which can be attributed to the games auto aim. The game will prioritize aiming at enemies over player inputs. This means that if you're trying to shoot a far enemy, even if you're pointing both sticks at it, the bullets will fire towards a closer enemy, even if it's in the opposite direction. The dash and sword attack have similar problems. The sword will always pull you towards an enemy if they are close, even if you're holding the other direction. The dash isn't nearly as bad as the gun, but there have been numerous times where I've tried to go to a specific spot, only to home in on a nearby enemy instead.The one problem that isn't related to homing is related to the smash attack, which is used to reflect enemy bullets. The smash hits a particular direction in a sort of semi-circle which can very easily be faced the wrong way. It's generally pretty consistent, but it has swung in weird directions before. Might be related to enemy homing after all. There is also a slight delay on it, which seems weird on a mechanic that is meant to be precise. It might make it difficult to use, especially if you're already used to deflecting/parrying attacks. Despite all this, the game is still fun, and despite it's problems I can recommend it. Just a few small tweaks to the homing would render most of my complaints moot, or possibly even the ability to turn of aim assist. If you're looking for a roguelike/light though, be aware that most playthroughs will play out the same way, regardless of upgrades obtained. The only variety to really be found is in the guns.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: 5/5 brawler.Overall it slightly suffers from repetition (the enemies start feeling really similar quite fast), but the gameplay feel really carries the game. To me the game became more fun as I learned how to optimally handle different enemies and enemy spawn patterns, so I guess repetition is partially a good thing in the sense of learning stuff.---A couple of design points about the game that notably affect how the game is played:- Enemies have no contact damage - they only deal damage when attacking or shooting. Most enemies clearly warn you when they're about to attack with an exclamation mark. Either be ready to avoid the shot, or stun them if you're close.- You have a stun attack with almost no cooldown, so it's possible to just stun any enemy constantly.- A single enemy is rarely an issue. You can keep (almost) any normal enemy stunned until they're dead.- Even though the game is really fast, it's much easier to handle than I expected - major part of this is the fact that you rarely need to react quickly. Most of the challenge comes from choosing which enemies to kill first, and keeping an eye on  that you aren't actively attacking.---About the rogue-lite mechanics:- As for the balancing of random drops during runs, this game belongs in the category where your personal skill is notably bigger part of your progression rather than getting lucky with drops - vast majority of equipment/drops are just small percentage bonuses, and your character's power doesn't change that much from run to run. There's a couple of nice to have upgrades, but I have never thought "oh damn I lost because I was unlucky with drops" (or vice versa).- There's also a skill tree where you can unlock passive bonuses in between runs, and some of those are quite powerful - but I'm more fine with that since it's not based on randomness. The tree isn't that big so It's quite possible that you'll unlock everything from the tree before even completing the game, so after that point it's all about just training to play better.---Additional notes about difficulty:- There's an "adaptive difficulty" setting which somehow tweaks the game to match your skills, eg. easier if you die a lot - I'm not sure about the details. Personally I turned the setting off because I'm not really a fan of the concept. I want to become better in the game instead of the game becoming easier, no matter if it takes me 2 or 50 tries. But hey it's there if you want it, having this as an option is never a bad thing.- There's a "game speed" setting in the accessibility options. This is a really great way to make the game easier to approach even if you don't want a lightning fast game - eg. with 80% speed it still feels fun to play, but also makes it a bit easier to keep up with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, challenging, and replayable. The graphics are beautiful, some incredibly fluid and incredible looking pixel art. _childDocuments_.review: Scourgebringer is an incredibly fast paced rouge-like with great freedom of movement. Its only flaw is that once you beat the game, it doesn't exactly have infinite repayable value because nothing major is going to change from run to run.In Scourgebringer, all battles take place in fairly small enclosed rooms. In these rooms anywhere from 4-8 enemies can spawn at once. You would think this would be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. After all, with so many enemies spawning in such as small enclosed space, how do you not take damage? The developers balanced this in three ways:	• Most enemies (except for the bigger ones) can die in like 1-3 hits. 	• All enemies can be stunned by using your heavy attack during the enemy's attack animation. The bigger the enemy, typically the bigger the window to stun	• When enemies spawn there's a few seconds where they won't do any attacksBy designing enemies in the above manner, the developers have essentially turned you into a predator seeking prey. You're not going to hide behind cover and slowly take down enemies while dodging their attacks (you'll get swarmed if you try). Instead, pretty much as soon as enemies spawn, you're supposed to take in your surrounding in like less than a second and seek out high priority targets one after another until everything is dead. It feels awesome >:DTo help facilitate you killing enemies as fast as possible, not only do you have your normal and heavy attacks, but you also have a dash that can basically cover half a screen. There's no cooldown on this ability, so you can constantly use this to go from one enemy to another. You can also basically stay in the air forever if you want. You also have access to a gun  that you can use in order to attack enemies at range. The ammo refills by attacking enemies with melee attacks, so while you can take down some enemies at ranged, you have to mix in melee attacks every so often. In addition, you can use the gun while at the same time using your regular attacks. So it's a great DPS boost to be in a boss's face and spam your regular attacks AND your gun at the same time. The heavy attacks can not only stun enemies, but it can be upgraded to reflect bullets. It feels very good to precisely hit bullets right as they're about to hit you and send them flying at the enemies face for major damage. Finally, you can unlock a "Dragon Punch" that makes you dash AND reflect bullets (i.e. a combination of the dash and heavy attack). This is incredibly useful, as you can reflect an entire stream of bullets back at the enemy's face. This is why it has a 2 second cooldown to balance it out (trust me, 2 seconds is a lot in this game).Not only are the enemies designed really well and you as the player have a lot of tools at your disposal to do cool ♥♥♥♥, the level design is also fantastic. Each new stage makes the game progressively harder so that you slowly master the game over time. For example, the 3rd stage has rooms where you can fall and take damage so you have to get good at staying in the air for long periods of time. The 4th stage has platforms where you can't move through but you can shoot through, encouraging you to master using your guns. The 5th and 6th stages….. are really hectic. I've beaten the entire game, and even now I find the last 2 stages incredibly difficult. The 5th stage introduces teleports all over the edges of the screen such that if you move through one side, you appear on the other side. This not only applies to you but ENEMIES as well. There were so many instances where I took damage because my brain didn't register that an enemy was attacking (since I always look near my player). The 6th stage is even more difficult making it so that there are hazards that you need to use your heavy attack in order to make them TEMPORARILY not hurt you. This involves adding these hazards near areas where you need to teleport in order to avoid taking damage. To be fair, a lot of rogue-likes make the last few stages incredibly hard so that you no longer feel like exploring every single room and instead get to the boss as fast as possible (e.g. Enter the Gungeon). So this game has excellent enemy design, level design, and you as the player can do a lot of cool ♥♥♥♥. So what's not to like? Well, the progression system. Basically, the way the progression system is designed, once you beat the game, there's not much replayability. Every roguelike has fundamentally two types of progression systems: the system within a run and the system outside a run. In this game, the progression outside the run is very well done and significantly changes the gameplay. The progression within a run however is fairly limited. While there are blessings that can be found that provide various passive boosts, you can only get 1 per floor (so 5-6 in total). These blessings are useful, but they mostly comprise of damage/loot increases. Usually nothing major. Apart from the blessings, there's not much else. You can buy guns, mods for the guns, and stat boosts. Once you unlock the ability to re-roll items, you can fairly consistently get the exact gun you want (for me it's the assault rifle) and the mods you want. The stat boosts only provide like +10% boost to damage per item so they don't dramatically change your run.Because the progression system isn't all that exciting within runs, you're quickly going to feel like you're playing the same game over and over again. It doesn't help that you will face the exact same boss and the exact same enemies in a row over and over again (i.e. there aren't alternative stages. There's only ONE stage 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6).While Scourgebringer may not have very high replayability value, the experience you get for beating the game is a great one. Pretty much all other aspects of the game are top-notch and worth experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: Crazy good roguelite.Very tight controls and movement, highly reactive and skill based combat, and straight to the point in its gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: I've never played such a satisfying game. You have so much freedom while moving and every time you're killing a bunch of enemies you feel so cool! You can even define how hard you want the game to be in the options: changing the HP drop rate, the speed of the game, the speed of the bullets the enemies fire... etc. And when you finish the last boss you unlock even more stuff to make the game harder. You're constantly able to challenge yourself more and more.It was a little bit too easy to unlock all the permanent upgrades, I was able to unlock all of them in basically 6 hours thanks to Instant Gift (why does that blessing even exist, It's legit too powerfull) Overall it's a great gameEven though it's playtime not being that big
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: I'll sing one major praise I have for the gameThe learning curve for the controls is interesting. The game starts out backbreakingly hard as you learn them, and more importantly, when to use what move when. When do you dash into enemies, when do you use the standard attack, when do you smash an enemy, or their bullets, to prevent/avoid an attack?It's a steep slope, but once you get a handle on it, the combat becomes incredibly fast paced and fluid, you feel like a machine mowing through enemies, weaving through attacks, or turning their attacks against them. There is still some jank with the controls, I'll admit. you can wallslide, which sounds good, but it'd be a lie if i didn't say a good chunk of my damage is me trying to get away from an enemy and ending up slowly sliding down a wall.Some actions auto-aim (there's a setting to change this I think) and that can always lead to something not going right. especially in levels with environmental hazardsStill, this is a fun, high skill game that keeps up the challenge and just generally feels really good to play!
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Overall recommendation: Strong recommendation!Summary: A roguelike (or is it roguelite?) game with slick movement, short levels (read: serotonin), fantastic freedom of movement, great atmosphere, and TONS of polish! I would say this is (IMO) far more fun than Dead Cells or Risk of Rain 2, but perhaps just a notch less fun than Hades, due to the lack of constant narrative progression. VERY addicting!Before I go to the pros and cons, I just want to say, BIG PROPS to the developers for polishing this game up SOOO darn much! Everything is snappy, quick, precise, and just how you want it. Bravo!Please support these devs guys!Pros:You should really go for this game if you prefer:-Fast and precise combat-Freedom of movement-Short bouts of playtime that you can fit between work sessions too!-Addicting gameplay-Fantastic art and music-Usually find roguelikes too tough! (It has an automatic adaptive difficulty setting and great accessibility options!)Bonus: The adaptive difficulty works like an absolute charm. The game never felt too difficult to do well, and never felt too easy to breeze through.Only the first level may feel easy to you since the game still has to measure your skill, but otherwise it's been adequate as heck!Again guys: Please support these developers! Wonderful game
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game plays as fast as Sonic is supposed to play. If you like hard games, pick this up. I'm not hardcore enough to 100% this game, but I was able to beat it in about 15 hours and it was a challenge the whole time. I only have a few complaints with the game overall: Some of the enemy design is repetitive, but it's different enough that it's not so noticeable across the levels. The gameplay (unless you have hold-x to attack on) is mostly mashing the x button as fast as you can while squeezing the right bumper to fly across the screen like a cannon. While that's really fun, it can start to hurt your fingers after a while. I would highly recommend using the accessibility option to hold X to attack so you can save yourself a bit of nasty RSI. My last complaint would be the lack of variety in gameplay over the course of a few runs. This game, being a rogue-lite, should offer a noticeably different style of gameplay from run to run, but it's roughly the same, albeit pretty fun, gameplay no matter what items or guns you pick up. If they added some more ways to build your character or some different "classes" I think this game would be a 10/10 in the genre. I hope we'll see more patches or perhaps some DLC for this game. Until then, I'll give it an 8/10. Thanks for reading my TED talk.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Fun action roguelite! Would recommend to anyone who likes games such as Monolith or Dead Souls. Very satisfying gameplay. Very tactile and feels wonderful to play. Would NOT recommend for someone looking to play a game for a long time -- this is a very clearly contained experience. If you're the type of person who can read a 2D room and figure out an immediate path of action, you will love this game for the few hours it gives you before the content starts becoming repetitive in a way that you don't like.Features persistent growth up until your first full clear of the game. Really lacks much in terms of growth once you've killed the fifth judge. You unlock a few extra upgrades and a Hades-esque challenge mode, but from what I've played there doesn't seem to be any extra incentive other than the fun of doing so to continue playing.There's a choice at the end of the game. There doesn't seem to be much of value to it -- it's basically just which cutscene plays at the end. Please tell me if I'm wrong -- I'd love to get more content out of this game than some vague hints about what happened before the events that take place during the game. The story of this game is a bunch of setup and intrigue but seems to have little to no delivery. Kinda disappointing in that.As for the gameplay: imagine monolith with gravity. Imagine Celeste with a sword and a gun. Very fun experience. Needs a lot more content to justify its asking price of $17 USD, though. To repeat: I love the game, but I wouldn't pay $17 for maybe 6 hours of unique content. However, I've also been playing this sort of game for upwards of a decade! Of course I'd only get six hours out of this -- I've played the games that this took inspiration from, so of course I'd not only like this, but blast through all of its substantive content.THE GIST: This game is great for newcomers who want minimal complexity from their roguelites. However, its asking price is a little steep -- I'd recommend you get it on sale unless the frankly beautiful appearance or the OSTs (feel free to listen to them -- great music!) happen to lure you in. For people who have played for a very long time, you may feel a bit disappointed, especially when its inspirations have so much more to offer for lesser or similar prices.EDIT: I was notified that there was a magic sixth world at the end of the roots. I will reach this. I will still maintain my opinion unless this opens the flood gates wide open.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little roguelike. Combat feels pretty smooth, dungeons are solid. The in-game randomness/roguelike aspects are pretty shallow, though. There are only a few pickups that really change the way you do combat ~ 90%+ of all pickups are some form of flat dps up. However, there are a lot of combat modifiers/difficulty enhancers that you can add from the menu.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: my relationship with roguelikes is contentious at best. the usual trend is that once I beat a run I've had my fill and tend to not want to play it much longer. and while that did happen again with this game, the time I spent with it was a lot more enjoyable. The combat is insanely fast paced and built around quick thinking and reaction time with a doom-esq industrial metal soundtrack that caught me by surprise the first time I heard it but was a nice compliment. However this game is not really based around build-crafting its more just based on your skill.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game with fast paced combat, character skills and progression. My favourite part and what I find the most immersive part is the METAL that starts when you get into combat. I am really liking the sound track and how it comes in at the start of combat and fades out after the last one dies. It has that fight for you life sound and beat to it. I don't know if this was their intent, but I love how you can absolutely get destroyed in the game, but you can also be like HULK fighting small insects, flying room to room.There is a lot more too it, but I still think it is  pretty standard rougelike game just with more enjoyable combat and atmosphere
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: good game.  the combat loop is absurdly good, but sometimes it feels like the items aren't impactful or interesting enough to make each run unique, so the replay value mostly comes from unlocking more upgrades and getting better at the game, which could probably be a turn-off. _childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: If you like platforming but is also a fan of hack and slash, this game is for you. If you played Celeste, Khyra is basically Madeline on crack, ectasy and a mix of the squirrel from Ice Age and a ninja. Celeste is a precison platform game, whilst ScourgeBringer is a precision hack and slash. It's an awesome game, very difficult, but also rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now, this game is waaaay too hard for me. I've bashed my head against it pretty hard, I feel like, including almost maxing the standard progression. In spite of this, the game informs me I have at least another area to go after my high water mark.That said, it's got stunning visuals, great music, and wonderful atmosphere. I wouldn't mind a tad more story and some hints as to how to handle tougher scenarios. Very mash-y, which may be a positive or negative.If I had to give a numeric score, it'd probably be a 3.5/5 from sheer tilt, but I still love it.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: it started out a lot stronger than it ends up being - which sucks but hey, thought there'd be more dialogue and story but that drops real fastit's fun- a lot of what feels like CORE mechanics to the game are locked away for the first hour or so, thoughbeautiful and fun, didn't like the rock ost so thankful you can change that i think scourgebringer doesnt really try to go out its way to be anything too new, more of a mix of games and it makes them work well .

_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible fast-paced free-moving roguelite platformer.The gameplay is fast-paced, you can even adjust the game speed if you want a faster gameplay or a slower, difficulty is adjustable too but I recommend keeping it to dynamic for the real Scourgebringer experience.Has a variety of enemies, more annoying than the others. Bosses are challenging and will beat you up if you are not careful.Music can go from a relaxing tune after you cleared a room full of enemies to a DOOM-like soundtrack when you encounter enemies in the next room.My final verdict. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great game.Almost every level requires you to adjust your playstyle, at least that's what I thought. I am glad I was wrong because this game rewards ruthless and efficient killing EVERYWHERE. Beware however that this game is quite difficult and the learning curve is a little steep for each stage. The only flaws are the lack of explanation for some in-depth mechanics, but other than that there should be no problems trying to enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions after 5 hours and 2 levels in: super fast and precise platform-action-rouge-like. And yet also tactical: You can approach each room as a hack-slash-shoot fest or you can slow down, play safer and use the environment to take enemies down one by one.Definitely a difficult game to play. Feels like there's a high skill ceiling and it's rewarding to master the skills the game wants you to develop; I was useless in the beginning but got better after a while.  At the same time, there are some accessibility options that allow you to tune the experience to your comfort level. (I haven't explored these much but they seem reasonable.)Exciting music and beautiful pixel animation and art round out the package.  I can play for 5 mins or a couple of hours, which is perfect for my schedule.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Cells meets bullet hell! In other words, think of it as a 2D platforming Hades!Much like Hades you likely won't beat the game in your first run.I'm honestly not a bullet hell God so I can't confirm that it's impossible to beat the game without a tiny bit of grinding.That said, the game feels a lot like Dark Souls in the sense that you have your parry and dodge so in theory you should be capable of beating any enemy if you have the skill. A key difference which brings it back to Hades is you have to clear rooms to progress whilst in Dark Souls and Dead Cells you can choose to skip a majority of enemies if you weren't grinding.Anyways, Dark Souls, Dead Cells, Hades, these are good games to be compared to, give this one a try and prepare to die!
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Scourgebringer is a very fun fast-paced rougelite that can't help but be difficult. I enjoy the game for its presentation and its gameplay, both of which are well done. Probably the most enjoyable part is smacking one enemy into another, especially in the third area. My two complaints, and they're both just nitpicks that can't be fixed, are that the fifth area's mechanics hurt my head too much at the moment, and that the item progression doesn't really feel like it makes much of a difference, besides health and shield pickups. Getting a damage boost doesn't really feel impactful when I still kill enemies in the same amount of sword swipes.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: It's lit!  Bad gamers use adaptive difficulty though you just gotta play for a bit and you'll pick it up quick. After a few rounds and some earned judge blood from killing elites and bosses you can upgrade your character which makes the game more fluent and in some cases easier. The gun a bit weird to implement to your gameplay if you play controller but just makes the game even more fun once you get used to it. Super fun super fast rouge lite and if you're not into metal music you can jut turn it off and play your own. Very much recommend
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: with just 1.6hrs in the game i can already see myself spending alot of time in this.mechanics are very simple, yet extremely satisfying and has a very high skill ceiling - i dont think replayability will be an issue. i will edit when i rake up 50+hrs (if i manage, if so, hello past self - you did yourself proud) but get this, if you are a fan of games like- wizards of legend (less intense)- super meat boy (with combat)- hyperlight drifer (less intense) - zero katana (closest game i can think of)- hades has a similar feel to it, with replayability and overall progression
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely my favorite roguelikes I've ever played. It feels incredibly slick once you get into it. You'll be flying through rooms and slicing up enemies like crazy. The game is definitely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ before you fill out your primary skill tree, and even after that the game is incredibly hard. _childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very worth the asking price, as it is very viable where replayability is concerned. This is one game that I feel falls under the category of Soulslike, although somewhat loosely. It is certainly one of the games that you could beat without any items or upgrades, as long as you have the necessary skill. It also has some light RPG elements, with a skill tree and a skillpoint system. Dialogue is very enticing, always leaving you wanting more, with several different NPCs that show up regularly throughout your travels, and at least one at the hubworld. The combat is very fast paced and put simply, easy to learn, difficult to master. I do feel like the difficulty in this game is a good bit higher than in other roguelikes, but that has just added to my experience. All in all, I would rate this game a solid 8.5/10. Very worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard and unforgiving. It's simple, and does what it says on the tin: it's a fast-paced roguelite set in a somewhat randomly-generated dungeon that gets more difficult as you go on.I can't help but notice that a lot of negative reviews - not all, mind you - are given by people with not much time invested into the game. Which is fair enough, but I think this game needs time to grow on you. What first appears to be a rather basic combat system slowly grows to be quite challenging, unique, and satisfying. Everything descends into a mess of hacking, slashing, &c; I'm personally not sure what's even going on half of the time, but I absolutely love it.You go from fumbling about in the first stage, getting killed by petty enemies, to flying through stage after stage, quickly understanding the layout, identifying the biggest threats, and letting loose an array of abilities to absolutely obliterate what was until recently a seemingly-unstoppable horde of monsters. But if you let your attention drop for even a second, a botched boss battle can leave you in confused tatters like you started.Does it have issues? Yes. It's a bit repetitive - not randomised enough, in my opinion - and the graphics could do with some retouching to make it easier to understand what's going on. But honestly, I've never felt like getting myself killed *wasn't* my fault, and all in all the punishing combat is just part of the fun.8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I was looking for a game similar to Celeste when I had found this. It's definitely gave me a feeling of Celeste but in a completely different manner than what I was looking for with gameplay which I absolutely loved. This game feels amazing to play with how smooth everything feels, how hectic situations can be, the soundtrack fits this game perfectly, the artstyle is absolutely fantastic. If you're looking for an a game with all the elements I stated previously and that can be insanely difficult yet so stylish, PLEASE check this out!
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Light recommendation for this rogue-lite. Has the theme of Monolith with less free movement due to the 2D-platformer approach compared to top-down comparisons like Monolith or Nuclear Throne. The combat mainly consists of smashing buttons fast enough and learning the movesets of mini bosses and bosses. However, I am hopeful for further improvements as the development team is working on updates post launch. If these improvements should fell short, the gameplay and the beautiful art style are anough for some enjoyable hours.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: ScourgeBringer, like many other games of it's kind, gives you varied selection of both movement and combat abilities. What puts it above these other games is how it manages to convince you to make the most of each of them without it feeling forced. Other games will either have enemies that can only be killed using certain abilities to make sure you're using them all or will have you fall into a loop of only using a couple of them because they're the most optimal in all situations.This coupled with the beautiful presentation makes for a damn fine game. I just wish there was more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.  I know that will make me biased, but man, I've played this a lot.  So I did have a friend get all kinds of confused and compared this to Monolith, which is also on Steam.  I mean.. I get the comparison, but to be honest, that game was more of a bullet hell the whole way through and you don't have to deal with gravity. Pros - The flow of combat is amazing and really requires you to think your attacks and movements through.The music is dynamic to when you're in combat, in a shop or just getting from place to placeThe pixel art is very well done.  It's not intricate, but not a single pixel is wastedCons - I'm not really clear on the story.  It does try to come up with some messages you find as you go through the different levels, but it doesn't come up all that muchThe modifiers that you get once you get the first true ending can be really brutal.  I have tried to have them all on.  Once.I wish there was more to do once you get through and start selecting your modifiers.  Maybe some story, additional options for where to go after beating a boss.All in all, my cons are just a wish list.  The feeling of this game is very cathartic when I'm going through the first few levels without even thinking.. just going on instinct.  If you dig this kind of game after watching some vids, go for it.  You will not regret.

_childDocuments_.review: ScourgeBringer is a game I've considered buying after falling in love with fast slice and dice action while playing Dead Cells. And I haven't been dissapointed, since this game can back up its "combination of Dead Cells and Celeste" claim. While I've never played Celeste yet, I can safely say that slice and dice and fluid motion aspects of this game much more satisfying than Dead Cells', it's like you are permanently in speed boost with further vision to play with. That's said, here are a few game aspects that you might want to consider before buying- Roguelite aspect of this game includes randomized map, shop, modifiers and stat upgrades. There are no attack/combo modifying items, items that grant defensive mechanics or resource management (besides traditional money). Despite that, this game doesn't suffer the same fate with your nostalgic favourite game which you've already memorized its map layout and enemy spawns etc.- This game highly promotes "flawless" gameplay. This was problematic for me when I was getting used to, but I got used to it by now (Probably took about 5-7 hours of gameplay). There was a "more heal drops" option that I haven't used, so consider that as well.- Game rewards fast gameplay and it is probably only fun way to play it (at least for me). Playing fast is much more dangerous though :D, so rewarding is more like a compensation for risk you took.- Game is very innovative for amount of content it has. Combat options preety much includes everything you can dream of. My favourite is smash attack, which works like casey in enter the gungeon, which doesn't require charging but has tiny lag before executing; so you have to time it well. There are 5 areas in game and last two have creative mechanics that i love and hate (because they are deadly and unfair :D)- Game took me 13 hours to beat and I died a lot during the process. Meta progression is very effective in this game. I've probably died in first area more than anywhere else. But unlocking stuff felt satisfying so no complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: It's taken us a while to decide what we wanted to say about ScourgeBringer. Our single-word review is 'promising', and while that can be a mixed compliment dependent on context, there's enough to say about the game in its current state that we think will make it easy to decide if it's up your alley.The moment-to-moment gamefeel and gameplay loop is without a doubt intoxicating. Core actions consist of dashing around from enemy to enemy, mashing on them with your sword, smashing them into walls, deflecting projectiles, and occasionally firing your gun-robot, which can take the form of anything from a simple revolver to a split-on-enemy-impact 'diffract laser', or the overpowered 'cross grenade', which, if you're enterprising, will happily carry you from run to run, at least on the lower chaos settings.In terms of 'rogue-like' depth, there isn't a lot present. Many of the upgrades you'll unlock feel like "should have been there in the first place" sort of stuff, and once you max out the tree, that's it: no cosmetics, nowhere to really 'dump' your extra currency into, save one specific in-game mechanism that doesn't necessarily 'reward' you per se. The room to room generation is random with enough variety, but enemy types per area are very samey. This can lead to developing a more intimate relationship with their tells and attack patterns, which is ultimately quite satisfying, but different perhaps than other types of more varied entries in this genre-pie. The boss for each area is the same per run, and mini-bosses are also static to an extent.We won't go into explaining each one of the game's systems in-depth here, but all-in-all, holding a controller in your hand and playing this game just feels satisfying. It doesn't suffer unduly from bloated difficulty or obtuse mechanics, there's nothing about it that needs an explanation beyond the tutorial, and if you like the look of dashing around the screen slaying dudes, this game is probably up your alley.The last thing we'll say, however, is that given our penchant for following and reviewing games in early access, it's interesting to us to identify their place along a spectrum of 'feature complete' to 'banking on future updates'. ScourgeBringer definitely falls into the latter camp: it feels like the 1.0 release was done mostly to have a finished product to sell, as opposed to being released because the game felt 'done'. There is a lot more variation that could be included and is borderline necessary/expected in this sub-genre now, especially when compared to other stand-out entries beginning to amerge alongside. When something like I, Dracula: Genesis has 400+ unique upgrades and isn't even out of EA, it can make your finished product with a paltry skill tree and no end-game besides 'increase enemy health number' feel lack-luster by comparison. This is also not to speak of the narrative aspect of the game, which is, to be generous, almost non-existent. The themes, setting, and intrigue are all there, but the in-game storytelling and dialogue is so sparse it barely serves as a coat of paint. And once you're done finding all the in-game explanatory text thingies... that's it. No more story for you.ScourgeBringer is worth a look if for nothing other than how engaging and intuitive its gamefeel can be, but hold off for a little while to scout out for further updates if you're unsure.Also, big shout outs to the game dev for being incredibly kind and responsive despite our snarky bug reports. It's probably no end of stress to troubleshoot your game days after the big launch, yet we had a soft-lock, game-ending bug fixed within 24 hours just because the dev was so on it. Big props for that.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has come a long way from Early Access. _childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: It's always a shame when you find a near perfect game but there is one or two things that take the perfection away. ScourgeBringer is one of the most skill-based, fast-paced games (if not the best in that regard) out there! If you want a combination/comparison is a mix of Celeste's visual/movement with some Doom Eternal action-esh? Double jump into the air, auto attacks will keep you floating for a good while, then you can dash in any diraction auto attack twice and your dash will be available again, resulting in a perma flying and dashing state. Combo that with your Power attack that interrupts enemies, knocks them away AND deflecting projectiles. While all that sounds insane, you don't actually have i-frames in your base kit so timing is king. The game plays well both with a controller and with keyboard-IF- you play with the keybinds a bit.Music is great, visuals are GREAT, story is... there... and yeah the game is HARD.So what makes it not perfect? As with most roguelites, there is both a permanent upgrade tree and run based upgrades. The tree is slowly adding more awesome mechanics to combat as well as other utilities but run based upgrades are lacking. If you ever played downwell or monolith, (which seems to get a lot of inspiration of) you will know that these upgrades are not a highlight of these games. The other issue I have is how the ranged combat works. You have an amazing melee game with great mobility and you top it with this ranged weapon mechanic where your magazine is small and only recharges with you auto attacking enemies, making the weapon very unreliable in combat. It's just there to compliment the rest of the combat, maybe taking the flyers or adding burst but it still feels out of place, adding that many upgrades or even ranged new weapons exist in the game, I am sure the whole mechanic could be removed and the game would be almost the same. Ofcourse my time with Scourgebringer is not very long so I may always change my opinion when I get deeper and further into the game, as is standard with roguelikes. Now if you like fast based combat and roguelikes, I don't think there is a better in that regard.No, Hades is amazing because it ticks all of the boxes but pure combat wise Scourgebringer is easily the best roguelike yet, it may not stand in time, I don't know, but I am looking forward to finding out because I am not planning of stopping any time soon.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: A rogue-like action platformer where you earn progress between raids to level up your character, but you need to complete the game with one life. Has similar feature to Dead Cells, but different enough to warrant a buy. Tons of fun to create new combos out of the moves you unlock to make the levels easier.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on game play up to 3rd boss.I highly recommend this game if you enjoy a rogue type game with "flow". There is a pattern with timing of the mobs and their skills, and every boss and mini-boss requires a maneuver (or set of maneuvers) to defeat unscathed. Controls are epic in that you can perform a dash through the air from target to target. Auto-aim is great for the melee and ranged weapon, so controls feel extremely tight and responsive.Levels are challenging and dying will happen often. The currency for purchasing skills is hard to come by at first and gets progressively easier. * Whenever you reach a Blood Altar and it offers the reward for "judge based on progress", you'll want that. I have earned up to 28 judge for grabbing this item once, and helps to build out the tree.I am currently playing on Steam, Xbox pass on PC and Console for the achievements, and for the enjoyment of the game. I give it a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly a gem, dashing around at high speed and slashing up your enemies is incredibly satisfying. i've been around almost since the game's conception and it's only been getting better and better as time goes on, refining gameplay, and the Devs even added options to ensure that the game is accessible to everyone, with an adaptable difficulty coming soon at the time of writing this review. it's always fun diving into the ScourgeBringer and experiencing the world with it's amazing art, and intricate lore. i'd highly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of roguelites, and i'd further encourage you to join the discord, it's a wonderful place with wonderful people, and the dev team even join in on the shenanigans from time to time.p.s. there's a secret gun that shoots pizza in the game :)
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't give it long enough. I will again in the future. I have recently fallen in love with both roguelike and roguelites. This does fit the bill, but I felt a distinct lack of replay value at the moment. I have to note though that I never made it very far. But the entire time the combat felt same-same. Other games feel like they require massive differences in strategy where this felt like it required changes to target priority. Still, I like it and will get it when it's on deep-sale in the future. Just for now, it's not for me (but it might be for you, and I don't want to dis what's clearly a decent game)
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: If Hyper Light Drifter was a rogue-lite. I love it! It's a neat little bundle of action and precise controlling with a dash of bullet-hell.I see some complaints about this game being "messy."It's only messy when you're flailing at the beginning of the game. Over time, you have to learn how to use each of your tools and also when to go in and when to avoid. Learning timing and tactics is very important in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Game is extremely good.  It is very difficult and has permadeath so if either of those are not for you then neither is the game.  It took me about 17 hours to get good enough for a 5 biome clear.  Controls feel very nice and although it might feel like you can't control the character at first, with time you will understand how the "unpredictable" movement works.My only criticisms are the meta progress and the repetitiveness.  As others have said the progress tree contains upgrades fundamental to playing the game, such that until you get certain things (fury, combo, smash repel) you aren't even playing the game.  There is no reason to gate basic moves like this.  As for repetitiveness, this has been addressed a bit with full release with the gun mod system; not everything feels identical.  But even so, from run to run you are playing the same way, fighting the same bosses (with the exception of the minis), and progressing along the exact same path.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this for a while now, on and off. It's a rogue-like and it's difficult but it's possible, it's got that level of difficulty where it feels great to manage to beat a boss or a level. The graphics are the cutest and oh boyyy this game runs so smooth on my mac that I wonder how much the programmers have slept, if ever.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely fun and addicting indie game that really gets you into the "just one more run" mentality. The combat feels fluid, with its mix between hack and slash, bulletstorm, and platformer meshing to make some lovely gameplay. I only wish that the guns could have more use than just extra damage which is what I mainly use them for, as some enemies are immune to bullets.The difficulty is good, as it always feels fair but is still quite a challenge. I'm writing this review after finally beating the "final" boss so it took me quite a few attempts. That being said, I'm not amazing at this game so I think most people will be able to complete it with enough effort as you gradually improve each run.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Exhilarating fast-paced hack & shoot platformer roguelight with different weapons & persistent upgrade tree.Can be difficult at first but once you get familiar with the different enemies & little combos it's smooth sailing from there.Also has some option to make it more easy or hard like "more / less HP drops", "slower / faster enemy speed" or "slower /faster bullet speed" to tailor it more to your desired level.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: First, hats off to the EULA. I wish there were more like this.Second, the game is tough. Fast-paced and unforgiving, as most of the current trend of rogue-like is.But it's quite fun still. It's fluid and I like the style.And even as the game rewards playing fast and risky, you don't have to let yourself swept in that pace though. You can play a little slower. Be careful and patient. This makes the game just a little easier.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: With only a few hours clocked I can safely say this is one of the best rogue-lites to come out as of 2020, and will probably go down as one of the greats if it stays supported. The movement and combat feels extremely fluid and you never really feel like your character is going somewhere you don't want them to. This makes the fights with even the most basic enemies very engaging, especially because the combat is very hyper-active in this game. The boss fights are pretty well laid out as well, with clearly defined attacks that you can dodge if you know how to react, but are still fast enough to require good reaction time. The game also works on a die-to-progress model with judge blood being used to further equip yourself for future runs, and more npc interactions unlocking with more repeats.I can safely recommend this game to anyone who even moderately enjoys the rogue-lite genre.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: As a kid who grew up playing Super Metroid and Megaman X+Zero.This scratches that twitchy rushdown wall clinging, air dashing, bullet deflecting, itch like no other game I've played.Controls are TIGHT. This is high risk, high reward, twitchy combat.Somewhere between Dead Cells and Megaman Zero.Absolutely worth the 20bux I paid.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just awesome.Sort of a strange Metroid / Hollow Knight style universe with a possibly darker story and undertones.Metroidvania or classic ninja platformer inspired combat, similar to old games like Strider, Ninja Gaiden on your reflexes for some intense stuff or even more modern game like The Messenger with similar action.  You get multidirectional dashing, a slash charged gun sort of like Hyper LIght Drifter, etc.Artwork and stuff aside, its a bit more arcade felt than a metroidvania though, and its randomy powerups and mazed levels give it enough to be a roguelite in that respect.  In the 80s it could have been dreamed up as a vector art asteroids + pong + metroid + rogue combo, and that is good stuff.Only downside so far is with the default controls, I remapped them more to my liking for a metroid style platforming game... also the default slash attack lures you into overusing it at first, it is a good attack and such, but has weaknesses, it might be better to map it to a secondary emergency attack and get used to timing the smash attack and dash especially after you get the unlock that deflects shots like a Jedi from Star Wars.Don't be fooled by its seemingly short level design that you see at first, there is a lot here, in an arcade format and you are best comparing it to something like a high score attack arcade platformer, closest thing on steam for difficulty in what I mean is probably Super House of Dead Ninjas... but this game is much cooler.
_childDocuments_.name: ScourgeBringer

_childDocuments_.review: Fast and furious. This is a really cool game. I was looking for a contemporary interpretation of Megaman Zero and this game, while actually very different from MZ, scratches my itch for slash-and-shoot 2d combat. The biggest difference between those games is that in Scourgebringer you are floating and dashing through the air most of the time. You have a few different slashes and projectile weapons at your disposal, which are a blast to use. The game locks you in a room with a few enemies and you have to fight your way through them, then proceed to the next room. This bite-sized style of gameplay really appeals to me, as the repetition allows you to quickly learn how to deal with the various enemy groups. It is a bit frustrating at first that when you die you return to the beginning of the game, but you get used to it and eventually it feels right. Aesthetically, this game is at the top of its class with stylish graphics, a tasteful amount of gamepad rumble if you're into that, and a kickass soundtrack. I think that you get a lot for what you pay, even if the game is still under development. I do think that this game has limited replay value because there is only one difficulty and a limited amount of content, so once you get good it loses some of its appeal. Overall though I would highly recommend Scourgebringer.

_childDocuments_.review: First time ever review (no spoilers) on any game on Steam! I had to get it out there for ScourageBringer!Just beat the game for the first time on the Old World update, and I have to say this was one of the most satisfying rogue-like action games I've ever played. There's a huge learning curve (this game is definitely not easy) especially if you're new to action platformers...but oh man once you get the hang of deflecting bullets, stunning, timing for all enemy moves, and dashing all over the screen while oblitherating everything in your path...it's such a satisfying feeling - it makes you feel like (excuse my otaku) captain Levi from Attack on Titan or something.The enemy bullet speeds and actions are perfectly timed to give you just enough room to react. I love the exclamation marks before the enemy unleashes their attack along with the choice NOT to include touch-damage...it really ads to the godlike feeling you get when you clump all of them up to finish them off. One thing that's unique is the fact that you flutter in the air when you slash in which you potentially never have to touch the ground in a room...it makes you feel like you're constantly "juggling" in a fighting game which is super satisfying..and happens in every room. The mechanics are super tight and feel just right for what the game wants you to feel like. No I-frame dashing like in so many other games which is makes it very unique - you're nearly forced to be attacking and killing enemies as fast as possible for most rooms. Lastly, the bosses are also just about right in difficulty - nearly all attacks are fair to dodge and the game gives you enough options to deal with each boss move.Time for the cons:I'd say this game is first and foremost an action hack-n-slash/platformer(?). As a rogue-like, the game unfortunately does not feel varied from run to run with the upgrades and gun choices. There's no "build" to go during your runs...you often just pick the upgrades and unlock that you need (rather than want) at the time. I really missed that feeling of creating a build to add more variety in each run like in the case of Hades and all the Slay the Spire copies. The permanent upgrades are mostly shallow passive effects aside from a few key unlocks that really add super fun mechanics to the action. I often find myself hoping to roll the one-time full-heal alter upgrade if I've made too many mistakes in a realm, find a bigger potion in shop, or find a select few guns that don't suck as much. You don't FEEL the impact of other upgrades. Or rather...there's not a heavy emphasis on decision-making like other popular rogue-likes. Again, that could purely be a design choice or something they're working very on as we speak. Perhaps the creators don't want the problem of "op builds", and want you to always feel like Captain Levi in every run which I can understand. Lastly, there's not much of a story element but honestly that doesn't matter too much...don't need a story to complicate what this game is trying to achieve.All-in-all, this game is super polished and gives you a feeling like no other. Graphics are super stylish and colorful, you can feel the theme in each environment/boss, and music adds to that Captain Levi feeling while you're flying through the screen. I feel like my reaction speed has increased by at least 15% playing this for about 15 hours. I don't quite want to give this game a score just yet as it's still early on. Thanks for reading this far in - I encourage you to give ScourageBringer a try...if you're up for a satisfyingly difficult challenge ;)

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 EDIT as of getting the true ending:ScourgeBringer is a stylish and interesting romp through a world-destroying interdimensional structure. It boasts an incredibly flashy combat system, gorgeous art, good music, and some serious drawbacks that hamper its flow.(-) Cons:---MAJOR CON 1: The movement controls and physics simply aren't designed to keep up with the difficulty curve later in the game. They are imprecise compared to area hazards and many projectiles. The dash, the auto-aim attacks, the jump height, all put you in more danger than they should in the latest floors.---MAJOR CON 2: Minibosses spawn adds. I personally always hate this mechanic so it's a bit more subjective, but the guardians (which you have to beat all of on a floor, and there are more of them per floor as you progress) feel like the devs thought minibosses needed to be propped up with artificial difficulty, and enemies that don't match their theme. The increasing numbers self-balance imo, without the new enemies.---MAJOR CON 3: Dragon Punch, an extremely powerful and versatile late-game ability that partially makes up for the janky parry mechanic, requires a frame-perfect input to use. No input buffering makes it unreliable and will regularly cause you frustration.- Lack of variety: 1.0 made this a ton better. There is a reasonable assortment of weapons included, but the mods for them, the blessings you can get for yourself are less punchy. Plus, with how necessary and straightforward it is to get a high tier gun, you wont be experiencing too much variety regardless. Expect to wield about 1-3 weapons on average.(+) Pros:+ScourgeBringer offers numerous accessibility options beyond auto-slash, up to and including complete invulnerability: a setting which makes for great fun, relaxation, and practice. It is sorely needed in other games, especially roguelites. I recommend playing with extra HP drops, which seems to level the playing field a bit when you're taking cheap damage on the 5th floor and other late-game content.+As stated, visuals are great and pixel art is slick. Enemies' stun animations are very satisfying.+Music is great; very doom-adjacent but does eventually get a tad repetitive.+Combat (for the most part) is extremely fast, which is a double-edged sword but when you're lucky, it looks great and is pretty satisfying to watch everything blow up.Summary:How do I recommend ScourgeBringer with all those complaints and massive drawbacks that make me feel more relieved to be finished with one true ending and uninterested in getting others? The game itself is solid and made with love. The devs are sweet people, and they did create a fun product. I think that SB cuts into its own flow in some places, but it is worth the price and does unique things, if you really like challenging and somewhat arcade-y slash-and-dash.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a fantastic synergy between the freedom of movement, dashing for positioning, rapid slashing for damage, the soul-satisfying reflect, ping-pong/stunning smash, and more. The game is a joy to watch and listen to, but it’s even more of a thrill to play. ScourgeBringer boasts what is less of a “2D platformer moveset” and more of an “on-your-toes problem-solving system”.I may not be that consistent at the game yet, but there's a really tangible learning and improving experience to be found here. In many fast-paced rogue-y games, I typically find myself mentally advancing at a poor rate or running into big skill-walls, so it was an unexpected pleasure to find myself consistently catching on to patterns, making plans, and wanting more. Also engaging is how the game’s roguelite upgrades provide new and impactful gameplay elements whose true value is derived by your application of them.For EA feedback, I've encountered some pretty unbalanced runs. In one run there'll be near-instant access to the boss, shop, and pedestal while other runs will require going through a long chain of chambers to exit the realm. Otherwise, I've clearly been enjoying ScourgeBringer in its current state and can't wait to see what the game's future brings.

_childDocuments_.review: my first review of this game was when i played it back in May, back then it was too difficult for me and felt like it lacked enough variation for me to put the time into getting past the (imo) high difficulty wall. Having gone back to it a few updates later when its in full release? I have to say my opinions have greatly changed. The drop rate of items per room, variation in abilities (with higher tier ones no longer being fully locked off for progressions sake) and items have all increased (the settings even have an option to make health drops more common!). The addition of an enemy beastiary, more lore, increased forgiveness of each level and addition of optional challenge rooms and unlocking of the abilities tree all add up to a great experience. Im actually able to consistently get passed the 1st area as opposed to how i fared my first run around. While I know im not the best at video games and my sour reception to the early build was most likely a partial result of that, the full release has made the game so much more enjoyable for me. Im glad to have bought it back then to support this kind of growth and its only fair of me to leave a review reflecting that change of quality.TLDR: the game is much more forgiving, diverse, and fun than it used to be back in much earlier versions. I recommend it to anyone who likes fast paced hack & slash, roguelite gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This game is friggin' dope. When I first saw this game I was intrigued, but skeptic. I think most can attest to regretting an early access purchase once or twice, so I was wary to commit, even at a discount. Then I noticed, perusing Xbox Game Pass for PC that it was included. I figured, 'why the heck not, it's basically free,' and started playing it. Got about ~45 minutes into playing it, quit out of Xbox, booted up Steam and purchased it at full price, (which is a reasonable price, even for just the content available right now, with more to come. ScourgeBringer is a joy to play. The movement and combat is extremely solid, simple, and fluid. Knowing nothing going into this, each upgrade you can acquire on the Chiming Tree adds a new layer of control and complexity. Eurogamer's description of ScourgeBringer being "Celeste meets Dead Cells," is spot on. It combines the simple to learn, difficult to master controls of Celeste and gives you free reign to use your surroundings, and even other enemies, against not only room to room enemies, but even bosses. While I would like to add my concerns or issues, I haven't had any, in the short amount I've played. Menuing is easy and cohesive, the game itself runs great and has been perfectly stable. I imagine that when I can complete a game like this, being very mediocre at roguelikes/lites and platformers, that it may not be difficult enough for some people's preferences, but it's very well balanced and will only continue to get better. Correction, just skimming through the updates I noticed the last projected update does have a Hard Mode, they're already two-steps ahead. All in all, whether you buy it on Steam, sale or not, try it on Xbox Game Pass, or find it elsewhere, this is a game that definitely deserves the support. The developers seem to be super open to feedback and have been hitting their update schedule consistently, so I have no doubt this will only continue to get better and better and is already an instant favorite of mine.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this review by giving a general overview of what this game has to offer:Gameplay is very fluid and controls are responsive, this aspect feels very polished and is what i expect the most from in the future. Variety when it comes to combat options is lacking but that can be ignored given the fact that 1. It's an early access game and 2. It's a fast-paced roguelite: having too many elements to consider can become a hinder in this type of games. Enemy variety is wonderful and very well done, as well as boss fights design.Current score: 7/10Pixel graphics are usually the way to go with this kind of games, and here they're very well executed. No complaints whatsoever. Color palettes for each biome and the whole gritty, opressive feel they give are in tune with the game's lore.Current score: (Consider it's pixel art) 10/10Characters (what little interactions you have with them) feel like a natural part of the world, which is something hard to achieve. Lore isn't really very developed, or it wasn't during the hour I played. My guess is that it might be added in the future or be only a background element. Not a big deal. Kinda cliché but meh, probably not the focus of any players interested in roguelites. Feels like a part of HLD's universe tho, which is a nice little nod to that game.Current score: 5/10Metalheads rejoice. The rest of you plebs might just have to deal with it. If you don't like the soundtrack you can kill the music and play your own tho, not a big deal. My only complaint with it is that the music feels like part of a different, more brutal game. Sound effects for actions and interactions are fine.Current score: 8/10With that said, I've played a lot of roguelike games up until now, and this one doesn't really offer anything the rest of them don't already. I read somewhere that this is what comes from combining Celeste and Dead Cells. My take on that is that this games feels like a very simple version of Dead Cells. On the other hand, the mobility is great and forcing the player to master it as the only way to avoid damage is wonderful, given the fact that you lack a dodge move, so devs play on the game's strengths by doing this.Is it enough to keep me interested? Sadly it isn't. I will give this game a positive review and keep it in my library in hopes that it will help the devs polish their game and achieve their vision. I believe this game can be wonderful and a work of art, since it already is a labour of love.Review might change in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Full game is out, old review is old. As of now, Scourgebringer channels all the best parts of traditional arcade games, and is quite fun to pick up every once in a while for a few runs. Doesn't really have the capacity for depth and constant replays like some sandbox-heavier roguelites have (this is less Enter the Gungeon/Binding of Isaac and more... I dunno, like, a mobile game, if mobile games were good. Not exactly right, but you get the idea.) Runs get repetitive fast, with the main variety being in guns (which all generally end up doing the same thing in different ways) and upgrades (which are fairly minimal - they're not bad, they just mostly work in ways that only minimally alter the moment to moment gameplay) but said moment to moment gameplay is quite good. It doesn't always feel as fair as I'd like in it's style of roguelite, but runs are short enough that I'm never too terribly bothered by the occasionally spotty attack telegraphing.Scourgebringer isn't really the kind of game that will give you a whole 2+ weeks of focused gameplay - it'll burn out fast if you play it that hard with anything other than the particular, slightly mad focus of speedrunners and the like, but the simplicity makes it easy to come back to after not playing, even for months.This is a good game, but... It's not yet worth the price. Yet. It's early access, there's plenty of things planed to be added, but, well... I'd say this is maybe a $7 game right now. I beat the current final boss in 2 hours, and that's just way too fast for a $15 dollar roguelite. Keep an eye on it, cause it's a very fun game, but if you buy it right now, it's more an investment than a purchase at this stage in the game.tl,dr: Very good core, but needs way more content to be worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: my go-to for early access games is to play long enough to determine if I'm going to play more at release or not, offer whatever feedback I come up with and then back off until the full release.This game is a "once it's done I'm 100% in" kind of thing.Movement feels amazing. Style through the roof. I saw "Celeste + Dead Cells" but I get serious Cave Story vibes from some of the enemy design, too, in a good way.The flip side of the absurdly responsive movement (Some games have double jumps. This game laughs at the concept of merely "double" jumping!) is that to make it not hilariously easy, your dash doesn't have invulnerability. That's gonna be the hardest thing to get used to, I think, and genuinely surprised me. _childDocuments_.review: For perspective, my favorite games of all time are some combination of Dead Cells, Wizard of Legend, Binding of Issac, and Enter the Gungeon. If you're anything like me, THIS GAME IS DOOOOOPE, and is a fresh take on the rogue-like action platformer. The focus is on movement and melee action, but unlike say, dead cells, you can "juggle" infinitely via your sword and dashes, but you've got a gun that you can use after charging it up. The downside, in my opinion, is repetition. The game takes place in a series of similar looking rooms with similar enemies, and although getting through these rooms is an absolute blast every time, if exploration and variety are your thing...you might want to wait. The good news is, as the game is still in quite early access, there's time to improve these things, and the recently released roadmap gives me confidence that this is going to be the case. So, if you're a fan of the genre, and the trailer looks good, buy it now. If you're on the fence, wait till the first big patch, and then buy it. Either way...buy it :-)

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Extremely tight, fast-paced gameplay that makes you feel cool when you play well.The game seems to be inspired by a lot of great indie games, beyond just the 2 that the devs explicitly mention in the description. The rogue-lite structure and overall visual design are reminiscent of Monolith. The ebb and flow between gun and sword combat (along with stuff like slashing bullets to deflect them) is similar to Hyper Light Drifter. The platforming and aerial combat remind me of Dustforce, surprisingly; never thought I'd get a Dustforce roguelite. Whether any of these games are actual inspirations or merely coincidental comparisons, I cannot say. Regardless, I hope these comparisons paint a better picture of how the game actually plays than simply calling it "Dead Cells + Celeste." It is a unique mixture of elements from many different games that ends of making it more than the sum of its parts.One complaint I have that does not pertain to the game's current length or difficulty (which will inevitably be improved upon when more levels are added) is the music. The music for each level is good, but I never get to actually listen to more than a few seconds of it at a time because it gets interrupted by the battle music. Battles are so frequent that the constant starting and stopping of the battle music gets fairly annoying. I suggest only playing the battle theme during the miniboss and keep the regular level music for the basic encounters. This would allow the regular music to shine more as well as make it easier for the player to go into a "flow" state, as discordant music is distracting.As for additions, I would personally love to see gameplay modifiers be added. They're a quick and easy way to make the game more replayable and potentially more challenging. For instance, a modifier that put spike traps on all floor tiles would take the "floor is lava" concept to the extreme, only allowing players to stand around for a brief moment before getting skewered. For the most hardcore players, a 1 HP modifier would make it so a single hit from an enemy would end the game. Lots of contemporary rogue-lites have this feature, so it would be great to see it here as well.I look forward to seeing what the game will be like when it is feature complete.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game but in early access.  Ignoring any criticism that they have planned on their roadmap, I think the game needs to rework its talent system. _childDocuments_.review: RELEASE UPDATE:So many changes. The core gameplay is still there, and it's great. They removed a few OP things but added in loads more.I've finally "beaten" the game since restarting my save for release.I'll be brutally honest here, this isn't the kind of rogue-y-ish game that has loads of variety. There aren't crazy items that combine in crazy ways to make runs interesting. The legs for this game rely mainly on your enjoyment of the combat loop. I love it, and now I have access to loads of difficulty modifiers to challenge myself with (after you beat it once). I'm pumped, and I will probably play this game for many more hours.If you want strong meta-progression like Rogue Legacy, you won't find it here either. You aren't really playing until you unlock most of the skill tree. The process of unlocking it is a bit of a tutorial, as it slowly introduces new moves and very lightly powers you up. You can also disable these at will for taste or challenge.It was long ago, but I remember my first tentative steps into the world of Scourgebringer. It was brutal. My time with it has paid off and I can now pull off sick moves and smash enemies harder, faster, better, stronger.Oh, I described this game to someone as "a top-down game with gravity". That might be a tip? The ground is for suckers. Stay fly.-----UPDATE:You might be able to tell from my hours, I like this game. It's great.They've release several updates since my original review. They are few and far between, but the quality is off the charts.The last two updates have added two new worlds that are so inventive and cool looking, filled with new enemies and completely new mechanics.This latest update has made some serious changes to the random generation of enemy waves and made the game better. It's harder, there are more enemies, the in-run economy has been improved.The fifth world is insane. I was having a good run, but this last world is a complete game-changer. It destroyed me. It's a bit trippy and takes the excellent mechanics of the game and turns it up to 11.I'm so excited for Flying Oak Games. You guys did a great job. One of the better Early Access experiences I've had.-----First things first, the game feels great. It's a blast. I love it. I would heartily recommend it.You have a double jump, you can run up walls, and 4 main moves. Sword slash, sword smash, dash, and shoot. Sounds basic, but what makes it interesting is that sword slashes keep you in the air, so you can basically stay up there as long as you want. Dash is great for closing distance, dodging, etc. The smash stuns enemies and sends them flying. If you smash them when they have a ! over their head, you get an extra strong stun and prevent them from unleashing a powerful attack that usually sends something deadly your way. Shooting is great for extra dps (you can slash and shoot at the same time!). You can take out enemies from range, but I don't use it for that purpose very often.The controls feel pretty good, but take a bit of getting used to. I started out using a d-pad, but I found analog to be superior option since it gives you greater control of your dashing and slashing.The game is filling out quite nicely. There are now 5 levels, each with unique enemies, sub-boss, and main boss. In addition to the new visuals, there are often new mechanics as well. You go room by room slashing, smashing, and dashing through enemies and being an all-around badass. Sometimes you get drops that give health or upgrade stats (ranged/melee damage, more pew pew, etc). There is also a shop and upgrade room on each level to give you some extra options to power up. The upgrades range from more passive boosts to more impactful abilities that can change the way you play.You collect a resource that you can use between runs to purchase passive boosts/skills.  Unlocking the passive boosts felt pretty quick once you start to get better at the game. I've amassed a fortune of currency, so I can unlock all of the new skills as they're released, so I'm not sure how a new player would fare. The new update has also added the ability to disable the skills/boosts if you'd like.The updates have brought more of all the good stuff, tightened up the game systems, and it feels pretty great now.The main course has arrived and it is delicious. And, there is still more to come.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone with well over 500 hours in roguelikes across the board, this one was a satisfying first for me. Where most games make use of fast movement and tight levels by applying bullet hell ideas, this game honestly is fairly tame as far as hectic enemies go. The far greater issue you run into is getting to each enemy in a timely manner to stun them and stop them from attacking you.The combat is EXCEPTIONAL. Easy to pickup, satisfying as hell, but it takes some effort to start getting perfect at it.Now, as I write this in Feb. 2020, I blew through the game in 117 minutes. I actually could've gotten a refund. But I didn't, as I'm SO excited for whatever they release next. And, I'm still working on 2 achievements.Phenomenal game, the music is great, and it's nice to have a roguelike that goes back to a persistent upgrade system rather than "RNG decides you can win this run from good items".Gameplay 8/10 - Reflecting bullets is weird because your character kinda moves forward when activating Smash. I'd take points off for lack of content BUT, it's EA, so I can't fault them. Boss fights are also difficult when your dash homes in on the enemy that's attacking you, but you need to dash to avoid the attack.OST 7/10 - Wonderful music, but not quite as amazing as say Crypt of the Necrodancer or Nuclear Throne. I could see some people getting tired of the battle music.Leveling 7/10 - Not a whole lot of thought put into it, you just kinda upgrade whatever you can next. But, it's nice to go to a persistent upgrade deck after all the other roguelikes abandoned that and went RNG-loot.Overall, easy 4/5 game, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: ScourgeBringer is a dynamic and challenging experience that immediately gives you the freedom to move swiftly and easily through its beautiful environments. You can double jump, walk up walls, dash an unlimited number of times, and swing your sword rapidly with no cooldown. Dashing through enemies restores your double jump. Swinging your sword rapidly slows your movement in midair, which gives you the ability to hover. You can also halt your movement with a smash attack, which stuns enemies/projectiles and send them flying. All of these abilities put together allow for very fast-paced action that feels smooth, controlled, unconstrained. Simply put, it's extremely fun to move around in the environments and to fight through the enemies that are thrown your way by the game.If you play this game, you can expect to face a large quantity of enemies that you fight in confined spaces. Most rooms contain two waves of enemies, and there is a small chance to receive an item after fighting them. Items, level design, permanent upgrades, and temporary powerups bring some strategy and decision-making to the game in a way that is interesting to explore.I highly recommend this game for someone that enjoys the thrill of tough, limited-health combat; and staring at beautiful pixels.
