_childDocuments_.review: Throughout a lot of my childhood and teen years, I never really got into 2D games. I was introduced to a lot of first-person and third-person shooters as a kid, so a lot of my interests were tailored towards that. As of recent, though, I’ve spent a lot more time branching out, and 2D games are a part of that. Most recently, that’s included Fez and Enter the Gungeon (which was a blast…I’m sorry). I was a little skeptical going into ScourgeBringer, though, as it wasn’t a game that piqued my interest at first. After spending several hours working through the game, though, I’m happy to say that I was completely wrong.In case you haven’t already heard of ScourgeBringer, it’s a 2D action roguelike published by Dear Villagers. They’re best known for games like Edge of Eternity, Hover, and A Normal Lost Phone. You take on the role of Kyhra in a post-apocalyptic landscape. A mysterious entity has wrecked the lands and as the deadliest warrior in your clan, it’s your job to stop it. You’ll travel to many different worlds and fight increasingly engaging enemies, using your quick thinking to approach each room.Speaking of worlds, the game has done well at creating a distinction between the current three lands. Not only are there unique, well-designed pixel art backgrounds, but there’s also music and enemy types to accompany that. It makes you feel like you’re in a completely different area, crafted with a lot of love and polish. Whoever was behind the art and sound of this game show that they have a lot of passion for their work, and deserve a lot of credit.There are a few things I wish were added in that department, though, which I’ll quickly go over. For one, there should be a lot more room designs when the game leaves Early Access. What they have is good, but to build upon that would go a long way. The backgrounds should change more as well, as having similar ones on the same world gets a little repetitive. Not something you’re going to notice much as a player, but it would go that extra mile.Despite how well designed ScourgeBringer’s atmosphere is, though, the gameplay is where things begin to shine. The attacks on the surface are quite basic, with only a few moves that you can do. What makes it more interesting is the combos you can pull off and the skills that enhance your attacks. You can combo together different attacks with your gun, do combo attacks to get more blood (money), and many more. It opens up a lot of room for creativity, especially given the skills and passives you can acquire.The great enemy designs improve this. A significant amount of the enemies feel threatening, forcing you to have to think quickly if you are to pass a room. The enemies also differ a lot from world to world, getting more difficult as you progress. Given the number of games I’ve played with an unfortunate difficulty curve, it was nice seeing it done successfully. You’ll approach each world with no knowledge of the enemies and not a lot of skills, but as you play, you learn their patterns and get the upgrades to deal with them correctly. It’s a gameplay loop that I never felt got old despite how tough enemies looked at the start.I’d be lying if I said there weren’t a few criticisms I had for gameplay, though. Some enemies, for example, never really seem to pose a threat to you. Throughout the ten hours, I played of the game, a couple of enemies only ever hit me three or four times. I understand that some need to be easy to kill to be extra income for the player, but I should know what their attacks are. Thankfully this was primarily in the first area and didn’t persist in the other two areas, but it’s still somewhere that I feel should be looked at.Outside of the enemies, there’s also the amount of content that is somewhat low. There’s currently only three worlds and a handful of different guns & Gifts of Blood (passives). This got me through nine hours, which isn’t bad for a $15 game, but it would be nice to see more. Thankfully though, double the content has been promised in about six to eight months with the full release. I’m personally excited about the content and will be returning to see what’s improved.Finally, I’d like to touch on ScourgeBringer’s options menu. This game does a pretty fair amount in terms of options, including a pretty unique piece on the difficulty. Instead of having your usual difficulty settings of Easy, Medium, and Hard, you can change the game speed. By default, it’s on 100%, which was used for this review, but you can turn it down if things feel too fast or your reaction timing is on the lower end. I doubt many players will use this, but it’s useful for those that want it for sure. Overall, no outstanding issues with the options.Score: 8/10Thank you to Dear Villagers and Flying Oak Games for providing a review copy. _childDocuments_.review: Although still in early access, this game is fantastic!  The controls are nice, crisp and responsive, and gameplay as a whole is awesome.  This game seems to be a mixture of Dead Cells (Combat) and Celeste (Movement/artstyle) with a dash of Risk of Rain (items dropping from enemies and cleared rooms).  The enemies can be a little repetitive, but each new realm (think floor) brings a new set of enemies and tactics that need learning.  Pros:- Responsive controls that leave room for learning and adaptation.  New players are able to conform controls to their liking in the options menu- A diversity of enemies.  A little repetitive (as mentioned above) but there are new ones to discover!- You can teleport to a previously cleared room via the map tab.  This makes traveling a bit less tedious.- Fast-paced combat and ruthless Judges (boss-tier enemies) make one's heart pound and blood pressure soar as you hack and slash your way thru roomsCons:-Judges can be absolutely ruthless to beginners (except for candlemask.  Candlemask is a pushover).  It took me maybe 5 tries before I could clear the Bodybuilder, and even then it is still difficult to kill.- There is very little diversity in the items you can get from rooms and the shop.  I hope that more will be added in later updates.- It is quite difficult to heal, which is a slight turnoff to me, but I can look past it easilyThis is my first rougelite ever played, and I must say it is a smashing introduction to the genre.  I look forward to playing more like Scourgebringer in the future!  One thing I would love to see is a zen/endless mode, where instead of trying to get to the next realm, you just keep on going in an already discovered realm."Raze Hell, raise rebellion"

_childDocuments_.review: Very very cool so far! Movement is tight as ♥♥♥♥ and it's very fun to keep combos going with the combat system being just as fluid but simple to grasp as the movement. Also digging the unlock trees and gun variety that really change the way you're playing run to run, even if it's not as crazy as some other games of the same breed (yet?). _childDocuments_.review: When I first reviewed the game it had just started early access and now that it is out I can say that the devs did not disappoint. More levels, more guns and more stuff in general was added. Plus the devs are amazing and took player feedback from the discord and are still active on there. Overall, my feelings of the game are the same if not better. It is one of the best feeling roguelikes I have ever played. The movement and combat is just god-like. It's kind of like celeste mixed with mercenary from risk of rain. You get to use this movement by moving through different realms that all have their own feeling. They each have specific gameplay mechanics, like teleporters or blocks that bullets go through. Paired with this is some truly amazing pixel art and music. The art is extremely clean and leads to some very unique enemies and the music is just breathtaking. I would describe it as like the DOOM 2016 soundtrack but more "pixel-arty." It has a little more synth and there is some more ambiance. Both this ambiance and the combat tunes completely slap. The only negatives for the game are a lack of replayability. You won't be playing for 100's of hours to unlock everything because there isn't too much to unlock but you will want to replay it for the juicy combat. Overall, I do hope the devs continue to add to the game, but if they don't that is ok. It is a complete package that any roguelike fan should pick up.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really comment on the late game or even the midgame, because I just haven't climbed that mountain yet. What I can tell you is that this game's combat really shines. It's tight, responsive, skill-based, unique, fast-paced action. Character builds will be mainly comprised of straight power-ups rather than strategic tradeoffs, but you can also swap out your gun, and there are some items that incentive playing in different ways (example: "Floor Is Lava" increases your damage by 10% for each enemy killed since the last time you touched the ground). And the game's rocking soundtrack also deserves a shout-out.My only complaint at the moment is the limited selection of minibosses and floor bosses. When I say "limited selection" I mean there isn't any selection; each floor's boss and miniboss will be the same each time. Looking forward to more variety being added later.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid, fast paste rougelike. I don't mind repetive gameplay as long as it's good repetive gameplay, which this game provides. The only "real" problem I have right now with this game is strange choice in what abilities are on the tree, rather then being basic mechanic of the game. We really don't need to have an upgrade that allows us to fast travel or deflect bullets - it seems to be natural fit for the game. Why would you make that an ability. Not to mention bullet deflection was ability I got after an hour or so, thinking the entire time that there just isn't bullet defletion at all. It's kinda silly as it makes boss battles that much easier - one attack of the first boss is nearly impossible to dodge without this ability and rather easy to dodge with it. I love to see how the game develops, right now it's about 7/10 without taking into consideration that it's early access and give or take 9/10 taking that into consideration. What I love the most is that game punishes playing safe by making enemies attacking you more often when you are not hitting them, not to mention that you relay on your smash to stun them when the time is right.

detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Buzz 'In general, apart from the traditional hunt for optional Steam achievements, the completion of Mutropolis takes about nine hours - a period by no means a record, but the impression of the game is extremely pleasant, as one of the best adventure games that have appeared in recent years.' 100/100 - itc.ua, Ukraine 'Mutropolis is a game with stunning art direction and challenging puzzles that is certainly a good choice for all fans of point-and-click and logic games, as well as a creative story that combines innovative concepts.' 92/100 - , Brazil 'As you probably guessed, my rating for this game will be high. And it will be quite deserved, because it's just a very good production. So if you like the atmosphere in the style of 'Stargate' (mainly film), interesting puzzles, good humor, finding references to pop culture works and a good audio - visual setting, this title is for you. I heartily recommend.' 9/10 - forum.przygodomania.pl, Poland ''Mutropolis' offers us eight to ten hours of gameplay in a lovingly created world inhabited by unique and charming characters. The classic point-and-click has a wonderful balance between story and puzzles and really won me over after a short time. It's tricky and challenging, but not impossible to solve. It is hard for me to avoid spoliers this time, as there are so many nice and funny moments that make the game really good for me and that I just want to share. 'Mutropolis' is quiet and comical rather than action packed and more detective game than Indiana Jones story. It really manages to surprise and delight with good ideas. Definitely already a small adventure highlight for me this year.' 87/100 - Adventurecorner.de, Germany About the Game A lovely SCI-FI detective point&click adventure - 10-15 hours play time It is the year 5000, and the greatest achievements in human history are forgotten. The pyramids, the Mona Lisa, The Fresh Prince of Bel Air – forgotten. Forgotten by everyone except Henry Dijon and his ragtag team of archaeologists. They left Mars to dig up lost treasures on the wild and inhospitable Planet Earth. Life is sweet, until Henry’s professor is kidnapped, and thing start to get... weird. Join Henry on a freewheeling adventure through the ruins of our civilization. Ask questions like, “Who was this Sony Walkman? And where did he walk?” Unearth extraordinary relics, rescue Professor Totel, and be the first to enter the legendary city of Mutropolis. One more thing - the gods of ancient Egypt are real and they’re trying to destroy humanity. - Have fun! Features 50+ hand-drawn scenes, crammed with cute, weird characters. Full voice over in English, text localizations in Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese, Korean and Japanese. Archaeological puzzles with a sci-fi twist. TONS OF LOVE! About Pirita Studio MUTROPOLIS is the debut adventure game from Madrid-based artists Beatriz Gascón and Juan Pablo González. As Pirita Studio, they've crafted a game full of adorable animation and hand-drawn wonderment. Henry's adventure combines old-school point & clickery with a fun, modern interface.

short_description: MUTROPOLIS is a lovely sci-fi adventure set on the abandoned Planet Earth. Play as Henry Dijon (hero, nerd, detective) in search of a legendary lost city. Uncover weird ancient artifacts. And PLEASE don’t get obliterated by an ageless evil. You’ve been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since the cataclysm, three thousand years ago, Earth has been uninhabitable. The survivors moved to Mars to start a new colony. The year is now 5000 and a small team of archaeologists, geologists and scientists return to Earth to catalogue the mysteries of the lost world.You play as Henry Dijon, a nerdy ginger archeologist who soon turns detective after his professor is kidnapped by an unknown supernatural assailant.I really enjoyed Mutropolis.It contains some wonderful characters and character development. There are your heroes, your villains, and your classic case of redemption. Each character has a distinctive personality and they’re all nicely animated. It’s easy to like them and care about their predicaments.The whole experience is very light-hearted and has a rich vein of humour running throughout. I very rarely laugh out loud at point and click adventures (mostly I just tear my hair out) but Mutropolis was genuinely funny and had some original comedy that constantly amused me. The use of comedy surrounding every day objects and scenarios we are familiar with was genius. Comments like “The plastic coating is unmistakable. Nobody knows what they did but they were considered very important.” When looking at a picture of a twenty first century bank note. There are a ton of jokes due to miscomprehensions and they mostly hit the bullseye. I thought the story was mediocre. It felt over familiar in a lot of places, but the characters, the environments and the puzzles felt original and they alone will drag you through. I was more than happy to spend time in Mutropolis, and spent extra time gaining the achievements.The puzzles in the main were logical but ever so original. Solving puzzles felt rewarding because they were quite intricate with lots of different parts. I spent a lot of time moving around areas, talking to characters, trying to reveal that extra branch of narrative that would nudge me along. Sometimes, it was because I missed an item and sometimes it was because I just hadn’t thought it through enough. I had to consult walkthroughs about three times. I was impressed by the puzzles overall. My only criticism is that objects of interest cannot be highlighted using the space bar. Usually that would not bother me but there are a couple of deviously hidden objects that you will need to interact with. The artwork in the game can confuse you and objects that you think are decoration actually play a part in the puzzle.The game looks gorgeous with a lovely art style. Everything is bold, beautiful and bright. There are quite a few locations to visit and every area feels distinct and varied. The characters are drawn very nicely and ooze personality just from the way they look.At first, I thought the voice acting sounded a bit odd but I soon warmed to its charms and really enjoyed the different character’s voices. It sounded professional and the ensemble of actors did an excellent job of breathing life into their personalities. There are some nice achievements to earn which is always welcomed.There are three acts. Gameplay will take you anywhere from nine to fifteen hours without guides. It took me eighteen hours to complete to one hundred percent. Act one is short and acts two and three are long. You control Henry Dijon, a nerdy archaeologist looking for his professor who was kidnapped by an unknown assailant. You are aided by a couple of techno nerds, a hard as nails combat vegetarian and a naive secretary fresh out of archaeological school. There are plenty of other characters to meet in your adventure. Not so many that they are insignificant, but just enough to feel attached and interested in their plights.The game follows the usual rules but there isn’t a lot of silly inventory combos like some adventures. You do need to combine items occasionally but it usually feels sensible and logical. The inventory GUI is easy to use. Whenever, I got stuck and thought I had tried everything, the answer was acceptable considering the verbal hints or visual clues around me. It is quite a difficult game however, and some of the solutions are quite intricate and do require you to pay attention to conversations and your surroundings.Examining and reading everything is quite important even if you don’t think so at the time. The game never swamps you in needless items to examine however. Almost everything has a purpose even if it is only to fill in the back story or provide a subtle clue.There is fast tracking through doors with a double click. Henry walks very fast anyway and screens are very rarely extended and are easy to traverse.Unfortunately, there is no option to turn highlighting objects on or off. This did stump me a couple of times with objects that I just didn’t see. An option to highlight meaningful objects would have solved this. I applaud the devs for introducing a bottomless pit of save slots to use. There is nothing more annoying than a miserly amount. Perfect for achievement hunters to mop up any achievements left over afterwards. Beautiful environments, well designed characters and an overall colourful and bold aesthetic made this game a pleasure to play. The subtitles were easy to read and can be skipped with the mouse button if required.Voice acting was very good and full of emotion and character. I didn’t spot a dev or family member in there at all.Special effects were good and the background tune wasn’t annoying like some games of this genre can be.Curator Info:

_childDocuments_.review: It looks like Application Systems Heidlberg wants to become the new LucasArts. After the really good Unforseen Incidents, Nelly Cootalot: The Fowl Fleet and Lamplight City they just released another fantastic point and click adventure with all the markings of a LucasArts classic - Mutropolis. I didn't have the game on my radar, so I was hit completely by surprise when it released a few days ago. And what a nice surprise it was! Is it a masterpiece? Yes, absolutely (for fans of the genre). It is a polished point and click adventure, with mostly object-orientated puzzles and multiple-choice dialogues. It uses its own distinctive visual style (reminds me a bit of Broken Age) and plays like a charm.The game is set around 3,000 years in the future, when humankind has long left the Earth to live on Mars and now sends archeologists back for research. You are a member of a small team of nerdy university archeologists working in a cave on Earth, when you discover something and the head of the expedition goes missing. Maybe there is SOMETHING on the Earth, not only old artefacts...The characters in the game are all quite loveable, even the ones that are not so nice. There is no real violence in the game, but many funny remarks and observations. While jokes about how the archeologists imagine and interpret the use of things they found are to be expected in this scenario, many other jokes are completely unexpected and would have been good in any scenario. The writing generally is above average and made me smile quite a few times.The game is fully voiced, can be saved anytime, loading times are short, ultrawidescreen is supported. There are no options when you click on an item, so you don't have to chose between look at/use/take... the game just picks the most obvious choice. The puzzles still don't solve themselves alone, so while this reduces your available options it doesn't make the game easier than its genre peers. The inventory can be acessed with the mouse wheel, quite convenient.Charming point and click adventure in the tradition of the old Lucas Arts classics.

_childDocuments_.review: is a lovely point & click adventure that stands out through its top-notch graphics, voice acting and humour. It’s a fantastic love letter to the old-school titles of this genre, while keeping things fresh through a unique, modern and gripping story.After a cataclysm that happened 3000 years ago, humanity fled to Mars. Now, in year 5000, a team of archeologists and scientists came back to Earth to find the legendary Mutropolis - a lost city believed to be a source of many treasures, similar to El Dorado or what was once believed to be the Atlantis continent. You play as Henry Dijon - the head of expeditions for team Sigma - a nerdy archeologist with a detective nose. When the team’s boss disappears, and when the police abruptly closes the case, Henry and his colleagues take upon themselves to find their missing boss and the lost city. Together with the quirky and charismatic characters that comprise Henry’s ragtag team, you’re in for an adventure in which new meets old, and where ancient Egyptian myths are brought to life. Literally.A lot of point and click games suffer from the "What do I do next? / Where do I go next?" syndrome and sadly  didn't manage to solve these issues either. The game does not hold your hand, and the dialogues with the NPCs or the text prompts when investigating an object rarely push you in the right direction. There are very few hints for what your next actions should be, and the clues for solving the puzzles are pretty well hidden. Playing  is like having to build a 1000-pieces jigsaw puzzle: you can partially combine some of the pieces that seem to fit together but you won't have an overview of what's going on until the end of each chapter (which takes a few hours of gameplay). There are too many locations simultaneously open for exploration, too many items in your inventory that don't have an immediate purpose. Brute forcing your way is also not the right approach, since the possibilities are too many. In that regard,  is aimed towards more experienced players of the genre, ones that are nostalgic of old point and click games that made you work hard for your next step. Perhaps this approach is less fitting for the new generation of gamers, which are rather impatient and for which walkthroughs are only a one click away. This doesn't mean that  is a bad game - it's actually very far from that. It's a great game, but a difficult one and if you want to play it without external help, you will need to arm yourself with a lot of patience and time. Also expect some mind-boggling solutions for some of the puzzles. The dialogues are very fun and witty, and like in any other point & click game you'll have some dialogue options that give you game progress, while others are present only for the purpose of character development or shaping their personality. These two types are extremely well balanced; unlike in some other games, where you can get lost in a ton of useless information, in  they're straight to the point while also giving you enough details about the character's background to make them likable and friendly. You'll end up wanting to talk to them not because the options are there for you to pick, but because you will genuinely want to get to know them better, to get to hear what hilarious things they come up with or listen to them banter at each other - so do yourself a favor and talk to everyone as much as possible. On top of that, all the lines are voiced and the voice overs are stellar, full of charm and emotion.  is, in my opinion, well worth its asking price of $20 for fans of this genre (but not only), and it’s aimed in particular at those that enjoy a challenge or are nostalgic of old-school point & click adventures. You’ll get 10-15h of an exciting narrative with a sci-fi / mystery thematic, exquisite voice-overs and graphics in what is ultimately a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made point & click adventure game with a unique story and lots of puzzles.You are an archaeologist in the distant future. Humanity left earth millenia ago and visits mostly for studying the past. The game starts on an archaeological dig back on earth but your studies are cut short when something unexpected happens. Back on Mars you and your colleagues do everything you can to get back to Earth and find out what happened. Mutropolis does almost everything right. The storyline is interesting, lots of subtle humour mixed in, lots of quirky characters, and the puzzles are just phenomenal. Sure, there's the usual "find stuff and then find a use for it" but there is also a good amount of unique puzzle designs to keep it interesting. Large parts of the story is somewhat non-linear, which means that you can work on different puzzles at the same time and focus on a different problem when you get temporarily stuck. My only (minor) criticism is in the later part of the game. You get a map so that you can fast travel to places of interests. That's perfect! But, to identify these places you have to pixel hunt the map first, and for every place that you check out there's a short animation, which drags it out quite a bit. There are also a couple of puzzles where you have to figure out a sequence of actions to perform to solve it and you have to start from the beginning each time you fail. It wasn't exactly that these puzzles were bad but that they ruined the pacing a bit. But overall, it's a fantastic game with a decent length (15 hrs to solve for me) and you shouldn't miss it! Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the year 5000 and you're back on a post-apocalyptic Earth, after humanity left for Mars thousands of years ago. As an archaeologist, you want to recover knowledge about the Earth that has been lost in all that time. One day, during an excavation, you and your colleagues come across a clue to Mutropolis, a lost legendary city. However, because of this find, trouble is just around the corner. Suddenly, a colleague of yours is kidnapped and from now on, you're on a rescue mission to save him.This setting is a great foundation for a bunch of funny references to our current era and the game offers some really good jokes due to this. But apart from good jokes, it also covers all the other things you want in this genre. These include tough puzzles, quirky characters, hand-drawn graphics, a nice voice-over and a slightly cheesy but overall good story.To sum up, I can recommend Mutropolis to all point-and-click adventure fans and anyone else who is interested. Only consider the difficulty of the puzzles if you're a newcomer to the genre.And as a last bit of info: This game also runs perfectly on Linux. Thanks for the excellent native Linux version Pirita Studio and Application Systems Heidelberg.Played with Manjaro Linux (Kernel 5.11.16, Mesa 21.0.2) on an AMD Ryzen 1700 @ 4GHz, an AMD RX 5700 XT and 16GB RAM.

_childDocuments_.review: and my twitch I was very excited for Mutropolis, as the setting and the premise sounded great, and while it's a decent adventure game it brings in all the issues the genre has had for the last years. 👍 +Great voice acting.+The humor was good and it made me laugh quite a few times. +Cool art style.👎-A lot of illogical puzzles, where you have to guess. -The story starts great, ends poorly. You play as Henry, "the head of archaeologists", in the year 5000, where most people, I assume, live on Mars, because Earth suffered some form of Cataclysm? many years ago. You return to Earth to search for the lost city of Mutropolis with his band of fellow archaeologists. Things go bad and one of your members gets kidnapped and you're tasked with finding him. The story starts intriguingly enough at first but as you reach the final chapter and see the ending it all falls quickly. A sci-fi, post-apocalyptic potential gets wasted with nonsense mythical Egyptian Gods with powers and they never even bother to explain or point out how ridiculous it is. I mean, sure, it's a fantasy game, people can always go wild with the themes, but it did not blend well at all in Mutropolis. The characters you meet are at least entertaining and will carry the entire story or journey. As for Mutropolis itself, its discovery was weak and gave me a sour taste in my mouth. So much they could've gone with the story but alas, it felt pointless. At least the jokes were funny. Story rating: 6.5/10Point and click adventure games are without a doubt an underrated and a wasted potential in modern times. I love the genre and I'll never stop playing it but every single indie developer goes the same route, same mistakes, and never even at least try to push the genre forward. There are so many amazing indie developers out there who I've seen going forward and making new stuff out of old quite a few times but p&c adventure game devs? F' that, we'll just hope nostalgia and boomers will be enough to buy our classics. I'm ranting too much but the genre is not getting too much attention and it will die out soon. You can do better for point-and-click games. If you managed to go through my rant, yes Mutropolis is just like any other recent adventure game released on Steam. It comes with references, illogical puzzles that are impossible to figure out unless you just guess randomly, pixel hunting which is always bad, and nothing else that will set it apart. I love the genre but it's boring me and I'm getting tired of it. Chapter 2 was a huge mess of guesses and misdirections but at least Chapter 3 redeems most of it. If you never played such a game, the short version is, you scan around with your mouse each screen you visit, and click on them, and then you have to combine objects you find to solve your way towards the objective. Half the time feels logical, other times you'll bash your head at why the hell a monkey would be strong enough to smash a screwdriver or figuring out the password to a computer based on some pictures with no given indication. It made sense once you guessed it because it is what made her happy but how would you even reach that conclusion? What if the password was made out of things she was not happy? What if it was chronologically based on? There are never hints or subtle dialogues for a lot if not all dumb puzzles so you just have to guess the developers logic instead of creating creative and mind-teasing puzzles that are well connected with one another. I could go on another 10 pages about some of the puzzle solutions but why bother. Next game, do better. Gameplay rating: 6/10Finally, I can talk about some good things, the voices. They're great and the voice actors did a pretty good job carrying the weak story and gameplay. I laughed quite a lot of times at some of their interactions and moments and it's what kept me going. The music was fine, nothing really stood out but nothing to complain and as for all the sound effects, same thing. Audio rating: 8/10Artistically the game looks unique and I enjoyed its art style. While the backgrounds are not the most detailed they do a decent job at creating the universe they wanted to. Character models look weird but in a good way, though Henry's pose was kinda stupid and the only character that would have his legs stay in a triangle position as if someone just placed something in his butt.As for bug and performance you can certainly expect a flawless experience. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 7.5/10If you're a big point-and-click adventure fan like myself, I'd say get the game and support the devs, they need it. If you're not into this, then I doubt Mutropolis will change your mind about the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The first months of 2021 turned out to be very productive for the adventure genre. Here you have the incredibly stylish «TOHU», the nice cyberpunk «Encodya», the fun «Henry Mosse and the Wormhole Conspiracy», and the very strange but mesmerizing «DOM RUSALOK». And now comes the new adventure "Mutropolis", promising us a great time to explore the lost cities of the earth. Did the game cope with this task? Definitely yes! The adventures of the Martians who arrived on Earth, which survived a huge cataclysm thousands of years ago, are filled to the brim with great humor, unexpected discoveries and positive energy. In its mood, the game reminded me a lot of "Gibbous - A Cthulhu Adventure", with such a reckless and daring mood that permeates every game scene. The characters are extremely charming in their infantilism, the story, albeit strange, but involves the player in itself very easily and naturally, you are interested in how it will end.Yes, the game did not know how to avoid things typical for the genre, so several times we will again have to deal with the moon logic of using objects, having absolutely no idea what to do next. There is no task log and tips here, so you will have to overcome these difficulties solely on your own. I am glad that there are few such places, but in general, the game is quite slender in its consistency. Locations are very tightly intertwined with each other, so even when there are many of them, it is difficult for you to get lost and forget your goal. I would like to note the very healthy and thoughtful humor that accompanies the adventures of the heroes, it is clear that the creators know how to joke without using dirty tricks. This is expressed even in small things that are not always noticeable at first glance, but involuntarily make you smile (which is only the spontaneity of the eavesdropping Egyptian goddess, constantly appearing in the frame, as soon as you start talking about her with other characters).«Mutropolis» is a very cute and fun game that is well aware of its strengths and diligently disguises its weaknesses. It was a very pleasant experience to be in it, this adventure will be remembered for me from the best side.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished Mutropolis, and I loved it.Mutropolis is a an extremely funny game, but it's organically funny, and manages to keep you laughing without being over-reliant on jokes or references.  I'm not even sure it's intended to be a full-on comedy, but it's a very humorous game.  In this traditional point and click adventure set in the far future, humanity has died out on earth but is thriving on Mars.  You are a Martian archaeologist on a team that explores earth, looking for old artifacts of humanity and making (tremendously inaccurate) assumptions about what life used to be like.  The team leader is obsessed with finding a legendary lost city called Mutropolis, and as he gets closer to his goal, he is mysteriously kidnapped.  The team ultimately decides to set out to find and rescue the professor, and there's a bunch of unlikely allies and strange antagonists along the way.In the game's first major set-piece, you scour the futuristic university to gather the materials for your expedition.  There are a number of long and complex puzzle chains here.  The puzzles are fair, but also quite challenging.  If you are not a fan of classic adventure puzzles, this might not be the game for you.  If you are, however, you will find that Mutropolis has some of the most interesting classic adventure puzzles in recent memory.  As a fair warning, you will probably get stuck in places, and may have to put the game down and come back to it and think of different approaches to the problems it presents.The game becomes arguably easier and more streamlined in the second half, when you undertake your rescue operation.  Here, you explore old Earth ruins and meet long-forgotten Earth natives as you attempt to locate and gain access to the lost city.The entire game is very polished, from the art and animation to the vocal performances and puzzle design.  The game's characters were interesting, from the strangely sympathetic antagonist, Cobra, to the oddly alluring goddess, Isis.  The actors turned in terrific performances, as well - In particular, it was a real treat to hear Sally Beaumont as both Carlotta and Ra; I am a fan of hers from other projects, and she hits it out of the park again with a humor in her performance that feels effortless.Publisher Application Systems, while they are not a huge publisher, undeniably has a knack for finding and putting out high quality adventure titles.  In the past few years, they have published some of my favorite adventures from Lamplight City and Unforseen Incidents, to Nelly Cootalot and Luna.  If you have also played and enjoyed any of these other games, I would definitely recommend Mutropolis.  Perhaps, in the year 5000, after the cataclysm, when archaeologists come to Earth from Mars and dig this catalog out of the ashes, these independent adventure games will finally go on to become mega-best-sellers and will finally find the throngs of adoring fans that they really deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: Mutropolis is fine. It's a point and click adventure game. The graphics are acceptable. The music is unobtrusive. The voice acting is good enough for what the actors had to go on. The problem is that the script and the storyline in general doesn't give them much.It seems like a really rich and exciting concept - a distant future where archaeologists dig up what's left of present-day Earth - but the setting is never really explored in a meaningful way. The running joke is that the archaeologists are all idiots and come to absurdly incorrect conclusions about their history, despite having perfectly well-preserved artifacts and plenty of contextual information to go on. It's not funny, it just makes the characters look stupid. The puzzles are also of the "fetch 27 things to mix together to create this one thing that you need to pass an arbitrary barrier" type, made even more ridiculous by the fact that most of the characters could resolve the problem with other tools and means already available to them. I know it's an adventure game and you need to accept adventure game logic to have fun, but this one really stretches it.It stretches it, but it doesn't break. Because aside from the really stupid characters and unfunny dialog and busywork puzzling, it's also not unpleasant. None of the jokes are actively offensive. The puzzles are busywork, but they're also familiar and not unduly irritating. Remembering patterns, trying to catch hints in dialog, finding the usual silly objects to combine to create another thing, it's all there. Definitely not a classic, nor a game i would recommend to anyone but the most hardcore adventure fans, but if you are an adventure gamer, pickings are slim, and Mutropolis passes the time well enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Why are there not more games like this?  This is a warm, positive game that still provides excitement and adventure, and stands out against the backdrop of the many dystopian point/click adventure games that clog the Steam store.  I live in a country with raging income inequality, a self-serving and ineffectual government, and a steadily decreasing quality of life.  Why would I want to be reminded of this during my playtime?I suspect conceptual development of dystopias is cheap and easy -- just take the the current crappiness trends of the real world and run with them, and so meet the much lower bar for credibility that comes with having a bleaker setting.  The Apocalypse comes with built-in drama. Being bright and positive risks being saccharine and dull, which seems far more damning that being bleak, and god knows such games that are cute and anodyne are bleak and dreary in their own way. These developers have taken the risks of attempting warmth, kind humor, and positive characters, and have come up with a lovely game in all aspects: as an adventure, as a narrative, as clever puzzles woven into the narrative, and as a collection of characters you grow fond of as the game progresses.  It's gently but intelligently humorous, and the intelligence is gratifying without any sense of showing off.  The art  is decorative but supports the narrative appropriately without getting in the way.  My whole family happily played it together, and we're sad it's done.  We hope for a sequel.  We finished last week and I miss it already.

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Some titles have demos that allow us to have an opening window for a story that the producers are trying to tell in a short time. This is precisely what happened with me and Mutropolis. My first contact with this title was at Gamescom last year (2020).Mutropolis is a point & click story with sci-fi outlines, presented by the Spanish studio Pirita Studio and with the finger of Application Systems Heidelberg as a publisher.It is a premise already seen, but what distinguishes Mutropolis from the other titles?Well, all its environment and characters have a very peculiar touch since they are all drawn by hand. It has more than 50 different backgrounds, between different locations. Attached to this, all the characters have voice acting. Well… not all, since some communicate in a different way. Some still communicate in a very old way… by emojis. Yes, yes, the emojis that we all use on our mobile phones. But how so? It is important to note that the whole story is set in a very distant future in the year 5000, where the population is already quite well based on the surface of Mars.The player will play the role of Henry Dijon, and many of the players have undoubtedly seen his personality represented in this character. Anyone who doesn’t call himself Geek should throw the first trowel!Henry is part of a team of archaeologists looking for the lost city of Mutropolis. Many believe that it is a legend and that no one will ever find it. The adventure quickly presents an outline of investigation and intrigue.This is where the player comes into action. At the base of operations where the entire group is in the search of the lost city. After the completion of the first pair of investigations, it is possible to open a mysterious door that gives access to a giant mural where it can be read “Mutropolis”. Everyone is in shock! Did they find the lost land?It is then, that at that very moment, Henri’s teacher is kidnapped.There are then two unanswered questions. Where is Totel? And where is the entrance to the city? This is the premise of the whole adventure that unfolds a little slowly. Although the story is quite interesting and has kept me motivated to finish it, the puzzles and research side of it are sometimes quite boring, breaking all the flow that the resolution of the previous puzzle has had in the player.It is quite common for the player to feel lost in this game genre, but in this case, it is noticeable that this feeling has been exposed to a higher level. It would be interesting to have some kind of “help” button, just to give some little hints for where to go or where to look.As mentioned, all characters have voice acting which makes everything more interesting, since it is possible to create some kind of relationship with the characters themselves and better understand their intentions. Not everything is as it seems and maybe some team members are not quite what they seem. In other words, they may not have the best of intentions.It is hilarious to perceive the connection between this group and their speeches. Now and then I was laughing at certain jokes. It’s what makes having the same joke level as an empty bottle of water … It’s not for everyone, but for those who like this is gold.The story is continued and told through chapters. However, it is possible to go back to a previous chapter if you have previously saved it. To proceed to the next chapter it is, as expected, necessary to solve the main puzzle which is divided into smaller puzzles. In general, there are no secondary puzzles, just small notes where it is possible to get achievements. Even these can be somewhat unexpected, so it is important to explore each nook and click on all the places where it is possible to do so.Mutropolis has an interesting story and captivating characters who, through funny lines, manage to connect the story points. The problem is in fact in breaking all the moments of fun through puzzles and small notes that can often escape the player. It is suitable for players who are more passionate about this type of research, who can tolerate a great deal of frustration, missing points, and moments lost between walking back and forth between different locations.

_childDocuments_.review: Want more Indie Gems? Visit my Group: Mutropolis is a Sci-Fi Point&Click that takes place in a far future. So far that even Dwayne THE ROCK Johnson is long forgotten. The story unfolds around a group of archaeologists who travel to earth in order to find remnants of our present civilization. And so, we accompany Henry Dijon and his team of brave scientists searching for relics of an ancient time and especially for the legendary city Mutropolis. Unfortunately, Prof. Totel gets kidnapped and so the team must go find him, fighting back wicked enemies and Egyptian gods. On their way, they must solve puzzles and make their way to the lost city Mutropolis.Mutropolis is beautifully hand-drawn, with futuristic environments in shiny colors and stylized humans. Every figure comes to live with simple mimics and thorough but economical animations. That is not meant in a negative but in a positive way, most of the reduced mimic is overtaken by the speakers who bring every talk to life. Mutropolis bribes with its charming humor that is never too much. The game is packed with ironic references to our present world, all regarded through the eyes of a future archaeologist. Whoever takes his time to look at every detail is rewarded with many little treasures. But not enough with that, every scene brings new twists, creative ideas and thrilling developments to the story that is gaining traction towards the grand finale. Depending on skill and diligence, the game takes between 8 and 12 hours. Thanks to the charming look and the clever puzzle design it is quickly becoming addictive. The story starts off innocent: Henry is searching for his missing prehistoric tool and has to reconstruct the “crime” by examining the “witnesses” and the “suspects”. Later the complexity is increasing. For example, a real crime scene must be investigated in search of useful hints that could lead to the whereabout of the missing professor. In the case of this game “creative puzzle” means nothing less than logic and coherent. Typical fetch quests are rare, instead multi-stage puzzles require a bit of thinking and combination; and of course, the most important thing for scientists: research. Information needs to be found in the same way as items. And there are multiple of these puzzles that often run parallel, so it is important to keep the goals in mind. That can get out of hand, and a helping system is completely absent, but all the more rewarding is finally solving a puzzle and making progress. There is a sweet spot in these kinds of point&click games, giving a challenge but at the same time not asking too much of the players patience, and Mutropolis is hitting bull’s eye. The hints are subtle enough to be helpful but not in-your-face. A side-effect of all this is that you have to run around a lot, and thanks to smooth transitions and Henrys decent speed that is not too tiring. For impatient player it may still not be recommended but let me repeat that there is no puzzle that cannot be solved by pure thinking, although trial and error can help a lot in the beginning. Still, there was no puzzle that didn’t require at least some time of pondering. Besides, Mutropolis avoids all the cliches many genre colleagues are coming across. For example, Henry is no naïve idiot but a nerdy scientist who has something to tell of everything you may encounter. A good use of anecdotes is combining them to a harmonious picture of the character. And these characters are part of a world building which hosts a story organically and where obstacles are not existing to annoy you but because you are not yet ready to go on. Sounds simple, but everybody knows Relaxo, and does that feel good to you? See!Henrys scientistic spirit lets you see the world through his eyes. To find out which pieces of a mummy are really part of the find, he needs the help of a mummy researcher who does not just pop out of the void but who is already part of the game. In every corner you can feel the love and the dedication Pirita Studio put into this little piece of art. With a lot of esprit and mind it addresses eye and brain at the same time. Last but not least, the soundtrack is a perfect fit as well as the synchro I addressed earlier. It is melodic and skillfully used, in calm places it is absent to leave some space for the atmospheric background noises and the overall scenery. Pirita Studio created a game that makes me think about the fate of my trash can as well as about the remnants of our civilization. The more impressive to know that the team behind consists of two people. Even though some hints would have been helpful to cross some brain-racking points, I had a fun time to explore a detailed world and to experience a funny and smart story. Absolutely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This was pretty good through Act 2.  Kind of tedious overall.  Way too much slow moving dialogue that wasn't all that interesting.  All the main characters are pretty boring and some of the more minor side characters are pretty annoying.  But good puzzles and reasonable flow to the story.  Kind of a 3 star effort through Act 2.  But towards the end of Act 2 a character is introduced that is so incredibly idiotic and takes the whole, up to that point, sort of realistic sci fi world and story in a completely silly and just kind of idiotic direction.  It's so dumb that at first I was convinced this new character couldn't really be who she claimed to be and was in some sort of disguise that would be soon uncovered.  But no.  The silliness just gets much worse in really bad Act 3.  The interactions with this new main-ish character are consistently painful -- bad dialogue, too much dialogue, too much slow moving animation around the screen, bad voice acting.  And the puzzles in Act 3 overall get more moon logicky and random, as the whole story just gets dumber until the ridiculous conclusion.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an exceptional Adventure! A must play for all Point n Click Adventure fans.I first heard about the game 2 weeks before the release and I fell in love with the art style and what the game promised through the Trailer. As a huge Point n Click Adventure Game fan I always look for these type of games and Mutropolis definitely delivered. At first the game might look a bit unfinished due to the chosen art style but as you keep playing it will be obvious that it was intended by the developers and in the end I actually got to love the aesthetic of the game.The puzzles are very well done with different levels of complexity that managed to get me stuck a few times but only because I was not thinking outside of the box. _childDocuments_.review: Such a fun little game. I especially enjoyed the clever, very funny writing and the characters. The first two chapters were the best, but for the last two I felt they were in a rush to finish. _childDocuments_.review: Charming. It has all the things that make for a good point-and-click: likeable characters, interesting and funny narrative, intriguing setting. Despite the superficial differences, Mutropolis has a lot in common with the Monkey island series. One complaint is that some counter-intuitive puzzles leave you stuck and having to turn to external walkthroughs. The characters don't even hint at a possible clue. This is a recurring flaw in the genre which you'd think they'd have learned to avoid by now.

_childDocuments_.review: Mutropolis needs more love. The game was entertaining, funny, original, and immersive. It almost felt like I wasn't playing a game despite some ridiculousness to the story. I loved all the characters, even the villains. It was funny how they viewed our present in the future when they didn't have the necessary context. I didn't know what Mutropolis would be, but I wasn't disappointed. It fits right into the game. They also did a great job of making you question the characters' motives.Most of the puzzles had just the right difficulty, but two at the end, I would never know what to do if I didn't have a walkthrough. These would be the third trial puzzle and whatever you were supposed to do with Max.I highly recommend the game. Just remember to bring your trusty trowel and possibly a bird suit.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great point and click adventure game.  The story was top notch.  The voice acting was really good.  The characters were charming.  There was a humor, but it wasn't forced like some point and click games try to just cram references and puns and are trying way too hard and it falls flat.  This one was funny without trying so the humor felt natural and effortless.  There were a few subtle nods to the point and clicks of old but not overdone at all.  I enjoyed the art style and the overall feel of the game.  The puzzles were challenging but logical.  I didn't find myself reaching for help until the very end.  I will certainly revisit this game again in a few months when the solutions are not fresh in my mind.  I look forward to seeing anything this game developer does next.  The length was longer than you get out of most point and clicks at about 9 hours and I think it was well worth the money.  Try this one if you lick point and clicks and are on the fence about it.  Edit: I just read that this game was made by 2 people wow blown away.  Amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: Ticks all of the point and click boxes for me; Pretty Graphics: Check Decent voice acting: Check Humorous dialog: Check Mostly fine puzzle design: CheckSkip dialog and skip scene: Check Hot-spot reveal: CheckBuilt in help mechanic that doesn't spoil the solution: CheckMade by Alasdair Beckett-King: CheckObviously that last one is a bit of joke but he is involved and that man does know a thing or two about making good adventure games.As I said above the puzzle design is mostly fine and enjoyable, there were a few times, in order to proceed, the solution was to just show an item to a character and it was never really obvious why I would show that particular character that particular item but otherwise I can't complain.There is also a bit of a quirk with the save system in that you cannot simply overwrite a save slot, you need to delete it first and then save. If your not careful you might end up loading an older save rather then saving a new one. You will get the hang of it after a short while though so its not a deal breaker.Overall Highly recommended.

Nevertheless,  has its moments, and if it's on sale and you need a decent adventure game to tide you over to the next great one I would recommend it. The art is quite nice (reminds me of a fully 2D version of ), the voice acting is mostly decent, and the game improves considerably in the third act after a very slow start. name: Dandy Ace
detailed_description: Dandy Ace is an over the top fast-paced roguelike experience that follows a fabulous magician seeking to combine and use his magical cards while fighting and looting his way to defeat the Green-Eyed Illusionist, Lele, who has imprisoned him in a cursed mirror. While battling your way through Lele’s ever changing palace, combine different cards with more than a thousand possibilities, each with their own playstyles and powers. Every run provides new challenges and combinations for players to explore as they progress closer to Lele. Play as Dandy Ace, the amazing hero, and survive the challenges of the extravagant, lavish and ever changing palace created to defeat him filled with bizarre creatures and outrageous bosses. Find all of the magical cards, gather shards and gold, and get help from his assistants and unconventional allies. Rogue-lite experience: Try, die and try again until you beat the Green-Eyed Illusionist with the replayability and adrenaline of a rogue-like with permanent upgrades that makes you stronger as you progress further with each run. 2D isometric fast-paced action: with lots of challenging but fair combat engagements. Battle your way through bizarre creatures and outrageous bosses while building up your own arsenal of magic. Create your own builds: Combine cards with more than a thousand possibilities, each with its own gameplay style and powers. Challenges of the ever changing palace: Explore the extravagant and lavish aesthetics of the game through the nonlinear progression of the palace, fighting off unique enemies and bosses, on your quest to defeat Lele and escape the cursed mirror.

_childDocuments_.review: More inspiration was taken from Dead Cells than Hades in all honesty.The combat is top down action, yes. However, everything else is very different. The biggest thing for me is that the experience was designed around a caster, and it feels like it. I died very early in the palace early on, many times, when I tried to play like Hades and ram my face into enemies to destroy them as quickly as possible. I started getting further when I realized I needed to play like a caster, staying on the edge of fights, needling inwards with ranged spells and using tons of status effects to make sure opponents can't do anything to you.All your abilities, including basic attacks, dashes, and all are in the form of cards that you can equip freely in one of four slots. Decide you don't want to dodge? Shove a bomb in that slot. Decide you don't want to do anything BUT dodge and use the damage effects from those to destroy your enemies? Fill every slot with blue cards. On top of that, every card has an active form for if you use it in a slot, but every card ALSO has an additional effect that applies if you attach it to an existing card. Got a card that gives you a spray of playing cards? Throw that on your big explosive burst. Now the burst causes homing cards to fly out of opponents it damages. You can freely change which cards you are using, and in what way, whenever you wish. You're not locked into abilities.Much like Dead Cells, you take branching pathways that are all different. Also much like dead cells, you have to obtain most things in meta progression, which isn't really my favorite element of modern roguish games, but what can you do? As well, after each room you finish you get to equip a Trinket which are very similar to the Mutations from Dead Cells, including being capped at a certain amount and paying to swap them later if you wish. So far they seem to do some interesting things and I'm excited to see what else will be unlocked later.The style of the game is very distinctive, and I am entirely biased towards this kind of thing. I've found the game very enjoyable overall, and I hope more people try it, rather than just immediately calling it a 'Hades Ripoff', which it most certainly isn't. At least try the demo and see for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Dandy Ace

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me say that I own and have thoroughly played nearly every action-roguelite game on Steam (check my profile if you want proof) so if you want perspective on this game from the perspective of someone extremely familiar with the genre, keep on reading. Dandy Ace is an exceptionally well-made action roguelite in the vein of Dead Cells x Hades, however I can see why the game isnt getting positive reviews across the board. I will admit that when I first played Dandy Ace, I felt as though it was a game with an identity crisis, attempting to be a series of other roguelites without really developing a unique personality of its own. After playing over 20 hours though, I can say that Dandy Ace keeps its cards close to its chest (pun somewhat intentional) until you've really put in some practice. When you first start off, much like dead cells, you have no real healing mechanics and a pretty slim selection of powers. Your first few runs will be short and not too fun since the game has a pretty respectable difficulty.As you progress through the game however, you will slowly gain abilities that vastly improve your survivability and this is where the game shows its true colors. The main combat mechanic revolves around using "playing cards" each with a different ability of either damage, movement, or status effect. You can hold 4 of these cards at a time and the game has you constantly swiching your build throughout a run as to never let it get stale. On top of that, once you have more than 4 card, you can use the extra cards as "sub-slots" on your main 4 which drastically alter the effects and use of these moves. This constant mixing and matching of different powers and effects is absolutely DOPE. Once you've unlocked a good portion of the abilities, you will find there is an obscene number of combinations for your build, nearly all of them viable and a blast to play. This variety keeps me coming back again and again to Dandy Ace even though I have nearly 600 games in my steam library.Overall, if you have any interest in roguelites or top-down action games, I HIGHLY suggest picking up this game. If you go in expecting more of Hades, you will be disappointed. Go into Dandy Ace with the knowledge that you'll have to put in a few hours of tough runs before you start to really experience the magic that is contained in this game. I would solidly put Dandy ace in the top 10% of all roguelites I have ever played and plan on spending plenty more hours blasting through Lele's cursed mirror.8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dandy Ace

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game!  I was worried it would be way too much exactly like Hades, but it really feels very different.  It's a lot of fun to mess around with the cards you find during the levels, that you can combine to build your powers and attacks.  At ANY TIME during your runs, you can swap out your cards, rearrange them to make completely different kinds of attacks and support abilities.  Great stuff!One worry is that there isn't enough variety of cards, but we'll see.  I suck at games like this, and have only made it to the 3rd level so far.  But, I'm having a blast and just want to play more.  So, that's good enough in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world filled to the brim with action-roguelikes, Dandy Ace is worth recommending mainly for two reasons: the charming and interesting theme and aesthetic (which reminded me of Dungeonland and is also fully voiced), and the brilliant spell card system akin to Transistor, in which every skill "card" can be used either as an active skill or as a modifier to an already equipped one. There are TONS of cards and synergies, and the game lets you explore and swap between them freely (even mid-battle).Apart from those, it is a competent roguelike with everything you expect these days to be able to stand near heavy hitters such as Hades or Dead Cells - there are several different tilesets, a bunch of different enemies, cool bosses with great character design, loads of unlockables, different difficulties, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR No regrets, just not good game. Kinda pretty tho. Lost my interest after the first couple hours. Review made on Patch 1.2.0.0.24Ok, so It took me 32.4 hours to beat this game in nightmare mode, I’m Brazilian so giving up is kinda hard. I do not consider myself to be a good isometric Rogue-like player, despite really liking the genre, but I'm going to put my review here.First of all I bought it because I really appreciate new Brazilian games and I will buy them whenever I think they are cool, É nois mlk S2.Second I'm going to right here the good and bad point of the game so people reading can have some reference:GOOD- The art direction is very good. Enemies vary enough from normal to nightmare mode so you not only understand that they are more dangerous but that they also have different abilities. The environment and animations are pretty nice and well rounded fitting the themes presented.- The interface and General UX is also visually interesting and a bit intuitive, save the "hold" to quit buttons and alike, which took me around 15 hours to understand how it worked somehow.- There is a CLEAR mixture of popular, already existing isometric/rogue-like game mechanics, such as Transistor and Dead Cells, which bring some familiarity to the mechanics.- The voice acting in english is really good, the characters have personalities and all, but in PT-BR the sound mastering sucks, I can't understand almost anything the characters are saying.BAD- Many enemies have instant attacks which makes the "no Iframe, no hitstun" game design policy of this game kinda boring to work around, since dashes (only recently updated to actually go through enemies) and blinks are a preventive maneuver and not reactive, once the enemies deal damage even before their animation ends.- Animations and movement directions are clunky, not only while moving around, but YOU ARE GOING TO DIE BECAUSE YOU GOT STUCK IN AN INVISIBLE CORNER or dashed to a wall, since enemies deal 20-25% of your life on hit.- Melee sucks in comparison to ranged, also because there are no hitstuns, dealing massive melee damage does not compensate for getting hit by 100 occasionally. Of course, this part is my opinion and I'm sure people that are better are going to find more ways to be good.- The Story does not End. The main reason I played this game (besides the one I mentioned in the beginning) and that I play games in general is for the Story. After you beat the game in each difficulty, Lele tells you that you actually are still trapped inside and the security ha gone up, but after nightmare mode, nothing changes, the game just shows credits D: Not even an interaction between Ace and Lele like the other difficulties. I really can't believe I got to 4 cells and the game simply didn't end, not even a new cutscene.- Following that, it is really daunting that jenny jenny and jolly jolly keep asking you why haven't y'all left that place yet, I consider this a negative feedback which does not make the player want to continue to play the game.- The Transistor Skill system used in this game is interesting by design, however it was chosen to not be implemented fully, leaving the Character passive slots aside. This, summed with many "death triggered" passives render many cards undesirable to play. Alongside that I believe I restarted the game a couple of times in nightmare mode due to getting "bad RNG" with the first 3 cards.- Thankfully they put the option to mute the narrator, because I simply couldn't stand the same lines after the first hour of the game.- The card shop/upgrade system, as per dead cells, was interestingly implemented with the possibility to upgrade the cards held instead of only buying.- The passive upgrade systems on Nyftar and Jolly jolly serve only to keep you in parity with the difficulty increase of each mode, they do not give you any meaningful upgrade.After thinking and writing about this game I really cannot recommend it to other people. Even if the majority of reviews of this game are positive, only 4% (to this date) of players have even got to beat hard mode, which is the second easiest mode in the game, people are simply playing a bit and giving a good review, but won't really finish the story after Lele tells them there is more (even if in the end you find out there is not).This review ends up with many others: The game is clearly unpolished when it comes to hitboxes and gameplay and I believe it will get better in the future, since the devs have been making somewhat consistent updates, but not right now.The only thing to keep in mind if you plan to play is that there are a couple of game design policies they adhere to that go against many good mechanics players like, such as hitstuns and Iframes.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad?Gameplay loop:1) You start with 3 cards (attacks) 2) Go through maze3) Use currency to buy upgrades / new cards at the end of the the level?4) Every 2 levels or so there is a boss. 5) Did you beat the boss? If so go on! If not go back to 1Why I recommend it:* The gameplay is fast. I'm not a fan of slow prodding combat.* You can really play with your attack (card) loadout.  With 4 slots and 4 upgrade slot you can lots of choices to play with different attacks* The runs are short. It's nice having to finish a full run in 25 minutes if I want. Why I will not recommend it:* Combat is very samey even with different loadouts. This is especially true on the higher levels. * One big problem is how the currency drop scales and how much damage the enemies inflict. This makes it not worth your time to fight the enemies until the last level. * Lots of bad/weird designs decisions. Much too many to list here.100% achievement in ~12 hours. On a scale from a single card to a royal flush I will give this game a straight.

_childDocuments_.review: An honest hard working magician on the verge of retirement has his career stolen by the Chad degenerate magician.• Dodges need I-frames desperately.• Enemy animations before attacking is super fast / borderline nonexistent.• Harder difficulties are just stat padded enemies.• The level of cards matters more than what those cards are.  This cripples any strategic element then turns it into a race to get big numbers.• Dandy kisses the floor despite having two hot assistants because his only means of survival is running away.• Kiting is NOT FUN.  Aggressive + short-range play styles needs more support.• Copies the Dead Cells progression system 1:1.  Which isn't a good thing because most of the "upgrades" feel like "sidegrades" or have very little impact. • Renewed my love for Tea, and Cupcakes.• Renewed my hatred for hooks.• The top hat is pretty cool not gonna lie.• Game play improvements are very unlikely to happen.  (developers already shot down i-frame, and animation concerns from other users on the Steam forums)• Not the worst game in the genre, but far from the "greats" (Hades, Dead Cells, etc)• The first boss is well done.  The others... not so much.• Dandy is starts surrounded in every single non boss encounter,  Very repetitive, and annoying without a good dash.• Enemy variety leaves more to be desired.  Although their designs are great!It isn't a bad game, but it isn't good.  It isn't a boring game, but it isn't fun.  With so many great titles populating this genre a game can't just be "average" anymore.  I want to see this game succeed, and end up on the same tier as the other "greats" although there is still some work that needs to be done before it can reach that point.Rating the game now as "not recommended".  The developers are interactive with the community which is great, but they respond to the most common critiques with justifications (see most of their pinned threads on the steam forums) for the poor decisions instead of any kind of willingness to understand/compromise...This leads us to believe that "improvements" won't happen, and time is better allocated to other rouge likes with enjoyable gameplay.  Nothing wrong for individuals that enjoy how things are, but its not for me - and if you are used to other action rougelikes then there is a solid chance it may not be for you either.

_childDocuments_.review: Dandy Ace~~~~~~~~~~Dandy Ace is a fun new character-driven roguelike, indie, dungeon-crawler. And when I say character-driven, it really is; the whole game is focused around two characters and their rivalry and their motivations (one of them being hatred). You get to play as Dandy Ace, a new hotshot magician in town, who has won the hearts of many with his charm and talent. But that didn’t sit well with his rival, Lele The Green-Eyed Illusionist. Lele was jealous seeing Dandy’s fame and success, he wanted his old glory back. So, he decided to trap Dandy and challenge him and his talents every step of the way.The journey to Dandy’s freedom seems slim to none but his is no ordinary talent. He will surely collect enough momentum to break free from Lele’s trap and beat him along the way. Gameplay:  The game starts off with a neat series of slide animations outlining Dandy and Lele’s rivalry, and setting off the stage for Dandy Ace’s epic journey throughout Lele’s trapped realm full of mystical creatures, beings, traps and defense towers. Dandy needs to reach Lele and defeat him in a mystical battle to earn his freedom, but he needs to find him first and that’s the tricky bit. The realm is locked into multiple areas and all of them are locked behind a magical gate, each requiring different keys spread throughout each area. Right from the start, Dandy will be out of magical cards to even out the field, Dandy will be given 3 cards to start with, and as you move forward by defeating enemies, Dandy will have a decent chance of getting more cards as drops with unique abilities and powers. Cards can be equipped with just a press of the button F if your slot is empty, otherwise a long press will lead you to an F shuffle menu where you cannot only replace your equipped cards with better ones, you can also upgrade them using Shards. Shards can be obtained by simply killing Lele’s goons, but be aware, if you die, the Shards will be gone. You can also use your extra collected cards by adding them to your existing equipped cards which gives a good boost, with passive abilities ranging from toxic secondary damage to explosion upon death, given from an existing set of four - a nice boost in damage. Secondary abilities are like side effects and don’t really matter what their primary effects are. I highly recommend you try different combos with your primary cards and secondary effect cards. You’ll get more and more variety that way; the only problem here is you won’t be able you collect all the cards in one playthrough. You’ll have to give it a multiple ending to get all the cards but due to lack of content Idk how many of you will be motivated to do so! But I’ll give Dandy Ace this, because of these awesome card attacks and the card secondary effect system, the game is so enjoyable and makes Dandy Ace stand out from the rest of the Roguelike’s, giving it a bit of re-playability. Combat: A great combination of Dandy Ace’s card system and its fluid movement machines made it an amazing experience. As soon as you get into the game you face an ambush and as you progress through the ambushes, enemy types and bosses get faster, stronger, and more powerful overall. The fast-paced style of the game kept me on my toes all the time. The enemy spawns were well thought out and genuinely got me off guard quite a few times. Each boss fight was unique and well thought out according to the boss’s powers and abilities. The same goes for ordinary enemies but from time to time they also surprised me with their overwhelming firepower and intensity. World design: Dandy Ace’s mirror realm is divided into multiple areas. Each is uniquely designed with its own unique elements and theme. Music and sound effects: The music didn’t really impress me that much; it really felt like a generic soundboard composition.But the game really shined in the sound effects section; almost everything played out nicely, befitting of the game's theme. The footsteps could use some retouching. Narration/Voice acting: The actors did a bang-on job with the narration, Dandy Ace, and Lele’s voice-overs. The tone of every bit of voice-over work for them were well thought out and scripted for their character’s style. Positives: + Unique fun plot+ Fun fast-paced gameplay + Unique card system with secondary effects+ Decent job with the sound effects+ Fantastic world design, befitting the game's theme + Fascinating-looking enemies and bosses + Interesting map layout + Challenging boss fights Negatives: - Music could use some re-touching - Footsteps as well- Felt the lack of content A rival’s jealousy can go a long way, so long that you can get trapped in a magical realm. Fight your rivals and everything that stands in between your freedom.8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!
