_childDocuments_.review: Dirt 5 is essentially an offroad version of GRID (2019) with a very similar UI and game progression. It is NOTHING like Dirt 4, which is either a good thing or a bad thing, depending on what you are after. You play an unnamed racer (with a name you can pick ingame, with proper matching audio) being groomed by famous racer "AJ" as the up and coming star of the offroad racing scene. You will race a wide variety of offroad vehicles, from sprint cars to rally Group B legends, from buggies to trophy trucks, from modern rally cars to mudrunners, this game has it all. You will participate in a wide variety of events, from races with multiple opponents, to time trials in extreme terrain, from point-to-point races to gymkhana maneuvers, from ultracross on ice to special throwdown events. There are 125 different events in the main game alone for single player, and the DLC "event packs" adds even more vehicles and events. The game unlocks gradually, so you get a feeling of accomplishment even if you did not win every race. After every race, you get XP (for level gains), D (for buying new vehicles and bonus patterns), and sponsorship rating (higher level sponsor bonuses).  You have to pick a sponsor, who may have special requirements for bonus pay during the race event. Each event may have its own achievement for extra pay as well. You can win up to 3 "stamps" per event, and you will need certain number of stamps to unlock additional events. The requirements are low enough so you can skip events that you don't like as well as not get first place in every event. For each race event, you gain some D, which is the currency in the game, that you can use to purchase additional vehicles. You also gain reputation points with your sponsor, which can unlock additional rewards. On the other hand, the unlocks are usually cosmetic. Another background pattern for your "race card", a "sticker" you can apply to your livery or race card, a lanyard pattern, a new livery for a vehicle (you may or may not have bought), and so on. The rewards feel not quite commensurate with the effort. In fact, the whole game feels very much like "Gravel" a similar offroad racing game from Milestone, albeit crossed with GRID (2019) game. The graphics are gorgeous, if a bit distracting, as there are often portions of the game where you drive into the setting sun or such. Given that you do NOT have a co-driver in this game, you have to rely on visual cues and your own memory of the tracck to navigate, it can get a bit hectic. The audio "commentary" was produced with the cohosts from Donut Media's James and Nolan, which are not bad. They are used only sparingly, which means they don't feel repetitive or tiring (unlike in Gravel, where the same announcement at every few events quickly turned the whole thing into repetitive droning). Unlike GRID, there is no nemesis system, where driving aggressively does not turn rival drivers into road rager driver from hell. There is also no team mate. It is everyone for him or herself. What is also interesting is there are usually several different choices of vehicles available for each event... Vehicles gets two grades: a performance grade (acceleration and speed), and a maneuverability grade (agility), with rating of S, A, B, or C (in descending order). Each vehicle thus, depending on its two grades, gets a "multiplier". Vehicles with not-so-good grades gets a bonus, like 1.1x or 1.2x, while vehicles with no disadvantage gets a normal 1.0x. The multiplier is applied to the winnings (D) and sponsor reputation when you finish the event. So if you can win with a "lesser" vehicle, you are definitely rewarded for it. On the other hand, for some events, you may have to purchase an 1.0x vehicle just to keep up with the AI. There seems to be a few too many different race variations with strange names. While it is somewhat explained in-game, the differences between the variations, like how is ultraross different from a stampede, was not really explained. The idea basically is to get to the finish ahead of everyone else, or as fast as possible. Though it was the "mismatches" that are the most interesting. For example, in one of the "throwdown" events called "Ankle-Biters", you have a trophy truck, which accelerates fast and have a superb top-speed, but manueverability is a bit suspect. You have to race a whole passel of Ariel Nomads, which are agile off-roaders much smaller than you are. Can you still win despite disadvantage in the corners? And there are several more throwdown challenges ahead. As pointed out earlier, this is basically GRID but with offroad tracks and offroad vehicles. It is NOTHING like Dirt 4, which are more rally car, buggies, and trophy truck racing. This also lacks the random rally stage generator in Dirt 4. In fact, rally is barely present in Dirt 5. All in all, Dirt 5 is, again, GRID turned offroad. It is exciting. It is fun, but the rewards doesn't quite seem commensurate with the effort in single-player, with a ton of grind, but that's the same way in GRID as well.  Dirt 5 feels like a successor to Dirt:Showdown instead of Dirt 4. It is also significantly different from Dirt 4, which may be a good or bad thing depending on what you are after. It gets an unenthusiastic recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered this game, expecting some good casual 'dirt' racing. Having been a long time fan of Codemasters, expectations were high, but tempered by underwhelming recent releases (i.e. GRID Autosport!). I hated it at first. Graphics seems almost grotesque, almost over stylised similar to recent Street Fighter games - but I know that's subjective. Weather, Particle Effects and Lighting are really impressive, but the textures used for car models, and sky/clouds looked (still look) terrible. HDR implementation was pretty good though (I play on a TV). Additionally however, the game kept crashing every 5 minutes, and graphics settings were buggy (playing on RTX 3090 + AMD 5800x). The DRIVING itself however is very satisfying and and track variation keeps things fresh and exciting, So I stuck with it intending to come back and try again later. After picking up after ignoring for several weeks, I found that updates had improved the driving physics as well as general stability. I got used to the graphics, and now having an absolute BLAST in career mode. It's a super fun game - where the different road surfaces seem more visceral then I have ever felt in a racing game, and well worth it IMO even in single player mode. Multiplayer is also great, having a lot of fun, but focusing on the career for now. I additionally Love how varied the racing styles are, it definitely provides some very challenging modes (Gymkhana, Sprint(!)) which are so fun to practice at, making it so satisfying to finally conquer. I would definitely recommend this game, as it offers something unique  - which has been missing for quite some time. For reference, other racing games I love/(play often) are Forza Horizon 4, NFS Heat, Gran Turismo Sport, Assetto Corsa, F1 2020 (not in any order).

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I'm a little less than 2 hours in. That's all it takes to see everything that Dirt 5 has to offer. Dirt 5 is, by all accounts, the weakest entry in the series. If you want something that's similar to Dirt 5 but actually fun, play Dirt Showdown. If you want anything related to rally, play any other game in the series. Pick ONE thing: any type of racing, the graphics, the physics, the atmosphere, the soundtrack, ANYTHING...and a different Dirt game will do it better. Dirt 5 was supposed to be the next-gen entry in the series, and it's a step backwards in every way.The biggest fault Dirt 5 has, above all else, is that it's just a complete bore to play. Most of the events feel very same-y, and even with the game cranked up to the higher difficulties with all assists off, for the most part its piss easy (except for the sprint races, which I'll get to. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I'll get to that). Most of the in-race challenges such as "overtake while drifting 3 times" or "trade paint in mid-air 3 times" can't even be done because within a few seconds you'll have rocketed to the front of the pack and you'll never see any opponents again before the race is over. If turning up the difficulty and turning off assists doesn't make the game any harder, what am I supposed to do? Play with my hands behind my back?Dirt is known for being thrilling, fast, and sometimes white-knuckle scary in the case of the Dirt Rally subseries, but Dirt 5 has zero sense of speed at all. 100mph in Dirt 5 feels like 50mph in any other game. The environments and tracks, while colorful and vibrant in appearance, have layouts that seem like they were generated by an algorithm rather than being interesting places for racing. I wouldn't be surprised if you could zoom the camera out on any given track and see some programmer's kid's outline of a stegosaurus.The graphics are surprisingly sad for a next-gen title. You can tell that they were probably contractually obligated to make the game hit 120fps on consoles because the lighting is flatter than yo mama's tiddies. The soft lighting engine from previous Dirt games is nowhere to be found. Even the damage model has been toned down drastically in comparison to earlier games in the series. Guess what? Crappy lighting + barely functioning damage model = all of the cars look and feel like plastic toys. Brroom Brrooom, I'm playing with Hot Wheels in the backyard :DLastly, the sprint races are so awful they warrant their own paragraph. Where the rest of the game is laughably easy, the sprint races will make you suffer a brain aneurysm born from unbridled rage. Doing laps in a sprint car feels like trying to ice skate with Dutch wooden clogs. The AI, being the cheating bastards they are, can do this effortlessly, while you fumble around the back of the pack like a newborn giraffe being immediately forced to run away from a bloodthirsty lioness upon entering the world. Even people who like Dirt 5 have filled forums across the internet with comments about how much they hate sprint races. This game was released on November 5th, Codemasters, so I think you waited a little too late to pull such a cruel April Fools joke on us.Okay, I'm done. Don't buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: The lack of motion blur makes this game literally unplayable for me.It is also an unfortunate reality that "motion blur" is the name given to anti aliasing in the time dimension, because it makes most people think of it as a gritty filter, and thus do not see it as an essential part of the image synthesis process. It is also unfortunate that temporal anti-aliasing is the name given to spatial anti-aliasing using samples from previous frames - it has nothing to do with temporal anti-aliasing at all!When games have fast movement and high resolutions, there's a lot of temporal aliasing  makes me sick.To counteract this, most games that have high resolution (high spatial frequency content) that moves too fast to be properly reproduced by the display refresh rate also have a temporal anti-alisasing method, most commonly known as motion blur. That a game with such HD assets (high spatial frequencies!!!) would not implement any basic form of motion blur to counter act this is astounding. Maybe I can play it when I get a 240hz display...

_childDocuments_.review: Are you looking for a sim racer?Are you running a low-end or older GPU that tends to struggle running modern games on anything more than medium?Do you want to have photorealistic graphics?Do you expect this to be a rally-centric game?If you answered yes to any of those questions, this game is not for you. I would highly recommend DiRT Rally 2.0 instead.Now that that's out of the way, HOLY HELL this game is fun. The cartoony but still high-end graphics fit the style of the game perfectly. The podcast hosts (who are actually two members of the Donut Media team, really awesome guys whose YouTube channel I've followed for ages) emphasize the "just here to have fun" theming of the game, with their podcast just being them being, well, themselves. The driving physics have a very arcade feel to them without sacrificing the "dirtiness" of the track. I don't entirely know how to explain it but it feels both realistic and yet incredibly arcade. the racing discipline choices are all fun, and they've done away with the old point-to-point rally stages, which while some people may be sad to see leave (myself included), makes sense given the theme and style of the game. This is a game about fast and/or offroad cars doing fast and/or offroad things, and it definitely nails that. Overall I think this is a really good game in the same category as DiRT 2. I love it.On a note of issues with the game, there are only two things I should point out:A lot of people (myself included) have had stability issues in game. Mine only crashed once before and since the latest patch hasn't given even the slightest issue, but given my limited playtime and how close I am to the recommended PC specs (R5 3600, 32GB RAM, 1660SUPER) I don't think I'm part of the larger affected groups. I will be updating this review after I've played more to confirm if there are any issues though.This game also currently doesn't have steering wheel support. While I personally don't see the use in playing this game with a wheel, as an arcade racer is more suited to gamepad anyways, I can see those who want to do it being somewhat miffed. Codies have confirmed that this is in the works and just took too long to be able to release in base game, but will arrive in a patch in the coming weeks, so if steering wheels are important to you then don't worry, it's on its way.TL;DR: This is a DiRT game to its core. Very much a back-to-basics arcade offroader and it honestly reminds me of DiRT 2. If you loved that game, this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for less than €6Enthusiast sim-racer here, and I like this game much more than I should.I own DiRT 3; 4; Rally and Rally 2.0. Obviously this game is not a rally game at all, it is much more like DiRT 3's rallycross on steroids and like Showdown.Handling wise it feels great using a gamepad. Game is obviously arcade, so if you are looking for realism do not even bother. I would say the handling feels more realistic than DiRT 4's 'gamer' handling, but less realistic than Forza Horizon 3 and 4's off-road handling. Surprisingly though braking feels almost like it is from a simcade title or DiRT 4's 'simulation' handling. People could say the brakes feel 'unresponsive' but it feels like cars actually have weight because of it. Will take a bit to get used to, especially if you are used to arcadey 'super-brakes'.Gameplay itself is fun. AI does seem to be pretty easy on the hardest mode, but that might just be for me. Given the nature of the discipline itself, do expect unavoidable contact with other racers though.The tracks are amazing with a lot of different location, I also heard there is a track-builder but I have not touched it yet.Sound department is great on both on-track and in the menus. Codemasters are really good in bringing the right music for most of their games. Menu is simple and clean with a lot of eye-catching colours. It might look a bit 'too childish/video game'-like, but me having spend way too much time into simulators find this a really welcoming thing. It makes it feel like a game to have fun in, not the typical "I need to win" thing. There is also this 'podcast' like thing that may put people off quite hard, but at least you can skip it. For me, it brings me back to the old Burnout 3 Crash FM radio.For controller support, I think it is what you usually find in most games. I use an Xbox One S controller and it is fine. I do miss the trigger vibrations, which Codemasters usually implement for all their games. Not a dealbreaker, but a bit disappointing. I have yet to try this on my Fanatec ClubSport Wheelbase 2.5, but I doubt I will. It did immediately pick up my wheelbase though. A godsend from this game is that you can select which controller you use as the primary device. Having 5 controllers plugged in this is great. It does not take any input from the other plugged in devices if you set it like that.Content wise I cannot really comment on with my 1 hour review yet. Though like I said, the tracks are amazing and with a track editor you technically should have quite a lot of hours of replayability. I have seen that there are campaigns locked behind DLCs.I think it mostly comes down to the pricing. I would definitely not recommend this game at the current €54,99. But if you can pick it up for around €15, I definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: ----------------------------------------------------------WARNING: do not buy the Amplified Edition but go for the Standard game instead. To this day it's unclear what the extra benefits of Amplified are gonna be. They already released a car DLC (Porsche Macan) that isn't even part of the Amplified Edition and in a recent video interview with the dev director on the DIRT YT channel it's stated that even the Standard game is gonna get extra free content. I still like the game but so far the extra money I paid for the Amplified Edition feels like a waste.  ----------------------------------------------------------Looking at the reviews so far I'm apparently one of the few who knew what he was getting into. I think the storepage and the trailers communicated well enough what type of game this was gonna be. I would say, as a FIRST IMPRESSION, after DiRT 2 this is my favorite game of the five. It has that 'playful' character of DiRT 2 and a bit of that Forza Horizon vibe, at least for me. Wether that's a good thing or not you have to decide for yourself. For me it's exactly what I'm looking for in such a racing game. If I want realism and get serious I jump into my car and drive to work. So DiRT 5 is a pure arcade racer now. Even the typical rally stages with a co-driver are replaced with a lot of other but fun modes. They also ditched the "Simulation" mode option from DiRT 4. I don't mind that because we have choice nowadays in what we want to buy and play. If this isn't your cup of tea don't spit in it and get your own flavor.         Some things I likeThe stylish and colorful presentation works great with the theme of this game. They also put a lot of effort in the soundtrack. You can feel the passion Codemasters has for the franchise. Like I mentioned, It's not  a rallygame anymore but more a 'party' game with those same cars. Graphics are absolutely effing gorgeous if you have the horsepower to dial it all up. With an i5 8500, 16 GB RAM and a 1070Ti, I get an average of 46 fps on 1440p with high settings, wich is reasonable but not great. And than you have Very high wich I'm not even gonna try. However, there's a feature to let the game take care of your settings automatically wich works surprisingly well. Now the average fps is around 70 fps without a noticeable difference in graphical fidelity. All in all it's way more taxing than I expected. A lot more than GRID (2019) for comparison.The new dynamic weather and daytime feature where weather conditions can change during a race is just awesome. A lot of variety in tracks and landscapes and most important, cars and race types including the newly added sprint cars.And finally there's a photomode. It's a bit clunky in that it takes some time to move the filter sliders around (it would be nice if it could be controlled with the mouse) and the processing of the image is a bit slow. I hope they add support for NVIDIA Ansel wich I still prefer but it's still a welcome addition. Things I like lessThe sound is pretty good actually but could be better. I'm missing a bit of grunt in the lower end of the engine sounds. Many cars just don't sound as mean and agressive as they should. It's just a bit underwhelming. The post race replay feature or in better words: the lack thereof. Where the hell is the replay option Codemasters? They finally included a photomode to accompany their pretty graphics engine and than removed the replay feature, wich was part of their games for as long as I can remember. I love watching replays with various camera angles after an exciting race and taking screenshots. Now you have to take screens during the race wich breaks the immersion a bit for me.     Although this isn't a sim by any means, DiRT always used to have some basic tuning options too adjust your gear ratios, suspension, break balance and such. That's ditched too. You still have your options for ABS, TC and SC in 3 levels in de game options btw.No wheel support... yet. This is just silly. CM should know there will be backlash about this. They say it's coming but it should be in the game during launch. At the moment there are some stability issues too. Many people are reporting random crashes. I had a few CTD's too but it looks a driver update from NVIDIA fixed it or it could be the day one patch CM released today. Anyway the game seems to use less VRAM now. All in all, again, as a first impression I think this is a worthy new next gen entry in the franchise even with the strange choice to remove some basic and obvious features. It's not perfect but it doesn't deserve the  exorbitant hate it's getting so I give it a thumbsup.

_childDocuments_.review: “Hey there! If you’re listening to this message then congratulations, not only did you enter your details correctly, but you also impressed me. Impressed me enough that I’m inviting you to the AJ Racing academy! As you may have guessed it’s been set up by yours truly, and my one and only is to push you out there a bit more, throw you in the deep end and see if you can swim and make Team AJ a dominant force in the world of extreme motorsports. So, no pressure. That’s you all signed up, welcome to the club.” From the main menu screen, you’ll be able to select the game type you want to play. The options on offer are Career, Online, Arcade and Playgrounds. Also, on the main menu screen there’s Garage and Profile. I decided to play Career, this then takes you to the Events pages, the first race takes place at Ultra Cross at Henningsvær. From this race the Events will branch out so that you can select the races and choose your pathway towards the final races and you being crowned DiRT champion.  For your first race you’re going to need a car, there are four cars on offer to you. However, only one car is currently available to you without the need of spending any of your One Hundred and Fifty Thousand dollars currently sat in your bank account. The car already unlocked is the Skoda Fabia Rally2 EVO, the other three cars available are the Volkswagen Polo GTI R5, the Citroen C3 R5 and the Ford Fiesta R5 MKII. Each of the cars have some stats, the Skoda Fabia Rally2 EVO has a Performance rating of A and Handling rating of B, Drivetrain (4WD), Power (275BHP), Weight (1230 KG) and Torque (420NM). The other cars have similar stats and they all cost Sixty Thousand quid. Me personally I kept the Sixty Grand and went for the Skoda, I haven’t tried the other card as of yet as the Skoda did me proud. I find this funny as many many moons ago, being seen in a Skoda was a big NO NO if you wanted to have friends ... my how times have changed. There are different types of events to compete in, you have, Ultra Cross, Rally Raid, Land Rush, Stampede, Ice Breaker, Path Finder, Sprint and Gymkhana. Some of these events you’ll probably love, others not so much, so you’ll be able to choose a path through the events you prefer. I’m more into racing than the Gymkhana so for now I have passed all of those events. The same goes for the Sprint events not one of my favorite events, so again I’ve passed them for now but I will get to the once I’ve finished the campaign. I’m currently on the fifth chapter of the campaign having chosen my races. These races take place all over the world, Norway, Italy, China, Morocco, Greece and The US of A. The race tracks are on different surfaces snow, mud, loose stone etcetera. The races take place at varying times of the day and night. While it may be nice and bright when you first set off across the start line it can turn dark while still racing. Not only can the time-of-day change but the weather can also change. It could be sunny out and then start pissing it down or you could find yourself in a blizzard or even a sand storm. This will impair your vision throughout the race, although the bad weather can disappear just as quickly as it arrived. Depending on the type of event will depend on the type of car you’ll need. After selecting an event you will then be given the choice of cars and trucks for that event. You may have to buy a new vehicle in order to compete in the event. I think you can unlock some cars as you progress, I say think because I can’t remember buying one of the cars I own. I have when it’s been able to just race with the unlocked vehicles. I have brought a few of my favorite cars and I have also wasted money on others. Two-Hundred and Fifty Thousand for a Brenthel Industries Unlimited Truck, one of the most expensive vehicles to buy and I found it bloody slow and useless.  As you complete events you will earn Experience Points, Reputation Points, Cash and Rewards. Gaining Experience Points will level up your character. This will allow you to unlock things later in the game. Reputation Points are earned from completing objectives within a race, you can increase the objectives by taking out Sponsorship Deals. Performing the objectives and leveling up that sponsorship will unlock new rewards and add a few quid extra to your cash. Rewards you will gain consist of new Liveries, Patterns, Textures, Stickers for your vehicles. You can also gain Cards, Lanyards, Stickers and Effects which can be used to personalise your profile. Customising your vehicles with different types of paint and varying colours, textures and patterns you can also give your vehicles a race number.So far, I have only played the Campaign but there are other game modes in which you can play. You have Playgrounds, here you have Discover, Create, Load and Published. You can create and upload your own playgrounds while also trying out other people's playgrounds. Arcade is where you can play Free Play and Time Trials.    There are quite a few options in the game, Video - Image Quality, V-Sync, Dynamic Range, Final Resolution, History Resolution, Render Resolution, Geometry Quality, Tessellation Quality, Shadow Quality, Volumetric Quality, Cloud, Quality, Procedural Quality and Global Illumination Quality (Low to Ultra High). Audio - Speaker Type, Music Positioning, Master and Music Volume, Vehicle, Sound Effects, Speech and UI Volume and Subtitles. Gameplay - Pad Vibration, Force Feedback Strength, Spring Intensity, Invert X and Y Axis, Steering Axis, Look Around X and Y Axis, Look Back, Accelerate, Brake, Handbrake Gear Up and Down, Next and Previous Camera. HUD - HUD Opacity, Show Speedometer, Speedometer Units, Driver Names, Show Minimap and Show Timers. Driving Aids – Career Difficulty, Preset, Transmission, Anti-Lock Brakes, Traction Control, Stability Management, Auto Brake and Tricksteer. While in the settings you can also run a Benchmark, this will give you details on Average, Minimum and Maximum FPS, along with Low 1% and Low 0.1% FPS. I’ve enjoyed playing DiRT 5 so far although I had the game crash a couple times and kept disconnected from the servers quite a few times in the first couple days of the game coming out. However, for the last few days I haven’t had any problems since.  While I have enjoyed playing DiRT 5 it has been very frustrated at times. It seemed like if I couldn’t get to first place as quickly as possible (starting from 12th position) then I would be stuck in the middle of a pack AI vehicles like I was a magnet drawing them all in. This made it hard to see where I wanted to go, and handling was a joke, then the AI’s would just would swerve suddenly one way only for it to turn sharply the other way across the width of the track in front of me and the other AI’s for no reason.  Positives + Looks great  + Multiple game modes + Multiple difficulties + Customise your vehicles + Remote Play Together+ Has AchievementsNegatives - Disconnected from servers - No steering wheel support - Crashed a couple times - No cards currently Have you got what it takes to compete in various race disciplines and be crowned DiRT 5 champion?  7/10

_childDocuments_.review: A Dirt game without half the content that makes Dirt the game that to me, represents the spirit of motorsport. No rally stages, no tuning, nothing besides flashy customization that you may or may not enjoy. Repetitive career with AI that seems to half the time pull off maneuvers that the car I drive cannot, while being terrible at a racing line and mostly ignoring my vehicle placement, banging into me because they want to drive their own line. There are pros, especially for more casual driving game fans who want an arcade-like experience with little braking necessary to navigate the track. There are phenomenal graphics, bright colors without oversaturation, beautiful weather effects that don't overpower you(i.e the rain is clearly heavy but not to the point where the track is invisible 0.02 seconds after your wipers go), and the cars, while a bit too shiny, are very well rendered and produced. Unfortunately, the look is the best part of the game, but the driving feel is nearly unarguably the most important, and that is where they missed the mark to me. If year 1 releases Rally stages and tuning, this game will end up feeling like a graphically updated Dirt 3, which would be a great arcade rally game, but right now.. It doesn't feel like Dirt to me. It's just another poorly coded racer that is unsure where it wants to excel so chose not to anywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game during the free weekend. In that time I completed the campaign and tried the multiplayer as well.I've played Dirt 3, Dirt 4, and Dirt Rally 1.0 and 2.0. I understand that these games fill very different niches for rally fans, with the first two being more arcadey and accessible, and the latter two being more hardcore, for rally sim fans.I'm honestly a fan of both titles. I play Dirt Rally to push myself to become a better driver, and I play the regular Dirt games to enjoy the thrill of rally racing without having to focus too much. Which is why Dirt 5 is a massive disappointment for me.The Dirt franchise has always revolved around the stage rally style of racing. Yes, there has always been other modes, like the equally popular RallyX mode, and the fun Gymkhana mode. Dirt 5 basically got rid of the core mode of the franchise in favor of emphasizing more on straightforward races against other AI players. They're not even RallyX races, which are tight, technical mixed surface tracks, but wide open tracks that offer basically no challenge. Think of the Cross Country races in Forza Horizon 4, and you get the idea. The other modes are basically a variant of these races, but on ice, or in a car that is next to impossible to control and is all about dirt oval racing. The closest you could possibly get to stage rally is the time trial rock climb mode, which, to give credit, can be fun, but just wasn't really for me. So by removing the mode the franchise is known for, they've removed the identity of the game, which is a shame. But hey, maybe other aspects of it will be good? Maybe the handling?The handling has always permitted a degree of mastery over the car while still providing a decent, yet accessible level of challenge. It was basically simcade, since you could entirely spin out your car, but mastering the driving meant some blistering times, more so without assists. Well, Dirt 5 has none of that either. All cars feel the same. A car with S class handling drives about as well as a car with B class handling in my honest opinion. Sliding around a corner is a matter of jabbing the handbrake button to initiate a slide, NFS style. Do some light counter steering but don't worry, you're at no risk of spinning out, unless you really really try. Jumping just feels weird too, with cars behaving in a weird way. It's like they're artificially creating the arc of the jump. The car also tends to straighten itself out during a jump. You can't turn just before the jump to pre-align the car in the direction you want it to go, it will angle itself in the direction of the flight. It's absolutely rubbish.So no stage rally, and no satisfying physics. What does this game have going for it then? Well. The graphics are nice. Uhmm. Yeah I guess.Basically, don't get this game. It contributes nothing to the franchise whether you're a newcomer or an old hat. I might have reviewed it slightly (only slightly) more favorably if it was a spinoff Dirt title (like maybe Dirt: Festival), spinoff Grid title (Grid: Offroad perhaps), or a new franchise altogether. But with the prestige of the Dirt franchise behind it, this game disappoints on all fronts. Do not buy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's code master racing game. It's a mixed bag as usual. It looks great except when it doesn't. The cars handle well except when they don't. Overall the game is very fun. _childDocuments_.review: To put it simply, the game is bad. I will now go on and list a couple of things as to why it is.1. Performance issues. I have a good pc. Not awesome, but good. I can play most recent games, at max settings, with over 60 FPS. Not this one though! I tried various graphical settings, and could't find anything to make the game run smoothly. It stutters most of the time, the fps frequently drop below 15 when there is a lot of stuff happening on screen. I've also had the game entirely crash 3-4 times. One time, it was so bad the game got stuck in half fullscreen, half windowed mode, and there was no way I could fix it.2. It doesn't look very good. I'm not very harsh usually when it comes to graphics. The trailer for this game looked freaking great! But even when I max the settings out, it looks bad. Sure, it's colourful. Sure, the environments are varied and creative. But there is aliasing everywhere. Everything in the distance looks kind of greyed out or blurry. 3. It doesn't play good. I've always thought of the Dirt series as an arcade-y rally racing game. This doesn't have any rally, and goes in 100% arcade, and not the good kind. The controls feel sluggish. The physics are really broken, in that you can sometimes hit a wall and the game will literally bounce you around 180 degrees. Also, one of the most annoying thing, terrain/weather have absolutely 0 effects on the driving. Meaning if you see a big puddle of water, you can drive straight through it, and won't feel any resistance, AT ALL!4. Some races are really infuriating/AI sucks. So one of the main selling points with this game was the variety of races. I'm all for it, except when some of those kind of races (I'm looking at you, ice races and the oval dirt sprint thing) are so broken and boring that it ruins the whole experience. Ice races are boring, and the AI is rubberbanding hard. You'll both come out of a corner, and the AI will just accelerate like it's on pavement while you're spinning your wheels. And the dirt/sprint kind of races are utterly boring and extremely hard.5. The UI sucks/lacking some key features. So first, for a PC game, it doesn't support the mouse to navigate the menus. Worse, the game doesn't even hide the mouse from your screen! So you better go tuck that cursor in a corner of the screen, or you'll be stuck with in in the middle for your entire race. The difficulty setting is broken. There is 5 difficulty settings, from very easy to very hard. After doing my first normal race, I found it very easy, and bumped it up to very hard. This suits me well for most races. However, when it comes to broken races like ice or dirt sprint, I can't even manage to get a podium finish on the easiest difficulty. The multiplayer is far from adequate. It only seems like it's 4 players per race (While you can be like 12 in career mode or something like that), and it's just long to find a match, and long to get out of one. When the race is over, you just have to sit there for like a minute, with no indication whatsoever of what is happening. The career progression seems like it's badly done. It's just one long string of events that you go through each after the other, and doesn't feel special. You get "stamps" when you win, what is that?If you want an arcade racing game, there are so many better options, in every way possible. I'm talking about every other Dirt Game in the series. I'm talking about every Forza Horizon game. Dirt 5 feels like they took their ok previous game OnRush, took out almost everything that made it a bit fun, slowed it down x2 and stuck in rally cars.

_childDocuments_.review: The negative reviews are quite shocking - people were expecting Dirt Rally 3.0 even after months of clear advertising about what this game really is - a *very* good arcade racer.Here's the thing, did you like Driveclub or Motorstorm? If so, then get this game. And set global illumination to "High" (as of the date of this review) since the ultra option is a substantial FPS killer for almost no change in quality. Outside of that, the game is gorgeous, the tracks are fun, the soundtrack is quite good, car selection is excellent, and overall, it's just a really, really fun time.Don't miss out, buy it, refund it if you don't like it but I'm afraid you'll get hooked :)

_childDocuments_.review: Kiddyfied trash .. everything in this game is made for 5 year old babies or even younger. It's like a teletubbie land .. WHEEE WHUUUU WHOOHOOOO ... the way characters talk is the way most parents talk to some 3yo baby "WHEEE LOOOK AT THAT WHOOO A RAINBOWW WHOOOO WANT YOUR MILK BOTTLE". It's making me so mad.At start of game, it throws you into game without giving you the chance to even choose controls or set anything up, just instantly into race. It won't even show keyboard buttons, I have controller connected and YES I want to play with controller, but I want to use mouse and keyboard in menus .. which is not possible.Well I did 3h stream on it and I think this is first and last time I play this childish trash, you can watch and decide for yourself - Here's also list of PROs and CONs:CONS:- Game is kiddyifed (made for 5yo kids)- Arcade handling- AI is way too easy even on "very hard"- Micro lag spikes (not network lag, frame lag, even tho it uses only like 60% of my graphics card and 25% of CPU). This stuttering makes it hard to drive properly.- NO replay feature- Races are way too short- 95% or more races are always in DARK or STORM, so you can't see anything.- Unable to re-map certain controls, which then overlaps with your custom controls. For example I changed "change camera" onto "select" button on my controller, but select is also reset car, which you can't re-map in options. so if you reset car it also changes camera. There are other buttons you're not able to re-map either...so terrible.- Game is generally RUSHED into, you see lot of small bugs / flaws that could easily be fixed.- No free ride / practice. You're able to freely drive (alone) on any track, but it's still limited, you can't drive backwards or explore.- No physical damage, you can smash into wall at like 150km/h and nothing happens, you only have a tiny fender bender.PROS:- Graphics are quite nice- Special effects are nice (like wind affects dust / dirt that kicks off from ground)- Playgrounds (players can create and share arenas that they have made)- Generally well optimized. I can run it in 4k maxed out with GTX 1080 (some stuff like AA and shadows turned down), but those micro lag spikes / stuttering is quite annoying. Could be because I have it on HDD and not SSD, but that's no excuse.- Constant kiddy talk "WHEEE YOU DOING GREEEAAATTT" even tho you can drive like total noob, from wall to wall... Ideas for developers:- Add free ride / explore options (1 open world map would be nice, where you can just chill and drive, maybe even with friends)- Add persistency (do not auto clean / repair vehicles, bushes should not "re-grow" when you drive over them..etc)- Add more realistic damage that doesn't let you drive into wall at 150km/h- Add proper replay system, so you can enjoy amazing graphics and make nice videos.- Ability to turn off the "teletubbie mode" where everything is kiddyfied, because it makes adults mad if they are being treated like little kids.I didn't get the game for free, but I got it with like 80% discount, that's only reason why I didn't refund it after I first tried it. If I paid full price for the game, I would have refunded it for sure. Totally NOT worth playing (unless you're 5yo who likes to WHEEE WHOOOOOO all day long with no sense of realism).I think developers nowdays need to make it clear that "This game is made for kids only". Not age rating, that youngest age is like 10 or 15 ..etc, but actually say that this game is NOT suitable for over 10yo kids, because it really is not.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you looking for a SRS BSNS rally game? If yes, turn around and walk back to DR2.Are you running a GPU that came out more than 2 years ago? If yes, turn around and walk back to Dirt 4.Still here? Ok, so this is a really arcadey, off-road racing game, made by the Onrush development team. It's big, loud and irreverent in the same sort of way that Forza Horizon games are. As someone who likes arcade racing experiences far more than sims, I've been enjoying it a lot.What it has:An upgrade of the Onrush graphics engine, targeting modern GPUs and Next Gen consoles.Time of day and weather changes during races.Nolan North and Troy Baker chatting the best sort of dumb garbage between races.A nice mix of different events and vehicle types.Booming soundtrack.Bright, colourful tracks.Playgrounds mode with a Trackmania style editor.Split Screen multiplayer.Ultrawide support.What it doesn't have:Point to point rally stages. (This isn't a rally game)Any sort of tuning.Rewind.The ability to run on a potato.VR.I like this, I think it's a better game than Dirt 4 in terms of gameplay, variety and spectacle.A note about Graphics: The game didn't look great all the time when set to auto, I think the dynamic detail and resolution reductions are way too aggressive. My recommendation would be to manually set everything to Native & High if you've got the power to run it like that. With everything on Native & High I'm getting consistent 70-80 fps at 3440x1440 on a 2080FE.

_childDocuments_.review: Dirt 5 is objectively a very nice game, reminiscent of Dirt 2 and Showdown combined together. The witty dialogue between the two commentators in the game menu is always entertaining to listen to - a real breath of fresh air. The game is colourful, engaging you can unlock all sorts of liveries, stickers cards and so on. The soundtrack unlike in Dirt Rally and 2.0 is there and it really hits right in the nostalgia taking me back to when I used to play Dirt 2 all day long. If you want a realistic simulator just don't bother playing it. This game is supposed to be competitive in a fun way whether you use a game pad or a keyboard. IT"S NOT A SIMULATOR! So to all the wheel and gear stick enthusiasts, just deal with it. You got two great rally games from Codemasters where you can practice your race car driver skills, now it's time for more casual players to enjoy their free time with a game like this.Although I enjoy it quite a lot I'm gonna put a few caveats here so that you know where the game lacks and what to expect.First you can play in snowy weather, however that's not supposed to ever happen in a tropical rain forest. I gotta be honest I found it silly when I learned I could drive through a blizzard in Brazil. No matter how you look at it it's scientifically incorrect.Second when you look at the global stats in the game menu you get a message that you're disconnected from the Internet or something along those lines and you basically have to go back and do it again. That in my opinion is something the devs need to take into account and fix because it gets annoying after a while.The third thing is if you don't have space shuttle for a pc don't even bother bumping the graphics on ultra. You pretty much get PS4 frames and it's not pleasant for the eyes. I was really hoping that my first gen RTX GPU would take some of the load off my processor but apparently you also need a CPU that's at least as good as the one shown in the recommended requirements. It really made me feel as if my rig's already obsolete. So yeah, that's my take on this particular game. Whether you wanna try it it's up to you. I give it a thumbs up because I can see the amount of work put in it as well as the fact that the devs had actually listened to all the Dirt 2 fans and made something very similar to it but a lot more visually appealing and dynamic.

_childDocuments_.review: My review so far for Dirt 5Summary:I genuinely cannot recommend this game, It's nothing like its predecessors and Dirt 5 brings nothing new to the table either. Dirt 5 is a super arcade racing game with some offroad tracks, but there's nothing to this game that caters to any racing fans, sim or arcade. Its easily the worst Dirt game in the franchise and this is because the tracks are boring, the handling is mediocre and there's absolutely no progression in the game, once you buy a car you can stick with it all the way and don't ever feel a need to save up and buy something new. The AI:They're terrible as well and the game offers no real challenge, the other drivers look stiff and unnatural.The Graphics (Running on RTX 3070 with R9 5900HX):I thought this game was supposed to be "Next Gen" but I cannot stress it enough that it looks like something out of the PS3/Xbox one Era, The weather effects and lighting are the only saving grace, everything else is so flat and boring. With everything maxed out you're in for a real disappointment. The Handling: This game feels so bad, cars have no real noticeable behaviour between terrains and the driving is flat and boring. Closing comments:Genuinely if I got this game for free I'd still be disappointed sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has many flaws. However, it 100% owns at satisfying the need for which I bought it. I have been desperately missing the kind of epic, imaginative, fairly unrealistic, elevation-diverse tracks of Motorstorm Pacific Rift and the early Need for Speed games (original through High Stakes) or, to an extent, DriveClub. This game scratches that itch that I've had for years. I would buy just about any racing game that had such visually stunning environments as Dirt 5. For that I forgive it the flaws that I am sure are detailed in other reviews. I also kind of love the aggressiveness of the AI...they make aggression-on Forza drivers seem like they are on a prescription sedative. I've been wrecked out of competition in many races already...and since there's no rewind, that's a big deal...and yet I enjoy that they are able to race me as combatively as most human multiplayer opponents do. It's a much better practice for online racing than the AI of a lot of racing games. An on/off switch for aggression would likely be welcome for a lot of players, but I'd be keeping it on!I will also say that I dearly hope the developers add a way to share paint schemes ala Forza. I'm not a good artist but I LOVE running the magnificent designs that the community produces. Switching up paint schemes is probably the #1 reason I keep coming back to games like Forza, and hopefully Dirt 5.

_childDocuments_.review: The ♥♥♥♥ is up with all the truck races?Well for the most part, I knew what I was signing up for with Dirt 5. It looked more arcadey like Dirt 2 from the first trailer and to an extent it is. But maybe it’s the rose tinted goggles of nostalgia, but I don’t remember doing the same courses over and over and over through the career mode. That’s what you’re doing in 5. A lot of the same races again and again against some pretty stupid AI. Also there is some nasty rubber banding going on. Sometimes I was clearly in the lead by a wide gap and I did not hit anything or oversteer and another racer will just come from nowhere, pass me on the last bend and win the race....after I’d been leading for all of 3 laps....♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥They added a playgrounds mode where ppl can make their own tracks so once I’m done with career mode I’ll hit that up more. It’s decently fun.But honestly, it just all feels overall very poor. I don’t know if it’s the lack of more courses or the very dull challenge but Dirt 5 just doesn’t feel great. It’s not awful, but it is pretty boring compared to previous Dirts.

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat a AAA $60 game in 8 hours thanks to the free weekend. Checkmate capitalism.On a serious note though, the game is good fun. Career is pretty short if you just take one path like I did for the sake of time, but it'll take much longer if you want to finish every single one. Very arcadey feel with the cars that isn't for everyone, though.Only complaint is inconsistent difficulty. I picked hard and turned all driver assists off, and Sprintcar races were way harder than the rest of the game; it felt like a completely different game the way they played out that I'm not sure they really deserve a spot in Dirt 5. Besides that, some races were pretty competitive, while others, including the final race, were stupid easy. It was actually rather irritating that I pulled into the front on the last race after just one turn and ended up winning by over 10 seconds. It made the whole presentation about how epic that was really disingenuous. Also, this may just be a one-off, but Dirt Rally 2.0 looks better than this game and yet somehow runs way better. I could get 60+ fps on there but fps varied wildly in Dirt 5 for some reason. Soundtrack is boss and playground for track creation is elite. Those are the high points for me.Pick this game up for some good clean (read "dirty") racing fun when it's on sale. I wouldn't pay top dollar though.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks pretty... when you only look at the cars (immaculate) or from a distance. On the default difficulty, I was just walking away from the AI. Ok, I'll try bumping it up and... on hard, I'm still mostly walking away from them? Ok, VERY hard it is... and we're right to pulling teeth.The physics model feels a bit... too simple? _childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell, the problem with Dirt 5 is that it strays way too far from what Dirt has always been good at. I preordered the amplified edition of this (mistake) and played it for a few hours when it was released (bigger mistake, should've refunded the game). I finally tried to get back into it the last few days and I quickly remembered why I didn't keep playing it.- Terrible AI. The AI is incredibly inconsistent in difficulty, and doesn't follow the same set of physics as the player's car. That leads to some incredibly frustrating races where you get curbstomped by the AI right after a race where you easily beat them. Not to mention the AI vehicles don't get pushed around by your vehicle, which leads to the ridiculous scenario where they can spin you out with ease but can't be spun out at all by you.- Some of the worst physics I've seen in a AAA racing game. Dirt 5 is solidly in the arcade zone for driving, but every once in a while it decides that there's going to be slight elements of a more sim-focused game. Those moments really ruin any possible enjoyment of the arcade physics and make this a frustrating 90% arcade and 10% sim game where it's the worst of both worlds.- Lack of content. There's been a fair number of cars and tracks added (as far as I can tell), but the game still feels like there's barely any content. None of the tracks are memorable, and there's a surprising lack of cars that Codemasters has the models for and could have easily included in the game. The cars that are in the game have no customization aside from the livery maker, which is a poorly implemented system that I personally found to be one of the worst livery making systems I've ever seen. A majority of the cars that you would expect to have a historic or real-world race car livery don't have them either, which for a game series with a history of including them is not a good thing.- Progression. The progression system in this game makes zero sense. As you level up you unlock stickers for your cars (which are all really dumb) and backgrounds and stickers for a calling card (think Call of Duty). After all that garbage is unlocked you finally get to the stuff that is actually desirable, such as different patterns for the livery maker and pre-made liveries that vary widely in how good they look. To top it off, once you unlock these things you still have to buy them. Astoundingly bad design choice.- The audio. The cars all sound fine, as you'd hope for from a series that's been around for as long as Dirt has. The in-game music is generic and repetitive rock, which gets old fast and I found myself turning off the music after only an hour.- The game tries to make some type of story with these "podcasts" and annoying voiceovers that feature YouTubers. Unlike the Dirt 3 voiceovers, these ones just do not work with the game and come across as Codemasters trying to appeal to the YouTube crowd. The great thing about previous Dirt titles was that they didn't try to force a story, it was just going out and racing.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure it's an arcade racer but, it's a real fun one.No ridiculous grind for getting cars, money's not too terrible to come by.Being an arcade, the handling isn't too tricky (with a couple exceptions) and it's just overall fun.Most tracks are fairly unique and that's great, however it'd be nice to have more, but they'll be adding more over time.Career mode is a fun time sink, and the Playgrounds mode (aka create your own course) adds a whole bunch of the game.Ideal game for someone looking for a fun, more laid back offroad racing game.Graphics are pretty good, nothing groundbreaking though (however the lighting and weather effects are very very good).Soundtrack is a 10/10, absolutely fantastic.The launch was a bit rocky but many issues are now resolved, wheel support now works and crashes don't happen anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: As another game trying to get a piece of Forza Horizon's action, Dirt 5 gives up its identity and the clear direction that Dirt 4 showcased.In an attempt to diversify its game-play and change its image (to one that shallowly mirrors that of Forza Horizon), along the flashy brightly coloured panelling in the UI, and corny radio commentators, Codemasters made a large effort to turn rallycross-type racing into the core game.This didn't work.The game fails utterly to satisfy those looking for the challenging driving of rally stages in previous instalments of the series, and can never hope to live up to the brimming theme-park of activities that other, longer established games provide. The tracks are too wide and easy to navigate (with the dubious addition of a mini-map), visually unimpressive and similar, and there's no open world to pad the repetition, or game mode buried under free play to play through an actual regular rally stage without other cars on the track.In a poor departure from convention that diluted the value of one of their main franchises, Codemasters failed to understand why people play the Dirt series in the first place. While developing Dirt 5 and being aware of how low quality the included content is, it's impossible that no one at the studio realised that if someone wants collectibles and a wider range of activities, they would just play Forza instead; and if they wanted the handling of frozen bread on an oven tray, they could just play Need for Speed instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another case of something that works more as a standalone title and not part of a previously beloved franchise. Also the type of game to get either through EA Play subscription or buy on a massive sale.Physics are as arcade as it can get, and while it is missing the core of what made the DiRT series so good (pure rally) it still provides fun in other aspects brought back with new twists every now and then, such as rallycross, rock climbing, gymkhana, landrush and point-to-point raids. It even comes with a track creator if you're fancy for some creative Trackmania-styled gameplay. Personally, the only discipline I really didn't find fun was the oval sprintcars.Expect around 30 hours of racing and stunts (including all the DLCs and achievements), so it's not something that drags on for too long to complete. Story is ok, although with a bit too much Donut Media propaganda and cheesiness.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unfortunately very average and probably not even worth the 75% discounted price that I got it for. In terms of the positives, here they are;- The game looks good- the UI looks goodIn terms of negatives;- The handling model which is really the crux of all racing games. - Even with all assists turned off, it feels like the game still interferes with the handling of the car- Snap oversteer at random moments - You straight up aren't turning if you're not either on the throttle or the brakes- All vehicles feel super twitchy when on throttle - There is no vehicle tuning in the game. If you don't like the way a car feels/handles you are SOL- Some vehicle classes/events just don't work with the game engine. The chief offender are the rock climbing events. The game engine just can't handle it. I am sure I am underselling the positives of this game. As I understand the community made tracks are a major highlight of Dirt 5. However, I had no interest in trying them because I got bored of the campaign and the handling model within 2.2 hours. I think it says something about how average a game when only 31% of players make it past the first chapter of the story which turns into a boring slog due to the lack of locations, event types and tracks. Poor entry in the Dirt franchise overall.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I wanted to give this game a try since when it came out, but I wasn't sure about it with the mixed reviews and all. Up until this free weekend, I tried it, and I don't think I can recommend this game. Some of the basic option settings are missing (window/full-screen, V-sync, anti-aliasing, etc.). I've played the entire "career" mode and didn't do every single race. The music is good, so I'll give it that, I guess. But I feel like Codemasters have had no idea what to do with this game. It's like they wanted to make an arcade racer but didn't want to give it a soul, and that what this game feels like to me, just shallow, repetitive, braindead AI, and feels way too easy even on Medium difficulty. All in all, I don't recommend this game, I would pay this game at least $5 or free if Codemasters decides to do that, but even then, it's not worth it. I'll stick to Dirt Rally 2.0 since that's fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Like most other racing games released on PC, I was pretty much expecting this one to receive mixed/negative Steam reviews right out of the gate. A lot of (very fun) racing games tend to get slammed, and I think it’s because the racing games community is so insufferably elitist and whiny about literally everything that they just can’t enjoy a game for what it is. I.E. if a game isn't 100% realistic, or it doesn't 100% cater to their needs, then it must be garbage. Or so they make it seem.This astounds me. I don't remember people being this dismissive of arcade racers ~15 years ago. Have fans of racing games really become so closed-minded and prickly? Or was I just not on the internet as much back then?Either way, I somehow feel obligated to swing in and review racing games for their own merits... especially in the case of Dirt 5, which is probably the best offroad racing game I've played in years. To address some of the "complaints":Now that that's out of the way, here are some reasons why I actually love this game:Finally, I do think there are some legitimate issues with this game, which some other people have already pointed out. Here are my main problems:I think that's pretty much all I have to say for now. In short: If you're looking for realism (or rally driving), then don’t bother with this game. _childDocuments_.review: If you want a realistic racing-sim, do not get this. Go get Forza Horizons 4, Asseto Corsa, or Project Cars 2. Or, one of the past Dirt games. This is an arcadey-fun and flashy game, (to be honest, it probably shouldn't have been called Dirt 5. It should have been called Dirt Arcade, or something, as it does not nearly reflect the legacy that Dirt 3 and 4 left, nor Rally, or Rally 2.)But what this game sets out to do, which is create a fun, arcade experience of almost cinematic feeling races, and a beautiful look, it does fantastically. This is easily the most fun I've had behind the wheel in a long time, and it's a fantastic change of pace from the more grounded, competitive, and precise racing games I've become used to. This is a racing game that prioritises fun, excitement, and spectacle over all else. You won't get punished for minor mistakes like you do in other racing games, even on the hardest difficulty. And although that experience might not be for everyone, it's certainly a more layed back, and casual approach to the genre, which is something I think is perfect for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I hoped for nothing less than a BANGER. I am an arcade racer, and although DiRT Rally 2.0 turned out to be far more accessible for me than I thought, after DiRT4 that never knew what it was and what it wanted to be, the road was quite long to a new truly arcade DiRT. So what did I get with DiRT5? As always with Codemasters for some time now, it’s a mixed bag.Advertised as a combination of DiRT2 and DiRT3, I would say this is more like DiRT3 splashed with a bit of DiRT Showdown paint.The career mode closes in around 20+ hours. A bit short, albeit exactly in the DiRT Showdown paradigm. Future downloadable content might extend that a little (no new locations in DLC confirmed, though). For such a short racing game, 10 world locations we’ve got is almost enough, especially with the very good dynamic weather system significantly changing the look and rules of every race.Nicely fun vibe to it, amped up by an accessible driving model and AI that will always catch up to you after one mistake, very often also near the finish line.The music choices are accurate for this kind of game. The career  thing – a bit odd given that it stands contrarily to the dominant  vibe. At least you can customize your badge and car liveries while listening to it (it’s worth mentioning you can’t customize anything else about your cars besides that). There is a broad selection of vehicles, fairly good amount of pre-made liveries.Initial technical quirks have been quickly ironed out with patches before the 3-day early access ended (there were frequent crashes to desktop, sound was cracking a bit when game switched audio tracks while starting a race).Visually it’s OK but resembling much more the simplified aesthetics of DiRT Showdown than DiRT2/3. Things like flying aircrafts spraying colourful threads above you greatly add to that  vibe while you race.Poor configurability. So far no way to turn on exclusive full screen, no AA options. There is a button present with a function to pause the podcast, but you have no way of mapping any key to it (!), at least if you don’t use a controller. All these may be fixed in the future of course.For the first time in Codemasters game (at least for me) NO RACE REPLAY FUNCTIONALITY which is exactly where I did all my beautiful screenshots.WHAT. A. FACE. PALM.The narrator says to me . TOO BAD I CANNOT WATCH IT MYSELF AFTER I FINISHED IT – THAT’S SOME SLAP IN THE FACE, EH? The photo mode is present… in-race only (!!!) which is so immersion-breaking that I think I will puke right now. Huge no-no from me and at least one point taken from the overall score. (building race tracks from pre-made elements and posting them for everyone to enjoy) is promising, time will tell. I’m glad Gymkhana’s back and that it can also be utilized there, but I very much wish they added modes like  or  to career to make it less bland.Overall DiRT5 is for people who know what they’re getting into, aware they won’t be experiencing DiRT Rally 3.0 here. It is a lot of fun. I recommend. Just keep in mind DiRT2 and 3 still stand higher for me in  DiRT branch. 7/10PS. Three more things: 1) Hiding that the game won’t have any wheel support to late November was a shot in the foot. Surely the game was catered mostly to arcade fans but it was a case of honesty. 2) As always I’m not touching multiplayer, so I won’t tell you anything about that. 3) All in all I don’t think Codies deserve the nasty treatment they get in Steam reviews; always makes me wonder if they’ll decide to publish any more of their games here.

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from the lacking wheel support in the beginning (mind that DiRT4, DiRT3 do support my wheel without issue out of the box from day one) this is a disappointing release. Why? => TL;DR: If you have DiRT games, don't buy this. If you have no DiRT games, then DiRT3 might be a better option. Also if you're interested in realism, please just stick to the DiRT Rally series and there's no way to compare the two series, they're two different things. This is Arcade Fun, DiRT Rally series is more realistic. So if you come complaining about that here, please don't. DiRT = arcade fun - wel it used to be, now it feels like a grind..... => Read The good/bad/ugly(shameful) points belowTHE BAD: - The career is repetitive and brings nothing new to the table, it even takes away a lot what we got in DiRT3 & DiRT4.  - Sponsor goals & career difficulty just aren't transparant how you gain money and/or points. - Cars feel lackluster and oversteer massively. Yes we are driving on dirt and we drive on ice and it is an arcade game, but the cars all feel wildly out of control. See that in context with mark below... - No options for sensitivity, deadzone etc for the GamePad... And let's not talk about the wheel support that is missing... I mean, come one. - Damage doesn't exist. I can live with that, it's arcade. But visual damage is just lacking a lot compared to competitors. Also, the dirt build up is so repetitive and doesn't hold up... It's as you progress through a race it's textures slapped on. - Online doesn't bring a lot of new things to the table, races aren't cool because there's no penalties in place. This then becomes WreckFest, but at least in WreckFest you have the bonus of Wrecking your opponent or the strategy of staying out of their way.. Here, there's no penalties what so ever... It is not engaging racing against other people, feels just like racing against AI... That is a real problem!THE (mildly) GOOD: - A cool system for building custom tracks. That is a nice point, however, it's cumbersome to build. Especially on PC... That port could've been better. MOUSE & KEYBOARD support hello?? The tracks you can build are also lacking compared to competitors, try TRACKMANIA in stead, you'll see what I mean. - The graphics are great. I love them, colorful, exactly on point for a game like this. Applying your own textures and customising the cars is fun, but is nothing new. It has been done before and brings nothing fancy or new to the table though... We've seen this before. - The sound, holds up pretty well. Nothing new here. If you don't like the commentating/podcast, just turn it off. If you don't like the music, you can turn it off. I sometimes like it, sometimes I don't. But we are given the option. I feel it wasn't needed to put such focus on the podcast/radio style - it is confusing and the "story" isn't really clear.THE GOOD: - Nothing really.THE SHAME: - They focused on buying awards before it was released... They should have focused on spending that money on deeper and richer features, wheel support, gamepad configuration of deadzone/filtering/sensitivity in steering and more texture/customisation options. As well as a deeper career mode where one feels engaged to play it. - They left out a lot of features of the great DiRT3 on which they could have built on, also some features of DiRT4 (which wasn't received well) that were good enough to build on. This feels like a grind. A grind for the player. The fun is over after 12 races. You've seen it all, there's nothing new to live up to or to expect. The storytelling is off, no incentive to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure how I feel about the game since I only played like half an hour, but I don't know if I'll play more, so.Dirt 5's not really for me, I don't know who it is for though.Rally is definitely like a very specific kinda driving thing with specific players specifically interested in it, and rallycross which this game sorta seems to be mainly focused around is... something like that, but just not the same. Every race is held on a dedicated track and the game is all about sponsors and stuff, and it seems like a really weird and awkward combination of like traditional racing, or F1, and rally. Is rallycross even that popular?I'm more into... various other kinds of racing with sports cars and things like that, games where the cars don't all look and drive the exact same way, games such as... Need for Speed Hot Pursuit 2 (2002). I can appreciate other good driving games too but this one is a little... well, the physics are noticeably arcade-y, they're not too absurd like a Burnout type game, but they're definitely not realistic, nothing like Assetto Corsa for instance.I don't really get who they were trying to make this game for, and the concept itself seems kinda simple, like there's not a whole lot of variety of gameplay in the game.The graphics are alright. It has that same sort of look, with the high saturation highlights and such.Uh... yeah, I wish I could give like a thumbs... middle, but I can't, so... I wouldn't really recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: DIRT 5 is a return to arcade racing without a rally mode, but it is sadly one of the weakest games in the series. Most of the pieces are here, yet they are a few notches below Codemasters’ stellar efforts from nine years ago. The career is bland, with a phoned-in story and limited variety. The vehicle handling is not quite right and the AI has annoying idiosyncrasies. Multiplayer is poorly implemented and it already lacks competitors. Only the Playgrounds mode, where people can build and race custom tracks, is a welcome surprise, although even that is held back by some technical problems. If you are desperate for an arcade racer then DIRT 5 may suffice, but this is a missed opportunity, much like Showdown. At least now there is a litmus test to determine if a DiRT game is good—without rally, not really.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game... I really did. But the more and more I play it, the less I can find anything positive to say about it.It's hard to imagine that just a few years ago, Codemasters was on the top, with titles like Dirt 3. Grid 2, some solid F1 games. The Dirt franchise itself has shifted gears entirely. For starters, there is not a single rally in this game; not one. It's all closed course offroad arcade racing, but without any sense of speed at all. I read someone else's review where they said it feels like you have a balloon tied to your car, and that hits the nail on the head. You feel so heavy and slow, but then your vehicle feels like it's on a damn slip-'n-slide. The racing is just not fun, no matter how vibrant they try to make it look.This is one of the VERY few games I've ever preordered, and I was so hopeful to see the franchise make a comeback, but the initial release was terrible, and each update that gets released every couple months is worse and worse. I've "completed" this game three times now, but then the next update comes out with 5 more achievements, some "new" events, and a new car or two. But it's all the same ♥♥♥♥. The events are on the same tracks, and it feels like such a chore to complete them all. The cars feel the same as all the others, and the only reason you should bother driving them is for their specific achievements. And the achievements themselves are the exact same every time around: "Win X event and X event," "Drive 30 miles in the newly released vehicle," "Collect all the stamps for this series." They call this content, but it's the same rehashed garbage you finished last time. It's boring, and every time I have to come back to get everything done again, I feel like my intelligence is being mocked for having paid money for this in the first place.Maybe I'm asking for too much when I say that I want something closer to Dirt 2 or 3 (at this point, I'd even take another Dirt 4), but somehow, somewhere Codemasters lost their direction and started pumping out uninspired racing experiences. This is one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of racing games from Codemasters, from the GRID series, to DIRT, even the F1 games, and I think the more of them you have played before this, the better you can categorise where this fits in terms of playstyle and what you're looking for in a racing game.If you're looking for a racing game that has variety, an arcade feel to the driving and discipline of each race, and splashing your cars with the brightest colours and decals, this is almost your type of game! (almost explained further down).If you're looking for something with more of a lean into the physics and strategy, the actual ‘rally’ side and stage races, and something with more of a serious look, I suggest looking to the DIRT/DIRT 2.0 side of the racing games, or GRID if your looking for the asphalt style gameplay.This game is similar to DIRT 2 and Dirt 3 in its presentation, but with the lack of the ‘rally’ side and more into the circuit races, land rushes and the ‘Stampede mode’ its a large chunk of its identity removed (maybe something they add in who knows).From the get go, it would seem there is some issues with graphics, bugging out and there being fewer options to turn graphics up for now, and with the lack of compatibility to use a steering wheel and pedals makes me raise an eyebrow, most other games released has this so why not DIRT 5? It could have been pushed back ever so slightly so this could be implemented possibly? Im sure in the next few weeks, these things will be ironed out, but it seems to be turning players off straight away from what i’ve seen and heard.If you fancy a couple of races kicking back and just enjoying playing a racing game, this is for you. If you're a more serious rally racer where you sit on the edge of your sofa genuinely so engrossed in getting the best split times on a rally stage, and you don't even see the sun coming up to indicate you’ve been playing 9 hours straight saying ‘one more race’ to yourself, I’d turn to some of codemasters' other titles. Where you get the best of both worlds, like DIRT 2 and DIRT 3, or even the GRID Series. It would seem the game follows suit like many other developers where games are being stripped down to make way for other areas, like more colours, faster frame rates, 4k and easier access for a wider array of gamers, rather than the focus of the specific range of fans.Don't get me wrong, i like this game and would recommend it to anyone, with the warning to play it, not to invest time and effort. Little effort is needed to play this game, sometimes that's what you want, other times you want more to bite into. Thats why its almost the game you want.I’d like to note that assuming this was still being worked on when we were all hit by the pandemic, they've still cracked out a decent game. I get people spend their hard earned cash on these games and expect certain things, but I've genuinely seen people say on forums and reviews that these coders or developers should be sacked or even that Codemasters should go bankrupt because it's not like DIRT 2 or 3. That they should have remastered one that was better to keep people happy. If developers don't ‘develop’ new games, and just remastered everything they did well, people would then complain that they make nothing new and churn out the same old thing over and over again, so be thankful that they made a new game, did some things different, may not be perfect but not everything is, if it was gamers would never buy the newest thing because perfection was already achieved.To the people who wish for people to lose jobs or for companies to go bankrupt (also as devastating for the people who work there and their families), all because you spent money on a game you didn't like or because there's a few issues 2 days after release… maybe your part of the problem. (reminder that you can refund games on steam under 2 hours played if you so wish).Enjoy what you want to enjoy and build your own opinion of this game, my advice to you? You like racing games? Enjoy what this game has to offer you :) Hope this helps people decide, stay safe! :)
