_childDocuments_.review: It's times like this I wish Steam had a 'maybe' button for recommendations, because DIRT 5 is a maybe. I bought this game 50% off whilst on sale, and I can honestly say that you should do the same if you want to try this game out, because you will be disappointed if you pay full price.The TL;DR for this review is simple: DIRT 5 is all show and no substance. It tries to be somewhere between pre-4 DiRT and Showdown and... that's kinda a bad thing. Whilst it does borrow features from 2019 GRID (also not a brilliant game), those are mostly cosmetic in nature.I think to understand where DIRT 5 is coming from, one needs to look back to DiRT Rally. DiRT Rally is where the series began to split into two. It was an experiment of trying out a more simulation-based gameplay style. It was a great success, and led to DiRT 4... which disappointed the arcade crowd. So DiRT Rally 2.0 came along, and rather than being an experiment, DiRT Rally became a spin-off series. So it took all the simulation-slanted gameplay with it and left us with... this.Now there are ways to make an arcade game great. GRID 2, for instance. At first, it worried GRID fans because they were scared of this becoming the future of GRID, but then GRID Autosport came along (remind you of anything?) and GRID 2 became celebrated as some arcady fun. DIRT 5 is not GRID 2. What made GRID 2 great was the racing. Yes, the controls made drifting overpowered and unnatural, but the racing was still great. Tracks were still challenging. GRID 2's style is what you'd expect if someone was to say that a particular game in a Codemasters racing series was overly-arcady. And if you like that sort of thing, you'd say "great, as long as the sim games still continue to be made".If you're not that experienced in Codemasters games in general, the above paragraph probably means nothing to you, so let me elaborate on why DIRT 5 misses the mark. Firstly, the tracks. They are WAY too wide. There is no challenge in them. You do occasionally actually have to hit the brakes, but generally, there's a huge room for error that means making a mistake costs you next to nothing. I also set the difficulty to very hard (the hardest setting)... and still dominated the next race - a raid track I had never driven before, nor was I driving particularly well at the time.So basically, if you enjoyed GRID 2 and expect DIRT 5 to be like that... you will be disappointed.Thankfully, it's not as ridiculously arcady as DiRT Showdown, but that's not a hard margin to beat. Take away the obstacles though, and the DiRT Showdown tracks... kinda start resembling the sort of thing you see in DiRT 5.Which leads to the stylistic nature of the game. Ugh... DIRT 5 might be all show and no substance, but that doesn't mean what is shown is a GOOD show. Gameplay is narrated by what appears to be a fictional podcast, featuring two American casters. Those familiar with Codemasters will see where this is going already, because Codemasters + overly aiming toward an American audience has... had mixed results in the past. Needless to say, this podcast routine gets old FAST. REALLY fast. To the extent that the game would be better with no narration at all. And the rest of the 'show'...? Sudden onset of heavy rain was a jarring experience for me after driving about 75% of a raid race in bone-dry weather. Overly bright lighting on overly dark tracks makes for irritating levels of visibility. And for the life of me, I could not find a replay option after finishing a race (despite all the livery customisation and show-focused track designs that would suggest the game was built for replays).So... my verdict...? 5/10. If you want to buy it, get it on sale. Otherwise, go play Forza Horizon. Forza Horizon does what this game is trying to do AND makes it fun AND challenging AND has a sandbox/free-roaming map to play on AND has better driving physics to boot.-------------------10 HOUR UPDATE-------------------Whilst a more in-depth experience doesn't necessarily alter the opinions shown in the initial review, more extensive gameplay has shown me that DIRT 5 isn't ALL bad. There are one or two tracks that are actually quite fun. And for more landrush-focused cars, the track width mentioned earlier in the review is generally alright. The AI can also pose a challenge on certain tracks - and be impossibly overpowered on others (like those dreaded sprint races). Many of the tracks are too open and flowy to really memorise well, even with the changing scenery, because the actual track geometry is so samey, whilst others you really get to actually enjoy the shifting terrain, landmarks and flow. A good example is a track that goes from being outside a stadium to passing through said stadium, to going through what looks like an indoor parking lot. It has tight turns, it has visually and mechanically distinct sections, it is essentially what I wish the rest of the tracks were.Another complaint I've developed is how the AI handles car characteristics. Some cars are overpowered in the AI control, despite their stats on paper being mediocre (I'm looking at you, F-150 Raptor), others keep up with the pack surprising well whilst a player in the same car might have to battle harder than they would in a competing vehicle (like the Mini buggy). And the AI seems to have less issue in slippery conditions which suggests they don't quite follow the same physics rules as the player, particularly when it comes to things like acceleration out of a corner on ice or snow... or in a sprint car.DIRT 5 is a great game to play whilst listening to podcasts or D&D livestreams or music. You don't need to pay a HUGE amount of attention, your interest is maintained by the constant influx of cosmetic rewards for race results and whilst the actual gameplay has it's limits, it isn't horrendous. I'll maintain my 5/10 rating, however.

_childDocuments_.review: I really recommend players to observe well the gameplay, trailers, and do a little bit of research of what the game has to offer. I have mixed feelings about this game, it is a bold change and a much more different approach to what DIRT 5's predecessors has to offer, such as DIRT 4, but my mistake is expecting too much out of DIRT 5 and not really understanding what this game tries to deliver, so in the end, I was disappointed. Make sure you do those things I mentioned above to not make a mistake like I did.DIRT 5 to me is more of an arcade and slightly casual approach to the DIRT racing games. To me its like Travis Pastrana's Nitro Circus but completely on four wheels. Lots of wicked jumps, paint-trading, some crashes and rolls, as well as allowing you to drive an extensive range of different vehicles from different classes. Some of these vehicles are crazy, ones I did not expect would come in a DIRT game, such as a stock Aston Martin DBX (Yes and you get to send it off of some 100m jump).However do mind that if you are someone who is looking for a sequel to DIRT 4 (Myself included), seeking for improvement and extension of what DIRT 4 has to offer, this is absolutely not the game you are looking for. Personally, you are way better of buying DIRT Rally 2.0 if you're looking for such things. I couldn't emphasize how important it is that this is not a racing simulation like the DIRT Rally series or even DIRT 4. Personally the cars feel like they don't have much of a character, unlike in other DIRT games. Its more of which car is faster and which is slower. Details of the cars are okay, but because it isn't a racing simulation, details such as the interior or the animations of driving in the cockpit (Shifting gears, pulling the handbrake, etc.) are massively lacking to me.There are no events like World Rally Cross or even any classic rally modes. DIRT 5 events are all about adrenaline rush, airtime on jumps, drifts, and absolutely sending whatever you are driving while looking good on TV. So, don't get your hopes up on expecting new World RX tracks, new mechanics in fine tuning your car for your next event, or basically, any aspect of racing simulation.However, if you like casual or arcade-ish racing games with great visuals and fun events, this is the game for you. For me, Not so much.EDIT : If you are looking for a worthy successor of DIRT 4, I can confirm now that DIRT Rally 2.0 is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be clear - Dirt5 is marketed wrong. This was a mistake. They've labelled it as Dirt5, but the reality is this should have been called Dirt Arcade, and it's led to a lot of angry players who expected the usual accurate rally sim game and ended up with brash Americans and lots of pink colours.And guess what? I absolutely love it. I knew this wasn't an accurate rally sim, and was much more in keeping with the classic Sega Rally games of yesteryear, and this is a supercharged modern version.It looks great, it plays great, it's a blast of a game to play, and it sure doesn't take itself seriously.For those who loved the likes of Sega Rally 1 & 2 this is perfect - if you want a modern version of that, with opponents in most races, and big fat bangy cars and lots of speed, this is for you.But yes, the name did suggest it was like Dirt Rally, which is a whole other ball game. Thankfully Steam do refunds.But even more thankfully, the way this game is is bang on to what I expected from it. So yeah, not for everyone!

_childDocuments_.review: OK I feel I have been a bit harsh on this game as in an attempt to fix performance problems I disabled "full screen optimisations" when in fact this just made it worse. So I've changed it back and it now runs smooth. This game is the best looking racing game so far with all the lighting, shadow and particle effects and is very demanding. I was getting stuttering as I thought an RX 6800 and a Zen 3 5600x should be enough to play game on Ultra at 4k. I was wrong and I was probably expecting too much from my GPU. I've managed to get  the game to play smooth at 120fps on 4k monitor with the following settings.Firstly I overclocked GPU RX6800 with:Minimum frequency of 2200Maximum frequency 2300Voltage (mV) 1025Vram 2150 (default timing)Power Limit + 15%Fan Curve: Fan Speed:    50, 60, 75, 90, 100Temperature: 50, 60, 70, 80,  90Then the following settings in game:Image Quality: HighVSync: OnDynamic Resolution: OnFinal Resolution: NativeHistory Resolution: 50% NativeRender Resolution: 75% NativeGeometry Quality: HighTessellation Quality: Ultra HighShadow Quality: MediumVolumetric Quality: HighCloud Quality: MediumProcedural Quality: MediumGlobal Illumination Quality: HighFidelityFX Ambient Occlusion: MediumThis was in order to maintain a solid 120 FPS and eliminate stuttering.History Resolution 50% is = to having anti aliasing on low so I do get a shimmering on the track but the game still looks beautiful and pretty next gen and I believe high fps is important in a racing game. Obviously those players with a RTX 3080/RTX 3090/RX 6800XT or RX 6900 will be able to play at 4k with better settings and may be able to do a Native Render Resolution or have 60 FPS as a target, which I tried initially but with some stuttering so I sacrificed image quality for FPS. I wish this game was more optimised and ran as smooth as Forza Horizon 4 but it does have many more effects and detail. There are a lot of tracks, they are often repeated with different lay outs and different weather conditions, time of day etc but I think there is great variety and I'm finding the game pretty addictive. The sound track is growing on me too and I like how it is a live music track playing around the racing circuit so it gets louder and quieter as you approach speakers then drive away.  And a good variety of cars to unlock that are based on real life cars with damage although the damage is visual only and doesn't effect your drive, which I prefer.It is a great arcade dirt racer and I hope it continues to be optimised so I can increase the game settings for better visual fidelity. It does have an annoying bug where the mouse pointer keeps popping up. Surely it is not hard to hide the mouse pointer if an Xbox One Controller is being used? I hope Codemasters fixes this as a priority.

_childDocuments_.review: This deserves better than a "mixed" rating. Sure wheel support should be there, but honestly youd be mad to play this with a wheel... it's just not that kind of game. Really, really good controls on a gamepad. Realistic? Not in the slightest. But FUN! Its just perfectly tuned for an arcade racer, giving you enough to do so you don't feel like you're driving a train, while staying very accessible. Here's the thing: rather than making you think "man these controls are easy" it makes you think "man I am GOOD at this" which is just something that's missing from so many pc racing titles.I also haven't yet noticed any obnoxious rubber banding, if you're better than the pack, you stay comfortably ahead. Plus paying some minor attention to racing lines does actually make a difference.I love simracers, but sometimes you just wanna kick back and blast a car at ludicrous speed around some corners, and on pc there's not a lot of games that do that well. This one, however, does.I will say Im only 1.5h in and the campaign already feels phoned in. I don't mind that much cause the driving is a blast, but I do miss when racing games had stories and a sense of progression. At which point did every racing game start showering you with enough cash to buy half the vehicle roster after like 3 races? Plus it just gives you the cars you need anyway! Why even bother with a money system then?Anyway, I'm having a blast with it, and I'm a bit surprised at all the negative reviews. I think its a great purchase on sale. Haven't played enough to say whether it would be worth a full price purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I want to like this game so bad.DiRt 2-3 were some of my favorite racing games ever, I even really enjoyed Showdown.But this game just isn't it.Pros:Lots of cars, and the roster is a lot more diverse than previous games.Good Soundtrack.Awesome environments and weather.The "fun" and colorful/festival vibes from DiRt 2 and Showdown.Decent arcade racer.Cons:Atrocious AI.Dated graphics.Handles nothing like a DiRt game.Terrible difficultly scaling.Terrible optimization and performance.Some of my biggest problems are with the AI, and the fact that they seem JUST that. They all drive like your completely invisible to them, meaning they will slam into you or run you right off the road if you get in their path at all.The difficulty scaling in this game seems all kinds of wonky too, you're either leaving the pack behind and racing by yourself. Or the AI is rubberbanding like crazy and performing manuvers that just isn't possible to do yourself.Handling isn't awful but something the DiRt series is known for is it's more realistic handling.The core series (not Rally or 2.0) have always had a much more arcady feel but this game handles more like a Need For Speed game than DiRt which kinda irks me.Graphics and performance are just bad.Oddly enough for a game that seems to be targeting the "next gen" crowd even cranked up to max settings the game looks very dated.Weather and environments look great, but the actual cars themselves which you would think would be the selling point have gross textures and terrible reflections.In fact, I'd even go as far to say that DiRt 3 or Showdown looks much better graphically. And those games are some years old.Graphics rather you like it or not can be kind of a big deal for racing games.But I would be able to overlook it, if it weren't for the fact that not only does this game look very dated, it runs like absolute poop. Even on high end setups.I run a Ryzen 9 3900x and a 2080 super and an barely pulling about 60-65 frames at 1080p lmao.Overall, sadly I have to give this game a thumbs down right now.I'll change that, if things improve. But right now you can pay half of this and get something like Forza Horizon and get a full AAA experience.(I should also note I paid $30 on cdkeys for this game, instead of the full $60 or I'd probably be pissed)

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to log a considerable amount of hours before finally reviewing this game.  You see that I've logged 26 at this time, which in itself is a testament to the quality of this game; there is no way I could've spent this many hours with any game if I wasn't enjoying myself.  I haven't played a DIRT title since DIRT 2, so bear that in mind when considering my opinion.  To me, this feels like a highly refined experience of what was offered in those early titles, namely the breakneck speeds, flashy lights, and buttery smooth driving mechanics.  The gameplay, for better or worse, has been streamlined so as to offer an experience that is easy to pick up and difficult to master.  If you're looking for strict-simulation then you should look elsewhere.  Also, the story is bare-bones and wholly uninspired, though the performances of North and Baker are entertaining to listen to, at least the first time around.  Codemasters recent acquisition by Take-Two could provide a wonderful opportunity to incorporate an honest story mode into the series, should they proceed further in that direction.  And I hope they do, because the racing mechanics in this game are so much fun.  You can be serious and improve your lap times, or you can drift around hairpin turns like a pro if you just want to relax and unwind after a long day.  The weather effects are some of the best in the business, and you will be simultaneously frustrated and amazed, racing at night in a heavy snowstorm, with strategically timed lightning strikes to illuminate the track at key turns during the races.  My point being that Codemasters has the assets and capability to make a fully realized career mode racing game, the likes of which has never been seen.  With the solid mechanics presented in DIRT 5, the series is in a good place.Edit 12/15/20 - EA swooped in and purchased Codemasters before the Take Two acquisition could take place.  May God have mercy on our souls.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game for free and I want my money back.No seriously, this has got to be one of the worst games I have every played. Not just racing games, but games in general.For one, the game runs like absolutely ass. I play at 3440x1440 and I can barely scrape 75ish FPS average on high. I only get about 90 FPS average on low. The game looks decent, but for the performance it demands, it looks terrible. I play FH4 at max settings and get a constant, fluid 120 FPS. Dirt 5 makes my 1080 Ti feel like a 750 Ti.Second, the physics are absolute junk. Cars feel arcade-y, but not like Forza Horizon arcade-y. They feel like they are on ice, and all RWD. The tail ends always want to kick out. Some of the vehicles you give it gas and it starts getting sideways going straight...on an entry level car. They are hard to control and are just not fun or engaging.I liked Dirt 3, I even liked Dirt 4. I don't mind the arcade feel that these games have, they are fun to play. I even liked Dirt Rally, even if I'm not very good at it. I've always been a big fan of the Dirt games, but 5 is just a slap in the face. There isn't even rally racing. Come on Codemasters.I have 8 TB of storage in my PC. I never uninstall games, in which I have over 300 of, because I like to be able to play them at any time. I actually uninstalled this game and moved it out of my main Steam library category. I'll never play this waste of space again. Don't waste your money, don't even waste your time trying, thinking you'll just get a refund if you don't like it. You will be sorely disappointed. Either play older Dirt games, or just get FH4 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: What to say, what to say... I don't write a lot of reviews but I need to get this written down (and hopefully out of my head until I die).I've played every Codemasters rallye game since "Colin McRae Rallye 1" (which my dad bought for me as a kid). And all of them were fun! Not perfect but all good and fun simulation-ish racers. That's why I bought Dirt 5 without reading any ratings - I was sure it was going to be a cool simulation-like racing experience like all the others and I wanted to support Codemasters to never stop what they are doing.I am so disappointed. I've tried a few online games and instantly fired up Dirt Rally 2.0 to ease my despair. My god DR2.0 was so good. Also started Wreckfest after that, also 1000x better than Dirt 5 - just no powerfull AWDs...What are my issues with this game, even after only playing for a few hours?1) Handling feels so synthetic. If you own an older Dirt Game and like the feel of "realism" don't buy this. It's a ♥♥♥ ARCADE RACER - even in hardest mode without any driving aids..2) Multiplayer is sh* (to be "fair" - that one was never really good in any codemasters racing games... but not as bad as this one)- you can't start an own game, can't choose track etc...;- there is only "matchmaking" which will throw you in any kind of game; - the game is out for a few days now and you hardly find any match (obviously, no one want's to play this way online);- no in-lobby communication (as usual... nothing new; why? I want to talk to my fellow racers! Take a look at how other games to this, e.g. wreckfest; nothing fancy, just a chat in between races is fine).- only arcade-style racing. why codemasters, why do you do that to your Dirt-Community?3) sound. wtf happend to the great sounds... ;-(4) to be continued if I ever start up this game again. _childDocuments_.review: The Arcade style DiRT games have always been a hit for me, but this title has something wrong. Everything feels rushed, unfinished and abandoned. Aside the games racing feeling repetitive and boring at times, the main aspect of this problem is the atrocious physics.Colliding with other vehicles feels horribly unsatisfying, closely meeting the look and feel of a 2000's flash game. On top of that, the player's car will glitch out and spin uncontrollably when in an accident roughly 90% of the time. It wouldn't be a problem if it was insignificant, but I mean downright clipping around basic surfaces and bouncing like a basket ball, which can make a winning race into an impossible one.Topping it all off are the lackluster damage engine, very basic damage system with the inability to repair vehicles properly when a race restarts.The photo mode camera is god awful. while it has some neat features it's completely unusable on keyboard and doesn't even have a button to take pictures, only a hide UI button (Which often forgets to hide parts of the UI).Wouldn't recommend, not even on sale. The game is rushed and done improperly, creating a mixed bag of beautiful graphics with horrible glitches and unsatisfying gameplay. Do not buy this title.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Terrible, repetitive and way too easy game, bad handling model and dead multiplayer. Sprint cars suck!I decided to give this game a go on the free weekend, and it was as big disappointment as i was expecting.Pretty much everything is wrong with this game.Let's start from the biggest problem, the handling model. For some reason, the handling feels wrong. It took me a while to put my finger on the main cause of this problem. There is no lift-oversteer. No matter what the situation is, lifting gas will make your car quickly straighten up and understeer. This causes loads of crashing into the outside walls and awkward moments, where you would want to oversteer, but can't and end up slowly going off the track because the car refuses to turn.Another very annoying thing is that some cars tend to be way too responsive to the steering. Little touch to the analog stick and the car snaps almost sideways.Then we have the game itself. The career mode is mostly pretty cool if you just want to progress to the last race and leave the rest of the races untouched. Playing through every single race gets really boring really fast. There is even multiple identical races, with the same track and car class.But still, the biggest flaw in the career is the fact it's so easy, you could probably win most of the races while reversing. You are oftenly 30 seconds to a minute ahead of the AI, even though the AI doesn't seem to have same physics as you, and their cars are more powerful.Talking about the AI, it's probably the worst AI i've ever seen. You can hardly even call them AI.They will stricktly follow the exact path they have been assigned to and don't care about other cars, be it another AI or the player car.The most annoying thing about the AI is that they create huge roadblocks and getting past them is nearly impossible when they go 4-wide into a tight corner. And they brake comically early for the corner, and nearly stop in the corners. Extremely frustrating experience.The AI is especially rage inducing in the sprint car races.Like many have already complained, the sprint races (in the sprint car) are absolute crap.The car is impossible to drive, the AI is unlike the rest of the game, way overpowered here, as they have way more grip. The AI will also keep constantly pushing you into the outside wall, and even touching the wall will end your race. No possible way to win a race after making even one mistake, as there is nowhere near enough laps to catch up again.The race lenghts don't make any sense either. One race might be over in under a minute, while the next one takes +7 minutes.The different race types are very confusing too. There are multiple different names for seemingly the same kind of race. 3 (or 5) laps around a track. Most of the game consist of these races. There are few other types of races. Ice circuits, gymkhana, sprint races and pathfinder, a sort of rock-crawling race.The pathfinder seemed to be the most interesting out of all of them, but there are a few glaring problems in it.First of all, there is only 3 tracks. When you drive them the first time, it's really interesting and fun, but after that, it feels just repetitive and pointless.Another thing is, that the absolutely terrible physics will freak out randomly during the race, and all sorts of weird things will happen. Your car can suddenly flip over, do a wheelie, get stuck on something or just fall through the floor.I can't comment about the online play. It's completely dead. Tried to find a game a few times, but not even a single soul online even during free weekend.With most of the negative things out o the way, some positives.The graphics and enviroments look really good most of the time, but the graphic style might not be for everyone.There are a few places where you can clearly see texture repetition though, kinda ruins it for me.Some areas (tunnels, etc) are way too dark and require you to momentarily drive blind.Car headlights are also way too weak, and on some car, the lights don't even seem to be on, but it still illuminates the ground in front of you,The weather effects are absolutely beautiful, not including the sandstorm. The sandstorm looks like ♥♥♥♥.The livery editor for the cars is a nice thing to have, even for being fairly basic. You can still come up with cool designs when combining different liveries and patterns.Sound effects are nice and crisp. Maybe a bit too much on the straight into you face territory.Cars sounds on the other hand are... lacking to say at least. Pretty much every car sounds exactly the same.The soundtrack is horrible though. It consists mostly of bland and generic, or absolutely ear-piercingly terrible radio-pop songs.Unless you are deaf, or have a completely garbage taste of music, do yourself a favour and turn of the music.Oh, and there is a track editor of some kind. You can make tracks, i guess.All in all, the game feels like an early alpha build. It's supposed to be a finished product, but it's clearly not.Even though pretty much all of the soul of the Colin McRae series has been lost, even dropping the rally events completely, the game could've had some potential. But at it's current state, it's not worth buying even if on sale. Find something better to play, like DiRT 3 for example if you can get a hold of a copy of it.

Maybe if you get it for €10 or so, as it isn't bad just "meh".Edit after 9.9 hours played:Game kept crashing but I finished the career mode despite this (crashed every 15-20 minutes, so roughly 30-40 crashes during my playthrough), so around 10 hours is what you can expect from the campaign. Now I feel done with the game, would rate it at a 6/10 if I didn't have the crashing issues, how this is considered a 9/10 or even 5/5 by some reviewers is beyond me. Saw little to no point in buying more than one additional car in every category, so had little use for the funds you earn, best cars locked behind paid DLC. Game tried very hard to get me in the store almost every time I started it. Becuse of this it feels more like a F2P and the base game only exists to get you to buy DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: (Similar to GRID 2019 but on Dirt)It’s 100% a gamepad/controller game, you feel that instantly. So don’t even bother with the steering wheels you got. There are moments where you feel the car is taking you for a ride rather than you taking the car for a ride. The game will hold your hand. This feeling you won’t be able to get rid-off, even with all the assists turned off. If you are used to racing games at times this gets really annoying to a point you want to throw the controller.Well… they are super similar to GRID 2019 but there is more of it. Whereas GRID lacked content here you have way more and with that more to see.I follow Donut Media on YouTube and well they are just the same in game. There were moments of SSX3 nostalgia when driving in deep snow and having similar voice overs and music.Music is actually not bad at all it fits the game, but there is not much of variety. So about an hour in I had to mute it.Looks like GRID 2019 though with other environments and assets.Not the best not the worst. Do however think F1 2020 and Dirt Rally 2.0 look better.You know those participation medals you got as a kid in school so everyone feels good. Well this game is like that everyone in this game is good. Being good in racing games does not feel at all rewarding in this game. This also comes down to the dumb AI, there is this fake difficulty as in the cars just outperform what the cars are able to do in order to make it feel more challenging.Well not much of a story, but Donut Media guys sure was enjoyable to listen to. I do hope they’ll do more stuff in the upcoming DLC’s. Yes as you guessed I finished it before the game even got officially released, 3 days before it got officially released. Took me about 8 hours, but then again I really took my time with extra races and so forth. So perhaps 5-6 hours long.Very bad, the game crash more than you crash with cars in the game. Had 7 crashes within 2 hours all from doing different things, so as you expect the game also runs quite bad, not really well optimized.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this game really, but the more i played the more i realized that this is going nowhere. Its just an endless grind with only rallycross races (90% of the races) and nothing else. Dlc's gave almost nothing new, only more and more grind.After 2 hours no more game modes, and there are no rally stages, no rallying mode at all, it doesn't feels like your'e playing a dirt game, even in older or less popular games like sega rally or gravel i had more fun than with this. First of all you cant crash out, or slide out other cars, you can bump into them yeah, but their car is like weights 20 tons and made out of solid steel, almost no effect crashing into them.This game is quite easy most of the times, (medium difficulty) the ai drives slow, with at least 50 meters behind you, but wtf sometimes in the last few meters before the finish line they turn into crazy rocket mode, and they can easily outrun you, they gain unfair speed just like that, and you only finish 3rd or worse, even though you where 1st for 5 minutes, there must be some hidden nitro button in the game that i haven't found yet?Most races are easy to win, while others are incredible hard like the oval races in sprint cars, those cars are crap.  You can finish hill-climbs with over 1 minute faster that your opponents, gymkhanas are laughably easy, the point to win needs to be at least twice as much as this.And no replay mode, really? You cant watch how you played, first time in a cmr/dirt game where you cant watch a replay the ♥♥♥? Also the game was running great for the first 15 hours, then suddenly started crashing like crazy in mid races, every 30 minutes. The game was running like a dream then suddenly became unstable, it's a fresh os with everything up to date, every other games runs flawlessly, only this not.Lots of bugs, like after your cross the finish line the winning cut-scene wont trigger, every other cars that was behind you cross the finish line and the game says you're 12th and shows you that you need to press reset like you're out of track or something.Sometimes you dont get rewards and xp from your sponsors, even though your only level 5 sponsorship, the only way to fix this is to exit game and re-enter.It happened a few times that after you jump high, and land on another vehicle, your car simply melt together with him and then physics goes crazy, like wtf with all those bugs really?The graphics is good , it looks gorgeous with everything maxed out, the soundtracks are ok, and lots of great cars in the game, but there are lots of gameplay issues and just not enough content in the game that made me quit.I should have known that games with mixed reviews (half negative) most of the times are not good, but i didn't listen to others. At first i hoped that this would be a great game like the other games in the dirt series, but quickly turned out that this game is awfully bad, and i spent a lot of money on another garbage again that goes to "my bad game list"Oh well lesson learned...

_childDocuments_.name: DIRT 5

_childDocuments_.review: These are just my impressions from the free weekend. First let me just say that this is the first game I've had to switch virus scanner for (to windows defender), which is a knock against it. Plenty of people seem to be having issues getting this game to run too, so maybe avoid this if you're not running the latest update of Windows 10.This feels like a budget title. The car handling is alright (for an arcade-style game), but everything surrounding that has had corners cut. You can't go off track for most of the race, because even light wooden fencing counts as an infinitely hard barrier. There's no more replays, so if you want to review how a race went or take screenshots after a race, you can't. The announcers (two podcasters) are the most unfunny and annoying people ever. Graphically it feels weirdly cheap. Things look vaguely blurry even on ultra settings. The game tries to wow you by varying the weather and lighting over the course of a track, which is nice but feels like a distraction from how 2010 the game really looks. Gymkhana is still there if you want to engage with it, and I'm still horrible at it. You can also avoid it entirely, I think.Overall I'd say it's not worth full price or even half price, but if it's super cheap it could be nice for a quick round of easy racing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a major issue where it starts in a window that can not be moved, and only 2/3 of it are showing on screen.  To play it I have to force quit the game 2 or 3 times, and it will eventually load full screen.Once it loads, then you can play it.  It does this EVERY time!  It's ridiculous and irritating!  Far too expensive to go gold with such a glaring bug. This is on a 10700K with a 3080.  This is the showcase system for this game.After it finally starts full screen, the game is decent.  Graphics are good, and speed and mechanics are fun.  It's a purely arcade racer, and that's just fine.  I don't need only sims in my life.  The menus and everything before the game starts are just awful though.  It's like a throwback from 1992 Extreme Sports.  It's confetti, tattoo art, and mismatched color schemes that will induce a migraine if you are sensitive to it.  Codemasters could have budgeted for an art department and improved this one.  That, however, is forgive-able, but the rest is similarly juvenile.  This really isn't for racing fans, its for console gamers who want to try a little racing.  I'd get a refund, but Iguess it ran on the computer in the background and it thinks I played it for 5 hours.  Live and learn.
_childDocuments_.name: DIRT 5

_childDocuments_.review: You have games pushing subtle micro-transactions, then you have DIRT 5 where the first thing you see after the logo is a "Hold A to go to the store".Regarding the actual game - I've beaten the career/story mode under 4 hours [half of the events], rest is pure grind. It's a pretty game with dynamic weather, some interesting tracks and classes, but I would never pay 54,99€ for this even if they included the DLCs [which by the way, also too expensive].Split-screen only works between controllers, bad luck if you have one controller and a keyboard. Playground is by far my favourite mode, you get to create and drive around player-made tracks which gives a lot of replay value, however in my eyes that isn't enough to carry the game out of lack of content.I'd be fine with the mediocrity if it wasn't for the price tag - thanks to Humble Choice I got this for 1 euro. Now 54,99€ and you don't even have access to all the content? Big no.P.S.: Turns out the Year 1 Access had some misleading advertisement, I recommend keeping that in mind if you're about to buy the game while they're still actively developing it.

I have reduced the music volume to take in the vehicle effect and the roar of the engines. I would rate this game a solid 9/10. Would have been near 10/10 barring the lack of music options.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially the game had stability issues (amped edition with 3 days early access) and online was lightweight to say the least, but in the last 4 days the devs have put out FIVE patches which cured a lot of issues with stability. When they add other features that are still missing (like wheel support, due to come mid November, and DLSS/RT options) this will be a top rated arcade racer for sure, it's already looks the business right now, the fidelity of the reflections and lighting and tessalation etc make the much better than other games and shows great promise once future content is added. I will say it grows on you and while not quite Dirt2/3 polish yet, once it is this will be right up there.REVIEW UPDATED TO NOT RECOMMENDED:Well three major patches later and the multiplayer problems are still unfixed, rubbish p2p system, often waiting 5 minutes between online games, no choice of modes, no choice of tracks, no working lobby system, no self hosting lobbies, utterly broken multiplayer experience. Sadly the devs seem to have no interest in fixing the biggest problem that this game has, frankly adding more content to the game in this state is a joke.AVOID THIS FOR ANYTHING OTHER THAN SOLO PLAYER, OR YOU WILL REGRET IT

_childDocuments_.review: OK - I like Dirt 5, it is fun!  But it is obvious that it was rushed to release in spite of the delays and is unfinished - to get a bit mean it should’ve been called Dirt 3 1/2 at this point because that’s where it appears to fit overall right now.  It is reminicent of Project Cars 3 as it relates to the fact that it is supposed to be a sequel to Dirt 4 (which is graphically and playably (word?) far superior to this).  The physics are less than arcade at best, more like a middle of the road app; cars float and shift around at the start of the races, bounce and spin if you wreck.   Even on an RTX 2080ti and an Intel i9-10900 it is unstable and has a hard time holding  60fps at high settings. But, as I said -  it is fun....it really is.  I hope Codmasters is working on a patch or 9 to fix this ‘cause I for one don’t want to give up on Dirt 5.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a huge fan of the dirt series since it was called Colin McRae Dirt all the way through to backing the early access Dirt Rally from the start and I have loved them all until this abysmal piece of trash came along. I even bought the early access pass for silly money. Take the rest of this review as me pouring out my hatred on codemasters while trying my best not to sound too negative.About 12 hours in and here is my take on this poor excuse for a Sega rally copy cat.First let us start with the best features – Great looking game, great weather and great dry to mud effects on the ground love that oh and of course cars plenty of them so if that’s all you’re looking for in a £50/$60 game then perfect! If you’re looking for more read on.Let’s start with something basic the handling of the cars…Turn traction control off, turn ABS off turn all driver aids off and the car still handles like a Sega rally arcade game, it is literally impossible to spin out.Next the crash damage – I don’t mind cosmetic only but this barely has any this isn’t Gran Turismo from the 2000’s it’s supposed to be a proper arcade rally game why would I not want to see my car fall to pieces as I run into a wall at 120 MPH rather than watch the car bounce off like a toy.Now after all that you’re probably wondering what about gameplay…What about the driving, the rallying, the emersion…Yea that last all but 10 seconds…As soon as you start any event everyone starts crashing into everyone and I mean everyone if you get through that you will win however if 2 or 3 manage to pull away you’ve got no chance…Not to mention the AI just randomly driving into trees and walls for no reason. You can also hit them at high speed and they won’t move but you will.Now lets talk about the day to night transition, let’s compare this to Dirt rally. You can start one stage in rally in the day that’s fine then do the last at night so over the course of 4-5 stages. In Dirt 5 that transition is done in about 1.5 minutes it is so bazaar and very off putting. Something else that is off putting is that the whole car seems to get dirty except the front of the car that stays immaculate.Right well that’s enough droning from me shame on Codemasters for really screwing this great series over, I am now redownloading my copy of Forza Horizon 4 because that is how you make an arcade racer game – Take my advice and everyone else’s don’t buy this garbage..If you really want to play a game like it get Sega Rally from the 90’s.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is some sort of 90's unicorn diarrhoea fountain with menu's that will cause headaches within seconds of start up and this headache will soon be added to by the sound of the announcers voices which are apparently youtube personalities who I can only assume have achieved popularity helping the mentally retarded feel like Elon Musk. If by what I can only assume is a mistake you don't immediately quit the game after entering the menu and actually try to play the game it sadly doesn't get any better. The way cars drive feels more reminiscent of a 2d top down racing game, which would actually have been more fun, shout out to gene rally. The reason I had originally bought the games was because of the promise of exciting multiplayer that was supposed to live up to the good old days of dirt 3 and honestly would have gone along way to redeeming the game if it had simply been dirt 3 copy paste but as of 2 months past the games release I have been unable to make the multiplayer work at all as it appears the good folks at codemaster decided that they too needed to give the mentally handicapped a self esteem boost.I'm honestly not sure how codemaster have managed to consistenly make every game worse since dirt 3 but if they were shooting to make the worst racing game ever made and too see how much they could charge for it I'm actually a little impressed. _childDocuments_.review: I normally, don't take time to review games, but I saw so many critical reviews of Dirt 5, it was clear to me that Dirt 5 is a criminally underrated game.   I thought I would share how Dirt 5 was the perfect racing game I was looking for my use case.     I have been searching for a simple, low barrier learning curve game that both adults and kids can have fun with in multiplayer, and boy Dirt 5 has delivered!  I was concerned because of all the negative reviews, but I decided to take a chance on Dirt 5 while it was on sale.  I love how in Dirt 5, you could just open up Arcade Mode and select whatever track you want.  The best part is that you can do split-screen multiplayer with up to 4 players, if you have 4 controllers!  I bought 2 controllers for this game and I am about to buy 2 more for the Arcade Mode alone.   I bought this on the recent Steam Sale for $14.99 and I have been having a blast with this!  I have never played a Dirt game before, so I had no expectations (or frames of reference) for Dirt 5  should be compared to other games in the series.   It's just simply a  game ticked all the boxes I was looking for in a racing game, and I love Dirt 5 for that!  This game isn't overly simplistic like Mario Kart/(or Wacky Wheel back in the day) when I was little), but the controls aren't too burdensome to learn and teach kids with a little patience.  My 8 year old niece has already got the controls down.  Her 5 year old and 4 year old brother are on their way learning it too.  Dirt 5  looks and runs grreat! The graphics on this game are gorgeous treat.  My Laptop is an Asus ROG STRIX G15 Advantage Edition, and has an RX 6800M, which is basically a desktop RX 6700XT.  I'm getting 80+ FPS with all the settings maxed out at 1440p.   I've also been convincing friends to buy the game so that we can race in online mode.  I do understand that one of the major caveats for why Dirt 5  has negative reviews is non-existent crossplay.  So if you buy this game for online multiplayer be sure that you and your friends all buy this on the same platform.Another caveat to Dirt 5 (and another major complaint in user reviews) is that this game plays a bit differently and  its style does not live up to the expectations set in place from previous Dirt branded games.  None of that mattered to me because I had no previous experience with the Dirt brand.

_childDocuments_.review: Just absolute fun.  This is the kind of racing you game hop into for pure gaming joy, its not like some of the past Dirt games that are more like Dark Souls driving where you have to play perfect or you lose.  And honestly, that's OK, it brings me back to the oldschool Dirt, like 1 and 2.  Some of the ideas they have come up with are just insane, makes me giddy!As for performance, i waited till after a couple days to purchase, seems they have ironed out most of the issues.  Mine runs flawless at 1440p ultra high settings on a 5700xt.  Graphics are INSANELY good.  Not sure why some are saying otherwise... most likely they don't have the hardware to push this games settings into the next gen look.  But lighting, reflections and weather effects are all incredibly well done.Overall, if you want just pure enjoyment from a racing game, pick this up for sure.  If you are looking for a more racing sim style game, id say hold off for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprint car races can go die in a fire, who in their right mind made these?  They are super broke considering the rest of the game is a cake-walk.  You can't control your car at all and the ai is basically glued to the ground and even when they hit walls, they lose no speed.  Game is mediocre otherwise, fun for a race here and there, but way too arcady for a Dirt game.  Also something about the art style is off-putting, cars look almost cartoony in a way, and the heavy use of TAA leaves blurry visuals and textures and awful ghosting. Even then, I was underwhelmed with the graphical fidelity, I expected more to be honest.Codemasters has also been pretty scummy with DLC and editions as of late.  The expensive edition was marketed as all DLC containing, but recently was renamed Year 1 edition, meaning you only get 1 year of content. _childDocuments_.review: Back to arcade racing by Codemasters is, by my opinion, quite nicely done. But few things need some polishing..Pros:1. Each car each feels and drives a bit differently.2. Visuals, especially changing weather and daytime (rain looks nearly as good as in Driveclub).3. Soundtrack type suits whole style of game.4. Variety of race types.5. Elevation on race tracks.Cons:1. Graphical issues (lightning flickering for me)2. Only few songs in soundtrack3. Number of unique tracks is really small4. Kind of boring and childish GymkhanaIn total, I'd give this game around 7/10 just because I like arcade racing in general. But I still got a feeling, that this game took Codemasters only like 6 months to complete as it's just really short and somehow feels more like "bigger expansion" to any existing game than an actual new game. I mean, you can complete whole career under 15 hours on hard difficulty and the only things left are online (practically dead) and playground (could be fun for some period of time). Definitely not worth the full pricetag, but once it's arouond 35 €, get it for the fun. If you're fan of arcade racing and don't mind missing rally parts, buy it. Otherwise, wait for sales and buy it just for fun.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, very enjoyable arcade racer (Definitely not a sim).- Super easy pick up and play, very controller friendly no need for a steering wheel, - Gameplay itself is fun, much like I expected from an arcade racer, AI seems a little odd on the occasional race but nothing game breaking, other than that relatively competitive racing on hard, very hard setting. - Track design is very good, plenty of variation, visually appealing, and depeding on weather all behave differently. e.g, dry track, more grip, same track covered in snow, less grip, extra slippy.- Graphically, very pretty on high to very high settings on a ultra wide 1080p screen, average 60 fps on Ryzen 9 3900x, 16gb ram and a Vega 56.- Online play, very much like previous dirt games, don't expect polite space giving sim racers here, this takes rubbing is racing to a whole new level, still fun though.- Overall if you've enjoyed previous dirt games, such as Dirt 2, Dirt 3, Dirt Showdown you will more than likely find enjoyment in this.- The creation mode is a added bonus, people are all ready coming up with very creative courses and ideas so this adds a fair amount of longevity to the game.- Now for the big one, Crashes and Bug's which everyone else's reviews seem to so heavily focus on, and i'm pleased to say after the most recent patch on 5th November all crashes i was experiencing have now gone and the game runs great, no crashing, quick load times and no bugs that I've noticed, well done to Codemasters for fixing a large majority of issues very quickly.As someone who's got quite a few hours in both a multitude of sim racers and arcade racers over many years, i can safely say this is definitely a pick up and play arcade racer, if your looking for a sim racer, you may want to look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews before I finish the whole game but MY GOD how awful this game is...I REALLY tried to enjoy it and even at the beggining I thought: "Well, this game isn't as bad as people claim it to be...". Yeah. While driving actual rally cars is pretty fun (despite the more arcade style compared to other Dirt entries) and the sense of speed is defenitely there (at least in cockpit view), which is very rare in racing games nowadays. Unfortunately my opininon started to change. Drastically. Apart from rally - ish (beacause there are no regular rally events - huge con) events we have truck rally, buggies, some weird nascar like ♥♥♥♥ etc. It reminds me of Dirt Showdown but this game can't even be compared to it. As I said before I have no problem with the game being more arcade and demolition derby oriented just like Showdown BUT there are so many flaws in this game I wanted to just quit at times. Soo, why my opinion changed? The truck races are extremely boring, most of the time they are on the same tracks, the sense of speed is quite bad and I guess that's it. Buggy events on the other hand have great sense of speed but physics completely ruin them. Most of the time you get knocked out of track by other racers or sent flying and spinning into space itself (I even managed to glitch in a wall one time). Other races share this problem but it's visible the most with extremely light vechicles. Speaking about crashing, let's mention the AI itself. In one event, there are up to 12 (!) races and as you might know - the dirt tracks are very narrow. You know what this means... AI exists either to crash into you all the time or slow you down by blocking the route, BUUUTThe AI in the front turns into freaking Forza Drivatars (well crashing into you and slowing you down is also a Forza AI trademark I guess) and ignores physics completely by staying 1km in front of you. What's weird this only started happening after chapter 1 and turning down the difficulty from Hard to Medium literally didn't change a thing. Oh and I forgot to mention that car specs don't matter because AI has it's own physics and overtakes you on straight while you drive the highest powered car. Ok, horrible AI covered, what's next? Oh yeah, the fact that most of the cars are basically the same and specs don't really work at all. What's good in this game is its soundtrack I guess but you don't hear it much because it plays from the speakers on the tracks so you hear it only when close by. I also respect that they tried to have kind of atmosphere and soul but that's it. Driving anything other that rally cars feels horrible, AI is horrible, difficulty doesn't really work and there are many bugs. The redeeming qualities are the soundtrack (which is barely hearable), sense of speed in rally cars, souds (hit or miss) and general vibe (which is kinda cringe at times but at least it's not as soulless as Forza's).Easily the worst Codemasters' game and one of the worse racing games I've played if I have to be honest.Can't recommend even on sale (EA play exists tho).

_childDocuments_.review: feels like one of the cleanest and streamlined versions of a Codemasters racer I think we'll ever see. It leans into what they do well and avoids much of the unwanted filler that sneaks its way into their games. The controls are a touch arcadey here, with forgiving mechanics and huge jumps, but not to the point where there are boosts and the like.+Visuals are fantastic. The neon presentation mixed with the truly impressive locales make this a great looking game all around. Environmental effects are stunning, watching the rain hit sunlight had a "wow" impact that I've not had in a while. The locations for races are inspired, visually interesting, and unique.+Car choice is small but it's an asset here. Instead of throwing a thousand cars at you with the requirement to constantly grind for a car which you may use in one race, you can jump into almost any race and be competitive with the starter vehicle. Buying more cars is about leaning into characteristics you prefer or as a brand/aesthetic choice, rather than a requirement for victory. This means you'll be getting more familiar with a smaller stable of cars, leading to a greater overall mastery.+Very solid soundtrack with some bands I love such as The Chemical Brothers, Wolfmother, Jack White, The Shoes, and many others. Even music in genres I don't care for are generally solid and do not detract from the experience.+A Codemasters racing game with clean menus??!?!?!?!!+The game controls well. It's a nice change of pace to see high performance cars in a game that don't handle like a Dodge Viper on a Vaseline coated ice rink.+I've been a regular follower of Donut Media content before playing this game so seeing those dudes pop up in this game was a treat.-I'm a fan of watching drift and Gymkhana events in real life. In this game the drift mechanic feels clunky. Adding these events to the mainline career rather than as fun diversion is disappointing.-As per usual in a Codemasters racing game, acting and "story" are god-awful. The guys from Donut Media are fun and affable and work OK with what I feel is a mix between script and ad-lib, but they stand in stark contract to the "professional" voice actors portraying racers they interview.-The game is a bit on the easy side.=The music volume starts off super low so I had to make some adjustments to hear it well in game.=Popups to remind you to buy the DLC. Annoying but that's capitalism at fault, comrade. Achievements tied to DLC however is awful. feels like Codemasters stretching their legs a bit and focusing back on what works without playing it too safe. I previously had negatively reviewed Dirt Rally 2.0 (which is a wildly different beast) since the devs seemed to stop supporting it abruptly. I can see why they would want to focus on Dirt 5 with its clean and sleek chassis.

_childDocuments_.review: After 17 hours, I have experienced basically everything this game has to offer. Several major problems with this release - only a few selections of tracks that are very heavily reused through the main campaign, cars are far too similar one to another in driving terms (even for arcade racing standards), selection of cars is really disappointing with many of them locked behind a paywall and most of the racing is done in death rally fashion instead of something you'll expect from this series. To be more precise, this game is far more similar to the Dirt Showdown spin-off, than to earlier installments in the main series. If you're looking for good arcade racing, Forza Horizon 3/4/5 is much better value for money. If you liked Dirt Showdown, wait for a sale and buy Year 1 Edition which has a lot of additional content.

_childDocuments_.review: After 100 minutes of playing, I have already seen whatever I have to see to give a decent review.GAMEPLAY & CONTROLSThe gameplay is a good average. The car doesn't feel connected with you at all. The controls are a bit 'off' as I never truly felt like I was driving the car fully. Even with all assistance and driver aid turned off, the driving still felt aided.Any competition is barely around unless you ramp it up significantly, but then it just feels like it makes everyone else drive super fast compared to you (not organically better if that makes sense).FEELThe game feels blunt, a bit TOO much arcade. It's like a 2010 racing game that got dropped in 2020.I'm not a fan of all the 'flashy' lights, screen animations, 'flashy' sound effect for every single thing that happens on the screen. The game feels unpolished and dull.I've played through all other Dirt games on Xbox and been quite happy with them, but this one doesn't feel right.It feels like the game tries really hard to be Forza Horizon (on the looks) but it missing a lot of key ingredients in the actual gameplay.SOUNDThe soundtrack is super boring. Like if they took the cheapest Good Charlotte rip-off punk band and have them screamed out a song in each race. Maybe it's not my type of music and it's really good if you're into that genre, I don't know.Sound design for the racing is OK, not more. Some sound effects sound cheap and out of place (big car crash sound when driving over a small pole, I'm looking at you).Would I pay $85.00 AUD for it, absolutely not.Was it worth $55.00 AUD from an alternative website, barely.If you're a really big fan of Arcade racing (more than previous Dirt games in my opinion), go for it.If you're like me and still want some sort of competition and driving feel left in it, wait for Forza 5.But since I've already bought it, I'll of course finish it off.Maybe I'll be back and give this review an update somewhere along the way.Cheerio[EDIT 24-HOURS LATER]So, I booted it up again today to try to find some love for it and it's nowhere to be found.I tried it on my TV to see if that would give me some better immersion to the game, but no, it didn't.- Controls are in fact awful. You feel so disconnected from the car when playing.- The driving feel is nada, zero, hasta la vista baby, gone. I'm guessing the game designers did play a little bit too much Mario Kart when creating this game since that's what it feels like you're playing. If you accidentally hit a wall you bounce back more than Nick Minaj bounces her bottom in 'My Anaconda Don't'.- Sound design is even worse when playing it on the TV. Was really trying to push the Subaru Impreza through one of the (few) tracks, and my God, it sounded like I was riding a chainsaw for 5 minutes. It's better Sound Design in Need for Speed Most Wanted from 2005.- The music is doing my head in. There must be some really cool dude that worked on Tony Hawks Pro Skater 3 that got picked to compile the stack of tracks for this game as well, as they literally have the exact same music. Thrash punk rock that annoys the ♥♥♥♥ out of you.Do yourself a favor and go for Dirt 4, Forza Horizon 4, or Dirt 2.0 if you want to play a racing game today, as this just feels like a half-hearted project that no one at the studio really believed in.And common Codemasters, you can do better! I've seen what your previous games look like and those are FIRE.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is very fun as long as you don't take it too seriously. More experienced racers will find the need to set the difficulty up significantly before the AI will become a challenge to beat. The environmental detail, variety and atmosphere helped by the high quality particle effects are the stand out feature of this game. The cars are very well detailed too and the sound effects are good. The vehicle headlights don't project very well ahead of the car in night racing which can be frustrating. The exact area you need to see will be pitch black while the periphery of the screen is illuminated which does not make much sense. The lack of replay functionality is disappointing especially since the environments look so good. The background music mostly qualifies as background noise and is not very enjoyable to listen to or memorable. Having to design your own livery for your car feels tedious and it would have been preferable to still have this feature, but alongside the ability to choose from finished and attractive presets. The game runs consistently well and looks good on older hardware like my GTX1060 6GB, but running it on more powerful hardware such as my RTX2080ti is rewarded with even sharper visuals while still maintaining consistent running.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the trailer for this game, I thought they were going to provide a new experience in Dirt where players are going to somewhat experience Dirt 2's festival vibes; however, it felt more like an evolved Dirt Showdown.Now, that's not bad. The moment I knew this, I immediately switched my mentality from a "Spiritual Successor to Dirt 2" to "Just a fun game where I turn off my brain and appreciate the graphics".The first thing that I want to get it out of the way are the physics in Dirt 5. They're unplayable but for Codemasters standard, they're sad. This is why I mentioned that they felt like a Dirt Showdown successor rather than a mainline entry in the series. Cars oversteer way more than they should be for dramatic effect and the physics goes completely bonkers if you flip your car. To me, the physics are what made the game from great to just decent.AI is okay to borderline cheating as they do not spin out, lose traction, drift, or even have a sense of awareness on your presence. This means that I do not agree on majority of the players where they claimed that the game was too easy.Content wise of the game are just enough. I completed the game in 50 hours as stated with all 40 achievements unlocked. So they're not long but not too short.Sound engine of the game are just decent. I felt like Dirt Rally (1 and 2) and Dirt 3 were better. The soundtrack was decent as well.Race tracks are plentiful and fun but I felt like it needed more countries. I just wanted to highlight that Brazil and China were my two favorite countries to race in.The graphics was something that I thought where it was not going to be impressive at all. In fact, I had an impression that they looked like a mobile game based on some comments I saw in YouTube. But I was wrong, they were more than just decent and borderline awesome.

It's just COLOURFUL, MAD and AMAZING FUN. The tracks and challenges are all so different from each other and events like the Morocco Rock Bouncer have to be seen to be believed... _childDocuments_.review: Playing this on the free weekend.Lots of people are showing dislike for this game but I disagree.  I love the graphics - everything about this game is great looking to me.This is really just an arcade racer and if that is all you want then this game is great.  Honestly, I've just had a busy week and was exhausted.  I turned my computer on, played this and it was just what I needed.  Mindless escape.One downside I have is that the races are too easy.  In pretty much every race, I leap to the front and unless I make a grave error, pretty much stay there.  There's not really much feeling of fighting for that number one spot.  Also, the racing where you literally climb up and down rock-faces is just weird.  It's difficult to know where to go and you can feel the computer correcting your falls and tumbles in an uncanny way - these races needed more work, I think.Also, no tweaking of cars.  You can change the livery of your car and make pretty patterns but that's about it.I've only played single player with my X-box controller and just delved into the campaign so this isn't a thorough review but I really have enjoyed my time with this game.  If you just want to kill some time with a straight-up arcade racer, I'd recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a fun and laid-back arcade racer DIRT 5 is definitely for you. It operates a lot like Need for Speed titles, where spectacle and enjoyment are more important than real-world accuracy. Each race in the campaign mode comes with 3 bonus objectives (ignoring the obvious goal to win) like overtake 2 cars in 10 seconds, or stay airborne for a combined 25 seconds, or drift passed 2 other drivers, etc which adds to the races in a refreshing way. Each car can be immediately customized visually (I'm not far enough into the game to do anything else) and the game offers pre-made patterns and logos to slap on the doors, roof, and hood.The one bad thing I've noticed though, is there currently isn't any wheel/pedal support. But this something that will obviously be patched in at a later date. A racing game with no wheel support is like point-n-click adventure with no mouse!

_childDocuments_.review: For those who only ever read the first couple of sentences in a review, I'll make this quick, THERE IS NO RALLY. Nope - Dirt 5 is just a series of races where you start with a bunch of cars, they all speed away from you and the objective is to finish in front of all them. The cars keep up with your speed so race/lap times don't mean squat.I've really tried to like this game, I really have, but after 6 hours if this nonesense I've finally thrown in the towel and written off the money I spent on this as a loss.If you want a nice arcade racer with rubber-banding/catchup, then this is not a bad game; but if you're looking for a Dirt game, you will 100% hate this.

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement over Dirt 4 by a long shot. Gone are the awful procedural generated tracks and rally racing all together apparently. If you want an arcade off road racer, play Dirt.  Arcade rally racing would be a nice touch, but I think the target audience here won't mind its removal. The new tracks and events are fun to do (even the gymkhana).  The removal of a rewind feature is pretty annoying. It’s a better direction for the Dirt series, if only it didn’t look so ugly.Why does this game look so ugly and run so badly? It looks like you're playing a game from almost a decade ago.  Texture quality and visual effects are all pretty bad. It looks low resolution and overly blurry.  The core driving experience isn't exhilarating enough to overcome how ancient it looks and feels.  This makes the racing feel disappointing.Looking at other reviews there’s some confusion.  Dirt has always been an arcade racing series.  Not sure why so many people are complaining that this is an arcade racing game. If you want rally racing go play the Dirt Rally series.

_childDocuments_.review: Inconsistent AI ruins this game.Some races I can put it on "very hard", turn off all of the assists and still expect to win by a decent margin, others...Look, I can accept that there are going to be some disciplines that I'm simply not as good at.  For example, I can't seem to get the hang of the trucks, thus if I start to lose consistently on any particular race I tend to go through a progressions of "cheats" to make it so I can simply finish a race on the podium. With trucks I generally start at Medium with low assists and I turn on high assists if the race is a bit much for me.  This is fine, I usually get a podium after a couple tries and I move on, changing my settings back to "Medium low assists".Then I got to Sprint racing.....  Oh my f**ing g**, this f***ing f*** of a f***ing discipline!   I started with my normal settings and, after losing miserably a couple times, turned on the traction control assists because I figured that's how I was losing speed.  Nope.  So I turned up stability controls and abs as well.  Still nope.  Not even close.  Race after race, try after try, for a g**d***ed hour!  Finally I decided I'd had enough so I bit my lip and condescended to use my super cheat...I put it on easy. Guess what?  30 minutes later-- still can't do better than 7th!  Generally I'm lucky to do better than 12th!  And that's after you factor out the countless restarts when I realize I'm just too far behind to even try for a decent finish!!!I can't stand this!  In some races I can have it on Very Hard with no assists and win by several seconds.  But in other races I can put on full assists on the easiest setting and I can hardly keep up with the back of the field?  I mean, isn't that, like, super out of wack at that point?  I should note, I play DR2 on the regs and I'm really quite consistent in that game from event to event.  I have very light assists and keep the difficulty on Medium in that game as well, I will win some Rally's by a decent margin and in other's I'll just be somewhere in the top 10 for my class.  This makes perfect sense!  I'm just better in some conditions than others. I can accept that.But being the g** of racing in some races and the worst racer on the planet in others?  The deviation is so great that I can't help but lay the issue at the developers feet!There's simply no excuse for a racing game to have _this sporadic_ of AI.  It feels like they prioritized the visual polish so far above the AI that we have a game that is waaaaaaay over the top in visuals (really, lightning blizzard again?  Really?  Do you know how often that happens in real life? sigh...) and is incredibly stupid to play in single player mode.I will give them this:  I love the handling and the feel of the tracks.  The environment and all it's trappings are great (when I'm not frustrated, it's super grating when I'm frustrated).  I love the selection of cars and I love that there are multiple disciplines.  I've even started to like the Donut podcast folks, it adds a touch of spice to the progression of career mode.  H*** when I hit a string of several races where the AI is either fair or, at very least, is unbalanced in my favor, I find myself having a great deal of fun.Then it aaaallll comes crashing down into an hour and a half long completionists nightmare.The AI disparity has fundamentally ruined the game for me.  Until it's fixed, I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: So torn on this one. Whether you enjoy this depends on what type of racer you are and your expectations. The Dirt series has gained justified noteriety for its incredible detail but Five doesn't quite deserve the Dirt brand. I can imagine the pressure on the dev to spice things up and make something different after all the previous entries in the franchise so it's hard to punish them too much for attempting something fresh.I'm an arcade racer so personally I love what this game is attempting. It's less hardcore sim (much less) and more colourful spectacle. It's brash, gaudy, and mostly fun. The mechanics are relatively simple with no car tuning to worry about and a selection of cars just large enough to offer varying combinations of "performance" and "handling". The better the car you choose, the lower the reward - and visa versa.I'm a visual guy and the graphics are stunning. (I'm playing on an RTX 3080 and 21:9 ultrawide monitor.) The tracks are extremely detailed with impressive water and mud effects. The day-to-night transitions and constantly changing weather are absolutely gorgeous to look at and drive through. One race was partly obscured by thick dust, which was equal parts annoying and delightful. Because this is all about spectacle, you'll find neon lights, laser light shows, and fireworks in the most unlikely locations such as the middle of a Chinese jungle. One ice track in particular throws off neon light reflections as dusk gives way to night that is the most gorgeous environment I've seen in a racing game. Fireworks line the final straight and explode in sequence as you cross the finish line.Being a casual gamer and playing on medium with no driving aids I found most tracks challenging enough to pay attention, yet forgiving enough to reward practice.I did have issues though. Some races I found nigh on impossible to win, partly coz I'm lame perhaps, but partly because some cars are utterly uncontrollable. The "left steering" circuit track is one example. You spend 90% of your time on the pathfinder tracks in the air, so steering becomes impossible. Or sure, maybe I should just slow down.The reputation score and bonus points I found to be largely unnecessary. Prize money is needed though to purchase vehicles. But overall I didn't really feel much sense of progression. Sure tracks are unlocked as you race but it seems to be done as a matter of course. Play the tracks in order and you'll get to play them all. With 10 hrs of gameplay, it doesn't feel like the vehicles are getting any faster.The DLCs I got with the purchase of this game seem pointless as they appear to just be more of the same tracks. Maybe there are extra cars... I don't really care enough to explore the vehicles in any great detail. In Need For Speed: Heat, I took pride in the vehicles that I purchased, sinking time into their aesthetics. Here the cars seem cartoony in comparison.Overall, this is very arcadey - some will love it, some will hate it. I get the sense there would be more love if it wasn't branded a Dirt game where there is a reasonable expectation of driving accuracy and deep tuning options for simmers.If you don't take your racing games too seriously and are just up for some colourful noisy fun then I think you'll enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: if you're looking for realism play Dirt Rally. it exists and is quite good at simulating rally. imo there is no point in the core series being "serious" if Rally exists for that purpose. this game is dumb fun and pulls off the fun-factor miraculously. great handling, graphics and AI. career mode is optional and thats how it should be for "fun" racers. not everything has to be realistic.overall codemasters did a wonderful job in giving the non-Rally series an identity. im sure Rally 3.0 is around the corner for the sim fans. im happy with dumb fun Dirt 5 myself.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately a very bland game with the usual "look, that is cool, we're cool" approach of some millennial (allegedly) commentators.I don't know why this game exists. There are better alternatives out there. Just play Forza 3 if you want obnoxious commentators and mostly short races.Dirt 5 does boast a nice selection of locales and tracks. At first glance. Almost half of the tracks are just reversed versions and half of the rest is just the same track with a few different corners...Most races, whatever their "category" are just your usual lap races, with 1 lap taking like 1 minute. About 5 or so are Point races while 5 more or so are Pathfinder "races", which could actually be fun, if they were implemented better. The game would need proper physics for that, damage models...and then you'd have to actually FIND YOUR WAY through uneven terrain. Instead these races are just point races with no opponents and a bit more challenge.Music is alright. Unobtrusive. Graphics are also alright, but nothing special.Difficulty is WAY too easy. I had to crank it up to "very hard" to even face somewhat of a challenge (in the form of all opponents just upgrading their cars ... they don't really drive better ... just faster, and mostly it's just one, not all). There is no nuance to the AI ... and the "campaign" is just a set of single races...about 120 or so of them. Not sure if the game just naturally gets more difficult in later stages, but I kinda doubt it. Driving is for the most part also not challenging, nor are the tracks themselves challenging or really standing out. I already can't remember a single one.For 55  Why would you do this to yourself? To let Codemasters milk you for extra content, that's why. No. Just skip it. I got it in Humble bundle and I regret having invested 3 hours into it.If you want to go "rallye arcade" go full arcade, go nuts. And screw Ghymkhana or whatever it's called. Make your game stand out ... OR craft a more realistic game, something like Dirt Rally, which is imho casual enough, but also not pretentious.
