_childDocuments_.review: A very different entry into the Dirt franchise, definitely more like GRID or Blur.Events are organised into 4 main categories/tournaments, of which some require DLC. There are a few different types of events, some are like a rally game (time trials or sprints) and then there are others that are far more arcade style (like GateCrasher or Gymkhana).Cars are very basic this time, with only a few options in each event type and no performance modifications or customisation (only cosmetic Vinyls that you can unlock or create). I had enough money half way through the game to buy every single available car (even from the DLC packs that I bought), and even then I had like 3000000 credits at the end when I unlocked and finished everything. Would have preferred if they added something to spend in-game money on, since it feels pointless to do the sponsorship's etc after a while since you will be flush with cash.The tracks are a bit boring and generic, except for the arcade events that are nice and wacky (honestly they are a lot of fun). After a while though, all the tracks feel like the same thing with little variation.There is a online mode that you can play, didn't pay too much attention to that since the game has an ample amount of events to enjoy (around 100 or so races). There are also user created maps called Playgrounds that you can play and rate afterwards, some are interesting and inventive.The game isn't bad, but its definitely not what you would expect from the DIRT franchise. I would pick it up on sale, and skip paying for the two extra cars (its an SUV and a Truck, both get outclassed by other cars in-game)

_childDocuments_.review: DIRT 5 is definitely a departure from the previous entries in the series. However, I don't necessarily think that's a bad thing. I think the game would have fared a lot better had Codemasters decided to embrace the game's differences, and made DIRT 5 into its own spinoff, rather than making it a direct follow-up to the previous DIRT games. Looking at the game on its own, I've really enjoyed it so far.DIRT 5 takes a much more arcade-style approach to a dirt racing game, and I rather like it. If you just want a fun, low-stakes dirt racing game, this is definitely the one for you. The game doesn't focus on having super realistic, unforgiving physics like other entries in the franchise, nor does it have simulation vehicle damage that will take you out of a race should you make a mistake. If you're a fan of dirt/off-road racing, and you want a game to kick back and have some fun with without being overly stressed about making small mistakes, I would highly recommend giving DIRT 5 a try. But if you're looking for a more realistic rally racing experience, this game isn't for you. Get DIRT 4 or DIRT Rally 2.0 instead.Also, if you're interested in the game, don't pay the full $60 for it. While this is a good game, I wouldn't say it's quite $60 good (though most games don't justify a $60 price tag in my opinion). EA/Codemasters does pretty frequent sales on the DIRT games, so just add it to your wishlist and wait for them to drop the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so unsure of how to rate this game honestly. While I do enjoy the DIRT Rally series I was fully expecting the arcade focused experience, and enjoyed it for a bit. That being said, this game just has so many little things that drive me crazy.'ConsOptimization- I have seen a little bit of both sides here, but the optimization (as well as settings for that matter) are pretty poor on my Nvidia RTX 2070 Super. It sits at about 60 fps on medium settings, which is worse than just about every other title I own, while not really looking that good. Gameplay- this one is only targeted towards two things: gymkhana and the sidecars. The former just feels unwieldy and inconsistent, while the latter is downright infuriating to control consistently. While the latter might not come up for everyone, it was leagues harder than the rest of an otherwise extremely easy game. (There is also something weird about steering left and right relatively often back and forth that creates this weird delay in turning. Super disorienting while playing but never came up in the campaign, and instead on the playground tracks)Campaign- Its just boring. While you can run through the campaign in just about 4 hours, completing every event available is miserable. I have become bored with the same tracks and the same races after only 4-5 hours. Technically there is a lot of content, but doing the same race 3 times at different points in the campaign is not fun or interesting. Stability- the game just crashes a lot, and it seems unclear as to why. I have probably had the game crash 15-20 times in 8 hours of total play time, and while they aren't bluescreening my PC like modern warfare could do, it is still fairly annoying. This is exasperated by the last con:Loading time- specifically when launching this game, it takes like a full minute before anything shows up. I have the game on an NvME drive that loads just about everything else in less than 10 seconds, let alone a minute later. Actual loading times once in game are quick and snappy, but the initial load has the speed of a game from 10 years ago.MehGraphics- I kind of touched on this, but the game does not look that good, and almost looks like dirt rally 2.0 but in the wrong resolution. It just looks extremely average, while beating up your pc in the process. Wheel support- This could probably be listed as a con, but since it has no bearing on my personal experience I will list it here. It is quite odd to not have wheel support at launch for a racing game, even if it is an arcade focused one. ProsAesthetic- thematically this game is really well done. It doesn't take itself too seriously and really pops from menus to gameplay. The game is just colorful and bright in a cohesive way.Gameplay- besides the things I mentioned before, the gameplay is fun. I have found it a bit too easy for the most part, but cars handle relatively well (except the minor steering issue). The cars do end up feeling quite similar to each other, but the handle somewhat consistently and remind me of driving cars in motorstorm, albeit with a bit of understeer at all times.Playground/User created tracks- This is probably the shining achievement of this game in the sense of something they nailed. The editor is relatively intuitive and the having community made tracks will certainly increase the longevity of the title in the years to come. Super fun to just play a bunch of tracks that are completely different from anything in the main game.Would I recommend this game? Probably not. At its current pricepoint it isn't worth it, but I would pick this game up at 10 bucks or something. There is some fun to be had with relatively mindless racing against a bunch of other racers on tracks around the world. I am hoping some of the minor issues end up being missing in the future, but the core of the game isn't fun, even if the package is nice and shiny. However, if you are looking for motorstorm on PC, I think this is the best option available at the moment, and considering the trend of current racing games it will likely stay that way.I think the people who should never buy this game though are any sim racer people. Dirt Rally 2.0 is literally better in every single way, and its not close. The game is dumb fun and should be treated as such. If you are looking for that experience you will likely enjoy this game much more than dirt 4, which had a bit of an identity crisis and stuck more in the rally direction.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy a more casual, less serious racing game, then you will enjoy Dirt 5. If you are one who prefers a more realistic, simulation style racing game over an arcade racer, then you may find you won't like Dirt 5. This game is by absolutely no means a sim racer. That isn't to say, however, it isn't fun, because it totally is. The handling is nice, albeit arcade-y, and the game looks great. The game sounds AMAZING, which is something that does stand out. This game is not perfect, the handling is good, but can sometimes be a bit awkward during jumps, or during major collisions, either against a wall or an opponent. I am getting a weird stuttering issue, where the game freezes for about 3 to 5 seconds, then resumes as normal. I'm not sure if this is my PC, or if it is Dirt 5, though this game is the only game having this issue at the moment. It isn't very frequent, maybe once every other race, so it is tolerable in single player, but obviously would ruin online play. On a side note, I am very disappointed that rally racing is not in this game. My PC specs:Windows 10 64 bitAMD Ryzen 5 2600 Six-Core Processor16GB DDR4 RAMZotac Mini Nvidia Geforce GTX 1080Running on a Raid 0 array of two 1 tb WD hard drivesI get 60 fps on high/ultra graphics at 1080p, I dip down to about 30-40 fps if I switch Volumetric Quality and/or Global Illumination Quality to ultra. Overall, I think this game is definitely worth playing, if you know what you are getting yourself into. Do not expect any sort of simulation racer, because you won't get that out of DIRT 5. 7.5/10, would be 8.5 if not for the lack of rally racing.

_childDocuments_.review: Dirt 5 is a disappointment. The cars handle like karts with pretty much only minor difference in handling between the different classes, the game's AI is bipolar, either drives as if it was blind or turns on the god mode there is no in-between. Bugs galore and physics that would make Einstein run screaming for cover. Instead of choosing a car based on your preference for its handling the cars you choose are just based on how many straights or corners the track has, then just picking a car which has S/A rank in performance or handling. There's no tuning, integral part of the previous games, it's even stranger considering these settings would make gymkhana levels in Dirt 3 somewhat enjoyable trying to find the tune that would fit your style.The game is a great example of thinking very little of your audience, playing it feels like the game's assuming I'm a 12yo with ADHD and diminished mental capacity. All the even slightly more in-depth mechanics and systems from prevoius Dirt and Dirta Rally games are gone replaced with bright colours and flashy visuals, trying to mask the lack of depth and sorta low amount of unique content. There's not a whole lot of tracks and most of the cars on offer don't matter as only the ones that excel in either category are the ones only worth the credits. I had hoped we'd get something like Forza Horizon 3/4 for the Dirt franchise, zany, loud racing game that offers more customization and content than the previous ones, what we got is a portable version.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing racing games since I was a 2 year old that was still getting the grasp of language. I started off with games like Daytona USA, Hard Drivin', The Duel: Test Drive 2, and gradually moved onto the bigger boys as I got older like the Need for Speed series, Gran Turismo, Forza, Flatout, Destruction Derby 2, Nascar 2004... and that passion for cars and racing has never died out. To this day I still play racing games every time one shows up that piques my interest. I say this because I've been around the block quite a bit and that has been no less truer with the DiRT franchise. I've played every game in the series, with the exception of DiRT Rally 2.0, and each of the entries all have their own unique thing about them that help distinguish them from on another. However, I knew nothing about DiRT 5 because I learned that looking at videos, promos, etc makes it hard for me to control myself. However, when I heard about the free weekend I installed it and gave it a try. So how does this game differentiate itself from the rest of the franchise?It sucks. That's what it does. This is one of the most boring racing games I've ever played in my 25 year long history with this genre.Okay, that means literally nothing, so let me explain. DiRT 5 involves no skill to play. Even with all the assists off and the AI cranked to max this game's handling model is so oversimplified to the point it practically plays itself. If this weren't the case this game wouldn't be bad. I'm not even kidding. There's arcade racers and then there's games like this that require little no input from the player you'd think it's made for mobile phones. Despite the emphasis on rough terrain cars don't act like it. The cars are just magnitizied to the track. I'll give you an example:In DiRT 2 you round a corner a bit too quickly. Even if you hit the brakes the momentum from your velocity and the weight of the car will cause you to keep sliding until you careen into the wall. In DiRT 5, you can SLOW YOURSELF DOWN AS THIS IS HAPPENING AND REMAIN IN THE SAME DRIFT to regain control like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Mario Kart! There's no sense momentum or physics. It's like playing Burnout without any of the takedowns, boost, and traffic dodging mechanics. This applies to jumps too. If ever your car gets off the ground it'll always force you to land on all 4 wheels. If you hit something and get off the ground, run over rocks, you name it, the car freaks out but sure enough it'll just land back on its wheels and you'll barely lose any speed.I'm just dumbfounded. When the community complained this game was a complete departure from the rest of the series they weren't kidding. This feels like a sequel to DiRT Showdown more than it does a mainline entry but, even then, DiRT Showdown had physics that weren't floaty. I just don't get it. A good racing game, even the arcadic ones, all know that good racing comes from a healthy balance of giving you just enough control of the car to where it feels like you're in control but you know at any minute a slip up will cost you big time. And if your game doesn't have that it at least needs to include other mechanics that put the player's driving at risk. Even Flatout 3 had this right and that game is a complete disaster. This game doesn't have that. It's too forgiving and therefore it is boring as sin. I feel the only reason why it's gotten so many high scores is because reviewers were finally happy that there is a DiRT game that is locked to "Journalist Mode.*Tracks are also repetitive. Despite flying through the events I feel like I've played the same tracks over and over again and despite the different vehicle classes they all feel the exact same. The graphics are abysmal. Like this is seriously one ugly modern game. Even with the render resolution set to my monitor's native resolution the game just looks blurry. Also there's no car tuning. At most we get a basic livery editor. All cars seem to have a locked class for "handling" and "performance." Performance is the only one that matters.Don't get this game. Seriously, just don't. If you're looking for a good simcade experience literally point to any other entry in the series; specifically DiRT 2 and 3 as they offer a plethora of different event types with rally included. Yeah, by the way, this game doesn't even have rally.What a shame. Truly.

_childDocuments_.review: It's no DiRT 2, at all. Not even as good as DiRT 3, but it's an alright addition to the series. It has some issues, however they're not huge deal-breakers for me. I don't find Gymkhana as fun as it was in the third one but maybe I haven't dabbled in enough on this yet. Bumping uglies and trading paint feels very underwhelming, especially compared to Codemasters other games, like their GRID series and previous DiRT games. Little things missing like tracking achievements and stat trackers along with limited sponsors and cars just make me wanting more...They introduce a couple of hit and miss race types. The sprint races and ice breaker races are an actual joke. Kinda seems they are purposely in the game to be funny. At the same time, the rock climbing/bouncing is quite the fun. Online doesn't seem to work very well. The wait is notoriously long just to find a race with one other person. The playgrounds aspect in retrospect is very thrilling. Loads of fun to drive around on playgrounds created by the community. Everything else this game has going for it is pretty spot on for me. The style, art, music, graphics, I mean this is one of the most beautiful racing games I've ever played and it makes doing the same races over again actually not that mind numbing because there's so much to look at. The handling takes some getting used to but once you get the hang of it, it makes drifting around each corner satisfying to the soul. The thing I enjoy most about it this game is that it's set up perfectly for the series to continue this way, while the rally series can continue to do it's thing. Best of both worlds, what's not to love? My only wish is that they added more things to do. I beat the career in a matter of days and with online being very limited I find myself with nothing left to do other than making races in arcade mode over and over again. Can't wait for new and hopefully improved content.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'm enjoying this game. But like any game it has it's pros and cons. Pros: + Playgrounds - This is a mode I can see gaining a lot of support, and the thing to come back to over and over again. It's basically Track Mania, but in Dirt form. Also you don't have to pay yearly for it thank goodness. + Career Mode - I like the setup. I'm a sucker for having a ton of events to complete in a nice organized way. Open world games are fine, they have their place, but I much prefer this quick start and go style of racing. + Gameplay - I prefer arcade style over realistic, sue me. Game plays pretty great, though presently a tad buggy more on that in the cons. I'm sure they'll iron things out like they always do. Cons: - Online - I admittedly haven't tried online yet, and I typically don't care about online modes, but my criticism here is the sheer lack of variety. You go into this mode, click race essentially, and then it will throw you into a race. That's....it. This game could have really used something like Dirt 4 had with daily challenges with leader boards etc. I really enjoyed that. - The AI - My goodness the AI is unpredictable. In one race they could all be dunces and you find yourself alone in 1st for nearly the entire race. Another race, same difficulty, there might be 1 AI so far in the lead you'll never catch them...for seemingly no reason what-so-ever. They just blow by everything and defy physics somehow. - Icebreaker Event - This game has a lot of event types, most are perfectly fun, but Icebreaker really isn't...I'm a longtime gamer, I play basically everything, and traditionally the thing gamers hate the most sans underwater levels, are the ice levels. Racing games are no exception to this, and even mind-boggling how this found its way into the game frankly. I can't think of a racing game I've ever played outside of Mario Kart that had an ice track in it. Am I alone here? How on earth did they think sliding around would be enjoyable? Reminds me of racing around in Hovercrafts in The Crew 2, yuck. Mercifully the way career is designed you can opt to skip these, but if you're a completionist like me be prepared to suffer...- Extra Cons - There's some other minor gripes I have presently, that I imagine will get ironed out over time. Graphical issues, odd lighting effect bugs in night stages, graphics being pretty mediocre overall especially textures, and crashing. I've had 3 crashes so far and only 3 hours played, not a good streak. Again, I really feel like these will all get sorted in time Codemasters makes really solid games I personally think. But it's clear they rushed this one to market to strike that new console iron while it's hot. Final Thoughts: This may read like I have more gripes than praise, but through a combination of being easy to please and generally honestly having fun playing the game, I give this game a thumbs up. I can absolutely see people waiting for a sale or waiting until they improve the game though, I wouldn't fault you for it. If you're looking for that "next gen" racer though this certainly isn't it. Forza Horizon 4 on PC has far superior graphics and it's a much bigger technical achievement. But that game is old now, and if you're like me you've done everything in it and want another arcade racing game to mess around with, then this is a fine choice.

_childDocuments_.review: 40 HOURS REVIEW: GENERAL APRECIATIONS:- GAMEPLAY:   Very fun and fast paced. (Action arcade) - CUSTOMIZATION:   very low, only stamps and color (no wheels or addons)- PHISICS: (OMG...)  Not phisics based. Although you can see very funny "air stunts". The Terrain can feel pretty real and satisfying! HOWEVER in Multiplayer things can go weird. it seems due sinchronization issues between cars.  This can look pretty funny or  disgusting  lol.    The Multiplayer feels quite messy in... a fun way?. Idk.   I can't say is well done, either say it isn't fun.- CONDUCTION:   Very arcadish. Easy to learn. hard to master - DIFFICULTY Ai:   Starts pretty easy but can turn very hard in the pregress ahead- TRACKS: I has a huge a mount of tracks, but for some reason they repeat a lot along the campaign. But they are very funny to race and see. - GRAPHICS:   Pretty good visuals and lightning. However some cars material can look a bit toy'ish. Could be a matter of optimization or artsyle. it is still very colorfull and enjoyful and dynamicly realistic. - WEATHER:  It has a large amount of weather stations with dynamic system which changes along the race. Pretty beautiful to see and race along!.MULTIPLAYER: Pretty low. But enabling the crossplay increases a lot. Also there is no lobby, only Match finder for every single play. (Pretty suck Multiplayer system)- SOUND: It's pretty good in engine and collition. Very immersive. However when many  nearby cars, I can feel I don't hear their engines. only mine or two others. I Like to hear a "dog fight" (engines). But i think is not the case. - MUSIC: it feels like you hear the same 3 tracks all the time. You hate them quickly. They must add more music  also the option to skip them.  - FX: The game has an awesome mud feel, along like "Motorstorm:Pacific Rift". The amount of teselation, particles and mud layers and pretty nice. - CAMPAIGN: It has a huge amount of tracks to complete. It has three modes, plus DLC campaigns. However it does repeat a bunch (varing the difficulty). Some tracks can feel lazy (Ice ones) and some other prety beautiful.CONS APRECIATIONS: - Ice tracks are repeated so often that is loose all the fun about it. Itsdesign are flat and very, very boring to race.- SPRINT CARS:  (are a nightmare to drive and enjoy) - MUSIC: You can't skip songs and they are too few. (I recommend hear your own) - Mirrors aren't real. Maybe due optimization. Less to render. However you can look back.- Some wheels look awkawrdly toy'ish. Not very big deal tho. -  There is no LOBBY for MPlayer, is a random matching every single race. No social options to interact with players. - Night can feel pretty dark. is very hard to see few meters ahead.  The game need wheter more light on road or more lightning from cars. - Party mode: can be fun, but also can be very, very confusing. No clear clues on what to do. MY OPINION: The game is pretty fun. also not perfect. but is one of the best offroad arcade I have played. I enjoy the campaign , sometimes trying hard. but always hours running. The game didn't sell it self well due the "DIRT" name. and its simulator pre-conception. Leaded to a lot of dissapointed simulator fans. Due its lack of multiplayer population i wouldn't recomend full price. But totally on a sale. Very good Game sold with the wrong name.  7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Received game with a bundle via Humble Bundle, so i didn't pay full price. With that said, I thought this game was a lot of fun. Positive comments:-Nice graphics,-Great sense of speed on faster track styles-Lots of variety when it comes to vehicle and track types to keep things interesting-Drifting around turns at high speeds is hella fun!Negative comments:-Collision physics are a bit unpredictable and weird-Some features require a controller and won't work with a keyboard and mouse, including:     -Livery Editor (car customization)     -Split screen (for remote play together)Overall:If you are looking for an ultra-realistic driving simulator, keep moving and look elsewhere. If you're pretty familiar with what this game has to offer and still think it looks interesting, you'll probably have a lot of fun with it like I have. I loved going through the career mode and bouncing between all of the different styles of races. One minute you're in a sprint car, the next you're on a drift track on ice, then suddenly a street race with fast cars. It's tough to pull off all of those while other games are only able to manage a single race type with a similar level of quality.

_childDocuments_.review: After 13 hours of playing and mostly completing the game, I think I've given it enough time to impress me. But it just hasn't. I'm a big fan of Codemasters and their games, I was kind to Grid 2019, but they've just gone downhill further with this title. Let me get my main gripes off my chest.- I waited over a month to get wheel support. By which time i couldn't refund the game. When wheel support was added, it's partially broken. None of the buttons, despite being the Xbox layout, are mapped correctly. The FFB is pretty darn poor and breaks often. Requiring a restart. I have a Fanatec 2.0 wheelbase and V3 pedals. Frustratingly I can't use my separate handbrake or shifter, because they're not supported by the game.- I get decent frame rate (100-120 fps) @3440x1440 with an i5 10600K and RTX 3080. But the game doesn't look anything special. It could be 2 or 3 years old graphically.- The career mode is flat and plain boring. Just a random assortment of races, with no real feeling of progression. Gets boring pretty darn quick. Once you've earned money to buy a few different cars, the cash becomes meaningless as do the sponsors to earn you more cash. I have no idea why you gain XP and level up, it unlocks nothing. And all the unlocks are pointless profile backgrounds and liveries. Yawn.- The voice over podcasts are plain annoying and add nothing to the game.- The AI is really poor. They just stick together and bumble around. They are a nuisance to get past and will just drive into you like you're not there. Most of the time it's laughably easy to get past them all on the first corner no matter what difficulty setting you have it on (which doesn't net you any more rewards or incentivise you for changing higher, by the way). But some tracks are suddenly impossible, no matter what you do. I'm looking at you, oval sprint races.- Only a few cars are actually enjoyable to drive. Others behave in a frustrating manner.- Paid DLC already... Really Codemasters. Clearly just holding back on content which could have been added to the game at launch, to grab more money.Look elsewhere. There is plenty better out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes actually, because this is essentially what this game is.DIRT Series used to leans toward the arcade point with 2 and 3 and this game and its studio tries to follow it. Well then, I will use Dirt 2 as a benchmark. +/-/= means better/worse/on par with Dirt 2.: +Compared to Dirt 2 which is kind of short on cars and tracks in the entire series. Feels like it's closer to Dirt 3 in terms of total contents. The tracks is built largely in the philosophy of Dirt 2 as well. Reused cars as per Codemasters practice but it is much better than the pathetic Grid 2019 (I did a counting there).: -A minus but not as awful as it seems. Yes there are inertia and weight transfers but most of the time the rear end is lagging in response speed, too controlled. You need to turn of TC/SM completely to get closest to Dirt 2 but still, lack of sudden twitching in similar horsepower levels. Then comes the Sprint Car which is undriveable on a joystick for me...There is cosmetic damages but the cars are very sturdy compared to 2/3. Not really a minus but I still prefer to have them more obvious and an option to turn them off.: --This is why it looks worse than it feels. 3rd person camera is done without many experience and finesse. Lack of vertical movements, not centered enough to where the bonnet is pointing when the car is sliding... and it amplifies the handling weaknesses.: =Maybe I'm dumb but I can't find much differences.: =This part maybe is closest to Dirt 2/3, except for the roadmap event orientation. I'm not familiar with Donut Media but their appearance is a plus.:Certainly not trying to comparing generations, but the palettes is less natural than DR2.0 to me, perhaps closer to FH/TC2 in my eyes. Also a different engine IIRC.: --In Dirt 2 we have (real) Rally, RX, Trailblazer, Rally Raid, Landrush. _childDocuments_.review: (Received through Humble Choice)Jack of all trades, master of none, if you can even call it that.There's a lot of variety in the game in terms of racing classes and tracks and event types, but at the same time it really lacks variety in those same areas. The career in itself doesn't have the  concept, and starts off well as it introduces the different racing disciplines available. But after the initial few races, it just falls apart as the progression ends up being just a whole lot of the same venues and cars over and over and over again. There are several duplicate races (same cars, same venue, same layout), and the overwhelming majority of the events are extremely easy even on the hardest difficulty. The exceptions to the easiness are Sprints with the sprint cars, which are incredibly difficult - 5 laps are somewhat more doable to get a win, but 3 laps? Come on. You don't even really need to purchase new cars, as the starter cars will 100% take you through the game, bar a few - most of the purchases just come down to personal preference. The car classes are decent in general, but there are a few bits that really bug me, such as the prerunner class - there are only 2? proper prerunners, while the ~10 others are just stock SUVs and pickups. Why?! Overall, the actual gameplay gets very boring after a while, even as a fan of racing games and the Dirt series.Furthermore, the career just has a very boring story overall - you rise through the ranks and make your way up through the tiers (which you can't even tell the difference between in terms of actual gameplay). The ending is very anticlimactic, and left me just feeling like "now what?". You need to complete about a third of the events to unlock the final events, and I honestly can't recommend doing anything more than that since it just gets incredibly boring over time to grind out all the events (I did about 75% of the events before giving up with the grind) with no extras to the story other than unlocking the throwdowns. The podcasts were a cool touch though, and I enjoyed hearing from the real guests!Graphics-wise, it's a very pretty game, I'll give it that. I ran it at max settings and it ran smoothly (Ryzen 5 3600, RX5700XT) while maintaining good looks. The environments and weather settings are well made and really do add to the atmosphere of each race, even if it is a bit weird at times (why does it suddenly go from a pretty daytime scene to night time with full blown aurora borealis in the sky as I go from one lap to the next??). The only complaint I have on this front are random bits of vegetation appearing and flashing in random places in the sky and near the race track, which can get really bad at times, but I learned to ignore it even though it was a relatively big issue.The physics aren't , and for an arcade multi-discipline racer they're very much passable. There are some very annoying bugs in the physics though, such as jumping on top of another car, which glitches you inside the car below and causes the physics to freak out. However, in general, they are far from the worst.The playgrounds are nice to mess around with, and I actually enjoyed some of the content there. The arcade time trials were also a plus in my book, as I personally like that sort of driving in general. I haven't tried the online though, so I can't give a comment on that.In conclusion, stay away from this unless you get it for REALLY cheap. Full price is an extreme no-go, but if you get it for free or nearly free (like the Humble Choice), then it's not a bad deal. The career is a flop with the variety becoming its downfall, and the other features just don't bring it back enough for me to justify recommending this game.

_childDocuments_.review: System and Setup:Windows 10 64bitIntel Core i9 10900KNVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 SUPERLG 27inch 1440p 144hz monitor 27GN850-BThe game runs well on my PC without any needed fixes or tweaks. With V-Sync turned off, Final Resolution set to Native (1440p) and all other settings on Ultra High, the game's frame rate hovers in the 70s, going as high as the 80s or as low as the 60s depending and how much is happening on the screen.Review:I can't say I have much experience with the Dirt franchise, but I have played Dirt 4 before 5, and just with that and the existence of Dirt Rally in mind, it's easy to see why so many people are aggrieved by the direction that the franchise has taken with its latest installment. When you have a franchise that attempts to reach as wide an audience as possible, and that franchise goes through so many fundamental changes between installments, the people who feel left behind are inevitably going to be left with sour grapes. Unlike Dirt 4's attempt to bridge the gap between serious rally sims and more arcadey extreme sports, Dirt 5 confidently breaks away from any pretense of being a simulator, instead embracing a multicolored, festival aesthetic and leaving the serious business rally races to the spin-off game, Dirt Rally 2.0. Unfortunately for Codemasters, racing sim heads are a very entitled niche and have no problem with rallying (heh) against anybody who they think has crossed them. Just look at Project Cars 3. Wait, doesn't Codemasters own Slightly Mad now? And EA just bought Codemasters!? These guys just can't catch a break, can they?+ Fun, arcadey racing. Expect high speend, a lot of big jumps and a lot of drifts.+ Good lineup of cars.+ Good lineup of tracks and race types, and the career mode lets you skip around if you don't want to do a particular race at the moment.+ Great licensed soundtrack. Forza Horizon is still the gold standard, but there are great tunes here that maintain the high-energy mood.+ Nice graphics for a crossgen game. Very colorful.+ Dynamic weather keeps the races interesting.+ Career's story is nice enough by racing game standards. Donut Media, Troy Baker and Nolan North do well enough to keep the player incentivized.+ Playgrounds mode provides for additional replay value, for those interested in a mode that feels closer to Trackmania or Trials./ You can apply pre-made liveries to your car or make your own custom designs from the pieces the game provides. However, it may take a while for you to get designs and pieces that you want, as you'll need to unlock them over the course of the game.- Online mode is already dead.- Sprint cars are a pain and expect a level of careful steering and acceleration control that the rest of the game does not. To be fair these races have been patched to be easier since launch, but you should still expect to approach them differently than you would with the rest of the game.- Spending most of a Gymkhana event trying to do just one donut and losing your mind in the process. You can try going to your Driving Aids and adjusting the Tricksteer setting to see if you can make it easier for you.It took me about seven hours to get to the end of the career and make the credits roll. If you want to do everything in the game, it's going to take you much longer. Accounting for adjusting settings and messing with the game's built-in benchmark, I have about 18 hours logged on this game and I still haven't gotten completed all of the sponsorships, earned all of the stamps, unlocked the final showdown race or completed all of the achievements.Well anyway, I guess I just wanted to speak up and say that I think Dirt 5 is an enjoyable racing game and while it may be an anathema to the people who want a racing simulator, that shouldn't stop anyone who just wants to make the pretty cars go vroom. Perhaps a full $60 is a bit too much of an ask for this one, but at $30 and under I'd say it's a good purchase.Recommended

_childDocuments_.review: (for reference; played on both steam and xbox free play day promotions; played by someone dubbed a "boomer" by an active codemasters employee for voicing a few of these wild opinions via private channel)A strange and confusing “tribute”. McRae would be turning six feet under. Block, Pastrana and every other name historically involved with this franchise would be embarrassed to be associated with it.On the surface, Dirt 5 seems like a “return to form” or some sort of revival of that early era of the franchise. The mathematical fact that Dirt 2 + Dirt 3 = Dirt 5 was bought up multiple times pre-release, by both marketing and the irritatingly chipper community liaisons. Sadly, the numbers appear to lie.It is worth remembering that the Codemasters who developed the primary iterations of this game are a completely different team to today, from the boots-on-the-ground devs to the studio leads calling the shots and making decisions. This is much less a “Dirt” game as it is the remains of the Onrush team and technologies (which was already gutted when Codemasters failed to support or advertise their risky new game) grafting Dirt IP and assets into this game engine. Putting it bluntly Dirt 5 is a completely different game dolled up into something it isn’t.The Onrush weather effects and landscapes are back and look as gorgeous as they ever did.Gameplay. In previous titles, cars and tracks were divided into assorted categories with unique course designs to benefit the individual physics of each vehicle discipline. Trophy truck tracks were fast and flowing with big air and banked turns to keep the slow-accelerating, heavyweight race trucks at speed. Rallycross tracks were tight and technical point-and-squirt affairs, to compliment the RX car’s quick handling and high power. Dirt 5 appears to allow any car to race on any track, and while at first this may seem to be a positive, the fact is that a painful majority of courses are very wide, very flat and very generic in order to allow each type of vehicle to have an easy, competitive race, with their only distinguishing features being the environment outside the track. Add the game’s slow, vague handling to the mix, alongside awkward collision physics and braindead AI, and Dirt 5 quickly becomes a completely unengaging and frequently infuriating driving experience.Cars snag on walls. Tracks limits are all solid objects, and either stop you dead or allow you to wallride around corners in thin air thanks to invisible barriers. Ram into the rear of another car at speed and you are likely to just slide under it like a Fast & Furious ramp car. There is no “rewind” function, and more often than you’d like you’ll find yourself getting dumped by AI in the final sector of the final lap of a race, being forced to start over again. Which is great fun when you’re tasked with navigating one of the enormous Baja rigs through a chokepoint or hairpin they are not designed for, with 11 raging AI frothing at the mouth to wreck you. And not in an exciting way.In terms of things like rubber banding, AI will gladly come to a halt mid-air rather than completing an expected flight arc. Physics does not exist to them.If you were not aware, stage rallying and hillclimb racing are not in Dirt 5. Contrary to the rabid opinions of Dirt’s fanbase, they would not make the game any better.To its credit, the game’s car list is pretty deep and varied. There’s a healthy mix of real, fictional, custom and concept cars with most corners of off-road motor racing represented. You can Google it. Particular highlights include the plethora of electric concept cars, the returning rally raid cars and some choice additions to Dirt’s existing roster.But as nice as these cars are, an absolute minimum of them (as in, three cars circa the last update) feature their real-life “hero” liveries. By default, each vehicle has a blank livery, and, if you’re lucky, the car you want to drive may have an unlockable livery you earn from ranking up in career mode. All of these are lurid pop-art messes from the questionable pen of Sean Bull Design. Compare these to the fictional paint schemes from previous titles, which all at least looked like legitimate racing team liveries. I don’t even know what half of these Dirt 5 “art pieces” are. Most of them are simply plain patterns with no numbering or sponsorship.There is technically a livery editor, but it is a typical Codemasters affair with patterns, changeable colours and sponsor slots. Everything in it must be unlocked and I’m not even sure you can manually edit colours with slider values  Codemasters’ F1.Onto music and sound design. Dirt soundtracks are hallowed ground in the hall of racing game music, being curated and segregated into different playlists and atmospheres for the separate sections of gameplay with impeccable variety and selection. It goes without saying that Dirt 5’s soundtrack falls flat on its face. 98% of the tracks in this title are completely generic edgy-british-indie ad-music that plays on loop in-race and in-menu. Apparently there’s Prodigy, High Contrast, even Stormzy hidden in here, but I’ve yet to hear them over the likes of “I’m Gonna Light It Up” on veritable repeat.Codemasters made a big deal about their partnership with “Donut Media” and other social media influencers who provide voiceover and audio context to the story (whatever that is). Apparently, they roped in racing game Youtubers to guest on these in-game “podcasts” as well. So it seems they ditched actual charismatic individuals in the motorsport world in lieu of influencers and internet commentators. Baffling.They say this game is meant to “capture the atmosphere” of, or be a tribute to, that early era of Dirt games. Aside from some returning voiceless AI drivers in the post-race results, and the tenuous art style, I cannot see anything to suggest it is. It's just wholly disappointing, even outright upsetting.Buy Gravel and a Dirt 3 Steam key. You will have a far more wholesome experience.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who really enjoyed Dirt 2 back in the day (mostly because I was 12 and the idea that Ken Block might want to be my friend in a video game was enough to blow my tiny mind), I really didn't expect this game to be a spiritual successor to it, that said it's kind of a welcome surprise. The over-the-top extreme sports style presentation doesn't appeal to me as much as it did back then and can trend towards being slightly unbearable at times, but it still gives the game a kind of vibrance and enthusiasm that I find more appealing than Dirt 4's more muted approach.From a racing standpoint, if you're looking for proper realistic Colin McRae style rallying or rallycross, then there's not much for you here and you're better off sticking with or buying Dirt Rally 2.0, but if you're down for a bit of arcade style racing that prioritises fun over everything else, then I can more than recommend this game.As an additional note, this game may end up suffering a bit from the trademark Codemasters 'just buy the season pass and we'll add some more mystery content at some vague point in the future that might feel like it could have been included on launch', but the car and track list included in the base game is still expansive and interesting enough to be worth the asking price imo.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the worst DiRT game, if not the worst Codemasters racing game in general.Normally Codemasters does an amazing job with visuals but this ♥♥♥♥ looks like it belongs on a PS3/Xbox 360. Cartoonishly smooth car models, lazy weather effects that just pop into existence on your windshield, terrain and track details loading in as i drive by them and even when they do properly load they are trash tier. Sound effects fares no better. Its surprising to hear what sounds like a man using a kazoo and shaking a box o rocks to imitate effects given Codemasters generally excellent history in this area. Voice acting was also bottom tier. Lifeless, monotone, and occasionally forced sounding. Music is decent, but by default it is disabled during races.Moving on to Career mode, the disappointment tour continues. There are very few event variations and several core disciplines are missing from the game entirely, such as Rally and actual Trailblazer. Rock crawling and Ice racing both feel like they've been designed by somebody who has never seen either of those events. The rock crawler is incredibly bouncy, and ice racing iis not nearly so slidey IRL. They use special tires for it that helps with control, which are absent in this game. Gymkhana is an exercise in nonsense, with vehicles acting like the ground is made of glass. Overall, the physics are *too* arcadey and cartoonish. AI vehicles are as strong as dumptrucks but my own vehicle gets flung around like a smart car. Which is a real problem when the AI are as determined to stay on their rails as these ones.Finally, we have missing core elements of the game. There is zero ability to tune or upgrade vehicles in any way. Not even the basic sliders seen in the classic DiRT arcade series (DiRT 2, 3, Showdown) and certainly no detailed options.If you are looking for a rally game, try literally any other title before this one. 3/10. It is technically a game, and worse exist... but not much worse.

_childDocuments_.review: CONS-game both looks and runs worse than dirt 4  and to artificially inflate difficulty a little later of ai cars have the ability to accelerate faster than you even when driving lower performance cars (eg f150vs aston martin) this is a major detraction from the games overall enjoyment factor for me -there is also a distinct lack of manual gearing intervention when automatic is selected for gearing wich is annoying and makes any car feel like a mule because game doesnt want to downshift to pick up revs so that the vehicle can actually accelerate as intended  -path finder has frequent physics glitches where the car becomes a rubber ball  -sprint cars are just plainly put undrivable -persistent weather effects even when the weather has passed like it being sunny im in first but yet there will be droplets spontaneously spawning on my windscreen -some cars have awful axhaust notes-audi s 1 quattro lights on the dashboard to indicate rev/shift are extremely bright and make the cockpit cameras un usable during bad weather/night time PROS -OVERALL the game is very enjoyable especially when racing super lites and all the rally cars (especially the group b cars) up to modern(idk they just feel dead compared to the other rallies)-pathfinding is pretty fun -some really nice tracks -the customisation options when you start out is very sparse but opens up considerably once you start progressing through the career -the donut media bois are entertaining enough to listen to -the music is alright but there are a few songs that tend to repeat more often than the others and it gets pretty damn annoying -the weather effects look really good especially the snow storm -the narrative so far is pretty ok seeing as this is a racing game and not an story driven rpg/jrpg

_childDocuments_.review: DIRT 5, the game that lets you do doughnuts in a Lamborghini without explaining yourself to a traffic cop. It's like a therapy session where the counselor hands you a steering wheel and says, "Drive away from your problems."The graphics are so intense, they make me question if I need glasses or if my screen just can't handle the sheer beauty of off-road chaos. It's like the developers crushed up rainbows, mixed them with adrenaline, and threw the concoction onto the tracks.The gameplay is a wild ride, like convincing your GPS that "shortcut" means tearing through a tropical rainforest in a rally car. It's not just a race; it's a vehicular circus where the only rule is that there are no rules. Sorry, Grandma, your Sunday drive etiquette doesn't apply here.The story? Well, it's the epic tale of you, your car, and the mud you leave in your wake. Forget Shakespeare; DIRT 5 is where poetry meets horsepower.

_childDocuments_.review: Dirt 2 is one of my favorite games in the arcade section of Dirt series and I thought Dirt 5 will be an ultimate successor of that game. But it's not. The visual style of menus is the only thing that can match with the parent's merits. Everything else is a mess. I've played the first "chapter" and I don't understand how they could have done this so much worse than the Dirt 2, which sourced them every gameplay idea for this one. The handling and FFB is horrible - you feel no details on the wheel, surface changes is vague, the ice track felt like you're driving on tarmac, and mud/gravel tracks felt like you're driving on marshmallow. There is no difference in handling cars of the same class and difference between classed is vague too. Track are simple and wide as hell. After the first lap you know all tricky parts... But honestly, the are no tricky parts - track feels the same, only decoration changes.Opponens are dumb and drive like maniacs. On medim difficalty they always get away from you after the start, no matter how hard you tried to make a perfect start and upgraded the car, then you catch them, outrun them and they stay behind sometime overtaking you on the straight like they on a NOS boost while you are running full throtle - that much of AI here. Physics is not there, graphics is blurry and outdated. But they added so much excessive particles effects - constant mud/rain/leafs being thrown into your windshield creating a complete mess on the screen.And at the beginning of the game I was stuck for 1.5 hours figuring out why on my Fanatec CS v2.5 + CS pedals V3 car is not moving - throttle is always revving 100% itself, gears can be canged, but car does not move despite in the menu game registers pedals movement correctly. It appeared Dirt 5 don't work properly with Fanatec wheels/pedals and there is a bug with the handbrake mapping - once the key for handbrake was changed I was finally able to start the race.I'm very dissapoined in this game and don't recomment anyone to buy it, unless it's on 80-90% off sale. Thank you Codemasters for letting us test this mess and save the money on other much more worth racing projects.
_childDocuments_.name: DIRT 5

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Dirt season since early on, and I feel this game is just full of gimmicks and polish with no real substance, nothing for a player who wants to push their-self or compete with the community. It's in my opinion this was a rushed game.TL;DRThe tracks are fair, but if you enjoy a good matchmaking experience, daily or weekly challenges against the community, or testing yourself in Time Trails against the community.  This game isn't for you. If you want a pointless story and a bare-bone racing game, it probably still isn't worth the full price.For example Matchmaking is a joke with no lobby choice, they just push you in a lobby with no preferences  and instead of continuing with the same lobby or voting for the next match, they push you back out to the beginning screen (design aesthetics horrible just a empty screen) to start the matchmaking screen again. There is not  loose rank or MMR so you don't have any sense of place, I'm not saying there should be a top 100 or pro ranking, but you don't get a sense if you were facing the best in the world or any notion if you are making any progress.  Previous Dirt Games and Trackmania had daily or weekly challenges to keep people interested, this game has none of that.Another place that is a complete joke.  Previous Dirt Titles had ghosts or split differentials that you could compare yourself to your previous best, other titles like TrackMania, lets you go up against other ghosts of times that are close to your own.  Also, after you complete a time trial you can't retry, you can only retry before you complete a race, what?!!.  Without the split differentials to compare to your previous self, you have no previous reference points to know if you are getting better or worst.  This might be from my previous overlapping skillset and might be subjective but story mode is one big grind with AI that stay at the same skill level.  The player seems to be grinding for irrelevant goals like throwdowns and liveries? Since you can unlock the best cars pretty easily there is no reason to continue the story mode since the relative growth is tied to an eventual "Throwdown", but you have no real stake in the story since the path laid for you is just race after race with no cohesion.  Usually you feel invested in the story, progress, or sense of accomplishment, but none of that is relevant in this game when you have no reference points.  Do you have all the levels?, maybe.  Do I care about anything in the story other then the final boss that I have no connection with?, no. Am I getting better against the stale AI?, don't know.

_childDocuments_.review: DiRT 5 from the outside seems like a worthy entry to the series, but after playing it for a bit, I noticed it's a DiRT game in name only like Showdown was.Not a bad thing exactly, though if you were expecting a sim the likes of DiRT Rally, then this ain't it chief. Rallying, which is a staple in every DiRT game (except Showdown) is nowhere to be found in 5. In a series centered around rallying, you would think that would be an option, but that's not the case unfortunately. So what game modes are there? Well let's take a look shall we?The standard race modeSame as Ultra Cross but on ice.You take a buggy and drive it across excessively bumpy terrain uphill against the clock.Off road oval racing in sprint cars.Basically a level editor: create your own stunt course and share it with the world.Cross country point to point racing in trucks and buggies.Closed circuit racing in trucks and buggies.Cross country circuit racing in trucks and buggies.Perform drifts, spins, jumps, etc. in a closed arena while earning the highest score possible against the clock. Since DiRT 3, any inclusion of Gymkhana in future entries tend to be polarizing. I personally see no problem with it, but YMMV.In a nutshell: No rally, but there is GYMKHANA!!!Think GTA 3 era level of damage. There's no mechanical damage either, so if you crash into a barrier at 100+ MPH... BOOM! Engine block is still intact and the car is still driveable. DiRT 1 - 4 had mechanical damage, so why not this one? Manufacturer pressure? If that's the case, then CM isn't really at fault here.Good:-The weather effects, wetness of the cars.-Cars will get dirty overtime from dirt, mud, etc.-The cars themselves don't look too bad either.Bad:-The cockpit has no working mirrors-The clouds remind me of a 2D skybox-Some of the texture work TAA appears to have been fixed as of update 4.00I mean... DiRT 2 and 3 looked better than this. That's not good.Specs for reference:RTX 2060 SuperRyzen 5 1600 @ 3.8GHz16GB RAM @ 3000MHzRunning on an SSDI didn't really notice any stuttering while playing, but I did notice my framerate fluctuating from 45 - 35FPS. The reason was the game's global illumination setting which for some reason destroys your framerates at its highest. Lowering it to high yields a boost to performance with an unnoticeable difference to visual fidelity. Despite that, I still see random framerate drops here and there on some courses. Optimization needs work Codies.Stop this. Just stop. Haven't you learned from DiRT 2? Not even Troy Baker can make annoying voice overs in a racing game exciting. Subjective, but I personally don't like the soundtrack. It's not my cup of tea.It's a decent arcade racer, but not the sequel to DiRT 4 you're looking for.EDIT: As of update 4.00, the game still performs poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much a "Not recommended" from me.This is not DIRT 5, this is Gravel 2. As in, there's no actual motor sports here, no rally, no realistic or quasi-realistic events; instead, there are these really shallow, one-off arcade races. No car customization, no car progression, no meaningful vehicle stats; none of the things characteristic to the DIRT games are present.What a super bland way to end the series of great rally games, not with a bang, but with this pathetic whimper.And yeah, the graphics are cute, and they made the day-night cycle, so it gets dark while you're driving. You know what other driving games have this feature? All of them. Project Cars has this feature. GTA 3 has this feature. You can't imagine anything less interesting, gameplay-wise, than a day-night cycle.Son I'm disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: The weakest mainline DiRT from the ones I played (2,3,5), probably more comparable in quality to DiRT Showdown.Not worth the full asking price.Environments/Locations are great, modes are fairly standard. I personally like the basic lap-mode and A to B races the most, while I dislike gymkhana (huge fan in DiRT 3) and feel neutral about most of the true new modes of 5. Car selection is good. Dynamic weather and time are good concepts, but dynamic time changes too abruptly. Weather effects are good, but sometimes too much (blizzard-like visuals). Night race + icy track + blizzard + thunder is a blindingly bad combo imho. I really like the fact most locations actually feature snow too, so while there are full snow locations it's not like they are the only ones - that makes the other locations a little more interesting. The livery customization is OK, but I got bored of it past customizing 5 cars. The playground mode mode where you can create and race custom made maps is a good idea, but I only tried it twice so far.The game is marred by meh and sometimes inconsistent AI, fairly bad physics/handling (I personally expected something closer to DiRT 2/3, but outside the comparison it still doesn't hold up - it has an odd feel to it, but is still fun more often than not) and a very lacking online experience with an online mode that might nearly be DOA at least as far as PC is concerned. All you can do is search for a lobby and once the race is done you get to search again, which is annoying as you mostly end up with the same bunch of guys as last time anyway => time waster. Again, compared to DiRT 2/3 it is sorely lacking.Unlike the handling aspect, I believe this comparison is less subjective: DiRT 3 offered proper player-made lobbies where you could set up races; especially privately organized events were a blast because you could set them up beforehand, then just load them in. That excitement, including the one from random MP is essentially gone. While I find the graphics decent for the most part, the game runs poorly (compared to most other games) and does have some ugly textures (particularly noticeable at the start sequence) as well. If you count the pros and cons, you might end up with 2 roughly equal lists.However, I put more weight on the con-side because those matter a lot more to me: The physics and car handling are the foundation of my enjoyment in a racing game. Added to it, the sp/mp experience takes a large part too, but neither scores particularly highly - especially compared to its predecessors (important, because it shows CM can do better).Conclusion:DiRT 5 isn't all bad, but far from good for me. Ultimately, it didn't meet expectations.

The tracks and events are fun and varied. Didn't like gymkhana but you can easily avoid it and progress through the career mode. Graphics are some of the best I've seen. The dynamic weather events are the best part. The music is terrible and V.O. was a waste of money. The story comes through a podcast but it's easily skipped. Really happy with the game and recommend it to any Horizons fans. Everyone else might want to try Dirt Rally.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people seemed to think this will be a simracing game so let me start with saying that  (even a bit to arcade for my taste in case of some car classes availible). Some people are experiencing technical issues so if you're hesitant maybe wait until patches roll out but I'd say DIRT 5 is worth checking out.+ Atmosphere of the game similiar to DIRT 2 that I loved+ Colorful and detailed tracks and locations+ Gymkhana returning+ Large selection of vehicles and vehicle classes+ + Playgrounds editor (although it is a bit cluncky to work with)+ DIRT Donut Podcast (but the way it is implemented in the game leaves me to think a lot of people might simply ignore it)+ Soundtrack (pretty much all of it with a few exceptions)- At times it feels a bit too arcade for my taste- The carrer lacks a build up similiart to that in DIRT 2 (racing till you earn your place in the XGames event that consisted of a few races; Here the "chapter ending" is just another race)- The story is implemented more as a background for the races and it feels like you could simply miss it if you won't "Stay a while and listen"- Gymkhana feels a bit chaotic (at least in comparison to what I remember from DIRT 3)Take my comparisons to DIRT2/3 with a grain of salt since it been a while since I played those games and I'm refering to how I remembered those games. _childDocuments_.review: This is an odd beast. Theres plenty good in the game itself, but plenty bad inside of its presentation at the same time.First and foremost, this should not have been a DIRT/DiRT title. Yes it is a rally-esque racer; plenty of off road and technical on-road tracks. Some sprints inside, and Gymkhana from (at least) DIRT3. Its fun even, if the brand optionals may be nigh impossible.But there is not a single, classic, rally sprint within the base campaign I've seen so far. Its all pack racing, barring one time-trial rock-climber and Gymkhana. Compounding the idea of this in my opinion is the game does not shut up. I think the deal with Donut Media was a bad choice in the end; Codemasters likely was pressured by something to make the most out of the deal. Which meant a lot of talking. Forza H4 knew to be quiet. A couple of lines here and there in game, but all mostly just for introductions and the optional story missions. Only coming back for massive milestone unlocks. Another game that had this problem is NFS Heat, it always wanted you to do the story every time you start it up and left the garage. And then still reminded you that you did it afterward.The only audience I can suggest this to is a casual, arcade, audience that follows the offroad scene only through the internet/youtube podcasts and so. Anyone looking for more proper rally within the series should look to DiRT Rally games.

_childDocuments_.review: So, to start off, I have played Dirt 4 and Dirt Rally 2.0, and I love both. Codemasters know how to make a good rally game, but it seems like they've decided rally sim isn't really their thing anymore. I came into this expecting Dirt 4 but with new locations, new cars, better graphics, and even more realistic gameplay and the only thing I got were new locations. Which I didn't like cause as far as I could see through going over the menu's. Normal Rally stages seem to have gone away. Which for a game supposedly about rally is, well, disappointing to say the least.Things I liked:Environment graphics and shading is to be expected from a modern game.It stars Donut Media, which is always a plus, love those guys.Things I didn't like:Driving felt horrible. As someone else said in their review, you hit anything slightly (other than other cars) and you're stopped. Driving feels like I'm in a FWD car, steering feels like I'm in a RWD car, and it turns out I'm in an AWD car, which doesn't really make much sense. I have tricksteering off and everything set to the most realistic driving experience possible and it felt the furthest from it.The music was so loud and in your face (of course there's audio options, but this was not what I expected from this game)Menu felt extremely cluttered.I thought the main Dirt series was supposed to be a mix between sim rally and arcade, so it'd be fun for anyone. But they've just gone full arcade. I'm just about to request a refund now.

_childDocuments_.review: You are probably going to love this game or hate it.Yes, there is no WHEEL SUPPORT as of right now.This game is some of the most fun I've had out of a racing game in awhile. This is the perfect game to just sit back and relax. Its wild, fun, colorful, and just downright awesome to sit through. I kinda wish there were some rally tracks, but I don't think that would've fit with the game. This game embraces its arcade style and features, down to its core. There's nothing really serious about it and I believe that's what CodeMasters was going for.My only problem with the game is that I wish it was better optimized, but I still manage to run it at 60fps at 1440p so I can't really complain. Graphics could be better for a next gen title, but I cannot ignore the lighting effects, the mud/water splashes, the weather effects and how it changes the physics slightly to add immersion.I would personally wait for a sale if I were you, but I preordered it since I just haven't played a DiRT game in awhile.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you are in any way, shape or form a fan of the Dirt franchise's previous instalments, this game is not worth your time and especially not your money. Codemasters should be ashamed at putting out this shovelware.How Codemasters went from producing the almost masterpiece that is Dirt Rally 2.0, to this steaming pile of barely mediocre garbage is beyond me. Going into this I was hoping (and expecting) for a Dirt 2 or Dirt 3 style handling model that strikes a lovely balance between simulation and arcade that we've all come to know and love from Codies, but instead we've been given these mobile game-tier physics that are so hilariously inconsistent and one dimensional that I had to check if this game hadn't been farmed out to some 3rd party developer.And not only that, before you even get to be subjected to the awful handling model that makes the original Watch Dogs look like Gran Turismo or Assetto Corsa, you get to be subjected to the incredibly annoying and cringeworthy contributions of Donut Media, who have been enlisted not only to record all of the voiceovers for the event tutorials/intros, but also some awful podcast that plays automatically seemingly at random in the menus.Graphically at least the game looks quite nice with great weather effects and lighting, but the removal of any and all forms of anti-aliasing other than TAA garbage is a huge letdown, with VERY noticeable ghosting, and odd sparkling of reflective surfaces like they have a fine golf ball texture to them instead of being smooth. The damage modelling may as well be completely removed too, with the procedural damage of previous Dirt games having been thrown out the window for a pre-generated damage model that looks garbage and doesn't match up to how the cars feel when colliding with each other and with the environment.The career races are very same-y, it does not take long at all for the game to start feeling repetitive which doesn't bode well, it's just as well the campaign is so short because I don't think I could handle racing through Brazil in buggies for the 827th time. The throwdown events against the supposed big bads amount to little more than a distraction, if anything they're actually easier than the campaign races because you don't have to deal with passing more than 1 braindead AI racer.Overall, don't waste your money on this trite. If you haven't got it already, go get yourself a cheap key for Dirt 3 and play that instead, it's a far more interesting and fulfilling game than D5 is, and unfortunately short of massive changes in the fundamentals of the game Dirt 5 will be destined for bargain bins and deep discounts ad infinitum. I can only hope that the next Dirt game doesn't repeat the same mistakes of this one, but given that EA now owns Codies I have a bad feeling we're only in for a lovely helping of Games-as-a-Service garbage with DLC and microtransactions galore.
_childDocuments_.name: DIRT 5

_childDocuments_.review: First hour with this title leaves me feeling very let down. I was so bored I couldn't stand anymore and just had to quit out of the game. I'm not even sure why but it's probably due to a combination of things rather than 1 single issue. The tracks so far all feel alike. Instead of the tracks using soft barriers in natural environments they instead all seem to use hard track barriers. Handling all feels the same...VERY boring (all assists off)...fairly child-like. Every track feels like a muddy slippery mess and the cars just feel benign. I can't quite articulate why, but I'd much rather play Dirt4 and Dirt 3 so far. Grid2019 felt fun...this feels BORING.  The driving itself is boring and the tracks are all boring thus far (I have not seen them all yet, to be fair).Right now...if I was asked to give this title an age rating I'd rate it for ages 12-16. I hope I change my mind, but as of this moment I'm thinking this was my worst gaming purchase of 2020 by far.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review after trying the game for just shy of 2 hours during the free weekend.This is quite an enjoyable arcade racing game, a good change of pace after putting a lot of time on some more realistic racing sims like DiRT Rally and ACC.If you seek an experience comparable to them, this is not the game you are looking for.The driving is fun, it is very easy when comparing to the more realistic games, which I like because you can focus on just going as fast as you can without worrying about losing control of your car etc. I drove with all assists disabled and still under no circumstances did I feel like the car didn't do what I wanted. (except once, but that was just me being stupid). You also don't really need to worry about hitting other cars or walls too much, in fact, more often than not the game actually tells you to trade paint.In terms of cars available, there is a very nice and wide selection and the tracks are fun to drive, very fitting for this more casual type of driving.I feel like the game's UI is bit of a hit or miss. Personally I like the very colourful and funky style, but can totally see some people really disliking it.The graphics are very nice. This was one of the first games I played on my new 1440p HDR monitor, and it looked fantastic with all settings on High, which is still below the Ultra High settings.TL;DRWould I recommend this game?If you are looking for some fun, casual driving, totally. However if you want a more realistic racing experience, I suggest you look elsewhere.I don't quite think the game is worth the full price, but if you see it on sale, I'd say that give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: About a year later, most bugs have been fixed, more content has been added, and the game works well on Linux through Proton now. No more asterisks*, this game is pretty damn good.The best way to describe it is that it's an offroad Driveclub, mixed with some hints of Motorstorm. This is where Evolution Studios ended up after all. The physics feel nice, track design is great, there's a good variety of content (now), and it looks stunning. Solid 8/10, It's a great arcade racer.And people seem to be upset about that last part, but it's not like these identity crises are new to the DiRT franchise. Remember that we went from DiRT 3, to DiRT Showdown, to DiRT Rally on the release timeline. Don't expect this to be anything like DiRT 4, and don't expect the eventual DiRT 6 to be anything like this. It's best to just look at each game in isolation, and this one is pretty good under that criteria.*Okay, one asterisk, the game still uses Denuvo. Don't buy it if you don't have a stable internet connection (or would prefer to avoid nonsense like this).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is going  be controversial with the whole 'Go back to Sim Racing!' or 'This isn't racing!' thing. In my eyes, it really isn't about that - This is not what the game was made to be for.DIRT 5 is an Arcade style off-road racing game. It wasn't made to be a Sim Racer, it was made to be an ARCADE. And for some reason, that's where a lot of people seem to be losing track of the game. If you want to play a a Sim Racing Rally game, go and play Dirt Rally 2. After all, that's what the game was meant to be released for. Now with that out of the way, let's talk about the actual game itself...I was lucky enough to be able to be given a Content Creators Key by Codemasters, and I thank them for handing me they key. I have to say, I thoroughly enjoyed it! But, I'm not going to look at it from the perspective of 'I got it for free and I must rate it highly', because that's not what this review is about. I'm going to look at it from the £45 PoV. So - Is it worth £45? No - It isn't. But the fun from the game is not to be forgotten about. There's multiple different classes of Off-Road, some wacky, some... interesting. The physics are exactly what you would expect from an Arcade game. The online is a bit of a cluster****, and right now as of this review, there is currently no wheel support put into the game - Which is a huge flaw for someone who usually would always use a wheel for these kinds of games & sim racers. The Graphics are very nice as well, and you don't need a crazy spec PC to play it too. The weather effects are pretty nice too! You can go from Racing into the burning heat of Brazil, and then jump straight into the Snowy lands in Norway, racing underneath the Northern Lights. Mighten I add, it was pretty damn beautiful. There's plenty of car customisation too - And I expect Codemasters to add even more in the future.So, to Finalise all this up, If you want to buy a sim racing rally game, this is not the game for you. If you want to play a casual, wacky, off-roading arcade racer, then you'll more than likely enjoy this. However, the Price tag for the amount of content there is inside of the game, will remain in question!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing this game... but I have to give it a negative/neutral rating.-Career mode is a joke, you can get casually playing in around 6 hours to end credits.-No performance upgrades or adjustment for cars. This game is nearing mobile game level of casual in regards of depth.-Basically 2 car choices per track type, there's one free car unlocked, and then you can select and buy another car from very few options. No sense of progression since once you can afford the first car, there is nowhere to upgrade after that.-Inconsistent difficulty. I was playing on Hard with all assists off, but still I was on 1st place the whole race on most events. Would've gone Very Hard, but on some events I was struggling to rise from the 12th place.-Lack of tracks. You race around the world but the track selection per one location is basically the same track with little variation (reverse, snowing or alternate route etc.)Apparently there is more content locked behind DLC's, but according to reviews, they seem to be very shady cash grabs.For the full price of 55€ and 75€ for bundled dlc's this game is very much NOT worth the full price.You should only buy this if you are looking for non-open-world game and can get this for a heavy discount. The physics feel less authentic, and the game has a more childish tone.While I do enjoy playing DiRT 5, it's definitely not for players who are looking for a more simulator-like experience. If you're looking for a more casual and relaxed racing game, DiRT 5 may be worth considering.However, I would recommend using a controller rather than a wheel to get the most enjoyment out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had an absolute blast with this game!Initially I had a rough time and I could see why people were complaining. But after adjusting the AI difficulty and messing with the driving settings, I was amazed by how much fun the game is. Is it perfect? Of course not. The sprint races are terrible and not fun (luckily there's not too many), the sponsor system is basic and repetitive and sometimes the graphics are a little inconsistent (probably due to the lightning on some areas). But if you don't take the game too seriously, it's amazing. The things I liked the most were: The driving - controls are responsive and it's super fun to go fast and drift; graphics - even after playing FH5, Dirt 5 still looks amazing and impresses me everytime I play due to being very vibrant; dynamic weather - some races start at night and end in the morning, others start with a sunny day and end very cloudy and raining with puddles everywere, the highlight for me were the thunderstorms during night races that blew me away the first time I saw it; race types - Gymkhana returns and its quite fun but the most enjoyable for me is Path Finder; car list - the amount is decent, but what I found interesting were some vehicles that I've never seen before and using cars I never thought for off road racing, like the Bentley Continental GT for instance.Overall, I understand the mixed rating as it might not be for everybody (especially for old Dirt fans). But what I did that really helped was appreciating the game for what it is and not what I want it to be and not treat it like it has to beat Forza or Need for Speed, simply treat it as an alternative when you're bored of those games.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, where landscapes overwhelm driving and weather, slightly changing during a race, adds a cherry on top. Oh, cars are there, but I assure you – the eyes will be absorbing all those forests, mountains, cracking ice and mud. Lots of mud! The racing itself is… casual. Press W and keep other fingers doing munching cookies, because difficulty in Dirt 5 is very low.W/o it you can’t customize a car. You can’t create custom racing tracks or stunt areas. It is a mystery to me why, as all those objects, unfolding menu creation and spinning road items can be easily placed with keyboard and mouse.I remember Dirt 3 for its trophies “drive with a certain cabin view and no HUDs, finish in specific times”. I remember Dirt Showdown for some derby mode challenges and spins.Dirt 5 has none of these. All it “challenges” is to complete a certain season and drive lots of miles. Thanks!So, if you want a chilled race in lovely sceneries, then yes, do get Dirt 5. Because who doesn’t want to race under a Northern Lights sky, right?
