detailed_description: Join Lucky on his thrilling journey through the Book of Ages, a magical artifact that opens doors to amazing worlds. Meet new friends, explore exciting lands, and recover the missing pages from the evil sorcerer Jinx and his villainous family, the dreaded Kitty Litter. • Featuring a huge variety of gameplay, from expansive 3D hubs, to story-based adventure levels, 2D side-scrolling challenges, rewarding mini-games, mind-bending puzzles, and thrilling boss battles. • Thousands of collectibles to gather, tons of rewarding secrets to discover, a cast of memorable characters, and an entire wardrobe of costumes for the stylish adventurer. • Designed to delight and challenge players of all ages and skill levels. • A complete re-imagining of the original Super Lucky's Tale, featuring redesigned and new levels, a fully rotatable camera, tighter movement control, and major overhauls to nearly every other aspect, including the story, cinematics, music, and more. _childDocuments_.review: An incredibly charming, Mario-like Jump 'n Run with clean graphics, tight controls, very catchy music (the music is REALLY catchy, alright) and a carefree attitude carried out by the overall happy-go-lucky theme of the game. New Super Lucky's Tale (NSLT) is an enhanced version of Super Lucky's Tale (SLT), including its DLCs, which I played on the Xbox One as part of the Gamepass. Contrary to my normal gaming schedule, I 100%-ed it back then, because I just had a ton of fun with it.While I haven't played NSLT all too much yet, judging by what I've seen so far, Playful took care of the biggest weaknesses of SLT. The camera is free look now and can be tilted and rotated to the hearts desire, and the levels have undergone an overhaul in many regards. It's the same game at heart, but still feels fresh due to the many big and small changes - lot of details added and tweaked and mechanics adjusted to keep the game fresh.It's a really nice platformer that doesn't try to do anything extraordinary. But the things it does are more than solid and varied enough to carry through without a hint of boredom arising. The difficulty is very manageable in the main game, though the optional DLC levels turn it up two notches without going completely overboard either - they are however meant for advanced players.I'm absolutely looking forward to a Super Lucky's Tale 2 now. (N)SLT is a game that's able to bring a smile to the face, and I'd love to see the adventures of the adorable fox Lucky continue.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Super Lucky's Tale is traditionally built. There are a number of different worlds, with each world eventually having a boss to defeat.However, before you get to the final boss, you must collect four-leaf clovers in one of the many levels in each world.Some of these levels consist of only one puzzle, other levels are small worlds in themselves with lots to discover and in other levels the game changes into a 2D platformer.A lot of variation, but in each level it is ultimately about collecting those four-leaf clovers.Here you can see a piece of gameplay: The game also works great on a steam deck: On the other hand, Super Lucky's Tale is not a particularly easy game, even though dying has little to no consequences.It is a game that, as befits a good platformer, relies on skill.The 2D levels in particular can get unexpectedly spicy when you jump onto rotating platforms at a rapid pace and dodge bee stings.Moreover, in these 2D levels, the depth is sometimes played with, so that you suddenly end up in a layer 'behind' the level. The biggest challenge is then to keep an overview.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A splendid Update to Super Lucky's Tale [SLT]; New Super Lucky's Tale [NSLT] adds a Ton of Improvement and Fixes to the Original 2017 Release.I was able to 100% Everything Including All Achievements. Thankfully, the grinding Achievements from Super Lucky's Tale did not return.Visuals - 4/5----------While largely Unchanged from SLT, NSLT adds far more Cutscenes with each Including far more Expression and Liveliness to the Game. These really Help bring more Flavour to the Characters, Story and Presentation.Lucky now Runs on Two Legs compared to All Fours In SLT. This really Helps Fit Him Into the Worlds around Him. His Attacks are Swift and much more Responsive. Several Levels have been adjusted to Include more Colourful Lighting and Warmer/Cooler Tones depending on the Setting. Almost All Cutscenes are done In-Engine but the Prologue and Epilogue change the Painted Style from SLT to a far more Expressive yet less Detailed Cartoon/Comic Style.Controls - 5/5-----------A Massive Improvement from SLT, Lucky Is more Responsive than ever. His Attacks are Swift and have far better Hit Detection, Making Combat much more Enjoyable and less Chance of Lucky being Suckerpunched from a Random Projectile or Enemy. His Movement Is far less Floaty than In SLT too; Giving the Player much more Control.Camera Controls are another much needed Improvement with a Full 3D Camera compared to SLT's 45 Degree Tilting Camera. This can really Help give Broader Perspective on each World that Lucky can Travel to.Again, Lucky's Double Jump doesn't gain much Height but He Is able to Clamber onto Surfaces far more Easily; Reducing the Number of awkward Jumps and Chances of Falling to Death.It Is also now Impossible to Die In Hub Worlds; Thereby Inhibiting the Loss of Player Lives while Exploring.Sound - 5/5---------Sound Quality is largely Unchanged; However, The Soggy Boggy Boy's Song has Changed to a far more Lively Track compared to the Slower Song from SLT. Lady's Meowmalade's Boss Track Is still as Pumping as before and the Overall Sound Design and Soundtrack Is the Same as SLT.Gameplay - 5/5-------------Lucky's Tailswipe has Increased to a 3-Hit Combo from the Simple Swipe from SLT. Combat Is far more Responsive and Pleasing to Perform; Especially with the better Hit Detection.While most Levels are Unchanged, The Spookington Hub has been completely Redesigned to Hauntingham and the Level for the Soggy Boggy Boys In Veggie Village has been Expanded and takes place at Night, Giving It a larger Platforming Aspect.Enemies Types are the Same; However, Some Bosses have seen Upgrades. Some almost Unnoticeable and Others far more Improved over Their SLT Counterparts.The New 3D Camera also Helps the Player In Navigating the Large Levels and prevent any Accidental Deaths from Falling.The DLC from SLT has been Flawlessly Implemented Into NSLT; Fitting the Narrative much more Smoothly.Overall - 19/20----------As a Fan of the Original SLT, I was Quick to Grab NSLT at Its Initial Sale Price and was rather Impressed with the Amount of Tuning that Plaful Corp. had made to the Game. 3D Platforming Fans that are New to Lucky's Adventure will be sure to Enjoy the Colourful and Free-Spirited Journey that Lucky takes on His Quest to Recover the Pages for the Book of Ages. Fans Familiar with the Series may want to Consider Waiting for a Sale but will be Pleasantly Surprised with what Is In Store.  Hope We will get to Continue Our Adventures with Lucky In a Sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: To make it short, an absolutely charming and awesome platformer true to the best traditions. Honestly, can’t really think of anything you could make better here. Scenarios vary a lot, whatever you can think of, be it 2D, 3D, puzzle-sections, runner levels, arenas and whatnot. Great quality in animations, voice-overs and music, innovative ideas and characters all around. You can literally feel all the love that was put into this game, no kidding. Difficulty also is very forgiving and more on the casual side (but still engaging enough to keep your attention, probably even good for children with a little experience). That said, I admit the game isn’t really that long if you’re rushing through it (only 6 worlds with 4-5 main levels mostly), but if you’re going for completion the time stamp is just ideal in my opinion. So, enough said, big recommendation from me, definitely one of the must-plays for every 3D platformer lover with a knack for the old stuff, at least I enjoyed every minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It ain't every day that you get to see an overhaul of a game being sold as a new release (especially one that bundles the previous version of itself as mandatory), and it also ain't every day that that overhauled release ends up being worth it.New Super Lucky's Tale (with the emphasis on "New") addresses pretty much every shortcoming its original version released with. The game is optimized now, and no longer hitches every odd minute. The worlds and antagonists have had a lot of work put into them to give them much-needed personality and liveliness. A lot of filler content is cut, and the remaining levels are refined to make full use of the newly-added free camera control. The cosmetics have had their prices rebalanced to be more reasonable and fun to acquire, and the overal story feels a lot more cohesive with DLC in it as an integral part, rather than an afterthought.Overall, the whole experience is way more enjoyable now, even if you have already played through the older version of the game. The game went from passable to recommendable, albeit still very simplistic and uninventive. But sometimes you don't want to be dazzled by new ideas. Sometimes all you want is a lightweight, easy to jump-in, polished platformer, and NSLT fits that like a glove.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: So, best thing to look forward to with this game is the furry fan art of Lucky’s sister.This is probably the closest we’ll ever get to a Tails spin-off game.It’s a platformer game with a Fox, I was sold from the start.I played Super Lucky’s Tale on PC and it was a charming as hell experience. I’m   very happy that it got an updated version that helped improve the game flow. The new one is essentially SLT 2.0. At it's core, it's the same game but with a ton of changes to make it better.Basically the same as the Ori and the Blind forest releases.To me, a great game is one that has deep exploration of the gameplay mechanics. And every moment of this game is a good solid/fun challenge. The worst games are those that are just walk from point A to B and press a button. It's not the destination that's interesting, it's the journey itself, and that's why this game is so great.On top of that, there is beautiful art, an engaging story, and hilarious characters full of personality to contextualize the gameplay and elevate this game to a level of greatness beyond other 3D platformers. This is the true successor to Banjo-Kazooie. This studio actually understands what made that game great and elevates those elements further, while cutting out the stuff that made BK not so good.It's so frustrating to hear when people say 3D platformers are out-dated and point to Yooka-Laylee as an example. No they are outdated, Yooka-Laylee is just not a well designed game.A lot of people slept on this one. Hopefully word of mouth spreads. I think nowadays games that are targeted to a younger audience have a harder time selling. They still have put out a very polished product but they are competing against legacy ip like the nintendo stuff, cheap mobile games targeted to children, and a lot of gamer's perception that these type of games are only for kids. It's a shame to see.Good 3D platformers will never be outdated!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so let's get to the point: If you are in the fence about buying this, wondering what the difference is between "New Super Lucky's Tale" and the older "Super Lucky's Tale", then it's pretty simple; this game 'NSLT' is a full remake. And more than just that, really. Here are the differences:- All levels are completely different. They retain the essence of the old version, but have been remade and redesigned from    the ground up. - Some new levels have been added.- Camera is no longer fixed. It's now 100% free and you can rotate it in every axis.- The progression dynamic has been tweaked to be more streamlined.- Completely new animations and in-engine cutscenes.- Revamped story. It now makes more sense.- Lucky runs on two limbs now instead of four. I personally loved the classic walking animation as it looked more fluid and    graceful. Lucky now looks like Mario when walking, running. A bit stiff in my opinion.- Lucky now has new moves, like sliding and a three-hit melee tail combo.- Overall control responsiveness has been improved. The old game was good in this aspect, but this one is an absolute   pleasure to play.- Better hitbox detection.- World feels a lot more interactive now.- Better balancing for acquiring in-game collectibles.- New costumes.- Polished graphics.- Improved soundtrack.- DLC has been integrated into the story.The only negative I find is that if you purchased the classic game (like me), you will have to buy this game separately and it is another $40 dollars. Is it worth it? That's subjective. I love this kind of games and I don't mind spending the extra money. Can you justify buying this if you already have the classic game? Absolutely 100%.I just recently installed the classic game and played it after having it sitting in my library for more than a year. I intermediately bought this game after when I found out about it and playing it ATM. I had a bit of buyer's remorse at first, but after playing through the first two world hubs, I've realized this is a completely different game. I don't feel like I'm playing just a polished version of the old one.Bit of an odd situation with this game, as both were released with a two year difference. But I totally understand what the devs did and why. The original game was good, but they were given the chance to improve upon that and get the game closer to their original view. They definitely accomplished that.As I mentioned in my other review: If you're a fan of oldschool 3D platformers, this is one little gem you must have in your collection. Both of them, in my humble opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a bit of vagueness on if it's a sequel or an enhanced port, this is actually a complete rework of the original Super Lucky's Tale. All levels have been remade from the ground up and the moveset as well as camera have been revamped while also integrated the previous game's DLCs into the campaign's story naturally, thus it's both familiar and new at the same time, preserving everything that made the original so fun and still feeling fresh enough to warrant playing it whether you're a returning or a new player.Regardless, if you like platformers more on the collectathon heavy side like Spyro, Crash, Donkey Kong and don't mind the aspect of pure fun factor over actual challenge, New Super Lucky's Tale is definitely worth buying. The only downside is that it's a little short, and honestly unless you're desperate for more of this kind of gameplay formula you'd best wait for a sale

_childDocuments_.review: , not to be confused with  (a separate, earlier version of the game) or  (The first game in the series, VR-only) is a very basic 3D platformer with some collect-a-thon elements and lots of adorable charm. This game feels like it’s aimed at, or at least made accessible to, younger kids. I feel like this would be a great first video game for children. Lucky has a very simple moveset, there are no upgrades to hunt for, and there isn’t even a run button. It sticks with a very approachable setup. Levels are on the shorter and easier side, but have  enough bite to them; they seem like the kind of challenges that would make a newcomer to gaming feel very proud and accomplished to conquer them for the first time. There’s also a decent variety of levels (including 3D platforming stages, 2D platforming stages, block-pushing puzzles, auto-running sections, and a few more), which I imagine could serve as someone’s introduction to a lot of common gameplay conventions. Controls and physics are basically perfect; I never had a single “I disagree” moment with any collision detection or camera movement. I didn’t notice any level design that accentuated weaknesses with the controls or physics. I only had a few problems with 3D perspective in space and distance-judging at times when Lucky’s shadow wasn’t visible, but a little bit of gameplay experience took care of that.For the experienced players, it does turn up the heat in the bonus post-credits zone and with some of the achievements. Some of them bordered on frustrating, but only  enough to make it feel satisfying to get them over with quickly.Complaints? I have a few. Mainly, it’s just too short. I beat the game in about 7 hours, with 100% completion in 12 hours. I don’t quite think that’s enough to justify a $30 price tag. Granted, this is full AAA production quality here (and I mean the good kind), and children might take much longer on this… but in comparison to any 3D Mario, this game just ends as soon as it’s starting to get really good. Also, Lucky is a bit… obnoxiously childish with his voice lines. You get to endure a constant stream of “HAHA! YEA! WHOA! AHHH!! COOL! LET’S DO THIS! HA! C’MON!” Really, I get that he’s a cartoon, and it’s probably okay for young kids, but I found it grating from the very start and got the initial impression I was playing a game for 5-year-olds. In contrast, I thought the other characters with their gibberish NPC dialogue were adorable, especially the kitten villains! I found myself rooting for the villains in this game, and I kind of hope the next sequel brings them back as good guys or something. It’s just Lucky who needs to tone it down a notch. Not even Mario and Sonic were this aggressively playful. (Speaking of Mario, check out how they used the Tick Tock Clock sound effect in the level “8-Fold Path” – They  what they were doing. .)In all, what’s here is super solid. I’d give it a 7 / 10. Fun, accessible, delightfully colorful, fair and not too punishing. Lucky’s voice might outstay its welcome, but the gameplay does not, not even close. If it were twice as long and kept up the quality, I’d probably give it a 9 or better. Good game!!

_childDocuments_.review: 3D collectathon platformers are pretty rare nowadays, and many of them are either disappointing like , or downright awful like . New Super Lucky's Tale is just decent. It doesn't excel at anything, but it's very polished. The controls and the camera are perfect, the graphics are clean and colorful, there's a decent variety in environments, featuring all your favorite platformer tropes from castles to beaches to graveyards.You might wonder, what's up with the weird title and how many Lucky's Tale games are there? Technically just one, but they keep remaking it over and over. The first one, simply called , was an Oculus Rift exclusive VR game. Then they remade it from scratch as a flat game, called , although it was stuck with a fixed camera angle. And then finally Nintendo reached out to them and they got enough budget to remake it one more time as New Super Lucky's Tale, and this time around they ironed out all the quirks and added a free camera. But the saga doesn't end here, the original VR game got a  (apparently with some enhancements too) just recently.The moveset is pretty simple, you can jump, swipe your tail and burrow underground, to either dig stuff up or avoid attacks or obstacles. There are no power-ups or any upgrade mechanics, the coins you collect are used only for unlocking outfits, which to be fair are all very cute. The levels come in both full 3D and 2.5D (sidescroller) variations, not unlike , and there are some puzzle challenges too.Now, the main issue with the game is the lack of any challenge. The collectibles are always in plain sight, the enemies are never a threat, the platforming segments are all slow paced and trivial. I 100%'d all 6 worlds in only 10 hours, and had 99 lives left over. Granted, the post-game chapter is a big jump in difficulty, but it still felt only moderately challenging compared to other games. and   are still way better games, but like I said, 3D platformers are a rare beast and if you've already played those this will do.

_childDocuments_.review: Differences to "Super Lucky's Tale"+ Improved graphics+ Improved story+ Better camera+ More costumes+ Altered levels+ More interesting NPC'sComing from playing "Super Lucky's Tale" this one does add some nice changes but I wouldn't say enough to justify it being sold as a different game.The game sports more artwork for cutscenes/story reasons and even a new ending which I hope will not just be forgotten as it can lead to an interesting sequel.Hub worlds have been changed and sadly no longer get stuff added to them to make them feel more complete, just an NPC from the world you just completed making it feel less satisfying. The statue in each world is also gone, would of been nice to have kept them in at least.Some levels have been completely made different and some even shorter making the game a lot easier which is ok but a bit disappointing as the original game was the nice amount of difficulty spike. Though some level changes now make the levels feel better and also make more sense to the world they are in.The bosses are still the same part from the final boss and you actually face Lady Meowmalade due to the DLC being included in this bundle by default. Costumes are now cheaper which I like as grinding in the last game was too boring. You even have costumes based off the bosses which was needed and I highly enjoy using and mixing up.Lastly, the camera is easier to control and move making some jumps and collectable hunting easier.p.s - Mail Golem is adorable please keep him

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original version a long time ago and enjoyed it so much, that I just had to buy this one and play it again.After playing this new version, I launched the original one to see the difference and wow, its a big one! In the new version, the graphics are smooth and the controls are tight! There are a few misses in my opinion. In Wigglemania the hitboxes are a bit messed up. When an enemy hits you, most of the time it won't register which of course is at your benefit, but its such a shame. What's even worse to me is the fact that in the original version, Lucky ran on all four and I thought it was so cute and playful. Now he's running oddly on two legs and it just looks wrong somehow. Feels like the animation is too fast for Lucky's pace. However, they've also changed the burrow animation and this one is for the better! I love how Lucky's tail pops out of the ground, it looks so cute. Burrowing was one of my favorite features in the original version and its even better in this one. The game has been made easier it seems, but it was never a hard game, so I don't think that matters. Maybe its just because the controls are suddenly on point, but its also super easy to get 100% achievements in this one.Of course the biggest change must be the fact that you are now able to control the camera angle and it makes a huge difference to the overall gameplay.Overall I would highly recommened this game to anyone who enjoys a casual game with a high cute factor. Huntingham alone is reason enough to play this game - Oh, how I wish Huntingham had been bigger!

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute and fun platformer collect-a-thon with tight and responsive controls, wonderful art direction, charming and crazy cast of characters, an adorable protagonist and an awesome soundtrack. It's got a lot of variety and fun gimmicks, plenty of collectibles and overall feels very polished and comfortable to play.The only real downside is that it's lacking a bit in the challenge department. The Guardian Trials steps things up a bit, but it would've been nice with some harder optional challenges, or a hard mode similar to Death Wish in A Hat in Time. That said, it's a great choice for younger kids or people who just want a fun and relaxing experience.This game definitely deserves more popularity, and I'd love to see a sequel some day. If you're into oldschool platformers like Spyro, Crash and Mario, don't sleep on this one. Heartily recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend a game enough for those looking for something new in the same vein as classic 3D platformers from the N64/PS1 era. This is it! Although the game is targeted to a younger audience, there's a lot that may keep you hooked no matter what the age: a fun and diverse selection of levels (3D, 2.5D side-scrolling, "runner" style levels, and a selection of varying bonus levels, just to name a few) and locations, cute characters, and whimsical and diverse soundtrack, just to begin with. Not to mention the Foxington hub world, designed for some pretty decently challenging stages!I should also mention that New Super Lucky's Tale ("NSLT") is not just a re-hash of Super Lucky's Tale ("SLT")... Well, it sort of is, but I like to think of it as a "re-imagining" of sorts. The new sliding ability combined with new animations, refined hub worlds, and new stages make the original SLT very difficult to come back to. The other big change that you can "feel out" when playing the game is the actual *flow* of the game. It's much more streamlined: using "pages per world" for unlocking new boss arenas in NSLT works a lot better than using "clovers per the entire game (a la "Super Mario 64"). This is something that you're going to have to judge for yourself, but after playing so many versions of this I can assure you that NSLT does it right.To play devil's advocate, I can agree that the game *could* be a bit longer, just because I'd love to see more of Lucky and this entire universe. Anyway, without a question this is one of my favorite recent 3D platformers, and I genuinely don't feel ashamed to say it's a 10/10 from me. :)

_childDocuments_.review: 10h 3/10 1 Yes, you can find one   No No Not really, you might already have all the customs needed before finishing the other achievements No No No No No difficulty options NoNew Super lucky's Tale is an amazing platformer. The game looks great, it feels very responsive and the level design is awesome. I did enjoy this game so much and quickly played through the whole game. The first world is good but doesn't shine yet, but from the second world, the game puts you in very creative level designs with funny tasks. Even a level where a very small part is a stealth section. New Super Lucky's Tale is has quite a lot of levels and each of them felt special and different enough. I had so much fun playing through the game. It reminded me back to the time we saw so many amazing 2d and 3d platformers from big companies, but this is one of the best ones!None of the achievements are missable as you can go back to earlier levels. I would recommend getting as many coins in each level so you can buy the customs you need for an achievement easily without going back, but I got them like an hour before completing all the other achievements, so if there is a grind, it isn't too bad. In each level you can get 4 collectibles, I would recommend trying to get all 4 on your first try or if you missing some, to go back directly and get it. You don't get any new moves or upgrades, so it will be the same difficulty later on and in that case, it is so much easier to get them all while you still remember the level from your first try. There are some level specific achievements, but a lot of those you'll unlock while playing through the game. I wouldn't  bother with a guide till later on when you're still missing a few and can't figure it out. A few of those are things like beating a specific boss or level section without getting hit. Those are the most challenging achievements in this game but are very doable with a few tries.

_childDocuments_.review: (New) Super Lucky's Tale is extremely enjoyable, wholesome and full of charm. It may not be complex but the controls and level design feel just right. Very smooth and polished.I had some chill fun with it all the way to 100% completion and achievements.A game doesn't need to have top of the line graphics to be beautiful, and NSLT's artstyle is a wonderful testament to that. I know many great indie platformers nail that too, but there's just something about NSLT's visuals that makes it feel right at home for me. It's just so clean and readable.The game's characters, both heroes and villains, are adorable and hilarious. Especially Lucky himself.About the only gripe I have is cutscenes being unskippable, which honestly doesn't matter as much as it normally would for me, cause I rarely found myself having to rewatch the same cutscene, unless I was replaying a level to do things I missed.In many other games this gripe could've had a much more negative impact for me, but it's extremely negligible in NSLT, and rarely gets in the way.I definitely recommend this game. Whether you're an adult or a kid, or a parent looking for something undemanding that your kid could play.I hope there'll be a sequel someday cause this was great. in the meantime, my compliments to the developers! New Super Lucky's Tale is just lovely.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a fun little 3D platformer in an era where good ones are sadly few and far in between.  NSLT doesn't really try anything new or daring over other 3D platformers, but considering how limited new options are today, just executing a basic, solid game in the genre is enough to stand out.  And NSLT is just that:  a solid little game that seems to draw inspiration from the Mario series.  (While it doesn't have the gravity and planetoid gimmicks, Super Mario Galaxy  like it was a big inspiration in my eyes.)Lucky controls well and has a simple, functional moveset that lets you chain moves together to navigate levels rather fluidly.  Lucky isn't nearly as speedy as some other platform mascots, like say Spyro, or have the sheer number of advanced movement options others might have, like sometimes Mario, but chaining moves and executing them to navigate platforming challenges quickly still feels satisfying.  The one option that probably stands out the most is probably burrowing.  While airborne, Lucky can dive, which has a homing effect somewhat similar to Sonic's, umm, Homing Attack.  But when it hits "soft" terrain, or you dive while standing on said terrain, Lucky will go underground and can speedily burrow just under the surface to avoid hazards, attack enemies, navigate puzzles, and more.  While the game is fun, it's not entirely perfect.  My biggest gripe would be the "marble levels", which make my vision feel funny after a bit between the static camera and how the board moves and sometimes also has some questionable physics.  I also feel the game is a wee bit on the short side.  Only 8 hours to clear all the stages, including post-game.  I don't have 100% in-game or achievements, which no doubt would tack on some more hours, but I can't see that taking more than 15 hours total.  A smaller nitpick is the difficulty.  The game is largely pretty easy.  It'll keep you on your toes and the post-game levels do offer up a good challenge, but some more challenging bits in the main game would have been nice, even if they were just optional side-passages for hidden pages and what-not.  And definitely would have loved more late-game/post-game levels on the tier of CH1P's or harder.  Other small nitpick is I feel Lucky's moveset could use more depth.  Maybe I'm spoiled in the sheer possibilities of Mario's moveset in Super Mario Odyssey, but having advanced movements that could let you skip or bypass obstacles, approach goals from abnormal routes, or skip parts of a level would breathe a lot of life into revisiting levels or speedrunning them.Overall though, NSLT is a good, albeit short and a bit easy, 3D platformer.  If you enjoy the genre then you really ought to consider picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: The base game of Super Lucky's Tale is well executed, although there is one major issue. It's easy.Like ridiculously easy. And that's okay, the game is a mascot platformer aimed at casual audiences and children. I'm absolutely fine with it being easy and was going to give it a recommendation even though I disliked the (to me, an adult who's been gaming since the 90s) excessively easy difficulty and simple puzzles. AND THEN THE DLC CAMEThe first DLC you'll encounter is Gilly Island, sandwiched before the final zone is a somewhat jarring difficulty spoke. But it's a spike in the case it goes from a 2 to a 4. More difficult sure but still easy. The statue puzzles however are FAR more difficult, and will genuinely challenge you at times. There were a few statue puzzles that took me longer than whole levels to work out, which is good I was into it.And if that was it, you'd see me recommending this game for what it was, but they didn't stop there.But the post game DLC where you do Guardian Trials is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ absurd. Forget going 2 to 4, this goes from 2 to 8. The levels are punishingly difficult, especially with the requirements for achievements, and with no built in restart button until the end of a level if you fail you are forced to either finish a failed run, or go into the menu to exit the level entirely only to reenter it. And sure (at least on my PC) a 5-10 second loading time between attempts isn't long, but it's just long enough for you to begin wondering why you're even bothering to do this. This wouldn't be so much of a problem if the difficulty gradually ramped up over the course of the game, but the two DLCs (and especially the Guardian Trials) were so obviously designed later on with the idea of placating adult players screaming about how easy the game was, that it comes off as jarring. The entire rest of the game is designed with casual gamers and children at the forefront of the devs minds, and it shows in a good way. But the game never grows. There's no new abilities or mechanics that cause you to go back to old levels to get stuff you couldn't on your first runthrough. There's nothing that has you learn or grow or change either as a character or as a player. It's just sort of a stale, frankly bland and cliche mascot platformer aimed at kids, right up until the post game where the intended playerbase goes up in age about thirty years.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is a massive improvement to the original "Super Lucky's Tale," where most of my issues and complaints were resolved or at least tweaked for the better. The story, cutscenes, music, gameplay, visuals, and collectibles feel smoother and generally like a completed concept, which made replaying some levels (that were the exact same from the original game) generally enjoyable.The only real issues were that some levels did not get changed enough (World 4, the beach area, is almost exactly the same down to the level layouts) and that you cannot skip cut-scenes or dialogue that are there to burn time. On the plus side, the coin achievements were reduced from 100K coins to just 12K, cutting the completion time for the game down by half (16.5 hours total to around 8.5).I would recommend this to anyone who wants a good 3D-Platforming experience, and you should absolutely avoid the original Super Lucky's Tale, unless you want to play them back-to-back to see the differences between the two versions, which is a cool concept.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: New Super Lucky's Tail is one of the better non-known platformers to come out in recent memories. The story is that Lucky Swiftail needs to find the pages of the book of ages to get back to his sister, but you have enemies you have to defeat to get back. There are 5 worlds with a mix of 4-6 levels in each one. You have to defeat the boss in each world to progress to a new one, but to get to the boss, you have to get a certain number of pages to unlock the door to get to them. The art is good and the controls and performance are where it should be for a game on PC. The music is good and the quality is top notch and I do like quite a few of the tracks. There are sliding puzzles where you have to move statues to certain spots to get a page. Most are easy but some do make you think. The worst mini-game and probably the worst thing about the game period, its the marble mazes. Controls are just so bad and the camera is static, so it's hard sometimes to see if you're about to hit a spike or not. The marble mini-games in Foxington aren't bad at all though. They're actually pretty decent. You do get Super Lucky's Tail with this as well and it's not bad, but this is the better version. Ultimately, we need more platformers like this. Mario may be the king of like, but we can still have other games like this as well. I finished it in under 8 hours, but I also played it on the Xbox, so I knew what I was mostly doing, so you might get 15ish hours. Definitely get it when it's on sale. If not, you won't be disappointed.

it could be i think.so yeah, i did enjoy going through it and finding all the secrets, but i expected a bit more of a challenge.. a newborn baby could probably finish this game.if i were to rate it... it'd probably be a 6/10.pros:- great control of character- interesting worlds, albeit a bit bland looking due to washed out colors and slightly less graphic quality- funny costumes you can purchase (reason to actually collect money other than just for a page)- mix up with 2D levels added in. not my favorite kind, but a welcome here and there for otherscons:- extremely easy levels with nothing to really challenge you- invisible barriers blocking you from exploring (i've died more from falling due to not being able to land on something than dying to something legit). i hate it when the game stops you from going somewhere you aren't quite intended to go. there are even parts that have no collision, so i fell right through the object i tried to land on- characters are bland and the dialogue is often a bore to sit through. characters also don't feel like they belong in the worlds, or the worlds just don't feel like a place they'd actually be in- washed out colors making the worlds look bland- inside ball mini-levels are annoying (honestly, who thought that was a fun concept?)hmm.. overall it is decent. nothing special though. i only recommend this if you're into 3D platformers and have absolutely nothing else to play.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS: Tight, clean controls - even further improved from the original release, from what I read - and a classic plaftormer's fun gameplay loop based on collectibles, a bit of puzzle solving, and the odd minigame here and there; classic "mascot" platformer, bright and colorful, similar to the new Spyro and Crash remakes that have rekindled the interest for this genre. Music is really good, graphics and character designs are incredibly well realized, story ties the stages together fairly well along with some awesome hand-drawn cutscenes, and gives the exploration a background purpose.CONS: Apart from being extremely easy, this game is built specifically with kids in mind. Its story, content and pacing is extremely childish, and unlike the Spyro and Crash remakes that are a revamp on old classics which were good for teens at the time, this is actually a fairly recent title that strives too much to bring back a type of 90's cheesy, childish vibe for kids (or rather, what adults at the time assumed would cater to kids) that was pretty much outdated the moment it was developed. It's almost, if not even more, as corny as Bubsy 3D.Lucky will try to break the fourth wall by looking into the camera as often as it's given the chance (the game design is built around this by purposefully starting each level with the character facing the screen);Every action, collectible pick up, enemy hit, world entering etc. is crammed with as many silly character grunts sounds as possible; the pages pick up animation and stage completion screen, Lucky's design with his short blue tablecloth cape and goofy oversized shoes, flailing in place but moving really slowly... so on and so forth.There are games that genuinely nail the cutesy look and experience by letting it be an organic and natural part of the design and writing of the characters and the world built around them - like A Hat in Time, just to give an example. This one, on the contrary, forces the "cute" down your throat by screaming "LOOK AT ME" every instant, a cautionary reminder that these exasperated style choices became extinct pretty much almost instantly in the foreground industry, or survived long enough to become more akin to a fetish.If you genuinely like that "cheesy 90's" cereal-box-game kids galore, or you aren't too bothered by it and are looking for a tight (albeit extremely easy) nostalgic toon platformer, this is a game I would greatly recommend - but I personally could not bring myself to play any further than the first few levels.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I expected a somewhat better sequel but was given a remake with improvements in some areas. And although the game is more vibrant with more animations and minor level changes, it's still the same pile of ♥♥♥♥ as the original. I'm not sure why they even bothered to remake it when they couldn't add anything significant that would warrant it. _childDocuments_.review: New super lucky's tales is probably one of the most solid and well rounded platformers out there that is just as good as those triple a platformers like spyro or crash bandicoot. A few cons with the game is that it's too short, not much customization, and the main game is too easy. The only real challenge in this game is the post game island because it really test every skills you've learned in game and it's hella fun. Overall the game is fun and it can also cost very cheap on sale, so thumbs up and I would highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: its fun but its also way too easy. if your interested in this game id wait til it goes on sale. i beat the story in one day. the final boss is kinda meh. the characters and npcs are cute and charming at least. theres nothing broken or game breaking its just not very satisfying to finish. the achievements are nice with a few funny names here and there. honestly this seems like a, and i dont mean this as an insult, "babys first 3d platformer". it has a similar gameplay to mario odyssey where theres both 3D and 2.5D levels but with only 1/3 of the challenge. also the audio mixing is terrible at times cause the music is way louder than the characters when they arent talking in off brand simlish. overall this games is a 6/10 imo. not bad but not good either.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is Super Lucky's Tale but with quality of life improvements and better world building. If you found the original version frustrating, this is definitely for you.I do have a complaint about the difficulty of this game. It's way easier than the original version and really has no way to challenge you with harder designs or certain challenges, not even Guardian Trials. The only tough parts are the achievements, like no damage Lady Meowmalade boss/Wrestlemania and maybe marble levels.Still, the game is full of personality, cute art and memorable characters. Decent variety of level design kept me engaged with this game.Recommended for 3D platform enthusiasts.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is a VERY charming and highly polished jump&run game with a low difficulty curve (tho it is engaging enough not to make the player fall asleep). If you're looking for a family-friendly platformer or simply want to jump&run a bit and relax from games like Crash4 or Donkey Kong, this is the game for you. Easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A really chill indie 3D platformer, with several individual levels featuring 2.5D sidescrolling gameplay. There is nothing that I have found to be very difficult but I’m ok with that, I still find the gameplay fun. You play as a fox who gets thrown into another dimension and has to find a way to get back back home by collecting little pages of some type of magic book (each level contains a secret page and another page for making it to the end of the level).If you like 3D Mario games, Crash Bandicoot, etc …you should enjoy this game also.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game on the Nintendo Switch and I had tons of fun! I decided to play the pc version and it works great here as well and I really enjoy it! It reminds me of the old platformers I used to play when I was a kid like Rayman (2 and 3), Crash Bandicoot, Prince of persia, Donald Duck Quack Attack etc. Lucky is an adorable little fox and overall this game is relaxing and great for boredom relief.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: As I said with Super Lucky's Tale, This game is made with heart and soul! It's made markable improvements from the original game, and might as well be a new game using the same level themes. It's made for kids so it's easy until the post-game stuff, but the fun artstyle and charming characters will keep you interested!Don't listen to any of the negative reviews! _childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fun 3D platformers i've played in quite a while :)  . I always loved these types of collectathon and it still holds up, proving these games can still exist today  ;) .Both 3D and 2D levels give something new and fresh everytime and doesn't get boring.Collecting everything stays highly fun and addictive.The best version of this game that has everything to offer.Understandibly easy and aimed for a younger audience, but could use more difficulty options for those that seek a challenge.Not that hard to keep track of your collectibles, but having completion percentage on your file and a result overview of each world in the menu would be nice.This series definitly has some potential and i'm hoping to see an official sequel getting made XD  .

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well-made, if somewhat unambitious 3D platformer. It's aimed at kids, and not particularly difficult. _childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: New Super Lucky's Tale is an awesome 3D platformer which should appeal to any fan of the genre. The Characters are fun, the platforming is tight, and the camera controls  (which is a common challenge for 3D platformers) are well done. The difficulty leans a little on the easy side which may turn some off, but it actually felt just right to me. This would be an especially great title for kids.The original Super Lucky's Tale was a fantastic mascot platformer on it's own, but this remake improves on that one in just about every single way. I also appreciate that you get the original game included when you buy this one on Steam so you can see what's been changed if you can't get enough of Lucky. Hopefully we'll see more games in this series. I'll definitely be keeping tabs on developer Playful Studios to see what they come out with next.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Mario / Spyro lite.This is pretty much a traditional 3D platformer with simpler gameplay and easier difficulty (except for few optional puzzles and achievement completion). Main character Lucky does not have many moves but the devs were really creative and managed to use them to full potential thanks to clever level designs and mechanics. Controls are simliar to other 3D platformers and most of the time are easy to handle. Graphics are not very detailed but it underlines the game's overall simplicity. Character designs are charming and game does have a very simple kid-friendly yet engaging story. During my playthrough I encountered only one bug (which required me to restart level) and very few minor graphical glitches. The technical state is good. I see three groups of people to whom I would recommend this game:1) If you are a parent and want to introduce your kids to classic 3D platformers or gaming in general, this could be a great entry point.2) Fans of platform games all-alike.3) Players who find other 3D platformers too difficult /control heavy/ stressful.

_childDocuments_.review: Have not played the original one so I can not comment on differences between them.This game was unexpectedly really fun, cute, and surprisingly humorous. I assumed this was a shovelware-type game made for children. It is a fairly easy game that I am sure a child could beat, but there is a decent amount of challenges in store. The controls are surprisingly good and the levels are fun and unique.The main critique I have seen for this game is that the 2 worlds that are from DLC in the original kind of feel out of place. Gilly's Island has some really cool themes, but the levels felt so massive and sandbox-y and there was not much in variety for them, as all the levels were mostly the same type of level. Foxtrot is a DLC that is post-game content of 16 different challenges. Some of these challenges were genuinely hard, (Especially trying to get the achievements related to them) however the challenges never felt unfair.All in all, I would recommend this game if you want a cute and funny casual 3D (And sometimes 2D) platformer collectathon.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Super Lucky's Tale was already a pretty fun and competent 3d platformer, but this remake is certainly the definitive version of it - I played both back to back and this version feels much smoother and polished, has removed a lot of the need to use a guide to find key collectables (repositioned, or no longer randomly gated behind events), bad levels have been scrapped and completely redesigned and other levels have been refined so they play better.Also if you care at all about achievements, they removed one that required about 10 hours worth of grinding,  so getting 100% isn't a complete chore now.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw gameplay and read reviews for this game I knew it would be right up my alley, but I had no idea it would become one of my favorite platformers of all time. It lies right in the middle of that 3D platformer sweet spot: It's accessible to kids and gamers with a lower skill level, but it's so well made and fun to play that even more advanced players will have a blast zipping through the levels and chaining movement combos together. The controls feel legitimately perfect and I wouldn't change a thing. Visually, it runs buttery smooth and the cartoony characters are incredibly cute and expressive. The least important part of a 3D platformer is story, but this one has so much personality I actually made sure to talk to everyone and read their dialogue. It's decently funny and can be surprisingly clever at times. 3D platformers can get a little too cutesy and quirky for me, but this one was never a chore in that regard. I saw another review compare it to Super Mario 3D World and I would say that's a great comparison. If you love 3D platformers, I guarantee you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I should probably write a review on this now since I’ve beaten it twice (once on Xbox and again on PC). I love this game a lot. But, to get it out of the way first: this is a very easy game for the most part. At it’s hardest, it gets to maybe mid-game Mario 64 levels of difficult. Definitely a game made for younger demographics. But, this game is just a joy to play. It’s happy, chill, colorful, and controls great. It’s just a very laid-back, stress-free, chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun, charming 3d platformer.I went in wary of the game being overly short and mindless, but I was pleasantly surprised. To be sure, this game is on the lighter and shorter side of things, if you've played a lot of old 5th and 6th gen 3d platfomers, this game comes short in terms of amount of things to do in comparison to the heavyweights from that time, but it still stands strong on its own merits. The levels are fun, Lucky plays and controls nicely and intuitively, presentation is pretty good, the boss fights are fine enough (the last 2 boss fights in particular are straight up good and very fun).Even though I ended up enjoying it a lot more than I would've thought, it really is rather short (I've 100%'d it and the achievements in my playtime pretty easily) and light on stuff to do. I kept thinking about the size and depth of the levels compared to just about any other major platformer from the past, and, in this game, they are very scaled down in comparison, with each level only having 4 tasks to do for pages, the vast majority of which are trivial to get in one play through. That's for the typical levels too, the 2d and autorunner levels are even quicker to blowthrough, and the ball levels aren't really my cup of tea. The latter worlds also noticeably had less pages to get too. Lucky's moveset being simple and unchanging makes things a bit samey as well, although this is certainly a valid gameplay design I will admit, I just like platformers where you unlock more abilities as you go along. Certain things are also a bit rough around the edges, like some animations being janky here and there, but that's minor.That all said, I still really enjoyed this game. The Guardian trials at the end of the game were pretty much unequivocally good as well, and redeemed a lot of problems with the game.As I played through the game, I could tell that, while it is skimpy on stuff to do, arguably bland, and is honestly too easy for the most part, the core of the gameplay is good and the potential for a really great game is there. I was thinking about how cool and how much better a true sequel could be. All of the extra story you get here and there helped out a ton for that point too, it seems like there's a lot of groundwork laid out for a sequel.I look forward to what's next out of this series.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Fabulous game and especially at the price it’s at. So of course my GF is now mad at me for singing it whenever I get a new clover page. So there’s that.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be one of the best platformer collectathons outside of a Nintendo property. The aesthetic, the music, the gameplay, the level design are all incredible. I absolutely loved every minute playing this game. It might be a remaster or the previously released Super Lucky's Tale but the quality of life improvements make this a must. The game is very easy and will not tax you one bit. I seriously hope we get a proper sequel to this iteration of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: New Super Lucky's Tale is a super-cute true 3D jump'n'run platformer which unites a lot of ideas from other known genre representatives.Difficulty ★★★☆☆☆☆☆☆☆ (add 2 stars for the normal version)First of, this game comes in 3 versions if you buy it in the bundle (release order):* Super Lucky's Tale (SLT)* New Super Lucky's Tale (NSLT)* Lucky's Tale VR (LTVR) The devs consider NSLT to be a remaster version of SLT. Then they ported SLT to consoles, they saw the need to repolish and redesign the game from the core to make it more enjoyable. The result is NSLT, which is in fact a remake, not a remaster. This is because they added new charcter moves, new story (intro and outro), redesigned a lot of levels and the world hub. It does not only feel like another game, it basically is another game with just the core idea of the normal SLT version.This is in fact not bad, because they ironed out a lot of game mechanical flaws from SLT in NSLT. To my surprise, they overworked all critical negative points I considered as really annoying playing the standard version. The devs really seem to have made their homeworks. Which means, if you just want to play this game once, go for NSLT. If you are still hungry afterwards to play with Lucky even more, feel free to also enjoy the normal SLT version, which is a little bit harder but still quite easy.* insta-deaths* limited camera control* too easy* bad aerial control* no coop* only Xbox controller buttons ingame* played through very quickly (less than 10 hours for one game)* no insta-deaths anymore* full 360 degree camera control* more fluent and better aerial control* still no coop mode ('A Hat in Times' shows that this genre can handle it easily with Steam's networking API)* no difficulty settings or new game+ hardcore mode* the changed running animation in NSLT looks awkward like a slapstick parody, the running animation of SLT was way better* super-cute game* fun game to kill some time* lots of achievements to collect afterwards* Foxington trials are pretty cool (this is the challenge level I expected from this kind of genre)* you get basically 3 games for the price of 1I had a lot of fun playing this nifty little game and if the devs keep up the good work, a sequel will be even better. Was totally worth my time.The only creepy thing is how happy Lucky is always looking. I don't know which mood-changing pills he gets, and how mmany, but has to be really good ones. He smiles in literally any situation, even when he gets bombed by a pirate ship. Way to go, never loose your cool, lil fella. Happy, happier, the happiest fox ever.Speaking of superlatives, the devs just won't make it for less than that:What is better than a jumping dolphin?A RAINBOW-trailed jumping dolphin!What is even better than a rainbow-trailed jumping dolphin?A rainbow-trailed jumping dolphin with LASERS!What is even better than a rainbow-trailed jumping dolphin with lasers?TWO of them!
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It's an easy game, but if you're looking for a good game to wind down with, as well as a throwback to 90s platformers, then this comes recommended. I also think it's a good platformer to let kids play if the bigger names are too daunting of an introduction to the genre.I played the original Super Lucky's Tale on Xbox One, and that was fun, but I think this is the better version all around. The camera control alone makes this on better. The original is still a good game, but if you're only gonna play one version of the game, make it this one.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: What's with that title? Super Mario Brothers was an improvement over Mario Brothers in every way, turbocharging it into the stratosphere. Here, "Super" really is just a prefix for the lulz. Which would be fine in of itself, but then there's the "New" prefix.Otherwise, it's a fine 3D collect-a-thon platformer! _childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute little platfomer.  Tons of heart and memorable characters. Decent amount of humorous pop culture references but it doesn't beat you over the head with them. The controls are as tight as you would want a platformer to be. It seems super easy at first, but don't be fooled; this game will test the limits of your sanity if you're going for 100%.  That said well worth the price on sale...heck it's probably worth it at full price. I loved this game and I'm not even a fox.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly solid collectathon. The controls are tight, the camera just works and the level design is clear and always fair. If you're looking for a challenge though, this won't cut it for you. It is clearly tailored to kids, which also becomes apparent in its character design and story complexity. The sixth world, Foxington, raises the challenge a little, but I'd still call this a fairly easy platformer. Minor annoyances include the fact that you cannot skip cutscenes (which I only found tolerable as I completed most levels in one go) and that you cannot mute the Simlish sounds all characters make while talking (unless you want to mute *all* effect sounds). I got 100% achievements in about 10 hours, so I'd recommend you wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from a person who has played 3D platformers before like A Hat in Time and Spyro, *New* Super Lucky's Tale... I wouldn't say it's the most inventive 3D platformer + collect-a-thon out there, but, as someone has put it before me, it's not so common, especially decent ones or aboveYour moveset for this game is pretty basic. You got your standard double-jump, basic tail attack and (Unique to this character as far as I'm aware) burrowing inspired by real-life foxes jumping into snow... that's it. There's no new moves you could learn in this game whatsoeverThe Collectibles aren't that much better since it's pretty easy to grab them (I mean really, I 100% this game in less than 11 hours. Just imagine how many hours I would get out of this if I wasn't going for everything considering that you could outright skip some levels if I wanted to do so). At least the coins you collect throughout the game have a novelty use in the form of cosmetic outfits. All of them are pretty adorable on Lucky, I can tell you that muchAs for the levels themselves: It does have *some* variation. Although it's limited to: 3D, 2.5D, Auto-runners and puzzle. Sadly, none of them would provide much of a challenge until you reach the very last world where it would show SOME form of challenge. Those levels do look pretty nice, I'll give them that. That and it's using those tropes you'll come to expect from older games like a 'Haunted area' and 'Water area'... ... ... Alright, here's some improvements from what I've seen from videos (Probably should play the older version eventually, but it's still worth noting):-You can finally control the camera freely-DLC has been better implemented into the game and became part of the base game-While the concept hasn't changed much, the story does make a bit more sense, especially with the edition of some DLC stuff from the previous game-And more that I might not notice because I haven't touched the previous version quite yet, but it's bundled with this version so I don't have much excuse if anyMy final thoughts: Stick to other 3D platformers that are great to play, but if you're tired of playing those games and just want a nice... decent and polished game that isn't Yooka-Laylee or anything worse... I do recommend this game, especially since it's hard to find these types of games that are actually enjoyable to play, more so if they're multi-platform since it's always a win in my book when you have options assuming they run great on said platform
_childDocuments_.name: New Super Lucky's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game is perfect for younger audiences, as well as people like me who are just really into 3D platformers. All achievements in 8 hours, really fun 100%ing experience. _childDocuments_.review: It certainly has better controls than Super. I still miss the running on all fours running animations though, it just added so much more personalilty that this game now lacks. It's still cute, but not as cute as it was. And while it added some QoL improvements it lacks some other obvious ones that I don't see how they missed when 'remaking' [more or less] this version. Like skipping cutscenes. Or retrying a level from the menu, you have to leave and re-enter instead. With a game that still has 'beat x without getting hit' achievements you'd think they'd let you do that.But it's a very solid, if still short, 3D Platformer. The story changes are hit and miss for me and overall hub design. I felt like there was more progression in Super than New. In Super you had to beat a level to unlock another and the hubs were pretty empty as you entered for the first time. Populating with not just characters but objects as you beat levels. It had a better sense of progression. In New the levels doesn't change (apart from the spooky one which is more linearly progressed and doesn't have a 'real' hub anymore). The levels are populated with plenty of characters by default and you just add one or two next to the level doors after beating them. They added a 'secret' sort of character which you find in each level that kind of hints at the final boss and it's a neat little tease of him and a little ominous. I'm glad it finally went on a real sale since I felt a bit ripped off only getting 10% off for buying Super to get New when the majority of this is the same game. Even if it's improved. It is nice to actually have real 3D with full 3D camera movement but the levels don't really feel like they were changed enough that it makes that big of a difference to me. The more static camera angles would still work like they did before if they just left it. But if you've never played this it's a good game to spend a few hours with. And thankfully there's no overly pointless grindy coin achievement which doubles your play time like Super did.

_childDocuments_.review: With the recent revival of 3D platformers going around, New Super Lucky's Tale can be considered one of the quieter examples of such. You may not hear about it quite as often as other examples, but that doesn't mean it's worth overlooking entirely.The first thing that must be said is that this game is undeniably geared towards kids. For the most part, this game isn't particularly challenging, it has a very cutesy colorful aesthetic, and it can all be beaten in a somewhat small amount of time. So, as a result, this review will be attempting to view it from that perspective; if you're older, I say it's worth a look if you enjoy cute games or if you like 3D platformers as a whole.Most of the game has you going from level to level fulfilling tasks to collect pages to restore to the Book of Ages and open other worlds. Each level has four tasks to complete -- finishing the level, getting 300 coins, finding a hidden page somewhere, and collecting all the hidden L-U-C-K-Y letters. The levels have a lot of variety between them, with some having you fulfill fetch quests, some being sidescrolling based, some being dungeon runners, among other things. Also interspersed throughout the worlds are special puzzle minigames, which I found to be a fun distraction and very rewarding to solve especially as they increased in difficulty.If you just go through the game from start to finish, it's very short, and can be finished in only a few hours. However, if you go for 100% completion like I did, the length of the game increases quite a bit. It never feels artificially long though -- the extra things to do add to the game experience and are very rewarding. There is also an entire extra world after the main game to complete as well, which features much harder levels than the main game.As a game for kids, I think I would have adored it. It feels like a perfect introductory platformer, as the game will nudge you in the right direction yet never feels like it's outright holding your hand, and like I said, it's not a particularly difficult game so that makes it a very great play for the younger crowd. If you're older though, the extra quests add enough difficulty to it that it can satisfy you as well, and the extra world provides a greater challenge for those kinds of players. There's something here for everyone, which is a hard balance to strike and I think it did it very well.On top of that, the game is just so unbelievably cute. Lucky's character design is just hard not to love, and the wide array of NPCs from the cat antagonists to the enemies and friendly NPCs add to it as well. And like I said, the game is very bright, colorful, and a joy to look at. It's all very reminiscent of a Saturday morning cartoon and will easily entertain anyone who is into that aesthetic.NSLT isn't anything you should go out of your way to play, but it's a cute, charming little platformer that enjoyed my time with and I hope it captures the attention of children who may grow up to become nostalgic for it in the years down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly more fun than I expected for being a simple and cute childrens platformer. Reminded me of Spyro a lot. I used to play Spyro 2, my favorite platformer, and put at least a hundred hours into it to 100% it for the fireball upgrade when I was only like 13. Played the remaster, got the same in 10-15 hours max. My point here is if you're an adult with gaming experience or especially people who do lots of platformers then New Super Lucky's Tale won't take you long to 100% either. I'm 6-7 hours in and 100%ed everything besides the post game so far. Still, I recommend it. The game is full of charm and you can tell the developers put a lot of love and effort into it.Pros-Cute and colorful graphics-Responsive controls-Can dress up the fox-Collectibles unlock outfits making them worth to collect because see reason above.-Variety of ways the levels are mixed up later on to keep things interesting-Level design is usually fun-Hilarious cat stereotypesCons-The only skill/power you get is digging and nothing else.-Lack of other characters besides random NPCs you prolly forget about from world to world.Rating: 8/10Some more opinions: -I would have loved to see Lyra and Lucas, your older sister and brother, at least more present in the story and/or as supportive characters. Your family basically becomes non-existent after the intro. I know it's "Lucky's Tale" but still just would have been nice. Maybe in the sequel if one is made.-Side levels where you play as other characters would have been interesting, too. Extra interesting if it's your family or other Guardians you play as. I would love to see this if they ever make a sequel.-Having power ups and more skills to explore the world with or introduce new mechanics would have been really fun, too! -Longer story would have been nice too, but it's a simple kids game so not a big deal.-Some place to relax or play mini games would be welcome too. I don't mean the carnival level where you complete mini games, as there's enemies and such but something like that only expanded on.-Thanks for the cute game <3Edit: After another couple of hours I finished the post game, seems they tease a second game. I hope so ^^ The post-game challenges were a nice change of pace in difficulty.

detailed_description: Trials of Fire is a tactical, deck-building adventure game set in a fantasy world in ruin. Savage combat and tough decisions await in the unforgiving wastelands of Ashe. Trials of Fire combines overworld exploration, multi-character combat and loot linked deck-building to create fresh strategic options on every run. Content added during Early Access 9 Playable Heroes 4 Game Modes + 1 Seasonal Quest 4 Lore Quests 345 Skill Cards 220 Items 42 Legendary Items 294 Narrative Encounters 56 Enemy Types 14 Bosses 40 Landmarks Issue combat commands to each Hero based on their cards. The combination of 3 Hero decks presents new and interesting challenges in every fight. Movement and positional play are critical to survival in combat. Use powerful card synergies to combine the unique abilities of your three heroes. Outside of combat encounters, the party's loadout of weapons, items and gear can be swapped or upgraded. New items and weapons are discovered while exploring the vast overworld of Ashe. Traverse an immense overworld map and author a unique adventure in a dangerous hunt for resources critical to the survival of Terralin. Every journey you take will be a Trial.

name: No Place for Bravery
detailed_description: No Place for Bravery is a 2D top-down action RPG which weaves together exquisite visuals, a stirring soundtrack and intense combat moments into a darkly haunting tale that explores the lengths we’d go to recapture all we hold dear. Peril awaits on every path through Dewr, a harsh world of ruined beauty and violent tribes. In this game, you must contend with fast-paced battles filled with dodges, parries and counterattacks. Making mistakes will be punishing and you’ll experience a lingering sense of fragility while facing the dangers of Dewr. After fighting in a cruel war beyond reckoning, the ex-soldier Thorn lays down his blood-stained arms. Resigned to a quiet life of tavern-keeping, Thorn's thoughts and dreams linger upon his long-lost daughter Leaf — until Thorn witnesses the reappearance of the one who abducted Leaf so long ago. With the company of his disabled foster son Phid, Thorn enters the fray once more, convinced the world needs his blade to make things right. The narrative of No Place for Bravery examines the role and duties of father figures and the consequences of their choices in a troubled world. The game, informed by the developers' personal life experiences and feelings, ponders where a parent's obligation ends and something more primal begins. In skilled hands, Thorn can weather every violent challenge right from the start, and his brutality only grows as you discover new weapons and items to turn the tide against your foes. Yet the messy throes of desperate combat take time to master. Do not despair if you should encounter a series of wretched defeats in your journey. A captivating blend of the low fantasy setting and achingly detailed pixel art makes Dewr's decrepit world croak with breathtaking life as Thorn carves his path through it. Every second that passes in No Place for Bravery pulses with an immersive, intense atmosphere that you’ll feel in your veins.

name: Curious Expedition 2
detailed_description: Curious Expedition 2 is a turn-based narrative roguelike that requires players to manage their resources and party members to keep insanity at bay and find glory. A grand discovery has been made: mysterious islands have begun to appear and vanish from the oceans as if by magic. The great Explorer Clubs are funding expeditions to these strange islands to bring treasures back for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. Are you bold enough to join the adventure? Key Features: Explore fantastical worlds in a variety of biomes, each featuring a new combination of dangers and opportunities. Manage your resources to keep your trek alive and sanity high. Balance greed against your survival needs to find glory without perishing. Procedural storytelling makes every adventure unique. Your characters form relationships, change loyalty, acquire illnesses, and more in response to the environment and your decisions. Embark on an epic campaign that combines procedural gameplay with handcrafted story to create a narrative experience that can be played again and again. The new Director Mode adds modifiers and features to every expedition that will make your adventures boundless in scope and even more challenging. Dice-based combat mechanics will require all your cleverness to survive fierce wild animals and legendary creatures. Join weekly online competitions and pledge yourself to an Explorer Club to compete for unique rewards. Outfit your party members with equippable gear to create builds that can take on any challenge. Set off on a variety of expedition types , each with their own unique goal and events. Will you seek out the legendary Golden Pyramid or choose to recover the Rainbow Orchid instead? Discover mysterious locations and come across all manner of unique cultures, flora, fauna, treasures and more. 4K-native graphics inspired by classic Franco-Belgian comics. Veteran Curious Expedition players will discover plenty of new content : new items, character types, enemies, biomes, tribes, events, and much more!
