_childDocuments_.review: There's a sort of romanticizing of the past that's extremely pervasive throughout the United States. Our media is referential and nostalgia reigns supreme, with glamorizing of the past being pervasive in our government and our society. Not everyone gets to have a good past, though, especially trans people, and even more especially, Kasio.It's a harsh, depressing reality for many trans people that our pasts are awful. If we're out, society treats us like garbage, and it we remain closeted, we end up living a false life with walls built as strong as possible in an attempt to survive. Society is actively regressing for us and it was even worse in 1993. That Kasio came home as herself to Achill, where she almost certainly knew that her family would be awful to her, was incredible. Queer solidarity is oftentimes the only way we survive. When cishet society shuns us and scorns us, we have to turn to each other. It's extremely accurate and relatable that Kasio spends all her time with Jack, Colum, and Shans, people like her who are queer. Without them, she has literally no one in Achill that she can exist with. It makes the eventual falling out she has with the Bandshee members even more depressing. The band was her found family and she felt like she destroyed that family. Given how the band members reacted to her after the night she had with Shans, it's sadly understandable why she thought that. One of many things that I love about If Found... was having Kasio be ace. It's rare to see ace characters represented in media and it was a nice and completely understandable aspect of her personality. It was also great to see her reaction to Shans being 19. Despite having presumably only lived as Kasio for around five years, she had to mature quickly to handle all the ♥♥♥♥ society threw at her. Not wanting to be with a teenager she had just met earlier that month, while awful for Shans, was the best thing she could've done. How they reacted showed their immaturity and general desperation to get away from Achill and be their true self.  The amount of self-hatred a lot of us not-cis people feel is overwhelming. It makes sense in a very depressing way that Shans would tell Kasio that she was essentially a freak. They were suffering under the weight of their family's expectations of them and they sadly took that suffering out on the person that didn't deserve it the most. The band let her down when she needed it most. They turned her into a Yoko Ono, but at least she had John Lennon. Kasio had nothing and no one. It's no wonder she almost died alone in the squat, trying to hide from everyone in her life.The writing was on the wall way before that line from Shans. It became inevitable that she would destroy her past, literally and figuratively, as referenced in the game's mechanic of erasing the events of her life that month. Maybe if she got rid of the previous 23 years of her life, she would be able to start anew with her family only knowing Kasio and not the fake pre-transition self she was forced to live, like she did with the band. The burning of Kasio's notebook in a desperate attempt to survive by any means necessary is a step that many trans people had to take in the 20th century. Get rid of all your possessions, your relationships with your family and friends, and upend your life to move to a new city where you live stealth, with no one ever knowing that you're trans. The worst part is, she burned the book and nothing changed for her. That she was eventually rescued by her family and friends had nothing to do with the burning. She burned it for nothing. I am very relieved that this game ended on a positive note. Having people accept her and support her was really touching because at the end of the day, it's what nearly every trans person wants. To be loved and accepted as we truly are by the people in our lives. If it had ended with Kasio dying alone in the squat, I wouldn't be recommending it to anyone. I wouldn't have given this my only 10/10. I wouldn't have changed my name to Cassiopeia. There are far too many stories about trans people where we suffer repeatedly and don't get a happy ending. I am so happy that Dreamfeel didn't go this route.The space subplot, to me, is a beautiful metaphor of Cassiopeia's past as Kasio. Jetting across the cosmos on a journey to stop the destruction of everything she knows makes perfect sense as being an allegory for her past when she just realized that she was trans, that she was Kasio.I believe that with the anomaly being pinpointed to her home in Achill, the planet wasn't about to be destroyed by it, but her world was. Knowing that she is a woman changed everything for her and it is completely understandable that she thought that her world was collapsing, especially if she were to tell anyone else about this. Given that she never told her family until she was 23, years after starting college, and that it almost destroyed her, it's an apt metaphor.I'm still torn on who the accountant McHugh is supposed to represent. My current self wants to say that it's perhaps Cassiopeia's persona if she had never transitioned. This "guy", stuck at a dead-end accountant job but still very much interested in space, helping Cassiopeia reach her younger self because "he" wants to not make the mistake of hiding who "he" is from everyone and repressing any trans-related thoughts. It also makes sense that any space agency like NASA or Roscosmos or the ESA didn't pick up on Cassiopeia arriving in Ireland, but only McHugh did. It's her metaphorical journey to her past. Cassiopeia was on a journey to find Brid McHugh's little artist and tell her that she could be a woman too, and McHugh was there to make sure "he" got a happy life as the woman "he" should've been decades earlier. Cassiopeia and McHugh surviving the anomaly and living through the strange phenomena occurring was, to me, indicative of the multiverse theory. They changed Kasio's past and helped her realize that she was trans, but they were still the same people they were before. The diverging of the timeline at the end of the VN, from Kasio's life up to 2016 and then Cassiopeia's life post-anomaly was a rather interesting choice I wasn't expecting. It makes me think a lot about how real the anomaly was to people besides Kasio. To me, it's like everything that happened in that separate post-anomaly timeline at the end of the game was Cassiopeia's way of trying to reconcile her past with the people still left in her life that she didn't have authentic relationships as herself with. From an art perspective, If Found... is simply the most beautiful game I've ever played. Getting to see the hand-drawn sketches of each scene and the characters interacting was wonderful. I love the background effects during the scenes where there would be multiple tiled pieces moving in the background. The concept of erasing to advance the game was a fantastic choice. The colors are so vibrant and eye-popping and really pulls me into the game, something that I love in VNs.From a music perspective, I am in love with the soundtrack. There's not a single weak track in it and it only gets better as the game progresses. 2 Mello did a bang-up job with his part, Eli Rainsberry's ambient/drone tracks are nice, and the inclusion of Threat, Operating Theatre, and Ensemble Eriu was perfect. Additionally, the new credits song with Loah's beautiful vocals is incredible.This is the only game I have ever given a 10 and I believe that won't happen again for a while. You should play it now. I may be biased since I changed my name to Cassiopeia, but that just shows the impact it's had on me.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 7th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Finding one’s self while doing a lot of erasing.If Found is beautifully drawn at times.  The art on display is exceptional, and oftentimes the story shows similar sparks of brilliance.  This is a game that will speak to some people and I’m sure those people will be happy to be heard, the problem with If Found is that the gameplay, if it’s called that, doesn’t work. If Found’s main mechanic outside of being a visual novel is erasing the screen, you’ll do that a lot, like a frightening amount of times. The problem is the gameplay doesn’t fit with the story or themes.  The story also involves a transgender female, and while it’s mostly good, there are a lot of clunky lines especially when focused on those who oppose her transition.  It’s almost like the writer didn’t want to write realistic antagonists to avoid harming those who identify with the main character, but that only makes the antagonists in the game awfully written and that affects the main character’s motivations.  It’s a house of cards. Pick this up if you care more about having a trans woman as the main character than the gameplay mechanic in the game.  I normally am a fan of visual novels and enjoy a great deal of them, so the idea of a less interactive game is not an issue, but this is a game that probably is better to watch on youtube rather than play yourself due to how monotonous the interaction with the game is. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: If Found is a game that I've been meaning to review for quite a few days now, but it's hard for me to express just how precious and  this little gem is. First off, Kasio is such a easily lovable character, and the other three main kiddos are very full of personality and charm too. They make it so easy to get caught up in the story, also helped greatly by the way the story is presented in the first place. It unfolds so smoothly and erasing everything to progress the story is quite satisfying and engaging (especially considering I went into this thinking it would play like your standard visual novel, just clicking to advance dialogue). Not to mention it's a delight to look at. The colors are gorgeous and the art style itself is really cozy and looks fantastic. Oh, and the music! After the initial track, it's so subtle for a while but before I even noticed it, it really came up and into its own. After finishing, I couldn't help getting the soundtrack especially to hear the last few songs again.The only real bone I have to pick is that the sci-fi bits toward the end feel a little out of place, especially since by that point I was so utterly invested in Kasio and what was happening with her that the other storyline only served to detract from the experience for me and break immersion. But regardless of that small qualm, this game has such a meaningful and heart-filled story to be told. Absolutely worth it, particularly if you love character-driven stories <3

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a visual novel. It is visual drugs, it is visual sex; the production and creativeness of this parallels the final scenes of 2001: A Space Odyssey more than it does a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ "novel". The vast majority of progression and interactivity in this game is you erasing the main character's own thoughts and experiences. Just as we do our own thoughts, willingly or not. Forced into existence, into our families, into our identities, we cannot hold on to the past. Not that we should not, but that we are physically incapable of doing so. Sometimes we can find a perverse pleasure in erasing our former selves. Other times it can be indistinguishable from some of the worst acts of self harm. If Found knows this, too well, and deliberately plays with this on every page. There's a kind of gentleness baked into this game, in every passage and diary entry that I actually found myself despising. I suppose when you stumble across such an emotionally raw story, you want it to parallel your own. This story very firmly sticks its feet and its visual metaphors into specific identity struggles and specific mental health struggles. I wish we got to see Kasio in Dublin, or abducted by aliens, or not surrounded by incredibly well drawn cute and comfortable punk rejects. But this story chose not to be these things for a reason. It speaks to crisis and circumstance outside my own - and I believe it totally "succeeds", if there's such a thing in art, in telling the story it wants to. If you're this far down in reviews, do yourself a favor and buy this game. Play it at night, with a pair of headphones on, and a glass of water by your side. Trust me - you'll need the hydration.

_childDocuments_.review: If found tells a very specific story about a transgendered woman who finds herself time and time again lost in life, trying to live (or loosing herself while doing it) finding friends, being discriminated by family, not believing love can be found (but It can be), and then perhaps finding herself on the opposite side of all this.I’m not trying to be painfully sarcastic here, life can really be like that. The only sure thing is that… there’s no sure thing. And it is how we deal with everything (life) that makes us who we are.This is a universal truth. No matter your gender identity or sexual preferences.We need stories like this, they need to be told. They must be because at some point, someone, somewhere, like me for example, they are going to hear this story. And it may be one of the few things keeping them from loosing themselves. Totally. Because they need to know somehow, someway: This is not just me. This is not wrong.And I’m not alone.If found’s story may not appeal to everyone and the setting it is based on may prevent some from looking into it (even with all those glossary entries) but underneath those details, there are words that I’ve found while playing that resounded painfully true. They hurt, because I know those words. They hurt because I’ve heard them before (and it won’t be the last time sadly).But as painful as it can be, reading those words made me feel better. I was somehow…relieved. This is me. I’m not alone.It may not be the solution to everything and it may have not changed my life whatsoever but perhaps… it may have just been the spark that started changing things.Having stories like “If found” being told is so important, because there are never enough of them. It’s so difficult to reach us, to let us know “everything will be ok”. “You are Ok”. That this story, could very well be the only story, that reaches you. It may sound dramatic but it may be the only chance you have. That is why it is so important to have this.The only thing I know so far is this: Any step we take, no matter how small, could be the most important one and the most difficult to take.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenominal. Wow what an experience this game was. Expect some difficult themes, thoughts, and events, as you experience the thoughts and life of a trans person living in Ireland, who is not understood / recognised her family and most of society around her. It is intermingled with a story line about a space anomaly that is about to destroy the Earth, which I won't say too much about. Throughout the game you read diary entries and letters, which have been partly crossed out at some later point by the protagonist, and dialogue between the various characters. The game is very visceral, and feels very real, and echoes the undoubtedly many similar experiences people like the protagonist have to go through when figuring out their identity.  The whole game builds up into a conclusion that, while it may not be completely satisfying, does feel enormously authentic.The only small gripe I have with the game is the erasing, which is the game's main mechanic for advancing through the story. At times, I kept wagging my arm around to erase and erase, it not always being exactly clear when  you can and can't erase. Would have preferred just clicking instead, but I do get what the developers were going for, so I don't fault it that much for it. In short, get it if you want an authentic but sometimes difficult story about a person struggling to find their identity with often limited support or downright hostility from their environment, and walk away with a new, unique experience after finishing it in about 1.5-2 hours, or in case you have gone through something similar yourself, in which case you might feel immensely strengthened by seeing that others are going through similar things.

_childDocuments_.review: If Found...'s simple story shines bright through the presentation of extracting information through erasing a journals past. Kasio's story via diary allows us to unravel the story gradually. Erasing the past journal memories felt like Kasio was getting help with a traumatic past and working through it, and the player has a role in uncovering it with erasing. Although erased, I get the impression it's still there, but just lives on in a vacuous black hole, affecting us, but the memories and trauma remain just an amalgamation of matter - not to be in this side of the universe anymore.A wonderful delivery of a visual novel.

_childDocuments_.review: This game went deep to say the least. Finishing it was like coming to the end of a long movie filled with personal boundaries and emotion.If Found features an immersive, interactive gameplay for which I do recommend you use a mouse (it'll be easier than using a touch pad). The story is set in Ireland and focuses on a transgender girl called Kasio, as we delve into her story and personal struggles through her journal, seemingly erasing all there is to see. There's also something else altogether involving the concept of space, but ahp- I've said too much. Go ahead and play this beauty for yourself ;)Stunning visuals and a heart-touching story. A nice touch are the click-to-view footnotes which explain (mostly Irish) terms and phrases that one might be unfamiliar with.Other than that, if you buy this game then get ready for a heartfelt adventure of discovery and self-preservation.

_childDocuments_.review: If found does some unique and interesting stuff in the interactive novel genre. More importantly, it's a really powerful, good story.I don't think it's a spoiler that you play as a trans woman coming home to small town Ireland as yourself for the first time. The game doesn't outright tell you this right away but the kind of person for whom this story is for will know immediately. Kasio and the rest of the cast are all very real characters, and the story is only fictional in the most superficial possible sense; I know so many people who've lived it. The Sci-Fi framing device does a good job of capturing the feeling of this kind of story, and helps characterize Kasio, though it did confuse me at points.The game does a great job of using the medium. I don't want to spoil how, but if you're really into that like I am, this is definitely a game that, though it doesn't require skill or use a lot of "gameplay" elements, should definitely be a game and not some other kind of media.I have no serious critiques of this game. It needed to be made. I'm probably going to play it every year for... a while. You should play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning game. Really beautiful and immersive artwork and mechanics, and the story completely swept me away. The characters all feel so authentic and unique, and the dialogue was so lovely. Would definitely recommend to anyone, but especially to trans people. _childDocuments_.review: I rarely ever feel the need to right a review (my only other being for destiny 2) but this game truly astonished me so here I am. The story is a wonderful depiction of the real struggles some LGBTQ+ youth go through/ have gone through, especially at the time the time the story takes place (If I recall the 1990's). It doesn't follow simple tropes or cliches and tells a wonderful and sometimes emotional story. Actually it was the first video game to ever make me shed a tear. All of this paired with the fantastic and unique art style, makes them game truly amazing (8.5/10). I suggest everyone LGBTQ+ or not, give this game a go.

_childDocuments_.review: If Found is a beautiful, intimate, and interactive story about memories, identity and understanding of self. It reads like an indie feature, but plays like a visual novel with an incredibly inventive erasing mechanic, which is central to not only the plot of the game, but thematically. Some of the scenes I felt the pain in erasing the words I had just materialized. As a film person, I would be so interested to see this become a film, but I feel like If Found is a type of experience you can only have with a video game, which is the highest praise I can give. If you have the two hours, please continue to support the projects from Annapurna's excellent publishing catalog and play If Found...Edit: Initially, I left a negative review because the game would not allow me to progress to the final chapter. After messaging with a developer, an icon was just missing from the bottom-right corner of the screen, but the game functions perfectly well. Thank you to Dreamfeel for helping me finish the game and reaching out!

_childDocuments_.review: If Found is an incredible piece of interactive art and storytelling. I will be revisiting this game again in the near future when I need a good two hours of emotional tsunami. If the devs happen to be reading this, thank you for making and sharing something that so comfortably nestled itself into my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: The most striking thing about If Found is how it is tactile. The feeling of erasing the words in a dog-eared, tired old diary envelops you deep into the journey of Kasio and the ones she meets along the way. Every word is savoured when you are rubbing them all away. There is beauty in impermanence, and If Found asks us to embrace it. There will always be more pages to write in after all.Every single screen of If Found is beautiful, and features incredible sound work by 2Mello and Eli Rainsberry. It is one of the most heart-felt and real narratives I've experienced in a game and I absolutely recommend it to all. Please, play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely story. This is most definitely a visual novel, not a game. I decided to play this without much prep. I had forgotten what it was about, and just wanted a chill story for stream.I had read people got tired of erasing, but I rather enjoyed the process. I was a little annoyed at the non erasing parts! You can also adjust the eraser size, so I had it big enough it only took about 5-6 swipes to clear my whole screen. I used the automatic erase maybe twice in the whole game. Good that it’s there, though.The art is fantastic and uses color, lighting and animation seamlessly. The music and sound design are splendid and help to progress the story. The setting is lovely and describes a small town where I would love to live. They even put in little references and pronunciations for the Irish names and traditions.The story is told through the eyes of Kasio, and we meet other characters through her journal. We are sympathetic to her from the first scene, and she always stayed true to character. She’s not perfect, and I even called her a bad name in a later scene lol. The game right now is $13, a little much for under 3hrs for a rather weak story. I did love the characters, and it made me cry and care for their well being. One friend came in stream and asked ‘what emo horror story is this’… and I wouldn’t go that far. If you’re talking parts of a story, it gets the characters, setting, themes, morals, perspective and point of view right.It lacks much plot aside from teenage life which seems out of place with a 23yr old, dealing with a mother and brother who don’t accept her transition, and other friends who do. There are hints at other conflicts, but none are explored well. There was a lot of potential for exploring the struggles of the alphabet mafia in modern society, in Ireland’s history, or in Europe compared to a small Catholic town. I think this is a strong outline for a better story, and maybe one day we’ll get one from the devs. I would love to see more projects from the developers. A lot of love and heart went into this project, and I hope you will give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Made me cry like a baby but that's OKAY!This game is a masterpiece from the wonderful visuals, the amazing soundtrack, and the captivating story that ties it all together. I don't have any problems with it really, I have seen people say that the erasing mechanic is annoying but the story is only 2 and a half-ish hours long and i never got tired of it (its fun to draw with the eraser). But on with the review, starting with the visuals. ALSO, do note this is a STORY, treat it like a book and not like a fps, this is an interactive visual novel and its a great one so please let me gush for a bit here.The art made for this game is constant eye candy, and i want to use a pretty early scene that i will be referencing for the music section as well, and that is the first morning in the big house. The contrast of what happened the night before with the morning is great, the breakfast scene is fun and heartwarming, just a great scene. More praises i have for the art is the different styles used, a standout favourite of mine is the scribbles that look like they were doodled on the side of a worksheet. They also use the erasing mechanic really well, erasing windows to peer inside a house, or peeling light away to show time passing, it doesn't feel "unnecessary" like a lot of reviews might lead you to believe.Moving on, the music in this story, made by 2 Mellow, is just so cozy. I wont dwell on it too long because I'm not a musician, I just have ears and think it sounds good. Though there are some things i want to talk about when it comes to the music, specifically on the Youtube uploads there are little producers notes that are quite fun to read, giving little bits of trivia on how the music was made. The Youtube releases also have my found my favourite song, though it was not used in the game, its just so beautiful, its called "Slán Abhaile" if you want to listen to it yourself. Close followups include "Where are you" and "If I could sleep", give them a listen.The story is great, I don't want to get into it because that's kinda what the whole game is, its good trust me.Overall 10/10 loved it, I know this is an old title but its been so slept on and that's just heartbreaking, if the devs do read this I hope you are doing well and I hope I hope I hope your are making more games, I will be there no matter what.

_childDocuments_.review: Not really my bowl of Wheaties, even though this game does have a number of cool elements going for it.  I couldn't relate to the space-related parts of the story at all.  If anything, the tortured black hole / alien metaphor for what was going on IRL was brutally heavy handed.  As others have written, the constant erasing threatened to bring on carpal tunnel syndrome (one of the scenes, I had to close the game and restart because I couldn't get the eraser to fill the screen to move on) and started wearing heavily on my patience.  As my taste in electronica leans more towards guitar-heavy stuff, I have to say I didn't care for the soundtrack at all.  I think it was supposed to enhance the sci-fi element of the MC's mental framework, but since I didn't like that element it just further alienated (pun not intended) me.  On the plus side, I really did dig the 90's feel of this game.  Love the Irish language inclusion with even a glossary that helps you better embrace the cultural differences if you're not from that side of the pond.  The anguish and torment of young adulthood also felt real:  The tense conversations with friends and family that lead to some spectacularly awkward moments.  Late nights eating junk food that you still dream about later.  And I did enjoy the overall artwork:  beautifully hand-drawn characters and landscapes against surreal backdrops.  I think in the end I can't recommend it based on personal hangups.  Couldn't relate enough to any of the characters (with the possible exception of Aunt Maggy, but she played too minor a role) to care what happened to them even towards the end.  Found the soundtrack jarring instead of blending with the story.  And I started getting bored with the UI about halfway through.  I wanted that eraser to just go away and scream at my monitor "Get on with it!!"

_childDocuments_.review: Erase, reveal. Erase again. Sometimes just pan. Click through dialogues. The eraser mechanic no doubt feels unique and fresh at first, albeit rapidly repetitive. I immediately liked the general tone, but how many times can you wipe the entire screen to reveal layer after layer of tacky video filters?For every few scenes with substantive artistic merit and fine composition, a dozen rough sketches blend into scarcely appealing outlines. There are some good flashes, certainly, but I reasonably expected to be impressed more. This art direction has more to do with hastily drawn doodles lifted out of a sketchbook, with an attractive and fitting color palette. Some lo-res character drawings looked too similar, and I sometimes found it hard to differentiate who's who.A very pleasant soundtrack provides excellent vibes throughout and uplifts the quality of the presentation tenfold, and quite possibly represents my most appreciated feature of this game.Identity, acceptance, coming of age. The main story elements are well rendered, through honest diary scribbles and mostly credible situations, often heartwarming or sad, sometimes both, that will naturally resonate extraordinarily with its intended audience.Additional disjointed story bits involve a lost space captain, a black hole, a mysterious photograph, and the impending end of the world, seemingly lifted from a parallel story that serves as a metaphor to protagonist Kasio's overwhelming life situation. This endless source of confusion and psychedelic imagery completely alienates the urgency of actual events and their resolve in favor of some imaginary alternative reality.Optional glossary entries shed insight on various mentioned elements of Irish culture, expressions, and places. Tap + for more info, as informative as annoying due to their high frequency. Ends up breaking the flow of the story with elements that are not central to the core, but nevertheless appreciable from a cultural standpoint.I did not personally enjoy this game as much as I hoped, but not recommending it would be doing a disservice to an underrepresented community. This narrative experience was obviously created with full care and sensibility. That it manages to sincerely touch some people is certainly all that matters.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say although the game is simple in nature it makes up for in it's trippy art style and an impactful story line. The themes that it discusses are belonging, rejection, realisation and coming of age. The themes themselves are done excellently as they are in tune with the issues in Ireland during the early nineties (1993), for queer people in Northern Ireland especially. There isn't really much else to say but i'm a sixth or a quarter Irish so it helped me connect with my Irish roots.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to get into this game, but sometimes, no matter how badly you want to experience a game or a story, there's that one mechanic in the game you just absolutely cannot stand. Sometimes that mechanic is something small enough to over look, but in the case of If Found, that mechanic was the main mechanic in the game. I absolutely hated the eraser thing, at first I didn't know the game had even started as I'm erasing through title screens, after about 10 minutes I realized "oh, you just erase everything" I hadn't even realized the game had started. I'm sure the game has a good story, unfortunately that one mechanic ruined the whole experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost! Epilepsy warnings! flashing and all, even my eyes could not handle some of the spacey parts of this game. I think the game is good for it's overall direction and lore (aside from the random cut-ins of the space adventure). I think I would still have to say no to this game, for the fact that it only left me with more questions and an unsatisfying experience in the end. I do not regret or feel this game is not worth playing and interpreting for yourself. I just simply think I could have used the two hours of my time reading something I actually enjoyed more.This is one of the weakest points of the game or more like interactive diary. For the erasing mechanics purpose, it is entertaining to see the progression through the short story there is. However, it certainly is tedious to have to shift around, erase, press buttons, and do all that for 2 hours straight.I really liked the main aspect of it being so relatable. Whether you fall on the spectrum, have similar identity problems, familial issues, and building relationships is all too human. This also is part of why I sort of dislike the game overall, it feels too human-like and personal that I felt attacked as the story unfolded and left the ambiguous relationship issues vaguely addressed. Certainly hooked me into wanting to know more about each person and what would happen as the years passed which is expected to be written out as the story it will end up being. I feel for anyone who has to go through the extra step of a different identity, it's already tough enough to figure out your place in this world as is.I guess I'm too focused on wanting a more fantasy-like story, I'm far too used to these realistic life stories that bring emotional turmoil and confusion my way. It hits too close to home and I felt really uncomfortable when it didn't feel like a fantasy world anymore. I like the ambiguity, but at the same time, the story just ended up feeling empty at the end. I didn't have enough time to really get to know the characters. I understand the purpose and reason of the way this game was written, for that reason alone it's a beautiful, meaningful one.

_childDocuments_.review: is a story -- one that deserves to be told -- but not a game. Initially it had a hard time pulling me in, and so for the first hour I was simply reading an incomprehensible bunch of gibberish. Things started to click in the second (and final) hour. There is no gameplay and there are no choices, but the player progresses the story by erasing layers of art with the mouse. This becomes really tiresome really quickly.Due to the narrative getting better to the end, I wanted to recommend it, but it's severely overpriced. Get it for 1-2 euro's if you're someone who reads books.

_childDocuments_.review: Got it with the May Humble Monthly. Not what i expected, and not in a good way.Can be completed with 100% achievements in an afternoon, which is nice.Drawings/graphics are great. Very detailed scenraios sometimes, and simple character designs that allow for some "cute" moments here and there. It's probable best thing about the game.Gameplay it's just like a visual novel, but instead of pressing a button to continue, you need to "wipe out" the screen with a virtual eraser. If feeling lazy, there is a button that automatically wipe it out for you. Not bad, not good. Kind of an interesting twist.The story, which it's the most important part of the game, it's also the worst part, unfortunately. You follow the misadventures of a young male that it's now a female that decided to change her name to a well-known wristwatch brand, but with a "K" instead of a "C". This girl decides that she is not accepted by her family (something that she desperately needs, for some reason) and ran away from home. The reasons she doesn't have this "acceptance" seems to happen because she have changed sex, and not because of voluntarely unemployment, neither because she gives a poo about anything but herself and definetly, not because she takes the dellusional decisions of angsty teen instead of the young adult she says she is. She then goes with other people "like her" and squat into a house where more things happens.There is also some sci-fi plot mixed in this that doesn't seem to make any sense, but probably has some relevance. Whatever that relevance was, it miserably blowed over my head and didn't look that it added anything to the overall plot.In summary, not my cup of tea.Music it's there. Nothing special about it, i fear.Not the worst thing i played, but i wouldn't recommend it either.It plays nice in the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm, neutral review.This is more of an interactive novel than a game with an 'erasing' gimmicky mechanic, as people have said. A short one too, so you might want to buy it on sale.If Found... is a harrowing tale of wanting love and acceptance of a queer person coming back to her home Island where she is considered a freak outside of social norms. Also, the "game" deals with friendship, heartbreak, and discrimination. There was a sci-fi bit that was strewn in but it wasn't interesting to be honest lol. As much as the story is compelling enough, it didn't feel as though it was wrapped up nicely. Maybe it's just a case of me wanting to have this game end on a certain way. But it still felt choppy for me.There was the ending black hole sequence that felt metaphorically heavy handed and padded a little bit. Gave the ending a little less of an impact. All things considered, it's an ok game.

_childDocuments_.review: If Found... is a game developed by DREAMFEEL and published by the wonderful people over at Annapurna InteractiveI'm not going to spoil anything in this review or say much, all I'm going to say is if you want a heartfelt story that touches on topics that many people in the LGBT+ community go through even to this day, then please, give this game a playIt's not too long (just two hours in length) and the gameplay is incredibly simplistic, borderline non-existent, but it really tugged on my heartstrings and is a wonderful game with some fantastic visuals and an amazing soundtrack to bootIf Found... is a short, casual and incredibly simplistic from it's gameplay aspect but ultimately wonderful story about acceptance, irrelevant of how you look, feel or act

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I have to leave a negative review. Don't get me wrong: If found is a beautiful visual novel. Everything was lovingly drawn by hand and looks nice. The soundtrack is also good and matches what you see.However, the story is complete rubbish. Some emo teenage LGBTQ transgender community story that only becomes somewhat interesting at the very end. And especially since the story is the core element of this "game", I unfortunately must write a negative review.If the idea was implemented with a more interesting story, this could be an exciting format for short visual novels.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game a 5/10. It had many positives like a wonderful soundtrack with ASMR elements that felt calming yet invigorating to listen to, an LGBTQ+ storyline and beautiful artwork (I also appreciated the little Irish culture footnotes.) Unfortunately, this game leaves much to be desired. It's less of a game than a visual novel, which okay, whatever floats your boat. BUT the erasing mechanism between every scene was tedious and boring and, if you're like me and feel the need to fully erase a scene without leaving unerased spots, it was a lot of work. The space chapters, while accompanied by an incredible soundtrack, were on-the-nose and cheesy, and the story behind the main character, with a misguided mother with good intentions and a snotty brother, running away from home felt overdramatic and I found myself disliking Kasio slightly for it. For the price, this game isn't worth it imo. I've played over 90 minutes and I still can't bring myself to finish it to be honest.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting if not fun way to blow off a few hours. Ftr, I would highly recommend  before you start, not due to spoilers but due to the potential nature of really bugging out the game a bit if you feel tempted to go into the settings and unlock all of the chapters from the get-go. You needn't worry about claims to any such badges of honour later anyway. It's not worth the pain. (Btw, ignore any instruction that the "Opening" chapter has anything to do with achievements. There isn't one. They either refer to "This Book Belongs To" or "What Happens Now". You're welcome.) Anyway, that's not why this game deserves two thumbs down.In fact, the starter story, the music (good if not memorable), and the interaction aren't anything to laugh at, and I did appreciate some of the little details, like the way the eraser whittles down. No, the turnoff comes from the majority of the story, which vapidly and bile inducingly details little more than a psychologically beaten outsider that cuts off everything to pan a life off the grid with her wishy washy new similar friends, herself so ignorant, callous, hypocritical and uncaring of everything around her that you wouldn't even pee on her if she were on fire. In short, nothing you having read or watched hundreds of times over, about someone who thinks they're so unique yet so obviously not, and you can't stand another one thinking they pwn the definition on "terrible upbringing" so much so yet the story continues to drown you in yet another scenario that only a certain percentage is really all that believable anyway. Hell, to anyone's lived it, seen it, or even been touched by even something remotely similar, it's an obscene joke. People this stupid don't always make it out alive. Sure her life sucks, her family disgusting, but in the words of Saliva, "you don't hear no crying ass *****ing from me, but it seems to be on everybody's CD."So if you don't mind wading through this kind of crap, go right ahead. Personally, I'm more disgusted with myself for having blown even a small wad on this game. It really isn't worth it, unless you really got the stuff to blow and it's burning a hole in your pocket. Or I guess a few extra really easy achievements. Even then I'd still recommend elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game Florence, which was created by the same people, I decided to try this one since some people in its reviews were mentioning that If found... is a better product. I heard of this game some time before, too, and after looking at its screenshots I quickly purchased it.I agree with the point that this game is better than Florence. Both have good graphics, but this one has better. I enjoyed the music here more than in that other game, too. Story is kinda longer compared to the ~30 minutes gameplay Florence has to offer.However, this game has almost no interactive elements. All you need is just to press the F key or hold and move your cursor. The same thing all the time. A small amount of interactivity exists in the last chapter of the game, but it doesn't add much to the story (as it basically ends after you click a few buttons) and doesn't really help the game to be more fun. I also experienced some bugs with some parts not being erased even though you do it all properly, automatic erasing occurring several times, not getting an achievement for using a pencil, etc.The story goes for longer than in Florence, but honestly it's not more detailed. If Found... unleashes a story about a trans young adult who's suffering from different problems on his/her life path. The game doesn't really introduce us into his story at the beggining, but tries and FAILS to do so in later chapters. At the same time, it goes too deep into describing secondary characters, but their biographies have nothing to do with the main scenario. Speaking of the main scenario, I found it hard to associate myself with any of the characters. And it's not a significantly bad factor on its own, the worse one is that the story feels too cheap. Sometimes your character does the most stupidest things possible, and there's no way to change it at all. All you have to do is to move your pointer all around the screen to get into next scene. That's the gameplay of this "game".While reading others' reviews I noticed that some people try to advocate this game having no gameplay by the fact that it's tagged as a "Visual Novel". In fact, a visual novel that is not ♥♥♥♥♥♥ should give its players options to do something other than pressing one button. So yeah, some may call it a visual novel, but it doesn't help as the so-called visual novel is still bad! Personally, I'd say that this is an interactive comic rather than a visual novel, but it's definitely not a game with an actual gameplay.Comparing If Found... to Florence once again, I can say that this game deserves even a more mixed review than that one. I got both on sale, and this one doesn't even deserve its cutted price of $6.5. I rated Florence with 4/10, while this game deserves my honest rating of 5/10. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this one in the Humble Bundle so decided to give it a try, even though I had an idea of what to expect. 'If Found' is obviously a game made for the woke army; Most characters are either gay or transsexual with weird or made-up names. The straight (or I should call them CIS probably) characters in the game are mostly evil. The story just did not do it for me personally. It does not really matter whether the characters would be gay, trans or straight.I'm not sure that 'If Found' can even be called a game. All you do is use your mouse as an eraser to get to the next page or drawing. I have to admit, a creative way of telling a story but get's tiresome quickly. You can use the 'F' key to completely erase a page and move on faster but somewhere in the middle of the game this did not work for me anymore. Does this mean I think the game is complete garbage? No. The drawings in the game were neatly done but what I liked most are the space parts combined with trippy music, which makes you feel like you are on acid. "If Found" is a game you are not allowed to 'hate' these days because of the message but it just did not resonate with me.

I wouldn’t recommend it to someone who isn’t already a fan of that type of thing. The gameplay is interesting, and I think it tied the themes up pretty well. I didn’t fully understand the later half of the storyline, but that’s probably on me. I really enjoyed the epilogues. The erasing and writing mechanics can be a little annoying but if you use a mouse (i was on a trackpad) its fine. I cried alot honestly, it was really relatable to me and its a beautiful story about finding yourself and family and the live we have all around us. It honestly meant alot to me, and I would probably play again some time. Great art, lovely story, overall great game.

_childDocuments_.review: If Found...reminds me of the works of Tillie Walden in both subject matter, theme, and art style. While it's not as robust and compelling as Walden's works, I think it tells a realistic, and important, story about growing up queer in the 90s. I had a harder time understanding the science fiction narrative and ultimately wondered why it was necessary--this is another thing like Walden's works, except she handles it masterfully--and I would have liked to see a bit more narrative in general, but what was there was moving and I enjoyed it. The sound design and soundtrack were great, and the idea of "erasing" and then "writing" was cool, but it ultimately started getting on my nerves. I can't say I'd recommend paying full price for this game, but if you care about the subject matter and get it on sale, I think it's worth the time you'll put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not one to play a story driven game, but I found the visuals intriguing and decided to give this a shotOh wow am I glad I did, because this was a very enjoyable and chill experience!'If Found...' is basically an illustrated short novel, you don't get that much control over the direction of the story.The story takes approximately 2 hours to complete, though this can vary depending on your reading speed and on how fast you want to go through the game.The main gameplay loop involves moving the mouse around the screen to erase what's currently on it and reveal the next thing.While this is monotonous and potentially straining on the wrist, it does help pace story.It is important to note that the entire screen can also be cleared using a single keypress, which is good for players who may not be able to, or simply do not want to, manually erase with the mouseWith the gameplay and length in mind, it is admittedly a little bit of a hard sell at full priceThough had I paid full price, I don't think I'd have any regrets about doing soI encourage anyone who's interested in the game to give it a try, the story is quite captivating and the visuals are uniqueJust keep in mind that most of what you'll be doing is reading

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. The story is wonderful, it's beautiful and heartbreaking at times. It's mainly a narrative with very little actual action needed from the player, who only really 'writes' and 'erases' the words as you go on. I think doing the game this way is best for the story, as the player can go at their own pace and feel immersed in what's going on, instead of just having to run along with it if it had been a movie or novel, a movie wouldn't be able to really linger in places the way some scenes need, and novel or comic would lack the visual or auditory senses that really push it a lot of places. The way all the different characters play against each other is nice too, it feels very real, the way some people react to certain things, even if sometimes those actions are hurtful.

_childDocuments_.review: just wow such a creative and sweet warm VN. _childDocuments_.review: I was excited to play the game because it looked visually appealing. However, I was slightly disappointed to find out that it is purely a visual novel, although a really good one.It truly captures the struggle and emotions of anyone who has ever tried to find themselves in life, especially those who struggle to find their identity and live with one that society considers to be somehow wrong even in the current day and age. It made me feel things. Everything from happiness to sadness, to frustration, and to feeling annoyed. It made me feel love and warmth in my heart. It would require unfathomable insight and research on the subject matter to capture its essence on the level it has been done here, therefore it is easy to think that it is seeded in the author's own real experience. But who knows? Maybe I am wrong.The game is so simple yet so complex.BTW - did I mention how much I like the art style? Something about it really speaks to me.

_childDocuments_.review: wow. Paint yourself a way through the story of Kasio and their friends, young adults trying to figure themselves out and carving out a place for themselves in a remote part of Ireland in the 90's. _childDocuments_.review: This is more of an interactive story than a tradtional game but isnt too bad overall.The story is about a trans person seeking acceptance from their family in 90's rural Ireland.As an Irish person it's nice to see a game that is set in Ireland and also that it fully embraces Irish slang and references, though there is a handy pop up to explain terms for anyone unfamiliar with modern Irish culture and slang.I also like the way it tells it's story in a way that is uniquely Irish but also really relatable to anyone who can identify with being "different" in a rural conservative area. Or even just anyone who understands how some people can be badly treated because of who they are in these types of places.I also quite liked the games visual style and effects and it has a pretty good soundtrack to boot.It might not be for everyone as it doesnt really have much in the way of gameplay, but i think it falls more into the category of a piece of art through the medium of a game. However if you enjoy a more artistic, story focused game it may be worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully narrated and written, with a stunning art direction to boot, If found is a heartfelt and poignant story about queer identities and the notion of family. The contrast between Ireland's catholic and traditionalist countryside culture and a rag tag group of teens and young adults, and their older relatives, makes for a powerful setting about conflicting ideals and the painful pursuit of acceptance and reconciliation. Like any good personal drama narrative, it alterns between moments of hope and warm, and profound sadness and hurt. The dialogue is often hard to read through, especially if you're queer yourself and have had to face mockery and discrimination, and perhaps more importantly the inner struggle with coming to terms with accepting your own identity and how that will impact your life and relationships. The story is accompanied by a beautifully evocative soundtrack by the wonderfully talented 2Mello, and interwoven with fragments of a metaphorical sci-fi story adding depth and bold visual flair to an already beautiful game.I heavily recommend it, with the forewarning that the story deals with difficult topics, such as depression and self-harm, but does so with the gravitas and respect that they deserve. I would refer to If found as a culturally and artistically important game. Truly and wondeful and emotional story from beginning to end.

_childDocuments_.review: If Found is one of the most aesthetically beautiful and touchingly queer visual novels I've played. What it's like to discover the person you are in a world where so many people want you to be something else doesn't often get explored with this level of sincerity. It touches on much of the pain of trying to hold on to what you want to be when everyone in your life wants to pry you loose from it, sometimes with brazen aggression and others with quiet, condescending rejection. But it also touches on the messy salvation that comes when you finally get to explore yourself.Something I've never seen explored in the genre is using the way you advance the story to convey emotion, and this game does that beautifully—the ways you move forward and peel away the current scene to move to the next scene changes dramatically depending on the context of the narrative, in a way that adds a lot of extra impact compared to the traditional click-to-advance gameplay. One piece of advice: the game gives you a button to erase everything for you, but try to stay away from using it. Having to use your mouse to manually peel away parts of pages or scenes is so much more intimate.For people who don't like visual novels or queer little indie games, this probably won't be your cup of tea. This game is for people who (or the friends and family of people who) have had to struggle against the current because of their identity. If that describes you, I cannot recommend the experience this game has to offer enough.

_childDocuments_.review: an interactive medium to tell a story about a transgender woman struggling with her family's acceptance and attitude. set in the 90s with her as a young woman still trying to own herself and her identity. this game showcases how video games can make excellent, engaging story mediums that mere words or simple images cannot achieve. it shows you, rather than telling, and it also lets you create the ending to an extent. even more so than that, you "erase" to create, which adds a mechanical layer of depth and meaning to the game that elicits more of an emotional response from the player. you see what she has crossed out, how she feels, and you slowly uncover her thoughts and feelings--only to erase it all again, anyway. more of an experience--less of a game. highly recommend. _childDocuments_.review: An absolutely wonderful story!!! As a trans male I was tearing up crying multiple times playing this game, it helped me realize that right now isn't forever and things will get better with my family as they slowly understand me better. This game portrays the coming out depression that most queer people go thru in an very accurate way, it was honestly very scary how it had me looking really far into myself and looking at my story in a different light. I related very much with the main characters mother being so...understanding in her own way? Me and my mother have a very similar relationship as they did in the beginning, makes me very hopeful that things with my mom will turn out similar. This game also portrays found family very well and how sometimes people in your found family wont be there forever. Its something most queer people have experienced. When blood family isn't understanding your found family is. And sometimes people leave your little found family, they may be back eventually after going on their own path for a bit, or sometimes you never talk to them again. It was marvelously portrayed with these characters. I looked on my little found family and remembered the ones who left and the ones who are still by my side and it hurt just a tad thinking about them but they where all so impactful on my life and this game give that same feeling10/10 Definitely check this game out if you are trans, queer, or honestly just had a bad relationship with your parents in your teens. Makes you think about alot.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of silly arguments about what does or doesn't count as a game. Personally, my only standard is how much any interactivity there is adds to the experience, and how worth it that experience is. By that metric, while If Found is not much of a 'game' by typical standards, it's an extremely good story and work of art that needs to exist in this medium. By all standards of queer storytelling, kinetic novels, interactive art installations, anything else you could compare it to, it clears by a wide margin. _childDocuments_.review: Visual novel.  Two stories in parallel, one about studying an anomaly on the edge of the solar system, another about a person dealing with issues of identity, self-image and family.Heads up:  I'm going to recommend this game at the end.  But I do have some issues...This game dances on a line between novel user interaction and labor intensive.  You go about revealing text, images and scenes by wiping out other text, images and scenes.  It's a poignant mechanism for the telling of the story, but it's also a lot of trouble, especially in a few places where it's hard to tell if you've done it enough to move on.The mouse pointer is sometimes awfully hard to see.  Maybe it's my eyes, but when it's a dot on the screen that I have to find it would be nice to have more contrast for it.There's at least one spot where it's possible to accidentally progress to the next scene before you've squeezed all the content out of the current one.  There might be more, but perhaps I was lucky enough to do things in the right order.There's an implication that it's possible to prevent a particular outcome, but I couldn't find a way to do it.  I found that a bit annoying.The music alternated between ethereal and too damn loud.  I'm not referring to the thrash band performance, which was appropriately loud; I mean there were scene transitions where I needed to yank my headphones off and the music was still loud enough for me while they're dangling from my neck.I got to the credits and epilogue in a little over three hours.  This is fine for a VN, and this one does have a lot of artistic content and mechanisms, but it's dancing another line with the current store price of $12.99.  Of course, nowadays lunch costs me that much and I'm much less likely to remember it.Avast Antivirus quarantined the game on me while I was in the epilogue.  This may have been a false positive; Avast has given me false positives in the past, and a full system scan didn't show anything else.I got the game in an HB monthly bundle.  All told, I'm glad to have experienced the story, especially for having effectively paid less than $2 for it.  If you can get it cheap, and if your antivirus software lets you, I suggest you give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: is a narrative-driven visual novel. This entry in the genre trades narrative complexity for a stunning, memorable artstyle, as it tells the story of an Irish teen struggling to understand their identity and start on the path to adulthood. While the "gameplay" centered on erasing the memories presented onscreen can grow into a repetitive strain over time and some portions of the game suffer from a lack of investment in the characters and story, this is overall a worthwhile experience that will be particularly appealing to those interested in LGBT, teen coming-of-age, or family drama stories.You play as Kasio, an Irish teenager caught amidst some inner turmoil as they come to learn their identity. How do they manage their family's difficulty in understanding, the twisting social connections of their friends, and the pressing needs of adulthood? This game tells Kasio's story over the course of one month when it all comes to a head, featuring some eye-catching aesthetics in the process. Erase Kasio's journal through picturesque landscapes and simple drawings alike as you find your way through the challenges of her life. follows the gameplay-minimal format that many of publisher Annapurna Interactive's titles are known for. Grounding one's expectations is perhaps a good place to start: the gameplay in this game is almost exclusively scrubbing back and forth. For the 2.5 hours runtime, the game expects you to just do that. The activity could be pain-inducing for those inclined to frantic mouse movement; in fact, this is one of the few titles with keyboard controls where simply using a mousepad may be preferable to a proper mouse.With that necessary preface out of the way:  is a gorgeous little game. The artstyle is its most notable element, with the blending of colors and words as the player wipes things away creating unique visages that capture the game's intended feeling of "erasing memories." The space motif plays a big assisting role here, allowing for sprawling portraits of starry skies to take up screens, creating stunning backdrops for character moments or sci-fi moments of danger. The looks alone can certainly compel a player along, as the hand-drawn pencil art captures the warm, casual tone of the game's characters and setting.As this title is more concerned about delivering a story over an immersive gameplay experience, it's worth considering the story on its own merits - and it has some ups and downs. The story centers on the LGBT experience in a time (the 1990s) and a place (Ireland) where visibility and acceptance were far from the norm. As much as this story can be boiled down to major themes like "a coming-of-age story," "a journey of self-discovery and self-acceptance," and "a teenage drama," the combination of all these parts means that players interested in memorable LGBT stories should be satisfied by this one here. Beyond that angle, though, there are some weaknesses - a main one being the side story about an astronaut. The purpose of the story does become clear by the end, but it was never given the dramatic weight it deserved despite being positioned as an equal-opposite to Kasio's story. A greater balance between the stories could've helped  feel like a more well-rounded affair. is a charming visual novel. More memorable for the feelings provoked from the images presented than the depth of the narrative, this one is a standout for those interested in LGBT coming-of-age stories. This Annapurna title ought to be found by players who don't mind some heavily repetitive motion for a few hours.  gets a B.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most emotionally resonant, genuine and impactful interactive narratives I've ever experienced. For everyone, but especially other trans and non-binary players, couldn't recommend If Found highly enough! Truly grateful to the devs for taking us on this wild and beautiful ride!If Found also embraces the idea that there's no universal trans experience, instead here's a unique and creatively-presented visual novel about a particular, well-written trans woman in a specific setting (Ireland) and time (90's). Doesn't try to speak for all trans people, and doesn't have to. But themes of found family (especially, queer found family), identity, letting go vs. remembering & reframing the past/memories - both joyful and painful, struggles with family-of-origin, figuring out your own self and interests and voice etc, will likely be deeply relateable for a wider range of trans and queer players. The type of narrative that leaves you feeling less alone, breaks you open in the best ways possible but also bends towards something hopeful.I found the gameplay in If Found wonderfully unique and immersive - definitely unlike anything I've read/played before! Adds to the experience for sure. As an FYI for disabled players and those with chronic pain or limited hand mobility-  the central gameplay mechanic involves long periods of holding down mouse button, moving mouse back and forth. In other words, repetitive wrist/hand motions.

_childDocuments_.review: If Found, an interactive visual novel, is a coming of age story about connection, isolation and self-discovery that centres around Kasio, a young Irish woman, destroying her diary in the remains of a crumbling old mansion. A record of the last 28 days, it tells the story of her return home, her conflict with her family, the friendships she made and the challenges she faced. Somewhere within its pages is also an explanation for the looming black hole that’s about to destroy the Earth!The gameplay elements consist almost entirely of sweeping the cursor across the screen to erase the diary, revealing something else underneath or progressing to a different part of the page, revealing more of Kasio’s story. As a fun extra, there is also a glossary entry for anything specifically Irish that is mentioned!If Found is very much a visual novel, it has a fixed ending and does not allow the player to affect the story progression in any way. However, the interaction is implemented in a unique and organic way that helps the player to connect with the narrative rather than being a distraction. The mechanic fits well with the style of the experience and works well for the most part but does start to get a little repetitive over a 2-3 hour playthrough.The game’s visuals and soundtrack are among its strongest features. The artwork is beautiful and has a cute, sketchy illustrative style, a little rough maybe, but very charming. The overall aesthetics also have a slightly trippy, psychedelic feel that serves to add intensity to the more tumultuous and dramatic parts of the narrative. These elements make use of much more vibrant and high contrast colour palettes than the muted and pastel shades that make up the bulk of the game.The music in If Found is diverse, including funky sci-fi beats, relaxing ethereal tones, melancholy notes and even some rockier numbers. The various types of music work coherently together, complimenting the different aspects of the narrative and blending seamlessly with the visuals. Additionally, the game makes nice use of ambient noise such as rainfall and footsteps to improve the player’s sense of immersion.If Found is a heartfelt and emotive interactive novel but its abstract double narrative is an unnecessary and unwanted distraction from an otherwise sincere and engaging story. While there is some replayability in the form of achievements and missable diary entries this is limited and as such the price tag feels a little steep for the short playtime. That being said, it is an enjoyable, thought-provoking experience with stunning visuals and some great music that I’m happy to recommend to fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: So, for a human being that doesn't really experience emotions anymore, this one is like being punched in the gut, kicked in the kidneys, locked in a box for four days, and then climbing out for a hug.I don't know, maybe it's just me, but I accidentally got way too involved in the story.This isn't really so much of a game. If you're looking for the typical point-and-click, "work out puzzles to advance the story" type thing, this isn't it. This is more like a movie that you advance at your own pace. You have a little "eraser," and you "erase" your way from scene to scene. If that sounds boring and repetitive, it actually isn't - the developers found a clever way to make the scene transitions decently varied and fluid, so erasing from scene to scene doesn't feel obnoxious or cumbersome. The only real "interactivity" comes at the very end, and I won't really give that away - just be aware that most of this game is essentially a "watch & read."That didn't for one second detract from my engagement, though. I'm actually usually NOT a "story game" kind of person - but with this Steam event going on, I went ahead and bought several storyline games, and this was one of them. I don't know why but even though it's not so much a game, it still captured me from beginning to end. The art is pretty, the visuals are eye-catching.. the music is all over the place, from ethereal to punk-ish to electro-whatever. So is the theme, really.. just like in the description, it goes everywhere - from space to the fast-food joint. The characters were very well defined and didn't feel one-dimensional at all.. and the storyline was great. I don't know how they did it but they made me care about the story.Fair warning though, if you actually get into the story, it'll kick you in the kidneys. I don't think anyone that likes a touching story will want to pass this one up. Recommend, recommend, recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Set on Achill Island of the west coast of Ireland in 1993, If Found tells the story of Kasio a trans woman coming home for Christmas after completing her Masters in Astrophysics in Dublin. Kasio is awaiting the decision of her PhD application and is dealing with her general sense of drift in her life and her struggles to come to terms with it. Over the course of the month of December, we witness her interactions with her confused and worrying mother, her angry and disgusted brother and her friends who are all just as seemingly lost and drifting as she is, trying to deal with the bleak situation on the island and the constant chatter and small-mindedness of the islanders.Oh, and there's a concurrent plotline where there's a black hole that will destroy the Earth….so …you know…there's that.....Mostly told through the medium of Kasios' diary, the structure of this visual novel is unique in that you progress through the story by erasing her diary entries. This helps to convey the sense of her world and her sense slipping from her as the story progresses. In-between these parts, you'll be erasing the scenes and dialogues to reveal the next ones. The art is exceptional, loose and very detailed at the same time, it also lends to the chaotic nature of Kasio's life at the time. It's all hand-drawn by comic artist Liadh Young and suits the game perfectly. The colour palette changes to depict the emotions in the scenes and, backed up by a superb soundtrack and sound design, each scene is set up just right. This helps to sidestep the issue many other games along with TV shows and movies have whereby the music is there to almost force to feel the way the directors want you to feel without them having to do any work in the actual scene.But, as with all visual novels, the devil is in the details or in other words the dialogue and story. And If Found has a profoundly deep and moving one. Kasios' struggle with coming to terms with her own new self is compounded by her families confusion over it and outright refusal to accept it. From her vicious brother (who may be top of my list of most unlikable characters in any game ever) constantly needling Kasio over what everyone else on the island thinks of her and her friends to her mother being so uncertain about how to even talk to Kasio that in her letters she simply addresses Kasio as "Child".This rejection is held in stark contrast to her friends who, namely Colum, Jack (Colums boyfriend), and Shans who have formed a band. Each of them is in a similar situation as Kasio, Colm and Jack with their openly gay relationship and Shans trying to find out where he belongs due to his half-Indian heritage and his own uncertain sexuality. These are prime societal issues now but in rural Ireland in the early nineties? This would've had people priming their torches and sharpening their pitchforks. The group invite Kasio to join them in their squat in a squalid old parochial house while they rehearse in preparation for their first ever gig. It's here, in the interactions between these characters that the dialogue truly shines. It's written incredibly authentically with the only concession to a non-Irish audience being the glossary that can be used whenever any Irish or any term that's unlikely to be heard outside of Ireland is used. The dialogue gives a sense of realism and fleshes out the world, gives it life. This is actually how people talk in Ireland and it's marvelous to see no corners were cut or edges rounded out. The parallel storyline of a black hole heading for Earth is where the game gets a little trippy. Set in the future where Kasio is an astronaut in space investigating the phenomena with her only contact being the vaguely named Control. The animations, colour palette and music changing to a wilder almost psychedelic tone. For me, this was also the weakest part of If Found. I felt the two stories meshed well until the end and then they never resolved the space one properly. It just peters out and doesn't seem to go anywhere. I got the point at the end of it, but I felt that with such a engaging story, it could've been ended better.Ultimately, your enjoyment of If Found will come down to if you enjoy a good story or visual novels. It's certainly a good enough game to convert people to the visual novel genre but it's so distinct from the rest of the genre that I feel it does stand out on its' own merits. If you are into visual novels then If Found ticks virtually every box you've got. The story is wonderfully poignant and well told, the dialogue is flawless and the characters are all fantastic. The artwork, music and overall production are to of such a high quality it's difficult to believe that this was done by such a small team.The themes tackled by If found are one that need more highlighting. The LGBTQI community scarcely get a look in most games and are shamefully under-represented in gaming. But representation for its' own sake won't help either. It need to be effective and genuine. And this is the part that If Found gets the most right. It manages to convey Kasios' story in such a way that you'll get it just with an open mind. You don't need to be LGBTQI to understand the characters or the themes here. Although, having said that, I'd love to read a trans reviewers take on this game.If I have to offer up any criticism at all, aside from the previously mentioned. I'd have to say the story starts quite slowly which is a bit bizarre for a game with a scant two hour playtime. If Found is a tale about how acceptance and love are vastly more important than understanding, about how our place in the world is defined so much more by how we see ourselves than anyone else and about how erasing the pain of your past and letting it go is often the only way to move forward.It's a game that needs to be played by everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: It was an amazing journey to do in one sitting. This is a short game about being different and feeling like an outsider from your own family and society expectations. It deals with LGBTIQA+ issues in a sweet manner without the usual idealization a tons of games suffer from: not all the stories and not all the characters are happy. It's also up to you to write the ending for it. Literally, after you finish the experience you can choose what would have been of every single character based on your experience with the game. This game is not trying to force feelings on you but about how you end up feeling about the situations in this game, it is all about how you felt about what happened. A lot of people won't understand the sci-fi bits, but they are mostly related about how you feel like a stranger in a world that rejects you, most of the time. Is a short story but it has enough potential and writing to make its point across. I'm a player used to games with hundreds of hours of gameplay, so after sitting for just a little while with this and crying a few tears, I have to say, it does get things right. These are the type of LGBTIQA+ games that we need to keep around, the real ones, the devs did an excellent job.
