_childDocuments_.review: Ok let's just get the cons out of the way first:* Interface needs a bit of polish and fine-tuning* Occasional bugs* The storymode is mediocre and the NPCs are rude (altho that is kinda true to my actual experiences with the wine industry lmao)* Needs a bit more content in certain places (but doesn't feel "unfinished" just like they could do a bit more to flesh out certain parts like Terroir management)All that aside? It's an extremely good and compelling combination of puzzle game and agriculture sim with mechanics challenging and subtle enough that even if you know what you should be doing you will not be able to produce the exact same perfect wines every year.If the idea of learrning about winemaking in a friendly way sounds fun, and you like games the mix puzzles with simulation, get it, and just play Endless Mode instead of story.Devs: this game RULES but consider tweaking story mode to make it more friendly and engagingAlso it would be awesome to have more grape varieties, a few more plots to buyAlso also it would be amazing to have reoccuring contests too for you to enter wines into or something like that.Anyway, I love it and hope to see the game improve!
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is the only thing this game has going for it. In the campaign, things are locked behind dialogue/story progression without telling you. Is the button I am clicking locked or bugged? No idea! The game makes no mention of HOW to actually improve the quality of your wine, so you just keep guessing wrong, keep bleeding money and then go bankrupt. _childDocuments_.review: I think the writing could be hit or miss for people depending on their humour, and it was mostly a miss for me. _childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: It sounded fun, I like wine, I like strategy, I like farm sims sometimes. Honestly it started off great I was drawn in by a lot of things at the very beginning but after it started,....just wow this is boring. It seems like there is possibly some deep game play in there somewhere, but my god it comes off as crazy simplistic, just playing tiles and clicking next turn. There is stuff to buy most seem to just give bonus to stuff, hidden in 3 different buildings that are never really explained or maybe they are, honestly the story mode was so incredibly bad I had to stop, you play an ungrateful brat that inherited a vineyard next door to a what appears to be a Karen, the story felt like some barbie mobile game. Part of me wants to try again and push through to see if it gets good but i'm afraid it may just make me hate wine and feel like I wasted my time. I wish there was a short tutorial that was not the story, endless mode might be fun if you already know what you are doing, IF there is depth to the game play, which I'm not sure there really is, it might just kind of look like there is.There are a lot of good things it has going for it, but feel like they would need to almost start over on a lot of the mechanics to really make it any fun in the long term.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: The game's biggest flaw definitely seems to be its story which gets in the way of the tutorial and, really, if I could just not deal with that, it would be great. I don't think I expect a deep, compelling, vineyard-based narrative, but the story does a poor job of keeping a thin tutorial held together. What I mostly want is the game to teach me how to play itself while also showing me the cost/benefits of engaging with certain mechanics (like the cost of wine bottle designs).As a "wine person", I think it's neat how much effort the game puts into certain details of wine growing. It's a cool touch and I'm glad it's there. Still, it feels like some of that came at the cost of explaining actual game mechanics and it leaves more guesswork than necessary which can be frustrating if you don't pick up on what you're missing really quickly.That aside, the game's core puzzle mechanic does a decent job of communicating limited time and resources to accomplish certain work at a certain point. More could be done to better communicate that and get the rest of the game to center around the idea the puzzle system is building towards, but I do think it's a solid basic mechanic! Its art style is simple and very pretty and I think it's the sort of thing I'll come back to now and again as a kind of mood game.Hundred Days is definitely a better game than not, it just trips over itself in places it doesn't need to.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Its so sad that this game's theme and game play is so fun but its design and story is so utterly trash. You literally need to spend HOURS grinding the same years over and over to unlock 1 advancement in tech, then for some reason you need to spend the same amount of time to be able to actually purchase the item to use, which may only increase your profits by a marginal amount. Want to make a new type of wine? Not only spend 20K unlocking it, then another 10K to research how to brew it THEN another 30K to get the equipment, another 20K to get some more tiles for it to fit and finally you can make a bad version of a new wine. All in all cost, 80K. How much you earn a year? ~3-5K. How long it takes a year to progress? 10-15 minutes. So 3-4 hours to only progress ONE extra wine. And don't get me started on how genuinely horrible the story is. It felt like i was being punished reading it. Why does every character just genuinely think your'e autistic? Overall they need to majorly balance/ make a fast mode/ get rid of every line of dialogue from the story. I hope they fix the progression because I want to actually play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I had really high hopes for this game going in, but after about 2 and a half hours, I can say it's just not for me. The major selling points of this game for me were the art style and the level of detail that it goes into to teach you about growing grapes and making wine. I really like that this game genuinely tries to educate you, but it feels like just that. Like I'm in a classroom taking noes. The game gives you way too much all at once and barely explains the core mechanics. I was confused for a majority of the game. Also, the story mode is poorly written, and the art style during the story mode is corporate and a little offputting compared to the rest of the game. The story mode only takes you about a fourth of the way through the game and you have literally no input in the story. Things just kind of happen without any input from the player.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some soul, and you can tell the devs truly care about winemaking.Unfortunately the following prevents me from recommending the game:1) Terrible dialogue and a trite "story" that barely lasts two hours. If you're gonna rip off Stardew valley in your intro, at least also steal their talent for storytelling and dialogue.2) Clunky UI, specifically navigating out of submenus is never as intuitive as you want it to be.3) ABSOLUTE TEDIUM. While farming and fermenting cards automatically appear, others such as cleaning, maintainance, advertising, pest control and selling have to be dug out of menus with multiple clicks EVERY SINGLE TIME. You have to manually sell your wine EVERY SINGLE TURN until you unlock the STORE building. And if you make the mistake of getting that too early, its ruinious upkeep will bankrupt you.4) I do not understand the point of the tetris job scheduling mechanics. Since the shape only changes when you upgrade your capacity and the shapes for each task are constant, it stops being a puzzle really quick.5) Somehow, this game brings my computer (2 year old macbook pro) to a crawl when there is fog (and sometimes when there isn't). How unoptimized can your code be?
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Hundred Days is a little puzzle and a little strategy. The cards you have turn into tetris pieces and the shapes give you a headache if you're not planning ahead. The game is at its best when it's throwing far too many cards at you to handle. It's quite hectic trying to manage them all without missing a beat. It gets even more interesting when you're running two vineyards at the same time!I enjoy crafting the perfect look for my wine by choosing the bottle and label. Even if it doesn't matter that much.Honestly, you can feel the developer's passion for wine while playing. Which really makes the difference!Learn more,
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game with Terroir being the only other legitimate winemaking game around.  But I just can't get into it, the core game loop just isn't very compelling.  Most of the time I feel like I have very little control over the wine I'm making and I'm just mindlessly clicking buttons.  Not to mention I've played less than 2 hours and I already finished the story. Overall, it's better presented than Terroir, but the gameplay just isn't there.Each system in the game does not work well together.  I feel like the story, the farm development/upgrades, and the wine production/selling are all on a different timeline.  The story happens incredibly quickly, your farm is expanded and upgraded incredibly slowly, only the speed of the wine production feels somewhat balanced.  Selling wine is the most annoying thing in the game though, just mindlessly clicking buttons every turn.  You sell very small quantities to individual buyers, and it really just feels like busy work that isn't interesting at all.In a lot of ways it is just too casual of a game to appeal to me.  It feels like a mobile game without the monetization of a mobile game.  The story, the interface, the gameplay, it all feels like a casual mobile game.  I'm not really sure who the audience is here, but as a wine lover who likes involved, challenging PC games, it isn't me.Just get Terroir instead, it'll keep you interested for longer and it is much cheaper.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for this game, given I worked in the industry for a short while, but ultimately I was disappointed. The art style is really beautiful, and it's best feature. The gameplay is frustratingly slow moving - by the time I'd finished the story I put 6 hours into the game, but actually only about 20% (maybe? hard to know) into gameplay. The tutorial at some point just stops, and leaves you guessing on how/when to expand, since the story does not guide you through expansion. I tried restarting in Endless mode, but the game progresses so slowly that 10 years had passed, repeating the same thing before I could expand. Just before I gave up I discovered you can get a bank loan to speed your expansion (something that would've been perfect to mention in the story/tutorial), but my frustrations at this game boiled over so I quit, with no desire to return.On to the weakest bit of the game - the story. It felt like it was written by a high school English student, or worse. It's overly long, and just not interesting. The sound effects for when someone is speaking are irritating, destroying the calmer atmosphere of the game. As others have mentioned, the 'puzzley' nature of fitting your actions into a grid tetris style is an interesting choice - but there's no puzzle aspect to it. If you can't do all that you want to in a month, there's no consequence to leaving one thing for the next month.Sadly I was just left disappointed with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: So it's a fun game. The graphics are simplistic, but very clean and has that "modern" kind of feel and aesthetic. Pros:-Aside from the graphics, there is some deceptively complex ideas being thrown in with the "casual" wrapper that is enjoyable-If you're like me, the game is friendly to "pick up and play" but there will be a bit of a learning curve along the way-Endless mode is a fantastic idea, and what truly should be the star of this game. Cons:-Story mode/tutorial doesn't do a good enough job at teaching you how the game is supposed to be played for success-The RNG, while mirroring unfortunate luck in real life, can be brutal and unforgiving, even if you've made the right moves up until that point-Gameplay loop loses a bit of its charm after a bit, becoming very apparent quickly of its repetitive natureOther thoughts:-Kind of wish in addition to endless mode, there is an endless sandbox mode that has all of the technologies researched from the start-I feel like endless mode, while great, should offer the option of what grape varietal to grow in the starter plot for more flexibility (and go through that process as well instead of dumping the player a few turns out from harvest)-Some potential balancing issues that need to be ironed out. Perfect example is the shop room for the warehouse. 500 upkeep per turn is rough at the point in the game it looks like a good idea to invest the 30k into having it in the first place-Speaking of rooms, could be an interesting idea to "turn off" a room to conserve the budgetOverall though, pros, cons, other thoughts all put together, it's a solid game. It has a learning curve to it, but has a very simple look and aesthetic to it that the difficulty might catch you off guard. Can't wait to see how it pans out through patches.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I just want say that despite not liking wine, I love wine-making games. And this one, well this one is one of the best! What starts out as a complex task is streamlined as you improve, giving a genuine sense of progression. You feel like you've earned high scores, and when RNG gives you a lower score than you feel you ought to have (a 74 for a 5* wine? grr) it feels natural, if annoying, as opposed to some other games where it can feel like you lack agency in your product. The story is much too short, and is in fact just a thin facade for the tutorial. It works fine as one, but it doesn't feel like it earns the title "story". A longer story, or a second one, would serve this (or future games) well. Perhaps a rivalry with another winery, giving the awards some much needed depth.Overall, if you like simple business tycoon games, or played Terroir until you eyes only see hexagons, give this a try! It's well worth it, and a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I don't consider myself a wine drinker; I prefer wines made from fruits that aren't grapes. But I do love a good management sim, and Hundred Days is a nice one. Besides the usual revenue-and-expense gameplay, your actions and your attention are played out on a tetris-like board. New business with not a lot of capabilities = small board. There is also a very nice tech tree that requires massive investment of money before you can a year or two later reap the rewards of upgrades now. The challenges are tough but fair, and there is a silly grape-customization tool, and now also a new California map and new grapes and things. Give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend the game in its current state. That being said, it has very solid gameplay foundation and great potential and the main problems are not that hard to fix. This game highly resembles legendary Game Dev Tycoon. The core gameplay mechanic is to create a product with a highest score using your resources in a most efficient way and dealing with some randomness. As Game Dev Tycoon successfully demonstrated, this mechanic could be very engaging if implemented correctly. The main problem with Hundred Days is that when you finally craft you 100/100 perfect wine - you do not get any real payout. This is a very frustrating experience, since you feel like all your efforts are worthless. Notice that this is a simple rebalancing act - reduce payout for mediocre 60-80 wines, and increase payout for exceptional 90+ wines (and special huge payout for 97+). Not only this would make your experience more rewarding, it would make it more realistic as well. Right now you can't implement this directly, since once you figured out the formula it is way too easy to continue delivery perfect wines - you need more controlled randomness (things like sun exposure, consumer interest shifting, variations of tannin/sweetness/body as oppose to them being fully controlled) to make it work.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Gosh, what a lovely game! It's a bit niche, but if you like these kinds of management/puzzle games, then you'll REALLY like Hundred Days.The graphics and the music are pleasing and soothing; you could spend hours just going turn after turn with how soft and pleasant everything is.The learning curve isn't too intense, but it also requires you to think more than not at all. You don't want to buy things earlier than you're able to afford managing them, but the trial and error is half the fun.The story mode is short but sweet. The characters have some amount of life to them, and the dialogue is surprisingly educational. I don't know where I'm going to use all this knowledge I now have about growing wine, especially since I don't drink wine, but it's... there now I suppose.Definitely a lovely game, would recommend anyone who likes management games that are on the more simple and chill side to give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I always have a love for farming games and this one is a cut above the rest. I never knew how much I wanted to become a winemaker. This game started a bit complicated with the terminologies and techniques but that ended up very charming because I can related to the protagonist since we both are city dwellers with with zero knowledge.  the first few minutes I am captivated with the characters and the pretty scenery but the long paragraphs of words started to get long and bothersome for me to read that I just skipped it. I wished they implemented more voice acting. I really liked when reading the letter we get to hear the voice of our character, it gives a nice touch. But that's it. The grapes are amazing, learning about them and their qualities, the little sketchbook about. I like how it explains things like tannin and how it affects the taste and what we can do to influence the wine. I have nothing else to say but WE NEED MORE GRAPESthe flavor system is still very much unexplored but I feel like that is part of the charm of the game, to go bold with our decisions and the risks. We definitely need more customization of the bottles, maybe like a free form design we could import or directly draw. I would think crossbreeding variants would be a nice addition to the game as well, the genetics etc, the possibilities are endlessoverall, I would give this game a 92/100, needs more body (inside joke in-game)
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a lovely art style. As someone very knowledgeable when it comes to winemaking I found myself really enjoying the experience. I wish there were some more options to automate specific steps in the process as clicking and selecting the same thing over and over in the later stages becomes very repetitive. You can automate some processes using employees but when it comes the winemaking process you have to make the changes every time and the more plots you own the harder it gets to keep track off. It would have been nice to have have the sliders and other settings default to what you used for last years vintage and then you can go from there if you need to do changes.The early games is very good but the late game is kind of disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This game left me with a mixed reaction. The story mode is too short and you can't really change the course of it, you have absolutely no power in this storyline, so much that you could skip everything and avoid feeling empty (like me) after you read each "chapter" unfolding before your eyes and then boom, suddenly the story becomes mildly engaging but credits start rolling and nothing else happens.Talking about the simulative part of the game now: If you think the game could go against you with some wild cards to alter the pace and let you face some difficult decisions this isn't the right title for you, selling to people IS repetitive, you just min-max whom you sell how much of a given bottle of wine and that's all. There's no connection with whom you sell the products to, they are just random people that buy an "x" amount of stuff for a "y" discount and the connection you thought there was if you followed the story mode isn't there at all. They are puppets, they have no name but most importantly they have no soul. They don't get mad or sad because you couldn't sell them what they wished for, they don't come back annoyed because the day before you couldn't satisfy them, they are just total strangers that happen to buy wine just for the sake of it, it would have been way more credible if "Gigi Barolo, The Innkeeper" wanted to buy these precious bottles to sell in his "Taverna de' Barolo", just a little flavor text to animate this action of local sale.Let's focus on the Special Orders now: basically, if you fulfill them they let you acquire fame.But what happens if you leave those special orders back as decades pass by? Do people get mad at you because you're not fulfilling their desires? You might think so.Do they deny the special order so that you can't complete it anymore?Do they get pissed off because twenty years passed and there's no sign of what they asked for?No, absolutely NOTHING happens, oh and congratulations for fulfilling an order that has been issued by someone in 2021 while you're in 2053! How comfy, how convenient, wildly unrealistic and unnecessary if developed like this.This is to say that a game where no consequences can alter your gameplay nor increase the difficulties you must face to achieve and hope for better days isn't really a game worth my time; I need to feel the pressure, I need to feel competitive and this game fails in conceiving what striving for the best wine feels like because after all, you are alone, nothing is disturbing your path.I'm at the point in which I do not care about votes on my wine anymore, I just mindlessly min-max to achieve better technology (oh boy, it costs so freaking much) and do nothing more than this because everything is peaceful and there's no other winery competing with you.You are just like story-mode Filippo, you are acting like him and nothing will stop your greedy money machine because YOU are the evil viticultor focusing on profits now.If there wasn't a story I would have appreciated the game much more, wanna know why? Because the story makes you feel like you could be the change, the story puts you on an emotional level and connection with the wine-making process but suddenly everything ends out of the blue, too soon you are left alone and become just a money printer, it makes you feel empty and wishing there was more to that story accompanied you in this journey.Even if the storyline is bad I just wished it didn't end so abruptly. The joy I felt by playing this game wears out faster than I thought.As an italian I will speak to you, devs: Sono estremamente deluso, la metà delle ore che ho sono perché ho scordato il PC acceso, per il resto il gioco non è male graficamente, da rivedere svariati aspetti.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this kind of games, so I do recommend. I dont want to go throught 100 games till I find good soils for some wines.Please give me a Lab where i can change pH of  the soil etc. Or give more choices for one wineyard when purchasing.- a lot of repetetive clicking- (yes if u upgrade your store u have less to do, but till there clicking every wine insteadt of a "sell all" button takes away a bit of fun.also having to go in 2 menu to always look if stuff needs to be repaired? give me a "keep tidy" button (at a cost, its ok if i need a room for that) so the cards for cleaning come automatic into my deck- you better remember whats good for each wine, otherwise you always have to open the book, as there is no indicator when e.g. starting the fermenting process which sugar content is good for that wine. yes its teaching but make it an option please.- you want a new yeast flavor? better destroy and replant a wineyard, as the lab can only combine existing flavors - no hotkeys yetpositive?- so while i complain a lot about gameplay comfort, I see it as a work in progress- its actually still fun to play, great atmosphere, so I'm just hoping for the future patches to make it the 9,5/10 it has the potential for, currently it's maybe a 7?thanks for the game, i like the love for details, the graphic and idea behind it
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some fun ideas but goes out of it's way to be tedious. You spend considerably more time cleaning equipment and doing maintenance than experimenting with different grapes and wine-making techniques. The gating behind the tech-tree and upgrade levels of various buildings is also a bit out of whack, leading to less of an economic simulator and more of a waiting game.I have enjoyed playing a little bit of it, but it is deeply flawed and I can't recommend it.It is roughly on the same level as 2017's , which is itself was enjoyable and deeply flawed, but this perhaps has more opportunity to become fun and interesting from its base than Terroir had.A good winemaking simulator could be an amazing game, but we're not there yet.

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, the story isn't the best, but it's pretty short.  It's not exactly bad, but the characters are kind of caricatures of what I imagine people who make wine would be like, and are a bit annoying.Once you get past that, though, the game is cute, surprisingly well balanced and deep.  A lot of "tycoon" games are either too easy or so tightly tuned that one wrong choice is impossible to recover from.  Hundred Days manages to hit a good balance between progress and challenging financial choices, and seems to be pretty forgiving if you, say, have a bad year's harvest.Also, it's a minor thing, but the dollar amounts are actually pretty accurate for real-world transactions!  My immersion!
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely little game :)The story is a nice introduction to most mechanics, and the game is easy to get into. I liked the characters in the story and their dialogues too. The real meat of the game however is in the endless mode, since the story isnt all that long. It is a lot of fun to optimize the wine production, tinker with each step of the process and end up with a great wine as a result! The game isnt perfect, but I'd recommend it nonetheless. It is quite grindy and slow, since getting upgrades is really expensive. Quality of Life features could also be improved, some functions are really hard to find since they are buried in slightly unintuitive menus. All in all though, if you enjoy wine or optimizing stuff in general, you might enjoy this game!

It's always exciting to unlock a new grape and figure out its perfect settings, and I've personally had a lot of fun with the bottle maker lol. There's definitely a lot of trial and error involved, but the satisfaction of finally getting things right is unmatched.I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes these types of trial and error games, and who like obtaining perfect scores. It's a super relaxing game to just open and mess around with after a long day :)

_childDocuments_.review: seems fun, but also feels like it's unfinished.. have mixed feelings about it. the lack of a proper tutorial makes the game experience very frustrating. for someone without any knowledge of winemaking, such a complex process needs a better tutorial. the existing 'tutorial' is not very good, and the fact that it is blended in with the 'story' makes it very tiresome. also, the story is not very interesting and to be honest, is a bit pointless. you are sent into having to deal with everything all at once:  growing grapes, making the actual wine, running a winery, having employees and so on. it gets overwhelming very fast. the game needs a lot of improvement.its a cute idea and a good initiative but as a game, it simply falls short of providing a fun experience. there are plenty of gameplay affecting bugs, resulting in wasted in-game money and frustration. some concepts are not laid out clearly, and you end up having having to spend some hours cluelessly fiddling with sliders. the price is alright for this kind of 'small' game, but at its current state, it's not worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like wine, but I love this game. I'll preface this with the fact I know very little about wine, but did once accidentally attend a wine tasting because it was disguised as a lecture on soil chemistry in vineyards. From what I can remember of the lecture, the game seems pretty accurate (though I'm sure one could argue the finer points). Story mode is interesting and it's nice to have new features explained organically rather than just following tooltips. Aside from story mode, the game contains 5 challenge modes (not counting the DLC which I also recommend), and a freeplay mode. The game is challenging but fun. I'm still struggling to complete the final challenge mode. But it's also quite restful and charming. You can name the ducks. There's a yeast lab to create new yeasts, and a grape lab to create new custom grapes to play around with. I think my only complaint is that some of the finer details of the game mechanics are really opaque. Does a different cap for your bottles make a difference? Does using fancy shaped bottles make it sell better? I still don't know. But it's not a big enough deal that it worries me.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for a few hours, I do have to say that I enjoy the game, but I have a few problems with the game.1. For me, I like he game because of its puzzle elements. The gameplay for placing cards on the board is like Tetris in a way, making you think about what should be the most important card to place in a limited amount of space. Some cards are timed based on the remaining days, and the game warns you if the card almost expires. 2. There is a great amount of research put into the gameplay considering the amount of knowledge the game likes to throw at you either in the story, the journal, or through the tooltips. This research shows that the developers dedicated themselves into learning about the winemaking process and loves to share it with others.3. Other things to note is the customization you can put on the bottles, a smooth and nice art style, enjoyable soundtrack, and it likes to keep you on your toes if you don't check your tools and fields as often.1. The only thing that I think I can put here is the story. The story is weak and also got on my nerves at times. It felt like the story didn't go anywhere and the writing is not that good. When the story did kick in at certain moments, it ruined the flow as you're immediately sent to the scene. I feel like if there was a smoother transition, or another way to tell the story (like using the journal more often or maybe phone texts?) then It could have been better. The story itself is short too and the conflict is basically non-existent. For the conflict, while intriguing, nothing came of it. All the main villain does is post bad reviews, and that is it. I expected a bigger conflict between you in the villain, like dealing with mysteriously broken equipment or lost customers, but it gets solved really quickly.I did not get into most of the characters because they felt narcissistic, such as the main character and the third character that helps you on the farm. These characters made me just want to skip dialogue because I did not want to read what they had to say. I understand if they want to give a story to all these characters, but the plot is so short that they are not fully developed by the end of it. This is a great wine making simulation with tons of detail and good puzzle elements, but just skip the story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything you're  looking for in a wine management sim, with some fatal UI and design flaws that prevent it from being good.  It is a highly complex game with a nuanced engine for deciding the quality of your wines - so many variables both plannable and random have to be contended with to make great wine. Even the progression as you get familiar with winemaking and grow your winery and its capacity is interesting.  The game introduces you to its mechanisms via a cute little campaign that is enjoyable but unfortunately only does the most basic job of informing you how to work things.  And now the flaw...The interaction design is extremely cumbersome.  The game just doesn't flow.  Everything you'd think about how wine making feels isn't in this UI. They seemed to randomly put interactive elements in opposite or far corners of the screen so you're constantly dragging your mouse back and forth to target tiny UI elements for basic game functions.  There are no hotkeys for anything.  One feature, your sales, is nearly a clicker game with the amount of tedious clicking you have to do until your winery is big enough to support some automation.  Adding to this problem is an unfortunate lack of solid information design - so screens which should have information on them because of how important it is require you to... you guessed it click to open, click to close to see the basic info essential to core gameplay.  They've included info ( i ) icons all over but they're mostly generic info about wine making and don't inform you about the game.One more topic - which is an odd one.  The mechanic they're using for time constraint - how many things you can get done in a day - is that cards pop up with things to be done or you can generate your own cards when you see something that needs to be taken care of.  Each card has a geometric shape and needs to be fit into a board Tetris-style.  Time management interaction design has to be in a management sim - we want limits.  However this particular mechanism is a very strange choice for this game.  I don't hate it - it probably could be done better to give more of a feel of a day of wine making, but it is functional unlike much of the UI of this game.  The interesting thing is that this mechanism isn't demonstrated clearly in their videos about the game - as if they're hiding it, as if they knew this mechanism would confuse people or give people the wrong impression about this game.  THEY'RE RIGHT! If they had shown this mechanism prominently since it is part of the core gameplay, people might have thought this game was a puzzle game rather than a management sim.  In summary I want to reinforce that this game is an AWESOME and COMPLEX management sim, plagued with shortsighted UI design and game design flow which in itself, isn't fun, is cumbersome, and doesn't align with the subject matter, wine making.  Is it salvageable? Well some things in this game aren't going to change - the weird time management mechanism is here to stay - that's ok, it is fine.  If the Game Designers REALLY do a flow diagram and look at two things: 1) What screens a player will visit every single turn and design a better way to flow through them as if you're a vintner wandering your winery every morning and afternoon; and 2) What are the clickable elements on the screen to progress the gameplay, where is the user clicking as part of their normal progression of a turn, and make that significantly less cumbersome, this game could really be amazing.  The engine is awesome, the underlying complexity of variables is top-notch, this is a failure of "play" and "flow", two core concepts in game design that got left out of this game.

Unlocking new technologies costs way too much money, meaning you have to grind many many years before you can even start making wines from all the different grapes. Another annoying aspect is that the warehouse always keeps 1 bottle of wine from each year, which never seems to be sellable. You end up with a list of 20+ wines which are kinda stuck there. There is no option to just discard them. Another thing I didn't manage to figure out is how to plant another type of grapes on the plot that you have used for other grapes before. So in order to try out new grapes you have to buy new plots of land which are insanely expensive (I only played with 2 types so far). _childDocuments_.review: Grab a glass of your favorite wine and settle in -- this is a lovely game to play on a relaxing evening.At its heart, Hundred Days is a love song to wine.  The winemaking is just detailed enough to get into the science as much as you want to, but just simple enough that you can churn out different wines or try new things without being punished too hard.  There is a puzzle element where your actions taken must "fit" inside a board that expands in size as you grow.  Board gamers will be familiar with this element.What you come away with after playing for a few hours is an appreciation for the process, a desire to run down to your local liquor store, an addiction to taking "one more turn," and a fondness for watching the changing of seasons and marking the passage of time.  Your 2020 Barbera might be poor, but your 2033 Chardonnay might win awards.  You learn, you apply what you learn, and pleasant background music accompanies you on this journey.There is a story mode and a new Napa Valley DLC to try out, but I'm still working on the main game and trying to unlock everything.  Even with that, this game was good enough that I bought another copy for a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad little game, but I couldn't call it "fun."  I played through the tutorial mission and then onwards a bit on free play after I succeeded there.  Three hours doesn't make me an expert, but it's enough to know I probably won't ever click the "PLAY" button on this one again.PROS:  Based on real wine knowledge.  Kinda cute in an indie way.  Easy to learn.  You can name your vineyard anything you want.  I always love that in a game.  I named mine "Reign of Terroir."CONS: You're basically placing tetris blocks in a square, making decisions on which blocks to place where and when -- and even that doesn't involve a lot of genuine decision-making, because the seasons determine when you are going to do things, so you're basically having to very occasionally make a prioritization decision when all your blocks won't fit, like "Do I weed this turn and prune next, or vice versa?"  Not super fun.  And once you get into free play, the gameplay gets very repetitive and it takes forever to accumulate any money and improve anything.  My fame was stuck at 10 -- no idea how to improve that, and the instant I upgraded my winery to level 2, I started losing money every turn and had to close my winery shortly afterwards.  So, for a game that is fundamentally about placing oddly shaped tiles in a rectangle, it sure gets grindy.Almost a thumbs up, but the core gameplay just didn't really engage me longer than a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall score: 7/10This niche game is about running a vineyard and creating and selling wines. You get to know all the ins and outs of winemaking, which is still a pretty much unexplored topic for games. The game clearly shows that the developers know a lot on winemaking and running a vineyard. Its unique artstyle and music and sound effects make playing this game a very tranquil experience. The game remains fresh for the first 10 hours or so, hereafter the game tends to become repetitive as you will have seen all if not most gameplay. Furthermore, you will have to set your own objectives as the game mostly runs as a sandbox game. Good and unique game for those very much into wine, winemaking and vineyard management. For most casual players, I would recommend waiting for a discount. Worth a buy for most players at  around 12 dollars/euros.Strong points:- Unique art style- Nice sound effects and music- Clear UI- Simple, but deep game mechanicsWeak points:- Very short story campaign (~2-3 hours)- No voice overs- Starts to become repetitive quickly- Game can become a bit of a chore once you run multiple vineyards- Game too expensive for what it offers for mostSuggested improvements:- More types of vineyards- More control over pricing of wines- Allow long term storage of bottled wines to benefit from aging

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, this game is right up my alley! The unfortunate thorn in my side for the upward momentum (late game post story, since I mostly played the story mode that switched to endless mode after losing) is the steep punishment in the form of non linear price that makes this game more of a time sink rather than an actual grind to making better wine. And speaking of the wine; other than going to an outside source to get some direction for which bar needs to be put where-it's be nice if more than vague text suggested the trial and error as a low quality wine could ruin the "zen" the player finds themselves in.Ultimately, there's just little tweaks I'd make to the main game that yes you ca find in endless mode (however I feel these options should also be available for story since that's the obvious play style this game was made for initially).The game's fine. It's relaxing, the music is soothing, the text bubble SXF is cute and when characters pop up it's not as jarring as you'd think in concept. I just feel like this game needed one more pass to be perfect and for me to give it the best chance. HOWEVER, if your still looking for a game that you can sink 6-8 hours into in a sitting (bc the learning curve for placing the isometric blocks isn't as steep as the price jump!) definately get this game (the dlc and free add-on in the grape lab are fun as well, making your own grape and having access to endless mode definately make the story mode more digestable; but in the end-I, personally, regret buying this gae )

_childDocuments_.review: Above all this game has that one more turn quality that keeps me clicking forward. The core mechanic is an interesting blend of a small scale puzzle game and one of resource management (turns and tiles). _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a game I wanted to love while following its development for over two years. Unfortunately, most reviews of this game are very fair. In summary, this game neglects the essence and passion of wine. Wine is not about what's inside a bottle. It's the story of how it got there, the people who laboured in making it, and how it came in to your life. It's the sharing of it over a meal with friends, it's the clinking of glasses at a wedding. It's about that one bottle you objectively now should hate, a wine from a time and place in your life when you didn't care or know it was cheap swill, you don't taste that now, but for a brief moment you experience those memories again and go back, if only for a little while.There is no depth to the game, there is no atmosphere. There is a teaser of character development and story, but blink and the cliche writing is gone in an instant and you're back to repeating the same dozen clicks each cycle. Occasionally you'll get a weather incident that may impact your grapes, or it might not. It doesn't matter, as you'll still do everything the exact same.There is no reward to the game, no sense of accomplishment. OK, I've figured out an arbitrary star system that tells me the exact formula my wines should follow, but so what? If I pull off an exceptional 99/100 vintage, there's nothing I can do with it. I just sell it for an extra $2 a bottle next year. I can't cellar it for a few years and pull out some bottles and sample them to see how my harvesting-crushing-fermenting-barrelling-bottling decisions have impacted the longevity of the wine. I think I could forgive these limitations, if only the game had a sense of atmosphere. The soundtrack, the one thing that should carry a game like this, feels like a repetition of the same free lackless soundscapes. One blends in to the souless next. They're not even attuned to the seasons. Just long drawn out orchestral melodies. This isn't a bad game, as a wine making simulator its even fun. I guess the reason I don't recommend the game is because it pretends to be something it's not. If the devs continue to build out the game and bring in an atmosphere that allow decisions to have outcomes, and passion to have purpose, I'll be keen to give it another shot.

_childDocuments_.review: UNDERRATED SOUND DESIGN!! In reality, I have 138 hours of experience in this game at the time of writing (used an alternate platform before buying on Steam to support Broken Arms).--=PROS=-- Difficulty: Hundred Days is on the "easier" side of sim games, especially if one has experience with more advanced sims than this (e.g. Cities: Skylines). After playing for some time, it's relaxing enough that I find myself returning to unwind, but engaging enough that I feel like I'm being lightly active with my mind and not just going numb. I also love the feeling that I can bust this game open again and it's really easy to pick it back up after being closed for months. More difficult games usually require getting re-oriented. I find Hundred Days to be quite meditative.Sound design: I really wish more people were talking about the sound design. There was CLEARLY so much effort put into the overall design of this game. The soft, warm colors. The INDUSTRY-SPECIFIC sound recordings!! When you place your stainless steel tank down on the board, you can hear a really pleasant, metallic CLANG! sound like someone just slapped the side of a large steel fermentor. You can hear the fresh, firm, juicy grapes bouncing off of each other like they are being poured out of a basket when they are harvested. The calm music and nature sounds that ebb and flow and match with the seasons!!! Playing with headphones is an absolute joy that a lot of modern games no longer bring me. Most games really overdo the dynamic volume range. Hundred Days just wants you to relax and enjoy the romanticized aspects of winemaking. I've had this game for over two years. It's so rare for me to find a game that I've binged on at one point, but still continue to periodically open it up just to see what's up. Last pro: YOU. CAN. NAME. THE. DUCKIES. --=CONS=-- Quality-of-life: Anyone who has zero knowledge about the science behind winemaking might get frustrated with the lack of explanation, specific to in-game, of why certain flaws happen. One might look up "Mercaptan" and think that timing the fertilizers/plant treatments in the game are causing wine faults. (After playing a lot, I don't think there is an effect). Myself, being a huge science nerd, found this to be a pleasurable excuse to go on excel-sheet binges to gather the RNG stats, and viticulture wikipedia page reading. I also had fun sifting through the forums to find more information about how the game works. And yes, the U.I. gets a little difficult to navigate at times. I often forget where I have to click to find a certain thing. Those who want the game to explain all of these details may feel put off by lack of explanations. I encourage players to ask questions on the Discord or forums. Fellow players are always happy to answer questions specific to Hundred Days.

_childDocuments_.review: Hundred Days is a simplistic management game about viticulture (cultivating grapevines) and all the steps necessary to succeed in it. Now I'm not an expert in viticulture and this game was the first time I was confronted with the topic, but like many of those kind of simulation games, the real process is dumbed-down for simplicity and enjoyability sake. It might look daunting at first, but the actual process is quite simple: Reduce / Increase the values of your grapes/wine by placing pieces on the board until you hit the correct value. Only very few things will have unexpected effects on your values, for example delayed harvest due to rain leads to lower acidity in your grapes, and therefor the results are fairly predictable. The entire gameplay loop can be learned in 15 - 30 minutes and only very minor things will change when unlocking later technologies.Hundred Days is a game for the ones who are interested in a simplistic representation of viticulture and expect a more relaxing gameplay rather than a challenging one. It might also get you interested in viticulture if it was the case with me, give that I wasn't interested in the topic at all before playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:I changed this review to negative because of the stupid unrealistic financial troubles in this game.I went bankrupt because I had an outstanding loan I had almost paid off and had no option to loan again. If I had a couple of thousand euros, I could have payed off the loan and take another bigger loan. I was only 70 euros short and went bankrupt.The second game, I was doing great, I had over 600+k money, no loans, and I thought, let's spend, I have a great income. But then I got a bit of bad luck and the 40k I had went down to -3k. The figures showed I was going to have 20k the next turn thanks to my income, but the game declared me bankrupt.Instead, I should have been offered a loan, or even better, it should have ignored it because it knew I was going to be back on track the next turn. A perfectly relaxing great going game ruined by spending money one turn too early...Old review:Yes, I recommend this game (played more hours offline than online on this one). It is a lot more fun than I initially expected!Although in real life, drinking wine gives me some kind of allergic reaction, it is fun to make it nevertheless. I hope a similar game will be made for whisky, because that's more my thing, but this is fun too.The game is not perfect however. There are some small bugs and frustration that are not game breaking (although sometimes you need to restart the game). This is mostly user interface handling with a controller (I play it on the Steam Deck) where selections might go outside of the screen instead of the scrollbar making sure it stays visible, and cards no longer working after canceling them because you remembered you first wanted to do something else (like look up information) and then click the card, and also sometimes needing to click lots of times before you reach the button you want (sometimes they are actually unreachable) while that could definitely work better if they worked out both ui-controllers better.Those things do ruin the immersion a bit and usually make me stop playing instead of restarting. I hope these bugs and quality of life things get fixed. The developer is responsive, but I don't get the feeling that a lot of changes will be made in the future. I hope I'm wrong.I certainly like how they represented time management in this game, by using a board where you place these tetris pieces. It seems weird at first, but it is actually quite a good system. Yes, you would like to weed that piece of land but you would also like to organize that tasting for your new wine because you really want to know the score and sell it. You can't do both because you are already harvesting those grapes on that other piece of land. But just like in real life, taking time to organize the pieces may save you some extra time while just doing stuff without thinking will make your time management bad.The graphics are nice, but you can see that for yourself in the screenshots.The music is nice too, it is never too active and usually you don't even notice when it starts or stops which is a good thing. Nicely done! Music is so important in games.So, a surprisingly big yes for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly strange game, combining management, tetris, education and grapes. I think it's excellent. You are the owner of a small vineyard slowly settling into the wine industry and expanding your commercial and technical abilities.What is striking is the amount of operational info that the game makes available about your grapes at every step, which gives away that this is an oenologists passion project, but the finesse of this system is that the info is totally optional to read and doesn't slow you down. Of course there is pride in tinkering your vines to stretch for the perfect vintage, but also the satisfaction of a well-run commercial arm that grows year after year. The latter does become more overbearing as you plunge deeper into the late game, and I found my vines became more like conveyor belts and the overall fun of the experience was a little dimmed. After I read the Vice article on this game I don't think this is really a criticism, as it ties in with the story: a small-town tale which pits the bucolic vineyards against Big Business.  Inadvertently I think this achieves the gaming holy grail of marrying mechanics to story, show don't tell - to grow your business efficiently you can very easily optimise the soul out of the winemaking. This is probably accidental, but all the same this is a fun game which managed to teach me something about grapes.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing whatever I could in Brewmaster (another great game on Steam), I needed something to scratch my alcohol brewing itch... I clearly found it in Hundred Days. Now this game differs from Brewmaster in that it doesn't "simulate" brewing together ingredients together in your home kitchen, instead it simulates the industrial operational decisions behind shipping your drink to thousands/millions of customers. Ie it's more turn-based strategy (with boardgame roots) than Brewmaster, and there's different decisions going on here than if you were only brewing for your 40 friends across the street. I've also only played the Piedmont mode in Hundred Days, not the Napa Valley or other Hundred Day modes, so my review below will be focused on Piedmont.The Good:- This game helps you gain an appreciation for the work that goes into making wines: pressing, fermenting, aging, crop thinning, treatments, sweetness, acidity, tannen, etc.- Game is challenging without being frustrating, and in specifics, there's room to go under if you choose poorly, but there's PLENTY of room to stay in business w decent profit & affording upgrades, even if your wine quality is a poor 52%.- Game has nice familiar similarities to various wine-making boardgames and other video games (ie Tetris) without feeling like it was outright copy-catting them.- Story mode gives you a nice sense of the atmosphere of a European vineyard, and escaping corporate life, but without fooling you into thinking running a vineyard is a holiday (there's stresses in running vineyards and competing in the wine industry, a lot of which the game correctly portrays).- You get a "good sense" of the cycles of cranking out Barbera and/or Chardonnary on a basic level in story mode before moving onwards to more advanced techniques and other wines.- There's a nice satisfaction feeling that first time I made a 100% quality wine (Barbera in my case) and the moments leading up to it, slowly unlocking upgrades, and seeing in tastings WHY you want those upgrades. This really helped make that feeling of reaching 100% all so satisfying.- Game is addictive once you're into the loop of revenue-generating towards planting new/better wines or technology upgrades towards more revenue.- Game does good job of encouraging you towards making both red and white wine types, with red typically being higher quality & better at meeting special orders, while white is higher volume & better at meeting regular orders for the masses.- CONTROVERSIAL COMMENT: I like the fact that the game simplifies the real-life fluctations in sweetness, body, acidity, tannen of wines to simple turn-based choices with basic math. This is a game for entertainment value, so keeping more complex details of real life vineyards out of the game helps to introduce folks unfamiliar w winemaking (such as myself) into the genre without feeling frustrating... even if in real life, you CAN increase the acidity of your wine after harvesting.The Bad:- This might be a bug, but after I hired employees, some of the cards I put on the board "didn't stick", resulting in some events not progressing. I found a workaround to this was to SAVE then LOAD and re-stick those problematic cards, but I shouldn't have needed to burn time on this.- If your vineyards have bad soil (ie poor acidity, altitude, sand, clay, or loam), you might only realize this hours in, and you can NEVER achieve over 81 on quality for certain grape types, and there is NOTHING you can do about it except restarting your entire game!!! Since there's Steam achievements centered around specific grape types, this makes it even more frustrating... Note that in real life there are ways to alter soil for grape compatibility at the cost of time & money, would've been nice to have the game mimic that too.- Grape Lab for custom-grapes should be integrated into game better. There needs to be tutorial and/or encouragement (via Steam achievement) to import Grape Lab grapes into your game and make a wine bottle of 100% quality of that type. Maybe even intentionally make 1 field in the game incompatible w base grape types (and too expensive/time-consuming to alter its soil), so players are forced to import a custom grape type?- There aren't Steam achievements for getting 85+ quality for all the base grape types??? I got 90+ quality for Erbulace and a perfect 100 for Grignolino. Even if these are easy things for players to get, I still wanna "feel rewarded" for getting 85+ on these!- Too easy to make poor decisions Early-game. I had to redo my game several times. Took me forever to figure out that I shouldn't be quick to upgrade just because I can afford it, and to focus my early upgrades MORE on the barrel aging, and LESS on marketing, etc. A lot of this can be alleviated by the tutorial guiding you towards recommending specific choices over others.- The per-turn costs need to be made more obvious in the tutorials. Each time you upgrade your buildings (ie Winery, Tool Shed, or Warehouse), the per-turn cost goes up, and for whatever reason, this wasn't obvious to me or others. Making it obvious will better help players determine the correct time to make these upgrades, they're useful, but players gotta know when yearly revenue can support it (including covering months your wine stock ran out temporarily).- Not being able to afford the cost of bottling feels like a "hidden gotcha" in the game, especially because it's your main source of revenue in the game. I've played the game enough to make sure I got enough reserve cash for it, but it REALLY isn't obvious to newbies. I recommend, on planting or harvesting, providing an estimate on the cost of bottling so players can adjust their spending to afford bottling (also provide bottling estimates when a player is considering a loan!!!).- Technology unlocks are uneven to field unlocks, ESPECIALLY for grape types. Mid-game, my new fields weren't compatible with unlocked grape types, forcing me to shove Barbera and Chardonnay everywhere until near endgame, when I finally had compatible grape-types to fields and could convert over.- Warehouse upgrades don't prove as useful as Winery or Tool Shed ones for early or mid-game. This can be alleviated by lowering the costs of Warehouse technologies & having the tutorial walk you thru some of them (like merchandising).- Some upgrade benefits aren't obvious, like auto-managing regular merchant decisions or hiring employees. Adding coverage of these in the tutorial can alleviate this issue.- Game story "ends too soon". I was 20 hours in when it ended, but my revenue-generating "gameplay" & unlocking all fields & wines and trying for 85+ quality on most grape types took me another 35 hours. Would be better to have the story instead stretch 50-60 hours to cover this "typical" game playthrough.- There's no reason to EVER focus on high quantity when planting seeds, as red wines won't profit if quality suffers, and even white wines "for the masses" on low quantity will profit you more than if you put them on high quantity. This feels like a poorly implemented quality/quantity feature.- I was hoping for more uses on flavorings in the wines (cherry, peach, black pepper, etc). If they can improve drink quality for certain wine types, this needs to be made more obvious.- Missing wine variants, like pink wines (combines a red wine with a white), sparkling wines (note champaign is a type of sparkling wine), sherries, etc

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game! It combines simulation, science about wine making and puzzling nicely. It is a fun challenge finding out how to make a particular wine well. It is also a good idea to make tasks, organizing etc. a little puzzling with the Tetris style task board. The player can choose in what area they like upgrades too, which i find convenient. The game looks nice with its art work and the whole experience including soft and charming music is feeling good and comfortable.pros:- nice feel good game- learning science of wine making by accident. I want to talk about wine with my one vintner friend now- lots of fun. I already mastered 3 wines and i want to find out how the others workcons:- the games performance is low. It should be possible to optimize much more here. Frame rate can drop and stuttering may appear here and there. I am playing this on my gaming PC because my laptop is too slow for some reason.- UI design def. needs improvement- game design leaves many questions unanswered. I usually save the game, buy a tech advancement, see that it works differently than i expected, reload my save and pay attention so something else.- story mode is a little too much like a Telenovela, but not annoying- financially too easyThe game reminds me of the DOS game Winzer from 1991 or so.Thank you for stealing my last couple of days and probably many more.

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend! Plus having to select the tannin level, sweetness level, body etc based on the soil/clay, season, weather conditions is insanely accurate and as a huge wine nerd this game combines both my passions! -Someone who works in the wine industry!
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Hundred Days is a fun, relaxing game and I don't have many gripes personally. The game isn't very complicated once you learn what you're doing and can be a bit repetitive at times, but it is fun (in my opinion) to see the outcomes of each vintage; the potential flaws, flavors, and so forth, and to live the fantasy of owning a vineyard!I have not played the campaign much, and have instead mostly played Endless Mode which I have enjoyed greatly! In Endless Mode you can modify your starting conditions such as decreasing price of tech, increasing starting cash and so forth. This will disable achievements if that is something you are concerned about/wish to get. My main complaint is that I wish there was an explanation of some kind for why wine defects, such as cork taint or reduction which decrease the wines rating once bottled and tasted, occurred. They already have a Journal that details the grape types and the levels of tannin, body, and other components you have tried in creating your perfect wine, so I don't know why they don't just add a portion about maybe explains discovered defects (Didn't clean your aging barrel? You get a Reduction etc).Otherwise, no complaints! Its a fun, relaxing game where I can pretend to be an (eventual!) wealthy vineyard owner in either Piedmont (base game) or Napa (DLC which I also recommend!). I look forward to what comes next with this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed it, a relatively straight forward game you pop in and there's your puzzle aspect with tile placement, your strategy layer with balancing the levels in the wine you make, your progression is through the story, tech, and equipment, and lastly you get the economy sim through all the wine selling/contracts and balancing that with your investments. There's not really anything else to it, but those features are all deep and interesting and just finicky enough for me to be really interested in getting them juuuuuuuuust right. I would recommend it for a cozy kind of production game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: awesome graphics, mechanics, story; worth the price. I whole-heartedly recommend!I usually do not play games with any puzzle-like mechanics but this game got this mechanic perfectly balanced. Sometimes you are just not able to fit all the pieces at the board, so you need to strategize a bit; and it makes perfect sense - there is only certain amount of things you can do in one day. The game is mimicking wine-making so incredibly well, that based on it I started to understand  and notice differences in wine in real life. It is very chill game, but still very interesting, entertaining, awesome graphics, awesome mechanics, totally worth the price and it has an educational value, too. I definitely recommend!

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: A solid wine-making game and one of the better strategy games on steam in general.If you have interest in wine-making and like puzzles / strategy, this is a must-buy.There are bugs, and there is late-game performance lag. The UI doesn't scale well for a fully-kitted vineyard operation, and I'd love to see more options for even further expansion of my premises and operations. None of the technologies for the warehouse are clear in what they actually do except for the tasting room and guided tours - the developer really needs to re-write descriptions or provide some in-game data showing marketing impact on sales. Endless mode doesn't quite have enough randomisation options for replayability to be maximised (I would like to see the option to randomise optimal values for each wine type, or perhaps even rename them to make random fictional wine types).However, the upsides outweigh these downsides for me. I played the demo for about 8 hours before release, seeing how much profit I could make and which technologies I could unlock and experiment with in that short timeframe. Since buying the game I've enjoyed an increasing difficulty curve and found it to be fulfilling to be successful. I would say that there's no real mid-to-late-game challenge, but this is where time limits come in for games like these, and the challenge scenarios do indeed rely on time limits. I'd love if the developer found a different way to present difficult challenges in the game in the future so we could have more varied scenarios - but I'll have to beat the existing scenarios first!
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Immersed in a neat and beautiful minimalist graphics, accompanied by nice soundtracks and full of wine culture to be discovered in the dialogues and playing, it turns out to be excellent and harmonious in the gameplay,  history and mechanics.Very current and original in many facets, such as the characters and their characteristics.A complete and well done tutorial and levels of customization also for type of bottle, label, name of wine and much more.Great Job!
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: If you like to play a very enjoying and relaxing game then this should be high on your list. The graphics, concept, and atmosphere make this something that stands out from other simulators that you usually see on the Steam store. When I first joined it was a struggle since I had no clue how to make any sort of Wine. But as it went on the game was able to hand you the right tools and make you use it later on for yourself in order to help you make the perfect wine. You can be completely new to wine and you'll still do good, the game is very simple and easy too. I would recommend this to anyone who needs some time off from stress in real life.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Hundred Days is a love letter to wine making. I think the charm of Hundred Days is that it unapologetic about its desire to bring the complexity of wine making in to a tile placement and planning game with a lovely art style. Hundred Days is not a thousand hour game I'm going to lose weeks to, but rather it is wonderful title that I continually think about since playing it. As someone that loves wine and has been a AAA game developer for nearly a decade, they made a game about a challenging industry where a lot of newcomers fail while working in a challenging industry where a lot of newcomers fail. Truly wonderful to see this kind of thing exist, and I'm so very happy to have played it. It certainly isn't a game for everyone, and that's okay. Kudos to the team - this is a favorite of mine in my library.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, it's polished, and has a lot of heart. It's also a nice mix that will satisfy both casual and sim-genre buffs. One thing to note is that to make money in this game you really need to look up how to formulate the best flavor pallets to achieve the high scores per wine. Easy enough when you get the formula down. But "winging it" on a first playthrough wont net you any high wine scores. I know the design was eased around this fact as money would be lacking in early game. You are granted some freebies for grape storage and other things when you're just maxed out and can't afford upgrades. This is why I say the game has a lot of heart, they went through the lengths to remove any pain points for new players.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my goodness this game was a blast! I was not expecting to fall in love and get emotionally invested in a wine making game but I am so glad it happened! Not only is the gameplay very engaging and satisfying, whether it's the puzzles or the wine making process, but the story is engaging and pulls you further into the world! If you're looking for a game with amazing art, entertaining gameplay, and an immersive story: This is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Hundred Days is a great example of a good turn-based management game. Within this game, you can play as the owner of a vineyard, making the best wines you can. The game forces you to manage your time and resources to the best of your abilities, requiring you to manage your vineyard to the best of your ability by only allowing so many actions at a time. This game does have some issues, like how it can become repetitive at certain points if you aren't careful and the campaign is more like a story within a game. These issues, however, are very minor in the grand scale of the game, I didn't experience any bugs or any glitches in the system. This game is very underappreciated for those who like turn-based management and want to understand the true world of winemaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: At first, it may sounds difficult to get all the different aspects on the wine making process. _childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics keep a good balance between gaming playability and realistic simulation, and more of that's coming in upcoming updates.Visually beautifulVery nice storytelling in story mode (especially for this genre!)Very replayable as different terroirs force you to keep changing tactics in different playthroughs
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: As an amateur winemaker, I was interested in a good winemaker simulation.  This game is it.  I love the variety of grapes, yeasts, and equipment options.  Upgrading the winery options over time, the good and bad years, weather, the ever-present possibility of pests and/or diseases and how to combat them, all make this game feel very authentic.  A beautiful soundtrack rounds it all out nicely.  The story line is over fairly quickly, and acts as a helpful tutorial to get your winery up and running.  Looking forward to the Napa DLC being completed, and hopefully the addition of a blending of grapes option in future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played a few hours of this so far and I have been having a great time! I work in the wine industry and really love the attention to detail this game has. _childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: It had some problems upon its first release....many due to lack of implementation pedagogical techniques. And it influenced me to try an Arneis.Nonetheless I am disappointed that when I switched computers, unlike the majority games on Steam, this one did not download a cloud save to my new machine. i.e. I have to start the game over.
_childDocuments_.name: Hundred Days - Winemaking Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike a lot of reviewers I am not in the wine industry in a traditional sense. I had the pleasure of working in the restaurant industry at a location that valued wine knowledge and passion. After learning about wine and all that goes into it, I also became passionate as a casual consumer, almost as a light hobby. I want to add this disclaimer because while my knowledge is lightly helpful in the game as far as understanding some of the logistics but I am not a professional, that being said here are my thoughts:This is such a fun game. I didn't think I would be so determined to master wine! All 9.6 hours have been in the last two nights! I was a little put off at first (first couple hours) because the story was fine, but I kept getting interrupted! I just wanted to play around with my vineyard and get to it! However, the writing was ok and the story wrapped up for the most part so I was able to play MANY years uninterrupted and just experiment. Personally I liked playing with trial and error. I am sure you are able to look up information that will allow you to master the wines much more quickly but I have enjoyed just messing around and seeing what I can do on my own. At first it seems like you will NEVER have enough money for all the cool things you can unlock but I'm only 9 hours in and sitting at about 2 mil. Which only happened because I was so in the zone making and selling wine I hadn't even noticed the money!I am looking forward to many hours of this game because even after unlocking all the land and upgrades I believe I will enjoy chasing after that perfect bottle and customizing the bottles and labels more than I have at this point,If you enjoy wine or simulator games I would get it. _childDocuments_.review: I want to get the negatives out of the way first.Story mode: kinda sucks, don't buy this game for the story. I'm sure there's a lot of cultural stuff going over my head, since I know the devs are based in Italy, but it doesn't work for most americans, I suspect.UI: some parts are pretty obtuse, and there is a lot missing in regards to employees in particular. The devs have been slowly making UI updates over the past few months, so I expect this to get better.Balance: wine quality seems to have less effect on the rating of the wine than it should. While this is actually mimicking reality, funnily enough, I think the game could tighten up the ratings spread but make it more difficult to get very high ratings.Now, I want to be transparent here. I am a fan of this game. In fact, this is the first game I've written a guide for and actually tried to be an active member of the community for, beyond playing the game. As someone who hasn't really been interested in wine, this game opened my eyes and really showed off the process and various steps of making wine. While it is quite simplified, the basics are all there and well represented.I also appreciate the fact that the devs are almost constantly active on the community discord. They've been doing an update a week pretty consistently, adding in new content as well as plenty of bugfixes and quality of life changes.Now, I know the devs read these reviews, so I have one request: Don't be like Paradox Games. In one of their community posts, they talk about several DLCs coming in the future, including 2 new regions (Bordeaux and Napa Valley.) Great, love new content. In the Bordeaux blurb, they talk about blending grapes and Cru wines. Now, if you want certain regions to have exclusive grape varietals, fine, that makes sense. But please do not lock features like this behind the DLC. At minimum, give us the ability to blend grapes anywhere.Other than that, I think the game is great. It's a first time dev team that's trying their best to create a quality game, and I think they've done very well. As long as the game keeps getting new features and fixes, they have a bright future ahead of them.
