_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the best games I've ever played. Easily top 3. The writing is hilarious, with just the right mix of humor and seriousness that you'll be left wanting more. I bought the edition with developer commentary, and finished the entire game before I realized I hadn't enabled them (oops!). Fortunately, there are some spoilers in there, so I went back and played it again. I finished it a second time and I'm still hoping for a DLC to get more story, with either the same characters or new ones. I feel like it's easy with games like this to have just one solution, or require specific choices to succeed. I tried taking different perks the second time around and didn't run into any issues. You'll definitely have to do some thinking, but nothing is impossible.I can't recommend this enough; it's my gift of the year to anyone who plays games. If they haven't already bought it considering how much I've raved about it
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Alas, Steam only allows me to give a single thumbs up to this game. I would give it a few more if I could.As usual with Suspicious Developments, the dialogues are amazing, down to every single line. The magic elements of the setting blend seamlessly into this very modern world. Each character is a different type of wizard and has a gripping personal story, related to how they unlocked their powers, and what they chose (or were forced) to do with them.The gameplay is extremely satisfying, the different powers and abilities create fascinating combos and interact in many ways with the environment. The progression system allows you to constantly unlock new interesting tactical options, as there are very little boring "+1 damage" perks. Most of them let you do something new, which gradually increases the game's complexity in a very organic way. And yet the levels are so smartly crafted that they remain doable no matter which perks you picked. (though your choices will of course impact the difficulty)Finally, even if you have a hard time with tactics games, this one has very customisable difficulty settings, including allowing you to double your actions each turn, which really trivializes the levels, so you can enjoy the great story without getting frustrated or stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great story with well written dialog and characters.  Interesting tactical gameplay, but in a far more casual way than XCOM.  More like a puzzle game where you get multiple chances to figure out the best way to do things.If you like tactics games and enjoy a well written story, this is worth playing.  Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: First the negative (mostly nitpicks but they were consistently on my mind): TBW Is a great tactical puzzle game wearing the skin of a strategy game, and I do feel like that can be misleading to some. The character abilities feel really personal and unique to them and are directly connected to who they are as people which takes a skilled hand, except . I really love the character, but the person we speak to out-of-mission and the person we control in-op feel disconnected. It's also likely that this person's first string of missions are the only ones where you don't "breach" contributed to this off feeling. Finally, the game's narrative is pretty short, which is great for pacing and level quality, but it does also mean that it is immensely dissatisfying when you miss a level up by 3 xp since you only have 10 or so opportunities to level. Finally, the tutorial was irritatingly hands-on but that was only 5 minutes of 15 hours.On a more neutral/positive note, the dialogue writing is very Millennial-Reddit, which isn't necessarily bad, but it is pretty consistent. The characters have pretty pull-your-heartstrings backstories that I found lackluster on paper, but the set dressing made up for it by a mile. Characters are basically going through a divorce, or finding their place in the world, or political activism, and it's not really anything you haven't heard before. But the way the setting puts a spin on things keeps it fun and lighthearted. It's like they wanted heavy topics but didn't want it to be "triggering" so they left it surface level, like in an action movie or something. This could have come across really tasteless, offensive, and stupid but it was genuinely really fun. It left me hoping to see more from this world without feeling underwhelmed at the end. Another neutral point that I can't fit in anywhere else is that the world map and history is just a loosely scrambled map of the middle east, with Turkey, Syria, and Libya on the left and a strange Iran(?) allegory on the right. It's not bad it's just something I noticed right away and was honestly a little underutilized imo. With all that said, I really enjoyed how each character was able to interact with the others in-level and how that reflected their relationships out of mission. Most of the characters feel relatively weak on their own, but they're able to pair off and clear forces 3-4 times their size because they compliment so well, and that feels great to pull off as a player. The last mission exemplifies this perfectly. The game also felt really responsive and there were no moves that took a radically long amount of time, which would have sucked to undo. The challenges were a brilliant way to reward the player (with cool and funny skins) and a great way to hint extra special/easy/fun ways to go about your missions. It felt like the developers really wanted the player to have fun and if the player did have fun, they'd be rewarded; something lacking in a lot of games honestly. The developers really did an awesome job with this game and I 100% recommend it to anyone who likes using their brain. I'd love to see a DLC or a sequel but I also feel it's far from necessary if they want to leave this as the complete package. Congrats on the successful launch and the Overwhelmingly Positive reviews, it was well earned!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: 29 Hours for 15 Quid - 100% completion on hardsome allowance for main menu AFK but all in all good time/money valueCharacters feel genuine, managed to get a good laugh out of me whilst still telling an interesting story with a few tasty twists.Simple gameplay, but satisfying when it all comes together, definitely worth a go!You will know if the story/dialogue and gameplay works for you within the first two hours - buy it - play it and if you're not feeling it after 90 mins get your steam refund, but my money's on you having a good time
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Love how unique the concept is and it plays ~so~ well into the game's unique humour - a perfect example of dry British humour. The sandbox-style gameplay is super satisfying and it has an unexpectedly enthralling storyline?? The visuals are great and music very well suited.Thoroughly enjoying it! Great game for those who aren't used to this style of gameplay, the difficulty scale is just right and the game brings in new mechanics to keep it fresh without throwing too much at the player all at once! The game seems to be perfectly set up for extensibility too, so I hope to see future content drops! It already has a level editor which is pretty awesome for replayability anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tom Francis has done it again! This is one of the best strategy/puzzle games I've ever played, with Tom's signature entertaining writing. I finished the story in 20 hours flat, but will be circling back to complete side-objectives and achievements.The gameplay is super diverse and keeps things interesting with all kinds of unique scenarios. I never found a level boring or too similar to one I played before. Some levels are just pure fun, while others require thinking hard about how to accomplish the goal, and the game strikes a good balance between the two. For those who want a challenge, the optional objectives in almost every level add an extra layer (or multiple) to the puzzles, without making them feel impossible. The mechanics are also super forgiving in that you can rewind all the way to the start of your turn, no matter how much you've messed up. This encourages experimentation and risky plays in a way that many strategy games don't.The story is great, and the dialogue even better. Lots of silly humor, as is to be expected of a Tom Francis game. I genuinely laughed out loud on several occasions throughout my play-through when reading the banter between characters, which (for me) says a lot. I love Jen so much. The story was split up into nice digestible chunks and it had some cool twists. I especially liked making connections on a board with thumbtacks and red string. All in all, there was much more to it than I was expecting of an indie game. 20 hours to beat is a lot of content and absolutely justifies the price tag.Art style and UI are great as well. Love all the different environments we get to play through.If you've read this far, just get the game already, or at least try the demo. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I only played it for a bit, and I enjoyed it. Loved the optional challenge rooms and optional "confidence" challenges. Big fan of how heavily the developer encourages experimentation, so much so you're basically not punished for it like in most games. Big fan of Tom Francis' work and his design philosophy when it comes to stuff like that.However I just wasn't in the mood for this kind of game at the moment, but will pick it up again down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like a dream on the deck, despite not quite being fully verified.Personally I prefer using the trackpad and playing it mouse style, but for those wondering don't worry, it's the perfect deck game.Imagine a mix between Into The Breach and Hot Fuzz and you're half way there!Another total gem from Francis
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Surprising little gem for such a quick development cycle! :DI've only played a little, but I'm already a fan.  Good variety of abilities and fun combos. The story is not dumped on you all at once with a lot of exposition or "cinematic" cut scenes, but dribbled out in a constant burbling stream. The writing is also fun.Cons: not much so far.  I did find the controller scheme to be somewhat confusing / unoptimized.  But using the mouse and keyboard on PC should be considered sufficient!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I instantly fell in love with this game when I played the demo a couple months ago when it dropped. Just the name had me smiling, thinking Harry Potter meets SWAT or Ready or Not.... That's not what I got.Instead I got a hilariously written, extremely charming Puzzle/Strategy game with some of the best characters I've met in awhile. And the game continued to defy expectations, because while goofy, the writers really managed to pull on some heartstrings. How the hell was my heart pounding in a turn-based game even during a bossfight?While short, TBW is a very solid game, and will have me coming back doing my best to 100% it for awhile yet. P.S.: I really appreciated that they didn't 100% hold your hand for some of these levels, they tell you "Hey, do this thing" and give you hints (if requested) on how to complete the objective. Made me feel smart.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Another wonderful entry in the studio's library of tactical defenestration games, and easily their best to date. The encounters get mixed up in a lot of ways for enemies, objectives, and even team composition, so you can't just slip into a dominant strategy to breeze through the whole thing. The story has some fun intrigue to it, and the dialog writing is hilarious, so I was often just as eager to hear some more team banter as I was to find the next plot twist. Also there's a cute cat so 10/10 for that alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what a game should be. It's polished, witty, enjoyable, and engaging. The gameplay is tight and fearless (it's not afraid of complicating itself with a host of abilities and several characters), and the storytelling elements are so well integrated that I hope and expect to see its methods in everything from indie to AAA titles. There are some really innovative things in here. All of that pales next to the feeling of chemistry between the characters. They're memorable, with their own personalities and real emotional stakes. They interact with each other and the excellent story in a way that's over the top in the best way. I finished this game feeling like real passion went into it.This game really deserves its "Overwhelmingly Positive" rating. It's great. Just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is an indie puzzle game for people who liked save-scumming XCom.It's got great writing, excellent mechanics, and just the right balance of seriousness and siliness. I'm not usually one to be bothered by reading text versus voice acting, and as a small team indie game I'm not really bothered by it here, but for the first time in any text-based game I've ever played I do wish that there was voice acting to match the quality of the writing. The characters are just so excellent that I'd like them to be brought further to life.It's a really fun game that was clearly made with a lot of love.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. It took me about 16 hours to complete the main storyline, and a few more to complete most of the optional goals.Gameplay wise: It feels very good to be able to rewind whenever your strategy doesn't work out. There is also no randomness to attacks hitting, so no situations where a great strategy is screwed up by RNG. It doesn't start off too challenging, but can get very challenging in the later chapters.Story wise: Dialogue between characters definitely includes a lot of humor. The plot isn't so complicated you need notes, but it does have a surprising amount of depth to it, and characters grow and change throughout the plot.Aesthetics wise: Tactical Breach Wizards has a unique art style and a great soundtrack. You can also change character's appearance by completing optional challenges in the course of normal gameplay.There are a few issues with the game as it currently stands - foremost among them is that you can only have one save file and some missions are not replayable (as well as most dialogue). I also think that the difficulty scaling is also slightly too fast if you don't want to do the optional side tasks. Other than that it's a great game.TLDR: If you like strategy, puzzles, witty dialogue, good writing, and/or throwing people out of windows, you'll enjoy this game. At least try the demo.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the Game of the Year for me, and one of the finest turn-based tactics games I've ever played. The Rewind and Foresee buttons shift this into puzzle game territory, filled with constant experimentation and optimisation. The design of the characters, abilities and levels are some of the smartest and most cleanly-executed I've seen in a long time, a toybox to combine in different ways without ever becoming overwhelming. The world-building and characters are compelling, and the writing is razor-sharp. Wholeheartedly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is shockingly good. The turn-based with "perfect information" trend is very popular these days, but this is by far the most intuitive and fun implementation of the mechanic. It is somehow both extremely forgiving and incredibly rewarding. The rewind mechanic lets you trial and error various strategies and rewind with zero penalty if your plan isn't going to work out. Then when you (sometimes accidentally) land on the perfect move and yeet everyone out a window with one well-placed grenade, you feel like a genius. Also the writing is great and genuinely funny. Tom Francis is a legend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game, one of my favorites.  The write is amazing, the I love the art style, core gameplay loop is engaging and fun.  Easily one of the best games I've ever played.  If you lose tactical, turn-based combat like Into the Breach or Fights In Tight Spaces absolutely give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for fans of a 'Tactical' turn-based nature, although I'd say if you're looking for a game similar to XCOM style tactics this is more like a puzzle game but with wizards and guns. That being said, I still had a lot of fun with it, easily got my moneys worth capping at about 20 hours to finish the campaign with a few 'side quests'. Really the game kept me playing through its writing which was surprisingly really good considering there was no VA. The dialogues were short enough to convey emotion and story, whilst simultaneously being funny and dramatic when they needed to be.If you wanna throw some enemies out of windows in a turn based format using Naval Wizards, definitely give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: More often than not when I play video games I skip dialogue. Not here though, I've never been more engaged in the conversations between characters than in this game, the characters feel so real and natural. The game play loop is amazing, the turn-based combat mechanics remind me of DND somewhat and it makes me appreciate the value that each potential action a character can take is. I can spend 50 minutes min-maxing that one turn to perfection and the feeling of completing all the optional objectives with the utmost efficiency is exhilarating. I wish they would make a DLC, I definitely want more banter between the cast.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: the story and world building are quite good and make the game more fun to play. you get invested in the characters, which motivates you to clear the missions. the gameplay is top-notch and reminds me of into the breach: a game where perfect information transforms a "tactics" style game into a hybrid puzzler. there's a nice balance between finding the "perfect" turn and allowing for different strategies
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Years ago I played a game called Gunpoint and had such a great time with it that from that point on I would have played anything that Tom Francis had his name on. However even if I hadn't picked up Gunpoint all those years ago then a picture of the chick with the suppressor and laser module on her magic wand would have gotten me onto this pretty quickly. You put an old guy with a wizard hat in operator ballistic glasses and give him a wizard staff in an AR15 upper and I'll be there. If you're not immediately taken by that extremely specific thing the actual game is compelling as well. This is an ambitious game for a small team but at heart it carries the same puzzle DNA that made Gunpoint such a blast. Using the aesthetics of turn based tactical gameplay to structure puzzles works very well, and as the scenarios become more complicated and the array of tools you have available increases, there's a fantastic sense of accomplishment in finding clean solutions. There's some great 'aha!' moments, but also a lot of flexibility in how you tackle each mission, especially depending on how you build out your characters.This is a fully featured campaign with a good cast of characters, a great main nemesis, and a fascinating setting that is sketched in very effectively. It's maybe a little clumsy in places but never in a way that brought the whole experience down. Moreover it has a great sense of whimsy in what is otherwise a pretty conventional looking military setting (within the bounds of the art style and premise). It's playful but still wears desert MARPAT. Not exactly a perfect fit for the Bad Company 2 shaped hole in your heart, but it's a rare type.If you enjoyed Gunpoint or Heat Signature then I probably don't need to tell you to give this a try, you'll already be there. But if you're on the fence about this, give it a go. Or give Gunpoint a go and ease yourself in. Reasonable chance you won't regret it.As an aside a game somewhere between this and Door Kickers 2 would go crazy.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Infinite Free Rewinds was such a good idea that I'm surprised that more tactics games don't use the same mechanic*. It not only lets you experiment and learn interactions, but also gives the devs room to add many more mechanics - a number which would overwhelm most players if they tried to map out an entire turn from the start to the end. It's no exaggeration to say that this one mechanic was the one missing piece which made me enjoy tactics games.Besides that, the rest of the gameplay is very fun and the writing is very funny. I recommend it.*I am relatively new to the genre so maybe there are plenty of games which use it - but I still think it's a great mechanic
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: After seeing this game several years back on a PC Gamer Showcase in 2022, I've been waiting patiently for this game. When I first bought it, I was as hyped as I was when I first saw it. By that point I had played through the demo 5 times. When I got to the first anxiety dream, my hype was dying down, so I stopped. Couple days later, I pick it up again, and now I can't stop playing. Once you get to act 3, the game is ADDICTING.----Dialogue? Phenomenal. Love the chemistry between all the characters. Story and backstory are carefully laid out through their words in a way that makes me wish I could make something as good. The witty remarks between them are so quotable.Story? Really good. Nothing more to say about the story as a whole without just recapping it. There are some really engaging twists throughout, and the settings and conflicts are really good.As I did have to return to the game after a period, an issue I have with other games is they either remind you of what just happened (annoying and belittling) or not tell you anything of the past (confusing), but the map feature in this game strikes the perfect balance. It's bulletin board style information is something I've wanted in the mystery genre for a while, but I really like its inclusion here.Gameplay? Also amazing. I've played few if any grid-based tactics games in my life, but this seems like a necessary game for fans of the genre. There is a barrier to entry if for some reason you can't understand the forsee phase, but anyone with half a brain or, if you're like me, 5 hours to play through it, will understand its intuitive nature. The abilities and especially the upgrades are so varied and interesting, allowing you to create mind-bending combos that you can plan far in advance. When you actually execute them, completing objectives with interesting combos make you feel amazing. Even when you complete levels on accident or you restart the level from the beginning 12 times do that for you.Visuals? incredible. The art style is unique, and the animation is buttery smooth.----Overall this was worth reminding myself about a year after I'd first seen in it, and then even more worth it as I waited for its release.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Loved how they didn't make industry standard mistakes:No "choices matter" (that only like a handful games get right).Dialog done in a way that if you missed an important part you get corrected on the drawing-board/map.Generally fast movement that gets slowed down if intercepted.No bugs when selecting another character while others are still walking.Fun story that I could not predict the mayor next steps of.Have not had a single crash.Only two downsides:Music loops too soon (would probably require double the soundtrack for it not to feel repetitive, or something that changes it each time its played within the same hour).The later levels have a lot of annoying opponents & features e.g. shield generators & gas-masks, they really don't add to the fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: You can't throw all your life's problems out a window...but it sure feels like they're all gone when playing Tactical Breach Wizards (TBW).I've completed TBW to 100% completion (all missions, dreams, survival challenges, and confidence goals on all levels). Rare is the game that captivates me to that extent. On the surface, TBW looks like a traditional tactics style game, where you're going to be weighing up the risks and rewards of potential moves. On the contrary, TBW is an *almost* completely open information game. You know exactly how your moves will play out, and exactly what the enemy will do (explained in universe as the ability of one of the wizards...you know, magic and stuff). What this does is replace the tension and emotional rollercoaster of games like Fire Emblem and XCOM with satisfying moments where you feel like an absolute genius. There's a freedom in TBW that I rarely see in games; sure, the levels are tight enough to the point where you have to think hard, but loose enough that you can approach problems in creative ways. This becomes especially true towards the late game, where your wizards have so many abilities that you've practiced over the course of the story that I'm certain there are near infinite ways to complete any given level. Oh, and the final level? That may be one of the most epic feeling boss fights I've played in years. It is the perfect capstone to an excellent 20-ish hour campaign.In a quirky little game about modern day wizards with guns and spells, one would be forgiven for expecting little out of the story. Yet TBW delivers the perfect kind of narrative; relatively simple plot, but interesting and memorable characters. It's the moments of interactions between all of the wizards, as well as the various villains, that make TBW an absolute delight. Sure, I have a few nitpicky criticisms. Not all of the wizard abilities are made equally, and some are much more interesting than others. It may just be personal taste, but many of the "deal damage" only abilities felt a bit lacklustre compared to the fun that could be had with all the various push, pulls, and other fun shenanigans. Outside of missions that demanded it for completion, for example, I don't think I ever used the bouncy ball (if you know what I'm talking about).In a similar way, some ability combos feel pretty broken, to the point of trivialising some of the levels. I was able to easily complete many of the final levels in a single round, and finding the lines of play that allowed that became easier as my knowledge of the wizards became deeper. It was an awesome feeling seeing how much I'd learned over the campaign, but at a certain point, it felt as though the difficulty plateaued. If there was one wish I had, it would be for the ability to switch off certain perks, just to try and challenge myself further. I would love to see if I could finish some of the later levels, for example, without any perks at all!Overall, however, TBW is a near perfect game for me. The gameplay was satisfying for the entire duration (though, as mentioned, this started to dip late in the campaign...until the final level, of course, where it peaked again), it didn't overstay its welcome, and it had a story with plenty of heart and humour. 9.5/10. I think if the feature I mentioned about removing/disabling perks was available, it would be a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is the funniest game I have played since the original Disgaea. Snappy dialogue, interesting characters, and a world that's familiar enough to be recognizable yet strange enough to be its own thing, PLUS a very tightly put together tactical turn-based breaching simulator makes this thing the complete package. If you like Into The Breach, or even just laughing in general, you'll love TBW.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent turn based tactical game! The rewind system is generous enough you never feed like you messed up your run because of a misclick, or accidental bad placement, but not so generous as to remove any challenges. Each character's abilities are simple enough to grasp easily but still have a wealth of interesting combinations and creative uses. The writing is quite funny and the game is generally lighthearted, yet very good at tackling the more serious aspects with care, and fully explores the characters without veering into grim or broody. My one criticism is the necromancer concept in this game is amazing, and it makes me vaguely annoyed that I didn't think of it, and now someone else has done it first. Best kind of problem to have.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare to wait for a game with such anticipation, and have it not only live up to expectations, but exceed them.Tactical Breach Wizards has a lot going for it, clever writing, witty humour, an interesting setting, compelling plot, satisfying combat/puzzle challenges and a decent amount of charm. No game is for everyone, but this game is for a lot of people.I love any game that offers difficult missions where you can try to get every single objective done, alongside the option of 'good enough, I'll be perfect later' and just move on to the next juicy bit of dialogue or another suprising missions with new toys.Do yourself a favour, and buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: More of a puzzle game with lots of solutions than an XCOM style game.You have perfect knowledge of the battlefield and every ability hits if there is line of sight.That said, this game is great. The dry humor of the dialog has made me crack of plenty of times. The art style is great, and there's a great mechanic between missions to help you understand all of the people and politics going on in the story.You can rush through the story, or take your time on a bunch of optional side missions that will unlock more cosmetic options (and are just satisfying as hell when you find a perfect solution). If a particular room is driving you crazy and you just can't seem to find the solution, you get the option to just skip it, so you don't lose the flow of the story. The game isn't trying to punish you, but present a fun story and innovative gameplay.What a little masterpiece out of nowhere.Cons: Steve Clark
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game contains the funniest jokes and all-around storytelling I've encountered in the past decade, if not longer. _childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic in every way that matters. the writing is extremely good for any expectation you could have of a game like this. The game also makes you feel very, very clever when you have some of those "aha!" moments using skills in ways you didn't think of before, up to and including being able to  I recommend it to just about everyone!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant game, I adored the puzzle like combat with goals set to encourage the creativity I needed to have to actually complete a mission.This game not only has made itself a special place in my heart because of the fun characters but also the countless ideas I get just thinking of stories which could build off of the outer world they have constructed for it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is both the best puzzle game I've played in years and the best tactics game I've played in years. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The concept is fantastic, but that just gets you through the front door. And once you're there, you realise. The gameplay is as good as you'd hope from the concept, the story is compelling, and the characters and writing are both AMAZING. Genuinely, I laughed out loud something like 20 times playing the story, at MINIMUM - it's probably closer to double that, because the writing and personality that every character has is so good and so funny. I love every single character we meet in this game. I've just finished it and I already find myself wanting DLC just to see more of the characters and their stories. I want to write fanfiction about Jen and Banks. I want to see the battle for Liboli. I want to fight Steve Clark again. This game is perfect. 10/10, tactical breaching is magic.

_childDocuments_.review: There are few problems in life you can't solve with a good defenestration. When those show up, just slam someone in riot cleric armour into them from the other end of the room.Tactical Breach Wizards is a hell of a game and 100% worth playing if you enjoy tactical or puzzle games, as it's probably best described as a "tactical puzzle" game. _childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Been loving this game. I often quickly grow weary of turn based games like this, but the gameplay is engaging and satisfying enough to keep me locked in. The story and dialogue is witty and funny without being a cringey quip-fest, and the idea of tactical wizards is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool and unique it makes me wish more properties used it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Put this on my wishlist years ago because I really liked Heat Signature and forgot it existed until it came out.Just finished the main story and about 1/2 of the side missions. I have got so much more I want to do! The real pleasure of this game is the total freedom you have to play around with it's mechanics, which could easily become trivial or repetitive but by slowly trickling new moves and more challenging puzzles TBW manages to pull off excellently.What this game (and the other games by this team) manages to do so well is throw a bunch of bespoke, clearly defined game pieces with their own rules into a play space and allow the complexity to arise from the interaction of those pieces. This game feels like a peak of that design philosophy and I thoroughly recommend it for that alone.On top of this there is a pretty fun story with some decent political intrigue. I think the dialogue is funny and sincere where it needs to be but I found that the characters lacked distinct voices. I think the humour relied a bit too much on self-awareness and snark to the point where it was nearly grating but there are some really funny moments in there too.In short: Highly recommend, if the dialogue isn't your cup of tea then it's all skippable.

_childDocuments_.review: Been a fan of this team, and when I found out they were doing a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WIZARD GAME I knew I had to get it. _childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I took a chance on this game, and it was the best chance I've ever taken.The story is brilliant, with brilliant characters all dealing with conflict. My favorite character has to be Zan, with his dream being about how he sees what confidence should be.The gameplay is brilliant, being complex and challenging. I didn't get bored once trying to figure out what my next moves would be.This is one of the most brilliant turn-based games I've played, and it's a must-play for those who love turn-based games.(Also, I want an assault staff!)
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Starting the first mission things are going well as you walk through the game's basics. At the final door, you must rescue a hostage and things go wrong. It’s a well-done start that keeps you intrigued as well as introduces you to the game well. Following that we’re introduced to Jen, a storm witch, and PI who's at the local police station. Things quickly get out of hand and Jen meets up with Zan who we played in the tutorial an old friend. It’s here the gameplay starts to come alive as you’re able to combo different abilities. Being a turn-based tactical game Jen features heavy knockback abilities meant to defenestrate enemies while Zan is a seer who can see one second in the future and is more focused on setup. Quickly the fun comes together as you can chain a knockback move into a predictive bolt, a move that triggers if an enemy moves into it. There are several difficulty options to keep things interesting as well as optional objects to add even further challenge. These optional challenges are extremely well done and add a whole new layer to the game so much so that I made sure to do everyone, this aspect shifts the game to be more of a puzzle game, and solving these optional objectives was immensely satisfying.  Over time the game adds more and more characters to play rounding out at 5 each with their unique kits that work well with the other 4. Throughout I found more use for some of them but the optional objectives made sure I was familiar with each character. Many solutions are creatively done and have multiple ways to solve them allowing for some diversity in how you play.  Aiding this is the smoothness of it all as well as the matching sound effects, each ability has a unique sound, and chaining together a whole string of abilities creates great moments. Further optional missions called dreams do away with some of the more realistic physics to create strange and challenging scenarios add some side content for those craving more and workshop support for player-made levels theoretically makes for an endless experience. As a reward for completing optional objectives, you unlock confidence points which can be used to put outfits on the characters, a fun little bonus. Storywise the game follows Zan mainly as he seeks to find out why his old partner(from the botched intro mission) is back and seemingly with ill intentions, what follows is a heartfelt story full of humor and real stakes as you seek to prevent World War 5. Many things are confronted in the game from themes of abusive religious authority, political intrigue, and deeper more personal emotional problems from each of our main characters. The team is loosely held together by a shared motive but each hides their trauma and has to work through it throughout the game. All of this could easily fall apart as there is a lot to the game but the pacing at which new aspects are introduced as well as the engaging and witty story keeps it together and fresh throughout the playtime. The tactical nature of the game provides a decent challenge that is adjustable and fun. All in all a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game that really makes use of the oddity that magical gameplay permits. Don't like how things would work out? Rewind time and try again. Got a point that can only be passed by triggering a landmine? Send a character in to get blasted, then magically revive her and throw her right back into the fight.  It's an excellent little game that I'm enjoying so far.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 at the very least. This game I saw randomly browsing steam, and it has gone far beyond all expectations when I saw the screenshots. _childDocuments_.review: This is the best game I've played in years. It has such heart, the writing remains funny throughout and the characters stick with you. The puzzles are so engaging and increase in difficulty at a perfect pace. What a masterpiece of a game, clearly made with love. It never outstays it's welcome. Amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully made game with characters I like, a story I got interested in, gameplay that gives me a headache in a good way, dialog that made me laugh quite abit, and plenty of bonus content to do. _childDocuments_.review: I instantly fell in love with the game. Fantastic story, hilarious characters and so full of both very creative writing and gameplay. _childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. Its mainly a puzzle game, where you control a few characters with different abilities to take out enemies and complete objectives. It is designed beautifully, with a surprisingly funny story to go along with it. The rewind mechanic works a lot better than I expected, encounters still feel challenging even with the ability to redo your turn as many times as you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and clever tactics game. The visuals are stylish, the music and sound effects weighty, The characters are all very well written and as the tone of the story shifted and the gravity of their situation became apparent I found myself caring about these individuals and their world. I suppose that is the mark of a truly impactful experience. I hope this small dev team is proud of what they have created, and I hope you try out Tactical Breach Wizards if you enjoy strategy, magic, puzzles, and perhaps feeling a little emotional.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me laugh and hardly any does these days... so I suppose that makes it particularly worth a buy.It's also a very competent tactics game akin to Firaxis' XCom, Invisible Inc., Showgunners... or many others at this point, perhaps making the humorous take even more important. It's as if someone was tasked with making yet another X-Com clone... but then they hired Terry Pratchett.Edit after 20 hrs: Yeah, the game clearly took some inspiration from Into The Breach, with the knockback mechanic and the maps being kind of a tactical puzzle, and very clever skill interactions. However, the story/mission arc is a very big part of the game, so I will maintain my opinion about this being a fully-fledged tactics game not a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It was definitely worth the wait. Being able to respec perks on the fly was nice, but the low number of respec points might put off the more creative thinkers. Lots of optional stuff, and the rewards for doing Confidence being purely cosmetic was nice. Excellent writing and characters, as is the norm from this development team. Will definitely be coming back to try out all the optional content at least once.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely excellent. Modern magic settings are awesome, and this game took that idea to it's fullest to be something really unique, feels like a D&D campaign I've been wanting to write for years.The characters and story are very well written, the gameplay is fun (so long as you enjoy turn base tactics) and there's a lot more to do after you beat the game. The art style is incredible, some kind of minimalist comic book look I have a hard time describing, but really enjoyed.A main story run-through with minimum side content took me about 14 hours, I suspect there's about 20-25 hours worth of content in the game not counting player created maps.For a 20$ game, this felt well worth it. Overall I'd give it 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is the product of a team of people who think about games the way an artist thinks about composition. There's a lot to say about it; the writing is fun, profound, and concise -- what other games take too long to say, Francis says with a line. The tactics are tight and  compelling. The story is complicated, but a crazy-red-string conspiracy board makes sure you understand it without feeling like a chore. The defenestration series of games is amazing, and I am ecstatic that their are true artisans in this industry, and that it's not all overblown "triple-A" Disney-funded garbage. The money I spent on Tactical Breach Wizards was well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the demo and loved it. Day 1 purchase was an easy choice.There's a solid tactics game here, with punchy hits and interesting tools, but what's keeping me interested/challenged are the optional objectives. Not every room is possible to clear in one turn, but every so often, that little side challenge is telling you that there is a way to do it if you can figure it out.The rewind mechanic doesn't feel like save-scumming or easy mode. The absence of RNG makes it that every shot hits, and it really is just down to setting up the perfect play and executing it. You can figure out some fun combos that leave you feeling very clever (I will never get tired of "Predictive-Bolt" plays).The dialogue is mostly just sarcasm, but thankfully you can skip it without much consequence if that's annoying to you (story might not make sense). _childDocuments_.review: This game is spectacular, and not at all a gimmick. The world building is fresh and fleshed out, and the complex plot and world elements are all introduced organically. I didn't think I would enjoy the "rewinding time" mechanic, but it enables the player to explore the unique and creative abilities of each character without the fear of messing up and executing a sub-optimal plan. Instead, it encourages you to optimize your plan to the greatest extent, and it is incredibly satisfying to put all the pieces together and breach an entire room in one turn. Perfectionists will enjoy this game without needing to sink tedious amounts of time into it. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth full price. Play the  to decide for yourself.The campaign is advertised at fourteen hours, but how much mileage you get from this game is very much up to you. The difficulty can be customized to make most encounters trivial, or very demanding. (Almost) every level has optional objectives you may strive for, and there are several completely optional levels that explore the game's systems outside the bounds of the plot. Finishing all of it on the highest difficulty took me an estimated 40 hours (accounting for my habit to leave programs running when I walk away from my PC).I like the plot, by and large. I have one glaring complaint about Act III, . Aside that single fly in the soup, I consider the story well-paced, clever, and the characters both likable and believable. It can also be skipped, if you would prefer.The gameplay difficulty is the game's greatest fumble in my opinion, though not nearly enough to retract my glowing recommendation. You will accumulate new team members and abilities as you progress through the campaign, and at first, the increasing complexity of possible puzzle solutions makes the game incrementally harder, giving a good sense of improvement over time. Unfortunately, there comes a point in Act IV where there are  tools at your disposal that it ceases to be necessary to use them in creative ways. Consequently, the difficulty buckles when it needed to be at, or at least near, its highest.All that being true, I think the greatest endorsement I can give this game may be that it is the first to earn a (real) review from me, in ten years of using Steam. Tactical Breach Wizards probably deserves your money, and absolutely deserves your attention.

_childDocuments_.review: Heat Signature was my favorite game of 2017, so I've been anticipating Tactical Breach Wizards for 7 years, and to summarize everything I'm about to write, not only has that anticipation been rewarded, this game surpassed every one of my expectations. If you are a fan of Heat Signature, if you enjoy puzzle-based tactics games, or if you enjoy strong comedic yet emotional writing, then this game is for you.If you are familiar with Heat Signature, slipping into Tactical Breach Wizards should be pretty easy for you, it's mostly a turn-based version of the positional targeting and timing gameplay of that game, but in a structured linear story rather than through somewhat randomly generated missions. Things start out slowly, with simple defenestration and ping-pong based take-downs, but as you add and upgrade abilities, the combat shifts into more complex order of operation based positioning that will see you performing debuff based setups, swapping positions with teammates and enemies alike, and setting up traps based on enemy tactics. While you never need to min / max these options to complete levels, the game deviously offers optional objectives that will highly encourage you to engage with the systems at play and really crunch your brain to find the best way to plan and execute. These optional stressors only unlock costumes, so there's never a gameplay demand to do them if you'd rather just brute force your way through.What this game largely improves over Head Signature, if it's something you value, is story and characters. Each of the cast members you meet, friend and enemy alike, are uniquely interesting personalities that are fun to listen to and even better when they interact. The humor comes largely from in-universe discussions; things like comedic misunderstandings or people responding with humorous retorts, rather than filling the game with references and meta-humor, though both are here in some quantity.While a majority of the game is light and humorous, it occasionally delves into deeper topics, mostly with regards to character's backstory, and includes subjects such as PTSD, anxiety, self-doubt, and when the ends justify the means. While the game is overall light and humorous, these topics are treated with the weight they deserve, and working through real emotions is what drives the character development of your little group of friends. Refreshingly, nobody's trauma is wrapped up in a neat little bow by story's end, as those things don't just go away, they require continuous efforts to heal.The story itself starts small, with localized tracking and information gathering, but builds over the course of the ~15 hour runtime to a strong international espionage tale, with reveals and twists that are built to and rewarding to experience. The set-up and execution of the final chapter has real gravitas, both in the story and gameplay, with both coming together to build on each other leading up to the final battle.Beyond the main game, you can replay levels with any character with all their upgrades to complete the previously mentioned optional objectives, as well as complete several puzzle missions, a handful of which serve as the post-game, opening up after you complete the main story.The only downside in all is that now I have to wait another 7 years for whatever this team decides to tackle next, but whatever it is, I'm sure it will be as worth it as their previous efforts have been.After all, Tactical Breach Wizards is my favorite game of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy tactics games, logic puzzles, or just good fun campy dialogue, you owe it to yourself to get this game. Tactical Breach Wizards is one of the few games I loved so much that I felt the need to 100% it and leave a review so other people can enjoy. I'm sad to finally put it down now, but more than satisfied with the story closure, and the workshop support for future replay ability once people get cooking on custom scenarios.A couple of things to note though:- Difficulty: The game can be challenging if you play on hard difficulty from the start, but there is no great incentive to do so  (with a number of custom difficult options making the game incredibly easy. Further, on normal difficulty, by late game you are virtually unstoppable if you choose your character perks correctly. As such, if you are a fan of  hardcore tactics games that really make you sweat, there are options here to make things harder, but you're unlikely to enjoy the main difficulty settings as the game is not overly punishing at base.- Character perks/leveling: I had fun here, but this one can be a negative, if you choose well you can create a handful of infinite loop combos powerful enough to melt bosses in a single turn. However if you choose poorly, you can seriously hamper your ability to perform in some of the more complex scenarios. I wouldn't say that any are inherently "bad" choices. But there are definitely several "why would you ever not pick this up" choices.-  Play time: if you are like me and insist on doing the optional bonus objectives for every level the first try (which is completely viable on normal difficulty if you play well), the game can take 20-30 hours to 100%. A tremendous value given the price to me personally, but your mileage may vary. If you don't care for bonus objectives or you play on hard difficulty, your playtime experience may be dramatically different.- Story/Dialogue: I needed to give this its own bullet. The storyline, dialogue, and worldbuilding genuinely had me on the edge of my seat the whole game. The writing was entertaining enough that I would replay levels just to see responses to other dialogue choices and had to take screenshots of some conversations that truly had me rolling.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the campaign and a handful of extra challenges at 19 hours. Unusually for me, I'm actually excited to go back and keep playing to complete the extra challenge levels, as well as the optional challenges on the main missions. The gameplay is is slick and offers a good variety of solutions to the various tactics puzzles that are presented. Being able to preview enemy actions and rewind your own actions (within a turn, not across turns) helps encourage experimentation and exploration of various possible solutions. It's evident that a lot of time and care went into balancing the various character abilities and crafting well-designed levels.The character designs are charming (I did find a few of the unlockable outfits bland, but apparently other people liked them) and the level art is good at balancing setting the scene with allowing important elements (like windows, enemy spawn doors, and interactable items) to stand out. I'm not terribly interested in super-realistic graphics, and this game is a perfect example of why: the visuals are pleasing to look at while serving both gameplay and setting.The setting definitely has the feel of being centered around the aesthetic. On one level, the setting is basically just modern-day except some people happen to have magic powers, with fictional political entities and geography, although there are definitely some parallels to real-life countries. The on-ramp of the setting is very gentle, and there's not really any lore dumping or excessive exposition. And when aspects of the setting are revealed, they're generally relevant to at least two of: the plot, the characters, the gameplay, and the sense of humor.The writing is one of the spots where the game *really* shines. The sense of humor suffuses every part of the game, even down to the graphics settings menu. I found myself taking screenshots of nearly every dialogue in order to share with friends, and then after even a short play session having trouble deciding which of the many dialogues to share.I do think that improvements could be made to the custom level editor. Some of the options in the UI are not very intuitive, and it's not clear how to configure things like enemy spawn doors (or if those even are configurable). Some of the objectivs are explicitly tied to certain characters and do not have the option to change the objective to relate to a different character.Another downside is the conspiracy board; I do like the concept, but mostly it felt more like a pop quiz to check if you were paying attention to the most recent cutscene rather than a really solid element of the game. However, as it's a board that you build up over the campaign rather than a whole bunch of separate boards, it does end up serving as a neat interactive record of the story so far which also ties the various missions to the setting's geography. I do think that if I dropped the game for one reason and picked it up again weeks or months later, it would be helpful in getting back up to speed on the story so far.Overall, I have no reservations about recommending this game, and it's easily my favorite game that I played this year.

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't a lot I can say about this game that other reviews haven't already praised it for repeatedly.A solid story that the game strings along to the player in a way that is both tangible and makes sense, well written characters with humorous dialogue and more depth to them than one might expect from a top down turn-based puzzle game, and a slew of content that doesn't slouch for the $20 price tag. _childDocuments_.review: Equal parts turnbased tactical shooter and puzzle game. Love the unique mechanical takes and how different the characters feel, both mechanically and in their personalities. _childDocuments_.review: “Throwing away your problems out of the windows sure does feel great”+Praises:This is an amazing turn-based strategy game w/ a fun cast of characters.First, what drew me into trying the demo is seeing wizards in a modern setting, bc it’s a setting I rarely see compared to Classical-Fantasy or Science-Fantasy. I find it amusing seeing witches dealing w/ magic bureaucratic procedures, (insert fantasy race) mafia, and militarized warlocks wearing kevlar.Secondly, each playable character have unique personalities, entertaining interactions & fun toolkits.Lastly, I enjoy how each chapter of the story is composed of multiple fairly challenging levels, and how they include optional requirements(for specific characters) for extra challenges. Fulfilling those optional req will reward skill points to unlock more abilities/upgrades for their respective character.Also, the feature to open the menu and provide immediate feedback( report bugs, errors, etc…) is something new to me, I understand not every studios is willing to implement this option, but that’s really cool~Neutral Additional Notes:The game has more achievements than I expected(61 to be precise, not complaining , just surprised). There are also optional stages separate from the main story’s ‘chapter select’ menu, if you can’t get enough of the turn-based strategy puzzles( I personally haven’t play much but felt the need to mention ); keep in mind that these optional stages are there to stimulate your ‘strategist brain’ and your characters won’t gain EXP-Nitpicks:Not a fan of tutorial missions that will not let the player progress unless they learn/use “the newly introduced ability”. There were times where I thought the amount of battles in each chapter felt excessive( tho it didn’t stop me from playing it until 2-3am and lose sleep). Personally, I wish this game had voice-acting even if it’s not a necessary thing that affects my enjoyment of the overall product. It’s also a shame that this title is only available on Steam( at the time this review is being written ), I think this indie project deserves more attention & more people should pick it up.In other words, you like XCOM? You like Mario+Rabbid? You like feeling like a war general at the comfort of turn-based combat? You have a potato PC?... this is for you

_childDocuments_.review: BUY THIS GAME. It's been 3 hours. I've played probably dozens of these room-clearing combat puzzle games, and I'm already on board 100%. You play as Wizard SWAT, so the tone is fun but takes itself somewhat seriously considering the concept. Rappelling down on a broomstick to kick in a glass window, making clones of yourself to fool trigger happy foes, etc. Gameplay wise you're breaching and clearing rooms like any good SWAT team, but unlike them you have a wizard that will tell you what will happen in the next second, and you can fully rewind to the beginning of the turn. In other words: No random chance. You *will* hit, you *will* send them flying through that portal, you *will* animate the dead to horrify their comrades on their turn. Think Into the Breach levels of prediction.I can't speak about the endgame difficulty yet, but as soon as they opened optional dream maps I realized I 100%'d them rather than move the actually fun plot forward, and I knew I had a great game on my hands.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nothing short of amazing. The gameplay is solid, the writing is both engaging and hilarious, and most impressively it's both player-friendly as well as challenging at the same time.I also love the map mechanic that has you piece together the story as you go by connecting different cards together. It really helps to stay on top of the story, which otherwise could easily become a bit cloudy with all the different characters and locations that are introduced.The upgrades and variation in characters for each level make sure the gameplay is constantly evolving, which means it never gets boring despite the core game loop remaining the same throughout the game.The game is also quite vast, as I'm currently already over 30 hours in and still haven't finished the main story, and that's while skipping over most optional stuff which I'm keen on checking out after I've completed the main plot.Truly GOTY stuff this tbh. I've also enjoyed Gunpoint and Heat Signature a lot, but Tactical Breach Wizards feels like their best game yet by a mile, which is impressive because those other games are very very good in their own right!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic tactics/puzzle hybrid. Everything about it is excellent:- Clean art style- Excellent overall presentation- Deeply engaging combat that can really give your brain a workout once your options expand- Cute characters- Snappy, witty dialogue- A surprisingly thrilling story with strong world buildingEvery bit of this game is a joy. From the humorous pre-breach dialogue to the delicious puzzle of gameplay to the surprisingly intimate inter-mission conversations with between characters, every piece feels thoughtfully designed, and the writer never missed an opportunity to squeeze in another joke. Your ever-expanding and -evolving combat toolkit provides a staggering number of options after the more constrained beginning, allowing you to devise your own strategies for every set of challenges the game throws at you.Highly recommended to any tactics fans, as well as anyone who's not really a fan of tactics games.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't beat it *quite* yet (on the final act), but I can tell you that this is one of my Indie games of all time, if not one of my favorite games.The game in my opinion isn't super difficult, but with the bonus objectives it gives you to earn "Confidence Points" (which let you unlock outfits between missions) let you self-select your difficulty on the fly. Having trouble with a level? Maybe forget about those challenges and just do your best to clear it! Finding it too easy? See if you can't get all the challenges done at once, maybe with some self imposed ones like not letting anyone get hit.Incredibly unique abilities, combined with the ability to rewind anything before committing, leads to some fantastic moments of completing a turn, not being satisfied with the outcome, and thinking of what you could do differently. Then you rewind, run it back, and do it another way! Hell, just like Heat Signature (Suspicious Developments' other amazing game, check it out), the game is such a fantastic sandbox I often found myself testing different combinations of abilities to see how their interplay worked, only to find and develop new strategies I'd never would've thought of without the safety blanket of a rewind!Master-class in clever puzzles, especially near the end of Act 3 there's an insaaane moment which I won't spoil. If this game doesn't have you rethinking the way you approach sandboxes in general, nothing will.On top of that, the writing is incredibly witty. A few laugh out loud moments, but I'm fairly easy to make laugh- over all though, tight, humorous dialogue throughout, and some REALLY thoughtful worldbuilding that gets me excited as both a writer and a player. The magic system is incredibly intricate both in game and in world, and it's very fun to see the interaction of it in both settings.♥♥♥♥ I love this game. To Tom and the rest of the team, thank you so much for this gem. In an industry that's had so much strife recently you've rejuvenated my belief in the games industry and made me excited to create again. 10/10 game, looking forward to 100%'ing it in the coming weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: This gem has a lot going for it. The story while not super in depth, has plenty to keep your interest along with great characters, great humor, but of course most importantly the gameplay is great. Each character is effectively their own "class" and they accent one another really well. The game also has bonus challenge missions that are actually decent as well. I felt glad to find them there because it meant more of an already great game and I'm not usually one to do challenge missions or such. I sat here for a bit trying to think of something to complain about, but I'm not sure I really have anything. This game is fantastic and is absolutely worth the 20 bucks (at this time). What else is there to say?

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is a delightful tactics game.  Its story is cogent and provides on theme visual aids to remind you of what's important right now. The world is engaging and whimsical, but that whimsy doesn't prevent the story from going some dark places and providing consequences for characters. The characters are distinct, the dialogue is snappy and provides almost as many possible directions as the tactical play. Speaking of the tactical play, environmental awareness is a huge element of the game. Very few character abilities do direct damage, so setting up ability interactions and angles to successfully defenestrate (or otherwise dispose of) an enemy is a central element of game play. I remember being challenged by this learning curve at the beginning, but by the time I picked up my third wizard and gained more abilities to play with it all started to come together. Of course the learning curve is helped massively by the ability to wind back actions to the beginning of turn and establish a perfect order of operations. I was occasionally frustrated by building a plan and then having a single missed element throw something off, but the ability to rewind to the beginning of the turn is a wonderful mechanic that encourages creative problem solving. You can always try again, so long as you're only looking at threats from this turn.I spent much more time on a turn on average than in any other tactics game, so if you're looking for something  with expansive levels and lots of movement this might not be it. Similarly, the story is short. If you're looking for a game where every decision counts the first time and every problem looks like something to be shot, stabbed, or exploded, this is not that game. If you want a game with a strong premise, where you iterate through a turn, apply some creative problem solving, establish an order of actions, and ultimately watch an insufferable narcissist fly through a window? This game does that very well, and I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: This a fun tactical game, with the added bonus that you only need to fully commit to your actions on a per-round basis, and can look ahead to see if any negative repercussions hit you when the round ends. The story is fun (though a bit mature given some of the dialogue), and the cosmetic unlocks give it fun goals to strive for. The extra dream missions are fun too, and I like the bit between rounds with the map and investigation. I look forward to completing the campaign and staying tuned to other releases from the developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the campaign and a few side missions, I can say for certain this is one of the best games I have played for years and is an easy game of the year contender in a year I feel I've played some amazing games such as 1000 X Resist, In Stars and Time and Shadow of the Erdtree.This is the first time I've played a game like this, playing on normal and going out of my way to do the confidence objectives.The continual ramp up in difficulty whilst giving you new abilities to strategize around felt perfectly paced, in line with a story that I thoroughly enjoyed and writing that made me laugh before, during and after every mission. There were no levels where I had anything short of a thrilling time, and some made me tense in ways similar to some disaster runs of Darkest Dungeon despite the lack of perma-death. I cannot recommend this game enough to anyone who has even the slightest interest in it, and most people who don't. Thank you Suspicious Developments for this game, and thank you allowing me to defenestrate Steve Clark.

There hasn't been a dialogue sequence that hasn't made me laugh yet, the plot is intriguing, and the characters are great.All in all, if you're at all into strategy/puzzle games, I don't see a reason why you shouldn't try this one out.

_childDocuments_.review: The level design is excellent, allowing for multiple ways to complete each scenario. You are pushed to test different techniques in order to complete the optional goals in each mission, and the rewind system means you can really test out different combinations of moves before you commit. Besides the gameplay, the aesthetic is phenomenal, with a fun and playful vibe running throughout. The little details, from the arcane-modern equipment the wizards carry to the snippets of funny dialogue really all work together to create an atmosphere that is very enjoyable to partake in. I haven't had this much fun playing a video game since Deep Rock Galactic, and I'm so happy I found this one!

_childDocuments_.review: A gang of irreverent ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tries to prevent World War 5 with the power of prophecy and extreme(ly nonlethal) violence.On the gameplay side, forced-movement-focused tactical combat so tightly designed it transcends into a puzzle game, smoothed out by the unlimited ability to rewind a turn after experimenting with a move. On the writing side, hilariously quippy dialog (that never descends into Whedonesque overindulgence) and a story that avoids the jingoist and fascist pitfalls you might fear from military aesthetic.It's everything you'd hope for from the capstone of the Defenstration Trilogy and more. An instant personal GOTY contender. I've been pining for a decade for a game about a spec-ops wizard in a chocolate-chip-camo robe, and I'm thrilled I was 100% right to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Indie games i've ever played. It's funny, it's well made, and the gameplay is magnificent. Extremely well made, the plot is good, i've not encountered a single bug yet and it's genuinely well worth the price. The game plays like a tactical xcom-y turn based strategy game. it's definitely not xcom, there's no chance to miss and characters have several abilities not determined by equipment. The game isn't difficult to complete, but when you start going for optional objectives it becomes like a puzzle with multiple solutions, only some later game optional objectives really (to me) seem to need specific skill upgrades to complete but you get perk resets as you progress so you can undo a couple after trying them out. Overall fantastic game highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun game. The dialogue made me laugh out loud in places. It's not the hardest or the longest, I'm a strategy game veteran and I completed the campaign on hard in 50 hours without having to replay a single level that I can remember (including the final boss). A couple of levels were tricky, but you can rewind any of your team's actions before the end of the turn, which is great for experimentation and does make things significantly easier.The amount of fresh ideas and inventive level design in this game is off the charts. Each of the main characters has their own unique level which works with their unique abilities and develops their back-story. My favourite was the necro-medic, who can resurrect people after shooting them first, and who has a level where she advances by resurrecting herself multiple times, which is every bit as mind bending as it sounds.Strongly recommend to anyone who likes tactical games and innovative, original game design.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: To anyone worried the game may be too easy, try it on the max custom difficulty and doing all the bonus objectives. It is possible, and very satisfying!I got stuck on one of the "dream" level's bonus objectives and had to refund some perks, then later realised you can do this for free in those levels anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, where do I begin ? The simple, satisfying, fun gameplay that is a perfect mix between XCOM and Into the Breach ? The expertly done difficulty curve ? The interesting characters that you get attached to over the course of their story ? The fact that this game actually managed to make me laugh ? The sadness when you finish the game, knowing that you need to move on ?It's great. Turn-based tactical RPG with a twisting, funny story. Will stick with you. Work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews for games I haven't finished but I want to make an exception because I'm playing this so close to release.This is a very good game. The strategy RPG maps are so tightly made that they almost feel like I'm playing a puzzle game, trying to figure out the best possible move. You're ability to rewind back to the beginning of the current turn gives you a ton of space to experiment and play and see how things work out, which makes this very beginner friendly, but with characters and maps complicated enough that veterans of the genre will have plenty to chew on, especially with the additional goals you can complete per map to unlock costumes. The characters have many useful perks making them customization to your specific playstyle. The smaller maps give it a brisk pace that is rare for this genre. If you liked into the breech this should be your next buy.The story so far is wonderful, the characters are all fun and likable, and it has a great sense of humor.Please play this it's so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: wonderful game, really.i know it says right there its _not_ 'into the breach' but it certainly reminds me of it given how both games are (nearly) perfectly readable, allow for a lot of freedom, and have super clever design.and that's the keyword right there: clever. pretty much every level and optional objective is unique in some nice little way, challenging you to think a bit different, try new things, gives you a hint towards an interaction you've not yet thought of.playing trough the campaign is a lot of fun and is (in my opinion) paced extremely well, with really funny and sometimes deep dialogue between quirky, lovable characters. the story is intriguing and, again, clever, and it has a clear start and end. very satisfying.the real proof of the love and effort that went into the game is all the little details across the entire game - from minor background elements, over extra quips for unorthodox results, to the way that the humor and the artistic voice is so ingrained into every aspect of it. it was a real pleasure to see and experience.extra points for including a really good demo! see for yourself if you'd like the game, its a really good vertical slice.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! Gameplay is good - basically it is a mix of a turn-based tactics and puzzle. If you want you can consider this as room-based turn-based tactics game, but if you want to beat game fully you'd need to clear the rooms in a specific way by  completing a (absolutely optional) goals which would reward you with cosmetic stuff. Even more - almost everything in a game is skippable. The intention of that is pure accessability -- you want to skip the dialogs? Ok. Just want to see the plot? Ok, pick the easy mode and skip levels you find hard to beat.Enough for accessability. I'm grasping this beautiful hame as intended - when completing optional goals you'd need to think more on the tactics, which not only more fun but makes you play better.The plot is interesting - its a nice irony on "noir/magicpunk/old movies/task forces". Writing is good, I sencerily interested in plot and chukling from time to time on a jokes.The progression opens up the multiple layers of a game, makes it more and more interesting.Graphics is ok. Behind the oversimplified style of textures lies a lots of artists work - main characters all have fetures that has direct reflection in plot and gameplay.The only downside of a game would be lack of whatsoever localisation, but I bet this would me changed in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It's got a nice aesthetic and concept, but not what I was expecting by what I heard about it. Dialogue is amusing, characters are interesting, world is fire. Game play has a nice twist to it, but this isn't a turn based tactical game like XCOM. The game feels more like if you don't solve it close to how it wants you to, then you're going to be rewinding over and over and over until you get close to how the game wants you to do the mission. That just doesn't feel like a tactical game to me.Also, the little sub-mission styles within the campaign just break the immersion of the story. I've only been at it for a little while, and I'm already finding myself getting frustrated that I'm getting force to push through these other missions that aren't related to the story. If you want that, please put it outside the main campaign, it wrecks the flow.Over all, it's feels like a good game, but it's not what I was expecting. Some will like it, some won't. Just feels like it could use a little more polish and outside feedback.
