_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. It is very similar to , which instead had a single playable character with a card deck of moves. Having a whole team with a certain set of skills makes the gameplay more convenient and efficient."Convenient" is what makes this game fun. The characters are strong and versatile which makes them fun and if you make mistakes you can always rewind. You can go for the perfect turn and try to clear as many enemies as you can take, which feels more like a power fantasy than the challenge oriented games of the genre.What it doesn't have is challenge. , for example, embraced that challenge, and made it so you could get stronger by completing side objectives, and unlock more characters which were weaker than these wizards but had their niches and strong suits. This game has optional challenges for the fun of it, with no benefits. Which is understandable as it is not its focus.Instead of challenge and replayability, this game offers a story. The story itself could be a little more succint for better impact, but it doesn't impose itself upon you. They've made it a point to make it skippable, which is good, but I wish it was more confident both in presentation and writing.It is a complete, enjoyable experience. A nice amount of quality levels and skill upgrades are neatly linked to the characters both by gameplay and narration.

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is a phenomenally written turn based tactics game. Given unique abilities with specific applications and upgrades to go along with them you have a plethora of options available to you at any given moment in game. And despite having a toolkit of abilities so broad, the enemy and level design still left me feeling challenged. If the game was riding solely on its gameplay it would already be a win in my book. However the characters and their interactions, each of their arcs, and the overall story are each just as good, if not better, in their own right. Coupled with unique worldbuilding that gives us a modernized world where magic developed alongside technology but not quite replacing it and you get a setting thats quite unlike anything you could compare it to and the team puts this unique setting to full effect without making the world or its concepts foreign. In fact, they're easily familiar to the average person. In short, Tactical breach wizards is a fun tactics game with lovable characters and the most pleasantly surprising game I've played in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is great. Between story, gameplay, and art, It has something for everyone. It's the best tactics game I've played, but I would recommend it even if you don't normally enjoy tactics games.Suspicious Developments have only improved with every game they've released (and if you've played Gunpoint, you know they started out pretty great already). The turn-based deterministic combat of TBW feels like an evolution of games like Into the Breach, generating interesting puzzles to solve nearly every turn. Each character has a set of 3-5 abilities which are simple on the surface but almost always have synergies or nuances to discover. Acquiring new abilities and characters deepens your pool of available decisions without ever feeling confusing. I spent my entire playtime, from the first level to the post-game content, thinking "ooooh I can do this! I never thought of that before". The controls and interface (as well as the excellent art direction) are polished to a mirror sheen, and I never had any problems to speak of. Overall, the game strikes a fantastic balance between complexity and intuitiveness that means you're unlikely to be overwhelmed while also constantly being engaged.Speaking of balance, the custom difficulty settings are extremely welcome. While it's unlikely that you'll ever find a level either impossible or trivial, everyone will have a different preference for how much thought they want to put into solving each turn. For me, I found the game the game most fun when I couldn't just fall back on familiar strategies, but rather had to find innovative answers to each problem, and it was simple enough to use these settings to keep it challenging. But I expect for players who aren't as interested in the strategy gameplay, they'll be able to use the same settings to keep it manageable so they can enjoy the great story.Tom Francis is an excellent writer. This is hardly a controversial opinion, but TBW shows it off even better than his previous works. The writing is consistently witty (I don't think I've fully laughed out loud at a game this much), but at its heart are a cast of compelling and likeable characters who you'll genuinely care for. It's impressive how much personality is packed into relatively few lines of dialogue; even the latecomers to the cast manage to feel fleshed out and interesting. As well as your party, the world feels surprisingly real despite its absurd magical elements. In the few short hours you spend in each location, I found myself feeling I understood what it was about, and genuinely caring for the people and places on display. The unfolding mystery as you chase the game's excellent villain and uncover her true agenda is consistently well-paced and satisfying, with twists and turns that surprise you in the most delightful ways. And, as is typical for a SusDev game, there's the occasional moment where the wit and charm gives way to unique, poignant, thought-provoking ideas. In the end, it was the writing, even more than the gameplay, that made me so eager to keep experiencing this game.I do have a few criticisms. The final arc feels a little rushed - it doesn't really give enough time to get to know the new supporting characters, or to feel the stakes of the climactic events unfolding around you. More dialogue in general would have been welcome; despite how rich and concise it is, I found myself desperate for more interactions. The downtime conversations between the party members are where some of the best writing is found, and I wish they happened more often. Finally, although the combat balance is mostly excellent, there are a few perks that feel a little too strong. On my first playthrough, I defeated the final boss in a single turn, thanks to Zan's ability to go nearly infinite with the right perks.Despite my criticisms, this is probably my GOTY. If you like puzzle games, tactics games, or just creative and compelling stories, I can't recommend TBW highly enough. It's an achievement in art, writing, game design, and more. 5/5

_childDocuments_.review: Clever writing, unique animation, the premise is a fun flip on fantasy tropes. It's like XCOM and DnD hooked up and someone got pregnant. Like with XCOM you'll find the maps are not all that distinct and the sort of challenges/barriers/enemies overlap. It's a puzzler in that sense with placement being a huge component of your play - especially on Hard Mode. You'll be hitting rewind a lot as you and try and figure out the best way to clear a room. The game presupposes you'll replay missions to earn confidence and maybe try out new skills/talents. It's a great game, with a few critiques. It's sort of like playing the save-the-village mission on XCOM2 each and every time. The maps change color scheme but the premise is more or less the same each time. There is no stealth option really - BREACH is in the name, and you burst into each room of baddies with an explosive ward. What that means though is every room is fought in the same manner, and it's up to you to puzzle your way through it.And the game revolves around specifically doing one thing - pushing people out of windows or off ledges and such. That was fun at the start, but it becomes a bit stale after you realize most of the time this is the go-to tactic. So the puzzle is always solving for the same problem: how to push people out of windows or into walls. Still, worth a pickup since the rest of the game makes up for the demerits. Good writing and a fun premise can carry the weight of good, if a bit one-dimensional, gameplay mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I love that the story focuses not on confident heroes, but insecure ones and highlights how they turn those insecurities and tribulations into strengths. The writing is funny, really funny, but beyond that there's a lot of heart to the characters and worldbuilding and draws engaging parallels to our world. It definitely left a much stronger impression than I'd expected and is far more than set dressing. Not just Bright if it was actually good, Bright if it was peak.It's a fun tactics puzzler that strikes a healthy balance in difficulty. It's very good at gently pulling you towards satisfying solutions and for the most part the bonus objectives are fair and satisfying. While you can certainly save them for replays, I found trying to complete them the first time you play through a level is a key part of keeping the game from being too frictionless.It also manages to give the player surprisingly deep skill expression for a puzzler. Initially, you focus on effective use of abilities individually and as you play with a more granular focus, you start to make use of synergy between characters' abilities and eventually make use of how you position each wizard. Cleverly, the game will lead you down this path through the order in which wizards are introduced. Early characters are individually strong while later characters can have greater impacts if you make further use of synergy and positioning. While this could have gotten too complicated for most, the generous turn structure gives you a lot of room to explore your options. It's one of the best and most thoughtfully structured games in recent years.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: While I love the idea of achievement hunting, my ADHD makes it difficult to accomplish any actual significant momentum towards completing most games that I play. So it should say something that I binged this game non-stop until I 100%ed it.The writing doesn't take itself too seriously, but still has enough wit and character to maintain an entertaining "pseudo-military banter" quality and avoids the comedic trap of being so un-serious that it ruins the immersion. The gameplay itself is engaging without being too difficult - which suits me just fine as someone who enjoys giving my brain a work out but doesn't want to get frustrated with something that I'm doing in my free time to wind down. And while it does clock in on the short end (as I said, I've 100%ed the game and it only took me just over 40 hours) at a dollar-per-hour investment it's more than worth the money compared to any number of other entertainment options I can think of.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made and fun strategy game with cute characters, and easy to consume. Recommended for anyone remotely interested in strategy games.As stated by the developers, it is very different from xcom despite the layouts, but it does capture the satisfaction of combining strengths of the different specialized characters to achieve your objective. There is no rng involved whatsoever and actions can be rewound to experiment different approaches. Customization of characters are limited and the campaign is entirely curated to tell its story. It reminds me of Shadow Tactics and Invisible Inc. in many ways. 9/10, more games should be like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is fun, witty experience that doesn't take itself too seriously, but has just enough of a logical plot for it to be gripping and interesting to follow. The gameplay is not only challenging, it is heavy on the variety AND rewarding the player for any solution they come up with. The humor is well paced, and helps characterize the people you meet AND offers a momentary pause for brains that might be overheating (like mine).  But most importantly, the game is fun for the sake of being fun. 20 hours of finishing the game and getting all the achievements, and I enjoyed every minute of it. I had so much fun on my initial 8 hour play session, I ended up not being able to sleep because my mind would generate a random level, I'd solve it, and then I'd wake up. A solid 9/10 experience

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. And I absolutely loved defenestrating enemies.After playing the demo in June, I was immediately hooked and took off work for the release date (something I've never done before). The premise is hilarious, the mechanics are very engaging, and the writing is fantastic on all fronts.It took me about 21 hours to play through on Hard with a good portion of the confidence objectives (had to toggle down to Normal difficulty for a single dream level), and that's with playing (and replaying...) the demo for about 3 hours. _childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tom Francis (and the team at Suspicious Developments) continues to be, in my mind, the best indie developer. Tom has devoted his career to making games where you throw people out of widows in increasingly inventive ways, and I like that. Tactical Breach Wizards is inventive, funny, well-paced, and deeply enjoyable. Tom's writing is frequently hilarious and surprisingly moving. It also has the most inventive final boss I've seen in the better part of a decade. My mouth literally dropped open when I realised that certain mechanics fit together the way they do. There's definitely some XCOM and Into the Breach DNA here, but Tactical Breach Wizards rises above mere imitation and uses these inspirations to create something new and interesting, and boy is originality in games hard to find these days, even among the indie scene. Treat yourself to this game, and then play Heat Signature and Gunpoint if you haven't yet, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the open ended puzzle aspect of this game.  You are given a set of tools and a tactical sandbox to play in, and it's up to you how you solve the issue. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a delight. Sharp and engaging puzzles, charming dialogue, enjoyable characters, and plenty of defenestration. Some may get annoyed with the quips, but it always felt like friendly ribbing to me, and I enjoyed it throughout. At the time of writing this review, I've finished my main playthrough, although I will no doubt go back and achieve all of the bonus objectives and challenge scenarios. I plan on 100%ing this game.If you're looking for a squad-based shooter a la Xcom, this is not that. There's no chance in this game, there's infinite rewinds to refine your strategy step by step. It's a puzzle game, for sure. That being said, it doesn't feel like a game where there's only one solution, it really feels like your perks and priorities will really dictate how you want to play a given mission, and that balance is extremely impressive. Progression feels meaningful, particularly by the time you get to the mid-late game and you start snowballing like *crazy* doing just an absurd amount of things. That blossoming feels totally natural and never overwhelming though.My one complaint, and devs, I would buy a DLC if it changed this, is that there aren't enough perk points to buy all of a characters options. I get that makes them crazy strong, but it's killing my inner completionist that I can't max people out.Fantastic game, a true indie gem, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game well worth full price. It isn't often that you get a complete, polished, and fun experience nowadays, but Suspicious Developments has accomplished that with style and grace.First, the gameplay is absolutely rock solid. The puzzle/strategy elements start off relatively simple and obvious, but as you gain more characters and pick which abilities to upgrade, you eventually create and execute your own unique style of problem solving in a very satisfying way. All the while, the game never feels overwhelming as the level design and progression are extremely smooth while providing a satisfying challenge. Not to mention, the deterministic nature means there's no random misses (a la XCOM) to cause your solutions to fail.On top of the already excellent gameplay, the writing was one of the best I've seen in a game. The story, full of intrigue, twists, and humor, never failed to keep me engaged and full of enjoyment. The characters were multidimensional with their own layered ambitions, and they each got time in the spotlight to develop as the story unfolded. Most importantly, what tied it all together was dialogue that was natural, witty, and brief enough to not overstay its welcome. The result was a fantastically well-written piece of work that not only complemented but also greatly enhanced the gameplay.Having played Gunpoint and Heat Signature, it seems to me that Tom Francis and co. have only continued to improve upon their game design and writing skills with each game. It's clear that Tactical Breach Wizards was a result of taking all of this experience and bringing it to the next level. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game, and I am eagerly looking forward to what they cook up next.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a good ol' 20 hours of fun, plain and simple.Encounters will get the brain thinking a bit, since even though you can rewind individual moves, you cannot rewind before a turn, so you'll often find yourself, at the very least, need to consider your options one turn ahead. Thankfully, the game communicates to you all necessary information possible, like what enemy will spawn out of a reinforcement door or how much damage an attack will do, and even if there is somehow information missing, you can just find it via Rewind.Plus, not only does going for the optional challenges add another layer of strategy you could delve into, but they do push you into how the game's mechanics function with each other, so I thought that was just a neat way the devs encourage you to synergize your team's mechanics more.The story's fine, and people who say otherwise are getting worked up over nothing. You control a group of goofy goobers trying to stop World War 5, and they all have distinct character traits and flaws, none of which obstruct the story or dialogue moments. My only gripe with the game at the moment is that if you've made a ton of moves in a given turn, but maybe want to redo your turn as a whole, your only option is just repeatedly clicking Rewind, which can get tedious when some levels can have you do up to 10+ moves in a turn. If the devs could add a rewind-whole-turn button somewhere, whether it be ingame or in the Esc menu, that'd be cool.Get it if you want a quick 20 hours of fun, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Takes the loose cannon detective character archetype from Gunpoint and throws it into an international military campaign with gameplay similar to XCOM. The worldbuilding heavily includes a unique magic system that is a joy to learn about as you progress, and from a gameplay perspective it allows for a lot of very unique mechanics that you wouldn't see in a typical tactical strategy game. It leans into this very heavily. Of all the actions you can take in the game, there are only maybe two (or three with upgrades) that are pretty much just "apply damage directly." Most abilities instead use repositioning and knockback, and you have a LOT of very clever magical methods to apply them. This system is carefully designed so that your moves can combo into each other and play off of each other, giving you a lot of flexibility with your strategy without letting you spam your way through everything. It makes planning a strategy very approachable with its generous rewind system, which would also make the game very approachable for those who haven't played something in this genre before.I had about 13 hours of gameplay for the main campaign and a bit of extra levels, but there are a lot of extra levels that I haven't played yet, many of which only unlocked after I completed the main game. I suspect they will take a similar amount of time as the main campaign. There are also optional objectives on every single level, which add a good level of replayability. On top of that there is apparently a level designer with workshop support. I think even without all of this I would still heartily recommend this game since the main campaign is very strong on its own, but I'm definitely not complaining about all the extras for people who want more.Overall this game was a lot of fun and I felt I would miss the characters and the world and the gameplay itself when I got to the credits. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, praise the developers for actually releasing a demo. It's such a simple spell, but seemingly mostly forgotten.Speaking of things the devs got right, level editor and community missions allowing you to summon even more fun. I have yet to try, but its inclusion alone is more than most these days.The fact that a game developed by a small band of software sorcerers has four times the playtime of products made by much larger and better funded circles of multimedia magi is also welcome. I was surprised when I completed the first act and saw how much more is waiting, and there is enough replayability potential to double it at least.The levels and enemies are varied, the characters' abilities fun and all of them have a place in the game and reason for existing. Yes, there are those that are objectively better than others and you feel their absence if they're not available in a given level, but I don't recall a single ability that was there just to fill space.Gameplay isn't the only thing that's fun, there's also the characters and story, the former especially sending me under the table like the Hideous Laughter spell on multiple occasions.Obviously no game is perfect and this one is no exception, with two or three frustrating sections including the final boss, but those are but small drops of bile in a big pool of uncorrupted mana.I have completed the game on normal difficulty, the challenge coming in a spike every now and then but otherwise breezed through. In the demo at least, the hard difficulty didn't deliver either.If I absolutely had to conjure up more to complain about, I would welcome voice acting, but now we're getting into the territory of things so tiny you need divination magic to see them.All in all, I'm as greedy as they come, but this is money I do not regret spending.

_childDocuments_.review: It is more joyous to do +3 damage by knocking someone into something than it would be to do +3 damage for any other reason.I think this is because somewhere, deep inside our brain, we feel as if it is the unlucky fool's fault for standing in front of a cliff,A window,A sparking exposed electrical panel,A staircase,and so on."Ha ha," we think. "Sucker should have known better."Gunpoint, famously, had enemies getting thrown out of windows.But I mostly remember Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, from my childhood. A button mapped to a kick, that gave an almost impossible snap to anyone, stumbling back, ending the fight in an instant --Tactical Breach Wizards brings back that joy, develops it, iterates it. Your abilities do not feel like puzzle pieces (as they tend to in Into the Breach), but genuine superpowers, and the game takes particular joy in making them feel like superpowers, and telling superpower stories with them - what would it really, really mean to be able to teleport into someone's place, to put them where you are? To jump out a window and fly around on a broom? To shoot someone in the head, but as like, a doctor?It tells a gripping, escalating action movie thriller with them, culminating in a multi-stage operation, with a striking visual style and a richly developed world dripping with silly puns.Also every time you defeat a level they do a punchline where two of the completed objectives are normal and one of them is silly and that's a really good joke.

_childDocuments_.review: I downloaded the demo earlier this summer and was already hooked. I bought the game two weeks ago and played for ~18h, just finished the finale (but am missing some of the bonus missions and bonus dialog sections - planning to play them all).Here is my review: + Tactical Combat: There are thousands of options how to approach a level. Positioning and movement matter a lot. Taking the right order of actions is really important and gets even trickier in the last arc. I found it very entertaining to play with the options. There is rarely a "perfect" solution, typically you have to make trade offs, e.g. between moving closer to the objective or stopping earlier to gather some mana. The "personal quest"-type bonus objectives make it extra interesting, I recommend going for them.+ Right Ammount of Difficulty: I never struggled finishing any level, not even the final boss fight. This is due to the game encouraging you to explore all the various interactions and also reverting, if you haven't thought everything through (I think it might be significantly harder if you choose to never revert). However I found it quite challenging to solve the "personal quests" for the various characters. + Theme: Really original concept of wizards doing SWAT tactics. Some of the abilities clearly reference classical fantasy tropes in a funny way (think of DND spells or abilities). + Dialogs: I found the dialog options of the characters very entertaining! You learn so much about the characters and their personality. I also enjoyed the subtle world building going on in these dialogs. Clicking through the dialogs (even the bonus dialogs with no story impact!) is really engaging. + Story: I liked the vilain(s) and the plot. I liked the character development of my wizards.+ Story Overview: Without spoilers. This game provided a really creative way of keeping track of the story in a thematic and interactive way, that I have never seen before. + Character features: The features are thematic and connected with their backstories. It is nice how they are introduced bit by bit to make it easier to learn. The level design is also quite rewarding in this regard - directly after learning a new feature, you will need it, but they never become irrelevant and are usually options to consider. I think there is only one feature that cannot be used in some levels.+ Feature balance: While playing my 18 h, I have not observed crazy imbalance between the characters and/or their features. Leveling the characters always felt like a meaningful choice. But I think, that some perks are more useful then others. 10/10, I will play through the campaign again with different perks and skins, for sure! After reading the bonus dialogs and the bonus missions. And did I mention that there is a mission editor and player created missions? I have to try them too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is both a disappointment, and one of the best games I've played all year.I haven't played much (if at all) gunpoint, but I did enjoy Suspicious' last game, Heat Signature, a lot. I hope I can make it justice someday with a proper review, but in short, all three games share quite a bit of trademarks, which include pseudo-stealthy tactical elements and providing the player with dummy OP weapons and abilities and setting them loose in multi-solution situations where they can have fun putting them to use. Tactical Breach Wizards applies these principles to an isometric, turn based squad strategy game very reminiscent of Invisible Inc. And it does this really, really, really,  well.In TBW you will advance through a linear story, sub-divided in preset levels following the adventures of Navy Seer Zan and Anxiety Survivor Jen as they try to avoid World War-- uh... (checks notes) 5! Cutting through levels meticulously designed to make the most of a plethora of skills and abilities that will be unlocked as you advance through the game. (Most) skills are really nice, and can be upgraded on top of that, giving you a lot of flexibility on how you build your team as you advance through the game, and it's pretty crazy how everything is so balanced that you can complete most of the game, including the bonus secondary objectives, with a massive amount of builds and strategies. There are no to-hit percentages, or locational damage, and you will be able to rewind any action during a turn, so while some missions can be tough sometimes, it's just a matter of finding the right combination of things to do in sequence.But gameplay aside, this game shines in the story department. Besides the fact that it is set in a world where magic users are commonplace, most levels will include a bit of banter between the characters before they start, and  single one of those is gold. They're dry, amazingly paced exchanges that will rarely not be at least snort-worthy. And this is consistent throughout the entire game. Just these conversations are well worth the price of admission and never fail to deliver. With that linear story, however, also come the negatives, and this is not as big of a problem in and of itself, but it more relates to the developer's previous game, Heat Signature. Contrary to TBW, HS was very very light on the story, but it offered a massive sandboxy universe where you could play however you wanted, with whichever loadout you wanted, and with total freedom when approaching each situation. You picked a random schmuck, each with their strengths and weaknesses, and played them until they died or retired, which provided incredible amounts of replayability and unexpected situations that were incredibly satisfying to get out of.TBW is almost the opposite: While there are many ways to resolve a situation, you will always be sure that each room has been painstakingly designed to be beaten with the team you ware with, using the abilities at your disposal. As a result, it feels much more like a puzzle game: Even though its puzzles can have several possible solutions, player expression is reduced to "do you want to play the next story mission or the next *side* mission?", changing your squad's clothes, and choosing which abilities to upgrade or respec. Which is a bit disappointing compared to the follow-up game I was picturing in my mind when I read the devs were working on a new one.The game does make a noble effort to provide a healthy amount of content, with not only the main story mode, but also opening "vr training"-like  side missions and a level editor as well. Having played it for 9 hours I have finished act 2 and a few of the dream scenarios so there is plenty to do in the game, but how much of it you will want to enjoy is highly dependant on being loaded into a challenge map with a gajillion of enemies and being excited about the prospect of finding where to move and what to do for each character for the next 30 minutes to play it.I really like this game and its story, but that feeling of "this is just a linear sequence of pre-designed puzzles" kept nagging me.Anyway, even though TBW does not reach the lofty expectations that its predecessor set, it does not detract from this very fun, very well put together game. If you are looking for a story driven, tactical, turn based, defenestration-heavy game, it can't get much better.8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Breach Wizards is already a game close to my heart.I beat the game in 14 hours. It was a super tight experience with a killer sense of dry humor ala Gunpoint. It's a little sad that there isn't more intermingling of mechanics, but each one is used well at worst. The characters are wonderful, the world building is amazing, AND each character has unique level-up upgrades and they're all super solid and do things and GOD it's just so tightly designed.As someone who enjoyed Suspicious Developments other games despite their flaws (Gunpoint's size and Heat Signature's...a lot but still fun), this is their best work by a fair margin. _childDocuments_.review: A really fun  defenestration simulator. _childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game.Has solid writing for the plot and dialogue; both feel very natural. It never takes itself too seriously but still manages to portray and discuss serious topics, i.e. mental health and global war. I went in expecting a more casual X-Com, but walked away with a deep appreciation for the thought that went into the characters and setting. The music is great, too; I particularly enjoyed how there are tracks for both the planning/dialogue before a breach, and after. If you're like me and was expecting more of a turn-based strategy game, like X-Com, it might be more helpful to think about it as a puzzle game; you can quickly rewind/undo mistakes, or reset the level entirely, without consequence. And you'll likely need to, as the mechanics can be fairly complex, with many different characters and enemies with their own unique abilities.I'd highly recommend it. At $20 it's very fairly priced. It's easy to pick up and learn, with a fairly high skill ceiling.

_childDocuments_.review: Tom Francis and team, you've done it again. Hands down my favorite game of the decade so far. Just a flawless work of art. This may strike some readers as silly, but I've never been a big fan of long-term negative consequences in games. Trade-offs and sacrifices are great, but making a gameplay mistake that continues to impact you hours later is always frustrating. I don't play games to find the  solution, I play them to find a  solution. There's no shortage of clever solutions in Tactical Breach Wizards, and you're never expected to get everything perfect. The fun is in finding a combination of tricks that achieve your goal. In this game, you don't have to nervously second-guess yourself about using up your resources-  you can use all the tools in your toolbox, and have a blast doing so. That sort of design is a throughline in Tom Francis games, and it's the reason Heat Signature was my favorite game of all time (until now). Character writing has always been strong in Tom Francis games, and this game continues to improve on that tradition. The addition of character animations adds so much to the experience, and the relationships between each character are great. The compelling story was a large part of the reason I blitzed through this game in a matter of days.I really can't recommend this game enough to everyone who's interested in strategy, tactics, strong character writing, stylistic pizzazz, and a hundred other things. Play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful game.the gameplay is really nice but the real star here is the writing.These characters, who have no facial expressions, have more personality then most AAA protagonists. Their conversations were funny and insightful, and i found myself really invested in each of them. The standard 'misfits save the day' story is elevated by some fun twists.The clever writing enforces very good puzzle and encounter design, rewarding you with thinking outside the box, fully engaging and leveraging each characters unique abilities.Finished the game in < 20h, grabbing most of the optional objective and doing only part of the "dreams" side content. could probably milk it for ~10 more hours.overall highly recomanded
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: You couldn't ask for more from a grid based tactical game.The writing is delightful, the rewind mechanism permits SO much experimentation.And man, the perks.Every one of them feels like "Are... Are you sure? That seems... A little TOO awesome. Are you certain you want to give me this?"Tactical Breach Wizards is a monumental achievement in game design.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Comparisons are odious, but Tactical Breach Wizards unfortunately walks into several, to its detriment. It's not as good as Into the Breach. When it comes to tactical puzzle games focused around moving pieces a compact board similar to Into the Breach but with a linear story with fixed levels and characters, it isn't as good as Mobile Suit Baba, even if it has a good amount more content. At least it's better than Chimera Squad.That only says so much, though. Taken as its own game, this is an excellent puzzle game with an interesting and varied set of pieces and a reasonably compelling plot, let down by a severe case Millennial writing, with almost every character being about as Whedoneqsque as they come, quipping their way through what might otherwise be a good story.The puzzles, meanwhile, are generally pretty good if you're going for optional objectives, and offer plenty of content and replayability, so that can't be faulted too much.All in all, a good game in the genre, even if it falls a little short of the best.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic addition to the defenestration trilogy. All of the characters here have charm and the writing is fantastic (typical for a Tom Francis game). Fun abilities, challenging levels, and more ways to throw a guy out of a window than you can shake a stick at makes this an easy recommend from me.And if the writing catches your fancy, check out Gunpoint & Heat Signature as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: review was written based on impression of earlier beta version of the game, it might not feature some newer details, so the game is even better than is blatantly praised belowGame is very fun, has a lot of good stuff:- Good and clever humour.- Interesting mix of magic and modern world as a setting.- Customisable difficulty you can change at any time. If you struggle with any bonus objectives you can lower difficulty to your liking. - Defenestration. Throwing people out the window is fun, and if you don't think so yet, you will grow to enjoy it!- Relatable and likeable characters, it's hard to pick favourite one.- Interesting story that, each character has their own backstory that is revealed throughout the playthrough, you might relate to something. The main plot of investigation is also not difficult to follow, partially because it also has...- Cork board map with red strings and pictures, you can move stuff around. Works as a good recap of the story so far in case you get lost with some details.- Fun gameplay with multiple solutions to same rooms. Watched someone else play through the demo and saw completely different solution to pretty difficult optional goal. There isn't just one solution to each puzzle, but it also does not mean it is easy to find one. Coming up with some plan and executing it well feels really satisfying.- While it looks like XCOM, you do not need to be worried about long term consequences of bad investments or anything like that. Every room's conditions are independent from last one. If your character gets wounded, they will be refreshed to full hp in next one. So it is more puzzle focused. - Sillyness. In every aspects of game. On some levels you might find shooting a friend a viable strategy.- Pretty good unexpected plot twists here and there, partially thanks to subverted expectations of some cliches.- Optional bonus objectives which either add to challenge, or to replayability, since you have...- Option to replay any mission from special menu, you can get better results by replaying with extra unlocked skills, or choose to replay with recommended amount of skills you have had at the time, up to you.- Fancy hats. Complete optional objectives to unlock more outfits for your wizards.- Music. Game has music. It is nice.- Bonus levels, they are optional, and if you really enjoyed gameplay, you there is free extra content for you. Which also includes...- Workshop support! You can create and play community created levels. Haven not been creative enough to create something good, so hopefully someone else of you will. *-*The level editor is pretty simple to get into. You don't even need to bother much with decorating level with different stuff, you just place for example "obstacle" into some square, and every time the level is loaded, it will be filled with different decorative items around while function wise level will be the same. Though as of moment of release it seems to be missing some stuff.- Although not a part of main game, in support pack you should have developer commentary that you can listen to by interacting with it throughout the playthrough. Looking forward to replaying the game and check it out too!If you like humourous story, or puzzle games, or games with freedom of ways to complete the goal, or cool wizards, or other games of this developer, "Gunpoint" or "Heat Signature", you should love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Wit, Wizards, Wackyness, are the core tenants of this game. That and a very solid tactical strategy game. The mechanics are solid and engaging while building on xcoms gameplay with a more puzzle solving style. Dialogue is campy and fun without feeling ham fisted or too "haaha arent I weird". story is decent and social commentary is good. Xcom for people who like Disc World.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely hope this gets indie game of the year, it's that goodMechanically my favourite tactics game I've ever played. There are absolutely endless ways to solve any given challenge and every mechanic and feature works flawlessly to compliment every other in a way that lets you solve challenges in whatever way you want, including some outright ridiculous and unique ways.Narratively one of the best stories I've ever experienced. This game balances a very delicate mix of serious, emotional, charming and goofy absolutely perfectly. The characters are just full of unique personality and charm, the humour is cheesy but not cringey or lame, like a very well executed dad-joke and it's done in a way that never detracts from serious or emotional scenes. The characters are also written in a very grounded and down-to-earth way that makes them relatable and easy to connect with, once you've gotten to know a character and gotten attached to them; seeing them struggle with and overcome not just physical, gameplay challenges but also their own mental ones is such a rolercoaster of emotions that genuinely brought tears to my eyes.I love this game with all my heart and I so wish I was better at writing so i could really do this game justice (it doesn't help that I can't talk about my favourite moments and characters without spoiling them)It was worth every cent and more, even if you're not that into tactics games please give it a try, even if it's just for the story, it's a decent challenge while not being too tricky and even has some good difficulty customisation so you can adjust it to whatever's more comfortable for youYou can tell the devs absolutely put their hearts and souls into this game and i cannot thank them enough for the effort they put in to make this as good as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the previews and trailers, I was expecting this game to be good, but it still managed to surprise me - it's SUPERB, genuinely one of the best games I've played in a long time. Not because of any one thing, but because it just does... EVERYTHING right.First and foremost, the whole concept of 'Tactical Breach Wizards' seems like the sort of thing that would be funny at the outset, but then the joke would wear thin after a while until you're just rolling your eyes at it. Tacticool Assault-Wand with shoulderstock and telescopic sights, breaching-glyphs, broomstick window-entry, yadda yadda yadda... but, instead of letting that happen, the game builds a fully fleshed-out Dungeonpunk world around the idea. A world where modern technology mingles with magic, and global geopolitics turn on access to mana-resources. It genuinely just... doesn't get old!Which is the other thing. They COULD have built this game around an excuse-plot - you're leading a Magical SWAT-team, go fight some arcane terrorists, end of line. But instead, they weave a plot that - absent the Dungeonpunk elements and stylized aesthetics - wouldn't have looked out of place in a CoD:MW game. One of the GOOD ones, mind you! Cynical politicians gambling millions of lives for their own advantage, ambitious PMC's muddying the waters, rebels fighting against the censorship of an oppressive regime... a mad dash to stop a renegade SpecOps operative from kickstarting World War 5! (Yes, this world already had four of those, just roll with it.)So, yes. A fascinating world, a captivating story, a cast of genuinely likable characters that you're gonna enjoy hanging out with and/or shipping when between missions... and gorgeous, heavily-stylized graphics that conveys the characters and the world wonderfully without needing to render every pimple on every enemy goon's face... and I haven't even mentioned the actual GAMEPLAY yet! Which, yes, works marvelously too. It may look like an XCOM-style turn-based tactical shooter, but it's honestly more of a puzzle-game. There's exactly ZERO RNG involved, nothing happens by chance, everything is predetermined, and your job is just to find a way to drive your ragtag band of arcane misfits through each encounter in one piece, while ideally fulfilling a variety of optional goals to unlock cool new costumes for them all. Indeed, it's the best KIND of puzzle-game - one where there's rarely just ONE correct solution to each 'problem'. Depending on what skills and upgrades you unlock, you'll be able to pull off all kinds of crazy strategies that the developers probably didn't even think of - and the game is built to not just allow that, but encourage it.So - grab your fully-kitted Assault Wand, strap on your camo-pattern robe and wizard-hat, and go blow in some doors like the Tactical Breach Wizard you are!

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is a masterclass in game design. _childDocuments_.review: The writing is excellent: Tom Francis's signature brand of self-deprecating British humor is firing on all cylinders.The UX treats the player with respect: You can undo moves that didn't quite do what you thought they would; you can restart the campaign from any level if there's a save glitch or something; you can adjust the difficult on-the-fly or skip levels if a level is too hard-or-easy-or-boring.The level design is perfect: The six years this game spent in development were spent well.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Ever want to play a fun turn-based enter-and-achieve game like X-Com Chimera Squad or Fort Triumph, but hate doing all that campaign basebuilding research?  Do I have a game for you.  In Tactical Breach Wizards,  Jen and her slowly growing team of Wizard Black Ops have to save the world, I think.   (At this writing, I am only in Act 2.)  They do this by entering an enemy-filled environment and knocking out or defenestrating the opposition.  If you said to yourself "Wizard Black Ops team," then I should add to that "traumatized wizard black ops team with self-worth issues covered by black humor" to give you an idea of the goofy but fun theme of the group.Pros* fun, variable ways to solve the problem situations at basic levels of difficulty.* incredibly fun writing not only gives entertaining sarcastic interludes, but also gives strong characterization to your team members much deeper than your usual turn-based team of murder hobos.  Even the enemies have depth, except Steve, the Traffic Warlock.  ♥♥♥♥ that guy!* leveraging each member's specialties is very satisfying, especially as they are strongly built for synergy.  The moment you realize that you can move X in, then move Y in and boost X so then X does something really cool is dopamine heaven.* There are a large number of added, extra scenarios built in that build no bonus experience to characters but are fun to troubleshoot.* There is no grind.  The only thing you CAN grind for is the confidence currency to unlock extra outfits, but in general I prefer the starting outfit or one other outfit for each character.  I have been finishing the confidence goals as I go, but more as a completion thing.  The confidence goals are also very thematic for the characters.* character perks are refundable before each scenario string (usually 4 in a string), so it is easy to experiment with different add-ons to a character for each string.Cons* at higher difficulties, I began to feel that each problem situation had only one or two "solutions" that I had to discover over playthroughs.* if you want a large number of squaddies to create variable groups like in X-com or Our Adventurer Guild, you will be stuck with a core team of five or maybe six by game end, and most of the way through Act 2, I still only have three team members.  (I am happy with this, but you may not be.)* If you find the humor cringe instead of black humor, you'll be skipping a lot of the set up scenes and missing much of the characterization.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, well worth the price, if you like puzzle games you will love this.TBW has amazing design on everything, the characters are very unique from each other and balanced very well, the levels cause you to keep looking for new ways to use their abilities and makes you use them in ways you don't think of, the world they build is a great setting and the story they tell in it is superb, allowing you to see deep into the characters of everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: What an excellent game! Once again, Suspicious Developments delivers. I fell in love with this team with Gunpoint, and really enjoyed Heat Signature, so I've been anxiously awaiting Tactical Breach Wizards since I first heard about it a couple years ago. It was absolutely worth the wait!The gameplay is excellent - it's tight, simple to pick up, and scales up nicely as you progress through the game and expand your arsenal of abilities. The difficulty, for me at least, was pretty spot on - challenging, but without being overly difficult. Once you got the hang of things, unlocked your full team, and upgraded your abilities sufficiently, it became more about finishing levels and dispatching enemies in style, which was its own kind of fun.Beyond the gameplay, I adored the art style and how simple and vibrant it was. The writing was also quite good - telling an interesting story that touched on a number of different ideas, ranging from mental health to personal identity to one's purpose in life. There were a few moments that were honestly pretty touching, and I thought that this was all delivered in a slightly over-the-top, cheesy way without being too much.Tactical Breach Wizards was a joy to play, and a game that I look forward to revisiting in the future! I highly, highly recommend picking it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely one of the best things I have had the luxury of experiencing. It's got the glib and quippy dialogue of the Loathing games, the tactical tinkering of games like XCOM and Into The Breach, and a heist crew to rival any good film out there with your dime bag damsels and devils. Please buy this game. Please play this game. Please tell your friends about this game. Because there won't be another one like it for a long, long time.Thank you to the Developers for creating this beautiful, action packed, hilarious experience. You deserve the world. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent dialogue, great TRPG combat with an emphasis on solving the fight instead of just smashing your way through (although you can also do that).  Not as crunchy as something like Final Fantasy Tactics, but a really fresh and fun take on the genre.  Did not expect to enjoy the story as much as I do, really interesting world and narrative that does a great job of balancing being silly and serious.  Belongs right up there with FFT, Gladius, Gears Tactics, etc., but is very much its own game.  Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant, an awesome puzzle game wrapped up in an XCom style interface, with a delightfully sardonic sense of humour.Though (sarcastically), what right does a game like this to have such a brilliant and thought out story, with characters that develop through the game (Except Steve, F Steve). Seriously, Rion's story caught me off guard, I loved it. I mean they were all great, but yeah. Cheers Tom, another hit.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly well made game. I couldn't really get into Xcom 2 as it was a little too harsh - in that game you are always on the back foot, having to plan hugely in advance, which both did not vibe with me. Here however the strategy only lasts until the room is done, removing that looming dread/fear of failure. Add to that the rewinding, foresight, etc, and playing this is a blast.I didn't enter the game expecting to be drawn in by plot - I was here for strategy. But the story is perhaps one of the standout best parts of the game for me, the writing is excellent. Not much to say here other than good job to the devs.My one small critique: the enemy's AI feels very static compared to our team. As opposed to xcom where enemies have access to many abilities, most of the enemies in this game are one trick ponys. Half of the time most of them don't reposition or optimise themselves, making fights a bit too easy. The optional objectives mitigated this, however I feel playing without them should still be fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended.Compared to most turn-based tactics games, every engagement in Tactical Breach Wizards feels much more like a puzzle to be solved. The only (potential) downside to this new paradigm is replayability. Once you've solved a particular scenario to your personal satisfaction, there's no real reason or motivation to do so again.Regardless, the game presented enough of these puzzles to keep me engaged from start-to-finish, with many more optional scenarios (and the prospect of user-generated content) to keep one entertained after the credits roll.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Gunpoint. The core mechanics were inventive, the story was interesting, and the dialogue (and the game as a whole) was sharp and got a great deal of laughs from me. I still redownload it every once in a while. I didn't even know that this game was created by the same developers, but it's clear that all the positive traits of that game are present here too. Every character I've met so far is very witty, and I find myself paying attention to what the characters are saying, something I don't frequently do in these kinds of games. Defenestration returns as a game mechanic, adding to the comedic value. The core premise is creative, blending traditional military tactics with urban fantasy into an unique visual style and a unique gameplay loop that encourages experimentation and rewards tinkering with the foresee mechanic. Another hit from this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I have heard tactics games called "Violent Puzzle-solvers" and Tactical Breach Wizards is definitely the most puzzle like tactics game I have played. With the ability to undo actions (there is a canon reason) you can refine and redo a mission until you get it perfect and achieve all the bonus objectives, but the upgrade system and variety of character abilities still means there is more than one way to "solve" a mission.What really surprised me about this game was how into the story I got. I wanted to keep playing just to solve the mystery! If you're familiar with Gunpoint you will recognise the wry wit, but Tactical Breach Wizards goes beyond great laughs to some seriously hard lines on the nature of geo-political conflicts and oppressive regimes.If you don't normally play tactics games or don't like particularly "puzzley" tactics game, I honestly would still recommend you play this just for the story.Well worth the 7 years of waiting!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little tactical puzzle game with great aesthetics and story and enjoyable quippy banter between characters. Each room that you breach is a puzzle to be solved, and they get progressively more devilish and complicated the further you get. The action is turn-based, and experimentation is encouraged by a rewind mechanic to let you freely undo one or more of recent choices, letting you try and try again until you get it right. I highly enjoyed my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I loved everything about this game! The gameplay, the story, the characters, the world, the art, the music, the writing, it's all amazing. Each mission feels like a puzzle, especially with the confidence challenges. Each character has plenty of unique skills that can each be upgraded to synergize with each other or even other character's skills. Easily one of my favorite games of all time. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I kept hearing this described as a tactics and puzzle game and the puzzle part had me hesitant. Tactical Breach Wizards is hilarious, fun, and not punishing to the player. The ease of backstepping once you understand the goal for the room is not only easy, but part of the fun. This is really special one.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Every aspect of the game is really well designed to actually be fun to play. The rewind and preview mechanics make experimentation very easy so you'll never get frustrated feeling that a plan went wrong because of interactions between the various combat mechanics. The tactics elements are really well designed around these features, allowing for a great range of ways to approach missions and it's really satisfying when all of the powers are set up to work together well.The dialogue is also fantastic throughout and the characters are far more endearing than I initially expected from the genre. The optional objectives, challenge missions, and player-created levels also add a lot of replayability. Definitely a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, had to force myself to stop playing.  Almost called off work to keep going!Gameplay presents itself as Xcom-like but to me it felt more like a puzzle game.  Rewind and try different combination of tactics and team skills until I found the perfect approach to clearing each room.   Incredibly satisfying resetting and finding out a room I struggled with could be cleared in a single turn.The story, writing, and characters are excellent, with the witty dialogue catching me right in the strike zone.Highly HIGHLY recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend this game.On the gameplay side of things, this is a game that has absolutely no RNG, responds quickly to your inputs, wastes little time with showing moves and attacks that happen in a turn, and thus feels very snappy to play. It starts feeling like more of a puzzle game with each room being a puzzle that you have to solve when also trying to complete character specific challenges, and it honestly feels great. The best features of the combat is that the game never lies about the information you get and that save scumming is essentially removed entirely by the ability to foresee enemy actions and plan accordingly, while also being able to rewind time on a step-by-step basis, letting you play with a scenario as much as you want to get the result you want.On the story side, the way I would describe it is that the setting knows its silly, but it takes itself seriously when it needs to, and so it comes across as very genuine and interesting. The characters are very like-able, the plot makes sense, but the twists and very smartly written dialogue, as well as the random bits and pieces of lore about the world that characters will bring up in conversation, makes this world fairly believable and fascinating to learn about. As an example, a podcast about anti-tank warrior monks is mentioned, and that concept and mental image alone is fascinating to think about.It's genuinely the best turn based strategy game out on the market because it doesn't follow a bunch of rules that are usually seen in these types of games, like having an actually interesting story with neat twists, using NO RNG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, always giving the player all the information they need to make informed decisions, never lying to the player, and not wasting time with overly long animations that are the same whether you've seen it one time or a thousand. More games should be like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: An urban fantasy themed light tactics game.  Checkers to X-Com's chess, fun and challenging without the stress of cascading failures potentially ruining dozens of hours of a campaign.  Many typical tactics game features, like rewinding turns and side missions, are incorporated into the narrative.  The writing is reminiscent of Hitchhiker's Guide - witty humor, sometimes a bit dry, very British.  Only a couple hours in, but there's some interesting lore and backstory backing it all up.  Art style is somehow detailed and minimalist at the same time, with characters and scenes offering many clever small details.Not everything is for everyone.  Check out the demo or some gameplay videos before committing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game that's well worth the money. The writing is charming and often laugh-out-loud funny, and the game itself is profoundly generous with the amount of stuff on offer. No end of bonus missions, optional objectives, outfits to unlock, and so on. It all comes together for a very polished experience from start to finish.If I had anything to quibble, it might be that on Normal difficulty, the game was a touch too easy for much of its run (especially early on), but this was easily fixed by trying to get all the bonus objectives on every mission as I played. I'd consider this a necessity for getting the most out of the game, and leans into the game's strengths as more of a series of puzzles than, say, something like XCOM. On the whole, a minor criticism.If you're at all interested, I'd highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely one of the best games I've ever played, I couldn't be more happy with this purchase. I've played through the whole of the main campaign and a decent chunk of the bonus stuff on the recommended difficulty (which took me ~30 hours?) but I cannot wait to replay this on something harder. The characters and the plot have me in a death grip and I have a horrible need to get as many people as possible to play this game. Tactical Breach Wizards is absolutely worth more than the 20 USD it costs and I couldn't be happier that I got to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Whenever a strategy game comes out, it is always immediately compared to XCOM. This game is not as difficult as XCOM, at all. It is, however, a blast to play. Without spoiling anything, the characters are incredibly interesting both in personality and skill sets. Mission tone is defined both by your enemies and the team you get going into each breach.The game is wonderfully paced with dialogue happening before and between missions and breaches. The story pacing is very engaging. The banter between allies is fantastic. The optional challenge objectives really force you to think of how you can domino your moves to complete all of them in one match.There are many strategy games that use a rewind function within or without lore to ease players off of save scumming and some of them even complicate the mechanic. In Tactical Breach Wizards, your ability to rewind is both based in lore and incredibly responsive. This encourages you to try and handle each move you make smarter than the attempt before without stealing away the immersion and engagement from the round itself.After you exercise your brain to complete a breach, you're drawn back into the story and reminded of the purpose you're doing each puzzle set. I find this to be very well done. Each breach gives you just enough time with each character to derive their personalities and motives without overstaying it's welcome. These scenes are all also skippable if you don't want petty narrative getting in the way of your attempts throw everyone out of windows.I didn't quite finish every challenge in every level, nor did I complete every challenge level. I did finish the story, and complete as many challenges as I could the first time I came across them.I thank the developers for creating this game for the world, and I am excited to see what they create next.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game!With the levels pretty short clear times (5-15 min a map) it feels more like a puzzle game than a tactical group-shooter like Xcom. Which I think is a good thing!There are a lot of optional challenges, I haven't completed yet and I estimate that I could probably fill another 20 hours with those.I also enjoyed the writing: I'd describe it as a parody of a Tom Clancy novel with pun-prone wizards. Pretty fun but engaging and well-paced.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: good game similar to into the breach, it is more forgiving but still has a difficulty curve. the story is good, a lot of soft successful worldbuilding. the dialogue is witty and doesn't feel like an afterthought or filler or a means to an end. characters are well rounded and don't feel flat. skill trees are interesting and new abilities/characters are unlocked throughout the story so that gameplay feels fresher. haven't reached the end yet, though

_childDocuments_.review: If you like strategy: If you like puzzles: If you like witty dialogue: If you like throwing things out of windows: If you like other Tom Francis games: If you like none of the above:  This sits next to Baldur's Gate 3 for my most anticipated games of all time. When this game was just a store page with a tech demo video, I got super excited for it and shared it with practically everyone I knew. When the game got a demo, I immediately played it (thouroughly) and recommended it to practically everyone I knew. When August 22nd came, I sat on the store page refreshing until the game was purchasable. Like BG3, at no point have I been disappointed by this game.Tactical Breach Wizards is very unique, and in a  way. The gameplay is novel, but flawless, the visuals gorgeous, the characters and story witty and (somehow) compelling.While the game is primarily a story-driven experience, there are muliple upgrade paths and a level editor, allowing for significantly more than the advertised 14 hour campaign.I firmly believe that  should experience this game

_childDocuments_.review: It's a hilarious game. The writing and setting are funny. Basically D&D in a modern setting. I had a great time. The difficulty keeps up with the skills you unlock. You're never insanely OP unless you play with all unlocked characters. The (gameplay) synergy between characters is great.All around recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game listed on the store page, it was an instant buy—and I sure wasn't disappointed! The most strong part of Tactical Breach Wizards is definitely the titular wizards. Each character is extremely distinct and has well-thought out abilities; each level is designed to further push the tactical limits of each wizard, allowing the player to discover something new up until the very last level. The game is so funny and fresh that I guarantee you'll crack a smile every two minutes you play—if you don't, you should probably just go ahead and ask Jen to defenestrate you. Check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is the strategy game I've be waiting for. This game is really funny, the humor is on point, and it does of course have some serious moments. The puzzles are awesome well thought out. The amount of time put into this game really shows and i loved every minute playing it.About the humor: I loved the 4th wall breaking and how it makes fun of itself at times. Good laughs all around and a lot of jaw drops. I've now got my wife playing and getting all my friends to play it as well.15/10 would highly recommend if you love turn-based strategy puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since I was hooked on writing in a video game but my god I loved every bit of dialogue the game threw at me. The combat scratched the tactical/strategy/puzzle itch I'd been looking for and I appreciated the ability to skip every level if I wanted to (luckily nothing was too hard that made me want to skip but good to have as an option nonetheless). All in all a fantastic game that I wish did not end.Definitely gonna check out the rest of the defenestration trilogy!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun!In TBW, you play a couple of wizards and witches to tactically breach through rooms to a compelling conspiracy with some nice twists; I haven't completed the game yet, but as of now I wanted to write a review anyway.The characters are pretty compelling; everyone's an adult who has various stages of has-it-together, but as far as I can tell, no one really has it fully together, and the main characters are decently complex with their own demons to fight. The dialog is punchy, and I've found myself chuckling quite a bit.I originally thought being able to rewind time during fights would make the game really easy, but it turns out fights are still tricky, and I often find myself looking at each round to ponder moves. Sometimes I'll go "wait, but I can tweak this more" and then rewind, and that round ends up better for it.And once you unlock more perks, the game really opens up; I surprise myself by how much I can move, or how much stuff I can do in a turn, as I'm unlocking things.Very recommended if you enjoy tactics games, and even if you're not particularly great, there's very distinct difficulty modifiers if you find it too hard (adding an extra action per turn, etc.)
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of my favorite games I played this year. It is definitely closer to Into the Breach than Xcom which was a concern of mine going in, but the way the characters synergize with each other in combat is brilliantly executed. The writing is genuinely funny too! Can't remember the last time I said that about a game.It you are remotely interested in turn-based strategic combat and wonderfully written characters then you have to play this. Simple as that.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A satisfying tactical experience with some of the most fun writing I've seen in a while. The infinite rewind system means you really have free rein to try the silliest strategies you can think of, and when they work it makes you feel like a genius. The last third is a bit wobbly and doesn't quite stick the ending, but I don't regret playing through this for a moment.Extremely solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, there's really just one thing I SPECIFICALLY love about this game. Like, the game's fantastic in several regards, but good GOD do I love the free, unlimited rewinds. Actually tactically playing out your plans instead of mentally crunching numbers and remembering every niche interaction is SUCH a blessing.Can't quite remember the angles needed to defenestrate a man? It's okay, just rewind until you figure it out. Don't want to crunch the numbers on how hard you're hitting a guy? Just hit them, and rewind if it doesn't work out. Did you accidentally place Banks one tile too far to the right, you stupid idiot? No. Never have I ever misplaced someone and had to rewind 10+ times to fix what was once a funny haha step into this room maneuver. Definitely.Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the art style & the writing, an endearing cast of characters in such a short time. Tactic puzzles with quick iteration via rewind are so good to work with, it was very rewarding to finally find a perfect solution to a battle that initially looked impossible.An awesome third game in T France & crew's series of defenestration games.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm seriously enjoying it!The gameplay is tight, focused and just challenging enough to require you to think about what you're doing. You are encouraged to experiment and find creative solutions to every encounter. Each character is totally unique and bring essential skills to the team.The story is engaging and detailed but the game still manages to maintaini a gameplay-focused pace without overly long needless exposition or conversation. The worldbuilding is also really neat- a really interesting take on both traditional and modern ideas about magic and how it would fit into existing societal hierarchies. Absolutely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is a funny, smart and very playable game that sits somewhere between a tactics game (move your team on a grid and use abilities every turn) and a puzzle game (no dice rolls, interesting ability overlap, small precisely-designed challenges). It really smartly takes the best out of both of these spaces, and creates a game that feels really enjoyable to problem solve in. Ability upgrades and new enemies constantly make unusual combinations possible, and each mission has bonus challenges that stretch your understanding.I particularly love Tom's writing in the game, which is funny and fast-paced. It tells a really good story in an engaging way, and it feels written in a way very few games are at the moment. I played the game several times during testing, but it still makes me laugh reading jokes I've seen four or five times. I really love this game, and I think you should check it out even if you wouldn't play a game in this genre or that looks like this normally!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great writing / music, fun and challenging combat puzzles, and an incredibly well designed + polished game.Blown away that this was made by 5-ish people.Is a steal at $20 and recommending it to everyone I know.If you enjoy XCOM-like games, puzzle solving, engaging combat, magic, incredible world building with great / funny dialogue, or any combination of the above, don't hesitate to get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a great game. It somehow manages to provide bite-sized tactical challenges with increasing complexity and difficulty without constraining the player to a single "best" solution. From the begging to the very end the game manages to keep this feeling of constant improvisation and adaptation, providing multiple options to get through the levels. It just feels great to play. And the story keeps up, with witty and playful writing, fun characters and simple but satisfying plot.It's one of those games that really knows what it wants to be and whose every little part fit together seamlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the campaign after 17 hours. I wholeheartedly recommend this game. The gameplay and puzzles really rewards creative thinking, and I felt like I was always finding new interactions to take advantage of. The writing is also amazing. The characters are all so unique and fun, and the dialogues are witty and hilarious. I was laughing after every scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to shamelessly copy another review that convinced me to buy this game for full price in hopes that if someone reading this is on the fence, it will sway them towards getting it.I love the writing.I love the story.I love the art style.I love the blend of Into The Breach/Xcom/Doorkickers gameplay.I love the challenges, the unlockables, and the other things that lend this absolute gem of a game more replayability.I hate Steve Clark, Traffic Warlock.Breach?Breach.

_childDocuments_.review: absolute banger of a turn-based strategy game - this is what you get when you take a classic like XCOM, and cut out all the annoying fluff like hit percentages and whatnot, while layering on innovative mechanics like the rewind (No need to savescum anymore :). Add to that a fun story with fun characters, and what comes out is probably the best game in the whole genre.My only two additions to the game would be:- an increase to the level cap, so after multiple playthroughs you could come into Rushwater PD with every perk and make Clark soup on the wall, because that's funny.- More of this, I'm shamelessly begging for a sequel or a DLC even though I have no idea how that would work (I'm no game developer, haha)
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.It's not hard, but it's still fun, engaging and sometimes demanding. Some additional conditions are pure puzzles with one right answer, but in most cases player have a lot of freedom.Story is good, dialogs are great (great and funny), characters are interesting and likeable ( <3 Dall ).Optional maps and map editor are another pros.Enough with reading comments! Just buy and play already!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards
