_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the story but haven't quite got all the confidence points yet (bonus challenges on missions to unlock cosmetic outfits). I had a great time, and I'm probably going to start a new game to try some of the other dialogue options.Loved the gameplay, tile- and turn-based made it feel similar to games like Shadowrun and X-Com. The variety of enemies and the perks you'll unlock through the game keep things interesting as you try to find the right combos to clear the room before the end of the turn. In-line with the previous two games, throwing people through windows is a core mechanic, and finding ways to chain movement powers to launch a goon into space is lots of fun.The story is also very well put together. It's linear but you have a variety of dialogue options (usually at least one of which is sarcastic) and a selection of epilogues. The graphics are simple but clean, and you'll see a lot of different environments throughout the game.The full game is a lot more of the same stuff you see in the demo, with enough new additions throughout to keep it fresh so it doesn't feel like a slog. If like me you enjoyed the demo then you'll almost certainly feel the game is worth the price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute masterpiece. It's surely in my top ten games of all time. The overall story, the characters, the writing, the RPG-like progression, the experimental gameplay (rewind time for no cost at any time, as often as you want), the sound design, the gameplay... it's all absolutely mind blowing. I wish all games were as slick as this.20 hours for my playthrough. I didn't maximise all the optional "Confidence" boosts, but certainly replayed a few levels to get it fairly high. I also didn't play any of the optional dream missions, so there's plenty more content if you dig into it.Buy it, play it, then be cursed to compare all other games to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and simple tactical game. The rewind mechanic makes things very forgiving when you're first learning how to play. Combat is focused around using knockback alongside direct damage to deal with targets which i find is a really fun way to handle enemies. The missions can be a bit easy but the inclusion of the optional challenges in each encounter were very fun and for the most part not annoying to do. Each of the characters are fun to play as especially once you start to unlock upgrades for each. The focus around knockback as a form of damage really helps everyone's abilities to synergize with eachother and make really fun plays. I enjoyed the story as well as the characters personalities and dialogue too.The only problems i have were i wish you were able to unlock every ability on each character. i dont see why we're limited on upgrades, especially when some upgrades are very negligable. I rarely ever used Zans illusion and only unlocked the ability for it to interact with things towards the end of the last act. the only times i needed it were when i left zan exposed in the middle of the arena with no cover to complete a challange. The other issue i had were some enemies in act 3 which were resistant to all form of attack you have unlocked at that point (knockback resistance, armor for direct damage, and gasmask health which makes you immune to debuffs). The only way to deal with these enemies early in act 3 is to chip them down slowly with 3 abilities. Fortunately by the time they become common you've unlocked characters and abilities to deal with them better.  over-all very fun and short game for those that want a break from the BS of x-com or to just try out more strategy oriented games
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend it strongly enough. The game has absolutely phenomenal writing and made sure I didn't skip a single cutscene or even cut any of the dialogues shorter than they could be. It's both a narratively strong game, and strongly narrative game—it manages to make you connect with the characters and plot despite theoretically the only character work being essentially talking head cutscenes. The difficulty was just right, and the various combination plays and the like mean that it's going to be one of the few games I actually end up replaying after completing the main story.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best turn-based tactics games I've played.  It feels satisfying from the start, and manages to continue integrating new mechanics and giving you new tools in a way that keeps things fresh and invites experimentation all the way through the final mission. Which would be enough to make it a very good game, but it also comes with an engaging story in an interesting sci-fi/fantasy setting, and writing that's very funny but still manages to land sincere emotional moments.The kind of game that makes me want to go play everything the developer has ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: where to start? This game is easily my favourite game of this year. I found myself literally laughing out loud at every turn. The art style is unique but does not distract from the fun puzzles tickling my brain at all. The story had enough twists to keep my interested but not too many to make me lose the plot. And the little missions where the characters reflect internally and learn Better self worth lessons are a Chef's Kiss. I would give this game all the Thumbs up if I could give more! _childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the breach wizards, stayed for the compelling story and characters. Everyone can praise the puzzle aspects and they're genuinely very good in that "we know what's going to happen, let's prevent it" kind of way, with a great mix of challenge and just the raw ability to skip a level if you just cannot. The game opens up a lot once the rest of the team gets pulled in and it's actually outstanding how much flexibility you actually have once you realize your options.But the character work and the heavy spy/political thriller vibes were absolutely not on my radar. I really enjoyed the writing and how much 'personalisation' actually went into the game's mechanics to make them not only work for gameplay but be important story beats. It makes the entire universe feel very alive and real when the abilities your team has in combat are referenced and even part of the narrative structure. It feels cohesive. I finished it in 30 hours doing most of the unlocks but not really going for completion and i can genuinely say they /flew/ by and i managed to enjoy my time. Heavily recommended if you're any sort of inclined towards tactical and puzzly turn based strategy games with a strong narrative and character-focused core.To note: I may be biased but i've been following Tom Francis for a long time and have been waiting for this for literal years.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a treat. Very rare that I finish a puzzle game and *want* to go back and try more. TBW is pretty compelling both in terms of gameplay and narrative. Like if a TTRPG party was a SWAT team. Loved that the game plays more like an evolving puzzle rather than an RNG tactics game. Everything will always hit and its up to you to manipulate the environment through careful sequencing in order to set up some massive dopamine domino arrangements. Very accessible without being hand-holdy and presents plenty of options to refine how you want to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Turn-based puzzle tactics! 10/10.Easily one of my favorite games this year.Good:- Genuinely varied cast of characters.- Rewind feature promotes experimentation, but doesn't trivialize the game.- Witty dialogue, got a number of good laughs out of it.- Visuals are great: despite the choice of a semi-low poly modeling style, the detail put in each environment and even the menus is fantastic.- I've lost count on how many defenestrations I've committed.- The game hasn't crashed in my entire playthrough, something you could easily take for granted, but which in my experience isn't common.- Controller support is good. I got used to the cursor quickly, despite it seeming a bit slow at first.Bad:- Nothing that I can think of.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Cool, fairly unique aesthetics blending fantasy wizardry tropes with tacticool police brutality, EXTREMELY well polished on release by today's standards (probably thanks to a large amount of alphas and closed betas), good setting, very solid writing, interesting game mechanics that relies very little on RNG (no 99% chance to hit here) and clearing rooms is quite satisfying to pull off, especially when that's by a hair's breadth.The game has no failed states beyond the current encounter: no XCOM ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ where you've got to restart entire campaigns after a couple bad runs; so don't be afraid to play on Hard even if you're terrible at puzzles/tactics (I know I am).halfway through the last act and I can tell that yeah, it's very good
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a fun game similar to Into the Breach, or Xcom without the miss chances. With time wizardry, you can redo your turns over and over until you get the perfect setup, or you can just go for it full ham and blast enemies out windows or into traps and more. Endgame has so much ability usage that there's dozens of ways to clear out enemies the best while still challenging you with different ways to play the game with optional objectives.Writing is snappy and amusing, yet with some depth to the story. Would definitely recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Just good game, made not for money, but to tell a story. Great non-vulgar humor, creative idea, good puzzles (includes player's missions), convinient and polished control. Gameplay is just like in Into the Breach, so maybe not for everyone. But i bought mostly to find out story, jokes and of course to support talanted people.

_childDocuments_.review: Review Edited at game completion, total runtime 11h and change. Absolutely outstanding. Game oozes character, the writing is superb, the band of misfits all feel unique, the worldbuilding is delightful and never forced upon you - it's just there, and the little glimpses at the setting are great. The art style is great, with beautiful little animations. Soundtrack is superb. Core gameplay is somewhere between a turn based strategy game and a puzzler. The levels are all handcrafted, and if you're going for the Confidence challenges you'll usually be executing quickly or in a certain way which again feels more like solving a puzzle. And any game that captures 100% of my attention for 12 hours straight must be doing something right.Strong recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem!Some of it reminds me of Into the Breach or Invisible Inc but the abilities you have here are often more interesting and can be used in a variety of ways to solve a level.Also, I wouldn't have expected this from a game like this but the dialogue and story writing is just delightful.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game a lot during the Beta and loved it, and the full release plays even better - it's a very polished game that you can tell a lot of thought and passion has gone into. It's a very slick, easy to get into but plenty deep tactical game, with a witty and well told story.The game mechanics are introduced at a very satisfying but gentle pace, the story is told via some very clever narrative aids (such as the classic detectives pin board where you have to link clues together with red string - very satisfying). The art style is lovely, and there is no shortage of content even without replaying anything.This isn't usually my preferred genre of game but it's tied all so well together it's impossible for me not to love it. So don't knock it until you've tried it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Turn-Based Defenestration Action. Without question one of the funniest and most entertaining games I've ever played, up there with Disco Elysium for me in terms of back to back jokes that make me laugh. There's only so many ways I can praise the writing, the characters are just so charming with their own quirks and personalities. I can't even write much about it it's just really great writing, nothing more to say.Really charming and cute art for a really unique and fun world idea. Seen a lot of "what if military and magic existed side by side" but "what if military aesthetic and traditional fantasy melded together seamlessly" is a new one. Everything about the world is really brilliantly designed to meld these two things perfectly. And when I say "seamlessly" i mean seamlessly. You have a bunch of guys in modern military gear breaching and clearing rooms with modern architecture and devices, but they're equipment and tools all have a fantasy element that doesn't look out of place or strange in the slightest. Nothing feels like it's too absurd or silly for whats going on beyond the intentionally absurd or silly, it all works really well together. The gameplay quality is exactly what you expect from Suspicious Developments at this point, slightly different from before but still holding their signature hallmark. The closest game I have to compare it to would be Into the Breach with its emphasis on positioning enemies and rewinding turns to get it right. (Only replace the various environmental hazards that instantly kill bugs with windows.) And just like Into the Breach it is an incredibly satisfying game to learn.They constantly remind you that you do not have to stress over getting confidence challenges first try or all at once, but every time I'm about to give up and say "ah i'll come back for that one" I figure out a combination I hadn't considered before and everything clicks. I have only unlocked 3 of the 4 characters and they are all a blast to play with unique and interesting toolsets and upgrades, and i'm excited to see what the fourth party member brings to the gang. While each character has a lot of unique tools, none of them on their own are particularly complex to understand. This is perfect because the emphasis is on the way they all interact and it has so much nuance no situation ever feels too simple or complex. You can always see the end goal and how to get there, it's just a matter of working out how to move everyone perfectly to get in spots that will let you fling them out of windows most effectively. All in all i'm still going through it and I have no question this is an all timer for me. It's encouraged me to finally go back and try out the first game in their Defenestration trilogy, as Heat Signature was another all time fave for me but that's because i'm a big space geek so I hadn't really had the drive. After playing this and to support the studio I will for sure be checking it out and keeping a close eye on whatever games they release, and eagerly await their next installment in Defenestration based gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It plays more like Into The Breach than an XCOM game when it comes to the combat (No RNG to hit rolls). Really though, the game isn't that hard on the base difficultly but the real fun is trying to complete all the optional objectives for each map. The game ends up feeling more like a chill spatial reasoning puzzle game than a hardcore tactical combat game. There isn't really a fail state in the game, you just rewind the last turn if you somehow let your characters die.Can't same much about the story, I really haven't been paying all that much attention to it. There is a conspiracy theory map minigame where you're connecting strings to stuff on a map that is made more annoying for not paying attention to the story. I think it's a fun idea but really if you are there for the story then it feels like more like a reading comprehension test than an interesting game mechanic. Doesn't ruin the game though.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I typically don't enjoy turn based games. At least I used to. This game has had me re-examine my view on an entire genre of gaming. The amount of skill expression and wacky moves in this game is ridiculous. 100% worth the time and money. The skins, and the reason you need to "unlock" them in the first place in just amazing. The WizTac outfits all look so clean, too. I love this game a near indescribable degree, although whether that's just me being bad at writing is debatable. The world building is just awesome, but I'll avoid spoiling that.I'm running out of synonyms for awesome just talking about all this stuff, so let me say this. I love this game. If you like games that make you feel smart as hell, strong as hell, and, you will like this game. It is worth the money. Also I just noticed this, but DEFENESTRATION TRILOGY. IT'S CALLED THE DEFENESTRATION TRILOGY. Every second makes me love these devs more.|| SPOILERS FOR: The game's ENTIRE playable cast. All of them. This assumes you've completed the game. Proceed with caution. ||Banks is a fantastic character, all her moves are fantastic. Ways to knock back armored enemies? Yes please. The only source of healing in the game? Lovely. Portable window for Jen to obliterate people with? Give me 2 uses of that, please!Rion is another great one. Dealing extra knockback to armor? How about just destroy it entirely? Becoming a dog! Knockback, but in reverse! All amazing.Dall's whole move-set makes me happy. An unlimited range charge that scales with how long you travel is so rewarding and interesting. Censer slam is the opposite range of the spectrum, and just looks so brutal. Teleporting yourself anywhere you can see has made my brain hurt countless times, and made me say "Hell yeah" just as much.Zan's prediction shot and ability to make a fake 6th member of the team reward being smart and calculating enemy actions. Needless to say, I love these so much, even if I'm stupid half the time. (Just rewind lol)Finally, Jen. Oh boy, did I have fun with her. 90% of her kit is knockback, and the fact that most levels have open windows of some kind combined with that (Also death's door) allow for amazing opportunities.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is a strong contender for my favorite turn-based tactics game. The characters interplay with each other so well, the ability to rewind move-by-move to the beginning of your turn is great for trying things out, and I love any game that counts your defenestrations in the after-action report. Really pulls out the stops to help you feel big brained.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Not an X-com style squad tactics game. At least not enough of one that it'll scratch that itch for you. It's more like a puzzle game using the structure medium of a squad tactics game.There's no macrogame or significant squad customisation outside of a short list of ability upgrades. You're locked to the operators you meet throughout the linear story who are in turn locked to their abilities. Fortunately the puzzle gameplay is also really quite engaging and I'd bet you'll enjoy it whether you're a puzzle OR squad tactics enjoyer.The core gameplay is room breach and clearing. Each room is a puzzle to be solved. How can you clear all the hostiles whilst completing the side objectives with the tools available. Clearing each room is quite easy on its own, the side objectives are the meat of the puzzle.On top of the puzzle gameplay is an engaging story and amiable cast that are fun to watch banter and progress through the story. If you have been on tumblr in the last 10 years and enjoyed the experience then you'll probably like the writing in this game
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely fantastic! It's got the strategy of XCOM or Into The Breach, but with a heaping dose of soul and light-hearted characters. I played it for the puzzle, I played it for the characters, I played it for the plot, I played it to see the next way they were going to evolve the mechanics, and I played it to unravel the mystery. It's clearly a passion project, you can feel the love for the medium and the fun the developers had oozing out in every scene. Thank you, devs, for sharing your love and passion with us, and I'll be there for the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Not really what I was expecting - this is actually more of a turned based puzzle game and less of a turn based tactical combat game. With that out of the way: it's GREAT! Very clever puzzle design, amazing theme and characters, actually funny dialogue if you're into this sort of witty sarcastic humor (which I very much am)... Feels very close to those bonus levels on Persona 5 Tactica, where you have to use your skills to reposition, push and pull enemies and objects to achieve your goal.Really really good, just know what you're getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: I have put hundreds upon hundreds of hours into XCOM, Xenonauts, etc and I say with confidence this is one of the best tactics games out there right now. The abilities unlocked as you go are extremely powerful, but it feels like you can unlock them in any order and still solve the puzzle of each mission. The optional missions and objectives are tough as nails and very satisfying, but are never pushed on you and are utterly optional. It is also, I think, the funniest game I've ever played. The writing is , causing me to actually laugh out loud more times than I could count. It keeps the humor strung throughout every aspect of the game, from mechanics to dialogue to mission debriefing. Despite taking on some heavier topics, the game is also written in such a way where the author isn't beating you over the head with any particular point of view, rather letting the characters do the work in a way that feels honest and allows you to decide how you feel about the story. The only downside is that it is fairly short. I beat the main story and a good amount of the endgame content in seven and a half hours. I suspect I could get another 3-5 out of trying to get every single optional objective done. After that, you'd just be replaying to see what happens trying to unlock abilities in different orders. Long term, I hope a DLC adds some longevity to what is a gem of a game that deserves an incredible amount of success. This was a labor of love, and you can feel it in every pixel.Editing in: I played the whole game on Steam Deck, where it played like a dream!

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this game. It's a great puzzle tactical game, with a good sense of humour. The characters are very endearing, and have a great chemistry together. _childDocuments_.review: My favorite game of 2024, hands down. The gameplay is kind of like XCOM, but with so much more personality—it's clearly made with skill and love. The difficulty ramps up at a reasonable pace, where you probably won't struggle too much in the first half, but playing around with different skill combinations, upgrading, getting new outfits, and watching the story unfold keeps it engaging. Then, the back half really starts to bring the challenge.It took me 29 hours to finish, but I could have done it faster. I kept restarting to try and nail all the side objectives or just to do things in a more fun way (lots of people out of windows). For a combat game, it has a surprisingly nonviolent streak, but it doesn’t feel childish at all. I also love the military/wizard art style—I've never seen that before, and I’m all in on the mix of assault rifles and wizards. This game has been such a pleasant surprise, something I didn't know I needed.I can’t believe these are the same people who made Gunpoint and Heat Signature. I really enjoyed both of those games, but compared to this, they had no story or personality. The developers have really come into their own. I’ll keep an eye on anything else they do, and honestly, even if this is the peak of what they accomplish as a studio, they’ve done something amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. I can't possibly be unbiased because I adore Tom Francis' dev logs, and loved both his prior games (Gunpoint & Heat Signature), but this is easily my game of the year.The gameplay is most similar to Into the Breach, but much looser. For instance, some abilities aren't locked to the grid, and the difficulty is much less finely-tuned to make every single encounter feel only-just-winnable. But neither of these things are to its detriment—I actually think difficulty is where TBW shines brighter than any other tactics game I've played before (and I've played a fair number).This is thanks to the "confidence" system. In short: every mission has one or more optional confidence challenges for you to complete. If you complete enough of them, you can unlock new outfits for your team members. There is zero gameplay benefit -- no additional experience, items, whatever -- for completing these extra tasks. Just some slick new skins, and the satisfaction of knowing you did things The Hard Way.This is, for my taste, perfect, because it means I can self-tune the difficulty of each mission depending on how I'm feeling at that exact moment. If I'm firing on all cylinders, I am absolutely spending 20 minutes on a single stage to get every last challenge down. But if I'm underslept or stoned out of my mind and want a breezy fun time, I can just do the mission regular-style.Thing is, most missions are ~pretty easy~ if you're familiar with tactics games and you eschew the confidence challenges. I like this system of totally-optional non-gameplay-rewarding challenges so much more than, for instance, the time-based challenges you get in a game like XCOM (complete the mission faster, get a better reward). This lets me chill out when I want to without feeling like I'm missing out on anything.I will shut up now, but I should mention before I go that the writing is absolutely stellar. I forgot how much I missed Tom's dialogue writing from Gunpoint. This is the best comedy writing I've seen in any game, ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh hey, new Tom Francis game, it's been a while. In Tactical Breach Wizards you follow a growing squad of wizards, witches and a cat (you cannot control the cat), who work together to breach rooms and knock out everyone inside them, each with their own unique style of magic.The game is played in turns, first you get to move your wizards and have them cast spells, then enemies get to react to your moves. You can rewind every move in your current turn, whenever you messed up something or didn't plan well. Before you commit to end your turn, the "foresee phase" will show whether your wizards will get hurt by enemies or will be safe. You're encouraged to experiment and see how things turn out and aren't stuck with any mistakes you make.Combat largely involves "knockback", a simple mechanic at its heart. A spell that does X amount of knockback to an enemy sends them flying X tiles in a particular direction, usually depending on the angle you cast from. If they hit an obstacle, the remaining knockback is taken as damage. If they hit a window, the window breaks (also they fall through it and cease to be your problem). Much time is spent pushing enemies around, keeping the dangerous ones away from you and trying to not get hit yourself. Every level is a hand-crafted encounter that feels like a puzzle where the solution is finding the best way to make the environment hurt your enemies. Many will seem overwhelming at first, until you think outside the box and discover a nifty opportunity or a neat trick you didn't see before.There is no randomness involved in the resolution of moves, you have all the information necessary to know how things will turn out. Not unlike chess, it's all up to how well you can plan ahead and exploit your environment.As the game goes on and enemies become more dangerous, your crew and toolset will expand. New characters bring along their own unique tricks, opening up your tactical options. Each excels at a particular role, some are good at pushing everyone around, others are better at support and making tougher enemies more manageable with debuffs, which makes them more vulnerable to attacks; then there are some that are just really good at moving around the map. They all play very differently from one another and have their own strengths to master, though they are introduced throughout the campaign one at a time, so you won't get overwhelmed and can slowly get used to them. All levels have optional objectives you can try to complete that require making the most of your squad's abilities to pull off great feats. They help a lot with learning some of the hidden potential of your wizards that you may not have realized at first glance. The reward for your characters is simply some costumes which have no bearing on gameplay, so if they become annoying or difficult to do, you can simply skip them for the time being and come back later whenever you feel like it.The progression of what characters and spells you have available is strictly determined by the story. However, you are rewarded with perk points between missions, which allow you to upgrade spells in small but significant ways. There isn't an overwhelming amount of them, and they all feel worthwhile. You can't unlock all of them in one playthrough, but still enough to make your spells significantly more useful.The campaign progresses strictly linearly (outside of "dream missions" which are optional). There is plenty of dialogue between the main cast, usually about the mission at hand, but sometimes also just about plain personal things and the past. A lot of the dialogue is funny and very tongue-in-cheek, but the characters and the world itself still feel genuine and well thought through. Sometimes you get to pick a dialogue option to get a different flavor of a conversation, but there aren't any long lasting decisions to be made.I've been waiting for this game for a long time and it's been worth it. It plays quite differently from Gunpoint or Heat Signature (both of which I love), but it still very much tickles that part of my brain that likes to indulge in experimenting with weird strategies that end up working surprisingly well and making me shout out loud "WAIT I CAN DO THAT??"Honestly I've been struggling to think of anything resembling a flaw really. The game is just realized so damn well. It's a good example of how far you can take mechanics that are simple at their core and make them shine through amazing level and encounter design. What elevates it to greatness for me are all the little moments in the story that I don't really want to spoil for you.Tyrannical Beach Witches is easily my favorite game this year so far, and I am almost kinda sad that I will probably be done with it soon. It is easily worth its full asking price, and when my money situation allows it, I am probably gonna grab the special edition at some point as well. I will have 15 years before Tom Francis releases his next game anyway, so I probably won't be in a rush.

The story of this game is exceptional with several interesting turns, it has very few plot-holes. Every protagonist is well thought out and deep, every line of dialogue is exceptionally written. _childDocuments_.review: I've been following the design and production of Tactical Breach Wizards since it was first teased, something like 7 years ago. And while I really enjoyed that process, I expected that, like Heat Signature before it, I would end up getting more satisfaction from watching the sausage get made than the sausage itself (even though Heat Signature is a game I enjoy a lot).I'm so happy to say that this game blew away my expectations.. It's so packed full of thoughtful, interesting design and clever writing, it's amazing. I'd say I don't know how they did it, but I do know how - they worked on it for 7 years. So I'll just say that the work shines through and it's brilliant.Let's start with the boldest and most successful design choice: infinite, instant rewind. This expands on the already generous rewind ability in Into the Breach, making it even more universal. After taking any action, you can rewind to the instant before taking it - or before the action before that, or before that, or so on, right until the beginning of turn. You even get to rewind after enemies act, seeing exactly if and how you left your squad vulnerable to them. Until you click that big red "End Turn" button which sends in another wave of enemies, everything is reversible.On paper, this seems like it would either take all the teeth out of the game's difficulty, or result in endless analysis paralysis, or both. But in practice, it frees up the design space delightfully. Enemy and level designs can be impossibly difficult on first blush, because the designers know that only the player's very best effort is going to count - there won't be any obvious blunders catching them out. And for the same reason, as a player, you can play with reckless abandon. Instead of studiously tabulating every variable in an impossibly complex mental model, you just put your plan into action. Want to see if you need two hits or three to kill that enemy? Don't do the math, just play it out - if it doesn't work out, a couple snappy clicks will rewind time and let you try something differentThis infinite CTRL-Z combines with a set of powerful player abilities to create an extremely expressive tactical combat system. Each ability and upgrade your squaddies get feels monumental, the kind of thing that would get derided as "OP" in another game, and then they get *stronger*. Jen can zap enemies out of windows; then she can zap multiple enemies at the same time; then she can zap twice as many as that; then she can do it *for free*. And the game's permissive and experimental attitude lets you fully explore all the possible implications and combinations of every ability. "Wait, if I push this guy left, then swap him with my heavy, then put put an interdimensional death portal behind him, then chain lighting through these other three guys, I can finish this level in one turn!" <- Sentence said while playing this game.Again, this might make the game seem too easy, and indeed, I was often finishing levels in 1 or 2 turns. But the ability to do that felt like a creative choice. Did I want to do the easy simple thing, and complete the mission in 3 or 4 turns, or the complicated cool thing, and finish it now? And the complicated cool things I came up with felt wholly my own. I would bet that every player who finishes the game has come up with a unique solution to at least one of the game's stages, especially the later ones. And even my abilities felt unreasonably powerful by the end, another player who clicked with different characters would have a different set of unreasonably powerful abilities all their own. That high-power-ceiling approach also allows the game to throw enemies and scenarios at you that, by the finale, feel insurmountable when you first approach them. But because you have so many strong tools at your disposal, and you can freely play with them, you can defeat impossible odds and feel truly accomplished for it.With all that, it seems kind of unfair that the writing in the game is as good as it is. The military action thriller plot is genuinely good, with believable (albeit occasionally over-glib) dialogue. While the game's concept started out as a parody, it doesn't feel that way. This is a silly world, and the people inside it recognize it's silly elements, but it's the world they live in and they take it as seriously as anything. And every fantastical element of the gameplay ties back into the plot in believable, consistent and often integral ways. The infinite rewind is not just a UI conceit - it's the central ability of your main character, Zan. Your team doesn't just forget that Banks, the necromedic, can revive people from the dead just because the scene has switched from isometric tactics to a dialogue diorama. It's all satisfyingly grounded, and culminates in a truly exciting final act, with surprising and poignant plot twists, and a mission that both in the fiction and in the gameplay requires every bit of skill and ingenuity the player and the squad can muster.There's so much more that I could say (I haven't even mentioned the great art style orthe cool conspiracy-board map system) but this review is 900 words long now, and I could be playing the game instead of writing it, so I'm going to stop now.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is probably one of the best games I have ever had the pleasure of playing. The story moves at a breathless pace, but it takes the time to flesh out and air out every characters flaws and the facets of their highly developed personalities. While the game starts out straightforward, funny, and simple, it very quickly shows that it isn't pulling any punches when it comes to mechanical or moral complexity. The writing in this game is sublime, and on top of hitting like a truck in some occasions it has easily the funniest one-liners and general dialogue I've ever read in a game. Perk choices are intensely meaningful to your playstyle, and can unlock amazing possibilities in nearly every breach whether it's for style or survival. On that note, the challenge of the game is perfectly tuned to whichever difficulty the player wants to seek out. On top of general difficulty settings to make the game easier than the intended experience, there are dozens of challenging puzzle levels for every different squad composition, and every single room in the game has multiple challenge conditions that can earn you points for aesthetic customization of the agents in the squad. That's not to mention the full level-creation suite and accompanying Steam Workshop support. This game stands as on of the great indie titans in my mind, and I will look back on my time in Liboli, Medil, and Kalan with as much fondness and respect as I can muster. One day, I hope to one day return to the world that the team at Suspicious Developments has created, because hearing what they and the people they've written have to say about the world both real and fictional has made me very proud to have experience their game.

_childDocuments_.review: Into the Breach is one of my favorite games of all time, and I think it represents the high-water mark for turn based strategy. Since it came out in 2018, no other game has really come close to scratching that strategy itch that it so perfectly tattooed in my brain.That is, until I played Tactical Breach Wizards. This game is the second coming, and I could not be more onboard. I could wax poetic on about how amazing the characters are, how laugh-out-loud funny the writing is, how perfectly the game ups the ante in story and challenge and complexity. But what it all comes down to is this: the gameplay is incredible. Its that same thrill, that same cascading dopamine rush of carving out the absolute perfect turn in the chaos of battle during the moment it mattered most. I haven't felt that rush since playing into the Breach. Frankly, I never thought I would again. But I'm so happy I got to experience it, and my time with this game was an absolute joy. Tactical Breach Wizards is simply perfect. 11/10 and my GOTY.

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game. The tactical part is a wonderful little puzzle box style tactics game, and the writing is absolutely incredible. _childDocuments_.review: Never would have considered myself a turn-based tactics game fan before this game, but Tactical Breach Wizards made me one. Probably due to the forgiving gameplay that turns mistakes into hilarious accidents and encourages you to try out different combinations and skills in unconventional ways. The gameplay is so smart, changing the scale of "fail or succeed" to "fail, succeed or succeed more flashily and hilariously." The characters are immediately endearing, the art is stylish, the writing is hilariously clever, the skills are smartly designed, the premise is entertainingly ridiculous. Honestly Suspicious Developments games have always been such a steal, but I do think this game only shows how much the team is leveling up. The only downside is I can't play as the cat, but I guess as he's not a wizard and shown no skills in tactics or breaching, I'll let it slide.

_childDocuments_.review: The tactics in this game are really solid. In general, you are doing some combination of damaging enemies or pushing them into environmental hazards. As you play, your characters automatically unlock powers at certain milestones, and they do a good job of teaching you how to use them. Some of the powers are really creative and open up your options a lot with effects like same turn revives, bouncing projectiles off of walls, and transferring damage. The progression system takes this further, with most of the perks modifying your powers in very unexpected ways. There is a spell that lets you send a holographic decoy for distraction, but a perk that lets the decoy interact with objects. This really changed the different ways I could clear a room. The more I played this game, the more I surprised myself with the different options, and I loved unlocking new characters or powers. By the end, it's almost overwhelming how many different things you can do, and yet every power feels unique with little overlap. The graphics are fun but simple, and makes it easy to tell where everything is, which is important to me in a strategy game. The music is not particularly remarkable, but serviceable. I think they went out of their way to keep it from blaring in your face, and I respect that decision in a game where I'm mostly scratching my chin and considering my next move. But I wouldn't mind if some of the menu or between-mission music had more going on. Most of the time you're not in a mission, you're reading dialogue. I feel like I have to talk about the writing at length because it's a big part of the vibe. This game has a LOT of breaches, and every breach begins with a dialogue exchange just outside the door. The writing is trying to invoke an overall vibe of a quirky and non-serious group of exceptionally talented people that, for the most part, have no conflicts with each other. Even if a character is openly disinterested in giving their full effort to the life threatening breach you are about to initiate, the most any other character will do is roll their eyes. As a result, this game has a bit of Tumblr syndrome. Everyone feels broadly painted with a brush of sarcasm/laziness that makes them kind of blend together. Here is an excerptPerson 1: "Tell me that skull isn't Gary!"Necromancer: "Does this skull look like a Gary to you?"Person 3: "I firmly believe anyone can be a Gary." Here's another excerpt with names. Jen is apparently a fan favorite based on the Beta, even though her only real trait is being the MOST sarcastic. She's half a pen stroke away from saying "I don't want to do adulting today." Jen: Oh my god, now I'm sad about Limp Arms Guy!Banks 2: I was never not sad about Limp Arms GuyZan: Should we breach this door and stop World War 5 or should we stop and write a book about Limp Arms GuyJen: *has to think about it* (Yes the game actually says this)Jen: Breach I guess. EVERYBODY talks like this. Sometimes it works but, for the most part, it just feels like none of the dialogue is character driven: It's quip driven. Characters trade off either being the straight man or stupidly uninterested in what they're supposed to be doing, which is weird for a game about breaching doors. And with no voice acting, they become even harder to distinguish. On the plus side, dialogue is short and does not overstay it's welcome. Some of it is even optional. This kind of quirkiness extends to the general plot, and makes me disinterested in it. None of the main characters have anything to disagree about for fear of souring the onslaught of quips, which makes their side of the story a non-story. The main villain is a very powerful wizard, but for some reason, one of her main goons is a pyromancer whose fire isn't hot enough to burn anything. The game jokes about this a lot. Why is the main villain hiring someone so underpowered? It was a funny bit. Lots of things in this game are just a bit and nothing more. I would care less if the game was consistent with its characterization, but every once in a while it will turn on a dime and ask you to treat a character like the badass they are or read someones deadpan monologue where they unnaturally spill their one and only character motivation. After convincing me not to take them seriously, it's hard to accept these bits as anything but unearned story fodder. Despite those flaws, there is a refreshing earnestness to the writing. We're in an era where it feels like a lot of movies and games are so determined to be in your face with colors and gags to set themselves apart from the traditionally stuffy and self-serious IPs of the past. It's almost cynical how quickly Borderlands-esque comedy has been co-opted by anyone without an original thought to write about. This game doesn't feel like that. It feels like they made something they wanted to, and their spirit really comes through in the writing, which I appreciate. All in all, I recommend the game for it's excellent tactics and light-hearted vibe even if the writing sometimes bothers me.

_childDocuments_.review: I wishlisted TBW as soon as I heard about it and bought it day of release. I was attracted by both the premise and the goofy looking mechanics. Gameplay wise the game is both fun and challenging. I haven't played too many games similar so I can't tell you how the mechanics compare to say XCOM, but the game allows for various approaches to each room. You can be as forceful or intuitive as you prefer. I especially enjoy the "Confidence" challenges, these are sub-objectives that can be completed for cosmetics, theres no rush to do them as you can replay any level once you've unlocked it and can replay later after youve unlocked more perks or in some cases even switching out what characters you use to further diversify the levels. Game runs great and really makes the most out of its artstyle. I've noticed some slight hiccups when exiting a level midway through, but no crashes!Where the game suprised me was its story and characters. At first the characters just seemed witty and fun, making decent jokes and having funny exchanges. As the story progresses you actually got some more depth out of them. It still keeps its light hearted tone but the characters are very dynamic, making you actually care about their development and want to root for them, Overall, a new favorite. You can tell the devs put a lot of love into the game and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Demo, and was thoroughly impressed. It's safe to say the full game lived up, or exceeded, my expectations. This game is fun, with enough challenge that you get to experiment with strategies, but still forgiving enough for it to still be fun.The Story is interesting enouigh, to get you hooked, but short enough to not get bored of it. And the world building is fun and immersive. I feel the tone of the game and story to be comedic if at times satirical.Overall this is a fantastic game, and probably one of my new favorites.

_childDocuments_.review: I hadn't seen much on this game before its release but after just finishing it, i have to say, what a blast! the writing was entrancing. i was hooked from start to finish! and every characters was dripping with personality! i couldn't help but laugh at every joke and feel remorse for every flashback, truly loved every character! (even steve clark) the story was just as good and the little breathers of physically piecing every information together between the major missions was a nice break. the puzzle of solving each encounter while grabbing the optional objectives was an excellent challenge of your understanding of each ability. i only missed out on a few objectives throughout the whole campaign! the gameplay itself was fantastic, with each ability came a new way to solve the problem. only one or two scenarios truly made me tired of it when trying to accomplish everything in one go, but the game says it can be done later with new abilities, so thats on my stubborn-ness. the outfits were also fantastic! bravo to the costume designer. i had so much fun switching costumes and seeing them in the cut-scenes! my only gripe is wishing there were more!Characters - 10/10Gameplay - 9/10Level Design - 9/10Writing (of characters and story) - 10/10Overall - 9/10if you enjoy games like gears tactics, x-com etc. i can't recommend this game enough! extremely enjoyable experience and one i will encourage others to try and definitely one i will be revisiting myself!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more polished games in the genre, the attention to detail is evident in:* The cinematic exposition on every level,* How every level is constructed like a puzzle with multiple avenues of arriving at a solution without being able to brute force your way out of it,* The tone of the writing captures the genre and is completely skippable if you just want to focus on the tactics,* How characters have their own niche and builds,* How the game plays it "fair" by telegraphing its actions,* Lots of bonus content/stages that enriches the story if you choose to participate, but does not deprive it from players who want to skip it.Also one of the most difficult/challenging final missions that requires you to think tactically (and thankfully the game gives you mulitple undos to test out your strategy).

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review the game is sitting at 98% positive, so I'm not so much trying to convince you to buy the game as I am creating a historical record showing that I also think this game is great.  This is a master class of a tactical puzzle game with the best dialogue I've read in any game in years.  It's up there with Portal 2's writing for me.It's so indy it doesn't even have voice acting, but like any great book, you'll have voices for these characters in your imagination in no time.  The premise is very stupid in exactly the ways I like, with various types of magic spells being treated just as seriously as machine guns.Obviously puzzle games with a narrative focus aren't for everyone, but this one tackles deeper topics than you might expect.  It's a geopolitical romp that isn't afraid to talk about drug trade, PTSD, proxy wars, religious police states, and child abuse.  I laughed a lot more than I cried playing this game, but it's worth noting that I did do both.Just like the recent trilogy of Shadow Tactics, Desperadoes 3, and Shadow Gambit, this is a game where save scumming is baked into the design, and like Shadow Gambit there's a narrative reason why you have infinite tries to solve any puzzle.  You might expect this to feel high stakes and be stressful because it looks like a SWAT sim, but using chain lightning to defenestrate a wave of terrorists in this game is as chill as doing a Sunday crossword because you can test every outcome without a penalty.You probably already guessed, but this is my game of the year for 2024.  It gets harder and harder to be a successful indy every year, so finding this degree of success in the current market for a team of this size is as implausible as expecting a ragtag team of hedge witches to take on a multinational PMC armed to the teeth and come out on top.  Completely unrelated spoiler-free metaphor of course.

_childDocuments_.review: It's my first Tactical game that I really played and absolutely loved. Being able to rewind because of a small mistake instead of having to completely restart the entire mission and I love that every mission is made with separate rooms that you can revist with different characters to experiment with abilities and earn more confidence points to buy outfits!!!I'm only playing on Normal and have been trying to accomplish every goal, and it's been alot of fun! The achievements are also fun, yet sometimes infuriating, if you're into achievement hunting. At first you'll end up making some stupid mistake like killing a hostage and it gives you an achievement, but then further down the line they get a lot more complex and "out of the box"... like having a specific upgrade and using it in a weird way.The game is alot of fun and awards you trying different methods. You have to think outside the box... and I think that's what separates this game apart form other tactical ones ^^
