_childDocuments_.review: After Gunpoint and Heat Signature, I fully expected this game to play well and tickle my brain in certain ways. What I wasn't expecting was a story and characters that matched up to if not surpassed how incredible the gameplay ended up being. The missions are bite-sized enough to play in short sessions, meaty enough to really dig your teeth into, challenging in ways that have you engaging with every facet of every mechanic, and forgiving in ways that a story-focused strategy game ought to be. The characters are lovable and layered in their own ways while also bouncing off of each other delightfully. The writing is a fair bit quip-laden, but not in a way that's groan-inducing, heavy-handed, or un-earned. If anything it juxtaposes perfectly with the rising stakes of the story and reflects the coping mechanism of laughing in the face of insurmountable stress that a lot of us in our 30's seem to rely on. The protagonists have strong tabletop RPG energy in the best way, and I was compelled all the way through to learn more about them, watch them sort out their issues, and see where they ended up. I went into TBW expecting a fun tactics game and ended up playing what, at this point, is my 2024 Game of the Year.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest, I was NOT expect the level of narration or gameplay that was delivered. This game is insanely well (and funnily!) written. Every character has unique and interesting abilities that no others have, allowing each team member to complement each other very well. Bonus points for using my favourite word; defenestration.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's a brilliant cross between squad tactics and puzzle games, with witty writing and clever level design. If that sounds like your niche, it's definitely worth the full price.I've had this wishlisted since forever, I remember liking the premise and the setting. Got it on release, not expecting a lot but curious. The first thing that you'll notice is of course the writing. It's snarky and actually funny, but also personal and introspective when it needs to. The characters feel realistic, each with their own motivations and struggles. The plot is interesting and thought out, I could see this being a movie, especially with the whole "military x wizards" setting.The gameplay consists of moving the squad and using their abilities to create interesting combos, with unlimited "undo" per turn to explore wildly complex strategies that you couldn't do in a usual game of the genre. The difficulty curve is just right, easy even, if you don't want to go the extra mile for the optional objectives. But they are set up in a way that motivates you to do them, and rewarding if you achieve them with a clever strategy. The level and enemy design is equally clever, varied and complex enough that every level feels completely new. It can get a bit repetitive as there's no other kind of gameplay between levels like base management or other meta-strategy, but that's ok, potentially material for a sequel.Overall, if you're into something more deterministic than XCOM with well written characters and plot, leaning more towards the puzzle genre, give this a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: For me, honestly a game of the year contender. Great characters, all with very funny and clever dialogue, a very refined gameplay model where each character's abilities fit and mesh together, and people getting thrown out of windows. It runs on my tin can laptop surprisingly well too, and I didn't encounter a single bug in my 17 hours.I haven't tried any of the player created levels yet, because if I keep playing this bloody game I'll lose all my friends and hobbies.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly as good as I expected when I first saw it announced. Which is to say, very good. Couldn't put it down once I got started. It's less of a tactics game than XCOM, more towards the puzzley end of the spectrum. It's closer to Into The Breach, but with larger, hand-crafted levels and linear character progression.It's not too taxing difficulty-wise, unless you aim to get all the optional objectives on the first run through. Each level feels like a sandbox for you to have fun in while trying to achieve an objective, not an intricately-crafted puzzle with just one solution to discover. You can go back and replay any mission at any time, and optional objectives only unlock cosmetics, so you're not missing any of the game if you breeze through the levels.To top it all off, the characters are great and the dialogue is legitimately funny.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't do any of the extra non-story missions, finished in 10 hours. Still worth it. Suspicious Developments is a real mark of quality. Plays more like a puzzle game than a strategy game; wouldn't call it better than XCOM, nor worse. They're very different. More forgiving than Into The Breach, just... I don't know, man, it's its own game. It's cool. It feels good to play. Have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface that I usually don't like these style of games, well no, I've always liked them in theory, but when I sit down and play them they usually don't keep my attention and I quit in under half an hour. Tactical Breach wizards is simply the best out of this genre of game, the combination of fun gameplay and pretty funny characters and dialogue really elevates the game. Can't wait to finish the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the game play, stayed for the writing. It's a genuinely hilarious and interesting story that had me invested from start to finish, and I would honestly be happy just to read a book written by whatever brilliant story writer these guys have on staff.The gameplay itself could probably use a little more tuning. For example, the Confidence goals often felt poorly thought out, and I had to mess with the custom difficulty to change number of enemy spawns and what turns they arrive on to make them even achievable in certain levels, but it was overall a fun way to spend 20 hours.Zero re-playability, though. The story is far and away the leading reason to play, and it is a very linear tale with a clear beginning, middle and end.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible play! The characters are so well written, the mechanics are fun, and the pacing is set so well that nothing feels rote or stale. As with games where I come to love the characters, I always wish for more, but this studio did such an incredible job telling a well thought-out story and every character had impact. HIGHLY recommend to anyone looking to sink 20ish hours into a realistic fantasy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is great, though the comedy lessens the more it goes on. It plays pretty well on Deck, though you only get about two hours of battery life on an original, non-OLED Deck. And it's super-fun, satisfying to go for extra mission goals, and pretty accessible for replaying past content. The only complaint is that the mission select (from the main menu only) basically resets the game in terms of perks and progress, and you'll need to replay your latest mission to get back to where you were previously. It's an absolutely minor detail, and only there if you're trying to replay the intro mission (which, for some reason, can't be replayed).
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the demo, i knew this was going to be good. You know, the GOOD good.-Simple, yet charming visuals, with many different aesthetic designs between levels that keep each one of them fresh. The low poly looks of the characters make me think a lot about OSRS, for example. (this is a good thing, for me at least)-Amazing story that keeps you hooked until the end, with many plot twists you will not suspect. The kind of story that makes you go ''Well now i wanna know what happens, another level it is.'' (And then another and another and...)-Incredibly well written characters. Many colourful personalities, resulting in a wonderful cast of people full of depth and/or little quirks that you'll love them for, even the ''bad'' ones. (Looking at you, STEVE)-A great deal of humorous moments, whether it's deadpan or just silly. Not too much to fall into cringe levels, but just enough to stay interesting and make you crack a laugh from time to time. (it's Wizard Spec Ops, how serious can it be?)-Superb gameplay with just enough brain-scratching. The bonus objectives make every level turn into a puzzle that is aching to be solved. The mechanics are fun to use, with every character feeling unique (All the different abilities and perks really make the possibilities endless)The only thing left to say about this masterpiece is that it was worth every penny i spent on it. With the free demo, you really have no reason not to give this amazing game a shot. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to really expect when I first saw the game on the storefront, but it's hard to deny that the name "Tactical Breach Wizards" is one of the most eye-catching titles I've seen in a while and with the overwhelmingly positive reviews, I had to try it. On the surface, as someone who doesn't really play puzzle games or turn-based tactics games, I honestly thought I'd play it, not like it and then refund it and move on. However, as I kept playing, the more interesting the puzzle aspects of the game became. With the variety of ways to deal with enemies and confidence points to help you think about situations more, the deeper the gameplay loop got. Every character has their own specialisation, their strengths and weaknesses and every character has some sort've way to synergies with other characters. My personal favourite character is Zan, as by using False Prophet I can easily clear both doors and objectives without going out of cover, I can also use it to drag aggro from more vulnerable characters that might either be out of cover or already injured.The characters themselves are phenomenal as well and the only thing that I can even complain about is that I wasn't given nearly as many conversations as I thought I was going to see. None of the main cast are annoying, they're relatable with having realistic struggles with their own doubts and fears, they feel human. My favourite character in terms of personality is Dall, out of all of them. Not only do I find her beliefs fascinating, but her own anxiety dream  pulled at my heartstrings.Overall I'd give this game a 9.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly fine puzzle game that can almost be mistaken for a tactical strategy if you're new to the genre. As long as you don't expect XCOM levels of tactical freedom and can tolerate high amounts of millennial banter (which constitutes about 80% of all dialogues), it's not the worst thing out there, even if a bit on the easy side.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the long wait.It's more of a puzzle box than a turn-base tactics game, especially if you want to achieve all the optional objectives in a single run. The story is great. Conflicts are engaging and writing can be humorous or serious as the situations call for.Took me about 20hrs to finish a playthrough while doing almost all the optional objectives, not counting the optional challenge missions. For this kind of game, I think it's sitting at a pretty good length. Wrap up nicely and doesn't drag on for far too long.Looking forward to what they are making next.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the funniest writing in a video game I've seen in a long time. Genuinely laugh-out-loud funny, as long as it's your type of humor. (It's very off-the-wall silly, which isn't everyone's cup of tea.) Far as the gameplay, it's pretty fun, but this is more of a tactical puzzle than it is XCOM, so make sure you're expecting that. The characters all are very well-defined both in terms of personality and in terms of ability set, and you can replay missions choosing the characters of your choice. My only real complaint is that controller support mostly feels like an afterthought (it mostly emulates a mouse cursor with the joystick, rather than snapping on the grid, etc.), but it's still controller-friendly enough to be played that way.All in all, solid contender for GOTY for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially a perfect game to me. My personal game of the year, probably a top 10 all-timer. Every piece of it is clever and impeccably designed. Even the credits section!- Very fun puzzly tactics; it provides so much freedom and so many cool abilities to get through each encounter.- Extremely player-friendly; lots of UI reminders and recommendations. The core design clearly has player fun and empowerment as a primary goal.- The script is razor-sharp, and the characters are incredible. Clever, constantly funny writing.- Exposition, world-building, and overall plot are communicated so well. The red-string board sections (where you connect people and places with goals and motivation) are such a lovely way to reinforce the story beats.- I love the "Confidence" bonuses (optional "achievements" to aim for in each encounter). I will finish them all!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy tactics lite games, wizards, low magic settings, and oodles of dry sarcasm, you will love This game does not mess around. You're into the action immediately, tutorialising is both short and very aware, and the writing, OH MY GOD, the writing. Sharp, clever, and incredibly funny in an understated way. So good.Art style is spare but it doesn't need to do any more than it already does. Information is easily understood, and the game brims with complexity even as it is ostensibly simple enough to understand at first glance.This is a stellar game, and while I obviously haven't finished it, I am willing to stake whatever reputation I have on this. Even if it may have post-launch hiccups, it's already smooth enough and I trust the dev to fix things as they need to.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards just has it all: insanely good and imo perfectly challenging gameplay, an interesting and actually well craftet story and fleshed out characters who interact in witty and occasionally very funny dialogues. Honestly just buy this, even if it's not on sale, the game is just that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Really quite outstanding. Gameplay is great. It's a small numbers tactical rpg with a high focus on testing different combos and orders of operations. Some tactics games in this vein can feel like puzzle games: where there is one successful solution that you have to find. This game threads the needle perfectly between problem/puzzle solving and improvisation. From a story perspective, this game is great. It's a very fun urban-fantasy setting. The plot is tight. The characters are all very interesting from start to finish. The game is pretty funny, but comedy is extremely subjective. The dialogue is very snappy and genre aware without fully breaking the fourth wall. The game also has multiple story segments that inform the combat in extremely interesting ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best writing I've seen in a game in a long time. The story is interesting and engaging, with hilarious quips throughout. The gameplay is also really fun - it's like puzzle Xcom. It reminds me of Into the Breach as well, with managing knockbacks, status effects, and environment hazards. A lot of levels have multiple methods of solving, and each character feels uniquely powerful. My only complaint is the limited respecs given, since you might want to try a build out and then realize you don't like it. At least this can be partially solved by trying the build in a challenge, where respecs are free.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game does so many things right and I became obsessed with it from the moment it started. The gameplay itself is incredibly addicting - it's like XCOM Chimera Squad but with zero RNG, more puzzle-like gameplay, and tons of wacky abilities with a huge broad spectrum of applications. Every single wizard feels useful, and you can build their kit however you like, and each mission has a plethora of challenging but fair bonus objectives that earn you sick drip as the optional reward.That alone would make this a solid game but the writing and story are just so top notch. It doesn't take itself TOO seriously and every character is a joy to see onscreen, and the writing is witty and painfully hilarious. But it knows when to pull back and punch you in the gut with emotional character moments and somber plot beats. You're fighting to prevent a brutal war from breaking out by stopping a band of ruthless mercenaries... and then one of the recurring bad guys is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ walking traffic cone with the power to summon GHOST TRAFFIC. And then outside of the main campaign there's a TON of extra content in the form of bonus missions to really flex your mind and see how far you can push the magic system. Now that I've beaten the main campaign I can't wait to get back into it and play all the bonus content.This is an easy 10/10 game for me, pick this up the moment you get the chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is a bit of a puzzle game disguised as a tactics game. There is no RNG in this game, both in combat and in level design. As such, the game is basically always "Solvable" There are never unpredictable factors, and the game lets you rewind every step. It literally wants you to win, but it also wants you to figure out  to win. There is some side content like challenge stages besides the main story, as well as a level editor, so if you enjoy it, there's plenty more to dig into. I really loved the writing in this game too. I loved the dialogue and how the different personalities bounced off each other. They managed to put in some character development into the game itself, and the characters were consistently funny to me. I don't think the designer/studio is known for making sequels or add-ons, but I would love to keep following these characters through more content.I had been looking forward to this game ever since the first piece of concept art was teased (not sure if they had even decided on it being a game at that point?) but wow, this game exceeded my expectations and I wholeheartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A great lite-tactics game in the vein of Into the Breach. Solid dialogue, very focused on comedy and character psychology! I really quite like the way they tie character progression into unique puzzle levels taking place in the dreams of the various characters, and the game often surprised me with witty bits of dialogue and human moments of stupidity that made the competence of the characters feel grounded in just enough imperfection to feel right.It reminds me of a time when smarmy horsemanure was fun, socially aware, and refreshing rather than an overbearing crutch used by hack writers. It manages to walk that fine 2000s nerd comedy line that, while certainly not to everyone's taste, will be more enjoyable to people with a taste for good banter.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of this game, really enjoyed playing through the story and am loving going back to try to nail all the challenges. Characters are great, good writing and story. Game play is excellent. Fiddling with how to approach each turn is such a rewarding loop. Art style is lovely, the universe is a great take on magic users. 10/10, looking forward to whatever these folks come up with next. No matter how long it takes em.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes a game just nails it. From the concept to the art style, character design to dialogue, moment-to-moment gameplay to the overall pacing, TBW just gets it right. This weird little $20 game is so charming, so creative, so well thought out, so filled with good ideas that I can't recommend it more highly.The whole world concept is brilliant, and the game knows you don't care why there's wizards everywhere so it just keeps on chugging along. The characters have clear and interesting design, visually unique and lovingly animated in both cutscenes and their attacks (my favorites are the disciplined precision of the Seer's Breach and the wild enthusiasm of the Witch's broom re-entry). The banter is snappy and heartfelt and very funny while still feeling natural and like it's not trying too hard. The game itself is turn based tactics on a grid, so very XCOM or Wartales, but the tools it gives you are much more exciting and the levels much shorter and punchier. Each mission last juuuust long enough for your plans to satisfyingly click into place, then it's on to the next one. It never outstays it's welcome, always leaves me wanting one more. It's paced more like Portal than a combat game - very precise and less-is-more in it's philosophy. Overall, it's the most immediately engrossing game I've played in a long time. I'm only in Act 2, so looking forward to more.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It's more like Into The Breach than XCOM. When you use a skill against an enemy, it's a guaranteed hit. No 99% and then a miss. You are encouraged to use the environment to kill the enemies, but environment kill is not the only way like Into The Breach. You can rewind any actions before committing all actions of the current turn. You can play with different approaches and see which one works (or which one works best for your play style).
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A total blast. Enjoyed every second of it and laughed wholeheartedly at the beautiful jokes. Wonderful characters, an engaging story, incredible and innovative ideas for powers and abilities... and all of this is just the cherry on top for the best thin in the game, the actual gameplay. The amount of options available to the player is unbelievable, opening up a thousands of different possible ways to beat a level.Even after 13+ hours the game doesn't feel stale nor repetitive, and I'm constantly discovering new ways to use the character's abilities. Definitely buy this. It's fun enough to be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing, for under $20 it was totally worth it. I Hope they make a DLC or a Sequel or anything & i'm playing it day one. This was a labor of love and you can tell in the product. The studio nailed this, with the story, the style, the game play, and the overall depth of the characters.  10/10 indie Game of the Year
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It's great for what it is and is clearly a well crafted game.The game-play loop is solving tactical scenarios, reading dialogue, developing your characters and tracking the conspiracy story on a virtual story board (which is an interesting touch that helps you keep track of the nuanced story).  Scenarios are very forgiving and puzzle like.  Each level is carefully hand crafted.A lot of variety to the mechanics and many satisfying combinations are possible.Cheesy yet well written dialogue that doesn't take itself too seriously and is surprisingly enjoyable.If it sounds appealing, the demo gives you enough to tell whether you'll find it compelling or not, so give that a shot first.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I got the special edition on sale, and I have to say, it's well worth the cash. The game-play is simple and easy to understand. The objectives are straightforward. It is intuitive and really desperately scratches that tactical game itch by using a "breaching" game with magical wizards that use modern military tactics (along with the humor). The writing if this game, it's narrative pace, along with the development of the characters are more alive that even some of today's AAA games. All in all I have played almost 24 hours worth of this game, and it has nothing but been the best. Definitely recommending this one especially to people who like to play tactical shooters like Xcom with the rich and ever dynamic storytelling. It was worth the wait (yes I had this on my wish list for awhile), for you can really feel the love the makers of this game put in it, because for the first time in awhile, I have genuinely fell in love with a videogame again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal game. Took me about 14 hours to finish, but I haven't cleaned up all of the optional content yet. Challenging without being frustrating (Thanks to the rewind mechanic & confidence goals), writing's a joy, and throwing people out of windows never gets old. Probably my game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: There are 6 acts of showing love:Words of affirmation.Quality time.Physical touch.Acts of service.Receiving gifts.Defenestration. (verb. the action of throwing someone out of a window)Like Gunpoint, Tom Francis & co enjoy to ravel in player experimentation: The dynamics, emergence and immersive moments of interplay between clear rules interacting with one another while allowing the players to always take a (literal) step back to reevaluate and trial-and-error your way to a solution that make you go 😏. Don't let its tile-based, turn-based coat fool you to believe an XCOM hoodlum to be underneath. With the probability gunk thrown out, TBW is more akin to a sokoban-puzzler nerd and I absolute adore and respect it for it. While some of the dialogue and character writing can be a bit too quippy for some peeps, I found it to be earnest in its cheeky and goofy nature. Dotting clues and reading in-character notes about every happening, the banter before breaching and even the post-level summary jokes all make this game feel just swell and somewhat light-heated (which is a very weird thing to say since the game also features a western coup against a foreign theocracy). Wizard Ops is as hell of a cool concept and I am glad they actively drifted away from the cop- / military propaganda you would default to in that situation.With that said, I wish they streamlined/polished some of the "content-throughline", as some stuff just feels oddly placed and a tad bit undercooked (Like the chats and dreams just being there on the wayside - just odd). Me when the game has a narrative-twist moment told through mechanics 🥰🥰🥰
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with really decent writing, great humor, fun cutscenes and a lot of QoL.The tactical combat itself can be tought of as a puzzle (if you want to earn outfits by completing challenging tasks during it) or quick paced turn based combat (if you dont care about the outfits)The quick pace extends to the level, which takes a handful of mins, so it can be taken in bite size chunks too.The QoL features are great and even include bypassing things you dont want to spend time on. ex. I had 0 interest in Dall (one of the characters) and could skip all her optional events (and still get the rewards) which was really nice.Play time seems to be 12-15 hrs for the campaign and more with all extras which is very fair value.Solid game, strong recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Struggles to present a challenge even on the hardest difficulty. Suffers from forced shuffling of your abilities, IE you will acquire a new spell and the Breach action moves from 3 to 4 to 5 and so on. The button for each action can be different for each unit when they should all be fixed keys. Cover mechanics are barebones. Equipment loadouts are not a thing. Most levels comprise a single room, offering low complexity. Enemy behavior is near perfectly predictable and very dumb, such as most goons with guns standing in one place and shooting at the nearest target. This makes the foresight mechanic almost entirely pointless. Boss fights are somehow easier than anything else. Occasional vaguely DEI adjacent design choices along with one blatant real world woke politics pandering incident. For most people this may produce a sigh and damage immersion at worst. Given the other issues with the game, that was the final push to cause me to refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those rare games that's just good on every level.  The concept is good; the idea of wizards as special forces operatives is not only fun but executed with lots of thought and attention to detail as to how it actually works.  The writing is good; every single cutscene has multiple lines that make me laugh but the story has teeth as well.  The mechanics are good; it's as much a puzzle game as a grid tactics game, the combination of the two yielding a truly tactical experience that rewards the player for good positioning, foresight, and discovering synergies between character abilities.Also, I got an achievement for defenestrating myself.  10/10 GOTY.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I've wanted to wait writing this review, until I am done with the game, but now that I am in the first  I have to compliment how incredibly entertaining the dialogue is between all the characters in this game!Furthermore, the stages are well built allowing for some incredibly fun solutions, when you try to go for the bonus objectives in each level. It made me audibly go "Wow!" for some of them.Whoever might read this, I highly recommend you try this game out, even if you have never tried a Turn-Based Tactics game before, as it is very forgiving with the rewind mechanic allowing to try out all the different possible approaches.Thanks for reading this!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A few years ago, I swore off all nighters. But this game is paced a little too well.It wasn't like civ, with it's one more turn mentality, I genuinely lost track of time. After all, each mission is only a few turns long; this isn't some slogfest, mopping up a bunch of low level enemies you ran past. Each mission will usually have at most half a dozen enemies at any time, all of which can be dispatched in one turn, if you can find a combo that works. And find a combo you will, because this game works on the rule of cool. Sure, some enemies are placed right next to windows - this is part of the Defenestration Trilogy, after all - but can you dispatch them AND pull off that deaths-door and charge combo? Probably, if you futz around with your turn enough.Beyond the difficulty settings, that make single solution puzzles nearly impossible, and the optional objectives, both written and unwritten, TBW offers a wide enough range of difficulty levels for almost anyone. I, with entirely unwarranted confidence, chose to play on hard mode. And to begin with, I was validated for that choice, easily completing the optional confidence goals. By the beginning of act 2, these occasionally slipped by me. By act 3, I wasn't concerned with them at all. In act 4, I started reaching for the "restart level" button more and more. But in all that, I managed to keep my team up every mission, if a little battered. And then came the final mission. For the final showdown, the game offers a unique battle of attrition. Far from unwelcome, this offered one final challenge to me. Having exhausted most of the resources offered to me, my team started dropping. The tank and the druid at the same time. And then the healer. But I was so close, I didn't reach for the restart level button - I had a radical idea. I threw my support off the rooftop with an enemy. And then, Jen, the final member of the team, was staring down the big bad Liv, both right at the edge of the building. And I pulled out my last gale grenade, and did it again, winning a pyrrhic victory.The written story of the game is expertly crafted - quippy without being grating, and yet entirely sincere at the same time, spinning up a bizarre world and following through with the implications. Some of the best video game writing out there. Stays out of the way when it needs to, but offers enough to let you piece together a mystery with red string and drawing pins. TBW is by far the most story rich entry into the Defenestration Trilogy.But fundamentally, the deal with Tactical Breach Wizards is, as with the whole trilogy: The machinery of state isn't sticking up for the little guy. So, as one of the little guys, you need to answer the question: How are you going to throw the system out the window?
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a ton of fun with this game. Mechanically, it's great. Writing-wise, also great. I honestly find myself hoping for more stuff in this setting, because it's just so FUN. I love it.The only thing that prevents me from giving a full-on "everyone should play this" recommendation is that the humor feels like it's something that people could find annoying and insincere. I don't think it is, to be clear, but it's very close to a style of writing that I see a lot of people talk badly about. Tactical Breach Wizards completely nails what it's going for as far as I'm concerned though, and it's just a total delight. I adore it, really.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay of Tactical Breach Wizards is more than solid, with a tactical-puzzler design similar to Into the Breach but a bit less weird and a lot more polished, as one would expect from a game that is not a roguelike and so can actually design its fights in detail. The difficulty does have a bit of weird curve with the highest point a bit past halfway before the tools you have access to become so powerful that even powerful late-game enemies can feel a bit nonthreatening with exceptions.The real thing that made me fall in love with the game, though, is the writing. I would honestly call it the most consistently funny piece of media I have ever consumed, and it does that in a way that doesn't detract from and often even enhances the feeling of humanity in each of the main characters. Their personal journeys feel both real and compelling in a way that I've seen very few other games pull off, even ones with orders of magnitude higher budget and sprawling dialog trees.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent and satisfying gameplay. Looks a bit like XCOM at first glace but when you start playing it actually feels more like a puzzle game. You're free to redo things as many times as you want during your turn, so you're encouraged to experiment and try different strategies to get the best possible solution to the level.And also you play as a SWAT team of spell slinging wizards ✨✨✨
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Perfected the game in 20 hours on hard, and enjoyed my time with it greatly.There's two parts to this game, the tactical and the dialogue. Some people may be put off by a game that 'tries' to be funny, but it succeeds with flying colours. Some parts actually made me chuckle involuntarily and nothing seems forced. Every character stays, well, in character without any off-kilter moments. As the game tells you in every mission, the side-objectives are 100% optional and only give you points to use for a limited selection of cosmetics. They do not give you extra XP, as some people may think. Some of them can be bloody hard, but every single one of them is possible. (At the time of writing) there is a side-objective in one mission where it wants you to use 3 actions in one turn, on one character but there's only 1 mana on hard. With a specific skill attributed, it is possible without increasing starting mana. The final fight really makes you think, and is a thematic end. The achievements for this game all make sense and none of them outstay their welcome. Overall, a hearty recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: While the game presents itself in a manner similar to SRPGs such as X-COM, if you take the bonus objectives in mind it plays much more like a puzzle game. The bonus objectives only give you unlock points for outfits, but they not only feel very satisfying to pull off and there's also usually many different methods to accomplish them per stage. Once you add in ability upgrade choices, it feels very customizable and incredibly rewarding.The humour is going to be a love it or hate it thing. There's tongue-in-cheek humour but for the most part it stays true to the established setting, leaving the characters feeling believable and endearing (except for Steve, ♥♥♥♥ Steve). I get the hunch that if you're not a person who can crack a joke (or appreciate them) in a stressful situation to ease the tension, then the humour won't land.While I'm 4 hours in, I've only completed Act 2 itself. Act 1 was finished in the demo and its save file let me continue where I left off, but the demo's playtime didn't add to my steam entry. I estimate that I'll probably net around 20 hours of gameplay out the campaign, and will probably net more playtime from challenge scenarios.I'd strongly recommend the game based off the level design, worldbuilding, character interactions, artstyle, and of course the gameplay itself. I'm unsure how much replayability it'll have, but I feel as though I'll have gotten my money's worth out of the content that the game has as-is.There's a few areas I'd love to see improved.- The pre-breach BGM is very nice, but we barely get to hear it.- Currently we can only see where enemies will move if they're about to hit a character. With a navy seer on-deck, we should be able to see where they'll be moving to if they're hitting a teammate or not. This includes reinforcements spawning on that turn.And long-term wishlists would be a map creator for players to make their own scenarios, which would give the post-campaign game a ton of replayability.Ultimately this game is REALLY fun and the setting is fantastic. I'd love to see more types of games within the setting -- there's definitely a ton to work with here.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Found this  game scrolling through Youtube, and could not be more happy about that, because it was amazing, the characters and the strategic gameplay are amazing. Simple story but entertaining and good. Highly recommend if you want to think and get through tough challenges or laugh at the jokes and ideas of the characters. Love Jen and Banks all the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: TBWs is an amazing game. Great core gameplay loop where each character has their times to shine and turn the tide of a room breach. But even better is the writing and humor of the game. I found myself constantly looking forward to the next cutscene/story beat as it made me laugh out loud constantly .I played this on the Steam Deck and outside of pretty small text at times it plays super well still. _childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: the game is fun, it was nice to see how different powers interact and feel like a genius when coming up with some of the solutions. you know a game is good when you come up with combos when not playingand writing is just *chef's kiss* superb. like, it's funny, witty and i just couldn't stop thinking "god i love these dorks"
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game caught me completely off guard. Did not know anything about it, Steam just recommended it to me and thought "Oh cool, xcom with wizards probably fun for an evening".But what I instead got is some of the best written and funniest dialogue I have EVER experienced in a videogame, a surprisingly serious and intriguing spy thriller story despite the general humorous tone of the game and absolutely world class turn based combat.Unless Space Marine 2 completely blows my socks off, this is probably my GOTY 2024. I have nothing bad to say about this game, thoroughly enjoying every second of it (except Steve, FK that guy). 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely an enjoyable game. It's a fun strategy game with great world building. Serious storyline while also taking itself not entirely seriously, leading to lots of funny jokes and all around good humor. The optional challenges were a great way to add an 'optionally harder' difficulty while still leaving it open for those who would prefer an easier experience. Altogether, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews. But seeing the credits, I feel obligated to. I can't recommend this game enough. I was merely expecting a fun little tactical simulator. I got that, for sure. The gameplay is immensely entertaining. _childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. More of a puzzle/tactics game than an Xcom but if anything I say that as a positive. _childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing tactics / puzzle game with impeccable humo(u)r! I've been following the development and wanted to play this for so song and I can wholeheartedly reccomend this.I really enjoyed the infinite rewind system that lets you experiment a lot before locking in that particular turn.The optional objectives are hard, but doable the first time you encounter them which is a more than welcome addition to the genre
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun tactics game, closer to "Into the Breach" than XCOM or even Fire Emblem, etc. Positioning and using the environment are extremely important, as most characters don't do much direct damage. Most choices in a single turn can be undone if you don't like their consequences, and most enemies forecast their moves. A little rough around the edges in some parts of the UI and there are still a few non-blocking bugs here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm sure you know what a high pain tolerance is and can figure out how that can affect someone.I have that, except for humor instead of pain. I usually don't find things funny, and I rarely laugh. It's a seldom discussed side effect of mood stabilizers.Now, I say this not from a need to overshare, but so that you can understand what it means when I say , not chuckling or smiling quietly to myself but laughing in a manner I had not done so for years. Good comedy is really hard to do, and doubly so in a game I feel, but this game manages to do it, and do it well. It would get my recommendation for that alone. It's past 5 am and I had just lost myself in the game play and narrative... and that's another thing, it's not  jokes, one-liners, or meme-esque puns, it's an actual interesting story that provides the framework for the humor. And it's a good story.Beyond the writing though, the game itself is tight. It's like X-Com for people who want to, you know, actually have fun playing. It doesn't tack on needless systems to bulk itself up with buzzword features (e.g.  or ). Each room is this wonderful tactical puzzle that can be brute forced if you just want to get through it, but gives you a sense of accomplishment when you find the more elegant solutions. And throughout the whole game it constantly reminds you of one fact we as gamers often forget: The joy in a game comes from playing it, not in beating it. Buy it, it's worth the full price, and we need to support developers who make games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: At about ten hours in and the game still running in the background as I write this, I have reached a fair ways into the game. I have not completed it, but at the current trajectory I am going I can safely say I will complete the campaign in the 14 to 15 hour mark described by the game's store page. All of this to say, I am not finished the game.But I've loved every second I've spent with it so far, immensely.The writing is amazing, with the switch between comedy and actual plot being seamless and engaging. And while on the surface the game may look just like a comedy, I genuinely mean it that the story and world building go places you cannot expect. The lore - much of which is well integrated into the story, I don't think I've encountered a lick of exposition that didn't make sense - is supremely interesting, and it gets you engaged incredibly quickly by interweaving character and overarching world conflict. The characters make quips, but the game still takes itself seriously, and you really feel yourself believing in the world. And the twists and turns and drama is incredibly good! Not to mention that the story uses the 4th wall lightly. I know some people might be worried about a "4th wall breaking comedy" as those have so-so reputations, but this game does it so tastefully - as well as not just using it for comedy - that it blows anything else I've seen with it recently out of the water.I wholeheartedly recommend. I'm not even usually much of a turn-based strategy game player, or a puzzle game player, but this game hooked me. If not for the game play, which is impactful and intuitive (not to mention the amazing animation, sound work, and OST, all of which really add to the experience), then for the world itself.I want this setting in a Dungeons and Dragons module. Please.
