_childDocuments_.review: I haven't completed the game - haven't even unlocked all characters yet - but so far I'm having a pretty good time. I started with the demo and I'm playing it in a slow burn, taking the time to get all the optional/challenge objectives done in every mission and every "side mission". I do have more than just four hours because I played the demo released earlier this year quite a bit and was looking forward to the game's release; it just seems that the playtime from the demo isn't counted. Don't worry though - if the demo's still live, I pleasantly discovered your progress from the demo is kept in the main game!This game has the vibe of a charming and unique indie gem. I'm a fan of military-style games, having previously played things such as Squad, Wargame, Gunner Heat PC, and Digital Combat Simulator World. I've never really been a fan of wizardry and witchcraft, and considered it more of a polar opposite of tacticool military settings. Well, the devs must have decided to challenge themselves to blend the two, and I have to say they've made it work. It's enough to retain me as someone who indulges in the tacticool, and it seems enough to retain people who are into all sorts of magicka as well with its usage of "vessels", "channels", and "scrying".I was expecting a title like Firaxis' XCOM. Rather, I found more of a puzzle game that somehow reminds me more of "Into The Breach" as well as "Door Kickers", and even makes me think of Super Smash Bros because you don't really do damage to enemies so much as you force them into environmental hazards. Especially knocking them off the level's platform. Well, you  deal direct damage at times and it's probably possible to gun everyone down in a mission, but that's not how this game seems meant to be played.In something like XCOM the unpredictability and random nature of the encounters are actually a key ingredient of the game's bread and butter. Not so with Tactical Breach Wizards: every level is a carefully crafted puzzle. You're not usually even killing enemies so much as knocking them out, tossing them into alternate dimensions of doom that inadvertently suck out their souls ("modern society" "office jobs" soul sucking, not an actual harvesting of the soul as might be expected in a world of magic), and defenestration. (The devs seem to have a thing for "defenestration" - don't worry, they repeat the definition of that word for you multiple times in the game if you don't happen to use it regularly in everyday life for some reason) Can you smack three guys with a lightning bolt so one goes flying into a wall, one gets tossed out a window, and one gets electrocuted - not from your lightning but from the strangely exposed electrical circuits behind them? Or maybe you want to just create a Portal of Doom­™ behind an enemy turret or heavy gunner so you can shove them into it - but of course those Portals of Doom™ aren't infinite.There are plenty of things to help you, enabling you to tailor the experience in real time. What if you suddenly cave and make things easier? Well, that's your choice, and the devs are clearly fine with it either way.All this adds up to the fact that this is not a frustrating game. It's not trying to use a heavy handed approach to create a meta-narrative. In fact, the dialogue and story so far is definitely too tongue in cheek and the game knows better to take itself seriously. It's enough of a brain teaser to keep you engaged. It's just . And really, that's all a game needs at the end of the day.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic puzzle tactics game, with an engaging story, great characters, funny humor and very fun levels. Each mission is tactically engaging, especially if you try to fulfil the optional Confidence Goals for each character. The difficulty felt just right, providing a degree of challenge without being overly or frustratingly difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Strongly recommend. A good, creative, open, flexible tactics game (more actions per turn, more movement, etc) allowing more creativity even if you're not a genius. Not enough has been said about the controls-- there is not a single menu throughout the combat phase; all the actions are selectable (use a controller!) from the "default" condition and become active as soon as you've highlighted them. Every possible additional button press has been pared down to the minimum. This is the antithesis of the Final Fantasy "combat via nested submenus" and it makes the experience FLOW. It's trivial to try a new approach, even if you're way down the road before you realize you could REALLY get some defenestration going if you just took a step to the left after breaching. I love the setting and there's a great balance of silliness and seriousness. Feels like you're a group of moderately goofy rejects in a pretty serious world (with assault staves) rather than an overtly comedic setting. I did read some complaints about the dialogue and while I had no concern for the right-leaning dog whistles (definitely cry more) I did give pause at the potential for "British chat syndrome" or overall videogame dialogue weariness. No worries here. The dialogue is in short chunks, is usually reasonably related to the plot/action, and the stacking dialogue bubbles were surprisingly helpful for context/sloppy readers. More games should do this. There are lots of options to pare down your time spent reading without losing the plot, like some chats being optional, dialogue options that skip to the end of a topic, and the ever-present SKIP button. Buy this game, friendos.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I would say I'm not into turn based strategy, but this just works for me. The rewind and forsee mechanics let me just try what I want to try and see if I think it's a good choice, instead of being locked into a mistake thanks to a miss click.To me this game is perfect. The gameplay feels super solid, the story is interesting and it's sense of humor is halarious.Go WIZTAC!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I first saw the demo in 2019. I have waited 5 years for this game. It has lived up to my expectations and much more. The game is funny, the tactics and confidence challenges are fun, and I love the character designs. My recommendation btw, once you get Dall, upgrade her swap to make swapping with allies free, it is busted and lets you do some pretty fun things.10/10 game, not even done yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is so bad it almost physically hurts to read. So I don't. I skip every cutscene and I'm having a blast with the actual gameplay. A fun twist on X-COM where you can plan out your turn and rewind if it doesn't work out. It changes the feel of the game so it's more like a puzzle game where you figure out the perfect solution one piece at a time.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of a turn-based breach puzzle combat game is nothing new. But having brilliantly crafted, fundamentally rule-breaking abilities (for both your team and the enemies) and masterfully put together maps create seemingly impossible challenges - with very satisfying 4D-big-brain solutions where you build a multi-step chain of actions with synergies and explosive consequences and satisfy even the optional objectives in a single turn. The "rogue wizard swat on a series of heists" theme perfectly fits the logic of the game. This is how magic should always be portrayed: highly consequential, but anticipated by the enemy, thus requiring creativity on how to use. The game is not actually hard (on normal difficulty, going for most optional goals), but it makes you feel smart why you figure out a map. And yes, as mentioned in other reviews, the writing is very charming as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is a great time. Brilliant puzzle combat mechanics that stay fresh throughout the campaign. A low-res art style that has more personality than games with 100 times the budget. Writing that is genuinely funny and at times moving, with well realised characters that I grew to care about. A complete story, but a world that I'd love to see more from in the future.An absolute steal at the price. You owe it to yourself to play this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice tactical puzzle game, very much in line with Into the Breach.While I believe Into the Breach had substantially more tactical depth and replay ability, Tactical Breach Wizards is much more approachable, and easier to recommend for those that don't want the high stress nature of rogue-likes, and/or would like there to be more quality writing in their games.The characters all feel unique, and an important part of the team. They each have plenty of personality, and the plot is sufficient to move the game forward.My biggest gripe is that the default difficulty is very low. I was hoping the extra objectives would spice things up, but taking on this objectives didn't feel like a challenge, so much as it felt like an incentive to play worse. Sure, I could set up my tank to do 10 knockback over the course of the map... or I could just complete the map in 1 turn before the enemy has a chance to move.Playing in hard mode may fix the difficulty criticism. But even if it doesn't, the game is still really good. I'd recommend it for fans of strategy and/or puzzle games, and strongly recommend for those that are looking for an experience similar to Into the Breach.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game.  The Tactical gameplay is fun, interesting, and more beginner-friendly than something like XCOM.  The real star of the show is the writing though.  Every conversation has the sort of wry humor I appreciate while still fleshing out the characters.  The game's less about a team of elite badasses saving the world and more about a team of reasonably competent individuals with varying levels of trauma finding themselves in over their head.  I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: when i played this game on the demo, like every indie i have i know in 5 minutes wether is bad or good. i kind of felt in love with the concept of wizards doing some military ops. fun and newand their chats!for me the game is relative expensive (i live in argentina) but man i bought this on day 1. i didnt get much time to play, but it is gooooodand im glad is a super seller now in the rpg fest, and has a lot of thousands of reviews putting this one in overwhelming positive. im not happy because i was right. im happy because if this game made it, then more are gonna follow its steps.and we get tactical breach wizards 2! a step forward for the indie game scene, that is for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: If you like what it is on the tin, you will like what is inside.The game is a really interesting and if you go for the optional objectives, pleasantaly challenging tactics/puzzle game. The writing is excellent, and I enjoy the between missions stuff almost as much as the missions itself. There is a sense of progression in your crew, unlocking new perks feels meaningful and changes the tactics you have available.Really nothing to complain about from my side, can only repeat, if you think you might like it, I am pretty sure you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: The dialogue is smart and snappy: think Buffy era television in the best way possible.  While many of the levels are not super challenging, combining your powers in various ways is good fun.  Also, the game has a clever little system for recaps that was thematically appropriate and added to the overall charm.If you want a clever genre twist on the classic tactics game with FANTASTIC writing, give Tactical Breach Wizards a play!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is THE latest, defining breakthrough in tactics games design - in exactly the same way that Into the Breach was over 6 years ago. Tactical Breach Wizards gives you so many toys, abilities, and different mechanics to play with, that you feel like a genius (and a little bit insane) every single turn. Please play this now. I hope every tactics game made in the next 10 years takes DETAILED notes from this one.Also, the writing honestly is surprisingly good. I normally don't enjoy story in video games, but I found myself laughing quite often, audibly gasping at a twist or two, and, honestly, getting really attached to the characters by the time the credits rolled. Please please please play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since Tom's last game but it's totally worth it.Writing is spot on, humour is sharp and gameplay is mind-boggling. Much like Gunpoint and Heat Signature, each level is a puzzle with SO. MANY. DIFFERENT. SOLUTIONS. It's amazing!I've had a lot of fun playing this game and look forward for the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the main story and I'm obsessed with getting every optional objectives in the mission, if you like games like desperados iii or shadow tactics this maybe up your alley, there's a pretty meaty demo to decide if it's your jam or not.The game challenges you to be creative as some of the enemies pose a real challenge either from their ability, map layout or most of the time, from multiple factors that you should wrangle in to turn the tides against the enemies.Great humor, fun gameplay design, would recommend/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly charming tactical strategy with a brilliant sense of humour. I playtested this game during development and I'm happy to see that the final product is just as fun with a huge sense of polish and style.The freedom to rewind actions makes the game a fun experience even if you're not a strategy fan and the almost puzzle-like design makes for a great challenge even if you are.The writing is excellent, the visual design is fantastic and the mechanics are intuitive.Buy this game, you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is challenging without being frustrating, simple enough to understand easily while allowing for complex interactions that keep it interesting.  The "foresee" mechanic in particular really emphasises the "puzzle" aspect of the game since you can try out different combinations of actions until you find something you like, but the way enemies interact with it also unlocks a bunch of interesting and thematic mechanics. The writing is snarky and funny, until it hits you with some actually quite serious moments, and it transitions between these two states flawlessly.  The characters are likeable dorky badasses with great dialogue and great character design.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is frankly sublime. Mechanics and levels that create tough situations you will feel incredibly clever to get out of, decisions that are constantly simple yet deep and rewarding, incredibly funny humour that doesn't undercut the tone or plot, characters that have depth and ooze style. This is a game that will suck you in and drag you along for the ride - my 20 hours were over the span of less than a week and were I not ill at the time my social life would have suffered even more for it. 10/10, if any part of this sounds appealing to you I promise you won't regret picking this game up.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story and the best pacing in a puzzle game I've ever experienced. I was hooked from start to end, but never felt like I had to slog through a few more levels in order to get to the next story beat---a feeling which I even had very slightly in the first act of Portal 2.I hope they make a DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A gem of a game. The game is short, but it's the perfect length for a snappy story, varied enemies, and mechanics that don't overstay their welcome. I truly enjoyed all the time I've had with it, and hope for more to come from the developer! The worldbuilding and character work are done with swift, deft strokes that give just enough to evoke a new world with characters like traffic warlocks, SWAT wizards, and World War 5 over magical resources. The tactics are engaging, with each character having unique skillsets that shine in different situations. It's a small game, but it's fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, I like the characters and story which are fairly sympathetic and contains many amusing moments.As for the gameplay, each mission is sort of like an x-com style puzzle you have to solve, which with the rewind function, are very forgiving.This might make it feel a little less difficult, but setting up all sorts of epic/amusing combos is always a blast.My best analogy for the game would be like a long series of wire-puzzles, just keep fidgeting until you find a way that works and find plenty of amusement along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I feel a tiny bit tricked. This is not a turn-based tactics game, this is a straight up puzzle game wearing the skin of a turn-based tactics game. But what a puzzle game! It's gorgeous and stylish and absolutely hilarious. At one point it says that an upcoming conversation and battle is entirely optional and can be skippped, and I'm wondering why would I possibly skip any aspect of this beautiful gem?The puzzles are great, it keeps tossing in new wrinkles at just the right speed so you don't get bored or overwhelmed. And if you do, just go do some dream missions. I love the optional goals in each scenario; they're supposedly meant for extra challenge, but if anything they're helpful hints for the most efficient way to tackle the room. I absolutely love this game. As a "patient gamer" who prefers to snag games in bundles or on discount, I have zero regrets at purchasing this on launch, and eagerly look forward to whatever this team does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I love it.It's funny, thought provocing, keeps your mind active and is just... man I love it.You can sink hours on end into it, or just put it on for like an hour of fun and continue some other time. You like tactial, turn-based games? Get it. You will not regret it.Congratz to the team. You did something very special with this game. I don't know how to descripbe it. Keep at it!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I love the writing, I love the story, I love the gameplay. I love this game, 10/10.This is EXACTLY what you want from a tactical puzzle game. Make no mistake, this IS a puzzle game - each stage is able to be approached many ways as each level is its own mini sandbox. And its probably the best of its kind. Just absolutely incredible. This is pure tactics, with clear information and the ability to undo every move instantly to find your perfect setup. This is the pinaccle of its genre, this is the game that things like XCOM and Into The Breach paved the way for - If you cared enough to read this and liked either of those games, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely satisfying tactical puzzle game, arriving at a delightful mid-point between the modern XCOM games, Into The Breach and Doorkickers. The tight and rewarding gameplay loop is married to Tom Francis' endlessly amusing dialogue and world building, all wrapped in a genuinely compelling narrative.If you look at the words "Tactical Breach Wizards" and feel a gentle tingle in your brain, this game will deliver on exactly the promise of that feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: First off: this game is less about tactical combat and more of a tactical puzzle. Battles themselves aren't that hard to win (at least on normal), the main interest comes in additional goals. They really open up the ways you can cunningly and unexpentantly combine all the tools and upgrades you have, to deal with enemies in a smart way. Pure chaos and joy. Dialogues and characters, even though mostly comedical, are surprisingly good and complex. Dialogues are fun and interesting to follow. Developers clearly put good work and their souls into this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent tactical puzzler. The design between level and characters is great and the pacing both in introducing game mechanics and narrative is well-done. The extra challenge goals in each level are a fun, and often got me engaged in rethinking how to use the characters' abilities. The game does not overstay its welcome. in fact, after finishing the story levels, I am excited to tackle the bonus scenarios and player made ones.My only two gripes are these:1. You get a limited number of times to re-allocate upgrade perks. You do not get to have all the perks, and for a game that mostly encourages experimenting with your tools, it feels odd to limit how often you can adjust you toolkit.2. Do not use the mission select from the main menu. It is somewhat bugged at the time of this review. If you choose to retry an earlier level through the main menu mission select, you will find your story progress has somehow regressed, and you won't be able access the campaign mode normally until you clear the mission selected. Use the continue button, and then select missions from there. If you do accidentally revert your story progress this way, it can be fixed by going  back through the mission select from the main menu, and then choosing and clearing the mission that you left off at in the story.Otherwise, this is an amazing game, lovingly hand-crafted thought out and well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is a tactical murder puzzler, most strongly similar to Into the Breach. You have a small squad of characters with unique special abilities, mostly some combination of damage and movement, and with these powers you clear maps of enemies, ideally by cleverly knocking them out of windows or into each other's lines of fire.The gameplay is very good. Not quite as good as Into the Breach, which is **sublime**, but definitely better than XCOM and XCOM 2, which I enjoyed and also rate finely.  Tactical gameplay is a given. What I did not expect, and is incredible, is how good the writing is. From the basic premise of "special forces, but they're also wizards", the developers have crafted a glorious team of eccentric underdogs trying to stop World War 5. It's emotional, it's funny, and it's smart about the dangers of militarism.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a banger. Great writing/characters combined with fun combat and abilities make the moment-to-moment gameplay fun and relaxing. The devs didn't bite off more than they could chew here - this game sticks to its strengths, and doesn't outstay its welcome.  The game isn't too hard or too long, so you can actually finish it and feel good about yourself, for once.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Lean, well tuned tactics game with a strong cast of characters in both personality and play style.Aside from the turn based strategy game play, you aren't going to get much more, but what is there is excellently done. For those who crave more, there are lots of additional challenges and maps to go at. As the rewards for challenges are purely cosmetic, they are totally optional for those who aren't as comfortable with the almost puzzle game like difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I followed developement after becoming enthralled by Heat Signature before. I played in the beta tests and already liked it a lot then.I love Xcom, played Phoenix Point quite a bit and loved this even more.Characters are great and well written, the humour is actually funny, the setting is well thought out and cool and the challenges are tough but open enough to allow creative solutions. There are options to skip the dialogue or the levels if you don't like any of those.Overall 10/10, worth the wait and my hype was justified.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Its a weird game in the best way.  Its doesn't take itself too seriously and the humor is great, and the actual puzzles do a really good job of testing your problem-solving skills, especially in the later levels when you have to start really piecing together all the wild things you team can do.The best comparison I can think of is Portal.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐If you liked Gunpoint and Heat Signature, you will love Tactical Breach Wizards. The writing is excellent: very funny while also managing to have good character development and some well crafted plot twists.They really nailed the core gameplay loop. It's just a lot of fun to puzzle through the exact chain of combos that will defenestrate all your enemies by turn 3. The story seems like it will be relatively short if you binge through it, but there are challenges that I think will enhance replayability. The characters' abilities are also very unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Best game I've played this year.You keep getting new abilities to play with, and when the enemies get tougher, you get more abilities and gameplay.Then you level up and upgrade your abilities which grant you the same kind of good synergistic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of a roguelike deck builder minus the part where you wager time to only occasionally get the necessary cards.Then the abilities of different characters and rewinding combine in many ways, and connect to the story too! The story is extremely well written/delivered/funny/serious.The difficulty settings and bonus objectives are really good and scratch the puzzle brain itch.They joke about spending too much time making this game but it was worth the wait. This game is too cheap for what I got out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously the funny thing here is yeeting people through windows, but there's a lot more to the game than just that. The difficulty is just right, experimenting with the many different ways to play is encouraged and satisfying, and the story is good. With its volume and variety of challenges on top of all that, it's easily worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Decent story, funny and clever writing. Expected a dynamic tactics game like XCOM or Battle Brothers, but ended up playing more like a puzzle game and is linear. Still a great tactics game. Lots of fun combos with the soldiers. Loved discovering the overpowered combos in the game. Very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent turn-based tactical puzzle game. Every ability in your arsenal interacts with each other in ways that aren't immediately apparent and lead to some hilarious combinations. The characters are all fun, the dialogue is great as to be expected from another one of this team's games, cannot recommend it enoughOne of my favorite game devs out there back with another amazing game
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently in the latter half of the game and so far I'm thoroughly impressed. I would consider myself a Suspicious Developments fan and have been looking forward to this game for years. But it really exceeds my expectations. The puzzle-ified turn-based tactical combat is really good! It shares similarities with Into the Breach, Invisible Inc., and Transistor but it also very much its own thing. Infinite rewinds set this game apart and give the player a lot of freedom to explore the characters' abilities and to discover interesting ways to solve the combat puzzles. The writing is great! The characters are well defined and the humor is specific and believable in a way that some of Avengers movies aren't. You know when all the characters sound too samey and make the same types of jokes and quips? TBR is not like that. Well, done! The writing is legitimately funny and gels with the way it's presented fantastically. The story is also very cool. I'm really into the idea of having the player make connections on a murder board to follow along with and reinforce the intrigue of the plot. I think they found a way to implement it well. Great game all around!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic turn based tactics game. The story is funny and compelling. The tactics feel great and like there are multiple ways to complete each mission. Being able to replay all of the missions with your current character loadouts (and change which characters come) makes challenging missions makes them feel different and unique even if you've already completed them. Despite not having randomly generated levels the ability to replay any level later with different characters, change up your perks, and modify your strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Fun gameplay really bad millennial style writing, yeah its a game about swat wizards which is really a fantastic premise, but just the way the dialogue is written really detracts from it. I only really care enough to write my review for this game because its such a fun and silly idea for a game that the devs pulled off really well... except for how its written.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tactical Breach and Clear game which plays as such when things go smoothly, and that plays more like a puzzle game when you're struggling to figure out the right path for your murder wizards. The dry humor helps to keep things light and the levels are broken into bite-size portions that keep things short and sweet. If you're on the fence about this one, the developer has asked that you buy it. Apparently they like money, and they would like to have some in exchange for this gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite tactics game since Into the Breach. The combination of fantasy wizards and military makes for an interesting setting. The story and writing are good laughs. There's plenty of optional challenges in most missions that you can come back to, and there's many bonus missions that are entirely optional.The best part is that the difficulty is customizable, so people that have played a lot of games in the genre and those that are brand new can both play the game in their style, and the difficulty can be changed whenever you want.I see myself coming back to most missions at least 1 more time to try different challenges or difficulties, and hopefully the player-created scenarios can deliver even more bang for my buck.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: X-COM quality combat, plus the rewind to try each round as many times as you like.  Great storyline with fantastic characters (except Steve Clark), surprise twists and excellent humor.  Throw in affordable defenestration?  How can you not love it!As for downsides?  No procedural maps, but there's enough variety to keep you busy for a while.  The advanced difficulty options offer plenty of customizeable replayability too.  And for this price by a small team, the problems barely amount to anything.Really worth the money, I'm already recommending it to everyone I game with.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Masterful design.  The models have loads of character even with low polycount, the writing is very engaging and funny without going too punny.  The gameplay is tight and nuanced, and even the interstitial content like chats, the corkboard, outfits and confidence, and upgrades are all meaningful and satisfying.  Amazing game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun if you're into your XCom style of strategy game. It has its own distinct style of play, with a whacky sense of humour and entertaining story and characters, set in a knowingly silly world. Being an indie game, it may lack the polish and size of larger studio games like XCom, but is clearly crafted with a lot of love.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really neat game that drips with style.  On the surface it seems similar to an XCOM-like in terms of how the characters behave, with some Into the Breach mechanics, but really it's more of a puzzle game... especially when playing with the (optional!) challenges for each level.  Which, you know, it has levels!  I really appreciated the act structure, the optional dialogue scenes, and all of the flavor.  From Gunpoint to Heat Signature to Tactical Breach Wizards, I genuinely can't wait for what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to leave a review after starting the game, but uh, been too busy completing confidence challenges to remember.Then i defenestrated a turret, and figured i gotta do that review.Game is very fun, the core mechanic is great (rewinding in a turn) and there are many ways to clear each level.Breach glyphs and suppression wards, of course modern mages would be spec-ops units!It's like Into the Breach but with Wizards with a goofy sense of humor (and cool outfits, wowie)10/10, you will want to clear all the challenges(and that is before we see what people make in the Workshop!)
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I've barely gotten one-third of the way through this game but I can whole heartedly recommend it.It's a very old school sense of self-serious comedy that skates on simple jokes taken to their logical extremes. I think if Sir Terry Pratchett were alive today he would have something quite witty and generous to say in this game's benefit.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: wise-cracking wizards in small-scale tactical encounters with lots of movement influencing skills (knocking enemies around) creating some great sequences where you have one character debuff an enemy to make them stagger more, a second character runs around to hit them from the right angle to push them back a couple of squares, into the path of the third character who is over-watching along that path and pops them with a super powerful shot.exquisite.add in the ability to see forward in time and rewind your moves and you’ll be plotting and planning for the perfect turn.characters are engaging and funny and the art style is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10  Great game can't recommend it enough easily the best game I have played in 2024.The tactical gameplay is excellent and the rewind ability makes it a fantastic brain twister where you try and figurer out how to reach your goals one step at a time and makes you feel like genius when you finally succend.Add to that a interesting story with fun characters and world that I hunger to know about and I really hope will be more fleshed out in another game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal experience. I won't be able to say anything about this game that hasn't been said a hundred times in the other reviews, but it's a spectacular game from both conception, to design, to writing. I've been following Suspicious Developments since Gunpoint and while both Gunpoint and Heat Signature were great, this game blows everything that came before it out of the water. Highly recommend. The humor is surprisingly on point, the writing fantastic, and the gameplay sublime, you couldn't pick a better way to spend 10-14 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This one is going to be an all-timer in the turn-based tactics genre. It's great at carefully doling out new abilities and options every few missions, gradually increasing your options without becoming overwhelming about it. You start out with nice straightforward one-two combos, and by the end you can break encounters over your knee in ways that make you feel smug and clever.I should also give a shoutout to the writing. Consistently funny and entertaining, with characters that actually make you want to get them through missions unharmed.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend, one of the most fun strategy games I've played in years. The dialogue made me laugh countless times, the narrative is compelling, and the characters are memorable & lovely. One of the few strategy/puzzle games where I didn't need to look up any of the completion goals, challenging but always forgiving, with lots of leeway. You will almost definitely love this game as much as I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical Breach Wizards is a neatly wrapped tactical combat game in a detective-themed visual novel packaging, which follows in the footsteps of two intensely well-designed videogames.The characters feel modern, with a lot of traditionally british wit, and the episodic plot is great for playing on the go or just in short bursts.Buy if you like: Gunpoint, Heat Signature, Invisible Inc, XCOM
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun tactics game with a ton of interesting abilities and a great sense of humor. XCOM + Into the Breach + magic in a modern world. Pushing dudes out of windows or using a prepared shot to insta-gib an enemy coming out a door just never gets old even after dozens of hours. Characters are all fun with plenty of meaningful upgrades to flesh out their kits, and the story is surprisingly compelling even with all of the jokes and gags thrown in. The best feature is definitely the rewind button, which comes in the form of your seer wizard powers. It really lets you puzzle out the best way to play each turn, and makes the conclusion to each round incredibly satisfying. Definite very strong recommend for any tactics fans, this game is an absolute gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This is what games should be. A culmination of a teams (or an individuals) vision, love and hard work brought to life. Everything is great about this game, the story, the art, the mechanics, the level design, even the soundtrack, all work together harmoniously and I can't praise one above the others.If you like tactics games then this is a no brainer.If you would like to try out a tactics game, then this one is a good starter.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game but I didn't expect how much I would like it.  The story is kind of a dramedy: it doesn't take itself 100 percent serious, but there are some moments that are played completely seriously, and it works with characters I cared about.  While the humor might appear slightly quipy, it is no where near as bad as other games, and that kind of humor is outweighed by the ones that actually made me laugh out loud.  As for the gameplay, its kind of hybrid between puzzle game and tactics.  The base damage of your attacks is almost always smaller compared to damage or instant KOs you can get from using the knockback of the attacks.  The ability to rewind allows you to set up over the top ability combinations that can take out the entire enemy force in a single turn, which is sometimes required for confidence goals (optional objectives that encourage you to up your game in exchange for fun cosmetics, which are fun to go for, but some of these objectives towards the end feel like they aren't worth it).  So overall I loved it and I look forward to see if the defenestration trilogy gets a fourth game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: The tactical combat is a lot of fun, it's accessible and easy to understand while also having plenty of depth for you to do really clever things with the enemies, environment and your team's unique powers.The characters and dialog are delightful, the conversations are really entertaining but also never stand in the way of getting on with the story.This is some of the most I've ever seen a game do in letting you determine how much you engage with it and the attitude of putting that lever in the player's hands to control extends to many aspects of the design. Strong recommendation for anyone who likes small scale turn based tactical games!
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is just a complete joy from start to finish. the game play is rewarding and tactical, the story is engaging, the characters are fun, and the humor is just perfect for me. i have never been as utterly obsessed with a game as much i was with this. not only is it funny, the setting and vibe are handled extremely well. just an overall polished game with almost nothing wrong i can think of. 10/10 game for me. does everything its trying to do perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Really satisfying tactical combat! You can play a level just enough to win, or churn away until it's "perfect" for your own personal amusement. And who doesn't love a good ole fashion defenestration? The game rolls out new abilities at a good pace so all the options don't feel overwhelming.The story is quirky, dialogue witty, and the characters are oddly heartwarming on occasion. Love them all so far. I was actually surprised a game like this had a story, but it really adds to the charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, small tactical breaching game. Or so I thought, turns out to be one of the most fun, brain-twisting and addictive games, with absolutely awesome writing and great character development. The characters work beautifully (dialogue and combat) and I simply cannot recommend it enough. Wish there was more. (And I wish I could defenestre people on a daily basis).
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Superb tactical puzzler with a amazing and effective concept: magic-based SWAT team.You command a small team taking on handcrafted levels with optional objectives for variety. Each member having different specialties allows you to combo their abilities which are enhanced by their perks (unlocked as you play). Into the Breach is the closest comparison I've played - turn-based action with all required information presented so you can make informed decisions along with having a full undo mechanic for each turn. This allows you try out new things or take your time to figure out how you're going to complete objectives.The team starts out with two old friends meeting each other by chance and getting quickly roped into an international hunt for a rogue element. The story then expands, containing a lot of geopolitical factors and is highly intriguing. I'd love to see more of the lore and world-building.Aside from the main missions, there are optional missions to test your skills which are accessible at any time. These also include character-focused missions, giving you more insight and dialogue.Having played the closed beta and demo during development, the gameplay is well thought out but I cannot get enough of the humour and writing that appears throughout Suspicious Developments' games. It's hilarious, self-aware, endearing and sarcastic in just the right places. The banter between the characters truly is my favourite part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: A really well-written game with genuine intrigue and funny dialogue that combines top-down tactical gameplay with challenging optional objectives. Each level becomes a puzzle in which you apply each character's unique abilities to beat as efficiently as possible. Characters can upgrade their abilities over time, so if a level's optional objectives seem too tough, you can come back later. On top of the campaign, there's plenty of bonus levels to scratch your head over.The characters are all a delight, all funny in their own ways with plenty of moments for development and introspection. By the end of the game, there was not a single weak link among them.A real gem, please try it even if you're not familiar with the genre, I'm sure it'll make a fan out of you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: the game has great story with some really well thought out plot twists and witty dialogue.on the surface the game looks very easy but as the game progressed i found it got more and more challenging (especially when trying to focus on confidence points) and in a really good way, it really made me think on strategy, and with the rewind feature i don't have to save scum (best feature).i recommend this game to anyone who likes good world building, witty dialogue and turn based tactic games like xcom and into the breach (with the game being alot like the latter), and i hope to see more from these developers
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun but that isn't even the best part about it.TLDR; Come for the fun yet challenging turn-based strategy puzzles, stay for the incredible characters and story telling.Tactical Breach Wizards has some of the best written dialogue of any media, let alone video game, I've ever seen. The characters sound natural and funny. The story keeps you wanting more. It's whimsical yet the developing story keeps you entertained. On top of it all the there is just so much care and devotion from the devs oozing from every crevice of this game. From the puns in the settings menu, to the in-depth character backstories, you can just tell that the 6 years it took to make this game were filled with blood sweat and tears. If you're just looking for a tactical, turn-based, strategy/puzzle game Tactical Breach Wizards has got you covered. But if you enjoy characters that feel real, and dialogue that will rival even the wittiest of speakers then you will love it.Thank you so much to the devs for making this. I cannot wait to dump more time into it and you've gained a fan for life. PS... The performance is incredible, It's not graphically intensive by any means. Speaking from my own experience here and obviously this may vary per PC but the game launches so fast! And I feel immediately immersed. Not to mention the beautiful menu and transitions between menus. I literally thought to myself a few levels in about how I didn't even really realize that I was already making full turns and finishing levels on my own. The path from launch > set options > start game > tutorial > finishing multiple levels - was seamless. Again, you can tell that the devs just care.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, fast paced mix of puzzle and strategy with a short, interesting story and healthy dab of character development dabbed on top.The story is carried by great dialogue writing and some hilarious banter. It's nothing that will rock your world but enough to add a nice layer of depth on top of the setting and characters we're given. I didn't have high expectations here and was very pleasantly survived, I'd put it at an 8/10.The gameplay is surprisingly impressive. Honestly I don't even like turn-based games very much - I've played more than my fair share and they all get rather boring after awhile. But this game solves a lot of the problems of traditional turn-based strategy RPGs that bore me. For example, in battletech and x-com, I typically find that by the endgame, every map involves your characters being outnumbered several to one. This means I will take 30 seconds to a minute to make my characters move, and then spend 5-10 minutes watching the AI move all their characters. This game loop becomes very boring as you end up with very little gameplay relative to time invested. In TBW most maps are complete within 1-2 turns. Almost every enemy can die in one shot if you plan out your actions properly and most of your time is experimenting in the most efficient and creative ways to kill enemies and reach objectives, rather than waiting for enemies to move so you can move as well. All in all for gameplay I'd give it a 9/10. Innovates a lot on classic turn-based formulas, rewards creativity and intelligence.Long story short, I highly recommend this game. It managed to keep my interest all the way through with both a charming story and a surprisingly good combat system that rewards creativity, innovation, and aggression while minimizing the boring and troublesome parts of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: In Tactical Breach Wizards, you lead a team of renegade wizards in kevlar through turn-based battles to unravel a modern conspiracy plot. Combine their unique spells in clever ways, or rewind time to try every crazy plan you can think of to punch a Traffic Warlock through a 4th story window.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactical Breach Wizards

name: Shattered - Tale of the Forgotten King
detailed_description: In the beginning, there was the King. From a thought, he conjured up the Void. From a glance, he made the world. And from a whisper, he created us. The world as it was is gone, lost with the disappearance of the King. As a Wanderer of these forsaken lands, it is up to you to piece together the fragments of reality and retrace the fall of civilisation through skill based combat, innovative open-world platforming and the testimonies of survivors… some more trustworthy than others. Ethereal exploration and epic battles A ruined continent of untold stories and mighty foes is yours to roam. For those who brave its paths, the world of Hypnos contains many secrets, some to aid you on your way and others to illuminate the road that led to your existence. Experience precision based combat and 2.5D platforming set to a complex branching narrative in the reality spanning action-adventure of Shattered - Tale of the Forgotten King . Are you ready, Wanderer? Features: A new world to discover : Explore a gorgeously rendered semi-open world with branching paths and mysterious secrets. Each new zone tells a story through stunning art direction and finely crafted design. Monstrous enemies to defeat: Observe your foes, anticipate their moves and use their own attacks against them. Switch between close-combat sword fights and long distance spell slinging to dominate the battlefield, and experience seamless transitions between full 3D and 2.5D battles. A tale 10 years in the making : The universe of Shattered is the culmination of over a decade’s worth of imagination and creativity: an epic reality conjured from the minds at Redlock Studio. Tale of the Forgotten King is but a first step into the world of Hypnos, with more games already planned. A story all your own : Not all survivors of Hypnos are trustworthy: though most will help you on your way, there are those who seek to use you for their own ends. The world will remember the choices you make during your adventure, and only those with focus and dedication will see through to the truth beyond. Constant progression : Whether through combat or exploration, the Wanderer will evolve. How is up to you. With your finite resources will you raise your strength or discover another truth of Hypnos? Buy a new weapon, or increase your spellcasting? The choice is yours but choose carefully: not every path can be taken. « I had travelled through forgotten paths for days, weeks and months to reach the Thousand-Door Palace. A place where only silence reigned now. Where the wind had stopped and the tides retreated with the Great Rift. The great Departure. And here I was, bathed in my mist of past and future memories, standing in this mythical place that remained, still. The only location anyone in Hypnos could have found with no map or compass back when the King still reigned. And I Remember the Silence In My Soul. The Bitter Raindrops In the Wind. »

For those who brave its paths, the world of Hypnos contains many secrets, some to aid you on your way and others to illuminate the road that led to your existence. Experience precision based combat and 2.5D platforming set to a complex branching narrative in the reality spanning action-adventure of Shattered - Tale of the Forgotten King . Are you ready, Wanderer? Features: A new world to discover : Explore a gorgeously rendered semi-open world with branching paths and mysterious secrets. Each new zone tells a story through stunning art direction and finely crafted design. Monstrous enemies to defeat: Observe your foes, anticipate their moves and use their own attacks against them. Switch between close-combat sword fights and long distance spell slinging to dominate the battlefield, and experience seamless transitions between full 3D and 2.5D battles. A tale 10 years in the making : The universe of Shattered is the culmination of over a decade’s worth of imagination and creativity: an epic reality conjured from the minds at Redlock Studio. Tale of the Forgotten King is but a first step into the world of Hypnos, with more games already planned. A story all your own : Not all survivors of Hypnos are trustworthy: though most will help you on your way, there are those who seek to use you for their own ends. The world will remember the choices you make during your adventure, and only those with focus and dedication will see through to the truth beyond. Constant progression : Whether through combat or exploration, the Wanderer will evolve. How is up to you. With your finite resources will you raise your strength or discover another truth of Hypnos? Buy a new weapon, or increase your spellcasting? The choice is yours but choose carefully: not every path can be taken. « I had travelled through forgotten paths for days, weeks and months to reach the Thousand-Door Palace. A place where only silence reigned now. Where the wind had stopped and the tides retreated with the Great Rift. The great Departure. And here I was, bathed in my mist of past and future memories, standing in this mythical place that remained, still. The only location anyone in Hypnos could have found with no map or compass back when the King still reigned. And I Remember the Silence In My Soul. The Bitter Raindrops In the Wind. »
short_description: The old world is gone, lost with the disappearance of the King. Reforge reality in this dark action RPG through skill-based combat, innovative open-world platforming and the testimonies of survivors… some more trustworthy than others. Are you ready, Wanderer?

name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters
detailed_description: 🔪 Return to Sehwa High, if you dare... About the Game Mina Park, a student of Sehwa High, awakens at night in her school. It isn’t long before she realizes that something is amiss. The once-familiar school where she spends her evenings studying looks twisted by something dark and sinister. She finds herself pursued by someone or something that looks eerily like her teacher. To survive, Mina must venture beyond the boundaries of her school and into the surrounding district. There, she will encounter strange creatures, mysterious strangers, and uneasy allies. The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters is an atmospheric, story-driven game. Immerse yourself in the warped Sehwa district as you encounter an engaging cast of characters, solve puzzles, discover revealing clues, and fight for survival against a relentless psycho. Heroines, forced to confront their worst fears, rarely emerge unscathed. Over the course of the story, Mina will encounter dangerous scenarios from which she could sustain permanent damage. Craft items to anticipate future dangers to avoid injury. Dark Song is now more fearsome and powerful than ever before. Falling into her grasp could spell instant death. Running and wielding your flashlight makes you an easy target. You must precariously balance the urgency of exploration with your absolute need to survive! Fear Dark Song’s relentless pursuit to kill you, now with an all-new AI. Craft items to prepare for critical life-or-death situations or risk permanent injury. Explore the nightmarish district of Sehwa and discover its dark secrets. Scavenge resources to survive deadly encounters and afflictions. Unlock tools and upgrades to reach previously inaccessible areas. Hide to avoid detection and certain death. Pass challenges to conceal your location. Featuring vibrant, hand-illustrated in-game visuals and comic strips.

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is how thou makes a good sequel - improve upon the first game in every aspect. Excellent job Devespresso Games.The story picks up right after one of the endings from the first game, but the story here is self-contained, with the events from the first game explained. So while you don't  to play the first game, I still recommend you do (shameless plug of my ).Our new protagonist, Mina, is this time the unlucky winner of the Coma raffle, dragging her into a corrupt and twisted version of our realm. With Ms Songs stalking her every move, many things will quickly go awry. But, ancient buried secrets will finally see the light of day, with Mina at the centre of it all. The first game only danced around concepts like the Coma, relics, shadows, etc. and left them shrouded in mystery. , as a good sequel should, treats us to a plethora of new information that fleshes out these concepts further and expands the lore. But, one area where I didn't feel the game grabbed me as the last one did, was its underlying themes. Here we have Korean shamanism and mysticism. I can't say I didn't enjoy reading up on it, and, , learning something new, but the themes of the first game were just more interesting.One of my main gripes with the first game was how its cast felt lifeless. While not perfect, it's improved, as the characters here have some substance now. Mina isn't bland as Youngho was; There is plenty of dialogue and character development here. But, sadly, your in-game actions do not affect Mina's interactions with others. Perhaps we could get "actions have consequences" in the next game, eh Devespresso Games?Again, a perfect fusion of exploration and survival horror. More blocked off paths, more enemies roaming the levels, more environmental hazards, and more of Ms S (✧≖ ͜ʖ≖). Simply more of everything, but in a good way.However, I was disappointed by one thing -   It removes some of the tension, as you can pretty much see anything without needing your light source. Other than that, everything else improved upon the foundation laid by its predecessor.; Many of the games secrets are tucked away in the far corners of the map. Be prepared for a lot of backtracking, as some locations are barred and require special items to unlock. Secrets only expand the lore and give background for certain characters. But take my word - . , with each level having one. Like in the previous game, there are no map markers for them. Instead, you get  during Mina's conversation with a particular NPC. So do pay attention, as these optional quests are far from pointless fluff and can have some  consequences.The survival gameplay also received improvements. Ms S returns deadlier than ever. You can still evade her by utilizing the same old  shtick or  her attacks, which now have more fluid animations. But, there is one new addition - . It helps you escape her embrace of death, temporarily stunning her. However, it is a consumable item. But it's still appreciated you have a way to escape certain death. However, Ms S learned her lesson the last time and came prepared. She isn't alone this time, with new monsters roaming about, making juggling your stamina levels and evading Ms S and her entourage a tad bit more difficult. But surprise, surprise, we have even more goodies - . Before going , know it complements the gameplay and adds tension, especially during puzzle solving. You can't hold your breath on command anymore. Now, it's part of the hide in locker mechanic. Personally, I like how they merged the two. If Ms S is in the room, a couple of random QTEs will pop up. This way, you are no longer 100% safe while hiding. Ms S always wants to know your location, so misclick and she will.It pretty much works the same way for puzzles (entering a password, removing an obstacle, etc.). Now, you need to focus on those QTE prompts, but also keep your ears peeled for that oh-so-familiar sound Ms S makes with her high heels of doom.  received very little change. It still gives you ample freedom to choose how you move around, with even more shortcuts but plenty of obstacles as well. In the previous games, burrows acted as portals used to bypass them. Now, they act as mediators, linking two different levels and making backtracking less tedious. You can still reach  any level the same way you did the first time you went there, but using these tunnels is much safer and quicker. Unlike the previous game,  offers a more diverse pallet of locations, each seeping with beauty and gruesomeness. You'll explore a police station overrun by poisonous fungi, shady and insect ridden Dokkabei market, tentacle infested hospital and a location both familiar and foreign. The level design shows how much love and effort was put into breathing  into this world; No re-used assets from previous levels, excellent backdrops with some areas having plenty of background  as well. And of course, it all superbly complements the games stellar horror atmosphere, elevating the tension in certain sections a fair bit.I adore the art style. It looks similar to that of a Japanese manga, but it's actually  (the more you know). The overall look is a lot cleaner and more detailed than in the previous game, and we even have some nice  in the form of manhwa pannels.Locations are insanely, and I do mean insanely detailed. Look to the left, BAM! - weird tentacles. Look to the right, BAM! - ghastly overgrown insects feeding on  from a questionable source. I would often catch myself just standing in place, taking in all of the beauty of those insect ridden, tentacle overrun, and parasite infested areas. Whoever the lead designer was - you have one weird and messed up brain, so please continue doing the lords work for the next instalment as well.Headphones are a must. Audio cues play a pivotal part in distinguishing the location of a potential threat. Ms S still wears those noisy high heels, so if you don't wish to experience her deadly embrace, use headphones. However, there was too much music as you explore IMO. It would have been better to have it completely removed, potentially making any rustling in the dark a cause for alarm. Lastly, we got some voice acting. It's in Korean, but there are English subs. It's sadly only during cutscenes, but a great addition nonetheless, and much appreciated.What more can I say?  exceeded my expectations and improved upon its predecessor in every way - more and diverse levels, enemies alongside Ms S, quick-use consumables, voice acting, better optional objectives, and greatly expanding the lore. So all that is left is to click  and Now, all that is left is to sit back and wait for the third game. Do hurry up tho Devespresso Games, I want to know if the  ﴾⏒ ͜ʖ⏒﴿.

_childDocuments_.review: "The Coma Vicious sisters 2" is a survival Horror, puzzle 2D Game which is a follow up game from the earlier game from "Devepresso Games" "The Coma: Cutting class." You don't need to play the first one to understand what's going on, you play as a highschool student named "Mina Park" In the Sehwa district of Seoul, South Korea. The graphics are very comic like, there are puzzles that aren't too difficult and there is a crafting option in some parts (Optional, but recommended)The story of "Vicious sisters" Takes place long after "The coma: Cutting Class" Which picks up 3 Weeks from the last event. Luckily you can play this without any prior knowledge to their previous game. Throughout this game you are going to be playing as "Mina park" Where after she comes into possession of an amulet she doesn't understand, she collapses and wakes up back at her desk. Only to find that she is in a more sinister, dark, twisted realm of the Coma. She must find her way out of the coma while surviving the night of the blood moon and a horror that looks like her English teacher. Through her run of escaping the school, she is going to have to make some detour routes because shadow people are not friendly and will kill you! She is going to be finding more of her Coma friends along the way, and even some other groups of people "Who I will not mention, because spoilers"These are going to be SOME of the characters you meet. The gameplay in "The Coma 2 vicious Sisters" Packed in way more than I thought it was going to. You're probably going to be playing for a couple of days or even 3. The gameplay is simple, yet remains tricky. In this section of the review I will go a little bit in depth for each part. - Each section of a level will have a spot for crafting. This is optional (But recommended) you're going to need to assist some friends if you want to learn how to craft objects, which they will tell you where things are, or what they need from Mina first. They are as follows  In Each level you have the opportunity to craft which will help mina not take a hit of permanent damage as she progresses though the story, each level you do without crafting, is 1 less health bar into the next level. Here is a snippet from what they had to say from their artbook.  - It's not so much combat as it is dodging and hiding. Throughout the game you are going to face many obstacles in your path, from  to Strange shadow people who slash from the walls, or maybe even some spooky goop that drops bodies from the ceiling which you will have to dodge. Each dodge you do consumes your stamina. Mina will also have mace or pepper spray on her that helps her be released from the grasp of a certain enemy that may grab hold of Mina which are done through quick time events. Which is also what you are going to need to do if you want to remain hidden from certain enemies, the more out of stamina you are, the harder it will be. - There are a few items and ailments Mina can have on her, however only a certain amount at one time. She can also only carry ONE pepper spray or mace at a time, so make sure to restock if you aren't familiar with the area. The consumables are mainly food that will help Mina regain her health, or water that will help her regain stamina, there are benefits to some like some beverages will make Mina not lose stamina from some time (Useful when running away from fast enemies when you're disoriented!) However cost the most from the vending machine. There are also bandages incase you bump into an enemy that gives you bleed damage and antidotes that protect you from poisonous plants. You CAN however look around some areas for clues and find a bigger bag space for your inventory.There's a small bit of variety to the OST It's not going to be overdone, it's mostly going to be some violins and piano, some of the areas will have some ambient sounds IE Hospital with a squeaky sounding wheelchair and a heart beating slowly or police sirens at the dokkaebi market. However the most important sound that you are going to be hearing the echo of high heels they're not really a part of the soundtrack and you should probably find a place to hide.The coma 2 Vicious sisters has a Manga artstyle to it. Outside of the Manga illustrations it's hand drawn, the characters, the environment, I always appreciate hand drawn art. From their words it allowed them to input more from the real word into the game. Here is another snippet from the artbook you can purchase.  (A Dokkaebi is a folklore goblin who is greedy and mischevious, you must never tell them your real name.)Now, I know what you're thinking "Hey Magical, is their outfi-" Yes, yes oh my god yes! Horror game with customizable Mina outfits there's absolutely different outfits for her. Then you'd probably say something like "Okay, calm down I ju-" Okay so check this out they are DLC, BUT! There are multiple different outfits, ones that make her look like a k-pop Celeb, one that makes her look like a gamer girl, even one with the same outfit with longer hair. "Okay, okay I get it" There definitely is replayability within this game, there are different routes you can take in this game leading to multiple endings. Not to mention if you just want to collect all the achievements because you love the game so much, all the more reason. I would recommend maybe making multiple different save spots for quicker access.I highly recommend this game if you are a fan of horror/thriller, the artsyle is a plus. The story was well done, the characters had personality and made you love them and hate them, even in the coma world. The combat quick time events were great, for a small group that didn't know much about making games, this one was really well done, to devepresso games. 감사합니다

_childDocuments_.review: Simple in terms of gameplay and straightforward with its scares, the original Coma game (now known on Steam as ) was a bite-sized appetizer; a side-scrolling horror hideathlon that, admittedly, I only checked out so I could fire up the much more appealing sequel guilt-free. I didn’t have much to say on it, though the little I did convinced me enough that I was no fool for playing through it first. was a pleasant surprise, and brisk enough for two consecutive playthroughs in pursuit of the true ending. , on the other hand, is everything a sequel should be—bigger and bolder, though not always for the best—it is the main course after the first game, with enough ingredients to scrutinise the recipe.Out of the frying pan and into the oven—it seems that Sehwa High, the primary setting of the Coma games and what lies in the centre of the eponymous shadowy realm, created by the unhealthy expectations the South Korean education system places upon its students, still has some demons to exorcise. This time, however, no punches are being pulled.Mina Park, best friend to Youngho (the protagonist of the first game), is whom you get to guide this time around, through the frightening depths of the collective subconscious of overworked students and reprehensibly-corrupt school officials. There’s no clever difference between how each character is played, but Mina’s misadventure is much more elaborate. A lot of effort was put into expanding the world of the games, not simply in a way where things already known are retconned or just built upon, but recontextualised for a thought-out-in-advance transition between the two. Yet, the shadowy realm in the first Coma was an allegory for the spartan education system its characters must go through. Here, it’s a lot more literal and a driving force behind what’s happening; closer in concept to young adult fiction than the message the first game was trying to get across. Even the collectible notes reflect this. They’re no longer about the corruption and injustices the students face, but lore—tales of ancient shamanic orders and character backstories.There’s still character drama, this time focused on the themes of friendship, loyalty, bullying, and standing up for yourself. It’s moving, though in no small part thanks to the touching soundtrack, but duller without that systemic scope that the first game tried to tackle.Everything else, however, and  is the bigger game. It even comes with its own cast of characters to be killed off one by one as the nightmare progresses! With lively spritework and yucky environments that consistently give you the feeling of something being stuck in the back of your throat, all spruced up by a gorgeously rich colour palette, it is another great example that horror doesn’t need to be all dark to be visually effective.The increase in size is also quantifiable; not only does  take around twice as long to beat, but it doubles the number of locales across the story, from three to six. Sehwa High has shrunk since the last visit—with now only one of its three wings making an appearance—but in its place are a police station and a demon-ran market, amongst others.The variety here isn’t just to be looked at. It gives the art team an opportunity to showcase their creative chops by figuring out numerous new ways in which they can muck up all these different locations, with protruding tentacles and amorphic shapes, but if you thought navigating one building in the first game was hard, then wait ‘til you get a load of this interconnected world!Of course, neither of these two games is particularly hard, yet  is going to take a bit more brainpower and consistent reflexes to conquer. It gives you a bigger maze to grapple with but takes away the ability to hide anywhere you want so long as you’re not out of stamina, as you could in the first game. Then, it equips its Thing That Should Not Be—the stalking demon wearing the skin of everyone’s favourite teacher—with a one-hit-kill punch that goes straight through Mina’s chest, provided she’s not carrying a can of demon-repellant mace (of which she can only carry one).Oh, is that it? Well, no, not really. You’ll notice that Mina also has a health bar—and since you can't use it to track damage from an enemy that always one-shots her, what good is it? Why, for tracking the damage taken from all the other threats lurking about!Even reaching the presumed safety of a locker or bathroom stall no longer means you’re out of harm’s way. Entering a hiding spot while on the run will prompt a quick time event varying in complexity, depending on how much time Mina’s spent running around and exerting herself.That being said, if you’ve mastered the art of dodging in a 2D space and running to the nearest locker to hide (you memorised where it is, right?), then congratulations, you’ll have the skill most important to keep Mina alive down to a tee, even if slipping up even twice in short succession while the big bad is around means it’s the end for her.There is a skill ceiling to which such a simple formula can be taken without resorting to making it frustrating, although I can’t shake the feeling that the game was scared of its own difficulty.Removing the bread-and-butter ability to hide anywhere, while beefing up the bad guys, calls for some compensation buffs to the player’s side, I agree; but having not one, not two, but  quickslots to use consumables from while filling the game out not only with more than enough of ‘em to keep even the least bit thorough player fully stocked, but also a currency that can be used to buy up anything you’re missing at vending machines, means you’ll be popping health and stamina recharges without a second thought at any crucial moment.Attached to more prominent side quests when compared to the first game, completing which lets Mina craft special items that help her avoid permanent damage at specific points, the puzzles are simpler than I hoped—down to a game of memory. Learn information in one place, and don’t forget it by the time you reach another. Do that a few times, then take the items you were awarded to the crafting bench to put together what you need.Those quick time events that pop up when trying to hide also overstay their welcome, since they’re used for every other interaction Mina has with her surroundings. They’re good for maintaining tension, but crafting or typing out numbers on a keypad didn’t have to be presented through the exact same sequence of randomised arrow key presses; as if a shortcut for having to design a unique minigame to simulate each interaction.However, the game managed to hide its true ending from me, just like its predecessor, as much as I’m ashamed to admit it. I tried in earnest, but in the end, I missed one crucial clue. I won’t make up any excuses, though I will say that the game broke its own rules a lil’ bit to hide it from me. Regardless, I should have known better.Falling short mechanically and a tad thematically,  is a great sequel and a bit too easy of a game, with a larger scope and production value when compared to the original, without ever getting to the point of bloating.I'll be back for my true ending...!
