_childDocuments_.review: So first I'd like to let it be known that you do not need to play The Coma to enjoy or understand its sequel, Vicious Sisters. However, due to the fact that characters from the original also appear in this game, and the sequel builds upon the foundation set by its predecessor, playing the original first is recommended though absolutely not mandatory.Having played the original The Coma: Cutting Class / Recut, I was glad to hear about its then upcoming sequel. Both games offer a good horror experience that focuses more on an uncomfortable atmosphere full of increasingly tense moments rather than a cheap and predictable jumpscare-fest. Just as its predecessor did before it, Vicious Sisters pulls from its native Korean culture and folklore to add gravity to an otherwise strictly supernatural situation. Much like  and  from Taiwanese developer , this works in its favor toward providing an advantage of making it a more unique experience over the majority of horror games often released within similar settings. This also has the added benefit that the sequel expands on both the story and the lore surrounding both titles; enriching the experience of the sequel if you've played its predecessor, or of the first game if you go back to it after playing this one.The Coma 2's game mechanics haven't been completely overhauled or reworked, but they have been improved and refined from its predecessor. Although some of the changes are subtle, it just feels a lot better whilst playing. One new addition is the use of Quick Time Events for example. So whereas QTEs would usually be annoying in most games, here it's made more of a hands-on experience than a passive one compared to the first game by adding to the already thick coating of tension. Whether this particular change is an improvement will be subjective to each individual player given the general sentiment of Quick Time Events in games, but it certainly adds another layer to the gameplay in this one. The game didn't crash for me once throughout its time in Early Access, but there were bugs here and there that were quickly resolved by the dev team more often than not. Since its full-release out of Early Access though, I haven't experienced any bugs nor any other issues to speak of. It's definitely a far more stable game now than it was during its pre-release period, which is the way it  be, but it pretty much ran so well from the beginning that this says more about the level of polish it has received since then than anything else.The Coma series does good horror. Again, it's not about jumpscares or too much of a focus on traditional horror tropes but about a consistent and permeating feeling of unease and dread punctuated with a tense ambiance instead. While once again comparisons can easily be made to its aforementioned contemporary, Detention, The Coma and its sequel pivot towards its own method of execution...and it's no secret that both are considerably influenced by the original Silent Hill trilogy. Where Detention is very much versed in the spiritual and supernatural, The Coma games go for a mixture of supernatural and preternatural; that is, something otherworldly, . Bodies strewn across ceilings, ostentatiously draped in shadows, littered around the environment, or stacked up on anthill-like piles. Decrepit yet imposing tendrils gripping the environment like uprooted and exposed veins leaving you wondering if these are branches from a perversely unholy world tree, or tentacles of a persistent unknowable being...and that's only the beginning. It looks as if these locations where always meant to appear this way by design, and may have you questioning who was its architect. With every step and subsequent encounter you'll be happy you're not in the protagonist's position. As several films continue to chase "proven" formulaic horror templates, it's great to see that at least in gaming we're privy to more varied interpretations, many of which come with a more focused vision. The fact that many horror games are coming from a multitude of diverse backgrounds, countries, and cultures lately only adds to this variety. The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters is a worthy sequel and a worthwhile purchase, even if you haven't played the first. The exploration can be rewarding as it offers up secrets and resources to craft traps and weapons, the characters are very well-designed and illustrated, the presentation retains that distinct  signature style found in all of their games thus far, the sound design and moments of voice acting are both believable as well as really effective in adding to and building upon its atmosphere. It's just an overall properly polished experience, and there's even room left at the end for the possibility of another future title.  Be sure to also check out their original  game and Devespresso's take on the Darkest Dungeon formula with . Easily Recommended			 Xbox Gamepad

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the first hour while covering this game for the Humble Choice Review: The Coma 2 starts with the character arriving at school for a normal day, and has the player learning how to move through the school and even buy food from a vending machine.  Then at the end of the first day which comes entirely too fast, everything changes. The player is involved in a strange ritual that teleports them to a shadow dimension complete with a mysterious group of cultists including your teacher, and all manners of shadow enemies ready to attack you. I don’t like horror and no, The Coma 2 isn’t the exception.  I still dislike The Coma 2, but I dislike it for the reasons why people enjoy horror games.  I found this game to be quite unsettling and focused on unnerving the player, rather than jump scares.  The animation and graphics are well done, and there is a solid story as well that had me interesting in learning more, but the gameplay is more focused on a defenseless player avoiding the enemies, and the setting made me realize I’d struggle to enjoy this game. But again, this is all good news for horror fans because the reason I no longer wish to play The Coma 2 is the same reasons people look forward to it. The only other thing I’ll say is this a Korean horror game which probably could be its genre, but due to that, the cutscenes are voiced in Korean and subtitled in English.  So ultimately I will recommend The Coma 2 to players who prefer scares and solid gameplay, graphics, and a unique story.  But if you aren’t a fan of horror, skip this one. If you enjoy this review or it has helped you, consider checking out my video review of the entire Humble Choice bundle, or subscribing to my youtube channel.

Through some adventurous exploration, I managed to get the good ending and overall I have to say my review stays true! I love this game! _childDocuments_.review: After the recent semi-disappointment of DreadOut 2, it's nice to see a sequel to a horror game starring an Asian schoolboy or schoolgirl not only live up to the first game in the series, but arguably surpass it.   Sounds obscure, I know, but there's a lot of horror games set in Asian high schools, and the first instalment of The Coma was easily among the best of these. The most unique thing about it was the side-scrolling 2D perspective, which the game utilised to surprisingly scary effect; while most horror games set in schools are in 3D, if not first-person. In fact, schools have become particularly done-to-death locations in horror games over the years, especially in the handful of years since the first Coma came out, so it's with great relief that I announce that...   Not  of this game takes place in a school. Phew!   But we do begin in one, and return to it later. In the meantime we get to visit some other fairly familiar (though not quite as familiar) horror video game locations, such as a police station and a subway. Beyond that, the gameplay is quite similar to that of the first, but more finessed and slightly more varied: explore spooky places, find notes and keys and other items that help you progress, avoid enemies. Even if that sounds dime-a-dozen to you, trust me when I say that it's done particularly well, and feels quite fresh thanks to the highly unconventional side-scrolling perspective. 2013's Dark Matter is a game that comes to mind as trying something similar, but that game evidenced far more flaws than this one does.   That said, there are  flaws in Vicious Sisters, but nothing that should dissuade anyone. The "stalker" enemies in the game - i.e. the most dangerous ones! - occasionally appear right on top of you, out of quite literally nowhere, thereby leading to the occasional cheap kill. (This isn't too much of a biggie, though, if you take advantage of the game's very generous save system, meaning you should never lose more than a minute or two's progress.) Said stalkers furthermore become a tad  relentless as the game progresses - a flaw I recall being in the first Coma, also - but again: save often, and you won't be inconvenienced  much (though it is a shame when horror game antagonists shift from scary to just-plain-annoying in some parts; and the climactic "boss battle" is a slight headache thanks to a bunch of unskippable cut-scenes you need to endure over and over every time you die).   On the whole, though, this is one of the best indie survival horror games you're liable to play, and quite possibly  2D one. And don't let the 2D graphics put you off if you're a newbie and are unconvinced that such a game could be frightening: give it a go, then decide. Hell, the price is tiny, and more so when on sale. I obviously can't promise that you'll like it, but you'll never know unless you try, eh? Nothing ventured, nothing gained...   Verdict: 9.5/10.(PS If you enjoyed this review, feel free to check out my two Curator pages: Cheers!)

_childDocuments_.review: A stylish game that serves as a great introduction to the survival horror genre and Korean culture. The game mostly consists of fetch quests, quick time commands, and exploration (with some backtracking) as well as a great sense of tension and atmosphere; there are jump scares, but they're not overdone and actually effective even if you've played the game more than once. If you're looking for really good Asian horror games I do think Detention by Red Candle Games is better overall but this is definitely worth checking out at least once.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not very easy to scare (mainly because I can tell what's coming before it happens) but this game is just a whole new level of awesome. The jump scares are genuinely terrifying at the beginning, and even though you get used to them you can never truly let down your guard. The second you do, you're toast. This game also does a really amazing job of actively using the sounds and visuals to make each moment intense, and keeps you anticipating new threats around each corner. The graphics are beautiful, the voice acting is on point, the story is actually interesting, and I just overall really like this game. This is my first recommendation, but boy am I happy to write it.

_childDocuments_.review: It so happened that I started my acquaintance with this game series from the second game, and I was very pleased that the developers quite skillfully and intelligibly entered a brief synopsis at the beginning of the game. A school horror playing on teenage fears of its teachers (even if the teachers are beautiful, walk in high heels and speak with a slight hoarse voice), inner sensations of the unknown, constantly floating in the margins of our consciousness, and of the illusory perception of our existence at the junction of spaces. And if at first the game seems to be the sister of my beloved school horror "Detention", then after a very short time it starts to show that it really has its own unique trump cards in the sleeve, its interesting features that greatly enliven the gameplay and create a sense of enthusiasm.The game is still at the Early Access stage, but it concerns only the volume of game content, because I did not notice any dampness in technical terms. On the technical side, this is a completely finished game, with very thoughtful mechanics, with no critical bugs. Game content is still somewhere around three hours of game time, and it also does not look like any cropped or boring at all. Developers are willing to share with players specific dates for the release of new chapters of the game, a fresh arrival will be literally in a week, so the game will definitely not be abandoned. Having already played a little and in the first part, it is noticeably noticeable how much more beautiful and expensive the game has become. Very cute animations, atmospheric backgrounds, dynamic cutscenes, just a magnificent frightening main antagonist of the game. The gameplay is pulsating with life (and death), the plot is very energetic with the events of the game, constantly moving somewhere, navigation through the game zones is executed in a very convenient style, so getting lost here is extremely difficult.“The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters” is a very high-quality and promising horror game that can give the player pleasure even at this stage of development, not to mention the moment when the game reaches the moment of full release.

_childDocuments_.review: is a Korean 2D survival-horror adventure game. You play as Mina Park, a high schooler whose childhood friend Youngho Choi has been stuck in a coma for three weeks with no apparent explanation. Because you're holding on to an amulet he was holding in his hand when he collapsed and have no idea it is a powerful dimensional relic, you accidentally end up in the Coma, a dark twisted parallel universe where you'll have to keep your wits about you to survive, save the world and maybe bring your friend back.There is basically two distinct ways to play the game (with two associated endings, not counting the ways you can die of course): either you rush through the story and get the somewhat bad ending, or you take your time, go through every nook and cranny, solve every riddle there is to solve, prepare everything you can and then you get the good ending.This game is a direct sequel to .This is an excellent specimen in its genre. If you enjoy 2D horror games, survival horror in general or have a soft spot for Korean culture, this game should be right up your alley.I would recommend it to you even more if you've played and enjoyed the likes of , , , , ,  or .Of course, if you've played the first game and enjoyed it, you absolutely should play the sequel, as it has improved upon its predecessor in every single way I can think of (better controls, more interesting levels, better story, improved soundwork, more variety of monsters, events, NPCs, you name it). If you haven't played the first game... maybe just skip it. Sure, it'll show you how exactly Youngho Choi ended up in the Coma, but I don't think you're missing much if you jump in directly with the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Although there are plenty who disagree with me out there, I could never really get into The Coma: Recut. The theme was appealing enough, though the gameplay itself was tedious and repetitive. Being that I’m both a horror fanatic and a glutton for punishment, I decided that I’d give The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters a run and see if the formula had been tweaked to my liking. Spoiler: I was awed by how vastly improved this iteration was within only moments of picking up my controller.The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters starts similarly to its predecessor. You’ll once again get a glimpse of the slice of life normalcy that is Sehwa High, though this time you experience it in the shoes of Mina instead. As expected, one thing leads to another and she finds herself far from the comfort of the Seoul that she knows, even if The Coma is nearly identical in many ways.There’s not much more that can be said about the story that won’t spoil parts of it, but there are a number of instances where connections are made between it and the original, and there were never any lulls in the story. For the most part, it’s still mostly fetch quests lined up back-to-back, but I honestly can’t complain as the constant loop of hide-and-seek has been toned down, and I had fun every step of the way.The changes in scenery are also nice; you may be starting at the school again but you’ll be exploring several other locations that each offer a unique experience. These environments keep the game fresh and they were clearly designed with a passion for the project. I can’t stress enough that the art and sound combine to create a very strong setting that few other titles in the genre can compete with. In classic horror fashion, you’ll also find notes everywhere that deepen your understanding of the lore and they do so without boring you to sleep; they’re not as needlessly verbose as many in the genre have made them in the past. I found myself increasingly invested in the story and setting as I progressed, and I played The Coma 2 nearly twice as long as I played the original in my first session.Why yes, section header, I did, but they’re nowhere near as dull as that description would make you think. The Coma 2 hits a sweet spot on the complexity spectrum for the experience that is is meant to create for the player. The locations are more memorable this time around as each is not only unique from the others, but each room, corridor, and space within them feels different from others in that same location; no longer will you bounce from classroom to classroom without being able to tell the difference. You’ll also find enemies to be varied as well, everything from the familiar shade of Ms. Song to a disturbing cleaver-wielding butcher will be hunting you as you travel through these locales, though you’ll be able to secure several advantages if you use your head and stay aware.The number one skill to develop is memorizing your hiding places. If you can do that, you’ll know exactly where to run when the most dangerous monsters show up. You’ll also want to work on your awareness, both in the visual and auditory spheres. Corpses fall from the ceiling while claws lash out in an attempt to rend your flesh, and you’ll learn to notice these before they have the chance to do so, though the game continues to introduce new foes as you progress. This goes double for the monsters that actively hunt you (like Vicious Sister) as you can hear their footsteps before they’re aware of you; it’s best to hide at this point as once you’ve spotted them, they’ve most likely already seen you too.Health, stamina, and consumables make a return, and you’ll want to manage them efficiently. Health can be recovered via consumables to varying amounts, but you’ll also have to keep an eye out for status effects that can further complicate matters for you, such as bleeding and poison. Other items help with your stamina, which you’ll want to keep at a decent level as it’s integral to your survival. You’ll be burning stamina when you’re sprinting away from dangers, though if it will also increase the difficulty of the quick-time events when you are hiding if it is too low.I can’t praise developers enough for using The Coma as a learning experience and applying that knowledge to build on its strengths while paring down its weaknesses. I was never able to have much fun with that title, but The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters had me hooked within minutes and I had to force myself to break away from it or I may have finished it in only one sitting. I won’t say that this game is the most terrifying one that I’ve ever played, as I never really felt on edge, but the horror elements integrated with the action mechanics to create a thrilling experience, and the story was very enjoyable throughout. If you liked the original, there’s no question that you’ll also find this sequel worth your time. On the other hand, if like me, you were unable to get into The Coma even though you thought the concept was promising, I’d recommend giving this one a chance s the gameplay has been vastly improved. I certainly enjoyed my time with it and I’ll be keeping my eyes open for more title from Devespresso Games in the future.Original SoQ Review:

_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: The story is uninspired, the characters bland and predictable, the gameplay repetitive and irritating. The map starts out alright but quickly devolves into a maze-like environment of finding the right doors to open, holes to crawl through, portals to take, etc. to get where you need to go. Gave it up some ways into the Hospital, where enemies are thrown in your path on an almost constant basis. This formula effectively strips away any and all tension or fear, making the game (especially the Hospital sequence) a neverending game of peek-a-boo: try to make any headway through the building and you're forced to constantly run and hide so the game despawns or moves the enemies for a few precious seconds out of the path you need to take.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: There are some improvements in gameplay from the original, evading the monsters is more responsive, and there's ways to plan for monster encounters that don't just leave it to chance, but I just don't enjoy the core gameplay of scavenger hunting around a giant map. Sometimes the game gives you markers to show you where to go, sometimes you have to piece it together from vague notes that are sprinkled around the map so you end up just running around, evading monsters, and checking every room in the hopes that it contains the next thing you need to advance the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: In the beginning, the game is quite scary - mostly beacuse I didn't know whot to expect - but after some time I got to know how the game works and I forgotten about the game's horror tag. Still, sounds of breaking glass, enemy's footsteps and other make good work in creating a climat.Comparing to the previous game, The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters made small, but really important improvements. The most important are more friendly-user inventory, items can be used without opening a backpack, better graphics, voice acting and comic-like-cutsecenes.Some of the characters were in the previous game and some are new, but both of them have the same problem - its hard to like (or dislike) them, when they say three lines in an hour of playing. Because of this I don't care what happens to them.I recommend this game to people, who are searching for a not so scary thing, with climat and who likes to explore a little and prefer to have a choice in killing some characters :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I don't play half the games included in my humble choice monthly subscription, but I am so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ glad I did this time. This game is incredible. _childDocuments_.review: Something korean... well this might be something different... aaaaand...it totally delivered! Thought the characters ingame still speak korean (which actually is quite interesting!) but the subtitles (or chat-boxes, since the notes and thoughts of mine are not voices) are still english and good to read.A 2D horror puzzle game, it plays like a point and click adventure with some parts being real-time "action" (delivered in running sequences and quick-time events). The AI is foreseeable and still has some shock-moment which combines into a really rewarding experience. Definetily recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters is a second chapter after The Coma Recut. It is a 2D side-scroll survival-horror video game (same as the previous chapter) developed by Devespresso Games. In this chapter, there is a new main character, Mina Park, Youngho Choi's best friend. It comes up with the same terrifying school as the previous chapter, but extended to the larger location including hospital, police station, market, and old school building. Some action movements have been upgraded and differentiated in a positive way. More puzzles and hints to againts the vicious sister have also been placed along with a nice sequal story in the coma dimension.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best adventure games I've played this year.1) well-detailed and stylish sui generis graphics;2) opens up some parts from 1st game plot, a good main story here as well;3) no bugs, cards, achievements – all here for a reasonable price;4) (almost) without dumb jump scares, the game got you twisted all the time playing because of the necessity  to listen to the steps and watch for the clues, bringing an all-around nice atmosphere;5) notably satisfactory localization, one of the few things with a reasonable amount of narrative that I fully played in my first language (russian) and enjoyed it.8.5/10Minor cons: meh-level soundtrack (except two ending melodies), miserable ~5 hours to the full walkthrough, kinda one-linear story – even though it's interesting – that has only two endings.Thanks, Devespresso!
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: In all honesty, the game isn't that bad. Story and Characters were fine to me, but that isn't the issue I had with the game.But horror is very weak, and many of it's designs are very poor.I hate how many save points I keep running into, it's endless and if I "Die" or anything I pretty much lost like seconds worth of progress.Even though the Dev said he will spread resources thin and wide, the problem I encountered is, I only ever used 2 items and that is it, meaning my loadout of Mace, water bottle, Chocolate, bandage, and bandage were unchanged until I found bag upgrade, in which it just added chips and coffee.The game is just to easy, even the peek-a-boo is very quick and hiding spots are pretty much at every corner. Enemies are a joke.I was unsure at one point in subway wondering is there even enemy here? I never encountered the vicious sister there.Having the tag of "survival horror" is an insult to the genre. _childDocuments_.review: Difficult review to write, I quite enjoyed the story, but the rest is really disappointing.After reading the reviews i expected the atmosphere to be much creepier than it was, this game gave me the ability to be completely unfazed when jumpscares happen, and all of this is all thanks to how annoying monsters in this game are to deal with, they aren't scary, they aren't difficult to deal with, they are just annoying,there is a lot of moving around in this game, so you'll run into enemies often, they are quite loud so avoiding them isn't hard, but many times they'll just pop out of nowhere forcing you to run away from them and then search for some closet to hide into, at which point some annoying QTE will happen, there is no suspense or excitement to these sequences, the monsters are easy to outrun and QTEs are a really inane and ineffective way to make things more interactive and interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good side scroll horror game with interesting detailed lore. Much better than the first game, in this sequel we can travel to new locations instead of just wandering at the school hallways, so it never feels boring. Exploration is fun, and although you can only run/hide/dodge the enemies, it feels enjoyable. Art style is beautiful, soundtrack is also good. Very recommended for horror fans who are into intricated lore and characters. Beware though the are a lot of backtracking especially if you want to get good ending or complete achievements. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters is much more entertaining than the original The Coma, though that game is a good one too. The quality of the story, lore, characters, music, and atmosphere is exactly the same, but the drawing, animation, and direction are significantly improved, which affects player perception a lot. The locations became a lot bigger, more diverse, and much more interesting to explore; at the same time, they are easy to navigate, which tells about good level design.Stealth from monsters in the first game was awful; it wasn't able to scare or thrill, only to annoy. Those creatures were just obstacles making the process of exploring locations inconvenient. The situation is much better in the sequel: the sounds created by prowling monsters are more loudly audible, it is easier to spot them; the new gameplay mechanics, such as the usage of a pepper spray to make a creature let you go for a moment, are a nice addition to the arsenal (kind of survival horror). Crafting of unique items might be perceived as a superfluous thing, but it makes sense, since it adds new secondary goals for exploring the dangerous darkness of this crooked version of reality, besides notes and consumable loot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: Mina, the friend of the hero of the first part, is worried that Yongho has fallen into a coma and is not going to recover. Immersed in painful thoughts, she spends less and less time studying, and her academic performance drops. Ultimately, the teacher asks the girl to stay after class to discuss the latest grades and... inexplicably, Mina ends up in the world of Coma. It seems like the episode is teaching us that hanging around Asian schools after school hours is not a good thing!The gameplay of the 2nd “Coma” is similar to the first part. We still explore locations, hide from opponents and solve riddles. However, for the continuation, new mechanics were invented, and in general the game became larger and more interesting. For example, during the passage of Mina, she will meet a sufficient number of opponents - both unkillable shadow pursuers and creatures that can be fought back.This won’t be possible to do right away, but over time, the girl’s arsenal will have special items that will help us defend ourselves.From time to time, Mina will be able to receive side quests from other characters. The most common reward will be components for the manufacture of additional protective equipment - a stun gun, a homemade trap, and so on. These items are optional, but will be needed at moments determined by the plot and will allow you to avoid injuries that permanently reduce the heroine’s maximum health.The game will start at Sehwa School, but later Mina will be able to visit the police station, the traditional Korean market, the hospital and the subway station. And ultimately, it will be possible to move between all locations using special wormhole portals. Many doors and secrets will not be immediately accessible - you will not have the necessary keys, items or solutions to the puzzles.Of the minuses, I can probably only mention the map, on which side quests are not very well marked. You will have to remember some places during the passage. But in general, the game is well designed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was good, although I would suggest you play the first game, before this one, you don't need to in order to understand what's going on, but I feel like it helps build the emotional impact. _childDocuments_.review: Everything to the floatiness of comic book character models, the fluidity of the movement, controllable gameplay, audios of footsteps, and the discovery of lore-heavy collectables all captured what a horror game should be. Devespresso Games truly expanded and polished their style and brand on this game by creating an atmospheric horror environment with scary monsters. I'm not afraid to say I was spooked a couple of times by the monster when I pressed the sprint button as quickly as I normally answer a phone call. This is one of those games I wish I could erase the member on so I could relieve the experience again, yes, it's that good in my opinion. A game of cat and mouse is presented in this one, but still, stuff like coins and items are fairly disputed and a lot of them are useful in the right situation to survive. For example, you can bandages to stop losing HP, water to increase your stamina or pepper spray to stun the monster when you're grabbed. The items are unlimited though, so there's a little resource management, especially at intense moments to choose what to use, still. This game is fairly balanced thanks to the number of items and coins you can find as well as the spread-out save spots making it beginner-friendly. Can I also say they incorporated the best non-combat climax I've seen, it had only taken me 3 tries, but it was very satisfying to plan out and use every resource at my disposal whilst there was an arcading-style brawl fight in the background which looks to me it could be its own game? It was especially a plus to be rewarded for exploring everything and every way to achieve the 'good ending', at least for me.  I got nothing but high praise for this game, I wish would Devespresso Games can hurry up and make more games because if they can improve on Coma 1 they can improve on their other games like Vambrace: Cold Soul which is a series I wanted to get into but won't due to the mix responds.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: So I played the first game before this and let me tell you, you do NOT need to. They let you know what happened in the first while also really expanding the lore. I was really really surprised by the notes, I usually hate reading a ton of notes in games, but in Coma 2 it made the experience better. This game is also a complete upgrade of the first. The pacing of the first is terrible, but this sequel seriously did a 180 and fixed everything wrong in the first. This is a great survival horror game and I had a blast.The only part I dislike about the game is one of the puzzles in the metro, I had to look it up, I was overthinking it. Other than that pretty much a 9.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst a definite improvement over the first game, The Coma 2 still tends to feel tedious and repetitive at times. The story remains interesting enough to keep you carrying on and the art/sounds are brilliant, but the gameplay still feels lacking in some respects. As with the first there's multiple endings, though only 2 this time I believe, a good and a bad. Honestly I wish they would do away with the multiple endings if they make a third game seeing as only one ending will ever be canon rather than your endings/saves affecting the story in any way. The game is still a very enjoyable experience regardless and as mentioned, a much needed upgrade from the first, but I still feel there could be some improvements made to make it just that little bit more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Well I guess they didn't need my advice after all.  Ok, first things first.  If you haven't played the The Coma already, you really ought to think about doing that.  Yeah, I know, I had a lot of complaints about it, and it's always tough to say that you absolutely  to play the original before playing the sequel.  There's just so much here, though, that's drawn straight from the first game that you're going to miss out on a ton of stuff if you're not familiar with it.This is about as direct as a direct sequel gets.  It picks up right where the last one left off.  Where our former hero is concerned, the figurative Coma has given way to a literal one, which made me feel a little better about the ending I got last time. So now you're playing as another student at the same school who finds herself in a similar predicament.When you put it that way it might not sound very creative, and it's true that the fundamental game here hasn't changed very much.  Yet while it may look the same from a distance, you realize as you play it that this is actually a total renovation.  They basically gutted the first game down to the frame and rebuilt every aspect with vastly greater attention to detail. I mean, let's just go down the list:For one thing, they've really expanded the lore and cast of characters. Your mysterious helper from the first game is now joined by her whole team.  They don't turn out to be very much help, actually; but you do learn a lot more about their organization, the Coma and the cosmos in which it all takes place.  On the other side of the equation, your favorite teacher also makes her return with a familiar  of heels.  That shouldn't be a surprise, by the way, considering that they put her picture in the banner image.  Adding a bunch of extra material like that isn't always a good thing.  Sometimes it can be a distraction; but here it works hand-in-hand with the story and the scope grows accordingly. This time it's not just you but the entire world that's in danger, so instead of just trying to get the hell out of there, now you're caught up in working to undo some kind of ancient curse. In the process you unravel all sorts of history, and they even succeed in building more characterization. It's a nice middle-ground sort of plot, where they manage to up the ante while still retaining a personal feel.On the gameplay side, in addition to the maze of twisty little classrooms all alike, you'll be happy to know that you visit several more locations, including a police station, a subway, a hospital, a market--that was the best one--which really breaks up the monotony of the school.  From a practical standpoint the variety also makes finding your way around a lot easier.A good chunk of what you're doing still boils down to running away and hiding in cabinets so as not to get murdered, but they spice it up a little with quicktime button-press type events that you have to pull off in order to stay hidden.  Well, on second thought that does seem kind of pointless and arbitrary, and if you really hate those things that may not sound like an improvement.  I'm not so good at them myself, but these weren't too hard and on the other hand at least it gives you something to do besides sit there and twiddle your thumbs while you're waiting for the all-clear.  I guess it's really no more immersion-breaking than a monster chasing you into a bathroom with no exits and then losing track of you and giving up.The assortment of items is pretty much the same, but with hotkeys available the stamina recovery juice is  now actually useable.  As a remedy for insta-death at the hands of your teacher, they were also nice enough to to include a few cans of mace that you can use to escape.  These little touches add up, and help keep things moving along much more smoothly. You can actually play the game now instead worrying more about gaming the system.Long story short, it really is a perfect example of a sequel done right.  Everything that was wrong with the first game, they fixed; and everything that was good, they made even better.The result is not merely an improvement, but some of the best survival horror I've played in a long time.Way to turn it around, game! You can find more indie game reviews at  or visit my   Thanks, and enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: You get to play a cute girl this time, Park Mi-na.I like the art style.  You get plenty of it, with key cutscenes getting dedicated art in a pan-and-scan over static art style.  This is a welcome relief from the monotony of renpy's ubiquitous talking-head-over-dialogue-box style.  The art is all higher resolution than Coma 1.As is normal with a VN, there are few speech clips that are the audio equivalent of talking head expression PNGs.  "Annyeong" when you greet someone, "eh?" for puzzled, "ehhh!" for shocked, etc.  This is fine.  They remain in Korean, which is less distracting than when they localize it with cheap Californian VAs.  Some key lines of dialogue are fully voiced.The English text translation is excellent, showing native-speaker-equivalent grasp of English.The gameplay mechanics aren't stellar, but they're there to support the story, not the other way around.  This game doesn't have the budget of Akiba Strip or Persona.  What's there is reasonable and adequate.One minor gripe -- on gamepad, I switched to joystick to d-pad for the QTEs for more accurate input.  Then I tried to run away, only to discover regular movement was not bound to both, so the monster got me right away.  This should be a trivial fix.The DLCs seem a little overpriced.  I'd probably pay AUD2 to AUD5 for all of them, but not AUD3 per outfit.PS: I can't stop thinking the mace is lip balm.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel of "The Coma: Recut", and let me tell you something:This is how you make a sequel !!!They kept the comic-like graphics, combined this again with very fitting BGM, mixed it all up with some new cool features and mechanics and created a very cool game.This time you play not as Young-ho, but as Mina Park, but the premise is the same:Somehow you get sucked into "The Coma" and have to find your way out.But this time with ghostlights, new monsters, craftable items, new riddles (some very easy, some a bit more difficult), a mobile device that will probably outlive us all and a little bit of voice acting. I really enjoyed the voice acting parts and I would have loved that for the first part, but nevertheless were both quite captivating.What's not to love? Quit reading this resume and start playing this game :)

_childDocuments_.review: The Coma 2 is a survival horror game that uses hand-drawn comic book-style art in side-scrolling scenes. It was my first experience with this kind of gameplay. From the very beginning of the journey, I found myself in a world where reality is mixed with nightmares, and my task is to try to understand what is happening and survive. The gameplay of "Coma: Vicious Sisters" is filled with various tasks, puzzles and battles. Your decisions must be quick and they matter, and every action can affect the outcome of your adventure. The sounds and details are carefully crafted to immerse you in this nightmarish world as much as possible.As I write this review, I am going through the game for the second time, to get all the achievements and endings. I recommend it for a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: Bigger and better than The Coma: Recut in every way, Vicious Sisters does a great job in presenting an intriguing world with lots of lore and great gameplay. Running through the halls of many new eerie locations, escaping the grasp of a crazed murderer, all the while trying to stock up on supplies was both fun and nerve-wracking. Very much recommended for fans of the original, horror, and side-scrolling survival games. Also, potentially quite interesting for anyone interested in Korean culture.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel surpasses the original in overall quality making it an above average title compared to other 'Clock Tower' inspired titles or other Survival Horror games in general. There are some small frustrating game play mechanics as well as a trite story which is almost an unwelcome cliche in anime and Asian horror games which tainted my experience however these can be easily overlooked as the overall time playing this game was enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun, scary time I had with this one!Even though the gameplay is not as challenging as in the first one, it still managed to improve upon every other aspect of its predecessor. The story is great, the 2D graphics are hauntingly beautiful, they almost jump off the screen, and there’s also some replay value with the different endings. Even the controls are much, much better, and not as unresponsive as in the previous installment of the franchise, making the escape sequences easier and more dynamic.This is K-horror at its best, a wild haunted house ride, that you shouldn’t miss, especially if you played the first game! Can’t wait to see what the developers come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and unique. Make sure you use multiple save files though, because I was saving over one file and ended up getting poisoned and now I have no backup and I keep respawning and immediately dying. Such a great game, and challenging enough to keep you guessing but not so frustrating that you want to throw your whole keyboard out the window.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: Good art, good voice acting, I liked the gameplay, it's quite satisfying to explore and loot stuff. The puzzles aren't too hard, they're pretty much on point, for the most part there's no need of walkthroughs, it flows naturally. The quick time events are a little bit too much, but it isn't a big issue in the game, it's doable. The ending is okay, but there's too much information after the credits, they should've just keep it all together, not everyone has the habit to stay for the credits and wait. :D I did, and it was worth it. Good game.Over all I liked it. 8/10.  I recommend 100%.You'll finish it in 9-10 hours. It has a good length.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a brilliant upgrade from the first game, what a great sequel!The art style remained the same, which is good, the only thing being some slight differences in character designs, which personally, I do prefer the way Mina looked in the first game, but other than that, all is well. Speaking of art, I didn't mention it in the first game's review, but some of the world building and the just, the backgrounds, some of them are absolutely amazing, I mean, wow, from the messy destruction to the grotesque walls of flesh, it most definitely delivers on the tone it's trying to make, just looking at some of the stuff and people just deformed and dead, fantastic, well probably not for the people.The music is great, simply great. The somber background music and the times when it queues the more sad music for those moments really help seal the deal, which is pretty nice.Moving on to the story, it is pretty good. It started off strong, continuing where the first game left off, giving us a lot more answers too. The memos and other background text and note collectables are still here, helping provide that sweet, sweet lore to our story-hungry mouths, with some old ones coming back, with them rewriting and adding more detail and combining some notes from the first game and putting them in this one. After all, they do help with the context, along with providing more backstory and, heck, even more updates on the side story drama that happens around the school from the first game! It was an unexpected surprise, but a welcome one. I quite hope to get more updates on that in a possible future 3rd game, would be cool.Now, while we're talking about notes, the note collecting has become a lot easier, well, certainly a lot simpler, they now stand out MUCH more than before, and you can (for the most part) clearly spot them. Well, provided you explore (and re-explore in some cases), that's certainly still something you should do if you want to get that full context and all the notes. Now there are certainly *some* that may pass by you without you seeing them. It happened to me, they can blend in with the background in certain areas...And giving some opinion on the endings, the true ending is great as it should obviously be, and whilst we got some answers during the story, it doesn't mean the endings didn't seed in some questions and... figures to wonder about, that's for sure. Meanwhile, the bad ending is, well, sad as hell, obviously. Well, it's unfortunate, that's for sure, and I can see it being gut punching for some people if you're not too keen on sadness.It also upped its scare factor, thanks to the enemies and where they may or may not spawn, the little sounds in the distance, and the sudden stuff, it got me a lot more than the first game did.Now, characters, the level of quality on them still remains the same, which is to say, good. I think all the characters have been great, Mina is intelligent (although for certain things she can sometimes not notice the impact of her actions), kind, and the sorts of stuff that will make a likeable main character, the villain, has gotten some more story and context added to her, so that's great and revealing, but not going to include any spoilers here, which means I can't talk much more about the rest of the cast. Other than being all great, some have more screen time than others and thus are more developed, with others being left in the dust, but yeah.Enemy design is quite interesting, Dark Song is cool and all by all means, but it's certainly nice having an addition to the villain cast, even if it's only a minor role, that thing was certainly annoying (and even got me a few times, both in scares and in hits).One more thing I'd like to mention is how cool it is of the devs to allow you to explore the whole map one last time before going through the point of no return, which is the door to the final boss. For those that didn't collect everything and want to, this will be of great use to them.I don't think I noticed any bugs at all, only thing I noticed was *spoiler for where a section of the game is set* Jan 6th the art book appeared in the game folder, seems it might have been fixed? Dunno, but I noticed it was there after I checked the DLC list and the art book dlc actually stated a size.Overall, fantastic sequel to a great game, great story line, good art style and music, simpler note collecting, nice characters, and it upped its scare factor, I think. At least it got me a lot more than the first game did.

_childDocuments_.review: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters follow after tragic events of The Coma: Recut, where you play as Mina Park on a journey to save her friend & classmate, Youngho. The game introduces a lot of features to speak highly of - such as extra locations, additional interactive elements (mobile phone, special match-sticks, pepper spray cans), gorgeous graphics and a commendable music score. But, it falls flat in its story progression, drags the player along with its uninteresting characters and forces them to play some of the most frustrating gameplay elements in a horror game. Moreover, you get QTEs (Quick Time Events) in a 2020 game title (surprise!) and there is a major lack of atmosphere & immersion factor to even make you stop playing the game altogether. In short, The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters is a pretty mediocre horror game packaged in a shiny wrapper. A major step down from the former title (The Coma: Recut) in terms of story, atmosphere and gameplay elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Something ominous is going on at Sehwa High. One night our protagonist, Mina Park, faces this reality as she wakes inside the school, where the atmosphere is dark and eerie and doesn't feel normal to her. She soon discovers that she is trapped between the world of the living and world of the dead. There is also a malevolent entity that wishes her dead, as well as eldritch servants that control this realm she must avoid. Unlock the mystery of what is happening at Sehwa High as you travel the community of Sehwa; why are you trapped here, who is behind this as well as how you can escape?As you explore the many regions, collect notes for story information. There are also torn pages scattered around with lore to collect, and even bonus art content you can use to change the launcher backgrounds. Hiding and escaping from the entities is possible with the use of QuickTime events; if you hit them in the correct sequence and you just may survive the encounter.Released on Nov 7, 2019, in Early Access, by the developer Devespresso Games, and published by Headup, WhisperGames. It reached full release on Jan 28, 2020. It is tagged Adventure, Horror, Single Player, and I have added Indie, Visual Novel, and Casual to the tags. It features an exceptional graphic design with hand-drawn visuals & comics, sensational animations, as well as a brilliant soundtrack and audio design that set the eerie atmosphere. A mind-boggling story to unravel as you try to escape. A tutorial is included as well as partial controller support (Xbox & Steam Controller Tested).What an incredible play! I decided to jump right into the title and skipped the tutorial, as I prefer figuring out the dynamics of a game on my own when possible; it did cost me some playtime, though, as I had to figure out some of the mechanics that the tutorial would have shown me. No regrets though, I have had an exceptional amount of fun discovering everything on my own. This is the best Korean Horror I have ever played. The atmosphere, animations, storyline, and translations were all done to perfection; I have been glued to it since I started playing, and it is not often that a title can grab my attention as this one has. The genre-blending the title presents is imaginative as well as captivating. For the priceline, and amount of game-time the title offers is an exceptional value for all you horror lovers. You do not want to miss this one! Add it to your cart and get playing now; you know you want to, just do it and get it over with.I did have one time I accidentally deleted my save file when I miss clicked; it would be helpful to have a confirmation for save file deletion to avoid this situation. Just don't derp and miss click as I did and have to start over. I made use of the 4 save slots after that. I felt there were too many save points making the game a bit too easy in some areas.The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters: A Spectacular Example of Korean Horror. A Must-have for Horror Fans & an Instant Gem!9/10Pro's+ Exceptional Graphic Design+ Sensational Audio Design+ Mind-boggling Story+ Partial Controller Support+ Steam Achievements + Steam Trading CardsCon's - I have nothing for this sectionKey provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: I desperately wish steam had a mixed reviews. I feel like this is a "good game", but I didn't enjoy it for most of the runtime. Even writing this right after the ending, I don't think I liked it.First, the positives:• This game is unbelievably gorgeous. That's clear from the promotional material but it's even more stellar in-game.• I am a SUCKER for good worldbuilding and this game just hits every personal guilty pleasure trope I can think of in this department. The supplimental lore snippets sprinkled around the corners of the world are ANYTHING BUT the filler they would be in a lesser game. They weave into into the greater story fantastically and build it up in a really enjoyable way.Now, the negatives• The pacing of this game felt really really off to me. (ignore my playtime. I finished it in less time) I just wasn't engaged for most of it's runtime. The pacing of games with fairly light mechanics is difficult to get right, so while some people might have been engaged, I certainly wasn't.• The horror really wasn't there for me. I consume a lot of horror media, and I feel like this is aimed towards people who are more sensitive to it. A few of the game's mechanics (hiding is the biggest culprit) rely on you feeling like a situation is tense for them to feel fun and engaging. Because I wasn't, some parts of the game were just a drag.Overall, I have absolutely no desire to play this game a second longer. It brought me moments of genuine joy (mostly near the end), but I also had to trudge through a swamp of mediocrity to get there. It also feels like that second statement shouldn't be true! This looks and feels like a good game, and I feel like I should have enjoyed it.Other things I felt like mentioning: • The story was a mixed bag for me. the final act is GREAT. some bits of writing are FANTASTIC (looking at you secret area near the end), but it falls flat a lot of the time. It's meant to draw you from place to place and I just... felt like I was filling out a checklist.• This game has some really well-handled puzzles! They all makes sense, and the hint system is legitimately really well done! I think the devs should be really proud of that• There's some absolutely BRUTAL localisation here. Did not expect to be called a thot by my best friend.• CPTSD representation??? It's a bit cheesy but it's a welcome surprise that ties into the themes of the game really nicely.• If you're the kind of person that gets annoyed when you can't skip cutscenes, you're in for a lot of that :/

_childDocuments_.review: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters is a console ported 2D visual novel/adventure game where you explore a school to unravel a supernatural mystery.  Gameplay consists of clicking through a lot of text and then walking around a 2D school, with a bit of inventory management and so on.It's pretty tedious stuff.  While the art looks fine, the implementation is not.  It's a bad console port.  There's console peasant childrens toy gamepad prompts.  The interface is clunky even for a console game, no specific changes were made to take advantage of the superior KB+M interface.  Gameplay is unengaging and not worth getting into for the sake of the story, which is unfortunate.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely wouldn't have finished this game if it didn't have save spots all over the place, because I hated one of the basic mechanics, instant death if you get caught by a particular monster that shows up every once in a while apparently randomly most of the time.  It's very difficult to run away fast enough and find a hiding spot before being grabbed.  You have less than a second to act usually when she appears on screen, and you have to know exactly where the nearest hiding spot is to have any chance of reaching it in time.  And even if you manage that, you have to successfully complete three QTE with no misses.  It was terrible and stupid.  I quickly just got the point of not even trying with this mechanic.  As soon as I got ambushed by this monster (except a few scripted times when it's unavoidable) I would just immediately reload.  Fortunately I lost very little time that way usually, since I got in the habit of saving every time I accomplished anything or made any forward movement, and that really wasn't any real hassle, since save spots are plentiful, and saving is very quick at these spots.Once I set aside this bad mechanic -- which is not at all central to the main gameplay experience and is instead just an occasional annoyance --  the rest of the game was quite well done and fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good sequel, but I prefer the 1st game.The 1st game's gameplay was compact in 3 small buildings, where basically all the action and story took place. And while this game expands on the amount of locations, it also just makes it feel less focused, and less interesting than in the original.The gameplay is a bit frustrating in how similar it is to the 1st game. The only real changes are the removal of the hiding anywhere button, and the introduction of the roaming enemies, which dont really pose too much of a threat. The amount of hazardous obstacles got increased to absurd levels, but the main problem of them not really being able to hit you, as long as you run through them, makes them also a non-threat. The main monster of the game can now 1 shot you, but despite that, its still really difficult to die in this game, if you played and learned from the 1st game.I also am not the biggest fan of how "lazy" the quests for safety items are in this game. Where all of them are literally "Talk to guy. Find 3 items. Talk to guy, again, to exchange 1 item. Go to Crafting desk. Craft.". Doing this once would be fine, but 4 times? The 1st game wasnt too original in how its quests looked like either, as they're all basically simple fetch quests, but there the game at least tried to make them feel a little bit unique, while here its impossible to not notice the similarities.But there are some things that were changed in this game, that I liked.Reduced amounts of endings. And while this sounds like a negative, it really isnt. The 1st game had 5 endings, where endings 1-4 were just "The same ending, just add a bit at the end", and getting all of them was just not fun. And the only important ones were basically ending 4, as it had all the small story bits, and ending 5, which was basically the True End of that game.There's also the Crowbar. Which is introduced pretty late into the game, and it allows you to open doors in old locations, making backtracking way more fun and rewarding, unlike the Art quest from the 1st game, for example. There are also the matches, which allow you to get more items, and even open some doors from the inside of rooms, which wasnt introduced as a mechanic, so finding it felt really great.Overall I like this game, its a good sequel, and I would recommend it. But I still prefer the original.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished "The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters" right after I played "The Coma: Recut" for the First time.(See my Review for that.)So right after finishing I didn't order my thoughts on the Game, so here goes my incoherent ramble on what I think about the Game.Let me start by saying that when "The Coma: Recut" is Resident Evil, "The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters" is Resident Evil 2.Both are great Games but the second does many things better than the first one (even though in the Case of RE the first one is still a great classic).Here is a Question some people may have answered already: Do you need to play the first Game before playing the 2nd? I think yes just because it is easier to follow the story and characters. It is a direct continuation of the first one with the same characters.A few things that popped out right after starting: - In cutscenes and in a few "Key Moments" there is a little bit of Voice Acting here and there.- Has the same style as the first Game but looks a bit smoother/crisper.- The second Game has Achievements on Steam. (Wondered why the first Game didn't have any...)- Almost the same control scheme and Gameplay as the first one.- Has DLC's but all of them are cosmetic and thus optional, so you don't need to spend any extra money just because you want to experience the full Game.- This time around the Game has a HUD so you don't confuse your buttons (I did that a few times in the 1st one, so yeah, nice QOL Change here).- Also new: Quick Action Slots for your consumables which is also a good QOL improvement. But on controller you can't "Quick Shuffle" the items, but you can move them around in the inventory. (Btw. I found that out by the END of the Game, going into your inventory actually pauses the Game this time around)- Inventory is pretty basic but this Game doesn't need a complicated or RE Style inventory.- The Maps look a bit cleaner (even though the Maps in the first one were good already) and they got also a QOL improvement because you can see all your Save Locations and Teleport Locations.- Stamina SEEMED to recover faster as in the first one but it could be that I am mistaken. Maybe there is no difference at all, but this was just my impression.- Animations SEEMED to be a little more stiff this time around, but I could also be mistaken here.- There are Quick Time Events for when you're hiding to add a little more tension (and for some people probably also frustration).- Now there are more hiding spots that also differ in how they make you visible (just changes the QT Events I think)So yeah, those are just a few thoughts that popped into my head here.What else? I think there was a lot more to interact with in the first Game but this here seems more streamlined and this is for the better imo.It still sucks that when you read a note on the wall for example, that the Game is not paused and the "Killer" comes right at you, but you can't do anything because you have to skip the text first all while she hits you. So here is a tip: Only read inside of rooms, never on the floors/in the hallways.Also there was a stupid instakill situation where the Killer spawned right in front of me after I entered an area, I couldn't react at all and got instakilled right away. I know that the Mace is intended to counteract that but apparently there was no indication that I lost my Mace and I didn't know that I used it. But that's on me I guess.You will use Dodge quite a bit more in this Game and it is also very generous. And it's nice that when you hide, you don't have to re-light your lighter, as in the first Game you always had to re-light your flashlight after exiting your hiding spot.As I said, a lot of QOL improvements over the first one. Sound Design was also spot on, you could always hear the footsteps and in which direction they were going.Overall I died a few times here and there but MOSTLY it was my fault. In my Review of "The Coma: Recut" I said that the Game frustrated/annoyed me more than anything else. Here it was not so much. Yes, there were a few moments that were kind of annoying, but nothing as bad as in the first one.Also I didn't use a walkthrough like I did for the second half of the first Game just because I was annoyed. Finished the Game in 9.8 hours, 31/35 Achievements, took my time, got Ending A (don't know if it's good or bad, it seemed good) and definitely recommend this more than the first Game.Yeah, that's it. Rambling's over...

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some nice changes to it that the first game didn't have.I personally don't like the quick time events, BUT I don't mind them either. It's not like they will ruin the entire experience, but I wouldn't say that they belong in a couple of places. This is just my opinion, so take this with a grain of salt.I like the story, and the characters, it's not insanely indepth, but it's fun to explore the entire game and look for items that will help you get further in the story. You basically have to look through EVERYTHING. Which I think is good, not bad. You get to see every map and try to open/unlock every door. So I had a good time going through everything that I felt that I could go through.Thank you, Devespresso Games for making such a cool visual novel horror game. Both of your games are amazing and I appreciate your hardwork.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, people are right. This is a really good sequel. Every aspect of the first game is improved. There is voice acting, the art is a lot more detailed and the gameplay is refined. It still is at its core very similar to the first game, just improved in every single way.The story continues where it left off at the true ending from the first game. There are multiple environments and the game uses the mechanics from the first installment to integrate traveling from place to place well. Puzzles are simple and satisfying and the stealth mechanic is A LOT better. Meaning you can't get soft locked like I did in the first game and they don't spawn in your face. There are new characters and they serve the story well. The game even explores new themes which I enjoyed quite a bit (bullying and standing up for yourself). And the comicbook style of cinematics is something I also enjoy very much.Hopefully a sequel or a new story in the same universe is being made. I really want to see more from these developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: So last time we were in the Coma, I thought it was an alright experience. It had a solid foundation to work with and its own unique style, but it didn’t fully wow me. However unlike films, sequels to video games usually tend to be better than their original. Did this accomplish that goal? Well…ProsThe atmosphere and soundtrack for this series continues to shineA very well crafted story backed up with more characters to interact with and more easily accessible notes that expand upon the world’s loreThe world of the Coma is even expanded upon this time going beyond just the school and the new locations look greatDark Song is back and this time she’s not the only threat you need to worry about as more creatures stalk around the cornerWelcomed new mechanics have been introduced to the game which adds more tension when hiding or even being grabbed by Dark Song herselfBack are the unlockable artworks for completing tasks in the game as well as a couple different endings, giving it a little more replayability. The resource management this time is definitely improved in my opinion with the introduction of a hot bar, no more having to stop in a hiding spot mid chase to quickly use an item. However...ConsThe blighted tentacles and the clawing shadows feel a bit less of a threat this time around, this might’ve been done to balance out with the newly introduced shadow stalker but I never had a situation where I had to deal with all three while Dark Song was chasing me. As a result of this, I never had to really worry about being afflicted with bleed or poison.  So in closing, is our second dive into the realm Devespresso Games has crafted worth the trip? Absolutely, I’m definitely more of a fan of this one than the last. This sequel not only fixes the few issues I had with its predecessor but greatly improved upon its original formula as any good sequel should do. I look forward to what the devs have in store for the future and hope we might return once again to this nightmare realm they’ve crafted so well. That being said I give the Coma 2: Vicious Sisters 4 sadistic shades out of 5!
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: The games and content are really fun.I watched the streamer play the game and followed him.For the most part, every time I play a game following a streamer it becomes less fun.But this game is different for the first time and is equally fun to play.Hopefully the next game will be more fun and interesting to play than Part 2. It's definitely worth the money. Just buy it and play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

You can hear the clicking of her heels when she is in the area, I imagine if you headphones on you probably could tell if shes coming from the left or right direction of the screen. It intensified the horror, much appreciated!2. It seems they added much more character depth this time around by not making them seem one dimensional. Cons1. Same as before controller is a must due to terrible keyboard controls2. they added choose your own adventure routes meaning... 3. The backtracking is 100 worse because the maps you explore requires quite bit of effort to travel especially at the end game and you have to go back to school to get x item and travel all the way back to end game map again. Because the maps and areas are much bigger than the first game4. ending  Honestly got frustrated and didn't finish the game because of it.... it depends on you automatically knowing without a guide and punishes you with zero wiggle room.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fantastic horror game that exceeded my expectations. I loved the first game, The Coma: Recut, and I was a bit afraid that this sequel would ruin it, but no!! It was amazing, I really enjoyed the new mechanics, like the crafting system, the quick time events, and the different locations. The only thing I regret is that I couldn't craft more items later, because I thought I wasn't doing the main quest, but overall, I loved it and I highly recommend it. The game has a great story, with interesting characters, secrets, and twists. The graphics are beautiful, with a hand-drawn style that fits the dark atmosphere. The sound design is also very good, with creepy noises and voice acting. I hope there will be more games like this in the future.+Mina smash
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Great storytelling, superb artwork / art style, creepy atmosphere, good puzzles, interesting survival mechanics (for a non-combat game the game does a good job of making the player feel interactive with evading the killers and environmental threats using QTEs and a dodging/running/stamina/item system). As someone who played a lot of DBD, this game made me feel right at home. When the game is on sale the deal is even better and there are some nice skins/outfits you can buy as DLCs to customise the main protagonist to your choosing. One thing, without spoiling, is that the game uses a kind of formulaic way of progressing through the various biomes that has you always doing a certain similar thing over and over again toward the end of each biome and I feel like that could have been adjusted a bit to seem less repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: Good game if you can get past though there's no english audio only subtitle. so stuck hearing korean audio which is fine, but can be odd if not used hearing korean speaking. i just wish they localized the character name, sometimes i wonder who talk and who mentioned. the gameplay very improved from first game, doge more usefull now, and more many hiding spot.  and why mina moaning everytime i cant open DOOR??downside is there certain item that need to be triggered first so it appear. it sometimes problem when in hurry to get some quest item, turn out i have to make detour to 1floor from 3floor, and cant be triggered other way. and vision range more wide now which make the game more easy. at first game vision range just around the character like fog. now its entire screen, so you can easily navigate around game without light the fire. and the ghost now actualy walk to hunt, can be hear its footstep, thats game changing. first game the ghost teleport instantly, the story good very intruguing. i wish some big publisher pick this. very potential if they can make its sequel 3d.

_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: This game totally blew my mind! The storyline was very interesting and captivated. I loved how our decisions on whether to do side quests shaped the game. Those quick time events? Intense! The graphics and music were amazing. And that ending? Totally unexpected, but in the best way possible. Can't stop thinking about it. _childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: A massive improvement compared to the first game, love the art style and story. Like the first game reading and understanding the clues are important to make sure you do not end up running around in circles. _childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played Coma 1, went into this game with zero expectations, completely clueless, but this turned out to be an amazing experience. During the first chapter I thought it was just okay, but then the game hooked me in and I couldn't stop. The mystery of the Coma was interesting  from the beginning to the end, I also read every note because they provided more background info about the world of the Coma. Gameplay is really simple but challenging enough to keep me going. Lots of exploration and revisiting old places, but that didn't bother me at all. Soundtrack is great, but my favorite thing is the art style. It's beautiful. The game also has 2 endings which I thought was really nice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, despite it being different to what I normally play. The artwork is amazing, and the soundtrack adds to the atmosphere. It did sometimes glitch/freeze, causing me to die (e.g., during quick time events, it would freeze and not register I had entered the commands), however the game is still worth playing!It was interesting to learn about Youngho's fate after the first game, as well as seeing Mina develop as a person/character throughout the events of the game.I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys thriller/high suspense games, with beautiful artwork.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an improvement over the first game. I don't mean that The Coma 1 is bad by saying this, but it more feels like a prologue for this game to tell the full story. It's so much scarier, the plot is more involved, there's more to the game play and your choices, and the atmosphere is so, so, so much darker.This is just a fantastic game, and a great expansion to the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters

_childDocuments_.review: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters takes place right after The Coma: Recut. So, it is recommended to play the first game before playing this one. _childDocuments_.name: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters
