_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the game with the good ending and 100% item completion, and I'm glad that they unlocked new game modes because I almost felt bad finishing it. Some people here do complain about the "backtracking", but to be honest, it didn't bother me at all. There's mechanics and upgrades that allows you to breeze through the place pretty efficiently and quickly, and most of all, you'll actually WANT to take your time and check around. I swear to God, there's a LOT to discover and even if you pass by a room 10x, 20x, you'll end up discovering something that was right in your face all this time but you didn't know it was... like a ladder, a vine, a hidden exit, etc. The fun you get from discovering the whole thing is highly engaging, and since the game allows for good movement mechanics and various ways to approach battles, you'll surely find what suits you best to enjoy your time playing the game. It will feel slow at first, but trust me on that: the game is well thought out on that front.Narrative-wise, it doesn't reinvent the wheel in any way. The story is pretty straight forward, but still has some small, intriguing elements that will actually push to discover everything you can find before finishing it. You'll get it in due time, but while the story is "good but not great", the visuals and the soundtrack highly makes up for it. The game is gorgeous and the soundtrack is really good, especially the Ash section of the tower.  Also, there's a few easter eggs here and there, and I discovered a whole area that's dedicated to one of my best NES game ever! I won't say what game, though.. If you know the game, you'll be glad to stumble upon this treat!So, do I recommend it? Simple: I Absolutely recommend it! The new "new game" mode just punished the hell out of me, so I'll keep at it for sure! And from what was hinted in the game, there's also Another "new game" mode waiting for me!?! Wow! I'm glad that there's more to do when it's done, so replayability is both to be expected AND a treat, since you'll probably want to return to the game when you're done anyway! It's simply THAT good. :)

_childDocuments_.review: A solid metroidvania with very enjoyable exploration and old-school platforming.Does things a bit different with deaths always sending you back to the very first room and makes it satisfying as you constantly unlock shortcuts and the occasional movement ability. Map could use a little bit more information or a personal marker/note system to keep track of all the paths you can't take until later.Secrets feel worthwhile and are fun to hunt down, especially as they can be rather clever.One  is how the game falls into the trap of letting you upgrade your character sky high without offering higher difficulty to compensate. The difficulty fell off a cliff towards the end and I was pretty much messing around even during the final boss.Up until that point the combat had been a decently challenging and fun part of the experience, being something of a mix between Mega Man and Castlevania. Boss fights were fun enough, though I beat them all on either the first or second try, which I believe often came down to boss attacks being fairly simple and minimal. And then character upgrades happened.Music is good with a nice touch of it switching to a softer and quieter version in save rooms.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The team has been really responsive and fixed pretty much every bug I was aware of that I could replicate consistently on earlier builds. To make the review more reflective of the current state of the game, I deleted a few sections of it talking about how buggy the game was at the time (which I copy pasted to a file just in case another build of the game ends up having the same issues)."Astalon: Tears of the Earth" is, for the most part, a great metroidvania / non-linear platformer. The gameplay mechanics are solid, the music is great, the story is alright. As far as the story goes, you play as three adventurers (Arias, Kyuli and Algus) on a quest to save their village from being completely poisoned by the Gorgons, devilish stone creatures that have come to life, which all conveniently happen to live in a tower nearby. After dying in a fight against the Black Knight, Algus faces Epimetheus, the titan of death, letting him reincarnate every time he dies at the tower's entrance until his goal is fulfilled and allowing him and his allies to grow stronger with each reincarnation.The gameplay is pretty similar to what you can find in other metroidvanias, which a lot of focus on exploration, platforming and combat. There are two mechanics that set it apart from the rest of the genre, one of which has given it inaccurate and unfair comparisons to Rogue Legacy, and people being led to believe the game is a "roguelite" at its core.The first one, and the one that makes people compare the game to Rogue Legacy and roguelites in general, is tied to the game's plot. Every time you die you face Epimetheus, and he lets you buy upgrades for your characters, which range from passive stat boosts to new active skills. However, instead of respawning at the last campfire you've saved at, you will always start at the tower's entrance, which makes exploration both harder and easier in a way. There are conveniently placed elevators (essentially warp rooms) around the tower, with one of them being in the second room of the first area, and since the tower isn't procedurally generated. Biggest issue with this mechanic is the lack of tooltips when it comes to purchasing upgrades using orbs you've gathered through your runs (and you get to keep the ones you don't use). Other than the character specific upgrades, you're not given information on what these upgrades do until you buy them, which can be annoying when you realize that you just spent all your orbs on an upgrade you probably didn't need at the moment. There's one in particular that might scare you upon purchasing (you receive more damage from enemies, but they drop more orbs), but it only lasts for one run so it won't make the game all that much harder all things considered. While the lack of tooltips was common in 8-bit and 16-bit era games, I would say it's an outdated approach to item/upgrade shopping.The other mechanic I have to mention is the character switching. The level design is good, and it's going to involve some backtracking early on since you can only switch characters at specific points in the map (campfires). Each character has unique abilities that you will have to make use of to progress through the dungeon. The three characters play really well and their unique abilities make them all useful at different points. There are a few puzzles here and there, but they're not particularly difficult.The combat is good and fluid, although I think the bosses should have been a bit harder. The first boss fight is probably the only hard one in the game, with the second one not being particularly hard, just kind of tedious, and every other boss being a bit of a pushover.All in all: Would I recommend "Astalon: Tears of the Earth"?  Yes, but keep in mind the two aforementioned mechanics that some people find frustrating to deal with, but fans find to be well put together. Something else I should mention is the length. It only took me a little under 10 hours to beat the game with 83% completion, and a bit above 12 to reach 100% completion. Might take about 20 hours if you're trying to get every single achievement. The unlockable game modes add some replayability as well.

_childDocuments_.review: So I picked this up ages ago and just now got  around to actually playing it. I have to say I did my self a disservice in  waiting so long. Astalon is a old school action adventure  plat former done in a classic retro 8 bit style. A classic metroidvania in every sense of the word.  Its game play is well done, music score epic, and a fairly decent plot. I wholly enjoyed it and have added it to my replay list.I feel that any fan of Metroidvania type of games should add this to their library as I had a blast playing it. Now that being said it does have some points which  some people may not like.  The three big ones I have noticed being talked about are below. First is that it is done in a retro style. that means gameplay and graphics are generally "less". Now I personally find this a plus as the game is intended to be like that but some people may not. Second is whole concept of dying and starting over at the start. Again personally I find this a excellent game mechanic but some people do not. This does get easier as through out the game you find various quick travel points open up shortcuts. But some of the back tracking does get tedious I will admit but I feel this just enhances the game. Third point is the concept of having several characters and needing to switch out.Which means having to find a campfire and then making it back. This is partially negated by the fact you get a item that allows you to quick switch without a campfire. Generally you  can probably get that item around about a third/halfway   into the game. I'm a bit torn on this one to be honest. I agree in that the item was needed, and getting it when you do in the general pacing of the game I feel is just about right. But Iam not entirely sure I would of put it where it was. But at the same time  not entirely sure where I would of put it  instead.  Maybe instead of  being a found item, have it be a purchasable item that unlocks after killing the second boss or something?

_childDocuments_.review: While a bit buggy and responsiveness can be a little clumsy, this is a game where you can feel the love and dedication on every screen. The art style is beautiful and I find it impossible to get tired of it. Progression is just the right amount of frustrating and backtracking never feels boring. The map is gigantic but it is a real joy to traverse, specially as you unlock shortcuts. I 100%d the main game, finished a gargoyle run, am working on black knight and ng+ files, normally I need to back off for a while after my first run when it comes to metroidvanias, but this game keeps me coming back.

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon: Tears of the Earth is an excellent Metroidvania, which features a multi-character swapping mechanic where each character has unique skills that allows them to access objects, and places, that other characters cannot. The main campaign features a fairly large map to explore, along with both RPG and Rogue Like elements to help you upgrade your team over time. Like any Metroidvania worth it's salt you can also find special items that grant you special abilities, and in some cases these are character specific. These range from the ability to slow fall with the mage-esq character, to the ability to deflect projectiles with a swing of the warrior-esq character's sword. If you're into the genre, you're likely to find the main campaign very enjoyable. There are a lot of secrets to be found.The extra content is a bit eh, if I'm being honest. I'm gonna talk about them here, and why they're eh so if you want to avoid spoilers on unlockables be aware that's what we're getting into.The Black Knight mode is more or less a speedrun mode where you get a character who can jump higher than the other characters, activate magic switches with his sword and spell, and heal by sitting in blood pools. It's neat, but much like the Richter/other Belmont mode in the CastleVania metroidvania games it's not as interesting as the main game. You can beat this fairly quickly as most content can be outright skipped.The second extra run, Monster Mode, is where the game starts to run into problems. Firstly, you basically control a gargoyle who has two mechanics: spitting fire, and flying. You cannot climb ladders. You have to fly up them. This is all well and good but when I played through I had the game randomly stop allowing me to fly on multiple instances. A quick glance around the discussion forum showed me I'm not the only person who had this issue - but the devs seem to be aware of it, so hopefully it'll get fixed down the line. The other major issue with this mode is you can only heal via RNG meat drops that heal five HP a pop. So any time you need to heal up you basically need to sit there grinding out on easy enemies until you get something like 30 meat drops to happen. It slows the game to a crawl and saps the motivation to even bother completing the run. Especially considering that unlike Black Knight mode this mode has no real plot relevance and just seems to serve as a semi-reference to the old Gargoyle Quest games.Lastly there is a boss rush mode, but I've not attempted it yet. I do see many people calling it the worst part of the game, however, citing the reasoning of incredibly punishing difficulty, and majorly grindy in soul (see also: experience) collection.Still in spite of the missteps with the "optional" content (all of them are required to unlock everything), I would say the game is absolutely worth playing. The $20 (at least here in Australia) price tag is a little steep, but I also don't feel as if I didn't get my moneys worth.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played.  It's exactly what I like in my games, especially this genre.  My only criticism (although I don't really have any suggestions to change it.)  Is depending on where you are on the map, sometimes it's easier to die to get to another point quicker than it is to go there from where you currently are.  To me, this is what I thought the future of gaming would look like back in the 80s; a natural progression of games from that era such as Zelda 2, Legacy of the Wizard, Metroid, TMNT (The first one), etc.  It's like they took all the elements from my favorite NES/Computer games and mixed them all together here.  If you miss 8-bit graphics, and old-time charm, I can't recommend this enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice retro metroidvania with tight controls and a fun and varied map. The three main characters play well and each have their advantages and disadvantages. The pacing is the most interesting part for me. Since there usually is no healing at the camp fires and very little during the game, health becomes more of a resource that fuels your exploration. Usually on a new spawn you make a plan on what you want to do next, pick a character to play and then go see if it works our. Along the way you may find places your current character cannot go so you keep them in mind for next time and see what else is there to find. I have not seen this concept before in a metroidvania and I must say it worked quite well for me.All in all I am very glad I picked this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good level design, art and music. Platforming and combat feel good, and since you have multiple characters at your disposal it also has an added layer of figuring out which one is better for each section.I'll address some of the points from the negative reviews. Yes, it does have more backtracking than the standard Metroidvania. Going back to the start when you die (and you will die as healing is very limited) is brutal at first, but the map has a few warp points and clever shortcuts that mitigate this. It also didn't bother me as much because the movement and controls are pretty smooth, and because killing enemies is never pointless as you get orbs to upgrade your characters.There are also a few unlockable modes that add even more value to this gem. While they don't have much story it's still a fun way to use the knowledge of the map and mechanics you've gained through the main story, giving you new ways to traverse and completely break the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon is a great little Metroidvania gem. While at first it might feel a bit linear and the abilities of your characters limited, fear not! Upgrades and items discovered along the way will greatly flesh out your moveset. Aesthetics are also very nicely done and closely respect the 8-bit NES limitations, so if that's your kind of thing, you will definitely enjoy the graphics. It totally looks and feel like a game that could've released on the later years of the system.Now, I've seen some people complain about how some of the level design forces you to go back with a certain character to unlock paths, causing unnecessary backtracking. Spoilers: You won't need to go back forever to a fireplace to switch characters. You will most likely unlock that ability not long after you start thinking how troublesome that is. I think its smart that the games forces you to play a bit with each character before giving you free reigns over who you want to main.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, exploration-focused retro-styled game with good combat, underwhelming world building and threadbare characters.Mechanically, this game is excellent. The combat and platforming are responsive and engaging, exploration and advancement require thought and are rewarding without being overly convoluted. It also has one of my favorite death systems, upon purchasing an item an orb appears at the location of your last death which gives a good amount of ablative HP, providing a welcome boost in an area that you struggled with before. That being said, it is not perfect. Fast travel points are critical and there is quite a bit of space between them at times, forcing players into long, repetitive runs for up to several hours at a stretch. Backtracking can be a long and difficult process because of how convoluted the paths are combined with how simple the provided map is. Overall however, these are minor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.While the mechanics and level design are top notch, what keeps this game from being one of my personal favorites is the lack of world building, narrative or interesting characters. The areas of the tower are all very similar except for a palette swap and slightly different enemies, the characters rarely interact and the narrative never evolves beyond the initial (solid) hook introduced in the first five minutes. What little plot it does have is also poorly sequenced, I experienced several plot beats out of order (referencing an event that hadn't yet taken place). It does have good sound design though.Completion level: Unlocked all items and characters, got the first ending.Comparable games: Shovel Knight, Hollow Knight.

Multiple modes of play once you finish the main game so it warrants multiple plays as well. Nice pixel art and catchy chip-tunes. Solid A.

_childDocuments_.review: Really excellent Metroidvania. The pixel art is absolutely gorgeous!I do wish that you respawned at the last campfire you visited. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent Metroidvania - helmed by Matt Kapp (of "Castle in the Darkness" fame) - featuring: multiple characters (each with unique abilities), an impressive pixel-art style, and a unique mechanic centered around Death. While dying always sends you back to the entrance - all bosses, shortcut unlocks, and secrets remain finished - plus dying lets you meet Epimetheus. This Titan of Death, holding a secret pact with one of the heroes, will impart various upgrades - some permanent, others temporary - in exchange for Orbs harvested from your foes.While lacking the scattershot mix of references seen across "Castle in the Darkness", I will say Astalon has much deeper gameplay and plot (yet never overdone). In some ways this adventure, with multiple heroes to play - all with bespoke abilities, and ways to be empowered - reminds me of what I wished "Legacy of the Wizard" was like on NES (versus what Falcom actually made). After finishing the 10-to-15 hour non-randomized Tower - a journey well-worth the price - players may even retackle Astalon using extra characters (with vastly remixed rules), or even face the ominous Boss Rush.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I could not put this game down. Excellent Metrodvania on the lines of Dragon Slayer 4/Legacy of the Wizard on the NES (just not as brutally unclear/unfair). Lots of references to other NES games.Your starting three characters share health and if any die, you're kicked back to the start of the castle with an opportunity to spend the "money" you earned for permanent upgrades - meaning you can't game over.The game handles all of its mechanics well: shortcuts are everywhere, character upgrades make things easier, upgrades exist for your map, health restoration, swapping characters and there's even a way to pay to get revenge on a boss you died to. Any mechanic I found vaguely annoying I found an upgrade for later to fix it.+Swappable characters w/ differing abilities/stats+Secrets are intuitive, never needed a guide to 100%+New shortcuts every few screens+Some humor+Decent music+Love the various gorgon artwork+Lots of accessibility settings+Tons of optional/semi-hidden content+Title screens are skippable+No frustrating platforming or frequent trolling+Final point of no return clearly marked+Minor puzzles around clever use of character abilities+Unlockable music, artwork+Unlockable +Multiple endings+New Game+ mode with new map-Three unlockable modes of challenging play after completion+Almost 20 hours for me to casually (no guides) 100%  the normal mode+Multiple save profiles with ability to copy them~Little way to restore health until late in game~Couple spelling errors~Not incredibly difficult (can't speak for boss rush or either NG+ mode yet)~Way to mark map would have been nice~Way to quick-select specific character (like FPS weapon-wheel) would have been nice~Lore got interesting. Wish there was more.-Number of purchaseable items not fully explained-Experienced a number of minor graphical glitches-Experienced a number of minor movement glitches-One campfire cutscene played out of story order-A couple of audio bugs-Boulder rooms occasionally bug out and double up on falling rocks-Very easy to accidentally skip text-Mouse cursor stays on screen even if using controller

_childDocuments_.review: This game got bugged for me, a lot. I wasn't even able to play it for a while, but then I found a solution for myself. If you run into issues with loading your save files, or some bugs, feel free to comment here so maybe my solution would also help you.Other than many bugs I've encountered and frustrated me, Astalon is a great metroidvania. If you've heard of this game, you've probably also heard that everytime you die, you're sent back to the where you start the game, not where you last saved the game. Also savepoints don't heal you, and you also don't have any healing abilites . So you go back to where you started a lot. From time to time, this makes things very frustrating but it also makes finding a shortcut becomes much more rewarding. There are ways of fast traveling, but you should first find the item to use it, which can be easily missed. If you're much more into exploration than combat, this game makes you explore everywhere. There are three main characters, and two unlockables, which in my opinion are unbalanced, and you find yourself playing exact same one that probably every other player plays with. But every character have their own use, so you technically can't defeat the game without using others.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game a lot. From an artistic standpoint, the visuals are detailed and interesting to look at, and the bright colour choices for the areas make the game lively. The choices for foreground and texture details make spotting secrets, well, not easy, but doable. There are very few 'invisible' secrets in the game.From a game play standpoint, it is very fun. However there are some drawbacks. Until you find the certain items, changing characters can be quite a headache and involves a lot of backtracking. The fast travel system is decent, but it can still be very frustrating to climb all the way up the Ruins of Ash, just to die three rooms before the next lift and have to do it all again from the beginning. Besides the two lifts in Ruins of Ash, however, the lifts are close enough to each other or have plenty of unlockable shortcuts that makes getting around the rest of the areas much easier. Much like its predecessor, Castle in the Darkness, Astalon: Tears of the Earth is full of extra areas to explore and optional items to pick up. All of these areas are just as intricate and fun as the rest of the game. Astalon is not as challenging platform-wise as Castle in the Darkness, but it still a worthy successor. Subteranae/Catacombs was my favourite place to explore. Cathedral is second, due to the amazing stained glass backgrounds.Boss fights are not particularly difficult, which was kind of a relief. Without text or hand holding, the fights telegraph what you need to do to defeat them fairly clearly. The biggest challenge of any of the fights is dodging attacks, but that goes without saying in this style of side scroll, 2D game. Beautiful visuals in the boss fights. Despite the simple design of the Gorgon Tauros, I was grossed out by the blood monster the first time I fought it. The Black Knight fights are a little too easy, but I fought him with Kyuli so that gave me an advantage. Every music track in Astalon is a banger, no bad tunes at all. There are upbeat tracks with lots of energy and calmer, eerie tracks to show tension. I hum along to the tunes every time I hear them.All in all, I recommend this game. I'm a big fan of Matt Kapp, having played Castle in the Darkness and Binding of Isaac: Rebirth a LOT. Astalon: Tears of the Earth has its issues, but overall is a very good game that deserves a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Ok let me start by saying that as of this review I am only to the first big boss during the actual exploration (so like 8% explored). So you can determine off of that what the worth of my review to you will be. But I am a firm believer that a game has about 40 mins to hook someone....and if it fails, then it gets forgotten.This game reminds me of Legacy of the Wizard on NES (aka Dragon Slayer IV I believe it was.) And just like LotW I feel like this is a game that I should absolutely love, but instead does well to make everything as complicated as possible for the player.Now I will say I like the different character classes you can choose from, and (like LotW) each one has specific skills that make them able to access areas that the others can't get to. So yes, expect a LOT of backtracking when you figure out you went one way, and brought the wrong character.Also the healing system in the game is competently asinine. All characters share the same amount of HP. So if one character gets hit, then the HP will be the same when you switch. (eg...you are at 30/30 HP. You are the wizard and get hit for 5 damage. So now you are 25/30. Then you switch to the Rogue who...instead of being 30/30, is also now 25/30.) I hear there are green orbs that, when dropped will heal you...but I have yet to see one. There are also "one use" orbs around the castle you can break to get a little HP back. But once used, they are gone.....unless........you pay to have them restored.Which brings me to my next issue: when you can't microtransact a person with real money, do it with currency in game. Buy items is nothing new in games....but this game goes WAY too far. Want the healing orbs restored? Buy them. Want to gain basic knowledge about what items do? Gotta buy that. Actually the store doesn't even tell you what items do. You just get a list of items and just select based off their names. And how do you get to this shop? Ummm.....when you die. Yep...so far the only way I have found is to die. But it gets worse. At least when you die you come back to life.....AT THE START. So now you don't just back track...the game back tracks  a Section Z kind of way.I love the mood of this game. The combat is not bad. The exploration, although tedious, is well done. But I can already see so many bad choices in how this game works...I can already tell I will not have the desire to finish it....which is heartbreaking because I really want to like it. I was a child in the NES days, and this has such a great NES style vibe. But I also know we have come a long way from those days, and QoL elements have been implemented to Metroidvanias. Astalon ignores that.So I am going to say no, but hopes that i will find something that makes me flip my thumb. So far...its not looking good.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun classic-style metroidvania! Starts out pretty tough, but gets easier as you find some early upgrades. The lack of healing and starting back at the beginning has a roguelite feel to it, but thankfully there's a good amount of shortcuts and fast travel points as it goes on. The only thing I don't like is that upgrades are mostly character-specific, which incentivizes focusing on just one, and it'll probably be the mage who's the strongest by far. The other characters have niche uses, but by the end I was mostly swapping between him and the rogue. Still, I had a lot of fun, and it's recommended for classic Castlevania fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon is a cool and good retro-metroidvania where you play as 1 of 3 characters to navigate the rooms of the tower you're ascending. Some rooms and switches and puzzles require other characters to solve so you must switch between them to navigate the rooms.  There is after-death progression to strengthen your characters. I'm not quite sure I like starting over at the very beginning of the tower after each death though, even though there are a lot of shortcuts to open to help with that. Very good 8-16 bit style music. The graphics are deliberately styled in a way that looks as if you're playing on an old-school tube TV.  It's good. Try it.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay 5/5:Gameplay is simple, but a lot of fun. In the Main Story you can switch between different characters in order to conquer the tower, each character has its specific traits to overcome obstacles. For people wondering if there is a New game+, there isn't but after beating it, the game offers few different modes to climb the tower anew which were actually pretty fun to do.Music 5/5:The music is amazing, everyone who loved the old Mega Man beats, will love these tunes. _childDocuments_.review: After seeing a few youtubers and redditors recommend Astalon, I felt encouraged to check it out and I am ecstatic that I did. The smoothness of the action of the characters and world map are reminiscent of the NES/SNES days with just enough quality of life upgrades to make it feel like how we remembered it. There is a constant feeling of progression watching the world map unfold with all of its shortcuts as well as gaining upgrades in the tower or after death. The game is perfectly paced and does not overstay its welcome. There are even a few bonus campaigns (for those truly drawn into the gameplay) that feel unique and change up the game mechanics. Easily my favorite metroidvania of 2021. I wish more people knew about this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I wanted to love.  The atmosphere, soundtrack, and story all had me intrigued, but the gameplay had too many weird quirks to overlook.  It's insistence on roguelike elements removes any sort of checkpoint system which makes backtracking and replaying annoying, especially since unlike roguelikes your runs won't be varying much.  Not only do shop upgrades not have any descriptions (you have to either google or guess what they do) but they don't do much to change the overall feel.  Not to mention that out of the 3 main characters, only one of them felt good to use in combat while the other 2 were traversal fodder (you also can't swap them on the fly unless you get a missable late-game upgrade).  Good foundation, but there's too much weighing it down for me to truly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy my time with this game, but there are glaring flaws that dampened the experience.Let me say first that the art style, music, and controls were great. The story was simple and short, but still intriguing enough to keep me engaged. The gameplay is standard metroidvania exploration, key collecting, and backtracking, but the way the main gimmick works is what sours the experience for me.You get money for every enemy you kill, but can only spend them every time you die. Every time you die, it's ALL the way back to the start of the dungeon. There are elevators that act as fast travel, but they are few and far between. There is almost no way to get health back in this game, so every hit you take can be a big setback. There are some green candles that refill a pittance of your HP and very rarely, when sitting at a campfire (save point) you can rest for a larger heal as well. The campfires are also the way you switch characters, which you need to do frequently. They are spaced out very well, and heading back can be a pain. There is an item which allows you to switch characters on demand, but if you aren't lucky enough to discover it early, expect loads of backtracking through constantly respawning enemy-filled rooms. Not being able to find the right item is a problem common with this genre of game, made painfully worse by the death loop mechanic.The characters themselves have loads of fun abilities you can find (and buy from death shop), which is definitely the best part of the game. When you finally can explore the dungeon and unlock new territory without dying too much, its an enjoyable experience. The way the hallways are connected to each other, you are constantly opening shortcuts for yourself, which is very gratifying. Overall, not a bad game. Definitely outclassed by others in the genre. If you enjoy metroidvanias, try to get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-The game is very well crafted in terms of music, graphics, and gameplay mechanics-The metroidvania gameplay loop (looking for secrets, finding upgrades,) is solid, with a rogue-lite twist following death-It has 4 game modes, 3 of which you unlock after doing various things in the main story mode.-There is a story and it is consistent-Swapping between characters is an interesting mechanic and having character-specific upgrades that deal with the normal area gating that happens in metroidvanias is interesting*Pros about the hidden modesCons:-While there is a story, it feels a little flat. The core motivation of going into the tower is clear and good, but character interactions feel a bit stale and cliche. This is certainly forgivable in a game that is an homage to an era of games where stories were not at the focal point. However, even then, people were trying new things. The endings also didn't feel super interesting.-Partially to the above point, there is a feature where your characters can rest by a campfire and they chat. Which would have been cool, but there are very few instances of unique dialogue. I think I only saw two unqiue cooking scenes, and the occasional reference to something that has happened. Resting is also something that rarely happens, so it feels kind of bad when I rest and the content is stale or repeated. This may be because the inclusion of the feature created expectations that it was going to be interesting, and then it was not. It would've benefited from being more frequent, perhaps commenting more on the oddities of their surroundings and unique places they have been able to make camp in. It just felt like a good but forgotten idea that made its way into the game.-Some of the bosses were repetitive. Without spoiling anything, some bosses have phases where you have to just wait until they change to do damage (this was very pronounced with the first and second bosses). Two instances of bosses also were pretty much copy-pasted and slightly upscaled mini-bosses. In total, I would say there are ~7 unique bosses (which is a good amount, but left me wanting tbh, especially when I would fight a not-really-mini-boss-boss).*Cons  about the hidden modes and the storyIn short, its a solid game with some cons but I had some fun so overall I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon: Tears of the Earth is a fantastic Metroidvania that takes notes from Mega Man, La Mulana, Bloodstained, Shovel Knight, and other retro-inspired platformers.  It’s got bangin’ music, tight platforming, a good variety of character abilities, and a healthy amount of exploring and secrets to uncover.  My small complaints are that it’s a bit buggy, and some of the playable characters are more powerful than the others; otherwise, it’s a solid game.  If you’re a fan of the genre, and have remotely some interest in checking this out, just pick it up and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game!First of all, it's a non-scrolling game which is my favorite style to play these kinds of open ended adventure platformers. There are some other games with that playstyle on Steam, like Alwa's Awakening, Mini Ghost, Bone Appetit and La-Mulana 1 & 2. While nothing can beat La-Mulanas, I think this might be my favorite of the others.I would've loved this to have more of the La-Mulana type cryptic riddles and puzzles, but you can't have everything. The sense of mystery in this game is great anyway.Haven't yet completed it but I just beat the third main boss of the game (I've beaten several other bosses too) and I think I'm now able to get to the final area. I have still a lot to uncover in the map and there's a whole full area I haven't yet tried at all (just opened the way to that area).I love how finding save points and especially the elevators feel REALLY good. While the game doesn't punish that much after dying, as everything you've done is done in your next game after death, there is still a somewhat stressful sense of danger as you don't get to restore health much at all during a run, so you really want to avoid getting hit and it feels bad every time you get hit by something. Every single new shortcut you open feels great, and every miniboss you get out of the way feels great.I've been able to get my characters pretty strong so they deal quite a lot of damage and can take quite a lot of hits, but I still ended up getting all sweaty and stressed up when I was trying to find the third main boss.You might end up wandering aimlessly at some points but just remember to check out any fake walls and use your new powers and skills and you'll be alright.This is a gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Our kids finally fell asleep and me and my wife wanted to go too. Wife went first and I wanted to check steam for sales before I go too.Killed the first boss and felt so pumped up. What kind of game is this? This game clicked like no other in a long time. I have to keep playing for a few minutes. After "few minutes" my wife went to toilet and was kinda surprised that I am still gaming. "BABE! Look at this F map! I can go here and there and this color means this and I have 3 characters and oh my god it so oldschool" "Will you come to bed tonight?" "OF COURSE!"21:00 I killed my first boss6:33 I finished the gameThis game captured not only the good old days of games, but also the good old days of stay up late, gaming as madman and going to school totally destroyed and out of energy. THIS GAME IS LIT!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, i have deleted my previous (good) review to write another one: this game is GREATLike, HOLLOW KNIGHT GREATIt is so well designed, so rich and full of stuff to uncover, it has a nice story, nice characters and it's very fun and challenging.All rooms, from the very first one to the last has some secret to uncover that will be accessible once you earn power ups that will make it possible to explore.Every character has a specific function and it gets more powerful and versatile the more you explore as you collect orbs (experience points) and develop it.Treasures and relics are very satisfying to earn as they are well buried beneath a difficult and complex dungeon.Each enemy has it's own path and attack pattern so they are quite distinguished and unique, same goes for bosses.I highly advice you to play this gem; easily the best metroidvania i've played recently since Hollow Knight.I hope there will be a sequel
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: It is *not* a rogue-lite. You aren't expected to eventually do "one perfect run" like in Deadcells/Hades/Isaac, it's a metroidvania but unlocks/upgrades happen over time with each death as you buy them at the shop between runs from the Titan of Death. It all felt really organic to me. Extremely tight map, controls, progression... like Castle in the Darkness but even better!===Addendum: June 23, 2021: Since last review, have finished the game with 100% map and found . Have also played through the additional game modes. The upgrade others have complained about that causes 10% more damage also results in enemies giving 10% more orbs (every time you purchase it). I think it's misleading to not mention that, along with the fact that a single 10% increase in damage the first time you buy it may not even result in any more damage actually being taken (assuming the damage values are rounded up/down). You buy it once to learn what it does, then avoid it until you are ready for it and want the increased risk/reward.While slightly controversial, I actually really liked the fact that the upgrades are a bit vague. You soon realize that the entire game is really a metroid-puzzle-vania. Everything is a puzzle! Rooms, enemies, bosses, upgrades. After the first boss, as you buy more and more upgrades, you die less and the game feel changes. It has that classic progression in mertroidvanias where you start of hitting and running everything, terrified of dying and then slowly feeling yourself becoming more powerful as the game goes on. Buy the end of the game, you're mowing down everything, even the last boss, especially if you go out of your way to fill out the map and find all the upgrades -- you're nigh-invincible. I really urge everyone to at least play to the second boss and reconsider your review. The game really opens up! And the extra modes/characters are also great and offer ways to sequence break majorly and speed-run the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A very well made metroidvania that combines the character swapping of something like the Lost Vikings. The first quarter of the game is probably the weakest, up until you get the ability to swap when you want as opposed to bonfires. Level design makes use of all the different characters with speed run potential for skipping areas if you know what you're doing.For more on the game, check out my .
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't enough praise in the universe for how good this game is! Every upgrade and bit of progression feels earned. Every secret chamber a joy to discover. Every boss defeated making you feel like the badass you'll be by the end of your adventure. This is a true love letter to NES games and I can't wait to see where the devs take this series. Plus, gotta give props for the great Castlevania reference (you'll see what I mean after you uncover the 'root' of the problem in the story. My only gripe would be that Algus is a bit OP, but that's splitting hairs after having 100%ed the game.Can you find all the secrets, unlock all the characters, and dismantle the dark tower? Adventure is calling fellow gamers!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Now I don't necessarily think I can fully review this game to its completion, from what I have experienced so far, this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece. It pulls you into its grasps and continues to hold you there until you have no other choice but to say "Uncle Uncle". The platforming and combat are incredibly fluid and the upgrades and items that you can get along the way directly impact the way that the game is played and are necessary for progression. And don't even get me started on the dash jump dude. Remember Super Mario 64? Yeah, that's what the dash jump is like in this game and it makes the game so much more fun and you feel so cool when you dash jump from one side of a platform to another. The story is captivating, and the bosses aren't super difficult but Astalon makes you work for the progression that you seek. So getting from Boss 1 to Boss 2 took me an entire area of exploring and puzzle solving to figure out. Funny enough, I played this game on my arcade stick and it really feels like I am playing an arcade game when I use it. So if you're lookin for an authentic experience, play it on an arcade stick. 10/10 Cheeseburgers for Astalon: Tears of the Earth.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended but beware: this game is EXTREMELY tedious until you find some veray important upgrades, which can take several hours.But once you have tthose upgrades, it is very fun to play.So, don't hesaitate to see an FAQ or look at the map to see where  to go first.Also, do read the guide about how to farm Orbs (the loccal currency): it will make your life much easier.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing 8 bit styled fantasy metroidvania. This game had me completely hooked. The progression and difficulty are spot on. Everything feels earned and satisfying. Upgrading the different characters and unlocking their individual abilities makes exploring the tower really engaging. The story was well told without needing endless lines of dialogue. The faux 8 bit backgrounds and sprites are among the best of any game in this style and the soundtrack is amazing as well. For my play through I had 20+ hours clocked in with still many secrets to go back and find. I can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic Metroidvania that's well worth your time if you're a fan of the genre.  The premise is straightforward enough but fun.  What starts as a mission to save your town's drinking water soon turns into a quest to prevent a sinister group of eldritch horrors, known as the gorgons, from breaking free from their tower prison and unleashing hell upon humanity.  Pros:+ Great retro graphics.+ Tons of secrets to discover throughout the tower.+Fun boss fights.+ A meaty upgrade system for your characters that basically allows you to set your own difficulty level.  + Different skillsets and combat abilities for each of your characters, making you want to use them all as you progress.   Cons:- You don't get to unlock new characters or really cool character abilities until the end of the game.- The 'true' ending is locked behind 100% map completion.  That just seems super arbitrary to me. - Compared to other Metroidvanias, this one is a little light on boss fights.Having played through several dozen Metroidvanias, I'd honestly put this one in my top 10.  It's a must-play for genre fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon may be the best game I've played in a long time. I don't remember anything that got me feeling such a sense of wonder and hype as it has. Be patient with it, and it will surprise you. Most of the bad reviews I've seen seem to just complain about the difficulty, but it's not that hard. It's challenging for sure, but it isn't brutal.There are some things I didn't like about the game: I don't like how it handles healing, long distance travel can be a chore and switching characters is kind of tedious. These are small blemishes on an otherwise perfect game 9/10This is the second game produced by DANGEN that I absolutely loved, the other being Iconoclasts. Clearly this is a publisher I need to watch.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Very well designed Metroidvania (despite people saying otherwise, this is NOT a roguelike).A quick rundown of its pros would be:-All starting 3 characters are useful. There aren't many instances of 'I will only play with X character because they're just better in all aspects"-Map design is fantastic. Every room is more akin to more of an old school platformer level that you have to navigate to get through, making traversing the map a lot more interesting than just "hold right/left".-Combined with that, enemy design and placement is very well done. Enemies are placed not to be something for you to kill, but to be part of the room, make the traps and jumps and whatever harder to do, while being placed in such a way that you oftentimes cannot mindlessly mash attack to clear them. They make exploring more interesting.-Loads of secrets, and they're not obtuse either. The game does a good job of giving the player hints.Cons:-The side content (boss rush, alt character modes, and unlockable main story chars) are generally lackluster.-The game does a poor job of explaining mechanics and upgrades.-Navigating the Mechanism when going for 100% completion is a PITA.-Some minor UI issues like individual rooms only being able to show 1 thing at a time, so if there was a door to unlock and an item in there, you'd only see one.But on the whole, Astalon: TotE is a very fun Metroidvania that combines its combat and exploration to make traversing even a single map interesting.  It is the Hydra Castle Labyrinth of the 2020's.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias I've played in a good bit. Soundtrack is great, controls are snappy. Leveling system is simply and easy to manage. The sense of increase in power is clear after a few hours of play when you start to one shot enemies that used to take 4 or 5 hits. Different character with different abilities, though I wish there was a better way to select between the characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent retro pixel-art Metroidvania by Matt Kap (among others), creator of Castle in the Darkness.Astalon shows a lot of improvement over Castle in the Darkness: the pixel art is larger and more detailed, the movement is smooth and responsive, the platforming is much fairer and less trolly, and the game maintains a smooth difficulty curve that produces genuinely challenging traversal without ever becoming frustrating. Afraid of running into something like Castle in the Darkness' infamous Torture Chamber here? Have no fear, you'll find no instant death traps here.The game is a classic Metroidvania in structure, with a large map broken up into numerous discrete zones, many of which culminate in a boss fight against a Gorgon, this game's version of the Big Bads, or your recurring nemesis the Black Knight. The map is quite expansive, and traversal is often complex and technically demanding, with crumbling blocks, pits, precise jumps, maze-like corridors, and hidden passageways, not to mention the monsters that infest nearly every room. This game features a *lot* of backtracking, especially if you want to get 100% map/item completion or the true final boss and best ending, but traversal is aided by strategically placed elevators (usually two per zone) and paired warp points linked to one another (usually one pair per zone). To break up the repetition, the layout of traps and monsters changes as you defeat additional bosses, meaning that rooms you thought were safe or predictable offer new challenges as you move about collecting your gear.And there's a lot of gear. One of the key mechanics of Astalon is that you control an entire party of adventurers: a wizard, a fighter, and a rogue, with two other optional hidden characters to unlock. Each one has their own attack and defense stats, as well as their own unique abilities, and most of the gear you find will enhance one particular character - for instance, a cloak of levitation can make the wizard fall slowly, while a pair of boots gives the fighter a ground dash.The various puzzles and rooms in the game will require you to make use of all of your party's abilities, and figuring out which character to use when is all part of the challenge. At the beginning of the game, you can only change party members at (frequent) campfires, so you might end up backtracking a little if you come to a room and realize you need another character to get through it, but midway through the game you acquire the ability to change characters on the fly. This eliminates the 'whoops, need a different character' events, but the game immediately begins giving you rooms and puzzles that require the use of multiple characters in quick succession, so your brain will remain engaged throughout.Monsters are a constant, and like with room puzzles, each monster might be better approached with one or another of your characters. Every character can fight, but their attacks have different properties - for instance, the fighter's attacks are short range but very fast, while the rogue attacks straight ahead at long range but does so slowly - and it will be up to you to optimize your strategy against each particular monster. The same is true of bosses: though there are no bosses which *require* a certain character, you might have an easier time if you bring the right one to the matchup.Speaking of bosses, and continuing the theme of treating the game like one giant puzzle, they are more cerebral than twitch. Boss patterns are clearly defined and attacks are telegraphed well enough in advance that your challenge won't be whether you can react in time, but whether you can figure out where to stand or what to do in order to avoid attacks and mount your own counterattack.The game is decently long, and I think it falls right in the sweet spot: it finishes on a high note, when you feel like you could use just a little bit more, one more zone, and never crosses over into tedium. I fully completed the game, 100% map/items, all three unlockable secret modes, and all achievements in about twenty hours, and I am fully satisfied as to the length and depth of the game. Not once did I think to myself, "I wish they would get this over with already." I've played much more expensive AAA games for much less.The only downside I can think of off the top of my head: While Matt Kap's music for the game is excellent, and reminiscent of Castle in the Darkness' OST, I think it might be a little *too* reminiscent. Several tracks crib from his previous game, and I might have preferred a little more musical adventurism.TL;DR: High-quality classic Metroidvania with a party system, visually and aurally pleasing, lots to see and do, right in the sweet spot of both length and challenge. No need to wait for a sale, worth it at full price.
