_childDocuments_.review: An excellent yet challenging 2D metroidvania with a smidge of Rogue. Astalon's biggest feature is probably the ability to switch between different characters, all with their own specialties, a little like Castlevania 3 on the NES. First that option is limited to the camp but the game opens up later on, allowing to switch on the fly.On the presentation side, the pixel art is charming and emulates perfectly the style of the NES era. The soundtrack feels like an 80's progressive rock OST, what in my book is always a good thing (think Ys OST from J..D.K.). The game manages to squeeze in some surprisingly endearing story bits and twists that make the quest to conquer the dark hallways of the Gorgon tower that much endearing. On this note, Astalon's presentation and setting feels very reminiscent of the Tower of Druaga series, in particular its horned helmet MC, and I wouldn't be surprised if it was a direct source of inspiration.Overall a lot to good things that makes this game an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game's biggest strength is that it feels truly labyrinthian, it has the most rewarding and satisfying exploration I've seen in a Metroidvania so far. Tons of hidden passages with genuinely meaningful rewards and power-ups. Exploring the map feels like solving a puzzle. The game is rough around the edges, but in a way it makes the exploration more enticing as it doesn't feel over-polished for player convenience. The player power-progression is also quite satisfying, although it can lead to somewhat underwhelming bossfights as you become too powerful.The downside of this game design however can be a frustrating player experience that may come from missing vital items that can be quite well hidden. Something like access to operating the lift is locked behind a hidden, obscured passage. I have also went through more than half the game missing the very vital  and it led me to multiple soft-locks. I found some of the music to be somewhat middling, but there's good tracks too. The art is very nice and stylized & I found the story just engaging enough to get me invested without getting in the way.Even problems aside I fully recommend this game to anyone who may be interested in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Another brilliant game from Matt Kap. This and castle in the darkness are incredible and just sucked me in. There's so much to uncover in this game and I can't put it down. Some really well blended ideas. Even though I don't love every decision they're all intentional and well-developed.  I looked a couple of things up, but nothing should have been beyond my reach if I'd spent some more time on it. Finishing up ng+ and it's a lot like zelda's master quest. Also there's a room where the stars say 'pee'
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best, most memorable metroidvanias I've played in years.  One of the main features is being able to switch between multiple characters who each have unique abilities and attributes, and this works pretty well although it can lead to some extra backtracking in some spots.  I never felt like this was excessive, though, and it certainly doesn't detract from how fun and satisfying it is to explore this world and discover the myriads of secrets hidden throughout.  The 8-bit aesthetic and music is done really well, and the game also has a decent story that has the potential to tug on the heart strings (it did for me, anyway, but of course your mileage may vary).  I need to revisit the game at some point because there's post-game content and extra modes that I haven't even done yet - great bang for my buck.  I super recommend this game, and I also recommend checking out the developer's other game Castle in the Darkness which I also thoroughly loved (it's the reason I got hyped for Astalon prior to its release)!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about halfway through, excellent so farEdit: Yeah it's really good. Great art direction, levels and bosses. Every piece fits. I could've used placeable markers for the map to remind me where I should check later, as it was hard to navigate and remember what you've missed. I hope they make a sequel/prequel
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:* Great feeling of progression* solid controls* the art style is fantastic (kinda has that msx2-ish (or really any limited color palette home computer)  style similar to games like la-mulana).  * Progression from death system is ok, thankfully you get something later so you can upgrade at statues and not have to die to get more powerful. * The tower is well designed, backtracking doesn't feel bad due to all the shortcuts you unlock as you go.The Bad:* really needed item descriptions, I went through 95% of the game not realizing I could get health drops from enemies because I couldn't tell what the uprade for that did in the shop.* generally way too easy* boss AI isn't very good, while the main "gorgon" bosses are ok, the other bosses and minibosses can all be trivially cheesed with Kyuli by just standing at the farthest range and firing arrows, black knight will actually NEVER attack if you just wall kick MMX style as he walks to your side then drop down and shoot while he walks away, he'll just pace back and forth until he dies.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: If you love shovel knight or castlevania or metroid style games then this game is a must, it offers outstanding sound and outstanding graphics effects with perfect animation i rate this game 10 out of 10, this game will put you in metroid Adventure with great variety of enemies to challenge power ups upgrades and magic items it has it ALL.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but if it helps someone with tastes similar to my own find this game...1) The platforming is really fun in this game and it is very fun moving through the rooms. I usually like games with lots of tech (ie. Celeste) and this was far more basic compared to that, but for some reason I still found the movement very satisfying.2) The music is KILLER! So good -- it has everything from adrenaline-pumping to melancholy, and its all super catchy. Didn't mind retracing my steps ever since the music was so good.3) The artistry in this game is amazing -- the application of light/shadow to gruesome (and unique!) statues throughout completes the mood. It made me want to discover every corner of the tower.4) The story is not super in your face and it is very simple, but you can discover the full picture if you choose and the character convos are enjoyable.Definitely try this game out!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is how a retro-styled game should be made. While the developers clearly love the old style games Astalon is based on, they didn't just repeat the past. The pixel art and graphics are beautiful, but the gameplay irritations that could plague games of that era are thankfully missing. The multiple characters are well implemented, their abilities remain useful well into the late game and it's fun to explore the old tower, where there are plenty of secrets to discover. If you're a fan of the NES Castlevania games (especially the third one), check out Astalon.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon: Tears of the Earth is a throwback to older platformers with a twist of roguelite elements mixed in. It's a good mix but the game leans more into exploration and discovery over combat.  For those who have played the  series, this is a smaller, shorter, less puzzle-challenging game.Disclaimer: It seems that from watching Youtube reviewers, that some may have a  making progress and find it a lot more challenging. This MAY impact how you view the game due to the mechanic that on death you respawn at the beginning of the castle. I've had the total of 20 deaths (mostly from arriving at the boss arena with low HP) and a few explorations late game but it wasn't a huge issue for me. There usually are elevators right next to the boss arena so dying there isn't as huge of an issue as one may expect.I will also use spoiler tags in this review if you don't want to be spoiled. Most of it will be the two unlocked characters andthe additional game modes.GAMEPLAYThe gameplay is like many others in the same genre. A platformer game with basic combat to boot. The core gimmick of this game is that . This adds a small roguelite twist where you keep some things but lose mainly progress. It's not a proper roguelite but adds a twist while still retaining a more traditional metrovania esque gameplay. Due to this mechanic, the game enables you to unlock shortcuts so that in subsequent deaths you don't have to start from the very beginning. The other gimmick is that, it mixes in  elements, where each of the three protagonists have a unique combat and movement skill that forces you to use all of them.Early game, you are forced to switch at the base camp before exploring, but that changes later game. That's the constant theme of the game in a nutshell that you start with the most basic setup that's workable and many of the quality of life issues you've had, get resolved as you progress through the game.  While the game doesn't have a hint system, some items like the  enable you to see if there are hidden adjacent rooms. Some of these are obvious by their looks and it was great to see that the ring is not needed but nice to have in ones that are very hard to see.Combat is a mix of all the older games between Kyuli, the archer rogue that can reach the end of the screen but is slow, Arias, the fighter with a very short range but fast attack speed and Algus the strongest mix with a decent short range. It is a good throwback to different protagonists in other games and there's also two addition ones that can be unlocked.  It's a decent mix and it is a simple combat system. The trio also have additional movement items that further differentiate from each other which is nice to see. That said I wish there was an item late game to enable dash on everyone since it's awkward to switch and then switch again to hit enemies.A few issues I had areOverall I would say this is a decent game and what you except with a few twists from the original formula. I enjoyed this rather quick game at 7 hours for the first class and was long enough for what needed to be done. I wouldn't mind it being 1-2 hours long but overall the climb, although simple, was very enjoyable.9/10GRAPHICSAs this game is a throwback to the earlier days, graphics are not it's strong suit compared to a modern game. The pixel art is amazing and it's really nice to see that each character has their own color identity. The art and design is what I would except from an older game. I think for me, my favorite part was the last cast of monsters you get to fight. I originally expected many to be recolored variants but many are original for most of it. With a few exceptions like the gargoyle whom all attack different, it was cool seeing both the scenery and the mobs change along with it. Even smaller details like the items or the detailing on the wall to show there is something there is amazing to see. With exception of copies of the same few mini bosses and  "repeat" fights it was fun to explore and see what each new area had to offer.9/10MUSICI love the chip tunes they have here. They fit along the music and inspire the hero to explore more to see the tower. It isn't on the tier of  but it's still a strong showing. I also like how there's two themes per area, one being the normal theme and the second subdued variant for when you're at the campfire. It's a unique thing but fits given how you can actually have campfire stories that heal you but also provide more context of the characters. The only issue I have is that there's only one sub boss theme for all the different sub bosses.8/10STORYAs with all the older games, the story is basically nonexistent. You are three heroes tasked to save the world by exploring this tower and vanquish the beast within.REPLAYABILITYThere are two extra modes that can be unlocked once you beat the game with certain conditions. They are 1 hour runs and while they work, I feel it's more a showing of how the castle map is adapted to fit the other modes in. It's basically two fixed characters with slightly different controls but the same base castle. On the flip side there is also New Game plus with a  map. It's a very nice touch and gives you a reason to play at least twice. It is much like a second quest, a lot harder but great to see the developer's touch. The other thing added is a boss rush which I'm not a huge fan of due to the long boss death animations. The boss rush is serviceable but with such a small pool of bosses, there isn't a lot of variety to be had. This is in stark contrast with others like Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow that had a long list of bosses and gave you a cool item you can use main game.[/spoiler]7/10SUMMARYOverall this is exactly what you except. A strong throwback to the older platforms but adding in new quality of life learnings as well as an interesting but simple twist on the old formula. This is what I was looking for as a simple platformer. It doesn't bring a lot new to genre except for the softer tunes during the base camp and cool long final boss fight. That isn't necessarily a bad thing but for me I found it worth the value and a great game to recommend to folks if you're also looking to find something to scratch that itch. However, I would recommend all the games mentioned in the review over this since they add a lot more than what this game as to offer. This is also a good game to introduce folks into roguelikes with a lot less to lose. As mentioned at the very beginning though, your experience may vary since if you are not great at platformers, you may struggle more and that can easily impact your view of this game. For this is a light, simpler challenge that have been set.33/40

_childDocuments_.review: A classic NES-style metroidvania. Lots of heart went into this game. If you like the genre and the artstyle, pick it up. Controls well, has excellent sound design, and plenty of secrets to find. This game is right up there with The Messenger and Shovel Knight as far as I'm concerned. Well worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best metroidvanias I've played, I think the generic anime style logo they are using undermines the actual in game art which is great.  The game is smart, making you loop your way around, showing you there was a way you didn't even realize often, the combat is fun, there is some gameplay twists, everything plays and looks good, I've played part way through a new game plus mode, and I just keep wanting a sequel cause this was just fun.  There were a few parts I got stuck, largely because you need more details on the map, so trying to get back to some places were not obvious, I did need an out of game map once or twice to go forward, and the upgrades and candle mechanic isn't clear in game, but otherwise exploration was fun, combat was fun, lots of challenges and secrets. A few hitches but overwhelming a good time.  9/10, I would put it just under the big classics like Super Metroid, SotN, Axiom Verge.  Hopefully we will see more.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I was uncertain at first, but glad I gave it a chance (difficulty seemed too steep at first). It turned out to be pretty fun overall, once I got the hang of it.The game does very little explaining to the player what things do, and it's obscure enough that information isn't abundant. It feels very much like an old NES game in that way, and in most other ways, honestly. Graphics, sound, controls, and even the scope of the game would be right at home in the 8-bit era, especially if you imagine it as one of those underrated gems that were hard to find at the game rental place and impossible to find in retail.My main complaint about this title is that boss rush seems to be MUCH harder than the regular game experience and I gave up on it, even after completing the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is an 8bit retro style adventure game that feels like a mix of the best old classics like Mega Man, Castlevania and other similar titles. You have to complete a big tower with enemies and bosses. There are many secrets and items to find. You switch between characters to use their special abilities and you can level up your characters through orbs collected from killing enemies. It is an excellent game through and through. Graphics, music, story, characters, game play: all top notch. For this genre I'd say it's a top title that you should get. The only 2 small things I didn't like was that you could not turn around when attacking and that the controller settings didnt include all the possible functions. Maybe they will fix that at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: The initial chunk of the game is tedious and frustrating, but eventually becomes a rewarding and engaging metroidvania experience.There should really be a way to heal fully. Even at the end of the game, it is still best to just die intentionally and restart from the beginning once your health drops to a certain point.Otherwise, it is worth sticking with.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game! Great mechanics, bosses, and exploration. My biggest issues is Boss Rush mode is ridiculous. I was looking forward to going platinum on this game, but Boss Rush Mode is so imbalanced, RNG random items, next to worthless upgrades, and insane timing to not get hit more than twice. I attempted so many tries to beat this mode that it has but such a bitter taste in my mouth that I will not be playing this game again. The poor implementation and imbalanced Boss Rush mode by the Developers is a big "♥♥♥♥ You" to the player.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that tries its hardest to strangle itself with its own design.I went in expecting this to be  1.5, and it's mostly what I got. It does the  thing with three characters, but for the first half of the game you can switch them only at checkpoint,s which results in some make-work backtracking as you slowly unlock rooms juggling between character abilities gating progress. Likewise, the checkpoints don't really matter  since you respawn at entrance after dying, so there's  backtracking between fast travel rooms.Them major boss fights are good, shame that there's only five of them. The music's decent, but manages to be less memorable than CitD's soundtrack, where every other track was a banger (I checked to verify that my memory wasn't making me wear rose tinted glasses). Clearly, more work went into this one than into CitD, but the result is almost lesser, somehow.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Metroidvania with good music and nes style art. The Beginning of the game is on one hand very enjoyable because boss encounters are challenging but on the other hand backtracking after dying or to progress on the tower can be annoying and tedious, this is mitigated half-way through the tower by providing you an item that lets you swap characters without returning to campfires. It's just a shame that later on the mazes thrown at you are more difficult than the bosses that you face. There is an upgrade system that may be the culprit here and putting less points there might have retained the difficulty in bosses I'm craving. Oh well! Another Issue with the Upgrade System in this game is that it heavily incentivizes buffing one character up. For me that was the blue swordsman, with certain item upgrades you can find in the tower he just becomes very oppressive. But reading other reviews, it seems to be a consistent problem people face with this game and other characters as well.  Backtracking to unlock rooms is still a thing even at 80%~ of the tower mapped. But it feels less tedious since teleport options and elevator options have increased a lot while exploring the tower. But you do have to go through 5 or more rooms to get back to where you were before to progress. I can wholly understand why it may become so tedious to some that they quit the game but for me personally the game is still very enjoyable even if I might get annoyed occasionally because of it.Edit1: Completion Status 100%, Beastiary 80%~Played the normal game to completion and unlocked two of three additional modes that I will be taking a look at. The game difficulty with all the upgrades was sadly pretty laughably easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: The developers of Astalon did well to replicate the nostalgia of the NES/SNES era with this Metroidvania title. The theme is dark/tragic, and the atmosphere reminds me a bit of Faxanadu.Normal difficulty wasn't hard at all, though I did get lost for a bit and need to backtrack and search for areas that I could access after finding new items or keys. I also death warped quite often since it's often quicker to respawn than travel to a warp point or lift.I got the game on sale for $9.99 and it's definitely worth that, but possibly not the full price since the game can be completed in 15-20 hours by a casual player. Still, the duration felt about right for the size and complexity of the game.I like that the mechanics of the game were simple and that new item drops were well paced. It's a solid, atmospheric game that could easily be expanded upon with more writing. I'd love to see a sequel with more plot and world to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic metroidvania game. I really enjoyed Castle in the Darkness, and this feels like a more polished version of that game, with a more reasonable difficulty level.There's tons of secrets to find, the upgrades are fun, the different characters are unique, I personally love the NES aesthetic, the music is memorable, and the game has a ton of content for the modest price.And there's no cryptic puzzles or unfair challenges, which a lot of similar games have. This one is very accessible.My only minor criticisms are that the extra game modes could use some more polish, but they're still a lot of fun.Anyway, this is one of my favourite indie games from the last few years!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Among the dozens of indie metroidvanias available on Steam this one might be one of the best I played. The exploration of the tower is simply superb the map contain all necessary information to make sure you can see places that still hold some secrets, the items you find slowly improve your exploration capabilities and the dungeon itself is very well designed and really makes you want to explore it's every nook and cranny. The story is simple but satisfying with constant tone and doesn't get in a way of exploration. Game also has decent amount of unlock able goodies that makes it fun to 100%.The only gripe I would personally have is the fact that you respawn at the start of the dungeon every time you die which is not that terrible as you unlock fast travel points through the adventure and sometimes when going through same rooms you'll take different path and find something new, but it occasionally breaks the flow of the game.This is just a nitpick thou as this is a really, really solid game worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you one thing: there is an achevement for opening 100% of the map in this game.And there are over 300 rooms in tis game, huge part of which are hidden or locked.And 38% of players have this achevement for unlocking every room on a GIANT map.Just imagine, how fun and addictive this game is, that almost 40% of people opened all map and 39% of players collected ALL ITEMS, believe me, it is not easy, but it is very satisfying.Backtracking seem hard at the begining, but soon you are able to find a shirt pass to every location, just an alevator here, teleport there, crushing a wall there.This game is a gift to metroidvania fans community, and i also want to admit level design, even if you will use all keys in an absolutely "wrong" places on other side of the map, you will be able to find anough keys to move on every time.This was about 20 hours of pure satisfaction!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rad little soulstroidvania, almost like a gentler La Mulana.You have a party of characters you can switch between, you can cash in souls for upgrades when you die, progression is item-based but there's tons of secrets and side content, and the controls are responsive and forgiving.If I have one gripe (and it's ultimately why I youtubed the ending instead of finishing my playthrough,) it's that the map doesn't give you a lot of information. The critical path through the game, you can follow that by following the map. But the map only sometimes flags important rooms, and only sometimes tells you if there's a hidden exit, and in general the way the map looks like it's layed out and the way the game is actually layed out are two very different things,This turns backtracking at the very end into the most tedious and unrewarding slog imaginable---but I'm saying this as someone who hates puzzle games and has a poor memory, so your mileage may vary.Overall, I think this is a gem of a game, and I'd love to see more in this series. If you like oldschool platformers and metroidvanias, give it a try, but be prepared to aim for the bad ending unless you want to spend hours wrassling with the map.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules. Sort of a classic Metroidvania experience meets Vampire Hunter D and the old NES game "Legacy of the Wizard." Also an immersive setting that suggests a larger world outside the scope of the gorgon's tower. Easy recommend for me.One caveat that I should mention, given a few negative reviews, is that you should make sure you're the sort of person who enjoys mastering the dungeon before playing Astalon. Learning how to navigate and discovering various shortcuts through what can otherwise be a treacherous labyrinth should seem like fun to you. If you want quick travel and other Skyrim-esque QOL features, you'll be frustrated by this game. If you don't mind spending some time with dungeon crawler games on their own terms, you'll appreciate many of the design choices of Astalon.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: The best metroidvania I've played all year and one of my all-time faves. Think of it as a cross between a metroidvania a Lost Vikings. You have 3 characters (later 5) that can each bypass certain obstacles, which you have to switch between to keep exploring. At first you can only do this at campfires, but eventually you get an item for this. When you die you respawn at the start, this could be annoying, but I did not personally find it so, it fits with the narrative the game is creating and you constantly unlock various shortcuts, fast travel, teleports that make the retraversal easier. At death you can also use orbs (currency that enemies drop) to upgrade your characers. As with all metroidvanias there are abilities to unlock and I found them interesting, they are divided across the characters (mostly the first 3) which is ususual, but it keeps the game from becoming overly mechanically complex (or overpowered) if one character had everything. The level design is very good with varied zones. The combat is fine, but this is a game played for the exploration. The narrative isn't super-strong but enough to give me a sense of these characters and wanting to see it through. I had a great time with it. Now to my one criticism. Gating the true ending behind 100% completion is just bad. I got to 95% completion by just playing the game and that was fine. I got another 2% by looking at a 100% completion map and finding everything I could and exploring any points I had missed. The 3% I had left I imagine were items not marked on the map and outside of exploring every piece of the map again room by room I had no way of knowing how to do that. It's not like I needed these items for the boss fight so I just looked up a guide on youtube. It's just a bad way for the true ending. Just have it activate once you've explored all the major areas, locking it behind getting everything is just bad. The game also hides the path forward or critical items behind false walls too often. Sometimes they are obvious, sometimes they are not. 2 red keys were behind this which I needed to progress the last areas I could see. That said all in all, I had a great time with this.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I agonized for like a year over buying this game and I regret not buying it earlier because it's right up my alley. Basically, it's like a linear metroidvania game that follows a rogue-like structure using Dark Souls-style shortcuts/elevators/etc. to provide meta progression. It's comparable to the difficulty of Shovel Knight IMO and the run-based progressions tend to provide pretty well placed checkpoints that limit your need to retread areas you've thoroughly mastered. It does not litter checkpoints all over, but the amount of stuff needed to beat to open up each checkpoint feels reasonable, especially if you consider each of those legs as the equivalent of about half a shovel knight level in distance from each other, which is challenging, but pretty fair if you gel with this kind of a platformer.I'm definitely sure that this will be too frustrating for some people and I wouldn't fault them for that either, but I would say this is within a pretty common realm of difficulty that shouldn't be too surprising if you play games like this. I waited for it to be on sale, but it's worth full price IMO. Also, it works really well on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best surprises that I've found this year. It's an amazing hidden gem. My only complaint is that the bosses (other than the first) are a bit too easy. However, regardless of that this is still a must play if you're even a little bit of a metroidvania/roguelite fan. Do yourself a favor and check this one out!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good metroidvania-ish game, I’ve taken to calling Astalon a exploration based puzzle platformer, as it plays in a similar vein, but areas are gated more by keys and buttons than power ups. That being said, genre is just a label, and it’s still a solid game.The gameplay is very fun. You switch between three characters, each with unique abilities, to solve puzzles as you explore each area. Earn points that you can spend to level up your characters and unlock new skills. Explore every corner of a huge map to find secret items and characters.The music and graphics use modern design to perfectly capture that NES feel. The monster designs are unique. The characters each stand out and both their sprites and portraits are quite expressive.My biggest complaint with the game is that it doesn’t explain certain things well. Namely: you have to manually unlock the elevator, there were a few items that didn’t work the way they were described in the menu / level up screen, and the method for getting the true ending is just obtuse.That being said, this falls into the ever increasing category of “games that go from decent to great when you play with a guide.” If you’re a fan of retro platformers, I highly recommend checking this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly deep and fun metroidvania that opens up in some really great ways as you progress.  I was engaged through the entire experience, and felt a ton of reward from exploring off the beaten path.  I didn't quite know what to expect coming in, but this has quickly become a favorite of the genre for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: "Astalon: Tears of the Earth" is an exceptionally well crafted metroidvania manifesting all the old charm of the genre while still feeling fresh and original. You follow the story of three heroes trying to stop a corruption that is rooted in a giant gorgon-fortress. They end up in a groundhog-day-like loop for one of them made a deal with death himself - reviving them and making them stronger each time they die. These upgrades will be paid with soul orbs that can be found as currency throughout the map. While this mechanic can get grindy at times and forces you to backtrack occasionally, you still feel that you make some progress at least and serves as a catalyst if you are not that skilled.The level design and the combat has this old castlevania-vibe but feels more accessible. The secrets, treasures and hidden areas are placed very well - at no point I was feeling complety lost or frustrated. The pixelart and the soundtrack are also huge selling points, even if the character-portraits look too "anime" for my taste.The main campagin has a lot of content and a fair amount of completion time. And if you are still hungry for more you can  start two alternate (albeit a little shorter) campaigns where you play as the antagonist and one of his minions.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good Metroidvania with a nice retro/nes touch and a focus on exploration and combat Just be warned that the game has some rough like repetitive to it. When you die, you'll have to start from the start of the game. However you'll be able to power up your characters between death and you'll find plenty of short cuts . This make the game a bit tedious, but it also gave the game a more retro like feeling.My only bigger complain is that the characters are not well balanced. Some are just overall way stronger than other.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but not quite great. Astalon has some really solid platforming Metroidvania fundamentals, but a few issues hold it back.My biggest complaint is the amount of backtracking required throughout the game. If you die, you go back to the entrance. Fortunately, there's a teleporter there which can take you back to most places. Except if you haven't unlocked the teleporter for the location you're exploring it turns into a slog to get back to where you were. It's exacerbated by the maze-like layout of a lot of areas. For the pros that are great at memorizing maps this will be no problem, especially since you unlock shortcuts as you go, but for someone like me who gets lost a bit easily this results in spending way too much time retracing my steps. I would have much preferred a traditional save/recharge room system. This is made a bit worse in the early game where to swap characters you have to go to special rooms. Pretty often you'll go along, find an obstacle that needs a particular character, then have to backtrack to get that character. It's also made worse by the key system. There are three types of keys you find throughout the game, and they're often hidden. Fairly often I found myself blocked by a locked door and having to comb through areas I had previously been to looking for hidden keys. I would have really preferred they kept the secret and hidden areas limited to stat upgrades so you wouldn't have your progress blocked so often.Next up, I don't like how each of your characters has separate stat upgrades that draw from the same money pool. It felt like the smartest thing to do was to focus on upgrading just one character and only use the others to get past obstacles. I feel like the game also should have done more to give each party member enemies and situations where they shined to encourage more experimentation.The main story gimmick (which you learn a few minutes in so I don't consider much of a spoiler) of the game feels a bit out of place. Every time you die, you get brought back to life and most of the party is supposed to forget everything. But it doesn't really make any sense given that you keep all of your progress. It feels like the story was designed for a roguelike, but they changed their minds during development. It's not awful, it just feels really awkward.Finally, there are WAY too many pop up spikes throughout the game. Seriously, it feels like 70% of the rooms have spikes popping up and down. Pop up spikes aren't a bad obstacle for a platformer, they're just way overused here.I think Astalon's fundamentals are still strong enough to be worth it for Metroidvania fans, but the flaws hold it back from being an unqualified recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Astalon a lot, but it's not for everyone. I wanted to clear up some of the negative points people have been posting just so others can have good information for deciding to buy or not.This game was enjoyed on a Steam Deck, which presented no issues, so that's a plus. Hence I recommend that or a controller since it seems native for it.Astalon borrows elements from metroidvania, roguelike, and just good ol' fashioned retro platforming, which I love. The story is lite but interesting, and it never felt under- or overwhelming in difficulty. I thought it was very cool that you could adjust the blurriness to emulate effects of TV distortion. These good points aside, I wanted to clearly depict some other aspects of the game that some people dislike and that people like me enjoy as a design decision.The first thing I want to clear up is breaking the game or it being too difficult. I've seen a couple people mention they reach a point that prevents them from finishing the game due to obtaining and using limited amount of keys in other areas that are necessary to progress in others. I don't think this is true, as some doors are solely for early access to an area or item, and I was not able to find an order of getting keys from a full map in a way that would make you stuck, so I agree with those that think this is not possible and that you should just keep looking.The game can be difficult, but nothing like a traditional roguelike. People mistake dying with difficulty. Most people are going to die a lot in this game, but all of the enemies drop currency and all but a few of the upgrades are persistent through your deaths. I've also seen arguments that the game is "grindy" because of this, but I never saw the need to grind upgrades unless you were just wanting to make parts of the game trivial with high health or attack.I think the one possible valid negative point I've seen is getting lost or confused on the map. For the most part the map is very clear, but just a small handful of times there seemed like there would be access to another frame on the map that actually required you to come from a completely different direction or secret passage. That can certainly be frustrating and I don't deny that being there, but part of many metroidvania games is the backtracking and unlike others this one at least rewarded you with killing enemies more than once in the much needed currency needed to obtain the next batch of upgrades. Because of this I was more forgiving about this aspect.All in all, I would recommend this for any fan of a softcore metroidvania with roguelike elements. I love the graphics and interesting items/characters!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon is an old-school metroidvania with some Trine inspiration.The story is nice and feels well exploited.The map is huge and full of hidden areas and shortcuts.  When you die, you go back to the entrance so you'll want to find them all.The fights are a bit difficult but usually you'll increase you stats when you are dead.I've thoroughly enjoyed the time I've spent on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: over 50% done with the game and its great so far. a fun rogue-like, castlevania style game. has great music, good sprite art (backgrounds are amazing), great songs, with a pretty good plot to boot. surprised this game hasent been talked about more and feels like i found a gem. really recommend checking this game out if a rogue-like, 8-bit style metroidvania interests you.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the most fun I've had with a metroidvania. The little exploration loops are very satisfying once you get a handle on the structure of the game. Finding a shortcut or an item  at the end of an "expedition" as your HP was running out was exciting stuff. Snazzy tunes, sharp art, and slick controls. Also they had the good sense to have big Castlevania-style knockback when you get hit.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding Metroidvania Game with 8-bit optics but feels modern.Astalon is a game that rewards exploration but does not force you to. The game should be quite challenging if you ignore all the site paths and quests. I likes the uniqueness of all characters even it was a bit tedious if you picked "the wrong one" to explore a certain are.I hab a blast. Best Metroidvania after Axiom Verge 1 for me. Better than Ender Lilies, Metroid Dread or Axiom Verge 2.I played all of it on Steam Deck. Ran perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely solid platformer, with a very good metroidvania-style map. I recognize most of the nods to other games, and the megaman-esque aesthetic is charming. I like the storytelling; there's a nice mix of clear story elements, and obscure hints pointing at other events in the past as well as the future. It's not a huge-scale, sprawling, epic adventure - it's a local, direct, straightforward one with little story threads and lore bits and pieces hinting at a much larger story. I like that, it's refreshing. I like the alternate portraits. They remind me of Record of Lodoss War, somehow.I'll look forward to another game like this. I'd love to see more in this series, too!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic metroidvania which becomes better and better, with lots of secrets to look forward to. If I could go into detail many of you would buy it, but that would spoil some good surprises.I almost did not buy it due to other negative reviews here, but I am glad I gave it a try.Almost all negative criticism has been vastly overplayed and concern aspects that around 30% through the playthrough become irrelevant.Don't let them fool you, this is a proper classical metroidvania and after having played I think the rogue-like label is just plain wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game, but a bit overrated imo if you consider its super high rating on Steam.Pros:Cons:If you don't mind the game's difficulty being tied to chip damage from awkward hazards and enemy placement.. and run backs, you'll enjoy this game. The exploration, controls and art direction are solid. I'd put it at a 7.5/10, recommended but with caveats.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome little game, fun game play with a great world. Story was fine outside of taking itself a bit too seriously at times. Balancing between characters needs work but its not too bad, the key system can be frustrating as it makes you derail from whatever track you're pursuing, but these aren't huge problems. Exploration was exciting and the rogue-ish elements work great with a metroidvania if you can get around it being a bit time consuming. The biggest draw of MVs for me is how it cements you into its world, always restarting at the same point and using some shortcut to get you close enough to where you died makes you incredibly familiar with each of the rooms, the genres synergize in an awesome way and the persistent money prevents you from ever feeling like you're just wasting time. One of my favourites in the genre and a game I know I'll come back to sooner than I'll admit.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This game keeps me coming back every single time. I'm always finding myself looking for secrets, wondering what the next power up will be, etc. I've 100% my first run, collectible items, upgrades, and map charting. But I don't think that I'll be playing anymore after that to get the other endings. Once I've gotten a taste of the item power-ups (like the dash and infinite wall jumps), starting another run without them just doesn't drive me to continue.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the dungeon crawler feel that came across in this game. It really has the adventure atmosphere down to an art form.The tower is great to explore, and the mechanics of the death and levelling systems give it a bit of a survival edge while you map it out.Overall a great challenge, but I don't recommend the boss rush mode. That was some frustrating nonsense.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I was worried reading some comments about the grind, but there actually wasn't that much. First 30 minutes is a bit slow as you build skills and accessible map, and your figure out what is what, but after that it's just a typical game of this genre - roaming around the map, looking for secrets, ways to access new stuff etc. Good 12-15h of content to complete the game, and even more if you want to try other game modes and get 100% everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly sturdy metroidvania. I got a lot more play and enjoyment out of this than I thought I would. Anyone who is a fan of the genre should check it out, as I had a great time exploring the whole map.My biggest critique would be that the game stays too much within the confines of its retro feel to a fault. The music, while nice at first, becomes repetitive way too quick (it's the same looping 16 bars of music in every area). This was major problem in early gaming, and in this case I had to mute the game, and play other stuff on my machine.Another issue is choosing ability upgrades, which don't have a description of what they do until you purchase them. Not the biggest problem, but it does callback to an antiquated era of gaming. Something that I feel like we were happy to leave behind. That said, if you're on the fence, definitely check it out. Worth the money, for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A very smart and polished metroidvania. Playing this gave me the same feeling I get when reading old D&D adventure modules: a playground of adventure and exploration, fighting monsters, uncovering secrets, where there's always something cool around the next corner, ready to bite your face off. The gameplay is fun enough that it doesn't make the backtracking feel obnoxious, and all the cool power-ups you find keep things from turning into a slog. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon is a really good Metroidvania that I recommend.The game world is huge and sprawling with tons of puzzles to solve. Figuring out how to solve puzzles in the game takes some thought and careful study of the environments. Because the game world is so large there were usually multiple fronts where I was stuck at any given time and there was some frustration with trying to figure out which one of the ten places is the one where I can actually move forward. At points the experience was just aimless wandering around to the different ends of the map trying to figure out how to make progress. Sooner or later I would have that next break through and keep making progress; that was always a thrill.      The game can be beaten with not even close to every puzzle being solved. I did have to look up a small handful of solutions. Some of the optional secrets were hidden way to well for me. There are three main bosses that need to be beaten in order face off against the final boss. That can done with only uncovering about 2/3 of the map. It took me around 20 hours to finish the game while unlocking the entire (I think) map. There are multiple characters that need to be used during the course of the game. Each character has different abilities. The chick that shoots projectiles was by far the most useful in most combat scenarios. Unfortunately, some of the other characters became little more than glorified keys to get past specific types of road blocks. Generally, the combat is fun and challenging enough that it doesn't just devolve into pointless busy work to stall progress or be too brutal to halt from getting to where you need to go. There are a ton of different enemies to fight that keeps things fresh. The look of the game is in the realm of 8-bit that has good animations. The graphics are more just serviceable than eye candy, but they are fine. The main focus is by far the game play. Astalon fires on all cylinders. The combat and exploration are both really solid and there is a ton of content in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun metroidvania. The art style is really nicely executed and oozes that comforting retro vibe, whilst maintaining a lot of quality of life features and modern-day polish that helps ease the experience of trekking across a huge tower, getting blocked by doors and finding your way around. The main game is pretty substantial in content with a ton of secrets to find, making exploration and keeping your eye out for suspicious looking walls a very rewarding endeavour.If I had any complaints, it's probably that for a while, needing to travel back to a camp to swap characters could feel a little tedious. This did mainly depend on what obstacle you've just ran into and how far back the campfire is, although this was alleviated later on. I also felt like it was rather easy to become substantially powerful in regards to stat upgrades, which made my time with most of the end bosses feel somewhat anticlimactic, although I suppose this is my fault for maxing my stat upgrades(?). Not big gripes, and the only real ones I had.Definite recommend to anyone looking for a retro-styled metroidvania with some cool twists, lots of polish and a bundle of cool secrets and bonus content to watch out for!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece!! The rogue-like death mechanic and character selection is quite unique and can be a little cumbersome at first, but you will soon acquire the powers and abilities you actually want. The dark story and ambiance yet fun and accessible gameplay is exactly what any metroidvania game should be about. Amazing backgrounds and Gorgon design. Unforgettable music and sound. Fun colorful characters in a dark world. There are some graphical and audio bugs that every experienced player will notice, but they are probably to be easy to fix and the developers I'm sure will notice too. Congratulations!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Castlevania 3 this is the game for you. It is an interesting take on that game's character switch feature mixed with the metroidvania genre. Superb gameplay and a memorable soundtrack will have you coming back for more as you progress. Truly a special game, that shouldn't be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: BARELY a recommendation, but it's because this game is very polarizing. It has very strong good sides and very strong bad sides. It avoids a trap a lot of metroidvanias make nowadays, which is making more or less a linear game in a map that suggests otherwise. You will get lost often, you will have a bunch of paths, a bunch of routes, entire optional areas and so on. The movement feels snappy, kinda like a mega man that's a bit more jank. The game utilizes its mobs and obstacles extremely well, and has some of the best room designs I've seen.On the other hand, the visuals, music and story all seem very uninspired and forgettable, the bosses are very boring with a lot of waiting between attacks, and the difficulty doesn't seem to scale that well.There are also some things you will either enjoy or really hate. There are no ways to heal except dying, and dying puts you at the beginning of the game (so you have to use teleports to get back to where you were), but you don't lose anything except your position when you die. You also can only upgrade after dying until later. One of the most obnoxious things though was the way the map was designed so you hit a true dead end while exploring and just have to go backwards like 10 minutes, and feel like you completely wasted your time, especially when it's to switch characters at a checkpoint, because some paths are character locked.But hey, I would rather be angry with a good game that pisses me off, than bored with a bland, safe game with nothing going for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Matt Kap's previous game, Castle in the Darkness. Astalon is another retro metroidvania that is just full of character, and expertly designed.The game lets the player control multiple characters, each with their own abilities both in combat and in traversal. Most rooms are laid out as mini-puzzles to make you deduce the correct way to progress, and there are plenty of shortcuts and secrets to discover. Shortcuts are necessary because, upon death, the player starts from the entrance room of the Tower and is allowed to buy upgrades and get stronger. Nothing is lost with death, but starting from the first floor makes learning the layout, the shortcuts and the movement tricks imperative. Exploration is a joy, because the rooms are so well thought out, and there are whole sections of the map that are completely optional or hide cool, useful items.While the gameplay is satisfying and distinct from other games in the genre, one could say that Astalon's retro look, while on point, is a bit generic and not particularly striking. It's certainly well executed, but a bit standard in its ways of homaging the games of yore. It was perfectly adequate for me, however. On the other hand, the OST is absolutely spectacular, with incredibly catchy tracks, epic boss music and some moodier pieces.I completely trust LABS Works at this point. Their metroidvania games are consistently great, well designed experiences that are just a cut above many other titles in an incredibly saturated genre. Can't wait for Castle in the Darkness 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Considering the fierce competition within the Metroidvania market, I feel like you have two options to stand out – be excellent, or be a bit different. Astalon goes for the latter, and it’s definitely not for everyone due to some interesting design decisions. Astalon has two big gimmicks – the ability to switch between three separate characters, each with their own traversal abilities, and some game design elements taken from roguelikes. How you get on with the latter will likely make or break the game for you.When you die you’re sent right back to the beginning of the game, with your levels, abilities and items intact. Any shortcuts are also left intact, including the extremely sporadic warp points, but there’s no doubt that you will spend a lot of time traversing the same ground. There is almost no way to recover health, and you can only spend banked experience when you die (at least initially). Death is expected, and in some cases encouraged. The clever interconnected world design means that you can skip huge swathes of the level using shortcuts once they’ve been opened.Where Astalon really excels is it’s sense of adventure and discovery – this is one of the most open ended metroidvanias I’ve played in a while, and it’s deliberate lack of direction reminds me of Rabi Rabi or La Mulana (though it’s nowhere near as cruel). You have one goal – get to the top of the tower, so you do have a woolly objective of “go up”, but probably around 50% of the map and items are completely optional, and Astalon strongly encourages going out of your way to explore. This open-ended nature does mean that the difficulty curve can snap about halfway through, as anyone who goes out of their way to find extra items and accrue more experience will be vastly more powerful than someone who sticks to the main path. This is particularly true if you funnel all your experience into one character rather than spreading it equally, and bosses can become laughably easy. There’s little reason to balance your party except to ensure that they don’t die instantly on sections that absolutely require specific characters, and this becomes a non-issue about the midpoint of the game.If you’re looking for a meticulously balanced experience, Astalon isn’t it. It has a bit of “kitchen sink” design, where so many options are open to the player that you almost can’t help but find the experience a bit uneven. However it’s so generous in content and so eager to reward you for your efforts that breaking it becomes part of the fun, and if you go out of your way to 100% it the endgame power trip of most metroidvanias becomes an absurd godmode run.So if you fancy a metroidvania that hits a little different give Astalon a go – I feel it stands out as one of the best in the genre, and that it seems to have slipped entirely under the radar is a crime.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! Don't miss it if you're a fan of the genre, it is easily one of the best metroidvania games I've played. The map is intricately designed, every room has thought put into it. Finding secrets is a blast.  Great controls, each character is enjoyable to play as. The graphics and sound are gorgeous while retaining an authentic "retro" feel. Well worth the asking price; I've paid twice as much for far less impressive games.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished up the Boss Rush and got the final secret unlocked. I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves platformers. It has an awesome retro feel all around. Music is great, gameplay is great, pixel art is awesome. There's a "story" but it isn't overbearing. It's a retro-platformer, it doesn't need some huge deep story. Easily one of the better of these games that I've played in a while, and with a small team to boot. It's worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: If there's been a problem with post-Indiepocalypse, its the glut of Metroidvanias. I say that as alot get lost in the shuffle, either from mediocre well-tread design, or just being overshadowed by breakthru titles. Astalon, it doesn't do that.Coolly intricate, with a VERY unique character-building system, and stupendous level design, ATotE is a serious head above "just another Metroidvania". Powerups are useful in multiple ways immediately, the game can be beaten without dying but once, and the level design is immaculately dense, both with the passage thru the tower, but also with secrets aplenty. I also seemed to either one-shot bosses or die over a dozen times one. Shout out to a new innovation sweeping the industry: Actually Good CRT Filters. Im so glad people figured this out.​Main gripe is the oddly-sluggish menus on the title screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing twist on the metroidvania formula. I've never played one that plays quite the same. Some games let you sequence break by braving a difficult endgame area early, or abusing complicated techniques to skip barriers. In Astalon, sequence is often just a vague suggestion. The dungeon is there and it's up to you to find your way through. While some areas require certain upgrades to access in classic metroidvania style, normal locked doors use one of three colors of generic single-use key. Get one of those keys and you can use it anywhere, in whichever direction strikes your fancy. Often you don't even need them at all; the tower is full of alternate paths and secret passages that can bypass them entirely. Your experience might be completely different than the next person's, especially if you aren't going for 100%.A solid recommendation for any metroidvania fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this a day before it went on sale and I'm not even mad.Great game, interesting secrets, and really good level design.I see many complaints in the reviews about having to travel through early areas too many times, but I disagree. If you do what the game wants you to do, which is thoroughly explore the early areas, you will find items and abilities that completely eliminate the frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first retro throwback Metroidvania I've encountered that borrows the concept of multiple characters with unique movesets from something like Legacy of the Wizard / Dragon Slayer 4 and I really enjoyed how that changed the dynamics of exploring the environment. Needing to pick the right character for the situation also meant that I had to balance out who was getting my upgrades so I didn't leave anyone too weak, which added a bit of strategic depth to spending my orbs. Each character is very distinct in terms of their movement abilities and attacks which gives them all a distinct flavor.Completing the game (non-completionist) took me between 10 and 11 hours, and going back to 100% my map and item collection took a few more. While the combat isn't particularly challenging, sometimes finding the right way forward in such a wide-open area can kind of evoke that "Nintendo hard" feeling. I eventually gave in and downloaded a map, but even with the full map in front of me, it was sometimes difficult to find how to progress. There's one ability in particular that's vital to getting almost anywhere after about the halfway point of the game, but if I didn't have someone else's map to guide me to it, I have no idea how many more hours I would have stumbled around looking for it. I don't think this is necessarily a negative - it's very evocative of game design from the era this is seeking to emulate, and Metroidvanias that are too hand-holdy can feel a little linear. If you didn't like feeling railroaded by Metroid Dread, this is basically the opposite -- they just toss you in the tower and say "good luck, kid".If what I've just described doesn't put you off and you like the genre, don't miss out on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I was expecting a maybe subpar Metroidvania, but this game is REALLY good. I mean, just secrets and modes galore. So much stuff to explore. I've beaten the main game and I'm going for the Black Knight mode now. It hasn't given me any indication that I can level up or heal, so if I can't figure that out I may not finish this mode, but the main game was excellent. I'm definitely keeping this developer on my radar.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: A really charming Metroidvania-esque game, with beautiful art and music. I didn't find it grindy at all (I think it's possibly been rebalanced in a few patches) however its secrets can be a bit obscure at times, and one or two vital items (not path-critical but the game is incredibly hard without them) are quite well hidden, so I recommend hitting up a guide if you ever feel stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: As a purveyor of fine metroidvanias and search action, this is definitely one of the best. The progression and exploration of the game is some of the most compelling I've ever seen in a game of this time. There's a TINY bit of Dark Souls in it's formula, but only the parts that aren't frustrating. You retain your currency upon death, and respawn at the beginning of the castle. You are then given the ability to spend your points on upgrades to make your next foray into the castle easier. A high ceiling of available upgrades means that the difficulty will come to meet you as time goes on, regardless of your skill level. Meaning that if you're having a hard time with any part of the game, it wont last too long before you're powerful enough to win.The sound and music is great. The art design is fantastic, and adds a tremendous amount of variety to different parts of the castle. Unique set pieces are everywhere, giving a great sense of mystery and character to the locations in the game, decorated with huge beautifully macabre pieces of sprite art. Additionally, the game features(as you may have guessed) a couple different endings for you to find. When completing certain milestones in the game, new game modes are also introduced. These game modes in turn reveal more story bits that contribute to the overall narrative. It's a complete package that had me coming back to it well after I had completed the main game. The rewards are numerous, and ever-flowing.It's not Metroid or Castlevania the way grandma used to make. It's a very unique take on the formula. But, it's beautifully executed through and through. Can't recommend it enough. Bravo to the devs. I can't wait to see what's next.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. I love the art style and music and characters, the mechanics feel really good, exploration is almost always worth it.That said I only finished the base game (at 100% map and items), the other modes I tried (2 and 4) felt unnecessarily punishing so I gave up for now (but might come back later).The story hints at a few things that are fun to imagine, and that I hope are explored in the additional modes or future sequels!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible retro-styled metroidvania. I had a great time exploring the map and getting upgrades and new abilities, and there are plenty of secrets to find; I highly recommend Astalon if you like that kind of stuff. There's some interesting level design here, and many clever shortcuts to the beginning of the tower can be unlocked that utilize the things you get from exploration, in case you get bonked too many times. Some issues/glitches occur in the optional post-game content, but the base game is a very solid well-designed experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty darn good metroidvania! Classic style with modern gameplay.Slightly reminiscent of Lost Vikings, with three different avatars with different skillsets, which influence their traversal and combat abilities + roguelike die/perma-upgrade/retry cycle.I'm really enjoying it, and suggest it if you like metroidvanias!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: I've nearly 100%'d this over the space of a week or so, and not many games grab me that way, so that should say a lot in itself.  is an excellent Metroidvania romp mixing traditional elements of the genre with its own twists.I mainly judge a game like this by how rewarding it feels to make progress. For me,  nails the balance of challenge and reward perfectly. The start requires patience as you inch your way into the tower and perhaps begin figuring out some soul upgrades, but once you unlock the lift to travel around more easily and start finding secrets and items, solid fun awaits - one particular item was super satisfying in a way I'd compare to some of the stuff in .Some of the game's design choices may seem unnecessarily obscure (like the lack of information on soul upgrades) but the game's presentation as a whole is so enjoyable that this can easily be overlooked.  is a Good Game. Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. After a point I was just fighting bad guys for fun, ending up leveling up a lot which made finishing the game easier.It really customizes itself well to how you want to play it, letting you set the challenge of the game for yourself internally as part of the narrative which is cool.I felt like some of the best items were found in the late game, but this might just be how I chose to explore the map more than anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. But it suffers from a number of design problems that serve to make the experience worse. It's definitely no game of the year. I'm sorry.The whole die-and-respawn-at-the-beginning thing doesn't really work. Most of the play time in this game is spent trekking through areas you've already seen, and not because you're looking for secrets but because you have to trek back to somewhere because you died from a cheap spike fall.On the topic of secrets, there are some obtusely hidden paths that you would LITERALLY never find without buying the complete map for 15k. And even that isn't the whole map - that one ladder behind a red key door you need the magic block to access. Who the heck would think to go up there? Absolute nonsense.And that brings me to the keys. Keys don't work. Not in this sheer volume. You ever notice how most games have unlockables that give access to new locations through clever design? It's because that works better. Keys have no place in a metroidvania at least in this way.The last problem is the AI. The enemy and boss AI is terrible and utterly unmemorable. Once I beat the final boss, I realized that I didn't even remember the patterns of literally any of the past bosses and I probably wouldn't remember the final boss either, because they're all terrible and too easy.Anyways, my true end run took 13 hours. I can't picture myself playing it again or grinding out that absurd achievement for buying every upgrade. Spending an hour killing the gold knight down the bottom of the castle is the antithesis of fun.Anyways, I enjoyed it. Would I recommend the game? Yes, but it's by no means the amazing game other reviewers are making it out to be. I had a better time with other metroidvanias on Steam, some of which actually cost less despite offering more content. Temper your expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite Metroidvanias.  Superb pixel art.  I especially like how many rooms have various giant statues in the background to give the area a distinctive look.  The gameplay is challenging but fair, where none of the design elements overly punish the player for mistakes.  This game also constantly introduces new varieties of enemies to keep things interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: change this to a recommended. a lot of good in here. nice plattforming, a huge map to explore, secrets to be found, passable combat.getting around remains to be a pain in the ass. long ways cluttered with cheap shot damage everywhere. death as a mechanic to regain health or alocate skillpoints. (others methods open up but slow as f)wrote all of this prior to my final review and changing it to a recommended:i had fun up to the second gorgon boss.i was not difficult exactly, i did not beat it to be fair, it was just such a drag to wait for it to reappear that it sucked the fun right out of the game.- traversal becomes a huge pain due to traps and long travel time from the entrance- cheap shots- item descriptions, even with the item that reveals them, lacking- lack of replenish forces a very defensive playstyle or using death as a way out- dying very often a better way to traverse- some gauntlets are so long with elite enemies at the end that invite outright cheesing them rather than runthrough them again
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets to have the rare honor of me actually bothering to complete it 100% and getting all the achievements, so I would definitely say I enjoyed my time with it. In terms of metroidvania games, I feel that this game did a great job at being both relatively clear where you needed to go next and including many secrets and paths to find throughout the tower. The fact that you have to switch party members in order to progress through many areas of the game might be tedious at times when you come to a dead end that only someone else can go through, but it also lets each character have plenty of time to be used and learned, which is helped by the fact that each character is quite well-balanced. Throughout my playthrough of the main story I never really left anyone unused which is great, since sometimes games with several characters tend to leave me using only a couple of them at once. It also helps that most upgrades for characters that can be bought or found in the tower are quite useful and can give you very useful abilities that can really help certain characters. Also, completing the game is helped by certain upgrades that let you find secrets much more easily, especially once you explore most of the tower, so I didn't need to spend an hour searching every room over and over for an obscure secret. Overall, I was pleasantly surprised by how well-made this game was, and I'm interested in seeing what may come next if there is ever a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon is a wonderful metroidvania game with great retro graphics and music, and some of the best map design in the genre. If you're into Metroidvania games I'd highly suggest getting this one, read on if you want some more details.I want to hone in on my favorite aspect of Astalon: it's fantastic map design.There are some parts of the map locked behind a powerup or boss kill, but the most common obstacle you'll face are locked doors. These doors can be opened with single use keys of differing colors. Once you're past the first area you'll often have multiple routes you can take towards your destination. Often times you will find one key and have multiple doors you can open with it, locking off the other doors until you find more keys. Very few of these doors do not lead to meaningful progress, and there are slightly more keys than doors to ensure you can't get stuck. this makes exploration feel very "freeform". On top of that, once you get some powerups enhancing your mobility you can skip quite a few doors entirely which is pretty cool. Drawback of course being that it's way easier to get lost on this map than the likes of Ori or Metroid Dread. That's a plus for me though.Speaking of powerups,  of them are actually required to get through the main game due to the doors being the most common obstacle. I personally like this design decision but I understand it if others don't. all secret rooms in this game are clearly indicated visually, and there are a lot of them. There's very little guessing as to where they are if you look close enough (no shooting or running into every wall to find them). These secret rooms can range from simple stashes of currency, to a powerup, to even more secret rooms or a door which lead to alternate paths or entirely new areas. Tightly related to this brilliant map design is the way health and death work in this game. There are very few ways to recover health and every death sends you back to the entrance of the dungeon (on top of allowing you to upgrade your stats). However, every powerup, elevator floor, warp point, and shortcut you unlock remains available to you after death. Each life becomes a careful game of managing your health and seeing how far you can explore, until you find the next shortcut/elevator/etc.I could gush on about the map design for longer but you get the point. I'd almost say it's worth getting just for that.Besides the great map design, the art and music is wonderful, and the setting/story is basic but works great.The game does not come without it's issues, though.- Movement is limited and sluggish until you get some powerups and even then only two characters get any marginally meaningful options (a grounded dash and an endless walljump respectively). You can find a universal speed boost halfway through the game but the base movement speed should've been as high as the boosted speed is now.- In tandem with this limited movement come un-engaging enemy/boss designs. Besides the first Gorgon boss and the encounters with the Black Knight I felt none of the bosses or enemies had any interesting things going on.(late game/100% spoilers)- The  being locked behind 100% is ridiculous. You can  and you will not get the  unless you have everything.- The  add almost nothing meaningful besides access to a few additional parts of the map. These could've been  instead, which would've been way less disruptive.★★★★☆
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very nice looking and very good to play, however it takes ages to built up points to buy ABILITIES like Strength/Defence and magic etc. I am actually enjoying the experience of how long it takes to get my abilities to help me beat the first baddie boss. I am going to buy more of these type of games - because the are fun and challenging!
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The level design is among the best of the indie metroidvanias on steam. There is also a good amount of exploration tools available that really made it feel fun to move around it. I had so much fun just exploring in this game. The character switching gimmick is kinda fun, at least once you get a certain upgrade after an hour or two. The combat is fine, it's nothing amazing but it never got in the way either. The graphics are good, the music is good, the characters are interesting. There's nothing bad about this game, and the movement and level design, which I think are the most important parts of this genre, are exceptional. Overall it's just an excellent game that deserves to be up there with the likes of Hollow Knight.
_childDocuments_.name: Astalon: Tears of the Earth

_childDocuments_.review: Astalon is, in simple terms, a Metroidvania. You explore a large tower, depicted in retro graphics similar to the NES, and explore while expanding your capabilities of navigating. There are some things that set it apart, however:-You start with three playable characters to tag between with different abilities.
