_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to anyone who can appreciate a story rich game, likes branching story manipulation, can appreciate a voyeuristic feel in gameplay, and understands what this game is (more below).  I cannot recommend this game to the fewer people who need deep profound stories, expects A list acting, expects an elaborate sci-fi story/setting, or expects a moderate or fast pace - This game doesn't have any of that.This is about 6 ordinary people who live together in the same European flat who died in a fire, and your job is to change their decisions (called possible corruption points) so they all live.  I have been able to get everyone to survive in 8 hours while simultaneously trying to reveal as many events as possible. There are some locked rooms that can be accessed by finding certain objects in different rooms, and certain dialog events will serve as hints as to where to find them.First, I want to respond to the most common criticisms (of the mere ~10% thumbs down reviews):? "It would be more fun if it was set up like a video editor or something" - Then go play Her Story, which this is not. What's the point of travelling thru time if you can't explore the physical location of the past?  Its not like it takes one minute or more to go between NEW events.  Any previously played events can either have their choice easily changed on timeline, or you can the timeline also provides a shorter summarized audio report of what happened.  I don't know how much closer they could get to fast video editing interface and still have it fit the premise, and if people don't like the premise, then don't get or play this game.? "It was pretty dull" - It is about 6 ordinary people with their own personalities and problems. The drama is not super deep or complex if that's what you are looking for, but it was real world enough for it to have some intrigue.  I personally did not have to relate to any of them to be somewhat intrigued, but some player will want to.- "I was also a little disappointed with how the final conclusion is portrayed. I feel like some sort of flash-forward mechanic could have been used to show us the fate of the characters rather than relying on us to just read what happens in their character profiles." - This I too was somewhat disappointed in, but it didn't merit a thumbs down for me because I was engaged in the story & choices. The only flash forward after the fire shows a specific point in time with the survivors right after the fire.Here is what you need to know - No spoilers:+Decent graphics and audio fit the drab dark setting of a burned out home. It is nice to be able to play in windowed mode (if you look for a guide like I finally did after saving all people + optimal ending for 3 of the 6), and resize the window dynamically like any other window without big black bars for whatever doesn't fit the aspect ratio.+The system for navigating between a choice and it effects is pretty good, though sometimes trying to navigate from an end result to its upstream causes doesn't always easily go to the choice it causes.+The voyeuristic feeling is nailed just as well as Do Not Feed the Monkeys or Beholder 1.?In order to access events for the first time, you must go to the physical area where events happen, which is fine with me because I'm not impatient and these ordinary people's lives were interesting enough for me (perhaps due to the voyeur factor). After that, already played event can either have an audio report summary replayed or you can easily change their decision from the timeline instead of replaying the entire event.

_childDocuments_.review: The actors all give wonderful performances and those performances are what's going to carry your enjoyment of this game through to completion.While the game suggests (and fully expects) that you experience the story from the beginning, only a few locked doors that you have to find keys for really stop you from experiencing this game in any order you choose. You can absolutely start your game seeing how the characters all die before working your way through events to try to change the outcome.Figuring out how to tweak the timeline in certain ways provides a fun and interesting challenge, especially near the end where you see how your actions can affect the survival of the people you're trying to save.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: If you own the game just jump into it and listen to the main menu song. It's an amazing indie song that I instantly fell in love with just by doing my video settings. If you don't intend to buy the game, the song is . I wanted to begin with the song because it also has a huge role in the game: Setting one of the atmospheres (Eternal Threads has two atmospheres, just like the bottom of an average lake). The one I'm talking about is this teen/young adults drama vibe, similar to Life is Strange. The other is a spooky, unsettling feeling that I had for the entirety of the game, I always felt like I was being watched, even though I was the one who was watching others. You'll understand what I'm saying when you're going to play the game. There are a lot of weird noises that you hear from time to time, objects falling or gadgets malfunctioning. I'm not going to elaborate, since it might ruin your experience.Eternal Threads is a walking sim, with limited interactions and with a very interesting premise (travelling through time, changing the fate of a HMO's residents and untangling their individual stories), which is, in my opinion, very well-executed by the writer and the developer. The game is ~9 hours long and it can become boring at times, but as with any other walking sim, you must have patience.The characters, as I was saying, are six stereotypical British teenagers and adults in their 20s, with a few other secondary characters scattered here and there throughout the story. If you don't like cheesy, cliché, melodramatic teen drama you won't like this game, but I absolutely live for these. Give it a try! It was in Humble Bundle's June Choice, so if you don't own it already, you can find it for cheap somewhere. it's definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is like a tell-tale game but you actually play every aspect of it. It does not seems to be much when you start the game, but the story that builds is very deep and you're quickly diving into the game's story. Characters are well-worked, with their own personality that will conflict with your progression and their own problems with the ones you will interact as well. This game is a hidden gem.It is a slow pace game tho' so many people will dislike this aspect, if you do not, go for it !
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how they managed to do the writing for this game. There are so many versions of the timeline with events influencing each other, but it all still makes sense and is fairly easy to follow.Every change you make cascades down the timeline changing other events, causing some to not occur, and creating new events which you can influence. _childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A nice short-ish time travel detective game. The story is interesting and pretty well written. It took me about 12 hours to get the perfect ending. I would suggest not to use a walkthrough for this game, as it rewards exploration and trying out sub-optimal branch will give you a different take on the story and character developments (You can always change back to the optimum choices later). I really like this game and I hope there will be a sequel.Lastly, I would suggest the devs add a zoom and crouch function so you can see the environment and objects easier for people who likes to scrutinise everything in detail. After end game you can go back and redo whatever you want, so I suppose it is slightly re-playable (3/10)Conclusion: An absolute steal on sale, don't even hesitate! _childDocuments_.review: Travel back in time to manipulate a bunch of strangers in a share-house until their combined fates result in them all surviving the house fire that killed them in the original timeline. So kinda like the sims except you don't get to make people have sex. This supposedly corrects the far future, but it's hard to imagine any of these people contributing meaningfully to the human race on any level aside from paying taxes. Maybe one of them accidentally crushes a bug and prevents a mutant insect plague.Their are two main challenges in the game1) Letting go of the notion that the virtuous choice is the one that leads to survival. Sometimes you'll get a bunch of stuff lined up and it seems like the best outcome for some people, only to find it leads to the death of others through random interconnections of events.2) The frustration that comes from getting very close to a solution for most people only to have everything unravel for one or two others. For me I had most of them saved after about 3 hours play time, only to spend the next 2 hours making things much worse for everybody before I turned it around. When I did there wasn't much logic to it, more trial an error. Saving the last person was pure luck and I still don't really understand what changed to make that happen.It is interesting though. The individual 'scenes' are actually well written, just long enough to convey the facts, emotions and relationships. Compared to the garbage that is being spewed out by Hollywood and the streaming services of late, this is a masterclass in tight and believable storytelling.I suppose the point is that all the characters are deeply flawed human being making serious and life-changing decisions the best they can. But I must say when it was all over I was glad to see the back of them. It also tries to show that the outcomes of our decisions are not guaranteed - sometimes good choices lead to bad outcomes and vice-versa. It's a sort of moral pragmatic relativism I find abhorrent.I could in theory go back and get the 'best ending' by finding the ideal outcome for everybody, not merely survival. There are 3 reasons not to do this:1) I'd not want to mess with the timeline any more than I'd absolutely have to.2) These people need to sort out their own messes. 3) My experience with the game tells me that the random way that the choices interconnect means it would be an exercise in random guesses and frustration, rather than logical progression.But overall it was fun figuring it all out, even though in the end left a bad taste in my mouth.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I almost never write reviews for games. I have no excuse for this.But I HAVE to say something about this one.This was genuinely incredible. I just spent ALL day playing this and I'm already planning to jump back in so I can make sure I get everything and nab all the achievements.I really don't know what I was expecting when I saw the description but I'm a sucker for time travel and "butterfly effect" plots. So I had some notion that I'd really enjoy this. But even then, I had no idea just now much I'd enjoy it.The characters are genuinely really interesting and relatable. The mysteries are intriguing and kept me constantly guessing. The part I was particularly impressed by is just how well thought out the cause and effect of every action was planned out. I cannot even imagine just how much time and effort that took.If I were to have ANY criticism of this game, it'd be:1. I want more thanks.2. The character models arem't... great. Compared to the rest of the environment (which is genuinely beautiful) they kinda stuck out like sore thumbs. It didn't ruin the game for me at all but I thought it worth mentioning.Seriously great game. I really hope we get more like this!

_childDocuments_.review: One word: Tedious.Should I give this game more of my time? Maybe, but after reading through other reviews I came to the conclusion that it's just not worth it.The concept sounds interesting, the game, imho, is not. All you do is "select event from timeline", followed by "walk to spot in the house to watch said event", and (sometimes) ending in "pick 1 out of 2 arbitrary choices". And that's it. Then you just move along and hope for the best, trying to save 6 people, who are mostly flat as a canvas. The voice acting is mostly fine, but the way it's recorded makes it evident, that these voice lines weren't spoken in tandem, but every person recorded them on their own. There is no fluidity, no humanity, no soul in them. They're lines read from a script ... and it shows.Other than that the game just starts off too tedious, establishing the characters and the events ONE WEEK prior to the actual incident. Yes, you HAVE total freedom to just jump to any event you want to ... but that chaotic approach just leads to chaos, since most of the events are locked and require prior choices to unlock, so going from back to front makes not a lick of sense.This sort of time travel puzzle stuff, again imho, works better with a really good mind-map that visualizes what has happened and how your choices affect those outcomes ... and not just having arbitrary choices. Funnily enough I think Life is Strange even did it in a more interesting way in one chapter back then.It woud help to just be able to view the events via the user interface, instead of physically having to walk to it every time and then having to rewatch everything or most of it, because by the time you've watched 50 events you're certainly not going to remember what choice lead to what outcome.So why not have a more detailed time line: Person A did X, which lead to Y and affects person B, which in turn affects person C and leads to event Z. Ultimately, the goal should be, since you're not allowed to prevent the fire, just find a way to get everyone out of the house on that fateful day. You could achieve this by finding clues in the game world, then watching and manipulating events, so you could still have your "physical space" in which you'd be walking around, and which also changes based on the decisions you've made, but you need to make this clear to the player. And then not just have 2 choices that are vaguely similar, but actually be able to really dig in. How about you can make it happen that a character's mother has to go to the hospital and then he has to go visit her at the exact right time? Or splitting up a couple, so they both move out? How about some environmental manipulation? All of that is pointless though if the story and characters aren't interesting enough to warrant a playthrough and if the user interface is chaotic.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that are hard to pin-down on recommend or no. The first 75-90% of the game is amazing. You're going through the game watching events, making and altering decisions, which features some amazing time manipulation stuff and amazing writing. The last bit is fiddling on the timeline screen flicking switches back and forth trying to unlock events you haven't found (there's a function that is supposed to show you what choices are needed to unlock events but for some reason doesn't work for all events making it rather pointless) and this part is absolutely tedious, featuring decisions that wouldn't make sense in the worst visual novels. I kept at it for I don't know quite long and I still couldn't figure out how to save the last member, because it was tied to an obscure event relating to another character as I found out via a guide. Eventually I just gave up and finished the ending via youtube. If I ever replay this game I'll play as long as it's fun and then do the same via youtube. So should you play this game oir not? That depends. The fun part of this game is amazing, but the unfun part is absolutely terrible. I think if you're willing to just tap out and finish the game via youtube you'll have a fun time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: It is an intersting concept - the overall story is appealing and I really wanted to know how it continues. The level design is also worth mentioning: it is tiny, but you unlock certain hidden areas overtime.For me, there still are a few issues: there is a timeline that might feel a bit clumsy at times - I accidentally kept selecting the wrong events while scrolling. Some of the narrative seems rather forced at times - dialugues are meant to be easygoing or "cool" but to meappeared rather stilted. The story also tends to jump from one central dramatic conflict to the next, moving on without really considering further implications. I would still definitely recommend playing it!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of the game is that you are someone with the technology to meddle with different events in time, and you are trying to get the timeline from deteriorating. For mysterious reasons, you have been assigned the task of meddling in a house fire that killed the people who loved in the house together. However, you can't just keep the fire from happening, you have to meddle more subtly and just make sure they get out in time or are elsewhere. The game plays like a visual novel about a slow moving drama between a bunch of housemates. It's well acted and well written enough, but very long. I was looking forward to the point where you are actually doing the event manipulation, but it just ends up being a choose your own adventure where the outcomes don't seem particularly tied to the decision you make. For example, one woman has left her husband and through the decisions I changed, ended up deciding to give her marriage another shot. I thought, "Oh, that means she wasn't in the house for the fire because she moved back in with her family," but actually it just meant she got out of the house in time once the fire started. There didn't seem to be any connection between what I chose and the way the narrative was influenced so it becomes trial and error, which was dissatisfying after spending so much time learning about the characters and their problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't recommend this game. The concept is interesting and some of the more atmospheric moments were quite good, if entirely out of place. The acting was passable too. Everything else was just a bit below average. The story and how it unfolds is something more akin to watching a bunch of episodes of any soap opera, with all the predictable drama that entails. The original premise is never followed up on, instead being an interesting backdrop to a paint-by-numbers story. Lastly, I really don't think this qualifies as a game and it certainly doesn't need the "Choices Matter" tag on Steam. The choices don't matter. You make the correct choice to complete the game, end of. I feel like the team behind this were close to making a compelling game but put too much time or effort into the narrative instead of creating an engaging game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Although the concept of the game is quite interesting (which is why I decided to buy it), it's actually not very well done, as a video game: it works better as an interactive, movie-like experience, with very little gameplay. At heart it's a puzzle game, but forcing you to watch each of the almost 200 small animation scenes to complete the game is a bit painful, and at a certain point, the game stops being interesting. Afterwards, the entire universe in which the story is framed is very little explored, and the relevance of the mission we have is not well understood, nor the final cliffhanger...It also has an annoying bug: if we try to run up the stairs, it stops (as if it were running into an invisible wall). I thought the game didn't hold as well as it could have.... It failed in the broader concept of sci-fi and the issue of time-travel with consequences was not the best achieved. There are other games out there that are simpler and more fun than this one.I think that without the support of some online guides, it will be very difficult to complete, because the game's tutorial is very brief and not very intuitive, and there are certain symbols and different colors that it is difficult to understand what indications they are trying to convey....I don't recommend this game for the average gamer (except if you are a hardcore fan of interactive graphic novels). Overall rating 4/10

When this happens, it could change this part later!", it's more like "Okay, let's just pick random choices and see what happens". _childDocuments_.review: This game is a lovely little gem that I'm happy to recommend. The vibe feels a bit like a crossover between "Her Story" and "Silicon Dreams" - you're not just focused on any single event, I found myself paying a  of attention to the overall 'emotional' mood of the household, and how the choices I made changed this. Furthermore, don't think the choices are in any way 'obvious' to get to 'the best ending'! I admit I struggled a bit in the beginning because I'm used to "tell everyone the truth ALWAYS" being the defacto good-guy playthrough style, but this game took me by surprise in that you end up making some choices that may not seem like the best way forward, only for it to actually lead to growth of the character in question. One thing:  I understand the Devs' decision to not include any way to 'fast forward' an event if you're watching it for the first time (i.e. there's no way to mash a 'skip dialog line' button or anything like that), and they do give all sorts of ways to check what an event was about or to make a different choice that doesn't require re-watching an event from beginning to end over and over. , if you're like me and end up googling "speed up eternal threads event" or "skip button eternal threads", I recommend simply grabbing a game like 2048 on your phone and idly playing that whilst you wait for a conversation/event to finish. I found that for 90% of the events, you're fine listening to the audio - so if you, like me, get a little antsy watching """slow""" (by which I mean actually realistic conversation lol) moments in the game, treating the events like little podcast moments whilst folding laundry or playing an idle phone game got rid of that antsy feeling for me and let me enjoy the game to its fullest!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a lot of love, the characters are fleshed out and interesting, and I found it fun figuring everything out. It's also nice to see a non-American setting, made me relate to the characters more as a Brit.The ending is a bit disappointing but not that bad, and it doesn't relate to any of the characters, they all get a proper ending (albeit in text form only).

Getting the perfect solution felt more akin to randomly clicking than deliberate choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of being a d-bag like other "reviewers" and starting the review by counting the tags that are already mentioned in the description, I'll tell you why I will not play this game despite my love for the time-traveling genre. And, you won't be like, "You don't say."So, the first issue is the atmosphere of the game. It's not horror, but it's always night. Why? Because you need more job to do if you will have daylight! It's from the perspective of game development.The second issue is how the game looks. Let's say it straight "Eternal Threads" looks wooden! Like a game for Play Station 3 from 2010-2012. Remember those times? The period when everyone was waiting for Play Station 4, so the game devs were trying to sit on two chairs and they were releasing games ahead to have a "semi-next gen game" that would be playable on both consoles.The third and ensuing from the second issue is the minimal requirement of 6 GB or more VRAM, not two as mentioned in the description. My 4GB VRAM laptop was barely having 13 FPS in full HD screen resolution (not even 4K). You ask why? Terrible game optimization, nothing more.The last and the most important issue is how the game presents the backstory of each case, you should investigate, through the "read to win" concept. That is the most despised thing for me. It means the developers were that lazy that they didn't even try to find an actor or just a dude from a bar who will be the narrator for 100-150$. "Nothing, the gamers will read the story," the developers said. If I want to observe a crime scene I can play "L.A. Noire" and stray around, *qham* Around much better designed crime scenes btw. *qham* *qham* in a game released 11 years ago *qham* *qham* *qham*
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed this game a lot, but it's not without flaws.The concept of having to save six people by altering a timeline you can scroll through and influence their decisions is really neat and I've never played something like this before.I'd say the first 75% of the game have been really enjoyable. Getting the perfect ending and saving all six people felt a bit tedious in the end though, because it was basically a trial and error game of trying lots of combinations to find the right outcome. Those combinations were variations of previous ones and they didn't feel unique enough to be as interesting as the start of the game.The game starts out very slow, but the characters have been well-written and if you're patient, their storylines will open up to you. I also enjoyed running around the house - which is essentially the single setpiece - and finding more and more secrets to unlock. This also means backtracking as a core game mechanic, which might not be something for everyone.After seven hours, I saved everyone and it felt rewarding. Good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Umm so I wish I could give this one a mixed review because honestly I don't think I will be talking to anybody about this game but then again it isn't exactly bad either. The acting is good and the whole butterfly effect is pretty well done, but the story is such a boring slice of life experience without high or low points in the characters lives. Every time I think "oooooo drama is comiinggg. something is gonna happeen" they end their hurdles in life either wholesomely or fairly calmly considering the situation. You crawl through 3-4 hours of story before you get to know if any of your choices mattered so it's a slog.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant hidden gem. You're essentially doing a Quantum Leap and putting right what once went wrong. Instead of becoming someone, you essentially tweak the choices multiple characters make. What I especially like is how there's almost 2 distinct wrongs in the game. The first wrong is that everyone dies in a fire, they need to survive. The second is to really put right what once went wrong and fix some deep personal issues.Getting everyone out alive is somewhat straight forward and enjoyable. The second 'wrong' is what I found the most interesting by far. Small changes to one person will have a knock-on effect for other people. The best part is this isn't a typical game where 'make everything better' makes everything better. People aren't so easy, and without a little strife or a few mistakes, you can't grow. There's excellent crossover here between different characters, where you need to consider the bigger picture.Fortunately, things don't get too complicated, and you can quickly change choices on a timeline without having to go through the same conversations over and over. This view also shows how dramatic some of the seemingly smaller choices can be. Changing one choice near the beginning can result in a huge cascade of adjustments all the way down the timeline. Don't worry though, it's all very manageable and understandable.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game was an interesting game with great voice acting that reminded me heavily of Tacoma. I really enjoyed the non-linear storytelling and the ability to mostly jump around and watch whatever I wanted when certain areas got a bit dry or repetitive, and I thought that their attention to detail about scenes changing around based on my decisions was spot on. Honestly, I'm surprised this game isn't more popular. This game is definitely worth it when it's on sale and honestly my only complaint is the ending, which as per the other comments, is definitely a bit of a disappointing cliffhanger. Still, despite the imperfect ending, I still really enjoyed it and I don't think it's a bad time at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A curious narrative game with an unique use of time travel. Being the voyeur into the lives of the six housemates was intriguing and over time they felt like real people. The setting was originally fresh (the north of England) and the worldbuilding interesting. I'd like to see a sequel at some point... the ending suggests that there is much more to the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: 6.5/10  ... solid concept, "meh" execution. This game deserves a sequel. In a different setting, also with more refined control over time (at least to the standard of say, a video player) that would be a 10/10Longer version:Ultimately it is worth playing; it could just really use some more QoL sauce.  You do have to get over an initial hump of filling out the mundane scenes, but it gets more interesting once you start digging in. Time travel / manipulation conceptual hook, awesome. You had my purchase at the time manipulation theme. I think the timeline screen stuff is the coolest part of this game. Execution of time travel concept, mechanically speaking, 6/10. Not enough control. Time travel mechanic badly needs a fast forward, optionally they could add more "on demand" powers like rewinding, pausing, and speeding up time. Maybe even the ability to watch the whole current timeline play out around you and control the whole timeline with precision, instead of running around scene to scene to play individual clips. That would be cool!I like how you can use changes to reveal information, manipulate the behavior of people to reveal things, and give them different options, including using this for providing context to yourself for your decisions. Need a full timeline view- I can't zoom out and I don't like scrolling through a zoomed in list. I would also like a "Tree view" where the main timeline expands out to multiple branches for each decision instead of just visualizing it collapsed into the main timeline. I get why they did this- it makes more sense to just have the one timeline and keep things simple. But I'd like a button to switch to expanded tree view on the timeline, where each decision point branches out (and potentially can merge back into the main if the decision was just flavor).  Sequel needs to take place in a different setting... Listening to people talk about clothes and relationships is MUNDANE. After a while, I literally took off my headphones, and finished a book I was reading while the non-choice related cut-scenes played out. Note: that was for the process of filling out the timeline without making any changes first, but I am updating this review as I play, and now that I'm making timeline changes systematically, it actually is getting more interesting in places (I won't be spoiling it for you). Further update after restoring the timeline 100%: I actually found some of the cut-scenes were somewhat okay.Narrative flow is mechanically kind of incohesive. You have to physically run from room to room to watch cut-scenes... At this point why even include the walking sim bits if they are so underutilized? Finding keys is not what I mean-that just felt like an unnecessary barrier.  I'm not saying we need enemies or survival mechanics or anything like that. Yeah, I just don't like walking back and forth from the basement to the top floor over and over to hear about someone's ex or even worse.Vocal performances range from "okay" to "acceptable, sort of bored/monotone" to cringe, "called on to read for the class in school" performances. Just sounded bored and I don't blame them, considering the subject matter. Update after 100%: the day-to-day scenes (unfortunately most of them) are the ones with meh acting. In the more emotional scenes you unlock, the actors do rise to the occasion in some of the more heartfelt scenes (except Tom is always bored/lost sounding).  Animation was fine, mocap. But unity is just ugly in my eye lol. In summary, the game is worth checking out on sale, but I was SO CLOSE to "Not Recommending" based on the subject matter of most of the conversations, the writing being cringe in some cases, characters are annoying to me and each speaks like they are possessed by the same seething, sarcastic jerk in many scenes. Also, what is with everyone just quietly leaving during the fire, sometimes after nudging the passed out drunk person next to them and listlessly say their name a few times, THEN quietly walk out. Wtf? Update after 100%: I think there is ONE scene of someone banging on doors as they left and shouting "Fire! Wake up guys! Fire!" As far as I can tell, one. However there's several scenes of characters in groups of 2 during the fire taking the time to explain there's no time to bang on the doors to save anyone else on the way out and inexplicably WHISPERING to each other during the escape. Cold. And I must say, the actors were really phoning it in for those catastrophe scenes. The coughing and choking sounds are like a light throat clearing and a sigh. I have seen better UK death scenes in Monty Python, guys.  This game badly needed to take place on a space ship or something! Or sherlock holmes style stuff. If I could make a sequel to this, I would make it vignettes in spacefaring society. How about a prison ship that is barely held together, has a bunch of systems go wrong, sabotage, factions rise up, and all sorts of interlocking puzzle elements for you to master on that ship. Or here's another one, adapt before landing on an alien planet. Or, We've entered an Anomaly. ETC. And yeah... the unity models are ugly, but that is a very minor criticism. The real takeaway is, though we do have a few good scenes when you dig in, I would rather have much more interesting characters to start with than "Alcohol alcohol alcohol. Ain't I cute?"P.S. I COMMAND you to read "The End of Eternity" by Isaac Asimov. It's very similar to this where the main character is a time altering agent. It's been my favorite book for like 15 years, man! Check it out! Yeah, it's dated, but the core concept is mind-expandingly cool. P.P.S. I decided the "real" reason they all died in this game was the main character snapped after having hear these jerks talk while saving them! Then the younger version cleans up and starts the cycle again. Lol!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: The marketing for this game is somewhat misleading. I would say that it's primarily a slice of life game, with the ability to alter outcomes. The voice acting was truly amazing. The gameplay could have been better - persistent flashing lightning in persistently dark rooms, the walking speed is too slow after a few hours (also you can't sprint up stairs), etc. - though that's not the focus of the game, so I'm not too bothered.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Really well-done narrative puzzle in the company of games like Tacoma, The Invisible Hours, or The Sexy Brutale. Navigate a fractured history of the final fateful week in a house full of vibrant, likeable characters expertly voice-acted and very well written, at both their high and (sometimes very) low points. The soundtrack is sparing but effective, with several catchy songs I wouldn't mind hearing as a collected soundtrack someday. The intriguing larger scenario that frames this game will clearly need further episodes to unfold and I really hope they're on the way! But even if they aren't, piecing a good timeline back together is a satisfying enough conclusion that this story is worth playing through even if it never gets a sequel. (It really should, though!!)
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Once I started this game, I just could not put it down until it was finished. I was so engrossed in the act of learning about these people's lives, and the ripple effects of their decisions. In some respects their stories are very common, but this only serves to make the characters feel real and relatable. The voice acting and story script are both superb, as is the way the narrative threads are woven together. I got about 90% there on my own, including saving everyone, but did have to use a guide to assist in seeing every possible decision point and getting the best overall outcome. For me this made the pacing and runtime perfect, but I think if I had tried to get it perfected on my own it would have started to get frustrating instead of fun. Game ran with no issues for me, and I appreciated the widescreen support, especially when traversing the timeline. Highly recommend this game for anyone who loves story-driven dialogue heavy games, and finds the idea of solving a butterfly effect puzzle box enticing. I very much hope there is a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I definitely recommend this game, it truly is a hidden gem. Almost reminds me of the tv show Quantum Leap.You play as a time travelling agent who has been sent back in time to save the lives of six housemates. Viewing events you can manipulate the choices made by the housemates in the week leading up their deaths to hopefully save them all.It's definitely a good game to play if you enjoy choices, time manipulation and a bit of detective work.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Such a pleasant surprise. It's so refreshing to play a game that's happy to tell a story that's so small and personal in an age of overblown wannabe blockbusters.Though the level of interaction is fairly minimal, mostly consisting of watching vignettes and fiddling with the timeline, I felt so invested in unpicking every detail of what was happening in that house.Criminally underrated -- please check it out so we can see what else this developer has up their sleeve in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I think Eternal Threads has a fairly unique way of telling a story, in a way that makes the house feel kinda creepy, mostly because of what happens in the story, without the use of boring jump scares.In my 8 hours of playtime I was able to get all of the achievements with the help of a guide.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Short game, finished it in about 8 hours with the true ending. I thought I had to a lot of backtracking and changing decisions to get the true ending but it was fairly easy. Gameplay could've been better, it was annoying to back again and again to the time chart to view events. Good story and characters. A needless . A good game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing this game on another platform, I had to write a review for what is truly a hidden gem. If the idea of being an agent tasked with fixing time anomalies by changing key decisions made in the past sounds appealing, I highly recommend this game. It's very fun to track down the specific decisions that lead to butterfly effects, and seeing how they impact the person's life. A detective game lives and dies by its writing, and luckily this game also features a great story featuring interesting characters with surprisingly solid voice acting. Don't miss out on this title, its lack of recognition is a crime.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Chances are if you saw this and thought "man that looks interesting" then you'll like it. In the vein of "Obra Dinn" or "Life is Strange" you get to peep in on people's lives and make little tweaks here and there to see the ripple effects.I though the overall presentation was solid, the character story arcs were satisfactory. Nobody was obnoxious and the writing wasn't cringy. From some other reviews I'll address a few things:1) There aren't that many locations and the house isn't that big. Moving from floor to floor can be a little tedious but I think it is an important part so that you can think about what you saw and what you might be seeing next. Just straight binge watching each vignette without a forced break I think would be unsatisfying.2) Why these people? They don't really explain what your point is beyond a vague "if you save a person's life that is like a million descendants in a thousand years" or what not. I think the revelation with the "ultimate ending" gives a lot more clues as to why you're there. It isn't necessaraly about the flatmates themselves but the presence of a temporal anomaly that is why you are tasked with saving them.3) I saw some critcisms about how the ripples make no sense but after unlocking every scene, I saw no glaring errors. Yes people react to the same  news in different ways but i f you think about it logically everything makes perfect sense. Some of the more "mysterious" behaviors get explained once you've unlocked every secret or node. One character in particular I thought didn't have a lot going on until I ended up unlocking a huge string of revelations and then all that previous behavior made perfect sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of interesting ideas here that unfortunately don't get worked with enough - the opening few choices make it look like you can influence your perspective (the burnt out house after the story) but the actual effects are very minor outside of finding where people put keys and passwords and the like. Wish that was explored more.Outside of the time shenanigans, what you get is a drama plot with points that can be predicted well before finding the optimal set of choices to save everybody interspersed with walking back and forth in a three-story flat with little/nothing in it. Still, would say it's an interesting experience
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads lets you feel like a proper investigator — a true detective — in the best possible way. You spend the game looking for evidence, witnessing events, and  the story of the people living in this house, both individually and together. But this isn't a passive investigation; the more you learn, the better you get to know these people, the more power you gain to affect what happens to them and to guide them to a better fate than dying alone in the dark and the smoke.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Got the best ending for everyone in about 6 hours. The rest of the time that I spend in game was changing the choices in order to unlock all of the possible events and get 100% completion of the game.  Overall, it was an interesting experience of an well written story. If you are into this type of games, it is worth trying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed Eternal Threads. The story was fun to play through and the characters were likable enough to sit down with for a couple of hours as their lives unfolded around them.The game-play itself is... well... it's a walking simulator visual novel mixed with some very light puzzle mechanics (such as trying to figure out what choices lead to what endings) and the occasional environmental puzzle that are mostly explained through flashbacks. The choices themselves vary in there usefulness, and I was finding that a lot honestly didn't seem to do much other than reveal bits of the characters background (which is fine, imo, it was nice to see little hidden details pop up and about.)I would say that as I got to the end of my play-through, it did seem to drag on and I found myself flipping back and forth constantly between the same ~3 choices to get all the endings and I found myself wishing I had an auto key to do it for me.Definitely think this games worth picking up if you want to sit back with a drink for a few sessions and just have a very low-key time to enjoy the story. However, if you're looking for something exciting this is not for you.P.S. There's a cheeky Easter-egg to hunt after you finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is criminally underrated. This might be one of the best time travel games I've played, and I've played (and loved) Life is Strange. In this game, you're interacting with events that already happened. You're a silent visitor from the future, trying to solve a mystery - what happened in this house during one specific week? Can you successfully manipulate the events to save everyone who would have died otherwise, and more, can you help their life take a turn for the better? This quickly gets complicated as new events get added and old ones become inaccessible as you change the timeline.The time travel aspect is really well executed, as are the characters. The UI is really well-designed to help you navigate the multiple events that happen - the game takes place over a course of a week, and each day, several things happen that involve one or multiple characters. The house feels alive and the characters feel realistic, and I immediately got sucked into their stories and problems. This might feel boring to some, but if you like mysteries and story-rich games, this is an amazing game. The only issue I had with it was the ending - there's a  that I didn't like, but it indicates that there might be a sequel coming. I really hope so, because I enjoyed the game immensely, and I would love to play more.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: "Wish Steam had a neutral option"Premise is good. You are in control of the timeline, playing God, able to easily see where decisions and events lead. Everything is laid out well and navigating the timeline is easy and fun.The events within the timeline are pretty boring. Six 20-30 somethings in a house, getting drunk, dealing with personal issues, getting pregnant, fighting, having sex, etc. And for gameplay all you can do is sit and watch the events play out.When some sci-fi aspects are presented to you and your player character directly it's interesting. But it's rare and ultimately leads nowhere but a cliffhanger, maybe for a sequel.Took me 9 hours to 100%. 100% can be achieved in one playthrough with no missables due to the malleable timeline.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I do not know why some would call this game boring. I thought it was AMAZING. The storywriting is on point and its so immersive. You get to play God and change the fate of the characters in the game and then you can go back and watch the other pathway had they chosen not do X.The writers made you want to learn more about each character and made you want to save them all, however you need to. It's definitely more of a visual novel with some light puzzlework on piecing it together to get the best possible ending which essentially just takes place in the bio section. It would have been 10x better if they added a cutscene of all of the characters endings that you achieved.I was a bit sad that the endings felt weak because there were some things building up that the ending didn't wrap up which was a little sad, and if you get the optional beam me up scotty ending just, acknowledge and ignore ya? If they come out with a sequel then this ending is even more incredible for what could be but I don't like to dwell if it doesn't happen.HIGHLY recommended if you like "Choices matter" games, cause this tops the cake.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not suitable for avid players to start, because it is not a game more like a story movie novel, the game after the modeling effects close to the future crime team, using the future technology projector loop to play the victims of the death, answer, play-off... modeling is good, but not suitable for starting
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this absolute gem of a game. I loved every second of it, the story was intriguing from the get go and continued until the very end. I loved all the characters and found the voice acting and animation good but not great, still good enough to pull me in to the stories and lives of the people in the game. There isn't much I could say negative about the game other than the timeline can get a bit confusing and it's hard to tell what changes affect what outcomes, still a very good game and I would like to see more games from this dev team in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: From 1 RunHidden gem of a game, this. I love the premise of taking control of a timeline of events to actually change the outcome. While there's only one location, it feels genuinely lived in and like it's its own character. Also helps that the characters are well voiced acted and performed. If your like me, a lot of time will be spent going through every single sequence. In games like this, that can feel like padding, but here you really do need to watch and learn as much as you can if you want to get the best possible outcome.Also, as someone from the North West of the UK, it's rare to see a game that gets British accents from my region right!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: this game surprised me in so many ways that i didn't think it would.at first i thought it was going to be some low effort and low quality game, but it ended up being one of the good ones to tell a story while at the same time bringing a fresh idea to the genre of story telling.after this game, i would love more of it. either a dlc where it's an another story (maybe even a story after the house fire), or just a 2nd game overall.tl;dr i loved my experience. would love more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this. I blasted through it in one day. I love that it shows that the kindest or simplest path doesn't always leed to the best outcome. It does a great job of showing the butterfly effect in action.  I think this is a great game to play if you're conflict-averse because it shows you that lack of conflict rarely results in the best result. Pressing a family member for an answer can give you the information you need to help them and have a better relationship. Saying no to someone toxic in your life frees you up to help someone who deserves it and feels grateful for the attention. I loved the sci-fi approach to showing humanity in its weird and complex ways. I really loved digging into this mystery too, it reminded me of Obra Dinn in that way. I hope they make more games that commit to the "choices matter" and actually sticking to it. Any criticisms I've had are purely subjective, such as minor inconsistentcies in a couple of events. The only plot hole I have is . I can forgive the above and i really really recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, dialogs, acting. Probably the best looking game on Unity I've seen so far. I was expecting more mystery and sci-fi though especially due to various "hints" on some sort of hidden truth and something supernatural involved, which did not materialize. Still, great narrative game with very satisfying ending. There is a cliffhanger at the end of the game which opens a possibility for continuation of the story. Hope the devs are working on the next installement.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: As a time traveler you should be able to stop a house fire with ease. All you have to do is fix the faulty electrical wiring, or stamp out an errant cigarette butt, right? This is the situation you face in Eternal Threads, but in this timeline, the blaze's casualties must be prevented with the power of kindness alone.You're presented with a series of events that take place over the course of a week and imperceptibly add up to the tragic fire. Thankfully, you're gifted with technology that can slyly edit some of the decisions made between the residents, ideally brewing up a butterfly effect that will get them out alive. Eternal Threads is a showcase of second chances, an invitation to reflect on the times in our lives when we didn't let cooler heads prevail.There is a sci-fi veneer that explains the time manipulation. You're cast as some sort of chrononaut in a dingy future, where time-travel has littered the fourth dimension with all sorts of reality-eroding radiation. It's all left pretty vague, and Eternal Threads quickly escorts you to a Northern England house in the much-more-relatable year of 2015, where a landlord and a handful of troubled college kids spend the prime of their 20s.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Really novel idea. It's exciting to play new game ideas especially when they are so well executed. great acting, visuals and sound. I warmed to all the characters, which is uncommon and needs great writing and acting to pull it off, but was needed so that I cared about saving them. I noted in some reviews people complained about running backwards and forwards between rooms, but that's what it was all about. As a player you get to know the house, what's in it and the people. Would have loved more puzzle elements, so please make another one and ramp up the puzzles. Great job, thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is a great indie adventure about manipulating a timeline: changing characters' decisions  impact other evens, allowing to make some other decisions and further influence the outcome of the story. Your goal is to save all tenants who died in a building fire. Ideally, you should also fix their personal issues.Aside from achieving one ideal outcome, you are also encourage to experiment with the decisions to see what they lead to. Moreover, it takes some "wrong" choices to find out some pieces of information to progress in the story.Overall, a very enjoyable experience that took me around ten hours to beat with all the achievements (used a guide to find only one last voicemail).
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A decent story-centered time-themed puzzle game that (like many games of its kind and due to the same lack of tangible gameplay beyond the puzzle aspect) suffers most from somewhat disappointing graphics, mediocre to sub-par acting, and often bland writing.I'd still recommend it based on how intriguing it can be to slowly uncover the bits and pieces of the characters' lives throughout the period covered by the game and then see how the different decisions along the way affect them AND because this is a decent first title for a new studio, but given how strong titles of similar theme like the VR game "Wanderer" are despite all their weaknesses, Cosmonaut Studios absolutely has to up their game if they want to continue with the theme and definitely has to get a handle on the skill and design shortcomings they revealed in this title when tackling their next one.So, if you're into time travel stuff and slice-of-life voyeurism, give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Treads takes players on an exciting journey through time, unraveling the mysteries behind a tragic fire that claimed the lives of several people. The concept alone had me captivated from the start - a time traveler trying to save those who perished is a compelling premise.The game does offer moments of decision-making, allowing players to shape the story's direction. However, I found that these choices ultimately lacked a significant impact on the overall narrative. It seemed as if the characters' fates were determined randomly, diminishing the weight of my decisions. For instance, trying to reunite a character with her husband and move them out of the ill-fated house felt fruitless as she remained in the house but just woke up to leave it in time.One area of disappointment was the lack of a deeper mystery surrounding the fire. I was hopeful that the game would explore potential motives or enemies related to the tragedy, but instead, the fire's origin remained shrouded in ambiguity. It would have been more engaging if the narrative delved into the motives behind the fire's outbreak, adding layers of complexity to the story.Despite these drawbacks, I did find myself drawn to the characters and their individual stories. The game's strength lies in its ability to portray the lives and emotions of those involved. Learning about the characters' backgrounds and witnessing their struggles added depth to the overall experience.Furthermore, the time-traveling aspect was a standout feature. The opportunity to explore different eras and observe how actions in the past influenced the present was undeniably intriguing. The potential for an even more profound impact on the story through time travel could have been explored further, but what was presented still managed to captivate my imagination.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is a fun time-manipulation game. Watch the timeline play out, and make choices for better and worse. Choices have consequences, both big and small. After 8 hours, or so, I completed the story with the best ending. Know there is more than one way to get a perfect ending.I enjoyed my time with the game, watching the lives and drama play out while trying different timelines to see what could happen. The voice acting is superb and really brings life to the story. The character movement is, for the most part, really well done. The audio for music and sound-effects are also very good. The ability to view any sequence in any order brings a sense of exploration and intrigue to the story. I chose to watch in order at first so I could understand the story better.However, there are shortcomings, which are to be expected with a smaller indie-team. The people look like mannequins, and are stiff with terrible mouth movements. I did encounter one bug in the timeline viewer that made it difficult to scroll to related events. Once you've uncovered most of the story, you are left to make changes to the timeline. This is fine, but because of the sheer number of nodes, it becomes a Where's Waldo hunt to find the changed elements.I recommend playing this game with as little knowledge of the story line as  possible. Forgive some of the shortcomings, and instead enjoy the voice acting and story telling. It's a great ride!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: tedious at times, but enjoyable enough...except, once you finish the main objective, that's the ending.  there's no elaboration or further development once you get the "true/best" ending for each character, and trying to work out how to do that is convoluted and illogical.  for a game that's ostensibly trying to build a bigger picture "universe"/set up a sequel, maybe devote more time to the actual outside premise and give more info/elaboration about the world in the true ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A nice short game detailing the lead up of a house fire and how the entanglement of the inhabitant's lives affected whether or not they survived!Puzzling which combination of events would lead to everyone surviving was really fun, as was exploring all of the alternative narratives!Overall a really nice humble bundle addition given that I probably wouldn't have found it otherwise!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games where choices matter but aren't written in stone, and you enjoyed Unheard or other "explore the narrative" games, and are interested in seeing different permutations of similar scenes along with completely new ones (or are willing to skip the completionist achievements), I highly recommend this one. After so many "no really good endings" games, it's nice to actually be able to get everyone out in one piece. I found the characters to be reasonably engaging and worth liking, although the models for them benefit from not looking too closely when they are expressing strong emotions. The voice acting is very good, the writing is consistent, and the effects of the changes make sense even when they wouldn't have been predictable until you tried them.The playtime listed is me doing a completionist run of the game, only consulting a guide when there were about five scenes I just could not get to pop.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: + Story+ Gameplay/gimmickCool little time manipulation game, could do with some QOL improvements. Overall a great experience if you can stomach cutscene simulators.To get the bad out of the way, the character models are not very good and the voice acting ranges from meh to okay/good. That's about all, nothing entirely damning. As for the game itself the timeline manipulation was done in a very nice way and the little bit of added discovery was great as well. The fact that you can change choices straight on the timeline is brilliant. I mean you would expect such a functionality for a game such as this, but not every dev actually adds it. Going into the details of the story would be spoiler territory, but the way it's been intertwined with the gameplay is great. And do understand that the story IS the gameplay, it's literally a bunch of cutscenes, that's it. If you can't stomach that, this is not a game for you. Only thing that is missing in my opinion is a "fast forward" or "skip line" option. Yes I understand that that would be skipping over the only stuff there is to do in the game. I also understand that if I want to 100% explore the choices/replay the game and not listen to the 1% changed scene for the third time, a skip button would be great. This is also why I didn't bother 100% the game, doing that for Obra Dinn was painful enough.Overall if you like time manipulation/story heavy games, this one is a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: First person perspective puzzle game+ fully voiced interactive story- a lot of pointless walking"you walk around watching holograms of the story, changing some timeline decisions to alter the outcome. as the story unravel you try to get the best outcome possible, and the game will show you what choices lead to this. interesting but slow"
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A quick note, if you dislike this type of game, nothing in this one will change your mind.That being said I enjoyed the hell out of it. It's fully voice acted, none of which came across as 'off' to me. Music and atmosphere was good as well. Similar to other games slowly piecing the story together, then altering it to get the 'best' ending was enjoyable.My only real complaint is that at times the time map could be more clear as to when a scene needs to be changed into a decision, but a little fiddling and you'll figure it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A nice concept executed in an overall ok way. The game features a pretty random sci-fi premise used mainly to frame the core mechanic, of going back and forth in the timeline of one week before a deadly fire that kills all occupants of a British shared house. You get to slowly learn about the characters and their issues, and this helps you figure out how to edit the timeline to eventually save them.I think the game could have done more with the premise. The timeline is influenced just by straight up changing the decisions of the characters at the press of a button (not, for example, changing environmental factors to influence them), and the correct answer is almost always to go for the "better" behaviour which then coincidentally also leads to the characters being able to spot the fire and run away before dying. It's not particularly complex in any sense, and really, it's mostly about discovering a story than solving some kind of puzzle. That said, it's still an interesting concept at least, and if you like narrative games it'll probably be your cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional (if somewhat unpolished) narrative adventure that truly embraces the concept of "choices matter."The endgame is a little awkward in that it relies on a lot of backtracking and trial & error tweaking, but the constant joy of revealing new branches or hidden choices/outcomes held my attention.  Cons: The UI is not a fun place to navigate.   The character models are uncanny at best, nightmare puppets at worst-with flappy lip sync.  Endgame or trying for the "perfect solution" can sometimes happen accidentally because of the complex links and the less-than-intuitive "map." Pros:  The house environment is realistic, with Unity lighting pushed to its limits.  Voice acting is superb.  Player choices make changes to the story, characters or house-- sometimes subtle, like where objects are located. sometimes major, like who is alive or dead (and where or how they died) or whether they can overcome personal traumas and neurosis.This short game is worth it for the avid adventure game enthusiast who likes to dig into a story and explore every route.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty interesting little title. If anything I recommend it for the creativity alone. The main mechanic of fiddling with a timeline to witness the butterfly effect is quite fun and it's something that is rife with potential. The game itself is decent. The voice acting ranges from good to bad-but-fun, and I overall enjoyed my time with it.The actual moment-to-moment gameplay largely boils down to watching events in a timeline until you find one where someone makes a choice between 2 options, then following that event down the timeline to see what the choice changes, trying to guide people towards the optimal resolution for their problems and make sure they survive the week. It's a fairly enjoyable mechanic, even though it seldom felt like I was really figuring stuff out, moreso just kind of flipping switches because it's all I had to do and eventually things fell into the right place."Still, I'd recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: It took me ~12 hours to watch/play this story-game to the good endingThere are ~150 story clips and ~30 decisions that can be made. Some are obvious, others are hard to work out what the best outcome is.There isn't any replay-ability once you've seen all the possible timelines, but it might take you a while to find some of the more obscure story lines.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A game labelled "Choices Matter" and the choices actually matter, insane.Really though, pretty cool game, all of the plot threads are interesting to explore despite how dull the actual environment is. Normally I wouldn't care about a week in the life of a landlord and 6 tenants but Eternal Threads made a premise fun to explore. It was a challenge trying to find the perfect timeline but I got it and was satisfied with the endings.The game is strictly narrative driven, there isn't much beyond that, so if you play games for action or puzzles or something such you might be bored with this game and miss a lot.That being said the game seems a little overpriced for a game you can likely 100% in less than 10 hours. _childDocuments_.review: It's basically a combination of The Invisible Hour and Gone Home with added choices (and thus consequences!)Gameplay is mostly about watching events around the house and "puzzle" here is figuring out the right combination of choices in these events to achieve desired outcome (or to unlock unseen events). It's almost FMV, just without videos part.The story itself is mostly stripped of "supernatural" (which is mostly just an outside flavour, frame in which it existing), topics within are pretty "regular/normal" though.Oh, and there's a landlord that has  rough love life! There's "abridged" mode that is apparently shorter by around 1/3 (if amount of events is anything to go by), although not entirely sure the point of it considering shorter version sadly locks you out of the "good" ending and thus getting some achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little torn about Eternal Threads. On the one hand, it's short — extremely short for the price tag — and, gameplay-wise, rather thin. The models are wooden, the textures are antiquated, the lighting is horrid, and the plot ends on a cliffhanger even with the best ending.On the other hand, I enjoyed it immensely and if they released a sequel tomorrow I would snap it up at twice the price.Eternal Threads is structured like a visual novel, but instead of playing through in a linear fashion and having to save compulsively to see different decision branches, you can skip around to any point in the story you choose, and switching between decision branches — and immediately seeing the results cascade down the timeline — is the core (arguably only) game mechanic. Your goal is to find the set of decisions that leads to the outcome you want.The nonlinear storytelling reminded me somewhat of Return of the Obra Dinn, which obviously is high praise, but the puzzle aspects were much thinner. The characters, however, I rapidly found myself getting very invested in, despite the fact that there's nothing really special about any of them. They're six fairly ordinary people, and writing ordinary people in a way an audience can care about is no mean feat. The voice acting backs up the writing with competence if no great verve, though it's a refreshing change of pace to hear not a word of Southern English in a game set in Britain. We're in Lancashire, and it sounds like it, and that made me a happy panda.If you're looking for a feast for the eyes, however, look elsewhere. The visuals do make a good solid try at being immersive, but they would have been dated fifteen years ago, and now they just look archaic, without any "old-school charm" to sweeten the pill. There are also some stability issues — I experienced roughly one crash to desktop every two hours of gameplay, though fortunately extremely frequent autosaving takes the sting off. Still, a polished experience this ain't.Also, pay attention to the content notice. They're not kidding. This game takes an unflinching (if brief) look into some pretty dark places, and if you've struggled with addiction or trauma you may well recognize what you see there. None of it is gratuitous and the overall arc of the story is hopeful, though the tone remains melancholy and somewhat morbid. Double especially mind yourself if you decide to 100% it — that can get emotionally taxing as you're asked to watch people you've probably come to like die over and over in slow, rather pathetic ways. It got to me after a bit.Overall, Eternal Threads was time well spent, and if I'd known how much I was going to enjoy it I'd have happily paid full price (I got it in the Humble Choice bundle for June 2023). I came to care about these people and their ordinary little lives, I enjoyed learning about and solving their problems grand and petty, and I kind of wish I'd had more time to spend with them. And I'd dearly like to know what happens next. sequel plzkthx
