_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Unique concept. Time traveling not as a weapon or a super power, but only used in order to watch the daily lives of six people over a week is both humble and powerful.- Amazingly built protagonists with solid characters, secrets and rich backstories. They're daily people like me and you with their personal fears and problems, yet they manage to shine and seem unique. You'll easily get emotionally attached to them.- Exceptionally written dialogues that feel realistic and immersive. You never get bored of diving into one more conversation.- Fantastic voice acting performances, that are so convincing and emotional like a well made movie.- The main plot is pretty simplistic, but experiencing all these small personal stories, watching all these human relationships evolving before your eyes is amazing. Even the filler scenes that don't really affect the final outcome contribute a lot to atmosphere's built up.- It's one of the few games that your choices have real impact and the outcomes makes sense. Also, it doesn't force you to make a decision in limited time or without enough clues, that you may regret later, like so many games do. You can always go back and change every decision when you're wiser. Although the gameplay is simplistic, trying to figure out the right combination of decisions inside this labyrinth of entangled events makes it challenging.- It's awesome that they managed to build a game of several hours that takes place inside a single house to be so interesting.- Nice music theme at the main menu and credits.The bad- Gameplay doesn't evolves. It's one dimensional from the beginning till the very end. Interactions are minimal and after a while all the mechanics feel a bit repetitive. They should have found clever ways to enrichen it like collecting more clues, keys and stuff around the house. This way it ends up being more like a movie with limited interactivity rather than an actual video game.- The design of the house seems a little bit generic with lack of details that could give it more personality, while the graphics are mediocre.- I would prefer that cliff hunger final scene to be missing.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I overall give this a "thumbs up" review but with some caveats that you should be aware of before playing.I don't think the trailers give a good sense of the gameplay or what the game is about- this game is 95% narrative-based. You'll spend most of your time watching short scenes of the characters at a snapshot of a point in time. You can bounce around to different scenes in any order you want, and in some key scenes can change a decision for a particular character, which amount to rest of the 5% of the game. It can be tiring having to watch all of these cutscenes, especially when they don't contribute to anything special in the narrative or plot development (and there are a good amount of these). You also can't fast forward them which adds to the tedium.However, if you go into this game with the right mindset and choose to get engrossed in the characters and their stories, it can be an enjoyable experience, and I can tell the developers put a lot of thought into creating a robust interwoven storyline to absorb.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A really good game that has a very intriguing story that changes constantly. If you're expecting action and quick decisions you'll be dissapointed, this is a puzzle game. The scenes are all voice acted and animated. This game has a really intriguing story about the six residents and their lives, and watching your changes affect the scenes directly is really cool. The changes in scenes is really impressive with the amount of different scenarios there are. One of my favorite things about this game is the setting, which takes place in a burned house. There is something unsettling about the rain and scorched house, and seeing things change locations when you change the time line never gets old. (there's some surprises that I won't spoil but the game is really good at unsettling you just when you start to get comfortable). The ending is insane and really makes me hope for a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game, from the technical standpoint its amazing, the atmosphere, the graphics, the sound, the voice acting..., and it is well optimized. You get to play some clone by the name 43 (hitman, anyone?) and you are sent back in time by some corporation in order to prevent tragic night's event when a fire claimed the lives of six young people. You basically explore a burned down house, and with a projector tool witness first hand how events in the house unfolded one by one, until the tragic night.In the meantime you do some decisions that will affect how events will play out, and that's it. You also use the timeline in order to travel to events you might want to change.There is a few mechanics about the timeline view, that I'm not sure I got them right, like the what does influence lock does?! I think I haven't read most of the tutorial text in the game, heheh.However at my first try I managed to save four people, except Ben and Jenny, but doing just one simple change on the time line brought me an "ALMOST perfect mission", or so the guy on the remote said. I also managed to unlock everything there was to unlock (I guess) and also found both temporal anomalies :)I'd say the game took me like more than 10 hours from 10 to 15 probably, but I am a slow player :) Also, don't look at my playtime... I mostly play in offline recently.If you like narrative, time-manipulating/traveling, character and choice-based gameplay, then this game is for you. But also if you like what you read about it, do not hesitate and give it a try.Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really great game with only few flaws I'll list below. 9/10.The stories are interesting and you really relate to and feel for the characters. And - most importantly - you like them, want them to survive, care about them and want them to have good lives in the end.The gameplay is made in cool way, I always looked forward to see new event and wonder whether it will suddenly become a decision or not. I ended up watching all possible decisions and outcomes.Now to the flaws:1) There's a weird glitch around the lower staircase which makes it almost impossible to immediately turn to another one when you get up or down. You have to go up the first stairs, stop, turn left  slowly and then try to go up the upper stairs, otherwise the glitch will teleport you a little and you will be going in completely different direction and face a wall.It's nothing horrible and game ruining, but it's super annoying. It's the reason why I didn't give the game 10/10.2) The "normal" outcomes for Neil and Linda are  better than the "best" versions of their possible outcomes. Their "best" outcomes are like Reddit users' wet dreams, but definitely not great in real life or realistic in the first place. *3) I didn't like that certain character could survive only if and when another character did something wrong, and couldn't basically decide their own fate themselves. Someone else did it for them, indirectly, and you are forced to let one particular thing happen even if you don't want to. *** **
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique game. It feels like... putting together a jigsaw out of relationships between characters, while the picture changes as you work on it. Be ready for a very very slow start (just watching initial events without changing anything takes quite a while) and being very thorough about exploring permutations if you try for best outcome ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is a mystery adventure game in the vein of Tacoma, with the twist of you being able to change events in the past to a degree to change some knock-on events in the timeline.With that interesting scifi setting you get to explore... 2020-ish UK and the lives of some common folks renting rooms in the same house. You are doing this to make sure they survive the night and thus future can be saved or something something. The scifi veneer doesn't really impact too much of the game.Visually, the game is a bit unappealing. You will spend the next 9ish hours in a burnt down house, at night, with a heavy rain outside, so most of your view will be illuminated by your own light and some monochromatic 3D projections of past events. It fits the dystopian scifi setting, but it's still "meh" to look at. At least it's high fidelity burnt house, so you will see some nice textures on various things...Story itself is a bit of a drag. It takes a long while to get anywhere and a lot of the events you see end up being a bit mundane. It's not a thrill a minute, nor is it concise, but eventually you have some payoffs with the characters building on their past actions.Your side objective with the game will be to improve the lives of the people you are saving by making them work through their emotional baggage. It mostly boils down to being honest and open each time the opportunity presents itself, which is rather predictable.The game has a few areas you need to unlock through finding secret keys. And by finding it of course means "watch all the videos until the key is pointed out in them and only then can you find it", which was rather disappointing. Because it's not like we can open a flimsy wardrobe door by just pulling on them hard enough...Overall, it's an okay game, but nothing stellar. It tells a down to earth story wrapped in a fantastical premise. So if you want an adventure drama about some UK people having a turbulent week, this is a good game for you. If you want a narrative mystery game, maybe check out Return of Obra Dinn or Tacoma first and then circle back to this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I was properly impressed by a game that didn't stoop to heightened scenes or unbelievable moments to create drama. This is just a bunch of slightly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up people trying to get by, and in caring for each other in the small, day-to-day, mundane ways... saving each others' lives. Good script writing, good direction. Picks a theme and sticks to it. Genuinely startled how much I liked it.

_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: OK, I have a HUGE issue with this game, and it's that there isn't about 40 different DLC packs to go along with it.  Not to mention 10 full on sequels - each of those with 40 different DLC packs.So, I will admit that within about the first 5 minutes of the game, I got really overwhelmed by everything being tossed at you - which, admittedly, makes sense for story and character purposes.  But then, after that initial overwhelm, this game is supremely easy to navigate, but JUST the right level of tricky to complete.  I never felt like the game was cheap and hiding things from me, nor was it every too hand-holdy.  I really did feel like a time detective.Speaking of that, this game beautifully marries my two favorite genres, which happen to be scifi and detective mystery.  They somehow also manage to squeeze some cool world building in there (aside from the main story) that really rounds out the edges.  On top of all this, the atmosphere they manage to pull out of a single indoor location - how it manages to be alternatingly eerie, horrifying, beautiful, tragic, joyful - all with tiny little changes.I'd imagine crafting a game like this with so many different....ahem...threads...is a time consuming process, but seriously now, are the sequel cases ready now?------------------------------VAGUE SPOILERS FOR THE ENDING------------------------------I'd be pretty happy just bouncing from case to case with any additional content or sequels - that was truly a satisfying enough gaming experience.  I truly hope that with the added "it isn't what it seems" element that they introduce that it doesn't do away with the core mechanics that made this game so special.Well done!!

Who knows.Overall it's quite an original concept and it's worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice thrill and a good ride all along.The premise is the accident was thought as some kind of error in the timeline and our job is to fix it, so it can be different experience of something like time travelling since our guy is literally just watching the past events unfold and make changes if part of those events have corrupted points.Gave me a spook twice outta nowhere that at certain point nearing the ending part of the timeline, I have to be so sneaky to get something fixed and it's actually nothing happening. xDThe additional ending is kinda trying to give an impression of a sequel, I guess.Some of the characters' conclusion events might be a bit vague on how it reached there, because there is only one pair I know that keep giving the impression of how annoying it can be to fix the order of what they supposed to do despite it should be giving same end result.Overall it is RECOMMENDED, for all that like story-driven narrative with time manipulation and some level of piecing stuffs together so it make sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is a pretty simple game: you're a time traveler whose sent back to 2015 to make sure several people survive a house fire. The game opens with saying in the future, time travel was discovered but in doing so caused 'radiation' to spew throughout the timeline, causing small events to be changed which in turn caused the future to be somewhat post apocalyptic.Pros: The time manipulation mechanic is very cool. If you played Life Is Strange, its fairly similar but much more expanded upon. You make decisions for some of the characters and this can either help or hinder their survival. In order to help them survive, you need to review the events and conversations leading up to the fire that makes for an interesting story involving the characters' current life troubles. There's some interesting puzzles that involves finding keys to open locked doors, but in order to find them, that involves exploring a particular time stream of events. So replayability is definitely strong if you want to see all the different scenes and combinations.Cons: Honestly there isnt a lot to complain about in this game. I would say the only 'negative' is lack of context regarding the backstory of the game. When the game ends, there's a kind of "twist" that happens but without a lot to draw from regarding the backstory, its hard to really understand what happened and what it means exactly. It seems to set up a sequel, but I dont see any updates regarding this. This honestly seems like it could be an episodic game to me but I dont think that was intended from the devs. However even with this, its a minor complaint.Conclusion: If you liked Life Is Strange's time manipulation but hated the cringe teen antics from the game, then you'll love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the overall idea of the game, the time travel story (subtle, not trying too hard to be a time travel game), the characters, watching the snippets of their lives (this part was similar to Tacoma). There were plenty of interesting twists to the story that I didn't see coming. I found the navigation of the timeline easy to use, and the game explains what to do and what's happening well. My favourite part was watching the clips and getting to know the characters, then exploring the house. I found the game quite easy. When something new is revealed, it is made obvious if it's important. The most challenging part of the game was trying to get everybody the perfect ending, which didn't take too long, but felt satisfying when I achieved it. I would definitely buy a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: The store page does not do this game justice. Eternal threads is a really great, solid game that I feel deserves more recognition. The investigation/exploration aspects are atmospheric and engaging. The timeline game mechanics are clear to understand and there are some nice quality of life features that help you use it more efficiently. The graphics are really good, the sound design and voice acting are solid. The narrative is engaging and makes sense. If you want to 100% the game, it isn't a massive time commitment and you get some additional plot but if you don't, you can still get a fully resolved ending. The game is easy and clean to navigate and I didn't encounter any bugs or glitches. The price is reasonable (I picked it up during the last sale.) and hopefully they will make the demo available again.Some of the other reviews are right, there's nothing revolutionary or mind blowing about this game but what there is, is an engaging, fun, well-polished, clean, cool, good looking experience, at a reasonable price, that's easy to play and navigate, and that doesn't take too long (or too short) an amount of time complete. Overall it's just an all-around solid game, which I think is rare these days. I highly recommend checking this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game if you're a fan of interactive stories and don't listening to british peopleGraphics are pretty nice for this price range, as for whenever you'll like the concept and will keep the game, I have to say the two hour refund window was not enough for me to decide, but I ended up liking it, guess it was worth the moneyThe game supposedly takes around 12 to 14 hours to fully complete I've also noticed several events that I believe should've been influence locked to another event, are not, which might make unlocking everything a bit harder than it should be
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... okay. It has a cool concept but it reeeeally does not execute upon it very well because the game gives you access to basically all events from the very beginning and thus there's no reason not to watch them all linearly and only make decisions when you need to unlock potential events. So it just becomes watching a story play out and very, very occasionally tampering with it. On rewatch you can at best skip to a decision point but if you accidentally restart a scene, tough luck, you're rewatching the entire thing, baby, no matter how long it is.As for the characters... ehh, the actors do a decent job but most of them aren't very compelling and tend to only have a few character traits. Raquel's the only one I ended up liking for her bisexual best friend energy but she's almost -too- perfect, to the point where her one traumatic backstory element is such a minor thread that gets resolved so easily it barely factors into anything else. Meanwhile every other character deals with their own problems in a fairly sensible way, though [spoilers]jenny having to wait until the last possible moment to tell ben about her pregnancy makes no real sense to me, other than as plot contrivance[/spoiler]. Mostly the story is just... not super interesting, though, and figuring out the best endings for each character is very straightforward once you go through all the events. Oh and the ending is cliffhanger nonsense that leaves several threads hanging for no real reason while introducing but not elaborating on several new questions and it's super unsatisfying.Also, the game's optimized like crap, it actually crashed on me once when trying to lower the graphics settings and the title screen/intro sequence definitely has it the worst, though it's not a particularly appealing game to look at even after that. Ehh.I don't dislike the game, it's a neat concept for sure, but this is a case where I wish had steam had a meh rating because I definitely found it... disappointing. I wanted more out of it than it wanted to give me. Don't regret playing it, but I'm probably going to forget about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Not only does this tell a story, you get to be the narrator. I waiting for so long it seems for this game to finally come out and now that I have played it, it was definitely worth the wait. I prefer single player games for this exact reason. If you are looking for any customers for a future release count me in.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game.I've seen some comparisons of this game and Return of the Obra Dinn, but I'd say this game plays more similarly to something like Her Story than it does Obra Dinn. There is a lot less onus on the player to do investigation of their own in this game, it's more about trying to find the right decisions at key moments to guide the plot in a direction that you want.The narrative and characters are well written, but have a 'daytime tv' sort of vibe. For those wanting a bit more thematically, sadly most of the plot is very grounded. There are a few moments that hint that there might be a big reveal of something else, something mysterious, going on , but those plot threads don't lead anywhere significant outside of one example, which also leads to a cliffhanger rather than any answers. A minor disappointment from an otherwise good game.The ending leaves room for a sequel, and in fact most likely demands one. I'm definitely looking forward to it. Would be nice if they played into the horror theme a bit more the next time around, but we'll see.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved my time with this game. It's a character driven/narrative puzzle game where you change events in the past to unlock new events/scenes until you successfully alter the course of history. The graphics are okay, but I really appreciate the writing and voice acting. It made me get to know and like each of the main characters and try to figure out the puzzle to get the best ending. Ignore my playtime since I alt-tab out of games, but I unlocked all 197 events/scenes and have a playtime of about 8 hours. If you enjoy story-driven games, I'd recommend Eternal Threads.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: It was an interesting game. I liked the concept and the characters were pretty good. It could admittedly get monotonous and boring walking around/listening. But seeing how everything ends up is sort of makes up for that. It's definitely a walking simulator with a little bit of detective work.The beginning loading screen could get annoying (the lady giving her speech each time you load the game) and there are flashing lights so watch out for that. Also pretty easy to get all the achievements if you're into that sort of thing.I'm excited to see what comes next from the team :)
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A choose your own adventure game that is fun for those who like figuring out what actions need to occur in order to prevent certain consequences. Performances and writing of the main story are good, at least good enough for you to get invested in some of the characters. Don't go into this with expectations of complex time travel lore, it is mostly there for the sake of justifying gameplay and to give a background for the actual story of the six house members.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent slice of life / investigation game that leaves you wanting more at the end.  It's a slower paced game, so keep that in mind if you're thinking about picking it up.The game is largely 'help six british randos solve their problems and make it out alive', but the main characters are interesting and have some fun side support, so it's interesting to see how the various decisions affect the timeline and the ways you can make things better for everyone.  Gameplay is largely just walking around and watching scenes and tweaking the decisions people make, there's a couple mild puzzles to figure out how to get places and the main puzzle of just resolving the scenario optimally in the first place.The main critique I have of it is just that there's a fascinating time travel premise behind it, but aside from some scattered rare commentary from your control operator through the game, not enough is done with it.  Hopefully the team makes a sequel or another game that expands on the universe they created.Still, it was an enjoyable 8 hours that I enjoyed experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A great little game with a well-executed premise; my only qualm is that it was a little short (I was able to get the best ending in ~4-5 hours, the rest of my time played is getting the other achievements). The writing was great, and each character seemed very human, having their own secrets and flaws that you can find out by tinkering with the timeline. My only complaint about the game would be that interacting with the timeline can be a bit clunky at times, but not to the point of it being a problem. The setting that the game sets up, inparticular, is a very interesting one, and leaves open the possibility of more games (or DLCs) with the same type of gameplay - something that I very much hope can happen!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: The Butterfly Effect...I really enjoyed this game and it's nice to see a British game developer making a solid title.  I especially enjoyed all the British dialects which I'm sure will confuse people as often we are portrayed as all from London.Your tasking is to save 6 housemates from a fire, but you can't stop the fire.  Any slight change can have an effect later on in the story.  I really appreciated the thought that went into the branching of changes as often a 'choices matter game' gets quite lazy toward the conclusion of the game and you realise nothing you could've done would've changed the outcome.  This isn't one of this games.  I really would recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: This one's a pretty good experience. The performances are decent, the writing is solid, the characters are compelling. The timeline is very satisfyingly put together, with changes rippling in ways that feel like realistic human reactions rather than ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unpredictable butterfly reactions. There are also connections between choices that make them matter as a network rather than being independent, you won't see every event having just put each choice to A and B (and some choices have a C if some previous event redefines a choice to be between different options)It does feel very low stakes throughout, the character's problems are at a low grade soap opera level, anything that's done can be undone and your POV character isn't taking things very seriously all of which contribute to an atmosphere in which things don't matter much. There is also a lot of watching to not much playing, there are a lot of events leading up to the fire and it takes a long time to view them all before making any changes (you can start making changes sooner, but you'd have to change them back sooner or later to see the original situation).The result is a whole that's a bit less than the sum of its parts, but they are such good parts. I enjoyed most of my play and after seven hours was ready for it to be a bit longer (but already had the achievement for watching every scene, I've no idea how some people spent an extra five hours to do that). It's a good game, but it feels like it's missing something to be great. Worth playing if you're into the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is among those pleasant types of games that don’t really invent anything new, but manage to take a lot of well established concepts and mechanics and combine them into an experience that hasn’t been attempted before. So while you’re playing, you’re enjoying the game as something that isn’t unlike what you already know, but when the time comes to analyze it and try to compare it to other titles you’ve played before, you realize – hey, this is actually quite new. And, of course, it wouldn’t mean much if the game wasn’t good, but luckily it is.The game is a first person narrative exploration adventure game, heavy on the interactive story and light on item manipulation. You play as a person sent from the post-apocalyptic future ravaged by excess time manipulation into the past to undo said manipulation and restore the timeline to how it originally was on a case by case basis. At least, that’s what you’re told but you don’t get to see much apart from the one case you will be working on during the entire game, where a house fire killed 6 tenants due to some time anomaly, as in the “intended” timeline they were all meant to survive.And if I start describing it mechanically, you’ll immediately have clear other game references in your head. For example, the location that you explore, after the fire happened, is very much your Gone Home-type gameplay, where you can look at some stuff, open locked doors and containers when you find keys and read notes that provide additional story. With the small twist being, that the configuration of things in the house actually change depending on the choices of the past.Exploring the past is basically just watching an interactive movie or playing a simple Visual Novel, where you watch episodes from people’s lives and at certain points you may get a choice between two options that may or may not affect the availability of certain future episodes or choices appearing in some of them. You get a visualization of a Timeline too, kinda like in Zero Escape games or Detroit: Become Human, and just like in the latter you can switch viewed choices within that Timeline, without the need to replay the scene. While visually the episodes play somewhat reminiscent to, say, puzzles in The Vanishing of Ethan Carter, events of the past in Return of the Obra Dinn or the scene reconstruction in Sherlock Holmes: Chapter One.So, as I said – the parts of the game are nothing new and you’ve seen these ideas done before. But this particular mixture, along with the aforementioned effect the choices of the past have on the things you may find in the time you’re physically exploring, leads to a somewhat novel experience. And I’m surprised this hasn’t been explored previously, at least not that I know of. Granted, for the sake of player comfort some of the time discrepancies are ignored – for example if you open a door in your time with a key that you can only find in the place where it is if a certain order of events happens, when you change that order the door is still opened and you still have that key. So, basically, all of the “location unlocks” are your permanent progression items.If this sounds like you spend vast majority of the game just watching a story, that’s because it is. Thankfully, the story is genuinely enjoyable, with a likeable cast of characters all of whom are well voiced and all of whom have some problems in their lives and some secrets that you may learn during the course of the game. It’s not necessary to learn everything about everyone to accomplish the base mission parameters of saving everyone, but there is a “perfect path”, that is supposedly representing the events as they happened before the time anomaly changed them (even though that perfect path isn’t necessarily without hurdles for characters to overcome and mistakes they must still make).Given the freedom of looking at the past events in any order, I do feel like there’s a preferred way of doing it – by just following a thread to its logical conclusion before trying to jump around and watching other possibilities. But the game does give you that option and you can, if you want, view stuff mostly out of order. I know some people played Her Story this way and were still able to enjoy it, so it’s nice that the game allows that.I enjoyed Eternal Threads specifically because the cast of characters was so strong and the mechanics were solid enough to keep me going. But I feel that if you’re not really into story-driven titles like this, you might get bored, because mechanically the game is super simple. And the story isn’t super over the top or crazy full of twists and conspiracies, it’s more of a slice of life type of thing with just enough mystery that feeds into the overall plot of time manipulation. But yeah – if you like story driven titles, VNs, interactive stories or good narrative exploration games, you might enjoy Eternal Threads a lot. I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Since I enjoyed the free demo, I was excited to play this game. It is a slow game that is best enjoyed a few hours at a time. You get to explore, find clues, learn more about characters, and solve a time travel puzzle. It is not a horror game but has a slightly creepy atmosphere, which added to the experience for me. It can be slow at times and frustrating if you get stuck, but when you do finally move forward it feels very satisfying. If you are feeling bored or stuck in the current section of the timeline, skip ahead, explore the house, or filter down to a certain character to focus on. The right answer can come about unexpectedly from decisions you didn't think of at first. The game certainly leaves itself open for a sequel, but you will still get a conclusion to the main story lines.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short game, but I really enjoyed the premise. I liked most of the characters, but regardless of whether or not I liked them, they at least felt like real people.Graphics are a bit dated, but it's the story that really captures youGameplay-wise most of what you do is go around the house eavesdropping and changing people's decision. All decisions are binary (either this or that choices) but they can lead up to very different chain of events, in which you will also make more choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: For being a pretty short game, this was very good. I beat it all in one sitting because the gameplay was so addicting. Would love to see a sequel. The only disappointment was the ending being a little underwhelming (though there is a slight plot twist) but aside from that, I loved the characters, their interactions, and basically just watching and manipulating a week in the life of these random people.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I just stumbled upon this game and I thought it was pretty good. I liked the time travel mechanics and how changing something in the past would affect the present. The story is good, though at times it can be a little slow, and sometimes it seems more like a movie or a walking simulator than a game. I'll admit the facial animations and character models aren't great and it often seems like their arms are made of rubber with how they bend. It just seems strange, considering the environment is very realistic and detailed. I finished the game in two days, so I can't recommend it at full price, since there's not much replay value.Still, I'd give this game a 8/10 and would definitely like to see more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna throw my review into the pile. Loved it, it's really a drama visual novel with a sort of time travel / timeline layer on top, I enjoyed working out how to solve everyone's problems and how drastic the changes I made were.Being from around the area the game is set in, I really enjoyed playing a game set where I live, the accents and mannerisms were very familiar to me. I'm sure most people reading this review aren't from the northwest of England but if you are, yeah, it's got that going for it.It's not the most graphically impressive game but it does the job, the house is full of little details and the environment work considering the house was on fire was very accurate to my mind. It also got the right sounds for a creaky post war terraced house.Took me about 8 hours to finish, think I saw most of the content of the game.I will say, the game does occasionally look like its going to veer into horror, and I can assure you this isn't the case, unless you find flickering lights scary.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: It's not too bad. However I feel like i was just trying to speedrun it after 8-9 hours of playing. The game made me feel cross-eyed at times and trying to find the perfect combination of choices was really just giving me a headache, when all I want to do right now is go to sleep.Eternal Threads is great at keeping you interested in its plot with the way it does its storytelling but I really felt like I was getting sick of it towards the end. I didn't feel super amazed by the ending, it was kinda interesting, but It also left me with a 'Eh' feeling. The only other thing I didn't really like was not being able to search every drawer myself until the timeline told me something interesting was there. As much as I appreciate being given hints, can I please just use my common sense and my way of thinking to find clues myself.I loved the characters especially Raquel, loved her personality to bits. I also loved how they squeezed so much story into such a small location, very well done. Great writing it was fun and interesting to listen and learn about everyone (before I was eager for the game to end).This is great if you like watching a movie 30 minutes at a time (equivalent to 1-2hrs), or if you just want something with a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: The game may seem to be about time travel, and it is, but it's more about the six characters you're trying to save. Every character has their own personality and they all feel very different from each other. I found myself hooked right from the start because of the characters, not because of the time travel aspect.I finished the game in about 8 hours with the best ending, taking an extra hour to get all the events I missed. I took a couple more hours to get the developers Easter Egg (which I recommend getting) and to see all the endings and how some characters ended up if I had certain characters they were close with dead. They put a lot of work in this game and I think it pays off. The graphics are decent. The environment is great and really fits the game, but the character models aren't great. The gameplay is very easy to learn, but can get complex when trying to unlock everything. The voice acting was good, but some lines could've been delivered a little better. The background sounds of the rain while walking around the house is very well done and really immersed me in the game. Despite the game not being horror, there are a few jumpscares that are put in the world that come up at times when you least expect it. The story is really well-written and I think it's worth the price. There are very minor bugs that don't ruin the game or the experience.I definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes slow paced narrative games with a great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is a fun, time-manipulation mystery game. I really enjoyed unraveling the mystery and figuring out how to save all of the housemates. To me the beauty of this game's design is that the choice of what order to view the events is entirely up to you as the investigator. I chose to start from the first event and work my way forward, but I also think it would have been fun to start from the end and work my way back or even jump around if you wanted to follow a specific thread or housemate. As a comparison to other games, the storytelling in Eternal Threads was reminiscent of Her Story and Telling Lies in terms of viewing video-like scenes and trying to determine how they fit into the larger picture. I was excited when I managed to obtain someone's ideal ending and then I had a lot of fun puzzling out how to obtain all of the ideal endings together.I still haven't even seen all of the events, so I know there is still more for me to puzzle out. Something to look forward to in the future.I read that some people experienced bugs. I didn't experience a single one during my entire playthrough so I'm not sure what to say about that other than I'm pleased I had a perfectly smooth experience.The game is on the shorter side (my actual playtime is closer to 9 hours) but I still think worth the price for supporting an indie game developer. I hope more games like this are produced. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems very interesting though my issues are the speaking is very hard to follow and almost need a translator for it, charchters also walk through doors when watching the videos. Also the second video where the guy meets somebody at the front door just keeps looping. I have watched it to the end, then ran around the house to try and find them with no sucess. I must say i am not happy with the game, especially at this price range and think its way past overpriced as many say 12 hours is the playtime, i paid 3 euros for games which have lasted way longer. So unless its on sale i say skip it and watch painty dry.. way more fun
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: A great game featuring time travel and the influence of decisions based in time.The game generally plays smoooth when V-Sync is disabled getting 60 FPS with a laptop (GTX 1060) on Ultra settings. So it seems that there are some issues with V-Sync.Agent 43's adventure was definitely interesting though the resolution events may be a tad boring. The logic puzzle was challenging but not hard. I eagerly await a DLC or sequel picking up where we left off.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: i love accents first of all, the time travel aspects is a passion of mine, but i love the flow of the game, was relaxing and entertaining getting to know the characters. im really enjoying this game, def break from the hack and slash non cerebral type of gaming, would love more of the same but with more intensity and choices and consequences. def recommend giving this game a try
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game as it was a fairly unique concept.  It is pretty short, I finished it in 8 hours.  And this type of story-based game really doesn't have any replayability.  But I really enjoyed getting to know the characters and piecing together the story.  I was pretty hooked on it for a few days.  I would buy more games like this and hope they make sequels or DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable and unique choice driven experience. The characters all came into their own by the end and we felt driven to achieve their best possible outcomes and understand their personal circumstances. Even shallow secondary characters got a decent fleshing out by the end (Ian is a good lad really and a great friend!) While the choice here is somewhat limited, even the smallest change can send ripples through the whole 7 day timeline thanks to the butterfly effect and we found ourselves questioning how to achieve a certain result using just those few key moments available to us. This is where the game earns it's puzzle tag, you need to think logically but also often outside of the box. Sometimes, the best outcomes require you to make the worse of two choices along the way.Would like to see a little more work on the 3d character assets and their animation but otherwise the environment was well done and felt believable. A sequel is an absolute must after the ending we get so hope very much to see another outing from the Eternal Threads team.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really great experience. It felt a lot like watching a TV show and getting to see how it plays out differently when each choice is discovered or changed. Strong recommend for anyone who likes story games. I saw a review mention that the story isn't that interesting -- I think I tentatively agree with this on first appearances, but I was still compelled to finish the game and I thought it got significantly better once it became clear there was more to the story than just the housemate's immediate trouble.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept, I do like the time travel aspect of the game (reminds me of the Zero Escape series).Soundtrack is okay. Character designs could be better. Their mouths sometimes don't move in conversations.There wasn't anything else to do once you've figured out the secret areas.My problem with the game is the replayablility. There weren't a lot of areas to explore and search through and for a game with a bunch of possibilities for the fate of each characters, the endings all felt really same-ish.I'd still recommend this game though, but get it on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty straightforward game. several people die during a house fire and you have gotta find a way to save them all by exploring a time span of 1 week in the house and changing small decisions that will ultimately save their lives. effort was taken to make traversing and changing key points quickly pretty painless, which is appreciated. though I do wish there was more "time horror" bits to keep things fresh, but you will mostly just be dealing with going room to room watching scenes play out in hopes of discovering a point where you can change something. I liked the characters, the atmosphere, and the time voyeurism. The price may seem a bit high, but I am always happy to support more games with spooky houses and time shenanigans.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Review edited following completion - Eternal Threads is an enjoyable sort-of-puzzly, sort-of-visual-novel, sort-of-am-dram-mystery-interactive-experience. The game's opening gambit is an apocalyptic sci-fi concept about time itself shattering, and a futuristic organisation trying to repair the timelines and save humanity.And to do that, you must.....stop six 18-30 somethings living in the north of drizzly England from dying in a housefire together. And to do THAT, you must.....reconcile their personal dramas?Eternal Threads is kind of fascinating in terms of the huge juxtaposition between the fantastical reason behind your actions, and the dreary, soap-opera mundanity of the problems your actions solve. You spend most of this game playing out scenes from the past, some of which are just dry, uninteresting conversations about weather, money, jobs etc, delivered in that quintessential British pedestrian cadence. It evokes a quote from Dr Who in me: "An ordinary man - that's the most important thing in creation."You play this game by selecting a scene in a house from a sprawling, flashy timeline that covers an entire week's events prior to the fateful housefire. When you activate an event, you watch the participants play out the scene as it happened XXX years ago. Some events are purely linear and informational. However, some events can be altered by forcing a housemate to make a different choice, which as you might expect can drastically alter future events, whether that's deleting them, adding new ones, or even adding new choices to scenes that previously just played out in linear fashion.I enjoyed this game very much from start to finish. I've seen complaints that the characters and stories are tedious and humdrum, but to be honest I think that's the point (see Dr Who quote). You can also tell from the credits screen that this game was made by a very small team on what was no doubt a small budget, so I think the decision to go for a simple, static environment for the story was the right call.Without spoilers, the game has a disgustingly cliffhangery ending that basically screams SEQUEL PROBS JOIN OUR SOCIALS but the game is not long enough for me to find this egregious. Overall, I heartily recommend if you enjoy mysteries, interactive novels, and Coronation Street.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, and you enjoy games with timeline shenanigans and temporal mystery, this game is for you. It's a tight little story with good voice acting.One real annoyance is that the movement on the stairs doesn't work the greatest. Now, that shouldn't be a deal breaker, but you will be annoyed when you can't walk up and down stairs fluidly, and you'll have to make that trip quite a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Threads is a single-player, first-person story-driven puzzle game of time manipulation, choice and consequence.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Threads

name: Half Past Fate
detailed_description: Love is in the air, but work, life, and spicy Ramen keep getting in the way! Half Past Fate is a rom-com adventure with a charismatic 3D pixel art style. Follow the journey of 6 ordinary people who found each other in extraordinary ways. From eight hours to eight years, this time-jumping saga will change the way you feel about fate forever. An inspiring and heartwarming slice-of-life story set in present day. Jump through time, witness how 6 people come together over a span of 8 years. Eat spicy ramen. Immerse in our familiar world through charming 3D pixel art visuals. Learn what's different between black tea and green tea. Change a flat tire. Relish in relatable stories about life, love, and the fate that brings us together. Cast Mara , the CEO and founder of Nanovolt, a struggling technology startup that's looking for funding. She finally locks down a major investor and prepares her final pitch... that is until she clashes with their VP, Rinden, the morning before the presentation. Rinden , investor and VP of Aurous. After immigrating to the United States, Rinden has always focused on investments in clean energy. He finally found the best startup to invest in, with the help of his business intern, Ana. Ana , 2nd generation Japanese & tea connoisseur. Growing up, Ana's always helped her parents' tea shop in Little Tokyo. However, at one fateful tea festival, she meets Jaren, a lost soul who wants nothing but learn more about what she's passionate for the most. Jaren , a dude who works at a retro game shop. After losing his connection with a girl at a tea festival, he puts on his detective hat, determined to find her again. Along the way, he makes new friends, learns about ramen, and even helps a stranger, Milo, change his flat tire. Milo , an aspiring film director who focuses on documentaries. While testing out his camera in the park, he meets his future best friend, Bia. Little did he know that their lives, for better or for worse, will be completely intertwined for the next 8 years. Bia , a Brazilian photography student who moved to the United States. Bubbly by nature, Bia tries to make friends wherever she goes, including even her friend's reserved sister, Mara. 4 years later, Bia would find out that their casual encounter at the theater has inspired Mara to create the future of our world.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game without knowing anything about it. The price on summer sale seemed alright and the game looked cute with it's art-style. I wasn't disappointed, I didn't expect much but after finishing it I can say this is really good game.Half Past Fate is a chill game, great if you want to sit back and relax. It offers a slice of life/romance story which is heartwarming and very enjoyable. My super manly cold heart of course didn't let me to shed a tear but i can see for some people this won't be the case. It probably will feel familiar to your life in some way at one point of another.There are six main characters and all of them are falling in love and must help them find that love. The story of all characters also intertwine at different points of the game and it's very well done. The game is fun from start to finish. Last chapter ended the game in the best way you could expect.The game has 12 chapters and each chapter takes place in a different timeline, it could be 8 hours ago or 8 years ago. You connect with each characters this way and you get to know them, their favorite things, hobbies and of course how they fell in love.While each character is different, has different background but they feel a bit too similar. I'm always for diversity and sure there is diversity, characters are of different ethnicities but that's not the kind of diversity i'm talking about. I wanted their character to be completely different like for example some side characters like that hippy guy, would've been nice to have someone like him there. Nevertheless character design is very good and it's fun learning about their life.Game has some humor, nothing to laugh your ass off, it's subtle and makes you smile but that's it.Gameplay is very basic but it's a good thing in this game, remember I said it's relaxing? That means I don't want any tedious, frustrating gameplay elements in such game and it delivers great gameplay.Each time you play as one of the six characters and have some kind of main task, it's pretty straightforward and easy, you run around, talk to people, pick up some things, give them to others or use them on something. Sounds like point&click game but it isn't, no puzzles, no thinking required.Besides main objectives you have some side stuff to do. Usually tied to achievements or just for learning some background about other characters (multiple non-playable characters appear on different chapters). They also have their own little stories often tied to mini-quests.Achievements are also very easy and since the game has chapter select you can't miss any. So a huge thank you to developers for adding chapter select and making all the actions required to do in multiple chapters to count without finishing the chapter or replaying the whole game. Thanks for thinking about us achievement hunters.This is a niche game, I doubt it sold much copies. I wish it had a gay couple to make things more interesting and appease to wider audience which would've helped to sell more copies because this game deserves to be played by more people. The game obviously is LGBT friendly which is clearly seen from multiple dialogues throughout the game while interacting with random characters but that's only couple of lines.The game also has that nostalgic atmosphere due to it's graphics and sounds. It feels kinda old but new at the same time which made me very happy.Graphics are very pretty, as I like to say - pixel art done right. I hate retro games with pixelated graphics, often developers go overboard and make it so minimalistic that it's hard to see things. Here it's done very well – retains that retro feeling and is pleasing to the eye.All the areas are really beautiful and are fun explore with lots of little details around. Overall graphics and art-style are gorgeous.I didn't expect a 2D game to support ultrawide and was prepared to play this in a window but to my surprise ultrawide works with the easiest fix you can imagine. Just put the resolution you want to play at in steam launch options and there you have it – perfectly working ultrawide. There are only couple of small issues. Sometimes some areas at the very edge of the screen might be hard to see and at the ending the text doesn't fit into the screen. Nevertheless i'm very pleasantly surprised.Music is done in a retro style too which again provides that nostalgic feeling. But it's pretty repetitive and gets old soon. Although it's not bad but i'd prefer more variety.There's no voice acting so there's nothing to talk about it. But this game doesn't need it anyway, would lose that nostalgic retro vibe instantly.I just wish the text wouldn't be pixelated, my eyes are often tired and sometimes it was tiring to read.Overall a wonderful game about love, being in love, finding love, being in those awkward situations, being hopeless, thinking another person will never answer you back with the same feelings. Buy it if you enjoy romantic stories and want a chill game. No, seriously guys this is one of those hidden gems, just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever just wondered if you were fated to be with your significant other or your destined soulmate hasn’t crossed your path? Waiting for that one day where you run into someone or randomly make eye contact and it all goes uphill from there? Or perhaps you just love romantic comedies and wish your life was more like one. Well, in Half Past Fate, it might as well be reality for the small town this game takes place in.In Half Past Fate, you follow three soon to be couples from different points of time throughout the game’s 12 chapters. You first join Rinden 12 hours in the past as he decides to get some tea as he waits for his business meeting to start. It so happens that he likes the barista working at his local cafe, though she doesn’t even know him, and he even has a blind date set up. However, right when he’s walking out a woman runs right into him, spilling his tea all over his suit. You soon find out this woman is Mara, a woman who is focused on making her invention a reality, but she needs to convince an investor to keep her startup company afloat. Of course, Rinden is the one she needs to convince. Next, you join Ana about a week in the past as she runs into Jaren at a Tea Festival. After finding out that Jaren, a guy that works at a retro game store, is new to the tea world, she takes him through each booth and decides to give him her number. However, Jaren smudged it and he sets off to track her down. Lastly, we go back a whopping eight years with Bia as she befriends Milo while she does her photography project. This soon blossoms to a crush from both sides, but both of them were never single at the same time.I’m sure that someone out there is worried over the story structure and trust me, I did too. Good thing is, the order works out. While everyone’s storyline happens at different times, they all start from when they first meet which is way better than choosing a seemingly random point. Then it goes from there as you come back at important milestones until you end at the present, which is the point where all of them are finally together. Not to mention that each chapter references another. It certainly helps that this takes place in the same town as you see the same characters popping up in other chapters and call backs. I certainly didn’t expect to meet the person that made a food documentary. You even get small cliffhangers in a couple that get resolved later on. That blind date Rinden mentions? You get to see how well it went. Half Past Fate is pretty easy to pick up. Each chapter more or less puts you in a new area for you to explore, talk to everyone you can, and examine everything to see what the character thinks. To progress through the story, you’ll basically be doing quick fetch quests as you locate an item another character needs to get information or another item so you can eventually get what you need. There are certain points where you need to figure out what to do, but it’s pretty easy to figure out what. Personally, this didn’t really bother me for the most part as I was more focused on finding out what happened next, talking to other characters, noticing all the references from other chapters, and exploring each area as I stared at the beautiful artwork. There was only one chapter where it didn’t fit in as well as the other chapters.Of course, the way the stories are told brings out negatives. Considering that we have three relationships fighting for space, I couldn’t help but think that one of them didn’t get much focus as the others. Each couple does have four chapters each, but it’s what is told within the chapter that makes it feel this way. Bia/Milo and Jaren/Ana chapters were more about they’re dynamic with each other and why you should root for them to eventually get together; while Rinden/Mara chapters are more focused on how they’re both focused on their business. I didn’t get any vibes that Rinden and Mara liked each other, more like Mara was only interested in Rinden giving her the investment she needs, despite both saying they find the other one cute. Sorry Rinden and Mara, I don’t think you guys would have normally stayed together.There are a decent amount of optional stuff you can do. Some of it are easy to run into them naturally, but the ones you can easily skip over can be seen through achievements. I don’t talk much about achievements, but Half Past Fate uses them well as you can use them to see what optional stuff you may have missed in a chapter. There are a couple multi-chapter achievements like finding all B.B. Bunnies, talking to a certain character, or finding the talking plant (yes I’m being serious). The chapter-based ones are more things that you probably missed or didn’t know you could do. Like the coffee creamer has one more interaction in Chapter 1 and you can actually figure out the problem with the printer in Chapter 5.To be honest, the only thing I expected from Half Past Fate was a cute game where you follow a few couples that are living out a rom-com scenario. It certainly delivered with it’s cute art style, upbeat music that never got old despite playing constantly, and a story where I could barely tear myself away long enough to eat before I went back to continue the story. While I do recommend Half Past Fate, I don’t to those who are expecting a dating sim or expecting a challenging puzzler as this is just a cute, relaxing, game that focuses on the journey the characters go on.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate

_childDocuments_.review: I am in disbelief in how the pixel art and animation for this game is so phenomenal and that at the same time the writing is so bland and aimless. The gameplay was uninspired fetch quests, but I'm okay with that because I play these games for the writing.Whether writing is good or bad is often subjective, but for the most part this game had little to no character or story development. Milo & Mara were the only characters that had any nuance. Most characters had similar personalities and their dialogue could be interchangeable. We don't learn much about the characters beyond what they do for work or what their hobbies are. For example: The character Ana was only playable in one chapter and all you're told is she likes tea, she used to work for her parents, and now she's an intern. Also, they never do anything with the concept of all the playable characters interconnecting. The game skips around time in a way that implies that all these couples stories are connected, but the character's connections to each other are minor and they never impact anything other than a few lines of dialogue. There was a few interesting story scenarios, but those were never really explored. Chapters often ended when things were finally getting  interesting. I love dialogue-heavy games and romance stories, but I cannot recommend this. Amazing presentation cannot save this game from its underdeveloped writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate

_childDocuments_.review: If you are an avid story game/visual novel enjoyer, I  recommend this one.Pros:- Cute and lively pixel sprites and art- Relaxing gameplay + pleasant musicCons:- It's short, I finished it in 5 hours. I wouldn't recommend it for the price, 100% wait for a sale- Writing suffers on an analytical level- Characters are bland (in my opinion)- It's me being nit-picky, but there is some inconsistencies with the portraits (since the game takes place over the span of 8 years, it did break my immersion when I unintentionally noticed some characters in the past wearing the same portraits as they did in the present.)I had honestly expected a little more with all the positive reviews but in sincerity, the overall game was just okay. It's a solid product, but there was more left to be desired.I lacked interest in majority of the characters as most of their conflicts and plot were circumstantial to their environments rather than about each character as individuals or even as couples. The amount of screen time for each individual also didn't feel very balanced out. Ex. As another reviewer had stated, Ana and Jaren's entire story was about Jaren chasing Ana down to obtain her number, which was comedic at times to read through, but did not amount to any sort of meaning for the central plot overall. Or in Milo and Bia's story, you're consistently with Bia for majority of their plotline compared to Milo, where he happens to be away for the most part.In short, It's a very simple, cute and relaxing atmospheric game. It's a good time-killer for a couple hours if you just need to wind down from a busy day, but that's about it. No compelling story, plot twists or exciting gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: If I have to be completely honest, at first glance the cute graphics absolutely appealed to me when I happen to stumble across Half Past Fate. Jumping into the game without any knowledge and expectations, I realized very soon that I will without a doubt enjoy this game. I guess it helps that I was always a fan of the "Fate" theme, that everything that is meant to be will find its way in one or another way. However, during that process, one sometimes has to overcome a lot of hurdles. But love is what makes all of it worth it in the end, doesn't it?Half Past Fate opens with Rinden who just wants to get some tea with his friend in the morning. Fortunately, the cashier happens to be a girl he is attracted to, the only problem here is that she doesn't even know that he exists. You see, Rinden isn't really good with girls and after finally shaking off the queue by fulfilling each customer's request, he finally manages to grab his tea although he fails to flirt with the cashier once again. This day couldn't get worse, until a mysterious but beautiful girl accidentally bumps into Rinden and along with this, spills her drink on his expensive suit.Rinden and the mysterious girl, however, aren't the only protagonists we will meet throughout Half Past Fate but there are six main characters in total available here that are playable as well. Since the whole game revolves around fate, it's evident that it means that the six protagonists are three couples that the player has to bring together with the help of destiny. I liked that this game didn't make it that easy for the couples to end up together but sometimes when a chapter ends I ended up getting frustrated because, as usual, there are a lot of unfortunate events that prevented them from knowing how the other felt.At first, I was slightly confused when the point of view changed with each chapter. Soon, I realized that there is actually a connection between each character, in one or another way, and they're all tied together. This made me feel excited when I happened to meet another character I was familiar with that showed up in another character's chapter. The thing I absolutely love about POV changes is that the player doesn't only know one side of the story, but the whole. This is especially important since Half Past Fate revolves around the feelings of the characters a lot. This way, I could understand their actions very well although I just wanted to avoid all the misunderstandings.And I was right, what is meant to be will always find its way! Although it's a long process, for some even years, I was so happy when misunderstandings finally get solved, characters can find each other and are finally becoming a real couple. Of course, a lot of comedy is available here as well that managed to lighten up the game a lot and kept me entertained until the end. An interesting feature here is that the game tells its story from a span of eight years ago until the current events. In the beginning, it was quite confusing to me when I jumped back and forth with the time, however, I got the gist of it pretty soon and a love story with a span of over eight years is pretty romantic, to say the least.Something that slightly annoyed me is that there is no way to save during a chapter. Luckily, a chapter doesn't last long and can be replayed anytime in the menu, yet I couldn't stop in the middle of playing. In total, there are twelve chapters available in Half Past Fate that revolve around all six different people. I found that many chapters are just hilarious and even though not all of them seem significant at first, I found that each of them was necessary so the player can understand the relationships between the characters better and along with that: Their feelings.Gameplay-wise, Half Past Fate is quite simple. When jumping into a new chapter I didn't know what to do but it became pretty clear when I interacted with a few objects or talked to various people. Each chapter is very linear and paying attention to the text is essential here. There are hints here and there so the player knows how to advance. The clue here is that the tasks are meant to be finished chronologically, so until the player interacted with a certain item or person, it's not possible to unlock the next task. Additionally, I liked that each chapter had a different theme, such as tea or games, that made the whole game very interesting to me.When it comes to the graphic, Half Past Fate is absolutely adorable. As aforementioned, the cute graphic is the first thing that I noticed about this game and I love the details the developers put into the game. When the player walks around familiar side-characters are walking around in the area although they cannot interact with some of them. Even when being inside buildings, there are a lot of different decorations or items the player can explore and some of them even unlock special achievements. Overall, I love the whole presentation of this game and the character sprites even have different facial expressions which greatly helped with the immersion.Half Past Fate turned out to be such a memorable game to me. Although each chapter turned out to be rather short, I felt like each of them was very meaningful and not a single one was unnecessary but greatly helped the player to understand the connection and relationship between each character. I have to admit I absolutely love the theme and message behind this game that revolves around fate and love. Luckily, there are even plenty of comedic moments that made the whole game even more entertaining. That being said, Half Past Fate is a wonderful rom-com game that warmed my heart during playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a perfect example of why there should be a thumbs in the middle option. If I had to pick one, then it's a thumbs down but still recommended if it's heavily discounted.- The graphical style, art, and character designs are all very good. Each of the eleven areas in the game are nicely drawn and convey the sense of a lived in world.- The story is told in a non-linear fashion, and it's done in a way that isn't confusing. There's twelve chapters, most of which take place over the course of a week, but a handful go back as far as eight years prior to the start of the game.- The technical writing is only average. That ordinarily wouldn't be a negative, but in a game that's purely story driven and lives or dies on the dialog, the technical writing just isn't good enough. There are a handful of funny lines and item descriptions, but a lot of the dialog feels unrealistic and stilted.- The narrative writing is mostly fine, but there are a ton of little nits that quickly add up. For instance, one of the main characters, Ana, is a marketing intern at an investment firm, but she's somehow allowed to attend high level business meetings and even speaks at them. And then you have a character like Jaren, who is without a doubt one of the most blatant writer self inserts I've ever seen in a game. To briefly summarize him, he's an unattractive geeky gamer who works at a video game store and doesn't have much romance luck. While being (unfairly) accosted at a festival, a cute Japanese girl approaches him, defuses the situation, offers to show him around the festival, and gives him her number and asks him to call her. You then spend Jaren's chapters trying to find her after he accidentally ruins the piece of paper she wrote her number on, all the while selflessly helping people. He's not a Marty Stu, but his character and story is blatant self-insert wish fulfillment for one of the developers.- This won't bother some people, but it bothered me because it's very bad writing - the developers wear their political beliefs on their sleeves, with characters openly lecturing the player about the virtues of things like "green" energy without being challenged. There are dialog segments in the game that are written as finger wagging lectures, and they're all awful.- The gameplay gets repetitive fast. It's adventure game style gameplay without puzzles, meaning that it's entirely a series of fetch quests. For example, in one section, you need to find someone who can read Japanese. But he can't read without his glasses, so you need to find someone who'll lend you a pair. But to get the glasses, you need to find a lost object and bring it to the person. The entire game is structured like this, so if you don't like what I just described, you won't like this game at all.This isn't a bad game by any means, and the boring gameplay isn't saved by stellar or even above average writing. I think it's still worth a shot if you can get it on sale for cheap because the story concept and the way it's told is nicely done, but overall, this is an example of a good idea with extremely mediocre execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? It is an adventure with very easy puzzles, more focused on the story. A bit like a visual novel looking and playing like a point'n'click adventure. The story is very lighthearted as well, it is a story about love and fate, how some little coincidences can change your life. It is about 6 complete different people that accidentially meet over the years. The game is divided into chapters, playing at different times and where you control different characters - until it all comes together. The graphic is quite unique, beautiful pixel-art and a kind of 2D paper-cut characters. Plays fine with m+kb or controller. Really recommended if you like casual stories - and tea.

_childDocuments_.review: Half Past Fate is a wholesome rom-com about six really dorky people. Half Past Fate follows 3 would-be couples across 12 chapters. Depending on how fast you read and how much you want to explore, you can run through the game in about 4 or so hours. This may sound kind of short for a game with a $20 price tag, but Half Past Fate proves the old adage of quality over quantity. This isn't the type of game that will make you ball your eyes out while instilling some existential crisis, but it  the type of game that'll keep you smiling until the very end. The writing is snappy, wholesome, and, downright adorable, with moments of honesty and humor sprinkled throughout. I'd call it junkfood-style writing, writing that will pick you up and heal you after a tough day.And with a plague currently threatening to eat the world, well, hey, I think some lovey-dubby writing is much needed. The core gameplay loop is essentially a fetch quest marathon. You need Object A from Character X, but first you need to get Item B for Person Y, who won't help you until you get Thing C from Dude Z, and so on. This might be a problem in a longer game, but I can say with honesty that I never found myself bored in the 4 or so hours I spent with Half Past Fate. Some chapters are definitely stronger than others (Jaren and Ana are definitely the highlights in terms of gameplay variety and cuteness), but the game loop is serviceable enough to keep your entertained as you make your way through the story. The game's not hard, and you will likely never be stuck trying to work out a puzzle solution, but I think that's fine. The reason we're really here is for the sappy romance, after all.Most of the background characters have a surprising amount of depth to their dialogue, meaning they can be spoken to multiple time for different results. You should definitely talk to every character a few times to get the full experience! Many of the set pieces can be interacted with to receive extra commentary from our main cast, too, which really gives a sense of life to exploration. Beautiful pixel art and a variety of set pieces act as a lovely backdrop to the action. There's a sort of homely feel to the game's art style; it invokes a real sense of comfort in moments of exploration. The sprite work is charming and packs an impressive amount of contextual animation to boot, which really helps the minute-to-minute progression of the story shine. The weakest part of the game. There are maybe five songs in the entire game? Each of the tracks are decent enough, but it can start to get repetitive towards the end. Nothing really stands out in this department, which is something of a missed opportunity. Given that we have six main characters, I'm surprised the developers didn't opt for unique themes for any of the cast members; more distinct music would have helped the chapters stand apart from one other. It's not a deal breaker by any means, but definitely an area of design that could have been improved. There's something for everyone between the 3 couples. As alluded to above, Jaren and Ana are a personal highlights for me. I'm writing this section just because I love them. They're easily the biggest dorks in the game, and I think their chapters have the strongest writing. Bia and Milo share a painfully relatable arc that I think anyone who's ever crushed hard on someone can attest to, while Rinden and Mara's struggles really drive home some of the problems of modern dating. No matter your past victories or failures in the field of love, I think it's easy to find something that rings true to you amongst the cast. Half Past Fate is an adorable, healing game about love. I highly recommend it to anyone going through a rough spot in life right now, or for anyone who just wants to spend a couple of happy hours smiling. It's video game junkfood, and I mean that in the most complimentary way possible.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a simple retro-style adventure game with a lovely story to follow. I love how detailed the developers built the universe in the game, we'll know by the end of the game how every story connects and influences each other. Not to mention all the small tidbits of the side characters that are also fun to discover along the game. And I like the aesthetics of this game too, this is one of the most beautiful pixel-style game I've ever played.I'd love to see another game like this again made by Serenity Forge, but next time I want a more branched storyline that give the players options to choose how the story go and discover many different endings.
