_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game because I liked the art style, and the environments are beautiful to walk about in, but as much as I tried to like it I just can't recommend it.Maybe my review might be a little skewed as I had initially thought this was a 'choices matter' kind of game, but it is in reality a very straight forward linear visual novel, and the 'puzzles' devolve to simple fetch quests.This would all be fine however:>The characters are pretty bland and unlikeable (maybe just personal opinion...)I get that it's supposed to be a wholesome game, but the way everyone is so...cordial with each other is kind of unrealistic and 'fake smile'-ey. Humans can have flaws and can still be wholesome at the same time.>Writing is lacking, with lots of inconsistencies with the characters themselvesE.G Ana is shown to be a huge tea snob herself, but doesn't like when others 'gatekeep' tea, she doesn't like games/nerds but immediately is all gushy at meeting the resident gamer nerd (Jaren)>Writing comes off offensive sometimes evenE.G Coffee + Tea mixture being snubbed at then described as watered down coffee, when it is a well-known drink enjoyed in many parts of AsiaE.G I didn't like how the game made it like we were meant to root for a 3rd wheel vs an engaged couple (spoilers: It's Bia)>Considering how most of the game is fetch quests/fidning people to exhaust dialogue options, I wish the characters walked faster/had a run buttonTBH I wish there was a 'mid' option so I didn't have to give a thumbs down, but I feel like the Very positive reviews don't accurately reflect this game's standing against other similar VN/Point and Click type games , so here's to balancing out a bit.Get the game heavily discounted if you enjoy walking about the lovely pixel art environments, but not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game where you follow three >soon to be couples< in 12 chapters.  Just know that you wont get ALL of their POV s (Point of Views)...  Just selected ones.  Also, you have to do an entire chapter in one sitting...  There is no Mid-Chapter save.  Yep.The game-play itself is like this: observe, talk, find what to do...  Whether it be sampling tea stalls or fixing a car.  There are hidden things to do as well and don't worry if you miss something --> you CAN replay Chapters later.Is it heart throbbing?  So romantic that it makes you clutch at your chest?  Nope.  I laughed once or twice, (it's hard to please me...) but otherwise I didn't really get attached to anyone.  I mean...  I was happy for them to find someone...  But otherwise it was like watching a story play out on the screen.  There wasn't anything overly dramatic or lewd, so it's just...  Peaceful I guess?Perhaps if we got to know the characters more it would be a little different?I don't like Mara.  Especially at the restaurant Chapter.  Rinden looks and feels like he is a sweety...  But he shouldn't let a woman like that kick him down.  And that waiter...  I will forgive the waiter...  Only because she had no idea what was going on.  But Mara...  She didn't even let Rinden do much of anything!  She even drove the boat!  Okay, okay...  I will ease up: IF RINDEN...  IS into this kind of a thing?  Fine.  Otherwise he needs someone...  Better.Ana and Jaren...  Yeah, I like those two.  If I knew more about them, I probably would like them more.Bia and Milo...  Alright.  I got no special attachment to them...  Except...  What happened to PEANUT?!Also this game has a lot of diverse characters.  It's a big city, so that makes sense.  There are also some "lessons" provided...  Like recycle or "else the Earth will die"...  And I swear...  That "Hippie" and what he said near the movie theater...  I am not going to comment on it...That's pretty much it.  I came, I played, it distracted me.  Thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Visual style, my number one reason of buying this game. The good balance of pixel art and 3D, as well as the pleasing color palette + Characters. Even though they seem silly, they all have unique and interesting personalities, along with cute character design.+ Dialogues. They are not boring or cringy, I really tried to speak to every character, including NPCs, just to see their reactions.+ Atmosphere. Game gives you really warm and cozy atmosphere of modern life. Coffee shop, festival, compact office, everything that you can relate to and yet that brings joy to interact with in the game.+ Overall, it is just relaxing. Good replacement for rom-coms that you watch to cheer up when you want to forget about an awful day. Engaging story, with a little bit of drama and lots of moments that will make you: awwww :D Cons:- No ability to skip dialogues. I just misclicked several times and was forced to go over some of the long dialogues. You can skip each replica, but not the whole dialogue, or at least I couldn't find that.- Unnecessary quests. Some quests didn't make any sense for me and gave an impression that they were added just for the sake of being there. But that's just my opinion

_childDocuments_.review: I already feel like a monster, but here it goes...I'm a sucker for multiple stories coming together across time and space (preferrably in a big city): I loved the hell out of Durarara!!!, Valhalla still remains one of my favourites, and Ever17 is so dear to my heart that I dare not speak of it. Even more minor projects like Quantum Suicide and Coffee Talk got my seal of approval.HPF, unfortunately, does not quite live up to the titles I've just listed. In no particular order: the timejumps are contrived and confusing (I don't really see why the story couldn't be told in a chronological order), the plotlines and characters !feel! way too numerous, and while the gameplay itself is passable (I just wish there was more than 1 music track), the end result is... literally one big Meh.I'm one hell of a sappy simp, but even I found nothing to care about here.Maybe it just feels rushed and unearned? Maybe focusing on just 1 plotline would be a better idea? ~O~ Beats me.(also, for the love of whoever's up in Heaven, is it possible to be less preachy and in-the-face about things? Please?..)

_childDocuments_.review: Link to review - Tl;dr - I sadly can’t recommend Half Past Fate. The basic idea underlying could have been enjoyable, but hamfisted writing intent on showcasing unrealistic cordiality ruined it from the get-go. Combine that with amiable yet undistinctive characters, a gimmicky timeskip blueprint, and tedious fetch quests galore and you have something that isn’t a fun experience. Though I always say support indie developers, I can’t approve a game I didn’t have fun with. Even if I did, you’ll only get a little over 7 hours worth of enjoyment from a $20 product, which falls under my $1 : 30 minute ratio.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love it! It's a really sweet series of stories that turn out to be all connected in the end. The story revolves around six main characters. It's a delight to see how they end up with each other: Rinden & Mara, Ana & Jaren, and Bia & Milo. Despite my complaints, I really did adore this game. _childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so manly, it turned me into a motherloving bear. Do you need to hear anything else, punk?While it's a little hard to type with my new claws, let me elaborate a bit. It's a RPG Rom-Com, that much is probably clear. And that by itself, while somewhat innovative, is not the reason why I'm recommending it. It's the sum of its parts, which are executed very well. The RPG part is simple. You play as one of six characters during a given event, which is a part of a greater whole. All the stories are connected, but let's focus on the gameplay for now. It plays a little like a point and click. Do this, talk to this person, in order to achieve this, which ultimately serves to progress the story. It's all well made, well explained, and lovingly executed. All puzzles, all dialogue, all animations are very pleasant and it's one part of what makes the game so fun. Oh yeah, have you seen the graphics? Great stuff.Then, there's the Rom-Com part. Maybe you're not really into romance, which is fine, and then the game is probably not for you. If you're ambivalent, read on. All characters are very believable and relatable. They're quintessential millenials, well, minus the existential dread I guess. There are six protagonists, and they're all well fleshed out and you really want to root for them. On top of that, there's a huge cast of NPCs, out of which many (all?) repeat and the game makes a point of letting you know they're the same people. From one perspective, the girl at the stall is just a saleswoman, but from another, this same girl is a friend and a coworker. This adds a lot of life to the game and makes the world even more believable. Alright, enough of this typing, I'm going to scratch my back against a tree now. And you should get this game! It's great.

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively short but cute game, a bit reminiscent of older 8-bit RPGs. Visually, the pixel art is charming and the character designs are nice. The color palette is lovely, and I found the subtle touches in things like the walking animations very nice (for some reason I was particularly in love with Bia's walking animation).As for play and story, it's more of a simple puzzle game where you're sort of along for the ride of the story. It follows the various stages of a new romance, and you can also follow the relationships of some of the NPCs. It was fun to try to spot the various NPCs in the chapters and discover their relationships to each other. The characters are generally well-rounded. The game doesn’t go too in-depth into their lives and personalities, but you get enough to make them feel distinct and to make you feel like they could be real people (I personally was very amused by Mara’s complete inability to not blurt out her nervous worries).The dialogue generally felt pretty natural, and the flavour text could at times be pretty amusing. The music is simple but pleasant and not too distracting. I liked that it seemed to have a source within the level, so going in and out of different areas would affect the way it sounded (such as getting quieter or louder as you entered and exited buildings).I only had a couple real issues with the game. First, a pretty minor tech issue: I had two instances where the game did not properly checkpoint and so a chapter would not show up in the chapter select, meaning I'd have to play the chapter before the one I wanted as well. The second issue was more distracting for me. I found it kind of strange that, while there are several LGBTQ couples within the game, all of the main couples whose stories you follow are hetero couples (and by all accounts appear to all be cisgender). I appreciated the LGBTQ representation, but it just felt like a disappointing decision to me to confine that representation to the background.Overall, it’s a sweet little game that doesn’t take long to get through, so I’d suggest checking it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much. It's adorable and heartwarming. The characters are likeable, the art style is stunning, and is some of the most beautiful pixel art I've ever seen. The achievements are also fun to aim for, as there's a lot of things you can miss. The music is good, but it does get a bit repetitive. My only other "complaint" is that I wish it was longer, because I enjoyed it so much. If you want a comfy, relaxing, short, and memorable game to play, this is perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:First-rate writing. Not just the dialog and story but all the myriad descriptions of people and things.First-rate pixel-art. Character design and animation are all top-notch.Low frustration levels. Puzzles in each level were just challenging enough to keep you engaged in the story.Excellent multicultural representation and inclusion. You also get to see the different concerns of different types of idealistic, enthusiastic people. From the artist couple (documentary filmmaker and photographer) to the retails sales couple (a game store employee and tea expert) to the tech start up people (start-up CEO and investment group rep).The meh:Sometimes environmental themes can come across as a tad heavy-handed, but it fit with the story well.If you're looking for same sex romance, you'll find it on the periphery here, but not among the protagonists.The bad:The "find the rabbit before you can save" system is unnecessary. _childDocuments_.review: Half Past Fate is a delightful little game with a pixelated retro-style to it. The game follows a charming cast of characters in a non-chronological sequence, allowing you to guess and be surprised at the appearance or relationships between characters. The setting is often bustling, busy, bright and cartoonish, yet has a sort of small town feel to it with how friendly the characters that populate the world are, as well as how often they appear within each others' lives.You play three different couples and experience how they meet and get to know one another, hence the whimsical name 'Half Past Fate'. The characters are all very diverse with different races, sizes, sexuality and personality, which gives a realistic feel to the game and yet still manages to keep a bright and cheerful tone. The puzzles in the game are also rather straightforward, if you get stuck it doesn't take too long to get unstuck. There are even quite a number of secret achievements you can obtain in the game based on how you interact with things.All in all, Half Past Fate is a cute game for those who enjoy bright, wholesome content.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. As a rookie pixel artist, everything about the game's presentation amazes me and really warms my heart with its very unique atmosphere and graphics. I would even say that it was a perfect blend of 2D and 3D graphics. The game also has a very good soundtrack, it always captures the feel of the moment perfectly.I want to get into my appreciation of the game characters and story, but something that I haven't seen people point out in this game is the AMAZING and sublime LGBTQ+ representation. Before playing, I saw the premise of the game and was not even remotely expecting anything but heterosexual couples, but the couples' diversity really makes me feel like this is the most wholesome experience I ever had in a game. This is representation done correctly and more people should be addressing it! If any queer fellas end up reading this, I really think you should give a shot at the game just to experience the great inclusivity this game has. Now on the gameplay side, the video I saw that made me wanna buy the game refered in a humoristic way the amount of glitches this game has (and it showed plenty of them). I can't fully relate to the experience, because it did happen to me (in the tires chapter I got stuck in a corner next to a truck and I had to restart that chapter), but it could've happened in any other game. The game is short and I wasn't expecting a very deep character development, but it is true that the characters lack depth. You barely get to know anything about them, but I think it works because the game's storytelling is putting puzzle pieces together that lead up to the present - and I must admit that only halfway I understood what was going on, because the way the events are presented to you are very confusing. Time leaps like a chapter is "4 days ago" and the next one is "8 years ago". In the beginning I wasn't really understanding the dynamics of it lol.I could mention that the main couple's plot  wasn't very good.  . But I could see why they worked out in the end, so it doesn't bother me much. The ending was very wholesome and I was too sentimental to think of anything else haha.This was a very fun experience! And I loved how Serenity Forge included a cameo of everyone (?) that took a part on the project with their own characters (and personal stories)! I will look forward to more of their projects from now on.(This was my first game review ever, hope I got my point across!)

_childDocuments_.review: On the positive side, it's a beautiful game, really cute and wholesome. For some reason, it went through the step-by-step instructions of how to change a tire, and I wasn't even bored during it! The game has its charms, for sure!However, it felt like extremely superficial and simplistic storytelling and it just didn't deliver on that aspect. It does not feel like I actually got to know these people and their romances, and sometimes the game framed things in ways that I simply didn't agree with - immediately getting angry at someone , yelling at and then throwing a drink at this person felt like a weird and bad reaction to me, and that happened two in-game hours before these two characters had their romantic high point in game. That couple died for me with that fight, so that put a sour taste in my mouth for the end of the game. Another couple barely gets to interact, so they still feel like strangers to each other by the end.The game survives its storytelling weakness by being pretty to look at, and NPCs occasionally have interesting things to say, but overall this game was disappointing to me. It seems like the best love stories might be lived by NPCs.On the puzzles, some of them were fun, some of them felt empty to me, like it was just a "we need another puzzle / fetch quest in this chapter" deal where something was squeezed in for filler.So, overall, I didn't really enjoy playing this, and I wasn't invested in these love stories while I played, which was the big problem. _childDocuments_.review: Half Past Fate is a console ported 2.5D retro pixel hybrid adventure game/Choose Your Own Adventure e-book with a romance theme as you must dating sim your way through a number of relationships over various time jumps.  Yawn. Needless to say this is badly written and in many cases downright cringey.  How do we know it's badly written?  Because if they could write professionally this would be on bookshelves and not self-published on Steam Direct with some bolted on adventure game gameplay. A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers.Because this is primarily a console game, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.Finally there's the problem of the eye watering $20 USD price tag on a retro pixel console game, clearly just a cash grab at that level of pricing.  For comparison, $20 USD would get you games like Euro Truck Sim 2 or Risk of Rain 2... or this trash e-book pretending to be a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this one! The characters and their stories were very cute, and the narrative of lives intersecting across time was neat. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game awhile back on Switch, but decided to pick it up again during a sale on PC. Reliving it was so nice and I truly adore the style of this game's narrative. The story has good pacing in my opinion, and it does such a good job of introducing you to the full cast, their individual past's, and their connections to each other, ALL without being overwhelming. Each character is pretty unique and I could see anyone finding someone to relate to. While a lot of dialogue is cheesy, and I kind of dislike how pushy all side characters are about love (every NPC bringing up dating & love, every cast's friend constantly trying to bring up dating) solely because it feels too unrealistic and bizarre, I still love the overall story a lot and the main cast themselves :) However, I get the idea that the story of the game is meant to make you see how any little event or interaction can turn into something meaningful, too. So perhaps they just hammered that in a little too hard for me, but I think its a nice message.I also feel the story is just interactive enough to stay interesting! I really like the gameplay, even though it's just fetch quests haha. It keeps me engaged. There's little replayability because the story is overall always the same, which is a downside especially for achievements. It's unlikely to get every achievement on a first run, but it's boring to replay.

_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate

_childDocuments_.review: A cute short game. I've played the spin-off before I actually played the main game and it was fun to recognise some of the characters who got their own stories in the spin-off! The pastel pixel art style was enough to draw me in in combination with the promise of some adorable meet-cutes and inevitable love stories. I loved getting to know the characters and their personal lives. I think my favourite romance out of all of these might have been Jaren and Ana. How they met and the way Jaren continued to put in effort to pursue Ana stole my heart. I think it was also cleverly done how the characters all linked up to each other in some way. _childDocuments_.review: Half Past Fate is a delightful rom com adventure about missed and rediscovered connections, following six interconnected characters over a period of several years in a chronologically asynchronous storyline.The core gameplay loop is fairly simple and intuitive. In each level, you take the role of one of the characters and have to discover the story by interacting with NPCs and doing various tasks until you meet a goal, in a pay-it-forward chain of quests that fall like dominoes until they're all complete. The game is entirely linear, and there are no real choices in this, but  the writing is good enough that you don't mind as you explore the world and the characters in it. I would say the presentation is very reminiscent of the investigation phase of Ace Attorney games with shades of To the Moon, if you're familiar with those.Each character is well written, and they all have interesting motivations and memorable personalities that endear themselves to you over time, though some are admittedly more likable than others. My favorite by far is Bia, the somewhat pollyanna-ish Brazilian immigrant with a passion for photography and a penchant for romance and altruism (sometimes to her detriment). However even the characters that come off as somewhat more abrasive, namely Mara and to a lesser extent Ana and Rinden, ultimately prove themselves to be good-hearted people who care about those around them and want the best for people, and show that love can affect them as much as any of the others. All six of the PCs are likable, and the NPCs are generally interesting as well.The game has a lovely aesthetic that makes the most of the pixel graphics to show a vibrant and well-constructed world with plenty of detail to be explored, with descriptive writing to match it and help accentuate it. One of my favorite bits is in one of the early levels when Ana explores a tea festival, and we get to explore both the myriad world of tea (something I personally enjoyed as a bit of an aficionado myself) while also coloring it through her perspective to show both more detail in the world and use it as an expression of her personality. The game is in general very good at this. The music is similarly chirpy, cheerful, and catchy, helping set the tone of the game well.One final note I want to express is how happy I am with the level of representation in this game. The characters come from a wide range of ethnic and national backgrounds, and with a decent amount of LGBT representation through the cast (though mainly the supporting cast). All of this is handled in a fairly cosmopolitan manner, normalizing relations with people of widely varying backgrounds. Considering the other forms of representation, I do wish there might have been more disabled representation, but overall I appreciate that the creators of the game made a decent attempt to be inclusive with their storytelling.All in all I thoroughly enjoyed this experience. The writing was delightful, the characters are likable,  the art design is charming, and the game design itself is engaging. For a roughly 8-10 hour experience of this quality I think $20 is a reasonable price, and getting it on sale is a no-brainer. I can highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys adventure games and visual novels, the romance genre, and just feel-good stories in general.

_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate

_childDocuments_.review: It's like an ensemble rom-com in videogame form. Think Love, Actually but much less witty/funny and much more wholesome. It's almost like these characters are addicted to being nice to each other and life always rewards them accordingly. Not realistic in any way, sometimes even too preachy and sugary but pleasant nonetheless.There are no real puzzles to solve or decisions to make, you just click through this short, feel-good narrative about people with loosely interconnected lives who just happen to stumble upon their soulmates. The art is very cute and the music is catchy but with very limited variety so you'll end up tuning it out after an hour.Decent little "game" but it could benefit from some smarter, punchier writing and maybe a few puzzles that don't literally spell out the solutions for you.6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Played the whole game yesterday and figured I should go ahead and review it before I play it again. I ADORED this game. The storyline was cute and sometimes cheesy, but cheesy is good when it's a rom com! None of the tasks were too difficult for me to figure out, which helped me focus on the story but still have an immersive experience. However, there are a lot of achievements to get, which encourages you to interact with the entire environment and talk to every character. I foresee myself getting a ton of replay out of this game, first for all of the achievements, but then just to watch the story play out again and again (just as I tend to rewatch my favorite rom coms over and over again). It is on the shorter side: it took me 4.7 hours to finish, which I can see as both a positive and a negative. For the price, if you only play it once, less than 5 hours of gameplay is not ideal. However, the plot does not drag out as it would if the game had been longer. Also, it is not a lofty task if you want to replay the game, you just need a free evening. My biggest issue would be that the chapters are not divided between the characters evenly. With 12 chapters and 6 characters, I expected each character to get 2 chapters. Some of the characters only had 1 chapter, leaving me to feel like I was missing out on getting to know those characters, especially given that one of them doesn't have their own chapter until almost the end of the game! I did enjoy all of the chapters, I just wish I would have seen more from some of the characters.It is clear to see how much time, effort, and love was put into the making of the game. I am excited to see what else the Serenity Forge team puts out!I could keep writing, or . . . I could play Half Past Fate again. If you like sweet, wholesome stories, you should play it too!

_childDocuments_.review: Half Past Fate is a really cute point-an-click style story about romance. You follow 6 people over the course of the timeline as they make connections (and miss connections) in one another's lives. The story, for some of the characters, starts 8 years prior to the "now" within the game, as the game slowly sets the stage for the events of the day through a series of flashbacks. As you wander through each chapter, you run into the other 6 characters, or friends/relatives of those characters. Sometimes, not even realizing it until later in the game. For example, .Serenity Forge also creatively inserts their team throughout the game, again, something that doesn't become obvious until the end, which was a creative way to credit their team (and something that I paid more attention to than I typically would with end credits).The "puzzles" within the game are pretty intuitive. I only got briefly stuck on progression at two points (both in chapters with Jaren), but didn't need to look up any walk through. I was able to figure both out after looking at everything in the chapters and paying attention to the additional clues in Jaren's responses. Even with having played through the game entirely in 5 hours, there are still 4 regular and 11 hidden achievements that I haven't discovered (despite looking at every item I could; chances are I didn't engage all the talking dialogue or have some items interact with each other). Definitely recommended for people who like slice-of-life games.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that makes you smileWhile games are (generally) meant to befun, they also usually deal with dark topics: violence, trauma, conflict, in a variety of setting that range from fallen utopia to full-fledged dystopia or a dark veil put unto our mundane world. From gritty realistic visuals to cutesy pixels, no genre is spared from this.Half Past Fate is none of that. It's a slice of happiness about several people whose fates and loves intertwine and who all look for better future, not only for themselves, but for everyone as a rule.It's relentlessly optimistic and offers a breath of fresh air, leaving you with a positive outlook towards life, and what drives (or should drive) each individual.Its colorful graphics, mixing 2D sprites for characters and lo-poly 3D for the environnement, are reminescent of the Playstation era and helps convey the joyfullness I described above. The music,also light-tuned, is fairly enjoyable, albeit kinda repetive in the course of each chapter.Sure, the game is highly linear and short (expect something like 6-8H if you're trying to go everywhere), the few "collectables" thrown at you are hardly a reason to attempt a new playthrough. But think of it as a sweet: a short tasteful sugar rush that gives a jolt of pleasure well deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a visual novel romantic comedy. There is a small element of role play in that you have some choice to some of the decisions your character makes (and your character perspective changes in each chapter), however, your actions don't seem to change the story significantly. It's a very non-linear story, with cute pixel art, and I think it would be more fun as a game if the story was scrapped and it was just experiencing city life in this world they've created because the aesthetic is quite charming. The general goodwill of everyone you meet stretched my suspension of disbelief. As a visual novel, it's fine. I would not recommend this as an "RPG" though. My first playthrough, I got through about 50% of the achievements. I'm probably not going to go back and play again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very cute and wholesome, but I expected just a little bit more out of it. It's a pretty relaxing game; the chapters are really fun to go through because there's so much to explore. I t was fun to learn stuff about tea. While the characters are pretty fine, I felt that they could have more character development. However, the game is actually pretty short so it wasn't possible to carry out a lot of character development for the main characters. I feel that Jaren, Rinden and Mara(chapter 12 changed my opinion on her) are written pretty well, while Ana, Milo and Bia could use some more work. Another thing that I didn't really like was not having the option to save your progress midgame.The concept of this game is fate, and they carried out this concept pretty well -- the characters have connections with each other. (Even the side characters have involvement, which is a really good job.) Jaren's quest to find Ana is my most favourite part of the game. The graphics are also very well done. (It was one of the reasons this game attracted me in the first place!) Final verdict : Story : 4.5/5Characters(main cast) :3.5/5 Graphics : 5/5Music : 4/5 (pretty relaxing, but could be better)Gameplay : 5/5 All in all, I recommend this game, but wait for a sale or something. _childDocuments_.review: I don't remember how I came across this game, but I'm glad I did. Once I started playing it, I just wanted to keep going. It was a lot like binge-watching a short, interactive series.What makes this game so engaging for me is the element of discovering how characters and events are connected to each other. I simply couldn't help wanting to /know/, which pretty much led to me playing and finishing the bulk of the game in one sitting. That goes without saying that the gameplay is very simple (with aspects of puzzle/mystery-solving), and I would recommend it to anyone who just wants to play a feel-good type of game.One more thing that I love about this game are the graphics. _childDocuments_.review:
Half Past Fate is a romantic narrative-adventure game about three relationships that form either over the span of eight hours or eight years.

Follow the adventures of six people who stumble their way through love and companionship in a hybrid 3D pixel-art world. Lead them through their daily struggles, quirky events, and life-changing decisions. Featuring a full cast of diverse characters with contrasting personalities, Half Past Fates takes you through intersecting stories over varying timespans that show how love can grow and develop in unexpected ways.
